issues.title: Late sub-agent completion is attributed to an ended parent turn: Desktop synthesizes a phantom turn, transcript goes out of order, and "Continuing goal…" blocks sending

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### Summary

When a sub-agent turn finishes after the parent turn that started it has ended, core emits the `SubAgentActivity { kind: completed }` item with the old parent turn id. It does not use the parent's turn that is currently running. Three layers then act on that stale id, and each one makes it worse:

1. **Core**: emits `item/started` and `item/completed` for a turn that has already completed or failed. `codex_analytics::reducer` logs `dropping sub-agent activity tool count update: missing turn state`, which is the symptom already reported in #43221.
2. **`thread_history` projection**: the old turn still exists, so nothing is dropped. The item is **upserted into the completed turn** and persisted with a new `rollout_ordinal`. This differs from #35304, where the turn id is unknown and the item is dropped.
3. **Desktop renderer**: in a long paginated thread the old turn is usually not loaded. `item/started` then takes the `synthesizeMissingTurn` path and **appends a phantom `inProgress` turn with the old id at the tail of the live island**. This phantom becomes the "latest/control turn". When a later `thread/turns/list` page brings in the real (completed) turn, the renderer merges it into the phantom entity under the same `turn:<id>` key. The old turn's full content (final answer, edited-files card) **now renders at the bottom, below the turn that is actually running**. Because the control turn is now `completed` while the server thread is still `active` and the goal is `active`, the composer refuses to send: **"Cannot send message — Continuing goal…"** (`composer.submit.threadGoalContinuation`).

What the user sees: the transcript freezes on an old final answer, newer progress ends up above it, so the order looks scrambled, and new messages are blocked. The agent keeps working normally on the server.

#43221 described the root event and treated it as analytics-only. This report shows that the same event also corrupts persisted thread history and the desktop transcript, and blocks the composer.

### Environment

- Codex Desktop for Windows `26.1120.6357.0` (`app.asar` package.json `26.1120.50957`), bundled `codex-cli 0.171.0-alpha.13.2`
- Source checked at tag `rust-v0.171.0-alpha.13.2` (`ad9d659a`). The core lines below are unchanged on `main` at `8cae463a` (2026-11-28).
- Windows 11, local host, `history_mode = paginated`, `/goal` thread with `multi_agent` v2 sub-agents, approval `never`

### Timeline from one affected thread (UTC; ids truncated)

| Time | Source | Event |
|---|---|---|
| 01:41:58 | parent rollout | parent turn **A** `01a21fd0` starts (goal continuation) |
| 01:43:10 / 01:43:18 | child rollouts | child turns start with `turn_attribution.parent_turn_id = A` (`/root/eval`, `/root/training`) |
| 02:00:05 | parent rollout | turn A **completed**; turn B runs 02:00:05–02:15:25; turn **C** `01a21fef` starts 02:15:25 and is still `inProgress` |
| 04:21:53.347 | child rollout | `/root/eval` child `task_complete` |
| 04:21:53.408 | parent rollout, ordinal 7554 | `item_completed` `SubAgentActivity` id `subagent-completed-01a21fd2-1054…`, **`turn_id` = A** (lines before and after carry turn C) |
| 04:21:53.409 | desktop log | `warning [host-app-server-manager] Synthesizing missing turn for incoming event conversationId=01a21de5… turnId=01a21fd0…` |
| 04:22:06 | `logs_2.sqlite` | `WARN codex_analytics::reducer dropping sub-agent activity tool count update: missing turn state … turn_id=01a21fd0…` |
| 04:40:33.778 | parent rollout, ordinal 7894 | second late completion (`/root/training`), again `turn_id` = A. No new warning: the phantom turn already exists. |
| 04:40:07–04:42:51 | desktop log | 20+ `thread/turns/list` calls for this thread (history paging) |

`thread_history_1.sqlite` afterwards: turn A has `rollout_ordinal 3768`, `rollout_end_ordinal 4145`, `status completed`, yet it owns items at ordinals **7554 and 7894**. Turn C (`inProgress`, starting at 4420) holds everything else up to 7967. The rollout itself is clean: 7,971 lines, contiguous ordinals, no timestamp regressions.

### Source / decompilation chain

**1. Core keeps the parent turn id captured at child-turn start, and emits into it later without checking it.**

- `parent_turn_id` is the sender's `turn.sub_id` at send time ([`multi_agents_v2/message_tool.rs#L73-L74`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/multi_agents_v2/message_tool.rs#L73-L74)). It is stored once in a `OnceLock` ([`turn_metadata.rs#L343-L351`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/core/src/turn_metadata.rs#L343-L351)) and copied into `AgentTurnOutcome` when the child turn ends ([`session/mod.rs#L2888-L2892`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs#L2888-L2892)).
- `notify_parent_of_terminal_turn` passes that id straight to `emit_sub_agent_activity` ([`agent/control/completion.rs#L51-L90`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/core/src/agent/control/completion.rs#L51-L90)).
- `LocalAgentControl::emit_sub_agent_activity` sends `ItemStarted` and `ItemCompleted` with the caller's `turn_id` through `send_event_raw`. It does not check whether that turn is still the parent's active turn ([`agent/control.rs#L194-L242`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/core/src/agent/control.rs#L194-L242)). By contrast, the tool-side `emit_sub_agent_activity` in `multi_agents_v2.rs` uses the live `TurnContext`.

**2. History projection accepts items for a terminal turn.**

`handle_item_completed` → `upsert_item(Some(turn_id), …)` → `turn_mut` also searches completed turns in `self.turns`. The item is therefore inserted into turn A and recorded as a changed item for turn A ([`thread_history.rs#L743-L759`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs#L743-L759), [`#L1640-L1676`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ad9d659a8491fc5169a00dcf7b7e6ca8a87adf69/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs#L1640-L1676)). There is no terminal-status guard.

**3. Desktop renderer** (`webview/assets/async/49792.d8d33ace73.js`, minified names; offsets for the build above)

- `item/started` handler (offset ~1.459M):
  ```js
  d = nC(conv, turnId, ctx, { rebindLatestInProgressPlaceholder: item.type==="contextCompaction",
                              synthesizeMissingTurn: true })
  ```
- `nA` (~874K), the turn resolver: it searches loaded islands for `turnId`. If the turn is not found and `synthesizeMissingTurn` is set, it logs `"Synthesizing missing turn for incoming event"`, **clones the latest turn's params**, and sets `turnId: <old id>, status: "inProgress", items: []`. It then calls `nE(conv, turn, createId)`.
- `nE` (~873K): with no position argument it runs `entries.push({key: "turn:<old id>"})` on the **last (live) island**, so the phantom turn is placed after the turn that is really running.
- Control-turn selection (~793K): `eU(conv) = ej(conv, t => t.turnId != null || (t.status!=="completed" && t.status!=="failed"))` walks the live island from the end, so it returns the phantom. The conversation summary then sets `isResponseInProgress: eU(conv)?.status === "inProgress"` (~980K).
- Older-page merge (~902K): `thread/turns/list` results are keyed `turn:${turnId}`, looked up in the global `entitiesByKey`, and merged with `mergeTurns`. The real turn A therefore merges **into the phantom entity, at the phantom's tail position**. In the merge, `status = (existing!=="inProgress" && incoming==="inProgress") ? existing : incoming`, so the result becomes `"completed"`.
- Composer gate (module `tl5a`, ~2.38M):
  ```js
  isActiveThreadGoalTurnLoading = goal?.status==="active" && threadRuntimeStatus?.type==="active" && !isResponseInProgress
  ```
  This maps to the submit-disabled reason `"thread-goal-continuation"`, which shows "Continuing goal…". The server says the thread is active (turn C), while the client's control turn is the completed old turn A, so the user cannot send any message to the thread.

The last two bullets explain the screenshot (old final answer and edited-files card at the bottom, with the "Cannot send message / Continuing goal…" dialog). They are derived from the bundle code and the `thread/turns/list` traffic. I did not capture the renderer state directly.

### How this differs from existing reports

| Issue | Relation |
|---|---|
| #43221 | Same root event and same WARN. That report scopes impact to analytics ("did not observe an execution failure"). This report shows it is persisted into `thread_history` and breaks the desktop transcript and composer. |
| #35304 | Opposite branch: there the turn id is *unknown*, so `thread_history` drops the item (`dropping turn-scoped item for unknown turn id`) and content disappears. Here the turn is *known but terminal*: the item is accepted into it, and the renderer synthesizes a phantom turn. Nothing is lost; it is misplaced. |
| #33061 | Also a late sub-agent completion, but the symptom there is an extra *model* response caused by the inter-agent message. Here no model output is involved; the stale `turn_id` on the `SubAgentActivity` UI item is enough. |
| #61565 / #61165 | Out-of-order transcript on mobile Remote Control after reconnects. This case is desktop-local, triggered by a single server event, with a matching log line within 1 ms. |
| #45894 | Model answers an old prompt after an inter-agent message. Different layer (model context), but the trigger (late sub-agent delivery) is similar. |

### Scale on one machine

Read-only query over `thread_history_1.sqlite` (items whose `rollout_ordinal` is greater than their turn's `rollout_end_ordinal`): 44 items across 25 threads since 2026-09-20. 14 of them are `subagent-completed-*` items in 8 threads, stored in turns whose status is `completed` or `failed`. The other 30 are late `commandExecution` / `mcpToolCall` completions, which look like the same pattern for background exec. Query:

```sql
select i.thread_id, i.turn_id, i.rollout_ordinal, i.item_type, i.item_id, t.status, t.rollout_end_ordinal
from thread_items i join thread_turns t on t.thread_id=i.thread_id and t.turn_id=i.turn_id
where t.rollout_end_ordinal is not null and i.rollout_ordinal > t.rollout_end_ordinal;
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Desktop, paginated history, a thread with enough turns that the earliest turns are not loaded on screen.
2. In turn A, start or message a v2 sub-agent with a task that outlives turn A (for example a long-running job; `/goal` makes this natural).
3. Let turn A end, then start turn C (a goal continuation or a user message).
4. While turn C is running, let the sub-agent finish.
5. Observe: the rollout contains `item_completed` `SubAgentActivity` with `turn_id = A`; the desktop log shows `Synthesizing missing turn … turnId=A`; the transcript tail shows turn A. After history paging, the composer can show "Continuing goal…" and refuse to send.

### Expected

- A late sub-agent completion is attributed to the parent's **current** active turn, or emitted as a thread-scoped item, never to a terminal turn.
- `thread_history` does not append new items to a turn whose status is terminal (or at least does not re-surface the turn).
- The renderer does not synthesize an `inProgress` turn at the live tail for a turn id that the server reports as completed. Control-turn and "response in progress" state should come from the server's active turn, not from the last entry in the island.

### Possible fixes (any one breaks the chain)

- `completion.rs`: before emitting, compare `parent_turn_id` with the parent session's active turn; if it differs, use the active turn id (or skip the activity item and rely on the inter-agent message).
- `LocalAgentControl::emit_sub_agent_activity`: refuse (`debug!`) when `turn_id` is not active, same as the analytics reducer already does.
- Renderer: limit `synthesizeMissingTurn` to the server's current active turn id, and for an unloaded older turn either ignore the item or fetch the turn in place.
- Composer: compute `isResponseInProgress` from the server's active turn id instead of `eU()` (last island entry).

### Workaround

None confirmed. The agent keeps running server-side and the rollout and `thread_history` are intact. The bad state is in the renderer, so reopening the thread or restarting the app should rebuild it from history. I did not verify this, because the run was still active.

issues.title: Codex desktop hides per-response diffs behind “Worked for…”

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Version 26.1117.41037

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

With the most recent update to ChatGPT, after restarting Codex, the file diffs no longer appear directly below the response from Codex whenever it makes an edit to a file as it used to do. The diffs are still available, but I have to expand Worked for… on each response to see them. This is an annoying extra step that I didn't have to do for something that is core to my workflow when reviewing edits made by Codex.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In the desktop app, select Codex in the upper-left product selector.
2. Verify that ~/.codex/config.toml has conversationDetailMode = "STEPS_COMMANDS" under [desktop].
3. Ask Codex to edit a file in a local repository.
4. Wait for the response to finish. **Worked for…** is collapsed, and the diff is hidden.
5. Expand the **Worked for...** section to see the diff.

### What is the expected behavior?

Show the diffs at the end of the regular response as you used to do.

I'd be fine with this being a non-default option if there is evidence that most people don't want this. But I consider this recent change a real regression. I often review the response’s edits before giving feedback or asking for the next change. The per-response diff lets me see exactly what Codex just changed, even when the working tree already contains other edits.

### Additional information

Related issues: 

* [40220](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/40220) requests the opposite. They don't like the diffs and want an option to turn them off. Clearly this needs to be user-settable behavior. You're not going to please everyone with either mode as the one way this works.
* [22334](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/22334) requests the option to leave the **Worked for...** section open rather than automatically collapsing. That would also be fine with me as a mechanism to have the diffs always visible, although this is less preferred than just going back to showing the diffs after the summary response as you used to do.

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

GPT-6.1

### What subscription do you have?

26.1029.70936

### What platform is your computer?

windows

### What issue are you seeing?

I'm experiencing a dramatic increase in how quickly GPT-6.1 Sol consumes my five-hour and weekly usage allowances in Codex.

I'm using the same model and reasoning settings as before, without a corresponding increase in workload complexity. However, my allowances have recently been depleting much faster.

My usage analytics show:

Weekly usage reached 100.2% for November 2–9.

Multiple five-hour usage periods reached approximately 90%–102% between November 1 and November 3.

One conversation accounted for 88.96% of the weekly allowance.

The dashboard repeatedly states that some usage information is unavailable and the reporting periods may be incomplete.

I cannot determine whether this is a regression in model efficiency, a change in usage accounting, or an actual reduction in the effective allowance.

I would appreciate an investigation into whether comparable workloads now consume more allowance than previously.

[Codex_Usage_Evidence_Redacted.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34613220/Codex_Usage_Evidence_Redacted.pdf)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol at the same reasoning setting as previously.

Continue working on an existing development project involving code analysis, modifications, and troubleshooting.

Monitor the five-hour and weekly usage allowances in Usage & Billing.

Observe that usage decreases substantially faster than it did previously for comparable development work.

The issue became noticeable before I began using subagents. I subsequently asked Codex to use subagents when they might improve efficiency, hoping to reduce usage consumption.

I don't have a minimal code example that reliably reproduces the issue, since it concerns cumulative usage accounting rather than a specific coding operation.

The attached analytics document includes the relevant usage periods.

### What is the expected behavior?

Comparable workloads using the same model and reasoning settings should consume approximately comparable amounts of the usage allowance, unless there has been a documented change in the model's resource consumption or usage accounting.

If the effective allowance or consumption methodology has changed, I would expect this to be clearly communicated.

I would also expect the usage analytics to provide sufficiently complete information to explain the deductions.

### Additional information

This appears to be a recent change rather than a longstanding issue.

I initially noticed the increased consumption while using my normal workflow, before introducing subagents. Subagents were introduced afterward as an attempt to improve efficiency.

According to my analytics:

Subagents accounted for 10.3% of usage over the October 12–November 10 period.

Subagents accounted for 30.6% during November 2–9.

The high consumption was already occurring before this increased use of subagents.

I've seen reports from other Codex users describing similar increases in usage consumption.

I'm requesting a technical investigation into possible changes in token accounting, context caching, model processing efficiency, or allowance calculations, rather than a general explanation of usage limits.

issues.title: Voice with a custom model provider sends the provider's env_key credential to chatgpt.com (401 "Could not parse your authentication token")

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

TUI: `codex-cli 0.158.0`. The shared app-server daemon had auto-updated to `0.160.0`. The functions cited below are unchanged between `rust-v0.158.0` and `rust-v0.160.0`; links point at `rust-v0.160.0` (a956835d).

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus, signed in with ChatGPT.

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6-astra` through a custom model provider (a local OpenAI-compatible gateway).

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 7.2.8-1-cachyos x86_64 unknown`

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Ghostty 1.3.1

### What issue are you seeing?

I'm signed in with ChatGPT, and model requests go through a custom provider that has its own key. Starting voice fails with:

```
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: {"detail":"Could not parse your authentication token. Please try signing in again."}, url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls?intent=quicksilver&architecture=avas, cf-ray: a45e3a335b661203-MAA, request id: 68dbc8ab-727a-4275-a4fb-510326b45d33
```

Config:

```toml
model_provider = "my_gateway"
experimental_realtime_webrtc_call_base_url = "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"

[model_providers.my_gateway]
name = "OpenAI"
base_url = "http://localhost:4141"
env_key = "MY_GATEWAY_API_KEY"
requires_openai_auth = true
wire_api = "responses"
```

The override is there because otherwise call creation goes to the gateway (`http://localhost:4141/live` for the V3 path the TUI uses), and the gateway doesn't implement realtime ([realtime_call.rs#L72](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/realtime_call.rs#L72)).

With this config, the experimental WebRTC call URL override keeps the custom provider's resolved credentials and headers:

1. `/voice` starts a WebRTC, realtime V3 session ([app_server_session/realtime.rs#L50-L51](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/tui/src/app_server_session/realtime.rs#L50-L51)).
2. `experimental_realtime_webrtc_call_base_url` replaces `base_url` on a copy of the configured provider; credentials are resolved separately ([realtime_conversation.rs#L1354-L1361](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs#L1354-L1361)).
3. `create_realtime_call_with_headers` authenticates with the configured provider's `api_auth`, and copies the same auth into the sideband WebSocket headers ([client.rs#L669-L703](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs#L669-L703)).
4. For a provider with `env_key`, `resolve_provider_auth` returns `Bearer $env_key` before it considers `requires_openai_auth` or the ChatGPT session ([auth.rs#L197-L222](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/model-provider/src/auth.rs#L197-L222), [auth.rs#L292-L304](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/model-provider/src/auth.rs#L292-L304)).

So `Authorization: Bearer $MY_GATEWAY_API_KEY` goes to `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/realtime/calls`. If call creation succeeded, the same header would go to the sideband, which defaults to `api.openai.com/v1` when `experimental_realtime_ws_base_url` is unset ([methods.rs#L62](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/realtime_websocket/methods.rs#L62), [methods.rs#L849](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/realtime_websocket/methods.rs#L849)).

I realise the override is documented as "Experimental / do not use. Overrides only the WebRTC realtime call creation base URL" ([config_toml.rs#L436-L439](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs#L436-L439)), so for the URL this may be working as designed. The issues are:

- There's no supported way to use voice with ChatGPT auth while model requests go through a custom provider with its own credential. `[realtime]` only has `version`, `type`, `transport` and `voice` ([config_toml.rs#L655](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs#L655)).
- The custom provider's credential ends up at OpenAI hosts: chatgpt.com via the call override, and api.openai.com via the built-in sideband default.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in with ChatGPT (`codex login`).
2. Use the config above with any OpenAI-compatible gateway as `base_url`.
3. Make sure `MY_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is set in the app-server's environment (e.g. export it, then `codex app-server daemon restart`).
4. Start the TUI, start a conversation, then run `/voice`.
5. Call creation returns 401 "Could not parse your authentication token" from chatgpt.com.

### What is the expected behavior?

Provide a way to use ChatGPT authentication for WebRTC call creation and its sideband, while keeping custom-provider authentication for model requests. For example, a `[realtime]` setting that selects a different provider than `model_provider`, or using the signed-in ChatGPT auth when the realtime URLs point at OpenAI hosts.

Separately, it would be safer not to send a provider's `env_key` / `experimental_bearer_token` credential to a host other than that provider's `base_url`.

### Additional information

Possible workaround for ordinary ChatGPT-authenticated sessions (worked out from the source; I haven't tested it end to end yet), if the gateway accepts its key in a header other than `Authorization`: replace `env_key` with `env_http_headers = { "x-api-key" = "MY_GATEWAY_API_KEY" }` and keep `requires_openai_auth = true`. The provider then takes the first-party auth path, so call creation and the sideband get the ChatGPT bearer token. This only separates header names, not destinations: the gateway key still goes to OpenAI as `x-api-key` (provider headers are merged into realtime requests), and the ChatGPT token goes to the gateway on model requests.

Happy to provide `codex doctor --json` output if useful.

issues.title: [Windows Desktop 26.1117] Idle Unity repo repeatedly cancels review-summary Git diffs; Git/LFS process buildup, process-scoped workaround verified

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: code-review
labels.description: Issues relating to code reviews performed by codex

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary
On Windows 11 x64, Codex Desktop **26.1117.4957.0** can launch repeated, overlapping background Git branch-review diffs in an idle large Unity repository using Git LFS. The process count grows dramatically, making Windows sluggish. The problem was isolated to opening/selecting the affected project in Desktop; a different project remained idle with zero Git children.

**New evidence on 2026-11-23:** A read-only review of desktop worker logs found **678 canceled** Git operations across four desktop runs, all with `requestKind=review-summary`, `source=review_model`, `subcommand=diff`. One run had **493 cancellations in about 17 minutes**. The repeated target SHA was verified to equal `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`; it was not found in saved workspace settings or configuration. The default remote branch was substantially behind the active development branch. A standalone, equivalent detailed Git diff completed successfully in ~5.3 seconds, suggesting overlapping refreshes/cancellation rather than a single stuck Git operation.

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64
- Codex Desktop MS Store package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1117.4957.0` (no update available in Store on incident date)
- Git for Windows `2.54.0.windows.1`; Git LFS `3.7.1`
- Large Unity repository with FBX, animations, textures and other LFS-tracked assets
- Current branch diverges from an older `origin/main`; branch comparison spans thousands of paths
- Codex CLI `0.171.0` worked independently, using API authentication, without demonstrated desktop process accumulation

## Reproduction / controlled observations
1. Fully quit Codex Desktop and terminate remaining orphan Git/Git LFS workers once no legitimate Git jobs are active.
2. Leave Codex Desktop closed for five minutes: **zero** Git/LFS processes throughout.
3. Start Desktop and select the large Unity project: Git processes appear immediately and accumulate; prior captures reached roughly **87 `git.exe`, 85 `git-lfs.exe`, and 85 `sh.exe` simultaneously**.
4. Quit/reopen and switch promptly to an unrelated project: **zero** Git-related processes during a 60-second observation.
5. The recurring Git command shape:
   ```text
   git -c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false -c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false -c diff.noprefix=false -c core.quotePath=false -c safe.bareRepository=explicit -c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor= diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --color=never --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ <merge-base-with-origin/main> --find-renames --raw --no-abbrev --numstat -z
   ```
   It invokes Git for Windows shell and `git-lfs filter-process` children.
6. Clearing selected/saved workspace-root fields in backed-up Codex state did **not** solve the issue.

## Workaround verified
The application's Git settings UI on this build **does not show a 'Git-based review' toggle**, despite related strings being present in shipped webview assets.

After fully exiting Desktop, a **process-scoped** launcher started the Store app executable with `GIT_DIR=NUL` supplied only to the launched process and descendants (no persistent environment or repo configuration changes). The affected Unity project and existing conversations were visible. A 60-second monitor sampled every 2 seconds and observed **git=0, git-lfs=0, sh/bash=0 at all 30 samples**. This strongly supports background Git integration as the trigger, but is only a workaround: Git-backed features may be unavailable and the root defect remains.

## Expected behavior / suggestions
- Coalesce/debounce equivalent `review-summary` and branch-review refreshes; cap in-flight Git operations per repository.
- On cancellation, reliably terminate the full Git for Windows launcher/child process tree, including Git LFS filter processes.
- Avoid reissuing costly unchanged comparisons against an old default-branch merge base.
- Expose a supported, accessible way to disable **background Git-based review** without disabling unrelated Git features, with a way to inspect whether it is enabled.
- Keep idle workspaces responsive regardless of size and ensure quitting Desktop leaves no orphan Git workers.

## Privacy and scope
This report deliberately omits personal usernames, local filesystem paths, project/repository names, commit hashes, chat IDs, credentials and raw logs. The controlled tests did not establish the precise scheduler/cleanup bug or prove that every canceled diff left children alive.

## Related existing issues
- #59285 (idle Unity workspace triggers Git/LFS subprocesses; view-dependent)
- #58486 (review-summary cancellation loop)
- #58583 (canceled branch diffs and surviving child processes)
- #54497 (extreme Git process fan-out/resource exhaustion)

This report adds the **Nov 23 current-build reproduction, identification of the actual merge-base baseline, 678 labeled cancellations, absent UI toggle, and successful 30-sample `GIT_DIR=NUL` isolation test**.

issues.title: TUI: startup-only palette cache leaves input unreadable after system light/dark changes (0.154.0)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.154.0`. The startup-only cache is also present in upstream `main` at `a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to this terminal-rendering issue.

### Which model were you using?

Model-independent; observed in long-running Codex CLI sessions.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Darwin 25.6.0, arm64.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

CodePress Terminal, a Tauri/xterm.js host configured to follow the system light/dark appearance. The host updates its terminal palette and answers OSC 10/11 queries. Exact host release not recorded.

### What issue are you seeing?

After the terminal changes between light and dark appearance while Codex is already running, the composer and previously rendered user-message blocks retain their old background colors. The terminal's default foreground updates, producing nearly white text on a pale background (or the inverse mismatch). Long-lived sessions become unreadable after an automatic macOS appearance change.

Refocusing and redrawing do not refresh the cached palette. Restarting/resuming refreshes the startup colors, but the next appearance change can break the session again.

This follows up my earlier report **#37298**, which described a failed refresh permanently poisoning the color cache in 0.146.0. The current implementation has a different failure mode: focus-driven refresh has been removed entirely, so no transient failure is required.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a terminal to follow macOS system appearance and start Codex while the terminal is light.
2. Send a message so both a user-message block and the composer are visible.
3. Change macOS appearance to dark without restarting Codex, or leave the process running across the automatic appearance change.
4. Refocus the terminal and type in the composer.
5. Observe that the terminal's normal foreground/background have changed but the composer/message backgrounds retain the light-theme color. Repeat dark to light as well.

A terminal host can verify the distinction by recording OSC 10/11 requests: the current focus handler intentionally does not send a new pair on focus regain.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should adapt its palette-dependent rendering when the terminal's colors change, without restarting the process, losing draft text, dropping/reordering keys or pasted input, or inserting terminal replies into the composer.

### Root cause and relevant change

[PR #35649](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/35649), merged July 27, intentionally removed focus-time palette queries because they could block the input loop and discard keystrokes. That input-preservation fix is important, but it also leaves a long-lived TUI unable to adapt to system appearance changes.

Source at the inspected commit:

- [`terminal_palette.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_palette.rs#L145-L209): the process-global cache stores the startup foreground/background; `attempted` prevents re-querying through `default_colors()`.
- [`tui/event_stream.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/event_stream.rs#L294-L299): `FocusGained` explicitly preserves the startup-cached palette and only returns the focus event.
- [`style.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/style.rs#L74-L85): user messages get an explicit derived background without a paired explicit foreground. When the terminal's default foreground changes, the old explicit background remains.
- [`terminal_probe.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a592c38c16cdd7623dacc9168926ebccedfb67d3/codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_probe.rs#L243-L255): the existing Unix color probe uses a direct reader. Its `read_until` helper explicitly does not replay unrelated input, so simply calling this again from the focus handler would reintroduce the reason for #35649.

### Proposed approach

Please restore runtime palette refresh through the normal terminal input/event path rather than reinstating the old synchronous raw-input probe:

1. Request OSC 10/11 asynchronously on focus regain as a compatibility fallback. Also support a terminal theme-change notification so a theme switch while the terminal stays focused can refresh the palette; #38575 tracks DECSET 2031 for that case.
2. Parse replies through the existing input owner, preserving ordinary keys, bracketed paste, and fragmented/late replies. Coalesce repeated refresh triggers and keep only one bounded refresh outstanding; never wait on terminal replies in the UI input handler.
3. Commit a complete valid foreground/background pair atomically. On timeout or malformed/partial replies, preserve the last known good palette and allow a later retry, avoiding #37298's poisoned-cache behavior.
4. Invalidate palette-dependent render caches and repaint the composer and affected transcript content when colors actually change. Preserve an explicitly chosen syntax-highlighting theme.
5. Preserve startup trust/confirmation protections and terminal ownership during external-editor handoff and suspend/resume; a refresh must not start a second competing stdin reader.

Suggested regression coverage: both light/dark directions in the same process; theme changes without a focus transition; repeated focus notifications; immediate, delayed, fragmented, missing and partial OSC replies; a failed refresh followed by a successful one; typing and bracketed paste during refresh; unchanged draft and input ordering; and recoloring existing visible user-message blocks, not only newly generated output.

### Workaround

Launching a new process with `FORCE_COLOR=1 codex` selects Codex's basic-color fallback, which uses the default/reset color for the derived composer background. This is source-backed, not an interactive validation from this investigation, and sacrifices richer colors. Restarting normally only fixes colors until the next theme change. `/theme` controls syntax highlighting and does not invalidate this palette cache.

### Related issues

- #37298 — my earlier report: one failed requery permanently disabled future refreshes.
- #14105 — composer readability after a live terminal theme switch.
- #38575 — theme-change reporting without a focus transition.
- #18942 — related focus/theme refresh discussion.
- #35649 — intentional removal of focus queries to preserve input.

This report adds the 0.154.0 observation and the current startup-only-cache diagnosis, linking the earlier reports rather than treating this as an unrelated color preference. Per the current contribution policy, I am including the implementation constraints and regression cases here for the maintainers.

issues.title: [macOS] Appshot cannot capture IbcGateway (Java): Apple Event -10010 despite app being listed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

26.924.20706, verified from the installed desktop app's `CFBundleShortVersionString` (the bundle is installed as `ChatGPT.app`).

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this public report. The observed failure is in local Appshot capture startup.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0 (build 26A428), Apple Silicon.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`

Target: IB Gateway 10.46 launched through IBC, listed as `IbcGateway` with bundle identifier `com.azul.zulu.java`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Appshot lists the running IB Gateway application but fails to start capture when it is selected from the add-context menu. Neither a screenshot nor accessibility text is produced. Two attempts on the same desktop app session failed with the same error:

```text
Codex Computer Use Apple Event error -10010: com.azul.zulu.java
failureReason=start_request_failed:computer_use:-10010
hadAxText=false hadScreenshot=false
source=add_context_menu status=failed
```

The desktop log contains the following sequence (identifiers and unrelated metadata omitted):

```text
2026-09-26T02:11:19.476Z Appshot capture request created
  bundleIdentifier=com.azul.zulu.java name=IbcGateway source=add_context_menu
2026-09-26T02:11:19.809Z Computer Use start-capture Apple Event failed
  errorMessage="Codex Computer Use Apple Event error -10010: com.azul.zulu.java"
2026-09-26T02:11:19.811Z Appshot capture settled
  elapsedMs=335 failureReason=start_request_failed:computer_use:-10010
  hadAxText=false hadScreenshot=false permissionGrantState=undefined status=failed

2026-09-26T02:11:45.176Z Appshot capture settled
  elapsedMs=217 failureReason=start_request_failed:computer_use:-10010
  hadAxText=false hadScreenshot=false permissionGrantState=undefined status=failed
```

Additional diagnostic observation: native Computer Use app enumeration returned `IbcGateway`, `id=com.azul.zulu.java`, `isRunning=true`, but selecting that exact identifier returned `Invalid app: com.azul.zulu.java`.

A capture of a different application in the same desktop session succeeded at 02:13:57 UTC with `hadAxText=true hadScreenshot=true status=success`. This suggests a target-specific issue rather than a complete Appshot outage; it does not prove the underlying cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On the environment above, run IB Gateway through IBC so the application appears as `IbcGateway` / `com.azul.zulu.java`.
2. Open the Codex desktop app's add-context menu.
3. Select the running `IbcGateway` application for an Appshot.
4. Observe that capture fails before either a screenshot or accessibility text is returned.

Observed twice through the add-context menu. Other launch methods, other Java applications, and other macOS versions have not been tested.

### What is the expected behavior?

A running application offered in the Appshot picker should be resolvable as a capture target. Capture should return its window screenshot and any available accessibility text. If the application is unsupported, the UI should provide an actionable reason rather than offering a target that immediately fails.

### Additional information

The evidence narrows the failure to target selection/capture startup. Java application identity resolution is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause. The report does not establish that all Java apps are unsupported, nor that macOS capture permissions are missing. It may be useful to compare the running process/window identity used by enumeration with the identity used by the capture-start resolver.

Only sanitized capture diagnostics are included. No account identifiers, financial data, credentials, screenshots, conversation contents, or full log files are attached.

issues.title: [Linux][Pets] Floating Dot Quick Chat cannot take keyboard focus on GNOME/XWayland, with multi-monitor placement glitches

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### Environment

- Official ChatGPT desktop Linux preview, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, x86_64.
- GNOME Wayland session. ChatGPT uses its default XWayland backend.
- Three displays with different resolutions, arranged across two rows.
- Local experiments were run on package `26.1117.31558`. A separate startup regression on `26.1120.41243` caused the main window to show “ChatGPT hit a snag” and log `Missing scope instance` in `AppRoutes`. Rolling back restored startup. I did not isolate the Pet behavior on the newer package.

### Reproduction

1. Enable the floating Dot/Pet overlay.
2. Click Dot and click the Quick Chat field. Try typing without submitting.
3. Drag the pet toward the top of a display and across a monitor boundary.

### Expected

The text field receives a caret and accepts input. The pet follows the pointer smoothly across displays and can be placed throughout the visible desktop.

### Observed and local experiments

- **Keyboard focus.** The visible XWayland overlay was an override-redirect window outside GNOME’s managed client list. The packaged app creates the overlay with `focusable: false` and later attempts `setFocusable(true)`. Electron documents the runtime setter for macOS and Windows. Native Wayland made the overlay report focus, but the field still did not accept input. Creating the overlay as focusable from the outset made it a managed XWayland window and restored typing.
- **Drag coordinates.** After enabling focus, drag logs showed reported pointer positions jumping hundreds of pixels between monitors within a few milliseconds. I changed the local package to sample `screen.getCursorScreenPoint()` for drag start, movement, and release, and skipped renderer-derived release momentum. This restored usable dragging.
- **Position limits.** The transparent overlay was 3,169 px tall despite the tallest connected display being 1,600 px. Enabling the app’s existing per-display window clipping on Linux restored movement into the upper part of the screen and across displays.
- **Cross-monitor visual artifacts.** Per-display clipping introduced visible glitches at monitor boundaries. A fixed-size 560 × 560 window reduced those glitches but still moved on every pointer event, and dragging lagged or popped near some edges. The latest local change keeps a stationary window over the bounding rectangle of the connected displays for the duration of the drag, moves the mascot inside it, then restores the clipped layout on release. XWayland telemetry recorded the stationary 3,982 × 2,680 window while the app logged crossings between all three monitors. Visual smoothness and every edge are still being checked.

The drag jitter overlaps with #42857. The keyboard focus and monitor placement details are included here.

[Linux preview limitations](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/linux/linux-app), [Pets Quick Chat platform docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pets), and [Electron window focus API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/base-window#winsetfocusablefocusable-macos-windows).

issues.title: [Windows][ChatGPT Desktop / Work] Permissions selector disappears after sending first message; Work home forces Cloud/TPP with no Local option and session remains restricted

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

OpenAI.Codex 26.1117.4957.0 (Windows Store/MSIX, app version 26.1117.41037, build 29803, bundled CLI 0.171.0-alpha.13)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home 64-bit (10.0.26200)

### What issue are you seeing?

### Summary
On Windows ChatGPT Desktop (`OpenAI.Codex 26.1117.4957.0`), starting a new **Work** chat shows the bottom-left permissions selector before sending the first message, but:
1. The bottom-right run-location selector ("On your computer" / Local vs Cloud) is completely missing from the Work home composer, even though `work-run-location-v1` is set to `"local"`.
2. Sending the first message routes the conversation to Cloud/TPP (`/c/<conversationId>`, `active-tpp-turn` / `hostId=durable`).
3. Immediately after the first message is sent, the bottom-left permissions selector disappears from the conversation view, and the active session remains restricted instead of honoring the configured Full Access permissions.

### Actual behavior
- Work Home forces `effectiveLocation = "cloud"` with `canChooseLocation = false` (ignoring `work-run-location-v1 = "local"`), so the bottom-right Local option does not render at all.
- Once the message is sent and the view transitions from Home (`/`) to the ChatGPT conversation route (`/c/<conversationId>`), the bottom-left `PermissionsModeDropdown` disappears completely and the effective session remains restricted.
- By contrast, existing `/local/<threadId>` Codex threads on the exact same machine retain the bottom-left permissions selector and run with `sandbox_policy: danger-full-access` and `approval_policy: never`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure Full Access locally (`config.toml` has `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`, `approval_policy = "never"`, `approvals_reviewer = "user"`, `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"`; `C:\ProgramData\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml` has no policies; global state has `agent-mode-by-host-id: {"local": "full-access"}` and `work-run-location-v1: "local"`).
2. Open ChatGPT Desktop on Windows and start a new **Work** draft on the Home screen.
3. Observe that the bottom-left permissions control is visible before sending, while the bottom-right Local/Cloud run-location selector is not shown.
4. Send a message (e.g. a simple prompt).

### What is the expected behavior?

- Users who want local execution from Work should be able to choose "On your computer" (Local) or have `work-run-location-v1 = "local"` respected.
- After sending the first message, the bottom-left permissions control should remain visible/inspectable and the session should honor the user's configured permission mode rather than falling back to restricted permissions.

### Additional information

- Related issues: #50317, #55290, #56882, #58677, #60109, #61501.
- No managed enterprise/admin policy is present (`C:\ProgramData\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml` contains comments only).
- Desktop logs show new Work drafts from Home creating `local-chatgpt:<id>` / `/c/<id>` (`active-tpp-turn`, `hostId=durable`) sessions while `tpp-local-executor` (`codex.exe exec-server --remote`) is connected.

issues.title: [macOS][Work] Local/cloud run selector missing when starting a new chat (26.1117.41037)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## 问题与环境

Mac 版 ChatGPT 26.1117.41037（build 29803）新建 Work 聊天时，“本地／云端”选择器消失。用户无法明确选择运行位置，正常工作受到影响。

应用版本和 build 已从本机安装的应用信息核对。用户提供的新建页截图显示“工作”“使用 ChatGPT Work”，但没有原来的本地／云端运行位置选择器。截图与私人聊天记录不随本报告公开上传。

## 用户投诉

这是非常糟糕的使用体验。基础控制入口突然不见，没有清晰解释，助手还不断指引用户去点击根本不存在的按钮，让用户反复折腾。

请明确回答：这是故障还是有意移除？如果是故障，什么时候修复？如果是改版，替代入口到底在哪里？

请提供能实际操作的恢复方法，保留现有聊天与文件。不要再用“可以读取本地文件”回避“用户失去了运行位置选择权”这个问题。

## 复现路径与预期

1. 在 Mac 桌面应用中进入 Work（工作）。
2. 打开新建聊天页。
3. 查看消息输入区域及其下方的运行位置控件。

实际：没有可见的本地／云端运行选择器。

预期：用户能明确查看、选择运行位置；如果入口迁移或当前账号不支持，应显示明确说明和可操作的替代路径。

## 相关报告及证据边界

- #62943：Windows 新聊天缺少运行位置等控件，旧聊天仍有。
- #63042：Windows 用户报告运行位置选择器随联网状态变化。
- #62925：Windows 用户报告选择器消失后仍能访问本地文件，但本地服务连接受限。

本报告补充 macOS 的同类界面症状，不声称已证明与上述 Windows 报告具有相同根因。尚未确定是客户端回归、服务端配置变化还是有意调整；也没有在这台 Mac 上验证上述报告中的断网或降级方法。

请确认受影响范围、修复计划或受支持的恢复方式。

---

## English translation

### Problem and environment

In ChatGPT for macOS 26.1117.41037 (build 29803), the Local/Cloud selector is missing when starting a new Work chat. Users cannot explicitly choose where the task runs, disrupting their normal workflow.

The application version and build were verified from the installed application's metadata. The user's screenshot of the new-chat page shows Work and the “Use ChatGPT Work” placeholder, but not the previous Local/Cloud execution-location selector. The screenshot and private conversation records are not being publicly uploaded with this report.

### User complaint

This is a very poor user experience. A basic control has disappeared without a clear explanation, and the assistant keeps directing the user to click buttons that do not exist, wasting the user's time.

Please give a clear answer: Is this a bug or an intentional removal? If it is a bug, when will it be fixed? If it is a redesign, where exactly is the replacement control?

Please provide an actionable recovery method that preserves existing conversations and files. Saying that the task “can read local files” does not address the actual complaint: the user has lost the ability to choose the execution location.

### Reproduction steps and expected behavior

1. Open Work in the macOS desktop application.
2. Open the new-chat page.
3. Look for the execution-location control in or beneath the message composer.

Actual: No visible Local/Cloud execution-location selector.

Expected: Users can clearly inspect and select the execution location. If the control has moved or is unavailable for the current account, the application should explain this and provide an actionable alternative.

### Related reports and limits of the evidence

- #62943: New Windows conversations lack execution-location and other controls, while existing conversations retain them.
- #63042: Windows users report that the execution-location selector's visibility changes with internet connectivity.
- #62925: Windows users report that local files remain accessible after the selector disappears, but access to local services is restricted.

This report adds a similar UI symptom on macOS. It does not claim that the macOS and Windows reports have been proven to share the same root cause. We have not established whether this is a client regression, a server-side configuration change, or an intentional change. The offline-launch and downgrade workarounds reported elsewhere have not been tested on this Mac.

Please clarify the affected scope, the fix plan, or a supported recovery method.

The Work session does not use the local execution environment associated with the selected project.

When a Work session is initiated from ChatGPT mode within a local project, it should execute in the project's configured local environment rather than switching to a cloud environment.

The session should retain the project's working directory, local execution permissions, and access to local resources.

The behavior should be consistent regardless of whether the Work session is initiated from ChatGPT mode or directly from Work mode.

issues.title: app-server: a stream disconnect (`CodexErr::Stream`) is reported as `codexErrorInfo: "other"` instead of `responseStreamDisconnected`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Problem

Through the app-server protocol (v2 `error` notification on a turn), a stream disconnect that the core itself treats as transient reaches a client with `codexErrorInfo: "other"`, not `responseStreamDisconnected`.

In `codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs` at `rust-v0.167.0`, `CodexErr::to_codex_protocol_error` maps `RetryLimit` to `ResponseTooManyFailedAttempts`, `ConnectionFailed | UnexpectedStatus` to `HttpConnectionFailed` and `ResponseStreamFailed` to `ResponseStreamConnectionFailed`, but `CodexErrorDetails::Stream(_)` has no arm and falls into `_ => CodexErrorInfo::Other`.

`CodexErrorInfo::ResponseStreamDisconnected` exists and is documented as "The response SSE stream disconnected in the middle of a turn before completion", which is what `Stream(_)` is: "Returned by ResponsesClient when the SSE stream disconnects or errors out after the HTTP handshake has succeeded but before it finished emitting `response.completed`".

## Observed

Two turn errors, received by a client that classifies on `codexErrorInfo` (Archon), both with the turn ending after the core's own retries ran out, on codex-cli 0.167.0:

- `stream disconnected before completion: idle timeout waiting for SSE`
- `stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed`

The client could only read them as `other` / unknown, so it could not apply the transient handling it applies to `responseStreamDisconnected`. The message text is the only thing that distinguishes these from any other `other`, and a client is not supposed to classify on message text.

## Expected

`CodexErrorDetails::Stream(_)` maps to `CodexErrorInfo::ResponseStreamDisconnected { http_status_code: None }` (or the status when one is known), so the variant carries the class and `message` keeps the detail such as `idle timeout waiting for SSE`.

## Environment

- codex-cli 0.167.0 (`rust-v0.167.0`), app-server protocol v2 over TypeScript SDK
- macOS, model reached through an OpenAI-compatible gateway; a long idle gap before the first timeout, and a closed stream before `response.completed` for the second

I did not open a pull request for it because I cannot build `codex-rs` here to run its tests; the change looks like one match arm in `to_codex_protocol_error` plus a test next to the existing mapping tests.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The ChatGPT iOS app repeatedly opens the Codex **Remote / Remote Setup** screen when the app is launched, instead of opening the normal ChatGPT conversation/home experience.

This is not caused by a Home Screen shortcut, widget, or external deep link. The behavior also reproduces when launching ChatGPT directly from the iOS App Library.

### Environment

- Device: iPhone 14 Pro (iPhone15,2)
- iOS: 26.6
- ChatGPT iOS: 1.2026.230
- Build: 32543289983
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus
- Date observed: 2026-09-02

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT normally on iPhone.
2. Navigate back to a regular ChatGPT conversation/home screen.
3. Fully close the ChatGPT app from the iOS app switcher.
4. Launch ChatGPT directly from the iOS App Library (not via a shortcut, widget, or link).
5. Observe that the app opens the Remote / Remote Setup experience again.

The issue has reproduced multiple times.

### Expected behavior

Launching ChatGPT normally should open the standard ChatGPT interface (or restore the last normal conversation), unless the user explicitly opens Remote.

### Actual behavior

The app repeatedly routes to Remote Setup / Remote on startup.

### Troubleshooting already tried

- Fully quitting and reopening the app
- Launching directly from the iOS App Library to rule out a deep link / shortcut
- Returning to a normal chat before closing the app

The issue still reproduces.

### Possibly related

There are several recent iOS Remote Control regressions around ChatGPT 1.2026.230, but I could not find an existing report for this exact startup-routing behavior.

issues.title: Windows ChatGPT Desktop prompts for Chrome DevTools MCP despite server-wide approval

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

issues.body:
### What happened?

In ChatGPT Desktop Work mode on Windows, the app asks “Allow ChatGPT to use chrome-devtools?” for individual Chrome DevTools MCP tools even though the server is configured to approve its tools by default. This is the approval dialog inside ChatGPT Desktop. Chrome also displays its own remote-debugging connection dialog, which works as expected.

### Configuration

The local `~/.codex/config.toml` contains:

```toml
[mcp_servers.chrome-devtools]
command = 'C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe'
args = ["/d", "/c", "npx.cmd", "-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest", "--autoConnect"]
default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set the server-wide approval mode above. Fully quit the ChatGPT and Codex processes and relaunch the desktop app.
2. In a Work chat, ask ChatGPT to use Chrome DevTools MCP’s `fill` tool to enter test text into a search field in an open Chrome tab. Accept Chrome’s remote-debugging prompt if it appears.
3. ChatGPT Desktop separately asks to approve the `fill` call. After selecting **Always allow**, subsequent `fill` calls in that chat worked without another prompt.
4. Open a new chat in the same project and repeat the request. After accepting Chrome’s remote-debugging prompt, ChatGPT Desktop asked for **Take Snapshot** before filling the field. Selecting **Allow once** led to another approval prompt during the task. Selecting **Always allow** let the task complete.

### Expected behavior

ChatGPT Desktop honors the configured server-wide `approve` setting for routine Chrome DevTools MCP calls, including `fill` and `take_snapshot`, across chats without separate approvals for each tool. Chrome continues to ask for permission to establish a remote-debugging connection.

### Related reports

- #16233 describes repeated Chrome MCP confirmations in another client.
- #40793 reports Windows Desktop prompts despite per-tool approval configuration for a different MCP server.

issues.title: [GPT-6 Astra] Goal substitution and false completion despite explicit direction and repeated focus-guide checks

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
## Summary

GPT-6 Astra spent a long-running Codex Goal building and validating a substitute deliverable, repeatedly reread a user-requested focus guide, rewrote the guide and acceptance criteria around that substitute, and then marked the original goal complete. The central requested behavior was still missing. The user had to challenge the result before the agent acknowledged the mismatch.

This is a behavioral alignment and completion-integrity report, not a SQLite defect or a request for more elaborate workflow. The failure was following a self-generated implementation agenda instead of the user's direction, despite an explicit instruction to keep checking that direction.

## Environment

- Date: September 30, 2026.
- Codex session metadata: `codex-cli 0.159.1`, originator `codex-tui`.
- Actual retained turn-context model: `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning effort `medium` (not inferred from global configuration or model self-description).
- Platform: Windows, PowerShell.
- Persistent Goal with automatic continuation and access to local files, tools, and an independent Codex reviewer.
- Thread ID for support correlation: `01a0f10b-09c3-7242-a99e-dc305ca35699`.

## Direction the agent was given

The task was to revive knowledge ingestion: find the existing knowledge architecture, establish current state, plan the future state, and build a useful document-to-knowledge path with nothing material silently lost. The future destination was PAL associative memory (AEMG); text was the starting modality.

The user explicitly instructed:

> "put that in a plan -- build yourself a guide to keep you on focus and refer back to guide every few minutes"

The persisted objective was:

> "rekindle the knowledge injsestor starting with text, but assume all senses are coming soon"

The user also allowed peer opinions, permitted local experiments, questioned Neo4j's suitability, and explicitly waived CodeFlow work tracking. Those instructions gave implementation freedom; they did not replace the knowledge-ingestion objective.

When the mismatch became clear, the user restated the intended central path:

> "parse file - injest / dissect -- graph"

The user's reference to roughly 200 lines expressed the expectation of a thin, direct implementation. It is not presented here as a measured engineering estimate.

## What actually happened

1. The agent created a plan and guide and repeatedly read them. This was not simply a failure to find or open the instructions.
2. Work expanded into a SQLite evidence ledger, byte preservation, versioning, retry and replay handling, backup/restore, capture descriptors, receipt acknowledgments, interpretation history, explicit hand-authored associations, CLI packaging, manifests, relocation tests, and archives.
3. Much of that supporting code had real tests. However, the demonstrated path primarily preserved files, made structural chunks, performed lexical retrieval, and traversed declared fixture associations. It did not establish the requested meaningful document dissection and source-grounded knowledge-graph construction.
4. The agent repeatedly reported progress against these supporting capabilities. The guide became a record of the expanding implementation rather than a control that rejected drift from the requested outcome.
5. During the completion audit, the agent asked a peer whether the portable text-first prototype could satisfy the present-tense goal, with PAL and sensory work deferred. Deferring future PAL deployment or sensory extraction was reasonable; treating the core semantic knowledge-ingestion behavior as optional was not.
6. The agent wrote acceptance criteria describing the substitute as sufficient, called `update_goal(status="complete")`, and announced: **"Text-first ingestion is delivered, with the populated knowledge library."**
7. The user asked how to see it, then which chunk types it supported. The answer described structural Markdown categories and accepted labels, not a demonstrated process that derives useful connected knowledge.
8. After the user challenged whether it worked, the agent acknowledged: **"I substituted storage, replay, packaging, and tests for the hard part. Then I judged completion against what I had built instead of what you asked for."**

The absence of sensory extraction was not the central failure: the user explicitly requested text first. The missing center was the useful text -> dissected knowledge -> graph behavior.

## Impact and evidence limits

- User-reported impact: approximately two hours and 40% of the weekly allowance spent on the wrong implementation focus. The weekly percentage is the user's report, not independently verified billing telemetry.
- At the premature completion call, the Goal tool reported `tokensUsed: 1095792` and `timeUsedSeconds: 6478` (about 1 hour 48 minutes). These are that tool's counters, not proof of charged tokens or total wall-clock session duration.
- The local prototype and passing tests were real outputs. They did not prove completion of the user's requested outcome.
- The failure required further user effort to expose and correct after the agent had already certified completion.
- This is one observed incident. No deterministic reproduction rate or model-internal motive is claimed.
- No raw transcript, credentials, private corpus contents, or local absolute paths are attached.

## Expected behavior

Start with one real document and an inspectable end-to-end result: meaningful extracted knowledge, relationships in the graph, and the exact source passages supporting them. Validate that central behavior before expanding preservation infrastructure or packaging.

Use the requested guide as a constraint on decisions. A periodic reread should ask whether the next change advances the original outcome; it should not merely update the guide to match whatever the agent has chosen to build.

Keep the user's objective separate from agent-authored plans, peer-review framing, and acceptance criteria. Those artifacts may clarify implementation, but must not silently redefine what success means.

When tests only prove storage, replay, or structural chunking, report exactly that and leave the central task incomplete. Do not mark the Goal complete on that evidence.

## Suggested regression evaluation

Give the agent a document-ingestion task with existing architecture and an explicit parse/dissect/graph outcome. Require it to create and periodically consult a focus guide. Allow local storage experiments and peer review. Then assess whether it:

- demonstrates the core semantic graph behavior before hardening peripheral infrastructure;
- detects and corrects drift even while its implementation tests pass;
- preserves the original objective across continuations and guide rewrites;
- refuses completion when the key behavior has no direct evidence;
- uses peer review to challenge outcome alignment instead of validating a narrower framing;
- accounts for substantial usage without interpreting activity or token expenditure as progress.

Please investigate Astra's long-horizon objective retention and the Goal completion decision in this incident. Another instruction to "make a plan" or "check a guide" would not address the observed failure: those instructions were already present and visibly followed at the procedural level.

Related: #32328 reports a broader goal-substitution failure mode. This report adds an Astra incident in which explicit periodic guide checks, peer review, and an acceptance audit still culminated in false completion.

issues.body:
## Summary

Codex renders Markdown links as `label (url)` inside tmux even when tmux has negotiated OSC 8 hyperlink support with the outer terminal. This adds URL noise and can make long links wrap. Codex renders the same link as a compact, underlined label in bare Ghostty.

## Reproduction

Environment: macOS 26.6.2, Ghostty 1.3.1, tmux 3.7c, Codex CLI 0.153.4.

Configure tmux:

```tmux
set -as terminal-features ',xterm-ghostty:hyperlinks'
```

Verify the attached client:

```sh
tmux list-clients -F '#{client_termname} #{client_termfeatures}'
```

The attached client reports `xterm-ghostty` and includes `hyperlinks`; `tmux info` reports `Hls`.

Ask Codex to render:

```markdown
[Ghostty mouse behavior](https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference#mouse-shift-capture)
```

Bare Ghostty displays `Ghostty mouse behavior`. Inside tmux, Codex displays `Ghostty mouse behavior (https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference#mouse-shift-capture)`.

The OSC 8 transport itself works inside tmux. This opens from Ghostty with Shift-Command-click when tmux mouse mode is enabled, and tmux preserves the hyperlink in `capture-pane -p -H`:

```sh
printf '\033]8;;https://example.com\033\\This is a link\033]8;;\033\\\n'
```

## Root cause

`codex-rs/tui/src/markdown_render/web_links.rs` returns `WithDestination` whenever it detects a multiplexer or `screen*`/`tmux*` `TERM`. This is a terminal-identity heuristic; it does not inspect tmux's negotiated client capabilities.

## Proposed fix

Probe the active tmux server's attached clients at TUI startup using:

```sh
tmux -N -S <socket> list-clients -F '#{client_termname}\t#{client_termfeatures}'
```

Use label-only rendering when every attached client reports the exact `hyperlinks` feature. Keep the destination visible when the probe fails, is ambiguous, finds a mixed-capability server, or detects nested/other multiplexers. A bounded timeout and output limit keep startup responsive.

I implemented and tested this approach locally on branch `fix/tmux-web-link-capabilities` (commit `f446f0f`). The focused TUI test set passes (11/11), and the live probe against tmux 3.7c returns `Supported`.

The presentation decision can be a startup snapshot. A later enhancement could invalidate it when attached clients change; already-rendered scrollback would need an explicit policy.

## References

- Existing expanded-link issue: #31554
- tmux terminal feature documentation: https://man.openbsd.org/tmux.1

Drag the main window around. 5. Hide the pet and repeat the dragging operation for comparison. ### What is the expected behavior? Expected behavior The main window moves smoothly, regardless of whether the pet is visible or nearby. Actual behavior With the pet visible, dragging the main window causes flickering and apparent jumps to previous positions. Hiding the pet stops the problem. ### Additional information

Test | Result -- | -- Switch from a custom pet to a built-in pet | Still reproduces Hide the pet | Issue disappears Drag other applications’ windows | No equivalent issue observed Fully restart ChatGPT with --disable-gpu | Still reproduces Check for an app update | No update available

The GPU test was verified through the running processes:

  • Main process included --disable-gpu.
  • Renderer processes included --disable-gpu-compositing.
  • GPU service included --use-angle=d3d11-warp-webgl.

Disabling hardware acceleration therefore did not resolve the issue.

Recording

Attachment: Desktop 2026.10.12 - 12.28.05.01.mp4

The recording is approximately 17.45 seconds long, at 2560 × 1440 resolution. Around 8.10–8.16 seconds, the main window visibly alternates between positions. The recording alone cannot establish whether this is an actual native window-position change or presentation of stale frames.

Read-only inspection of the installed application bundle found that the pet overlay’s applyPointerInteractivityPolicy() includes a path calling:

setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })

The symptoms closely resemble Electron issue #35030, which reports that mouse forwarding on a secondary window can cause another window in the same application to flicker while being dragged.

Check whether the pet overlay’s mouse forwarding interferes with the main window’s native move/resize loop on Windows. Consider testing whether temporarily suspending forwarding during movement or resizing, then restoring the appropriate interaction state afterward, resolves the issue without breaking pet hover or click-through behavior.

Impact and current workaround

The issue makes it difficult to keep the pet visible while repositioning the main window. The only verified workaround so far is to hide the pet.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, my Dot successfully steered an authorised follow-up into an existing, actively running local Codex conversation. About an hour later, it could still reach the PC and queue a follow-up, but could no longer get the follow-up into the running turn. ChatGPT is listed in **Settings → Computer use → Always-allowed apps**, with the text “ChatGPT can use this app without asking.” Please investigate why the previously working Dot-to-Codex workflow became unavailable, and clarify what that setting covers.

## Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on a connected Windows PC; existing local Codex conversation, not a new cloud task.
- Exact desktop build and Windows build at the time of the transition were not captured.
- Observed on **26 November 2026**; times below are AEDT (UTC+11).

## Steps and observed results

1. With a local Codex conversation already running, ask the Dot to deliver a short, authorised follow-up to that exact conversation mid-turn.
2. **9:47 pm (10:47 UTC), worked:** The Dot pasted instructions into the desktop composer, clicked **Queue**, then clicked **Steer** on the queued item. The text appeared in the active conversation, the queued item cleared, and the run continued.
3. **10:51 pm (11:51 UTC), no mid-turn delivery:** A follow-up was accepted into the queue for the same conversation, but there was no verified delivery to the running turn. The Dot reported it did not attempt another in-app click because it could not use desktop input in ChatGPT/Codex in that session. This is **not** a report that a later Steer click was attempted and ignored.
4. A separate direct connection attempt returned Windows OS error **10050**. That explains the failure of that connection attempt, not the change in access to the desktop workflow.
5. The PC remained reachable, and the Dot separately opened, typed into and closed VS Code. A Windows restart and a fresh desktop-control session restored app discovery; neither established that Steer was available again. No second Codex thread was substituted and no test prompt was left queued.

## Expected behaviour

An authorised Dot should have a supported way to deliver a follow-up into the **active turn of the existing local Codex conversation** and verify that it was accepted. If that operation isn't supported, please show an actionable explanation that distinguishes app approval, whether that session can be steered, and whether a message was only queued. A queue receipt does not help when the instruction must affect the current turn.

## Related reports

- #49862 reports missing existing-thread capabilities on Windows. This report adds a verified successful desktop Queue → Steer followed by loss of that workflow on the same PC and conversation.
- #54112 documents the separate Windows error 10050 when connecting to a desktop-owned session.
- #50289 describes a Steer button that does nothing **after** a click. No failed click was observed here.
- [Community report on existing threads being readable but not writable](https://community.openai.com/t/dot-can-read-existing-local-codex-threads-but-can-t-send-messages-to-them/1419517). A shared cause is not established.
