issues.title: Reasoning models compact at 30 to 40% of the window because the context estimate keeps counting old reasoning tokens

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm using a bring-your-own-key reasoning model (chat completions, thinking on) through the Copilot CLI agent host in VS Code. During tool-heavy work my sessions compact every few minutes: 19 compactions in 107 minutes. Each one fires when the runtime thinks the context is about 80% full, but by then the model server has only seen 30 to 40% of the window. So I keep losing context while there's plenty of room left.

From what I can tell, the local context estimate counts each earlier assistant turn at its full output token count, and for a thinking model nearly all of that is reasoning. Most reasoning-model servers drop old reasoning when they build the prompt (Qwen3- and DeepSeek-R1-style chat templates do this), so it never takes up space in the real prompt. The estimate also doesn't seem to use the provider's reported `inputTokens`, so nothing pulls it back down.

The model has a real window of 262,144 tokens, and I set `maxPromptTokens` to 223,232. In my sessions:

- `session.compaction_start` fires with `trigger: "threshold"` and `currentTokens` between about 180k and 205k. `session.compaction_complete` says `tokenAccountingBasis: "local_full_context_estimate"`.
- For the request right before each compaction, the provider reports about 65k to 110k input tokens. Across 513 compactions, the estimate is a median 2.2 times the provider's number.
- The provider's number is the right one. I sent an over-limit request on purpose, and the server's "request resolved to N input tokens" matched a linear fit of the reported usage.
- Usage does reach the runtime. 105,258 of 105,265 `session.usage_record` events have `usage.inputTokens`, and 105,247 of those are above 0. My gateway includes cached tokens in `inputTokens` (only 481 records have `cacheReadTokens` above 0), so the provider totals aren't understated.
- Between two compactions, the estimate grows by about 100k tokens while the provider's prompt grows by 10k to 50k.
- I regressed that growth on content type over 23 cycles. Reasoning text adds about 0.21 tokens per character to the estimate and roughly nothing to the provider's count. Tool results add about 0.16 to the estimate and 0.09 to the provider's count.

### Affected version

The runtime that ships with VS Code 1.148 (Copilot CLI agent host). I also reproduced it outside VS Code with runtime 1.0.117 from `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` 2.0.4.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I wrote a small OpenAI-compatible mock server and an SDK script for this, and I'm happy to share them.

1. Point a BYOK model at the mock with `maxPromptTokens: 64000`, which puts the threshold at 51,200.
2. Have every model step return about 12,000 characters of reasoning and one tool call, with a 2,000-character tool result. Report the reasoning as about 3,020 output tokens, as a thinking model would. Report the prompt size as chars/4 of the request without the old reasoning, which is what a server with one of those templates actually tokenizes.
3. Run 30 steps and watch `tool.execution_complete.toolTelemetry.metrics.context_current_tokens`, which carries the runtime's running estimate.

What happens:

- Each step adds 3,283 to the estimate and about 570 to the provider's count. Compaction fires at an estimate of 52.6k while the provider reports 21.3k, a ratio of 2.46. Chat completions and the Responses API behave the same way.
- If the mock reports 50 output tokens instead, each step adds 313 and nothing compacts. The difference of 2,970 per step is exactly the extra output tokens.
- If the mock reports `input_tokens: 0` instead of the real number, the estimate hardly moves (13,260, 13,573, 13,886 against 13,263, 13,576, 13,889). That's why I think the estimate doesn't use the provider's input count at all.
- The runtime does resend the old reasoning (`reasoning_content` on chat completions, `reasoning` items on Responses). It's the server that leaves it out.

### Expected behavior

Compaction should start when the real prompt gets close to the limit. Some ideas for getting there:

1. After each response, take the provider's prompt count (`prompt_tokens` or `input_tokens`, plus cached tokens when the provider reports them separately) as the base, and only estimate locally what was added since.
2. When there's no provider count, don't charge old reasoning at its full output token count. At most, count what the request actually contains.
3. Say which basis triggered the compaction in `tokenAccountingBasis`, and put both numbers on `compaction_start`, so a mismatch like this shows up in the logs.

### Additional context

This looks related to #5517, where a pasted PDF was counted at its encoded size (620k estimated against 31k real). In both cases the local estimate drifts far from the provider's count and nothing corrects it.

I also looked at the VS Code side. The agent host's BYOK bridge passes provider usage through to the runtime, so the estimate and the decision to compact seem to live entirely in the runtime.

The repro ran on Windows 11, x64.

issues.title: Copilot app: user extensions never start in sessions linked to a pull request

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In the GitHub Copilot app, user extensions in `~/.copilot/extensions/` never start in a session that has a pull request linked to it, either a PR the session created or a PR session. These sessions get none of the extensions' tools or hooks. Sessions without a linked PR load the same extension normally.

The app log suggests the app decides not to reconcile extensions for these sessions. Every `extensibility live-session refresh completed` line for a PR-linked session shows `extensions_reconciliation_needed=false`. Sessions without a PR show `true`. Both kinds show `extensions_stale=true`:

```
session_id=<PR-linked session, busy>  ... extensions_stale=true skills_stale=true extensions_reconciliation_needed=false
session_id=<PR-linked session>        ... extensions_stale=true skills_stale=true extensions_reconciliation_needed=false
session_id=<session without a PR>     ... extensions_stale=true skills_stale=true extensions_reconciliation_needed=true
```

I checked this on one machine across 4 app runs over 2 days. Every PR-linked session showed `false` and every session without a PR showed `true`. The one exception was a session without a PR that logged `false` once, about 10 seconds after it was created.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot app 1.5.0 (commit 6ff6e7f1), Windows x64. The CLI is 1.0.115 / 1.0.116.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a user extension that writes a heartbeat file when it starts. For example, `~/.copilot/extensions/probe/extension.mjs` calls `joinSession()` and then writes `<sessionId>.alive.json` to a temp folder every 30 s.
2. Restart the app.
3. Open a session that has no linked PR and send a message. The heartbeat file for that session appears and keeps updating.
4. Open a session whose workspace has a linked PR (`created_pr_number` is set, e.g. after the agent opened a PR) and send a message. The session runs normally, but no heartbeat file ever appears for it. The app log shows `extensions_reconciliation_needed=false` for that session ID.

Right now on my machine, 4 sessions without a PR have fresh heartbeats. Two PR-linked sessions that are busy at the same moment have none.

### Expected behavior

User extensions start in every interactive session, whether or not a pull request is linked to it.

### Additional context

- This looks related to #5380, where extensions don't start for sessions created with `create_session` until the user switches to them. Here, though, the session is in the foreground and actively running, and the extension still never starts.
- Use case: a desktop PR review tool hands a prompt (e.g. "resolve the merge conflicts on this PR") to the session that owns the PR through a small extension. PR-linked sessions are the most important case for this, and they are exactly the sessions where the extension never runs.
- Related feature request: a supported way for an external tool to send a prompt into an existing session. Today `ghapp://sessions/<id>` only opens the session, and idle sessions shut down after about 10 minutes, so an extension is the only option.

issues.title: Fork PRs created from the GitHub Copilot app can't enable "Allow edits by maintainers" (`maintainer_can_modify` silently ignored)

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the Copilot agent opens a PR from the user's fork into an upstream repo (`gh pr create --head <user>:<branch>`, using the `GH_TOKEN` the GitHub Copilot app provides), the PR is created with "Allow edits by maintainers" off. Trying to turn it on afterwards with `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}` and `maintainer_can_modify=true` returns success but leaves the value `false`. `gh pr edit` on the same PR fails with `Resource not accessible by integration`.

The token appears to be a GitHub App user token (`X-OAuth-Scopes` is empty). My guess is that it lacks the access to the fork that this setting needs, and GitHub drops the field without reporting an error.

Impact: maintainer and bot workflows can't push to these PRs. For example, our `/fix:link-cache` bot falls back to pushing to `refs/pull/<n>/head` and fails with `! [remote rejected] HEAD -> refs/pull/12889/head (deny updating a hidden ref)`.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.109, run by the GitHub Copilot app in a remote (cloud) session.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In a Copilot app session on an upstream repo where you have a fork, have the agent push a branch to the fork and run `gh pr create -R <upstream> --head <user>:<branch> ...`. Maintainer edits aren't turned off (no `--no-maintainer-edit`).
2. Run `gh pr view <n> --json maintainerCanModify` and get `false`.
3. Run `gh api -X PATCH repos/<upstream>/pulls/<n> -F maintainer_can_modify=true --jq .maintainer_can_modify`. It exits 0 and prints `false`.
4. Example: open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io#12889, which has `maintainerCanModify: false`, and its failed bot push in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry.io/actions/runs/46047662218

### Expected behavior

Fork PRs created by the agent have "Allow edits by maintainers" on, matching `gh pr create`'s default. If the token can't set it, the agent or app reports that instead of failing silently. A setting to choose the default would also help.

### Additional context

- I couldn't find a setting for this in the app's `.github/github-app.yml` reference or in the cloud agent customization docs.
- Workaround: tick the checkbox by hand on each PR.
- Possibly related: PyGithub/PyGithub#3297 (discussion: `maintainer_can_modify` has no effect).
- Side note: in the same session, `gh issue create -R github/copilot-cli` with the app's token also failed with `Resource not accessible by integration (createIssue)`.

issues.title: Copilot CLI ACP mode ignores fusionTier=high and uses Standard routing

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Summary
With `fusionTier` set to `high`, a `copilot -p` run routes the request through **HydraFusion** (`session.fusion_resolved`, `syntheticModel: "hydrafusion"`, a solver plus judge cascade). The **same prompt** sent through `copilot --acp` is routed by **`auto_v2`** instead (`session.auto_mode_resolved`, `routingMethod: "auto_v2"`, one model). No `session.fusion_*` events appear, so the configured tier has no effect.

This is the **runtime** counterpart to #5354. That issue covers ACP not *advertising* Fusion or a tier option, and explicitly did not test which backend `auto` executes. This report shows what actually executes.

### Environment
- Copilot CLI **1.0.116** (`copilot --version` → `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.116.`), Windows 11 x64, installed with `winget install --id GitHub.Copilot --exact`, auto-update disabled during tests
- An individual plan on which Fusion Standard, High and Max are all available (all three verified in `-p` mode on the same machine and account, minutes apart)
- ACP clients: (a) a minimal stdio JSON-RPC client; (b) T3 Code 0.1.11 as a full ACP host. The results were the same.

### Steps to reproduce
1. `copilot config fusionTier high` (confirm with `copilot config fusionTier` → `high`)
2. **Reference run (`-p`):**
   ```
   copilot -p "<PROMPT>" --model fusion --max-ai-credits 30 --output-format json --no-custom-instructions --disable-builtin-mcps --no-ask-user
   ```
3. **ACP run:** start `copilot --acp --model fusion --max-ai-credits 30` in an empty test repository and send **only** these three requests. No `session/set_config_option`, no `session/set_mode`.
   ```json
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,
     "clientInfo":{"name":"acp-repro","version":"0.0.1"},
     "clientCapabilities":{"fs":{"readTextFile":false,"writeTextFile":false},"terminal":false,
       "_meta":{"github.com/copilot":{"events":["assistant.turn_start","assistant.idle","session.idle",
         "session.model_change","session.auto_mode_resolved","session.fusion_route_started",
         "session.fusion_resolved","session.fusion_completed","assistant.fusion_phase_completed",
         "session.usage_checkpoint"]}}}}}
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"<path-to-empty-test-repo>","mcpServers":[]}}
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"session/prompt","params":{"sessionId":"<sessionId from id 2>","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"<PROMPT>"}]}}
   ```
   `session/new` returns `models.currentModelId: "auto"`.

`<PROMPT>` (synthetic, identical in both runs):
```
Do not call any tools. In at most 6 lines: identify the bug in this JavaScript and give a corrected one-line version. function avg(a){ return a.reduce((s,x)=>s+x) / a.length; } Consider empty arrays and arrays of numeric strings.
```

### Expected
The ACP session routes the request the same way the `-p` run does for the same configured tier, or the CLI states that `fusionTier` does not apply to ACP sessions.

### Actual: sanitized telemetry

**Reference `-p` run, `fusionTier=high`:**
```json
{"type":"session.fusion_resolved","data":{"syntheticModel":"hydrafusion","policy":"standard",
 "policyVersion":"hydrafusion_v4_2026-11-10","pattern":"cascade",
 "ruleId":"cascade_sol61_medium_luna6_high_opus55_medium",
 "primaryModel":"gpt-6.1-sol","judgeModel":"gpt-6-luna","repairModel":"claude-opus-5.5",
 "scores":{"reasoning":0.4192,"codeGen":0.3831,"debugging":0.437,"toolUse":0.03}}}
```
It was followed by `assistant.fusion_phase_completed` for `primary` (gpt-6.1-sol) and `judge` (gpt-6-luna, verdict `accept`), then `session.fusion_completed`. *(The `policy: "standard"` label on a High run matches #5457; this report does not rely on that field.)*

**ACP run, same setting and prompt:** event sequence `session.auto_mode_resolved → assistant.turn_start → session.usage_checkpoint → assistant.idle → session.idle`. **No `session.fusion_*` events.**
```json
{"type":"session.auto_mode_resolved","data":{"chosenModel":"gpt-6.1-terra",
 "selectionReason":"Copilot Fusion selected GPT-6.1 Terra since the task has medium complexity.",
 "categoryScores":{"code_gen":0.3831,"reasoning":0.4192,"tool_use":0.03,"debugging":0.437},
 "candidateModels":["gpt-6.1-terra"],"routingMethod":"auto_v2","fallback":false,
 "availableModels":["gpt-6.1-terra"],"hasImage":false}}
```
The session usage was a single model call. The `session.usage_checkpoint` reported `totalPremiumRequests: 1`.

### Confirmed vs inferred

**Experimentally confirmed (CLI 1.0.116):**
1. `-p` with `fusionTier=high` routes through HydraFusion (cascade), as above.
2. `-p` with `fusionTier=standard` routes through `auto_v2`, and that event carries `"autoTier":"balance"`.
3. `-p` with `fusionTier=max` routes through `syntheticModel: "hydrafusion-max"` (`policy: "max"`).
4. ACP with `fusionTier=high` routes through `auto_v2` with **no `autoTier` field** and no `session.fusion_*` events: once with the minimal client and once with T3 Code (a fresh `copilot --acp` process started **after** the setting was changed).
5. The routing classifier's scores are **identical** in the `-p` High run and the ACP run (reasoning 0.4192, debugging 0.437, code_gen 0.3831, tool_use 0.03). The same task was classified the same way, but only `-p` took the HydraFusion path.
6. In ACP `configOptions`, the `model` select lists **two options with value `"auto"`**. After `session/set_config_option {configId:"model", value:"auto"}`, `reasoning_effort` disappears and **no tier or routing-profile option** is advertised (consistent with #5354).
7. `fusionTier` is user-scope only: `copilot config --repo fusionTier high` and `--local` are rejected. 1.0.116 has **no** `--fusion-tier` flag (see also #5290). `--auto-tier` / `COPILOT_AUTO_TIER` select only `auto`-type routing profiles (efficiency, balance, intelligence).

**Inferred, not demonstrated:**
- That ACP sessions do not read `fusionTier` at all. They might read it but have it overridden. Only the routing outcome was observed.
- **Fusion Max over ACP was not tested.** This report makes **no claim** about Max in ACP.
- Each ACP observation is based on one run per client. The `-p` and ACP results were consistent with each other, and the identical classifier scores make chance routing variance an unlikely explanation.

### Why the ACP client is not responsible
- The minimal client sends only `initialize`, `session/new` and `session/prompt`. It changes no model, mode or configuration option.
- T3 Code additionally sends `session/set_config_option {configId:"model", value:"auto"}` at session start. Reproducing that call alone produces `session.model_change {source:"sdk", previousModel:"auto", newModel:"auto", reasoningEffort:null}`, which is a no-op for routing. Both clients produced the same `auto_v2` routing.
- The same machine, account and setting produce HydraFusion routing in `-p` mode immediately before and after the ACP runs.

### Requested (any one would resolve this)
1. **Honor the configured `fusionTier` in ACP sessions**, exactly as in `-p` and interactive mode.
2. **Expose Fusion tier selection through ACP configuration options** while the model is Auto (e.g. a `select` with `standard` / `high` / `max`), so ACP clients can choose the tier per session. This would also resolve #5354.
3. **Provide a supported launch argument or environment variable** (e.g. the documented `--fusion-tier`, or `COPILOT_FUSION_TIER`) that ACP hosts can pass per `copilot --acp` process.

If tier selection is intentionally unsupported over ACP, please document that limitation and the supported alternative.

issues.title: Browser Use activation fails on Windows Unicode profile paths: false registration conflict and broken native launcher

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`/browser-use:activate` fails on Windows when the Browser Host is installed under a profile path containing a non-ASCII character (reproduced with `U+00E9`) and the console code page is 850.

There are two separate encoding problems:

1. The registration reader decodes `reg.exe query` output as UTF-8, although the command emits the active Windows console encoding. A correct registry path is misread, producing the misleading error **"Browser setup belongs to another installation."**
2. The generated `native-host.bat` contains UTF-8 absolute paths but does not select UTF-8 before `cmd.exe` parses them. Node starts, but receives a corrupted host-module path and exits with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Edge therefore cannot connect.

Repeating activation without correcting these problems does not help. This was not a conflicting Copilot installation or a disabled browser extension.

## Affected versions and environment

- Serving GitHub Copilot desktop app: **1.5.0**, stamped build, not a local source build.
- Bundled CLI/SDK installation directory: **1.0.115-7** (distinct from the desktop app version).
- Browser Use plugin: **0.2.1**.
- Browser Native Host: **0.2.1**.
- Edge GitHub Copilot extension: **0.2.2**, enabled.
- Node.js: **v24.12.0**.
- Windows; PowerShell; active console code page **850**.
- Browser: **Microsoft Edge**.

The extension and host were confirmed compatible after the repair. Their different product versions were not the cause.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows with a non-ASCII character in the profile/local-app-data path, and a non-UTF-8 console code page. For example, use a synthetic profile name containing `U+00E9`; no real username is required.
2. Install and enable the matching GitHub Copilot extension in Edge.
3. Run `/browser-use:activate`, which invokes:

   ```text
   node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>\scripts\activate.mjs"
   ```

4. Observe that setup reports a repair but exits with code 1, even though the registered manifest belongs to the current installation.
5. Repeat the same activation; observe the same failure.

Relevant excerpts from the failed activation:

```text
Browser Host setup for 0.2.1 was repaired.
FAIL  Browser setup belongs to another installation. Run /browser-use:activate.
WARN  No Browser runtime is currently connected.
WARN  Browser compatibility could not be verified because no runtime is connected.
Summary: 12 passed, 2 warnings, 1 failures.
[copilot-browser] Browser verification failed. Browser registration remains installed.
```

## Expected behavior

Registration should be compared using Unicode-safe Windows registry reads. The generated native-host launcher should preserve non-ASCII paths, irrespective of the caller's console code page. A correctly registered host should start and connect to Edge without a false installation-conflict diagnosis.

## Diagnosis and isolated reproduction

The affected bundled helpers are in both `scripts/nativeMessagingRegistration.mjs` and `scripts/doctor.mjs`:

- `readRegistryDefaultValue`: runs `reg.exe query <key> /ve` via Node's `execFile`, then parses the implicitly UTF-8-decoded stdout.
- `launcherContent`: emits a UTF-8 batch file containing the absolute Node and native-host paths.
- `launcherRuntimeIsAvailable`: checks the launcher shape and executable's existence, but the original format passes this check even when `cmd.exe` cannot decode its host path.

A direct .NET registry read confirmed that the actual HKCU native-host registration exactly matched the current manifest. Reading the same registration using the original Node helper failed the equality check.

A bounded regression harness extracted those helpers from backups of the original scripts. It generated a temporary launcher and synthetic host module under a directory containing `U+00E9`, executed the launcher under CP850, and checked exact stdout. Both original script copies failed:

- Unicode registry-path equality.
- Actual batch execution: `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the corrupted synthetic module path.

Missing-key behavior and launcher-runtime inspection passed. The harness restored the original console code page and removed its temporary fixture directory.

## Local repair and outcome

With explicit user approval, the two installed scripts were backed up and locally patched:

- Read the registry through .NET using an encoded PowerShell command; return the value as ASCII Base64 carrying UTF-16LE. This avoids dependence on console-output encoding and preserves absent-key behavior.
- Emit `chcp 65001 >nul` before the non-ASCII command line in the generated Windows launcher.
- Update launcher-format inspection consistently, so standard activation regenerates the old launcher and its integrity record through the existing repair path.

The same focused regressions then passed: **8 passed, 0 failed**, versus 4 failures before the repair.

The unmodified activation command was rerun, without extra arguments or bypassing verification:

```text
Summary: 15 passed, 0 warnings, 0 failures.
Browser activation verified. Browser is available.
```

Browser discovery independently returned `product: "edge"` and `status: "online"`, with extension 0.2.2 and host 0.2.1. The persisted launcher hash matched its activation record.

No Edge profile changes, browser restart, global code-page change, or permission bypass was required. This is an unofficial, reversible local workaround that an update may overwrite; an upstream fix should cover both the registry decoder and the native-host launcher, with Windows Unicode-path regression tests.

No real usernames, full local paths, browser instance IDs, credentials, or project data are included in this report.

issues.title: ACP: a content-filtered model response ends the turn with `stopReason: "end_turn"` and sends no message

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
## Summary

When the model's response is blocked by content filtering, `copilot --acp` sends no `session/update` for the turn and answers `session/prompt` with `stopReason: "end_turn"`. The ACP client sees an ordinary finished turn with no reply, and the user gets a blank turn with no explanation.

The interactive CLI handles the same case: the session records `finishReason: "content_filter"`, `contentFilterTriggered: true`, and an `assistant.message` that reads "The model returned no content because the response was blocked by content filtering." The ACP layer drops both the message and the stop reason.

## Version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.117 (also seen on 1.0.116), Linux x64, ACP protocol version 1 (client offers 2).

## Repro

Use a stub BYOK endpoint so no real model call or harmful prompt is needed.

1. Run an OpenAI-compatible stub that streams an empty assistant delta, then `finish_reason: "content_filter"`. (Or an Anthropic stub that streams `message_start`, then `message_delta` with `stop_reason: "refusal"`, then `message_stop`.)
2. Start `copilot --acp --allow-all` with `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` pointing at the stub, and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=openai` (or `anthropic`).
3. Send `initialize`, `session/new`, then `session/prompt` with any text.

## Actual

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"stopReason":"end_turn","usage":{"inputTokens":5,"outputTokens":0,"totalTokens":5,"cachedReadTokens":0,"cachedWriteTokens":0}}}
```

No `agent_message_chunk` arrives between the prompt and the result. Both stub variants (OpenAI `content_filter` and Anthropic `refusal`) give the same output. The session's `events.jsonl` has the `content_filter` usage record and the filtering notice as an `assistant.message`.

A control run with a normal stub reply sends an `agent_message_chunk` with the text and `stopReason: "end_turn"`, as expected.

## Expected

- `session/prompt` returns `stopReason: "refusal"`. The ACP spec defines it for this case and asks clients to show it.
- The filtering notice reaches the client, for example as an `agent_message_chunk`, or in `_meta` with the refusal category when the API supplies one.

## Impact

ACP clients such as T3 Code already render `stopReason: "refusal"` as a visible failure. With `end_turn` they record a completed turn with no reply, and users read it as a lost answer or a hang.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Editing a skill requests sandbox-bypass approval despite an explicit read-write grant for the skills directory.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.117

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Enable sandboxing and add the skills directory to `sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.readwritePaths`.
2. From the repository root, ask Copilot to edit a skill.
3. Copilot requests sandbox-bypass approval.

### Expected behavior

The explicit read-write grant permits the edit without a bypass prompt.

### Additional context

- Changing the working directory to the skill's directory before requesting the edit avoids the prompt.
- The documentation does not explain precedence for conflicting grants on the same path.

issues.title: macOS: Entra broker MCP sign-in (Azure DevOps remote MCP) never cached — MSAL keychain save fails with -34018, account picker every session

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, the Entra account-broker sign-in for the remote Azure DevOps MCP server (`https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`, configured in a workspace `.github/mcp.json`) succeeds, but MSAL can't save the token to the keychain. Every new session opens the "Pick an account" window again, even though only one account exists.

Log lines from every session start (redacted):

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ...
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_sdk::session] received MCP OAuth request without a registered MCP auth handler
[ERROR] Connecting to azure-devops...
[WARNING] [rust:mcp_client::oauth_entra] Entra scope binding validation bypassed for an unbound scope {"scope":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.default","environment_variable":"COPILOT_ENTRA_ONEAUTH_SCOPE_BINDING_MODE"}
[WARNING] [rust:oneauth] [MSAL] ERROR -[MSAIMSIDTokenResponseValidator saveTokenResponseToCache:configuration:oauthFactory:tokenCache:saveSSOStateOnly:context:error:]:368 MSAL.xplat.macOS 12.1.0 Mac 26.6.2 ... Failed to save tokens in cache. Error MaskedError(MSAIMSIDKeychainErrorDomain, -34018)
[ERROR] Successfully authenticated with azure-devops
```

`-34018` is `errSecMissingEntitlement`. The embedded MSAL/OneAuth broker appears to lack the keychain-access-group entitlement it needs to persist tokens, so nothing is cached. Mid-session re-auth ("MCP connection requires authentication; requesting bounded owned recovery") also happens about every 1 to 1.5 hours.

### Affected version

1.0.116

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, add `{"mcpServers":{"azure-devops":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>"}}}` to `.github/mcp.json`.
2. Start `copilot` and sign in through the "Pick an account" window.
3. Quit and start a new session.
4. The account picker appears again. Logs show `MSAIMSIDKeychainErrorDomain, -34018` on each save.

### Expected behavior

The Entra token (and refresh token) is persisted and reused silently across sessions, like other remote MCP servers whose tokens Copilot stores in the keychain or `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`. If the broker cache can't be written, the CLI should fall back to its own token store instead of prompting every session.

### Additional context

- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (Apple Silicon), Homebrew install
- Single work account; Azure CLI is signed in to the same account
- Related but different: #5250 (concurrent broker sign-ins), #4695 (duplicate cache keys on Windows)
- Workaround: run the local `@azure-devops/mcp` server with `--authentication azcli` and disable the remote server via `disabledMcpServers`

issues.title: Copilot CLI 1.0.116 refuses session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory calls from extensions

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In Copilot CLI 1.0.116, calling `session.rpc.metadata.setWorkingDirectory({ workingDirectory })` from a user extension fails with an RPC error and emits a refusal warning:

```text
✗ Command /start failed: Request session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory failed with message: Relaxing session permissions is not available to extensions

! Refused session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory from extension user:start: Relaxing session permissions is not available to extensions. The session owner must make this change; an extension author should remove this call.
```

The call failed with Allow All enabled for the session (`/allow-all`), after the extension's folder-trust check (`session.rpc.permissions.folderTrust.isTrusted`) passed. The target directory was the session's startup working directory, unchanged between session start and the call.

In `copilot-sdk/extension.js` and `copilot-sdk/generated/rpc.d.ts`, the bundled 1.0.116 `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` JSDoc for `metadata.setWorkingDirectory` describes host use and does not state that calls from extensions are refused. Some other extension-restricted methods in `copilot-sdk/extension.js`, such as `gitHubFetch.*` and `gitHubRelease.downloadAsset`, state `Refused for extensions.` or `Extensions cannot use this method.` in their JSDoc comments.

Related issue: #3035 (where a commenter noted an extension calling `session.rpc.metadata.setWorkingDirectory` as a workaround in the desktop app with CLI 1.0.94-3).

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.116`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Reproduction outline:

1. Enable experimental extensions (`"experimental": true` in `~/.copilot/settings.json`).
2. Create `~/.copilot/extensions/repro-cwd/extension.mjs` registering a `/repro-cwd` slash command via `joinSession` from `@microsoft/copilot-sdk/extension`, with a handler reading the session's absolute `workingDirectory` via `session.rpc.metadata.snapshot()` and calling `await session.rpc.metadata.setWorkingDirectory({ workingDirectory })`.
3. In Copilot CLI 1.0.116 started in a trusted folder, enable `/allow-all` for the session and run `/repro-cwd`.

The output above came from an interactive run of a user extension named `user:start`. Running `/repro-cwd` from the outline above is expected to fail with `Request session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory failed with message: Relaxing session permissions is not available to extensions` and a `Refused session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory from extension user:repro-cwd` warning.

### Expected behavior

If refusing `session.metadata.setWorkingDirectory` for extensions is intentional:
- Document the restriction in the release notes and in the bundled `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` JSDoc for `metadata.setWorkingDirectory`.
- Consider either allowing a same-directory call to succeed without modifying session permissions or the permission primary directory, or providing a host-mediated working-directory change with explicit session-owner confirmation.

### Additional context

- Operating system: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 SP6 (Linux 6.4.0-150600.23.81-default)
- CPU architecture: x86_64
- Package-content comparison (not a runtime test of older releases): The strings `Relaxing session permissions is not available to extensions` and `extension_refused` are absent from cached `1.0.113` and `1.0.114` `prebuilds/linux-x64/runtime.node`, and present in `1.0.115` and `1.0.116`.

issues.title: ACP does not advertise Copilot Fusion or its tier configuration when Fusion is available interactively

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot Fusion is available in the interactive Copilot CLI, but ACP advertises the routing model as **Auto** and exposes no Fusion/Auto-tier configuration.

This prevents ACP clients such as T3 Code from displaying Fusion and offering its tier selector. The behavior reproduces directly with `copilot --acp`, without T3 Code.

Enabling `COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS=DYNAMIC_AUTO_TIERS` for the ACP subprocess did not change the observed advertisement.

This report concerns **model discovery and configuration parity**. It does not establish that `auto` cannot route to Fusion internally.

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105.
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use an account for which Fusion is available in the interactive Copilot CLI's model picker.
2. Launch the same CLI version as an ACP server:

   ```sh
   copilot --acp
   ```

3. Send newline-delimited JSON-RPC requests through stdin. Initialize the connection:

   ```json
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":1,"clientCapabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"fusion-acp-repro","version":"1.0.0"}}}
   ```

4. Create a session, replacing `/absolute/path/to/workspace` with an existing workspace:

   ```json
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/new","params":{"cwd":"/absolute/path/to/workspace","mcpServers":[]}}
   ```

5. Inspect the returned model options and session configuration. Observed:
   - The routing model has ID `auto` and display name `Auto`, not Copilot Fusion.
   - Duplicate `auto` options were present.
   - No Fusion/Auto-tier configuration option was advertised.
   - With the initial Claude selection, configuration IDs were `mode`, `model`, `reasoning_effort`, `agent`, and `allow_all`.

6. Select Auto, substituting the returned session ID:

   ```json
   {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"session/set_config_option","params":{"sessionId":"<session-id>","configId":"model","value":"auto"}}
   ```

   The resulting configuration IDs were `mode`, `model`, `agent`, and `allow_all`. `reasoning_effort` disappeared, but no Fusion/Auto-tier option appeared.

7. Restart the server with the dynamic-tier feature flag and repeat:

   ```sh
   COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS=DYNAMIC_AUTO_TIERS copilot --acp
   ```

   Fusion naming and tier configuration were still absent.

The advertised `/model` command was also tested through ACP. It returned:

```text
The model-picker dialog is only available in the interactive CLI.
```

### Expected behavior

When Fusion is available for the authenticated account, ACP should expose enough metadata and configuration for clients to:

- Identify the routing option as Copilot Fusion where appropriate.
- Discover supported tiers and the current selection.
- Change tiers through the supported ACP configuration interface.

Keeping `auto` as the stable underlying model ID is fine; a separate model ID is not required.

If Fusion tier selection is intentionally unsupported over ACP, please document that limitation and the supported alternative.

### Additional context

**Environment**

- macOS, Apple Silicon (`arm64`).
- Copilot CLI: `1.0.105`.
- Affected ACP client: T3 Code desktop nightly `0.1.8-nightly.20261104.4179`.
- Direct ACP reproduction bypassed T3 entirely.

**Cross-surface observations**

- Interactive Copilot CLI: Fusion available.
- VS Code Agents Window: "Copilot Fusion" with "High" tier visible.
- Regular VS Code Chat: Fusion not visible.
- T3 Code via Copilot ACP: Auto available, no Fusion tier selector.

The regular VS Code Chat observation may have a separate cause and is included for context, not as evidence of an ACP defect.

**Investigation findings**

- T3 reads advertised ACP model/configuration options and preserves their names. The direct reproduction demonstrates that the missing metadata exists upstream of T3's picker.
- Repeating the probe with T3's Copilot-specific client capability metadata also did not expose Fusion or tier configuration.
- The inspected VS Code Agent Host implementation explicitly enables dynamic Auto tiers and uses discovered Fusion-tier metadata to present `auto` as Fusion.
- That VS Code source checkout references Copilot runtime `1.0.106-6`, so its behavior is not a same-runtime comparison with CLI `1.0.105`.
- No model-generation request was used to verify which backend `auto` ultimately executes.

**Related reports**

- github/copilot-cli#5298 - Fusion alias requires the dynamic Auto tiers flag in `1.0.105`.
- github/copilot-cli#5290 - documented `--fusion-tier` argument is missing in `1.0.105`.
- github/copilot-cli#4975 - HydraFusion unavailable in experimental mode.

These appear related, but none was confirmed to cover ACP model/configuration advertisement specifically.

**Documentation:** https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/models/copilot-fusion

*Prepared with GitHub Copilot in T3 Code using Auto model selection. The specific underlying model was not exposed by the session.*

issues.title: Agent Plugins 1.0: `.instructions.md` files and `applyTo` frontmatter in `com.github.copilot/rules/` are silently ignored

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When packaging a plugin using the **Agent Plugins 1.0.0** format (`"$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json"`), Copilot CLI loads skills (`skills/`), MCP servers (`mcp.json`), custom agents (`com.github.copilot/agents/`), hooks (`com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json`), and LSP servers (`com.github.copilot/lsp.json`), **but silently ignores standard GitHub Copilot `.instructions.md` files placed in `com.github.copilot/rules/`**.

According to the [CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#components) and the [VS Code Agent plugin authoring reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/agent-plugin-reference), `com.github.copilot/rules/` is the Copilot-specific extension directory for plugin rules/instructions. Across the Copilot ecosystem (`.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `~/.copilot/instructions/*.instructions.md`, and VS Code Agent Plugins), the standard Copilot rule format is `*.instructions.md` with YAML frontmatter (`description`, `applyTo`).

Through black-box testing on Copilot CLI `1.0.109`, two cumulative issues prevent `.instructions.md` plugin rules from working across VS Code and Copilot CLI:

1. **`.instructions.md` (and `.md`) files in `com.github.copilot/rules/` are completely ignored.**
   Copilot CLI only discovers files ending in `.mdc` inside `com.github.copilot/rules/`. Files ending in `.instructions.md` or `.md` do not appear in `/env`, `/instructions`, or `copilot instruction list`, are never injected into the prompt, and produce no warning even with `--log-level debug`. Meanwhile, VS Code loads `.instructions.md` from the exact same `com.github.copilot/rules/` folder.
2. **Copilot frontmatter (`applyTo`) is ignored in plugin rules, and `alwaysApply` semantics are inverted for glob-scoped rules.**
   Even after renaming a file from `.instructions.md` to `.mdc`:
   - `applyTo` is ignored; Copilot CLI only parses `globs` (and requires a non-empty `description`), whereas VS Code parses `applyTo` and ignores `globs`.
   - Omitting `alwaysApply` or setting `alwaysApply: false` on a glob-scoped rule (e.g., `globs: ["**/*.yaml"]`) causes `copilot instruction list --json` to report `"defaultDisabled": true` (`0/1 enabled` in `/instructions`). As a result, **glob-scoped rules with `alwaysApply: false` (or omitted) never fire out of the box** when matching files are read unless the user manually enables them in `/instructions` in every session.
   - Counter-intuitively, a rule must set **both** `alwaysApply: true` **and** `globs: [...]` to be enabled by default (`"defaultDisabled": false`) while still scoping activation to matching files rather than injecting globally at startup.


Also, it seems there is another issue with instructions on command like :  **`copilot --plugin-dir <dir> instruction list` ignores `--plugin-dir`.**
   Unlike `copilot --plugin-dir <dir> skill list` (and interactive `/env` / `/instructions`), the `instruction list` subcommand ignores `--plugin-dir` and always prints `No instruction sources found.` unless the plugin is installed into `$COPILOT_HOME`.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Run the following self-contained reproduction script in an isolated `COPILOT_HOME`:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/repro-plugin /tmp/repro-copilot-home
mkdir -p /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules /tmp/repro-copilot-home

cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/plugin.json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "repro-plugin",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Minimal reproducer for plugin instructions"
}
EOF

# 1. Standard Copilot .instructions.md file -> SILENTLY IGNORED
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/standard-copilot.instructions.md
---
name: "Standard Copilot Rule"
description: "Standard Copilot instruction file using applyTo"
applyTo: "**/*.yaml"
---
Follow standard YAML conventions.
EOF

# 2. .mdc with globs and alwaysApply: false -> DISCOVERED, BUT DISABLED BY DEFAULT
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-disabled.mdc
---
description: "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply false"
globs: ["**/*.yaml"]
alwaysApply: false
---
Follow MDC YAML conventions (disabled by default).
EOF

# 3. .mdc with globs and alwaysApply: true -> ENABLED BY DEFAULT & SCOPED TO GLOBS
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/repro-plugin/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-enabled.mdc
---
description: "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply true"
globs: ["**/*.yaml"]
alwaysApply: true
---
Follow MDC YAML conventions (enabled).
EOF
```

#### Step A — Test `instruction list` with `--plugin-dir` (Bug 4)

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot --plugin-dir /tmp/repro-plugin instruction list
```

Actual output:
```text
No instruction sources found.
```
*(Whereas launching interactively with `copilot --plugin-dir /tmp/repro-plugin` and running `/env` or `/instructions` **does** find the `.mdc` files, and `copilot --plugin-dir <dir> skill list` honors `--plugin-dir`.)*

#### Step B — Install the plugin and inspect `copilot instruction list --json` (Bugs 1 & 2)

```bash
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot plugin install /tmp/repro-plugin
COPILOT_HOME=/tmp/repro-copilot-home copilot instruction list --json
```

Actual output:
```json
[
  {
    "id": "plugin-rule/repro-plugin:mdc-glob-disabled",
    "label": "repro-plugin: mdc-glob-disabled",
    "description": "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply false",
    "location": "plugin",
    "type": "plugin",
    "sourcePath": "/tmp/repro-copilot-home/installed-plugins/_direct/repro-plugin-xxxx/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-disabled.mdc",
    "defaultDisabled": true,
    "applyTo": [
      "**/*.yaml"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "plugin-rule/repro-plugin:mdc-glob-enabled",
    "label": "repro-plugin: mdc-glob-enabled",
    "description": "MDC rule with globs and alwaysApply true",
    "location": "plugin",
    "type": "plugin",
    "sourcePath": "/tmp/repro-copilot-home/installed-plugins/_direct/repro-plugin-xxxx/com.github.copilot/rules/mdc-glob-enabled.mdc",
    "defaultDisabled": false,
    "applyTo": [
      "**/*.yaml"
    ]
  }
]
```

Notice that:
- `standard-copilot.instructions.md` is completely missing from the discovered sources.
- `mdc-glob-disabled.mdc` has `"defaultDisabled": true`, so in a session (`/instructions`) it starts unchecked (`•`) and does not trigger when reading a `.yaml` file.
- `mdc-glob-enabled.mdc` has `"defaultDisabled": false` and `"applyTo": ["**/*.yaml"]` (mapped from `globs`, while an actual `applyTo` key in frontmatter is ignored).

### Summary of observed behavior matrix

| File in `com.github.copilot/rules/` | Frontmatter | VS Code behavior | Copilot CLI `1.0.109` behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rule.instructions.md` | `description` + `applyTo: "**"` | Loaded (global) | **Silently ignored** |
| `rule.instructions.md` | `description` + `applyTo: "**/*.yaml"` | Loaded (glob-scoped) | **Silently ignored** |
| `rule.mdc` | `description` + `applyTo: "**/*.yaml"` | Loaded (glob-scoped) | Discovered, **`applyTo` ignored**, disabled by default (`defaultDisabled: true`) |
| `rule.mdc` | `description` + `globs: ["**/*.yaml"]` + `alwaysApply: false` (or omitted) | Loaded, **`globs` ignored** | Discovered, **disabled by default** (`0/1 enabled` in `/instructions`; never triggers unless manually toggled per session) |

### Expected behavior

1. **Support `.instructions.md` natively in `com.github.copilot/rules/`**: Since `com.github.copilot/` is GitHub Copilot's own client extension namespace in Agent Plugins 1.0, Copilot CLI should discover `*.instructions.md` files alongside `*.mdc` (matching `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `~/.copilot/instructions/*.instructions.md`, and VS Code's plugin loader).
2. **Support Copilot frontmatter (`applyTo`) and intuitive activation defaults**:
   - Accept `applyTo` (string or array) in addition to `globs` so a single `.instructions.md` file works identically in both VS Code and Copilot CLI without duplicating metadata.
   - Treat glob-scoped rules (`applyTo` / `globs` without `alwaysApply: false`) as enabled for pattern-matching by default, rather than disabled for the whole session unless `alwaysApply: true` is also set. When `applyTo` is `"**"` or `"*"`, treat the rule as session-wide.
3. **Honor `--plugin-dir` in `copilot instruction list`**: Match `copilot skill list` and interactive sessions so plugin authors can validate `com.github.copilot/rules/` during local development without reinstalling the plugin on every edit.
4. **Document the `com.github.copilot/rules/` file format and frontmatter contract** in the [CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#components).

### Additional context

- **OS:** Linux (`x86_64`, Ubuntu / WSL2)
- **Shell:** `bash`
- **Impact & current workaround:** As VS Code deprecates its legacy Local harness in favor of the shared Copilot harness, organizations migrating shared engineering harnesses to **Agent Plugins 1.0** need a single plugin package to deliver skills, MCP servers, agents, hooks, LSPs, and `.instructions.md` rules across both VS Code and Copilot CLI. Currently, the only way to avoid duplicating every rule file in `com.github.copilot/rules/` is to include both `applyTo` and `globs` + `alwaysApply: true` in each `.instructions.md` frontmatter and commit relative `<name>.mdc -> <name>.instructions.md` symlinks alongside them (which breaks on Windows checkouts when `core.symlinks=false`).

issues.title: Voice server permanent deadlock when pid file is deleted while server process survives (bind-loser exits before writing pid)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
## Summary
Voice server enters a permanent deadlock ("Failed to connect to or spawn the voice server after 3 attempts: voice server did not write a valid pid file within 8000ms") whenever its pid file is deleted (e.g. by OS temp-directory cleanup) while the server process itself is still alive and holding the named pipe.

## Root cause (traced in shipped 1.0.84-1 win32-x64 build)
Voice IPC uses two independent records of server liveness that can desync:
- A Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\copilot-voice-<hash>` (kernel object, survives independently)
- A pid file at `%TEMP%\copilot-voice\<hash>.pid` (the client's *only* source of truth)

Both `<hash>` values are derived deterministically: `sha256(cliVersion + "|" + sha256(USERPROFILE).slice(0,8)).slice(0,8)`.

Sequence that produces the deadlock:
1. A server starts, wins the pipe, writes its pid file. It keeps running (idle-shutdown only arms once its connected-client count reaches 0; clients that die without a clean disconnect can keep that count above 0 indefinitely, so a server can persist for days).
2. The pid file is removed independently of the process (observed cause: Windows temp-directory cleanup). The pipe is untouched — it's a kernel object, not a file.
3. `app.js` client logic reads the pid file to decide whether to connect or spawn:
   ```js
   let p = readPid(t.pidFile);
   if (p !== null && isAlive(p)) { connect(t.address) /* ... */ }
   // else: falls straight through to spawning a new server — never attempts connect(t.address) directly
   ```
   A missing pid file skips the connect branch entirely, even though `t.address` is already known deterministically and the pipe is live and accepting connections.
4. The client spawns a new server. The new process computes the same pipe name, tries to bind, and loses to the still-running original.
5. In `voice-server.js`, the losing branch exits **before** ever writing a pid file:
   ```js
   S === "lost" && (log("bind-loser..."), await i.dispose(), process.exit(id)) // id = 10
   // ... pid file write (Lo(t.pidFile, process.pid)) is further down, never reached here
   ```
6. The client waits the full pid-file timeout (`$_n = 8e3`, 8000ms) for a file that can never appear, then retries (`WJe = [0,100,500]`, 3 attempts total), then throws the error above.

Every retry repeats step 4-6 identically — this is a **permanent** deadlock, not a transient failure. It only resolves if something external kills the original server or manually restores the pid file.

## Suggested fixes (either alone fixes it)
1. In the client (`app.js`), when the pid file is missing/stale, attempt `connect(t.address)` directly before spawning — the address is already computed deterministically, so this costs nothing and immediately closes the race.
2. In the server (`voice-server.js`), on `bind-loser`, write the *winning* pid (which is discoverable from the bind failure) to the pid file before exiting, instead of exiting silently with no pid file at all.

Either change means a deleted pid file can never produce an unrecoverable state as long as the real owning process is still alive.

## Environment
- Copilot CLI 1.0.84-1, win32-x64
- Reproduced by manually deleting `%TEMP%\copilot-voice\<hash>.pid` while a previously-started voice server process was still running; the next voice-triggering CLI invocation failed with the exact reported error, deterministically, on every retry.

## Workaround used
Killing the orphaned server process (identified via its named pipe and boot-time server log) releases the pipe, allowing a fresh spawn to bind and write its pid file normally. A local `sessionStart` hook now detects this exact signature (dead/missing pid file + live matching pipe + exactly one candidate `copilot.exe --prefer-version <version>` process) and self-heals by writing the correct pid before the CLI ever attempts to connect.

issues.title: Tool call hangs after extension startup fails

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

After I resumed a large session, an extension failed inside `joinSession()` before reporting ready, and its process exited.

The CLI continued to offer the extension's custom tool. I asked the CLI to call it. The CLI started the call, but the handler did not run and the call reported no error. I aborted it after 9 minutes 38 seconds.

This issue concerns cleanup and dispatch after extension startup failure. A separate large-session attachment defect triggered the failure in this run.

### Environment

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.82
@github/copilot-sdk 1.0.9-preview.2
Node.js v24.18.1
Linux x86_64
```

### Confirmed startup trigger

I traced the installed 1.0.82 `app.js` bundle. `joinSession()` sends a `session.resume` request containing registration options rather than session history. The host still serializes the resident session's full event array while attaching the extension:

1. `handleSessionResumeCore()` handles `session.resume` and calls the host's `initializeSession()` with `replayEvents: false`.
2. The host's `initializeSession()` ignores that option and passes `session.getEvents()` to `seamHost.initializeSession()`.
3. `seamHost.initializeSession()` calls `JSON.stringify(events)`.

Node.js v24.18.1 rejects JavaScript strings longer than 536,870,888 UTF-16 code units and throws `Invalid string length`. I estimated each serialized event array's length from its session event log. Extension attachment succeeded below the limit and failed above it.

In the run that reproduced the stale registration, `joinSession()` failed with `Invalid string length`. That session's `events.jsonl` file was about 1.2 GB.

Honoring `replayEvents: false` would remove this trigger. Registration cleanup must still handle every startup failure.

### Reduced extension

```js
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { joinSession } from "@github/copilot-sdk/extension";

await joinSession({
    tools: [{
        name: "stale_tool_probe",
        description: "Verify extension tool lifecycle.",
        parameters: {
            type: "object",
            properties: {},
            additionalProperties: false,
        },
        skipPermission: true,
        handler: async () => {
            await writeFile(
                new URL("handler-ran.marker", import.meta.url),
                "handler ran\n",
            );
            return "handler-ran";
        },
    }],
});
```

### Observed sequence

1. I stored the reduced extension under `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/extensions/stale-tool-probe/extension.mjs`.
2. I resumed the large session.
3. `joinSession()` failed with `Invalid string length` before the extension reported ready, and the extension process exited.
4. I asked the CLI to call `stale_tool_probe`. The CLI started the call instead of rejecting it as an unknown tool.
5. The call was still pending when I aborted it. `handler-ran.marker` did not appear.

### Expected behavior

- The CLI offers an extension's registrations only while the extension is ready and connected.
- Startup failure or process exit removes every registration owned by that extension.
- A tool call fails promptly if its owning extension is unavailable at dispatch or exits while the call is pending.

### Actual behavior

- The failed extension's tool remained available after its process exited.
- The call did not reach the handler or report an error.

### Related issues

#4590 reports a different `session.resume` failure involving hook-processor disposal during extension reconnects.

#3856 reports the inverse symptom: Extension tools disappear after a resume.

issues.title: MCP tool result image content blocks are not surfaced to the model

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When an MCP server returns an image content block in a tool result (per the MCP specification: content array item {type:"image", mimeType:"image/png", data:<base64>}), the image never reaches the model. Only the text blocks and structuredContent of the same tool result are delivered.

Verified from the agent side (Copilot CLI 1.0.80, Windows):
1. The MCP server's wire format is spec-compliant. Capturing the raw stdio JSON-RPC response for a screenshot tool shows content[0] = text block and content[1] = a valid image block (mimeType image/png, correct base64 PNG payload).
2. 2. Across multiple calls (window screenshot, region screenshot), the image data never appeared in the model context; only the text metadata block arrived.
3. 3. Static inspection of app.js (1.0.80) shows image handling only in two paths: user-attachment sanitization (file_data / image_url / input_image) and the mcp-sampling converter for user-role messages. No conversion path exists for MCP tool-result image blocks, and tool results are assembled through the native session layer (session.mcp.apps.callTool).
User-attached images (paste / drag-drop / @file) work fine, so the model and plan support vision. The gap is specific to images returned by MCP tools.

### Affected version

1.0.80 (Windows 10.0.26200, PowerShell)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure any MCP server whose tool returns an image content block (e.g. a UI-automation server with a screenshot tool; any tool returning {type:"image", mimeType:"image/png", data:<base64>} reproduces it).
2. 2. In an interactive Copilot CLI session, ask the agent to call that tool and then describe what it sees in the image.
3. 3. Observe: the agent only receives the text blocks / structuredContent of the tool result. It reports the image metadata but cannot see the actual pixels, and often states the image content is unavailable.

### Expected behavior

When the selected model supports vision, image content blocks inside MCP tool results should be passed to the model (like user-attached images), so agents can act on screenshots and other tool-generated images.

### Additional context

This blocks a whole class of computer-use / UI-automation workflows: MCP servers that follow the spec and return screenshots as image blocks work in other agent CLIs that surface tool-result images, but not in Copilot CLI. Current workaround: agents must rely on structured reads only, or the user must manually attach the image.

**Issue submitted by GLM-5.3 via rpacu MCP**

issues.title: CLI repeatedly ignores commit instruction, tool rejections and reminders to check its rules

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI repeatedly proposed adding a `Co-authored-by` trailer despite the user explicitly instructing it not to. Even after the user rejected commands and repeatedly told it to check its rules, the assistant failed to find and apply the instruction until after a third rejection.

### Affected version

1.0.114

### Steps to reproduce / observed sequence

1. The user had explicitly instructed the assistant not to add `Co-authored-by` trailers to commits, then asked it to commit work in a continued session after history had been summarized.
2. The assistant proposed staging and committing with the prohibited trailer. The user rejected the command.
3. The assistant guessed that the problem was the length of the staging command and retried a shorter command with the same trailer. The user rejected it and reminded the assistant to check its rules.
4. Rather than finding the instruction, the assistant asked the user to identify the rule. The user told it to read the rules and figure it out.
5. The assistant searched repository instruction files, attempted a history search that did not return the relevant local result, and then guessed that the problem was the combined shell command. It staged the changes and again proposed a commit with the trailer. The user rejected it a third time.
6. Only then did the assistant search local session history successfully, find the explicit prior instruction, and commit without the trailer.

### Expected behavior

The assistant should honor the explicit instruction when preparing the commit. After a rejection and reminders to check its rules, it should review relevant available instructions and conversation history, rather than repeatedly guessing or asking the user to restate them.

### Additional context

Observed on macOS. The prior instruction was available in local session history, and a successful search resolved the issue. This report describes one observed session; reproducibility under other session and memory configurations has not been established.

- The detailed transcript shows match counts for grep and rg searches with automatically corrected flags, and shows clean results when expanded.
- Copilot Fusion shows shell commands interrupted with Ctrl+C as aborted instead of pending, including after you resume the session.
- Organization custom agents use their configured model when it is available and you haven't specified a model with --model.
- The Issues and Pull requests tabs become available without restarting Copilot CLI when you add a GitHub remote to the current repository
- Fix interactive turns failing when an MCP tool advertises a null anyOf in its output schema.
- Keep Git configuration and hooks read-only in sandboxed repositories granted write access through readwritePaths, even when automatic working directory access is disabled
- Git authentication for plugin marketplaces no longer opens an extra console window on Windows
- On Linux with non-setuid Bubblewrap 0.11 or later, sandboxed commands can start when a denied path under a read-only mount does not yet exist.
- Keep the current CLI session signed out after /logout instead of automatically signing back in with another available credential.
- Keep newer notifications in /settings visible for their full duration when an older notification expires.

2026-11-27

- Add sandbox.userPolicy.network.extraCaCertificates, in user or managed settings, to trust custom CA certificates for sandboxed commands through TLS-intercepting proxies
- Add explicit tool exposure so custom agents can opt in to tools
- Fix Page Down stalling at a pinned prompt in a 10-row terminal with tabs enabled.
- Approving an MCP server's tools for the session or for a location no longer also approves Copilot's built-in requests, such as shell commands or memory stores, when the server's name matches a built-in permission type. The approval still covers that server's tools, including after the session is resumed.
- Starting in autopilot now asks before launching each extension, instead of denying every extension with "no one to approve"
- Restore original binary skill assets when rejecting a Forge draft and preserve edits made after generation.
- `/mcp search` explains why a registry server can't be installed instead of showing an endless installation spinner.
- Quitting a local CLI session with /exit or Ctrl+D discards queued prompts so they don't run after the exit summary.
- Copilot CLI starts without plugins when it cannot read or parse config.json, leaving the file unchanged.
- Match MCP server names regardless of capitalization in `/mcp` commands and `--disable-mcp-server`, with exact matches taking precedence.
- Answering a permission prompt keeps the composer draft unchanged.
- On Linux and macOS, stop child processes of a GITHUB_ASKPASS sign-in helper that is still running when it times out.
- Keep existing repository settings files read-only for sandboxed commands and agent edits in writable Git worktrees on macOS and Linux.
- Git commits, branch creation, and stashing work again in linked worktrees the Copilot CLI sandbox can write to.
- Fix indexed search results for regular expressions that join groups of alternatives.
- Stopping Copilot CLI in ACP mode with Ctrl+C no longer reports a false shutdown error or exits with a failure status.
- Prevent repeated notices about organization-required plugins when resuming a session or when authentication refreshes.
- Use a recognizable Copilot CLI name for voice input in Windows microphone privacy settings.
- `copilot help extensions` no longer says your own and plugin extensions load with -p; an extension starts there only if its launch is already approved, by --allow-all-tools or --yolo or by an approval saved earlier
- Built-in searches no longer fail when Copilot sends flags such as line numbers and result limits, or a list of paths, as text.
- Resume shared sessions even when their selected model is unavailable, so you can choose a different model with /model.
- PowerShell hooks on Windows preserve native program exit codes, so exit code 2 is treated as a warning or denial rather than a hook failure.
- Show an error instead of silently switching providers when a repository pins a model to an unavailable provider.
- Only announce a new session checkpoint after automatic compaction if the checkpoint was saved.
- Trusting a folder for the current session reloads MCP servers once and shows a single reload summary.
- On Linux, Copilot accepts keyboard input again if the interactive shell opened with `$` is killed.
- Subagents respect the tool list in their custom agent file, even when the file has no prompt.
- Load connected Copilot Connectors when resuming a CLI session while GitHub sign-in is still finishing.
- Background agents can continue their conversations after restarting the CLI and resuming a session
- Pressing Enter more than once on the folder trust prompt trusts the folder and reloads plugins once, instead of restarting every extension for each extra key press
- Subagent details in /tasks show the reasoning effort the agent uses when the requested level isn't supported.
- Running tasks in `/tasks` stay on one line and keep their spinners visible in narrow terminals.
- Successful non-interactive CLI runs exit with code 0 when a session write fails temporarily but the final save succeeds.
- Remove extra blank lines below wrapped text in narrow terminals, including task descriptions and IDs in /tasks.
- Keep the MCP tool cache disabled across reloads when `COPILOT_MCP_TOOL_CACHE=false`, so Copilot neither reads nor writes tool snapshots.
- `/sandbox policy` identifies grants that point to broken symlinks and warns that they can prevent sandboxed commands from starting.

issues.title: shell: parallel shell calls still fail on 2.4.2 with Store PowerShell 7 (os error 5 / 0xC0070005)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/service
labels.description: Background service and server

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, when the agent issues two shell tool calls in the same turn, exactly one of them fails before it starts because process creation for Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 (MSIX) is denied. Sequential shell calls never fail. Reproduced on the current latest release (2.4.2).

This looks like the same job-attachment problem as #63892, and the same user-visible symptom as the closed #64803, but it still reproduces on 2.4.2 with the packaged shell, and the proposed fix in #64137 was never merged.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.4.2 (npm `@opencode/cli@2.4.2`, published 2026-11-26; latest at the time of writing)
- Client: OpenCode Desktop 2.4.2
- Model and provider: not relevant (failure happens in the shell tool before any model interaction)
- OS: Windows 11 25H2, `10.0.26200.9974` (x64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal (`WT_SESSION` set, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset)
- Shell: Microsoft Store PowerShell 7.7.0 (`Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`), resolved through the app execution alias `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.exe`
- Install/channel: release, npm install; process daemon `opencode-pty` 0.6.0 (`~/.cache/opencode/bin/opencode-pty/0.6.0-3ca87f140ff90483`)
- Active plugins: superpowers (`superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git`), no others

## Reproduction

1. On Windows 11 x64, install PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store (7.7.0) and let OpenCode resolve it as the shell for the shell tool.
2. In a single turn, ask the agent to run the shell tool twice in parallel, e.g. `Write-Output A` and `Write-Output B`.
3. Exactly one result completes; the other returns, before any command output:

```text
failed to spawn C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.exe:
Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

4. Repeat the same turn: every round fails the same way, with exactly one failure.

## Expected Behavior

Both shell tool calls start and return their output.

## Actual Behavior

One of the two parallel calls fails at spawn time with `os error 5` (Access is denied). Which one fails is not deterministic, but the count is: exactly one per parallel round, 7 rounds out of 7. Sequential calls (single call per turn) never failed across 10+ invocations.

Using the packaged EXE path instead of the alias changes the error code to the one reported in #63892:

```text
failed to spawn C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.7.0.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.exe:
OS Error -1073283067 (FormatMessageW() returned error 317) (os error -1073283067)
```

`-1073283067` is `0xC0070005`, with the same one-of-two concurrency pattern.

## Additional Context

### What was ruled out

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same alias, 15 sequential spawns from PowerShell | 15/15 succeed |
| Same alias, 8 concurrent `Process.Start` calls | 8/8 succeed |
| Same alias, Node `child_process.spawn`, 2 concurrent x 10 rounds | 0/20 failures |
| OpenCode shell tool, 2 parallel calls, Store `pwsh.exe` | exactly one failure per round, 7/7 rounds |
| OpenCode shell tool, 2 parallel calls, `powershell.exe` (5.1) | both succeed |
| OpenCode shell tool, 2 parallel calls, `cmd.exe` | both succeed |

The alias itself is healthy (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell` reports `Status=Ok`), and the daemon still resolves it even after both `WindowsApps` directories are removed from `PATH`, which matches the analysis in #64803.

### Why this looks like the job-attachment path

The two error codes split exactly along the lines described in #63892: the app execution alias returns raw `5`, the packaged EXE returns `0xC0070005`. In both cases only the second concurrent packaged process fails, while a plain `powershell.exe` or `cmd.exe` is unaffected. That is consistent with `CreateProcessW` + `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST` hitting the MSIX container job (`AddProcessToContainer`), and with the immediate jobless retry running while the first packaged process is still alive. A retry that waits for the container job to drain, or skipping the job attribute for packaged executables, would presumably fix both issues.

### Workaround in use

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "shell": "C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe"
}
```

With `shell` pinned to Windows PowerShell 5.1, parallel shell calls work reliably. This only works around the spawn path; the user's own terminals keep using PowerShell 7.

### Related

- #64803 — same symptom, closed as completed on 2026-11-19
- #63892 — same root area, `0xC0070005` on the packaged path, closed as completed on 2026-11-19
- #64137 — proposed fix for the Windows pipe spawn retry, closed without merging

### Logs

The failure is not written to `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`; it only surfaces in the tool result. No log excerpt is available.
