issues.title: [FEATURE]: Native secret references for provider and MCP credentials (OS credential store or secret manager)

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Login and credentials

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

It has been suggested before, but every earlier request is closed. #4318 (OS credential store) was closed automatically after 60 days without activity, and its closing comment asks for a new issue if the request is still relevant. It still is, so this is the new issue, with a real-world case.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

OpenCode has no native way to read a provider key or an MCP token from an OS credential store (Credential Manager, Keychain, libsecret) or from a secret manager. Today a secret ends up either in a plain file (the config, `auth.json` or a `{file:}` target) or in an environment value. The workarounds in #7487 and #58653 (a local plugin that runs a command at startup, or `{env:}`/`{file:}` with an external tool) help, but they are not built in, and both requests were closed as not planned on 12 November 2026.

Why it matters in practice: the API returns resolved credentials (#53465, still open). We run OpenCode as a long-running service with several agents and MCP servers. In October 2026, agents that read these API endpoints printed our provider keys into session transcripts, and we rotated those keys. In November an MCP token also ended up in a transcript, and we are now rotating credentials on several machines again. Keeping secrets out of plain files will not fix #53465 on its own, but together with a fix for #53465 it would close the gap.

Any one of these would work for us, in order of preference:

1. A secret reference in the config, for example `{secret:<store>:<name>}`, resolved at use time from the OS credential store, with an opt-in backend for cloud secret managers.
2. The opt-in keyring backend for `opencode auth` and MCP credentials that #4318 proposed.
3. An official, documented plugin hook for resolving credentials, if the maintainers prefer to keep this out of core.

issues.title: codemode: report a tool listing as changed only when the schema changes semantically, not when JSON member order changes

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: status/repro-simulated
labels.description: Reproduced with a simulated model or mock

labels.name: area/mcp
labels.description: MCP servers and tools

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/linux
labels.description: Linux

issues.body:
## Summary

Code Mode treats a tool listing as changed when the only difference is JSON object member order in the MCP `inputSchema`. Because member order is not semantically meaningful, these are false positives: the model gets a "Changed tool listings supersede the previously listed ones" update, and the previous listing stays in history. Any MCP server or proxy that re-serializes schemas with a non-deterministic encoder triggers this on every request.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.4.2 (also affected on `dev` at the time of writing)
- Client: local service + TUI
- Model and provider: Not relevant
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Terminal: Not relevant
- Shell: zsh
- Install/channel: prod
- Active plugins: none related

## Reproduction

1. Point an MCP server at a layer that decodes and re-encodes JSON without preserving key order — for example an MCP aggregating proxy that unmarshals `inputSchema` into a map and marshals it back. With such a proxy, 20 `tools/list` requests in one session returned 4 different property orders while the canonical schema (keys recursively sorted) was identical in all 20.
2. Use Code Mode with two MCP servers. Note the rendered signature of one tool, e.g. `{ category?: string, refresh?: boolean, includeEngines?: boolean, includeDisabled?: boolean }`.
3. Continue the session until the catalog is rebuilt with the same schema in a different order.

## Expected Behavior

No catalog update is emitted when the schema is semantically identical. Object member order should be normalized before rendering and before deciding a listing changed.

## Actual Behavior

An update is emitted with the same fields in a different order:

```text
The Code Mode tool catalog has changed.

Changed tool listings supersede the previously listed ones:
  - tools.example.info({
  includeEngines?: boolean,
  includeDisabled?: boolean,
  category?: string,
  refresh?: boolean,
}): Promise<unknown> // ...
```

Stored history shows this is not a rare edge case. In one deployment, 2409 `core/codemode` notices across 328 sessions contained 582 consecutive transitions where the tool set was identical and every listing matched line-for-line as a multiset, but the text differed. A further 192 transitions had real content changes; 1166 changed the shown tool subset and are not attributable. The 582 order-only transitions appeared across 62 sessions.

## Additional Context

`packages/codemode/src/codemode/tool-schema.ts` renders object fields in wire order:

```ts
const properties = Object.entries(schema.properties ?? {});
```

`packages/codemode/src/codemode/instructions.ts` then compares the previously shown signature with the newly rendered one, so any reordering reads as a change.

Suggested fix: canonicalize the JSON Schema (sort object keys, recursively, preserving array order) when building the rendered signature or the value that feeds `Instructions.diff`. That keeps genuine changes — added, removed, or retyped fields, changed descriptions — while ignoring member order.

This is distinct from #55529 / #62176, which were about the size and scope of catalog updates; here each notification is small and correct in shape, just triggered by a non-semantic difference.

Note: the MCP proxy in this reproduction has its own report — its encoder documents that field order is not guaranteed. Fixing either side removes the symptom for this deployment, but normalizing on the client protects against any server or proxy with the same property.

issues.title: Desktop: model picker stays empty when /api/provider+/api/model 503 during server init — no retry, provider.updated does not refetch

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: status/repro-plausible
labels.description: Likely from reading the code, not observed

labels.name: area/desktop
labels.description: Desktop app

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Symptom

On macOS (OpenCode Desktop 2.3.2, Electron 44.9.1, darwin/arm64), the model picker can come up **empty or partial** after app launch, even though the server has a complete, healthy provider/model catalog.

## Root cause

The desktop app requests the provider/model list **once**, ~6s after the bundled `opencode-cli serve --service` process starts:

- a `GET /api/provider` + `GET /api/model` arriving during server init (e.g. while the models.dev catalog fetch is still in flight, or the box is under heavy load) gets **HTTP 503**,
- and the app **never retries**: later `provider.updated` server events (which fire once init completes) do **not** trigger a refetch.

Observed in the server log across one day:

- 13× `GET /api/provider → 503` during a heavily loaded morning (the server itself logged `Failed to fetch models.dev … TimeoutError after '10s'` in the same window),
- 2× `/api/provider` + `/api/model → 503` immediately after a clean restart at low load — and then **zero further attempts**, despite `provider.updated` events arriving ~4s later.
- The same `/api/model` endpoint returns the full catalog (557 models, 37 ms) as soon as init has completed.

## Repro

Launch the desktop app on a loaded machine (or slow models.dev reachability), open a chat within the first ~10s of the service boot → picker renders from a failed fetch and stays empty.

## Expected

- retry `/api/provider` + `/api/model` with backoff until success, or
- treat `provider.updated` as a signal to refetch the list.

## Workaround

Manually opening the model picker triggers a refetch (non-obvious), or restarting the app after the server is ready. A fresh catalog is then served: `/api/model` → 200, 557 models in ~37ms.

### Description

The desktop app listed two phantom projects (`gabri`, `Default Project`) under **"Projetos fechados recentemente"**. There is no supported way to remove them:

- the API exposes only `GET /api/project` and `PATCH /api/project/{projectID}` - no delete;

They could only be removed by editing persistent state directly: deleting rows from the `project` table in `opencode.db` and setting `recentlyClosed.local = []` in `drafts.sqlite` (with the app closed, otherwise it rewrites from memory).

### Plugins

None.

2.0.16

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let the app auto-register the home dir and `Default Project` as projects (happens after the persisted app state is cleared).
2. `GET /api/project` returns 3 projects; the sidebar shows the extras under "Projetos fechados recentemente".
3. Try to remove them: there is no UI action and no API endpoint.

### Screenshot and/or share link

N/A - described above.

### Operating System

Windows 11 - Windows NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)

### Terminal

OpenCode Desktop (Electron 44 / Chrome 152), not a terminal.

Suggested fix: expose `DELETE /api/project/{projectID}` (and/or a supported location removal) and add a "remove project" action in the app for both open and recently-closed projects.

issues.title: claude-agent: bound idle claude processes and stop finished subagents early

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/providers
labels.description: Providers and model lists

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

issues.body:
### Problem

In `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/claude-agent/claude/sessions.ts`, every primary session — including subagents — spawns its own `claude` subprocess (required by the Claude Agent SDK's 1-session-per-subprocess model) and keeps it alive for `IDLE_MS = 5 * 60_000` with no cap on total idle processes.

During subagent-heavy workflows (missions, parallel reviews, exploration), many finished subagent `claude` processes remain resident in memory simultaneously for 5 minutes even though most finished subagents never receive another prompt, and disk `resume` already handles follow-ups.

### Proposal

1. Stop finished subagent `claude` processes immediately on `session.execution.succeeded` (or after a much shorter idle grace period, e.g. 15–30s), relying on existing session `resume` if a follow-up arrives.
2. Add an LRU cap on warm idle `claude` processes (evicting the oldest idle non-waiting process when a new one starts), and allow configuring the idle timeout / cap.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: ios app: pairing with opencode pair --remote fails - QR contains JSON, pasted connect URL never prompts for server password (health 401 loop)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

issues.body:
## Summary

Pairing the iOS OpenCode app with `opencode pair --remote` fails in two ways: (1) scanning the printed QR code errors with "Invalid URL format" because the QR encodes a JSON object instead of a URL, and (2) pasting the plain connect URL into the app's server-address field silently does nothing — the app polls the server's `/auth/connect/<code>/global/health` endpoint, receives 401 forever, and never shows a password prompt. The server side is verified working: opening the same one-time connect URL in a desktop browser signs in and loads the web UI.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.4.1 (server, on the desktop machine)
- OS (server): Windows 10 Pro 25H2 (10.0.26200, win32 x64)
- OS (client): iOS (iPhone; app version not visible in the app UI)
- Terminal: xterm-256color (OpenCode desktop app terminal); shell cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: `opencode-mobile@latest` configured globally; it fails to load on 2.4.1 (`Plugin must export a default definition`). The failure is identical with the official pairing flow and the server-side flow was verified working via desktop browser, so the plugin is unlikely to be the cause — noted for completeness.

## Reproduction

1. On the desktop: `opencode pair --remote` (remote access already accepted). It prints a one-time URL like `https://<route>.<id>.opentunnel.xyz/auth/connect/<code>` plus a QR code.
2. iOS app → scan the QR code.
   → Error: `Invalid URL format: https:// {"code":"…","urls":["https://<route>.<id>.opentunnel.xyz"]}` — the QR payload is a JSON object, the app parses it as a plain URL.
3. Instead, copy the printed `https://…/auth/connect/<code>` URL and paste it into the app's server address field, then submit.
   → No password prompt, no error, no navigation. Nothing happens.

Server log while the app sits on the connect screen:

```
role=server GET /auth/connect/<code>/global/health http.status=401   (repeats ~1x/second indefinitely)
```

## Expected Behavior

Scanning the pair QR (or pasting the connect URL) should complete the pairing handshake, prompt for the server password when remote access is enabled, and then show the machine's sessions.

## Actual Behavior

- QR scan: immediate error `Invalid URL format: https://` followed by the raw JSON payload (`{"code":"…","urls":["https://…opentunnel.xyz"]}`).
- Pasted URL: app appears idle; server log shows endless `GET /auth/connect/<code>/global/health → 401`. The password prompt never appears, so pairing can never complete. Reproduces consistently across multiple pairing attempts and fresh one-time links.

## Additional Context

- Control test: opening the same fresh connect URL in a desktop browser signs in with a session cookie and loads the full web UI (project list renders). Server, tunnel, and one-time link are all healthy — the failure is in the iOS app's connect flow.
- Workaround that works today: open the one-time connect URL in the iPhone's browser (Safari) instead of the app — the web UI loads and is usable from the phone.
- Suggested fixes: (a) encode the connect URL (not raw JSON) in the QR, or parse the JSON payload in the app; (b) when `/global/health` returns 401, surface the password prompt instead of polling silently.

prs.title: fix(tui): let Esc cancel a prompt that has not started
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #53652

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

On a cold Location, a prompt is admitted before its execution starts. Until `session.execution.started` arrives the session reports `idle`, but `session.interrupt` is only enabled for `running`, so Esc does nothing. When it does reach the server, `POST /interrupt` returns `interrupted: false` and the run proceeds.

This makes the preparation window visible and cancellable:

- A pending user inbox item with pending status `starting` counts as busy. The footer shows the spinner and `esc cancel`.
- One Esc cancels: it sends `session.interrupt` with `resume: false` (which does not wake the pending input) and cancels the still-pending inbox rows.
- A cancel intent interrupts again if `session.execution.started` arrives anyway, covering the race.
- The footer shows `aborting…` until the session settles.
- `session.interrupt` no longer requires composer focus.
- The cancel path does not take the undo/take-back restore, so it does not enter the revert path that #57581 is fixing.
- A new prompt or 30 s clears a stale intent.

Measured on the local server: cold-location admission is ~0.9–1.3 s vs 16–21 ms warm.

- New `packages/tui/test/session-interrupt-starting.test.tsx`: idle session with a `starting` inbox row, one Esc sends `interrupt?resume=false` and cancels the inbox row, a later `execution.started` sends the interrupt again, and `aborting…` clears on idle.

prs.title: fix(core): coalesce completed sibling wakes for nested subagents
prs.body:
When a nested subagent spawns multiple child subagents in parallel and goes idle, each completing child previously woke the nested parent individually (`SubagentReport.deliverReport`). With N concurrent children, this triggered N separate parent LLM turns—re-reading the full cached prefix each turn—and cascaded N intermediate `state="running"` reports up to the root session.

### Before / After
- **Before:** Every completing child unconditionally called `deps.wake(parentID)`, waking a nested parent once per sibling.
- **After:** For nested parents (`parent.parentID !== undefined`), completed child reports are still committed and admitted into the parent's inbox immediately, while `deps.wake(parentID)` is deferred until either:
  1. all other running direct sibling subagents settle (ignoring Code Mode `agent()` children and cancelled jobs), or
  2. a bounded hold timer expires (`DEFAULT_MAX_COALESCE_DELAY = 60s`), preventing a slow or blocked sibling from holding finished reports indefinitely.

### Safety & Invariants
- **Top-level sessions unchanged:** Parents with `parentID === undefined` still wake immediately on every child completion.
- **Errors and cancellations wake immediately:** Non-completed outcomes (`error` / `cancelled`) bypass coalescing and wake the parent immediately at every depth.
- **No stranded reports on quiet/failed sibling exits:** Any sibling settling without delivering a report (empty/control-only period, deleted child, automation child, or inbox `LifecycleConflict`) flushes a pending wake once no siblings remain. Staged `revert` still suppresses wakes.
- **Restart recovery:** On boot, `SessionRestart` wakes any idle nested parent that still has an unpromoted `source: "subagent"` synthetic notice in `session_inbox`, so a deferred wake cannot be lost across a server restart.

### Verification
- `bun test test/subagent-report.test.ts test/subagent-completion.test.ts test/subagent-idle-e2e.test.ts test/subagent-lifetime.test.ts test/tool-subagent.test.ts test/session-execution.test.ts test/codemode-agents-e2e.test.ts` (111 pass, 0 fail)
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core` (0 errors across 2,046 files)
- `oxlint`, `prettier --check`, and `ast-grep` effect pattern checks clean on all modified files

prs.title: fix(mcp): fall back to legacy when a slow stdio server refuses initialize
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #66577

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Since #65282 an unset `protocol` probes a local server with `server/discover` and gives up after 5 s. The SDK then sends the legacy `initialize` on the same connection. A server that is still starting reads the probe late, which moves that connection to 2026-07-28, and refuses the `initialize` (Python `mcp` 2.3: "the initialize handshake is not accepted"). The stdio path only respawned on `ConnectionClosed` and `EraNegotiationFailed`, so the connect failed.

This adds `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` to the errors that respawn the server once for the legacy handshake, where `initialize` arrives first. It is the stdio counterpart of what `negotiate` already does over HTTP: a probe timeout falls back to legacy on a fresh transport.

With `pool: true` the shared connection never goes legacy, so it has no respawn to fall back on. The pool retries on the Location's own connection only when the failure says the server was reached, and this error did not say so. It does now.

A slow server now connects on the legacy protocol, the same as a slow server over HTTP. Pinning `protocol` to `"2026-07-28"` still gets the modern protocol.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests, with a fixture that behaves like the Python server (the first request decides the connection's era). Each fails without its own change, with the error from the issue, and passes with it: one for the respawn, one for the pooled path.
- Ran the server from the issue (Python `mcp` 2.3.0, 6 s start) through `McpClient.connect` with no `protocol`: fails on `dev` after 7 s, connects with the change.

prs.title: fix(core): decode stored MCP OAuth metadata once and keep sign-in on the effect clock
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66931, which parsed MCP server configs once at the boundary.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Stored MCP OAuth credential metadata is now decoded with one schema, so a corrupt or old credential can't crash a sign-in, and two small sign-in bugs are fixed.

**One schema for stored metadata.** `oauth.ts` used to read `credential.metadata` in pieces: `discovery` through a schema, `client` through an unchecked `as StoredOAuthClientInformation` cast, and `redirect_uris`, `issuer` and `scope` through `typeof` / `in` checks. Now one `Metadata` schema (`scope`, `issuer`, `discovery`, `client`) is decoded each time a credential is read. Each field falls back to absent on its own, so one bad field doesn't discard the rest. The client keeps the fields it doesn't name, because the SDK reads more of them (for example `token_endpoint_auth_method`).

```diff
 earlier credential metadata: { client: "corrupt" }
 start sign-in
-TypeError: client is not an Object. (evaluating '"redirect_uris" in client')
+the client is treated as missing and a new one is registered
```

**Token expiry on the effect clock.** `toCredential` computed `expires` with `Date.now()`, while `connectProvider` checks it with `Clock.currentTimeMillis`. It now takes `now` from `Clock`, read after the token response arrives, for both login and refresh.

**Pasted redirect keeps the localhost rewrite.** Some authorization servers (Clerk) send the browser back to `localhost` instead of `127.0.0.1`, and the token exchange has to repeat that redirect. The browser callback already handled this by its `Host` header. A pasted URL dropped the host, so the exchange sent `127.0.0.1` and the server refused it. `OauthRedirect.submit` now also passes the parsed URL to `received` (an added third argument, so the other providers are unchanged), and MCP takes the host from it.

```diff
 paste http://localhost:PORT/callback?code=…&state=…
-token request: redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:PORT/callback   (refused)
+token request: redirect_uri=http://localhost:PORT/callback
```

Behavior changes: a stored `issuer` or `scope` that isn't a string, or a stored client whose `redirect_uris` holds a non-string, now reads as absent instead of being partly used. No public API changes.

### How did you verify your code works?

Three tests in `packages/core/test/mcp-oauth.test.ts` that fail on `dev` and pass here:
- `ignores a corrupt client saved by an earlier login` (TypeError before)
- `stores the token expiry on the effect clock` (expected `3601000` under `TestClock`, got a wall-clock time)
- `redeems a pasted code with the localhost redirect a server sent the browser back to` (got `127.0.0.1`)

`packages/core`: MCP and provider OAuth tests, `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`. `packages/server`: `bun typecheck` and MCP tests. Root `bun run check`.

Not a UI change.

prs.title: fix(core): return whole lines from read and show grep matches in long lines
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No public issue. Fixes reports where read's inline `... (line truncated to 2000 chars)` marker got written back into files and broke valid JSON.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`read` returns lines whole, and `grep` shows the part of a long line around the match instead of the line's start.

**read.** Every line was cut at 2000 chars with a marker inside `content`, even when the page had room, so a 40 KB one-line JSON came back as 2 KB plus the marker. Lines now come back whole within the existing page limits (2000 lines or 50 KB). The cut was also what kept paging moving past a huge line, so a page that starts on a line over 50 KB now returns a new `line-too-large` result instead of text:

```ts
| { type: "text", offset, next?, content }
| { type: "line-too-large", line, bytes, next? }   // new
| { type: "directory", next?, entries }
| { type: "media", mime, name?, uri }
```

```diff
 Read file mixed.ts, lines 1-119
 ...
-120: <svg zzzzzzzz…(2000 chars)… (line truncated to 2000 chars)
-121: …
+[Output truncated. Continue reading with offset: 120]

+Read file mixed.ts, line 120
+Line 120 is 202 KB, more than the 50 KB one read returns, so it isn't shown.
+[Output truncated. Continue reading with offset: 121]
```

- A page never ends mid-line. A line that doesn't fit the room left starts the next page; if it can't fit any page, that page is `line-too-large` with `next` past it, so paging can't loop.
- There is no text field on `line-too-large`, so nothing from it can end up in a file. The message is built from `line` and `bytes` only for the model.
- A line over 50 KB is never read into memory. Once a page has lines, an unfinished line that can't fit ends the page right away instead of being scanned to its end. `bytes` is the size that was over the limit, so invalid UTF-8 that grows when decoded reports its decoded size.
- Reads past the end of the file keep only the lines after an oversized line, as the 50 KB tail budget already dropped earlier lines.

**grep.** A long matching line was previewed as its first 2000 chars, so on a one-line file the match itself was usually missing. The preview is now a 2000-char window starting 1000 chars before the first match, from ripgrep's own byte offset, with `...` at each cut end. Lines of 2000 chars or less and the result limits are unchanged.

**Why.** Three tasks replayed against six small models (360 runs, simulated tools with these limits): a lookup and an edit inside ~290 KB one-line JSON files, and a lookup in a 200-line file whose line 120 is a 195 KB string.

| | today (2000-char cut) | whole lines + message | + grep window |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct | 81% | 90% | 96% |
| confident wrong answers | 8 | 2 | 0 |
| files corrupted | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| average tokens per run | 149k | 127k | 28k |

The cut prefix looks like real content, so models answered from it or decided the rest wasn't there. Most "it isn't in the file" answers came from grep reporting a match whose preview didn't contain it. Naming shell commands in the message did worse than the plain message, so it names none.

**Trade-off.** A line over 50 KB can't be read with `read`; grep, now showing the match, is the way into it. Reading inside a line would need a character offset in the schema, which nothing so far says models need.

Careful review: `collect` and the scan loop in `packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.ts`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- In packages/core: `tool-read-filesystem`, `tool-read`, `ripgrep`, `tool-search` and `codemode` tests pass, and `tool-read-filesystem` and `ripgrep` pass 5 reruns each. Tests that asserted the marker or the head-only grep preview are updated, with a few assertions inside them for `line-too-large`, the grep window, and invalid UTF-8 pages.
- `bun run typecheck` in packages/core; `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` in packages/server, packages/sdk and packages/simulation: clean.
- By hand, through the real read code: a 300 KB one-line file returns `line-too-large`; a 40 KB one-line JSON comes back byte for byte and parses; a 200-line file with a 200 KB line 120 pages 1-119, then `line-too-large` with `next` 121, then 121-200; offsets past the end and negative offsets end correctly; `"one\n"` plus a 50 MB line with `limit: 2` returns `one` in 1.7 ms instead of scanning all 50 MB; a 50 KB line with CRLF fits, 50 KB + 1 doesn't.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(deploy): pin the localized docs runWorkerFirst routes for the site Worker
prs.body:
## What failed
`deploy-site / site-deploy` has failed on `dev` since #66778:

```
##[error]The site's Worker config in the artifact is not the pinned target (.github/release/targets/site/dev/worker.json)
```

## Root cause
`deploy-site.sh` won't deploy unless the artifact's `worker.config.json` is exactly the same as `.github/release/targets/site/<mode>/worker.json`. #66778 changed `services/site/cloudflare.config.ts` so the Worker also handles the translated docs paths: for each locale except `en` it adds `/<locale>/docs`, `/<locale>/docs/*` and `!/<locale>/docs/pagefind/*` to `assets.runWorkerFirst`. The pinned targets weren't updated, so the artifact no longer matched them.

## Fix
In the dev and production site targets, append those 51 entries (17 locales) to `assets.runWorkerFirst`, in the order the config produces them. Names, routes, domains and bindings don't change.

This changes what production is allowed to deploy, so it needs the release owner's review (see `.github/release/README.md`).

## Verification
After `bun install`, I built `worker.config.json` for `dev` and `production` using the same calls as `services/site/script/build.ts` (`resolveAndParseConfig` followed by `writeWorkerConfig`). I compared each one with its pinned target using the deploy script's own test (`jq -e --slurp '.[0]==.[1]'`): `true` for both updated targets, `false` for the old ones. I didn't run the full site build or the deploy itself, since that needs Cloudflare credentials.

---

prs.title: fix(core): parse MCP server configs once before connecting or signing in
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Part of an internal audit of the MCP service (config boundary item).

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A broken MCP server config now fails just that server with a clear status, and nothing past the point where a server is registered ever sees a raw URL or command string.

Each server's config is parsed once, when its entry is created, into a typed `McpTarget`:

```ts
type Target =
  | { type: "local";  config; command: string; args: string[] }          // command can't be empty
  | { type: "remote"; config; url: URL; redirect?: URL; metadata?: URL }  // every URL already parsed
```

If parsing fails, the entry gets a connection that only reports `failed` with the reason, it isn't registered as an OAuth integration, and it never reaches the pool, `McpClient.connect` or `McpOAuth`. `McpConnection.Spec`, `McpClient.connect`, `McpOAuth.authorize` and `McpOAuth.connectProvider` now take the parsed target instead of the raw config.

```diff
 mcp add broken { type: "local", command: [] }
-status: failed "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'command.command.includes')"
+status: failed "MCP server command is empty"

 mcp add broken { type: "remote", url: "not a url" }
 status: failed "Invalid MCP server URL: not a url"
-integration mcp_… registered, sign-in throws in loggedFetch
+no integration registered

 mcp add x { type: "remote", url: "https://…", oauth: { redirect_uri: "not a url" } }
-status: connected, sign-in dies with an uncaught TypeError from new URL()
+status: failed "Invalid MCP OAuth redirect_uri: not a url"
```

The same applies to `oauth.auth_server_metadata_url`. The public config schema is unchanged, so one bad server still can't stop the rest of the config from loading.

The `?codemode=false` rule now lives in one place: `McpTarget.dialUrl` decides whether to add it (used by `client.ts`), and `McpTarget.withoutDialParams` strips it from an echoed protected resource (used by `oauth.ts`). The pool key is unchanged: it already keys the inputs to that rule (`url`, `codemode`).

Behavior changes:
- A remote server with an unparseable `oauth.redirect_uri` or `oauth.auth_server_metadata_url` is now `failed` instead of connecting anonymously and crashing only when someone signs in.
- A remote server with an unparseable `url` is no longer registered as an OAuth integration (`integrationID` is absent).

`McpClient.connect`'s option `config` is renamed to `target`. These modules are reachable as `@opencode/core/mcp/*` deep imports, but nothing outside `packages/core` uses them; no SDK or plugin API changes.

A follow-up stacked on this branch decodes stored OAuth credential metadata with one schema and fixes two small sign-in bugs.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Extended `marks an MCP server with an invalid config as failed` in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts`; on `dev` it fails at the integration check, the empty-command message, and the `redirect_uri` status. It passes here.
- Removed `rejects an invalid redirect URL` from `mcp-oauth.test.ts`: it asserted the old uncaught `TypeError`, which can no longer happen because the redirect is parsed before sign-in.
- `packages/core`: MCP tests, `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`. `packages/server`: `bun typecheck` and MCP tests. Root `bun run check`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(cli-rs): find in session, and the TUI fixes since #66776
prs.body:
### What it does

Ports find in session (#64870) to the Rust client, and the TUI fixes from #66795, #66813 and #66841 that Rust still
lacked.

**Find in session (#64870).** As in TS, it's behind the temporary `session-find` experiment.

- `/find` and `session.find` (`<leader>f`, `super+f`) open a find bar, which loads only when it's opened.
- Matching follows TS's rules, including the `İ` case folding from #66841. Matches are found across the whole session,
  not only the part of the transcript that's loaded, and moving to one brings it into view.
- Only the rows around the current match are mounted, as with scrolling, so a long session doesn't grow memory while
  find is open (TS mounts every row). Parts that aren't mounted are counted with OpenTUI's own Markdown parser, the one
  the renderer uses, without building widgets, so "N of M" and the selected match never shift when a part mounts.
- Code blocks a plugin draws can't be counted without the plugin. While find is open, only parts with such a block
  that may hold a match mount for real, with their real keys, so a plugin never gets a render for a block that isn't on
  screen. A plugin answering `Keep` counts as drawing the block only when it already has a widget there.
  Those rows unmount, with `fence-gone`, when the query stops matching them or find closes.
  `parity/deviations/MS1-find-plugin-fences.md` records the cost: 250 plugin-drawn blocks take about 5 MiB of Rust
  heap and 20 ms. Mermaid and LaTeX are drawn by the client and never mount for find.
- Matches are highlighted in the prompt, Markdown, code, tables and compaction summaries, in the new `find.*` theme
  colours. The theme schema, the experiment list and the keybind fixtures are regenerated.

This fixes `dev`'s Rust check, which fails since #64870 on
`complete::slash_names_and_aliases_match_the_typescript_sources` (TS has `/find`, Rust didn't).

**TUI fixes (#66795, #66813, #66841).** Their authors already changed `packages/cli-rs` for some of them. These are the
rest:

- the session list keeps its selection and prefills the real title when renaming;
- polling the v1 migration retries transient errors;
- hidden autocomplete rows are detached, and the prompt stash keeps shell mode;
- tab titles fade less on narrow titles, and a hidden primary agent is reported as current without being listed;
- Markdown table grid lines use the theme's border colour, with find highlights in cells too;
- a shown permission request stays until it's answered, and locationless catalog events refresh every loaded location.

The footer keeps the Zed editor selection when the session's location arrives after the first Zed poll; it used to be
cleared and never restored. Every later session prompt still clears it, as in TS. This was also a race in the `E.5/zed`
scenario on GitHub Actions.

A stalled plugin host holds keys only once: past the limit, its notice that it began the stalled command no longer
clears the stall, so the next bound key doesn't wait the limit again. This and a missing terminal-snapshot route in a
theme-switch test showed up as races on GitHub Actions.

Regression tests cover the startup prompt, collapse scroll and switching Home between worktrees. #66731, #66636, #66818
and #66798 need no Rust change.

### Checks

`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy`, `check:drift`, and the UI, TUI, local, mini, mermaid, ACP and CLI suites with the TypeScript
interop tests. A new P-APP scenario, `E.8/find`, matches TS at all 12 checkpoints. 46 differential cases (setext headings, nested and lazy lists, reference links,
autolinks, inline HTML, tables, fences) count the same mounted and unmounted, and stepping through every match of a long
session visits each once. A new `find_long` perf case takes 48 ms over 200 turns. `perf compare` for `scroll`,
`scroll_all` and `stream` shows no regression (within ±0.02%). The merge lane's gate ran on this commit.

prs.title: refactor(core): register Code Mode's execute tool from a plugin
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None

### Type of change

- [x] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Code Mode's `execute` tool is now an ordinary tool, registered by an internal plugin (`tool/plugin/codemode.ts`) and built on `context.tool.call` from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66919. Until now the registry built it inside `Tool.snapshot`, ran its nested calls through a private path, and session context passed it Code Mode's services on every request.

```diff
 Tool.snapshot(policy, options)
   place tools: direct, or inside Code Mode
-  build execute here (CodeModeTool.create with the registry's run, permission, services, api, agents)
+  execute is a registered direct tool; Code Mode is on when the request offers it
   catalog of the tools inside Code Mode, as before
   a call to execute that runs long moves to the background, hooks and all, as before

 execute
+  refuses to run when another tool calls it
+  its tools: context.tool.list().codemode
+  each call in a program: context.tool.call(name, input, { codemode: true })
```

- **Plugin API, additive:** `Tool.Calls` gains `list()` (the tools the call may reach, `{ direct, codemode, namespaces }`), and `call` takes `{ codemode: true }`. With that option it reaches only tools inside Code Mode, uses their Code Mode schemas, and plugins may rename it only among those, as Code Mode did before.
- **The plugin** gets the Location's file services, the OpenCode API and `agent()`/`llm()` itself, by flag, instead of session context passing them to `snapshot` (`SnapshotOptions` drops `services`, `api` and `agents`).
- **When Code Mode is on:** the request has to offer `execute` (registered, not hidden, not denied), not only leave it allowed. On a cold Location, tools stay direct until the plugin registers it. `execute` stays last in the tool list, and the name stays reserved for the tool `CodeModeTool.create` makes.
- **The prepared runtime is keyed by the set of tools** rather than the inventory object, so the catalog and every execution still share it.

Unchanged: the catalog in the system prompt, the background job around `execute` (its `execute.after` hooks still see the script's final result), the top-level call to a Code Mode tool, and automations' `Tool.check`.

**Tests:** setups that build the registry themselves use `toolNodes` (`Tool.node` plus the Code Mode plugin) in place of `Tool.node`, or `registerCodeMode()`. Tests that run `CodeModeTool.create` directly give it `directCalls`. The test of per-call IDs inside Code Mode is gone, since `tool.call`'s tests cover them. One new test: `execute` refuses a call from another tool.

No flag: same behavior, different home.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Full core suite passes, apart from two shell tests that also fail on `dev`.
- Server `codemode-api` test passes, and `bun run check` passes.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(scripts): skip upstream-only maintenance on forks
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #35666

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`triage-close-issues.yml` and `triage-close-prs.yml` run on a daily schedule with no repository guard, so they also fire on every fork that has Actions enabled. Both jobs run scripts that hardcode `anomalyco/opencode` (`script/github/close-issues.ts` and the default `--repo` in `close-prs.ts`). On a fork the job holds a fork-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` but talks to the upstream repo: listing issues works because they are public, then the first comment/close fails with `403 Forbidden` and the run dies. #35666 has the reproduction, and the triage bot confirmed it still happens on current `dev`.

I put the guard in the scripts rather than in the workflow YAML. Both now read `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` (set automatically by Actions) and exit 0 with a short log line when it names anything other than `anomalyco/opencode`. That covers every invocation path — scheduled runs, `workflow_dispatch`, and manual runs from a fork — instead of only the two jobs. `close-prs.ts` still honours an explicit `--repo`, and running locally without `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` behaves exactly as before. On the canonical repo nothing changes.

Three earlier PRs (#35664, #39727, #47262) added a YAML-level `if:` guard instead; all three were closed by the automated stale-PR cleanup rather than reviewed, so the guard never landed. There is no open PR covering this now.

### How did you verify your code works?

Ran both scripts locally with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=someone/opencode GITHUB_TOKEN=dummy`: each prints `Skipping anomalyco/opencode-only maintenance in someone/opencode`, exits 0, and makes no API calls (including `close-prs.ts --execute`). With `GITHUB_REPOSITORY=anomalyco/opencode` and no token, `close-issues.ts` still exits 1 with the original `GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable is required` message. Passing `--repo someone/opencode` on a fork still reaches the normal token check, so the explicit override is preserved. `git diff --check` is clean, and the repo-wide `bun run check` used by the pre-push hook passes all 35 tasks.

### Visual

Not applicable — maintenance-script-only change, no user-facing surface.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable — maintenance-script-only change.

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(site): multi-language V2 docs
prs.body:
Adds the language framework to the V2 docs at opencode.ai/docs, following the site's and data app's locale mechanism. **Merge together with #66786 and #66838**: the picker lists every site language, and those PRs add the translations; this PR alone would show English fallbacks for 17 options.

**URLs**: English stays at `/docs/<slug>/`; other languages use `/<locale>/docs/<slug>/` (the site's `oc_locale` cookie and `x-opencode-locale` header apply). `/v1/docs` is untouched.

**Content and fallback**: translations live at `src/docs/content/<locale>/<same path>.mdx`. Every locale × page is prerendered. A language without a translation renders the English page in that language's chrome with a notice, canonicalises to the English URL, and is left out of that language's hreflang and sitemap entries. A translation whose heading depths no longer match the English page is stale and serves the same English fallback. Translated pages reuse the English heading ids in order, so anchors work across languages; a translated page's frontmatter title drives its h1, `<title>`, sidebar and pagination entries, and search result; UI section/group labels come from the dictionaries. A noindex page and its translations keep robots noindex, emit no hreflang, and stay out of the sitemap.

prs.title: fix(core): keep MCP needs_auth and event follows through connection teardown
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Found in an audit of the MCP service.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes two MCP lifecycle bugs by changing the state they come from, so the bad states can't be written down anymore.

**1. A pooled server that loses its sign-in showed "failed" instead of "needs_auth".** When a live request on a shared connection got a 401 it couldn't refresh, the connection ended through `closed(reason: string)`, and the Location turned every close into `failed`. So every Location holding that server told the user to reconnect instead of signing in. `closed` now carries the same `Failure` the connect path already uses, and a refused request always ends through it, shared or not:

```diff
- readonly closed: (reason: string) => Effect.Effect<void>
+ readonly closed: (failure: Failure) => Effect.Effect<void>   // { status: "failed" | "needs_auth", error }

  // refused request
- if (input.shared) return yield* input.events.closed(message)
- yield* stop
- yield* input.events.failed({ status: "needs_auth", error: message }, false)
+ input.events.closed({ status: "needs_auth", error: message })
```

**2. A reconnect could permanently end an event subscription.** `stop()` clears the connection's client, then waits for the old scope to close and announces the emptied catalogs. Through all of that the server entry still said `connected`, so `follow` reopening in that window found "connected, no client" and failed with the terminal `EventsUnavailableError` ("offers no events"). `servers()` also reported `connected` with no tools there.

- `McpConnection` keeps one tagged state, `Idle | Connecting { scope } | Connected { scope, client, tools, prompts, skills }`, instead of five optional fields cleared one by one.
- A server entry keeps a `phase` instead of `status` plus a separate `attempt`. The phase never says "connected":

  ```ts
  type Phase =
    | { _tag: "Starting"; started; settled }   // an attempt is in flight, with its startup latch
    | { _tag: "Idle" }                          // nothing in flight, nothing wrong
    | { _tag: "Disabled" }
    | { _tag: "Failed"; failure }               // failed or needs_auth
  ```

  The connection's own tagged state is the only source for "connected". The reported status reads it in exactly one place: an `Idle` server is `connected` while its connection is live, and `pending` (between connections) otherwise. So "connected with no client" can't be written down, and no variant gets reinterpreted as another one. I chose this over giving the phase a connected variant that holds the client, because that copy would go stale the moment the connection tears itself down (a session-expiry reconnect or a shared connection closing), and keeping it current would mean syncing two fields again.
- `follow` checks the client itself, so a torn-down connection means "wait and reopen", not "no events".
- Phase changes are a pure `next(phase, transition)` over a `Transition` union (`Connecting | Settled | Disabled | Failed`). `advance(entry, transition)` is the only place that writes `entry.phase`. It is also the edge for side effects: when a change leaves `Starting`, it opens that attempt's startup latch. Before, `disconnect()` and replacing a server left that latch closed, so an `awaitStartup()` already waiting on it sat out the full 2s grace window.
- Every switch over `Phase`, `Transition`, the offline status and the connection's state lists each case and ends with `default: return absurd(x)`, so adding a variant fails typecheck at each of them. Questions like "is it starting?" or "is it disabled?" go through small exhaustive helpers (`starting`, `disabled`) rather than single-case `if`s.

Smaller things in the same code:
- The four catalog kinds were listed by hand in five places. They're now `McpConnection.KINDS`, and `changes` is checked against it.
- `subscribe(..., { cursor: null })` on an ended subscription resumed from its old cursor, because of `??`. Explicit `null` now starts from now, as documented; leaving it out still resumes.
- `unavailable()` takes only offline statuses and ends its switch with `absurd`.

No public API change: the `Mcp.Status` shapes that the server and SDK expose stay the same. The only visible difference is that a server being torn down now reads `pending` for that moment instead of `connected`.

One behavior to review: `awaitStartup` now stops waiting as soon as a server is connected, not after its connected announcements are published. `tools()` reads the connection directly, so a model call sees the same tools either way.

`pool.ts` changes are limited to the `closed` signature and the kinds loop, so they shouldn't get in the way of https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66914.

Review follow-ups:
- **An interrupted connection attempt no longer leaves its scope behind.** `McpConnection`'s state is now just `Idle | Connected`. Until a connection exists, the attempt owns its scope through `acquireUseRelease`, and the release closes it unless `Connected` took it over. So no exit, interruption included, can leave a half-open `Connecting` state. Dev had the same gap with `state.scope`. I found nothing that actually leaked through it, because `McpClient.connect` already closes its transport when interrupted, so there's no failing test for this one.
- **A server whose registration fails no longer holds up `awaitStartup`.** `replaceServer` now leaves `Starting` through `advance(entry, { _tag: "Settled" })` on every exit. This also happens on dev. New test: "stops waiting for a server whose registration failed".
- **Only a resumed subscription keeps its `seen` list.** One given a cursor, `null` included, starts with an empty list, so a replayed event is delivered again. The cursor test now covers this.
- The pooled needs_auth test now waits until the status is neither `connected` nor `pending`.

### How did you verify your code works?

New tests in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts`. Each one fails on `dev` and passes here:
- `MCP pool > reports needs_auth in every Location when a shared connection's credential is refused` (on dev both Locations read `failed`)
- `MCP events > keeps following events while a reconnect tears the old connection down`. It holds the old connection's teardown at its tools-changed announcement, then calls `follow`. On dev that fails with `EventsUnavailableError: The MCP server offers no events.`; now its first update is `pending`, and the status is `pending`.
- `MCP events > resumes an ended subscription from its cursor unless subscribed again from now`

Checks:
- Exhaustiveness: temporarily adding a `Phase` variant, a `Transition` variant and a connection state variant failed typecheck at all 8 switches (`next`, `settle`, `starting`, `disabled`, `status`, `offline`, and the connection's `current` and `opened`). Adding an `Mcp.Status` variant failed at `unavailable`. All reverted.
- `packages/core`: the MCP test files and the other test files that use the MCP service (277 tests). `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` pass.
- New tests with `--rerun-each 10`: 40/40.
- `packages/server`: `bun typecheck` and the MCP tests pass.
- Root `bun run check` passes.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

### What does this PR do?

Each subagent runs its own `claude` process, about 200MB, and a finished subagent kept it for the 5-minute idle timeout. Running many subagents piled these up.

prs.title: feat(core): support native Windows machine workers on the home
prs.body:
Adds native Windows machine-worker support on the home (Option 1 — Windows-aware home, paired with `anomalyco/opencode-worker#2`):

### Before
- `MachineDriver` hardcoded `path: posix` and `shell: "sh"`, `Hello.home` required a leading `/`, and `EnvironmentPath.rooted` refused `<machine>:C:\…` / `<machine>:C:/…`.
- `Environments.ready` always returned `true` for machines even when offline, so `FileAccess` could ask for permissions against an offline machine before failing.
- `ShellSelect.name` did not recognize Windows shell paths (`C:\…\pwsh.exe`) on a POSIX host, and PowerShell permission scanning expanded `$env:X` / `$HOME` from the home server's environment on remote machines.

### After
- **Wire (`packages/core/src/machine/wire.ts`):** keeps `protocol: 3`, adds optional `Hello.shell` (omitted = `"sh"` for backwards compatibility), and allows Windows drive/UNC paths in `Hello.home`.
- **Per-hello rules (`driver.ts`, `worker-client.ts`):** `Machine.rules(hello)` picks `path.win32` when `os === "win32"` (else `posix`) and `hello.shell ?? "sh"`; `MachineDriver.Interface.environment` reflects the latest `hello` dynamically via getters.
- **Paths & offline checks (`path.ts`, `environments.ts`, `file-access.ts`):** accepts `<machine>:C:\…`, `<machine>:C:/…`, `<machine>:\\server\share\…`, and `<machine>:~\…` on Windows machines while rejecting drive paths on POSIX machines and drive-less `/foo` on Windows machines with `NotAbsolute`; `Environments.ready` checks `machines.list()` online state; `FileAccess` fails offline machines with `Machine.NotSent` before path resolution or permission prompts.
- **Shell (`shell/select.ts`, `shell/parse.ts`):** recognizes Windows shell paths/`.exe` on any host and stops expanding the home server's `$env:X`/`$HOME`/`$PSHOME` during remote machine permission scans.

prs.title: fix(core): share pooled MCP connections across equivalent configs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/66870, which fixed pooled MCP servers dropping `skills` because the pool copied fields by hand.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Two Locations with the same MCP server config could still open separate pooled connections, because `McpPool.key` used `JSON.stringify` on raw config values. A server loaded from a config file always carries `timeout: {}`, while one added at runtime carries no timeout, so they never matched. The same happened for `protocol` left out vs `"auto"`, `oauth`, `headers` or `environment` left out vs `{}`, and different key order inside `timeout`, `oauth` or `clientInfo`.

The key is now one object per config type, serialized with the existing `canonicalJson`, with defaults filled in:

```diff
-JSON.stringify(["remote", config.url, ..., config.protocol, config.timeout ?? null, ...])
+canonicalJson({
+  ...spec, // satisfies Record<keyof Spec fields, Json>
+  timeout, // satisfies Record<keyof TimeoutConfig, Json>, each field ?? null
+  protocol: config.protocol ?? "auto",
+  oauth, // false, or every OAuthConfig field ?? null, secret fingerprinted
+  disabled: null, // doesn't change the connection
+  ...
+} satisfies Record<keyof Mcp.RemoteConfig | "credential", Json>)
```

Each object `satisfies` a record over every field of the config it keys, so adding a field to `RemoteConfig`, `LocalConfig`, `OAuthConfig`, `TimeoutConfig` or `McpConnection.Spec` fails to compile until it's keyed or set to `null` on purpose. Before, a new field was silently left out and two different configs could share one connection.

Smaller changes in the same spirit:

- `McpPool.key` takes a union: a remote config needs `credential`, a local one needs its resolved `cwd`. Forgetting `cwd` used to compile and key every directory under `null`.
- The private fallback connection and `McpClient.connect` now get the input and `Spec` spread whole instead of field by field.
- The pool's two sets (`unpoolable` and its `legacy` subset) are one `Map<string, "refused" | "legacy">`.
- `Mode` has a `Joining` state, so `Shared` always has its connection instead of an optional one.

Pool keys only live in memory, so changing their format has no migration. No public API change.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `keys equivalent configs alike` in `packages/core/test/mcp.test.ts` fails on `dev` (`timeout: {}`, `protocol: "auto"`, `oauth: {}`, `headers: {}` got a different key from the bare config) and passes here.
- Removing a field from one of the key objects fails `bun typecheck` with `Property 'pool' is missing ...`.
- `packages/core`: `bun test test/mcp*.test.ts` (213 pass), `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`. Root: `bun run check`.

prs.title: feat(core): let tools call other tools through context.tool.call
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

A tool can call other tools from inside its `execute`, through `context.tool.call`. Until now a tool couldn't reach another tool at all. The only way was calling its `execute` directly, which skips input checks, hooks and permissions.

```ts
execute: (input, context) =>
  Effect.gen(function* () {
    const found = yield* context.tool.call("grep", { pattern: "TODO" })
    return { output: found.output }
  })
```

This is the first step toward running Code Mode, and saved Code Mode tools, as ordinary tools on top of this, rather than through the registry's own path.

**How a nested call runs**

```
context.tool.call(name, input)
  find name among the tools this request offers (registry ID like demo_echo, or Code Mode path like demo.echo)
    not offered, or denied for this agent → Tool.Error: No tool named "x" is available to this call.
  new call ID, nested under the calling tool, so permission prompts show on the call the model made
  execute.before hook → input checks → the tool → execute.after hook   (same path as a model's call)
  → its result, or a Tool.Error
```

- **Which tools it can reach:** what the request offers, directly or inside Code Mode, after the agent's permission rules. A tool hidden or denied for the agent can't be reached through another tool either.
- **Nested calls:** a call nested two deep now shows its permission prompt on the outermost call too. `Permission.nested` resolves a parent's own parent when it registers.
- **Which call it belongs to:** nested calls run under the call the transcript shows (`CodeModeTool.Parent`), as Code Mode's do, so a shell command started through `tool.call` is recorded under the visible call.
- **Progress and stop:** a nested call's progress updates are dropped, since they'd replace the outer call's, and a stop is left to the outer call to handle. Code Mode's nested calls already work this way.

**Plugin API:** `Tool.Context` gains a required `tool: { call }` field (new `Tool.Calls` type). OpenCode sets it on every call it runs. A plugin that builds a `Tool.Context` itself, usually in tests, now has to supply `tool`, so this is a small break at the type level. Inside core, contexts are built without it and the registry adds it when the tool runs. `Tool.check`'s `CheckInput.context` leaves it out.

No flag: nothing calls it yet, and it doesn't change existing behavior.

- New tests in `packages/core/test/tool-registry.test.ts`:
  - A tool calls another and gets its output; a bad input fails with the tool's validation error; an unknown name fails.
  - Hooks fire for each nested call, and each gets its own ID.
  - A tool reaches tools by registry ID and by Code Mode path, but not one denied by the agent's rules.
  - A tool inside Code Mode calls a direct tool.
  - Calls nested two deep run under the outermost call.
- A new `packages/core/test/permission.test.ts` test covers a prompt from a call nested two deep showing on the outermost row.
- `bun run check` passes, and `typecheck:tsc` passes for core, schema and plugin.

prs.title: fix(core): keep the MCP SDK out of startup and type MCP errors
prs.body:
Every Location loaded `@modelcontextprotocol/client` at startup, even with no MCP servers configured. The built-in `opencode.mcp.skill` plugin imported `mcp/client.ts` only to check `instanceof SkillMismatchError`, and that pulled in the whole SDK. The import boundary test missed it because it only looked at `mcp/index.ts`.

```diff
 plugin/internal.ts
   plugin/mcp-skill.ts
-    mcp/client.ts
-      @modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills
+    mcp/errors.ts   (no SDK)
```

What changed:

- The MCP tagged errors (`NeedsAuthError`, `ConnectError`, `SessionExpiredError`, `SkillMismatchError`) now live in `packages/core/src/mcp/errors.ts`, which imports nothing from the SDK. `mcp/client.ts` re-exports them, so `McpClient.NeedsAuthError` and the rest are the same classes as before. Tags are unchanged.
- `mcp-skill.ts` and `connection.ts` import the errors from `errors.ts`. `connection.ts` used to match `"MCP.NeedsAuthError"` and `"MCP.SessionExpiredError"` as strings because the client module is lazy. It now uses `instanceof`, so renaming a tag can't silently turn off session recovery or the needs-auth handling.
- `test/mcp-import-boundary.test.ts` now also builds `plugin/internal.ts` (every built-in plugin, all loaded at startup) and walks the static imports from both entries. It fails if any static path reaches the SDK and prints the chain. On `dev` it fails with `internal.ts -> mcp-skill.ts -> mcp/client.ts -> @modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`.

I left `EventStreamRejectedError` and `EventStreamTerminatedError` in `event-stream.ts`, which already has no SDK imports. I also didn't retype the `McpClient.Connection` error channels. Adding `NeedsAuthError | SessionExpiredError` next to `Error` gives no type-level benefit. A real typed union would need a tagged error for every plain `Error` the client produces, which is a larger change.

No public API change.

Checks: `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, `bun run check` from the root, and the core mcp, skill, plugin and tool tests plus the boundary test.

prs.title: feat(mcp): trust private-network server certificates on first use
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #40111. Stacked on #60039 (per-server `tls` config); once that lands, this diff is just the first-use flow.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Trusting a private-network MCP server's self-signed certificate becomes a first-use decision instead of up-front TLS config:

1. The first connect to an `https` server at a private IP fails with the presented certificate — fingerprint, subject — and the command to trust it.
2. `opencode mcp trust <url>` shows the certificate's subject, validity, and fingerprint and asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the confirmation (required without a terminal); `--force` is only needed to re-pin after the certificate rotated.
3. The pin is stored per project in a new `mcp_trusted_host` table (new migration). Later connects are pinned by fingerprint, so a rotated certificate fails the connection instead of being silently accepted, and certificates without IP SANs work because the fingerprint is the identity check.

The trust hint is only added for actual TLS verification failures (self-signed, expired, alt-name, and the Node-style codes); network, protocol, and HTTP failures keep their original message. Hostnames never qualify — the IP literal in the config is the trust boundary, not DNS. An explicit `tls` config takes precedence.

prs.title: fix(core): keep Code Mode agent() children from notifying the parent or leaving jobs running
prs.body:
Part of #66691. Follow-up to #66278.

## Problem
A Code Mode script awaits each `agent()` child itself, but the children still behaved like `subagent` tool children toward the parent session. In a script with 78 `agent()` calls:

- the parent got a `<background-result kind="subagent">` notice for every child (mostly "Subagent completed without a text response"), and one transcript row per child
- 4 children returned while a shell command of theirs was still running in the background; when it exited, the child woke on its own and reported to the parent again, starting new parent turns after the script had ended

## Changes
- `session/execution/subagent-report.ts`: a child carrying the `codemodeAgent` marker settles quietly, like an automation run's child. A follow-up the parent sends through a Job still reports.
- `session/compaction-subagents.ts`: the same rule for compaction checkpoints, so finished `agent()` children no longer take the idle subagent slots.
- `tool/plugin/codemode-agents.ts`: when an `agent()` call returns, fails or is interrupted, the child's background jobs are cancelled and its own subagents stopped (the same cascade `opencode.session.interrupt` uses). Nothing is left to wake the child once the script has its result. The child's instructions now say to wait for the commands it starts.
- `codemode-agents.md`: documents both.

No script API change. Guarded by the existing `codemode_agents` flag, since only sessions created by `agent()` carry the marker.

## Not in this PR
- Foreground commands in an `agent()` child still move to the background after the shell tool's timeout. With this PR that command is stopped when the child answers, instead of waking it later; failing the call with a timeout (as automation runs do) is a follow-up.
- Restart recovery for shell jobs owned by `agent()` children.
- Continuing an earlier child or keeping a long-running process across calls. That needs an explicit handle and is a design discussion, tracked in #66691.

## Tests
- `subagent-report.test.ts`: an `agent()` child that goes idle puts nothing in the parent's inbox.
- `codemode-agents-e2e.test.ts`: after two `agent()` calls the parent session has no synthetic messages; a background job a child left running is cancelled when `agent()` returns.

All three fail on `dev` and pass here. `bun run check` passes. The full core suite passes except 25 ripgrep and search tests that fail the same way on `dev` on my machine (no local `rg`, and the tests block the download).

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #66766

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

When automatic compaction is due and a background summary is still being written, `usePrecomputed` waited on it with a bare `Fiber.await(held.fiber)`. If that request stalls, or keeps failing and getting resent under the retry policy, the session stays on `session.compaction.started` with no terminal event until the chunk timeout.

The wait now has a limit, `PRECOMPUTE_WAIT` (2 minutes, about twice the 30-60 s a summary takes per the `PRECOMPUTE_LEAD` comment). When it runs out, the background summary is interrupted and `usePrecomputed` returns `undefined`, so `compact` summarizes in the foreground as it already does for a failed or unusable held summary. A summary that finishes within the limit is still swapped in as before. The span also records `compaction.background.timed_out`.

I picked 2 minutes so a slow but healthy summary isn't thrown away. Happy to change the value.

prs.title: refactor(core): cache the normalized models.dev catalog
prs.body:
Every server process decodes and normalizes the models.dev catalog once, and the result is only a pure function of the catalog body, the `recommended`/`speeds` flags and the UTC day (prices are dated). In a release build that is one of the largest one-time allocations a process makes, and it repeats for every session server and CLI command.

This writes the finished snapshots to the cache directory, keyed by the catalog digest, the app version and the UTC day, so the next process can start from them. The KV metadata row already carries the body digest, so a cache hit skips loading and decoding the multi-MB body as well. Dev checkouts report `local` and never reuse an entry. A missing, foreign, stale or corrupt file just falls back to the existing path.

Measured with a `--single --skip-web-ui` release-style build, RssAnon after boot plus the first `/api/model`:

| | cold | second process, warm cache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| run 1 | 218 MB | 172 MB |
| run 2 | 222 MB | - |

The normalized file is 6.5 MB, the saving is about 46-50 MB per process. Cache misses pay one write; nothing new runs on a hit.

Verified with `bun run typecheck` and `bun test test/models.test.ts` in `packages/core` (38 pass). New tests cover the warm read, the digest-only metadata hit, and a corrupt file falling back to the bundled snapshot.

### Summary

On touch / no-hover devices the always-visible user-message chevron was given room by floating a 20px `::before` at the end of the first text line. When the bubble is capped by `max-width`, that float reduces the text's usable width, so a trailing word wraps even though the bubble has visible free space.

This change reserves the chevron's space in the bubble's inline-end padding and adds the same 20px to the bubble's `max-width` under `@media not (hover: hover)`. The text keeps the same usable width as on hover devices, and the chevron still has its own space.

- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

- On no-hover devices, replaces the first-line float with `padding-inline-end: 32px` on the text and widens the bubble by 20px via `calc(var(--user-message-max-width) + 20px)`.
- Adds two wrapping stories (`WidthCapWrapping` and `CharacterCapWrapping`) and a component regression spec (`message-bubble-wrap.spec.ts`) that mounts them with touch emulation, checks `(hover: none)` is active, waits for fonts, and asserts the prompt stays on one line without overlapping the chevron. prs.title: refactor(sdk,server): split ServerOptions, unify ServerFetch, and clean SDK seams
prs.body:
Splits `ServerOptions` cleanly into `AppOptions` + `HttpListenerOptions`, unifies `EmbeddedHost` with `ServerFetch` (fixing `withoutParentSpan` and `DebugHandler` context parity), and moves internal SDK `embed` hooks out of the public surface with `@deprecated` backwards-compatible bridges.

### Before
- `ServerOptions` bundled HTTP listener settings (`hostname`, `port`, `password`, `cors`), internal `simulation`, and core runtime options into one flat schema, causing `createEmbeddedRoutes` to silently accept and discard `password` and leaking `cors`/`simulation` into SDK `CreateOptions`.
- `EmbeddedHost.create` duplicated `ServerFetch.makeWithContext` (omitting `withoutParentSpan`, leaking `forkDetach` on `ServerFetch`, and passing only 2 logger context keys to `toWebHandlerWith`).
- Public `@opencode/sdk/effect` exposed internal `embed?: EmbedOptions` (`LayerNode.Replacements`) on `OpenCode.create`, while both SDKs leaked `session`/`event` alongside documented `sessions`/`events`.

Extracts the Session Core inbox delivery rules into one pure `SessionInbox.plan(pending, reach): Boundary` function and replaces `SessionRunner`'s `force` / `continuation?` / `stepped?: true` flag soup with a `Position` union.

issues.title: Pasted ANSI leaves escape-sequence corpses in the prompt, and an unterminated bracketed paste wedges the editor (Ctrl+C dead)
issues.body:
## What

Pasting terminal output that contains ANSI escapes puts the escape bodies into the prompt as literal text, and an unterminated bracketed paste leaves the editor unable to accept any input — Ctrl+C included.

## Why

`pi-tui` 1.4.0, `components/editor.ts`:

`handlePaste()` filters pasted text per character:

```ts
let filteredText = cleanText
  .split("")
  .filter((char) => char === "\n" || char.charCodeAt(0) >= 32)
  .join("");
```

ESC (0x1b) is dropped and the rest of the sequence is kept, so `\x1b[38;2;111;63;32m` is inserted as the visible text `[38;2;111;63;32m`, and `\x1b[<35;153;17M` as `[<35;153;17M`. A pasted screenful of coloured/mouse-reporting output turns into thousands of characters of that. The comment a few lines above already documents this same class of leak for tmux csi-u re-encoding.

`handleInput()` then handles `isInPaste` before every keybinding and returns:

```ts
if (this.isInPaste) {
    this.pasteBuffer += data;
    const endIndex = this.pasteBuffer.indexOf("\x1b[201~");
    if (endIndex !== -1) { ... }
    return;
}
...
if (kb.matches(data, "tui.input.copy")) {   // Ctrl+C, unreachable while isInPaste
    return;
}
```

If `\x1b[201~` never arrives — another process on the same tty reads it first, the paste is cut short, or a split read loses it — every later keystroke, Ctrl+C included, is appended to `pasteBuffer` and dropped. The session cannot be typed into again; only a new paste (its own terminator closes the stale one) or killing the process recovers.

## Repro

1. Start `pi` in a pane whose tty is shared with another process that can read stdin — e.g. a `sudo`/`SUDO_ASKPASS` fallback doing `read -rs … < /dev/tty`, or a tool that hands the terminal to a child.
2. Paste terminal output containing ANSI (truecolor SGR, SGR mouse reports).
3. The escape bodies appear as literal text in the prompt. If the paste terminator was consumed by the other reader, the editor stops accepting input permanently and Ctrl+C does nothing.

Observed on macOS in a multiplexer pane (pi 1.4.0), where a password prompt owned the tty while the paste was in flight.

## Suggested fix

- Strip whole escape sequences (there is already a `stripTerminalSequences` helper) before the per-character filter, so a pasted ANSI stream degrades to plain text instead of escape corpses.
- Bound `isInPaste`: clear it on an idle timeout or on a lone ESC, so one missing terminator cannot wedge the editor.

issues.title: Recheck the output budget after mid-turn compaction

### What do you want to change?

Before sending the next request after a tool batch, check the output budget using the same estimate that sets `max_tokens`. If compaction does not leave enough room, reduce the retained tool output and continue, or explain why Pi cannot continue rather than sending the starved request.

### Why?

On Pi 1.6.0 with Qwen3.8-27B via llama.cpp (32,768 context, default compaction settings), fetching a changelog left a calculated output cap of `32768 - 22982 - 5420 - 4096 = 270`. issues.title: TUI: URLs in inline code and fenced blocks get no OSC 8, so wrapped rows and trailing CJK text give a wrong link target

## What happened?

URLs that pi renders itself inside inline code or inside a fenced code block never get an OSC 8 hyperlink, so after pi hard-wraps the line the terminal's own URL detector decides what the link is. In two cases the target is wrong:

1. A 434-char authorize URL in a fenced block at width 80 is rendered as 6 rows with zero OSC 8 sequences. Row 1 is a valid URL, rows 2-6 are not links, so ctrl-click opens the URL truncated.
2. Inline code containing `http://localhost`, immediately followed by full-width punctuation and text, renders no OSC 8 either, and the terminal matches `http://localhost），把` as the href. Clicking navigates to a URL that is not in my message.

Why it matters: OAuth login URLs are long and usually printed in a fence, so case 1 breaks the click. Case 2 silently sends the browser to a wrong URL.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne`, terminal width 80.
2. Ask for a fenced code block containing a URL longer than the pane (an authorize URL is enough), and for inline code `http://localhost` followed by `），把` on the same line.

Render-level check, no terminal needed: construct `Markdown` from `packages/tui` with hyperlinks capability on and count OSC 8 sequences in `render(80)`. Both cases emit 0; the same URL written as prose emits one per row.

## Expected behavior

Anything pi lays out itself that is a URL should carry OSC 8 when the terminal supports hyperlinks, so `wrapTextWithAnsi` re-opens the full target on every wrapped row, as it already does for prose links.
