prs.title: feat(mcp,coding-agent): support the stateless MCP protocol 2026-07-28
prs.body:
Adds MCP `2026-07-28`, the stateless protocol revision, to `pi-mcp` and to pi's MCP extension. Servers on the earlier versions keep working as before. Refs #10416 ## Problem Up to `2025-11-25`, every connection starts with an `initialize` handshake, and over HTTP the server keeps a session. `2026-07-28` removes both. Each request carries its own protocol version, client info and capabilities in `_meta`, and a client discovers the server with `server/discover`: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant pi participant Server Note over pi,Server: legacy (2025-11-25 and earlier) pi->>Server: initialize Server-->>pi: capabilities + Mcp-Session-Id pi->>Server: notifications/initialized pi->>Server: tools/call (session header) Note over pi,Server: modern (2026-07-28) pi->>Server: server/discover (_meta: version, clientInfo, capabilities) Server-->>pi: supportedVersions, capabilities pi->>Server: tools/call (_meta again, Mcp-Method / Mcp-Name / Mcp-Param-* headers) ``` A pi that only sends `initialize` cannot talk to a server that only speaks `2026-07-28`. ## How pi picks the protocol `mcp.json` entries gain `protocol`: ```diff { "mcpServers": { "remote": { "url": "https://example.com/mcp", + "protocol": "auto" } } } ``` `auto` is the default for every server. A pinned `"2026-07-28"` connects with that version only and never falls back. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[connect with auto] --> B{remembered from
the last connection?} B -- yes --> C[use it] C -- fails --> D B -- no --> D[server/discover] D -- discover result with a
mutual version --> M[modern] D -- UnsupportedProtocolVersionError --> R[retry once with a listed version] --> M D -- other error, non-auth 4xx,
timeout, or no discover result --> L[initialize: legacy] D -- stdio server exits --> S[restart without the probe] --> L ``` Legacy servers usually reject the probe right away, so `auto` costs one round trip once per session. A legacy stdio server that exits on the probe is restarted without it. One that never answers it waits for the request timeout; `"protocol": "legacy"` skips the probe for such servers. ## What changed ```text packages/mcp/src/ ├── rpc-peer.ts # new: JSON-RPC engine (ids, timeouts, progress, cancel), moved out of McpClient ├── client.ts # lifecycle + typed API; legacy handshake or discover, then requests of either kind ├── protocol/ │ ├── modern.ts # new: _meta, resultType, discover result, modern error detection │ ├── http-headers.ts # new: Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-* (x-mcp-header), value encoding │ └── types.ts # version constants, McpProtocolMode, McpNegotiatedProtocol ├── transports/ │ ├── streamable-http.ts # stateless requests: no session, no GET stream, no resumption │ ├── http-errors.ts # new: HTTP errors, importable without loading the transport │ └── transport.ts # transports opt in with `modernProtocol` └── config.ts # shared `protocol` field packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/mcp/runtime.ts # probe, remember, re-probe; subscriptions/listen ``` The first commit only moves the JSON-RPC engine out of `McpClient`. It changes no behavior, and the existing tests pass unchanged. It is easier to review on its own. A modern request in `McpClient`, including multi round-trip requests (the server asks the client for input before it can finish a request): ```text requestModern(method, params) loop rpc.request(method, withModernMeta(params, version)) on UnsupportedProtocolVersionError: switch to a mutual version once, send again readModernResult(result) complete -> return result input_required -> answer each input request with the setRequestHandler() handler of the same method (roots/list from `roots`) send again as a new request with inputResponses + requestState (at most 16 rounds) ``` Over Streamable HTTP, `send()` reads the version from the request's `_meta`, so the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header always matches the body. JSON-RPC errors in 4xx bodies become responses. Cancelling a request closes its response stream. Behavior in pi with a `2026-07-28` server: - Tools whose `x-mcp-header` annotations are invalid are left out of the tool list and reported. - `roots/list` input requests are answered with the session directory. Tool calls that ask for elicitation or sampling fail, because pi supports neither. - A `subscriptions/listen` stream stays open to follow tool list changes. It reopens with backoff, and tools are refreshed after it reopens. - Every request asks for `info` and more severe log messages for `mcp.log`. Modern servers only log for requests that ask. `pi-mcp` API: `McpClient` gets the `protocol` and `logLevel` options, `listen()` and `negotiatedProtocol` (`{ era: "legacy" | "modern", version }`). `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and `SupportedProtocolVersion` keep their meaning (legacy versions). `MODERN_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` and `ModernProtocolVersion` are new. Clients default to `legacy`, so existing `pi-mcp` users see no change. ## Conformance The MCP conformance suite (`@modelcontextprotocol/conformance@0.2.0-alpha.11`) now also runs its `2026-07-28` scenarios. The baselines for `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-11-25` are unchanged, even though HTTP servers are now probed first. | Version | Scenarios | Fully passing | Checks passing / failing | |---|---|---|---| | 2025-03-26 | 2 | 2 | 15 / 0 | | 2025-06-18 | 5 | 5 | 53 / 0 | | 2025-11-25 | 19 | 16 | 192 / 8 | | 2026-07-28 | 33 | 23 | 323 / 14 | Known `2026-07-28` failures, listed in `test/mcp-conformance/README.md`: - elicitation in `sep-2322-client-request-state` (pi has no elicitation) - re-registration when the authorization server changes (SEP-2352) - the suite's CIMD client id - the issuer and resource mismatch scenarios, where `pi-client` fails by design because pi refuses the sign-in ## Testing - `npm run check` - `./test.sh`: everything passes except two tests unrelated to MCP. `footer-data-provider` timed out once and passes on rerun. `pi-env`'s `ssh.test.ts` fails on machines whose login shell is fish. - New tests: `client-modern.test.ts`, `streamable-http-modern.test.ts`, `modern.test.ts`, `http-headers.test.ts`, plus protocol detection, re-probing and listen cases in `mcp-extension.test.ts`. --- AI disclosure: this change was driven by @dmmulroy using Opus 5.5.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): cap codemode's nested call rows to bound progress …
prs.body:
Trying to fix a problem when running a codemode script that makes many nested calls can crash pi with a V8 OOM. In RPC
mode, about 1700 retries of a blocked read reached the 4 GB heap limit.

executeCodemode kept a row for every nested call and published a copy of all rows when each call started and finished. The work grew as O(n²), and RPC queued every update until stdout drained.

This caps the rows at NESTED_CALL_LIMITS.maxCalls, as NestedCallRecorder already does. Later calls still run. They are counted in details.omittedCalls and details.omittedCost, and they send no updates. The renderer, the failure summary
and usage totals still cover every call.

Tests: a suite test runs 260 faux classifier calls and checks the listed calls, the omitted count and cost, usage and the number of updates. A renderer test checks the omitted-calls line and the cost total.

prs.title: feat(interactive): auto-reload resources on file change (no manual /reload)
prs.body:
## What

Adds an opt-out file watcher so edits to local resources are picked up automatically, without running `/reload`.

Watches the agent + project resource directories:
`~/.pi/agent/{extensions,skills,prompts,themes}` and `<cwd>/.pi/{extensions,skills,prompts,themes}`.

## Why

Iterating on extensions, skills, prompt templates or themes currently requires a manual `/reload` after every edit. This makes that automatic while staying unobtrusive.

## How

- **settings**: new boolean `autoReload` (default `true`) — defaults, TypeBox schema, getter/setter, and a toggle in `/settings` ("Auto reload").
- **ResourceLoader.getWatchDirs()**: exposes the directories worth watching (only existing ones).
- **interactive-mode**:
  - `fs.watch(dir, { recursive: true })` over each watch dir, started after `init()` and re-armed after every reload (picks up new dirs / toggled setting).
  - **1.2s debounce** coalesces bursts of writes (editors often save several files).
  - **Idle guard**: if a turn is streaming/compacting, the reload is deferred and retried until idle — never interrupts a response.
  - `handleReloadCommand({ auto })` runs quietly (no modal box, brief status line) for watcher-triggered reloads.
  - Watcher torn down on shutdown.
  - Ignores transient editor artifacts (`*~`, `*.swp`, `*.tmp`, `.DS_Store`).

## Notes / scope

- Covers the same resources as `/reload` for extensions/skills/prompts/themes/keybindings. Does **not** hot-reload `mcp.json` (already-spawned MCP servers don't reload live by design) or `settings.json`.
- Recursive `fs.watch` is native on Windows/macOS; on platforms without recursive support it degrades gracefully to no watch (per-dir try/catch), leaving manual `/reload` working.
- Can be disabled via `/settings` → Auto reload → false, or `"autoReload": false` in settings.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.build.json`: clean.
- `npm run build`: clean bundle.
- Verified recursive `fs.watch` fires on Windows against the real prompts dir.

releases.name: v1.7.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **[Terminal session resume](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/terminal-setup.md#program-resume):** Compatible terminals can reopen the current pi session after a restart with its original profile, tool restrictions, and instructions.
- **[Image generation in codemode](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md#generate-images):** Generate images with Radius, or set the aspect ratio and size when using OpenRouter image models.
- **GitHub Copilot prompt caching:** Changing the thinking level preserves the prompt cache on supported Claude 5.x and GPT-6 models. Supported Claude 5.x models also keep the cache when tools change, and Copilot Claude models support [cache warming](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#model-and-thinking).

### Breaking Changes

- Removed telemetry reporting from pi for new installs and updates (`/api/report-install`), the `enableInstallTelemetry` setting (`SettingsManager.getEnableInstallTelemetry()` / `setEnableInstallTelemetry()`), and `PI_TELEMETRY`

### Added

- Added program resume through the [Program Resume Protocol (OSC 7577)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-resume): in terminals that set `OSC7577_TOKEN`, interactive mode reports `pi --session <id>` for the current session, so the terminal can bring it back after it restarts. Pi removes the token from the environment of every process it starts. See [Terminal setup](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/terminal-setup.md#program-resume)
- Added optional `{ aspectRatio, size }` as the third argument to codemode `models.generateImages()`
- Added `--agent-dir <dir>`, the command-line form of `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. The resume command pi prints on exit and reports through OSC 7577 now includes it when the config directory is not `~/.pi/agent`. Without it, a session started with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` came back with the default directory's settings and auth: a terminal resumes the command without the environment pi was started in. This is for setups that keep a separate pi profile per project, for example a shell function that sets `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` for one directory tree. Terminals that resume programs, such as Rex, need a rule that trusts the longer command; see [Terminal setup](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/terminal-setup.md#program-resume)
- The OSC 7577 resume command now repeats the restriction and resource flags pi was started with (`--tools`, `--no-extensions`, `-e`, `--skill`, `--system-prompt`, and similar), as typed, so a terminal cannot resume a session with other tools or instructions, possibly more access, than it had. The command printed on exit is unchanged. A terminal rule must trust each flag combination; see [Terminal setup](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/terminal-setup.md#program-resume)
- Added Radius image generation to [codemode](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.7.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md#generate-images). Radius image and classifier models are now listed in the built-in catalog as well as through provider discovery

### Changed

- The default model for `cloudflare-workers-ai` and `cloudflare-ai-gateway` is now `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3`, because Cloudflare deprecated Workers AI Kimi K2.6 and K2.7 Code
- Changed the `ant-ling` default model from the retired `Ring-2.6-1T` to `Ling-3.1-flash`. Existing `models.json` files can keep `thinkingFormat: "ant-ling"` as a deprecated alias for `"deepseek"` ([#11800](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11800) by [@lvisei](https://github.com/lvisei))
- Replaced the retired `qwen4-max-preview` with `qwen4-max` on Qwen Token Plan Individual
- Preserved the GitHub Copilot prompt cache when changing thinking levels on supported Claude 5.x and GPT-6 models or changing tools on supported Claude 5.x models. Copilot Claude models now support cache warming, and GPT-5.3 Codex and MAI-Code receive mid-conversation system messages where they take effect ([#12316](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12316))

### Fixed

- Fixed `/llama` "Download model" downloading the typed text instead of the highlighted result when the query looked like `owner/repository` and the user had moved the selection with the arrow keys ([#12465](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12465))
- Fixed key hints that named the wrong keybinding or a hardcoded key: the extension editor and session rename now name `tui.input.submit`, `/hotkeys` names `tui.select.cancel` for cancelling autocomplete, and the settings submenu, `/config` selector, session selector and fullscreen copy setting follow remapped keys
- Fixed a console Ctrl+Break on Windows ending pi without restoring the terminal, which left the shell in the alternate screen with mouse reports typed into the prompt. A child process in the same console can send Ctrl+Break too. pi now shuts down normally on it ([#12133](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12133))
- Fixed print, JSON, and RPC modes not reporting an invalid `models.json`, so a typo such as `"contextWindow": "32000"` showed up only as `Model "..." not found` or `No API key found`. `createAgentSessionServices()` now returns the error as a warning in `diagnostics`, so every mode and SDK runtimes report it; interactive mode shows it as a warning instead of an error, as reported in [#12522](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12522) ([#12523](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12523) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed `app.message.followUp` (Alt+Enter) ignoring an open autocomplete menu and queuing the half-typed text. It now applies the selected suggestion like Enter: a completed command name is queued, and other completions are inserted without queuing
- Fixed running `!` commands showing the wrong cancel shortcut. The hint now names the configured `app.interrupt` key ([#12518](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12518) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed `!!` commands counting toward the context estimate even though the model never sees them. Large outputs no longer trigger early compaction or crowd out recent history ([#12513](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12513))
- Fixed Kitty images disappearing in Konsole and regular mode clearing the screen and scrollback when an appended image extended past the bottom of the screen ([#12548](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12548))
- Fixed Amazon Bedrock Kimi K3.1 and GLM 5.3 ignoring the selected thinking level ([#12462](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12462)). Kimi K3 and K3.1 also no longer send earlier reasoning back to Bedrock, which could make later turns fail
- Fixed GitHub Copilot models using `openai-completions` losing their reasoning state between turns ([#12418](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12418))
- Fixed codemode image generation reporting success for failed OpenRouter responses. Image and classifier usage now includes reasoning tokens when reported; image usage distinguishes image output tokens, and OpenRouter costs use the reported total or the model's image output rate when estimating

## What happened?

The [root contribution guide](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/CONTRIBUTING.md#L253-L269) and [developer guide](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/docs/developers/contributing.md#L231-L247) say `npm run link` links the entire `docs` tree and that every edit is reflected immediately. The [docs-site README](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/docs-site/README.md#L18-L28) describes the public sections as copies. Neither description tells contributors when they need to run the command again.

## Expected behavior

The three guides should reflect the [link script](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/docs-site/scripts/link-public-docs.mjs#L8-L17) and [public directory list](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/docs-site/src/app/public-docs.js#L3-L5). Edits under `docs/users/` and `docs/developers/` are available through directory links without running the command again. Changes to `docs/index.md` or `docs/_meta.ts` require rerunning `npm run link` from `docs-site` to refresh the copies. Internal directories such as `docs/design/` stay outside the preview.

## Client information

Verified on macOS using the existing link command in a temporary copy of the upstream checkout. Edits in both linked directories were visible through their links immediately. The copied files reflected source edits after the second run.

The workflow runs on pushes to `main` and `feat/e2e/**`, nightly, and by manual dispatch. Its Linux sandbox matrix uses no sandbox and Docker. The same section should distinguish this workflow from the [integration checks in the main CI workflow](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/940e9b7925/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L3474-L3505). The local Podman commands are documented separately and still apply.

## Client information

Documentation discrepancy on `main` at `940e9b7925`, verified by comparing the guide with the workflow files on macOS. No CLI session or credentials are required.

prs.title: fix(core): keep what the person typed in a reduced compaction request (#9455)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a compaction request does not fit its window, #15936 reduces it by cutting every text part to 4,000 characters, the user's own messages included. This PR keeps the text the person typed in that reduced request.

- **The person's prompt is marked where it is sent.** The CLI's interactive and OpenTUI modes mark the part that holds a prompt a person submitted, and headless mode does for a person's message sent as stream-json input. ACP marks a prompt a person wrote, and hosted serve marks a prompt that reaches the model as written. A plain `-p` prompt, slash-command expansions, a Mod's or a scheduled prompt, mid-turn messages and hosted input queued during a turn are not marked. Core marks the first text part of a person's prompt unless the front end marked the prompt itself, as ACP does, since it puts the instruction last. The mark is never sent to a provider. The CLI stores it in the session file; ACP and hosted serve record the turn without it, so after a resume their earlier turns are cut as before.
- **A reduced request keeps the marked text.** It is kept whole, up to a cap of 32,000 characters. The IDE context the CLI puts in front of the prompt after marking it is recorded where it is put there, and is cut like other text and closed again, so a prompt that itself opens with a reminder block is kept as typed. A prompt retried with Ctrl+Y keeps the mark of the send that failed. Unmarked text, including attached files, tool output and every turn of a session recorded before this change, is cut exactly as before.
- **It never asks for more than the plain cut.** Each character kept beyond the plain cut is charged as a whole token against the summary's output budget, so a request the server accepts in its plain form is also accepted with the text kept, at any density up to a token a character. The kept request is used only on the first send, and only while the summary keeps at least half of its budget and its minimum: at the 20,000-token budget cap, that is one message of up to about 14,000 characters. Past that the request is the plain cut, as today. A rejected kept request is retried with the plain cut, even when the two differ by only a few characters. If a kept reply has no output count and no closed `<state_snapshot>`, the truncation check would drop it for the smaller budget, so the plain cut is sent once instead.
- It also corrects a code comment that came with #15936. Not every writer escapes tags inside a block's body: the reminder that ends a todo-list result holds the list as JSON. #15936's design doc already says so.

## Why it's needed

The summary prompt asks for the user's exact phrasing and for every user message, but a reduced request held only the first 4,000 characters of each, so a long request, often a pasted spec or log followed by the actual ask, reached the summarizer without its end. On a mock backend that enforces the window, with 5 requirement sentences spread through each long request, the sentences that reached the summary request rose from 15, 10 and 10 of 25 to 23, 19 and 16 of 25 for requests of 6,000, 9,000 and 12,000 characters, in English and in Chinese alike.

This is the second half of the work split out of #14953. It differs from the plan I posted there on 11-02 in three ways:

- Parts 1 and 2 of that plan are one PR. Telling typed text apart by its position in the turn failed in several layouts: ACP puts the prompt last, and memory recall, the IDE context, task notifications, an earlier summary and restored files all sit beside it. So the text is now marked where it is sent, and only marked text is kept.
- The kept text keeps its start only, not its start and its end. Eliding the middle would create cut shapes that the closing rule for cut text was never measured on.
- Condensing older turns to the user's messages, part 3 of that plan, is not in this PR.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Use an OpenAI-compatible provider, or a local mock, that rejects any request whose prompt plus `max_tokens` exceeds its window, and log the requests it receives. Build a session with a few large file reads and one typed message of about 10,000 characters whose last sentence is distinctive. Then set the window low enough that the compaction request no longer fits, and run `/compress`.

- Before: the message reaches the compaction request cut to its first 4,000 characters, followed by the truncation marker.
- After: it reaches the request whole, and the summary can name its last sentence. Compaction succeeds as before.
- A message of 4,000 characters or less is the same before and after. A message over about 14,000 characters, or several long messages that together pass that budget, are cut as before.
- A slash command's expansion, and a session recorded before this change, are cut as before.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Real provider: OpenRouter `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`. Before is `main` at this branch's base and After is this branch. Each session was built once with After through stream-json input, which marks the person's message, and restored for both sides, so both compress identical histories. `/compress` ran with the window set to 32,768, so every compaction request took the reduced path; a recall question ("list every requirement I gave you") then ran with the window at 262,144. Each long message carried 5 requirement codes spread through it.

| Scenario | Before: typed text in the compaction request | Before: codes recalled | After: typed text in the request | After: codes recalled | After `max_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3,000 characters (control) | whole | 5 of 5 | identical request | 5 of 5 | 20,000 |
| 6,000 | first 4,000 | 3, 3 | whole | 5, 5 | 18,030 |
| 9,000 | first 4,000 | 2, 0¹ | whole | 5, 5 | 15,030 |
| 12,000 | first 4,000 | 2, 2 | whole | 5, 5 | 12,030 |
| 9,000 Chinese characters | first 4,000 | 2, 2 | whole | 5, 5 | 15,030 |
| 18,000 (past the budget) | first 4,000 | 1¹ | identical request | 1 | 20,000 |
| 6,000, sent with plain `-p` (unmarked) | first 4,000 | 3 | identical request | 3 | 20,000 |

Two numbers are two runs; a request and its repeat were byte-identical. Every compaction was a single request answered 200 with finish `stop`, with no rejection and no retry. `max_tokens` fell by exactly the characters kept, and the kept text actually cost about 0.2 prompt tokens per character in English and 0.58 in Chinese. No request carried the mark, and no recall named a code that had not reached its compaction request. Total cost about $0.30.

¹ The stored summary was cut short by the existing step that strips the summary's analysis block: the model quoted the compaction directive in its summary, and the quote was read as an unclosed block. Both sides run that code.

The recall question ran at 262,144 because, under the 32,768 window, both sides sent it with `max_tokens: 1`. That looks like the post-compaction estimate issue (#15486); it was not traced here.

Unit tests cover:

- the mark: its shape, its absence from requests on the native, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and Responses routes, its survival through the session file, and the resume checks that drop a completed local command's input;
- each place it is set and each exclusion: no human input, internal sends, a Mod's prompt and side queries; ACP's model-only prompts, runtime Goal continuations and attachment-only prompts; hosted prompts that are not new input, were rewritten or extended, or had memory joined; and a request its front end already marked, as ACP sends one on the shared agent loop;
- keeping: the recorded IDE prefix cut and closed, a prompt that opens with a reminder block kept with and without that prefix, a prefix the text does not bear out, a lone opening tag the person typed, and the cap with a block it cuts inside;
- the retry: marked when the entry it dropped marked the same text, and left as it is otherwise;
- the budget: smaller by exactly the characters kept; used at exactly half of the plain budget and not one character past it; the plain cut when the summary would fall under its minimum, on the retry and on the payload-overflow path; a retry only a few characters shorter than the kept request; a kept reply with no usage and no snapshot, followed by one plain send, and one that counts its output only as total less prompt, carries a closed snapshot or is only analysis, sent alone; and a sweep over session shapes, lengths and scripts in which the kept request is accepted wherever the plain one is.

At `fff3048c30`: the core suites under services, core and utils ran 16,928 tests, of which 16,895 passed and 33 were skipped; none failed. The ACP integration, hosted harness and prompt ledger suites pass, 3,683 of 3,683. Core and CLI type-check clean. Before the rebase, each of 20 guards was reverted on its own and turned its tests red, and so does each check added in review: the skip for an already-marked request, the character comparison on the retry, and the plain resend.

At `3d0b69a7b2`: the core tests for typed-prompt, partUtils, compactionInputSlimming, chatCompressionService, client, llm-content-generator, session-api-history and environmentContext pass, 1,487 of 1,487. The CLI ACP integration, hosted harness, prompt ledger and `use-llm-stream` suites pass 4,328, with 5 skipped. Core and CLI type-check clean. Each of the 18 checks added in round three (the recorded prefix, the shared slim options, the fallback's three conditions and the retry mark) was broken on its own and turned its tests red.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests; a local mock provider for the request-level comparison; OpenRouter `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` for the end-to-end run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the kept text comes out of the summary's output budget, by at most half, so a summary longer than that budget, which the plain request would have fit, is dropped as truncated. Keeping is all or nothing per request: past about 14,000 characters of typed text (less in a tight window, and counted over all messages), the request is the plain cut. Text denser than a token a character, such as rare CJK characters or emoji, can make the server reject the kept request; the retry then sends the plain cut. The text after a marked part's recorded prefix is kept as typed, which in the CLI includes the framing around a paste, a prompt that a `UserPromptSubmit` hook rewrote, and the worktree notice and workflow size note the interactive CLI joins into the prompt before marking it, a few lines each. A send that fails before its entry reaches history leaves its retry unmarked. Core marks the first text part, so a caller that sends the human-input flag with another part first and marks nothing gets that part marked: headless mode does this on a first turn that carries a startup-worktree or recovered-agents notice, where the notice is marked and the text is cut as before.
- Not validated / out of scope: whether keeping the text improves task outcomes; marking a plain `-p` prompt, slash-command expansions, mid-turn messages and hosted input queued during a turn; keeping as much of a long message as the budget allows, and keeping its end; condensing older turns (part 3 of the #14953 plan); recording the mark in ACP's and hosted serve's turn records; tests for ACP's sandbox/SSH marking branch and for the minimum-output floor. The end-to-end run used stream-json input; the interactive, OpenTUI and ACP front ends are covered by unit tests only. Windows and Linux are covered by CI only.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Sessions recorded before this change have no marks and are cut as before, and the mark is not sent to providers.

Design doc: [English](https://github.com/yanyukang2003-ux/qwen-code/blob/fix/9455-keep-typed-text/docs/design/2026-11-17-keep-typed-text-in-reduced-compaction.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/yanyukang2003-ux/qwen-code/blob/fix/9455-keep-typed-text/docs/design/2026-11-17-keep-typed-text-in-reduced-compaction.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #9455. Follows #15936. The round-4 findings from #14953 are answered in a comment below.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

压缩请求放不进窗口时，#15936 会把每个文本片段截到 4,000 字来缩减它，用户自己的消息也一样被截。这个 PR 让缩减后的请求保留用户亲手输入的文字。

- **在发送的地方给用户的提示打标记。** CLI 的交互界面和 OpenTUI 会给装着用户所提交提示的那个片段打标记，无界面模式对以 stream-json 输入发送的用户消息也会打标记。ACP 给用户写的提示打标记，托管模式给原样发给模型的提示打标记。普通的 `-p` 提示、斜杠命令的展开内容、Mod 或定时任务的提示、对话进行中插入的消息，以及托管模式在一轮进行中排队的输入，都不打标记。core 给用户提示的第一个文字片段打标记，除非前端已经自己打过标记，比如 ACP，因为它把指令放在最后。标记从不发给模型服务商。CLI 会把它存进会话文件；ACP 和托管模式记录这一轮时不带标记，所以恢复会话之后，它们较早的轮次照旧截断。
- **缩减后的请求保留有标记的文字。** 整条保留，上限 32,000 字。CLI 在打标记之后放到提示前面的 IDE 上下文，会在拼接处记下长度，并和其他文字一样截断、重新补上结束标签；所以用户自己以提醒块开头的提示也按用户输入保留。用 Ctrl+Y 重试的提示，沿用失败那次的标记。没有标记的文字，包括附带的文件、工具输出，以及这次改动之前录制的会话里的每一轮，都和以前完全一样地截断。
- **请求的总量从不超过普通截法。** 比普通截法多保留的每个字，都按一个完整的 token 从摘要的输出额度里扣除，所以服务器能接受普通版的请求，保留文字后也一定能接受，只要文字密度不超过每字一个 token。保留版只在第一次发送时使用，而且只在摘要还能保有至少一半额度和最低输出空间时使用：额度为 20,000 token 上限时，就是单条最多约 14,000 字的消息。超出时请求就是普通截法，和现在一样。保留版被拒后，重试发送普通截法，即使两者只差几个字也是如此。如果保留版的回复没有输出用量、也没有完整的 `<state_snapshot>`，截断检查会因为额度较小而丢掉它，这时改发一次普通截法。
- 同时更正一条随 #15936 合入的代码注释。并非所有写入方都会转义块正文里的标签：待办列表结果末尾的提醒以 JSON 形式放入列表。#15936 的设计文档已经写明了这一点。

## 为什么需要

摘要提示词要求引用用户的原话、列出每一条用户消息，但缩减后的请求里每条消息只剩前 4,000 字，所以长请求（常常是先贴一段需求或日志、最后才是真正的要求）送到摘要模型时没有了结尾。在一个严格执行窗口限制的模拟后端上，每条长请求里均匀埋 5 句要求：6,000、9,000、12,000 字的请求，送进摘要请求的句数分别从 25 句中的 15、10、10 句提高到 23、19、16 句，英文和中文结果相同。

这是从 #14953 拆出来的后半部分工作。它和我 11-02 在那里发的计划有三点不同：

- 那个计划的第 1、2 部分合成了一个 PR。按片段在一轮中的位置来判断哪些是用户输入的文字，在好几种布局下都会出错：ACP 把提示放在最后，而记忆召回、IDE 上下文、任务通知、上一次的摘要和恢复的文件都和它并列。所以现在改为在发送的地方打标记，只保留有标记的文字。
- 保留的文字只留开头，不再同时保留开头和结尾。从中间省略会产生新的截断形态，而被截断文字的补闭合规则从未在这些形态上验证过。
- 把旧轮次压缩成只剩用户消息（那个计划的第 3 部分）不在这个 PR 里。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

使用一个兼容 OpenAI 的服务商或本地模拟服务，要求它拒绝提示加 `max_tokens` 超过窗口的请求，并记录收到的请求。建立一个会话：读几个大文件，再输入一条约 10,000 字、最后一句很有辨识度的消息。然后把窗口调小，让压缩请求放不下，再运行 `/compress`。

- 改动前：这条消息进入压缩请求时只剩前 4,000 字，后面跟着截断标记。
- 改动后：它完整进入请求，摘要能说出它的最后一句。压缩和以前一样成功。
- 4,000 字以内的消息改动前后相同。超过约 14,000 字的消息，或几条长消息加起来超过这个额度时，照旧截断。
- 斜杠命令的展开内容，以及这次改动之前录制的会话，照旧截断。

### 证据（改动前后对比）

真实服务：OpenRouter `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`。改动前是这个分支所基于的 `main`，改动后是这个分支。每个会话都用改动后的版本通过 stream-json 输入（它会给人的消息打标记）建立一次，再分别在两边恢复，所以两边压缩的是完全相同的历史。`/compress` 在窗口设为 32,768 时运行，因此每个压缩请求都走缩减路径；之后在窗口为 262,144 时提一个回忆问题（"列出我给你的每一条要求"）。每条长消息里均匀埋了 5 个要求编号。

| 场景 | 改动前：压缩请求里的用户文字 | 改动前：复述出的编号 | 改动后：请求里的用户文字 | 改动后：复述出的编号 | 改动后的 `max_tokens` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3,000 字（对照） | 完整 | 5/5 | 请求完全相同 | 5/5 | 20,000 |
| 6,000 字 | 前 4,000 字 | 3、3 | 完整 | 5、5 | 18,030 |
| 9,000 字 | 前 4,000 字 | 2、0¹ | 完整 | 5、5 | 15,030 |
| 12,000 字 | 前 4,000 字 | 2、2 | 完整 | 5、5 | 12,030 |
| 9,000 个汉字 | 前 4,000 字 | 2、2 | 完整 | 5、5 | 15,030 |
| 18,000 字（超出额度） | 前 4,000 字 | 1¹ | 请求完全相同 | 1 | 20,000 |
| 6,000 字，用普通 `-p` 发送（无标记） | 前 4,000 字 | 3 | 请求完全相同 | 3 | 20,000 |

两个数字表示跑了两次；同一请求和它的重复运行逐字节相同。每次压缩都是一个请求、返回 200、结束原因为 `stop`，没有被拒绝，也没有重试。`max_tokens` 正好减少了保留的字数；保留的文字实际每字约耗 0.2 个提示 token（英文）和 0.58 个（中文）。没有任何请求带有标记，回忆中也没有出现未进入压缩请求的编号。总花费约 0.30 美元。

¹ 存下来的摘要被现有的"去掉摘要中分析块"的步骤截短了：模型在摘要里引用了压缩指令，这段引用被当成了未闭合的块。两边运行的是同一段代码。

回忆问题在 262,144 窗口下运行，是因为在 32,768 窗口下两边都以 `max_tokens: 1` 发出了它。这看起来是压缩后估算的问题（#15486），这里没有追查。

单元测试覆盖：

- 标记本身：它的结构；它不会出现在原生、OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic 和 Responses 各条通道的请求里；它在会话文件中保留下来；以及恢复会话时丢弃已完成本地命令输入的那两处检查；
- 每个打标记的地方及每种排除情况：没有用户输入、内部发送、Mod 的提示和旁路查询；ACP 的仅供模型的提示、运行时目标续跑和只有附件的提示；托管模式下不是新输入、被改写或扩展、或拼接了记忆的提示；以及前端已经打过标记的请求，比如 ACP 在共享 agent 循环上发出的请求；
- 保留：记录的 IDE 前缀被截断并补闭合；以提醒块开头的提示在有、无这段前缀时都整段保留；和文字对不上的前缀；用户自己输入的孤立开始标签；以及上限截断落在块内部的情况；
- 重试：被移走的条目标记了相同文字时打标记，否则保持原样；
- 额度：正好少掉保留的字数；正好在普通额度的一半时使用保留版，多一个字就不用；摘要会低于最低空间时、重试时、以及请求体过大路径上都用普通截法；只比保留版少几个字的重试；没有用量、也没有 snapshot 的保留版回复之后改发一次普通截法，而只给出总数和输入数、带有完整 snapshot、或只有分析内容的回复只发一次；以及一组覆盖不同会话形态、长度和文字的测试，凡是普通版被接受的地方，保留版也被接受。

在 `fff3048c30` 上：core 的 services、core、utils 三个目录 共运行 16,928 条测试，16,895 条通过、33 条跳过，没有失败。ACP 集成、托管模式和提示账本的测试 全部通过，共 3,683 条。core 和 CLI 类型检查无错误。变基之前，20 个保护条件逐一改回后都让对应测试变红；评审中新增的检查也是如此：已有标记时跳过、重试时比较字符数，以及改发普通截法。

在 `3d0b69a7b2` 上：core 的 typed-prompt、partUtils、compactionInputSlimming、chatCompressionService、client、llm-content-generator、session-api-history 和 environmentContext 测试全部通过，共 1,487 条。CLI 的 ACP 集成、托管模式、提示账本和 `use-llm-stream` 测试通过 4,328 条，跳过 5 条。core 和 CLI 类型检查无错误。第三轮新增的 18 个检查（记录的前缀、共用的截断选项、退路的三个条件、重试的标记）逐一改坏后，都让对应测试变红。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

单元测试；请求级对比使用本地模拟服务；端到端测试使用 OpenRouter `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：保留的文字从摘要的输出额度中扣除，最多扣一半，所以如果摘要比剩下的额度长、而普通请求本可以容纳它，这份摘要会被判为截断而丢弃。保留按请求整体全有或全无：用户输入的文字超过约 14,000 字（窗口紧时更少，并且按所有消息合计）时，请求就是普通截法。密度超过每字一个 token 的文字（比如生僻汉字或表情符号）可能导致服务器拒绝保留版，此时重试发送普通截法。有标记的片段在记录的前缀之后的文字都按用户输入保留，在 CLI 中这包括粘贴内容外面的说明文字、被 `UserPromptSubmit` 钩子改写过的提示，以及交互模式 CLI 在打标记之前拼进提示的 worktree 通知和工作流规模提示（各只有几行）。请求在条目进入历史之前就失败时，它的重试不带标记。core 标记的是第一个文字片段，所以如果调用方传了用户输入标志、却把别的片段放在前面且自己不打标记，被标记的就是那个片段：无界面模式在带有"启动于 worktree"或"恢复后台 agent"提醒的第一轮就会这样，被标记的是提醒，用户的文字照旧截断。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：保留文字是否能提升任务完成效果；给普通的 `-p` 提示、斜杠命令展开、对话中插入的消息和托管模式排队输入打标记；在额度内尽量多保留长消息，以及保留它的结尾；压缩旧轮次（#14953 计划的第 3 部分）；在 ACP 和托管模式的轮次记录中保存标记；ACP 沙箱/SSH 打标记分支的测试，以及最低输出空间的测试。端到端测试使用的是 stream-json 输入；交互界面、OpenTUI 和 ACP 前端只由单元测试覆盖。Windows 和 Linux 仅由 CI 覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。这次改动之前录制的会话没有标记，照旧截断；标记不会发给服务商。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/yanyukang2003-ux/qwen-code/blob/fix/9455-keep-typed-text/docs/design/2026-11-17-keep-typed-text-in-reduced-compaction.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/yanyukang2003-ux/qwen-code/blob/fix/9455-keep-typed-text/docs/design/2026-11-17-keep-typed-text-in-reduced-compaction.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

属于 #9455 的一部分，接在 #15936 之后。#14953 第 4 轮的评审意见在下面的评论里逐条回复。

prs.title: fix(core): skip incomplete worktree snapshot pairs in unkeyed recovery
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Skip a snapshot candidate when a member is missing during the unkeyed search used by historical worktree recovery. A restore with an explicit archive key still selects only the requested pair. Complete candidates still undergo the existing file, metadata, and ownership checks.

## Why it's needed

An older session can lose its retained-worktree binding after the checkout has been removed. If an interrupted snapshot write leaves a tar-only or JSON-only remnant, the fallback search aborts before reaching the intact snapshot. This hides recovery in the session list and prevents restoration even when the user's files still exist in a complete archive.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Prepare a historical worktree session whose recorded workspace resolves to the registered repository. Use a checkout with modified tracked content and an untracked file. Capture a complete snapshot, remove the checkout, and reproduce the sidecar state with no recorded archive key.
2. Add an earlier incomplete snapshot candidate with the same session prefix. In Web Shell Session Overview, select Restore snapshot for the session. Confirm that the original commit, modified tracked file, untracked file, and ownership marker are restored.
3. Restore a session with a complete, explicit archive key and an unrelated incomplete pair beside it. The explicitly selected archive should still restore. Check both incomplete-member directions with the Core suite and the real Git restore regression.

### Evidence (Before & After)

In the historical fixture, the parent listed the session without a Restore snapshot action. A direct request to its registered workspace returned HTTP 500 with ENOENT for the incomplete pair. With the candidate, clicking Restore snapshot in Chromium returned HTTP 200 and restored the original commit, modified tracked file, untracked file, and ownership marker. A direct restore request for the explicitly keyed control returned 200 on both revisions. Core checks cover both tar-only and JSON-only remnants.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Local Node.js 22.22.3 |
| Linux | Candidate pending hosted CI |
| Windows | Candidate pending hosted CI |

### Environment

An isolated temporary Git repository and a loopback Serve daemon for the Chromium check. Local preflight exited 1. With the complete CLI supplement, 31 workspaces reported 134,325 passed, 24 failed and 235 skipped. The standalone Node and Bun checks passed. The script unit suite reported one failure in the workflow size assertion, which also reproduced on the parent and passed separately when given the exact base SHA. Across the original runs and supplements, 26 failure identities were retested against the exact parent. Fourteen reproduced with matching failure signatures, nine passed on both sides, and three failed only in the parent retest. Build, typecheck, lint, and the Serve startup bundle check passed.

## Risk & Scope

- Missing members are skipped during unkeyed selection. Explicit keys never fall back to another archive.
- The optional retention pin-store optimization is outside this change. The normal archive flow can preserve a transcript cwd under the removed checkout. Web Shell reports HTTP 404 when it routes the restore through that cwd. The exact parent and candidate both reproduce this through the supported archive flow. That workspace-routing defect is a separate follow-up.
- The existing archive format and restore commands apply.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18446

prs.title: feat(review): tiered sandbox cutover, CLI capability gate, and external content-allowlist downgrade
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR completes Phase 2-A of the tiered review sandbox rollout by switching the automated pull request review workflow from single-tier container enforcement with an unsandboxed fallback to unconditional tiered fail-closed isolation.

- The sandbox preflight step now separates container readiness from the policy handed to the review runner and always emits the tiered policy instead of falling back to unsandboxed execution on hosted fork pull requests or same-repository pull requests.
- When either the container daemon or the digest-pinned sandbox image is unavailable, the preflight emits a step output that forces hardware isolation on the review execution step. Because the flag is bound through expression-context step outputs rather than mutable environment files, later steps cannot clear it, and the review runner never falls back to an unpinned default image tag or blames an image-pull outage on the pull request under review.
- Fork heads (and unreadable heads on payload-less triggers) on the persistent self-hosted runner pool continue to fail closed with a non-zero exit before emitting outputs or starting the review agent, protecting both CI credentials and the shared host.
- The workflow test suite is updated to verify the new step-output wiring, assert that no unsandboxed fallback remains, and replay the preflight shell logic directly across ready, missing-daemon, failed-image, self-hosted fork refusal, and payload-less lookup scenarios. Both the English and Chinese design documents are updated in sync to record Phase 2-A completion and the remaining follow-up scope: [English design](docs/design/2026-11-24-review-tiered-sandbox.md) | [简体中文设计](docs/design/2026-11-24-review-tiered-sandbox.zh-CN.md).

## Why it's needed

Phases 1 (#18226) and 2-B (#18280) landed trust classification, mandatory high-risk path escalation, hardened containers, host-tmux bypass refusal, and the local microVM execution bridge in the review runner, but the CI review workflow still passed the single-tier container policy when Docker and the sandbox image were ready and fell back to unsandboxed execution when they were not. Under that setup, external fork pull requests and high-risk manifest or workflow changes ran inside shared-kernel containers rather than escalating to hardware isolation, and hosted fork pull requests whose container preflight failed ran install and build scripts directly in the review step's environment alongside CI credentials. Switching CI unconditionally to tiered mode with hardware-isolation handoff on container outages closes both downgrade paths while letting reviews degrade cleanly to static inspection when no hardware backend is attached.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Confirm that when both the container daemon and digest-pinned image resolution succeed, the sandbox preflight emits the tiered policy, marks container readiness true, leaves the force-hardware output empty, and exports a digest-pinned image reference; trusted same-repository low-risk pull requests execute in the hardened container while external fork pull requests and high-risk paths escalate to hardware isolation (or fail closed cleanly to static review without downgrading to a shared-kernel container).
2. Confirm that when the container daemon is unreachable on a hosted runner reviewing a fork pull request, the preflight still emits the tiered policy with the force-hardware output enabled rather than falling back to unsandboxed execution, and host-only interactive probe subcommands refuse cleanly.
3. Confirm that when the container daemon answers but image resolution fails on a same-repository pull request, the preflight emits the tiered policy with the force-hardware output enabled so the review runner refuses execution cleanly at the phase boundary without invoking a container against an unpinned default image tag.
4. Confirm that on a self-hosted runner, a fork pull request or an unreadable head on a payload-less trigger exits non-zero with an error annotation before writing any step outputs whenever container readiness fails, while a payload-less same-repository head resolved through the read-only token succeeds with tiered plus force-hardware enabled.
5. Confirm workflow syntax, shell static analysis, formatting, linting, and all workflow meta-tests pass without warnings or regressions.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (CI workflow, workflow meta-tests, and design documentation only).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### Environment (optional)

Verified locally on macOS with workflow expression and shell static analysis, formatting and lint checks, full workflow meta-test replay suites, review sandbox unit suites, and end-to-end replay feeding real preflight outputs directly into the compiled CLI review subcommands.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: When Docker or the GHCR sandbox image is temporarily unavailable on the review runner pool, same-repository pull requests will no longer fall back to unsandboxed execution and will instead degrade to read-only static review until container readiness recovers or a microVM bridge is configured.
- Not validated / out of scope: Provisioning production microVM runners or cloud provider-VM HTTP/SDK data planes (tracked as follow-up work in the design doc); running live GitHub Actions jobs on the self-hosted review pool.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: CI reviews never fall back to unsandboxed execution; external fork pull requests and high-risk changes now require a hardware-isolated backend to run repository code and otherwise disclose refusal cleanly in their execution boundary report.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #18226 and #18280.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本次 PR 做了什么

本 PR 完成了分层评审沙箱落地的 Phase 2-A：将自动化 PR 评审工作流从“单层容器策略 + 无沙箱降级”切换为无条件的分层 fail-closed 隔离策略。

- 沙箱预检步骤现已将容器就绪态与传递给评审执行器的策略解耦，始终输出分层策略，彻底移除托管 runner 上外部 fork PR 及同仓 PR 回退到无沙箱执行的降级路径。
- 当容器守护进程不可达或 digest 固定的沙箱镜像解析失败时，预检通过步骤输出下发强制硬件隔离标记。由于该标记通过表达式上下文步骤输出绑定而非可变环境文件传递，后续步骤无法清空它，评审执行器也不会在镜像拉取失败时回退到未固定摘要的默认镜像标签，或将镜像故障误归因于待审 PR。
- 在持久自托管 runner 池上，只要容器未就绪，fork PR（以及无载荷触发器中无法读出源仓库的 PR）仍会在写入任何步骤输出和启动评审代理前直接以非零状态拒绝退出，同时保护 CI 凭据与共享宿主机。
- 同步更新了工作流元测试套件，校验新的步骤输出绑定、确认不再存在无沙箱降级，并通过真实 shell 直接回放容器就绪、守护进程不可用、镜像拉取失败、自托管 fork 拒绝与无载荷查库等全场景；同时同步更新了中英文设计文档以记录 Phase 2-A 落地及剩余后续计划：[English design](docs/design/2026-11-24-review-tiered-sandbox.md) | [简体中文设计](docs/design/2026-11-24-review-tiered-sandbox.zh-CN.md)。

## 为什么需要这个改动

Phase 1（#18226）与 Phase 2-B（#18280）已在评审执行器中落地了信任分级、高风险路径强制升级、容器硬化、宿主机终端旁路封堵与本地微虚机执行桥接，但 CI 评审工作流在 Docker 和镜像就绪时仍只传入单层容器策略，而在不可用时回退到无沙箱执行。这导致外部 fork PR 和修改高风险清单或工作流的 PR 仍在共享内核容器中运行，且托管 runner 上容器预检失败的 fork PR 会直接在携带 CI 凭据的环境中执行安装与构建脚本。将 CI 无条件切到分层模式并在容器不可用时联动强制硬件隔离，彻底关闭了上述两条降级路径，并在未接入硬件后端时平滑退化为静态审查。

## 评审验证计划

### 验证步骤

1. 确认当容器守护进程与摘要固定镜像均解析成功时，预检输出分层策略、容器就绪标记为真、强制硬件隔离为空并导出摘要固定镜像；受信同仓低风险 PR 在硬化容器内执行，外部 fork PR 与高风险路径升级至硬件隔离（无可用硬件后端时干净拒绝并退化为静态审查，绝不降级到共享内核容器）。
2. 确认托管 runner 评审 fork PR 时若容器守护进程不可达，预检仍输出分层策略并开启强制硬件隔离，绝不回退到无沙箱执行，且宿主机交互探针子命令干净拒绝。
3. 确认同仓 PR 在容器守护进程正常但镜像拉取失败时，预检输出分层策略并开启强制硬件隔离，评审执行器在阶段入口干净拒绝而不会使用未固定摘要的默认镜像拉起容器。
4. 确认自托管 runner 在容器未就绪时，fork PR 或无载荷触发器下无法解析源仓库的 PR 会在写出步骤输出前报错并退出 1；而通过只读令牌解析为同仓 PR 时正常输出分层策略与强制硬件隔离。
5. 确认工作流语法、shell 静态分析、格式化、代码检查与全部工作流元测试通过且无回归。

### 证据（改前与改后）

N/A（仅涉及 CI 工作流、工作流元测试与设计文档）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ |

### 运行环境（可选）

已在 macOS 本地完成工作流表达式与 shell 静态检查、格式化与 lint 校验、完整工作流元测试回放、评审沙箱单元测试，以及将预检真实输出直接馈入编译后 CLI 评审子命令的端到端联动验证。

## 风险与影响范围

- 主要风险或权衡：当评审 runner 池上的 Docker 或 GHCR 镜像临时不可用时，同仓 PR 不再回退到无沙箱执行，而是退化为只读静态评审，直到容器恢复或配置微虚机桥接。
- 未验证或不在范围内：生产微虚机 runner 部署与云端 provider-VM 的 HTTP/SDK 数据面（留作设计文档中的后续工作）；未在生产自托管评审池上运行线上 GitHub Actions 任务。
- 破坏性变更与迁移说明：CI 评审不再回退无沙箱执行；外部 fork PR 与高风险变更在未接入硬件隔离后端时不再执行仓库代码，并在执行边界报告中如实披露拒绝原因。

## 关联 Issue

延续 #18226 与 #18280 的后续工作。

prs.title: feat(core): fix Gemini/Vertex long-stream transport and support native multimodal tool outputs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR improves the Google GenAI / Vertex AI (`gemini`) transport and native multimodal tool-response handling in `@qwen-code/qwen-code-core`.

On the transport layer, it routes all Gemini and Vertex HTTP requests through Qwen Code's bundled `undici` dispatcher (with `headersTimeout: 0` and `bodyTimeout: 0`) so long-running reasoning and multimodal turns are not prematurely aborted by Node.js 22+'s default 300-second headers timeout. It adds connect-phase timeout handling with a retryable timeout error, reuses the shared stream idle and max-lifetime guards with socket-closing abort cleanup, honors opt-in SDK retry options with `Retry-After` and jittered backoff outside single-attempt mode, avoids abort-listener accumulation on shared turn signals via `AbortSignal.any()`, normalizes trailing `/v1beta` segments across both explicit and environment-provided base URLs, and fixes `DOMException` brand preservation and fallback-clone credential redaction in proxy error handling.

On the multimodal layer, it retains tool-returned audio and video natively inside `functionResponse.parts` for Gemini 3+ models while automatically promoting audio and video tool outputs to a follow-up `user` turn for Gemini 2.5 and earlier models. It also enforces presence-as-true `InputModalities` gating across user turns and tool responses, introduces shared prototype-safe media MIME normalization helpers, splits trailing reattach-boundary bundles with `role: 'user'`, and removes strictly unsigned empty-text parts without discarding signed thinking parts.

## Why it's needed

Long reasoning or multimodal Gemini / Vertex turns on Node.js 22+ currently fail after ~300 seconds because `@google/genai`'s internal global-dispatcher reflection does not lift Node 22+'s built-in undici `headersTimeout`, and Gemini streaming previously lacked the shared idle/max-lifetime stream guards used by OpenAI and Anthropic paths. In addition, tool-returned audio and video parts were previously converted to text placeholders instead of being delivered natively to Gemini 3+ models (or promoted safely for Gemini 2.5 models), breaking multimodal tool workflows such as inspecting audio and video files.

Because the transport fixes and multimodal tool-output support both touch the Gemini content generator and are designed to land together as a single cohesive Gemini compatibility upgrade (more than half of the diff consists of unit and real-HTTP transport/compatibility regression tests), they are grouped into this self-contained PR.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run TypeScript typechecking for `@qwen-code/qwen-code-core`:

```bash
npx tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

2. Run the Gemini transport, compatibility, proxy-redaction, and media-MIME unit/integration test suites:

```bash
npx vitest run \
  packages/core/src/utils/media-mime.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/utils/runtimeFetchOptions.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/index.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.transport.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.compat.test.ts
```

3. Verify lint and formatting checks pass cleanly (`npm run lint` / `prettier --check`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-facing TUI/UI change. All 6 core test suites passed locally (`206 / 206` tests passed, `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` clean), including real-HTTP compatibility tests covering connect timeout, idle stream timeout, proxy credential redaction on `DOMException`, and `>300s` header-wait survival on Node.js 22.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 22.x local unit and real-HTTP loopback tests (`vitest`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `prettier`).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `@google/genai` does not expose a public fetch hook, so the bundled `undici` dispatcher continues to hook `apiClient.apiCall` (extending the existing isolated-transport wrapper). Connect timeout bounds only header arrival and clears before streaming begins so healthy long streams are governed solely by `stream-guards`.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux native CI runs (will be covered by GitHub Actions CI on this PR); OpenAI Responses / Chat Completions multimodal changes are kept separate in the companion PR (`feat/openai-responses-multimodal-and-chat-audio`), which shares the exact byte-for-byte identical `packages/core/src/utils/media-mime.ts` and `media-mime.test.ts` files so either PR can merge first cleanly without conflict.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Gemini 2.5 and earlier models automatically receive follow-up `user` turns for tool-returned audio/video to remain backwards-compatible, and `docs/users/configuration/settings.md` is updated to reflect Gemini timeout behavior.

## Linked Issues

N/A (independent companion to the OpenAI Responses multimodal & Chat Completions audio PR).

本 PR 改进了 `@qwen-code/qwen-code-core` 中 Google GenAI / Vertex AI（`gemini`）的传输层稳定性与原生多模态工具结果处理能力。

在传输层方面，本 PR 将所有 Gemini 与 Vertex HTTP 请求统一路由至 Qwen Code 内置的 `undici` dispatcher（`headersTimeout: 0`、`bodyTimeout: 0`），避免长耗时推理或多模态回合在 Node.js 22+ 下被默认 300 秒响应头超时提前中断；新增可重试的连接阶段超时保护，复用公共的流式空闲与最大生命周期守护并在提前结束流时关闭底层连接，在非单次尝试模式下遵循显式配置的 SDK 重试参数（支持 `Retry-After` 与抖动退避），通过 `AbortSignal.any()` 消除共享回合信号上的监听器泄漏，对显式配置与环境变量来源的 base URL 统一归一化结尾 `/v1beta` 路径段，并修复代理错误脱敏时 `DOMException` 品牌保留与退回克隆场景下的凭据脱敏问题。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 运行 `@qwen-code/qwen-code-core` 的 TypeScript 类型检查：

```bash

```

2. 运行 Gemini 传输层、兼容性、代理脱敏与媒体 MIME 相关的单测与集成测试套件：

```bash
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/index.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.transport.test.ts \
  packages/core/src/core/llm-content-generator/llm-content-generator.compat.test.ts
```

3. 确认代码规范与格式检查全部通过（`npm run lint` / `prettier --check`）。

### 验证证据（改动前后）

N/A — 无用户可见 TUI/UI 变更。本地 6 个核心测试套件全部通过（`206 / 206` 用例通过，`tsc --noEmit` 0 错误，`eslint --max-warnings 0` 与 `prettier --check` 全部通过），包含覆盖连接超时、流式空闲超时、`DOMException` 代理凭据脱敏以及 Node.js 22 下超过 300 秒响应头等待的真实 HTTP 回归测试。

### 测试平台

| :--------: | :----: |

| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |

### 测试环境（可选）

Node.js 22.x 本地单元测试与真实 HTTP 回环测试（`vitest`、`tsc`、`eslint`、`prettier`）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与权衡：由于 `@google/genai` 未提供公开的 fetch 钩子，内置 `undici` dispatcher 延续并扩展了现有的 `apiClient.apiCall` 隔离传输包装；连接超时仅约束响应头到达并在收到响应头后立即清除，确保健康长流完全由 `stream-guards` 管理。

prs.title: fix(desktop): fail the AppImage smoke check when a host library is bundled
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The release smoke check for the Linux AppImage now fails when the extracted image ships its own copy of a library that must come from the host. Previously it only rejected a dynamic dependency that was neither bundled nor on the host baseline list, so an image carrying a host library passed silently. The AppImage closure test grows a case for the bundled `libwayland-client.so.0`, and the desktop README explains both directions of the check.

## Why it's needed

The AppImage's bundle directory leads `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so any host-baseline library inside the image shadows the host's newer copy instead of falling back to it. On Fedora 43+/Bluefin an AppImage-built `libwayland-client.so.0` lacks `wl_fixes_interface`, so the host's `libEGL_mesa.so.0` cannot be dlopened (`undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface`), no EGL vendor is available, and the Desktop window stays a gray rectangle (#18486). The CI build root is Ubuntu 22.04, whose Mesa does not reference that symbol, so the same shadowing never shows up there and the current gate cannot catch it from runtime behaviour. Rejecting the package state itself turns the failure into a build-time error that describes the fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js` — passes.
2. Confirm the new assertion is discriminating: restore the pre-PR `packages/desktop/scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js` (only that file) and rerun; the test fails with `expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/`, then passes again with the PR version.
3. The same fixture technique as before: a fake extracted root plus a fake `readelf` on `PATH`, so no real AppImage or Linux host is needed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

```
# pre-PR verifyAppImageClosure + PR test
control exit=1
  expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/,

# PR verifyAppImageClosure + PR test
restored exit=0
Desktop release helper checks passed.
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Plain `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js` on macOS (Node v22.23.4), no install required.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a legitimate application library that happens to share a soname with a host baseline entry would now block the release instead of shipping. The alternative — silently shadowing the host's copy — is the bug being fixed.
- Expected release effect: **the next `Desktop Release` dispatch (and the daily `Desktop Checks` dry run) fails at `Verify Linux installer runtimes` before publishing.** The released `Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.28.4_amd64.AppImage` already carries `usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0` and the three wayland siblings, and this PR does not change packaging (`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` sets only `bundle.linux.appimage.bundleMediaFramework`; there is no `--exclude-library`, linuxdeploy hook or `usr/lib` prune), so the rebuilt image trips the new rule. `publish` needs `build`, so that dispatch publishes nothing on any platform. This is deliberate: the image it would publish is the shadowed one from #18486, so failing is better than shipping it. It stays red until a separate PR excludes the wayland family at packaging time.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real EGL/Mesa failure was not reproduced; that needs a Linux host with current Mesa and a built AppImage. Removing the libraries at packaging time is that separate PR, because the bundler exclusion is not reachable from the Tauri config and cannot be validated on macOS — its acceptance is `npm run smoke:linux-installers` green on a real built AppImage, which no unit fixture can show (also worth checking the `wl_fixes_interface` case the reporter hit).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.
- UI verification: N/A — the change is to a build-time verification script and its README; the user-visible behavior it protects (the AppImage rendering instead of a gray window) is not reachable from any local CLI/TUI/Web surface on this host.

## Linked Issues

Refs #18486 — this PR does not resolve it: the image users install today is unchanged until the packaging change lands.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Linux AppImage 的发布冒烟检查现在会在解包后的镜像自带某个本应由宿主提供的库时失败。此前该检查只拒绝“既不在镜像内、也不在宿主基线名单上”的动态依赖，因此镜像里打包了宿主库反而能静默通过。AppImage closure 测试新增了打包 `libwayland-client.so.0` 的用例，desktop README 也补充了该检查的两个方向。

## 为什么需要

AppImage 的 bundle 目录排在 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 最前，因此镜像内任何宿主基线库都会遮蔽宿主更新的副本，而不是回退到宿主库。在 Fedora 43+/Bluefin 上，用 AppImage 构建的 `libwayland-client.so.0` 缺少 `wl_fixes_interface`，导致宿主的 `libEGL_mesa.so.0` 无法被 dlopen（`undefined symbol: wl_fixes_interface`），没有可用的 EGL vendor，Desktop 窗口只剩一块灰矩形（#18486）。CI 构建环境是 Ubuntu 22.04，其 Mesa 不引用该符号，所以同样的遮蔽在 CI 上永远不会暴露，现有门禁也无法从运行时行为发现它。直接拒绝这种打包状态，可以把故障变成一个说明修复方向的构建期错误。

## 审阅验证步骤

1. 执行 `cd packages/desktop && node scripts/test-release.js`，应通过。
2. 确认新断言确实有区分度：仅把 `packages/desktop/scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js` 还原为 PR 之前的版本并重跑，测试会以 `expected: /AppImage must not bundle host-baseline libraries: usr\/lib\/libwayland-client\.so\.0/` 失败；换回 PR 版本后再次通过。
3. 沿用原有夹具手法：伪造的解包根目录加上 `PATH` 里的假 `readelf`，无需真实 AppImage 或 Linux 主机。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：若某个应用库恰好与宿主基线名单中的 soname 同名，现在会阻止发布而不是继续发货。另一种选择——静默遮蔽宿主副本——正是本 issue 的缺陷。
- 预期的发布影响：**下一次 `Desktop Release` 派发（以及每日 `Desktop Checks` 试跑）将在 `Verify Linux installer runtimes` 处失败，不会发布。** 已发布的 `Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.28.4_amd64.AppImage` 自带 `usr/lib/libwayland-client.so.0` 及三个 wayland 兄弟库，而本 PR 不改打包（`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` 只设 `bundle.linux.appimage.bundleMediaFramework`，没有 `--exclude-library`、linuxdeploy 钩子或 `usr/lib` 清理），因此重新构建的镜像会触发新规则。`publish` 的 `needs` 含 `build`，所以那次派发在所有平台上都不会发布任何东西。这是有意为之：否则发出去的就是 #18486 里那个被遮蔽的镜像，失败好过发货。在另一个 PR 于打包阶段排除 wayland 家族之前，它会一直保持红色。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：未复现真实的 EGL/Mesa 故障，那需要装有当前 Mesa 的 Linux 主机以及构建好的 AppImage。在打包阶段移除这些库属于那个单独的 PR：打包排除无法通过 Tauri 配置触达，也无法在 macOS 上验证——它的验收标准是在真实构建的 AppImage 上 `npm run smoke:linux-installers` 为绿色，这是单元夹具证明不了的（也可顺带确认报告人遇到的 `wl_fixes_interface` 情况）。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。
- UI 验证：N/A —— 改动对象是构建期校验脚本及其 README；它所保护的可见行为（AppImage 正常渲染而非灰窗口）在本机无法通过任何 CLI/TUI/Web 入口触达。

</details>

prs.title: test(acp-bridge): pin a granted conditional close actually tearing the session down
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds two bridge tests that pin the granted half of the conditional close. The explicit-path case spawns a session on a child that negotiated active work and answers a `sessionClose` probe for `onlyIfUnheld` with `{closed: true, holds: []}`, calls `closeSession(id, undefined, {closeIfUnheld: true, reason: 'scheduled_task_deleted'})`, and asserts three outcomes: `sessionCount === 0`, exactly one `closeIfUnheld` probe was sent, and the emitted `session_closed` event carries `reason: 'scheduled_task_deleted'`.

On the explicit path the reason is pinned as a literal rather than read back from the caller's `closeOpts`. `closeSessionImpl` re-emits `closeOpts.reason ?? 'client_close'`, so a read-back would let both sides move together and would stay green if the hand-off were dropped.

That explicit path cannot witness the `reason: opts.closeReason` hand-off in `closeIfChildUnheld`, because the spread of `closeOpts` already carries the same literal. The second test, `emits the detach reason when a detached session closes unheld`, closes a detached session with no `closeOpts`, so the hand-off is the only source of the reason and dropping it turns that case red.

There are no production code changes.

## Why it's needed

Issue #14389 Item 1 records that the conditional close added in #14276 has no coverage for the outcome it exists to serve. All five sites that assert on `closeIfUnheld` either exercise a refusal or check the option bag against a stub that closes unconditionally, so a granted close that silently failed to tear anything down would stay green.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the bridge suite and confirm both new cases pass:

```
cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/bridge.test.ts
```

Then confirm each test bites. Replacing `reason: opts.closeReason` with `reason: 'client_close'` in the `closeIfUnheld` branch makes the detach case fail with `expected 'client_close' to be 'last_client_detached'`; it was reverted before commit. Invert the assertion on `sessionCount` in the explicit-path case instead and that one fails there too.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this is a test-only change; the observable behaviour of the bridge is unchanged.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS host, `npx vitest` against the checked-out tree. No sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the test asserts on probe counts and the emitted event payload, so a future change to the probe protocol will need this case updated alongside `bridge.test.ts`'s existing close cases.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full monorepo build, repo-wide lint, and the full test suite were not run. Only `packages/acp-bridge` was exercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

References #14389, Item 1 only. The issue tracks six items and Items 2–6 are untouched, so it must stay open — this PR does not close it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增两条 bridge 测试，把条件关闭「被批准」的那一半钉住。显式路径那条测试在一个已经协商了活跃工作、并对 `onlyIfUnheld` 的 `sessionClose` 探测返回 `{closed: true, holds: []}` 的子会话上建立会话，调用 `closeSession(id, undefined, {closeIfUnheld: true, reason: 'scheduled_task_deleted'})`，然后断言三件事：`sessionCount === 0`、只发送了一次 `closeIfUnheld` 探测、发出的 `session_closed` 事件带有 `reason: 'scheduled_task_deleted'`。

在显式路径上，原因值写死为字面量，而不是从调用方的 `closeOpts` 读回。`closeSessionImpl` 会重新发出 `closeOpts.reason ?? 'client_close'`，所以读回会让两边一起移动，即使交接被丢掉测试也仍然是绿的。

但显式路径无法见证 `closeIfChildUnheld` 里 `reason: opts.closeReason` 这次交接——`closeOpts` 的展开本身就已经带着同一个字面量。所以有第二条测试 `emits the detach reason when a detached session closes unheld`：它在没有 `closeOpts` 的情况下关闭一个已分离的会话，此时交接是原因值的唯一来源，丢掉它这条用例就会红。

没有生产代码改动。

## 为什么需要它

Issue #14389 的 Item 1 指出：#14276 引入的条件关闭对「它本来要服务的那个结果」没有任何覆盖。所有五处断言 `closeIfUnheld` 的地方，要么走的是拒绝路径，要么是把选项包和一个无条件关闭的 stub 对比，所以一次被批准、但实际上什么都没拆掉的关闭会一直保持绿色。

## 审阅者验证步骤

### 如何验证

先跑 bridge 套件确认两条新增用例都通过：

```
cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/bridge.test.ts
```

再确认每条测试真的会失败：把 `closeIfUnheld` 分支里的 `reason: opts.closeReason` 改成 `reason: 'client_close'`，分离用例会以 `expected 'client_close' to be 'last_client_detached'` 失败；改动已在提交前还原。反过来把显式路径用例里 `sessionCount` 的断言改掉，也会在那一处失败。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 这是纯测试改动，bridge 的可观察行为没有变化。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

本地 macOS 环境，在检出目录上用 `npx vitest` 运行，未使用沙箱。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：测试断言的是探测次数和发出的事件负载，将来改探测协议时需要连同 `bridge.test.ts` 里已有的关闭用例一起更新。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：没有跑完整 monorepo 构建、全仓 lint 和完整测试套件，只跑了 `packages/acp-bridge`。
- 破坏性改动 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

仅引用 #14389 的 Item 1。该 issue 登记了六条内容，Items 2–6 未处理，因此必须保持打开 —— 本 PR 不关闭它。

</details>

prs.title: fix(serve): fail closed on unreadable worktree sidecars during session deletion
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR aligns session deletion with the existing worktree sidecar safety predicate so that dangling symlinks, symlink loops, and unreadable sidecar parent directories are never mistaken for missing sidecars during deletion. Both the archive and delete fast paths now share a single synchronous non-following absence check where only a genuine missing entry skips strict classification, while preserving the synchronous batch-coordinator prefix for sessions without worktree sidecars.

In addition, post-deletion worktree sidecar cleanup now inspects the entry without following symlinks before unlinking it, while continuing to tolerate unreadable or non-directory archive parent paths and treating an unlink failure (such as a searchable but non-writable archive directory) as a warned, non-fatal step so cleanup of the remaining session sidecars is never interrupted after the transcript has been removed.

## Why it's needed

When a session's worktree sidecar was a dangling symlink or a symlink loop, deleting the session previously bypassed strict worktree classification entirely: the transcript was removed with an empty error list and no preservation warning, while the managed checkout remained on disk. Worse, the broken symlink itself also survived cleanup in the chats directory, which caused subsequent deletions of unrelated healthy worktree sessions in the same workspace to fail cleanup with an unreadable-sibling-sidecar warning and orphan their checkouts as well.

Consistent with the established session-deletion contract (which preserves an unverified checkout with an explicit warning rather than trapping the user with an undeletable session), deletion now enters the strict path, preserves the checkout, emits the preservation warning, and removes the broken sidecar link along with the session record so sibling worktree cleanups remain unaffected.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Create an isolated git workspace and start the daemon against it, then create a session owning a managed worktree with uncommitted work and replace its worktree sidecar (either active or archived, or as a self-referencing symlink loop) with a dangling symlink pointing to a missing target.
2. Delete the session via the daemon session-delete endpoint: confirm the request succeeds without blocking record deletion, the transcript and broken sidecar link are removed, the managed worktree directory, uncommitted file, and branch remain intact, and daemon stderr emits a checkout-preservation warning citing an unsafe sidecar file type.
3. Immediately delete a second healthy worktree session in the same workspace: confirm its transcript, sidecar, checkout directory, and git branch are all cleanly removed with no unreadable-sibling-sidecar warning.
4. Confirm a genuinely missing sidecar still takes the synchronous fast path without emitting warnings; an unreadable archived sidecar parent does not take the delete fast path, emits an access-denied preservation warning, and fails closed during transcript resolution (returning an access-denied error with the active transcript preserved); a non-directory or read-only searchable archive parent does not abort cleanup of the remaining active sidecars after transcript removal (warning if unlinking the worktree sidecar fails); and archiving a session with a dangling sidecar still fails closed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI daemon/session-maintenance change — N/A for screenshots.

Observed against the local bundled daemon on Linux (Node 26.12.1):

- **Before (`main` / installed v0.28.7):** deleting an active or archived session with a dangling or self-looping worktree sidecar returned HTTP 200 with no errors and no preservation warning, removed the transcript, left the broken symlink and managed worktree + branch on disk, and caused the immediately following deletion of a healthy worktree session in the same workspace to preserve and orphan its checkout due to `unreadable sibling sidecar`.
- **After (rebuilt bundle from this branch):** active, archived, cross-state, and symlink-loop cases all emit `qwen serve: worktree cleanup preserved checkout action=delete session="<id>" reason="unreadable sidecar (unsafe sidecar file type)"`, keep the checkout (including uncommitted work) and branch intact, and remove the broken symlink so the following healthy worktree deletion cleans its checkout and branch cleanly without warnings. Unreadable/non-directory archive parents emit the corresponding preservation warning on HTTP delete and do not interrupt sibling active sidecar cleanup.
- **Automated checks & mutation witnesses:** core session-service and permission-probe unit tests 301/301 passed (0 skipped); CLI session-archive unit tests 160/160 passed; full real-daemon HTTP route integration suite 45/45 passed and hosted-harness suite 11/11 passed; Prettier, ESLint, and core/CLI/integration TypeScript checks all passed. Eight independent mutation witnesses (reverting the delete fast path, treating non-missing stat errors as absent, reverting sidecar removal, dropping the stat error guard for non-directory parents, dropping the non-fatal unlink guard for read-only searchable archive directories, and both real-daemon bundle regressions for the HTTP delete case) were all killed and restored byte-identically.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Isolated Linux git workspace with local `node dist/cli.js serve`, isolated `HOME` / `QWEN_HOME` / `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`, and no model credentials.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Follows the repository's existing session-deletion contract (preserve the unverified checkout with a named warning and allow the user to delete the session record, matching corrupt regular-file sidecars) rather than refusing deletion outright, so a broken sidecar cannot lock a session permanently into the sidebar. Only the worktree sidecar deletion cleanup in core was changed (one guarded non-following existence check), leaving unrelated sidecar types untouched.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows runners will be validated by CI; the root-with-dropped-capabilities Linux permission lane relies on the repository's kernel permission probe (locally verified on non-root Linux where the probe is true and the case runs unskipped). The background retention sweeper's quietness when scanning unreadable sidecars is unrelated and left out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18475

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

本 PR 将会话删除路径与既有的 worktree sidecar 安全判定对齐，确保删除过程中悬空符号链接、符号链接环以及不可读的 sidecar 父目录不会被误判为 sidecar 缺失。归档与删除两条快路径现在共享同一个同步、不跟随符号链接的缺失判定——仅真正缺失时才跳过严格分类，同时为真正没有 worktree sidecar 的会话保留同步的批次 coordinator 前缀。

此外，删除会话后的 worktree sidecar 清理现在在移除前也改为不跟随符号链接地检查条目存在性，同时继续容忍归档父目录不可读或非目录等错误，并将 unlink 失败（例如可遍历但不可写的归档目录）降级为告警而非致命错误，确保在 transcript 删除后不会中断其余会话 sidecar 的清理。

## 为什么需要

当会话的 worktree sidecar 是悬空符号链接或符号链接环时，删除会话此前会直接绕过严格的 worktree 分类：transcript 被删除且错误列表为空、无任何保留告警，而托管 checkout 遗留在磁盘上。更糟的是，损坏的符号链接本身也残留在 chats 目录中，导致随后在同一工作区删除其他完全健康的 worktree 会话时触发不可读兄弟 sidecar 告警，进而连带孤立健康会话的 checkout。

与仓库既有的会话删除契约保持一致（对无法核验归属的 checkout 保守保留并发出明确告警，而不让损坏 sidecar 把会话锁死在侧边栏中删不掉），删除路径现在会进入严格流程、保留 checkout、发出保留告警，并将损坏的符号链接随会话记录一并清理，避免影响后续健康 worktree 会话的清理。

## 评审验证计划

### 验证步骤

1. 创建隔离的 git 工作区并启动本地 daemon，构造一个拥有托管 worktree 且含未提交改动的会话，将其 worktree sidecar（活跃或归档位置，或自引用符号链接环）替换为指向不存在目标的悬空符号链接。
2. 通过 daemon 的会话删除接口删除该会话：确认请求成功而不阻塞记录删除，transcript 与损坏的符号链接均被移除，托管 worktree 目录、未提交文件与分支均保持完好，且 daemon stderr 输出指出非常规 sidecar 文件类型的 checkout 保留告警。
3. 紧接着删除同一工作区中第二个健康的 worktree 会话：确认其 transcript、sidecar、checkout 目录与 git 分支均被干净删除，且不出现不可读兄弟 sidecar 告警。
4. 确认真正缺失 sidecar 的会话仍走同步快路径且无告警；归档 sidecar 父目录不可读时不走删除快路径、发出权限拒绝保留告警，并在 transcript 解析阶段 fail-closed（返回权限拒绝错误且保留活跃 transcript）；归档父目录为普通文件或只读可遍历目录时不中断 transcript 删除后的其余活跃 sidecar 清理（unlink 失败时记录告警）；带悬空 sidecar 的会话归档仍保持 fail-closed 拒绝。

### 验证证据（修改前后）

非 UI 的 daemon／会话维护改动，无截图（N/A）。

在 Linux（Node 26.12.1）使用本地打包的 daemon 实测：

- **修改前（`main`／本地 v0.28.7）：** 删除带有悬空或自环 worktree sidecar 的活跃或归档会话返回 HTTP 200、无错误、无保留告警，transcript 被删除，损坏符号链接与托管 worktree 及分支遗留在磁盘，且紧接着删除同工作区健康 worktree 会话时因 `unreadable sibling sidecar` 被迫保留并孤立其 checkout。
- **修改后（本分支重建的 bundle）：** 活跃、归档、跨状态及符号链接环场景均输出 `qwen serve: worktree cleanup preserved checkout action=delete session="<id>" reason="unreadable sidecar (unsafe sidecar file type)"`，完整保留 checkout（含未提交改动）与分支，并移除损坏符号链接，使后续同工作区健康 worktree 删除无告警且彻底清理。归档父目录不可读或非目录时，HTTP 删除输出对应保留告警且不中断兄弟活跃 sidecar 清理。
- **自动化检查与变异见证：** core 会话服务与权限探针单测 301/301 通过（0 skipped）；CLI 归档/删除单测 160/160 通过；完整真实 daemon HTTP 路由集成套件 45/45 通过、hosted-harness 套件 11/11 通过；Prettier、ESLint 与 core/CLI/integration 类型检查全部通过。八个独立变异见证（回退删除快路径、把非缺失 stat 错误当缺失、回退 sidecar 移除、去掉非目录父目录的 stat 错误保护、去掉只读可遍历归档目录的 unlink 非致命保护，以及真实 daemon bundle 上针对 HTTP 删除用例的两路回归）全部精准击杀并按字节还原。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测 |

### 运行环境（可选）

隔离 Linux git 工作区，运行本地 `node dist/cli.js serve`，隔离 `HOME` / `QWEN_HOME` / `QWEN_RUNTIME_DIR`，不涉及模型凭据。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：遵循仓库既有的会话删除契约（保留未核验的 checkout 并发出命名告警、允许用户删除会话记录，与损坏常规文件 sidecar 保持一致），而非直接拒绝删除，避免损坏 sidecar 把会话永久锁死在侧边栏。core 中仅改动 worktree sidecar 的删除存在性检查（一处带错误保护的不跟随检查），不触碰其它类型 sidecar。
