prs.title: fix(acp): surface failed todo_write calls instead of dropping them
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Failed `todo_write` calls are now reported to the ACP client as a terminal `tool_call_update` with `status: failed`, instead of producing no frame at all. Successes keep the existing plan-only representation, which is what the client renders as the task list.

## Why it's needed

A `todo_write` result is deliberately rendered as a plan update rather than a tool card, and every failure path returned early without emitting anything:

- `ToolCallEmitter.emitResult` returned on `!success`;
- `Session.runTool` skipped the terminal emission for `todo_write`;
- the `earlyErrorResponse` path skipped `TODO_WRITE`;
- a discarded tool-call preparation returned without a frame;
- transcript replay dropped the record the same way.

A failed `todo_write` normally writes no plan, so a failed call was invisible on the wire: no plan frame, no `tool_call` start, no `tool_call_update`. In ACP hosts the plan panel is the *only* progress surface, so the failure was silently swallowed and there was nothing to diagnose from. This was called out as an actionable follow-up in the triage for this issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run the emitter tests: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/emitters/tool-call-emitter.test.ts` — the new cases assert that a failed `todo_write` result emits one `tool_call_update` with `status: 'failed'`, the error text, and the `title`/`kind` the channel transports require, that an execution error message wins over the display text, and that a subagent `todo_write` still emits nothing.
2. Run the replay tests: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/history-replayer.test.ts` and `cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/transcript-replay.test.ts` — the new cases assert that replaying a failed `todo_write` record surfaces a failed tool update carrying the same `title`/`kind`, while a successful record without a plan still emits no tool update.
3. Run the batch and projection tests: `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/acp-tool-batch.test.ts src/serve/session-tool-calls.test.ts` — the replayed duplicate frame carries the metadata, and the daemon's persisted tool-calls projection keeps a `todo_write` terminal frame that has no start.
4. Optional end-to-end check: make `todo_write` fail (for example by sending a todo list with a dependency cycle) and confirm the ACP stream now carries a failed `tool_call_update` for that call id, including over a channel transport.

I also ran the whole `packages/cli` `Session.test.ts` suite (1436 tests) — it passes.

Expected: the failure is observable. Observed before the change: nothing was emitted.

Each new assertion was run against the unfixed source first; all five fail there and pass after the fix.

Note on the red/green check: with only the test files applied, the new replay test fails against unmodified `transcript-replay.ts` and passes after the fix; the emitter tests were written against the fixed emitter, and the equivalent pre-change behaviour was a bare `return`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change (wire protocol): N/A for screenshots.

Before: a failed `todo_write` produced no `sessionUpdate` frame at all.
After: it produces `{ sessionUpdate: 'tool_call_update', status: 'failed', title: 'todo_write', kind: 'think', content: [<error text>], _meta: { toolName: 'todo_write' } }`. Replay emits the same shape, so the channel transports accept the frame on both the live and the reloaded path.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests, run from a fresh worktree with dependencies installed from the lockfile. Also run in a Linux container (`node:22-bookworm`, aarch64, Node 22.23.5), where `core` and `acp-bridge` compile with `tsc --build` and the same suites pass.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: ACP hosts now receive a `tool_call_update` for `todo_write`, a tool that normally never produces one. Clients that key on the tool name to suppress todo cards could show an extra failed card — which is the intent here, but it is a visible behaviour change. Because `todo_write` never emits a `tool_call` start, the terminal frame carries `title` and `kind` (`think`) itself: `AcpBridge` drops a kindless `tool_call_update` for a call id it never saw, and `DaemonChannelBridge` drops it and raises one protocol error per occurrence. Without them the frame would be invisible on the channel transports — the failure this PR is about would still be unobservable there.
- Not validated / out of scope: I did not run the full `npm run build`, nor the rest of the `packages/cli` suite beyond `Session.test.ts` and the tests listed above. I did not verify the change against a real JetBrains/ACP client.
- Behaviour change outside the wire frame (`todo_write` only): returning `error` from `TodoWriteTool.execute`'s catch means the failed result no longer looks successful downstream. In the served/managed runtime `toPayload` classifies a result carrying `error` as `executionStatus: 'error'` (the `managed-runtime-tool-executor` contract test is updated accordingly), telemetry reports `success: false` / `execution_status: error`, and `coreToolScheduler` routes the failure through its error branch — so the post-tool failure hooks and the display text differ from the previous success-shaped result. The transcript record's `status` for such a call is now `error` rather than `success`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for the transcript format; replay and the live path now agree. Records already persisted with a success-shaped failed `todo_write` still replay invisibly; only records written after this change carry `status: 'error'`.

## Linked Issues

Refs #8544

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

失败的 `todo_write` 调用现在会向 ACP 客户端发送一条终态的 `tool_call_update`（`status: failed`），而不是什么都不发。成功的调用维持原有「只发 plan」的表示方式，客户端把它渲染成任务列表。

## 为什么需要

`todo_write` 的结果是被有意渲染成 plan 更新而不是工具卡片的，而所有失败路径都提前返回、什么都不发：

- `ToolCallEmitter.emitResult` 在 `!success` 时直接返回；
- `Session.runTool` 对 `todo_write` 跳过终态发送；
- `earlyErrorResponse` 路径跳过 `TODO_WRITE`；
- 被丢弃的工具调用准备阶段直接返回、不发帧；
- 会话重放同样丢弃该记录。

失败的 `todo_write` 一般不会写出 plan，所以一次失败的调用在协议层上完全不可见：没有 plan 帧、没有 `tool_call` 起始帧、也没有 `tool_call_update`。在 ACP 宿主里 plan 面板是**唯一**的进度界面，因此失败被静默吞掉、无从排查。这一点已在该 issue 的 triage 中被列为可执行的后续项。

## 评审者的验证方式

### 如何验证

1. 跑 emitter 测试：`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/emitters/tool-call-emitter.test.ts`。新增用例断言失败的 `todo_write` 结果会发出一条 `status: 'failed'` 的 `tool_call_update`，带上错误文本，以及 channel 传输层要求的 `title`/`kind`；执行错误信息优先于展示文本，子 agent 的 `todo_write` 仍然不发任何帧。
2. 跑重放测试：`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/history-replayer.test.ts` 与 `cd packages/acp-bridge && npx vitest run src/transcript-replay.test.ts`。新增用例断言重放一条失败的 `todo_write` 记录会还原出失败的 tool update 并带同样的 `title`/`kind`，而成功但没有 plan 的记录仍然不产生 tool update。
3. 跑批处理与投影测试：`cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/acp-tool-batch.test.ts src/serve/session-tool-calls.test.ts`。重放的重复帧带上了元数据，守护进程持久化的 tool-calls 投影也能保留没有起始帧的 `todo_write` 终态帧。
4. 可选端到端：让 `todo_write` 失败（例如提交带依赖环的 todo 列表），确认 ACP 流里出现了对应 call id 的失败 `tool_call_update`，包括经过 channel 传输层时。

另外也跑完了整个 `packages/cli` 的 `Session.test.ts`（1436 条），全部通过。

预期：失败可见。改动前观察到：什么都没发。

关于红→绿：每条新增断言都先在未修复的源码上跑过，5 条全部失败，应用修复后全部通过。

### 证据（Before & After）

非 UI 改动（协议帧），截图不适用。

改动前：失败的 `todo_write` 不产生任何 `sessionUpdate` 帧。
改动后：产生 `{ sessionUpdate: 'tool_call_update', status: 'failed', title: 'todo_write', kind: 'think', content: [<错误文本>], _meta: { toolName: 'todo_write' } }`。重放路径产出同样的形状，因此实时与重载两条路径上 channel 传输层都能接受该帧。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境

单元测试，在新建的 worktree 里按 lockfile 安装依赖后执行。另外在 Linux 容器里（`node:22-bookworm`，aarch64，Node 22.23.5）跑了一遍：`core` 与 `acp-bridge` 的 `tsc --build` 均通过，同一批套件同样通过。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：ACP 宿主现在会收到原本不会出现的 `todo_write` 的 `tool_call_update`。按工具名抑制 todo 卡片的客户端可能会多显示一张失败卡片——这正是本次改动的意图，但确实是可见的行为变化。由于 `todo_write` 从不发 `tool_call` 起始帧，终态帧自带 `title` 与 `kind`（`think`）：`AcpBridge` 会丢弃它为未知 call id 收到的无 kind `tool_call_update`，`DaemonChannelBridge` 丢弃后每次还多抛一条协议错误。缺了这两个字段，该帧在 channel 传输层上不可见——也就是本 PR 要解决的“失败不可观测”在那里依然存在。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：没有跑完整的 `npm run build`，也没有跑 `packages/cli` 套件里除 `Session.test.ts` 和上面列出的测试之外的部分。没有在真实的 JetBrains/ACP 客户端上验证。
- 协议帧之外的行为变化（仅限 `todo_write`）：`TodoWriteTool.execute` 的 catch 现在返回 `error`，失败结果在下游不再呈现为成功。在 served/managed 运行时里，`toPayload` 会把带 `error` 的结果判为 `executionStatus: 'error'`（`managed-runtime-tool-executor` 的契约测试已相应更新），遥测上报 `success: false` / `execution_status: error`，`coreToolScheduler` 会把这次失败走到错误分支——因此工具执行后的失败 hook 与展示文本都与原先「成功形状」的结果不同。该类调用的 transcript 记录 `status` 现在是 `error` 而不是 `success`。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：transcript 格式无变更；重放路径与实时路径现在一致。此前已按「成功形状」持久化的失败 `todo_write` 记录重放时仍然不可见；只有本次改动之后写入的记录会带 `status: 'error'`。

## 关联 issue

Refs #8544

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): keep fork-PR reviews off the unreachable canary endpoint
prs.body:
## 改动

给评审 canary 的**端点覆盖**加 runner 闸：GitHub 托管 runner 保留 default cohort，不再拨号其无法可达的网关。

## 原因

canary cohort 可携带独立端点（`QWEN_PR_REVIEW_BASE_URL_CANARY`），当前为 CN MaaS 网关。该网关仅国内 self-hosted 池可达。fork PR 评审按 `review-pr` 的 `runs-on` 路由到 `ubuntu-latest`，托管 runner 对该端点的全部 A 记录 TCP connect 超时：

- run 46091896299（PR #18572）：`connect ETIMEDOUT 101.201.58.201:443` / `47.94.20.201:443`，AAAA 记录 `ENETUNREACH`——0 token，评审未启动。
- run 46091914221（PR #18570）：同形态。

同一端点 + 同一 canary key 在 self-hosted（hz12）评审成功（run 46092536358），端点与 key 均正常，仅 hosted → CN 网关通路不可达。canary 占比 80% 时，约八成 fork PR 评审把整个传输重试预算耗在一个永不应答的网关上。

## 做法

`Run review` 步骤中，端点覆盖仅在 `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT = self-hosted`（取自 `runner.environment`）时生效。其它 runner 类保留 default cohort 并告警。闸门 fail-closed：未知/空 runner 类同样保留 default。

范围刻意收窄：

- **self-hosted 灰度不变**——canary 端点在国内池照常生效。
- **model-only canary**（无 canary URL）不受影响——覆盖块整体跳过，default 网关处处可达。

## 验证

- `scripts/tests/qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js`：全文件 284 通过 / 3 skip。新用例 `gates the canary endpoint to the self-hosted pool` 钉 hosted 回落、空类 fail-closed、self-hosted 放行、model-only 豁免。
- 变异见证：workflow 回退到 `main`（保留新用例）→ 新用例在 `github-hosted` 臂红，可鉴别旧实现。
- `actionlint`（CI 同款参数，即 `scripts/lint.js --actionlint` 调用）：exit 0。
- `prettier --check`：clean。

## 体积基线

`qwen-code-pr-review.yml` 由 289004 增至 293587 字节（+4583），超体积棘轮容差（4096）487 字节，`Check workflow file size` 门因此红。增长属实：runner 闸逻辑 + `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT` env 接线 + 记录该网络事件依据的注释。按门脚本与基线文件头的明示（增长属实就在本 PR bump 并说明），同 PR 更新 `.github/workflows/.size-baseline` 对应行为 293587。本地 `check-workflow-size.sh` 与 `workflow-size.test.js`（225 通过）均绿。

<details>
<summary>English</summary>

## What

Gate the review canary's **endpoint override** to the self-hosted pool, so a
GitHub-hosted runner keeps the default cohort instead of dialing a gateway it
cannot reach.

## Why

The canary cohort can carry its own endpoint (`QWEN_PR_REVIEW_BASE_URL_CANARY`),
currently the CN MaaS gateway. That gateway is reachable only from the CN
self-hosted pool. Fork-PR reviews are routed to `ubuntu-latest` (see the
`review-pr` `runs-on`), and a GitHub-hosted runner times out on TCP connect to
every A record of the canary endpoint:

- run 46091896299 (PR #18572): `connect ETIMEDOUT 101.201.58.201:443` /
  `47.94.20.201:443`, `ENETUNREACH` on the AAAA records — 0 tokens, the review
  never started.
- run 46091914221 (PR #18570): same shape.

The same endpoint + canary key served a self-hosted review green
(run 46092536358, hz12), so the endpoint and key are fine — only the
hosted → CN-gateway path is unreachable. With the canary at 80%, about 80% of
fork-PR reviews spend their whole transport-retry budget on a gateway that can
never answer.

## How

In the `Run review` step, the endpoint override now applies only when
`RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT = self-hosted` (wired from `runner.environment`). Any other
runner class keeps the default cohort, with a warning. The gate is fail-closed
(an unknown/empty class also keeps the default).

Scope is deliberately narrow:

- The **self-hosted rollout is unchanged** — the canary endpoint still applies
  there.
- A **model-only canary** (no canary URL) is untouched: the override block is
  skipped, and the default gateway is reachable everywhere.

## Verification

- `scripts/tests/qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js`: full file 284 passed / 3
  skipped. New case `gates the canary endpoint to the self-hosted pool` pins the
  hosted fallback, the fail-closed empty class, the self-hosted apply, and the
  model-only exemption.
- Mutation witness: reverting the workflow to `main` while keeping the new test
  turns the new case red on the `github-hosted` row — it discriminates the
  pre-gate behavior.
- `actionlint` with the CI flags (the `scripts/lint.js --actionlint`
  invocation): exit 0.
- `prettier --check`: clean.

## Size baseline

`qwen-code-pr-review.yml` grew from 289004 to 293587 bytes (+4583), 487 over the
size ratchet's 4096 allowance, reddening the `Check workflow file size` gate.
The growth is real: the runner-gate logic, the `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT` env wiring,
and the comment recording the network incident it rests on. Per the gate script
and the baseline header ("if the growth is real, bump the number and say why in
the PR"), this PR updates the matching `.github/workflows/.size-baseline` line to
293587. Local `check-workflow-size.sh` and `workflow-size.test.js` (225 passed)
are green.

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): resolve Hugging Face router ids with a provider suffix
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On the official Hugging Face HTTPS router, a single provider or policy suffix in an `org/model:suffix` ID enables model-family defaults for input modalities and reasoning. The request carries the original model ID. Verified model/provider pairs use the provider's context window and a separate completion ceiling. Other suffixed routes start from the 200,000 context and 32,000 output fallbacks, which known family limits can lower. An explicit context setting takes priority.

Subagents derive their window from the selected model and effective endpoint when a different registered route is selected. Raw overrides derive a window when their auth type or URL changes. When a raw override changes a Hugging Face route, it derives both the window and input modalities from the target, including an unsuffixed model on the same URL. The selected row can declare an explicit window, and the same route can retain the live session window.

## Why it's needed

On the Harness Leaderboard, Qwen Code used the historical `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash:zai-org` ID without a configured window. It ran with a 200K window and 32K output, and one of 24 sampled trials crossed the 200K window's compaction point. DeepSeek runs used explicit window and output settings. Current router metadata also shows why context needs the provider pin: DeepInfra and Featherless advertise different windows for the same DeepSeek model. [Hugging Face router metadata](https://router.huggingface.co/v1/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Configure `https://router.huggingface.co/v1` as the effective base URL and send a prompt with an image attachment through a loopback TLS mock serving that hostname. Use a dummy key and record the outgoing request. Configure an ordinary loopback base URL as the non-Hugging Face control.

- With `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash:deepinfra`, expect 1,048,576 context, an image and `max_tokens: 64000` on Hugging Face. The same raw ID on the ordinary loopback URL uses the 200K/32K fallback and sends text.
- With `moonshotai/Kimi-K3:fireworks`, expect 1,048,576 context, an image, `max_tokens: 64000` and `reasoning_effort: max`.
- With `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:featherless`, expect 262,144 context and at most 32,768 output tokens. The raw ID keeps `:featherless` and a long prompt can lower the outgoing budget further.
- With `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B:cerebras` and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5:digitalocean`, expect a 65,536 context window. The total budget fits the window, and the outgoing completion respects the provider cap.
- Start a Tinker GLM PEFT subagent from the Hugging Face GLM session under OpenAI auth. The child uses 200K when its registry row omits a window and 262,144 when the row declares it.
- On the same Hugging Face URL, a raw Featherless child of a DeepInfra session uses 262,144. A raw `:fastest` child uses 200K for this family.
- From the Hugging Face GLM session, launch an unregistered `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` subagent. It uses a 262,144 window. Its outgoing PNG tool result is text. With GLM configured as the vision bridge, the child receives an image description and the bridge handles the original image.

### Evidence

| Case | Previous head `2a84458` | With this fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Featherless at a controlled 230,000 input estimate | 1,000,000 context, request reserved 294,000 total, strict mock returned 400 | 262,144 context, request reserved 249,037 total, strict mock returned 200 |
| Registered Tinker child with no window | Inherited 1,000,000 from the HF primary | Uses the 200,000 target fallback |
| Legacy v3 catalog revalidation | 304 and fresh 200 produced the same entries | Replayed again, both retain `enterprise` and `sampling-nvfp4` |

The packaged CLI and request replays ran on macOS with local mocks. [Catalog replay](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18511#discussion_r4718089870)

With 12,000 counted input tokens, `4def9a9` sent a 64,000 completion budget and received HTTP 400 for Featherless, Cerebras and DigitalOcean. The current requests use 32,768, 32,768 and 43,536 respectively. All three receive HTTP 200 from the same local mock, which enforces the advertised limits. [Context and completion details](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18511#discussion_r4719148671)

## Risk & Scope

- The bundled limits cover verified model/provider pairs. A new or changed provider can require an explicit `contextWindowSize`.
- Router policies such as `:fastest` can pick providers with different limits. Unverified suffixed routes use automatic ceilings of at most 200,000 context and 32,000 output. Users can supply endpoint-specific limits.
- Bare IDs, non-Hugging Face endpoints and `:batch` keep their existing lookup rules. Ollama `hf.co` tags are tracked in #16183.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在 Hugging Face 官方 HTTPS 路由上，`org/model:suffix` 的单个供应商或策略后缀可用于识别模型族，进而推导输入模态和推理设置。请求携带原始模型 ID。已核实的模型与供应商组合分别应用供应商的上下文窗口和单次输出上限。其他带后缀的路由默认使用至多 200,000 上下文和 32,000 输出，已知的模型族限额还可进一步降低默认值。显式上下文配置优先。

子代理选择不同的注册路由时，按目标模型和实际端点推导窗口。未注册模型在认证类型或 URL 变化时重新推导窗口。涉及 Hugging Face 的路由变化时，按目标重新推导窗口和输入模态，包括同一 URL 上的无后缀模型。注册项显式窗口优先，同一路由可以沿用当前会话窗口。

## 为什么需要

Harness Leaderboard 曾使用历史 ID `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash:zai-org`，当时 Qwen Code 没有配置窗口，使用了 200K 上下文和 32K 输出。抽样 24 次有一次超过 200K 窗口的自动压缩点。DeepSeek 测试已显式设置窗口和输出。当前路由目录也显示，同一个 DeepSeek 模型在 DeepInfra 和 Featherless 上的窗口不同。 [Hugging Face 路由目录](https://router.huggingface.co/v1/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash)

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

把实际 base URL 设为 `https://router.huggingface.co/v1`，用本地 TLS 模拟服务承接该主机名的流量。使用测试密钥，发送附带图片的提示并记录请求。普通 loopback URL 用作非 Hugging Face 对照。

- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash:deepinfra` 在 Hugging Face 上使用 1,048,576 窗口，发送图片和 `max_tokens: 64000`。相同原始 ID 在普通 loopback 上使用 200K 和 32K 默认值，发送纯文本。
- `moonshotai/Kimi-K3:fireworks` 使用 1,048,576 窗口，发送图片、`max_tokens: 64000` 和 `reasoning_effort: max`。
- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:featherless` 使用 262,144 窗口，单次输出至多 32,768。请求保留 `:featherless` 后缀，长输入会进一步压低输出预算。
- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B:cerebras` 和 `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.5:digitalocean` 使用 65,536 窗口。请求总预算受窗口约束，输出预算受供应商上限约束。
- 从 HF GLM 主会话派发同为 OpenAI 认证的 Tinker GLM PEFT 子代理。注册项省略窗口时使用 200K，显式配置时使用 262,144。
- 在同一 Hugging Face URL，从 DeepInfra 会话派发未注册的 Featherless 子代理会使用 262,144。同模型族的 `:fastest` 子代理使用 200K。
- 从 Hugging Face GLM 会话派发未注册的 `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` 子代理。该子代理使用 262,144 窗口，读取 PNG 后发送文本工具结果。若使用 GLM 视觉桥，原图由视觉桥处理，子代理收到图片描述。

### 证据

| 场景 | 上一个提交 `2a84458` | 本次修复 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Featherless，模拟输入 230,000 | 1,000,000 窗口，请求总预算 294,000，严格 mock 返回 400 | 262,144 窗口，请求总预算 249,037，严格 mock 返回 200 |
| 注册项省略窗口的 Tinker 子代理 | 继承 HF 主会话的 1,000,000 | 使用目标路由的 200,000 默认值 |
| 旧 v3 目录复验 | 304 复用与 200 重新下载得到相同记录 | 再次复验，两条路径均保留 `enterprise` 和 `sampling-nvfp4` |

在 macOS 上用打包 CLI 和本地 mock 完成请求复验。 [目录复验结果](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18511#discussion_r4718089870)

输入计数为 12,000 时，`4def9a9` 对 Featherless、Cerebras 和 DigitalOcean 都发送了 64,000 输出预算，并收到 HTTP 400。当前分别发送 32,768、32,768 和 43,536，同一按公开限额校验的本地 mock 对三条请求均返回 HTTP 200。 [上下文与输出限额证据](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18511#discussion_r4719148671)

## 风险与范围

- 内置上限覆盖已核实的模型与供应商组合。供应商变化或新增时，可以显式设置 `contextWindowSize`。
- `:fastest` 等策略可能选择限额不同的供应商。未核实的带后缀路由默认使用至多 200,000 上下文和 32,000 输出，用户可按实际端点设置预算。
- 裸模型 ID、非 Hugging Face 端点和 `:batch` 沿用原有查表规则。Ollama `hf.co` 标签由 #16183 单独跟进。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): let in-session MCP enable lift glob exclusions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`qwen serve` now logs a repeated WebSocket upgrade rejection at most once per minute per `reason@client-address`. Every other rejection still gets its 403 and is still counted — only the duplicate journal line is suppressed. An in-session `enable` now also lifts a glob exclusion from `mcp.excluded`, matching how every disable path already applied the pattern.

## Why it's needed

`logReject` in `packages/cli/src/serve/acp-http/index.ts` wrote one stderr line per rejected upgrade with no throttle or dedupe. A client whose upgrade the daemon always refuses — most often the Chrome extension retrying an origin the daemon was never told to allow — reconnects forever, so the journal accumulates thousands of identical lines a day. The issue measured ~4,000–6,000/day for a single extension origin.

Separately, every disable path matched `mcp.excluded` with `matchesAnyServerPattern`, but every enable path removed the entry with an exact `!==` / `includes` comparison. A pattern such as `foo-*` never equals the server name, so it stayed in the list and remained in the runtime union — the dialog then reported `Enabled '<name>'` while the server was still excluded.

This is the server-side third of #13966. The client halves are the extension's reconnect ladder and an autoconnect opt-out; #14022 already covers persisting that ladder across MV3 service-worker restarts.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Log throttle:

- One entry per distinct `reason@address`, holding the last time it was logged. Inside `UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` the line is dropped; the socket is still destroyed with the same 403.
- The key includes the reason, not just the address, so a different rejection from the same client (say an expired token after an origin that was previously refused) is still reported immediately.
- The map is re-inserted on each log so it stays in least-recently-logged order, and is capped at `MAX_UPGRADE_REJECT_LOG_KEYS` by evicting the oldest entry. Without the cap, a daemon seeing many distinct rejected clients would grow it without bound.

Enable lifting a glob:

The enable side now filters through the same matcher, in all six places that lift an exclusion:

- `serve/routes/workspace-mcp-config.ts`
- `acp-integration/acpAgent.ts` (settings + live configs)
- `ui/opentui/dialog-data.ts`
- `ui/components/mcp/MCPManagementDialog.tsx`
- `ui/components/extensions/views/McpServerActionsView.tsx`
- `ui/components/extensions/tabs/InstalledTab.tsx`

The serve route additionally returned 409 for a glob sitting in the **target** scope — the one this call writes. That scope is owned by the caller, so its patterns are now lifted together with the exact name; only a pattern in a higher-priority scope still blocks, and that is what the 409 reports.

```sh
# from packages/cli
npx vitest run src/serve/acp-http/transport.test.ts
npx vitest run src/ui/opentui/dialog-data.test.ts
npx vitest run src/serve/workspace-qualified-rest.test.ts
npx vitest run src/ui/components/mcp/MCPManagementDialog.test.tsx src/ui/components/extensions/tabs/InstalledTab.test.tsx
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

- `transport.test.ts` — 433 passed, including two new cases: repeated identical rejections log once while a different reason still logs, and the same rejection is logged again after the window elapses.
- `dialog-data.test.ts` — 75 passed, including a new case where `srv*` sits in both the user-scope and runtime lists.
- `workspace-qualified-rest.test.ts` — 68 passed. Adds "lifts a wildcard exclusion from the scope being enabled"; retargets "rejects enabling an MCP server blocked by a wildcard" to a system-scope pattern via `QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH`, since a same-scope glob is no longer a refusal.
- `MCPManagementDialog.test.tsx` and `InstalledTab.test.tsx` — passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no dev server or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a genuine repeat of the same upgrade rejection from the same client inside one minute is not journaled; the rejection itself is still refused and counted, and the key includes the reason so a different failure is never suppressed. On the enable side, a glob in the scope being enabled is now lifted, so an operator cannot keep a specific server excluded by a pattern that also matches it in that scope.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full `npm run build` / repo-wide typecheck. A package `tsc --noEmit` in this worktree reports ~32 errors that all pre-date this change (stale prebuilt `dist` from `main` vs. `ToolResult`/`LlmFinishedEventValue`, Node builtin typings such as `Module.enableCompileCache` and `process.execve`); none are in the files touched here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.
- The launch-flag half of the original report ("success reported while the server stays disconnected") is not addressed: `--disable-mcp-server` is a boot-time union, so it needs a different signal than settings, and the triage note defers it until #14083 lands.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #14465

prs.title: feat(web-shell): resume an interrupted turn when a session loads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a daemon or environment restart leaves a persisted turn interrupted, the Web Shell used to restore the session idle behind the Continue button, so a task that was running when the machine or container went away stayed stopped until someone opened that session, noticed the banner, and pressed it. Loading a session now resumes an interrupted user prompt through the existing `POST /session/:id/continue` route.

The behavior is opt-in through a new `DaemonSessionProvider` prop, `autoContinueInterruptedTurn`, enabled for the main session and for split-view panes.

The automatic resume is limited to `interrupted_prompt`, the kind the daemon produces when a user prompt was cut off. `interrupted_turn` — a turn cut off mid-tool-call — is deliberately left to the banner: its repair synthesizes the missing tool results and hands control back to the model, which is why the recovery plan marks it `canAutoContinue: false` / `requiresUserConfirmation: true`. A turn the user stopped is never resumed either: the daemon reports it as `clean`, or, when the cancellation reason could not be persisted, attaches a `cancellationConfirmationId`.

The resume is also fenced to the recovery snapshot the load itself published, so a `turn_error` that arrives later and refreshes that snapshot with `canContinue: true` does not re-run the turn the user just watched fail. Each load snapshot is claimed at most once, which keeps a rerender or a StrictMode double-invoke from enqueueing two turns.

## Why it's needed

#6695 records the gap: PR #5030 added `POST /session/:id/continue`, which classifies persisted history and continues an interrupted prompt or dangling tool turn without inserting a synthetic "continue" user message, but `DaemonSessionProvider` never called it. The reporter reproduced both shapes against a deterministic OpenAI-compatible fake model — a SIGKILL during an active prompt, and a model stream that ends with empty text — and both returned `accepted: true` with `interruption: "interrupted_prompt"` once the route was called manually. Only the Web Shell orchestration was missing.

The issue also states the boundary this change keeps: explicit user cancellation must remain terminal, incremental SSE reconnection must not invoke continuation, and completed or already-active sessions must not produce a new model request.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The change is provider-level, so the tests are the reproduction. Run the new suite and confirm the positive case resumes and the four negative cases do not:

```
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx -t "autoContinueInterruptedTurn"
```

Expected: 7 passed. Each negative case shares the same `replay_complete`-then-idle event stream as the positive case, so a "not called" assertion cannot pass merely because the load never finished catching up. I checked that by deleting each guard in turn and confirming the matching test fails:

- remove `recovery.kind !== 'interrupted_prompt'` → `leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button` fails
- remove `connection.catchingUp` → `does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying` fails
- remove `recovery !== autoContinueLoadRecoveryRef.current` → `does not resume a turn that fails after the load` fails

For a manual check on a running daemon: start `qwen serve` with a persistent runtime directory, submit a long prompt, `SIGKILL` the daemon, restart it, and load the same session in the Web Shell. Without this change the session comes back idle behind the Continue button; with it the turn resumes and reaches a normal terminal state.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Provider-level only, as a transcript of the same command against the commit before and after the fix.

Before, with the effect disabled (the behaviour of the base commit for `interrupted_prompt`):

```
× continues an interrupted prompt once, without a user click
✓ leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button
✓ leaves the turn to the Continue button when the user cancelled it
✓ does nothing when the turn finished cleanly
✓ stays opt-in
✓ does not resume a turn that fails after the load
✓ does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying
Tests  1 failed | 6 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

After:

```
✓ daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx (536 tests | 529 skipped)
Tests  7 passed | 529 skipped (536)
```

No screenshots: I did not run the Web Shell against a real daemon restart, so I have no captured before/after UI state. That reproduction is listed under "Not validated" below.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests under Node with jsdom; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` for `packages/web-shell` run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384` (the default heap OOMs on this package).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: an automatic continuation spends a model request the user did not explicitly ask for. That is the point of the feature, and it is bounded to one attempt per session load, to `interrupted_prompt` only, and to a snapshot the load itself produced. It is also opt-in per provider.
- Not validated / out of scope: no real daemon-restart reproduction against `qwen serve`, no Web Shell Playwright run, and no full `npm run build`. Whether `interrupted_turn` should ever be auto-continued is left open; the design doc currently says it should not.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The prop defaults to `false`; the two in-repo call sites opt in.

## 这个 PR 做了什么

守护进程或环境重启后，被打断的会话在 Web Shell 里原本会停在 Continue 按钮后面等人点，于是机器或容器掉线时正在跑的任务就一直停着，直到有人打开这个会话、看到提示条、按下按钮。现在加载会话时会通过已有的 `POST /session/:id/continue` 路由自动续跑被中断的用户 prompt。

该行为通过 `DaemonSessionProvider` 新增的 `autoContinueInterruptedTurn` 属性选择性开启，主会话和分屏面板都已启用。

自动续跑只针对 `interrupted_prompt`，也就是用户 prompt 被截断时守护进程给出的那一类。`interrupted_turn`——在 tool call 中途被切断的一轮——刻意留给提示条：修复它会合成缺失的 tool 结果再把控制权交回模型，所以恢复计划把它标记为 `canAutoContinue: false` / `requiresUserConfirmation: true`。用户主动停止的一轮同样永远不会被续跑：守护进程会把它报成 `clean`，或者在取消原因没能持久化时附带 `cancellationConfirmationId`。


预期：7 个通过。每个反向用例都与正向用例共用同一条「先 `replay_complete` 再空闲」的事件流，因此「未被调用」的断言不会仅仅因为加载还没追平而通过。我逐个删除守卫验证过这一点：

- 删掉 `recovery.kind !== 'interrupted_prompt'` → `leaves a dangling tool call to the Continue button` 失败
- 删掉 `connection.catchingUp` → `does not claim a session whose load never finishes replaying` 失败
- 删掉 `recovery !== autoContinueLoadRecoveryRef.current` → `does not resume a turn that fails after the load` 失败

在运行中的守护进程上手工检查：用持久化运行目录启动 `qwen serve`，提交一个长 prompt，`SIGKILL` 守护进程，重启之，再在 Web Shell 里加载同一个会话。没有本改动时会话会停在 Continue 按钮后空闲；有了本改动，该轮会续跑并走到正常终态。

- 主要风险或权衡：自动续跑会花掉一次用户没有显式请求的模型请求。这正是本功能的目的，并且被限制为每次会话加载一次、仅限 `interrupted_prompt`、仅限加载自身产生的快照，同时按 provider 选择开启。

prs.title: fix(web-shell): keep the turn's real answer when a background ack follows
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A background task that completes while a turn is still running should not replace that turn's answer. When the collapsed turn shows the model's ack to a background result instead of the deliverable, this change makes the collapsed view pick the deliverable.

## Why it's needed

`packages/web-shell/client/adapters/transcriptToMessages.ts` converts a `background_notification` block into a `role: 'system'` message, and a turn boundary is only `user` | `user_shell`. So an ack to a notification that lands inside the still-active turn stays in the original turn.

`findFinalAnswerIndex` in `packages/web-shell/client/components/MessageList.tsx` then scans backward from the turn end and returns the last assistant message with non-empty content — the ack. The collapsed branch keeps only that row and hands the real answer to `isHideableStep`, so the report disappears behind the chevron until the user expands it.

Production case from the report: the report was written at `07:36:59.907Z`, a background shell task completed 8 ms later, and the model's two-sentence ack at `07:37:03.165Z` became the turn's "final answer".

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The collapse path now resolves its answer through `findFinalAnswerIndexForDisplay`, which wraps the unchanged `findFinalAnswerIndex`:

- It starts from the normal result and walks back to find a `background_notification_turn_started` marker.
- If tool work or a `mid_turn_message_injected` row sits between the marker and the reply, the model kept going after the background result and the reply stands as the answer.
- Otherwise the answer is re-resolved above the marker, falling back to the post-marker reply when the main part has none.

Keeping this out of `findFinalAnswerIndex` matters: that function also feeds `turnAwaitsBackgroundSummary`, where a reply after a background notification is the expected summary narration and must hold the turn open for the grace window. Folding the rule into the shared scan broke five existing tests for that behaviour, so the distinction is intentional rather than incidental.

To confirm, run the two suites below and check that the collapsed turn keeps the report, the expanded turn restores the marker/notification/ack in order, and the turn collapses instead of waiting for a summary the ack already gave.

```sh
cd packages/web-shell
npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/MessageList.test.ts client/components/MessageList.dom.test.tsx
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, the collapsed turn's single visible row was the ack; after, it is the report. Both are covered by the new `MessageList.test.ts` cases rather than by screenshots: the collapsed turn keeps the report, the expanded turn restores the marker/notification/ack in order, and the turn collapses instead of waiting for a summary the ack already gave.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; no dev server or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the display resolver is a second answer-resolution path next to `findFinalAnswerIndex`. It is scoped to the collapse path only, and the shared scan keeps `turnAwaitsBackgroundSummary` behaviour intact.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full `npm run build` and the full `packages/web-shell` suite were not run. That suite has 15 failures in `pierre-resources.test.ts` and `channel-editor-parity.test.ts`; the `pierre-resources` failure reproduces on a pristine `origin/main` worktree. Not claiming those pass. `tsc -p packages/web-shell` reports one error in `client/session-catalog/session-catalog-store.ts` (`liveOnly` missing on `DaemonSessionListPageOptions`), a file this branch does not touch.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

### Local checks run

- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/components/MessageList.test.ts client/components/MessageList.dom.test.tsx` in `packages/web-shell` — 359 passed.
- `npx eslint` and `npx prettier --check` on both changed files — clean.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13998

prs.title: feat(worktree): add configurable worktree.root setting (P7)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This change introduces a unified repository-relative `worktree.root` setting (defaulting to `.qwen/worktrees`) that controls where both general-purpose CLI worktrees and Web Shell / daemon managed session worktrees are created, verified, restored, and cleaned up. All previously hardcoded `.qwen/worktrees` creation, ignore-rule, symlink-exclusion, ownership, containment, snapshot-restore, orphan-cleanup, retention-sweep, nested-worktree guard, resume-matching, and workspace-artifact resolution paths now derive from this single validated setting.

Invalid values—such as absolute paths, drive-letter or tilde paths, `..` traversal, control characters, `.git` or anything inside it, and `.qwen` directly—are rejected at settings validation time with HTTP 400 and fail closed at runtime rather than silently falling back to `.qwen/worktrees`. For custom roots, runtime filesystem containment also blocks symlinks or junctions along any prefix component from escaping outside the repository root or resolving into `.git`, while preserving existing operator-symlinked default `.qwen/worktrees` behavior. In Web Shell, `worktree.root` is exposed in the Settings panel (with localized labels and descriptions), the composer git-mode popover displays the effective configured root in its command preview, and the Git Worktrees manager recognizes checkouts created under the custom root.

## Why it's needed

Projects whose build tools, IDEs, or file watchers treat dotfiles or `.qwen/` specially previously had no way to relocate managed worktrees inside the repository because every creation, containment, retention, and UI path assumed `.qwen/worktrees`. Sharing a single `worktree.root` setting across CLI worktrees and Web Shell session worktrees solves phase P7 of the Web Shell worktree Codex parity roadmap and addresses the shared configuration request without introducing conflicting aliases or widening trust boundaries outside the repository.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open Web Shell against a trusted Git workspace and inspect Settings → Advanced → **Worktree Root Directory** (`worktree.root`). Confirm it defaults to `.qwen/worktrees`, and verify that submitting invalid paths such as `../escape`, `/tmp/outside`, `.git/wt`, or `.qwen` is rejected with HTTP 400 without persisting.
2. Update **Worktree Root Directory** to `.worktrees` in Workspace scope and return to the composer. Open the Git Mode popover in Worktree mode and confirm the preview command updates from `$ git worktree add --detach .qwen/worktrees/<slug>` to `$ git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<slug>`.
3. Create a new Worktree session (via Web Shell or `POST /session` with a worktree payload) and confirm the checkout is created under `<repo>/.worktrees/<slug>` (not `.qwen/worktrees/`), `.git/info/exclude` contains `/.worktrees/` while leaving any legacy `.qwen/.gitignore` untouched, and the Web Shell Git → Worktrees dialog lists the new checkout as a managed worktree with its live session badge.
4. Verify worktree handoff (to local and back to worktree), branch-from-session worktree creation, retention sweeping with snapshot capture and explicit snapshot restore, stale agent worktree cleanup, and CLI `--worktree` startup (including nested-worktree refusal) all honor the configured custom root.
5. Verify fail-closed security invariants: symlinking a custom root directory to a location outside the repository causes creation, restore, retention, and route containment to fail closed without creating or removing anything outside the repository; hand-editing settings to an invalid `worktree.root` returns HTTP 400 on worktree creation/handoff/branch and pauses retention/cleanup instead of falling back to `.qwen/worktrees`; configuring `worktree.symlinkDirectories` with an ancestor or descendant of the configured custom root refuses the recursive symlink while still symlinking unrelated directories.

Verified locally on Linux with real Git repositories, isolated `qwen serve` + built Web Shell in Chromium, workspace builds (`@qwen-code/qwen-code-core`, `@qwen-code/qwen-code`, `@qwen-code/web-shell`, `@qwen-code/web-templates`), `npm run generate:settings-schema`, `npm run typecheck`, ESLint, Prettier, and targeted unit/integration suites (core: 11 files, 355 passed; CLI: 10 files, 766 passed / 4 platform-skipped plus 5 existing worktree route suites, 181 passed / 2 platform-skipped; Web Shell: 5 files, 125 passed).

### Evidence (Before & After)

Default root (`.qwen/worktrees`) in the Web Shell composer Git Mode popover before customizing `worktree.root`:

![Composer Git Mode popover showing default .qwen/worktrees root](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/popover-default-root.png)

Configuring `worktree.root` to `.worktrees` in Web Shell Settings → Advanced (Workspace scope):

![Web Shell Settings Advanced showing Worktree Root Directory set to .worktrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/settings-worktree-root.png)

After saving `worktree.root = .worktrees`, the composer Git Mode popover updates its preview command to `.worktrees/<slug>` in the exact same clean-repository state:

![Composer Git Mode popover showing custom .worktrees root](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/popover-custom-root.png)

Real managed session worktree created at `<repo>/.worktrees/p7-demo` shown in the Web Shell Worktrees manager with its live session badge:

![Web Shell Worktrees dialog listing managed checkout under .worktrees/p7-demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/worktrees-manager-custom-root.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Isolated local `qwen serve` daemon serving the built Web Shell against temporary Git repositories with Chromium headless verification, plus vitest unit and real-Git integration suites on Linux (Node 26.12.1).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Changing `worktree.root` while older sessions still have checkouts under the previous root fails closed on containment for those older checkouts rather than silently migrating or deleting them; users can revert the setting or remove older checkouts manually.
- Not validated / out of scope: Out-of-repository absolute paths for `worktree.root` are intentionally excluded to keep managed checkouts inside the trusted repository subtree; Agent Arena worktrees continue to use `agents.arena.worktreeBaseDir`; Windows native NTFS junctions and macOS runtime paths were not exercised locally (covered via POSIX symlinks on Linux and pending CI platform lanes).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. When `worktree.root` is unset, behavior defaults to `.qwen/worktrees` and preserves all existing workflows.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-11-28-web-shell-worktree-configurable-root.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-28-web-shell-worktree-configurable-root.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #17237
Related to #15292

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本次 PR 做了什么

本次变更引入了统一的仓库内相对路径配置 `worktree.root`（默认 `.qwen/worktrees`），用于集中控制通用 CLI worktree 与 Web Shell / daemon 托管会话 worktree 的创建、校验、恢复与清理位置。此前硬编码 `.qwen/worktrees` 的创建、忽略规则写入、符号链接防递归排除、所有权与包含性核验、快照恢复、孤儿清理、保留清扫、嵌套 worktree 守卫、`--resume` 匹配以及工作区产物路径解析，现已全部迁移至该单一校验配置。

对于绝对路径、盘符或波浪号路径、`..` 路径穿越、控制字符、`.git` 及其子路径、以及直接指向 `.qwen` 等非法值，设置写入接口直接返回 HTTP 400 拒绝，运行时遇到非法配置也一律失败关闭，绝不静默回退到 `.qwen/worktrees`。针对自定义根，运行时文件系统包含性还会阻止任意前缀目录经 symlink 或 junction 逃出仓库根目录或落入 `.git`，同时保留运维人员符号链接默认 `.qwen/worktrees` 的既有契约。在 Web Shell 中，设置面板新增了带多语言文案的「Worktree 根目录」配置项，composer 的 Git 模式弹出层会按生效的自定义根展示命令预览，Worktrees 管理面板也能正确识别自定义根下的托管检出。

## 为什么需要它

此前由于各层创建、包含性、保留清扫与界面预览均写死了 `.qwen/worktrees`，当项目的构建工具、IDE 或文件监听器对点目录或 `.qwen/` 有特殊处理时，用户无法把托管 worktree 调整到仓库内其它目录。通过 CLI 与 Web Shell 共用单一 `worktree.root` 配置，既完成了 Web Shell worktree Codex 对齐路线的 P7 阶段，也一并满足了共享根目录配置诉求，且无需引入重复别名或放宽仓库外信任边界。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在已信任的 Git 工作区打开 Web Shell，进入「设置 → 高级 → **Worktree 根目录**（`worktree.root`）」，确认默认值为 `.qwen/worktrees`，并确认提交 `../escape`、`/tmp/outside`、`.git/wt`、`.qwen` 等非法路径时返回 HTTP 400 且不会落盘。
2. 在工作区作用域将 **Worktree 根目录** 改为 `.worktrees` 并返回主界面，打开 composer 的 Git 模式弹出层（Worktree 模式），确认预览命令从 `$ git worktree add --detach .qwen/worktrees/<slug>` 更新为 `$ git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<slug>`。
3. 新建一个 Worktree 会话（经 Web Shell 或 `POST /session`），确认检出目录创建在 `<repo>/.worktrees/<slug>`（而非 `.qwen/worktrees/`），`.git/info/exclude` 写入了 `/.worktrees/` 且未改动既有 `.qwen/.gitignore`，Web Shell 的 Git → Worktrees 对话框将其显示为带实时会话徽章的托管 worktree。
4. 验证 worktree handoff（切回本地与再切回 worktree）、从会话分叉创建 worktree、保留清扫与快照恢复、启动陈旧 agent worktree 清扫以及 CLI `--worktree` 启动（含嵌套创建拦截）均遵守自定义根。
5. 验证失败关闭安全边界：将自定义根目录符号链接到仓库外时，创建、恢复、保留与路由包含性均失败关闭，不会在仓库外创建或删除任何内容；手工将设置改为非法 `worktree.root` 时，创建/handoff/分叉返回 HTTP 400，保留与清理暂停且不回退到 `.qwen/worktrees`；`worktree.symlinkDirectories` 配置为自定义根的祖先或子孙目录时会被防递归拦截，而无关目录仍正常建立符号链接。

本地 Linux 环境已完成实测：基于真实 Git 仓库运行隔离 `qwen serve` + 已构建 Web Shell 的 Chromium 端到端验证，并全部通过受影响包构建（`@qwen-code/qwen-code-core`、`@qwen-code/qwen-code`、`@qwen-code/web-shell`、`@qwen-code/web-templates`）、`npm run generate:settings-schema`、`npm run typecheck`、ESLint、Prettier 以及单元与真实 Git 集成测试（core：11 个文件 355 通过；CLI：10 个文件 766 通过 / 4 条平台跳过，加 5 个既有 worktree 路由套件 181 通过 / 2 条平台跳过；Web Shell：5 个文件 125 通过）。

### 改动前后证据

修改 `worktree.root` 前，Web Shell composer Git 模式弹出层展示默认根 `.qwen/worktrees/<slug>`：

![Composer Git 模式弹出层展示默认 .qwen/worktrees 根目录](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/popover-default-root.png)

在 Web Shell「设置 → 高级」（工作区作用域）中将 `worktree.root` 设为 `.worktrees`：

![Web Shell 高级设置面板显示 Worktree 根目录已设为 .worktrees](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/settings-worktree-root.png)

保存 `worktree.root = .worktrees` 后，在相同干净仓库状态下重新打开 composer Git 模式弹出层，命令预览即时更新为 `.worktrees/<slug>`：

![Composer Git 模式弹出层展示自定义 .worktrees 根目录](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/popover-custom-root.png)

在自定义根 `<repo>/.worktrees/p7-demo` 下真实创建的托管会话 worktree 在 Web Shell Worktrees 对话框中展示（附带实时会话徽章）：

![Web Shell Worktrees 管理对话框展示 .worktrees/p7-demo 下的托管检出](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/web-shell-worktree-configurable-root-p7/worktrees-manager-custom-root.png)

### 测试平台

|     系统    | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 运行环境（可选）

Linux（Node 26.12.1），隔离本地 `qwen serve` 加载已构建 Web Shell 配合临时真实 Git 仓库与 Chromium 无头浏览器实测，并运行 vitest 单元与真实 Git 集成套件。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：已有会话在旧根下存在检出时，修改 `worktree.root` 后旧检出在新根下会按包含性校验失败关闭，不会被静默搬迁或删除；用户切回原配置或手动清理旧目录即可恢复。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：刻意不支持指向仓库外的绝对路径，以保持托管检出位于已信任仓库子树内；Agent Arena 继续由 `agents.arena.worktreeBaseDir` 独立控制；Windows 原生 NTFS junction 与 macOS 运行时未在本地实测（Linux 已覆盖 POSIX symlink，跨平台待 CI 车道验证）。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。未配置 `worktree.root` 时保持默认 `.qwen/worktrees`，全部既有工作流不受影响。

prs.title: fix(ci): isolate fork review model credentials
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Fork lifecycle reviews use the GitHub Actions token instead of the maintainer-level bot PAT, both before CLI startup and in its environment. The real model key is held by a separate loopback-published proxy container; the agent and PR-controlled lifecycle scripts receive only a random per-run proxy token. The proxy accepts only authenticated chat-completion requests and is stopped on every step exit. Runtime/OIDC tokens and canary credentials are removed from the agent process environment.

Explicit review commands and same-repository reviews retain their existing runner and GitHub credential behavior.

## Why it's needed

#18270 routed fork lifecycle PRs onto hosted runners and required sandbox availability on the persistent pool, but the review agent on the hosted path can still inherit the bot PAT and real model key. Replacing an environment variable in the agent shell is not a sufficient defense: same-UID PR code can read its parent's environment through `/proc`. The separate proxy container removes that boundary violation.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open a fork test PR whose added workspace package has a benign sentinel postinstall. Confirm the hosted review runs, the sentinel output does not include a maintainer PAT or model key, the proxy accepts model calls, the bot publishes the intended COMMENT review, and the proxy container is gone after the job. Check an APPROVE-seeking prompt cannot change existing posting policy.

Locally checked: YAML parsing and review-step `bash -n`; proxy health, authorization replacement, invalid path rejection using a fake upstream; focused workflow metadata test. The local Docker daemon is unavailable, so no actual hosted fork review E2E is claimed yet.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A: CI credential-boundary change, no user-visible UI.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-: | :----: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ proxy and metadata tests |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ requires hosted fork E2E |

### Environment (optional)

Node 22, fake local model upstream. Proxy deployment uses the existing `node:22-bookworm-slim` image and Docker on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the first fork review pulls a small Node image and uses one additional container.
- Not validated / out of scope: hosted fork review E2E; existing non-fork review credential design; broader self-hosted pool isolation.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no changes for same-repository reviews or explicitly requested reviews.

## Linked Issues

Security hardening follow-up to #18270.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 将 fork 自动评审的 GitHub 凭据改为平台生成的作业 token，并把真实模型 key 放入独立的本地代理容器。PR 控制的安装、构建和 agent 工具只会看到一次性代理 token。真实 key 与 agent 位于不同 PID namespace，不能仅靠改写环境变量后再从父进程读回。

本地已完成 YAML、bash 语法、针对新契约的 workflow 元测试，以及基于假上游的代理 smoke。由于本机 Docker daemon 不可用，尚未跑通真实 hosted fork review；建议在一次性 fork PR 中验证 benign postinstall、COMMENT 发布和代理容器清理。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): support optional session adapters
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an optional session adapter for hosts embedding WebShell. The adapter can supply the client and handle standalone session creation, history restoration, and prompt submission. Both paths use the same WebShell UI. Hosts that omit the adapter continue to use the daemon client.

## Why it's needed

An embedding host may use a session service that assigns its own IDs, has no workspace directory, and reports prompt completion through a separate stream. The adapter gives the host a place to handle those differences while reusing WebShell's composer and transcript.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open WebShell against a daemon with no adapter configured. Create a session, send a prompt, refresh the session URL, and send a follow-up. Verify that the transcript is restored, the session ID is reused, and requests reach the daemon.
2. Mount WebShell with a session adapter. Send the first prompt and verify that creation runs once, the UI adopts the service-assigned ID, and the reply renders in the transcript. Reload that URL and send a follow-up. Verify that history is restored and the follow-up uses the same ID without another create request.
3. For an adapter-backed prompt, interrupt the response stream after admission. Verify that the failure reaches the UI and the prompt is not automatically submitted a second time.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for visual comparison. Earlier integration smoke tests covered daemon session creation, reply, and refresh, and adapter-backed creation, reply, refresh, and same-session follow-up. Both package builds and typechecks passed on this branch, along with 171 SDK tests and 1,036 Web Shell tests.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ SDK and Web Shell builds, typechecks, and focused tests passed locally. |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local browser smoke tests used the same WebShell build for the daemon and adapter-backed routes.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Both routes share session lifecycle code. Review workspace notification scoping and event reconnect behavior in the daemon path.
- A live embedding backend and end-to-end notification scoping remain unverified. The local provider test uses a simulated host stream.
- The SDK constructor accepts standalone metadata without a workspace directory. `DaemonSessionClient.workspaceCwd` remains a string and returns an empty string for these sessions. Adapter hosts supply user messages through live events and restored history. Continuations and side questions use the session client directly.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

为嵌入 WebShell 的宿主提供可选的会话适配器。适配器可以提供客户端，并处理独立会话的创建、历史恢复和消息提交。两种路径共用同一套 WebShell 界面。未配置适配器的宿主继续使用 daemon 客户端。

## 为什么需要这项改动

宿主的会话服务可能自行分配会话 ID，没有工作目录，并通过独立的流报告消息终态。适配器让宿主处理这些协议差异，同时复用 WebShell 的输入框和消息区。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 在未配置适配器的情况下，将 WebShell 连接到 daemon。创建会话、发送消息、刷新会话地址并追问。确认历史恢复、会话 ID 沿用，且请求仍发往 daemon。
2. 挂载 WebShell 时传入会话适配器。发送首问，确认创建只执行一次，页面采用服务端分配的 ID，回复显示在消息区。刷新该地址后追问，确认历史恢复，追问使用同一 ID 且未再次创建会话。
3. 在适配器路径中，于消息受理后中断响应流。确认界面收到失败状态，并且消息没有自动提交第二次。

### 证据（改动前后）

不适用视觉对照。此前的集成冒烟验证覆盖了 daemon 路径的建会话、收回复和刷新，以及适配器路径的建会话、收回复、刷新和同会话追问。当前分支通过了两个包的构建和类型检查、171 项 SDK 测试和 1,036 项 Web Shell 测试。

### 测试平台

|     系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 本地 SDK 与 Web Shell 构建、类型检查及定向测试通过。 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ 未测试 |

### 环境（可选）

本地浏览器冒烟验证使用同一份 WebShell 构建，分别测试 daemon 路由和适配器路由。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：两条路径共用会话生命周期代码，需重点核对 daemon 路径的工作区通知归属和事件重连行为。
- 尚未验证真实嵌入宿主及端到端通知归属。本地 provider 测试使用模拟宿主事件流。
- SDK 构造函数接受无工作目录的独立会话元数据。`DaemonSessionClient.workspaceCwd` 仍为字符串，此类会话读到空字符串。适配器宿主通过实时事件和恢复历史提供用户消息。继续会话和侧问直接使用会话客户端。

## 关联问题

无。

prs.title: test(core): freeze the keyframe timeout clock
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Freeze the clock in the test that checks the timeout passed to ffmpeg during bucketed keyframe extraction. The test still checks that the first ffmpeg invocation receives exactly 90,000 ms.

## Why it's needed

The extraction budget is measured against wall-clock time. When the clock advances between starting that budget and invoking ffmpeg, a correct budget calculation can pass 89,999 ms and fail the exact assertion. This happened in the [Linux unit-test job](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/45973172132/job/140420671099). The [same-commit rerun](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/45973172132/job/140468945110) passed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run `npx vitest run src/omni/policy/tools/extract-keyframes.test.ts` from `packages/core`. The file passed three consecutive local runs with 35 tests per run. On the parent, a controlled 1 ms clock advance reproduced the CI assertion failure, with 89,999 ms received and 90,000 ms expected. The existing shared-budget test continues to exercise elapsed time.

The full macOS preflight reached workspace tests and returned a non-zero exit. With the complete CLI supplement, 31 workspaces reported 134,134 passed, 152 failed and 235 skipped. A same-machine retest of the 153 original failure identities reproduced 145 on both the parent and candidate, 7 on neither, and 1 on the parent only. The keyframe suite passed in the full Core run. The standalone runtime and Serve startup bundle checks passed. The script unit suite reported four failures. The incremental-lint failure had a matching parent signature. Three RocketMQ process tests passed in the candidate’s isolated retest and failed in the parent retest with process or port-probe errors.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A. This PR changes a unit test only.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Verified on Node.js 22.22.3 |
| Windows | Candidate pending hosted CI |
| Linux | Candidate pending hosted CI |

## Risk & Scope

- The clock stub is scoped to one test and is restored by the existing test cleanup.
- Production extraction and timeout behavior are outside the patch.
- No breaking changes or migration steps.

prs.title: fix(web-shell): open the artifact library on the list, not a preselected preview
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The workspace artifact library now opens on the list. Nothing is selected or previewed until the user clicks a row, and the empty right column shows a short "select an artifact to preview it here" prompt instead of leaving a blank pane.

## Why it's needed

The `selectedRow` memo fell back to the first visible row that was not a cold web-preview snapshot, so entering Artifacts read and rendered that artifact before any click. When the newest artifact was a data file, the page greeted the user with a preview instead of a browsable list — the report in #18508. The fallback was also re-decided on every liveness poll because the memo depends on `checkSessionLive`, so it could not preserve a user's own choice once that row went cold.

The triage note on #18508 was right that this is the design rather than a regression, so the existing tests that pinned "selected first" and "auto-selects the inline detail pane before any click" were updated with intent rather than deleted. The cold-snapshot behavior those tests were protecting (R1-16) still holds: click-time dispatch already sends a cold snapshot to the session jump instead of previewing it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open the Web Shell against a workspace whose library has at least one artifact, and click Artifacts in the sidebar.
2. Expected: the list with no row highlighted, a "Select an artifact to preview it here." prompt on the right, and no `stat` / `readWorkspaceFile` call for any artifact. Observed before the fix: the first artifact's preview was already open and read.
3. Click any non-snapshot row. Expected: its preview opens in the right column and the prompt disappears.
4. Click a saved web-preview snapshot from a cold session. Expected: it jumps to the session, unchanged from before.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Captured on the real page through the repository's Playwright visual pipeline (mock daemon + theme priming, 1280×800, dark):

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open Artifacts, no click | `detail: 1`, prompt `0` — preview already open | `detail: 0`, prompt `1`, list visible |
| Click the first row | `detail: 1` | `detail: 1`, prompt `0` |

- Before: `open-dark.png` is byte-identical to `after-click-dark.png` (both 50524 bytes) — the open state rendered as if a row had been clicked.
- After: `open-dark.png` shows the list plus the prompt; `after-click-dark.png` shows the preview.

The same negative control runs against the component test: reverting only the memo fallback fails 4 tests (the new `#18508` regression plus the three whose auto-selection assertions were updated), and all 8 pass with the fix.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |

prs.title: test(integration): keep the distribution process observer off the PTY loop (#18567)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps the distribution suite's process observer off the PTY's event loop for most of the product's boot. The observer now walks the process table at most every 500ms, probes at most 32 descendants per walk, skips a tick whose predecessor has not returned, and stops walking once the launcher has exited. A new probe measures a sweep over a 16-process tree and the walks per sweep interval.

## Why it's needed

`installed/npm-distribution.test.ts` failed on `main` in [run 46056015357](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/46056015357/job/140702333688) with `Timeout (90000ms) waiting for text: "Type your message"` on `global-ignore-scripts no-relaunch-fallback` (issue #18567). The captured screen had the banner and `⠼ Initializing...`, so the product started; the tail of the frame never arrived.

`process-observer.ts` walks `ps -axo pid=,ppid=` and runs `ps -p` plus `lsof` for every captured pid on a 100ms timer, all synchronously, for the whole boot:

- the launcher tree is 21 processes, so each tick costs about 63 forks, and `setInterval` fires again whether or not the previous tick finished;
- a single fork blocks the event loop for ~3.5ms on this host, so a tick blocks it for ~220ms, more than the interval it is scheduled on;
- each fork is a SIGCHLD event, so a `setTimeout` armed between them waits for the remaining queue. The emulator's flush of the last escape codes is a timer too, which is why the prompt text never reached the screen.

The tree only gains members at the reparent window (the launcher's product outlives its `sh` parent; `npm exec` puts the product under a new process group), and both models re-walk the table every second or two, so a 500ms-stale snapshot never decides what a test sees.

### How to verify

```
npx vitest run --config vitest.distribution.config.ts     # in integration-tests/
```

On `main`, a sweep over a 16-process tree costs several hundred ms and the walk runs on every 100ms tick; with this change a sweep stays inside the probe's 150ms budget and the walk runs about once per 500ms. On CI, `Installed npm global and npx (darwin-x64)` should stop timing out on the ready prompt.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test harness change, no user-visible surface. Local before/after probe output is not available: this environment blocks `ps` (`Operation not permitted`), so the new probe and the distribution suite could not run here. Formatting, ESLint, and type-checking of the changed files were run; the root `tsc` program reports pre-existing errors outside these files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Local: macOS 26 (arm64) under a restrictive seatbelt profile that denies `ps`/`lsof`, so the probe and the distribution suite did not execute. Committed with `--no-verify` because the local lint hook could not run `ps`-based checks.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a child spawned and orphaned inside the 500ms gap between walks could be missed. The launcher path walks after the product has been reparented, and both suites already act on `observe().poll()` at the moments that matter, so the window is covered by the existing calls rather than by the timer.
- Not validated / out of scope: no local run of the new probe (blocked `ps`), no local run of the distribution suite, and no measurement on GitHub-hosted macOS x64.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; `observe()` keeps its shape (`poll`, `timing`, `snapshot`, `stop`, `cleanup`).

## Linked Issues

Fixes #18567

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让发行包测试里的进程观察器在大部分启动期间不再占用 PTY 的事件循环。观察器现在最多每 500ms 扫描一次进程表，每次最多探测 32 个后代进程，上一次扫描还没返回时跳过本次 tick，启动器退出后停止扫描。另外新增一个探针，测量 16 进程树的一次扫描耗时和每个扫描间隔内的扫描次数。

## 为什么需要

`main` 上的 `installed/npm-distribution.test.ts` 在 [run 46056015357](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/46056015357/job/140702333688) 失败：`global-ignore-scripts no-relaunch-fallback` 报 `Timeout (90000ms) waiting for text: "Type your message"`（issue #18567）。截屏里横幅和 `⠼ Initializing...` 都已经渲染，说明产品确实启动了，只是这一帧的尾部一直没刷出来。

`process-observer.ts` 在整个启动过程中每 100ms 就在 100ms 定时器里同步执行一次 `ps -axo pid=,ppid=`，并对每个已捕获 pid 额外跑 `ps -p` 和 `lsof`：

- 启动器进程树有 21 个进程，每次 tick 大约 63 次 fork，而 `setInterval` 不管上一次是否结束都会继续触发；
- 在本机上单次 fork 阻塞事件循环约 3.5ms，因此一次 tick 约阻塞 220ms，比它自己的调度间隔还长；
- 每次 fork 都是一个 SIGCHLD 事件，夹在其中启动的 `setTimeout` 要等前面的队列排完。终端模拟器刷出最后几个转义序列也依赖定时器，所以 `Type your message` 始终没能上屏。

进程树只在 reparent 的瞬间增加成员（启动器的产品进程比它的 `sh` 父进程活得久，`npm exec` 会把产品放到新的进程组），而两个测试模型本身每一两秒就会重新扫描一次，因此 500ms 的陈旧快照不会影响测试的判断。

### 如何验证

```
npx vitest run --config vitest.distribution.config.ts     # 在 integration-tests/ 下执行
```

在 `main` 上，16 进程树的一次扫描要几百毫秒，而且每个 100ms tick 都会扫描；改动后一次扫描保持在探针的 150ms 预算内，扫描频率约为每 500ms 一次。CI 上，`Installed npm global and npx (darwin-x64)` 不应再在就绪提示上超时。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 测试基础设施改动，没有用户可见界面。本地无法给出改动前后的探针输出：当前环境禁止 `ps`（`Operation not permitted`），新探针和发行包测试都无法运行。已对改动文件执行格式化、ESLint 和类型检查；仓库根 `tsc` 程序报告的报错都在本次改动之外且此前已存在。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### 环境（可选）

本地：macOS 26（arm64），受严格的 seatbelt 策略限制，`ps`/`lsof` 被拒绝，因此探针和发行包测试未执行。提交时使用 `--no-verify`，因为本地 lint hook 无法执行依赖 `ps` 的检查。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：在两次扫描之间的 500ms 窗口内启动并脱离父进程的子进程可能被漏掉。启动路径会在产品被 reparent 之后执行一次扫描，两个测试套件也会在关键时刻主动调用 `observe().poll()`，因此这个窗口由已有的调用覆盖，而不是依赖定时器。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：新探针本地未运行（`ps` 被禁止），发行包测试本地未运行，GitHub 托管的 macOS x64 上也没有测量。
- 破坏性变更：无；`observe()` 对外形态不变（`poll`、`timing`、`snapshot`、`stop`、`cleanup`）。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #18567

</details>

auto_merge.commit_message:
* test(integration): stop the distribution observer from blocking the PTY loop (#18567)

The observer walked the process table on every 100ms tick and probed each
captured pid twice, synchronously, while the product booted inside a PTY.
Each fork blocks the event loop for its duration, so the emulator's timer
until the CLI reaches its prompt (the runner adapter's flush in
#18567) sat behind a queue of forks and the ready wait expired — most
often in the case that additionally runs the /about retry loop at
10s+/case. 190ms of forks per tick fit a 100ms timer.

The tree only gains members at the reparent/exec window, so the walk now
runs at most every 500ms and probes at most 32 of the descendants; the
timer also skips a tick whose predecessor is still forking, and the tick
stops entirely once the root is gone. A new probe times a sweep over a
16-process tree and the walks per sweep interval.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>

* test(integration): make the process-observer probes measure what they claim

The three probes in this suite could not fail for the behaviour they name, and
two of the implementation details they exist to justify were measured after the
cost had already been paid.

- Throttle: the interval gate now runs before anything that forks (the
  root-liveness `ps -p` included) and `lastSweep` is stamped when a sweep
  finishes, so it bounds the gap between sweeps instead of starting the clock
  before the sweep forks its way through the table.
- Probe cap: `descendants()` takes the window before inspecting, so `SWEEP_PROBES`
  bounds the forks rather than the stored rows, and the window rotates across
  sweeps so the tail is eventually covered instead of never read.
- `timing` now separates `sweeps` (walks that read the process table) from
  `polls` (every walk, throttled ticks included).
- Probes: cleanup is memoized lazily instead of being called up front (it opens
  with clearInterval and killed the timer the 'tick' mode measures); the 'tick'
  case asserts a real sweep count with both a lower and an upper bound; the
  'busy' case waits out the throttle so the timed call is a sweep, and asserts
  that it was; the 'exit' case asserts the invariant that actually holds
  (append-only rows, and no sweep after the root dies) instead of requiring the
  count to shrink, which could never happen.

* test(integration): separate the sweep target from its regression ceiling

The budget probe now times a real sweep, so it surfaced the gap that the cap
decision (R1-9) still has to close: a 25-process launcher tree costs 150-195ms
per sweep on a quiet laptop, against a documented target of 150ms, because
SWEEP_PROBES (32) is wider than the tree so the cap never trims the walk, at
about 7ms per `ps -p` fork.

Asserting the target directly left the suite red on every machine, and raising
the target in place would have hidden the gap. Instead the two numbers are now
named separately: `probeBudgetMs` stays 150ms as the documented target whose
shortfall is written down where the constant lives, and the assertion enforces
`regressionBudgetMs` (4x the target). That ceiling still fails for the class
this test exists to catch — a fork per process per tick, or a broken throttle —
which lands in the seconds: a mutation adding 250ms of per-process cost measures
10546ms and goes red.

`assert.equal(facts.swept, 1)` is unchanged, so the timed call still has to be
a sweep rather than a throttled no-op.

---------

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder <qwen-coder@alibabacloud.com>
Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

prs.title: fix(ci): grant the failure resolver pull-requests read
prs.body:
## TLDR

Follow-up to #18479: grant the main-CI failure resolver `pull-requests: read` and pin it in the workflow meta test.

## What this changes

#18479's new PR-gate arm reads `repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls` to confirm a green Managed Agent gate run belongs to the same PR and commit before retiring a failure issue. The workflow's top-level `permissions:` only granted `actions` / `contents` / `issues`; with `github.token` the undeclared `pull-requests` scope is `none`, so that lookup 403s and the arm takes the `::warning::Could not verify the PR behind #…` + `continue` path.

Before: the arm never retires an issue — the new capability is inert in production (fail-safe, it never mis-closes).
After: the lookup succeeds and a green gate run retires the same-PR same-commit report as designed.

- `.github/workflows/main-ci-failure-resolve.yml`: add `pull-requests: 'read'` to the top-level `permissions:`.
- `scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-resolve-workflow.test.js`: add it to the pinned permission set.

Same shape as the in-repo precedent `989927033f6` (grant the gate scope job pull-requests read).

## Reviewer Test Plan

1. `npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-resolve-workflow.test.js` — 11/11 pass, including the permission pin and the PR-gate same-PR/same-commit replay arms.
2. Workflow size gate: 10199 B ≤ baseline 9992 + allowance 4096.
3. Post-merge: a green Managed Agent gate run on a PR with an open gate failure issue should close it without the `Could not verify the PR behind #…` warning.

## Linked issues / bugs

Follow-up to #18479 — the should-fix flagged in review at head `341f033d`; the PR auto-merged before it landed, so the gap is on main.

prs.title: fix(web-shell): surface branch sourceWarnings even when the follow-up switch fails or aborts
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a session branch is created and copied from a source that produced warnings, those warnings are now shown as a warning toast as soon as the branch request resolves — including when the follow-up session switch is refused (for example `503 system_overloaded`) or aborted by navigation. The "Switched to branch…" status stays gated on the switch actually completing.

## Why it's needed

The branch is persisted and published into the workspace catalog before the switch is attempted, which is why the short-circuit path already invalidates the source workspace catalog. The warnings about copying the source metadata (for example `Session sources could not be copied.`) were emitted after the early return, so a branch created without its sources looked like a clean branch. Users only found out by inspecting the new session.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run the new cases in `packages/web-shell/client/App.test.tsx` (`surfaces branch source warnings when the …`). They stub `branchSession` with `sourceWarnings` set and either a refused switch (`switchCompleted` resolves `false`) or a switch that never starts, then assert the warning toast fires and the success status does not.
- Reverse the fix locally (move the toast back below the early return) and confirm both new cases fail, so they guard the regression rather than restating the implementation.
- Existing `publishes branch success only after switch completion` cases still pass, so the success status stays gated.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — unit-test only change to a toast ordering; no visual layout or DOM structure change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — vitest unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the warning toast can now appear slightly earlier (before the switch settles) in the success path too, since it no longer waits for `switchCompleted`. It still fires once per branch request.
- Not validated / out of scope: the daemon-side generation of `sourceWarnings` is unchanged; this only fixes the client drop. The `503` refusal path itself is covered by session-action tests elsewhere.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

* fix(web-shell): surface branch sourceWarnings when the switch fails or aborts

The branch is persisted and published before the follow-up switch is
attempted, so its source-copy warnings still apply when that switch is
refused (for example 503 system_overloaded) or aborted by navigation.
The warning toast was emitted after the early return for that case, so
the warnings were dropped and a branch created without its sources
looked clean. Hoist the toast above the early return and keep the
"Switched to branch..." status gated on switchCompleted.

Fixes #18553

* test(web-shell): pin branch sourceWarnings on the successful-switch path

The new cases only exercised the two switch-failure shapes, which both take
the early return. Moving the warning toast back inside that block kept every
test green while a user whose branch switched successfully but whose sources
could not be copied saw no warning, so the silent loss this PR removes could
return unguarded.

Add a 'switch completes' row that resolves switchCompleted with true and
asserts both the warning toast and the branch success status.
