prs.title: test(web-shell): harden artifacts right-panel entry test coverage
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds four focused DOM tests and corrects a design-doc status line, with no production code change. It hardens the artifacts header entry introduced by #17689 (the entry that opens the session artifacts list as a right-panel tab): the persisted-tab serialize/parse round-trip, the close affordance for a restored zero-artifact artifacts tab, and the floating drawer's focus restore to the header entry.

## Why it's needed

#17689 merged at head `6fcccaefa4` before its round-5 review findings were addressed. Two non-blocking inline findings and the independent verification report left concrete coverage gaps. A serialize arm that dropped a tab's `id`/`title` would keep the existing kind-only assertion green while the tab silently vanished on every reload, against the design's "a persisted artifacts tab restores across reload". The `artifactsTabActive` join that keeps a close affordance for a restored zero-artifact tab had no App-layer witness, so mutating it to `false` or a wrong id prefix shipped green. And deleting `rememberArtifactPanelTrigger()` — the call that lets the floating drawer return focus to the header entry on close — left every committed suite green while focus dropped to `BODY` (the verification's surviving mutant M1, an accessibility regression). This PR pins each of those behaviors with a test that a single-point mutant reddens, and aligns the design-doc status line with the verification actually completed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/web-shell`, run the focused suites: `npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t artifact` (72 passed), the four component suites `ChatContextHeader` / `ArtifactPanel` / `ArtifactsListPanel` / `EnvironmentPanel` (258 passed), and `client/build-artifact.test.ts` (46 passed against a freshly built dist). `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes as a package gate, but excludes `client/**/*.test.tsx`, so it is not evidence that the added test file typechecks. ESLint on the changed test file and Prettier on all three changed files are clean. Each new assertion is load-bearing — the mutation witnesses below were run on this branch's original base, whose `App.tsx` was byte-identical to the merged `6fcccaefa4` at that point, and each production edit was restored byte-identical afterward. After merging main moved `App.tsx`, the independent follow-up at `8365a90f` re-derived and re-ran M1–M7 against the current file, re-ran the key cells on a trial-merge tree, and restored every production edit:

| Mutant (single production edit) | Pinning test | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serialize artifacts arm drops `id`/`title` | custom chat header round-trip | KILLED — `expected undefined to be 'artifacts:session-1'` |
| `artifactsTabActive = false` | restored zero-artifact close affordance | KILLED — `expected null not to be null` |
| delete `rememberArtifactPanelTrigger()` in the list-panel opener | drawer focus restore | KILLED — `expected <body> to be <button>` |

### Evidence (Before & After)

Tests and a documentation status line only (no user-visible production change). The drawer focus restore was additionally re-confirmed in headless Chromium against the live daemon at a narrow viewport (800×900), where the panel floats as a drawer: open from the focused header entry, close with the drawer's own toggle, and read `document.activeElement`. Probe result:

```json
{
  "entryLabel": "Artifacts (4)",
  "pressedBefore": "false",
  "drawerListRows": 4,
  "pressedOpen": "true",
  "drawerGone": true,
  "focusAfterClose": { "tag": "BUTTON", "isArtifactsEntry": true, "label": "Artifacts (4)" }
}
```

Focus returns to the artifacts entry (`isArtifactsEntry: true`), not `BODY`; the list row count matches the badge (4 == 4). The drawer open state:

![Artifacts drawer open at narrow viewport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17689-artifacts-entry/pr17689/follow-up/drawer-open.png)

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment

Vite dev server proxied to the local `qwen serve` daemon (`127.0.0.1:4170`); headless Chromium (playwright-core) for the focus probe; vitest/jsdom for the DOM tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none — tests and a documentation status line only; no production code change.
- Not validated / out of scope: upstream macOS and Windows lanes. Later local verification at `8365a90f` used Node 24 to pass the full web-shell suite (623 files / 17,634 tests) and the root build/typecheck/bundle, then used the resulting bundle for a further ten-check real daemon + Vite + Chromium verification. These local passes are not upstream macOS or Windows lane results.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design document updated in both locales (status line only): [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-18-artifacts-entry-opens-right-panel.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-18-artifacts-entry-opens-right-panel.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17689, addressing its round-5 review findings (serialize round-trip pin, zero-artifact App-layer witness, drawer focus-restore coverage, and the design-doc status drift).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

## 为什么需要

#17689 在 head `6fcccaefa4` 合入时，其第 5 轮评审发现尚未处理。两条 non-blocking 行内意见与独立验证报告留下了具体覆盖缺口：serialize 分支若丢掉 tab 的 `id`/`title`，既有的「仅判 kind」断言仍会绿，而 tab 会在每次刷新时静默消失，违背设计中「持久化的产物 tab 跨刷新恢复」；为恢复出的零产物 tab 保留关闭入口的 `artifactsTabActive` 连接没有 App 层见证，把它变异成 `false` 或错误 id 前缀都能绿着上线；删除 `rememberArtifactPanelTrigger()`（让浮动抽屉关闭时把焦点还回头部入口的调用）后所有已提交套件仍绿，而焦点落到 `BODY`（验证中存活的变异 M1，属无障碍回归）。本 PR 用「单点变异即转红」的测试钉住上述每一处行为，并把设计文档状态行与实际已完成的验证对齐。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/web-shell` 下跑聚焦套件：`npx vitest run client/App.test.tsx -t artifact`（72 过）、四个组件套件 `ChatContextHeader` / `ArtifactPanel` / `ArtifactsListPanel` / `EnvironmentPanel`（258 过）、`client/build-artifact.test.ts`（对新构建 dist 46 过）。`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` 作为包级门禁通过，但会排除 `client/**/*.test.tsx`，因此不能作为新增测试文件通过类型检查的证据。改动测试文件的 ESLint、三个改动文件的 Prettier 均通过。每条新断言都承重——下列变异见证在本分支的原始基线上运行，当时其 `App.tsx` 与已合并的 `6fcccaefa4` 字节一致；main 合入使该文件变化后，独立跟进验证在 `8365a90f` 针对当前文件重新构造并复跑 M1–M7，并在试合并树复跑关键格；每次生产编辑后都字节级还原：

| 变异（单点生产编辑） | 钉住用例 | 结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serialize 产物分支丢 `id`/`title` | 自定义头部回环 | 被杀 — `expected undefined to be 'artifacts:session-1'` |
| `artifactsTabActive = false` | 恢复零产物关闭入口 | 被杀 — `expected null not to be null` |
| 删列表面板 opener 里的 `rememberArtifactPanelTrigger()` | 抽屉焦点恢复 | 被杀 — `expected <body> to be <button>` |

### 证据（前后对比）

仅测试与文档状态行（无用户可见生产改动）。抽屉焦点恢复另在窄视口（800×900，面板浮动为抽屉）下用无头 Chromium 对真实 daemon 复确认：从聚焦的头部入口打开、用抽屉自身 toggle 关闭、读 `document.activeElement`。探针结果见上方 JSON：焦点回到产物入口（`isArtifactsEntry: true`）而非 `BODY`，列表行数与徽章一致（4 == 4）。抽屉打开态截图见上图。

### 测试平台

macOS ⚠️ 未测、Windows ⚠️ 未测、Linux ✅ 已测。

### 环境

Vite dev server 代理到本机 `qwen serve` daemon（`127.0.0.1:4170`）；焦点探针用无头 Chromium（playwright-core）；DOM 测试用 vitest/jsdom。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：无——仅测试与文档状态行，不改生产代码。
- 未验证/范围外：macOS 与 Windows 上游车道。后续在 `8365a90f` 使用 Node 24 完成 web-shell 全量套件（623 files / 17,634 tests）和根 build/typecheck/bundle，再用所得 bundle 完成真实 daemon + Vite + Chromium 的十项验收；这些是本机通过结果，不等同于上游 macOS/Windows 车道。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。

设计文档双语更新（仅状态行）：[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-18-artifacts-entry-opens-right-panel.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-11-18-artifacts-entry-opens-right-panel.zh-CN.md)。

## 关联 Issue

#17689 的跟进，处理其第 5 轮评审发现（serialize 回环钉、零产物 App 层见证、抽屉焦点恢复覆盖、设计文档状态漂移）。

prs.title: feat(web-shell): decouple ChatEditor daemon toolbar and upload imports (slice 6b)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR implements Slice 6b of the unified chat surface roadmap by decoupling the shared composer editor and workspace file-upload hook from all remaining daemon-only toolbar and availability imports, burning down the managed host entry point's transitive daemon value-import ratchet by fifteen edges (from thirty-one down to sixteen).

- **Backend-neutral service availability bridge:** Extracts a backend-neutral service availability context and unavailable-error base class with zero daemon imports so the shared file-upload hook no longer imports daemon availability modules. The daemon availability context re-exports the exact same React context instance and the daemon unavailable error subclasses the neutral base error, preserving full runtime compatibility with all existing daemon providers and error checks.
- **Explicit composer integration injection:** Replaces static value imports of the daemon-only voice dictation button, live-voice button, and git branch-picker popover inside the shared composer editor with an optional integration prop populated by the two daemon chat hosts (the main application column and the split/side chat pane). Managed hosts omit the prop, eliminating all thirteen voice, live-voice, session-catalog, and branch-picker daemon edges from the managed host bundle graph.
- **Fail-closed gating and state cleanup:** Aligns git branch chip visibility and toolbar width measurement with actual control availability (keeping the draft git-mode selector working independently even when the branch picker is omitted), gates the mobile add-menu live-voice action on integration presence, and resets active voice and live-voice flags if integrations are absent or removed.
- **Tightened boundary ratchet and tests:** Removes all fifteen decoupled edges from the bidirectional managed-host AST boundary ratchet (thirty-one to sixteen), switches file-upload availability tests from module mocking to the live daemon availability context provider, and adds tests verifying omitted/removed integrations in the composer and integration wiring in both daemon chat hosts.

## Why it's needed

After Slice 6a locked in the fail-closed AST boundary guard and cleared the first sixteen leaf daemon imports, fifteen of the remaining thirty-one transitive daemon value-import edges in the managed host graph came exclusively through four static imports in the shared composer editor (file uploads, voice capture, live voice, and the git branch picker). Managed sessions never expose daemon voice controls or the daemon git branch picker, yet still pulled all fifteen daemon modules into the managed host dependency graph. Decoupling those four imports leaves only the sixteen transcript, message, and notification edges for the final Slice 6c cleanup.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run the web-shell unit test suite covering the AST boundary guard, file upload hook, daemon availability, composer editor, split chat pane, branch picker popover, voice and live-voice buttons, managed sessions page, workspace binding creator, build artifacts, and main application voice/branch/upload tests. Confirm that the boundary guard passes with zero chat-core violations, zero unresolved specifiers, and exactly sixteen remaining managed-host daemon edges (all fifteen composer/upload edges removed).
2. Confirm that in the shared composer editor, omitting the optional integration prop hides voice, live-voice, and branch-picker controls without leaving phantom branch measurement elements or a broken mobile live-voice menu item, while keeping the draft git-mode selector functional and resetting active voice state if integrations are removed.
3. Confirm that file uploads under a live daemon availability provider still halt the remaining queue and map unavailable errors identically to main.
4. Build both the main web-shell package and the standalone managed-host bundle, run ESLint, Prettier, and the full-repository TypeScript typecheck (including integration test typechecking), and run the Playwright Chromium end-to-end suites covering branch checkout resolution, git-mode selection, managed attachments, split persistence, and voice capture, confirming zero console or page errors.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-user-visible internal module decoupling; daemon and managed chat surfaces retain identical UI and runtime behavior).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS development environment: Vitest (12 affected web-shell test suites / 1,337 tests passed, including the AST boundary guard at 16 remaining edges and 47 build-artifact checks, plus 48 main-shell voice/branch/upload tests), web-shell and managed-host production builds, ESLint (`--max-warnings=0`), Prettier check, full-repository `npm run typecheck` (including integration-tests `nodenext` resolution), and checked-in Playwright Chromium end-to-end suites for branch checkout resolution, git-mode selection, managed attachments, split persistence, and smoke voice tests (29/29 passed).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Any future daemon host that renders the shared composer editor directly and expects daemon voice, live-voice, or branch-picker controls must pass the daemon composer integrations constant (currently both daemon production chat columns do so and are covered by unit tests). Managed hosts intentionally omit it so daemon modules stay out of the managed bundle.
- Not validated / out of scope: The final sixteen transitive daemon value-import edges in the managed host graph (transcript viewport, turn outputs, tool approval notifications, and system/status messages) plus the final CI bundle-artifact check are deferred to Slice 6c.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. No HTTP/SSE routes, OpenAPI schemas, storage keys, i18n keys, or user-visible behaviors change.
- Design documentation: [English design doc](docs/design/2026-11-27-chat-editor-daemon-decoupling.md) | [中文设计文档](docs/design/2026-11-27-chat-editor-daemon-decoupling.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #17460

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

本 PR 实现统一聊天界面路线图的切片 6b，将共享输入编辑器与工作区文件上传 hook 从全部剩余的 daemon 专属工具栏与可用性导入中解耦，使托管宿主入口的传递 daemon 值导入棘轮减少十五条边（从三十一条降至十六条）。

- **后端中立服务可用性桥：** 抽出零 daemon 导入的服务可用性上下文与服务不可用错误基类，使共享文件上传 hook 不再导入 daemon 可用性模块。daemon 可用性上下文直接复用同一个 React 上下文实例，daemon 不可用错误继承该中立基类，与全部既有 daemon Provider 与错误判定保持完全运行时兼容。
- **显式编辑器集成注入：** 将共享输入编辑器内对 daemon 专属语音转写按钮、实时语音按钮与 Git 分支选择浮层的静态值导入替换为可选集成属性，由两处 daemon 聊天宿主（主应用列与分屏/侧边窗格）显式注入；托管宿主省略该属性，从而从托管宿主打包依赖图中彻底消除全部十三条语音、实时语音、会话目录与分支选择 daemon 边。
- **Fail-closed 门控与状态清理：** 使 Git 分支标签可见性与工具栏宽度测量与实际可用控件保持一致（未注入分支选择器时草稿态 Git 模式选择器仍独立可用），按集成是否存在门控移动端添加菜单中的实时语音入口，并在集成缺失或被移除时重置活跃语音与实时语音状态。
- **收紧边界棘轮与测试覆盖：** 从托管宿主双向 AST 边界棘轮中移除全部十五条已解耦边（三十一条降至十六条），将文件上传可用性测试从模块 mock 切换为真实 daemon 可用性上下文 Provider，并补充输入编辑器省略/移除集成以及两处 daemon 聊天宿主正确注入集成的回归测试。

## 为什么需要这个改动

在切片 6a 落地 fail-closed AST 边界守卫并清除首批十六条叶节点 daemon 导入后，托管宿主依赖图中剩余三十一条传递 daemon 值导入边里有十五条全部经由共享输入编辑器的四处静态导入（文件上传、语音转写、实时语音与 Git 分支选择器）引入。托管会话从不展示 daemon 语音控件或 daemon 分支选择器，却仍被迫将这十五个 daemon 模块打入托管宿主依赖图。解耦这四处导入后，仅剩最后十六条转录、消息与通知边留待收官切片 6c 一次性清零。

## 评审测试计划

### 验证方法

1. 运行涵盖 AST 边界守卫、文件上传 hook、daemon 可用性、输入编辑器、分屏聊天窗格、分支选择浮层、语音与实时语音按钮、托管会话页、工作区绑定创建页、构建产物检查及主应用语音/分支/上传用例的 web-shell 单元测试套件，确认边界守卫零聊天核心违规、零未解析说明符、且托管宿主精确仅余十六条边（十五条编辑器/上传边全部清除）。
2. 确认共享输入编辑器在省略可选集成属性时隐藏语音、实时语音与分支选择控件，不残留无效分支宽度测量节点或移动端实时语音菜单项，同时草稿态 Git 模式选择器仍正常工作，且移除集成时活跃语音状态能干净复位。
3. 确认文件上传在真实 daemon 可用性 Provider 下发生传输失败后仍能阻断剩余队列并将不可用错误映射为与主分支一致的错误码。
4. 同时执行主 web-shell 包构建与独立托管宿主构建，运行 ESLint、Prettier 与全仓 TypeScript 类型检查（含集成测试模块解析），并运行覆盖分支切换冲突处理、Git 模式选择、托管附件上传、分屏持久化及语音转写的 Playwright Chromium 端到端套件，确认无控制台报错或页面错误。

### 对比证据（修改前 & 修改后）

N/A（非用户可见的内部模块解耦；daemon 与托管聊天界面保持完全一致的视觉与运行时行为）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 测试环境（可选）

本地 macOS 开发环境：Vitest（12 个受影响 web-shell 测试文件 / 1,337 项测试通过，含精确收紧至 16 边的 AST 边界守卫与 47 项构建产物检查，另加 48 项主应用语音/分支/上传用例）、web-shell 与托管宿主生产构建、ESLint（`--max-warnings=0`）、Prettier 格式检查、全仓 `npm run typecheck`（含集成测试 `nodenext` 解析）以及内置 Playwright Chromium 分支切换、Git 模式、托管附件、分屏持久化与语音冒烟端到端套件（29/29 通过）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：未来若新增直接渲染共享输入编辑器并需要 daemon 语音、实时语音或分支选择器的 daemon 宿主，需显式传入 daemon 编辑器集成常量（当前两处生产 daemon 聊天列均已注入且由单测覆盖）；托管宿主有意省略，以确保 daemon 模块不进入托管打包产物。

- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。未改动任何 HTTP/SSE 路由、OpenAPI schema、存储键、国际化文案键或用户可见行为。

prs.title: fix(autofix-pr): harden tracked-state guard, watch consent, and in-place skill rules
prs.body:
## TLDR

Addresses all 11 review findings (3 Critical and 8 Suggestion) from pull request #18521 after it merged: blocks forged git-tracked watch state files committed on a pull request branch, requires explicit watch consent when scheduling in-place watches, fixes in-place skill handling of clean local commits ahead of the pull request head and resumed local-checkout work, and aligns CLI help, user documentation, and sibling design docs.

集中修复 PR #18521 合入后遗留的全部 11 条评审发现（3 条 Critical 与 8 条 Suggestion）：拦住 PR 分支中通过 `git add -f` 提交的伪造状态文件、为定时 in-place 排程补齐显式 `--watch` 同意门控、修正 skill 对检出中 clean 领先提交及恢复期本地工作的误拦截，并同步对齐帮助文案、用户文档与关联设计文档。

## Dive Deeper

Following the merge of #18521, automated review identified three critical issues and eight polish/consistency items on the merged code:

- **Security — forged git-tracked state files and PR-number mismatch**: A contributor could force-add and commit a crafted in-place watch state file on a pull request branch so a maintainer resuming in-place mode would adopt forged handled comments, push counts, or instructions and bless the checkout with a trust anchor. In-place preparation now fails closed before network calls and again under the watch lock whenever the watch state file is tracked in the git index (case-insensitively across platforms) or records a different pull request number.
- **Explicit scheduled-watch consent for in-place mode**: One-shot in-place runs previously produced state indistinguishable from a scheduled in-place start, allowing scheduling to accept an unconsented one-shot state. Preparation now accepts a watch consent flag alongside in-place mode and records that consent in state, so scheduling refuses one-shot in-place states while preserving compatibility with already-scheduled watches and resumes. Non-collaborator refusal text also names one-shot in-place alongside worktree one-shot mode.
- **In-place skill semantics for clean unpushed commits and resumed local work**: Resuming an in-place watch whose checkout holds uncommitted edits or local commits no longer hits the worktree-only warning that claims a later push from the user's checkout would be refused; instead it reports them as the user's own work and proceeds safely. Likewise, when synchronization reports a clean in-place checkout with local commits ahead of the pull request head, rounds no longer route to discard or stop — they continue so the user's commits push along with the fix once approved. One-shot starts inside an already-running watch also report that the existing watch continues running.
- **Consistency, deduplication, and test coverage**: Updated ownership-refusal guidance for unscheduled in-place watches to suggest the in-place watch command instead of the bare worktree command, updated CLI option help and comments, scoped all worktree-only statements in user documentation and sibling design documents (both English and Chinese), shared take-over and repository-mismatch helpers across classic and in-place preparation, and added discriminating tests for remote-head fetch on resume and same-session take-over.

### Before / After & Verification Evidence (改动前后实测对照)

Before this change, scheduling accepted a one-shot in-place state that had never consented to scheduled rounds; after this change, scheduling refuses unconsented one-shot states and preparation rejects forged git-tracked state files committed on the branch:

![Before vs After watch consent gate and git-tracked state refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/037da12e57b129609a90e4e25b59786d713bac4c/03-followup-forged-state-and-watch-gate.png)

Verification suite results on the follow-up branch across CLI helpers, integration chain, core tool, bundled skill contract, and tool surface budget:

![Verification test suite results on the follow-up branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/037da12e57b129609a90e4e25b59786d713bac4c/04-followup-verification-tests.png)

## Reviewer Test Plan

How to verify:

1. **Forged git-tracked state file refusal**: On a pull request branch where a contributor force-added and committed a watch state file under `.qwen/tmp/`, run `/autofix-pr <pr> --in-place --watch` (with or without take-over). Verify preparation refuses immediately stating the state file is tracked by git, leaves the tracked file untouched, and writes no trust anchor. Also verify an untracked state file whose recorded pull request number does not match the requested pull request is refused.
2. **One-shot in-place watch consent gate**: Prepare a one-shot in-place watch without the watch flag and attempt to schedule it. Verify scheduling refuses and directs the user to start a scheduled watch with `--in-place --watch`; verify preparing with `--in-place --watch` (or resuming an already-scheduled in-place watch) allows scheduling cleanly.
3. **Clean local commits ahead and resumed dirty checkouts in in-place mode**: On a scheduled in-place watch where the user committed cleanly ahead of the pull request head, verify synchronization reports the local commits without attempting discard or halting the round, and pushing carries the commits on top of the pull request head once approved. On a resumed in-place watch with uncommitted edits or local commits, verify the start no longer warns that pushes from the user's checkout would be refused, and a one-shot run inside a running watch reports that the existing watch continues running.
4. **Take-over guidance, documentation, and regressions**: Verify another session hitting an unscheduled in-place watch receives take-over guidance naming `--in-place --watch`, same-session take-over does not falsely mark the watch as taken over, resuming when the remote head advanced fetches the new head so behind-vs-unknown reporting stays accurate, and user documentation plus both English and Chinese design docs match the implemented behavior.

## Testing Matrix

|          | 🍏  | 🪟  | 🐧  |
| -------- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm run  | ❓  | ❓  | ✅  |
| npx      | ❓  | ❓  | ✅  |
| Docker   | ❓  | ❓  | ❓  |
| Podman   | ❓  | ❓  | ❓  |
| Seatbelt | ❓  | ❓  | ❓  |

## Linked issues / bugs

Follow-up addressing all 11 review comments from #18521.

prs.title: feat(verify-pr): add host capability probes and per-round VM staging
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This change closes the remaining host-side Phase 2 gaps for hardware-isolated `/verify-pr` microVM rounds so operators no longer need ad-hoc shell glue to probe host readiness or prepare per-round VMM workspaces, and also folds in the five deferred non-blocking test and documentation follow-ups recorded at the end of PR #18400.

First, it adds fail-closed host capability probing for both Linux KVM and Apple Silicon macOS. On Linux, probing opens the KVM character device directly without following symlinks, checks cgroup v2 controller availability and non-root VMM user/group identity, and verifies real Firecracker and jailer executable versions. On Apple Silicon macOS, probing checks that the local virtualization binary carries the Apple virtualization entitlement via `codesign` (rejecting unsigned or hollow binaries) and executes a live deny-default Seatbelt enforcement probe in a clean environment that must simultaneously pass inside-sandbox read/write positive controls and block outside-sandbox canary read/write negative controls. The runner CLI now exposes a dedicated probe subcommand and a `--probe` mode for backend selection that refuses mixing live probing with manual capability flags or omitted option values.

Second, it adds an official minimal deny-default macOS Seatbelt profile template and fail-closed per-round asset staging for both Firecracker and macOS virtualization backends. Per-round staging copies read-only golden kernel, initramfs, and rootfs images into independently owned files inside approved roots while verifying single-link non-symlink sources, distinct destination inodes, SHA-256 parity, no overwrites, and automatic rollback of every newly created file and directory on error. For Firecracker, it atomically writes the jailed configuration and console log, applies non-root ownership when running as root, and verifies on-disk configuration parity against the validated launch plan before spawning so tampered on-disk configurations (such as an injected network interface) are refused fail-closed. The orchestrator accepts an opt-in staging flag while preserving full backward compatibility with manual staging and legacy container, manual VM, and waived flows.

Third, it lands the five deferred follow-up refinements from PR #18400: deterministic assertion that the guest bridge listen backlog is at least 128, deriving the slot-saturation hold count from the bridge's declared connection cap, parameterizing input-promotion rollback coverage across all three staged filenames, wrapping burst failure-attribution dumps so dump errors never mask the original test failure, and aligning the historical R3 section wording in the bilingual round-input hardening design documents with the subsequent R4 section.

## Why it's needed

Until now, hardware-isolated backend selection trusted manual CLI flags without verifying whether KVM or macOS Seatbelt was genuinely enforcing, and running a real Firecracker or macOS microVM required out-of-tree scripts to create jail directories, copy golden disks safely, author Seatbelt policies, and write Firecracker configurations. Moving live capability probing, Seatbelt policy rendering, per-round asset derivation, and on-disk Firecracker configuration verification into the repository eliminates that unreviewed glue, prevents hollow binaries or permissive sandboxes from passing readiness checks, blocks tampered on-disk VM configurations before spawn, and retires all five follow-up items deferred from #18400.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run the focused host-probing, runner, channel, and credential-scan script unit tests on macOS arm64 and confirm that live Seatbelt enforcement passes its positive inside-sandbox read/write controls, rejects a permissive allow-default profile, rejects symlinked and hardlinked profiles, denies outbound TCP to a local canary listener (while an unsandboxed control reaches that listener), and refuses a hollow virtualization binary lacking the virtualization entitlement via real `codesign`.
- Verify CLI backend probing and selection behavior: confirming structured JSON output with non-zero exit when no hardware backend is ready, zero exit when a hardware backend or provider is configured, automatic hardware backend selection under live probing, and usage error exit code 2 when mixing live probing with manual flags or passing missing/invalid option values.
- Verify per-round asset staging and rollback behavior for both Firecracker and macOS virtualization plans: confirming independent destination inodes, SHA-256 parity, overwrite/symlink/hardlink/vault/approved-root refusals, broken-symlink profile rejection, complete rollback on mid-staging or pre-launch failure, acceptance of key-reordered valid Firecracker configs, and fail-closed rejection when an on-disk Firecracker config injects a network interface.
- On a Linux host with `/dev/kvm`, cgroup v2, and Firecracker/jailer installed, confirm live CLI probing reports KVM ready and selects Firecracker, and confirm an end-to-end hardware round with opt-in staging boots a real Firecracker microVM with zero manual directory/disk/config setup, completes guest vsock input/model-proxy/artifact exchange, writes a `microvm` boundary declaration, removes all per-round jail artifacts on teardown, and leaves read-only golden kernel/rootfs hashes unchanged.
- Verify the five PR #18400 follow-ups: the bridge burst test deterministically fails if the guest listen backlog is lowered back to 32, slot-saturation counts follow the declared guest cap, promotion rollback fails cleanly on each of the three staged input filenames without touching sentinel files, and attribution dump errors cannot hide the underlying burst failure.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI host verification tooling, tests, and design documents).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

- **macOS arm64 / Node 24.18.1:** 4 focused script test suites passed (**76 passed, 0 failed**), including live `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` positive/negative filesystem controls, permissive/symlink/hardlink profile rejection, live local TCP canary outbound denial (with unsandboxed positive control), and real `/usr/bin/codesign` hollow-binary rejection; full repository `npm run lint` and Prettier passed cleanly.
- **Linux aarch64 / Node 22.23.5 (authorized KVM host):** all 12 `/verify-pr` script unit test files passed (**549 passed, 9 environment skips**); reverting the guest listen backlog to 32 deterministically killed the burst test; live CLI probing detected `/dev/kvm`, cgroup v2, `Firecracker v1.18.0`, and `Jailer v1.18.0` and selected `firecracker`; a zero-manual-staging end-to-end Firecracker/KVM round completed with 15 guest assertions passed, no NIC, no directory share, `complete` output, `destroyed` teardown, `microvm` boundary output, zero residual jail/disk files, unchanged golden kernel/rootfs hashes, and pre-launch blocking of a tampered on-disk Firecracker config injecting a network interface.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Live macOS Seatbelt probing executes `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` in a temporary directory and assumes Apple's `system.sb` base profile remains available on supported macOS versions; if Seatbelt ever stops enforcing or changes incompatibly, the probe fails closed rather than silently falling back to an unconfined VMM.
- Not validated / out of scope: Live macOS `vfkit` microVM boot was not run because no `vfkit` binary is installed on the local macOS test machine (macOS verification covered real Seatbelt enforcement, TCP denial, and real `codesign` entitlement checks). Windows IPC, cloud `provider-vm` / Agent Sandbox allocations, external model endpoints, and changes under `packages/`, `.github/`, `.qwen/skills/`, or `/review` are out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Opt-in asset staging defaults to off, manual backend selection flags continue to work identically, and legacy `container`, manual `vm`, and `waived` `/verify-pr` flows remain unchanged.
- Design documentation: [English design doc](docs/design/2026-11-27-verify-pr-vm-host-staging.md) | [中文设计文档](docs/design/2026-11-27-verify-pr-vm-host-staging.zh-CN.md) (and historical R3/R4 cross-reference sync in [English](docs/design/2026-11-25-verify-pr-round-input-hardening.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-25-verify-pr-round-input-hardening.zh-CN.md)).

## Linked Issues

Follows up on #18400 (retiring all five deferred R5 suggestions) and advances the tiered microVM roadmap from #18181, #18221, and #18277.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

本次改动补齐硬件隔离 `/verify-pr` microVM 的阶段 2 宿主侧缺口，使维护者无需手工胶水脚本即可完成真实宿主能力探测与每轮 VMM 工作区安全派生，同时一并落盘 PR #18400 在第 5 轮评审中登记延期的 5 项非阻断测试与文档收尾改动。

第一，新增面向 Linux KVM 与 Apple Silicon macOS 的 fail-closed 真实宿主能力探测。Linux 侧不跟随符号链接直接打开 `/dev/kvm` 字符设备、核验 cgroup v2 控制器与非 root VMM 用户/组身份，并实测真实 Firecracker 与 jailer 可执行文件版本；macOS Apple Silicon 侧通过真实 `codesign` 校验本地虚拟化二进制包含 Apple 虚拟化 entitlement（拒绝未签名或空壳二进制），并在纯净环境中运行真实 deny-default Seatbelt 活性探针，必须同时满足沙箱内读/写正对照通过且沙箱外宿主 canary 读/写负对照被拒绝。Runner CLI 新增独立 `probe` 子命令及 `select --probe` 选项，并显式拒绝把实时探测与手工能力旗标混用或省略参数值。

第二，提供仓库正式托管的最小 deny-default macOS Seatbelt 策略模板以及面向 Firecracker 与 macOS 虚拟化后端的 fail-closed 每轮资产 staging。每轮 staging 将只读 golden kernel、initramfs 与 rootfs 独立拷贝到批准根目录内，强制校验单链接非符号链接源文件、目标独立 inode、SHA-256 一致性、禁止覆写，以及任意步骤失败时自动回滚清理所有新建文件与目录。对 Firecracker 后端，自动原子写出隔离配置与控制台日志、在 root 运行下安全赋权，并在启动前校验磁盘配置与已验证启动计划深度一致，从而 fail-closed 拦截被篡改的磁盘配置（例如被注入网卡）。编排器新增默认关闭的可选 staging 开关，完整保持对既有手工流程以及 legacy container、手动 vm 和 waived 流程的向后兼容。

第三，落盘 PR #18400 登记延期的 5 项收尾改进：为 guest bridge 监听队列不低于 128 增加确定性断言、从 guest 源码常量派生槽位饱和保持数、将输入提升回滚用例参数化覆盖全部三个暂存文件名、把 burst 失败归因转储整体包入异常捕获以确保绝不掩盖原始失败错误，并使中英文输入加固设计文档中历史 R3 段落与后续 R4 段落交叉对齐。

## 为什么需要

此前硬件隔离后端选择只依赖人工传入的布尔旗标，无法核实 KVM 或 macOS Seatbelt 是否真正生效；运行真实 Firecracker 或 macOS microVM 仍需仓库外脚本手工建 jail 目录、复制工作盘、手写 Seatbelt 策略并生成 Firecracker 配置。把实时能力探测、Seatbelt 策略渲染、每轮资产独立派生与磁盘配置一致性校验正式收口入库，消除了未经审阅的外部胶水，防止空壳二进制或宽松沙箱通过就绪检查，在启动前拦住被篡改的磁盘 VM 配置，并完整收尾 #18400 遗留的 5 项建议。

## 审阅测试计划

### 验证步骤

- 在 macOS arm64 上运行聚焦的宿主探测、编排器、通道与凭据扫描单测，确认真实 Seatbelt 活性探针通过沙箱内读写正对照、拒绝宽松 `allow default` / 符号链接 / 硬链接策略、阻断向本地 TCP canary 的出站连接（同时无沙箱正对照可连上该 canary），并通过真实 `codesign` 拒绝缺少虚拟化 entitlement 的空壳二进制。
- 验证 CLI 能力探测与后端选择行为：无可用硬件后端时输出结构化 JSON 并返回非 0，有硬件后端或 provider 配置时返回 0，`select --probe` 自动选出硬件后端，混用 `--probe` 与手工旗标或参数缺值/非法时返回退出码 2。
- 验证 Firecracker 与 macOS 虚拟化计划的每轮资产 staging 与回滚行为：确认独立目标 inode、SHA-256 一致性、拒绝覆写/符号链接/硬链接/vault 越界/批准根目录越界、拒绝悬空符号链接策略、中途失败或启动前失败完整回滚、接受键序重排的合法 Firecracker 配置，以及在启动前 fail-closed 拦截注入网卡的篡改磁盘配置。
- 在具备 `/dev/kvm`、cgroup v2 与 Firecracker/jailer 的 Linux 主机上，确认 CLI `probe` 报告 KVM 就绪并自动选出 Firecracker；确认开启 staging 的端到端硬件轮次在零手工目录/磁盘/配置准备下成功拉起真实 Firecracker microVM、完成 guest vsock 输入/模型代理/产物上传、写出 `microvm` 边界声明、销毁后彻底清零每轮 jail 产物，且只读 golden kernel/rootfs 哈希不变。
- 验证 #18400 的 5 项收尾：将 guest 监听队列改回 32 时 burst 测试确定性失败、槽位饱和保持数随 guest 上限常量派生、三个暂存名各自被阻塞时均干净回滚且保留哨兵文件、归因转储异常不会覆盖原始测试失败。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A（非 UI 的宿主验证工具、测试与设计文档）。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 运行环境（可选）

- **macOS arm64 / Node 24.18.1：**4 套聚焦脚本单测通过（**76 通过，0 失败**），覆盖真实 `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` 读写正负对照、宽松/符号链接/硬链接策略拒绝、真实本地 TCP canary 出站拒绝（含无沙箱正对照）与真实 `/usr/bin/codesign` 空壳二进制拒绝；仓库完整 `npm run lint` 与 Prettier 均通过。
- **Linux aarch64 / Node 22.23.5（授权 KVM 主机）：**全部 12 份 `/verify-pr` 脚本单测通过（**549 通过，9 项环境跳过**）；将 guest 监听队列改回 32 时 burst 测试确定性击杀；实时 CLI 探测检出 `/dev/kvm`、cgroup v2、`Firecracker v1.18.0` 与 `Jailer v1.18.0` 并自动选出 `firecracker`；零手工 staging 真实 Firecracker/KVM 端到端轮次通过 15 项 guest 断言、无 NIC、无目录共享、`complete` 输出、`destroyed` 清理、产出 `microvm` 边界、零残留 jail/工作盘、只读 golden kernel/rootfs 哈希不变，且在启动前拦截注入网卡的篡改磁盘配置。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：macOS 实时 Seatbelt 探针依赖 `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` 与 Apple 的 `system.sb` 基础策略；若宿主环境不支持或策略不再强制生效，探针会 fail-closed 拒绝，而不会静默回退到无沙箱 VMM。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：本地 macOS 测试机未安装 `vfkit` 二进制，因此未运行真实 macOS `vfkit` microVM 启动（macOS 实测覆盖真实 Seatbelt enforcing、TCP 拒绝与真实 `codesign` entitlement 校验）。Windows IPC、云端 `provider-vm` / Agent Sandbox 分配、外部模型端点，以及 `packages/`、`.github/`、`.qwen/skills/`、`/review` 均不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。资产自动 staging 默认关闭，原有手工后端选择旗标行为不变，legacy `container`、手动 `vm` 与 `waived` `/verify-pr` 流程保持完全兼容。
- 设计文档：[英文设计文档](docs/design/2026-11-27-verify-pr-vm-host-staging.md) | [中文设计文档](docs/design/2026-11-27-verify-pr-vm-host-staging.zh-CN.md)（并同步收紧 [英文](docs/design/2026-11-25-verify-pr-round-input-hardening.md) / [中文](docs/design/2026-11-25-verify-pr-round-input-hardening.zh-CN.md) 中历史 R3 与 R4 的交叉说明）。

## 关联 Issue

跟进 #18400（关闭全部 5 项第 5 轮延期建议），并继续推进 #18181、#18221、#18277 建立的分层 microVM 路线。

</details>

issues.title: compaction: loose scan can delete a user turn that pastes the summary header

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Where

`crates/tui/src/compaction.rs:330-345` (as of the Pinvou fork's `pinvou3-clean` head `cc2adf8ef`, which tracks this repository's maintenance line).

## What

When compacting a history that has no provenance-stamped checkpoint carrier, the engine locates "the first user message that starts with the summary header" via a loose scan and `retain`-deletes it before inserting the new stamped checkpoint in its place. The code's own comment acknowledges it "cannot tell a pre-provenance carrier from a user turn that pastes the whole summary header".

Concretely: if a user genuinely typed (or pasted) a message that begins with the compaction summary header in a pre-provenance-era session, the next compaction silently deletes that user turn and replaces it with the checkpoint. That is engine-side data loss of real user input — the downstream app's display-side hardening (keeping bare carriers visible in the UI) cannot recover a turn that no longer exists in the transcript.

## Suggested fix

Before deleting a matched user turn, require evidence that it is actually an engine-written carrier rather than user content, e.g. any of:

- carrier-adjacent metadata/topology evidence (the assistant-turn pattern the engine itself produces right after a compaction),
- an explicit engine-only marker,
- or (minimal) restrict the loose scan to sessions whose checkpoint history is engine-managed, and keep pasted-header turns in place — insert the new checkpoint after them instead of replacing them.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Session predates the provenance stamp (no `<!-- codewhale.compaction-checkpoint.v1 -->` carriers).
2. A user message begins with the summary header text (typed or pasted).
3. Trigger compaction. Observe the user turn is removed and the stamped checkpoint takes its position.

Changelog Archive

Older releases of Codewhale (v0.8.39 and earlier). Recent releases live in CHANGELOG.md.

[0.8.39] - 2026-05-17

Fixed

  • Feishu/Lark bridge startup order is guarded. The bridge now keeps ThreadStore initialized before startup opens persisted thread state, with a regression test to prevent moving it below its first use.
  • /model picker opens instantly with the curated list again. Reverted the v0.8.38 live-catalog rework: the picker no longer makes a blocking network call on open and once again shows the curated auto / deepseek-v4-pro / deepseek-v4-flash rows. The /models command still lists the live provider catalog.
  • "Approve for session" groups by command family again. Session approvals are keyed by a lossy, arity-aware fingerprint once more, so approving cargo build also covers cargo build --release. Denials keep the exact per-call fingerprint from #1617, so denying one call no longer over-blocks later, different calls to the same tool.
  • Docker first-run state directories are writable. The image now pre-creates /home/deepseek/.deepseek with deepseek ownership so the documented named-volume launch can create runtime thread state on first use (#1684).
  • Runtime API system prompt overrides survive the first turn. Threads created with a system_prompt override now keep that prompt through mode/context refreshes before the model request is built (#1688).
  • Compaction keeps a user text query in tool-heavy histories. Automatic compaction now pins the latest user text message when the retained tail only contains tool calls/results, avoiding OpenAI-compatible Jinja template failures on the next request (#1704).
  • Pager jumps land at the visible bottom. Pressing G or End in the pager no longer overshoots the render clamp, so k/Up scrolls upward immediately afterward, and mouse wheels now scroll pager overlays directly (#1706, #1716).
  • Mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling preserves composer drafts. When composer_arrows_scroll is enabled, Up/Down now scroll the transcript even with text in the composer instead of replacing the draft with input history (#1677).
  • Multiline composer arrows move between input lines. Plain Up/Down now move the cursor within multiline drafts before falling back to input history, while single-line mouse-wheel-as-arrow scrolling remains unchanged (#1721).
  • Third-party reasoning_content streams no longer corrupt text output. Generic OpenAI-compatible providers that stream answer text in reasoning_content now render it as normal text unless the selected provider is one whose reasoning-content semantics are supported (#1673).
  • macOS system theme detection recognizes Light mode. When COLORFGBG is missing or unusable, theme = "system" now falls back to macOS appearance detection and treats a missing AppleInterfaceStyle key as Light mode

Release notes

Sourced from gix's releases.

gix v0.91.0

Bug Fixes (BREAKING)

  • share received packs and shallow metadata A straight-forward wiring of the core.sharedRepository flag.

    Fetching into a shared repository must make received packs, pack indices, and shallow boundaries accessible according to core.sharedRepository.

    Pass the repository policy through pack-writing and protocol-fetch options. Create immutable pack and index files with appropriate initial permissions, share new destination directories, and keep .keep markers private. Preserve pre-existing markers and their ownership so the receiver does not remove another operation's marker. A tempfile constructor accepts creation permissions without bypassing the process umask.

  • apply sharing to loose object writes A very straight-forward wiring of shared repository permissions down to loose object writes.

    Shared refs are insufficient when loose objects remain private. Propagate the resolved repository policy through object-store initialization and each handle's loose-object writes, applying it before publishing objects and to newly created fanout directories.

    Keep objects read-only. Runtime configuration changes and reloads affect the next write through the current handle without changing other handles, including cloned and thread-safe round trips. Cover both object hash formats and update the existing repository-size guard for the measured Windows layout.

  • preserve configuration permissions during branch deletion and clone Straightforward, it leverages the new config_file_mut() to change the configuration, which automatically feeds the lock file with the shared permissions settings.

    Deleting branch configuration and adopting a cloned remote's object format must preserve an existing configuration file's explicit permissions, even when core.sharedRepository is enabled.

    Use the existing FileTransaction for both updates. This preserves the configuration mode and follows the transaction's symlink and locking behavior while retaining branch deletion's partial-success error reporting. Regression coverage checks that an explicit 0600 config stays private, matching Git.

  • apply sharing to reference, index, and worktree writes This change is mostly tests, and the shared_repository_permissions wired through to gix-index, gix-merge and gix-ref. Tests mostly rubber-stamped, but made it use test scripts more.

    Reference, index, and linked-worktree metadata writes must apply the effective

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

Besides that, the tracing of all commands was greatly improved.

Changed

    Keep gix and its plumbing on Rust 1.88. The supported library API does not require a broad move to Rust 1.99, as experimental module gates can use inline bodies with include! on the existing MSRV.

    Declare Rust 1.91 for gitoxide, gix-tix, and internal-tools to match the tooling dependencies, and make gitoxide-core's Rust 1.88 requirement explicit. Document the per-crate MSRV policy and express Tix's existing seven-day log retention with Duration::from_hours.

prs.title: fix(tui): open inline skill completion after CJK text
prs.body:
## What and why

An inline skill mention (`/my-review` or `$my-review` inside a message) only opens the skill completion popup when the `/` or `$` follows whitespace or an ASCII bracket or quote. Chinese and Japanese text has no spaces between words, so `请用$my` or `请用/my` shows nothing, while `please use $my` lists `$my-review`.

This is the same check #7258 relaxed for `@` file mentions. `is_inline_skill_mention_start` now also accepts a CJK character before the trigger, using the same `codewhale_tui_kit::translation::is_cjk`, so `（$my` and `看看，/my` open the popup too. A `/` after ASCII text, as in `path/my`, still doesn't open it.

One side effect: in `是/否`, the popup briefly lists every skill right after the `/` is typed and closes once `否` is typed, because skill names are ASCII and the partial no longer matches. Pressing Enter right after a trailing `/` picks a skill, which is what `please use /` already does.

## Where this came from

Bug fix, a sister of #7258.

## How I tested it

- Added `inline_skill_popup_opens_directly_after_cjk_text`. It covers `请用/my`, `请用$my`, `（$my` and `看看，/my`, and checks that `path/my` stays closed. Without the `is_cjk` line it fails on the first input with `left: []` against `right: ["/my-review"]`.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib` filtered to `inline_skill` (6), `slash` (88), `skill` (121) and `mention` (90): all pass.
- `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib tui::`: 3998 passed. The 1 failure is `config_panel_golden_at_eighty_and_one_twenty`, and it fails the same way on `main` (a66823523) on this machine. Its Reduce motion row renders `○ Off (ef...` here.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features --locked` with CI's `-D warnings` and allow flags: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it): n/a, bug fix

prs.title: fix(engine): preserve pasted summary headers during compaction
prs.body:
## What and why

Compaction could replace a real user message that began with the exact legacy summary header. This change uses checkpoint structure and provenance to choose what it can replace. A bare header follows the normal user-text retention budget. When a pasted header shares a message with a tool result, the result stays only if its matching call survives.

The next compaction replaces the previous verified checkpoint. A legacy checkpoint can be identified during restore when the saved system summary matches it. An older save with only a bare history row keeps that row as conversation text. Under pressure this can make compaction preserve the original history and report that it could not shrink it. The published era-based retention API keeps its existing behavior.

## Where this came from

Closes #7562. Thanks for tracing the compaction-time deletion and separating it from the restore case.

## How I tested it

- The baseline compaction path dropped the pasted text. The isolated harness used the production selection, replacement, and shrink checks and reported `test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s`. With a fixed summary response, two consecutive passes reduced the fixture from 2,429 to 809 and from 3,068 to 809 estimated tokens. The pasted text survived exactly once, each tool result kept its matching call, and the previous checkpoint was replaced.
- The same harness covered an older bare TUI snapshot and a snapshot with separately saved summary data at both a tight and a wide budget. It also verified both era options on the published retention API.
- `cargo check --locked --offline -j 1 -p codewhale-engine --lib` passed. A separate crate type-checked both era calls against the Engine library metadata. Format and whitespace checks passed.
- The local Engine libtest build stopped with SIGKILL during compilation after 27 minutes, before executing any libtest cases. The full regression target for CI is `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-engine --lib compaction::tests::compaction_safe_legacy_paste_shrinks_twice_with_complete_tool_pairs -- --exact`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`.
- [x] Formatting passes and regression tests cover the changed behavior.
- [x] Updated the compaction survival contract for this fix to existing behavior.

prs.title: feat(ci): add the maintainer gate and regression stage (#7433)
prs.body:
## What and why

Implements the protocol in #7433: a maintainer gate before agent work, and a regression stage after it.

- **Part 1 — startability is a grant.** The Agent task form no longer self-applies `agent-ready`. The metadata contract test now rejects the default instead of pinning it. CONTRIBUTING, ISSUE_TRIAGE, AGENT_ETHOS (en/zh), FLEET (en/zh), the fleet-manager skill and the remote-smoke runbook say that absence means not startable.
- **Part 2a — behavioural guards.** `crates/engine/tests/behavioural_guards.rs` holds one positive assertion per promise, each citing its issue: the agent-ready gate (#7433) and the tool-call fallback id rule (#7423). A rename can no longer invert it silently.
- **Part 2b — behaviour statements.** `scripts/check-behaviour-line.py` requires `Behaviour: <old> -> <new>` or `No-behaviour-change: <why>` on fix/feat/perf/refactor commits in the push range; it is wired into `scripts/preflight.sh` and the helper-contract CI step.
- **Part 3 — regression stage.** `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` names the per-slice review receipt (`review --base <sha> --path <path> --write-receipt`, then `--check-receipt`) as the regression pass. A receipt with unresolved risk blocks the candidate until a maintainer reads the findings.
- **Part 4/5 — triage standards.** ISSUE_TRIAGE gains Startability, the regression threshold, the severity mapping (`p1` minimum, `release-blocker` by maintainer decision, `p0` only for data loss/security/release path), the closing standard, and the #7432 disposition.
- **Part 5b — docs drift.** `scripts/check-docs-drift.py` requires a touched feature row to update its summary and to name its flag or id on the docs page it points at.

## Where this came from

Refs #7433. The protocol is forward-looking; #7432 is left open for the maintainer to resolve by restoring the parent index or correcting the docs.

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --test behavioural_guards` — 2 passed
- `cargo test -p codewhale-skills --lib` — 194 passed
- `bash .github/scripts/agent-task-metadata.test.sh` — passed
- `PYTHON=python bash scripts/check-behaviour-line.test.sh` — passed
- `python scripts/check-docs-drift.test.py` — 4 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed
- `python scripts/check-behaviour-line.py main HEAD` and `python scripts/check-docs-drift.py main HEAD` — passed on the four commits in this branch

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

issues.body:
## Problem
On iOS, child sessions can disappear from their parent in the sidebar when the parent is pinned or moved to a group.

## Reproduction
1. Create a parent session with a child and grandchild.
2. Give the child a different stored group from its parent.
3. Pin the parent or move it to another group, then open the sidebar.

Expected: the family remains together under the parent. Actual: descendants can be separated from their parent because placement is applied before the hierarchy is built.

## Evidence
A focused regression against the previous sidebar model fails two assertions and passes with the family-placement fix. A synthetic iOS simulator fixture exercises a parent, child and grandchild.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading to 2026.11.10, openclaw doctor reports that root MEMORY.md and USER.md for agent main are excluded from automatic context because their memory provenance is untrusted (last tracked write in early November; the files were later edited by the operator on the host and via shell). The docs (concepts/memory-provenance, cli/memory) explain how files become untrusted, but I couldn't find a supported way for the owner to review a file and mark it trusted again. Once untrusted, later owner writes keep it untrusted.

Questions:

Is there a command or UI action to accept the current content as trusted after review, for example openclaw memory trust --agent main --file MEMORY.md?
If not, is it planned? For now we work around it by having the agent read the files explicitly at session start.

Self-hosted, Docker, OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Agent "main" running on OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (Docker, self-hosted). Its root MEMORY.md and USER.md had been edited over time both by the agent and from the host shell.
2. Upgrade the gateway to 2026.11.10 (6ea542f) and run `openclaw doctor --fix` (migration), then start the gateway.
3. Run `openclaw doctor`.
   Observed: "Memory provenance" check -> "Agent "main": MEMORY.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-11-03T15:20:40.220Z, session agent:main:main." Same for USER.md (last tracked write 2026-11-02T08:02:03.575Z).
4. Start a new main session. Gateway log shows: "excluding MEMORY.md from automatic memory context: memory provenance is untrusted" (and the same for USER.md).
5. Look for a way to restore trust after review (`openclaw memory --help`, `openclaw doctor`, docs concepts/memory-provenance and cli/memory): no command or option found.

### Expected behavior

In 2026.11.7 (the version we ran before upgrading), root MEMORY.md and USER.md for agent "main" were loaded into automatic context on every main session. After upgrading to 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), they are excluded with "memory provenance is untrusted" (per docs: concepts/memory-provenance).

Expected: after the owner reviews the files, there should be a supported way to mark them trusted again (CLI command, doctor fix, or Control UI action), so they return to automatic context. The docs describe how a file becomes untrusted, and say later owner writes keep it untrusted, but describe no way to restore trust.

### Actual behavior

After upgrading to 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), root MEMORY.md and USER.md of agent "main" are no longer included in automatic context.

Evidence:
- `openclaw doctor` -> "Memory provenance" section, under "Fix now":
  "Agent "main": MEMORY.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-11-03T15:20:40.220Z, session agent:main:main."
  "Agent "main": USER.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-11-02T08:02:03.575Z, session agent:main:main."

issues.body:
### Bug type

Field incident report (production occurrence on latest stable; minimal standalone repro not yet isolated)

### Summary

On `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)` on native Linux `ext4`, `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-wal` (inode `174741`, held open by the running Gateway) was unlinked and recreated as a 0-byte file (inode `197613`, alongside a new `-shm` inode `197619`) while the Gateway was live and serving requests. Two seconds later, `audit/events` failed with `database disk image is malformed`, `evictOpenClawStateDatabaseAfterCorruption` evicted the shared-state handle, and ~3 minutes later `infra/sqlite-wal` fired `sqlite_wal_sidecar_identity_mismatch` and terminated the Gateway with `SIGKILL`. Restart then exited `78/CONFIG` on `SQLite integrity_check` failure.

Related prior issues: #163453 (closed stale as `not_planned`, no corruption), #156424 (open, `audit_events` index corruption), #126821 (open, WSL2 recurring corruption). Checked `v2026.12.1-beta.1` release notes; no matching fix for live WAL sidecar inode replacement is listed.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)` (npm global)
- Node.js: `v26.12.1` (bundled SQLite `3.54.0`)
- OS / kernel: Linux `7.0.0-44-generic` (native VPS, not WSL2)
- State filesystem: local `ext4` (`/dev/sda1`, `rw,relatime`, not network storage)
- Services: `openclaw-gateway.service` (systemd user) + `openclaw-node.service` (`openclaw node run ...`, which also holds a read descriptor on `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`)
- State DB size: ~304 MiB (`openclaw.sqlite`); main agent DB: ~9.0 GiB

### Observed Timeline (UTC, 2026-11-28)

1. `01:10:57Z` — Prior Gateway ended with `SIGKILL (gateway.restart_shutdown_timeout)` during a scheduled `--safe` restart; new Gateway (`PID 1858793`) started and opened `openclaw.sqlite-wal` (inode `174741`).
2. `02:20:20.181Z` — Last clean `audit_events` row written (`sequence=1939898`).
3. `02:20:26Z–02:20:38Z` — A periodic user timer ran 5 `openclaw gateway call sessions.list --json` CLI invocations (`[gateway/ws] client connected ... client=cli` at `02:20:28.082Z`, `02:20:29.959Z`, `02:20:31.821Z`, `02:20:33.644Z`, `02:20:35.525Z`). Verified separately while Gateway was stopped that `openclaw gateway call` opens `openclaw.sqlite` and updates `openclaw.sqlite-shm` mtime.
4. `02:20:31.784Z` — `stat` confirms both sidecars were newly created at this exact timestamp:
   - `openclaw.sqlite-wal`: `ino=197613`, `size=0`, `birth=02:20:31.784832863Z`, `mtime=02:20:31.920833829Z`
   - `openclaw.sqlite-shm`: `ino=197619`, `size=32768`, `birth=02:20:31.784832863Z`
   - `openclaw.sqlite`: `ino=179535` (unchanged, `birth=2026-11-25`), `mtime=02:20:38.921883577Z`
   - No backup service (last backup ran `2026-11-27 21:00Z`), manual `doctor`, or external SQLite writer ran at `02:20Z` (all local monitoring scripts use `?mode=ro`).
5. `02:20:33.887Z` — First corruption error in Gateway log:
   `[audit/events] audit event persistence failed: database disk image is malformed`
6. `02:20:35.302Z` — Cascade of `Error: Shared-state worker lost its retained native database` (`sessions/upstream-links`, `cron`, `tools`, `gateway`, `device-token`) and `Auth profile store ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite is unreadable; run openclaw doctor --fix. | AUTH_PROFILE_STORE_UNREADABLE`.
7. `02:23:20.011Z` — Periodic `infra/sqlite-wal` check tripped and self-killed Gateway:
   ```json
   {"level":"fatal","subsystem":"infra/sqlite-wal","message":"SQLite WAL sidecar identity mismatch; terminating without SQLite cleanup","event":"sqlite_wal_sidecar_identity_mismatch","databasePath":"~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite","descriptorDevice":"2049","descriptorInode":"174741","sidecarPath":"~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite-wal","targetDevice":"2049","targetInode":"197613","databaseLabel":"openclaw-state"}
   ```
8. `02:23:26Z–02:23:31Z` — Systemd auto-restart failed with `status=78/CONFIG`:
   ```text
   SQLite integrity_check failed for ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite: *** in database main ***
   Tree 19 page 19: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 20 page 77653: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 236 page 348: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 235 page 544: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 234 page 7388: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 234 page 234 right child: Child page depth differs
   ...
   Tree 101 page 77632: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 276 page 74163: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Tree 102 page 13649: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
   Page 350..17060: never used
   ```

### Forensic Damage Breakdown & Recovery

- Corrupt B-tree root pages were confined strictly to 3 actively written tables and their indexes: `sqlite_sequence` (19), `audit_events` (20 + indexes 21, 22, 229–236), and `plugin_state_entries` (101 + indexes 102, 276). All other 105 tables (`cron_jobs`, `secret_store_entries`, `device_pairing_paired`, `agent_databases`, `task_runs`, `subagent_runs`, etc.) were readable.
- `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` stalled in `Preserve original state` (documented separately on #178359).
- Recovery succeeded via offline `sqlite3 .recover` (0 errors; 35,606 orphan rows isolated to `lost_and_found`), dropping `lost_and_found`, rebuilding `sqlite_sequence`, `VACUUM`, restoring `user_version=40` / `auto_vacuum=2` / `journal_mode=WAL`, verifying `PRAGMA integrity_check = ok` and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check = []`. Gateway and `openclaw-node` restarted cleanly.

### What Is Established vs Unproven

- **Established:** On native Linux `ext4`, `openclaw.sqlite-wal` changed inode (`174741` → `197613`) at `02:20:31.784Z`—37 ms before a concurrent `openclaw gateway call` CLI WS connect (`02:20:31.821Z`)—while Gateway still held an open FD to inode `174741` and `openclaw-node` also held `openclaw.sqlite` open. B-tree corruption appeared 2 seconds later.
- **Unproven:** The exact internal call path that released Linux per-process `fcntl` locks or unlinked `-wal` under the live Gateway (e.g., whether an intra-process `fs.openSync`/`fs.closeSync` on the DB/sidecar cleared POSIX locks and allowed a concurrent `openclaw` CLI close to unlink `-wal`, or an `openclaw-node`/CLI interaction). Preserved raw pre-repair files are available locally if specific read-only diagnostics would help.

## Summary

Repository advisory publication and private-fork administration are still bundled with contributor skills, despite the skill ownership guide assigning private maintainer operations to `openclaw/maintainers`.

2. Read the GHSA skill: it owns advisory PATCH/publication, private-fork checks, and publication verification.
3. Follow the release skill's GHSA route, which still relies on the contributor bundle.

## Expected content

The maintainer repository owns the advisory-only procedure. Core directs maintainers to install and read it before an explicitly authorized advisory operation. Its policy references select the actual OpenClaw source checkout.

## Actual content and impact

The procedure lives in the contributor bundle, increasing that catalog's maintainer-only content and leaving no canonical maintainer installation route for it. This is an internal workflow ownership issue; product behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence and scope

Verified at `b3ba96f88c9a777800a15324f99410c9d32977e5`. The owner map assigns organization administration and private operations to the maintainer repository. The GHSA bundle is a single Markdown file with no helpers or tests. Preserve its procedure, licensing, disclosure restrictions, and explicit publish-permission requirement; land the destination before removing the core copy. No advisory operations or installed-skill changes are part of this move.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Opening or reopening a local Claude session from the Control UI catalog makes the composer ask for microphone options using the catalog entry’s key. The Gateway returns `No session found` because that key does not identify an OpenClaw chat session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Chromium, load the bundled Control UI with a Gateway fixture that exposes a resumable local Claude Code session. Use an operator who can read and continue the session.
2. Open the Claude session’s catalog entry, before continuing it, and inspect the Gateway RPCs. Reopen the original catalog URL and check again.
3. As a comparison, continue the session by sending a message, then reload the adopted OpenClaw chat.

### Expected behavior

Opening the catalog entry shows its native history without asking Talk for capabilities for the catalog key. Once the session is adopted, the composer can fetch microphone options using the adopted chat’s own key.

### Actual behavior

The composer sends `talk.catalog` with the catalog key on both the initial open and the reopen. The real Gateway logged `INVALID_REQUEST` / `No session found` for the original key; the logs do not identify which UI action initiated the call. The Chromium fixture reproduces the invalid call on the catalog route, not on reload of the adopted chat. Sending the first message still navigates to the adopted chat in the fixture.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (source package version in the reproduction build).

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (WSL); Chromium Control UI.

### Install method

Local source build. Browser regression test uses the bundled Control UI and a simulated Gateway.

### Model

Not applicable; the fixture does not request inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Local Claude Code session catalog → OpenClaw Control UI. The failed request is a Gateway RPC, not a model request.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The unpatched Chromium run recorded two `talk.catalog` requests with the catalog key on initial open and two on reopen. The patched run recorded zero on both and passed all three access scenarios: writer can continue and reload the adopted chat with history preserved; reader can view native history but cannot send; restricted Visitor cannot read or continue the catalog session.

### Impact and severity

The Control UI sends an invalid RPC when opening a local Claude catalog entry. The fixture did not show blocked adoption or lost history.

## Solution

Skip Talk discovery and dictation on external catalog routes. Keep Talk scoped to the adopted chat once it has a real Gateway session key.

## Out of scope

Redirecting old catalog URLs, changing permissions, or treating the error as evidence of lost session activity.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When model setup, through setup activation or the onboarding wizard, has written its config and a later step fails, the config write guard rejects setup's restore of the previous config as a size drop if setup more than doubled a small config, so setup fails with "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update …" (reproduced on main `cf95c48d9d` with two in-process regression tests).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out main at `cf95c48d9d`.
2. In `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, add a case next to "restores a first config write when its activation is not applied", with the same `setup.activate("api-key", true, { apiKey, onActivationCompletion })` call and `complete()` step, but with `fixture({ authMethod: "api_key", fresh: true, addProviderDuringLogin: true })`: the starting config is small and has no provider, and the sign-in adds the provider with its model catalog. No reloader runs, so the Gateway never applies the write and `complete()` restores the previous config. Expect the error to contain "The previous connection was restored on disk", as the existing case does.
3. In `src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`, add a case for the onboarding wizard: write `{ gateway: { mode: "local" } }` as the starting config, then pass a candidate that adds one provider with one model (the file's `providerConfig` and `modelDefinition`) to the file's `rejectActivation` helper, with a `createWizardInferenceConfigTarget(writeWizardConfigFile)` target and an activation error. Expect that activation error to be rethrown, as the other recovery cases in the file do.
4. Run `pnpm test src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Both new cases fail; the other 48 cases in the two files pass.

Outside these tests, setup reaches this restore when its config write succeeds and a later step fails, for example when a running Gateway does not apply the write (#183964 describes a hand-written first-run config with `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`). The restore is rejected when the setup-written config is at least 512 bytes and the restored config is less than half of it. Both points are from the code; they were not run end to end for this report.

### Expected behavior

Setup restores the config it had before the failed activation, as the existing restore cases in both files do. The setup activation case then reports "The previous connection was restored on disk, but the Gateway could not apply it. Restart the Gateway before chatting.", and the wizard case rethrows the activation error.

### Actual behavior

Both cases fail with:

"Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it preserves existing settings, then retry. If the saved config is already invalid, run openclaw doctor --fix first."

The config write guard logs one rejection per case, with the size drop as the only reason: `size-drop:1674->438` for setup activation and `size-drop:811->235` for the wizard. Each log line also reports the rejected payload saved next to the config.

The message's next step does not apply, because the blocked write is setup's own restore. In the code, the guard throws before writing (`src/config/io.write.ts:447-456`), and setup rolls back the new credential only after the config restore succeeds (`src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts:157-161`). These tests did not check the config file or the credential after the failure.

### OpenClaw version

main `cf95c48d9d` (package version `2026.11.5`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64), Node v24.22.1

### Install method

pnpm source checkout (in-process regression tests)

### Model

`openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `example/fixture` (synthetic test fixtures; no live model call)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> fixture providers registered by the tests (no network)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# Setup activation case, main cf95c48d9d with only the test changes:
Config write rejected: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:1674->438). Rejected payload saved to <state>/openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-20T09-42-49-284Z.
 × |infra| src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts > setup activation credentials and configuration > restores a size-dropping first config write when its activation is not applied 3164ms
Received: "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it preserves existing settings, then retry. If the saved config is already invalid, run openclaw doctor --fix first."
# Onboarding wizard case, same run:
Config write rejected: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:811->235). Rejected payload saved to <state>/openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-20T09-43-02-176Z.
 × |infra| src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts > wizard recovery restores a size-dropping provider write 2159ms
Received: "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it preserves existing settings, then retry. If the saved config is already invalid, run openclaw doctor --fix first."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

- Affected: setup activation and the onboarding wizard, as observed in the tests above, when they fail after writing the config and the config before setup is small compared with what setup writes, for example a new or nearly empty config.
- Severity: setup cannot put the previous config back, and the error asks the user to correct an update they did not make.
- Frequency: both cases failed in every run on main `cf95c48d9d`. How often real setups meet the size condition is not measured.
- Consequence: setup's restore is rejected, and the error's next step does not help.

### Additional information

- Cause, from the code: setup's restore is written by `captureSetupInferenceFileUndo` (`src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts:73-104`), whose write options never include `allowConfigSizeDrop`. The guard rejects a write when the config is at least 512 bytes before it and less than half that size after it (`src/config/io.write-safety.ts:586-593,603-613`). Setup activation and the onboarding wizard restore through this helper. The Gateway's automatic Codex setup also calls it; this report does not cover that entry.
- The restore helper and the guard are unchanged on main through `f7558cc8ff`, and the same code is in v2026.11.6.
- The same rejection follows the false connection-change error that #202459 addresses: in its provider-install setup test with the original, smaller fixture config, on main `0b4d5d08`, the guard logged `size-drop:1470->640`.
- #183964 fixed two other restore failures in the same path. #155427 changed this rejection's user-facing message. Draft #202108 passes `allowConfigSizeDrop` for the restore of its new first-agent step.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw update --yes` from 2026.11.3 to stable 2026.11.10 (WSL2 Ubuntu, systemd user gateway, npm/linuxbrew install, Node v26.12.1) fails in validating → candidate-doctor, then rolls back. The gateway never stops during that first attempt and stays on 2026.11.3.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d) on WSL2 Ubuntu with a systemd user gateway and Node v26.12.1, stable channel, with the gateway running.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite dry-run --session-sqlite-all-agents` on 2026.11.3 (observed result: 0 targets / 0 issues).
3. Run `openclaw update --yes` targeting npm latest 2026.11.10, with output redirected to a log (not piped to tail/head).
4. Observe the candidate-doctor failure and rollback below. The live gateway stays up on 2026.11.3.
5. Run `openclaw update repair --yes`. Observe `Stopped the managed Gateway for Doctor repair.` About 80 seconds later the Ubuntu WSL distro reset (Windows `wsl.exe` / `wslhost` spawn; WSL `system boot`). The repair process died, and `openclaw update status` showed an abandoned in-progress run (`phase: requested`, `status: running`, dead driver PID). After WSL came back, the gateway was healthy again on 2026.11.3.

### Expected behavior

Candidate Doctor should finish session repair (or skip/retry a store that is mid-close) without aborting the 2026.11.10 update. `update repair` / `doctor --fix` should not leave a stuck in-progress run if the environment restarts under them.

### Actual behavior

The update failed in validating → candidate-doctor and rolled back to 2026.11.3. The gateway did not stop during that first attempt.

Admission checks: config: warn, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok. The sqlite_stat4 / STAT4 schema issue is not the blocker here.

Phases: requested (~48s, package-install ok) → staging → validating (~522s). candidate-doctor ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` for ~59s in the canary snapshot. Built-in triage then timed out.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (847611d) installed; update target 2026.11.10 (npm latest / stable)

### Operating system

Windows host + WSL2 Ubuntu; systemd user service on port 18789

### Install method

npm / linuxbrew global install

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model-related)

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model-related)

### Logs

```
Failed: validating
Failed: candidate-doctor — Exit code: 1
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure):
  Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed:
  Error: Agent database resources are closing: [redacted-path]
Failing check update (doctor-failed)
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: this WSL2 Ubuntu systemd-user gateway install, upgrading 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.10
- Severity: blocks the upgrade to current stable
- Frequency: the `openclaw update --yes` attempt failed; the follow-up `openclaw update repair --yes` was interrupted by the WSL distro reset
- Consequence: remains on 2026.11.3; after the WSL reset an abandoned update run stayed visible in `openclaw update status`

### Additional information

Several agent DBs are large (main is about 2.4 GiB). The live gateway stayed up during candidate-doctor; readonly SQLite workers were visible while session repair ran. OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI was already running on the Windows host. I am not claiming Tray caused the WSL reset; I am reporting the timing.

Related: #205202 (same 11.10 candidate-doctor / blocked-by-session-repair-failure family; different inner message, possibly redacted). #204226 and #201561 (update repair / doctor leaving the gateway or update record unsettled). Not a match for #204834 (TRANSCRIPT_COLD) or #204078 (migration source changed after a read-only open).

Last known good on this host: 2026.11.3. First known bad target: 2026.11.10.
