issues.body:
## Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), Linux, claude-cli backend. Gateway-hosted, Discord-origin top-level requester.

## Summary
A subagent B (task-owned completion to parent A) spawns two grandchildren C1/C2 and calls `sessions_yield`. C1 finishes first and wakes B with a partial settle turn (C2 still running). In that turn, B calls `sessions_yield` again and gets `already_pending` with the guidance "This turn owns no new claim, so no yield is needed: end this turn normally." B ends the turn with an interim message ("waiting for C2, will send the verdict later"). When C2 finishes, B is woken again and produces its real final answer — but A never receives it as a completion event. A receives exactly one completion event, carrying the run id of the *first* partial settle turn, delivered ~1 s after B's second turn ends. The subagent shows as delivered.

## Steps to reproduce (minimal)
1. Parent A: `sessions_spawn` child B (hidden, `context: "isolated"`, default task-owned completion).
2. B: spawn C1 and C2, then `sessions_yield` → `{"status":"yielded"}`.
3. Make C1 finish noticeably earlier than C2.
4. B's settle turn for C1: call `sessions_yield` again without `acknowledgment` → `already_pending` (`pendingChildren[0].wakeArmed=true`), message ends with "end this turn normally".
5. B replies with a short interim message and ends the turn.
6. C2 finishes; B's next settle turn writes the final answer and ends.

## Expected
A receives B's final answer from step 6 as the child's completion, per:
- `docs/concepts/subagent-yield-handoff.md` (phase table, "Successor completion: Deliver the orchestrator's result to its original requester"; "earlier partitions are ordinary settle turns"; "an outstanding required final still cannot [finish silently]"; "Yield closes the old execution, not the delegated work").
- `docs/tools/subagents/announce.md` ("The wake names the siblings that are still working, so the parent can act on the ready results or call `sessions_yield` again to wait for the rest"; "For nested work, … The child's own final answer is what travels onward to its parent").

## Actual
- A gets one completion event whose run id is the step-4 partial settle turn (`announce:requester-settle:<B>:<C1 run>:yield-1`), delivered right after step 6 ends.
- The event is consumed by A as B's result; the final answer from step 6 (run `…:<C2 run>:yield-1`) is never delivered as a completion.
- Observed 4/4 times in one day with the same shape. A control case where both grandchildren finished in the same partition (single batch run id listing both children) delivered the final answer correctly.

## Suspected cause (from reading the installed dist; not a live repro)
- `sessions_yield` returns `already_pending` (no real yield) when pending children exist and no `acknowledgment` is passed, and always appends "end this turn normally".
- In a partial partition the settle turn has adopted B's paused run; ending the turn without re-pausing finalizes that run with the interim reply.
- The later partition's turn has no `sessions_yield`-paused row to adopt (`adoptPausedSubagentRunForFollowUp` requires `pauseReason === "sessions_yield"`), so its reply is not the task's completion.
- The finalized run's announce waits for the remaining descendant, then delivers with the first partition's identity.
This contradicts the docs telling the parent it may "call `sessions_yield` again to wait for the rest".

## Suggested fix direction
- In a partial-partition settle turn of a nested requester, `sessions_yield` should actually re-pause the adopted run (or the runtime should keep the task open until the partition with no pending members), so the last partition's answer is the one delivered.
- At minimum, `already_pending` guidance for a task-owned nested requester must not say "end this turn normally" while siblings of the current yield cohort are still pending (relates to #189980 / PR #190011).
- Regression: nested requester, two grandchildren finishing at different times, re-yield in the first partition, assert parent receives the second partition's final answer exactly once.

## Workarounds in use (limitations)
- Parent inspects the child's session history when the completion lacks an explicit final marker (manual; no automatic continuation).
- Child sends the final answer with `sessions_send` (separate from task-owned completion; duplicates possible).
- Passing `acknowledgment` to the second `sessions_yield` appears to take the real yield path in source, but the docs say it "does not claim the child again or rearm its completion"; untested.

## Privacy
Generic behavior and public version only. No transcripts, account/channel identifiers, user names, credentials, paths, or project data.

Related: #189980, #190011

issues.body:
# OpenClaw Bug Report: Nested Tool Activity Lifecycle Error Causes Consumer Closed

## Summary
When an agent run ends and the `agent_end` hook fires, reading nested tool activity throws `Error: Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid`. This exception is not caught, propagates through the model fallback chain, and ultimately causes the Feishu channel consumer to close. The user's message is lost with no reply.

## Environment
- OpenClaw version: 2026.11.7 (from plugin list)
- Node.js: v24.22.2
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-106-generic (Ubuntu)
- Channel: Feishu (Lark) via `@openclaw/feishu` plugin (community, v2026.11.7)
- Model chain: `minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (primary) → `agent-plan/ark-code-latest` (fallback #1) → `kimi/kimi-for-coding` (fallback #2, removed after this incident)

## Root Cause
**File**: `prompt-image-preparation-CG4H4TiY.mjs:387`

```javascript
if (!r) throw new Error("Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid");
```

`readNestedToolActivity(n)` returns `null` when the nested tool activity data is corrupted or incomplete. The error is thrown during `agent_end` hook execution, not caught by the fallback error handler, and propagates up to close the channel consumer.

## Complete Timeline (2026-11-28 00:02:56 → 00:05:09, UTC+8)

```
00:02:56.679  Session dec1192e: MiniMax 429 rate_limit → trying sticky fallback ark-code-latest
00:03:27.593  ark-code-latest candidate_succeeded (4 consecutive successes)
00:04:01.251  ark-code-latest candidate_succeeded
00:04:49.402  ark-code-latest candidate_succeeded
00:04:50.008  agent_end hook failed: Error: Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid
00:05:08.469  ark-code-latest candidate_succeeded
00:05:08.471  agent_end hook failed: Error: Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid
00:05:08.970  trying sticky fallback ark-code-latest before MiniMax
00:05:09.005  candidate_failed: ark-code-latest → MiniMax (errorHash: sha256:14ac8d9d6d11)
00:05:09.010  candidate_failed: MiniMax → kimi (same errorHash)
00:05:09.017  ERROR: Embedded agent failed before reply: Plugin feishu consumer is closed
```

## Key Observations

1. **Error object reuse in fallback chain**: Both `candidate_failed` events share the same `errorHash: sha256:14ac8d9d6d11`, indicating the same error object is passed to both fallback attempts (ark-code-latest and MiniMax). This is misleading — it appears as if both models failed independently, but it's actually the same nested tool activity error being re-thrown.

2. **Empty error message**: The `provider-error` log for this failure shows `message: "", stack: []` with `causeName: TypeError`. The actual error text is lost during error observation/redaction, making diagnosis harder.

3. **No provider-error log for the nested tool failure**: The error originates in `prompt-image-preparation-CG4H4TiY.mjs` (agent harness layer), not in the model provider layer. Therefore it doesn't produce a `provider-error` log entry — only `model-fallback/decision` entries.

## Frequency

- **2026-11-27**: 11 occurrences of `consumer is closed` across different traceIds
- **2026-11-28**: 1 occurrence (the one documented above)
- **2026-11-27**: 63 occurrences of `ConnectTimeoutError` for ark-code-latest (separate issue, network-related)
- **2026-11-27**: 12 occurrences of `Automation candidate agent-plan on runtime openclaw is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route` (separate issue, automation config)

## Impact
- User messages are silently lost with no error reply
- The Feishu channel enters `runtime not initialized` state after consumer closed
- Recovery requires gateway restart or channel reconnection

## Reproduction Path
1. Configure model chain with `minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` as primary and `agent-plan/ark-code-latest` as fallback
2. Trigger a session that uses nested tool activity (subagent spawn, code-mode execution, etc.)
3. Have the primary model hit rate limit (429)
4. Let the fallback model succeed multiple times, then have the nested tool activity become invalid before agent_end
5. The agent_end hook throws → consumer closes → message lost

## Suggested Fix

**Immediate (defensive)**:
- Wrap the `agent_end` hook execution in try-catch to prevent consumer closure
- Log the nested tool activity error but allow the agent to complete gracefully

**Root cause**:
- Investigate why `readNestedToolActivity` returns null — is the activity data being garbage collected too early?
- Add validation before throwing: if the activity is genuinely gone, handle it as a no-op rather than an error

**Error handling**:
- The fallback chain should not reuse the same error object across candidates — each candidate should have its own error context
- Error observation should preserve the original error message for non-provider errors

## Logs

### agent_end hook failure
```json
{"0":"agent_end hook failed: Error: Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid","_meta":{"logLevelName":"WARN"},"time":"2026-11-28T00:04:50.008+08:00"}
```

### model fallback decision (candidate_failed)
```json
{"event":"model_fallback_decision","decision":"candidate_failed","candidateProvider":"agent-plan","candidateModel":"ark-code-latest","errorHash":"sha256:14ac8d9d6d11","fallbackStepFromModel":"agent-plan/ark-code-latest","fallbackStepToModel":"minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash","fallbackStepChainPosition":1,"fallbackStepFinalOutcome":"next_fallback"}
```

### consumer closed
```json
{"0":"Embedded agent failed before reply: Plugin feishu consumer is closed","_meta":{"logLevelName":"ERROR"},"time":"2026-11-28T00:05:09.017+08:00"}
```

## Source Reference
- `prompt-image-preparation-CG4H4TiY.mjs:387` — error throw site
- `model-fallback-attempt-ebq-li-c.mjs:438` — `recordFailedCandidateAttempt` function
- `failover-error-CNdro0XW.mjs:290` — `describeFailoverError` function

issues.body:
# Bug report — Android onboarding fails when named operator roles are enabled

**Date:** 2026-11-27
**Gateway:** OpenClaw 2026.11.10, Linux VM, loopback bind, Tailscale Serve managed ingress
**Client:** OpenClaw Android 2026.11.70, Solana Mobile Seeker (Android)
**Severity:** High for onboarding; no data loss

## Summary
Pairing the Android app to a Gateway that has `gateway.roles` configured cannot be completed with the QR/setup-code flow. The app reaches "Connecting Gateway" and stalls at "Checking node access". Manual setup with the setup-code token fails with `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`; only the Gateway master token works. Node approval is a second, separate step the app references but does not identify clearly.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure the Gateway with named operator roles (`gateway.roles` present).
2. Enable managed Tailscale Serve with `gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true`, auth mode token.
3. Install the Android app, open Pair Gateway, scan a QR from `openclaw qr --url wss://<host>`.
4. App connects the node, then stalls at "Checking node access".
5. Retry via Manual setup using the setup-code token: fails with AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH.
6. Enter the Gateway master token: connects, then shows "Approve node access" asking the user to run `openclaw nodes pending` / `openclaw nodes approve <id>` on the Gateway.
7. After approval, tapping "I have approved" often leaves the app on the same screen even though the Gateway logged a successful operator connection.

## Expected
One flow completes onboarding, or each failure names the exact missing step and the identifier needed.

## Actual
- QR flow stalls with an amber "Checking node access" and no actionable error.
- Manual setup rejects the bootstrap token with AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH and no hint that a master token is required.
- Gateway logs: `operator role policies require a verified user identity for this authentication method; reconnect through the trusted proxy or Tailscale, or use the shared gateway token/password` (code AUTH_VERIFIED_USER_REQUIRED) when a bootstrap/device token attempts an operator session.
- Node approval is a separate queue from device approval. The app shows a request id but the copy affordance is unclear, and `openclaw devices list` shows nothing pending while `openclaw nodes pending` does.
- The approval screen can remain stale after the Gateway has already accepted `client=openclaw-android mode=ui role=operator`.
- Force-closing the app can drop the saved manual gateway entry, sending the user back to manual setup.

## Impact
Onboarding took roughly an hour and required copying the Gateway master token into a phone. For client deployments this is a non-starter: it exposes full operator credentials and depends on the user reading Gateway-side CLI output.

## Suggested fixes
1. Detect named operator role enforcement during pairing and either (a) issue a scoped device token that is permitted for operator sessions, or (b) tell the user explicitly that the master token is required and why.
2. Map AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH to a message that distinguishes bootstrap token vs gateway token.
3. Unify or cross-reference the device and node approval queues; show the node request id with a copy button, and state the exact commands.
4. Subscribe to the pairing resolution event so the approval screen clears itself when the Gateway approves.
5. Persist the manual gateway entry across app restart and force-close.
6. Consider a "node-only" onboarding path that never requests operator scope.

## UI defects observed
- **Unclosable model-refresh banner.** When the Gateway has providers without credentials (OpenAI here), the app shows "some models could not be refreshed… tap refresh to retry." There is no close/dismiss control. Tapping Refresh does nothing.
- **Banner eats half the screen when the keyboard opens.** The banner does not collapse or move, leaving roughly half the viewport unusable while typing. No way to dismiss it.
- With only one configured provider (DeepSeek, working key), the warning is noise: all usable models remain selectable.

## Evidence
```
19:16:06 authReason=token_mismatch client=openclaw-android mode=ui role=operator
19:16:18 [gateway] device pairing auto-approved role=node
19:16:18 closed before connect: operator role policies require a verified user identity
19:41:51 client=openclaw-android name=Vince's GeekerSOL mode=ui role=operator auth=token
19:46:44 openclaw nodes pending -> e8b8f4b5-c1c0-4be8-ae77-dc4fdd3ac56a
```

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Runs on a CLI backend (`claude-cli`) never report the model that serves them while they work. The run emits no `lifecycle` event with `phase: "model"`, so `recordAgentRunModel` is never called and the sessions row keeps `activeModel: null` / `activeModelProvider: null` for the whole run. Embedded, harness and worker runs publish that phase as soon as the first message names its model.

In a new chat nothing else names the model either: no assistant message is persisted until the run ends (`chat.history` has only `inFlightRun` with `text` and `tool`/`item` events). A client can therefore not show which model is answering until the first run is over, although Claude Code states it at the very start (`system` `init` record, and `message.model` on every `assistant` record).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent whose model runs through the Claude CLI runtime (`agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`, e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`).
2. Start a new chat and send a prompt that keeps the run working for a while (a few tool calls).
3. While the run works, call `sessions.list` for that session and `chat.history`, and watch the `agent` events of the run.

### Expected behavior

As for embedded runs: once the backend names its model, the run publishes `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` with provider and model, and the sessions row shows `activeModel` / `activeModelProvider` while the run is active.

### Actual behavior

- `sessions.list` during the run: `hasActiveRun: true`, `status: "running"`, `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`, `activeModel: null`, `activeModelProvider: null`.
- No `lifecycle` event with `phase: "model"` for the run.
- `chat.history` during the first run of a chat: only the user message plus `inFlightRun` (`runId`, `text`, `startedAt`, `events` of stream `tool`/`item`); no field names the model.
- The model first becomes visible on the assistant message persisted at the end (`provider: "claude-cli"`, `model: …`).

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Claude models through the Claude CLI runtime (seen with `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-2`)

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → `anthropic/<model>` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli` → local Claude Code CLI (`stream-json`)

### Impact and severity

UX friction for clients that tell the user which model is answering (and warn when it differs from the selection): for CLI-backed chats this is unknown for the entire first run, and for later runs only the previous answer is evidence. A silent model difference would surface only after the run.

### Additional information

Source reading (2026.11.5, and unchanged on `main` at 58ed1818bb):

- `phase: "model"` is emitted in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.model-state.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-entry.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-attempt-runtime.ts` and `src/gateway/worker-environments/inference-runtime.ts`; `src/infra/agent-events.ts` turns it into `recordAgentRunModel`, which feeds the row's `activeModel`.
- The CLI path has no counterpart. `src/agents/cli-output-stream.ts` reads the `system` `init` record only for `onNativeTools(parsed.tools)` and does not use its `model`; `message.model` of `assistant` records is not used for this either.

Suggested direction: in the CLI output stream, when a non-subagent `system` `init` record (or the first `assistant` record) names a model, emit the same `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` event for the run with the CLI backend's provider id and that model, de-duplicated like `publishMessageModel` does. Backends whose output does not name a model simply emit nothing.

Found while building a client on the Gateway protocol; analysis was AI-assisted and checked against a live run.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a turn started with `openclaw agent` spawns a subagent and calls `sessions_yield`, the CLI returns as soon as the turn yields, with exit code 0, `status: "ok"`, `meta.yielded: true` and no payloads. The reply the agent writes after the subagent finishes lands only in the session transcript, and the caller never gets it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a turn whose agent spawns one quick subagent and then yields:

   ```bash
   openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:yield-repro --json --timeout 300 \
     --message "Call sessions_spawn with task 'Reply with the single word child-done.', then call sessions_yield to wait for it. When the child's result resumes you, reply exactly CONTINUATION-REPLY-OK."
   echo "exit=$?"
   ```

2. Read the result's `status`, `result.payloads` and `result.meta.yielded`.
3. A few seconds later, read the session: `openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:yield-repro"}' --json`.

To make it deterministic I also ran it against a scripted Anthropic Messages stub (custom provider, `api: anthropic-messages`) that answers `sessions_spawn`, then `sessions_yield`, then the text `CONTINUATION-REPLY-OK`. The result is the same.

### Expected behavior

The `agent` request stays open past the yield and returns the reply from the turn the subagent's completion resumes, as the closing comment on #76145 describes for spawn plus `sessions_yield` ("the original CLI Gateway request remains pending past the `accepted` frame until the final response", fixed by #120601). `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.live.test.ts` (the Gemini fan-in case) expects the same thing: the original `expectFinal` request returns the parent's final token. That comment also asked for a new issue if a current build returns before the synthesis after `sessions_yield`.

### Actual behavior

The CLI exits within a second of the yield, before the subagent's first model call. Stdout:

```json
{ "status": "ok", "summary": "completed",
  "result": { "payloads": [], "meta": { "yielded": true, "terminalReply": { "disposition": "empty" } } } }
```

The subagent then finishes, the parent session's continuation turn runs and writes `CONTINUATION-REPLY-OK` into the transcript. The session has no channel, so nothing delivers that reply anywhere.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (6ea542f) and main 9239eeb2df3 (packed locally)

### Operating system

Linux (x64), Node 26

### Install method

npm global (2026.11.10); `npm pack` of main for the main run

### Model

A scripted Anthropic Messages stub (embedded runtime), and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` on the claude-cli runtime. Not model-specific.

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw agent` -> local gateway (loopback) -> embedded runner -> stub provider; or -> claude-cli

### Additional provider/model setup details

Fresh profile, default agent `main`, no channels, no fallbacks. Session key passed with `--session-key`.

### Logs

| Build | Runtime | CLI exit | CLI result | Continuation reply in transcript | CLI returned vs. reply |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.11.10 | stub (embedded) | 0 | `ok`, `yielded: true`, `payloads: []` | yes | yield 899.91, CLI exit ~900, reply 902.05 |
| 2026.11.10 | claude-cli (Haiku) | 0 | `ok`, `yielded: true`, `payloads: []` | yes | yield 037.0, CLI exit ~045, reply 053.4 |
| main 9239eeb2df3 | stub (embedded) | 0 | `ok`, `yielded: true`, `payloads: []` | yes | yield 304.79, CLI exit 305.17, child's model call 305.28, reply 306.00 |

Transcript order on main (seconds): user 301.8, `sessions_spawn` (via `dispatch_action`) 304.4, `sessions_yield` -> `{"status":"yielded"}` 304.79, `subagent_completion` 305.7, assistant `CONTINUATION-REPLY-OK` 306.0.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: anything that runs agent turns through `openclaw agent` and reads the reply: scripts, CI jobs, agent-to-agent relays.
- Severity: blocks the workflow. The caller gets an empty "completed" result, and the real answer is only in the transcript.
- Frequency: every time a turn spawns a subagent and yields, on both runtimes I tried.
- Consequence: we lost replies this way and now refuse `sessions_yield` in turns started by `openclaw agent`, waiting for the subagent inside the turn instead.

### Additional information

<details><summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Code at 9239eeb2df3:

- `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts:670` calls the gateway `agent` method with `expectFinal: true` (`:695`) and sets the exit code from the final response's `status` (`:766`), so the CLI returns whatever the first final frame carries.
- `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-dispatch.ts:457-527` builds that final response when the yielded attempt ends (`status: "ok"`, its empty `result`) and emits it at `:527`. The only thing that waits for a later reply there is `settleFollowup` (`:168`), which runs only when a `followupCompletion` owner exists.
- `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts:425` sets `followupCompletion` only from the subagent admission path, so a top-level turn started by `openclaw agent` has nobody waiting for the continuation.
- `src/commands/agent.test.ts:559` (local `--local` path) also treats `{ yielded: true }` as a completed outcome with no terminal reply.

`src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` is unchanged between v2026.11.10 and 9239eeb2df3, and I found no merged change since then that makes the `agent` request wait for a yielded turn's continuation (`git log v2026.11.10..origin/main --grep yield`).

I haven't found the first bad version: I didn't run the build from #76145's closing comment (2e6457b8e6e), so this may be a regression or a gap that the live test (live-only) never caught in CI.

Possible directions, for a maintainer to choose: keep the `agent` request open for a yielded top-level turn until its continuation ends (what #76145 describes), or return a distinct non-final status (for example `yielded` with the session key) so a caller can wait with `agent.wait` or read the transcript instead of taking an empty "ok".

Related: #76145 (closed, same symptom on 2026.4.12), #110946 (`--json` reports `ok` without a final reply on timeout), #166639 (tools in the settle continuation after `sessions_yield`; a different cause).

</details>

issues.body:
### Summary

Since #198100 (v2026.11.10), a change to the system prompt's Runtime section (for example `active_node` when the macOS app opens or quits) is sent as an appended `openclaw.system-update` note (`details.kind: "prompt-update"`). This fixes the prompt cache (#192364, verified on our install). But on `openai-completions` the note is projected into the request as `role: "user"` (the session prompt projection builds `{ role: "user", content: n.content }` for system-update messages). The text then looks like a user turn that claims to change the system prompt. That is the standard shape of a prompt injection. Our agent judged it fake and ignored it, so the runtime change never reached the model.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`), macOS gateway, webchat channel
- Model: local Qwen3.8 Flash-Next through an `openai-completions` provider
- macOS app installed (source of the `active_node` flips)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a webchat session on an `openai-completions` model. Send a message.
2. Open the macOS app and use its window. Send a message. A `prompt-update` note with the new `active_node` is appended.
3. Quit the macOS app. Send a message. A second note with `active_node=unknown` is appended.
4. Ask the model whether anything unusual arrived in its context.

### Expected

The model treats the note as a trusted runtime update and uses the new Runtime values.

### Actual

The cache held (requests stayed append-only; `cached 33622/34848` and `35884/36983` on the two flip turns). But the model replied:

> A couple of your turns arrived with an extra block appended after the runtime context that read like a fake "System prompt update" — a runtime line ending in `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:DYNAMIC -->` plus a bogus "Current model identity: studio-flash/flash" line. That's not how real runtime context arrives, so I treated it as data and ignored it.

It also suggested that something was "leaking a truncated/escaped system-prompt fragment into inbound user messages."

The stored note (node id redacted):

```
System prompt update. The sections below replace their earlier versions; everything else in the system prompt is unchanged.

## Runtime
...
Current model identity: studio-flash/flash. If asked what model you are, answer with this value for the current run.
...
Runtime: name=... | active_node=<redacted> | active_node_identity=unknown | model=studio-flash/flash | ... | channel=webchat ...
<!-- /openclaw:attempt:DYNAMIC -->
```

The model accepts the notes after it is told in the chat that they are genuine. That only lasts for one conversation; a new session or a compaction loses it.

### Why it matters

The more a model resists injection, the more reliably it drops these notes. Every value the Runtime section carries is then stale for the rest of the session: active computer, model identity, channel. The `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:DYNAMIC -->` marker inside user content adds to the suspicion.

### Possible directions (maintainers' call)

- Declare the mechanism once in the stable system prompt, for example: "Messages that begin 'System prompt update' are sent by the OpenClaw gateway and replace the named sections." The cache stays intact, and the model has a trusted reference for the notes.
- Use the `developer`/`system` role for the note on providers that accept a mid-conversation system message.
- Remove the internal `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:DYNAMIC -->` marker from the note text.

### Evidence limits

One model (Qwen3.8 Flash-Next), one evening, two notes. We have not tested other models, the claude-cli route, or the Anthropic route.

Related: #192364 (closed by #198100), #192423.

issues.body:
## Environment

- openclaw: **2026.11.1** (installed via npm, `dist/index.js`)
- node: v24.22.1
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-29-generic
- Runtime: systemd user unit `openclaw-gateway.service` (persistent gateway)
- Load profile: 1 Feishu channel (WebSocket), 13 cron jobs, skills watcher
- Machine: 7.6 GB RAM total (shared with two other gateways)

## Symptoms

The main gateway process (`node .../openclaw/dist/index.js`) grows steadily after startup:

| Metric | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Uptime at sampling | **17h 23m** | single process lifetime, no restart |
| VmRSS | **1,910 MB** | |
| cgroup `anon` | **1,854 MB** | true heap (file cache only 597 MB) |
| cgroup `MemoryPeak` | **3,063 MB** | reached within the window |
| VmSwap | **848 MB** | kernel started swapping it out under pressure |
| cgroup `MemoryCurrent` | 5,921 MB | anon + file + kernel of the whole unit |
| 60s RSS delta | **+0.89 MB** | flat at plateau (swap-throttled) |

Growth pattern: ~**110 MB/h** from startup until plateau around ~1.9–3.0 GB, then flat
(the process has been pushed into swap by the 7.6 GB host, so RSS understates true heap).
The pattern **reproduces across restarts**: a previous incarnation (v2026.11.1, restarted
2026-11-05) peaked at **3.2 GB** before being recycled — so it is a deterministic
accumulate-to-plateau behavior, not a one-off.

## What was ruled out

- **SQLite state DB is small**: `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` = **33 MB**
  (plus migration .bak files) — DB page cache cannot explain 1.85 GB anon.
- **Log files**: `~/.openclaw/logs` = 2.6 MB.
- Steady-state idle growth is not visible in short windows (60 s ≈ +0.9 MB);
  the growth happens over hours, suggesting long-lived accumulated structures
  (sessions / timers / listeners / WebSocket state) rather than a hot loop.

## Correlated observations

- 61 "slow SQLite query" warnings in logs over the same period (host is CPU/RAM
  constrained, but queries taking seconds point at growing in-process state).
- Feishu WebSocket reconnects cleanly after restart; memory resets to ~150 MB
  at startup (restart is the only mitigation found).

## Reproduction

1. Start `openclaw-gateway.service` on a small host (7.6 GB) with a Feishu channel
   and ~13 cron jobs.
2. Sample `ps -o rss= -p <main PID>` / `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<unit>/memory.stat`
   every hour.
3. Observe `anon` climbing ~100 MB/h until ~1.9–3 GB, `MemoryPeak` ≈ 3 GB,
   swap usage appearing, then plateau.

## Expected behavior

Gateway anon memory should stabilize (a few hundred MB for this workload) instead
of accumulating ~3 GB per day-cycle. If growth is expected (e.g., session cache),
please document a tuning knob (cap/TTL) — currently there is none visible.

## Suggested investigation areas

- Session/conversation objects retained after sessions close (LRU/TTL missing?)
- WebSocket reconnect state from the Lark/Feishu channel accumulating
- Timers/listeners registered per cron tick (13 jobs) never released
- `v8.getHeapStatistics()` snapshot after N hours to identify the retaining set
  (heap snapshot on demand would help: `kill -USR2 <pid>` if supported)

---
Environment note: submitted by an assistant operator; `gh` CLI token expired at
filing time, so this may be pasted manually.

issues.body:
## Summary
Separate shared Android data and policy from feature-specific owners, consolidating demonstrated duplicate implementations while preserving app behavior.

## Problem to solve
Generic JSON accessors live beside node invocation helpers even though chat, Gateway parsing, settings, voice and Wear consume them. Chat model identity policy also lives in a Compose picker but is used by controllers. Talk route parsing imports a model predicate from setup readiness while readiness imports that parser back. These dependencies make otherwise independent app logic harder to change and test.

## Proposed solution
Use the existing shared data owners, migrate every affected caller, and remove replaced implementations. Deliver narrow PRs with source/history evidence, focused Android validation and independent review.

Initial candidates:
- Move unchanged generic JSON accessors to the existing shared JSON owner.
- Move cron list parsing and summary contracts from runtime orchestration into the existing cron data owner.
- Consolidate model identity policy outside the picker.
- Remove the Talk config/readiness dependency cycle.

## Rejected consolidation candidates

Wear text projections accept different malformed-input shapes, so merging them directly would change behavior. Installed-skill readiness predicates are already shared; an additional classifier would add complexity for a negligible reduction.

## Impact and compatibility
Internal maintenance work; no intended user-visible behavior, protocol, permission, credential, persistence or dependency changes. Releases and deployments are outside scope.

## Alternatives considered
Keep feature-local helpers when their semantics differ. Avoid broad extraction-only rewrites, duplicate compatibility aliases and new abstractions without a concrete responsibility.

## Implementation intent
Maintainer-requested cleanup campaign. Each PR will link this issue and record its own validation and compatibility evidence.

## Delivery status

Remote-verified merges: **25/120** — Contracts/chat 12/40, Settings/domain 7/40, Voice/Wear 6/40. All twenty-five PRs have verified remote merges and native completion.

Latest changes:
- [On-device Dictation readiness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207017) makes Settings use the recognizer's availability owner and removes the unused Gateway Dictation projection. Both flavor suites, lint, source verification and visual comparisons passed; exact-head CI and security review passed before merge.
- [Native Talk transcript accumulation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195894) removes the competing native transcript string and reuses the existing segment merger. Baseline reproduced word loss on silence and mute; the fixed replay passed 131 tests per flavor, including one temporary mute probe, plus lint. Fresh independent review was clean; exact PR-head CI passed. Contributor credit is preserved.

**Campaign target remains unchanged.** The latest bounded source and older-PR audits found no further substantiated, independent cleanup within the current constraints. Scope choices remain with the maintainer; no artificial PR splitting or expansion into dependencies, security boundaries, migrations or unrelated areas.

Compilation, focused Android tests, Kotlin lint, staged-content guards and independent source review cover each candidate. The Connection PR retains one unresolved local combined-run timing failure, separately from its passing hosted run. Dictation's strict locale audit retains 21 untranslated new entries, separately from passing source verification and required CI. The twenty-five merged changes remove 132 production lines overall; no runtime or performance savings are claimed.


The first eleven PRs have verified remote merges and completed native closeout. Generated PR checkouts were removed by the native workflow; authored source and proof checkouts remain retained. JSON merged as `81bc5ec79fe43f8b1859e627f87bb6ce5102b0f0` after both [original CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45794879799) and [native qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45798910575) passed. Its initial job timeout remains historical. Connection merged as `a4eddbe9a1ef49c84937c563200a0a5fc066f993`; Skills merged as `47897931150c352a3cbd8c2e2f4bf118e0d9b455` after their current-head CI passed. Earlier CI setup failures are recorded in each PR.

Talk merged as `04a1ca3846dba2f45c6ede20fea57032b4b19031` after the patch-identical rebase, 138 passing tests per phone flavor on combined source, and [current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45810646185). The first eleven native completion records are confirmed. Nine enrolled source checkouts are finished/released with owner retention pins; two unenrolled source checkouts and the proof checkout remain retained. No task source checkout was deleted.

Renewed discovery qualified three additional cleanups. Share queue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206008 merged as `4cb16b351987b2628d54212be17355a12c2cd0fa`; its generated checkout is removed, native completion verified, and source retained. Wear avatar https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206028 merged as `0a0f5ce4494c2384e7669098b00d400ead327bdd` after current-head CI passed; native completion and generated-checkout removal are verified. The latest two changes have verified remote merges. Local two-flavor proof and full committed-range review passed at `94aeae8e166d29d7f5a8df703212ae2b665ba323`; [current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45923020797) passed. Gateway results now have one data-only owner, with 21 production files and 21 test files dropping direct transport-owner references. Initial proof passed 1,169 tests per flavor. Streaming state cleanup merged as `df78bb4a3ac7dc55792e922d2ba0b01adce2185c` after [current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45941275558) passed; [native completion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206382#issuecomment-7210319455) and generated-checkout removal are verified. issues.body:
## Summary

After a session is rewound to a point before a lossy ("quality degraded") compaction, `/status` still reports `Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)`. The compaction count resets, but the degraded flag doesn't, so the status contradicts itself and wrongly warns that details may be lost.

## Observed (2026.11.6)

1. A long Telegram DM hit a budget compaction. Both summary attempts failed and the safeguard committed the floor without a summary, which set `compactionQualityDegraded: true` on the session entry.
2. The session was rewound with `sessions.rewind` to the user message just before that turn. The active path no longer contains the degraded compaction, and context was back to its full pre-compaction size (~501k tokens).
3. `/status` then showed `Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)`.

## Cause (upstream main 9514f1d04c9)

`src/config/sessions/session-message-cut-plan.ts`, `buildMessageCutSessionEntry`, is used for in-place rewind/switch as well as fork. It spreads `currentEntry` and clears the transcript-derived accounting (`compactionCount`, `contextTokens`, `contextBudgetStatus`, `transcriptByteCompactionLatch`, `memoryFlush`, …). It does not clear `compactionQualityDegraded`, so the spread carries it over. `formatCompactionStatus` in `src/auto-reply/reply/compaction-notice.ts` then prints the degraded label from the stale flag.

The field doc in `src/config/sessions/types.ts` says "cleared with a new session". A rewind keeps the session id, so it never clears.

## Expected

After rewind or branch switch, the flag should reflect the new active path:

- It should be cleared when the repointed path contains no quality-degraded compaction. That's the case here, where the rewind went to before it.
- It should be kept, or recomputed from the active path's compaction events, when the path still includes one.

At minimum, `compactionQualityDegraded` should be reset alongside `compactionCount` and rebuilt the same way on the next turn.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issues.body:
### Summary
In `TalkModeManager.kt` (`2212–2285`), continuous native Talk stores recognized speech in `lastTranscript = trimmed` on each partial or final callback and restarts recognition after `350ms` when `onResults` fires, while `checkSilence` waits `silenceWindowMs` (`700ms` default) before sending the turn. If the user speaks a second phrase after the `350ms` recognizer restart before `silenceWindowMs` elapses, `handleTranscript` overwrites `lastTranscript` with the new partial/final text instead of accumulating finalized segments like PTT (`PushToTalkTranscriptMerger.merge(pttFinalSegments, pttLivePartial)`), dropping the earlier finalized phrase from the outgoing `chat.send`.

### Reproduction / Reachability
1. Start continuous native Talk (`stt-tts`).
2. Speak a phrase that produces `onResults("Send the agenda.")`, triggering the 350ms recognizer restart while the silence timer is still waiting.
3. Continue speaking (`"Then book the room."`) in the restarted recognition session before the silence window expires.
4. Observe that `finalizeTranscript` sends only `"Then book the room."` instead of `"Send the agenda. Then book the room."`.

### Expected Behavior
- Continuous native Talk accumulates finalized recognition segments in `pttFinalSegments` and merges them with `pttLivePartial` via `PushToTalkTranscriptMerger.merge(...)` until `finalizeTranscript` or `stop` clears the turn.
- Note for rebasing onto latest `main` (post-#187722 native mic mute): migrate the two new `lastTranscript` references introduced by #187722 to the shared segment merger (`pttFinalSegments` / `PushToTalkTranscriptMerger.merge(pttFinalSegments, pttLivePartial)`).

### Candidate Fix & Verification
- Branch: `saariuslystoned/openclaw:fix/android-talk-retain-finalized-phrases-20261108` (`892517d2c724c7551ca49b03ddb574b18d7ec323`, parent `954f1a4fea0fd69ff0f951c9ebf7f2af79b86f33`)
- Files:
  - `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManager.kt`
  - `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt`
- Verified Base-RED -> Fix-GREEN with `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests "ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest" --tests "ai.openclaw.app.voice.PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest" :app:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug` and installed on physical Google Pixel 10 Pro XL (`63310DLCQ000RV`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a conversation bound to an ACP session (`acp.backend: acpx`, thread binding on Discord), `/compact` is handled by the Gateway as a local command and never reaches the ACP harness. `handleCompactCommand` (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts`, bundled in `commands-handlers.runtime-*.mjs`) has no ACP branch: it resolves the session entry, runs `runSessionMutation({ kind: "compaction" })` and calls `compactEmbeddedAgentSession`, which compacts the OpenClaw-side mirror transcript of the ACP session. The harness keeps its full context. The command still replies `⚙️ Compaction finished (resulting context unknown)`, so the operator is told a compaction happened when the model context was not touched.

The only manual-compaction target resolver in that path is `resolveManualCompactionCliTarget`, which covers CLI backends (`agentHarnessId`); an ACP-bound session falls through to the embedded path. Checked on `main` `3e9ac5fc6ce`: `commands-compact.ts` has no reference to ACP.

The harness itself supports manual compaction through a plain prompt: `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.113.0` receiving `session/prompt` with the text `/compact` runs Claude Code's compaction (`tool_call` "Compact conversation", `rawOutput: {"trigger":"manual","preTokens":39000,"postTokens":16696}`) and writes a `compact_boundary` (`compactMetadata.trigger: "manual"`) into the Claude Code transcript. So the fix is routing, on the Gateway side.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `acp.enabled: true`, `acp.backend: "acpx"` and an acpx agent running `npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.113.0`.
2. Spawn a thread-bound ACP session on Discord and exchange a few turns.
3. Send `/compact` (native slash command) in the bound thread.
4. Inspect the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl`) for `"subtype":"compact_boundary"`.

### Expected behavior

In an ACP-bound conversation, `/compact` reaches the harness (for example as a `session/prompt` with `/compact`, or through an advertised ACP command), the harness compacts, and the reply reports the harness result. If OpenClaw decides not to forward it, the command should say the bound harness was not compacted instead of reporting success.

### Actual behavior

The Gateway compacts its own mirror transcript and reports success; the harness receives nothing and its transcript has 0 `compact_boundary` entries. The OpenClaw session history shows a `kind: "compaction"` row with `tokensBefore: 417, tokensAfter: 963` (the mirror), followed by the command reply `⚙️ Compaction finished (resulting context unknown) • Context ?/1.0m`. The reply-path log shows `run=none` (no ACP turn was started).

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (npm global); `main` `3e9ac5fc6ce` unchanged in `commands-compact.ts`

### Operating system

Linux 7.0.14 (Proxmox LXC), node v24.22.2

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Harness model claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code 2.1.x via claude-agent-acp 0.113.0)

### Provider / routing chain

Discord thread binding → ACP dispatch → acpx plugin → `ssh forge 'npx -y @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.113.0'` → Claude Code

### Additional provider/model setup details

A context-engine plugin of ours (`nexus-context`, `ownsCompaction: false`, delegates `compact()` to the runtime via `delegateCompactionToRuntime`) is registered; its log line below only shows the host calling it. Disabling it is not needed to see the defect: the command handler never consults the ACP session manager before choosing the embedded path.

### Logs

```
2026-11-27T20:39:29.915-03:00 [plugins] backlog-v2 message_received: session=agent:arthur:acp:28be091c-fb29-4079-91a0-1b7652053dd3 messageId=1576019666134900766
2026-11-27T20:39:30.041-03:00 [nexus-context] compact requested: session=agent:arthur:acp:28be091c-fb29-4079-91a0-1b7652053dd3 tokens=? budget=1000000 force=true target=threshold origin=host sources[sessionKey=key,sessionTarget=key,runtimeContext=key]
2026-11-27T20:39:41.187-03:00 [sessions/lifecycle] slow session lifecycle operation ... operation=compaction mutationKind=compaction ...
2026-11-27T20:39:41.208-03:00 [plugins] backlog-v2 reply_payload_sending: session=agent:arthur:acp:28be091c-fb29-4079-91a0-1b7652053dd3 kind=final run=none ...
```

Direct adapter control (same adapter version, plain ACP JSON-RPC client over stdio, 2026-11-27 23:47Z):

```
P1 {"stopReason":"end_turn", ...}
UPDATE tool_call {"sessionUpdate":"tool_call","title":"Compact conversation","kind":"think","status":"in_progress","_meta":{"claudeCode":{"toolName":"compact"}}}
UPDATE tool_call_update {"rawOutput":{"trigger":"manual","preTokens":39000,"postTokens":16696,"durationMs":9030}}
P2 {"stopReason":"end_turn", ...}
transcript: "subtype":"compact_boundary","content":"Conversation compacted","compactMetadata":{"trigger":"manual", ...}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See logs above.

### Impact and severity

Affects every ACP-bound conversation on a channel with native or text commands enabled. The operator has no working way to compact a long-running harness session from chat, and the success reply hides that: it was noticed only by reading the harness transcript on the remote host. Severity: blocks a workflow (long Claude Code sessions run to the harness's own threshold), with a misleading success message. Frequency: always.

### Additional information

`/acp steer <text>` forwards text to the harness through `AcpSessionManager.runTurn` (`handleAcpSteerAction`), so `/acp steer /compact` is a plausible workaround; we have not yet verified it end to end. The docs (`tools/acp-agents/bindings.md`) list `/acp ...`, `/status` and `/session` as Gateway-local in bound conversations and say nothing about `/compact`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In Android Settings -> Voice, the "Dictation" readiness row is driven by the Gateway's transcription provider catalog, but the chat composer's dictation uses the on-device speech recognizer, so the row can say "Needs setup" while dictation works, or "Ready ... via Gateway relay" while dictation is unavailable on the device.

### Steps to reproduce

Derived from the code and docs; not yet run on a device.

1. Connect the Android app to a Gateway with no realtime transcription provider and open Settings -> Voice. Then use the composer microphone.
2. Repeat with a Gateway that has a transcription provider, on a device without on-device recognition for the current language.

### Expected behavior

The row describes what dictation actually depends on. `docs/nodes/talk/client-ui.md` and `docs/platforms/android.md` describe Android dictation as on-device.

### Actual behavior

From the code:

- The row shows the Gateway transcription state: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d7861f77da916625c08c30bcbc8ad762f32f63/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/SettingsScreens.kt#L775
- That state is parsed from the catalog's `transcription` group: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d7861f77da916625c08c30bcbc8ad762f32f63/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/GatewayTalkSetupReadiness.kt#L180-L181
- Composer dictation creates an on-device recognizer: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d7861f77da916625c08c30bcbc8ad762f32f63/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatDictation.kt#L108-L121

```kotlin
val active = SpeechRecognizer.createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer(appContext)
```

`talkSetupReadiness.dictation` is read only by this row. The Gateway-transcription microphone path has no caller in the UI.

Expected visible result (not yet observed): "Dictation — Needs setup — No Dictation provider is configured on the Gateway" while the composer mic works; or "Ready" while the composer shows "On-device speech recognition is unavailable."

### OpenClaw version

main at d1d7861f77d (source reading)

### Operating system

Android (source analysis; no device run)

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

Android app -> `talk.catalog` (settings row) vs on-device recognizer (dictation)

### Impact and severity

Affected: Android users reading the Voice settings to diagnose dictation.
Severity: Low (misleading status).
Frequency: always when the two states differ, per the code.

### Additional information

Found by reading source during the Speech & Audio focus week. `GatewayTalkSetupReadinessTest.kt` pins the parsing only. The "unavailable" message is also what a missing language pack produces, with no next step.

### Summary

Offer an explicit migration conflict policy that preserves existing target files and imports the remaining independent items.

### Problem to solve

Someone moving into an established OpenClaw agent may have customized one skill and want to import many other files. A conflict can stop the entire plan. `--overwrite` permits replacing the customization, while repeating `--item` requires identifying every item that should still be imported.

### Proposed solution

Offer a keep-existing option for plan and apply. Show each conflicting item as skipped with its reason. Apply only independent items for which the provider can preserve this choice. If another item requires a skipped input, identify it as blocked. Keep the existing backup and credential choices in effect.

### Alternatives considered

An exact `--item` list is practical for small imports. The requested policy lets users state their intent directly for a larger import and see the same disposition in the preview and final report.

### Impact

This would let users onboard into an existing agent incrementally while preserving edits that matter to them.

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance example: the source has three independent skills. One target already exists with different bytes. A keep-existing preview identifies that conflict. Apply preserves those bytes, imports the other two, and names all three outcomes. [Current options](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/cli/program/register.migrate.ts#L19-L46) and [conflict preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/commands/migrate/output.ts#L175-L181).

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a read-only comparison of two local Template sources that summarizes changes to declared plugins, skills, MCP servers, and automations.

### Problem to solve

An agent Template can add a scheduled job or change which MCP command will run. Reviewing a revised Template one source at a time makes these changes easy to miss among unrelated workspace edits. A maintainer deciding whether to distribute a revised Template needs to see what adding the new revision would set up.

### Proposed solution

Accept the same local source forms as `templates inspect`, for example `openclaw templates compare ./previous ./candidate`. Use the existing Template reader on both sides. Group added, removed, and changed requirements by identity. For an automation, show a changed schedule. For a pinned dependency, show the old and new version. The command should work before installing either revision, starting a job, or resolving external credentials.

### Alternatives considered

A source-control diff is useful when both revisions share a repository. It also includes formatting and unrelated file changes. Two separate inspection reports work across directories but leave the reader to pair up entries and interpret their differences.

### Impact

Template authors and operators can identify consequential changes before creating a new agent from a revised package.

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance example: revision B reorders two skill declarations, changes a plugin pin, and changes a daily automation to hourly. The comparison reports the pin and cadence changes once each. A reordering that leaves the effective requirements identical produces no requirements change. [Declared Template requirements](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/docs/cli/templates.md#L306-L334) and [current single-source inspection command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/cli/templates-cli.ts#L82-L90).

issues.body:
### Summary

Give operators a **Retry announcement** action on an individual run whose job finished and whose channel announcement definitively failed before sending.

### Problem to solve

A scheduled command can update an external system successfully and then fail to post its receipt because the channel account is disconnected. Once the account is repaired, **Run now** executes the command again. The original receipt is the part the operator needs.

### Proposed solution

Show the recorded destination and allow an authorized operator to submit the retained announcement through the existing delivery path. Offer the action only when the original content and route are available, no send is pending, and the delivery record establishes that nothing reached the recipient. Keep the attempt and its outcome attached to the original run. An ambiguous or partial send should remain visible for manual review.

### Alternatives considered

Manual copy and paste requires reconstructing the text and destination. Existing transient retries help before a failure settles. This request covers recovery after an operator repairs the channel.

### Impact

Operators can recover a missed notification without repeating a chargeable agent turn or a command with external side effects.

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance example: a command increments a counter once, and its announcement fails before transport. After reconnecting the account, retry the announcement. The recipient gets the original text, the run shows the new delivery receipt, and the counter is still one.

A [reported missed announcement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162198) illustrates the workflow. The [documented delivery rules](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md#L95) distinguish definite failures from ambiguous sends. The [current manual run command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.ts#L278-L282) submits the job for execution.

No, proposing the idea only

issues.body:
### Summary

Let a board owner see which ready cards are candidates for the next worker batch, in order, using the current board and owner limits.

### Problem to solve

A ready queue can contain urgent and routine tasks for several agents. Listing the cards shows their status, but an owner may already be at capacity on a different board. Calling `workboard dispatch` to find out can claim cards and start paid model work before the operator has reviewed the batch.

### Proposed solution

Add a read-only preview such as `openclaw workboard dispatch --board ops --max-starts 2 --dry-run`. For the current ready queue, show the proposed candidates and explain material exclusions such as an existing claim or owner capacity. Reuse the dispatcher's selection policy. Mark the result as a snapshot since eligibility can change by the time real dispatch runs.

### Alternatives considered

`workboard list --status ready` is a useful inventory but does not apply cross-board capacity or the per-pass cap. A receipt from an actual dispatch arrives after workers may have started.

### Impact

Board owners can correct assignments or reprioritize cards before spending worker capacity on the wrong tasks.

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance example: agent A has a ready card on board ops and is already at its one-card limit on another board. Agent B is free. A one-start preview identifies B's candidate and explains A's deferral. Calling the preview twice creates no claim, worker run, or board mutation.

[Dispatcher selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/extensions/workboard/src/dispatcher.ts#L168-L216) and [dispatch CLI contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/docs/cli/workboard.md#dispatch). [#205625](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205625) describes the narrower problem of silent skips on an actual dispatch.

### Summary

Let operators apply proposed daily, weekly, and monthly retention counts to a read-only listing of one backup namespace.

### Problem to solve

Before tightening retention, an operator needs to know whether a particular recovery point will survive. `backup list` shows the inventory. The current remote create dry run returns a local archive plan before calculating remote retention. A real upload evaluates retention and deletes expired objects in the same operation.

### Proposed solution

Provide a retention preview for an existing namespace that lists the archive keys it would keep and expire under the supplied counts. Label the inventory time and namespace so the operator can tell what was evaluated. Reuse the retention selector used by upload. The preview should require only list/read access and leave objects and namespace ownership untouched.

### Alternatives considered

A spreadsheet or script can approximate the policy, but must duplicate the UTC day, Monday-week, and month rules as well as protection for the newest archive.

### Impact

Backup administrators could review the actual recovery points at risk before changing a schedule or enabling pruning on an established archive.

### Evidence/examples

I ran the [existing selector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/infra/backup-retention.ts#L62-L101) with two archives at 09:00 and 12:00 UTC on November 23, one on November 22, and an unrelated `owner.json`. With `keepDaily: 2`, it selected only the 09:00 archive for deletion. A preview over that inventory should name that key, leave all objects present, and explicitly describe the result as conditional on the inventory staying the same. [Remote dry run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/commands/backup-remote.ts#L92-L96) and [retention after upload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f538874baa1b78bcac088b122c46cff3e829fc10/src/commands/backup-remote.ts#L171-L183).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During Watch Live (Wear OS realtime Talk), the phone relay sets the state back to Listening on every `inputAudio` event the Gateway echoes for each microphone frame, so the Thinking state shown while the agent works is overwritten within one frame, and each of those events republishes the full Talk snapshot to the watch.

### Steps to reproduce

Derived from the code; not yet run on a watch.

1. Start Live on the watch and ask something that makes the agent work for more than a second (a tool call, a slow model).
2. Watch the status label.

### Expected behavior

The watch shows that the agent is working until the reply starts. Phone Talk handles the same event differently: `inputAudio` only updates its listening flag.

### Actual behavior

From the code:

- Every `inputAudio` event forces the Listening state: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d7861f77da916625c08c30bcbc8ad762f32f63/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkController.kt#L361-L363

```kotlin
"ready", "inputAudio" -> {
  updateActiveStateIfCurrent(owner, currentSessionId, ActiveTalkState.Listening)
}
```

- The Gateway relay broadcasts one `inputAudio` event per appended audio frame (`src/gateway/talk/relay/operations.ts`), and the watch microphone streams 20 ms frames whenever it is not playing.
- Each state update publishes a snapshot with no de-duplication: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d1d7861f77da916625c08c30bcbc8ad762f32f63/apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkController.kt#L811-L814

```kotlin
private fun setSnapshot(snapshot: WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot) {
  _snapshot.value = snapshot
  onSnapshot(snapshot)
}
```

Expected visible result (not yet observed): "Thinking" disappears after the watch's short local override and the orb reads "Listening" for the rest of a long agent run. Whether roughly 50 snapshot messages per second over Bluetooth also causes lag or resyncs needs a device run.

### OpenClaw version

main at d1d7861f77d (source reading)

### Operating system

Wear OS + Android (source analysis; no device run)

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

Watch -> phone relay -> Gateway realtime relay

### Impact and severity

Affected: Wear OS Live users on any turn where the agent takes time.
Severity: Medium (wrong status during the wait; possible message flood).
Frequency: every such turn, per the code.

### Additional information

Found by reading source during the Speech & Audio focus week. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` asserts THINKING but sends no `inputAudio` afterwards, so the overwrite is not covered.

### Summary

Let a reader select the first and last utterances of an agenda item in Meetings and download just that passage with its speakers and timestamps.

### Problem to solve

A team may need to share the decision from a ten-minute agenda item in a much longer meeting. The current Markdown export includes the full transcript and any saved notes. Omit the whole-meeting summary and apply the existing export size limit to the selected content.

Copying text from the browser can lose speaker and timestamp boundaries. The full host-side export requires filesystem access and still needs editing.

### Impact

Meeting participants can share the relevant decision with another team while keeping unrelated agenda items out of the artifact.

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance example: in a meeting with three agenda items, select a passage from the middle item across a transcript page boundary. Downloaded Markdown contains both endpoint utterances, their speaker labels and available timestamps, and no speech or summary from the other items. A small selection can be exported when the whole file exceeds the browser limit. issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
`buildRuntimeLine` includes `active_node=<node id|unknown>` (and `active_node_identity`). On `openai-completions` routes the Runtime line is relocated into the **first user message** (`relocateNonBehavioralRegion`). `active_node` changes whenever the macOS app's node goes away (app quit) and again when the app window is next used after a relaunch. Each change rewrites message 1, so every token after the system prompt has to be re-prefilled. On a local OpenAI-compatible server with a ~90k-token conversation that is a 67–85 s reply instead of ~1 s.

Same class as #167990 and #155685 (changing per-session values inside the cached prompt region); here the changing value is presence-driven, so it flips mid-conversation without the user doing anything in the chat.

### Steps to reproduce
1. `openai-completions` provider pointing at a local server with prompt caching (here: Kapitsa serving Qwen3.8 Flash-Next; untested on other servers, but any exact-prefix cache is exposed).
2. macOS app running and connected as a node; use the chat (Control UI webchat, or `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:cachetest --model <local>`). Send two messages: the second reuses the cache.
3. Quit the macOS app. Send a message. Message 1's Runtime line now says `active_node=unknown`; the cache breaks right after the system prompt.
4. Relaunch the app and move the mouse over its window. Send a message. `active_node=<mac node id>` again; the cache breaks again.

### Expected behavior
A presence change does not rewrite earlier messages. The current active computer is a per-turn fact, as the CLI path (`buildCliTurnAppendContext`) and the agent-harness path (`activeComputerContext`) already deliver it.

### Actual behavior
The value lives in message 1 and changes there. Captured with a logging relay between the gateway and the model server (full request bodies diffed):

| Step | `active_node` in message 1 | Server-reported cached tokens | Request diff vs previous |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | mac node id | 20,922 of 21,118 | append-only |
| app quit | `unknown` | 20,591 of 21,252 (system prompt only) | only index 1 differs: `active_node` |
| app relaunched, untouched | `unknown` | full reuse | append-only |
| app window used | mac node id | 20,591 of 22,090 (system prompt only) | only index 1 differs: `active_node` |
| control | mac node id | 22,112 of 22,285 | append-only |

In the real ~90k-token webchat session the same flip cost 67–85 s (`prompt 91091 (cached 21651) in 67427 ms`).

Gateway log for the same event:
```
[prompt-cache] cache read dropped 90602 -> 21651 ... for studio-flash/flash via boundary-aware:openai-completions; systemPromptSuffix(system prompt suffix digest changed (sections: Runtime)) ... providerPrefix=message:1.content
```

Side note: the drop diagnostic's tracker is keyed per session but its "previous request" skipped the intervening macOS-app turns in our logs, so `sections: Runtime` was reported against an older baseline. That made the trigger hard to attribute; I have not chased it further.

### Proposed fix (tested locally)
1. Drop `active_node` and `active_node_identity` from `buildRuntimeLine` (`src/agents/system-prompt-runtime.ts`).
2. In the embedded path, add `buildActiveNodeContextText(requesterProfileId)` as a `conversation-data` fact in `buildRuntimeFactsContext`, passing `requesterProfileId` from the call site the same way the system-prompt params do (`readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority(attempt.admittedRunContext)?.profileId`). Runtime-context carriers are append-only on openai-completions/ollama since 2026.10.10, so the fact rides the newest message.
3. In `buildCliTurnAppendContext`, append the active-computer text unconditionally. Today it is skipped when `resolveSystemPromptUsage()` returns the system prompt (a new claude-cli session's first turn), which relied on the Runtime line; without step 3, step 1 would leave that turn with no active-computer fact.

After applying this to the 2026.10.10 dist and restarting: quit and relaunch both reused the full history (`cached 22810/23018`, `23038/23304`), request bodies stayed append-only, and the active-computer line appeared in the newest message. Known gap: `settled-tool-finalization` runs skip runtime facts, so they no longer see the value.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

### Operating system
macOS 26.4.1 (arm64)

### Install method
npm global (Homebrew Node 26.12.1); macOS app 2026.10.10

### Model
Qwen3.8 Flash-Next (local)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw gateway → `openai-completions` custom provider → local OpenAI-compatible server (Kapitsa) over an SSH tunnel

### Impact and severity
Every quit/relaunch of the macOS app (including updates and reboots) costs one full re-prefill per active local-model conversation. On large contexts that is a minute or more per affected reply. Only measured on a local server; cloud prefix caches should see the same message-1 rewrite, but I have not measured that.

prs.title: fix(agents): show Doctor's restore-first warning before deleting a held store
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Follow-up to #207257. After deletion history is lost, Doctor holds back some agent stores and tells the operator to restore them first (`openclaw agents add … to abort deletion and restore`). `openclaw agents delete` on such an agent asked a plain "Delete agent?" with no hint of that, so a held store could be deleted without the user ever seeing Doctor's advice.

## Change

- Doctor's per-store restore-first guidance moved, unchanged, into `formatHeldAgentStoreGuidance` (`src/commands/doctor-agent-deletion-held.ts`). Doctor's journal repair calls it; nothing else formats it.
- `agents delete` reads Doctor's recorded recovery holds (`readAgentDeletionRecoveryHoldsInWorker`, the same record `agents add` checks). For each held store of the agent:
  - Interactive: the confirmation starts with `Warning: Doctor holds back a store of agent "<id>" because its deletion history was lost. Continuing deletes it without restoration:`, then Doctor's guidance, then the usual question.
  - `--force`: the same warning is printed to stderr and deletion proceeds. `--json` stdout is unchanged.
- Agents without a hold keep the ordinary confirmation.

Gateway: the CLI confirms locally before it calls the Gateway's `agents.delete`, so both CLI transports (through the Gateway and offline) show the warning. The Gateway method has no confirmation of its own.

## Not covered: Control UI

The Control UI delete dialog does not show the held-store warning. The UI has no hold state on the wire, and adding a protocol field for it is deliberately parked (decision D56): the UI lists only configured agents while holds are mostly on unconfigured stores, deletion moves files to Trash, and Doctor already prints the restore-first guidance. Reopen if a real report shows a Control UI user deleting a held store.

## User population

CLI users deleting an agent whose store Doctor holds back after a lost or unusable deletion journal.

## Evidence

- `agents.delete.test.ts` "shows Doctor's restore-first warning for a held store before confirming": a registered `retired` store, a reconstructed deletion journal that holds it, then `agents delete retired`.
  - Interactive: the confirmation contains `Doctor holds back a store of agent "retired"` and Doctor's `openclaw agents add 'retired' … to abort deletion and restore`; cancelling changes nothing. The configured `ops` agent (no hold) keeps `Delete agent "ops" and prune workspace/state?`.
  - `--force --json`: stderr carries the same warning; deletion proceeds and the registration is removed.
  - Red on main `98b9f17b`: the confirmation has no warning.
- `doctor-agent-deletion-journal.test.ts` and the rest of `agents.delete.test.ts` stay green (40 tests): Doctor's held-store text is byte-identical after the move.

prs.title: improve: skip unused model catalogs during provider auth and entry discovery
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw looks up synthetic provider auth or reads static catalog discovery entries for the embedded agent, it can ask plugins for their entries while explicitly excluding manifest model catalogs. Even then, discovery expanded the selected manifests’ model rows and indexed their owners. Each lookup paid for work whose result it discarded.

## User Impact

These lookups skip the unused catalog work automatically. Full discovery still registers providers that need a runtime hook, including when manifest providers are excluded. Provider ordering, credentials, and configuration stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The discovery planner knows both the requested mode and whether manifest providers are eligible. It keeps every selected plugin record for entry coverage, passes an empty list to manifest preparation only for this flag combination, and returns entry providers before filtering for full discovery. This keeps a missing entry from counting as complete coverage.

## Evidence

The regression uses one plugin with a discovery entry and another with a mixed static/runtime catalog. On the parent revision, the two entry-only lookups read 64 model IDs across 32 static models. The changed implementation reads zero. In strict mode, it returns an empty result before opening the partial entry. Full discovery still registers the runtime provider.

An isolated 1,024-model fixture counted ID reads through the production catalog planner on both revisions. Provider results and registration order matched in all five calls.

| Discovery call | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Entry-only, manifest providers included | 1,024 | 1,024 |
| Entry-only, manifest providers excluded | 1,024 | 0 |
| Same call with complete coverage required | 1,024 | 0 |
| Full discovery, manifest providers excluded | 1,024 | 1,024 |
| Same full call with complete coverage required | 1,024 | 1,024 |

The public synthetic-auth caller was also exercised on both revisions using a real plugin entry module, its generation-scoped metadata snapshot, and 1,024 manifest models. Two successive auth captures returned the expected distinct hook results, and the subsequent synchronous lookup returned undefined on both revisions. The fixture counted 3,072 model ID reads before and zero after across those three lookups.

All 55 tests across provider discovery, synthetic-auth entries and discovery, and the embedded agent’s static catalog passed. This measures model-row work. Whole-Gateway RSS and the ARM first-turn memory limit remain separate questions.

prs.title: improve: defer browser profile setup for configs without a browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting OpenClaw built the browser profile validators even when the config omitted the entire browser section. A local text inference command paid for the profile name, driver, endpoint, and engine checks before it could run its first turn.

## User Impact

Configs that omit the browser section can skip that allocation. A config with a browser section, including `browser.enabled: false`, pays the one-time cost when its shape is first read. Config keys, validation errors, and generated schemas stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional browser object already knows when it needs its shape. Its `profiles` getter now uses Zod's cached factory to construct the existing validator once. Browser schema inspection and clones share that validator.

## Evidence

- In 20 alternating fresh process pairs on Node 24.22.1 and Zod 4.6.7, constructing the isolated schema and first parsing an absent browser took a median 2.430 ms on the eager version and 1.218 ms on the deferred version. Median retained heap growth after GC was 315,704 and 120,824 bytes respectively, a difference of 190.3 KiB. First use of a browser shape paid the deferred setup cost. These figures measure the schema in isolation.
- From the built CLI, two fresh `infer model run --local` processes each loaded the real schema, completed one loopback Responses request, returned the expected text, and exited successfully. A construction counter at the emitted profile-name validator recorded zero for an absent browser and one for a disabled browser. Device latency and whole-process heap savings remain unmeasured.
- The full root parse constructed the validator immediately on the parent revision. At this head the count was zero after an absent-browser parse and one after an empty-browser parse. The regression checks clone identity and JSON Schema inspection, alongside the existing browser engine and endpoint refinements.
- All 21 focused browser, schema, hints, and startup tests passed. The generated base config schema and config docs baselines matched. The production build, including declarations, targeted type-aware lint, and the affected TypeScript test shard passed. Independent source review covered the full moved validator and the public inferred browser config types.
