prs.title: fix(macos): treat failed port inspection as unknown, not free
prs.body:
Closes #190152

## What Problem This Solves

macOS `PortGuardian` asks `lsof` which process listens on a port, and `lsof` can fail in ways that say nothing about the port: missing from `PATH`, exceeding the 5 s deadline (a wedged SMB/NFS mount), or exiting non-zero for another reason. The old code folded all of those into "no listener", so every caller read the port as free: `gateway install --force` / launchd repair overwrote a hand-started Gateway, `ManagedNodeGatewayMigration` took custody, and child start skipped attach and spawned a second Gateway ("Gateway stopped after five failed starts").

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing answer is not a negative answer, so `PortGuardian.inspect(port:)` returns `PortInspection`: `.free` (lsof ran, exited 1, no diagnostic), `.owned(Descriptor)`, or `.unknown` (timeout, pre-flight failure, unexpected exit, unparsable output). `lsof` runs with `-b` so a stalled mount cannot block the probe, and the call goes through `ShellExecutor.runDetailed` because the old `run` discarded the exit code.

`lsof -b` writes its own `avoiding readlink(...)` / `WARNING: can't stat()` notes to stderr even on a clean no-match, so "stderr is empty" cannot identify a clean probe; any other `lsof:` diagnostic is a failed probe. Every consumer handles `.unknown` conservatively: persistence ensure returns `.skipped`, repair withholds evidence, migration preserves the existing owner, attach never spawns a child on an uninspected port, and Onboarding says the port could not be checked. Everything lives under `apps/macos/`: no shared package, CLI or protocol surface, and no `Codable` type changed.

## User Impact

* Failing probes no longer replace, migrate, or double-start a Gateway; the app waits for the next probe.
* Healthy machines are unchanged: a successful `lsof` with no match is still `.free`.
* Diagnostics and Onboarding report that the port could not be inspected instead of "nothing is listening".
* Accepted trade-off: an inconclusive probe during migration records one failed attempt and retries next launch instead of stealing a running service.

## Evidence

Throwaway workflow on hosted `macos-26` (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3), proof head `7f95387`, base `main` `f91f580b7f`. One unrelated pre-existing build break is patched in the jobs only (`ChatMediaVideoAttachment.swift` uses `VideoPlayer` without an availability guard); it is not in this diff.

```
Build complete! (692.57s)                                          # swift build --build-tests
✔ Test run with 8 tests in 1 suite passed after 5.845 seconds.     PortGuardianDiagnosticsTests
✔ Test run with 92 tests in 1 suite passed after 26.338 seconds.   GatewayProcessManagerTests
0/440 files require formatting, 6 files skipped                    swiftformat (0 errors)
```

### Ordinary managed startup (the blocker)

The packaged `OpenClaw.app` with **no** `disable-launchagent` marker and **no** `--attach-only` flag, a clean state dir, Onboarding already seen, no LaunchAgent installed — so `installation` resolves to `.managed` and `gatewayHosting` to `.app`, and the app reaches `startAppHostedGateway` on its own. `lsof` resolves through `/usr/bin/env`; a stub first on `PATH` decides which probe the shipped code runs.

```
# lsof exits 1 with a stderr diagnostic: the scan could not be trusted
STUB_CALLS=12  CHILD_MAX=0  LISTENER_MAX=0
[ai.openclaw:gateway] gateway ws connect failed ... Could not connect to the server
PASS: startup was not refused as an externally managed Gateway
PASS: an unreadable port never produced a Gateway child
PASS: the app published an unknown-port diagnostic (not silent free)

# lsof exits 1 with no diagnostic: this is what an idle port returns
STUB_CALLS=3  CHILD_MAX=1  LISTENER_MAX=1  CHILD_NOW=1
PASS: an idle port starts a real Gateway child
PASS: the idle-port child owns the listener
```

The `.external` early return at `GatewayProcessManager+Hosting.swift:341` (the path the old `--attach-only` + `disable-launchagent` fixtures took) never fires: the app log has no `externally managed`. The child PID reported by `lsof -Fp` is not the app process, proving a separate Gateway was started.

### The shipped app-hosted start, with a real broken `lsof`

`app 1` calls `startAppHostedGateway` on a real `GatewayProcessManager` (supervisor launcher replaced to observe the launch count). Zero child launches:

```
[proof-app] app 1 supervisor launches: 0 (active=false pid=nil)
```

### The real packaged app, Onboarding connection page

A packaged `OpenClaw.app` started with `--attach-only`, clean state dir, no `openclaw.json`. A stub `lsof` first on `PATH` decides which probe runs. Rows are OCR of the app window, lowercased.

Base (`main` `f91f580b7f`), scan fails — the page still promises the install:

```
on this mac recommended
private to this computer. installs and starts automatically.
```

Candidate, same binary (`sha256 1eb00eba931a…`), driven down both probe answers:

```
# lsof exits 1 with a diagnostic on stderr: the scan could not be trusted
on this mac recommended
could not check whether port 18789 is free. startup walts until it can.

# lsof exits 1 with no diagnostic: this is what an idle port returns
on this mac recommended
private to this computer, installs and starts automatically.
```

### A real latest-stable → candidate upgrade

`v2026.11.10`'s CLI installs the service on one home; the candidate reads that state back:

```
"runtimeIntent": { "status": "known", "stored": true,
  "revision": "1bc195fdd5574fdc428cbdf21d22d26ab48967b02544cf82e62cff7801a4bad7",
  "pin": { "runtime": "bun", "path": "<old>/bin/bun" } }
PASS: LaunchAgent byte-identical | pin store byte-identical | 12/12 PASS
```

### Not covered

`gatewayNodeResumeCommand` is app-written, so a CLI upgrade cannot seed it; `app 3` covers it (fresh `UserDefaults` readback). Every changed file is macOS-only; `xcode-27` is unavailable to forks.

prs.title: fix: move ended one-time automations to run history
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

A one-time automation that failed or had unconfirmed delivery stayed in the Paused list, even though nothing was scheduled. Over time those entries accumulated, and Run history did not offer a way to try the task again.

## User Impact

- After its final attempt, a one-time automation leaves the list whether it succeeds, fails, or has unconfirmed delivery. Failure notices point to Run history rather than telling people to re-enable an ended job. Transient retries and explicitly scheduled next checks still work.
- Administrators with unrestricted run-history access can select **Retry** on eligible failures in **Automations → Run history**. Retry starts a fresh attempt, not a delivery replay; check uncertain delivery before retrying. Jobs with authority tied to their original identity aren't automatically recreated.
- Doctor reports the old entries it finds. On repair it backs up cron state, moves recognized ended failures to Run history, and preserves the existing run or reconstructs the last recorded outcome if older history has expired. When an explicit keep-after-run or cleanup policy has no faithful conversion, Doctor keeps the definition paused and explains why. It does not rerun anything. The retired option is removed from the CLI, tool, protocol, and editors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler records history and retains the definition privately in the same transaction that removes the ended job from the list. This lets Retry look up the original run without putting the job back in Paused or returning its definition in the history response. The implementation reuses the existing history retention, scheduler admission, and Doctor backup, rather than introducing a separate archive service.

Related automation cleanup PRs may overlap in schedule settlement, Doctor cron repair, Gateway/agent tool schemas, and the Control UI automation editor. Those cleanups are not folded into this change.

## Evidence

I merged main `2ab7b31a13d95` without rebasing and fast-forwarded the verified repairs to `52aac6873c4668462d3f313575bc1eca30c603b6`. Both new commits include the daniel-lxs co-author trailer.

I preserved running background commands and held legacy cleanup policies for backed-up Doctor conversion. Local checks also exposed and reproduced three additional defects: the reader worker discarded the private Retry view, no-prompt Doctor skipped SQLite-only legacy policies, and alert delivery receipts could not settle after a definition was retired. I fixed those at their existing owners.

I ran the final focused checks locally with Node 26.12.1:

| Check | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cron lifecycle, recovery, settlement and persistence | 466 | 0 | 0 |
| Gateway Retry, delivery and invitation boundaries | 134 | 0 | 0 |
| CLI | 64 | 0 | 0 |
| Doctor migration and ownership | 34 | 0 | 0 |
| UI unit tests | 48 | 0 | 0 |
| Control UI browser flows with a mock Gateway | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Plugin contracts, state migration, ownership and scenario fixtures | 67 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total across 50 test files** | **815** | **0** | **0** |

All 10 targeted production/test typecheck graphs passed. Production lint, changed-file formatting, the normal pre-commit line-cap gate, and `git diff --check` passed. The complete cron selection passed after the cross-store fixture assertion was corrected; the unchanged 36-case authority matrix passed again after its fixture-only extraction.

The simplify pass kept the scheduler, history and Doctor owners. I updated terminal assertions to read retained outcomes, changed terminal-write fault injection to exercise deletion, and preserved the delivery, authority, restart and no-replay checks. Existing Doctor ownership projection and authority scenario data moved to their existing helper modules to satisfy file-size gates. Against merged main: production +758/-242 lines; tests/fixtures +736/-683; other files +25/-35.

**Still draft and under the existing landing hold.** I posted no PR comments and requested no re-review. No clean independent review is claimed; the earlier local review failed its read-only sandbox preflight. Full CI, PostgreSQL/Windows/native lanes, and the separate runtime/update proof were not run here.

ClawSweeper's remaining real-Gateway proof is terminal settlement, exact-run Retry, and a background command finishing after its executor ends while its later turn is refused exactly once. The separate VM work must cover **v2026.11.5**, **9.x extended-stable**, and **10.x** updates to this head, preserving settings/history, legacy keep policies before Doctor and queued/running cases, plus the old updater round trip. Full original-review base-red/head-green runtime evidence remains pending.

The screenshots below are historical UI-only evidence from the earlier candidate, using the real Control UI with a deterministic mock Gateway. They do not prove this head's runtime behavior.

### Clean comparison

**Before — failed run has no Retry and the ended job still has a Paused group**

![Run history with a failed staging-build check and no Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8d099e8-b593-42a6-a9ab-f827272913e2)

prs.title: fix(qa): stop failing subagent recovery when tool calls are disabled
prs.body:
Related: [QA Smoke evidence on #207258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207258#issuecomment-7235075201), #207052

## What Problem This Solves

QA Smoke reports that empty subagent recovery failed when a finalization request keeps tool definitions for prompt caching. The definitions are present, but `tool_choice: "none"` prevents the model from calling them.

## User Impact

The smoke check accepts both ways of disabling tool calls: no definitions, or an explicit `"none"` choice. It still rejects a finalization that leaves tools callable. No runtime behavior or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the existing assertion and its failure message change. The scenario still requires exactly two finalization attempts and verifies the single completed write, including its contents and modification time after Gateway restart.

## Evidence

I ran `qa run --qa-profile smoke-ci --scenario subagent-empty-completion-recovery --concurrency 1` through the repository's Crabbox wrapper on AWS, using the same lease for both revisions.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway responsive while scanning large model catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #145675
Alternative to #145676
Related: #156054

## What Problem This Solves

When an operator configures a large model catalog (500-1,000+ entries), `projectCatalog` and Gateway `models.list` evaluate routes, credentials, and public model projections in uninterrupted synchronous loops. Across a persistent `openclaw gateway` daemon and controlled 500-1,000 model scans, this blocks the Node.js event loop for roughly 0.9s to 22.9s at a time, stalling concurrent health checks, control-plane RPCs, and channel traffic until the scan finishes.

## User Impact

- Concurrent loopback HTTP requests stay responsive both on a running `openclaw gateway` daemon serving live CLI/WebSocket `models.list` calls (`GET /healthz` median `2,482.6 ms -> 16.4 ms`, max `5,205.1 ms -> 154.0 ms` across 1,011 models) and in controlled in-process benchmarks, and repeated `prepared.read()` calls on a prepared catalog avoid multi-second synchronous projection stalls (see Verification gaps below for live external cloud-provider network discovery).
- No configuration, schema, migration, or caller API changes are required; public synchronous reader contracts remain unchanged and the change can be reverted cleanly.
- Operational boundaries:
  - The `8 ms` budget (`CATALOG_SCAN_YIELD_BUDGET_MS`) is a cooperative checkpoint between model entries during asynchronous preparation. It cannot preempt synchronous work inside a single model evaluation, non-per-entry setup/sorting, WebSocket JSON serialization, or the final single-frame live readiness publication pass, so it is not a hard real-time latency bound; in standalone `projectCatalog` benchmarks, median scan wall time stayed within `-0.3%` to `+2.9%` while `models.list` end-to-end wall time in direct in-process benchmarks dropped by removing redundant read-time work.
  - Callers that pass a `withCurrent` authority wrapper without a synchronous `assertCurrent` callback disable inter-entry slice yields inside that wrapper (after pre-wrapper selected-account settlement when applicable) so wrapper-scoped invariants hold.

## Why This Change Was Made

Catalog preparation and `models.list` now split static preparation from live synchronous publication while keeping one shared harness-availability owner:

1. **Cooperative sliced preparation, static warming, and shared availability ownership:** `projectCatalog` and `prepareModelsListResult` (`provider-config`, `default`, `all`, and `configured` views) yield via `node:timers/promises` `setImmediate` after `8 ms` slices while warming host route evaluations, static native policy and non-`openclaw`/`auto` host configuration, memoized harness policies/support contexts/provider ownership, shared configured route overrides, and static public display/thinking fields. Prepared catalog policies and memoized support contexts feed the shared `resolveAgentHarnessAvailabilityDecision` owner in `src/agents/harness/availability.ts` (preserving the single-owner routing boundary from `28c26865b241` across catalog projections, model commands, spawn/model resolution, and execution while skipping plugin-registry scope entry on ordinary `openclaw` or empty-harness `auto` reads).
2. **Reasserted authority and single-frame live publication:** Slice resumptions and publication boundaries recheck the path's active guards (caller `CurrentReadAuthority`, independent draft and publication scopes, and entry-to-stale transitions on owner currency and `authValidUntil`), while `notePendingAccountCatalogPreparation` and `accountCatalogEpoch` coordinate `projectCatalog` rescanning when concurrent selected-account outcomes publish. New static warmers (`prepareOnly`) stop before revocable native readiness (`evaluateNative` / `readModelCatalogReadiness`) and live `harness.supports` probes so final `projectCatalog` projection and synchronous `prepared.read()` re-evaluate live readiness, `harness.supports`, and alternative-runtime exclusion in one synchronous frame (while preserving existing preparation-time checks for picker-alternative base selection, heterogeneous default previews, and initial `provider-config` projection), and `src/agents/model-auth-*.ts` stays untouched to preserve the provider-config fast path landed in #156054.

Thanks to #145676 and its author for earlier investigation on #145675; with the provider-config comparison fast path landed separately in #156054, this PR implements cooperative slicing and static warming against current `main`'s catalog preparation, shared harness availability owner, and multi-view Gateway projection paths.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- `src/agents/harness/availability.ts`:
  - `resolveAgentHarnessAvailabilityDecision` accepts optional `preparedPolicy`, `prepareOnly`, `resolveSupportContext`, and `withRegistryScope` hooks so prepared catalog projections reuse memoized policies and support contexts through the single shared owner for runtime override precedence, implicit Codex fallback, forced-runtime handling, and `fallbackRuntime: "openclaw"` without entering plugin-registry scope when `policy.runtime` is `"openclaw"` or `"auto"`.
- `src/agents/model-catalog-decision-runtime.ts` & `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.ts`:
  - `createCatalogProjectionReader` warms per-entry host evaluations, static native policy, and static route projections in `8 ms` slices (`CATALOG_SCAN_YIELD_BUDGET_MS = 8`), rechecking active `authority?.assertCurrent?.()` and entry-valid-to-stale transitions across credential expiry, secret-snapshot revisions, personal-catalog currency, owner currency, and selected-account observations on slice resumptions and before publication.
  - `notePendingAccountCatalogPreparation` and `accountCatalogEpoch` synchronize concurrent session-metadata `projectCatalog` and `prepareModelsListResult` callers across `0..M` selected-account discovery publications, retiring per-provider and auth-alias `evaluations` entries and resetting `projectedCatalog` whenever account outcomes update, and caching `projectedCatalog` only for unretired, authority-free callers.
  - `createCatalogDecisionRuntimeResolver` preserves no-registry policy selection and `openclaw` / empty-harness `auto` scope-free fast paths, memoizing `resolveProviderRefOwnership` per normalized provider, `resolveAgentHarnessPolicy`, and `buildAgentHarnessSupportContext` while delegating runtime overrides and fallback decisions to `resolveAgentHarnessAvailabilityDecision` and keeping CLI-binding short-circuits, `auto` selection hints/priorities, and live `harness.supports` checks intact.
- `src/agents/model-catalog-view.ts`:
  - `createCatalogNativePolicyPreparer` exposes `prepareNativePolicy` to warm static harness policy and per-provider merged host configuration while preserving the `openclaw` / `auto` short-circuit (no extra `resolveMergedModelProviderConfig` or `apiKey` getter reads on ordinary rows) and stopping before revocable `readModelCatalogReadiness` checks.
  - `createModelCatalogView` accepts an optional shared `resolveOverrides` resolver and reuses cached donor projections when route variants match while keeping narrowed runtime donor sets isolated.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.ts` & `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-runtime-choices.ts`:
  - `createScanAuthority` combines active `preparationAuthority`, `draftAccountSelection`, `publicationScope`, and entry-valid-to-stale transitions on personal-catalog and target-projector currency across `provider-config` inventory warming and logical-visible catalog preparation while keeping `withCurrent` wrapper entry counts bounded.
  - `createModelsListPublicProjector` and `prepareModelPickerRuntimeChoices` cache static display/fast-mode fields by `(provider, id)`, worker-placement `agentRuntime` by `(id, source)`, and main-row thinking profiles, keying per-entry projections by `(runtimeChoice, selectedRuntime.id, selectedRuntime.source)` and filtering picker alternatives against the live selected runtime on each read so live harness fallback transitions update the main row, `runtimeChoices`, and `defaultModelRuntimes` consistently while keeping alternative runtime donors' `thinkingLevels` isolated.

</details>

## Evidence

Validated on Linux x64 (`Node v24.22.1`) against baseline `e4517b0ef2f4` with candidate full-diff SHA-256 prefix `1fff33a7554f` (`git diff --binary --full-index`):

- **Persistent loopback `openclaw gateway` daemon + live CLI/WebSocket `models.list` RPCs (`pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --tailscale off` built on `e4517b0ef2f4` vs `e4517b0ef2f4` + `1fff33a7554f`, `models.mode: "replace"` with 10 loopback providers / `1,000` configured synthetic models, external HTTP probes polling `GET /healthz` every `25 ms` paired to server-side RPC execution spans by JSON-RPC request ID):**
  - Returned model sets and SHA-256 digests were identical before and after (`1,011` rows on `view: "all"`, `1,001` rows on `default` view, `1,000` synthetic rows; idle `openclaw gateway call health` baseline `/healthz` max `4.7 ms` before, `18.7 ms` after).
  - Across 3 measured `pnpm openclaw gateway call models.list --json --params '{"view":"all","refresh":true}'` runs after 1 warmup (`218-230` `GET /healthz` samples per run, `0` timeouts, `0` missed ticks), 3-run median concurrent `GET /healthz` latency dropped from `2,482.6 ms` (`2,468.9-2,484.2 ms`) to `16.4 ms` (`15.8-16.4 ms`), P95 dropped from `4,933.7 ms` (`4,931.3-4,937.4 ms`) to `21.4 ms` (`21.2-22.6 ms`), and max dropped from `5,205.1 ms` (`5,181.9-5,208.5 ms`) to `154.0 ms` (`135.4-160.7 ms`, `-97.0%`), with CLI WebSocket RPC wall time `5,528.7 ms -> 5,713.1 ms`.
  - On `default` view (`--params '{"refresh":true}'`), concurrent `GET /healthz` median / P95 / max dropped from `2,457.5 / 4,892.9 / 5,139.8 ms` to `15.9 / 21.2 / 164.7 ms`; on `--params '{"view":"all","preparedOnly":true}'`, max `GET /healthz` latency dropped from `5,184.7 ms` to `136.7 ms`.
- **Controlled concurrent `GET /healthz` benchmark (1 warmup + 3 measured runs per case, 10 providers, child-process HTTP client probing every `25 ms` while `projectCatalog`, `buildModelsListResult`, and `requestModelsList` run in-process; post-fix measured on `e4517b0ef2f4` + `2f34f262a262` prior to the refactor-only shared-availability delegation in `1fff33a7554f`, pre-fix baseline from `2b3579b7274c` on the same host/harness):**
  - At `N = 500`, median `GET /healthz` latency during scans dropped from `458.4-2,769.7 ms` (max `906.2-5,593.9 ms`) to `15.2-19.2 ms` (max `24.7-59.7 ms`), and median max event-loop turn gap dropped from `899.3-5,488.8 ms` to `13.0-47.0 ms`.
  - At `N = 1,000`, median `GET /healthz` latency during scans dropped from `2,904.1-11,226.7 ms` (max `5,950.4-22,906.4 ms`) to `17.4-41.5 ms` (max `39.4-115.1 ms`), and median max event-loop turn gap dropped from `5,782.5-21,636.6 ms` to `15.5-91.1 ms`. In separate segmented `prepareModelsListResult` measurements on `e4517b0ef2f4`, the 1st synchronous `prepared.read()` took `35.3-36.6 ms` at `N = 500` and `72.4-81.1 ms` at `N = 1,000` across the three picker views, and `15.0 ms` / `36.6 ms` on `provider-config` (down from `3,899.1 ms` and `14,179.8 ms` before the fix on `default` view).
- **Focused unit and regression tests on `e4517b0ef2f4` + `1fff33a7554f` (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`):**
  - New regressions (real `setImmediate` callback interleaving without fake timers, mid-scan authority/owner/expiry abort before evaluating remaining rows, shared `resolveAgentHarnessAvailabilityDecision` fallback and runtime-override delegation, uncached retired-owner projection, dual-branch selected-account publication alignment, `"openclaw"` fast-path default-override normalization, and live `supports()` main-row + `runtimeChoices` + `defaultModelRuntimes` fallback) fail before the production fix and pass with it; compatibility invariants (including no-registry configured runtime preservation and scope-free hot reads) pass both before and after:
    - `src/agents/model-catalog-decisions.test.ts` - pass (`21.4s` standalone wall time; Vitest `17.0s` across `37` tests, including shared-availability fallback/override delegation and full-state `prepareChatMetadataModelProjection` + `models.list` dual-branch account-publication join)
    - `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-result.runtime-choices.test.ts` - pass (`22.0s` standalone)
    - `src/gateway/server-methods/models.prepared.test.ts` - pass (`20.4s` standalone; combined 3-file catalog/Gateway run `79` passed)
    - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts` & `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts` - pass (`53` passed across 2 files; `18.3s` and `19.1s` standalone)
    - `src/agents/harness/policy.test.ts` & `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.native-demand.test.ts` - pass (`18.5s` standalone on `15` native-demand lifecycle tests)
- **Targeted static, boundary, ratchet, contract, and `check:changed` checks (on `e4517b0ef2f4` + `1fff33a7554f`):**
  - `git diff --check`, `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `oxlint` (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm lint:tmp:tsgo-core-boundary`, `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:database-worker-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:database-dialect-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, `pnpm check:test-timeout-race-ratchet --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4`, and `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4` - all pass.
  - `pnpm check:changed --base e4517b0ef2f4e366668e0e00a909297e5a9bf3b4` across the 8 changed files - `33/34` sub-checks pass (sole non-zero item is an unrelated historical changelog bot-attribution line in `CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130` already present on baseline `e4517b0ef2f4`).
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test:contracts:plugins` on `e4517b0ef2f4` + `1fff33a7554f` - pass (`1,097` passed; regression-only shared plugin contract check; its fixtures do not exercise large-catalog event-loop contention).

CI: runs after maintainer approval.

Local review: autoreview P0-P2 on e4517b0ef2f4..4d1db294f358: scoped-clean (0 P0-P2 findings).

prs.title: feat: use one check script for model-free automations
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

## What Problem This Solves

Today, writing an automation that checks something without a model starts with a choice between a condition script and a script payload. They share the same saved state, but have different result formats and cannot be combined.

## User Impact

- Use one JavaScript check to stay quiet, post a message through the automation’s delivery, or append a message to a configured agent prompt and run it. Configure it in the Control UI, use `--check-script` in the CLI, or send `check` through the automations tool or Gateway. Shell command jobs keep their separate operator policy.
- Run `openclaw doctor --fix` after upgrading. Doctor backs up cron storage, reports each conversion, and carries over saved state, once behavior, execution limits and tool restrictions for jobs it can convert. If it cannot preserve what a job does—such as a script waking an existing conversation, a condition starting a shell command or system event, or a result it cannot safely translate—it pauses the job and reports why. Recover the original definition from the backup, edit the check, then re-enable it.

## Why This Change Was Made

One executor and one check result replace the two JavaScript execution paths. Shell commands do not become agent-callable checks. The draft touches shared automation schema, run finalization, Doctor, CLI flags, and the Control UI editor; those are likely conflict points with the sibling automation cleanup PRs.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The draft head is `ca0e135843943c7c02f5b9e63994452335dabd1c`.

I reproduced the dropped flat/dotted check fields, incorrect validation classification, failed quiet check-only completion, and state loss on check-budget edits before fixing them. Focused local CLI, Gateway, scheduler, runtime, storage, Doctor, and UI suites passed after migrating the affected fixtures. The last backend rerun passed 104 tests; the final UI run passed 72 tests. Core/UI production and affected cron, Gateway, Doctor, and UI-test typechecks passed, along with changed-file lint/format, the UI copy baseline, and generated Gateway validator verification. The SQLite tests cover backup, conversion, state/tool-cap preservation, unsupported-job pausing, idempotency, and legacy finalized-script state recovery. These are local boundary tests, not released-install upgrade proof.

The simplification pass removed the retired script executor path and the opt-in screenshot-only regression test while preserving timeout, authority, cancellation, delivery, state, and recovery coverage. The generated Gateway validator change is required for the new public check contract; it is generator output, not a hand-written workaround.

Runtime proof still needed: a real Gateway quiet/post/wake flow with an actual agent/model and delivery, state/once/pacing and restart behavior; fresh-install and real upgrades from supported older releases, including 9.x extended-stable and 10.x, with the old updater round trip and in-flight legacy recovery; accessible annotated before/after captures from the real editor. A final production build and final-head CI are also not verified. Local independent review could not start because Codex failed its read-only sandbox preflight. I kept the PR draft and did not request a hosted re-review.

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

prs.title: fix: keep your account's model access in managed worktrees and other workspaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A chat can require an OpenAI access program that the account offers. When that chat's session is bound to a managed worktree, turns that run in the worktree (for example, a subagent reporting back to its parent) were refused before any model request with "This … program is not advertised for the current account, model, and runtime". The same account in the same chat passed for ordinary messages. Users saw subagent results fail to come back.

## User Impact

Turns that run in a workspace other than the agent's main one (managed worktrees, child sessions, cron jobs with a workspace, compaction with a requested workspace) now see the same account facts as the main workspace. The access check is unchanged: a program is still allowed only when the account's current credential advertises it, and no request reaches a model without it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The facts an account is offered (`providerOutcomes`) belong to the agent and its credential, not to a directory. They live in the prepared catalog inventory, and every inventory row is already guarded per provider: a source fingerprint (provider config including the resolved key, the providing plugins' versions and install hashes, auth profiles and order, env) plus the credential identity. But the inventory was stored per catalog owner, and owners are keyed by workspace because a workspace can add plugins. So an owner for a second workspace started empty, and in static mode (turns never rediscover) it had no account facts. Only `chat.send` avoided this, because it deliberately prepares its catalog from the main workspace.

Now a non-configured owner is offered the configured owner's inventory for the same agent, and the existing retention guards decide which rows hold for its own config and credentials. The seed is used only when the plugin set matches exactly (a workspace plugin could otherwise provide the same provider id with different code). The owner key, plugins and models stay per workspace. The seed applies at retention time, so a rejected seed does not hide the provider's generated models.

Named edges, not coded:
- If the configured owner has recorded discovery failures, a seeded worktree run owner retries that discovery until its lease ends.
- Before the configured owner's first discovery, or right after a provider config or sign-in change and before rediscovery completes, a worktree turn can still be refused. A main-workspace turn recovers on rediscovery. This is not a regression.

## Evidence

- New `prepared-model-runtime.workspace-inventory.test.ts`. Each case prepares the worktree turn with the dispatch's plugin generation, as report turns are prepared. The entitlement is keyed by account and credential identity:
  - `gives a worktree run with the same direct key only the account facts of its own credential` and `… with the same stored account …` see the main workspace's outcomes. Both fail on the merge base (`[]`).
  - `… with a different direct key …`, `… with a second stored account …` and `… with a signed-out credential …` inherit nothing.
  - `drops the account facts on the next worktree turn after the credential rotates`: after a sign-in change, a turn pinned to the old generation is refused ("superseded"), and the next turn sees no old-account facts.
  - The negative cases pass on the merge base by construction, since it never shares facts. With the retention credential guard disabled, the second-account, signed-out and rotation cases fail. The direct-key case is caught separately by the provider-config fingerprint, which includes the resolved key.
- Real in-process Gateway fixture (synthetic HTTP only; not committed because it clones the repository): `chat.send` and then a requester-settle completion into a parent bound to a real managed worktree. Merge base: the ordinary turn passes and the completion is refused (`OPENAI_ACCESS_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE`, not advertised). This branch: both pass. The worktree-bound `chat.send` turn passes on both.
- Prepared model runtime, prepared model catalog and access-program suites plus every direct importer of the changed files: 64 files, 475 tests, all pass.
- `findConfiguredOwnerCandidates` moved unchanged to `prepared-model-runtime.configured-owner.ts` so the owner module stays within its line cap.
- Production (read-only): every refusal of this kind came from a session bound to a managed worktree. Each worktree was created minutes to hours before the first refusal, and none of those sessions ever had a successful report.

prs.title: fix(agents): one tool-result bound on every route, untrusted-content wrapper intact
prs.body:
## Problem

A tool result that is too big for the model is cut differently on each route, and on two of them the cut is unsafe or loses data:

- **Codex app-server dynamic tools** kept a prefix only and appended "rerun with narrower args". When the result was untrusted network content, the cut removed the wrapper's end marker, so the rest of the turn ran with an open untrusted-content region. Production (one team deployment, 7 days): 719 cut results in 102 sessions, **292 of them with the wrapper left open** (`github_read` 227, code-mode `exec` 59, `sessions_history` 7, `wait` 1).
- **Agents API** cut a prefix with no notice and no file.
- **Copilot** forwarded results with no bound at all (no production Copilot sessions in the window; found by reading the code).
- **Embedded** (#206880) bounded at the per-result cap, which is looser than the context guard's budget below 32k-token windows and with images. The guard then cut again with no file path.

## Solution

One bound, `boundToolResult`, for every route that executes OpenClaw tools:

- **Budget:** the strictest one the result meets later: the per-result cap, then the context guard's weighted share with images and other blocks reserved first. A bounded result is a fixed point of both the transcript cap and the context guard, so the saved-file path survives. Unknown window: the 16k default.
- **Cut:** head and tail (the existing truncator); the full text goes to an owner-only file (`writePrivateTempFile`). The notice is harness-neutral: `[... N chars omitted. Full output: <path>]`. A route whose model cannot open a Gateway file gets the same cut with a size-only notice: the Codex app-server (its native file tools run under its own sandbox policy, local or remote) and the Agents API (file tools run in the hosted VM). A path is named only where OpenClaw's own `read` opens it (embedded, Copilot). If the budget cannot hold the whole path, the notice names the size only.
- **Untrusted content fails closed, per frame:** a frame is one `wrapExternalContent` region (warning, start marker and metadata header, body, end marker with the same id), found inside any text block, raw or JSON-escaped, so several wrapped values in one JSON block (`web_search`) count one by one (`findExternalContentFrames`, next to the writer). Frames and the text between them are kept whole, in order, while they fit; the first piece that does not fit keeps its ends and loses only body (head and tail); everything after it is left out. One trusted notice, `[... N chars omitted. Full output: <path>]`, follows the cut outside every frame, with the true count. A frame whose ends cannot fit (forged or hostile metadata, an image taking a small window's share) is left out whole: untrusted text never reaches the model outside a frame. When images alone exceed the context share, the bound reserves what the embedded context guard will keep (the images that fit plus its image-omission notice, one shared formatter), so the guard drops images without cutting the framed text again. Results with no frames keep the head-and-tail cut.
- **Where:** `runAgentHarnessToolInvocation` after result middleware (Codex dynamic tools, Agents API); the Copilot bridge calls it directly (`boundAgentHarnessToolResult`, private harness SDK subpath); embedded keeps its `afterToolCall` call site. Copilot registers the file to the run's owner (the sandbox workspace for sandboxed runs), so its own `read` can open it.

Codex `skills_read` stays whole-or-error: its check now uses the same budget as the bound, so a skill that passes is never cut later (an attempt budget smaller than the model window used to let a 12k skill pass and then be cut while reported as a success).

Deleted: the Codex prefix-only cut and its "rerun" notice, the Agents API silent prefix cut.

**Agents API serialization:** the adapter joins the bounded blocks with newlines and a 54-char placeholder per image into one function-output string, then applies its own cap. The bound reserves exactly what that serialization adds (`resultBound.reservedChars`, computed from the adapter's one `serializeFunctionOutput`), so the single cut leaves room for it and the adapter's cap never cuts a bounded result. The bound never adds a block (its notice goes into a text block it keeps; it only removes others), so the reserve computed before the cut covers the output. One cut, so the omitted count in the notice is true.

Not in this PR: Tool Search's whole-result omission (3 unrecoverable omissions in 7 days in production) stays. Removing it is safe only where the model can read the saved file; on Codex and Agents API a partial page would show a continuation cursor with no way to read the omitted records. It returns once those routes can read the file.

## Security boundary

This changes how untrusted content is cut on every route. Before: the Codex route dropped end markers (292 open wrappers in 7 days), and on the other routes several frames in one result could lose markers or leave untrusted text outside a frame. After: every frame the finder matches is either whole, or cut in its body with both ends kept, or left out; the omission notice is ours and sits outside every frame. Residuals, named, not fixed here:
- A forged frame (raw tool output that copies the marker format) whose metadata is oversized is left out whole, and so is everything after it. Accepted: fail closed is the rule, and the saved file (where the reader can open it) still holds everything.
- A start marker with no matching end marker is plain text and gets the plain cut; markers in another encoding (`\u003c`, HTML entities) are not found. The writers produce neither.
- A cut JSON block is no longer valid JSON; its frames stay whole.
- A spill file read back with `read` has no wrapper (same as the `web_fetch` precedent).
- The two MCP serving paths stay unbounded: there, wrapped values sit inside JSON the tools build, and that needs an owner at the tools that wrap them.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A recovery hint for size-only routes (Codex, Agents API), which only report the size today.
- One fit predicate for `skills_read` and the bound, with the default budget inside `resolveToolResultBudget`.
- Move the bound out of `embedded-agent-runner/` under one name.
- Check the bound is not above Codex's own tool-output limit for dynamic tools.
- Spill provenance so `read` wraps a spilled untrusted result; a spill size cap with a truthful notice; a retention rule.
- Stage the spill file into the executor's filesystem for Codex and the Agents API; Tool Search's omission can go after that.
- A per-turn aggregate budget on the Codex, Agents API and Copilot routes.
- Carry provenance on the block (wrap after the cut) instead of finding frames in text.
- The two unbounded MCP serving paths, once the tools that wrap JSON values own their bound.
- A truthful notice when a tiny budget (reserve close to the cap) shortens the notice itself.

## Gaps

- Two MCP serving paths (`mcp-http.handlers.ts`, `src/mcp/plugin-tools-handlers.ts`) have no tool-result bound; out of scope.
- Agents API: if image placeholders alone exceed the per-result budget (hundreds of images in one result), the text budget clamps to zero and the adapter's cap cuts the placeholders.
- Codex and Agents API results are cut with a size-only notice; the omitted middle is not recoverable there (it was not before either). Staging the file into the executor's filesystem is a follow-up.
- CJK text is over-cut when the context budget binds.
- Images: when images alone exceed the context share, the bound does not drop them; the embedded context guard does (as on `main`). On Codex and Copilot such images pass as on `main`, where no route budgeted images. Moving image omission into the bound is a separate change.

## Evidence

Red on `main`, green here (same tests):

| Route | Test |
|---|---|
| Codex | `skills_read` with a 16k-token attempt budget and a complete 12k skill: refused whole, not cut; a wrapped network result at 128k through the dynamic-tool bridge: one closed frame with head and tail, a size-only notice and no Gateway path; mixed text + image within the shared budget. The small-window and image cases live in the bound's fail-closed suite below, which every route calls |
| Copilot | oversized result bounded before the SDK, file equals the full text |
| Agents API | an image block before one oversized wrapped page: output starts with the image placeholder, keeps the warning, start and end markers with one id, and the notice's omitted count equals exactly the chars cut (at the previous head the output ended `<<<END_EXTE`); a header plus two wrapped pages that fit the 32k budget by one char before the joining newlines: all four markers kept, output within the cap |
| All routes (`tool-result-bound.multi-block.test.ts`, 14 of these red on the previous head) | one helper checks every case: no untrusted text or filler outside a whole frame, every start marker closed with its id, exactly one notice outside frames with count = original − kept, and the real context guard, run after the bound, passes every text block unchanged. Cases: header + page at 4k/8k/16k/128k; two pages at 4k/16k/128k (second left out whole); 14 pages at 4k/8k; 200 small pages at 128k keep whole bodies; one JSON block with 5 wrapped values at 4k/8k, cut mid-way; image beside a page at 4k/8k/16k (a browser snapshot's shape; red one commit earlier, where the guard re-cut the frame after dropping the image); spill on: the notice names the file and the file holds the full text |
| Embedded | a forged envelope with a 200k metadata header is left out whole with the notice; 16k-token window: the bound's output passes the context guard unchanged and keeps its path; spill write failure keeps head + tail with a size-only notice |

Consumer suites pass; tests that pinned the Codex prefix cut were rewritten to the bound's contract. A producer's own spill path is also withheld from size-only routes. `agent-tools.prefix-stability` passes. Typecheck: core, core tests, extensions, extension tests.




Supersedes #207205: its multi-block end-marker cases are covered here frame by frame; its MCP-path bounding is left out (see Security boundary).

prs.body:
## Problem
`security-fast` fails on every PR based on current `main` again:
```
Protocol event coverage check failed:
  - [ios] allowlist entry "controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed" is now handled; remove it from scripts/protocol-event-coverage.allowlist.json.
```
#206640 (`18356ea02fce`, iOS PR pills) made iOS handle `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed`, but the allowlist still says iOS does not handle it. This is the same failure as #207259 with a different entry. #207258 runs this check on `main` pushes so that the next stale entry shows on `main`.

## Solution
Remove the iOS `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed` allowlist entry. The Android entry stays: `apps/android` has no handler for the event.

## Evidence
- `node scripts/check-protocol-event-coverage.mts` on `origin/main` `2595c38a`: the failure above.
- The same check on this branch: `Protocol event coverage OK: 75 gateway events; ios handles 30, allowlists 45; android handles 26, allowlists 49.`

prs.title: fix(cron): decouple command jobs from agent heartbeat startup
prs.body:
## Summary
- skip agent heartbeat-timeout resolution for command payloads
- keep command jobs runnable while agent database startup admission is pending
- add a regression test proving command execution does not consult agent heartbeat state

## Root cause
The generic timer watchdog resolved an agent heartbeat timeout for every payload. For host command jobs this metadata is irrelevant, but the gateway resolver asserts agent database admission. A command scheduled during gateway startup therefore failed before its argv ran.

## Verification
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/service/command-timeout.test.ts --reporter=default` (4 passed)
- `git diff --check`

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

| --- | --- |
| ![Native GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333e056f-5322-429d-a30e-f3d785d89120) | ![Plugin GitHub connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef691381-28d5-4da0-9261-6b99f58de6b5) |

| Native mobile | Plugin mobile |
| --- | --- |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548
