prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat responsive while tool renderers load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat startup can repeat initial-history work, wait for optional tool presentation, and reproject unchanged sidebar rows when only readiness changes. An ordinary Gateway hello can invalidate pending initial-render recovery by replacing an already-cleared connection. Archived-session notices can also collapse below the normal composer surface and move the footer.

The first-row scheduling budget has a separate ordering defect: a cheap loading or empty projection consumes its one decision before populated history arrives. The first expensive transcript projection can then run without the existing cold-start yield.

## User Impact

Live tool output and previews remain available while optional row rendering loads. Early boot editing retains its editor, draft, selection and scroll through pane adoption; authoritative archived/incognito/view-only state still replaces input through the existing banner owner. Ordinary replacement notices share the composer's responsive minimum height.

The first populated transcript projection now owns the existing 15 ms cold-start decision. Cheap projections, restored panes and accepted submissions remain immediate; loading and empty states stay visible. No configuration, migration, protocol change, deployment or restart is included. Final performance qualification failed below; the PR remains unmerged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Transfer a matching early history/live-output lease into the pane. Preference changes replace the lease, and failed replacement retires the connection.
- Keep optional rendering and retry inside the row boundary, with eager previews outside it. Remove the obsolete presentation facade; disclosure policy remains with the thread expansion owner.
- Carry prepared snapshot/Details facts forward. Readiness-only updates leave unchanged sidebar rows stable while preserving status, approval, history/search, pagination and pin-wake consumers.
- Preserve connection identity when hello has no bootstrap credentials to retire. Token/profile retirement still replaces the connection; stale-client, navigation, global and storage guards remain authoritative.
- Preserve normal first-commit boot-editor adoption. The discarded metadata/chrome gate is absent: intentional early local editing must not wait for session metadata.
- Share existing responsive composer minimum-height rules with ordinary replacement notices. Preserve narrow-container, landscape, native-resting and short-pane precedence, compact/hidden exceptions and natural growth. No Details animation change or arbitrary maximum height.
- Keep the one-shot cold-row budget until the first projection that would render rows. Measure that projection alone, retain the existing threshold and task-yield owner, never re-hide admitted rows, and prevent a disposed pending task from publishing. The viewport, composer, header and Details remain mounted.

The scheduling defect predates this PR: the construction-time decision is present in [PR #196482](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196482). Earlier pane admission exposes the loading-first order. The 15 ms measurement covers transcript projection preparation, **not** subsequent Markdown rendering, row mounting or geometry. The profile does not establish that the measured workload crossed that threshold; the fresh unprofiled comparison must establish the effect.

The existing real-Gateway benchmark also gains a default-off cold CPU diagnostic mode: `--cold-cpu-profile --route chat --reloads 0 --prime-reloads 0`. It retains full raw/mapped samples, native long-frame attribution and clock/counter snapshots, with explicit coverage limits and cleanup. The ordinary and existing warm-profile paths remain separate; diagnostic captures cannot become ordinary timing acceptance.

Candidate: `fbb33335d3c6c2a08ccac813306d26359ce92ff3`, tree `2ea06ed47877870945099c6a3d6759063198b072`. Frozen integrated baseline: `e11a36d08b9a9fc81d2c6634fd6e252f8f954dad`. The native final-patch refresh preserved the signed correction history and integrated current-main tests; it did not replay abandoned readiness designs. Prior receipts retain their original source and baseline identities.

The Latest test correction now awaits the actual destination after clicking, then retains the existing idle wait and final distance ≤1 assertion. Its owner test demonstrates that stable geometry can coexist with a queued manual command; releasing the existing commit and animation-frame owners reaches the exact tail. Product scrolling is unchanged. This fixes the test's premature observation boundary without claiming that retained CI facts establish the exact cause of the earlier 846 px result.

Versus the frozen baseline: UI/runtime +216/−308 (**net −92**); diagnostic tooling production +383/−30 (**net +353**); combined production **net +261**. Tests +1955/−446 (**net +1509**), diagnostic docs +36, other workflow/manifest/allocation metadata +39/−11. Positive production growth supplies the missing cold CPU attribution capability and the first-populated-projection lifecycle boundary. The test ratchet passes with unchanged shared allowance 400 plus allocation 1109. No checker or performance threshold was relaxed.

## Evidence

**Publication status: NEEDS WORK; final performance failed, CI disposition pending.** Exact-source native95166 passed UI types, scoped formatting/lint and all22 scroll-owner cases; its wrapper then failed an incorrect21-case expectation. That failed receipt remains unchanged. [Remaining native proof86448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904919483) authenticated the six original evidence members byte-for-byte and passed lifecycle8 plus reply-attribution9, including both motion modes, zero skips/todos. The verified aggregate is **39 cases:22 carried+17 newly executed**. Complete logs/reports, restored source, joined children, native completion and separate automatic cleanup were independently verified. Archive SHA256: `aa3c2af824b0fe8a2ef7cde0d0f3802b1322a0130798bd1eb91bc04d3e151d33`. The [full unprofiled comparison85014](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904508017) against frozen e11 completed all48 observations and failed as detailed below. Current [merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45906761470) has an external WebKit dependency-install failure and a separate Cron delivery-error visibility assertion under investigation. The exact-head ClawSweeper review is PASS, but it preceded the final performance result and does not accept that result. No current-source performance pass, merge or deployment is claimed.

**Latest completion contract.** [3492 merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897473527/job/140175632528) observed 846 px from the bottom after the first Latest click and geometry-idle helper in the no-preference case; 464 sibling tests passed. The retained failure artifact had no scroll timeline. Source and existing sibling E2Es establish that geometry-idle does not certify queued `afterCommit`/animation-frame command completion. Both corrected sites poll the same exact ≤1 destination, wait for geometry idle and check ≤1 again. A missed command still fails; a transient arrival followed by drift still fails. The new owner test documents the pending-command contract and is not presented as a product RED or reconstruction of that CI capture. Later [b8bd actual-merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45900330670) passed, including the formerly failing shard; that does not causally attribute the difference to the Show correction.

**Show callback contract.** [3492 merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45897473527/job/140176064462) found TS2745/TS2769 for a zero-argument `Show` child. The canonical `_deferred` parameter satisfies Solid rc.18's API. Solid checks `function.length`, so evaluation intentionally moves into its conditional memo; this is not a type-only or emitted-runtime-equivalence claim. The threshold, yield and content policy stay unchanged. [Exact b8bd native proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45899284660) passed `tsgo:ui` and all eight lifecycle cases, zero skips/todos; full logs/report and separate native completion/automatic cleanup were verified. Archive SHA256: `2d950a2cdba313c62d039d25e5d6fabd36e3b534f7cbce34f44e6c6aba5f007b`. Those owner bytes are unchanged in the integrated candidate; exact final-source UI types passed in95166, and lifecycle8 passed in86448.

**Scheduling-owner regression.** The original-order 3492 regression failed against its parent because populated rows appeared before the held yield, then passed with the correction. Disposal checks actual row rendering after unmount. The existing threshold measures projection preparation only; no claim is made that this explains all measured CPU work. Earlier scoped review passed. Final narrow autoreviews are complete with no findings: the b8bd Show invocation correction with full component/dependency/lifecycle context, and final fbb Latest tests/allocation with owner/caller/sibling context. Relevant runtime owner bytes are unchanged through integration; earlier unchanged scopes retain their prior reviews. Review did not execute tests.

**Historical browser correctness, explicitly carried.** The [3492 native proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895287144) passed nine full reports: lifecycle8, New Session6, inline7, menu1, guest2, Incognito1, auth5, boot9 and composer-height20 — **59 passed, zero skips/todos**. All 11 complete logs and original reports were verified; paired assets passed. Native completion and automatic cleanup were separate verified outcomes. Archive SHA256: `cb766a3eb6f3a1a118945809b309759e83f65158b68729a42b1e4b01609181eb`. This is exact3492 proof, not a claim that all59 were rerun on the integrated candidate.

The [earlier c5 browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45876546173) passed all51 original browser cases. Six responsive-height cases failed under the original CSS with computed `auto` instead of 88/92/112/0/52/92 px, with no mixed setup/global error; restored final CSS passed all20 height cases. Three ordinary full-size modes also verify actual height equality. Compact/hidden behavior and natural growth remain covered; arbitrary expanded drafts or long notices are not promised equal heights. Archive SHA256: `3a51aecbec763645b626bb946b05e374847c3e1c741b4ae45706995b21efa090`.

Two earlier test corrections retain their own proofs: the roles fixture installs its intended roster before navigation ([14 cases passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45880721725)); inline trail assertions await the real lazy row's exact attributes/titles rather than its visible placeholder ([seven cases passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45883664223), plus held-import owner proof). Neither adds a production wait or weakens the expected result.

**Final-source performance failed.** [85014](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45904508017) compares exact `fbb33335d3c6c2a08ccac813306d26359ce92ff3` against frozen `e11a36d08b9a9fc81d2c6634fd6e252f8f954dad`: all24 original-order arms,48 observations,28 median/p95 cells and eight A/A observations are complete, with no exclusions. The unchanged consumer returned **16 adverse /2 STOP /10 improved /2 equal; `accepted=false`**. Cold long-frame blocking median rose111.05→147.05 ms (+36 ms/+32.418%); warm rose61.75→87.80 ms (+26.05 ms/+42.186%). Both were adverse in7/10 pairs. Cold row and Details paint medians rose670→680 and888→910 ms; warm rows/Details/FCP improved524→482 ms. A/A variation remains visible without subtraction or waiver. Both source and baseline differ from8037, so cross-run changes cannot isolate the Show correction or integration. Archive SHA256: `15fc2eb2a5d0e769703ed00ba716b3209f60793cd490b83bfbad4afe7eae55c5`.

The complete workload returned0 with restored source and joined children. The original wrapper returned1 only because GitHub quota prevented its separate cleanup settlement; that receipt remains unchanged. One later native closeout reconciled the associated run and verified the exact claim/key absent. Performance failure remains independent of successful evidence collection and cleanup. A source-frozen, matched cold CPU diagnostic is being prepared to attribute the post-hello work; it is not a timing-acceptance rerun.

**Historical performance remains visible.** [c5 run27555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45878083907), against7ce, retained all24 arms/48 observations/28 median+p95 cells and eight A/A observations. Its unchanged consumer returned **11 adverse /5 STOP /`accepted=false`**. STOPs were cold FCP p95 +25.6 ms/+43.986%, cold LoAF median +67.7 ms/+40.931% and p95 +94.13 ms/+44.574%, warm helloPublished p95 +174.465 ms/+30.570% and helloHandled p95 +174.845 ms/+29.351%. Cold LoAF was adverse in9/10 pairs; both warm hello metrics in8/10. Archive SHA256: `b257f8254214d29b55e4a004d429523f6b7b824daa4dec2ff424968def670f6a`.

[3492 run8037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895852511), also against7ce, retained the complete same24/48 method and returned **6 adverse /0 STOP /20 improved /2 equal; `accepted=false`**. Cold LoAF median improves139.15→135.60 ms and p95202.555→202.365 ms (4/10 pairs adverse). Residual adverse cells: cold helloPublished median +7.10 ms/p95 +11.045 ms; cold helloHandled median +7.20 ms/p95 +9.595 ms (each7/10 pairs adverse); cold CLS median +0.000346393 (5/10); warm helloPublished p95 +4.09 ms (4/10). All five prior STOP cells are below STOP in that run. A/A variation is retained without subtraction or waiver. Cross-run instrumentation differences prevent a pure source-effect estimate. Archive SHA256: `0cd08de4c91a8191f29dfd734f3456df2059355f42502d19a545bbebf3d7d63d`.

The zero-adverse acceptance expression is the established agent-authored consumer, not a separately located repository rule. Its field remains unchanged and visible; the inclusive20% STOP rule is unchanged. The final comparison uses the same24 arms/48 observations/ten alternating pairs/seven metrics/median and linearp95, with common unprofiled instrumentation in both arms and explicit CPU/attribution-off checks. It now binds the final integrated product and e11 baseline; no historical performance result transfers to it.

**Diagnostic limitations.** The matched cold CPU pair identified extra/coalesced transcript construction, sanitization and commit geometry; lazy row-module evaluation occurred after the dominant frame. The pair also showed more work over the common recorded window. Sample weights are elapsed time; thread-clock counters and overlapping categories are separate. Missing source mappings and the unprofiled navigation prefix remain explicit. Both arms completed with required coverage, but the producer failed its9MiB uncompressed artifact cap. A separately reviewed native retrieval recovered all21 original files (14,620,735 raw bytes;987,249-byte archive) without rewriting that failure. Recovery SHA256: `07f9e4616400e98f0fae5310cef523b25588f590c407ac859e603300a16fb118`. Diagnostic recovery is not ordinary timing acceptance.

**Review moves.** The [durable ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201971#issuecomment-7017925894), Revision13 on b8bd, has no source findings but requires Latest command-completion evidence and final-source performance qualification. The destination assertions/held-owner contract and exact reply-attribution9 proof, including both motion modes, address the first move. The completed final comparison failed two STOP cells; its required performance disposition remains open. The [one exact-head review request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201971#issuecomment-7205049030) produced durable Revision14 PASS on fbb with no source findings or before-merge items and the Latest move addressed. Its optional final-comparison move was still based on a pending result; the measured failure above supersedes that pending status and keeps this PR unmerged. No second same-head review was requested. The optional isolated real-Gateway first-frame capture remains **unperformed**; no extra capture was added solely to refresh a rating. Mounted ordering tests, mock-Gateway suites and built-fixture timing are cited only for their actual scopes.

History attribution remains preserved: `9cca9afa702d9d213139ca5ac37cb2945db88280` introduced unconditional connection replacement; [PR #138964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138964), commit `91095dcd9bf41721f4320d13618e885f1641fe21`, later reordered retirement and added captured-connection guards. Native tooling prerequisites [#205904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205904) and [#205926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205926) are merged. Separate follow-ups remain redundant publication baseline validation and the observed task-owned Python pipe deadlock; neither expands this PR's runtime scope.

The preceding published stack head was [`a1082cd`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/a1082cd41e471e4d43b5db9206406173ee6b76f6). Its complete tree, `d95e2b57ae202ec9124b20fd3fec0875ee41986e`, matches both the local single-parent candidate `a880b8b` and the resolved merge of the [punctuation head `1c417ad`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/1c417ad24db195e273a1105f0be9cdd0e7f0836b) with the [coordinator head `1a1060d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973/commits/1a1060d376d44835a4b49d765c4ae096e847c58a). ## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205630.
Part of #205630

Dictation users need an explicit choice between recognizer output and conservative punctuation, with a chance to review the result before inserting it. Technical strings, negation, numbers, existing draft text, and selected recipients must survive that process.

**This remains an incomplete implementation draft.** It integrates the proposed Control UI flow and repairs the reported submission bug, but does not claim full M01 acceptance, human design approval, real microphone/browser/accessibility qualification, or passing required CI. Keep the issue open.

## User Impact

The existing default is Off. Opting in adds original/refined review, explicit insertion, reprocessing of an unsent original, and target-scoped Undo.

| Setting | Implemented behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Off | Preserves the established capture and submission path. |
| Verbatim | Preserves recognizer-provided words, punctuation, and casing. It cannot restore acoustic words or marks already changed by the recognizer. |
| Automatic | With explicitly resolved `en-US`, changes only an eligible unprotected opening letter at the beginning of a field and an eligible missing final period. It does not infer internal sentences or rewrite grammar. |
| Explicit punctuation | Requires a separate enablement and a bounded spoken-mark grammar. Introduced `insert …` phrases are supported; the only bare shorthand is `hello comma <one plain word> period`. Ambiguous punctuation words remain text. |

Locale and policy are frozen before asynchronous capture work. Session locale takes precedence over an enabled profile and then the saved preference. Missing or unsupported locale/context, non-Latin input, and explicitly identified mixed-language input retain the original. Arbitrary Latin-script code switching is not detected or qualified. Only synthetic `en-US` fixtures have been qualified; no physical client or speech-provider combination is claimed as tested.

Finishing an opted-in capture stops for review. Side chat keyboard/form submission retains that decision even if cancellation retires the capture. Main chat keeps provisional captions out of menu/history/deferred-send actions while recording. Recording phase changes no longer invalidate their own frozen draft revision.

Approved insertion replaces the captured selection, including the insertion owner's spacing joins, as one isolated rich-editor edit. Untouched recipient identities survive. The native textarea fallback uses the existing mention binding for exact edit metadata and restoration during the existing Undo transaction. Identical-result insertion makes no edit. Unknown write outcomes are disclosed and not retried; Undo is retired when the field, editor, binding, or owning revision changes.

**Rollback:** choose Off or remove the preference. Subsequent captures use the established path, unrelated voice settings and committed draft text remain, and an already admitted utterance retains its frozen policy unless explicitly reprocessed. No automatic reversal of a committed edit is promised.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture, provider session, finalization, and commit queue remain authoritative. A private helper freezes the capture’s selected policy and bounded draft context, prepares a validated review, and ties the eventual insertion and Undo to the captured draft target. It does not add a plugin API.

The deterministic engine returns bounded edits at half-open UTF-16 offsets and validates ICU grapheme boundaries, original revision/schema identity, replayed output, protected strings, permitted edits, lexical coverage, and idempotence. Model confidence cannot bypass validation. It adds no provider/model call, punctuation request queue, transcript store, or cloud fallback. Translation, paraphrasing, spelling correction, number-word normalization, ordinary Talk response rewriting, and external-application insertion are outside this change.

Only a strict versioned browser preference is stored. Invalid/future values disable refinement visibly; unvalidated fields are dropped by the existing settings writer. The setting is excluded from Gateway preference synchronization. The new native metadata capability is owned by the existing textarea binding; it does not add a history manager or persistent transcript/recipient store. Existing whole-draft composer-task replacements retain their previous transaction path.

[The issue's automated review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205630#issuecomment-7178173319) and [formatting draft #205791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205791) require a shared preparation/preference decision. Neither draft is an accepted M11 parent, and enabled-together compatibility has not been demonstrated. Maintainers still need to decide private versus plugin placement, preference ownership, initial client/locale qualification, and reference hardware. No public SDK/RPC/schema or retention approval is assumed.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep consecutive commands on one line in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

While the assistant works on iPhone, every command can become its own row and the list keeps growing. This happened when an OpenAI turn kept waking after a command: the earlier operations stayed in the chat, but tapping the working line showed only the last two. Eight operations inside one uninterrupted OpenAI run already folded correctly. With eight direct Claude CLI calls, the line already stayed folded, but tapping it showed only the latest command.

## User Impact

Tap the current step to see all eight operations in order, including the failed command. When the turn finishes, the commands share a disclosure above the answer. A new user message or visible commentary still separates stretches of work. No setting or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An automatic continuation can change the run ID without starting a new turn. The transcript now keeps those linked steps together and gives their membership to the existing inspector. A code-mode batch title and the command it ran describe two linked operations, not two copies of one command. An imported Claude CLI shell call is different: its title and command belong to the same operation.

## Evidence

On an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, the focused regression covered three eight-operation histories, both running and finished. On the starting revision, the single OpenAI run passed twice; the resumed OpenAI turn failed twice; the direct Claude CLI history failed only while running. Each OpenAI outer result was a separate message, and one outer call owned both a skill read and a shell command. All six passed with the fix. One tap on the working line opened all eight steps in order and identified the failed command. The uninterrupted OpenAI run kept its existing “Worked” disclosure; the resumed OpenAI turn and direct Claude CLI calls finished with “Ran commands.” The first command no longer moves the text or claw down 5 points. On settlement, the icon center stayed fixed and the top of the first letter differed by one physical pixel. A streaming answer kept the same position as on the starting revision, with or without tools.

![A resumed OpenAI turn while it is still working, light appearance. Before, on the left, six earlier commands each have their own row above the working line. After, on the right, only the working line "Running git diff --stat" shows.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b21479d-1d5a-472f-8d10-2a2425108b1e)

![One tap on the working line. Before, on the left, the sheet lists only the last two steps. After, on the right, it lists all eight in order and marks the failed one.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a280712e-fd29-4361-b472-7040de74a6b6)

![The finished turn. Before, on the left, all eight rows stay above the answer. After, on the right, one "Ran commands" disclosure sits above the answer.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4dcf27e-1f8f-4d65-8fa9-7b68c55aaab4)

![The running comparison in dark appearance.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edbf212a-56d4-4a64-9adc-e048a0749298)

![Eight direct Claude CLI calls, one tap on the working line. Before, on the left, the sheet shows only the latest command. After, on the right, it shows all eight.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec359e02-9ea5-42fe-b1be-602083114a5a)

Of 20 existing chat-history methods, 14 passed and the same six failed on both revisions. Five failures were identical. The existing assertion at `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatSessionsCodingTests.swift:537` expects “Ran commands, read files”; once the group forms it gets “Read files, ran commands.” No existing expectation was changed.

The comparison used fixture data, not a live model service. It did not cover a physical iPhone, other providers, or the full test suite.

Stacked on #206685.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(ios): keep child sessions with their parent when moved
prs.body: Closes #198377 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: iOS children appear outside their parent family when stored child pins or groups differ from the parent. ## User Impact Families stay in their root's section in both the sidebar and Sessions screen. Child placement actions are unavailable; stored child metadata remains unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Decision needed:** Should iOS replace independent child group placement with parent-owned family placement and remove child placement actions? **Author’s design:** Yes. Keep the family together so moving the parent moves the whole family. This deliberately replaces the independent child placement retained in #190403; it is not a claim of web parity. Stored child placement is preserved. The iOS owner still decides whether to ship this policy. - Align child pin controls with the root-only policy shipped in #140748. Family grouping also follows the parent rather than splitting descendants across sections. - Resolve the shared roster hierarchy before section placement, without applying sidebar status filters a second time. - Preserve stored child fields and existing recent-activity preview behavior; this is not a Gateway data migration. ### Child placement eligibility during search (f72edc1efc7) > Review [P2]: *Preserve child placement eligibility during sidebar search* (`RootSidebar.swift:686`). - Sidebar text search could remove a parent before building the tree, making a matching child appear eligible for Pin/Unpin and Move to Group. - The sidebar now derives menu eligibility from the unfiltered browsing tree, preserving existing Home and status promotion rules. - Regression: `RootTabsPresentationTests.sidebar search keeps child placement actions unavailable` covers a search matching only the child. - On the iOS simulator, the regression failed with the pre-fix depth policy and all 62 tests passed with the fix; SwiftFormat 0.63.1 lint passed on both changed files. ### Same-state upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.10 (iOS simulator, head 0ed88daf24f) > Review: *latest-stable-to-PR native upgrade proof*. Setup: one scratch Gateway, one fresh iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2), paired once. The categories, pins and parent links live on the Gateway. Seeded over RPC: categories **Research** and **Delivery**; parent "Website refresh" pinned in Research; child "Landing page audit" with `parentSessionKey` set to the parent. | 1. Stable v2026.11.10 | 2. PR build installed over it | 3. PR build, parent moved to Delivery | |---|---|---| | | | | | Categories and pin present; the child is listed separately | Installed in place, with no erase, uninstall or re-pairing. Pairing and all Gateway data kept. The child is now indented under its parent | After `sessions.patch` moved only the parent, the child follows it into Delivery | Accessibility excerpt after the move: ```text StaticText identifier: 'SessionGroup.Header.Delivery', label: 'DELIVERY' Button label: 'Website refresh, just now' Button {22.0, 662.0} label: 'Landing page audit, 1 min. ago' # indented 12 pt under the parent ``` The organizer readback before and after the move keeps the pin, both session IDs and the child's parent link. The child's own category stays null, as expected for inherited placement. The Gateway hostname in the sidebar footer has been replaced with `gateway.example:8492` in all three captures. Limits: this was tested in the simulator against a scratch Gateway, not a physical phone. The step 3 capture was taken after a relaunch, with the app reading the moved state at launch. The PR build reports bundle version 2026.11.3 and stable reports 2026.11.10; versions are Info.plist metadata, so the commit is what identifies the build. ## Evidence - Regression verified red on the old implementation: 11 tests ran; the new test failed exactly its two placement assertions. After the fix, all 17 grouping/status-filter tests passed. - Native simulator proof passed one XCTest with lint enabled. It checks both child menus (Rename present; Pin, Unpin and Move to Group absent) and placement in Research. - Synthetic retained server metadata is tested, not an actual latest-stable binary upgrade. The stored pin badge can remain visible without owning placement. - AI-assisted implementation and two independent reviews; [redacted work record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/WORK-RECORD.md) (summary, not a full transcript). ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/3A71B087-3EF0-4413-9F5C-A5A10ECFF47A.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/C7C66171-EAC9-44B3-9539-54987CA30E71.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/E9D225FF-BF6D-4B76-A283-D9A761EC380E.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/FEDCBC25-7C60-47A5-AF89-3CB4F8235E42.jpg)

prs.title: fix(ios): keep session pins personal to the signed-in profile
prs.body: Related: #198377 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: pinning a session on iOS changes shared session metadata instead of the signed-in user's personal navigation. ## User Impact iOS pins follow the signed-in profile's personal shortcuts, the same as web. Existing shared pins stay stored but are no longer shown as personal pins; users can pin those sessions personally. Connections without personal preferences get a profile/sign-in explanation and never fall back to shared writes. Personal-only pins (hiding legacy shared pins, refusing profileless pins) is the requested product behaviour. ## Why This Change Was Made - Align iOS with the personal-navigation contract in the [user-model documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model) and with web, which already maps `session:` entries in `ui.railShortcuts` to the Sessions Pinned section. - Re-read before writes and compare the exact snapshot, preserving unrelated shortcuts and reporting conflicts. - Keep session eligibility, child-session filtering, grouping and layout unchanged. - Preserve stored shared pin metadata without importing it into personal pins. ## Evidence Lint-enabled Xcode 27.2 run of the final apps patch: ```text LINT_BYPASS=0 KIT_TESTS=13 tests in 1 suite passed SIM_TESTS=xctest=0 swift-testing=19 rc=0 STATUS=PASS ``` **Profile isolation and cross-client refresh** (iOS simulator against an isolated Gateway with a second, trusted-proxy-authenticated profile B). Another Owner client pinned X and iOS showed it as pinned. A pin that belonged only to B was not shown as pinned in the Owner app. An unpin made on iOS was read back as unpinned by a separate Owner client. Storage readbacks show each profile's write left the other profile's shortcuts unchanged. [XCTest output](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/native-rpc-xctest.txt) · [storage readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/profile-isolation.jsonl) **Seeded upgrade.** A v2026.11.5 Gateway and app were seeded with an existing personal shortcut and an existing shared pin, then upgraded in place to this PR (same simulator, data kept). Before: the shared pin is in Pinned and the personal shortcut is not. After: the personal shortcut is in Pinned and the shared pin is shown unpinned but still stored. Gateway readbacks before and after the upgrade match byte for byte, including the legacy pin timestamp. [stable seed](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/stable-store.json) · [after upgrade](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/head-store-after-ui.json) · [stable XCTest](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/upgrade-stable-xctest.txt) · [head XCTest](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/upgrade-head-xctest.txt) | | Before (v2026.11.5) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | Existing shared pin | | | | Existing personal shortcut | | | **Matched base/head.** The same iOS XCUITest ran against separate disposable Gateways on the merge base and on this PR, with the same signed-in profile confirmed at each checkpoint. Merge base: Pin set the shared `pinned` field and timestamp, and personal shortcuts never changed. This PR: Pin added the session to the profile's personal shortcuts only, and shared pin metadata stayed identical at every checkpoint. Unpin reversed each. [Result](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/MATCHED.md) · [base readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/matched-base-checkpoints.txt) · [head readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/matched-head-checkpoints.txt) **Missing profile.** iOS is an ordinary client of the same auth and profile model as web, and handles a missing profile the same way. Web refuses to persist a pin or shortcut when the profile is missing or the preference read is not `ok` ([`server-prefs-profile-runtime.ts:97-109`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/669ae72f7a9bbd48daf36b66ee2e044d32ea7353/ui/src/app/server-prefs-profile-runtime.ts#L97-L109)), and its test verifies `no_durable_identity` sends no write ([`server-prefs.navigation.test.ts:316-325`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/669ae72f7a9bbd48daf36b66ee2e044d32ea7353/ui/src/app/server-prefs.navigation.test.ts#L316-L325)). iOS matches this: the native method test verifies `no_durable_identity` shows the profile-required explanation after one read and attempts no write, with no fallback to shared pins. Normal sign-in always provides a profile on both clients; a connection without a durable identity is refused before the preferences handler, and the store stays unchanged. Preference tests also cover mixed arrays with compare-and-set snapshots, absent versus empty preferences, idempotent repinning, empty keys and unrelated shortcuts. [Full evidence](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/EVIDENCE.md) AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix(docker): avoid pre-boot Doctor delays on container recreation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recreating a container on a monitored deployment caused 104 seconds of lost readiness against a 60-second limit. The entrypoint ran a full repairing Doctor before starting the Gateway; its original-state capture alone was still running after 51 seconds.

## User Impact

Container activation starts the Gateway directly. Gateway boot retains its existing in-place state migration owners, and installed plugin packages converge through the shared post-ready job introduced in #206926. Keep the same state/config mounts, stop the old replica first, and back up state before upgrading.

Activation no longer takes Doctor's full pre-repair recovery capture. Explicit Doctor repair retains its normal recovery capture behavior.

Docker recreates no longer run entrypoint Doctor to write its agent `.pre-startup-migration-*.bak` checkpoint group. They now behave like `npm -g`/manual installs: in-place boot migration, with boot preimages only in a launcher trial. The boot credential owner still retains its shared-store backup.

**Named upgrade edge:** already-bound automations carrying an old copied-state authorization ID are not automatically rebound during boot. This matches direct npm/Git replacement behavior. Execution refuses with an explicit recovery action (`src/cron/inference-binding.runtime.ts:315-318`):

> To keep using it: `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profileId>`.

Follow that command to adopt the intended account explicitly; Doctor's existing stopped-writer repair can also recover verified historical paths from retained upgrade receipts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The entrypoint's Doctor child predates migration-on-boot and shared post-ready plugin convergence. Delete that child, its signal forwarding and argv classification, and its container-local capture marker/Doctor reader. Delete the obsolete Doctor-child tests and old-shape refusal control; retain direct command execution, PATH handling, preserved-state upgrade checks, and unsafe-store refusal. Boot also invokes the existing unattended cron account-adoption owner when the canonical inventory contains an unbound job; explicit Doctor repair remains available.

No new hook, option, durable state, retry, timer, or notice. Production source: +267 / -405, **net -138 lines**; whole change: **net -235 lines**. No changes to either updater implementation.

## Evidence

- Reported deployment readiness loss: 103.988 seconds; capture still running at 51 seconds. Gateway boot itself was approximately 9.05 seconds. Remaining pre-boot Doctor/orchestration time cannot be split exactly because Doctor logs lacked timestamps.
- Syntax checks pass for the entrypoint, both Docker fixture modules, and the Docker lane shell script; focused formatting checks pass. Targeted lint reports zero warnings/errors.
- The new real-database boot regression fails on unchanged main boot code because the legacy job has no inference binding, then passes with the existing adoption owner called from boot. It preserves authored job fields and run history and makes no network request. The migration first shipped in 2026.11.5; direct older-image upgrades and manual npm/Git replacement need the same repair.
- Warm second-boot inventory precheck: **4.8 ms** out of **4566.7 ms** total boot (~0.11%) in the isolated source fixture. The already-bound job is preserved and adoption is not invoked again. Existing maintenance live-read admission avoids the snapshot fallback (previously 6108.5 ms). Temporary timing instrumentation is not shipped.
- The full focused batch recorded 33 passing tests and six state-fixture failures. On unchanged main `53fc384687db`, both retained-deletion cases and the non-trial in-place migration case also hit the unchanged 120-second timeout. An isolated branch rerun reproduced only that timeout, not the earlier borrowed-owner error. The corrected large-DB custody fixture passes in 109.596 seconds; the earlier borrowed-owner signature remains unproven after the timed-out batch.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed production-equivalent `b8bd1ad3fd70` against `539f37f1d483`. Its remaining finding is the historical already-bound-account edge explicitly accepted and documented above. The subsequent source delta only fixes the large-DB test's existing maintenance scope.
- Full build and packed acceptance proof use exact-head hosted CI because the local host was overloaded (load approximately 70); the local full build was not completed.
- Existing `container-image-upgrade` uses the shipped 2026.9.2 state corpus, not a latest-stable image. The separate `published-upgrade-survivor` lane uses `openclaw@latest`; these are distinct proof contracts, not an image-to-image stable upgrade claim.
- Initial hosted proof: [Package Acceptance run 46104235808](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46104235808). The root-image default cell reached readiness and its public history checks, then failed because it expected Doctor's removed agent checkpoint. That checkpoint came from Doctor's schema-backup owner (`doctor-schema-migrations.ts:76-78`, `doctor-migration-backup.ts:483`), not its original-state capture or boot's build-named trial preimage.
- The fixture now drops only the agent Doctor-checkpoint, paired-checkpoint-ID, and backup-transcript assertions. All canonical session/transcript, schema, integrity, workspace, and shared credential-backup assertions remain.
- The supplied lane log has no container-start/readiness timestamps or process trace; it cannot supply an exact time-to-ready or independently establish child-process absence. The entrypoint source and process-boundary tests verify that activation directly executes the Gateway without an automatic Doctor child.
- [Package Acceptance run 46107913725](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46107913725) passed both default and Compose activation. Its unsafe cell correctly refused without a listener; only the assertion's old Doctor diagnostic text differed. The assertion now checks boot's actual cause text, `Agent schema markers disagree for`, retaining every other unsafe assertion.
- Neither main's entrypoint Doctor nor boot repairs this deliberately unsafe fixture state. In the exact-head Linux container, `doctor --fix` exited 1 and left version 19 / metadata version 18 and both session heads unchanged. Boot's refusal and exit 78 are unchanged in effect; no production error string or repair mechanism was changed.
- Corrected the fixture lock collections to the owner's actual nullable type, `GatewayLockHandle | null`; no casts or runtime behavior changes.
- Redispatched both existing lanes at `a5b235b55a83e18897efd7ad72cf0d107263186d`: [Package Acceptance run 46113558328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46113558328). Results pending.

prs.title: improve: avoid loading unused agent runtimes for chat commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Built-in chat commands such as `/help` load side-question and CLI tool-construction code they never call. This leaves extra JavaScript resident in the Gateway listener.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181432. This does not claim to resolve the reported field RSS or OOM.

## User Impact

Simple commands can complete before loading the side-question runtime. Tool-free CLI runs can prepare without loading MCP tool construction. Matching, authorization, session-start capture, tool policy and cleanup ownership are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load the side-question implementation inside its existing matched and authorized handler, as its Gateway and TUI callers already do. Load MCP resolvers at their actual projection owner, before admission. The second boundary still matters when a real tool-free CLI side question runs.

Production code is net **−3 lines**. The existing import-boundary test gains 12 lines. A 461-line benchmark extension supplies a reusable real-Gateway command → quiet residency → first/warm tool and side-question workload.

## Evidence

Pinned baseline: `26e765ff9e8050e4a68da6f922d979fdb7134596`.
Candidate: `50686fb4c9722d4fb091aa024c3b7c5a60bfc0a3` (tree `82e3ace62bce3d265fc39efa6fa57f34335b2412`).

- The MCP boundary regression failed on the baseline; 139 focused tests across seven files, formatting, lint and a full build passed on its signed checkpoint `c190d6ff`.
- The added BTW exclusion failed on `c190d6ff`, at the expected source assertion. On the exact combined candidate, all **55 focused tests** across the import boundary, command handler and side-question runtime passed; targeted formatting/lint and the **full build** passed. The real Gateway smoke completed **17 turns** (two help replies, eleven verified writes and four verified side answers), kept the main transcript message count unchanged during side answers, and joined both owned processes without forced termination. [Combined proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e98a508e7ccd66cd1c51d6886d49b35d).
- The ordinary predecessor smoke delivered two distinct saved help replies and eleven verified file writes with saved final replies. Its Gateway exited 0 without forced termination. This is driver qualification, not an A/B result.
- Both production and full-tree unused-file scans passed with **zero findings**. [Graph check and archived qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3c73e9fa3432cd80c4bd81d1159cd42f).
- Two scoped local ClawSweeper reviews found no actionable source issue. Both reports are **inconclusive** for runtime verification because their local checkout has no dependencies/build; remote validation is separate.
- A historical, separate one-process snapshot comparison for the MCP-only checkpoint had 87 fewer scripts, 2.65 MiB less disjoint code/source shallow size, and 4.31 MiB less post-snapshot listener heap. Those are diagnostic observations, not whole-process RSS acceptance or measurements of the combined candidate. Both snapshots logged an existing cleanup-receipt failure despite process exit 0.
- The predecessor and repaired candidate builds printed the same Control UI budget warnings at their displayed precision: largest CSS gzip 57.3 KiB against 56.9, chat-boot JavaScript requests 21 against 20, and chat-boot JavaScript gzip 1306.5 KiB against 1305.0. This is build-warning attribution, not UI load-performance proof; no Control UI code is changed.
- Smoke scope: RSS samples arrived at roughly 100 ms (largest interval 101.63 ms); peaks are sampled, not continuous maxima. Transcript verification checks message count, not byte identity. The combined smoke also logged an internal worker-cleanup receipt failure despite Gateway exit 0; source-owner cleanup success is not claimed. Paired shutdown logs will distinguish matching behavior.
- Follow-up outside this import repair: BTW command-authorization freshness across its pre-existing image/typing awaits. This PR does not claim late-revocation coverage.

- CI attribution: [security-fast job 140872730260](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46110372271/job/140872730260) failed the mobile event-coverage check: iOS already handles `session.tool`, so its allowlist entry is stale. Tested merge `d17318b2418c7f8ac1239be2f8ec2d9169b8ebc5` differs from first parent/main `f91c7d0a1ba82e6d472f6a0d3da5e89998609181` in only this PR’s six files. None is a checker, helper, event catalog, allowlist or mobile scan root. The exact checker/helpers also match the personally inspected source. This attributes the deterministic failure to main; the gate remains red, not waived.

### Prospective acceptance — frozen before the formal cohort

Committed workload:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-channel-turn.mts --listener-help --entry openclaw.mjs
```

Five fresh processes per arm on one qualified Linux x64 8-CPU/16-GiB lease, Node 24.22.1; serial **AB/BA/AB/BA/AB** pairs. The identical committed controller runs on both arms. Each source switch receives a complete native `pnpm build:runtime` generation with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_WORKER_DEPLOY_BUNDLE=0`, outside measurement; local worker entries remain built. This qualifies the local, unsealed Gateway, not remote worker deployment. Required full candidate build is separate. Adjacent processes with the same source reuse that generation only after its complete runtime output inventory verifies unchanged. Each process gets a 10-second pre-launch interval. Source bytes and build identity are recorded independently.

Each process uses fresh synthetic state and a loopback mock provider: two `/help` replies; a checkpoint 57–58 seconds after the first send; one cold and ten warm write-tool turns; one first and three warm `/btw` turns after those writes. Side replies must arrive through `chat.side_result` without changing the main transcript. The same PID/start time must survive all phases, and owned children must join without forced termination.

Primary win: post-help listener RSS median falls by at least **2 MiB**, with at least **4/5 pairs lower**, alongside removal of the demonstrated eager imports. Report median, p95 and range for RSS, startup, first/repeated help, cold/warm tool and BTW latency, main-thread CPU and total listener-process CPU; preserve per-pair adverse cells, peaks, protocol/provider counts and host load. CPU counters have the recorded Linux clock-tick resolution.

No snapshots, profiler preload or forced GC in this cohort. Latency uses real terminal events; transcript verification is outside each latency window. CPU runs through the final side result and excludes controller, subprocesses and shutdown; RSS includes all listener isolates. This sequence measures first BTW use after ordinary tool turns. A fresh first BTW immediately after help, and CLI/MCP first-projection latency, remain separate qualification gaps before landing.

Every user-facing metric must hold or improve. A worse metric remains a hold requiring explicit owner acceptance; any 20% adverse cell stops landing. No automatic regression acceptance, silent outlier removal or substituted runs. Failed/incomplete arms invalidate the cohort. Historical snapshots and smoke runs do not count as formal samples.


Formal cohort: **incomplete and invalid for performance acceptance**. The [initial comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f6e549debcf2d6a71cbef373f97bb415) completed one baseline process. Its candidate build and the [same-lease continuation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a3f59471c1d1a0b57f8e7aedf1156fa2) both failed before any candidate process. No baseline was repeated or replaced; no combined-candidate RSS/latency/CPU win is claimed. Both failed cohorts and the original baseline evidence are preserved. The frozen prospective-body SHA256 remains `5d49a29ba95a996630f0b6537529ef1199cffde75190a460db45f98c214c3927`.

A separate [build-lifecycle diagnostic](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cfc4f33db4da888365727d03d1a468dd) identified the surviving child: Control UI metadata invoked `git show -s --format=%ct` for the candidate, whose commit object was absent from the remote partial checkout. Git started a promisor fetch and index-pack; those children remained after Vite/esbuild exited. The managed owner correctly rejected the build and verified physical termination. This was not an esbuild leak or evidence of a listener regression.

Proof-provenance repair imports a verified 8,875-byte bundle of the two task commits into that same workspace, without moving HEAD or refs. Its SHA256 is `13346a40e73ea68417bffac0ccf46e27e89a763a75cd874916566b10bc3086d5`. Candidate commit, tree, timestamp and unchanged source bytes are verified; `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` confines subsequent metadata reads to local objects. The [native runtime build](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_02d22d620f98bbe7962d55eb6d16582b) then passed, with no known surviving children and no network Git child observed by the 100 ms process census. Its archive SHA256 is `deb000ea9727632a8ecb9ec6fa91f38c20b013f603babe4ec1b539cfbab7668f`. This qualifies the repaired preparation, not performance. The old lease is verified released.

The [fresh cohort attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3bf05cec68869e5b0fb3093928dab91d) failed during native hydration-script installation, before dependency qualification or the controller ran: exit 7, `provider-error`, `commandMs=0`, and zero new samples. Crabbox 0.84.0 reported `command stage retirement unconfirmed: signal: killed` and retained its native runtime. The installed revision is `76d26bddec6cbf305e90b8d9fc1166d24f9d9f95`; its `internal/cli/remote_runtime_posix.go:79` requires a nonce-bound completion/retirement receipt even after SSH exits successfully. Lease readiness is not that receipt. No workload retry, manual stage cleanup, provider switch or replacement lease was attempted after this refusal. Native stop returned successful release; an independent exact-lease inspect returned not found. That historical lease was released. Its next execution prerequisite was resolving the installed Crabbox completion/retirement-control failure through its native owner; an unchanged retry is not qualification.

A separate [Crabbox transport repair](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/3235) now adds canonical cancellation/deadline state alongside the original SSH process error. Review caught private-cause exposure in its initial revision; signed `b802770dad3410849041ec5fcdc4734c5e1ef5fa` uses `ctx.Err()` and passes 24 transport cases, including the actual workspace-owner path and real deadlines, plus sibling cancellation checks. The task-local controller SHA256 is `680aaba5ef0aa3a5deb20bd87edc02f4fe44c7e651e93bae71e8d0a686502fe0`; all six matching companions passed native source/build and controller-bound manifest verification. The installed CLI is unchanged. This does not establish the original cleanup failure's cause. A separate synthetic CLI cancellation reached readiness, received one SIGINT on its exact task-owned controller, printed canonical cancellation and released its workspace owner; no benchmark samples were collected by that probe.

The next [native attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9c7e2e2136fd6bb2530e145912020313) completed hydration, selected-source frozen installation and exact source/tree admission, then stopped before any benchmark process: the task controller rejected 397 untracked entries, all inside the receiver-owned active source capsule. No source changes or benchmark samples were present. The corrected controller exempts only its own executing capsule after validating its location, regular payload/bundle, preserved native Git owner and carrier identity. All three source checks still reject other capsules, unrelated untracked files and unexpected tracked changes; eleven focused guard checks and independent source review passed. The prospective acceptance rule and workload are unchanged. The upstream privacy correction and complete runtime pack are now qualified; no performance result or merge is requested.

The prepared fresh controller keeps all ten processes separate from the invalid historical cohort, verifies exact objects/source admission and process-group extinction, and records actual lease/deadline binding. Its SHA256 is `659b35bcbf8a2b70ba5bc3ccaa1fe08cfa68960ffe7a8a03b3c33ce27a0f808a`. These source checks are not execution evidence. The prospective performance rule is unchanged; paired performance and the two cold-use qualification gaps remain open.

Named follow-up: `ui/vite.config.ts` advisory commit-time lookup should not initiate network fetching from a partial clone. The observed failure is on the pinned baseline build code; this PR does not change UI metadata or weaken process cleanup.

CI is terminal. All executed test jobs completed successfully; the inherited mobile event-coverage failure remains, with failed [aggregate job 140876582967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46110372271/job/140876582967) and commit status. No waiver, merge or auto-merge was requested.

prs.title: fix: match goal checks to the goal indicator
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Goal checks in the OpenClaw web chat show the raw title “Get Goal” and a bullseye icon, while the goal strip uses different artwork. The row also does not distinguish a running lookup from a completed one.

## User Impact

Goal tool rows now use the same icon as the “Pursuing goal” strip. A lookup reads “Checking goal” while running and “Checked goal” once completed. Failed or unknown outcomes keep a neutral “Check goal” label alongside the existing outcome indicator.

This does not start, resume, complete, or otherwise change a goal. Shell command labels, grouping, and expandable tool results are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The web icon registry now owns the existing goal-strip artwork; the strip and details view consume it instead of maintaining a separate SVG. The three existing goal-tool mappings pick up the same artwork without changing shared metadata or native clients.

The change adds outcome-aware copy in the existing row presenter. Production: 14 lines added, 19 removed. Tests: 16 lines added to the existing rendering suite; no icon snapshots or permanent screenshot harness.

## Evidence

- 71 focused tests passed, including goal lookup outcomes, goal actions/details, and the shared display contract. The four new outcome cases failed on the base and passed after the fix.
- Built the Control UI and exercised the expanded goal lookup in dark and light mode. Both browser scenarios passed, including access to the original result.
- Targeted lint, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reported no actionable findings on the final local change. This was a source-context-bounded review, not a repository-wide audit; the implementing agent ran the tests.
- Full local UI typecheck was blocked before checking source because declaration dependencies are shared through external worktree symlinks. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad validation lane.

Captures use the real bundled Control UI with synthetic Gateway history, not a live agent run. Same 1280×650 viewport, fixed time, expanded group, and 800×480 crop. Before: `b62eec8f6587`; after: `59dacbeac615`.

prs.title: fix: show readable tool actions in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Expanded activity groups in chat expose tool names and routing arguments such as `ToolSearch select:mcp__...`, `Session Send`, and `Sessions 200`. These labels make the activity hard to scan, and a list limit or session identifier can look like a result.

## User Impact

User impact: tool discovery reads as “Selected tools” or “Searched tools”, chat listings read as “Listed chats”, and message actions show their recorded state and a known destination name. Full arguments remain available when expanded; terminal command previews stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared tool-row presentation now names the action instead of falling back to a technical title plus the first argument. It handles direct calls, OpenClaw MCP names, and dispatcher-wrapped calls.

A completed tool call alone does not prove that a message was sent: accepted, queued, and explicitly deferred receipts have distinct labels. Unknown destination keys are not presented as names. This is display-only; tool execution, delivery, permissions, grouping, and spacing are unchanged.

## Evidence

- The new cases reproduced the issue on the base (11 failures, 18 existing cases passing); the completed change passes all 52 focused tests across tool purpose, lifecycle, and addressed-session consumers.
- The bundled Control UI was exercised through the chat page with synthetic Gateway history. Both before and after retain the original tool arguments on expansion and the same shell command. The corrected UI also passed a dark-mode run with the resolved theme asserted.
- Targeted lint, formatting, i18n baseline/verification, and diff checks pass.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed `b210869fbd51..050fe5b88f3b`, including the unchanged tool-normalization and send-receipt contracts: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. This was source review, not a separate execution of the tests.
- **Validation limitation:** local `pnpm tsgo:ui` rejects the worktree's shared dependency links before type checking. The bundled browser build succeeds; full UI type checking remains for PR CI. No live message was sent by these fixtures.

### Clean comparison

Same synthetic review-and-chat-lookup history, expanded activity group, light theme, 1280 × 900 viewport, identical crop. Before: `b210869fbd51`; after: `050fe5b88f3b`.

prs.title: fix(ui): make empty composer hints look distinct from drafts
prs.body:
Related: #150234 and #184991 (placeholder and theme history).

## What Problem This Solves

In the light-mode Web UI, the empty hint in chat, Cmd+K Compose, and `/new` is dark enough to look like text you already typed. It makes it harder to tell at a glance whether the composer is empty.

## User Impact

Empty hints are visibly lighter on desktop and mobile Web UI, while typed drafts keep their existing color. The default dark-mode hint is unchanged. No settings or migrations are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat and palette composers share one placeholder color, including the mention-enabled chat editor. This separates empty hints from general secondary text without changing that text elsewhere. Light palettes choose the hint color against the composer surface so it remains readable.

## Evidence

- Exercised chat, Cmd+K Compose, and `/new` in Chromium at 1280 px and an emulated 390 px using the real Web UI with synthetic Gateway data. Confirmed the lighter hint, unchanged draft color, unchanged default dark hint, and the hint returning after clearing a mention in the rich editor. The default light hint measured 4.86:1 against the composer surface.
- All 13 tests in the theme contrast suite passed. `git diff --check` passed. No live provider or broad E2E run; automated local review was unavailable.

Top: desktop chat. Bottom: phone-width Cmd+K Compose (left) and `/new` (right). Light mode, Chromium, synthetic Gateway data. Before: baseline `2595c38a47d4`; after: the same verified patch on `dc166897b811`.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep the harness request type internal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled main’s production and full-tree Knip reports flag `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` as an unused named export. The request type still belongs in the same module because it describes the side-question callback.

## User Impact

No runtime or public SDK change. This removes only the unused named export; the callback’s request and response shapes and policy are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact diagnostic recurs on unchanged source. The package export map, harness SDK entrypoints and exact-symbol search did not identify a consumer of the named export. Keeping the alias private preserves its local references without weakening Knip.

## Evidence

- [Original scheduled failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089297581/job/140806522333) and [latest repeat](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46107655266/job/140864184640).

prs.title: fix(doctor): decide config-flow's graph steps and update history without writing
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` stops the Gateway and runs its config flow on every run, even on a healthy install. To make that stop conditional later, each step must report truthfully whether it has work. The config flow's `pending` answer stayed `work` on every healthy install because three of its owners had no read-only check: the migration graph steps that decide inside their writers, interrupted update reconciliation, and the config repairs. Two of those writers also did needless work on a healthy store: the Skill Workshop proposal retirement opened the state database for writing just to look for retired tables, and the transcript directive pass copied the state database into private scratch to inspect agent database leases it did not need.

## User Impact

No visible change: Doctor still stops the Gateway and runs every step. On a healthy install Doctor no longer opens the state database for writing to look for retired Skill Workshop tables and no longer copies the state database to inspect leases. The Doctor trace now reports each graph step and the update history separately; `config-flow` still answers `work`, now only because of `config-repairs`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each graph step's writer now reads a read-only predicate at its owner first and writes only when it finds work; the `config-flow` check calls the same predicate. Every SQLite read runs inside `decideDoctorPendingFromLiveStores`, so an unheld store answers `undecidable`.

| Input | Predicate (owner) | Writer change |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy-state-steps.config-machine-state` | `hasDaemonRuntimePinMigrationWork` (completed pin receipt for this source, read without creating `control/services.sqlite`) and `hasLegacyConfigMachineState` (retired machine-owned config fields) | same functions; no behavior change |
| `legacy-state-steps.transcript-directives` | `hasHistoricalTranscriptDirectiveWork` over every discovered agent database; an unfinished cursor is work | the lease inspection (a state database snapshot copy) runs only once a database needs the pass, and still runs before any admitted work |
| `legacy-state-steps.orphan-session-keys` | `checkOrphanedSessionKeysPending`: the migration's own pass without its write | the deferred plugin migration read runs only when a legacy JSON store exists |
| `legacy-state-steps.shared-auth-store` | the detection's `sharedAuthStore.hasLegacy`, the only thing the writer acts on (also in the detection preview) | none |
| `legacy-state-steps.delivery-queues` | `hasDoctorDeliveryQueueWork`: retired queue files or pending legacy entries | same count, shared |
| `legacy-state-steps.workspace-aliases` | `collectRepointedWorkspaceAliasFindings`, the function the writer already checks first | none; `undecidable` when the process environment names another state root, since the collector reads through it |
| `legacy-state-steps.skill-workshop` | `hasSkillWorkshopProposalRetirementWork`: retired tables (live catalog through a read-only connection), legacy proposal files, earlier exports | reads first; a store with nothing to retire is never opened for writing or locked |
| `legacy-state-steps.acp-session-metadata` | `checkLegacyAcpSessionMetadataPending`: the migration's own pass without its import or rewrite | the pass moves beside its importer (`state-migrations.acp-session-metadata.ts`, the session store module was at its line cap); the deferred plugin read runs only when a source exists |
| `update-history` | `readInterruptedUpdateCandidate` + `canSettleInterruptedUpdate`, the gate `reconcileInterruptedUpdateRuns` applies; read through a read-only connection, `undecidable` on PostgreSQL | none; no update or settlement code is edited |

What each check cannot decide, and answers `undecidable` (counted as work): PostgreSQL state or agent databases (config machine state, transcript directives, Skill Workshop, update history); a store nobody holds; any warning the writer would emit (orphan keys, ACP metadata), since skipping the step would drop it. Over-approximations that answer `work`: an unfinished transcript cursor while another process holds an agent database (the writer would wait); an archived ACP index whose rows were already imported.

`config-repairs` keeps `work`: the config repair sequence runs about 30 stages, several with side effects outside the config file (plugin links, auth profile stores, Tailscale identities, OAuth shadows), and none has a read-only answer yet.

## Evidence

Tested commits: base `22a3aec1c89` (red), head `4f57954471c` (green and guards). The PR head differs from the tested head by a rename of the moved session key canonicalizer (`canonicalizeLegacySessionKeyForAgent`, for the export-name collision check) and by merges of `main` that touch none of these owners (`doctor-sandbox`, openshell, ACP spawn, cron notice delivery, iOS and similar). Cells: Linux Docker, systemd user Gateway, npm install of a local pack under the unpublished version 2026.11.13, Telegram and X channels, three agents, no network. The healthy store was seeded with the base build, settled with two `doctor --fix` runs, and restored byte-identical (sha256 over all files) before every run. Method: `strace -f` plus a preload recording write-intent `fs` calls and `node:sqlite` opens, write statements and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE` with their JS callers, limited to the `doctor.config-flow` span and to each `doctor.pending.config-flow.*` span.

**Red (base, healthy install).** `config-flow` answers `work` with `legacy-state-steps`, `update-history` and `config-repairs` at `work check=default`. Inside the `doctor.config-flow` span:

```text
doctor.config-flow 6294.4ms: rw-opens=1 snapshot-copies=1 store-writes=6 begin=0 fs-writes=0
  sqlite-open ~/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=rw <= openOpenClawStateDatabase < readDatabaseProposals < retireProposals
  sqlite-open ~/.cache/openclaw/.../owner.sqlite?mode=rw (snapshot staging) <= assertNoOpenClawAgentDatabaseLeasesReadOnly < hasActiveAgentDatabaseLease < migrateHistoricalTranscriptDirectives
  sqlite-write ~/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=rw PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL / wal_autocheckpoint / journal_size_limit / synchronous / foreign_keys (connection setup of that writable open)
```

The snapshot copy stages a private copy of the state database (staging directory, token store, `database.sqlite`), about 0.26 s on this small store before cleanup.

**Green (head, same restored store).**

```text
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.config-machine-state 4.4ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.transcript-directives 26.1ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.orphan-session-keys 2.5ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.shared-auth-store 0.1ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.delivery-queues 19.7ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.workspace-aliases 51.7ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.skill-workshop 6.5ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps.acp-session-metadata 48.9ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.update-history 3.2ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.config-repairs 0.0ms pending=work check=default
doctor.pending.config-flow 0.0ms pending=work check=owner
```

The nine new inputs cost about 0.16 s together (strace run; 0.12 s in the plain run). Every `doctor.pending.config-flow.*` span shows no writable open, no snapshot copy, no store write, no `BEGIN` and no write-intent `fs` call. In the `doctor.config-flow` span the Skill Workshop writable open and the snapshot copy are gone:

```text
doctor.config-flow 4597.8ms: rw-opens=1 snapshot-copies=0 store-writes=6 begin=0 fs-writes=0
  sqlite-open ~/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=rw <= openOpenClawStateDatabase < readLegacyMigrationReceipt < recoverAuthAliasMigration < maybeRepairLegacyAuthProfileStores < runDoctorRepairSequence
```

One writable open of the state database remains: on base the Skill Workshop open came first and later readers reused that handle; now the first opener is the config repair sequence's auth alias recovery (`config-repairs`), which reads its migration receipt through the writable handle. That is the next owner to convert. The span durations above are single runs and not a timing comparison.

Whole `doctor --fix` on the healthy install, head: 104 decisions trace `none check=owner` (95 on base). Not `none`: steps `client-credentials` (no check), `database-migrations` (`undecidable` inside the stop), `config-flow` (`config-repairs`), `service-definition` (no check); contributions `auth-profile-migration`, `session-transcripts`, `state-integrity`, `codex-session-routes`, `legacy-cron`, `skills`, `memory-search`, `final-config-validation`.

**Guards** (base, then head on the same restored store, then head again without restoring; each seed applied while the Gateway was serving):

| Seed | Base | Head, first run | Head, next run | Result content (base vs head) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| runtime pin receipt row deleted from `control/services.sqlite` | receipt rewritten `complete` | `legacy-state-steps.config-machine-state=work` | all new inputs `none` | identical receipt |
| transcript directive cursor deleted in the `work` agent database | cursor rewritten | `legacy-state-steps.transcript-directives=work` | `none` | identical cursors |
| retired delivery queue file `delivery-queue/fixture.json` | archived as `.migrated` | `retired-state=work`, `legacy-state-steps.delivery-queues=work` | `none` | identical |
| retired table `skill_workshop_collection_reviews` | table dropped | `legacy-state-steps.skill-workshop=work` | `none` | identical table list |
| `agents/work/sessions/sessions.json` with an orphaned `main` key | imported and archived | `legacy-state-steps.orphan-session-keys=work` | new inputs `none`; `agent-databases=work` | identical; archive and run-record names differ only by timestamp |
| `sessions.json` row with legacy ACP metadata | imported to `acp_sessions`, archived | `legacy-state-steps.acp-session-metadata=work` | new inputs `none`; `agent-databases=work` | identical `acp_sessions` rows; names differ only by timestamp |

All runs exited 0. After either session store import the next run's `agent-databases` input (the agent database plan from #206707) answers `work`; a base second run was not taken, so whether base behaves the same is not shown. Not seeded through the CLI: the shared auth store, a repointed workspace alias and an interrupted update run (unit tests only).

**Tests.** `src/commands/doctor-config-flow-pending.test.ts` (whole file audited; 10 cases added, 2 extended, none removed): every input traced in order with the step at `work` only through `config-repairs`; per sub-step, seeded work answers `work`, the real writer runs, and the next check answers `none`, with no store file changed by any check beside held stores (runtime pin receipt and a retired config field; an agent database with no transcript cursor; an orphaned `main` key; a missing shared auth ownership record; a retired delivery queue file; a retired Skill Workshop table and the legacy proposal directory; legacy ACP metadata; an interrupted update run that the reconciliation would settle); the workspace alias input `undecidable` for another state root and `none` for the process's own; and `undecidable` without sidecars for every new SQLite-reading input when no connection holds the store. Writer regression: Skill Workshop retirement beside a held healthy store leaves every file unchanged; on base it fails because the writable open removes the clean-close seal (`expected [ 'state/openclaw.sqlite.seal' ] to deeply equal []`). The new cases fail on `main`, where the inputs do not exist (11 failed, run on `22a3aec1c89`). Owner suites: ACP metadata, legacy ACP migration, upgrade-survivor ACP, stale receipt, orphan keys, `state-migrations.test.ts`, Skill Workshop retirement, transcript directive batching and large corpus, runtime pins, config machine state, workspace alias, preflight migration input: pass. Generic guards `doctor-health-contributions.pending-read-only.test.ts` and `doctor-maintenance.stopped-systemd.test.ts`: pass (75).

**Checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: every lane passes except the dead-export scan, which reports `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and `requestChatSessionSnapshot` in files this PR does not touch (inherited from `main`). The session store's assertion and max-lines baselines shrink with the moved ACP pass. Session identity ratchet: OK.

**Review.** autoreview, Codex route (gpt-6.1-sol, high), `--max-priority P2`, with 14 owners and callers as committed source context plus `state-migrations.doctor.ts`, and the read-only contract in the prompt; the report lists the files inspected. Pass 1: two P2, both fixed: the workspace alias collector reads through the process environment, so the input now answers `undecidable` for another state root; and archive-recovery work could start without the lease inspection, which now runs before any admitted work. Pass 2: scoped-clean.

**CI on `95370d29f71`** (tested merge `04c6fd8f216` onto `main` `98b9f17b660`). Two jobs fail, both inherited from `main` and reproduced there without this change:

- `security-fast`: the protocol event coverage check reports that the iOS allowlist entry `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed` is now handled. `node scripts/check-protocol-event-coverage.mjs` fails the same way on `98b9f17b660`; this PR touches no protocol, iOS or allowlist file.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-10`: `test/scripts/changed-lanes.test.ts > fails real changed-check lint for an all-lane mixed diff and passes after repair` (`Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`). The same case fails on a clean checkout of `98b9f17b660` (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/changed-lanes.test.ts -t "all-lane mixed diff"`); this PR touches no changed-lanes or lint tooling.

Nothing was rerun for green. An earlier head failed `check-source-contracts` on an export-name collision introduced here (`canonicalizeSessionKeyForAgent`); fixed by the rename.

**Not proven.** macOS, Windows, pnpm, Bun, Git installs, PostgreSQL, large stores, checks beside a serving Gateway, the shared auth store, workspace alias and interrupted update guards through the CLI (unit tests only), a timing comparison.
