prs.title: test(channels): retire stale registry coverage and trim fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The registry sentinel only compares a test manifest with a copied channel list. Related fixtures carry unused inputs or compute an expected value through the implementation under test.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Retire the inventory-only assertion while retaining five real session-binding adapter cases and all sanitizer, queue and catalog behavior checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the obsolete sentinel and its two routing entries. Compare sanitizer output directly with the independent visible-text expectation, trim unused queue fixture overrides, require the catalog alias that every caller supplies, and name the metadata test after the behavior it exercises.

## Evidence

- 430 retained cases pass across sanitizer, queue, catalog, session-binding and routing suites.
- Both original and simplified sanitizer checks reject a deliberately miswired IRC sanitizer.
- The retained Feishu adapter check rejects missing registration while the removed inventory assertion passes.
- Routing deletion was checked with a disposable Git index; the shared index and source were restored.

prs.title: fix(ui): skip Talk discovery on external catalog routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening or reopening a local Claude catalog entry in the Control UI logged `INVALID_REQUEST` / `No session found` against the Gateway. The composer forwarded the catalog route key (`agent:<agent>:catalog:<catalog>:<host>:<thread>`) into `talk.catalog`, but a catalog entry is an external identity the Talk resolver can never resolve to a chat session.

## Solution

`ComposerMicrophoneOwner.syncCatalog` is the single owner of Talk/dictation discovery for both the chat composer and the standalone dictation control. It now treats a catalog session key as disconnected for discovery and leaves both capabilities `unavailable`, so no request is sent. Adoption navigates the pane to the `sessionKey` returned by `sessions.catalog.continue`, which restores ordinary session-scoped discovery with the adopted chat's own key.

## Impact

- Catalog routes issue zero `talk.catalog` / `talk.config` requests and no longer produce misleading Gateway diagnostics.
- Adopted chats keep full Talk and dictation behavior, scoped to their real key.
- Ordinary and guest session behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Discriminating tests, red on the base and green with the fix, at three boundaries:

- **Real Gateway + real browser** (`ui/src/e2e/catalog-route-talk-discovery.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`): injects a fixture session-catalog provider, opens the catalog route in Chromium, and records every `talk.catalog` / `talk.config` the composer issues.
  - Base: `talk.catalog` carries `agent:main:catalog:codex:gateway%3Alocal:…` on open and reopen.
  - Fix: only the ordinary session key (`agent:main:main`) is sent; zero `:catalog:` requests across open, reopen, and focus refresh.
- **Owner unit** (`composer-microphone-picker.test.ts`): zero requests for a catalog key, zero on focus refresh, then a single `talk.catalog` scoped to the adopted key after adoption.
- **Catalog browser E2E** (`external-session-catalogs.e2e.test.ts`, the file ClawSweeper's review named): the pane-ownership suite asserts no `talk.catalog` carries a `:catalog:` key on open or reopen, and that adoption resumes discovery with `agent:other:adopted-native`. On the base both entrances record one catalog-key request each; with the fix they record none.

```
# base (fix reverted), real-Gateway e2e talk requests:
talk.catalog { sessionKey: "agent:main:catalog:codex:gateway%3Alocal:…" }   # bug
# fix, real-Gateway e2e talk requests:
talk.catalog { sessionKey: "agent:main:main" }                              # ordinary session only
```

Consumer tests: `chat-composer-microphone.test.ts`, `chat-composer-actions.test.ts`, `composer-direct-dictation.test.tsx` — 77 passed. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean.

## Notes

ClawSweeper's review pointed at this same owner boundary and asked for real behavior proof against an isolated Gateway; the new real-Gateway e2e above supplies it. No change to Gateway permissions or session scoping.

prs.title: fix: complete root updates of a system service that runs as another account
prs.body:
Related: #204775
Follows: #206343

## What Problem This Solves

A common Linux layout is a root-owned global npm package with a systemd system unit that runs the Gateway as a service account (`User=openclaw`, state in that account's home or the unit's `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Since #206343, `sudo openclaw update` on such an install stops before the package is replaced and prints a manual procedure. That protects the service's data, but the update never completes on its own.

## User Impact

A plain `sudo openclaw update` now completes on this layout. Root replaces the package; every step that touches the service's state runs as the unit's account, with the unit's effective environment and `--profile`:

- Before the package is replaced, the new release's update checks (config, database schemas, retired state) run as the service account against the service's state. A problem there stops the update with nothing changed.
- After the package is replaced, root stops the unit. As the service account, the new release backs up the databases it migrates and the configuration and runs Doctor and the migrations (the existing `update migrate`). Root starts the unit and waits until systemd runs the new release and the service account's own `openclaw gateway health` reaches it.
- Once the installed updater has exited, a transient root unit (`openclaw-update-settle-<id>.service`) writes the update record into the service's state as the service account (`update finish`), so the account's `openclaw update status` shows it, and retires the backup. If the installed updater put the previous package back after a later failure, that unit instead stops the service, restores its state as the service account and starts it again.

If the new release does not come ready, the state is restored as the service account (only after the unit is confirmed stopped), the step fails so the installed updater restores the previous package, and the unit starts again once that package is back. The new package is never started on restored state; if the stop or the restore cannot be confirmed, the unit stays stopped and the backup is kept, and the failure says where.

The #206343 refusal stays, with its procedure, when the steps cannot run as the account: numeric, empty or root `User=`; an account that does not resolve; a `HOME` it cannot write; no root-owned `runuser`; an unreadable effective environment (for example an `EnvironmentFile=` root cannot read) or sandboxing that hides the state; an invalid answer from the account's admission; and a caller whose state or config overlaps the service's, such as `sudo env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<service state> openclaw update` (the installed updater would write that state as root before any candidate step runs). Each refusal names its reason. Single-account installs, units that run as the updating account, other installations and unrelated units are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater cannot change, so the work sits in the two places a published updater calls into the new release: `update admit` before the swap and the update Doctor child (`update-migrated-finalize --doctor`) after it. Both reuse existing owners: unit discovery and the root-read effective environment (`readSystemdServiceExecStartAsRoot`), the immutable path's `runuser` switch (now one helper for both), the systemd identity and lifecycle owners for stop/start, and the externally supervised `update migrate` / `restore` / `finish` commands that already own the backup, Doctor migration, restore and run record. No new protocol, config option, flag, stored field or schema.

### Trust boundary (for the service-owner and security review)

Root owns the package and the unit; the unit's account owns its state. Privilege only goes down:

- **Who decides the account and environment.** Root re-derives everything from systemd and NSS: the unit's `User=` (must be a named, resolvable, non-root account), its effective environment read as root through the existing `readSystemdServiceExecStartAsRoot` reader (inline `Environment=` and `EnvironmentFile=`), the `--profile` in its `ExecStart`, and whether sandboxing (`RootDirectory=`, `BindPaths=`, `PrivateTmp=`, `ProtectHome=` and similar) hides the state. Nothing the service account wrote chooses the account, unit, environment or paths.
- **How root switches.** Root runs only a root-owned `runuser` (`/usr/sbin/runuser` or `/sbin/runuser`, regular file, owner root, not group/other-writable) with a fixed `PATH` and nothing else; the unit's environment reaches the account's process through an owner-only file and applies only after the switch, so loader variables such as `LD_PRELOAD` from the unit never affect a root process, and no environment value appears in any argv. The account runs this release's own entry point (`node <root>/dist/index.js update admit|migrate|restore|finish|gateway health`). Both immutable-update `runuser` call sites now build their argv through the same helper (unchanged argv).
- **What root hands over.** A fresh root-owned directory in root's sticky `/tmp` (checked: real directory, owner root, sticky bit), mode `0711`, holding files created with `O_EXCL`, then `fchown` to the account and `fchmod 0400`: only the account can read them and nobody but root can replace them. Root never reads them back. They are removed when the step ends, or by the settle unit.
- **What root reads back.** Only exit statuses and the last line of bounded output (admission verdict up to 1 MiB, parsed with the same `parseUpdateAdmissionVerdict` the installed updater uses, exit code and candidate version cross-checked, the combined verdict revalidated; migrate/restore/finish up to 256 KiB, reading only a `^[a-z-]{1,32}$` status word). No path from the account's output is used for anything. Readiness is decided by root from `/proc/<MainPID>/cmdline` and its own `package.json`, plus the exit status of the account's `gateway health`.
- **What root executes as root.** `systemctl`/D-Bus start and stop of the selected unit (through the existing `captureSystemdServiceIdentity` with `rootServiceAccount` and the systemd lifecycle owner), `systemd-run` for the settle unit, and the package manager the installed updater already runs. The settle unit's script is a constant in this release; its single argument is JSON of root-derived values.
- **The private stage.** Installed updaters stage the candidate in a `0700` `.openclaw.update-stage-*` directory. For the account's admission only, root adds the traverse bit of the account's permission class (owner, primary group, others) to that one directory and restores its mode afterwards; any other ancestor the account cannot traverse makes admission refuse.
- **Stops.** A stop counts only when systemd reports the unit inactive or failed and both its current and its pre-stop cgroup are empty; otherwise nothing is restored and the backup is kept.
- **When it refuses instead.** Numeric/empty/root `User=`, unresolvable account, a `HOME` the account does not own and cannot write, no root-owned `runuser`, unreadable effective environment, sandboxed state, a caller whose state or config overlaps the service's (canonical paths, so `sudo env OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<service state>` and aliases), or any invalid answer from the account's admission. Each refusal happens in candidate admission, before the package is replaced.

Threat cases tested (unit tests at the boundary, account process replaced by a stand-in that answers as an account could): malformed verdict, admit verdict with refusal exit, verdict for another candidate, verdict that claims the account check itself, output past its bound, failed run; migrate success exit without a status word, a status word with shell metacharacters, output past its bound; restore failure; unconfirmed stop; processes surviving in the cgroup; the scheduled settle script executed against stand-ins (kept update recorded from indented output, rollback restores then restarts, restore without a status or with a populated cgroup leaves the unit stopped, same-version different-build treated as rollback); settle scheduling failure restores; unit secrets kept out of root's `runuser` environment and out of the settle unit's argv; handed-over files `0400` owned by the account. Each admission case was shown red by disabling its check.

### Update behavior

- **Published drivers with candidate admission (2026.9.7 through 2026.11.10), package installs:** reach this through the candidate's `update admit` and its Doctor child. Proven below with 2026.11.10.
- **What a 2026.11.10-driven hop cannot do:** that updater writes its own run record, report, snapshot and diagnostics into the caller's state (`/root/.openclaw` with plain `sudo`) and finishes with its own messages. The service's run record is therefore written separately by the settle step, as the service account. The updater's closing lines still include text about root's own state ("gateway.mode is unset", "Gateway service inspection is unavailable; automatic service restart was skipped ... run `openclaw update repair`") although the service was restarted and verified; this text comes from the installed updater's finalization against root's state and is not changed here.
- **A `main`-driven hop:** goes through the release path in `src/update/`, which this PR does not touch (it belongs to the update-path owner). Observed in the cell: the next `sudo openclaw update` run by the new release refuses at its own schema preflight against root's state and changes nothing. The change that path needs is in the issue thread, not here.

## Evidence

Linux Docker, systemd as PID 1, root-owned global npm install of the published **2026.11.10** driver, system unit `openclaw-gateway.service` with `User=openclaw`, `HOME=/var/lib/openclaw`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/openclaw/.openclaw`, state seeded by the 2026.11.10 Gateway (state schema 40, agent schema 42) plus a retired delivery-queue file that exists only in the service state, a local registry serving the candidate as `latest`, and a 1-second `/readyz` probe for the whole cell. Every step runs inside the container as a script; the host only starts the container and the scripts. Candidates are packs under unpublished versions.

| Cell | Driver → candidate | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Red, `sudo openclaw update --yes` twice | 2026.11.10 → `origin/main` `8b36e346b45` as 2026.11.13 | exit 1 both times in 49 s / 48 s, `service-account-mismatch` before the swap; package 2026.11.10, schemas 40/42, MainPID unchanged, 0 restarts; 0 entries under the service home not owned by `openclaw`; no not-ready probe during either attempt |
| Green, `sudo openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.10 → this branch `bce55cc1b18` as 2026.11.26 | exit 0 in 837 s, "OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.26"; schemas 40/42 → 42/45; unit running the new build (new MainPID, 0 restarts); 0 entries not owned by `openclaw` before, after and at the end; longest not-ready run 18 s (20 of 1,395 probes); the service account's `openclaw update status` shows the run `succeeded`, after `2026.11.26` |

Which account ran each state step (process owner from a 250 ms process sampler in the green cell):

| Step | Owner |
|---|---|
| Candidate `update admit` launched by the installed updater | root |
| `update admit` against the service's state (through `runuser`) | `openclaw` |
| `update migrate --backup-root /var/lib/openclaw/.openclaw-update/system-service-<id>/native` | `openclaw` |
| `gateway health --json` readiness check | `openclaw` |
| `update finish` (settle unit, after the updater exited) | `openclaw` |

Admission validated the service's own state: its warning names `/var/lib/openclaw/.openclaw/delivery-queue/seeded.json`, a file that exists only there. The backup lived under the service home owned by `openclaw` and was removed by `update finish` (82 entries after the update, 65 at the end).

Recordings (terminal, 4x speed):

- Red, attempt 1: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd14dc3b-e849-4608-afab-21867463bcfc
- Red, attempt 2: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7732eb9a-2efd-45ba-8113-86d9df3c39a6
- Green: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be49933d-11f6-41e6-aedb-d381ac2f640e

**Further cells (running; this section is updated as they finish):** failure (the new Gateway refuses to start), fallback without `runuser`, numeric `User=`, explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, custom unit name, `ExecStart --profile`, and controls (unit running as root, the service account's own run, an unrelated unit present), each on base and head where the control applies, plus the green, failure and explicit-state cells re-run on the PR head.

The pass on the PR head is reported below.

- Drivers other than 2026.11.10 were traced from the admission contract, not run. Git installs do not run candidate admission and are unchanged.

- pnpm/Bun installs, `KillMode=process` survivors and `EnvironmentFile=` units were not run in a cell; the custom-unit, `--profile` and numeric-`User=` variants are listed below as they complete.
- The settle step's own output goes to its unit's journal, not to the updater's output.
- No macOS or Windows (Linux systemd only).

prs.title: fix: return to notification settings after choosing agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Saving an agent selection under Settings → Notifications left the picker open until the Gateway replied. Even though the browser had sent the selected IDs, the account and inherited browser rows still showed the old choice. Escape did not dismiss the pending picker.

## User Impact

Save now closes the picker and returns focus to **Agents**. The row previews the selected scope and says **Saving…** until the Gateway confirms it. On failure, Settings shows the last confirmed scope and the reason. Reopen the picker to review or retry the submitted choice, even after visiting another Settings page on the same connection. A newer open draft is not replaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker owns only the open draft. The existing Web Push command owner already knows the connection, preference layer and readback result, so it retains the submitted agent IDs for that layer. Other preference writes stay gated while the picker can reopen for editing. Nothing changes browser subscriptions, OS permission, Gateway storage or notification delivery policy.

## Evidence

On main `26ff231013c4`, a held preference write kept **Research** checked in the dialog but left both summaries at **All agents**. On `7a01e32e3057`, Chromium verified focus return and the account/inherited preview before the response; reopening and editing while pending; refusal without overwriting newer edits; recovery after navigation; and a retry that stays pending until readback. Also exercised a device-only change and refusal after leaving the page. The real Control UI and its Web Push owner used synthetic Gateway responses and a synthetic browser registration, not live push delivery.

The production-bundle browser regression, 39 focused preference/owner tests, two browser layout checks, scoped typecheck, lint and formatting passed. No full CI suite or independent local review was run; the bound review tool was unavailable.

### Clean comparison

Both frames show the same point: **Save** was clicked and the preference write was received, but its reply was still held. Real Control UI in Chromium, 1100 × 850 emulated desktop, light theme, reduced motion, synthetic account and push registration. Before: `26ff231013c4`. After: `10cfd101002e` (same tree as the locally tested commit).

**Before**

![Before: the picker stays open with Research checked and Save disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d36c5a6-224c-4410-a9d8-dcb2557fc707)

**After**

![After: the picker is closed and the Agents row shows Research and Saving](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30903408-a75b-466c-a2ed-2b1ccda31f3f)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: the disabled Save button in the still-open picker is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e67088e-0983-4225-95f5-b05b0923611e)

**After**

![After: the Research choice is outlined in Settings while the write is pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd43fd00-fe03-4b34-bb47-8dadb01edddc)

<details>
<summary>Reopening during a save and recovering from a refusal</summary>

**Before refusal:** The original picker reported the error and kept Research checked.

![Before: refused write with the selected agent retained in the open picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc05fdd5-9f51-4492-88bd-bcd726d191d0)

**After refusal:** Settings shows the actual refusal, rolls the row back to All agents and explains how to retry.

![After: Settings shows the Gateway error and recovery beside the agent selector](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7081bb0-526e-4390-bb23-554334a2f070)

**Reopened before the reply:** The picker allows editing while another write is pending, but cannot submit a second write yet.

![Reopened while pending: Research checked, Saving status, and Save disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dde4eb73-5367-4056-bb25-ffbf0fd6a81d)

**Newer draft:** Support was checked while the first request was pending. Refusing the first request did not replace that draft.

![Reopened after refusal: Research and Support remain checked and Save is available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36d562b6-00aa-4c6c-9468-0ed2e12ef2d3)

</details>

Co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4db0c57e-a1a7-40ff-b300-b642f46b79e9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a614eb8c-19c6-431b-ae96-e16ae8a0346b)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(doctor): check sandboxes the runtime enables per agent
prs.body:
## Problem
`openclaw doctor` and `doctor --fix` decided whether sandboxing is on from `agents.defaults.sandbox` only (#201988). With sandboxing enabled only per agent (`agents.entries.<id>.sandbox.mode`), Doctor gave no Docker/Podman warning and built no missing image. The first sign of trouble was a failed sandboxed turn. The runtime resolves each agent's sandbox with `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`.

## Change
Doctor now resolves the defaults and every configured agent through `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`, the runtime's own resolver. This is the same pattern as #205395.
- An agent's own `sandbox.mode`, backend and images count. A gateway role that requires a sandbox covers every agent's resolved images.
- Each container engine is probed once, and each distinct image is checked and offered for build once.
- When the engine is missing, the note names the agent whose mode enabled it ("set sandbox.mode to off for agent \"work\""). An enabled mode is named before a role-only requirement.
- Sandbox settings the runtime resolver rejects (for example a relative SSH workspace root) are reported as a Doctor warning instead of failing the step.

## User impact
Doctor and the runtime now agree on which sandboxes exist. Users with per-agent sandboxing get the Docker/image warning and the build offer they were missing.

## Evidence
- Red on main, green here: `doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker.test.ts` "follows an agent's own sandbox mode when the defaults leave it off (#201988)": the engine note and pending image work.
- Adversarial review (Fable) found four gaps in round 1, all fixed and tested here: a role requirement hid an enabled agent; duplicate prompts per image; a throw on an invalid SSH root; role-required agents' own images.
- `doctor-sandbox*.test.ts` 32/32; `tsgo:core` clean.
- Not in scope, pre-existing: the Codex bwrap network-namespace hint still reads the defaults' `docker.network`.
- Upgrade check from the latest stable: `openclaw@2026.11.10` wrote the state, and the config was given `agents.entries.work.sandbox: { mode: "all", docker: { image: "openclaw-sandbox:w11-missing" } }`.
  - `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` on 2026.11.10: no sandbox image finding.
  - This branch on the same state: `Sandbox base image missing: openclaw-sandbox:w11-missing`.
- Lint fix after CI: the engine field uses the named `SandboxContainerEngine` type. Local ClawSweeper on `90fc97dc`: clean.

prs.title: fix(doctor): lint --all reads client credentials from source state
prs.body:
## Problem
`openclaw doctor --lint --all` reports a false device-pairing warning on a healthy migrated profile (#204769, three reporters on 2026.11.10): "Could not read the local device identity … Client credential migration is incomplete or stale". `--only core/doctor/device-pairing` on the same profile is clean.

`--all` runs every core check inside a private state copy that holds only `state/openclaw.sqlite`. The client credential store (`client/credentials.sqlite`) is bound to the source state file's identity, so it cannot be copied: a copy is never "ready", and copying it would put private keys in a temp directory. Inside the copy the shared database exists but its credential companion does not, so the credential reader refuses.

The same mechanism also gives a false `--all` warning from gateway health for a remote Gateway, or a loopback one without a shared token: the Gateway call loads the local device identity first. (Found by adversarial review.)

## Change
The lint runner already routes source-bound checks (auth profiles, heartbeat migrations) to the source state. Device pairing and gateway health join that set, because both read the client credential store. Every `--all` check now sees the same credential state as a direct check. The private state-database view stays in place: the existing test that `--all` never opens the source state database still passes.

## User impact
- No false "client credential migration" warning from `doctor --lint --all`.
- Leftover legacy `devices/*.json` pairing files, previously missed under `--all`, are now reported, as `--only` already did.

## Evidence
- Red on main, green here: `doctor-lint.state-isolation.test.ts` "gives --all the same credential-reading findings as direct checks on a migrated profile" (device pairing + gateway health, remote Gateway config). 19/19 in the file.
- Upgrade check from the latest stable: installed `openclaw@2026.11.10`, let it write its own state (`doctor --fix`), then ran `doctor --lint --all`:
  - 2026.11.10: `local-device-auth-unreadable` (the false finding).
  - This branch, against the same stable-written state: no device-pairing finding; `--only core/doctor/device-pairing` is still clean.
- `doctor-lint.test.ts`, `.oauth`, `.sqlite-preservation`, `.snapshot-cleanup`, `doctor-device-pairing.test.ts`: pass. `tsgo:core`: clean.

prs.title: feat: let Knowledge learn from your Gmail through Composio
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge can learn from conversations, Granola meetings, Memory and Slack, but not from email. Email is where a lot of commitments, decisions and introductions actually happen. Today an owner has to repeat them to the agent by hand, or they never reach Knowledge.

## User Impact

The Scribes tab gains **Learn from Mail**. It runs once or on a schedule (weekdays at 8 AM, 12 PM and 4 PM) and has these options:

- **Starting from**: the last 7 days (the default), the last 30 days, or today.
- **Also threads you wrote in**: on by default.
- **Change…** settings, as the other editable scribes have.

It reads Gmail through the Composio CLI, read-only, and picks the threads worth remembering. From those it saves decisions and commitments in both directions (what the owner promised, and who is waiting on whom) and news, keeping the people and project pages current. It never sends, drafts, labels, archives or deletes mail.

Setup on the Gateway host:

- Install the `@composio/composio` plugin.
- Install the Composio CLI.
- Run `composio login` and `composio link gmail`.

The page checks that the Composio plugin is installed and turned on. It can't see the CLI's sign-in or linked accounts. Each run checks those first and stops with a `Scribe status: failed` line that names what is missing (CLI not installed, signed out, or Gmail not linked).

## Why This Change Was Made

Josh decided to build Knowledge scribes for mail, calendar and Drive through Composio, mail first, with a decision model deciding which threads are ingested. gbrain's email-to-brain and open-loop guides inspired the extraction rules. No code was copied from them.

- **Read-only boundary.** Gmail is read only through `skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/gmail-read.mjs`. It allowlists three Composio tools: `GMAIL_GET_PROFILE`, `GMAIL_LIST_THREADS` and `GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_THREAD_ID`. The slugs come from Composio's Gmail toolkit page. The script runs `composio` with `execFile`, never a shell, and checks thread IDs before the CLI sees them. The skill tells the agent never to run `composio` itself.
- **Gate.** `gmail-normalize.mjs triage` applies a deterministic prefilter first. It leaves out mailing lists (List-Unsubscribe, List-Id or bulk Precedence headers), automated senders, calendar notices (found by the iCalendar MIME method, with the subject as a fallback), bulk Gmail categories, and spam or trash. A thread the owner wrote in is always kept. Updates mail is kept too.
- **Decision model.** Each kept thread carries a `decision_evaluate` input (contractVersion 2): a boolean `ingest` question and a `kind` choice, over the subject and short excerpts of the newest messages. With no decision model, or an unavailable, error or abstaining answer, the agent applies the same criteria itself.
- **Checkpoint.** `Knowledge scribe checkpoint · Learn from Mail` records each thread's triage outcome with its history ID and a digest of its message IDs. A skipped thread is triaged again only when its messages change.
- **Sources.** Each ingested thread is one source, keyed `gmail:<address>/<threadId>`. It has complete snapshot manifests and keeps its Gmail deep link. Senders and recipients are matched to person pages by `email:<address>`.

Design choices that differ from the plan in the epic:

- Snapshots are `complete`, not `partial` as in Slack, because each run reads the whole thread.
- The decision state is JSON per thread, not a single `list` batch. A boolean answer would cover the whole list rather than each item, so a batch can't give one answer per thread. GPT-6 Luna, the decision model used for the live check below, also rejects `list` state as unsupported input.
- Each scheduled run ingests 10 threads and triages at most 80.

## Evidence

- **Tests.** Focused Vitest passed on Crabbox AWS (run `run_d375c9f0db957cc4065d3ec60b2d7f71` and earlier runs) for gmail-scripts, scribe-mail-fields, scribes-state, scribes-view, scribe-slack-fields, skill-packaging and slack-read-normalize. The last full run passed 68 of 68.
  - The Gmail reader is tested against a stand-in `composio` binary. The test checks that only the three read slugs ever reach the CLI, and covers pagination of thread lists and of long threads, invalid thread IDs, and each failure class.
  - The normalizer tests cover the prefilter cases, HTML and plain-text quoted replies, calendar MIME parts, digests that don't change with labels, and hashes that stay the same across reads. They also run the output through `chat-transcript.mjs` and `source-manifest.mjs`.
- **Checks.** Typecheck for `tsconfig.extensions.json` and the extension tests, oxlint on `extensions/knowledge`, and format all pass on the final head.
- **Inherited failure.** `check:changed` reports one dead-export failure, `src/agents/harness/types.ts: AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest`. This branch doesn't touch that file.
- **Live decision model triage.** The scribe's rubric was run unchanged through `decision_evaluate` against `clawrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna` on eight synthetic Gmail threads. Six were built as saved Gmail threads, run through `gmail-normalize.mjs triage`, and evaluated with the rubric it emits. Two more checked borderline cases. Every call returned `status: ok`. The run marks a thread for ingestion when `probabilityTrue` is at least 0.5.

  | Thread | Prefilter | P(ingest) | Kind |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Personal request (introduction ask) | kept | 0.97 | relationship (0.55; commitment 0.44) |
  | Commitment (contract by Friday, owner replied) | kept | 1.00 | commitment (0.99) |
  | Lyft receipt | kept | 0.00 | routine (1.00) |
  | Newsletter | list-mail | 0.00 | routine (1.00) |
  | GitHub CI failure | automated-sender | 0.06 | routine (0.96) |
  | Calendar invite | calendar-notice | 0.25 | scheduling (0.93) |
  | Coffee time proposed by a person | (borderline) | 0.84 | scheduling (0.94) |
  | Thank-you note | (borderline) | 0.04 | relationship (0.59) |

  The split is clean: every thread to keep scored 0.84 or above, and every routine thread scored 0.25 or below. The rubric was not changed. For prefiltered threads the rubric was run on the same state shape to check it. A real run never sends those threads to the model.

  The coffee scheduling thread counts as ingest because the rubric treats an open request to the owner as someone waiting on them. The receipt passes the prefilter because its sender (`receipts@`) is not an automated local part, so the model is what keeps it out.
- **Not verified live.** No Composio CLI, login or linked Gmail was used. The Composio CLI is not installed on the test host, and installing it needs owner approval. Response shapes come from Composio's documentation and public callers. A live Gmail run is still to do.
- **Review.** An independent review found one P1 and three P2 issues, all fixed and covered by tests:
  - Long threads now read every page before the thread file is written.
  - The check for unchanged threads uses a digest of message IDs instead of the newest message ID, so deleted messages are caught.
  - HTML `<blockquote>` replies are now treated as quoted text.
  - The calendar check now reads each MIME part's own headers.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(update): publish fixed sentences and no third-party text in failure reports
prs.body:
## Problem

The public update failure report (filed to a GitHub issue after the user reviews it) published third-party and private text, while hiding the OpenClaw causes maintainers need.

Published on `main`, shown by the new tests:
- npm output lines, including an email and a private scoped package name.
- The npm package spec in the phase line and in the `npm view <spec>` remedy (`@acme-internal/billing-sdk@1.2.3`).
- Fork versions, custom tags, build IDs, non-hex SHAs, and the rollback outcome's error text.

Hidden on `main`: every recent auto-filed update failure report reads `[redacted-diagnostic]` for its cause. Maintainers had to ask each reporter for the local output. The known causes include:
- the backup SQLite header probe timing out or hitting an unreadable file;
- a plugin-migration obligation conflict;
- another update executor owning the installation.

## Fix

The public report publishes fixed sentences and closed values only. Free text from errors and from npm is never published.

- **npm/bun:** the report keeps `npm failure code: <allowlisted code>` and the fixed remedy for that code. npm's own lines stay in the local record (`openclaw update status --json`).
- **Package specs:** published only for `openclaw` or an official-catalog plugin package, with a release version or channel selector. Otherwise the report shows the name alone or `<spec>`.
- **Throw-site sentences:** three throw sites now set a public `code` on their error, and the existing code→sentence table (`UPDATE_PREFLIGHT_DETAILS`) supplies one fixed sentence per code:
  - the backup SQLite probe: `backup-sqlite-probe-timeout` / `backup-sqlite-probe-failed`;
  - the plugin-migration conflict: `plugin-migration-obligations-changed`;
  - the executor admission refusal that names the lease owner: `update-executor-owned`.
- **Identity lines:** published only in the shapes OpenClaw writes; otherwise a placeholder (`[redacted-version]`, `[redacted-tag]`, `[redacted-build]`, `[redacted-sha]`).
  - Shapes kept: release versions (including corrections and a Git `v`), hex SHAs, OpenClaw build IDs.
  - The rollback outcome publishes its status only.
- **Bug fix:** npm facts no longer print an extra `Failing check [redacted-check]` line.

## How other harnesses do this

| Harness | Public/user-submitted report | Free text from logs |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes | `hermes debug share`: public paste built from an allowlist (counts, codes, versions, config-key shape) | none in the public route; raw logs only through the private route |
| Codex CLI | `/feedback`: note, plus diagnostics after consent, sent to OpenAI | raw log/rollout bytes attached; no whole-bundle redaction |
| Pi | local debug bundle the user shares | transcripts and logs retained; env values masked by variable name |
| opencode | manual GitHub bug form | user pastes logs; docs ask them to remove secrets |
| Claude Code | `/feedback`: transcript to Anthropic, optional public issue | token-pattern redaction for local archives only |

This change follows the Hermes public-route model: fixed fields and codes, no log lines.

## Impact

| User group | Failure class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Every Gateway or CLI user who files an update failure report (both routes prepare the same report: `src/gateway/server-methods/update-report.ts:79`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-report.ts:73`) | Update/Doctor: undiagnosable or over-sharing failure reports | `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.ts` `renderBoundedDiagnostics`; `src/infra/update-npm-failure.ts` `formatNpmFailureFacts` |

Local diagnostics are unchanged. Only the public issue body changes.

Behavior outside the report: these errors now carry a specific `.code`, so a run's reason or fact code can show the new code instead of `unexpected-error` / `finalization-failed`. No code branches on the old values.

## Evidence

- New tests that fail on the merge base and pass here (vitest-source):
  - `src/infra/update-npm-failure.test.ts`: a private scoped package, an email, a token in a registry URL, a home path and a hostname in npm output must not appear. On base, the scoped package and the email leak; the other three were already redacted and stay as guards. Each case also checks the published code (E401, E404, EACCES, EAI_AGAIN, EEXIST).
  - `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts`: the real probe failure (ETIMEDOUT and an unreadable source under a home path) publishes its fixed sentence and never the path.
  - `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.test.ts`: plugin-migration conflict and executor-owned refusal publish only their fixed sentence; fork version, tag, SHA, build ID and rollback text are redacted; corrections and `v` tags stay.
  - `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-cancellation.test.ts`: the real executor admission refusal carries `update-executor-owned`.
- Related report suites pass: 18 files, including update-failure-report, update-run-report, metadata-diagnostics, rollback-report and update-handoff-failure.
- Upgrade check from the latest stable, in scratch (`env -i`, own HOME, state dir, config path and npm prefix): a fresh `openclaw@2026.11.10` updated to this branch's packed full build with `openclaw update --tag <package> --yes --no-restart --json`.
  - Result: `ok`, the `openclaw doctor` step completed with exit 0, and `openclaw --version` reports the candidate.
  - An earlier attempt was stopped by an external SIGTERM during activation and rolled back cleanly. The rerun had no interruption.
- The installed candidate prepared a public report from a real failed update record (a private registry URL with a token in npm config, plus a private scoped `--tag`). No token, registry host or package name appears in the report.

prs.title: refactor(tests): trim ordinary projection and permutation samples
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## What Problem This Solves

Test maintenance includes repeated ordinary projection and permutation examples alongside stronger module and guard coverage. This piece trims those examples in 16 existing suites, reducing maintenance by **655 net lines** (660 removed, 5 added).

## User Impact

No production behavior or configuration changes. Each touched module keeps an existing covering suite. The ordinary assertions listed below are deliberately retired; the surviving keepers are not claimed to reproduce every removed example.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain authority, stale-input, cancellation, persistence, delivery-settlement and release guards while shrinking ordinary examples in place. No new files, support modules, production edits, inventory edits or baseline edits. Unused imports and fold remnants are removed.

<details>
<summary>Per-file evidence: TRIM 16, DELETE 0; named existing keepers and retired ordinary oracles</summary>

| Test file | Net removed | Deliberately retired oracle | Existing covering keeper / retained guard |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `ui/src/components/canvas-widget-view.test.ts` | 9 | Already-loaded full-access widget remount/listener/read-count sample. | Same suite: client replacement; stale source/client; guest nonce; denial; timeout and teardown. |
| `src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts` | 8 | Malformed optional-preload parser fallback sample. | Same suite: actual enabled asset bytes, disabled UI 404 and preload admission cases. |
| `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` | 63 | Ordinary placement, preview deduplication and frozen-input permutations. | Same suite: actual coalesced result plus unanswered/interrupted turn boundaries. |
| `extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-view.test.ts` | 28 | Weekday schedule and disconnected-source detail wording combination. | Same suite: missing/unauthorized source disables Start; connected source starts. |
| `src/commands/onboard.test.ts` | 19 | Literal Windows/WSL2 ASCII guidance wording sample. | Same suite: real wizard migration lock before reset/noninteractive dispatch. |
| `src/plugins/contracts/scheduled-turns.contract.test.ts` | 63 | Custom tag/full-handle/top-level ID and undefined-cron positive payload examples. | Same suite: real cron.add validation, tagged delete and bad-tag/unload guards. |

prs.title: fix: explain when a new session can’t use the selected project
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you select a project in New Session, OpenClaw checks whether the session can use it. If the check finishes and neither workspace option is available, OpenClaw says the check failed and asks you to select the same project again. The disabled workspace options give the same retry instruction to people who can’t start sessions.

## User Impact

- **Before:** “Couldn’t check the checkout. Select the project again to retry.”
- **After (composer, callers who can create sessions):** “This session can’t use this project. Choose another project or workspace.”
- **After (checkout picker options):** “This session can’t use this project.”

A check that actually fails still offers a retry. If you can start sessions and another project is available, you can select it and start with the prompt you already wrote. If you don’t have access to create sessions, Start still explains that permission is missing, and the disabled checkout picker options stay neutral.

## Why This Change Was Made

New Session already distinguishes a failed check from a completed result. It now uses that distinction in the composer and checkout picker. A result with no options doesn’t say why the project is unavailable or whether another one will work.

**Skill in practice:** Name the fact the reader can rely on. Keep the retry instruction for a failed check, but don’t tell a read-only caller to choose another project. No permissions, checkout choices, retry behavior or draft handling changed.

## Evidence

Two focused Chromium scenarios exercised the production-built New Session page with controlled Gateway replies:

- **Caller with create access:** The first check for **Garden plans** failed. Selecting it again retried the check. It returned no usable workspace and stayed blocked after another selection. No create request was sent. **Field notes** offered both workspace options. Selecting it preserved “Review the planting schedule.” Pressing **Start session** sent exactly one create request, with that prompt and the Field notes project ID.
- **Read-only caller:** Both disabled checkout options exposed the factual sentence in their titles and accessible descriptions. Trying to start showed the unchanged “You don’t have permission to create a session.” No create request was sent.

Both browser scenarios failed on the original wording and passed with the change (2.87 s and 1.38 s test time). The permanent regression failed on the base only for a completed check. All 54 cases in that test file passed on the patch (3.89 s wall time). Scoped types, lint, formatting, English copy and i18n checks passed. This verifies the UI and its requests, not live permissions or filesystem provisioning. Full CI was not run locally.

**Screenshot comparison:** Garden plans after the completed check, in the same light-theme desktop composer. Before: `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: `6ff0807f3978`. See the [400 px composer and read-only picker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206414#issuecomment-7210756718) for the other views. The picker annotations quote the verified option titles; the clean screenshot does not paint a native tooltip.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Start asks to retry the completed check for Garden plans.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70bf8977-ea88-42a1-ba67-23ccacfe3d4f)

**After**

![Start explains that this session can’t use Garden plans. The prompt remains in the composer.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03931555-4aa9-4685-b473-87561c160c40)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The outline marks the instruction to retry the same project.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/503e6f69-a48a-41bd-956a-73343f69120a)

**After**

![The outline marks the factual project notice with no retry instruction.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f57b4bd-d322-4e78-a28a-f33e747323a5)

prs.title: fix: keep large tool catalogs from breaking agent replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connecting a large direct MCP catalog can make an agent's model requests fail before it can reply. One observed rejection reported a 1,070,975-byte tool description against a 1,048,576-byte limit. The limit applies to an individual description, not the sum of all independent tool definitions.

## User Impact

Newly prepared, oversized direct Codex catalogs use existing deferred discovery while preserving exact declarations, executable tools and account scope. Embedded OpenAI-family requests reject an oversized final description locally with a recovery hint, including compaction/side-question paths without a policy plugin. No callable schema is truncated.

This is a **partial mitigation, not a complete native request-size guarantee**. Explicit direct-only tools, strict function-only surfaces and native-owned saved declarations retain their contracts. Existing native threads are not migrated. This proposal has not been installed on a live agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Codex deferred surface rather than dropping tools or inventing another search/execution layer. Decide loading once from registration so a smaller currently executable subset has the same namespace contract. A 768 KiB serialized-catalog threshold reserves space for native expansion but is heuristic, not a final native size measurement.

For embedded OpenAI-family transports, check the serialized tool view at the shared encoder boundary, or the final observed payload callback for non-encoding transports. Check UTF-8 description bytes, including namespace/Chat Completions wrappers and JSON projection. Other API families keep their own limits. Custom transports bypassing both observation and the shared encoder are outside this gate.

Search/schema/execution results retain existing runtime budgets; this patch adds no competing result-budget owner. Server-provided compact meta-tools remain the preferred solution for large integrations.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132442 (deferred discovery description compaction; separate from this legacy direct-catalog transition).

## Evidence

Base: `d8c456001c10d87403c14768fdef671616f1fcb9`.

- Regression checked against the base implementation: no-plugin compaction did not reject the oversized description; a large direct Codex bridge did not expose deferred declarations. Candidate tests exercise the request wrapper and real bridge, including registered/available subsets and strict function-only preservation.
- Inspected pinned Codex 0.172.0 source (`3d86e43b075adeba2193ec5c22ac92f55afd82e6`): final Code Mode descriptions are constructed in the native app-server. This OpenClaw patch cannot certify their final byte length.
- Final focused validation: 5 files / 104 tests passed through the repository test-project wrapper, 4 shards, 129.45 s. Includes existing prefix-stability and tool-result budget tests.
- Targeted typed lint and formatting passed. Plugin SDK declaration preparation emitted 14922 files; this is not a full CLI/package build.
- Scoped production type check passed using canonical strict extension configuration/ambient declarations, including the real Codex bridge.

Remaining acceptance: broad CI/full package build, packaged native inference/compaction proof, and a native app-server final-description guard. No live compaction success is claimed; no installed runtime, main branch or general fleet rollout was changed.

prs.title: fix: stop suggesting a send when removing a queued message fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you choose **Remove** on a queued message or **Discard** on a pending chat message, the browser can fail to confirm the removal. Chat then tells you to reconnect and send the message you were trying to remove.

## User Impact

Chat now names the exact control you clicked—**Remove** in the composer queue or **Discard** on an inline pending message—and suggests trying it again only if that control is still available. A message can remain in the transcript after those controls disappear. Removing the local copy does not cancel a message the Gateway already received.

**Before:** “Couldn’t save this message. Free browser storage or reconnect to send it.”

**After (Remove):** “Couldn’t confirm that your browser removed this message. If Remove is still available, try it again.”

**After (Discard):** “Couldn’t confirm that your browser discarded this message. If Discard is still available, try it again.”

## Why This Change Was Made

The single-message removal action knows it didn’t confirm a change. It doesn’t know whether storage refused the write or another pane changed the item. The alert names the action without guessing what happened to the message. Saving a message, clearing several paused messages, and canceling queued work on the Gateway are separate actions and stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Remove:** In the real Control UI, we queued two messages offline and entered a separate draft. With browser-storage writes temporarily refused, Remove showed the old alert on main and the new one on the patch. Once writes worked again, Remove cleared just the chosen row and the alert. The other row and the draft remained. The fixture received no send requests in either version.
- **Discard:** We withheld the Gateway’s acknowledgement of a send, disconnected, and made the browser refuse a storage write. Discard showed the new alert. Once writes worked again, we dismissed the alert, which covered the inline control in this one-message view, and selected Discard. The local row disappeared without another send or any cancellation request. In a separate run, reconnecting instead left the message visible but neither Remove nor Discard available. The fixture observed the existing reconnect request using the original message key.
- The focused bundled-browser regression failed on main at the new alert and passed on the patch, including the removal, ordering, and reconnect assertions. UI typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting, localization checks, and the focused copy check passed. Screenshots were inspected at 400 and 960 pixels wide. The alert has no expandable details; **Report a bug** is unchanged. The Gateway was a controlled fixture: this isn’t proof of live delivery or permanent storage exhaustion.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Chat suggests sending after Remove fails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/506a0eb6-5e35-4369-84ba-e1dce35580fa) | ![Chat suggests retrying only while Remove or Discard is available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1140f6f3-6120-4b20-83ac-e60c6c6e0f97) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The old alert recommends a send after a removal attempt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46056797-16af-4025-a141-fcd65ebf0ea0) | ![The new alert makes retrying conditional on a removal control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/340e6acf-4689-40df-b9ab-195b03acaefc) |

Offline queue in the Control UI, 400 × 760. Before: main `7857d5ae3a5a`. After: reviewed tree `44314d58ab3c`. The fixture temporarily refused a write to browser storage.

### Skill in practice

“Couldn’t save this message” fits a save attempt, not a removal. Following both controls to the same result let us give one conditional next step without adding another error renderer or changing what happens on retry.

Independent review found that seeing a message in the transcript does not mean it can still be discarded. The correction was verified with the inline Discard and reconnect cases above.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(macos): let users move the app window from chat and panel headers
prs.body:
Closes #206808

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, dragging blank space in a Control UI chat or panel header can leave the OpenClaw window stationary. The reporter reproduced this with a physical trackpad on OpenClaw 2026.11.10 and macOS 27.2.1. In a standalone comparison, the previous WebKit-to-AppKit handoff left the window stationary even when the button was held.

## User Impact

Dragging blank header space should move the window without a settings change. The code keeps the native title-bar path and double-click zoom and excludes non-movable and full-screen windows from manual movement. Requests must arrive within 500 ms of the native press and while the button is still held.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Dashboard records the native press and allows an existing trusted main-frame request to claim it once for the same window. It then follows the pointer instead of asking AppKit to start a Window Server drag after the asynchronous WebKit hop. The bridge constrains the frame and clears drag state on release, close, or app deactivation. Existing trusted-source checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **macOS build and focused regression suite:** [Fork CI log](https://github.com/machine3at/openclaw/actions/runs/46106537574/job/140860456055) verifies checkout of exact PR head `1b77cbfa59b12ff5d5c4d39bb208b1b7c3a74583`. The final fixture starts within the visible frame, preserving both the exact pointer-delta assertion and the separate clamp test. No production bytes changed since the original review.

- **Local review:** An independent DeepSeek Flash source review compared `6deafbdf9dc` with `d5fc4a533d8`, covering native and web call sites, event ownership and lifecycle, and regressions. No blocking correctness finding in that pass. Subsequent changes add focused host-wiring coverage and fix the test fixture only. The real WebKit message receiver is not driven by the focused suite.
- **Outstanding full-app behavior proof:** Before and after product bundles were built. They have not been launched in an isolated runtime session to capture both header drags, native dragging, and double-click zoom. The PR remains draft pending that evidence, as requested in the [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207157#issuecomment-7232800586).

prs.title: fix(ios): keep connection messages from flashing when chat reopens
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you return to an iPhone chat, “Connecting to…” can already be above the composer and disappear a moment later. A cold launch with no reply can have the opposite problem: switching between “Connecting” and “Not connected” restarts the wait, even though the chat never connected.

## User Impact

A quick return no longer flashes a connection message. A disconnected message that is already visible stays visible when the app is temporarily inactive. On a cold launch, chat waits three seconds from its first pending connection status, even if the wording changes. Foreground reconnects still wait one second. The connection itself and its wording are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Time in the background is not time spent waiting in chat. The strip ends its wait when the app enters the background and starts a fresh one when it returns to the foreground, without waiting for the app to become active. While the connection is still pending, the existing strip timer keeps the deadline from the first post; other messages keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the light-appearance recording showed “Connecting to…” on the first readable chat frame after returning from Settings. It disappeared about 0.77 seconds later. After the fix, neither the light nor the dark recording showed a connection message on return.

On a cold launch with no reply, the revised app showed the message **3.06 seconds after the composer became readable**, or **3.89 seconds after the header**. It stayed visible for the rest of the recording. Holding a local test server’s handshake for 0.5 or 2 seconds showed no message; a 5-second hold showed the message until the connection recovered. An ordinary cold launch against a local test server did not reproduce the return flash.

The clock-controlled background test failed before the fix for both first connections and reconnects. The updated test also covers a visible disconnected message through an inactive interruption, and a wording change without a new deadline. All 11 iOS connection-status tests and all 9 shared status-strip tests passed. The iOS build passed SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint.

![First frame after returning to the chat from Settings, light appearance. Before, on the left, "Connecting to OpenClaw…" is already above the composer. After, on the right, no connection message shows.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04bfeb66-7d07-483b-bdce-096e7a30e561)

![The same return in dark appearance. Before, on the left, "Not connected to OpenClaw" is already above the composer. After, on the right, no connection message shows.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5f2f021-d2c9-4567-84db-46d4c042ed07)

![Cold launch against a server that answers quickly, frame by frame. Before and after, no connection message shows.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9c74779-8a90-46bf-a286-60141edc53df)

![Cold launch with no reply, frame by frame. Before and after, "Connecting to OpenClaw…" appears at about four seconds and stays.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d92aaeb4-5a31-4586-9990-4c453b18b6f3)

I used an iPhone simulator and a local test server. I did not test a physical iPhone, a real slow network, or a physical Control Center gesture.

Stacked on #206685. The connection strip this change builds on comes from #206678.

prs.title: fix(discord): render long Markdown tables before splitting messages
prs.body:
Closes #207086

## What Problem This Solves

On Discord, a reply containing a Markdown table that crosses the 2,000-character message limit arrives partially as raw `| ... |` pipe text regardless of `channels.discord.markdown.tables` (`code`, `block`, or `bullets`). The outbound chunker split the raw Markdown first and converted tables per piece afterwards, so continuation chunks that started mid-table had no header row and passed through unconverted.

## User Impact

- Long Markdown tables sent to Discord keep their configured rendering (`code`, `block`, or `bullets`) cleanly across every split message chunk instead of leaking raw pipe rows in continuation messages.
- `tableMode: "off"` continues to leave raw Markdown tables untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **`extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.ts`**:
   - Convert Markdown tables (`convertMarkdownTables(text, tableMode)`) inside `discordOutbound.chunker` before running `chunkDiscordTextWithMode` whenever `tableMode !== "off"`. Because `convertMarkdownTables` is idempotent on already-converted fenced code blocks and bullet lists, downstream `prepareDiscordOutboundText` stays safe while `chunkDiscordTextWithMode` balances code fences across chunks.
   - Resolve `tableMode` from account/channel config in `discordOutbound.sendPayload` before delegating to `sendTextMediaPayload` when `ctx.formatting?.tableMode` is unset.
2. **`src/infra/outbound/deliver-core.ts`**:
   - Resolve `tableMode` via `resolveMarkdownTableMode({ cfg, channel, accountId })` into the chunking formatting options passed to `planOutboundTextMessageUnits` whenever `params.formatting?.tableMode` is unset, so shared outbound delivery honors per-channel/per-account table settings during pre-chunking.
3. **`extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts`**:
   - Added Red → Green regression tests verifying long tables crossing 2,000 characters in `code`, `block`, `bullets`, and `off` modes across both `discordOutbound.chunker` and `discordOutbound.sendPayload`.

## Evidence

- Reproduced Red state before implementation edits (`pnpm vitest run extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed 3/4 new assertions: `expected 9 to be +0` raw pipe lines leaked outside fenced code blocks in `code`, `block`, and `bullets` modes).
- Verified Green state after final edits:
  - `pnpm exec oxlint` on all 3 modified files: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all 3 modified files: `All matched files use the correct format`
  - `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed
  - `pnpm vitest run extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.interactive-order.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **4 passed (4) files, 56 passed (56) tests**

prs.title: fix: explain when a previous automation run keeps the agent from starting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A recurring automation can fail before its agent starts when OpenClaw confuses the new run with work from the previous run. The saved error asked for a “physical store scope,” even when the job already had one. It didn’t tell the person whether the agent had started or what kept it from starting.

## User Impact

**Before:** “Session controller identity requires a physical store scope”

**After, when the previous run still holds the conflicting work:** “The agent didn’t start because work from the previous run was still active. Wait a moment, then try running it again.”

**After, when a conflict prevented startup but can’t be attributed to the previous run:** “The agent didn’t start because OpenClaw found conflicting session records for this run. Wait a moment, then try running it again.”

**After, outside automation startup:** “OpenClaw found conflicting session records and couldn’t tell which session to use. Try again in a moment.”

New failures show the explanation in **Error details** and activity history. Already-saved failures keep their original wording. This changes what a failure says, not which runs succeed. [#207148](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207148) addresses one cause of the overlap separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automation preparation knows that the agent hasn’t started. It names the previous run only if outstanding work belongs to that exact run’s session, not merely because the same session controller was involved. Other callers don’t make claims about the automation. Session matching, the active-run refusal, scheduling, and the diagnostic warning are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Ran three occurrences of a synthetic **Morning briefing** job through an isolated scheduler with its real occurrence admission, session store, and run history. The first occurrence finished. The harness then held its session to simulate remaining work. The second failed before a model call. After the harness released that work, clicking **Run now** in the real Control UI sent one forced-run request. The fixture transport forwarded those exact parameters to the scheduler and the third occurrence succeeded. Simulated model calls: **1, 0, 1**. The failed history entry remained; the saved job’s latest error cleared.
- The first occurrence already showed **Completed** while the fixture held its session. That label doesn’t establish that it’s safe to retry immediately, so the error doesn’t recommend a blind retry or a settings change.
- Both new copy expectations failed on the prior wording. An additional negative control held unrelated work on the previous run’s original controller; the revised error does not blame the previous run. All 24 tests in the affected cron state file, the separate isolated-run reproduction, and all 17 controller identity tests passed. Four browser cases covered both new explanations and both historical wordings. **Review run** selected the stored record without running or editing a job.
- Scoped typecheck, lint, format, and copy checks passed. No production automation or live provider was used; full CI was not run locally. The coordinating session reviewed the full five-file diff and found no actionable issues. This was source review, not an independent automated review.

Matched Chromium captures: the same synthetic job, light theme, 1100 × 720. Before: `fd1942854a6b`. After: `f9d4fd4fa724`.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Saved error asks for a physical store scope](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7fac4ac-4e09-46aa-9ce2-9d21511ec3de)

**After**

![The error says the agent did not start and identifies unfinished work from the previous run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a921771-27cc-47a7-8c3b-8a1b2fe9313c)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The saved storage wording is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/422b021d-c416-4135-8f8e-8919b03f1e3a)

**After**

![The previous run’s work and the unstarted agent are highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ca9f954-c533-4720-b083-aac654e9964d)

### When the previous run is not the cause

![Conflicting session records kept the agent from starting; no previous run is named](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93210df7-681e-45e1-a918-6f6ce28f967f)

[Annotated fallback, isolated-scheduler history, and the **Run now** recovery check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207180#issuecomment-7233020860)

## Skill in practice

The [OpenClaw writing skill](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-writing/SKILL.md) calls for both the known cause and the status of the reader’s work. Here, naming the previous run requires evidence from that run, and the agent’s startup status comes from the point where preparation failed.

Reported by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/20ba7cdc-26db-47f3-ba96-9ff1a5dc8e35)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: make automation billing accounts explicit
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Vyctor Brzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/c14a2bf3-3d4e-4c7c-b7db-9c4c9f1b616b)
- [Merge repair and local verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-s98cd1ab4)

## What Problem This Solves

Creating an automation can quietly lock in the billing account from the moment it was created. The editor doesn’t show that choice, and jobs without a saved account can be refused even when the agent has a working sign-in.

## User Impact

User impact: Automations use the agent’s normal account selection unless their model ends in `@profile`. Edit the model to choose a specific billing account. If that account is removed or revoked, the job won’t silently charge another account on the same provider; configured fallbacks on other providers can still run.

For upgrades, Doctor backs up cron state, turns each compatible saved account into an explicit model and account choice, preserves the recorded runtime where present, and reports each conversion. If Doctor can’t verify the same route, it pauses the job and tells you why. No jobs are deleted. Jobs without saved accounts are left untouched unless an earlier owner transfer left the job awaiting a new account choice. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` before starting a manually upgraded Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model field already accepts an account suffix, so the billing choice can live alongside the model instead of in a second hidden record. This also removes the old account-adoption flow. Parallel automation cleanup PRs may touch the automation editor, scheduling API, or Doctor’s cron repair flow; this draft does not redesign them.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The repair head is `115d6e9553f1e0c7c63926aed6ffa6816e2853a3`; its merge commit includes the requested daniel-lxs co-author trailer. This remains a draft, with no hosted re-review requested.

I reproduced both ClawSweeper findings locally. Before the fix, the Doctor cron flow kept only one of four jobs, and startup deleted both migration-pending rows during sibling quarantine. After the fix, Doctor converts compatible accounts before generic repair, pauses mismatches, and preserves pending rows through startup and sibling saves. The three continuity cases now assert the explicitly pinned model rather than changed defaults. The Template test preserves rejection of an explicitly selected foreign personal account while allowing an unpinned job.

I verified 393 distinct focused tests across 21 files locally, without a VM, including SQLite migration, Gateway validation, CLI/session routing, and isolated/session cross-provider fallback. The final eight-file run passed 56 tests in 262.94 seconds; the other 337 cases passed on unchanged inputs. Core TypeScript, targeted lint, formatting and the PR diff whitespace check passed. Provider HTTP was intercepted by the integration fixtures, not live. CI timing is not available.

The pr-simplify pass retained the existing model/account owners and the required migration, with no new state owner. The current main-to-head change removes the hidden binding/adoption path; production-oriented files are +570/-1924 lines and tests are +436/-4075 lines. Local autoreview did not run: its selected Codex installation failed the read-only sandbox preflight. I did not broaden permissions or request a hosted review.

Runtime proof still needed: shipped-entry-point runs for fresh unpinned and pinned jobs, native CLI selection, and real cross-provider fallback; real upgrades from supported 9.x extended-stable, 10.x, and v2026.11.5 through the old updater round trip and full Doctor, preserving settings, jobs, history and approvals. Full CI, packaged builds, broader test/UI type lanes and final-head independent review remain unverified. No Control UI source or layout changes.

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: keep the automation run ID when the CLI stops waiting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone runs an automation with `--wait`. The Gateway accepts the run, but the CLI can lose its ID if the wait deadline expires during a history request. Without the ID, the caller cannot use the error to look up that specific run.

## User Impact

The wait error identifies the accepted run. The user can check its result on the same Gateway without starting the automation again. A timeout is not a claim that the automation succeeded or failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A history read shares the remaining wait budget. When that budget times out in transport, the CLI now uses the existing wait-timeout error instead of returning the generic Gateway timeout. Shorter RPC timeouts and other transport errors still propagate.

## Evidence

In the compiled CLI against an isolated Gateway, a disabled synthetic automation received one manual run with a 1 ms wait. Before the fix, the generic timeout omitted the ID even though history contained one receipt. With the fix, both the JSON error and human guidance included the same ID. Following the guidance returned that receipt with status `error`; no second run was started. The regression failed on the base and all 65 tests in the CLI suite passed with the fix. Applying the published patch to upstream `e85cda36996c` produces the exact Git tree used for these checks.

prs.title: fix: place Workboard cards where they are dropped immediately
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Dropping a Workboard card made it reappear in its old lane or position until the Gateway replied. On a slow connection, a completed drag looked as though it had missed its target.

## User Impact

The card appears where you dropped it and stays dimmed while the move is pending. When you move the focused card to another lane, focus follows it without scrolling. If the move is rejected, the board keeps confirmed changes and shows the error. No setup or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The board already knows the intended lane and order. It can show that placement without recording a successful write. The card and any peers that must make room stay reserved until settlement. Each receipt updates the confirmed card; a conflict supplies the current card, and a lost acknowledgment triggers a fresh read. This does not change Sessions boards, status-menu actions, or dashboard layout.

## Evidence

- Chromium exercised a native drag from Triage to Backlog, with the real Control UI and Workboard plugin and a synthetic Gateway holding the response. Main (`1f0332980951`) held the card in Triage; the change (`05cd7033f8c8`) showed it above the target in Backlog before the response. Both used the same 1280 × 760 viewport, fixtures, and reduced-motion setting. This tests response ordering, not production latency.
- The browser also opened the moved card, rejected a subsequent move, and refreshed from a canonical result that differed from the last confirmed location. Focus on a different card was not stolen during recovery.
- A real-view regression covers a dense drop in which a peer reposition succeeds and the dragged card conflicts. All 50 focused Workboard tests passed, along with the browser plugin typecheck, formatting and scoped lint (two existing reactivity warnings). No live Gateway or full CI run is claimed.
