prs.title: fix(browser): keep a blocked subframe request from failing the whole action
prs.body:
Closes #206202

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a browser action such as `browser evaluate` fails with `browser navigation blocked by policy` (or a DNS error) when the page itself loads an embedded frame that the navigation policy denies, an ad or tracker iframe pointing at a private address or at a host the local resolver answers `0.0.0.0` for. The frame is stopped, which is right, but the action's own result is thrown away even though the evaluated function finished and the main page never left its allowed origin. On a network with an ad-blocking resolver (Pi-hole, AdGuard) every page that embeds a sinkholed ad frame fails intermittently, depending on whether the frame loads while the action runs; the reporter lost two Amazon page reads in a ten-run measurement and the agent told the user the browser was "blocked by policy".

## User Impact

Guarded browser actions (`evaluate`, clicks, typing, hovers, waits) now return their result when a frame the page embeds is denied or unresolvable; that frame stays blocked and never reaches the private destination. A denied navigation of the page itself (the main frame), an authority revocation, and a caller's cancellation still fail the action exactly as before. No configuration change; the `allowedHostnames` workaround for sinkholed ad hosts is no longer needed for actions. Download waits (`browser download` and `wait --download`) keep stopping on any denied frame request, as before: the guard cannot tell which frame will deliver the attachment, and a download that never starts should fail at once with its cause rather than after its timeout; an unresolvable frame host still lets such a wait run to its timeout, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withPageNavigationRequestGuard` in the browser plugin intercepts every document request during an action, including iframes, and recorded any failed policy check as the action's error. The request already says whether it is the page's own navigation (`isTopLevel()`, computed by the navigation fence from the frame tree), and the page-open guard in the same file already uses it to let a denied subframe pass as an abort while only a main-frame denial blocks the page. The action guard now does the same: a subframe document whose policy check fails is cancelled with the same source-preserving CDP cancellation the main-frame path uses (so an already loaded frame keeps its current document instead of showing an error page), and is not recorded, reported as a policy denial, or handed to the interaction caller through `onPolicyCheckStarted`; the caller keeps failed checks to recover a main-frame denial during an abort, so a subframe check left there would have resurfaced the same error on cancellation. The guard still tells its caller about a denied subframe, as a new `subframe` policy event that does not fail the action: the explicit download wait (`waitForDownloadViaPlaywright`, from #146297) stops on it the way it stops on a main-frame denial, because Chrome never starts a transfer the policy denied, whether the attachment was requested by the page or by a frame it loaded; without that event the wait would run to its timeout. The interaction caller ignores the event. A check that failed because the caller cancelled, or because the navigation authority was revoked meanwhile, still fails the action: the policy check asserts that authority itself, so the guard hands it an assertion that tags a revocation where it is thrown and records the revocation instead of letting the frame pass; no second authority read is made. A cancellation Chromium never acknowledged (both CDP cancellations fail with a real protocol error) is recorded, so a frame request the guard could not stop never passes silently. The main-frame path (preserve the source document, notify, throw) is untouched. No new option, dependency or schema.

One deliberate behaviour change rides on this: the Browser panel operator-input burst (#197927) shares the guard and used to stop and report a policy denial when a keystroke sent an iframe to a blocked host. That was the same false positive the reporter hit, raised by a frame the operator never touched; the denied request is cancelled before it commits either way, so the burst now continues and only a committed subframe URL the policy rejects still stops it. The burst's Chromium test and `docs/tools/browser-control.md` say so. The page-open guard's handling of a non-policy subframe error while an authority check is configured is unchanged and out of scope.

## Evidence

### Tests

`extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-session.navigation-guard.owner-boundary.test.ts` (drives the real guard and fence over a fake CDP session): two new cases, a denied (`SsrFBlockedError`) and an unresolvable (`ENOTFOUND`) subframe document request during the action, expect the action's result back, one source-preserving `Fetch.failRequest` (`Aborted`), and no policy-check or policy-denied callback to the caller; two control cases, the same denial on the main frame still rejects the action with the denial, preserves the source document and notifies the caller, and a subframe check that fails while the navigation authority is revoked mid-check (the mocked check calls the authority assertion it was handed, as the real one does) still rejects the action with the revocation. The denied subframe case also expects the `subframe` policy event, and the unresolvable one expects no event. `pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts`: one new case in two modes, an explicit download wait and a click-triggered download whose guard reports a `subframe` denial reject with the denial instead of waiting for their timeout; the existing clicked-download policy case now expects the capture's abort signal on the result check, as the waited one already did. `pw-session.create-page.navigation-guard.test.ts`: the pending-fulfillment case uses two main-frame denials, since a denied subframe no longer takes part in the source-preservation report; its event observer reads the new event shape. The shared test harness types the mocked guard with the guard's own call shape.

Run in an isolated Linux container on `main` `6f255f9fbce` with only the test file changed: 2 failed, 3 passed (`promise rejected "Error: browser navigation blocked by poli…" instead of resolving`; `promise rejected "Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND ads.invalid …" instead of resolving`; both controls pass on main). With this change, this file plus the guard's neighbours (`pw-session.create-page.navigation-guard`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.navigation-guard`, `pw-session-navigation-fence`, `pw-tools-core.browser-ssrf-guard`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.policy-abort`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.operator`, `pw-tools-core.downloads`): all passed (counts in the bench record below); the create-page suite's existing denied-child-frame preservation cases are among them.

Real Chrome (Chrome 158 in the same container, this change): the browser plugin's live navigation-guard suites `pw-session-navigation-stale-interception`, `-authority`, `-cors` and `-between-actions`: 4 files, 25 passed; the Chromium operator-input suite: 4 passed. Two existing cases changed with the behaviour: the stale-interception "page cancels a paused denied child document" case now completes the action and checks the denied URL never joined the page's frames, and the operator-input "iframe navigates to a blocked address" case now expects both keys delivered and the frame still on its old document. Denial reporting for a main-frame request whose interception retired stays covered by the fence unit test and the CORS suite's denied-document case.

Bench record for this head (isolated Linux container, node runtime): the eleven unit files above plus `pw-tools-core.interactions.batch`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.set-input-files` and `pw-tools-core.last-file-chooser-arm-wins`: 11 files, 145 passed; the owner-boundary file on unpatched `main`: 2 failed (the subframe cases), 3 passed.

Test lines are net +167 against `main`: no existing unit case drives the real guard with a document request the page issues during an action; the one file that drives the real guard and fence held a single cancellation test, so the two subframe cases, the two controls and their shared page helper are new, as is the download case in its two modes; the two Chromium cases are rewrites of existing ones.

### Full-product proof

Proof gap: the full-product run (built Gateway and CLI with a real Chrome, on `main` and on this change) has not been done yet; it follows on this PR before it leaves draft. Planned: the reporter's steps (`openclaw browser open https://example.com/ --label t`, then `openclaw browser evaluate --target-id t --fn` injecting an iframe to a private address, to a sinkholed host and to an `.invalid` host) through the built Gateway and CLI with a real Chrome, on `main` and on this change; the live navigation-guard tests on a real browser. Not run yet.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone selects a new priority or assignee in a Workboard card, the picker closes but still shows the old value until the Gateway replies. Saving labels leaves the picker open for that same wait.

## User Impact

The card and its details show the selected value immediately. Saving labels closes the picker. A rejected edit shows the confirmed value and an error; reopening the label picker restores the submitted choices for retry. There is no migration or new setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

A preview belongs to the specific card version being edited. It does not change the saved card, its revision, or which actions the user can take. The server still decides what was saved. An older success or conflict cannot replace a newer card, and a property edit does not move the card behind a neighbor at the same position. Bulk operations, drag, archive, and full-form editing retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

On `1f0332980951`, Chromium selected **High** and sent the update, but the drawer still displayed **Normal** while the reply was held. On `e2662aa09a1c`, the same interaction displayed **High** in both the drawer and the board. The browser test also switched tabs during the save, rejected the request with a newer **Low** priority, retried against that revision, then exercised assignee rollback and label draft and keyboard-focus recovery. These are real Control UI controls with synthetic card data and explicitly deferred Gateway replies, not a live backend timing measurement.

All 45 focused owner and editor tests passed, including stale success and conflict receipts. The Workboard browser-source typecheck and formatting passed. Scoped lint found no errors and three existing Solid reactivity warnings. No full CI run or automated local review was performed.

Both frames show the same click after the update request was sent and before its reply. Chromium, 1120 × 760, light theme, reduced motion. The published head `bd4bbcbe5fba` has the same source tree as the tested commit.

Three test fixtures carry unused data: an unread lifecycle capture, setup metadata inputs and a returned root field, and a duplicate channel entry never selected by the config-write cases.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. All 78 affected cases and their assertions remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the unread capture and unused setup fixture fields while preserving directory and environment setup. Keep only the channel entry selected by the config-write resolution cases. The separate origin/target authorization fixture remains intact.

prs.title: fix: show chat reactions as soon as they are selected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you select a reaction in a connected chat, the picker closes but the message still shows its old reactions until the Gateway responds. Reopening the picker during that wait offers to add the same emoji again instead of removing it.

## User Impact

Your reaction appears or disappears on the message immediately. You can reopen the picker and change your mind before the request finishes. If the Gateway rejects your change, the chat shows its error and restores the confirmed reactions. There is no setting or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Connected clicks now use the same per-message, per-emoji pending state that already presents reactions during reconnect. The Gateway still owns saved reactions and channel delivery; the chat never saves an unconfirmed reaction to the transcript cache. A late request releases only its own pending change. If the chat has no identified profile to display, it still waits for the Gateway rather than guessing who reacted.

## Evidence

On main `1f03329809`, selecting 👍 on a message with a peer’s 👀 left only 👀 visible while `session.reactions.set` was held. At `f8e7dbe53c`, the same click showed both reactions with the request still held. This was the real Control UI in Chromium with synthetic chat data, a 760 × 620 viewport and reduced motion; no external channel was contacted. The matching screenshots are transcript crops, not measurements of production latency.

The browser flow also checked the reopened picker, rejected write and rollback, retry, and rapid remove/re-add with the older removal rejected. Four existing reaction browser scenarios and 23 reaction-owner/offline-metadata tests passed, as did the UI typecheck and touched-file lint and format checks. Full CI and an independent local review were not run.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: only Riley’s eyes reaction is visible after selecting thumbs-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/481c5aca-8270-4f5a-889d-764ab76fdfe7)

**After**

![After: eyes and thumbs-up are visible before the reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9406e4e1-1834-4f32-83f0-79be6ff2f68c)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The existing reaction is outlined; the selected thumbs-up is missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/272e711a-168f-4b69-ae5f-fdb1ecd91c33)

**After**

![The outlined message tab includes the selected thumbs-up, with a total of two reactions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8c15d5e-c8b8-4c38-8e0d-5485fc89dee6)

Credit: @vyctorbrzezowski requested the interaction audit and informed the intended behavior.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4db0c57e-a1a7-40ff-b300-b642f46b79e9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/56b7bc59-ab79-4272-85b7-b62ae2eb0172)

## Worked on by

prs.title: fix: preview the selected profile picture while it uploads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you choose a new profile picture, the Avatar row keeps showing your old picture while it says “Processing…”. You cannot tell whether you chose the intended image until the upload finishes.

## User Impact

The Avatar row shows the cropped picture as soon as it is ready to upload. The profile header and the identity other people see do not change until the Gateway confirms the save. If it refuses the upload, the row returns to the saved picture and explains the failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already has the validated image it is sending. It can preview those exact pixels without changing stored profile data, fetching the image again, or making other identity views accept local image URLs. The existing profile request lifetime also retires the preview on reconnect.

## Evidence

In the real Control UI, I chose a synthetic sunrise image while the test Gateway held the avatar upload reply. On the base revision the editor kept the previous silhouette; with this change the editor showed the sunrise while the header still showed the silhouette. I rejected the upload, saw the error and original picture, selected the file again, accepted that upload, and then edited the display name. This was a Chromium run at 1040 × 760, light theme, reduced motion, with synthetic profile data and a controlled Gateway reply, not a live account upload.

The focused profile test file passed all 24 tests, including reconnect during image processing or upload and late success and failure. The UI production typecheck, focused boundary lint and format checks passed. No broad CI or live account test was run. Comparison: `09b560001d5db` → `7dc6584fa5ef` (identical tree to the locally verified `41db5fc01bd50`).

### Clean comparison

**Before** — the previous picture remains in the Avatar row.

![Before: previous silhouette while the selected picture uploads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2ee0409-7b97-40b9-b8d8-e6a3d8cf3efc)

**After** — the editor shows the selected picture during the same pending request.

![After: selected sunrise while the upload is pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0abc7822-d97c-4737-866f-d18a4199f2f9)

### Annotated comparison

![Before: the previous picture in the pending Avatar row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f91cd70-09e3-4946-8614-29add0050201)

![After: the chosen picture in the pending Avatar row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76ea90a6-e1c2-44ad-8abe-d4f9fe7e06c0)

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4db0c57e-a1a7-40ff-b300-b642f46b79e9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/72ac9149-5276-4b14-bc32-740d2e91c38c)

prs.title: fix(setup): don't block a failed model setup's restore as a config size drop
prs.body:
Closes #202461
Related: #202459

## What Problem This Solves

When model setup has already saved its config and a later step fails, for example because the Gateway does not apply the change, setup tries to put the previous config back. If the config was small before setup and setup more than doubled it, OpenClaw's config write guard blocks that restore as a suspicious size drop, so setup fails without undoing its change.

## User Impact

User impact: when setup activation or the onboarding wizard fails after saving its config and the only reason its restore is blocked is `size-drop`, setup now restores the small config it started from instead of ending with "OpenClaw blocked this config update …". That message asks the user to correct the proposed update and retry, but the blocked update is setup's own restore, so there is nothing for the user to correct. The other write guards can still reject the restore, for example when setup had also added `gateway.mode` to a config that had none (see Not covered). From reading the code, before this change a credential that setup had already activated also stayed active: setup rolls it back only after the config restore succeeds (`src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts:159-163`); Not covered says what the tests and runs below show about that step. No new options, config, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup's restore is one conditional write built by the shared helper `captureSetupInferenceFileUndo`, and its write options never included `allowConfigSizeDrop`. The config write guard rejects a write as `size-drop` when the file is at least 512 bytes before the write and less than half that size after it, so restoring a small pre-setup config after setup added a provider and its model catalog trips the guard. The helper now sets `allowConfigSizeDrop: true` on that restore write. The setup activation and onboarding wizard restores both go through this helper, so the allowance is set once, where the restore write is built, rather than at each caller.

Setup reaches this restore when its config write succeeds and a later step fails. For example, a running Gateway does not apply the write (#183964 describes a hand-written first-run config with `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`), or, with default reload settings, defers it, as in the Gateway runs below. Credential activation can also report a false "connection changed" error after a plugin install, which #202459 addresses; the released CLI run below hit that error before its restore.

Boundaries of the allowance:

- It is hardcoded in the helper and applies only to the helper's conditional inverse write. That inverse is computed from this setup's own before and after configs, can only undo this setup's own changes, and refuses to write if any of those keys changed since. No caller sets the option, and a caller's own value is overridden. The other write guards still apply: `unreadable-config-before-write`, `gateway-mode-removed`, the pinned config path, and the check that newer settings have not superseded this setup. The accepted restore still records its `size-drop` reason in the config write audit. Merged #143147 hardcodes the same allowance, with a comment, for an avatar replacement that can shrink the config.
- #155427 made the message for this rejection path-free; it did not change whether setup's restore may shrink the config. This PR leaves that message as is.
- #81828 asked to let `skills.update` callers request `allowConfigSizeDrop`. This PR adds no such option: no RPC, CLI, or caller parameter can turn this allowance on or off. Draft #202108 sets the same allowance for the restore of its new first-agent step.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.ts`: in `captureSetupInferenceFileUndo`, the restore write's options gain `allowConfigSizeDrop: true` after `expectedConfigPath`, with a one-line comment. No new exports, parameters, or files.
- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts` and `src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`: one new case each (see Evidence).
- Against `cf95c48d9d`: `setup-inference-transition.ts` +2/−0, `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` +28/−0, `setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts` +27/−0.

</details>

## Evidence

Runs added for the review. They used synthetic API keys and loopback fake model servers only; paths, ports, and tokens are redacted.

- Behavior, on a Gateway built from source at `cf95c48d9d` (not the npm package): a failed activation whose restore drops the config below half. Before this change the guard blocked the restore (`size-drop:1106->535`); with this change the restore was written.
- Behavior, on the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` CLI: `openclaw onboard` reached the same restore, but that config was not small enough to cross the size-drop line, so the guard did not block it.
- Upgrade from the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` to a package of this change: doctor migrated the databases, and the existing settings and the stored credential still work.

The upgrade item has a complete run on the released package. The before/after behavior samples come from a source-built Gateway; no run on a published entry point crosses the size-drop line.

### Gateway run: before and after, with a restore below half

Each run started from a fresh, isolated state directory and HOME. The Gateway was built from source at `cf95c48d9d` (`pnpm build`), not the npm package, and listened on loopback with default config reload. The client was `openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate` with a synthetic OpenAI API key. The built-in OpenAI provider reached an OpenAI-compatible fake server at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1` through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` in the Gateway process environment; the config did not contain that address. OpenClaw applies config `env.vars` to the process environment and keeps a value already set there (`src/config/config-env-vars.ts:624`), so the provider sees the same variable either way. No fault was injected: with default reload, the Gateway deferred applying setup's write (both runs' Gateway logs show "config reload deferred", and the after run's reply says so), and setup then restored. The config before setup was the minimal Gateway config our harness writes: `gateway` settings and a log file path (327 bytes on disk in both runs). OpenClaw's config writer adds `meta` when it writes the restore, and the restore also keeps an empty top-level `agents` object (see below), so the restored file is larger than this start.

- Before (the build without this PR's change): the RPC failed with "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update …". The config write audit holds one rejected write whose only blocking reason is `size-drop:1106->535`, and the rejected payload (535 bytes) was saved next to the config as `openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-21T17-34-21-915Z`. The config on disk stayed setup's candidate (1106 bytes, the size of setup's write; it was still the same after a second setup attempt and a Gateway restart). Each of the two setup attempts sent one model request to the fake server.
- After (the same build plus this PR's production change): the RPC reported "The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in." No write was rejected and no `.rejected.*` file was saved: the audit records the restore as a `rename`, with `size-drop:1106->535` listed under `suspicious` and not as a blocking reason. Without `meta`, the restored config equals the config before setup except one added empty top-level `agents` object (`"agents": {}`), which the earlier runs also left. After a second setup attempt with another synthetic key and a Gateway restart, the config on disk was unchanged and the running config had the same top-level keys as the restored config; none of the keys only the candidate had (`auth`, `plugins`) were present. Each of the two setup attempts sent one model request to the fake server.
- Builds: both carry the local package version label `2026.11.7`, a `package.json` change only, not a published version. Apart from that label, the after build differs from the before build only by this PR's production change; its diff has the same SHA-256 (`66cfd15b…`, `git diff --binary --full-index`) as the production diff of `2ff2bd4ee53f`. In the built output, the restore write's options (`expectedConfigPath: …, allowConfigSizeDrop: true`) occur 0 times in the before build and once in each of the restore helper's two bundled copies in the after build.

```text
# before: cf95c48d9d source build without this PR's change; Gateway console log
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.models, agents.defaults.model, auth.profiles, plugins.entries.openai, meta)
[reload] config reload deferred: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during prepare: Plugin openai reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup; the previous plugin configuration remains active.
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.; retrying automatically after admitted work and cleanup settle
Config write rejected: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:1106->535). Rejected payload saved to <state>/openclaw.json.rejected.2026-11-21T17-34-21-915Z.
[gateway] request handler failed: Error: Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it p...
# before: client output of openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate --json
"message": "Error: Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update because it looked like it could overwrite or remove existing settings. Your current config was left unchanged. Correct the proposed update so it p...",
# after: the same build plus this PR's production change; Gateway console log
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.defaults.models, agents.defaults.model, auth.profiles, plugins.entries.openai, meta)
[reload] config reload deferred: PluginRuntimeApplicationError: Plugin operation failed during prepare: Plugin openai reload is waiting for retained work, calls, or previous-generation cleanup; the previous plugin configuration remains active.
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.; retrying automatically after admitted work and cleanup settle
Config write anomaly: <state>/openclaw.json (size-drop:1106->535)
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (meta)
[reload] config source revision 3 accepted (write)
[gateway] request handler failed: Error: The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in.
# after: client output of openclaw gateway call openclaw.setup.activate --json
"message": "Error: The Gateway did not complete activation (deferred). Resolve the reported problem, then retry the saved sign-in.",
```

<details>
<summary>Earlier Gateway runs that stayed above the line</summary>

Earlier Gateway runs from the same harness also wrote the fake server's address into the config's `env.vars`, and three of them, including a before/after pair, also wrote `gateway.reload.mode: "off"` (the #183964 shape). With those extra bytes, every restore stayed 27 to 49 bytes above half of the setup-written file: for example `1239 -> 668`, where half is 619, and `1196 -> 625` against 598 in the one run with default reload settings, where the Gateway deferred the activation. Those restores were written both before and after this change, so the change does not alter a restore that stays above the line.

</details>

### Released CLI onboard (`openclaw@2026.11.6`)

With the released npm package, `openclaw onboard` (manual setup, Groq, the Groq provider plugin installed from npm, a synthetic key against a loopback fixture) failed with the false "connection changed" error that #202459 addresses and then wrote its restore. Onboard's two earlier writes took the config from 1297 to 1492 bytes; setup's write took it to 2049 bytes, and the restore to 1508. Half of 2049 is 1024, so the guard did not block the restore.

<details>
<summary>Starting config of this run</summary>

That run's starting config also held a Groq provider block that we add to route Groq to the fixture, which made up most of its 1297 bytes. Without that block, and if the restore again removed the same 541 bytes (2049 − 1508), the restore would still stay above half (computed from this run's readings; not run).

</details>

### When the size-drop guard blocks the restore

The restore is blocked for this size-drop reason only when the config before setup is small compared with what setup adds: the setup-written file must be at least 512 bytes and the restored file less than half of it. The minimal Gateway config above is one such start; a config that already holds more than setup adds is not. How often real setups start from a config that small is not measured.

### Upgrade from `openclaw@2026.11.6` with existing settings and a stored credential

In an isolated HOME and state directory, the released `openclaw@2026.11.6` npm package ran `openclaw onboard --non-interactive` with the built-in OpenAI provider and a synthetic API key. Then `config set` wrote `skills`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` (900, not the default), and `logging.level`, and a file was placed in the workspace. Next, a package built from `cf95c48d9d` plus this PR's production change (the repository's packaging script, local version label `2026.11.7`) was installed over it, and `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran.

- Doctor exited 0 and printed neither its maintenance-deferred notice nor a migration refusal. It saved pre-migration SQLite backups and reported "Upgraded agent database schema … v38 -> v43". `config validate` passed before and after the upgrade.
- Stored credential: `openclaw infer model run --local` went through a loopback proxy that checks the API key against the stored synthetic key. Before the upgrade it succeeded with the stored key; a control request to the same proxy with a different synthetic key got HTTP 401; after the upgrade `infer` succeeded again with the stored key. A credential probe read the same result before and after: `readable`, `present`, `type: api_key`, key hash matching the synthetic key given to onboard, profile id `openai:api-key`.
- Settings: hashes of the `gateway` settings, `skills`, `logging`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, `agents.defaults.model`, and the auth profile list were the same before and after, and the workspace file was unchanged. The whole config without `meta` did change: doctor reported writing its own config migration records ("Updated config", with a backup).
- Environment: the CLI commands in this run set `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT` to a unit name that does not exist. The variable is the documented selector for this install's systemd service; pointing it at a missing unit is our test-isolation use, not a documented one. It keeps the CLI from taking another, older Gateway service installed on the host under another account for this install's service. Without it, doctor refused the forward database migration, naming that service's older version; from the code, doctor cannot rule out that service sharing this state, the conservative case that #190194 keeps. From the code, the variable only changes which systemd unit counts as this install's service; it does not skip migrations or backups. The same CLI environment also set `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external`, `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, and `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BONJOUR=1`.

### Focused tests

For the focused tests, "Before" results were taken on main `cf95c48d9d` with only the test changes applied. "After" results were taken on `cf95c48d9d` with this PR's change applied, the full diff of commit `2ff2bd4ee53f`.

Two new cases with no padding or invented config fields. Each asserts that the setup-written file is at least 512 bytes and that the restored file is less than half of it, so the case keeps exercising the size-drop guard if the fixtures change.

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, "restores a size-dropping first config write when its activation is not applied": the same flow as the existing case from #183964 (activation completion deferred, no reloader, so the Gateway never applies the write and setup restores), but the starting config is small and has no provider, and the sign-in adds the provider with its model catalog. It expects "The previous connection was restored on disk" and the restored config to equal the starting config apart from `meta`.
- `src/wizard/setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`, "wizard recovery restores a size-dropping provider write": the onboarding wizard's config target starts from `{ gateway: { mode: "local" } }`, writes a candidate that adds one provider with one model, and the activation is rejected ("promotion refused"). It expects that error to be rethrown and the restored config to have no `models`.
- Before: exactly these two cases fail; the other 48 cases in the two files pass. Both fail with "Activation failed and recovery could not complete. OpenClaw blocked this config update …", and the guard logs one rejection for each, with the size drop as the only reason: `size-drop:1674->438` for the activation case and `size-drop:811->235` for the wizard case.
- After: all 50 cases in the two files pass, and the run logs no config write rejection.

<details>
<summary>Mutation check, timing, consumers, targeted checks, local review</summary>

- Mutation check (not part of this PR): with only the production lines reverted on the final tree, both new cases fail again the same way.
- Time, per changed test file with this change (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `setup-inference-activate.test.ts`, 42 tests, 112.83 s Vitest duration (the new case: 2.38 s); `setup.inference-recovery.integration.test.ts`, 8 tests, 18.97 s (the new case: 1.04 s). The consumer run below took 73 s.
- Consumers pass: `src/system-agent/setup-inference-transition.test.ts`, `src/gateway/config-reload.activation.integration.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-setup-auto.test.ts`, and `src/wizard/setup.inference-verification.test.ts`, plus the changed wizard recovery file.
- Targeted checks: `oxfmt --check` and oxlint pass on the three changed files; the two tsgo typecheck commands selected by `pnpm check:changed --dry-run` pass; the test-lines ratchet reports `Net test lines: +55; allowance: 400`; `git diff --check` passes.
- Local review: autoreview on the full diff against `cf95c48d9d` reported scoped-clean: no accepted or actionable findings (overall: patch is correct, 0.94). pr-simplify on this diff suggested no changes.

</details>

Required [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44732444060) passed on commit `2ff2bd4ee53`. The dependency and sensitive-path checks also passed.

Not covered:

- Credential rollback after the restore: the focused tests activate no credential before the restore (no Gateway claims the write in the activation case, and the wizard case's activation fails at once). In the Gateway runs, there is no credential reading: the CLI's credential listing refuses to run while the Gateway is running ("This command is offline-only"), so the rollback is not shown there either. The rollback ordering described under User Impact is from reading the code.
- From the code, if setup added `gateway.mode` to a config that had none, the restore is still blocked by the `gateway-mode-removed` guard and setup reports the same message; this PR only allows the size drop.
- The Gateway's automatic Codex setup also calls this helper. This PR does not test that entry (its tests mock the helper) and does not claim it is fixed.
- The run that crosses the size-drop line uses a Gateway built from source, not the npm package; the released-package CLI run reached the restore without crossing the line.
- Model calls went to loopback fake servers with synthetic keys; no real provider account was used. This change is in the config restore after a failed activation, not in the model call.
- The tests and runs used Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64) with Node v24.22.1 only; the change is one write option with no platform-specific code.

prs.title: fix: show dashboard keyboard moves and menu sizing while saving
prs.body:
Related: #207112 (pointer drops; independent change).

## What Problem This Solves

On a session dashboard, pressing Alt+Arrow to move a widget or choosing a size from its menu leaves the old layout on screen until the Gateway replies. A successful keypress can look like a missed one, and the next arrow key navigates the old order.

## User Impact

The widget moves or resizes as soon as you give the command. Focus stays with a moved card, and plain arrows follow the displayed order. Auto height uses the mounted widget’s reported height; without a measurement, the card keeps its saved row span. A refused change returns to the confirmed layout and shows the existing error. No setting or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The board view previews only the changed layout entries. It does not publish a provisional board snapshot, replace the mounted document, or announce success before the write settles. A replacement snapshot takes precedence, even while a request is outstanding. Pointer drops, cross-tab transfers, removal, and permissions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- In Chromium, held the real dashboard’s outgoing board update after Alt+Left. On main, Sample inventory remained in the right column (x = 526 CSS px). With this change it moved to the left (x = 16) with focus intact. Rejection restored the right-hand position; an accepted retry kept the new order and ArrowRight focused its neighbor.
- The LG menu preset immediately occupied eight columns rather than six. A newer snapshot changed it to three while the request was pending; a later refusal did not undo the newer layout. A mounted HTML widget test exercised the Auto menu with no measurement, then a 300 px content report and refusal, retaining the same iframe.
- All three regression assertions failed against the unchanged base. On the PR head, 59 focused unit/browser tests and the keyboard/menu dashboard flow passed, as did UI type checking, scoped lint and formatting. The tree combined cleanly with #207112 at `68b3d2256075`, and the combined keyboard/menu flow and pointer regression tests passed. Neither PR needs to land first. No merge or deployment was requested.
- Screenshots use the real focused Control UI dashboard, synthetic report data and a held Gateway reply. Both frames show the same point after Alt+Left at 1040 × 600 CSS px, light theme and reduced motion. Before: `2777a471696e`. After: `01ad19ccf157`.

## What Problem This Solves

Renaming a project kept the editor locked while the Gateway saved. Even after the Gateway confirmed the new name, opening Rename again could show the old one until the project list refreshed.

## User Impact

The editor closes on submit. The details and table show the proposed name, and the Rename button says **Saving…** until the Gateway replies. You can close the details or inspect another project while it saves. A refusal restores the last known name, identifies the affected project, and leaves the attempted name ready to edit or retry the next time you open Rename. The project ID, repository, checkout, and filesystem path do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the display name is predictable. The Projects page previews that field without modifying the last confirmed list, then uses the returned name before refreshing its catalogs. A pending write does not reorder rows, move the selection, or admit another mutation. Empty and unchanged names remain blocked, and the existing dialog still handles IME input.

## Evidence

- Exercised the real Projects → Rename controls in Chromium with two synthetic registered projects. The mocked Gateway independently held the write and the subsequent list refresh; these are controlled states, not latency measurements. On main `1f0332980951`, a second Rename opened with `Field notes` even after `Team handbook` was accepted. On `16d029eec0b6`, the pending title and row showed `Team handbook`, focus returned to the saving control, and a second Rename opened with the accepted name during refresh.
- Rejected a subsequent rename, reopened the retained draft, checked unchanged-value validation, edited it, and retried successfully. No live Gateway or filesystem was modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix: Codex OAuth profile stays blocked until the weekly reset while purchased credits remain
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile stays blocked until the weekly usage window resets when the included usage is exhausted but the account has purchased credits, even though Codex keeps serving requests on those credits.

## User Impact

User impact: after buying Codex credits, `openai/gpt-*` turns work again on the next probe instead of failing (or silently falling back to another provider) for the rest of the week. Accounts with no credits, depleted workspace credits, or a reached overage cap keep today's block-until-reset behaviour. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage probe read only `rate_limit.limit_reached` and the window reset time and never looked at the `credits` object the same endpoint returns. Because an exhausted weekly window reports `used_percent: 100` until it resets, every half-open re-probe re-confirmed the block, so the profile could not recover before the reset even though requests succeeded.

Codex's own client treats remaining credits as "not limited" (its usage notice is suppressed when `credits.unlimited || credits.has_credits`, see [`usage_notice.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/usage_notice.rs)). The probe now applies that rule to the personal case only: an exhausted window returns `available` when `credits.has_credits` or `credits.unlimited` is set, `credits.overage_limit_reached` is not, and `rate_limit_reached_type` is the plain `rate_limit_reached` state (or absent, as in older payloads). Depleted workspace credits, admin-set workspace usage caps (`workspace_*_usage_limit_reached`), an `unknown` reached type, and a reached `spend_control` keep today's behaviour, because a credit balance does not prove those caps allow more spend.

`usage.ts` was already over its line cap, and the line-cap ratchet rejects growth, so the usage payload schema and its pure classification moved unchanged into a sibling module, `usage-wham.ts`. The request, HTTP-status handling, half-open re-probe, and store mutation stay in `usage.ts`; the new rule is the only behavioural change.

## Evidence

**Live observation** (2026-09-21, OpenClaw 2026.9.5, ChatGPT Pro account, native gateway):

- After a genuine "You've reached your Codex subscription usage limit" error on Sep 20, the profile carried `blockedUntil` = the Sep 25 reset with `blockedReason: "subscription_limit"`, `blockedSource: "wham"`.
- Credits were purchased afterwards. The usage endpoint then reported an exhausted window **and** credits, and direct requests to the Codex responses backend returned HTTP 200 for both `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`.
- OpenClaw kept logging `Provider openai is in cooldown (rate_limit)` and `Auth profile "openai:…" is temporarily unavailable for openai/gpt-5.6-luna` on every turn; each 5-minute re-probe only refreshed `lastProbeAt`. Clearing the stored block by hand restored service immediately, which isolates the probe classification as the cause.

<details>
<summary>Observed usage payload (ids redacted)</summary>

```json
{
  "plan_type": "pro",
  "rate_limit": {
    "allowed": false,
    "limit_reached": true,
    "primary_window": { "used_percent": 100, "limit_window_seconds": 604800, "reset_after_seconds": 363981, "reset_at": 1790322562 },
    "secondary_window": null
  },
  "credits": { "has_credits": true, "unlimited": false, "overage_limit_reached": false, "balance": "2269.83…" },
  "spend_control": { "reached": false },
  "rate_limit_reached_type": { "type": "rate_limit_reached", "details": "default" }
}
```

</details>

**Tests** (`pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-wham.test.ts`): 117 passed. The existing WHAM-aware cooldown suite (probe headers, reset mapping, half-open re-probe, stale-result guards) is untouched and still passes against the extracted classifier. New `usage-wham.test.ts` covers the classifier directly:

- exhausted window + purchased credits, + unlimited credits, and + credits with no reached type → `available` (15 s burst cooldown, no block);
- eight negative cases still block until the reset: no `credits` object, `has_credits: false`, `overage_limit_reached: true`, both `*_credits_depleted` states, both `*_usage_limit_reached` states, and `unknown`;
- a reached `spend_control` is not overridden by credits;
- baselines: non-exhausted window → available; exhausted window without credits → blocked until reset.

Before extraction, the same credit cases were run through `markAuthProfileFailure` and the half-open re-probe against the unmodified probe: both failed (`expected 1700363981000 to be undefined`) while the negative cases passed, so the rule is what the tests pin.

**Checks** (Linux, Node 26.9, pnpm 12.4): `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `pnpm check:changed` clean across all of its lanes, including the line-cap growth ratchet, the core-tests typecheck, and the dead-export scan (the scan caught one needlessly exported constant on the first pass; it is module-private now and the scan was re-run clean); `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; `markdownlint-cli2` clean on the three edited docs pages.

**Docs**: one sentence added to the three pages that describe the subscription-limit block (`docs/concepts/model-failover.md`, `docs/providers/openai/runtimes.md`, `docs/plugins/codex-harness/app-server.md`).

In Settings → MCP, turning a server on left its switch visibly off for as long as the Gateway took to save. The page could say “Saving…” while the switch looked as though the click had done nothing. Turning a server off had the same problem in reverse.

The selected switch now moves immediately and keeps keyboard focus. If the Gateway refuses the write, the switch returns to the saved position, the error remains visible, and the operator can retry. An on switch is not a connection or a grant of tool access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing save action knows which switch the operator changed. It previews only that row’s requested configuration while the write is pending. ## What Problem This Solves

After someone clicked **Archive** or **Restore** in Skill Workshop, returning to Learned skills still showed the skill in its old list until the Gateway finished both the write and the next inventory read. The counts did not change either.

## User Impact

The row and both counts move immediately. The row says **Archiving…** or **Restoring…** until confirmation. ## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(agents): let agents delete retire an unconfigured but registered agent
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Fixes #205927 (with #207212, which stopped maintenance from recreating the deleted directory).

An agent removed from `agents.entries` by hand, whose directory was then deleted as Doctor advised, keeps its row in the shared agent-database registry. `openclaw doctor` then prints `Skipped missing registered agent database …` on every run, and no supported command can clear it: `openclaw agents delete <id>` answered "not found" because the agent is not configured and has no deletion record.

Doctor deliberately does not drop a registration just because its file is missing (#203130: the startup upgrade copies state without databases over 64 MiB, so that rule deleted real registrations). The removal therefore belongs to explicit agent deletion.

## Change

- `openclaw agents delete <id>` and the Gateway `agents.delete` method accept an agent that is not in config but still has a registered database. They run the existing journaled deletion: paths that are already gone are skipped, the registrations are removed with the journal, and config is not written. Confirmation and `--force` behave as for any delete.
- If any of the agent's paths still exist, the confirmation lists them before anything moves to Trash.
- Doctor's `Skipped missing registered agent database` warning names `openclaw agents delete <id>` for unconfigured, non-reserved agents. A configured agent's missing database (the upgrade-shadow case) keeps the old text. The orphan-directory note names the same command instead of "remove stale dirs".
- An id with no config entry, deletion record or registration is still "not found". Nothing happens automatically: no config edit, Doctor run or maintenance cycle removes a registration.

## Update behavior

Doctor wording only; no migration, schema, stored row or update-path change.

## User population

Gateway and CLI installs that retired an agent by removing it from config and deleting its directory. Two reporters on #205927.

## Evidence

- `src/commands/agents.delete.test.ts` "retires an unconfigured agent that is still registered":
  - files gone: Doctor's state migration reports the missing store on two runs, `agents delete retired --force` exits 0, the registration is gone, the deletion journal is complete, then two Doctor runs are silent. Red on main `fe1e8208` (no command pointer; delete answers "not found").
  - directory remains: the confirmation lists the existing agent directory; cancelling changes nothing; confirming moves it to Trash and removes the registration. Red on main (no prompt is reached: "not found").
  - unknown id with no config entry, record or registration: still "not found".
- Guards green: `state-upgrade.large-agent-db.test.ts` (#203130: a database omitted from the upgrade copy keeps its registration), `state-migrations.media-persistence-targets.test.ts`, `agent-deletion-journal-initialization.test.ts`, `doctor-state-integrity.test.ts`, and the Gateway `agents-delete` integration, upgrade and drain suites.
- Real Gateway, isolated (own port, empty HOME and state, `env -i`). Configure `main` and `retired`, start and stop the Gateway, remove `retired` from config and delete its directory, start the Gateway, then run the CLI against it:

  ```text
  main fe1e8208
    doctor: Skipped missing registered agent database <state>/agents/retired/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.
    openclaw agents delete retired --force -> exit 1: Agent "retired" not found. Run openclaw agents list to see configured agents.
    doctor x2 afterwards: warning on every run; registry rows: main,retired
  this PR 53a60cd2
    doctor: Skipped missing registered agent database <state>/agents/retired/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite. If agent "retired" is retired, run openclaw agents delete retired to remove its registration.
    openclaw agents delete retired --force -> exit 0: Deleted agent: retired   (Gateway log: agents.delete ✓)
    doctor x2 afterwards, same Gateway still running, no restart: no warning; registry rows: main
  upgrade: state created by v2026.11.10 (latest stable), then this PR: same result as above
  ```

## Accepted edge cases

- A completed keep-files deletion whose files remain can be deleted again, this time with its files (moved to Trash; the confirmation lists them).
- `agents delete` does not refuse a store Doctor holds back after a lost deletion journal; Doctor still prints its restore-first guidance.
- If the registration points at a database on an unmounted volume, the confirmation says none of the agent's files were found on disk; deletion removes only the registration.

Final head `1c7963b9` (`53a60cd2` with `main` merged in, to pick up the protocol-allowlist fix from #207259). On that build, the same isolated-Gateway run again: Doctor warns before the delete; `agents delete retired --force` runs through the running Gateway; `doctor` and `status` are then silent on two runs each, without a restart; the registry holds `main` only; the directory stays absent. Local review on `1c7963b9`: patch is correct, 0 findings.

prs.title: fix: restore scheduled account access on CLI backends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled task on a CLI backend can stop before producing output with `Scheduled account ... is unavailable: missing recorded creator channel`, even when its named account still exists. Reauthorizing or resuming the task does not repair that account lookup.

## User-Facing Impact

Local scheduled creators can resolve their existing account through the channel already carried by the run. Missing accounts still fail closed, explicit providers retain precedence, and the recorded tool cap is unchanged.

## Why This Approach

Use the existing channel only in shared scheduled-account policy resolution. Keep the run's provider untouched so an announcement sent to another channel does not change where timeout events are routed. External and unknown creator origins retain their existing authorization rules. CLI reply-authority snapshots already carry the same channel into this resolver.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing-channel failure with a real configured-account lookup through CLI preparation.
- A cross-channel regression failed against the first implementation; the final policy-only change preserves the source event route. The fixture uses distinct account rosters to prove both boundaries.
- All 48 original focused tests passed. On the refreshed candidate, the full runtime build and all nine scheduled CLI / Gateway hot-reload tests passed. Core and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting, and the line-cap check passed for the unchanged product diff.
- Initial CI failed an existing Gateway shutdown race. Native baseline refresh includes the already-landed fixes in [#206527](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206527) and [#206930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206930), preserving the exact two-file product delta. Fresh [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46093285813) passed on `ed39c299c87ad8d68943afd22fe6d735fab4f2f0`.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper review found the production fix correct. Applied and retested the non-blocking account-roster suggestion; the refreshed candidate's signature, parents, and unchanged product delta were independently verified.
- The earlier original-base `check:changed` run hit an unchanged release-owned `CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md` bot-attribution error; that unrelated file is untouched.
- Live scheduled-task verification remains blocked by deployment: the native updater refuses the installation’s preserved source checkout as dirty. The running release remains unchanged; no post-fix scheduled task was run.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve preparation lock ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A slow update can lose its preparation lock while its process is still alive. A competitor can start and mark that update interrupted; late preparation or Gateway cleanup can then delete a successor's lock. The early-release recovery runner also needs to retain ownership while its finishing child runs.

## User Impact

Live preparers retain custody until release or exit. Competitors receive the existing update-running refusal. Recovery finishing records its outcome without deleting its parent's lock, and stale cleanup preserves a successor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the pinned fs-safe provider at the existing lock path and retain the acquired release capability through cleanup. Recovery keeps that capability in its parent until joined finishing and failure recording settle. Only ordinary facts cross into the finishing child.

Remove the separate hard-link/reclaim loop, unconditional prefix deletion, PID-based child release, caller-supplied PID, and obsolete previous-lock result. The provider records the reclaimed run under its guard so recovery can still settle an interrupted predecessor.

Production +122/-82 (net +40), for acquisition-bound release and the restored recovery lifecycle; tests +432/-46 (net +386). No dependency, config, schema, protocol, or public SDK change.

Release-note context: slow or concurrent updates cannot evict a live preparer or erase a successor during cleanup.

## Evidence

- Signed source `6950ad9d510ad33ce63806f4bd36f00120eeec24`, frozen base `fd1942854a6b4f363d7e89222a93cea2253f5562`; ten files.
- Relevant owner/sibling coverage now passes across focused runs: 8 store, 73 recovery, 28 Gateway-trial, 16 public Gateway RPC, 46 preparation and 10 preparation-failure cases (181 distinct cases). The first batch had three 120-second timeouts and a subsequent database-admission failure while the host slept; recorded 395/940-second suspensions match the inflated failure durations. Both affected files then passed all 56 cases awake with unchanged timeouts and source.
- Production types and the services, other-core and Gateway-server test type projects passed. Targeted lint reported zero errors/warnings; formatting checked oxfmt/Bun parity. Tracked source stayed unchanged.
- Final `pnpm build` passed at this exact signed head (5m13.5s), including declaration emission, CLI bootstrap guards and local plugin builds. Build metadata records the same source commit. Normal ready-PR CI and the current-head hosted review remain pending. Proof uses the task-owned native review checkout with its own frozen dependency installation after selected Testbox capacity was unavailable; the source worktree remains code-only.
- The earlier normal [343cc4c merge run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46101549551) exposed the newly merged recovery caller: two type jobs referenced removed lock APIs, and its held-run finishing test left the lock behind. This was a PR integration defect, not an inherited CI failure. The new adapter and seven regressions address that owner boundary.
- New coverage retains custody through gated finishing, build failure and delayed error recording; preserves another owner during unheld outcome recording; settles the reclaimed predecessor; and releases custody if predecessor recording fails. Existing store, preparation, Gateway settlement and public RPC regressions remain.
- Independent source review found no P0-P3 findings. Formal P0-P3 review's only finding was an INDEX-only incomplete migration; staging all five reviewed adapter files resolved it. The recovery integration commit matches the reviewed combined candidate; the final head adds the compiler-verified closure-initialization fix. The formal report was not marked scoped-clean; no additional source defect was established.
- The acting maintainer and independent reviewers inspected fs-safe 0.28.2. The formal review also received its complete acquisition/reclaim/release source and types. Formatting, whitespace, syntax and privacy checks passed; the later closure-initialization type fix is compiler-verified without casts.
- Historical Testbox proof reproduced both original lock failures against baseline production and passed the earlier candidate's owner tests and build. Those results do not certify this revised head. No installed-upgrade or operator Gateway execution is claimed.

## Stored-data Compatibility

The lock retains `runId`, `pid`, `startedAt`, and `deadlineMs` with the same meanings. The provider's ownership token is JSON-compatible whitespace. Reclaimed-run and release facts exist only in memory; no new field is persisted. The JSON reader, trial/history stores, finishing arguments, and launcher contract remain unchanged. No migration is introduced.

## Named Follow-ups

- **Early-recovery abrupt-parent-death settlement:** existing commands are detached. Actual macOS orphan survival is UNKNOWN; Linux cleanup is asynchronous. This patch proves normal joined lifetime, not crash/orphan settlement.
- **Early-recovery run-row finalization after acquisition failure:** source inspection shows run creation precedes acquisition. Terminal-row handling for acquisition/bookkeeping errors remains a separate audit; no runtime verdict is claimed.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207040, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207085, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207062.

prs.title: fix: keep saved system-event automations running after an upgrade
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After upgrading from `2026.9.37` or `2026.10.34`, a saved main-session system event could stop with “Automation has no recorded inference account” even though the agent had a working account. When no model was configured at all, the job instead said “Session event was not admitted,” which suggested retrying a job that could not run.

## User Impact

The updater’s Doctor now records the eligible stored account for the main session’s model. New system events use the same selection. A configured API key still works without a stored account. If no model is configured, the job stays failed and tells the operator what to configure. No new setting or job recreation is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

System events run in the main session, but job creation and Doctor skipped them when recording inference accounts. The fix uses the main session’s model rather than a subagent default and passes the actual preparation error back to run history. It does not weaken the account check or count queue acceptance as success. Related: #202699 (broader inference-selection policy).

## Evidence

I used each released CLI to create and run a saved job, upgraded with that release’s own updater, verified the installed commit `90a9b366c43a7258f158ba21edf321ad7e832d5f`, and checked terminal history for the same job ID. Request counts are HTTP requests carrying the saved event to a loopback model on AWS CrabBox.

| Configuration | From 2026.9.37 | From 2026.10.34 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stored account | Passed, 1 request | Passed, 1 request |
| Configured key, no stored account | Passed, 1 request | Passed, 1 request |
| No model configured | Failed: “No model is configured”, 0 requests | Failed: “No model is configured”, 0 requests |

**Red on main, green on the fix:** `adopts the main session's account for a saved system event, not the subagent model` failed on `9a63b7f1ccfaa` because Doctor left `inferenceBinding` absent. It passed on the fix. The earlier end-to-end control on unmodified `563eef9` reproduced the stored-account and no-model errors from both releases. The key-only row is a positive control, not a claimed regression.

Production typecheck and touched-source lint passed. Six CLI diagnostic tests initially failed and passed on a targeted rerun. The 9.37 key-only updater initially failed during Doctor in the parallel matrix and passed on an isolated fresh replay. I did not test an external inference provider or managed-service restart. The CrabBox lease was released.

Co-authored with @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-system-event-jobs-fail-after-upgrade-s1a499a54)

prs.title: fix: keep inline Canvas cards usable after their sandbox reloads
prs.body:
Closes #205427

## What Problem This Solves

An inline Canvas card in an open chat can go blank if its sandbox iframe reloads. The message stays visible, but the card's controls disappear.

## User Impact

The card renders again and accepts input without a chat refresh or a new message. This restores the authorized document, not unsaved text in its previous browser document. No new permissions, Dashboard changes, or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the message subscription tied to the retained frame's current window. After validating a new readiness notification, the inline host retires the previous render and private port, cancels any inspection using that port, and replays the document already authorized for the card. Inspection waits for the new port to become ready.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on official main at 645643d0fa458b3201e6345aebd57c0c722303bf: the authenticated Chromium session could fill the persisted card's textbox before reloading the outer frame. After reload, the textbox was absent for the 10-second assertion window.
- On the candidate, the same isolated Gateway and Chromium test passed: the outer element was retained, the restored textbox accepted new input, the inner document still could not read the top document, and the browser issued only one Canvas document read. Three unrelated scenarios were filtered out.
- 56 focused tests passed across routing, mounting, layout, inspection, and widget ownership. The UI build, production UI and focused test typechecks, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. The build's advisory report flagged the same CSS and chat boot thresholds on the equivalent QA baseline and candidate.
- Local autoreview of the staged candidate against the base above: no P0 findings. See [current GitHub checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205428/checks) and the hosted ClawSweeper review on this PR; the local review is not a Diamond rating.
- Pit manually tested Gabriel's earlier candidate in the Mac app. This is not automated WebKit evidence for the upstream port.

### Chromium / isolated Gateway: terminal evidence

The local regression run used an authenticated chat with a persisted synthetic card. These are excerpts of the captured Vitest output, not GitHub Actions output. [Read the exact assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/205d3d95208cf2da0727c6f49b927c895dbf1170/ui/src/e2e/chat-widget-sandbox.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts#L265-L297): they type before reload, reload only the outer frame, check its identity and type again, then check document isolation and the single Canvas read.

**Before — upstream `645643d0`**, with the regression test applied but no production fix:

```text
TimeoutError: inputValue: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.
  - waiting for locator('openclaw-canvas-widget-view .chat-tool-card__preview-frame').first().contentFrame().locator('iframe').contentFrame().getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Local note' })
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 3 skipped (4)
```

**After — same base, with the six-file patch published in `205d3d95`:**

```text
✓ reads persisted Canvas bytes through an authenticated browser connection 4662ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 3 skipped (4)
```

The other three cases were excluded by the test-name filter. This records Chromium on Linux, not WebKit on macOS.

Credit: Gabriel validated the original fix; Vítor Cepeda Lopes supplied the handoff and tested it in the Mac app.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/770f19d8-b23c-4317-9f5b-d8b9030fa3d9)

prs.title: fix(agents): run sessions_spawn children in one-shot agent --local
prs.body:
## Problem

In a one-shot `openclaw agent --local` run, `sessions_spawn` never works, on any runtime. The tool returns `{"status":"error","error":"published reply runtime missing for main"}`, so a user who asks for a subagent gets a blocker.

There are three causes, one after another:

1. **Admission.** Agent-turn admission reads its dispatch facts only from the Gateway's configured publication (`loadPublishedGatewayReplyDispatchRuntime`). That publication does not exist outside a Gateway, so the loader returns nothing and admission throws (`agent-run-admission-phase.ts`).
2. **Lifecycle reads.** The child's completion wait (`agent.wait`) went to the websocket Gateway client, because `bindGatewayLifecycleRequest` treated local contexts as unhosted. It failed with "requires credentials".
3. **Lifetime.** Subagent completion and the announcement back to the parent run as detached root work. The one-shot process closed its databases as soon as the parent turn returned. Completion then failed with `Database maintenance resource admission is closed`.

## Solution

One owner per step; no second implementation.

- **Dispatch facts.** The request context supplies them (`loadReplyDispatchRuntime`). A Gateway keeps its configured publication. The local context loads the target agent's run generation under the same lease contract, through one shared projection (`projectReplyDispatchRuntime`).
- **Lifecycle reads.** The local context uses the Gateway's own `createGatewayInstanceRuntime` with the shared method registry. `agent.wait`, `chat.history` and agent turns therefore run in-process through the same server-method owner. The runtime and registry load on the first turn or lifecycle read, so a one-shot run that never dispatches another turn loads no extra modules. The hand-written local facade and its `internal-facade.runtime.ts` barrel are deleted.
- **Global registration.** The process-global lifecycle registration moved from the runtime factory to the Gateway kernel. An embedded host never replaces a live Gateway's registration; `gateway.boot` runs a local command inside the Gateway process. Test fixtures that stand in for a listening Gateway register the same way.
- **Lifetime.**
  - Local agent turns are admitted as root work.
  - Both one-shot database owners wait for root work to go idle before they close the databases (`waitForLocalBackgroundWork` → `waitForGatewayRootWorkIdle`): `runWithLocalStateOwner`, and `agent exec`'s temporary state before its cleanup. The wait is event-driven: release notifications, no timer.
  - Long-lived subscriptions never count, using the existing `isActiveRootWork` rule. Every root-work kind a one-shot can reach is finite.
  - While it waits, the CLI prints `Waiting for N background tasks to finish. Press Ctrl-C to stop.` Ctrl-C stops the wait.

- **Hosting Gateway.** If a Gateway already hosts the process (BOOT.md runs a local command inside it), the local context defers to it: the Gateway's publication, execution tracking and lifecycle runtime. Only a true one-shot process supplies its own.

## User impact

- One-shot `agent --local` users on the embedded and Codex runtimes: `sessions_spawn` now runs the child, and the parent gets a continuation turn with the child's result.
- One-shot commands that start no detached work exit as before, with no wait.
- Gateway users: dispatch facts, execution tracking and the global lifecycle registration are unchanged. For BOOT.md turns, lifecycle reads (`agent.wait`) now use the hosting Gateway's runtime in-process instead of a websocket call back to the same Gateway.
- Other one-shot commands can also be interrupted while they wait: `templates add` through the CLI signal gate, `agent exec --state-dir` through its own signal bridge.

## Accepted edge cases

- **Failure retries on timers.** If a subagent completion fails and retries on a timer (`subagent-registry-run-wait.ts:126-145`, `subagent-registry-completion-runtime.ts:212-224`), no root is held during the delay, so the one-shot process can close before the retry runs. The run stays persisted as pending, and registry recovery delivers it on the next Gateway start (`initSubagentRegistry`, `server-startup-bootstrap.ts`); a later `--local` run does not restore it. The normal path has no gap: the child's lifecycle-end handler takes its root before the child turn's root releases.
- **Results after the first turn.** In `--json` mode the first turn's result prints before the wait. The continuation turn's reply goes to the session transcript; the terminal shows only the waiting line. A parent that waits in-turn (`agents_wait`) returns the child's result in its own reply.
- **No end-to-end `agent exec` spawn test.** The isolated process fixture cannot run `agent exec` on the base or here (auth-owner and model-resolution setup), so exec's wait is covered by the shared wait's unit tests only.
- **Ctrl-C** stops the wait, not the children. The databases then close under any child that is still running. That is the behavior main has today for any detached work.

## Evidence

- New process test `src/cli/agent-local-subagent-spawn.process.test.ts`: real CLI child, fake Responses server. The parent spawns through `dispatch_action` → `sessions_spawn`, the child replies, and a parent continuation turn sees the child's result.
  - Red on main: `published reply runtime missing for main`.
  - Green here.
- `gateway-work-admission.idle.test.ts`:
  - no work, or only a subscription, returns at once;
  - detached work is waited for and reported once;
  - an interrupt stops the wait.
- `local-request-context.test.ts`: a one-shot context supplies its own dispatch facts and lifecycle runtime; inside a hosting Gateway it supplies neither and uses the Gateway's.
- Consumer tests of every changed module pass. Two `subagent-spawn.production-boundary` cases also fail on the merge base under load: in isolated runs, "timed-out collector child" failed base 3/3 and head 1/3, and "consumed-session Stop authority" failed base 1/3 and head 0/3.
- `--local` cold start, 20 interleaved base/head pairs on a fake Responses server: median time to first model request 15.5 s on the base, 14.4 s here. Both sides show the same slow outliers from host load (30-42 s). Modules loaded before the first request: 6,371 on both (+2.9 KB).
- Gateway bench (fake provider, both routes): 48/48 turns pass on each side. Median later-turn time: Codex route 1,625 -> 1,443 ms, embedded 1,079 -> 1,112 ms. In an interleaved run, first-turn times moved in opposite directions on the two routes, with the same spread on both sides. On the Gateway path this change only moves where the lifecycle runtime is registered.
- Behavior suite (gpt-5.4-mini, 3 trials, embedded and Codex routes), `subagent-spawn`: base 0/6 real delegations (`published reply runtime missing for main`, or no tool found); head 4/6 return the child's answer, 1 delegated and still pending at the end of the turn, 1 (embedded) did not find `sessions_spawn` through `tool_search`. Other cases: no new failures.
