prs.title: feat: links to a setting open and highlight its row in Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw tells someone to change a setting, for example after a reply fails because no fallback model is set up, it can only name the Settings page. The person lands at the top of the page and has to hunt for the row. Many rows, including browser-only preferences and rows that plugins draw, had no stable name a link could use, so nothing could point at them reliably.

## User Impact

- A link such as `/settings/infrastructure#gateway.publicOrigin` opens the page, unfolds the group that hides the row, scrolls it to the middle of the screen and marks it with an accent edge bar and a short wash. Focus moves to the row, never into its control, and nothing is changed. The bar stays until the person clicks or types; with reduced motion the page jumps and the mark stays still.
- Every row on every Settings page now has one stable setting ID: config rows use their config path (`gateway.publicOrigin`, `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`), one agent's rows use `agent.<path>`, browser-only preferences use `local.<key>`, native app settings `device.<key>`, profile rows `profile.<field>`, and other rows `<page>.<name>`. Rows that repeat per item use one pattern plus the item, such as `providers.openai`.
- Plugin Settings views declare the IDs they draw in `controlUi.settingsViews[].settings` (`plugin.<id>.*`, `channels.<owned channel>.*` or `plugins.entries.<id>.*`). The host refuses a row ID the view did not declare. A channel detail opens from `/settings/channels?channel=<id>`, so `/settings/channels?channel=whatsapp#plugin.whatsapp.linkedPhone` lands on the WhatsApp plugin's linked phone. Plugins published before this change keep loading; their views simply have no linkable rows until they declare IDs.
- The Channels page row that opens a channel is now `channelsPage.channel.<id>`; `channels.<id>` stays the channel's config path.

## Why This Change Was Made

One list owns the IDs: `src/shared/control-ui-settings/` maps each hand-built page to the settings it shows, with the disclosure that hides a row and the config section that holds it. Generic config rows need no entry; their config path is their ID. One arrival owner in the Settings shell resolves the link (including renamed IDs and the nearest enclosing setting), waits for rows that render after Gateway reads, and keeps the mark on a row the page redraws.

The arrival and the setting list load with Settings, and the mark is drawn inline on the row, so the chat and new-session boot bundles and the shared stylesheets stay at their current size.

`pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` keeps it deterministic in lint, `check:changed` and CI: every row on a Settings page must carry a listed ID or be marked as a status/action row, every listed ID must be drawn exactly once, bundled plugins may draw only the IDs their manifests declare, and `config/control-ui-setting-ids.txt` keeps published IDs: removing one needs an alias so old links still land.

Two nearby fixes came out of checking every row: a config setting with several object shapes (such as `channels.twitch` or a secret provider) was drawn in both the common and advanced groups of the Advanced page; it is now drawn once. Rows in a channel detail sit flush with the dialog edge, so their mark reaches past the text there.

Accepted edge cases: a row the page redraws within 10 seconds of arrival gets the mark again, unless the person has clicked or typed. Rows that only exist with live data (native app, push notifications, cloud workers) are checked statically, not opened in the browser suite.

## Evidence

- Captured with the real Control UI against a mocked Gateway in Chromium at 1280×800, dark theme. Before: `main` at 3f4e2bd3a4c6e. After: the pre-rebase implementation with the channel-detail spacing change (368b856b26386).
- All **10 Chromium Settings deep-link tests** passed on the final integrated source against the mocked Gateway. Coverage includes generated and hand-built pages, model and plugin rows, the theme importer, MCP server switches, per-agent tool access and command allowlists, and provider account priority.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance` against a local build of c635b051de14e: chat boot JS 1336655 → 1336663 B gzip with the same 21 requests, new boot JS 820731 → 820739 B, total CSS unchanged (346225 B gzip, 1783458 B raw).
- `pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` OK; `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck all, SAFETY, SQLite, plugin boundaries, Plugin SDK surface and the other gates pass. Lint fails only on `max-lines` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-session.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts`, `src/wizard/setup.ts` and `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, and the dead-export scan only on `src/state/state-upgrade-tree.ts: skipEntry`; this PR does not touch those files and they fail the same way on `main`.
- Unit and node suites for touched owners pass (UI lib, components, config and search pages: 9901 passed; `memory-page.browser.test.ts` "keeps the header and every tab panel on one column" also fails on `main`, and `talk-device-navigation.test.tsx` timed out only in the full parallel run and passes alone).
- Test-line check passed against 6c1efeaf6b3ec: +1,049 net lines, 400 allowed and 649 allocated for the ID checker, browser flows (including delayed custom editors), arrival lifecycle and plugin manifest checks.

prs.title: fix: show the permission fix when backup has no safe temp directory
prs.body:
Closes #207042

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw backup create --verify` cannot find a safe temporary directory, it tells the operator to wait for another state operation. Waiting does not change directory permissions.

## User Impact

Terminal and JSON errors now identify the unsafe directory and give the applicable `chmod` command without telling the operator to retry. Backup still refuses to create an archive without a safe temporary directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The discovery wrapper added retry advice to every failure. Removing that sentence preserves the underlying error's own remedy, including wait instructions for real maintenance. No retry logic, permission checks, or archive formats change.

## Evidence

I ran the CLI on AWS Linux with initialized SQLite state and both temporary-directory candidates under a disposable home. The published head `138e394` has the same source tree I tested.

| Test home | Main `ddf0e26` | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0775`, terminal and JSON | Both exited 1 and advised retrying after the current state operation. | Both exited 1, reported that no safe temporary directory was available, and gave the `chmod go-w` remedy. No retry advice or archive. |
| Changed only to `0700` | Exit 0, `verified: true`. | Exit 0, `verified: true`. |

The regression assertion failed before the fix and passed after it. All seven selected backup and admission tests passed, as did formatting. A separate deep-directory control failed archive verification on both the unpatched base and the PR. I removed the test data and released the AWS machine. I did not run the full suite; local automated review produced no report.

In the [failed PR CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46085623063/job/140794903027), all five cases in the affected Bun shard passed before worker cleanup failed. The shared-state read-capacity suite reported `Worker resource cleanup closed without a receipt`. I compared its failure annotation with an [earlier scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46076577020/job/140765956302): the suite, error and stack matched exactly.

Reported by @daniel-lxs.

prs.title: fix(cron): post job notices directly; keep the turn as hidden repair input
prs.body:
## Problem

#207186 fixed the case where a cron job notice (auto-disabled, or a fallback failure alert) was lost because the owner conversation's model could not run. The notice still reached chat only as a model turn's input, and was posted directly only after that turn failed before start. A turn cancelled before start (supersession, restart) still lost it. The notice also never reached the conversation's channel as written; there the user saw only the agent's reply about it.

## Fix

`src/gateway/server-cron-targets.ts` posts every job notice directly through the session notice writer (`postSessionNotice`), without a model turn. The post needs no requester: it is fixed runtime text sent to the job owner conversation. It writes one chat row and a durable send to the conversation's channel, unless the notice is private or the conversation denies automatic sends (`session.sendPolicy`).

The notice's turn stays as the agent's repair turn (#188105), with its input hidden from chat (`cron_failure_repair` provenance, the same authority path as `cron`). Its error payloads are suppressed, as for repair turns, because the user already has the notice. When there is no session to post into yet, the turn keeps its visible input, so the notice still shows exactly once. The posted row is not replayed to the model, so when the repair turn fails for good before it starts (the owner conversation's model cannot run), the text is queued as context for the next turn, as #207186 did. The #207186 settle-time fallback is removed.

## What users see

- Chat: the fixed notice as a system notice row, then the agent's reply when the model works. Before, it was shown as a user-role row.
- Channels: the fixed notice, then the agent's reply. Before, only the reply.
- A dead model: the notice still shows once.
- Session notices (plugin notices too) now honor `session.sendPolicy`: a conversation that denies automatic sends keeps the notice in its transcript only. Before, `postSessionNotice` sent to the channel regardless.

## Accepted edge cases

- Owner guidance typed into a notice's repair turn does not join it as owner continuation. Repair turns already work this way.

## Evidence

- `server-cron-notice-delivery.test.ts`: owner model with no usable account. Chat shows the notice exactly once, as the posted assistant row. The next turn gets the notice as context.
- `server-cron-failure-repair.final-effect.test.ts`, auto-disabled case with a working model: the repair still applies and chat shows the notice exactly once, as the posted row, not the turn input.
- `runtime-session-notice.e2e.test.ts`: a conversation with `sendPolicy: deny` gets the transcript row and no channel send.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles. The send policy is loaded lazily on the delivery path, because its owner reaches the channel plugin registry, which loads the notice writer.
- Not covered by a test: the private branch (`deliver: false`, one expression) and the channel send itself.
- Cron failure-alert, delivery-outcome, startup-notification and Gateway notification suites pass.

prs.title: feat(ios): Talk lives in the composer card, with mute, camera, End and a language choice
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. On iPhone, turning on Talk (the live voice conversation) used to stack a separate "Listening" strip with its own mute button above the composer, while the composer underneath kept the text field, the **+** button, a tinted camera disc and a waveform button. The state was said in two places, the composer grew taller, and there was no way to choose the language Talk listens in.

## User Impact

With this change alone, on iPhone:

- Talk now lives inside the composer card. While Talk is on, the card shows one row: a microphone button (Mute), a live level mark, one status phrase (Connecting…, Listening, Muted, Waiting for a reply, Speaking, or a short problem such as No mic access or Offline), the camera switch, and a red End button with a close mark. The card keeps its resting height, and there is no separate strip above it.
- The End button ends Talk in every state, including while the agent is thinking, instead of turning into an inert Stop.
- Mute reads as a selected button and leaves Talk on. When microphone or speech access is missing, the row offers a Settings button.
- If Talk starts while a draft is typed, the keyboard goes away and the draft is held under the Talk row.
- Settings › Voice & Talk gains a **Language** row. It opens a list with Automatic first, then the phone's own languages, then every other language speech recognition supports, each named in its own language. Talk reads the choice each time it starts listening.
- On a device without voice support, a voice switch that is already on can still be turned off.
- Talk is no longer restored on launch: a fresh launch starts with Talk off and doesn't ask for the microphone. Explicit requests (Siri's live voice, the Watch, the Gateway) still start it.
- The header avatar's VoiceOver label uses the same status phrase as the composer.
- The camera switch is a plain glyph like the composer's other secondary controls.

Nothing else in the app changes look with this pull request. The connection strip and the app toast come from the pull requests just before this one; onboarding still uses its old setup steps until the next one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Talk said its state twice and made the composer jump between two layouts. Folding Talk into the composer card gives it one place, one phrase and one exit. The Language choice lets someone talk in a language other than the phone's first one without changing the phone's settings.

## Evidence

- Builds for the iOS Simulator (app, unit tests and UI tests) with the SwiftFormat lint and strict SwiftLint build phases; both lint phases report no findings over the app's file list.
- `native-app-i18n verify` reports no changes after regenerating the catalogs; `git diff --check` is clean.
- iOS unit tests: `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`, `TalkChatPhaseTests`, `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`, `TalkSpeechLocaleTests`: 289 passed, 0 failed.
- OpenClawKit tests (`swift test` on macOS): `ChatComposerPrimaryRoleTests` and `ChatTalkPresentationTests`: 15 passed, 0 failed.
- UI tests: `testTalkStartsInTheComposerAndEndsBackToIt`, `testTalkSaysEachStateInOnePlace` and `testMuteReadsAsSelectedAndLeavesTalkOn` pass. `testTalkOverADraftKeepsTheDraft` fails: after Talk starts over a typed draft, tapping End doesn't end Talk within three seconds. It fails the same way, at the same line, on the full approved build that this series adds up to, so it isn't caused by how this change was split. The cause is in the test, not the app: while Talk is on, the held draft keeps a hidden copy of the main button with the same identifier, and the test taps that copy. Once a draft is typed, the copy sits about 40 pt below the visible row, so the tap lands on nothing. Tapping the End button on the Talk row ends Talk over a draft in about 1.5 seconds and brings the draft back. A fix that changes only the test goes in before this lands; with it, all four Talk UI tests pass.
- Screenshots below come from the app's built-in demo chat and Talk fixture in the iPhone 17 Pro Simulator, with no Gateway or account. "Before" is the app with the earlier pull requests in this series applied, not `main`. The Simulator can't run Talk on that build, so the Before Talk screens set Talk on with a temporary debug hook that is not part of this change; the muted Before screen shows that build's own "Microphone muted" line.

Talk on, listening (light and dark), Before | After:

![Talk on and listening, light. Before: a separate "Listening" strip with its own mute icon above the composer, which keeps the + button, the text field, a tinted camera disc and a red waveform button. After: one row inside the composer card with a microphone button, a level mark, "Listening", a plain camera glyph and a red End button.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce557bba-e362-4436-82f2-59a6bedf6872)

![Talk on and listening, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16d0be13-bff2-4ee5-bd2f-ab70482db7be)

Talk on, muted (light), Before | After:

![Talk on and muted, light. Before: the strip reads "Listening" with "Microphone muted" in orange under it. After: the row shows a crossed-out microphone and "Muted".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66efbc58-5dc5-463d-8232-752c5228f453)

Settings › Voice & Talk (light), Before | After:

![Settings, Voice & Talk, light. Before: five switches, with the two that are on dimmed. After: the same switches, the two that are on at full strength, and a new Language row that reads Automatic.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b5be0f2-50e1-4b25-a92f-9018962cb567)

Settings › Voice & Talk › Language (light), After only:

![The Language page, light, After only: Automatic with a checkmark, then English (United States), then the other languages, each named in its own language.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afe27157-95d0-4d91-b97a-ca606949c704)

Not checked: Talk with a real microphone, voice provider or Gateway (the Simulator has neither microphone access nor voice support); a real device; iPad and macOS layouts; Dynamic Type sizes other than the default; VoiceOver by ear, including whether it can reach the held draft's hidden controls while Talk is on (the UI test framework can see them, although the code marks them hidden).

prs.title: feat(ios): one toast for the whole app, with Undo and Try again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the app tells you what happened in many different ways, and often not at all. Copying a message leaves no sign that it worked. A failed archive, pin or rename on the Sessions screen shows a raw error line at the top of the list. A failed host switch opens an alert that says "Could Not Switch Gateway" with the system's error text. Live Voice opens its own alert, the camera has its own floating label, Voice Wake has its own banner, and chat failures sit in a banner inside the transcript. On a chat's details page a failed export shows nothing until you go back to the chat. None of these offer a way to try the action again, and none of them can be undone. The Control UI uses one toast for all of this.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees one toast for the whole app: a small capsule under the top bar that draws above sheets and stays clear of the keyboard and the Send button. A toast without an action leaves after two seconds and one with an action after five. While VoiceOver or Switch Control is running, a toast with an action stays until it is dismissed. Swiping the toast up dismisses it, and VoiceOver offers a Dismiss action.

- **Confirmations:** "Copied" after Copy Message and after copying the build info in Settings, "Image copied" from an inline widget, "Command copied" from the Gateway problem banner, "Photo taken" and "Video recorded" when the agent uses the camera, and the command Voice Wake heard, in quotes with a microphone icon, when Voice Wake fires (VoiceOver reads "Voice Wake heard “…”.").
- **Undo:** archiving a chat from Sessions or the sidebar says "Archived" with Undo, and snoozing says "Snoozed until …" with Undo.
- **Try again:** a failed archive, unarchive, pin, unpin, rename, snooze, wake, delete or fork names the chat ("Couldn’t pin “Release notes”.") and offers Try again, which repeats the same action. The same holds for a failed export on the chat's details page, a failed change to a chat's access, Web search, skills, connectors, model, effort or speed, a failed host switch, and Start Live Voice.
- **Host switches** name the host in plain words ("Couldn’t reach Studio.", "Studio needs a secure connection.") and only offer Try again when trying again can help. A switch refused because a draft or recording is in progress says what to do first ("Send or clear your draft first.").
- **Chat failures** show as a toast. The transcript's banner keeps only the model sign-in problem that the composer acts on.
- The old Live Voice alert, the "Could Not Switch Gateway" alert, the file-share alert, the camera label and the Voice Wake banner are gone.

Talk in the composer and the setup steps still look as before; later pull requests in the series change them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenClawToastPresenter` in OpenClawChatUI owns the toast: one at a time, its kind (confirmation, warning, failure), its optional action (Undo or Try again) and how long it stays. `NodeAppModel.toasts` is the app's one presenter. Views reach it through the `openClawToastPresenter` environment value, model code posts to it directly, and the chat's status strip holds a weak reference so a failed settings change can post there. The toast is drawn in its own pass-through window (`ToastWindow`, `ToastLayer`), so it shows above sheets and full-screen covers without taking touches from them, and the chat header reports its bottom edge so the toast sits under it. Every place that had its own alert, label or banner now posts a toast instead, and the camera HUD, the Voice Wake toast view and the Sessions screen's error line are removed. Failures keep their own text and their retry closure, so Try again repeats exactly what failed. The string catalogs are regenerated.

## Evidence

- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `GatewayConnectionControllerTests`, `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`, `OpenClawAppDelegateTests` and `SidebarGatewayPickerTests`, 376 of 376 passed.
- OpenClawKit package tests on macOS (`swift test`): `OpenClawToastScheduleTests` and `ChatErrorToastTextTests`, 11 of 11 passed.
- UI tests on the same simulator: `testToastConfirmsCopyMessage` and `testToastOffersTryAgainWhenExportFails` passed. `testToastShowsAboveAnOpenSheet` checks that the toast shows above the open Settings sheet with the right text and that the sheet stays open, then fails on its next assertion, which looks for an "OpenClaw Gateway" row that the redesigned Settings page no longer has. It fails at the same line with the finished series applied, so the test needs an update rather than the code. `CommandSessionsMutationUITests/testRejectedPinKeepsLoadedSessionsUsable` skips without a synthetic Gateway and was not run against one.
- The iOS app and its test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the app's screenshot-mode demo data (no Gateway) on the same simulator. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`. Each pair repeats the same action: Copy Message in a chat (light and dark), a failed export on the chat's details page, and Voice Wake firing while the Settings sheet is open.
- Not checked:
  - A real Gateway: host switch failures, Sessions row actions, and the Archived and Snoozed toasts with Undo (the demo data can't archive or snooze, so there is no Undo screenshot).
  - The camera and Live Voice toasts on a device.
  - VoiceOver and Switch Control timing on a device, iPad, and landscape.

![Copy Message in a chat, light. Before: nothing confirms the copy. After: a "Copied" toast under the chat header.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8ee59e4-1ceb-4ff3-9bbc-5dbd59106c99)

![Copy Message in a chat, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d77a1866-556d-40fe-8236-ac723e8bc744)

![A failed export on the chat's details page, light. Before: the page shows nothing. After: a toast reads "Couldn’t export this chat." with Try again.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3d5fead-fe67-41bb-a1e7-3d06928fa33b)

![Voice Wake fires while the Settings sheet is open, light. Before: nothing shows above the sheet. After: a toast above the sheet shows the heard command, “Summarize today’s calendar”.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a1e8696-e2e4-4e19-9636-a10652e90d03)

In each image, Before is on the left and After is on the right.

prs.title: feat(ios): connection problems show in one strip above the composer, named by host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the iPhone app is still connecting to OpenClaw, or has lost the connection, nothing in a chat says so. A person can type a message without knowing it can't go anywhere yet. Some problems show only as a banner at the top of the app, which does not name the OpenClaw it means. Saved connections are listed as "Paired Gateways" with raw addresses, and there is no way to give one a name a person recognizes.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this one:

- **One strip above the composer carries the connection.** When something is wrong, a single line above the composer says what, and names the connection: "Connecting to …" before the first connection, "Reconnecting to …" after a drop (with a spinner and no button, because the app keeps trying on its own), "Can’t reach …" or "Not connected to …" with Try again once the app stops trying, "Sign in to … again" and "Approve this iPhone on …" with Settings, and "Can’t verify …" / "Verify … again" with Trust or Settings. While connected the strip says nothing. A waiting state holds back for a moment, so a quick reconnect does not flash. A bare IP address reads "OpenClaw"; a name drops the address's port.
- **One place, not two.** In a chat, the app's top problem banner leaves out a problem the strip already shows, and the strip's button runs the same recovery the banner offers. When Talk is on, Talk's row in the composer already says the connection is offline, so the strip shows only a problem that has a button.
- **A failed approval answer for lack of connection** shows as the strip's "Can’t reach …" instead of an error line in the approval card.
- **Saved connections have names.** The connection page in Settings is titled with the selected connection's name (or "Connection"). Its list is "Saved connections"; each row has a menu with Rename and Forget, a connection that is not the selected one also gets Keep connected or Disconnect, and Rename opens a "Rename connection" dialog. A saved address that nobody has named takes the host's machine name when it connects.
- **The sidebar's connection control** uses the same names, says "Add connection" and "Manage connections", and its menu shows a second line (for example the port) when two saved connections would otherwise look the same.
- Smaller layout fixes that come with the strip: the activity pills, the approval card and the composer keep their places when the strip comes or goes; a tap outside the effort bar closes it except on the strip, whose button stays usable; and the sidebar footer leaves room for New Chat.

Still old until later pull requests in this series:

- A failed change to access, Web search, skills or connectors still shows in the chat's error line, and a failed or refused switch between saved connections still shows the "Could Not Switch Gateway" alert. A later pull request moves both into the app's toast.
- Talk keeps its current controls; a later pull request moves Talk into the composer.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI shows connection trouble in one place, next to where you type, and names the machine it means. The phone now does the same with one status strip owned by the chat view model (`OpenClawChatStatusStrip`): each owner posts its own status with a priority, and the strip shows the most important one. The connection is the only owner in this pull request. `ChatConnectionStatus` turns the app's existing connection state and retained problem into that status, and reuses the recovery the top banner already offers (`GatewayProblemPrimaryAction`), so a problem has one recovery wherever it shows. Connection names live in the saved connection registry, so the sidebar, Settings and the strip read the same name. The chat header's old status pill code, which nothing showed any more, is removed.

## Evidence

Before is on the left and After on the right in the first three images. The last two show After only.

prs.title: fix(agents): re-pause task-owned nested requester yield while grandchildren pend
prs.body:
Closes #207095

## What Problem This Solves

When a nested subagent delegates work to two grandchildren and waits for their results, the parent task could receive an interim progress report as the final answer, and the real final answer was never delivered. After this fix, the nested subagent correctly goes back to waiting whenever a grandchild is still running, so the parent receives exactly one completion carrying the final answer.

- Problem: A task-owned nested requester B spawns C1/C2 and yields. C1 settles first and wakes B through an adopted turn. When B calls `sessions_yield` again from that adopted turn, the settled grandchildren are already unbound from the original turn (`requesterTurnRunId` is cleared at settle), so `claimSubagentYieldInRuns` returns `nothing-pending` for the no-`waitFor` case. The tool answers `already_pending` with "end this turn normally" guidance, B's adopted run finalizes, and the interim turn is announced to the parent as the completion. When C2 settles there is no paused row left to adopt, so B's final answer never reaches the parent.
- Solution: In the no-`waitForMessage` claim branch, a task-owned run (`expectsCompletionMessage`) that still has wake-armed, unsettled grandchildren in its session now claims `task-children-pending`, and the requester yield callback treats that claim as a real yield (`onYield` → `markSubagentRunPausedAfterYield`), re-pausing the adopted row so the last partition's settle adopts the same task lineage and delivers the final answer.
- What changed: `subagent-registry-run-pause.ts` (new `task-children-pending` claim), `openclaw-tools.requester-yield.ts` (claim → yielded), regression tests in `subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts`, and a per-file `max-lines` override in `.oxlintrc.json` for that test file.
- What did NOT change: guidance wording (no overlap with open PR #190011), settle-wake mechanics, tool schema, UI, and the silent/collector/main-session paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The violated invariant: a task-owned run with wake-armed pending grandchildren must stay paused (`pauseReason="sessions_yield"`) so every later partition settle adopts the same lineage; only the last partition's turn finalizes and announces. Fixing at the registry claim layer reuses the existing re-pause API instead of touching guidance text or the settle-wake design.

- Best fix: yes — smallest diff at the owner of the claim decision; the `hasPendingWork` error ordering is preserved.
- Alternative: rewording the `already_pending` guidance (the issue's "at minimum") was rejected because it only nudges the model and overlaps open PR #190011; keeping the task open at the runtime level would be a larger redesign.
- Risk / non-goals: grandchildren that are paused or not wake-armed still yield `nothing-pending` (nothing can wake the session, which is correct). The claim/pause race where a grandchild completes in between is the same as on the first yield and is covered by the existing settle sweep.

## User Impact

Nested subagent tasks whose grandchildren finish at different times now deliver their complete final answer to the requesting task exactly once, instead of an interim partial report. No config, API, or UI changes.

## Evidence

TDD red/green on the real registry + SQLite + lifecycle + announce path (no module mocks):
`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts`

Before the fix (production changes reverted), the two new regression tests fail:

```text
× nested requester yield partition (#207095) > claims a wake-armed pending grandchild as task-children-pending
  → expected 'nothing-pending' to be 'task-children-pending'
× nested requester yield partition (#207095) > re-pauses an adopted nested turn so the last partition delivers the final answer
  → expected { status: 'already_pending', …(2) } to match object { status: 'yielded' }
Tests  2 failed | 4 passed | 50 skipped (56)
```

After the fix, the full e2e file passes, including the end-to-end assertion that the outer requester receives exactly one wake containing "final answer" after the second partition settles:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  56 passed (56)
```

Behavior matrix (claim layer, `it.each`, all green after the fix):

| Task-owned row / grandchild state | claim |
| --- | --- |
| wake-armed pending grandchild | `task-children-pending` (was `nothing-pending`) |
| silent row (`expectsCompletionMessage=false`) | `nothing-pending` |
| grandchild paused by yield | `nothing-pending` |
| grandchild without armed wake | `nothing-pending` |
| no grandchild | `nothing-pending` |

Adjacent consumers all green (10 files, 167 tests): requester-yield callback, requester-cron-authority, participation-ceiling, sessions-yield-tool, yielded-run-settlement integration, attempt.sessions-yield, gateway sessions.send-yield-resume / initial-transfer-custody / lifecycle-dormant, and cron delivery-dispatch.automation-yield.

Checks: oxlint 0 warnings / 0 errors on the changed files; oxfmt clean; `tsc --noEmit` error set byte-identical to the base commit (pre-existing declaration-portability diagnostics only, none in the changed files).

What was not tested: a live multi-model gateway run; the claim/pause race is covered by the existing settle sweep rather than a new test.

prs.title: fix: stop sending internal steering errors to the chat
prs.body:
Related: #207117

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat run is stuck in a long tool call, every message the person sends meanwhile is steered into that run. One example is a Codex run waiting up to 10 minutes for an OpenClaw change approval. Codex accepts each message but reads it only after the tool call returns. After 60 seconds the steering receipt times out, and the chat later gets the runtime's internal error once per message: `Codex accepted steering but did not confirm transcript consumption | Codex steering transcript consumption confirmation timed out`. In the reported case, one WhatsApp chat got four copies.

## User Impact

The person now gets a plain notice instead: "OpenClaw could not confirm that input. It was not sent again; check the conversation before retrying." Talk already uses this wording for the same state. The runtime's error moves to the Gateway diagnostic log as a warning. Input custody is unchanged: the message is not replayed, the running tool is not interrupted, and the runtime still reads the message when it can.

This covers every runtime that steering reaches. For example, a backend that fails after accepting input also stopped sending its raw error text.

Not fixed here: each steered message still gets its own notice, so four messages still give four notices. #207117 also asks for at most one per run. That needs a change in the dispatcher too: if steering returns no reply, the dispatcher's missing-reply fallback can send a generic notice instead. I left that for a follow-up, so this PR does not close the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel steering in `runActiveReplySteer` delivers the indeterminate outcome's `errorMessage` to the sender as the reply. That field holds whatever the runtime reported: Codex's joined cause chain, a backend error, or the question path's plain message. This PR fixes it at that presentation boundary. One fixed notice there covers every runtime. Fixing each producer would leave the next producer to leak the same way.

I kept a visible notice rather than dropping the reply. #166754 surfaces receipt uncertainty on purpose, and the notice tells the person their message was not lost and should not be resent. Suppressing the reply would also run into the missing-reply fallback above. Queueing the message as a new turn would break the no-replay rule that #166754 and #184062 enforce, because the runtime already holds the input.

The question-answer path (`agent-runner-question-input.ts`) is unchanged. It already delivers `QuestionAnswerUnconfirmedError`'s plain message. On the steering path, question answers now get the generic notice. Both texts end with the same "It was not sent again; check the conversation before retrying." The issue's code pointer named the question path. The reported text actually comes from `CodexSteeringAcceptedUnconfirmedError` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-steering.ts`, through this steering path.

## Evidence

- **Production (OpenClaw 2026.11.10, Codex harness, WhatsApp DM, Default agent without `tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges`):** four messages sent during a 600-second approval wait each produced `reason=question-response-indeterminate` about 60 seconds after dispatch. When the run ended, the chat got four copies of the error above. All four messages were in the Codex transcript by then.
- **Codex source check (`openai/codex` main, 2026-11-25):** in `codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs`, accepted steer input goes into the turn's `pending_input`, which is read only between model steps. A steered message therefore waits for the running tool call, as observed.
- **Regression test, red on `main`, green with this change:** `agent-runner-steer-adoption.question-recovery.test.ts` ("retains accepted input until its unconfirmed / backend-error outcome settles") drives `runActiveReplySteer` against a backend that accepts input, then reports an unconfirmed receipt or fails. On `main`, the reply text is the runtime's error (`transcript confirmation lost`, `backend failed after accepting input`). With the fix, it is the plain notice. The test previously asserted the raw passthrough. Custody assertions in the same test are unchanged: admission stays `question-response-indeterminate`, no followup, no cancel, no abort.
- **Updated test:** `agent-runner-steer-adoption.question-receipts.test.ts` asserts the shared "not sent again" sentence on both entry points, instead of the question-only wording.
- **Checks:** the 44 steering-related `src/auto-reply/reply` test files pass. So do the nearby gateway `chat.send`, Talk, TUI and subagent-announce suites, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, oxlint and `git diff --check`.
- **Not shown:** a capture from a real channel. I had no channel test account for an isolated Gateway with a real runtime. The Control UI is not affected; it shows its own "send failed" text for this ack.

prs.title: feat(ios): chat details as a session profile with media, files and automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, a chat has no details page. The agent and title in the chat header can't be tapped, so there is no place to see where a chat runs (its worktree and branch), the pull requests it opened, the images and files it produced, the automations that belong to it, or how much of its context it has used. Renaming, archiving, exporting and resetting a chat are either missing or hidden in the header's more menu. The Control UI shows all of this on a chat's session page.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **Tapping the agent and title in the chat header opens the chat's details.** In a saved chat the page shows the agent, the chat's title and when it was created, then Export, Archive (when the chat can be archived) and Reset, and these sections:
  - **Environment:** the worktree or repository, its branch, and how many lines the checkout adds and removes.
  - **Pull requests** the chat opened, each opening the existing pull request page.
  - **Media and files:** a strip of the chat's images and files with **See all**, which opens a gallery with Media and Files tabs. A file opens in the share sheet and an image in Quick Look.
  - **Automations** scoped to the chat, with their schedule in words (for example "Every 6 hours") and whether a run failed or the job is paused. A row opens that job's page.
  - **Context:** how much of the context window is used, with **Compact**.
  - **Edit** in the bar renames the chat.
- **In the main chat, the same tap opens the agent's profile:** its avatar and name, Export and Reset, the main chat's media and files, the agent's automations, and its context.
- Each section loads inside the page, so the page opens at once. A section that is still loading or failed to load says so, and a failed one can be tapped to try again. Empty sections explain what will appear there.
- **The header's more menu gets shorter for a saved chat.** Rename, context usage and Archive now live on the details page, so the menu keeps New chat, Pin, Move to group and Delete. The main chat's menu keeps Pin, Rename and Move to group; its context usage moves to the agent's profile.
- The line counts on the pull request page use thousands separators ("+2,280").

Some parts still behave as before until later pull requests in the series. A failed export, a file that can't be opened and a failed rename show in the chat's error banner when you go back to the chat, not in a toast on the page; a later pull request adds the app-wide toast and its Try again.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ChatInfoPage` owns the page. `ChatInfoVisit` captures what the header knew when it was tapped (the chat's view model, the Gateway, the agent and the checkout's changes), and `ChatProTab` drops the visit when the chat or its owner changes, so the page never shows another chat's data. Media come from `artifacts.list` and `artifacts.download` through `IOSMediaArtifactLoader`, which also makes small tile thumbnails and caches them for the life of the app, so the gallery shows the strip's pictures without reading them again. Automations come from `cron.list` and open the existing Control UI cron page for the job (`DashboardPageScreen` now accepts query items). The transcript export moves from `ChatProTab` into `ChatInfoPage` with `writeTranscript(for:in:)` unchanged, and its existing test now calls it there. `OpenClawChatLineCounts` is shared by the pull request page and the checkout row. `ChatActionsMenu` takes `hasInfoPage` so it doesn't repeat what the page offers. The screenshot fixture gains chat-info data for the UI tests, and the string catalogs are regenerated.

## Evidence

- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatActionsMenuTests`, `ChatInfoAutomationTests`, `ChatInfoEnvironmentTests`, `ChatInfoMediaTests`, `ChatTranscriptFileExportTests` and `IOSMediaArtifactLoaderTests`, 29 of 29 passed.
- UI tests on the same simulator, 13 of 13 passed: `testChatHeaderOpensItsInfoAndStaticAgentRow`, `testSessionProfileStripAndGallery`, `testChatInfoMediaCatalogStates`, `testChatInfoOpensBeforeSlowCatalogsAndRetriesFailure`, `testGalleryShowsTheStripsThumbnailsWithoutReadingThemAgain`, `testAFailedThumbnailReadIsTriedAgain`, `testSavedCheckoutShowsItsOwnLineCounts`, `testDiscoveryPagesInBothAppearances`, `testDiscoveryDynamicTypeAndFailureHeight`, `testDiscoveryRowsWithMixedLoadingAndFailedCatalogs`, `testMediaTilesUsePicturesWithoutMovingTheirNeighbors`, `testChatActionsAndNewSessionOptionsHaveSeparateEntryPoints` and `AdaptiveLayoutUITests/testChatToolbarFitsCurrentWindow`.
- The iOS app and its test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the app's screenshot-mode demo data (no Gateway) on the same simulator. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`: the "Launch plan" demo chat, where tapping the header opens nothing. After is the page that tap opens, from the UI test run, plus the agent profile, the gallery, and the empty states.
- Not checked:
  - A real Gateway with real artifacts, cron jobs and a real worktree.
  - Export, Archive, Reset and Rename against a Gateway.
  - VoiceOver on a device, iPad, and the page in landscape beyond what the UI tests cover.

Before is on the left and After on the right in the first two images. The last four show After only, because these pages did not exist before.

![Chat details, light. Before: the "Launch plan" chat, where tapping the header opens nothing. After: the details page that tap opens, with Export, Archive and Reset, Environment, Pull requests, and the empty Media and files and Automations sections.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/530db422-3426-4162-926d-39443929936b)

![Chat details, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df6f6017-7fff-44e4-b23d-d1e8ffc8fd18)

![Agent profile, light, After only: the page the same tap opens in the main chat, with the avatar and name, Export and Reset, Media and files, Automations and Context.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51408f10-5986-4f6e-96e7-c7cad02293c6)

![Chat details with content, light, After only: a strip of two images and one file with See all, and two automations, one reading "Run failed" and one "Paused".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/129458a3-571d-495f-9b9b-55d87f7bb846)

![Gallery, Media tab, light, After only: a grid of the chat's images.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc9bb1c4-66db-4b8c-be3c-7e55faa81a65)

![Gallery, Files tab, light, After only: four PDF files with their sizes.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3f57592-16d9-4afb-9716-01e6a675145f)

prs.title: feat(ios): search everything from a full screen with the field at the bottom
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone and iPad, the search button at the top of the sidebar opens a small field that only filters the session titles already loaded in the sidebar. Pages, Settings screens, archived sessions and the text of past messages can't be found from it. The Control UI's command palette searches all of those from one field.

## User Impact

- The sidebar's search button opens search full screen. The field sits at the bottom, on top of the keyboard, with a close button next to it.
- Before you type, search shows your three most recent sessions under "Recent".
- As you type, results are grouped into pages and commands, sessions, archived sessions and messages, with All, Pages, Sessions and Messages filters above them. A filter shows a count once its results are in. The All filter shows a short preview of each group, with "Show more" to open that group's filter.
- Pages and commands include the sidebar pages, Settings and its screens (Connection, Voice & Talk, Permissions and the rest), New Chat, and the Gateway's skills and plugins by name. Sessions match by title: an exact title comes first, then the most recent. From two characters on, archived sessions and message text are also asked of the Gateway; a failed message search says so and offers "Try again".
- Offline, search says "Offline. Searching what’s on this device." and searches only what the app already has.
- Choosing a result opens it: a page, a Settings screen (Skills and Plugins open filtered to the chosen item), a new chat, or the session.
- Pulling the sidebar's list down past its top also opens search. The search button fills a ring as you pull and gives one haptic tick at the point where letting go opens it.
- The Sessions screen gets a search button in its bottom bar, next to New Chat.
- The sidebar no longer filters its own list. It always shows the 15 most recent sessions, as it does when nothing is typed today.

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this one alone, the sidebar footer (connection control and New Chat) keeps its current spacing, and failed session actions in the sidebar still report through the sidebar's error text; later pull requests in the series change both.

## Why This Change Was Made

Search follows the Control UI's command palette, so the same query finds the same kinds of things in the same order on the web and on the phone. It opens as a full-screen cover in place of the sidebar, without the sheet slide, because a cover owns its keyboard inset and the field can then sit right above the keyboard. Results stack upward from the field, so the best match is closest to your thumb. A result is opened only after the cover is gone, so a Settings sheet never competes with the cover's dismissal.

The inline sidebar filter and its state are removed rather than kept next to the new search, so there is one way to search. The new ranking and pull-to-search logic have their own unit tests.

## Evidence

- The app and its test bundles build for the iOS simulator with SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint as build phases, with no lint findings. The string catalogs regenerate with no further change (`native-app-i18n verify`), and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Unit tests (iPhone 17 Pro simulator): `RootSearchRankingTests`, `RootSidebarPullToSearchTests`, `RootSidebarStabilityTests` and `RootTabsPresentationTests` ran 71 tests; 69 passed. The two failures, `roster insertion above viewport preserves the visible rows` and `pinned automations stay discoverable through selection and search`, fail the same way on the previous pull request in the series, without this change. This pull request does not touch the code either one checks.
- UI test: `OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCappedSearchPreviewStartsUnderFilters` passes. It does not exist before this change. `ChatScrollPerformanceUITests/testSidebarOpenCloseHitches` (its button lookup changes here) was skipped, because it needs a live Gateway session.
- Screenshots: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, the app's screenshot fixture with sample sessions (no Gateway, no account data). Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`. prs.title: fix: open the exact saved conversation when resuming by key
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Someone pastes the full key of a saved conversation into `openclaw resume`. If it falls outside the recent-session picker, the CLI can silently open a different, newer conversation whose key contains the one they pasted.

## User Impact

An existing agent-qualified key opens its own conversation even when it isn't among the 50 most recent sessions from the last seven days. Partial names and keys still search the recent list. The picker, qualified global sessions, and commands copied from the Control UI keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already resolves a saved key. The CLI now asks it for an exact match before searching the bounded recent list; it doesn't fetch an unbounded history or store another index.

## Evidence

In an isolated Gateway, `agent:main:review-notes` was nine days old and `agent:main:review-notes-today` was recent. Both were saved. Before the change, the compiled CLI opened the newer conversation when given the older one's full key. With the change, the compiled CLI opened `agent:main:review-notes` for that same key, although only `review-notes-today` appeared in the picker. No chat message was sent in either run. The focused regression failed on that wrong key; the resume and session-picker suites passed with the fix, including the partial-key fallback. The patch applied to upstream `e85cda36996c` produces the exact Git tree used for these checks.

prs.title: feat(ios): Settings pages for tools, chat display, your profile and notifications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who use OpenClaw on iPhone can't change several settings that the Control UI offers. The iPhone Settings screen has no place to turn reasoning, tool calls or commentary on or off in the chat, no way to see or turn on the agent's skills and plugins, no notifications row, and no way to edit the personal instructions an agent keeps for you on a shared OpenClaw. To change any of these, a person has to go to a computer.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this one, Settings gains:

- **Notifications** in the General section. Its value says "Off" until iOS allows notifications and the app is set up, and a line under the title says when it is waiting for OpenClaw or for Apple. Tapping the row turns notifications on or opens iOS Settings.
- **Chat** in the App section. It opens a page with the transcript's display switches (Reasoning, Tool calls, Keep commentary, Wrap code lines), a Follow-ups choice (Automatic, Wait for reply, Send now) and, when the connected OpenClaw offers it, the agent's Verbosity. The chat follows these switches. Before this change one switch covered both reasoning and tool calls; a person who never touches the new switches keeps that earlier choice. With Keep commentary off, the commentary an agent writes between tool calls goes away once its run finishes.
- **Tools**, a new section with **Skills** and **Plugins**. Each opens a searchable list of the agent's skills or the server's plugins, with their status, source, why a skill can't run (for example a missing program or environment variable), and Enable or Disable when this connection may change them. A skill also offers "Try in chat", which puts "Use the … skill." in the composer and returns to the chat.
- **Personal instructions** in the App section, only on a shared OpenClaw that lets this connection read and write your personal file for the agent. It opens an editor for the instructions the agent uses for you.

The Settings → Chat page that the iOS docs already describe now exists.

The rest of Settings is unchanged by this pull request. The Skills, Plugins and Chat pages already look as they will at the end of the series; later pull requests in the series change other parts of the app, not these pages.

## Why This Change Was Made

These pages are the iPhone versions of the Control UI's chat View switches, skills and plugins settings, notifications setting and personal instructions. They read and write the same Gateway settings the desktop uses. When connected, the Chat page loads the desktop's View switches from the Gateway's UI preferences and saves changes back there, so a choice made on one device shows on the other. The chat reads its display options from one place, `ChatPreferences.displayOptions`, which keeps the earlier single switch's choice when the new switches are unset. The chat view's keyboard dismissal moves into a small extension file of its own, with no change in behavior.

## Evidence

Before is on the left and After on the right in the first three images. The last four show After only, because these pages did not exist before.

prs.title: feat(ios): approve a command from a card that answers its own request
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, an approval request that belongs to a chat has no place in that chat. After the previous pull request in this series, the app no longer covers the whole screen with the old "Exec approval required" dialog, so a command waiting for approval only shows up as **Needs approval** in Sessions and in **Settings → Approvals**. A person in the chat where the agent is waiting can't see the request or answer it there. Tapping an approval notification also doesn't take them to the chat that asked. The Control UI shows the request as a card in its chat, above the composer.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **A card above the composer in the chat that asked.** It reads "Worker wants to run a command" (with the agent's name) or "Approval needed" for other kinds, a countdown to when the request expires, and the command in a box that expands to show the host, node, agent and expiry.
- **The card answers its own request.** "Allow once", "Always allow" (when the request allows it) and "Deny" resolve that chat's request, even if another approval is selected in Settings → Approvals. While the answer is sent the card shows "Resolving…"; afterwards it shows the outcome with "Dismiss".
- **Notifications lead to the request.** Tapping an approval notification opens the chat the request came from, when that chat belongs to the active agent; otherwise it opens **Settings → Approvals**. The prompt that suggests turning on notifications now appears only for requests without a chat.
- The full-screen approval dialog's code is removed; requests without a known chat stay in **Settings → Approvals**, which is unchanged.

Some parts still behave as before until later pull requests in the series. When an answer fails because the app can't reach the Gateway, the card still shows the error text; a later pull request moves that message to the chat's connection strip.

## Why This Change Was Made

An approval waits on the agent in a specific chat, so that chat is where the person can judge it. `ChatSessionApproval` asks `NodeAppModel` for the pending request whose source session matches the open chat (`pendingApproval(forSession:agentID:)`, which reuses the session matching the Sessions list already uses) and draws `SessionApprovalCard` through the chat's composer accessory. `resolveSessionApproval` selects the card's own request before it resolves, so the card never answers a different request that happens to be selected elsewhere. `currentApprovalSource(for:)` is the one check for whether a request's source is still current, shared by the attention list, the card and notification routing. The old dialog, its metadata rows, its expiry text and its smoke test go away; the notification-permission dialog keeps a private copy of the button helper it shared with the old dialog. The iOS docs describe the new flow, and the string catalogs are regenerated.

## Evidence

- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `NodeAppModelInvokeTests` and `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`, 280 of 280 passed, including the new "the session card resolves its own request rather than the selected inbox review".
- UI tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `testSessionRowsReadTheirStateLine`, `testSessionRowsHoldAtTheLargestTextSize` and `testSessionsHeaderDotOnlyForApprovalsTheListDoesNotShow` passed; they fail without this change, because the demo Sessions fixture's approvals reach the list only through `pendingApprovalAttentionRequests`.
- The iOS app and its unit and UI test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the app's screenshot-mode demo chat (no Gateway) rendered in the app's unit test host on the same simulator, with one synthetic pending command approval whose source is a chat. Default text size and AX3, light and dark. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`: the same chat with the same pending request shows nothing. After shows the card above the composer. The render harness was added only for these runs and isn't part of this change. At AX3 the transcript grows, while the card's title, command and buttons stay close to their default size.
- Not checked:
  - A real Gateway, a real approval request and a real notification action.
  - The UI test `verifyApprovalNotificationsNavigation` (its assertions change here); it needs a synthetic Gateway approval fixture and wasn't run.
  - The card inside the full chat screen with its header, VoiceOver on a device, iPad and landscape.

Before is on the left and After on the right in each image.

![Light, default text size: the chat with a command waiting for approval. Before shows nothing; After shows the card above the composer with Deny, Always allow and Allow once.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4729437-b31f-4162-94b1-3ddf615e59a1)

![Dark, default text size: the same chat, with the approval card above the composer in After.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1aada42c-7223-4c8f-ad8d-444f277ced2f)

prs.title: fix: let recurring automations start while a previous run still has work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A daily automation could finish one run, then fail before starting the next with `Session controller identity requires a physical store scope`. This happened when background work still held the earlier run’s session. The error looked like a store configuration problem even though both sessions were in the right store.

## User Impact

The next occurrence can start a fresh session without interrupting or taking over the previous one. No configuration change or migration is needed. This does not re-enable disabled jobs or change who may run an automation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stable job key already serializes preparation. The new occurrence has its own session ID; also claiming the ID from the previous job row made two different controllers match. Drop only that old ID from the lookup. The physical store, job key, current session ID, and lifecycle revision still identify the new run.

## Evidence

- Forced the same chat-linked `current` job twice through an isolated Gateway, with the first run’s session still in use. On base `58e358887b85`, the second `cron.runs` entry recorded the exact error above. With the fix, both occurrences reached the local fixture model endpoint, used different session IDs, and left the first session’s work active. No production monitor or external model account was used.
- The committed regression also failed on base and passed with the fix (1.64 s). All 72 focused cron tests passed across five files, including session serialization, isolated runs, and creator-access revocation. The cron TypeScript shard, touched-file lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Manually reviewed `58e358887b85..b544660623df`. The published head `aa11482bd3f8` has the same tree. [Required CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46099028405) (12 min 15 s for the workflow), and [hosted ClawSweeper passed with no findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207148#issuecomment-7232662609) on that exact head.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

prs.title: feat(ios): a message sends at the tap and its state replaces its time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, sending a message in a chat feels slow and its outcome is hard to read. After you tap Send, nothing appears in the transcript until the message has been prepared and saved, and while attachments go out the composer is locked behind "Preparing attachments…" and "Sending attachments…" rows. When a send fails, the app shows the raw transport error (for example "gateway request timed out after 15000ms") instead of saying what happened to your message, and many other failures in the chat read the same way.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **A message appears at the tap.** It goes into the transcript dimmed while it is checked, prepared and saved, and becomes solid once it is confirmed. The composer clears and stays open for the next message, including while attachments upload.
- **The message's state takes the place of a time under the bubble.** A message saved while a reply runs or while the connection is down shows "Queued". A failed send shows "Not sent · Try again", and a send that timed out shows "May not have sent · Try again". Tapping the line sends the message again. A message that is still on its way shows nothing extra.
- **Attachments show their own progress.** A photo or file in a message that is uploading carries a small ring, and the "Preparing attachments…" and "Sending attachments…" rows above the composer are gone. Send works while an image is still being prepared.
- **Failures read as plain sentences**, for example "Couldn’t send your message.", "Couldn’t change Fast mode." or "Couldn’t update this chat’s settings." The raw error goes to the log instead of the screen. Upgrade notices say "Update OpenClaw…" instead of naming the gateway.
- **A message can be written and sent while a reply runs** when the connection supports it, and it waits as "Queued".

Some parts still look old until later pull requests in the series:
- Failures still appear in the chat's error banner ("Something went wrong" with the new sentence). Showing them as a toast comes with the pull request that adds one toast for the whole app.
- The composer's Talk control, the sidebar and Settings are not updated yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

A chat should respond at the tap, as Messages and the Control UI do, and a message should say only what you can act on. The send goes through the existing outbox, so a message that can't leave the phone keeps its place in the transcript with a way to try again, instead of disappearing back into the composer. One rule decides what shows under a user message (`ChatUserSendPresentation`), and one helper turns failures into a sentence plus a log entry (`reportFailure`).

## Evidence

- OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS: the chat view model suites (`ChatViewModelTests`, `ChatViewModelOptimisticSendTests`, `ChatViewModelOutboxTests`, `ChatViewModelOutboxSettingsTests`, `ChatViewModelAttachmentTests`, `ChatViewModelProgressCardActionTests`, `ChatUserSendPresentationTests`, `ChatInputHistoryTests`, `ChatFileAdmissionTests`, `ChatFileAttachmentRequestTests`, `ChatSessionCompletionOwnershipTests` and the session management and history suites in the same files): 548 tests in 19 suites passed, 0 failed.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatAttachmentRailTests`, `ChatMessageBubbleEquatableTests`, `ChatTranscriptTimeTests` and `ChatModelPickerPhoneTests`, 27 passed, 0 failed.
- UI test `testLongModelPreservesComposerControlsAcrossFirstSend` passed.
- The iOS app and its test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `native-app-i18n verify` reports `changed=false`. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the demo chat in screenshot mode (no Gateway, no account data) on the same simulator, before and after. Light: a message right after Send, and the same message a moment later while the reply runs; a send that times out. Dark: the send that times out. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`.
  - The timed-out send uses a demo-only launch option that this change adds. Before ignores it, so in Before the send goes through and the demo reply arrives; After shows "May not have sent · Try again" under the message.
  - The demo transport sends almost at once, so the dimmed state is only on screen for a moment, and in the "right after Send" pair the two sides look nearly the same.
  - The screenshot test was added only for these runs and isn't part of this change.
- Not checked:
  - "Queued" and "Not sent · Try again" on screen. The demo chat can't send while a reply runs or fail with "Not sent", so these are covered by the unit tests above, not by screenshots.
  - A real Gateway, a slow connection, or uploading large attachments.
  - VoiceOver on a device, larger text sizes, iPad and landscape.
  - The macOS app.

Before is on the left and After on the right in each image.

![Light: a message right after Send. The demo sends almost at once, so the two sides look nearly the same.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d5a157b-872a-46f2-a523-1840c48b78df)

![Light: the same message a moment later, while the reply runs.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1626b0a7-ea2f-481b-b4cd-413b91b16a5e)

![Light: a send that times out. Before ignores the demo option and the reply arrives; After shows "May not have sent · Try again" under the message.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2150f714-9a53-44f5-93f8-9d8600e0d4a1)

![Dark: the send that times out, with "May not have sent · Try again" under the message in After.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f8d9650-6f1d-45be-b7ab-5d8c6914fc08)

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw workboard list` finds no visible cards, it prints no card rows and gives no explanation in a terminal. Someone checking a board cannot tell whether it has no cards, the filter excluded them, or the matching cards were archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

The list already has the cards selected by board and status before it hides archived cards. Using that information lets the CLI explain an empty list without another request or a change to the scripted output.

## Evidence

The original terminal regression got no output for a status filter with no matches. The focused command tests cover an empty board, a filter with no results, a board with only archived cards, redirected text, and JSON. An isolated Gateway and the compiled CLI were used to check the terminal output and follow the archive hint back to the original card. No human usability study was run.

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the composer's + opens a pop-up menu that mixes attachment sources (Photo Library, Camera, File) with chat settings (Verbosity, Skills, Connectors). Skills and connectors are nested submenus of checkmarks. A connector's tools sit one more level down, under "Tool Access", and they read "Enabled for this session". Recent photos can't be picked without opening the full system picker. While attachments load, the composer shows a staged chip and a separate "Preparing attachments…" line, so a person can't tell which file is still loading or which one failed. The Control UI already offers an attachment sheet with recent photos, skills and connectors, in plainer words.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees this on iPhone:

- **The + opens a sheet** titled Add, with a close button at the leading edge. The sheet opens with the keyboard down.
- **Recent photos.** The top row has a Camera tile, the most recent photos and videos, and a tile for more photos. Tapping a photo's corner marks it with its number. Marked photos are added in that order with the Add button, which counts them ("2 photos"). Tapping a photo itself adds it right away, together with any marked photos. Before Photos access is granted, the row offers "Show recent photos". If access was refused, the row reads "No access to Photos" with "Change in Settings".
- **Photo Library and Files** are rows under the photos.
- **Use a skill** opens a page of the chat's skills, with a search field. Tapping a skill puts `/skill` in front of the draft, closes the sheet and gives the draft the keyboard back. A skill that's off for this chat offers "Turn on and use". The switch button opens a page with a switch for each skill. Skills can't be used while the draft has attachments, and the page says so.
- **Connectors** shows how many are on ("2 on") and opens a list. Each connector shows On or Off and opens a page with "On for this chat" and a switch for each of its tools, under Tools. "Changes apply to this chat only." "Reset tools for this chat" clears a chat's tool choices.
- **Attachments become tiles in the composer.** Each picked item gets a tile at once. A tile shows a spinner while it loads. If it fails, it shows a warning mark, plus Try again when the file can be read again. A tile keeps its size from the pick to the staged attachment, and each tile has its own remove button. A staged photo opens in the viewer.
- **Plainer messages.** Attachment errors say what happened and what to do ("Couldn’t attach photo.heic.", "photo.heic is too large to send.", "Voice note is over the 5 MB limit. Record a shorter one."). The chat settings reasons now say "Update OpenClaw to change tools.", "Reload this chat before changing its tools." and "Off for this agent. Turn it on for this chat." instead of naming sessions and capabilities.
- Verbosity and the branch menu are no longer in the +.

On macOS, the composer keeps its menu. The macOS string catalog changes with the shared strings.

Some parts still look old or work differently until later pull requests in the series land:
- The composer can still show the old "Preparing attachments…" line while attachments stage. A later change removes the line and its string.
- A message can't be sent while an attachment is still loading. A later change lets it send at the tap.
- The tile spinner is this change's own. A later change replaces it with the app's shared ring spinner.
- The sheet doesn't show the connection status strip yet. A later change adds it.

There's no new setting, data format or Gateway method. Skills and connectors change the same session overrides as the old menu.

## Why This Change Was Made

A sheet has room for the things the menu couldn't hold: a strip of recent photos, a searchable skills list, and a page for each connector with its tools. It matches the Control UI's attachment picker. Separating "add something to this message" from chat settings puts web search and access with the shield (an earlier change in the series) and leaves the + for what goes into the message. Per-item tiles tell a person which attachment is still loading or failed, and let them retry or remove only that one.

## Evidence

- The iOS app and its test bundles build for the simulator with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatAttachmentRailTests`, 13 of 13 pass. They cover the tile sizes, the failed and preparing tiles, cancelling a tile, and the error wording.
- OpenClawKit package tests on macOS (`swift test --filter 'ChatComposerAddRulesTests|ChatViewModelTests'`):
  - `ChatComposerAddRulesTests` (photo marking order, a tap on a photo, a skill in front of the draft): 6 of 6 pass.
  - `ChatViewModelTests`: 391 of 397 pass. The same 6 tests fail, with the same 13 expectations, on the previous pull request in the series without this change. They test model and effort patch ordering and the new-chat draft, which later pull requests in the series finish.
  - On the previous pull request and on this one, the test file doesn't compile on its own. One test (`a send waits for a slow settings save only up to its bound`) is missing its first line until a later pull request in the series. To run the suite, I added that line in my working copy only.
  - One test, `send reapplies thinking gate after model patch rollback`, never finishes on the previous pull request in the series either. A later pull request rewrites it together with the send path it waits on. I skipped it.
- UI tests on the same simulator: `testAddingRecentPhotosFocusesDraft`, `testChatComposerAddSheetPutsASkillInFrontOfTheDraft`, `testChatComposerAddSheetReachesSkillsAndConnectorTools` and `testWithNativePhotoPickerAttachment`, 4 of 4 pass. The recent-photos test needs two photos in the simulator's library; I added two generated images.
- Screenshots come from the demo chat in screenshot mode, with no Gateway or account data, on the same simulator with the status bar fixed at 9:41. A temporary UI test, not part of this change, opened the + and its pages. The recent photos are two generated color images and one of the simulator's sample photos.
  - Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`. Before has no recent photos, so the photos row pairs with the system photo picker, which was still loading when the screenshot was taken.
  - The same temporary test, run against a build of the whole series, shows the same + sheet, pages, marked photos and staged tiles. Only the chat header's sidebar button differs, and a later pull request owns that button.
  - The composer tiles come from a temporary unit test that draws the composer with one staged photo, one photo still loading and one failed photo. The demo chat can't make an attachment fail. Before shows the same state as the old composer draws it: one staged chip and "Preparing attachments…".

Before is on the left and After on the right in each image.

![Light: the + opened. Before, a pop-up menu lists Connectors, Skills, Verbosity, File, Camera and Photo Library. After, the Add sheet has a Camera tile and recent photos, Photo Library and Files rows, then "Use a skill" and Connectors with "2 on".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02078a1e-5278-497c-b328-ab2032903ca1)

![Dark: the same + opened, before and after.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fdac44-459a-4082-9c65-2ef22d2cbc5d)

![Light: recent photos. Before has no recent photos, so it shows the system photo picker, still loading. After, two photos are marked 1 and 2, the title reads "2 photos" and an Add button appears.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd4bb47c-847a-454b-91b1-75b826b2e479)

![Light: skills. Before, a Skills submenu of checkmarks with a disabled skill, Release OpenClaw and Auto Review. After, the "Use a skill" page lists /autoreview and /release with a description each, a "Search skills" field and a switch button.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c597baff-69d8-448f-92ec-906c6798d279)

![Light: connectors. Before, a Connectors submenu with Linear and GitHub checked. After, the Connectors page lists GitHub and Linear, each "On".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae3d442b-81a9-4463-8287-113e3ef34b18)

![Light: one connector. Before, the GitHub submenu has "Tool Access" and "Enabled for this session". After, the GitHub page has "On for this chat" and, under Tools, a switch for "Search code" and one for "Create issue".](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7072c898-da23-42b9-8aab-9b80fe9124a1)

- Skills and connector changes against a real Gateway. The demo chat answers them locally.
- The camera. The simulator has none.
- Limited Photos access and a refused Photos permission on screen.
- Large files, unsupported images and voice note limits on screen. The unit tests cover their messages.

- The Mac app, beyond the package compiling and its tests running on macOS.
