prs.title: fix: let source updates wait for a Gateway that is still starting
prs.body:
Related: #161158

## What Problem This Solves

A source update can report a restart failure when the native Gateway command returns exit 2 (still starting), even if the replacement becomes ready shortly afterwards. The updater keeps the new runtime but leaves recovery artifacts behind and reports a failed update.

## User Impact

The stock source-server updater keeps waiting for verified readiness after a native pending result. Activation completes only after the managed Gateway serves the checkout's version and build and passes the existing readiness checks. If verification remains unavailable or does not succeed within the bounded update window, the update still fails and reports the retained recovery artifacts.

## Why This Change Was Made

I reuse the update readiness verifier for exactly `openclaw gateway restart` and `openclaw gateway start`. Arbitrary shell callbacks keep their current nonzero-exit failure contract, including exit 2. This covers activation and restart of a restored runtime, including the older three-argument adapter, without interpreting custom shell scripts or increasing standalone restart timeouts.

This is partial coverage of #161158. Custom native callback chains and the separate open-but-unresponsive listener question remain outside this change.

## Evidence

- With only the updater restored to base `4e06d657fcd`, both native pending-to-ready regressions fail with `New runtime restart failed (2)`. Both pass with candidate `c29c12d62e0`. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte after the isolated baseline run.
- All 99 scenarios in the four affected source-updater suites passed across split runs: `test/scripts-update-gateway-build.test.ts`, `test/scripts-update-gateway.test.ts`, `test/scripts-update-gateway-legacy.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/update-gateway.test.ts`. One batch reached its 20-minute limit; I ran the remaining legacy case and bootstrap scenarios separately. No assertion failed in that batch.
- Regression coverage includes native restart/start pending then verified, unverified readiness, a throwing probe, real callback failures, custom callback exit 2, and legacy activation/recovery.
- Script and root-test typechecks passed (`tsconfig.scripts.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`), along with targeted script lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`.
- One local review found two issues, fixed before publication: load the verifier before the checkout changes, and retain the recovery-path report when a probe throws.

Tests used an empty inherited environment, a throwaway HOME, an unavailable user runtime directory, and service-command shims. Native lifecycle and readiness results were mocked; source-update integration tests used real temporary Git repositories and runtime promotion. No live Gateway restart or live released-version upgrade was exercised.

Upstream [CI run 46097665023](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097665023) is `action_required` with no jobs: the fork workflow needs maintainer approval before it can run. Security-sensitive review, dependency review, and PR context/evidence checks passed. The aggregate CI gate remains red because CI has not executed, not because a test failed. The repository failure-classification helper found no test failures to rerun.

prs.title: feat(ios): pull request pills open a page with checks and Open on GitHub
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A chat on iOS had no way to show the pull requests its agent opened or worked on. The Control UI shows each linked pull request as a pill with its state and checks, and opens a page with the details. On the phone, a person had to leave the app and look for the pull request on GitHub.

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. It builds on the activity pills above the composer and the Goal sheet from the previous pull requests in the series.

## User Impact

With this pull request alone, a person sees:

- **A pill per linked pull request** in the activity row above the composer, after the subagent, Goal and progress pills. The pill shows the state (open, draft, merged or closed) with GitHub's mark, the number, and a mark when checks are running or failed. VoiceOver reads the repository, number, title, state and check rollup.
- **A pull request page** when they tap the pill. It shows the state badge, repository and number, date, title, author with avatar, changed files and line counts, and the branch. A Checks card lists the counts (passed, failed, running, skipped) and, once the details load, each check by name. **Open on GitHub** is a glass button pinned to the bottom; the list scrolls under it with the system's soft edge.
- **Stale details stay readable.** If GitHub can't be reached or rate limits the refresh, the page keeps the last details it received, says so, and offers **Try again**. If the pull request is no longer linked to the chat, the page says so.
- **Hide and restore.** Long-pressing a pill offers **Hide** and **Open on GitHub**; the page's more menu offers **Hide**, **Copy link** and **Share…**. Hidden pills stay hidden on this device for this chat. The chat's more menu gains a **Pull requests** submenu with **Show #N** for each hidden one (and **Show all** when there are several).

What still looks old until later pull requests in the series:

- The spacing between the pill row and an approval card is the earlier fixed padding; it changes with the connection strip pull request, which owns the metric it uses.
- The line counts on the page are drawn inline here; a later pull request moves them into a shared view used by chat details, with the same text and labels.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iOS app should read like the Control UI. The pill, the page and the hide behavior follow the web's pull request pills and reader, adapted to native iOS: a pushed page in the activity sheet's navigation stack, a context menu on the pill, and a pinned glass action.

How it works:

- The view model asks the transport to watch the current chat's pull requests (`controlUi.sessionPullRequests.subscribe`) when the chat's progress target is ready, and applies each `controlUi.sessionPullRequests.changed` push for that chat. A reconnect clears the watch so the next push re-establishes it; the last snapshot stays on screen meanwhile.
- The page asks the Gateway for the reader overview (`github.detail`, or `github.sessionDetail` for a non-github.com host) only when the Gateway advertises the method, and falls back to the pushed snapshot otherwise.
- The pull request snapshot types, which were macOS-only, move into shared code so iOS can decode them.
- The demo and screenshot fixtures publish three linked pull requests (open, merged, and one without details), with flags for failing checks and a pull-request-only view, so the screens can be checked without a Gateway or an account.

## Evidence

Before is this series up to the previous pull request, not `main`. After is this pull request. Light and dark appearance, iPhone 17 Pro simulator, the app's local activity fixture (no Gateway, no account data).

Before is on the left and After on the right in each of the first three images. The last four are After only.

![Light mode, the activity row scrolled to its end: Before ends with the task progress pill, After shows three pull request pills, #4182 open with checks running, #4191 without details and #4170 merged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c11f3370-46c0-48b1-affb-1024636664e0)

![Dark mode, the same row: Before ends with the task progress pill, After shows the three pull request pills](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16e9e0bd-c7fc-49a7-86a2-906e77004704)

![Light mode, the same row with failing checks: After shows a red failed mark on #4182](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea8ae950-7c38-4e09-8554-c6e59e192f96)

![After only, light mode: the pull request page with the Open badge, repository and number, title, author, files and line counts, branch, the Checks row and the pinned Open on GitHub button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd388012-f277-44ba-9a0e-c7f732c02792)

![After only, dark mode: the same pull request page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daa71df8-e5d7-4553-9f53-43cee25d58bd)

![After only, dark mode: sixteen checks scrolled under the pinned Open on GitHub button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c148768c-524d-4b49-ac12-b4bb5fcff54d)

![After only, light mode: long-pressing a pull request pill shows Hide and Open on GitHub](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d946acc-9190-466a-a68a-522280a8ab79)

The page and the menu are new, so they have no Before; in the Before build the row ends with the progress pill.

Verified:

- The app and its test bundles build for testing, with SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint as build phases, and no lint findings.
- `swift test` on OpenClawKit: `ChatActivityTests`, `ChatGatewayEventSubscriptionTests` and `ChatPRVisibilityTests` pass (22 tests in 3 suites). The package's test target only compiles with a one-line local fix to an unrelated test in `ChatViewModelTests.swift` that a later pull request in the series restores; that fix is not part of this change.
- UI tests: `testPullRequestPillsOpenTheirSheet` and `testActivitySheetsShowFailuresInPlace` pass; `testActivitySheetsShowFailuresInPlace` also passes on the Before build.
- The string catalogs were regenerated with the repository's extraction script, and its verify step reports no changes.

Not checked:

- A live Gateway with real GitHub data, rate limiting, or a reconnect during a watch.
- Dynamic Type sizes other than the default, and iPad.
- The macOS app beyond compiling the shared package for its tests.

prs.title: fix: check recorded automation owners before running
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

## What Problem This Solves

An older automation can look like it has a human owner even though the owner was never saved. A scheduled trigger or command can also start after its recorded owner's profile is gone. This draft addresses those two cases; it is the first slice of the single-owner cutover.

## User Impact

- A scheduled occurrence with a recorded human owner checks for that profile before running its trigger or payload. If the profile is gone, the run stops before doing that work and tells an administrator how to select a new owner.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` backs up the cron store and saves a directly recorded creator profile as the owner when no owner was saved. It leaves an existing owner (including a transferred one), the tool list, and the enabled state intact for those jobs.
- If the record says the creator was a profile but provides no usable profile ID, Doctor pauses the job and reports how an administrator can claim it on the Automations page. No job is deleted by this repair. Other unattributed jobs retain existing behavior in this slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now writes the owner once instead of having each store read infer it. The scheduler checks the saved owner at the start of the occurrence, before either the trigger or payload can act.

## Risks and Remaining Work

This slice does not loosen existing tool, channel, approval, sandbox, session, or provider checks. It adds a refusal when the profile catalog is unavailable, the saved owner is gone, or a direct-profile record still needs Doctor. Migration trusts only the same direct creator stamp previously used by the runtime reader; it does not infer a person from delivery or channel settings. Profile presence is not a substitute for permission to use a tool or target.

The full owner-based permission snapshot is not implemented. Other stored authority fields, per-effect rechecks, account-bound scheduled Discord `channel-edit`, and pauses for jobs with no direct creator profile remain out of this slice. Gateway wire types, CLI, agent tool schema, and Control UI are unchanged. Expect overlap with sibling changes in scheduler admission, Doctor cron repair, and automation docs.

## Evidence

- I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or force-pushing. The tested head is `5d25582c9142efe043d1c8e09ddd242668096b06`.
- I reproduced both ClawSweeper test findings locally: one stale owner-decoding assertion and all three transfer-recovery cases failed. The repaired store test keeps the separate-authority and older-writer assertions; transfer recovery now creates real isolated profiles and retains its successful-run assertions.
- I ran 173 focused tests successfully across `store.definition-integrity.test.ts`, `service.session-payload.test.ts`, `timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts`, Doctor `cron/index.test.ts`, and `cron/store-migration.test.ts`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1` locally, without a VM. Doctor coverage verifies persisted owners, transferred-owner preservation, unchanged tool lists, both enabled states, separate runtime authority, backup reporting, incomplete-attribution pausing, and repeat repair.
- I ran the owner-admission and Doctor regressions against main's production files: the scheduler case and both Doctor cases failed as expected. I restored the candidate bytes and reran the full focused selection successfully. These are in-process regression controls, not shipped-Gateway or upgrade proof.
- I passed core, cron-test and Doctor-test typechecks, focused lint, touched-file formatting, and the PR-to-main whitespace check. Whitespace warnings across the merge's first-parent range are confined to unchanged main changelog/vendor-patch files.
- I completed pr-simplify without removing behavior or assertions: shared fixture setup and the existing note assertion helper avoid duplication, and two adjacent warning appends are combined. The main-to-head delta is +61/-10 production TypeScript lines, +87/-4 test lines, and +8 documentation lines.
- I attempted local Codex autoreview at P0-P2 against the merged main base. No review was produced: sandbox preflight rejected the installed Codex executable. I did not broaden permissions or request a hosted re-review.

Not verified: live shipped-Gateway missing-owner rejection before trigger/payload work, valid-owner execution and administrator recovery; real upgrades from supported older releases, including v2026.11.5, 9.x extended-stable and 10.x, preserving transferred owners, tool permissions, enabled state and runtime authority; the old updater's round-trip regression; final-head CI and rendered error-state proof. The PR remains draft.

Contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski (GitHub: `vyctorbrzezowski`).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Vyctor Brzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/6c93da9d-2399-422f-8930-dcdd44684b58)

- [Follow-up conflict repair and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-sb3373e2c)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: feat(ios): read and edit a chat's Goal in its sheet
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, the Goal pill above the composer opens a sheet that only lists the goal: its objective, then rows for status, time and tokens. A person can read the goal but cannot pause, resume, edit or delete it from the phone. The Control UI can do all of that.

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. This one makes a chat's Goal readable at a glance and editable from its sheet.

## User Impact

With this PR alone, opening the Goal pill shows:

- The status and elapsed time under the sheet title (for example "Active · 40s").
- The objective in a card, with a progress bar and "184k of 500k tokens" when the goal has a token budget, and the latest note under it.
- An Edit button that turns the objective into a text field, with Save and Cancel.
- A Pause or Resume button, and a trash button that asks "Delete this goal?" before it deletes.
- Messages in place when a change fails or cannot be confirmed. The goal and the typed draft stay as they were, and the person can check the outcome or try again.

While a resume request is running, the Goal pill reads "Resuming goal…". If the answer never arrives, it reads "Goal resume unconfirmed".

The controls use the Gateway's `sessions.goal.update` and `sessions.goal.clear` methods. They are offered only when the Gateway supports those methods and the connection has write or admin access. Without that access, the sheet stays read only.

Still old until later PRs in the series: the pull request pills and their sheets, which a later PR adds next to the Goal pill.

## Why This Change Was Made

A goal is long-running work the agent pursues for a chat. When it runs away, hits a limit, or needs a better objective, the person should be able to act from the chat on their phone instead of switching to a computer. The sheet asks the Gateway for each change and shows only confirmed state, so a failed or lost request never leaves an edit or deletion on screen that did not happen.

## Evidence

The Before screenshots are the series up to the previous PR, not `main`. Both use the app's built-in activity fixture in screenshot mode (no Gateway, no account data).

Before is on the left and After on the right in the first two images. The last two are After only, because their demo chat does not exist before this PR.

![Light mode, the Goal sheet: Before lists the objective with Status and Time rows, After shows "Active" under the title, the objective card, a token bar with "184k of 500k tokens", the latest note, and Delete and Pause buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d3f2b29-ee4b-466f-aea2-dcea312c9462)

![Dark mode, the same Goal sheet: Before is the plain list, After is the card with the token bar, the latest note and the controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/536b7842-6b90-4ea4-958c-ad726486d021)

![After only, light mode: the Goal sheet of a short goal, with "Active · 40s" under the title, Edit, the trash button and Pause](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba594f23-f999-450c-8c5d-1c9fc3271287)

prs.title: improve: test label handoffs without prompting for an approval check
prs.body:
Follow-up to #206987.

## What Problem This Solves

The live handoff test told the agent exactly which approval file to check. It could pass without showing whether the agent would resume the task on its own.

## User Impact

This tightens QA coverage. No production prompt or configuration changes. Both cases get the same user request: **“Continue the label task.”**

## Why This Change Was Made

The drafting conversation holds the user’s rule, the receipt location, the completed item lookup, and the assistant’s old pending status. The continuation has only a pointer to that conversation. The fixture appends history to Gateway-created session IDs without replacing their entries.

A passing turn must recall the task and result from that specific source. It must also observe the unique ID from the current receipt; simply repeating the old “pending” report cannot pass. The test checks the resulting file and rejects a repeated catalog lookup.

## Evidence

The [live regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0fda8b65279329d794ed284031c99aa996a4c3d2/qa/scenarios/agents/recalled-blocker-followthrough-live.yaml#L93-L150) passed on integrated head `0fda8b652793` in 41 seconds. Captured results:

| Current receipt | Fresh receipt seen | Repeated lookups | Label written |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Approved | Yes | 0 | Yes |
| Pending | Yes | 0 | No |

The 19 focused QA helper tests, repository production extensions typecheck, targeted lint, and formatting passed on the same two-file patch before integrating `main`. Local autoreview could not start its read-only sandbox and supplied no verdict. Development runs with a display-only pointer or an unregistered source were not counted as passes.

[ClawSweeper passed this head with no findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207144#issuecomment-7232511807). The [required CI gate failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097705884/job/140835993680) on a different scenario: [subagent-empty-completion-recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097705884/job/140833202061), “expected two exhausted tool-free finalizations.” The same scenario and assertion failed on [main run 46093045417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46093045417/job/140818456433) and [main run 46089297581](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089297581/job/140806521580), both before this PR. That scenario does not use the changed transcript-seeding helper.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

<!-- openclaw-publication:d565825e-6870-4e64-b463-0be5de1cbba8 -->

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: feat(ios): the working line says what the agent is doing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, while the agent works, the line under the transcript shows the claw and a running timer ("11s"), and nothing else. It doesn't say whether the agent is starting up, reasoning, or running a tool, so a person can't tell what the run is doing or whether it's stuck. After a reconnect or a history reload, the line can't name the call that is still running. The Control UI already names each of these states on its working line.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **The working line says what the agent is doing.** Next to the claw it reads the startup phase ("Preparing workspace…", "Preparing this turn…", "Waiting for a response…"), then "Thinking" while the model reasons or between tool calls, then the running call in the tool row's own words, such as "Running cat palette.txt". The timer is gone.
- **Phases don't flash.** A label stays on screen for at least 0.4 seconds (a tool's title for 0.6 seconds), so a phase that passes faster is skipped instead of flashed. "Thinking" doesn't show before the Gateway reports a phase.
- **Under streamed answer text the claw stays without words.** VoiceOver still hears "Working".
- **The running call survives a reconnect.** When history reloads mid-run, the line still names the call that is running ("Running cat west.txt"), finished calls aren't repeated, and a call that ended while offline shows as finished.
- **Tapping the working claw opens the run's calls in the tool sheet.** The sheet follows new calls as they arrive until you scroll it yourself, and keeps earlier calls across the agent's notes between them.

Some parts still look old until later pull requests in the series. The activity pills above the composer show only what the previous pull request added; the status strip, the pull request pills and the Goal page come with their own pull requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The working line is the one place a person looks while a run is in progress, so it should name the current step instead of counting seconds. `ChatRunStartup` now tells reasoning and tool output apart from answer text, `ChatNarration` keeps live commentary and calls in order (including CLI runs that stream one cumulative text), and `ChatTypingIndicatorBubble` draws the line and holds each label long enough to read. The view model keeps a running call's name and completed steps when history reloads, so a reconnect doesn't reset the line. The tool sheet gains a live selection for the current run, which the claw opens.

## Evidence

- UI tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): 9 of 10 passed. `testExternalRunShowsStatusAndToolsBeforeReplyText`, `testHistoryReloadDoesNotDuplicateTheWorkingTools`, `testOpenWorkingClawListKeepsCallsAcrossCommentary`, `testPlainTurnWorkingLineFollowsTheRunInOrder`, `testReconnectFinishesTheCallThatEndedWhileOffline`, `testReconnectKeepsTheRunningToolNameAndCompletedSteps`, `testSettledSingleCallOpensDetailAndBackFindsItInTheTurn`, `testStreamedReplyIsNotDuplicatedWithSavedRow` and `testWorkingClawNarratesTheOnlyActiveToolRow` passed.
  - `testKeyboardOpenPreservesTranscriptAndFollowsLiveEdgeAfterSend` fails before it reaches this change's assertions: it doesn't find the "Worked" row of its demo chat. It fails at the same line without this change.
- OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS: `ChatAssistantRunGroupTests`, `ChatRunStartupStatusTests`, `ChatSessionsCodingTests` and `ChatWorkingProgressTests`. 47 of 48 passed. The one failure, "CLI assistant text keeps its place before each live tool", finds the CLI notes but not the live tool rows between them in the transcript projection. It fails the same way on the final state of the series. I couldn't run these suites on the iOS simulator, because another test target in the package doesn't build for iOS.
  - To build the test target on macOS I restored one missing line in an unrelated, existing test file (`ChatViewModelTests.swift`) for the run only. That line isn't part of this change.
- The iOS app and its unit and UI test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. OpenClawKit builds on macOS. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: demo chats in screenshot mode (no Gateway) on the same simulator, taken at fixed times in each run. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`.
  - Before and after, light and dark: a run with a call in progress. Before shows the claw and "11s"; after shows "Running cat palette.txt".
  - Before and after, light: the same run after a reconnect. Before shows the claw and "4s"; after shows "Running cat west.txt".
  - After only, light: a plain "Hi" turn at "Waiting for a response…", "Thinking", and the streamed answer with the claw alone. This demo turn comes with this change; before it, the demo answers at once, shown as the Before of the "Thinking" pair.
  - The same screens on the final state of the series match the After screens for the working line.
  - The screenshot test was added only for these runs and isn't part of this change.
- Not checked:
  - A real Gateway, including a live run, a real reconnect and a CLI-backed run.
  - VoiceOver on a device, larger text sizes, iPad and landscape.
  - The Mac app's chat on screen (OpenClawKit only builds and runs its tests on macOS).

Before is on the left and After on the right in each of the first four images. The last one is After only.

![Dark mode, the same run: Before shows the claw and "11s", After shows "Running cat palette.txt"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1b6c83f-7552-4b5e-a5ab-22e3904c2083)

![Light mode, the run after a reconnect: Before shows the claw and "4s", After shows "Running cat west.txt"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae22bbe8-43af-4992-808b-bfa54031342a)

![Light mode, a plain "Hi" turn: Before answers at once, After shows the claw and "Thinking"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9627ef39-0220-4622-a769-c5869346fad6)

prs.title: feat(ios): activity pills above the composer, and a Subagents sheet that can stop a run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, a chat doesn't show what is going on around the conversation. When an agent launches subagents, there is no place to see which ones are working, which have finished, or to stop one; the only sign is the parent's own reply. A chat's Goal isn't shown at all. A task plan appears as a wide "Now: …" bar above the composer that cuts its sentence. The Control UI already shows all of this as a short row of pills above the composer, each opening a sheet.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **A row of activity pills rests on the composer.** In the Control UI's order: the working subagents ("2 working", led by their avatars, with a light shimmer while they work), the chat's Goal ("Goal active", "Goal paused" and the other states), and the task plan ("Task progress", with its current step and a count when it has steps). The row stays on one line and scrolls sideways when it is full. The wide plan bar is gone; a plan without steps is a short "Task progress" pill, never a cut sentence.
- **Each pill opens a sheet.** The Subagents sheet lists the running and finished subagents on two tabs ("Running 2", "Finished 2"), with each one's model and time. The task progress sheet lists the steps with the current one marked, and can refresh, dismiss or clear the saved plan. The Goal sheet shows the Goal's status, time, tokens and latest note. A draft in the composer is kept while a sheet is open.
- **A running subagent can be stopped.** Swiping a row in the Running tab shows a Stop button. The subagent moves to Finished as "Stopped". If the stop can't be confirmed, the sheet says so in place.
- **A subagent's conversation opens as a native chat.** Tapping a subagent pushes its chat with a Back button, its task as the title, and "Message subagent" in the composer. Going back returns to the parent chat.
- **The sidebar button in the chat header is round,** the same glass button as the other header controls.

Some parts still look old or are missing until later pull requests in the series:

- The Goal sheet is read-only here. The controls to pause, resume, edit and clear a Goal, and its final layout, come with the Goal pull request.
- Pull request pills and their sheet come with their own pull request.
- The connection status strip above the pills, and the approval card's place in the same dock, come with later pull requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pills read the state the chat already has: the session's child sessions for subagents, the session's Goal (`OpenClawChatSessionEntry.goal`, decoded here), and the existing progress card. `ChatActivityRules` turns that into pills in the Control UI's order, `ChatActivityDock` places the row above the composer and owns the sheet, and `ChatActivityChildren` keeps the subagent roster, including children outside the loaded page of sessions. Stopping goes through a transport protocol (`OpenClawChildStopTransport`) so the Gateway transport and the demo transport share one path. The subagent chat reuses the existing chat screen with the child's session key instead of a separate view.

## Evidence

- Navigation regression (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.2): 1/1 passed on the port. Edge-back keeps the voice note in the subagent chat; after finishing and removing the attachment, both the edge gesture and Back return to the parent chat.

- Current-main port: the app and UI test bundle built, with SwiftFormat and SwiftLint enabled. `native:i18n:verify` reported `changed=false` (5101 entries). On iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 27.2), 6 unit tests and all 15 scoped UI tests passed. On macOS, all 12 `ChatActivityTests` passed. The port keeps the current sidebar and the route to a subagent chat. The visual evidence below remains from the original approved cut.

- The iOS app and its unit and UI test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases, with no findings. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChildActivityTranscriptTests` and `SubagentStopTests`, 6 of 6 passed.
- OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS: `ChatActivityTests`, 12 of 12 passed. OpenClawKit builds on macOS.
  - To build the test target on macOS I restored one missing line in an unrelated, existing test file (`ChatViewModelTests.swift`) for the run only. That line isn't part of this change.
- UI tests on the same simulator, 15 of 15 passed: `testActivityPillsOpenTheirSheetsAndKeepTheDraft`, `testActivityPillsSitInOneRowAboveTheComposer`, `testActivitySheetsShowFailuresInPlace`, `testNativeSubagentConversation`, `testNativeSubagentSwipeStopsWithoutLeavingList`, `testSubagentCodeScrollAndNativeEdgeBack`, `testSubagentHeaderRemainsStableOnFailure`, `testSubagentHeaderUsesSessionChatControlFrames`, `testSubagentPickerKeepsEqualWidthsAcrossDigitChanges`, `testSubagentScrollEdgeDark`, `testSubagentScrollEdgeLight`, `testTaskListProgressTagRendersAsBar`, `testWaitingSubagentRemainsInRunningAndOffersStop`, `testLandscapeSubagentHeaderShowsTitleOnOneLine` and `testLandscapeChatHeaderKeepsFirstMessageClear`.
- Screenshots: the demo chat in screenshot mode (no Gateway) on the same simulator, with its activity demo data. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`.
  - Before and after, light: the chat with subagents, a Goal and a plan; the chat with only a Goal; the chat with a plan without steps. Before and after, dark: the chat with subagents, a Goal and a plan.
  - After only, light: the Subagents sheet (Running and Finished), a swiped row showing Stop, and a subagent's chat. Before has no such screens.
  - The same screens on the final state of the series match the After screens for the pills, the Subagents sheet and the subagent chat.
  - The screenshot test was added only for these runs and isn't part of this change.
- Not checked:
  - A real Gateway, including stopping a real subagent run and a reconnect while the sheet is open.
  - VoiceOver, larger text sizes and iPad.
  - The Mac app's chat on screen (OpenClawKit only builds and runs its tests on macOS).

Before is on the left and After on the right in each of the first four images. The last four are After only.

prs.title: fix: let unpinned automations use live inference accounts
prs.body:
Related: #202699 (first, non-breaking cut)

## What Problem This Solves

An automation created without a recorded inference account stops running after its session switches to a stored account, even though an interactive turn works. It fails with "Automation has no recorded inference account." The same refusal blocks stored-account fallbacks, scheduled CLI runs on native login, and creation on non-stored credential routes such as AWS SDK.

## User Impact

Unbound automations use the account an interactive turn would select. Session-target jobs follow the session's current account choice, including an explicit switch, and fallbacks select credentials live. **Existing recorded bindings, including automatically captured ones, stay authoritative.** Explicit `model@profile` pins, replacement and revocation refusal, #207097's auto-disable for a signed-out recorded account, configured-key recovery of a dead binding, native-CLI credential isolation, schedules and run history are unchanged. Unbound jobs need no migration or manual adoption.

## Why This Change Was Made

This removes the refusal instead of building another account-authorization layer around it, and reuses the existing live-selection planner and fallback chain. Removed with it:
- its startup scan;
- the Doctor lint and adoption for unbound jobs;
- the refusal classification, alert text and operator-refusal cause added by #205873. Those only described a refusal that no longer happens.

Doctor's receipt-backed restoration of recorded accounts after a state upgrade is kept. Binding capture at creation and `current` target behavior are unchanged. This PR does **not** soften existing bindings or stop capturing them for new jobs; that would change a working path.

Review follow-ups in this revision:
- An unbound session-target turn now keeps the session's explicit account as the fallback runner's locked profile, the same as an interactive turn. Before, admission checked only the provider's normal order.
- Creating a job whose selected profile is a configured AWS SDK profile keeps the job unbound instead of refusing it for lacking a stored secret.
- Docs limit the interactive-parity wording to credential selection.

## Evidence

Head `b777e9effd2b07a8677f9f01b47a02e51a7c891b`, rebased on main `adb37164c59d`. Mergeable: clean.

- **Real model via ClawRouter, Studio Crabbox `local-container`, isolated Gateway.** Unbound session job; the owner switches the session to stored account B.
  - Base `adb37164`: `error`, "Automation has no recorded inference account…", no provider request.
  - Fix: `ok` / `succeeded`. The main turn ran on B (HTTP 200, 1024-token limit). A separate Activity recap ran on the utility account A (240-token limit).
  - A relay mapped the synthetic account aliases to one real ClawRouter key and sent upstream model `gpt-4.1-mini`. It recorded aliases and statuses only, never credentials or headers.
- **Upgrade from latest stable `2026.11.11`.** Jobs were created and run on stable, then the fixed source build took over the same state and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0. After that, the default model moved to `gpt-4o`, the account order became b,a, and the session switched to B:

| Job created on 2026.11.11 | After upgrade + drift |
|---|---|
| Explicit `model@openai:a` | `ok`, account A |
| Automatically captured account A | `ok`, account A (drift would select B if the binding were lost) |
| Configured key | `ok`, configured key |
| Unbound session job, session switched to B | `ok`, account B (refused on base) |

  Run-history counts matched before and after the upgrade for all five jobs. No inference-account startup warnings appeared, and `doctor --lint` reported no cron-inference-accounts finding.
  **Gap:** the harness's row-level `cron_jobs.job_json` snapshot queried a nonexistent `id` column and captured nothing. Binding preservation is therefore shown behaviorally (above), not by a stored-row diff. The disabled cron-expression job's settings were not separately compared. `2026.11.6` was not run: its CLI failed `models auth paste-api-key` in a fresh state before any job existed, so no PR code was involved.
- An earlier comparison against a synthetic endpoint, before the rebase, covered all five cases (session switch, explicit pin, auto-captured binding, configured key, failing primary with stored-account fallback). Base refused the session switch and the fallback; the fix ran all five.
- **Tests on the rebased head:** 13 directly affected files passed across 4 Vitest shards (gateway, infra, cron, commands). Two new regression tests, one for each review follow-up, failed on the previous head and pass now.
- `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint, core and test typechecks, and all ratchets pass. The dead-export scan reports only `src/agents/harness/types.ts: AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest`, an untouched file inherited from main; it is not claimed green.
- Independent Astra review of the rebased diff reported two P2s, both fixed above with red-then-green tests. It confirmed: no remaining references to removed symbols; recorded-binding enforcement unchanged; native-only credential stripping intact; #207097's classification intact.
- No UI change, so no screenshots. Managed artifact upload returned HTTP 401, so evidence is inline. All proof leases stopped (`cbx_b77f7c83bd4d`, `cbx_00660f730d5c`, `cbx_ec885a275d37`).

prs.title: refactor(subagents): simplify ACP spawn relay ownership
prs.body:
Closes #207021.

## What Problem This Solves

ACP spawn and parent progress relay maintenance crosses repeated eligibility checks, unused relay inputs, and lifecycle guards already enforced by the event owner. This is the maintainer-requested R6 cleanup of that circuit.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. ACP admission errors, thread delivery, captured parent targets, progress buffering, stall notices, and terminal cleanup retain their contracts.

The coordinator approved the remaining mechanical test migration after L8/R4 merged [#207016](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207016). That migration is included. Current source head: `48535d539a9fd82683c9a2436cce3cc933de043d`; normal PR CI is green in [run 46099378808](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46099378808). Ordinary full-subagent coverage is complete across [run 46098767036](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46098767036) and its scoped infrastructure retry; unrelated broader failures are recorded below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requester resolver now returns the final parent-stream decision. Spawn prepares one optional relay context for both the initial and remapped run ID. The relay consumes its run-scoped subscription and timer lifecycle instead of repeating their guards. Unused environment, owner ID, and child-session ID plumbing is removed.

### Circuit map and writers

| State / inputs | Writer and effects |
| --- | --- |
| Request policy, target, mode, requester routing | Existing policy owners validate configuration and request facts. The requester resolver reads the binding/session route and decides whether to stream. Failures retain their distinct error codes. |
| Child creation entry, runtime rollback handle, binding | The ACP adapter's initialize phase writes the child row through the session accessor, initializes the ACP manager, and binds the prepared thread. The adapter retains the local creation/rollback handles. |
| Delivery plan, run ID, optional parent relay | Dispatch records child lineage, starts the relay before the Gateway call, then replaces that relay if the Gateway returns a different run ID. The shared spawn pipeline registers the run and owns failure sequencing. |
| Pending text/kind, replaceable assistant snapshot, item snapshots, activity timestamps | Only this relay's event callback and flush/stall timers update these process-local fields. Assistant, item, ACP diagnostic, and lifecycle streams retain distinct handling. |
| Disposed flag, timer handles, event subscription | dispose sets the flag once, clears every timer, unsubscribes, and removes the void-returning host abort listener. Terminal delivery, timeout, host abort, and spawn failure use the same operation. |
| Parent event delivery | The captured target and routing policy go to the existing session-event owner. Relay emission does not create a competing target or authority owner. |

### Deleted duplicate or dead paths

- The old stream helper re-tested subagent identity, lack of active binding, and lack of thread context, although the requester resolver's usable-route result already required all three. The final decision now has one owner; the old helper and four intermediate result fields are gone.
- Relay construction re-tested facts already established while capturing the parent target. One prepared optional context now serves both run IDs.
- The event bus selects only the subscribed run and skips inactive registrations. dispose synchronously unsubscribes and clears timers, so the callback's run-ID/disposed checks and the timer callbacks' disposed checks were redundant. Public late notifyStarted calls and repeated dispose calls remain guarded.
- Pending text already implies a pending kind; a non-prefix snapshot implies a nonempty previous snapshot; clearing an empty pending buffer needs no separate branch. The replaceable snapshot was already checked before storage.
- childSessionId, ownerAgentId, and env had no relay readers. The copied environment and flattened initialized-session ID therefore had no remaining consumer.
- Single-use flush scheduling and snapshot-flush wrappers are deleted. The existing void abort callback remains necessary for the EventTarget contract. No new helper extraction was used to reduce complexity.

### Complexity and necessary remainder

Measured with code-sloppiness 0.2.0+vk.4 on frozen base b5c0a7d34784f087cdc0e89932044ff116660d68 (run 11) and production-identical head cc51b2ad279f0dd6bf30b2e965a562835e7aded8 (run 25; the subsequent commit only migrates a test). Both are complete four-file selections without parse failures.

| Function | Before CC / SLOC | After CC / SLOC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spawnAcpDirect | 56 / 453 | 50 / 450 |
| startAcpSpawnParentStreamRelay | 68 / 243 | 58 / 227 |

The targets are not halved. The remaining decisions are retained deliberately:

- Spawn distinguishes participation, ACP-enabled policy, missing requester context, sandbox policy, inherited allow/deny restrictions, session/thread requirements, target resolution, sender policy, allowed-agent policy, child admission, resume ownership, runtime options, cwd failures, binding failures, reservation failures, and pipeline failure. These have distinct existing errors or effects. Initialization preserves conditional lineage/tool-policy/workspace stamps and optional binding; registration preserves run/session cleanup and inline/completion behavior. Removing these decisions changes supported contracts. Extracting their single-use branches would only move the metric.
- The relay retains its event protocol: assistant snapshot/delta selection, replaceable output, commentary opt-in, item/preamble identity and prefix replacement, prompt/runtime diagnostic phases, status-tag visibility, and terminal success/error/duration handling. Buffer limits, flush boundaries, four distinct stall diagnoses, delivery warnings, and idempotent disposal remain necessary.

The requester resolver changes from CC 10 to 13 while absorbing and deleting the CC 7 stream-decision helper.

These nested sections are already included in the parent CC numbers:

| Retained section | CC | Contract requiring its branches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ACP initialization | 9 | Incognito parent reads, conditional child policy/workspace stamps, optional thread binding |
| ACP dispatch | 6 | Optional creation event, optional relay, and Gateway run-ID remapping |
| Registration builder | 4 | Inline-vs-parent completion and persistent-vs-one-shot cleanup |
| Relay event callback | 33 | Stream-specific payloads, commentary/tag visibility, snapshot replacement, terminal events |
| Visible progress buffer | 8 | Stall recovery, kind boundaries, bounded UTF-16 tail, immediate/timed flush |
| Item snapshot handling | 5 | Repeat suppression, prefix deltas, replacement of pending snapshots |
| Stall notice selection | 6 | Not submitted, no runtime event, no visible output, later output stall |
| Event emission / disposal | 4 / 2 | Delivery diagnostics and one-time resource cleanup |

Physical production lines: 56 added, 99 removed, net **-43**. Tests: net **-1**, removing assertions on deleted unused relay arguments and migrating the incognito requester assertion. Metadata: one obsolete identity-allowance row removed.

Decision-line census using git grep -c -E 'if \(|\? |&&|\|\|' on the four production files: spawn 54→51; relay 62→58; requester 17→13; runtime 18→18 (151→140 total). This counts matching lines separately from AST CC. Retired helper/plumbing production references are zero; all known callers and tests use the final decision contract.

### Mechanical caller updates and coordinator authorization

The owned ACP caller and its test are updated. config/session-identity-allowlist.txt drops only the ACP relay row, matching the ratchet's measured reduction from two identity-check sites to zero.

The coordinator explicitly authorized R6 to edit `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.incognito.test.ts` after L8/R4 merged [#207016](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207016). The test now supplies the three explicit run/stream options and asserts `streamToParent: false`. Its existing memory-backed delivery assertion is preserved. This fixes both TS2739 and the runtime assertion on removed intermediate fields.

### Open PR overlap

Other work touched the ACP spawn surface when this branch started: [#197123](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197123), [#188442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188442), [#192627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192627), [#188492](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188492), and test cleanup [#206929](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206929). Their changes are not incorporated.

## Evidence

- Current-head P0-P2 branch review is scoped-clean. Its unchanged-predicate context caveat was checked directly on base and head: sessionRelayRouteUsable already requires a subagent requester, no active binding, and no thread context. Formatting and git diff --check pass.
- [Normal PR CI 46099378808](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46099378808) passed on source head `48535d539a9fd82683c9a2436cce3cc933de043d`, testing merge checkout `8d82759287ca49fe311f0fb1eaf940a06da7c0df` against captured main `4e06d657fcd58e8838ddeb7e3710a6feb026ed8d`. All selected runtime, types, lint, guards and security checks passed.
- [Full coverage 46098767036](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46098767036) passed its build-artifacts job. The canonical plan routes 178 ordinary subagent test files; all rows containing them finished, with no reported failing test inside `src/agents/subagents`. Ten separately configured live/e2e files are outside that ordinary plan; no live-channel proof is claimed.
- The only unexecuted ordinary-subagent group in the first full attempt was blocked before tests by a public ripgrep asset download returning HTTP 403. After the asset returned HTTP 200, one scoped infrastructure retry ran that row: [job 140848929021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46098767036/job/140848929021). Its unit-fast, agent-core-runtime and storage-state groups passed. The row failed only on `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-state-read-capacity.test.ts` worker teardown, outside this change. No product test was rerun to claim a fix.
- Broader full-run failures remain visible: the unused CLI export `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`, missing native translations, worker cleanup receipts in node-host/system-agent/Doctor/shared-state tests, Doctor archive fixtures missing `schema_meta`, and the sibling native-reasoning prefix performance timeout. None of those paths changed in this PR. The CLI export failure matches [scheduled main run 46093045417](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46093045417), with byte-identical source. Main's sampled prefix/worker cases passed; those intermittent failures are not claimed fixed or deterministically inherited.
- Earlier direct-head [CI 46098172462](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46098172462) passed all selected runtime rows, all source test-type stripes, production types, core/extension lint, the identity ratchet and security. Its only failure was the same CLI export. The corrected incognito runtime/type, lint and ratchet failures from the earlier source revision are cleared.
- Source work remained code-only. No Testbox was allocated and no shared installation was changed. Native preparation preserves the exact source head; no release or publication outside this PR is authorized.

prs.title: fix(plugins): ask the activation resolver instead of reading plugin policy by hand
prs.body:
## Problem
Three places re-derive settings instead of asking the owner the runtime uses (#205672 cases 2 and 3; #201988 follow-up). Each one gives a wrong answer when a setting is set only in the per-entry or per-agent config.
- **`/tools` browser notice** (`src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.ts`) reads `plugins.allow` by hand. With an empty allowlist and `plugins.entries.browser.enabled: false`, it blames `plugins.allow`, which is not the cause.
- **OpenShell File Transfer gate** (`extensions/openshell/src/worker-workspace.ts`) does a hand-made exact-id check. A padded deny entry (`" File-Transfer "`) passes it, so agent workspace binding does not keep the operator's File Transfer restriction.
- **Doctor Codex bwrap hint** (`src/commands/doctor-sandbox.ts`) reads only `agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.network`. An agent's own network setting changes how the runtime starts that sandbox, but Doctor ignores it. The result is a wrong network-namespace probe and a wrong hint.

## Solution
- The browser notice and the OpenShell gate call `resolveEffectiveEnableState`, the same resolver the plugin loader uses. This is the same fix as #207215.
- The bwrap check reads `docker.network` from every container sandbox that `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent` resolves (already used for the engine since #207213), including sandboxes a gateway role requires. It probes the network namespace when any of them has no egress. Whether the check runs at all still follows a mode-on sandbox, as before. The hint no longer names one engine for every sandbox.

## Impact
- Users with an empty allowlist see a correct `/tools` browser notice; a padded File Transfer deny entry now keeps its restriction.
- Users with a per-agent sandbox network get the correct Codex bwrap check on Linux.
- No config, schema or wire change.

## Evidence
- New tests are red on `main` and green on this branch (inventory blame rows, the OpenShell padded-deny row, and the bwrap resolved-network rows). Controls pass on both.
- The plugin-activation diff is the one Fable 5.2 reviewed (no finding). It applies to current `main` without change.
- The bwrap change had two Fable 5.2 rounds. Round 1 found three issues: role-required sandboxes were skipped, the test did not prove "any", and the hint named one engine. All three are fixed. Round 2 found no regression.
- Accepted edge case (round 2): when a gateway role requires a sandbox, #207213 counts the defaults entry as a sandbox. Its network (`none` unless set) can start the network-namespace probe when every listed agent has egress. The result is an extra check, not a missed one. A warning appears only on hosts that deny the network namespace.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop utility fallbacks when the caller cancels its own attempt
prs.body:
## Problem

A utility task that cancels its own work makes the fallback chain run the next utility model.

- The Activity recap, titles and transcript summaries pass a currency guard (`assertCurrent`) to `runUtilityCompletion`. The guard throws when the task's own work goes stale: the recap's session changed or a newer recap took over ("Activity recap lifecycle or utility model changed"), the title owner retired, or a newer transcript capture owner took the lane.
- When it throws, the caller's abort signal is still live. The fallback runner's only cancel fact is that signal (`resolveChainStopReason`, `model-fallback-attempt.ts`), so it counts the throw as a model failure and starts the next utility model.
- Real-user log signature (a production team Gateway, 4.35 h): 72 `model_fallback_decision candidate_failed` on the utility primary with the recap's self-cancel error; 19 of them went on to a configured utility fallback that the runtime does not offer, each failing with `model_not_found` and a "Activity recap deferred" line.

## Change

`runUtilityCompletion` (the one owner every utility user goes through) wraps the caller's `assertCurrent` on the fallback path. When it throws, a local controller is aborted with that same error and the error is rethrown. The chain receives `AbortSignal.any([caller, local])`, so the existing caller-cancel stop applies. No error-name or message match, no new error class, no runner change.

- A real model failure with a current caller still falls back (test).
- The no-fallback path is unchanged: with one candidate there is no next model to stop.

## User impact

- Recaps, titles, transcript notes and composer predictions that go stale stop at once instead of trying the next utility model, and a stale recap no longer produces a fallback `model_not_found` error or a retry delay. The chain logs one `model fallback chain stopped reason=caller_signal_aborted` line instead.
- Not changed: progress narration and the session observer already cancel through their abort signal.

## Evidence

| Test | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `utility-completion.runtime.test.ts`: guard throws the recap's `AbortError`, caller signal live | 3 model calls | 1 |
| `conversation-label-generator.test.ts`: title owner retires during the utility attempt | `gpt-mini`, `utility-backup` | `gpt-mini` |
| `summary-model.test.ts`: a newer capture owner takes the summary lane during the attempt (real lane-generation guard) | `utility-test-model`, `utility-backup` | `utility-test-model` |
| Guard present, model fails with a timeout | falls back | falls back |

- Each red was run with main's `utility-completion.ts` against the new tests; all green with the change. The three touched test files pass in full (19, 21 and 18 tests).
- `tsgo:core`, core test typecheck and oxlint on the touched files are clean.
- Adversarial review: land. Its one gap is taken: composer prediction's custom runner called the raw caller guard (`composer-prediction-completion.ts`), so its throw bypassed the wrapper; it now calls the candidate's guard. The review also confirmed that the wrapper sees only the caller's guard: the operator-model check, the timeout and the closed check inside isolated completion still fall back as before.
- Local review on head `e0b861ed`: patch is correct, 0 findings, security cleared.
- Live proof gap (named): the self-cancel is a timing race (the session changes or a newer task takes over during the model call), so an isolated Gateway run cannot trigger it on demand. The tests drive the real guards (recap error shape, the title owner's guard, the transcript lane generation) through the real fallback runner. Production confirmation is the post-deploy log count: the recap self-cancel fallback decisions should go from 72 per 4.35 h to 0.

prs.title: fix(ai): key the malformed-tool-call argument digest
prs.body:
Related: #202672

## What Problem This Solves

The bounded diagnostics published for a rejected terminal tool call carry `argumentHash`, which is `shortHash(text)` - an unsalted, fast, non-cryptographic hash of the raw argument buffer.

Published that way, the digest confirms guessed content. It identifies a buffer *to someone who already has the content*, but an observer who holds only the digest can test candidate buffers and learn which one was rejected. That is the opposite of the property the field is documented to have:

```ts
/**
 * Bounded, content-free diagnostics for a rejected terminal argument buffer. ...
 */
```

"Content-free" holds only while the digest is not a bare function of the content.

## User Impact

A published `argumentHash` no longer confirms guessed argument content. The digest still identifies a buffer within an install - operators keep correlating repeated rejections of the same buffer - but it cannot be used to recover what the buffer said.

This matters most where the digest leaves the install: it is written to the provider-error log line, and it is rendered into user-facing failure copy, where a user pasting that copy into a bug report publishes the oracle to whoever reads it.

## Why This Change Was Made

From the digest published in a log line, a dictionary over realistic tool-argument shapes recovers the exact rejected buffer. Recovering

```
{"path": "/tmp/openclaw-stub-target.txt", "content": "partial
```

took **83 candidates** over plausible keys (`path`, `file`, `cmd`, ...) x plausible paths x truncation points - no knowledge of the secret needed, only the shape of a tool argument.

A faster hash would not help; only keying the digest does. This change derives it with a per-install secret, mirroring how the config journal already fingerprints config snapshots (`config-journal-fingerprint.key` -> `createHmac("sha256", key)`).

The secret lives beside the other install-scoped material in the state directory, is created once with `0600`, and is never logged or exported. Hosts own the digest so the package keeps its current freedom from state-directory access; the plain digest stays the fallback when no host provides one, so embedding hosts are unaffected.

## Evidence

The recovery, from the published digest alone:

```
$ node .openclaw/tmp/dictattack2.mjs
candidates tried: 83
RECOVERED from the published digest alone:
  "{\"path\": \"/tmp/openclaw-stub-target.txt\", \"content\": \"partial"
  (key=path value=/tmp/openclaw-stub-target.txt truncatedAt=61)
```

Recovering that payload took 83 guesses because the payload was a plausible one; a payload drawn from a narrower space takes fewer. The digest is a confirmation oracle, which is the property being removed.

New coverage:

- `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.digest.test.ts` - *"uses the host-provided digest when one is configured"*, *"falls back to the plain digest when no host digest is available"*, and *"never exposes the rejected buffer in the digest"*.
- `src/llm/diagnostic-digest-key.test.ts` - the digest is stable for the same value within one install, differs for different values, differs for the same value across installs, and never contains the digested value.

Existing coverage kept green: `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` and `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` still pass, including the truncated-sibling case that requires truncated sibling arguments to stay rejected.

Focused tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.digest.test.ts \
    src/llm/diagnostic-digest-key.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

Whole package suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/ai/
 Test Files  170 passed (170)
      Tests  2480 passed | 3 skipped (2483)
```

Format and lint on the touched files:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check packages/ai/src/host.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.digest.test.ts \
    src/llm/diagnostic-digest-key.ts src/llm/diagnostic-digest-key.test.ts \
    src/llm/ai-transport-host.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <same files>
✓ No problems in 6 files
```

## Scope

Only the digest derivation changes. Rejection behaviour, JSON repair, streaming, recovery, and failover are untouched, and the diagnostic field names and shapes are unchanged - `argumentHash` is still a bounded digest string of the same length class, so consumers that gate on its shape keep working.

Note that `argumentHash` becomes install-scoped rather than globally stable: two installs digesting the same buffer produce different values. That is the point - it is what makes the digest unconfirmable - and it matches how the config journal already scopes its fingerprints.

**Interaction with the open PRs on #202672.** #202717 propagates the bounded diagnostics into the provider-error log line, and #203004 also renders the digest into user-facing failure copy. Both are shaped against the digest's current form. This change alters the digest's derivation but not its shape, so both remain valid; if this lands first, they may want to rebase.

I am not touching #202717's own content-exclusion gate, which is a separate and independently correct hardening (that PR restricts the logged digest to OpenClaw's own digest shape, so a provider-crafted `cause` cannot inject arbitrary text into the log line).

## November 7 current-main refresh

Published head: `fabedf1d10bb952cfa91b21823ba1d57e4faad23`; qualified base: `d4d6fe725bff2be867784d666e1d2118b9e2f41a`. Refreshed onto main without conflicts using the managed, history-preserving base-integration workflow (not a history-rewriting rebase). The 16-file focused patch is unchanged by this refresh; all 16 published blob hashes match the locally reviewed/tested candidate. No budget increases, coverage reductions, or unrelated source fixes were added.

Current-candidate verification (Node 24.22.1; frozen dependency install):
- Production core, agents-root test, and gateway-other test typechecks passed.
- Seven focused authority/identity/prefix/plugin suites: 89 tests passed. The rebuilt standalone Gateway/TLS + actual HTTP read/unsent-draft test passed (8.934 seconds test time), including role revocation, disconnect, profile replacement, and multi-person steering controls. It uses a deterministic model fixture, **not live-provider inference**.
- Native focused lint: 13 files clean; formatting: 14 files clean; whitespace and line-cap ratchet passed. Test-line ratchet: 6,556,905 / 6,556,914 (9 lines headroom). This resolves the prior-head ratchet failure without changing its ceiling or this PR's exact 893-line allocations.
- Independent current-candidate Auto Review: scoped-clean P0–P2; no actionable finding. This is source review, not maintainer approval.
- Full-repository lint is **not green**: max-lines errors occur in four files identical to the pinned base: `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`, `src/agents/plugin-model-catalog.ts`, and `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.ts`.
- `pnpm build` completed its reported phases, producing the runtime exercised above, but the tool then failed workspace artifact synchronization on size. This is **not a clean build-tool completion claim**. Its UI diagnostics also reported JS gzip overages (largest bundle 547.9/547.4 KiB, chat boot 1260.1/1258.8 KiB, new boot 779.7/778.7 KiB). No UI files or limits were changed. Generated task build/compiler artifacts were cleaned afterward.

Current-head GitHub CI completed successfully on `fabedf1d10bb952cfa91b21823ba1d57e4faad23`: **130 terminal checks (69 success, 60 skipped, 1 neutral), zero pending/failing checks, and all 3 commit statuses successful**. The [aggregate CI/security gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42360572400) confirms CI and applicable security-review requirements passed; all six Security High boundary checks succeeded. Full unauthenticated REST pagination was checked because the native display caps checks at 100. GitHub reports the PR cleanly mergeable. Prior-head results below are historical, not inherited proof. The PR remains open for maintainer product/SDK and security review, not merged; no new hosted diamond rating is asserted.


### Prior-head CI result (November 5)

Run [41972784926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972784926) completed on `dbe22b7be800`: all applicable test/type/build jobs passed. The only failing root job is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,480,148 test lines versus ceiling 6,480,128 (20 inherited main lines on the tested merge; own +893 exactly allocated). The aggregate CI gate follows that failure. No further baseline increase was made.

Related: #166721

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin tools being unable to identify a verified Control UI requester even though the Gateway has authenticated that person. Tools requiring both a person and owner permission fail closed because operator UI turns intentionally have no transport sender ID.

## User Impact

Plugins can opt into a separate, live `context.requesterProfile` (`{ id, assertCurrent }`) for a proven single-person Control UI turn. `requesterSenderId`, `senderIsOwner`, and resource policies retain their meanings. Existing plugins need not change; new consumers must fail closed on older hosts or unsupported/unproven turns.

**Maintainer product/SDK and security decision requested:** please assess the optional public shape, initial Control UI-only scope, and rejection once multiple people steer a turn. This proposal is for review, not an accepted contract. Maintainers can request changes or close it if another direction is preferred. No merge, deployment, or production-state change is requested or performed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the private profile, reply snapshot, participant, admitted-run and plugin-lifetime owners. Match the exact agent/session/run and host-issued operator authority. Recheck identity and invocation in the final synchronous effect admission after awaits; resource/owner policy remains independent. Preserve synthetic-ingress rejection and original-client liveness without restoring ingress execution context around plugins. Steerers never replace the requester; ambiguous turns fail closed. No new store, config, protocol or OAuth mapping. Already-dispatched work cannot be retracted.

### Related identity work and dependencies

Pinned main `a5b6c876b9c5d806a7808a970333d3aba609b8a6` retains the gap. Bounded searches and patch comparisons found no duplicate factory fix:

- #187952 `f9ed2281`: hook/memory observation, not factory authority. Shared `requester-profile.ts` needs reconciliation; this fixes source liveness rather than adding a context snapshot.
- #177356 `4780daa5` and #188164 `6e19a644`: overlapping MCP alternatives, not factory fixes. No OAuth/store dependency; single-participant semantics align with #188164. Do not combine both wholesale.
- #164607 `28be4999`: channel-link Profile UI, not external-account verification. No link-management or sender-ID promotion here.
- #164825 `0421a29e`: optional setup display name; presentation remains distinct from authentication.
- #163765 `4f0365c1` / #162164: native personal sign-in/Dashboard work. This consumes admitted identity; device admission and Shared owner fallback are unchanged.
- Landed #159850 / #164593: preserve participant/steering and Shared owner naming semantics.

No hard dependency on these open PRs; shared requester/caller owners may need textual reconciliation. No new native, MCP or profile-UI qualification is claimed. Trusted-plugin contract, not in-process isolation; JSON/prompt/client claims, names or pairing confer no personal authority.
## Evidence

### New protected-effect runtime qualification

The current E2E launches the **built Gateway through its real CLI as a separate owned process**. Public `system.info.pid` must equal the child PID and differ from the test process. A real TLS proxy forwards WebSocket traffic to the Gateway; trusted-proxy authentication/device admission remain separate from profile roles. Public `chat.send` drives the native agent and disk-loaded V2 plugin. No client object, profile binding or run/participant authority is fabricated. Model transport remains a deterministic HTTP fixture, not live-provider inference.

| Case | Observed effect boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Personal administrator | Three model requests drive read → consume result/draft → completion. One real HTTP read and one draft POST. Service persists `.eml` with `X-Unsent: 1` and verified profile ID; sender absent, independent owner true. |
| Personal non-admin | Public `users.setRole`, then a fresh connection: neither protected tool exposed; explicit allowlist fails closed before model/protected HTTP dispatch. Artifact unchanged. |
| Role revoked during preparation | After read, plugin awaits unprotected preparation. Public `users.setRole` commits revocation. Release reaches explicit final-guard refusal: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. Preparation does not consume cancellation in place of the guard. |
| Disconnect during preparation | Presence first confirms live connection, then server-observed retirement. Release reaches final-guard refusal: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |
| Profile merge during preparation | Public `users.merge` returns a different canonical profile. Final guard refuses: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |
| Second participant during preparation | Second human `chat.send` steers a shared session. Test-plugin RPC probes the original captured guard and confirms the existing several-participants error without reading process-private maps. Final guard refuses: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |

All data/services are synthetic and owned; no peer-send operation exists. Assertions inspect actual request counts and persisted bytes, not merely a post-return error. Fixture closes Gateway, clients and servers.

- Standalone E2E passed: **8.865s tests / 15.72s Vitest** with built runtime. Owning gateway-other types, type-aware lint, format, whitespace and line/test budgets pass. Full `pnpm build` exits 0; its unrelated CSS-budget diagnostic is retained, not suppressed.
- Fresh full-candidate Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2): **scoped-clean**, no findings; not independent test execution or maintainer approval.
- Production unchanged from `ba43c981`, whose [canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41224971308) and [CI/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41225661116) passed. New-head CI/seconds remain separate.
- Earlier **19 factory**, **93 V1/V2/optional**, **10 profile-authority** cases, authenticated chat E2E, steering/participant/prefix checks, core/test types and focused lint passed. Factory success regression is red on pinned main: missing tools.

Type repair: reproduced CI’s `Duplex`/`Socket` mismatch, used the actual `Duplex` contract, and passed the owning gateway-other typecheck (gateway-root excluded this file). Runtime logic unchanged.

**Historical CI at the original head:** `1da24df421a0591b42398d52228afca92d761078` passes [canonical CI 41243692223](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41243692223), including the owning test types and selected runtime checks, plus [CI/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244386624). GitHub reports mergeable/clean; the PR remains open and unmerged.

Earlier `3971b5a` CI passed requester proof but timed out in untouched restart/resume (180s, classification unknown). Exact local shard-order replay passed all 13 cases; that is not a causal fix or proof of inheritance. The later type-only fixture correction is independently reproduced red/green. No CI rerun, timeout increase or guard change. ClawSweeper rated the standalone proof **diamond 5/6**, with no findings or before-merge items, at pre-type-correction `b316ade8`; runtime logic is unchanged.

**Limits:** no live-provider inference: no isolated model credential, and configured remote-proof doctor failed before allocation because Blacksmith CLI is unavailable. No paid provider/new credential selected. New full-E2E baseline attempt hit a 240s command bound during compiled-subprocess preparation: no product verdict, not red proof. Factory regression retains its red comparison. Codex app-server, native-device, peer-send and rollout proof remain outside scope.

No new production logic in this update. Production remains **+124 net lines** using existing owners. The 403-line boundary and 490-line standalone fixtures cover distinct authority risks with exact allocations; shared budget unchanged.
## Historical focus-week conflict and CI repair

Prior repair head (November 5): `dbe22b7be800ef631a8311e69030be39fc11f2bf`. Integrated main through `6f975afb9213581bc225dba2417f638c49c828e2`, including the separately approved inherited test-budget correction in #193183. The PR remains open and unmerged; this repair does not approve its product/SDK contract or security design.

- Resolved the original `gateway-personal-caller.ts` conflict by preserving both the requester's source/ambient synthetic-caller checks and main's attended-session creator semantics. No product or public-contract expansion was introduced by the repair.
- Repair head `279ada00da472fca109787e1c39e6cff81bb653c` passed **70 focused tests**: requester-profile/prompt-prefix (33) and account-authority (37), plus core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks. Full-candidate P0–P2 AutoReview was scoped-clean. These are prior-head results, not a claim that current-head CI has passed.
- The subsequent main integration was conflict-free. All 16 PR-specific files remain byte-for-byte identical to that reviewed repair; the candidate remains +1,078/-8 against integrated main. Ordinary commit hooks and whitespace checks passed. No runtime or standalone E2E rerun is claimed for this mechanical integration.
- **Prior-head inherited CI issue (superseded by the November 7 qualification above):** the canonical test-line ratchet reports 6,480,151 lines against a 6,480,127 ceiling, 24 over. This PR adds exactly 893 test lines with matching 893 allocations; the remaining 24-line debt is inherited from the integrated main baseline. No scalar or allocation was increased by this repair, and the failure is not relabeled green.
- Fresh GitHub CI must qualify `dbe22b7be800ef631a8311e69030be39fc11f2bf`; older successful CI and runtime evidence above remain historical. No merge, CI bypass, or security approval was performed.

### Credit

Thanks to @PollyBot13 for the report/causal investigation, @jonathanlindsay for the concrete contract/use case, @Canvinus and @apps3000 for related MCP/hook work, and @TheAngryPit for the profile/native-identity work. Credit is for context and design constraints, not approval of this proposal.
