prs.title: feat: rename saved model accounts in Models
prs.body:
Related: #202695

## What Problem This Solves

People can connect two model-provider workspaces that use the same email. In Settings → Models, those accounts can look identical, making it hard to tell which workspace or subscription you’re looking at.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway administrators can rename a saved account without signing in again or restarting the Gateway. Leave the name blank to restore its default. Known subscription plans appear beside the account name; names controlled by configuration and accounts owned elsewhere remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admin-only Gateway operation updates only the selected saved profile’s display label. It leaves credentials, authorization, profile IDs, and routing priority unchanged and publishes the new label to the running Gateway. A plan badge uses a known stored tier, not a new usage request. Reconnect name preservation moved here from #202667, which can shrink to the optional sign-in naming prompt after this lands. No sign-in prompt is included here. For xAI, reconnect preserves a custom name only when the previous and new OAuth credentials carry the same nonempty issuer and subject. An email match alone never carries the name to a replacement or unverified account. Token refresh rotates the grant without overwriting a saved label or restoring a label the user cleared.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI and isolated Gateway: two synthetic same-email accounts could be named independently; Enter saved, Escape sent no write, and clearing restored the default. Names and plan badges rendered correctly, and browser reload read back the result without restarting the Gateway.
- The isolated Gateway, real CLI, and synthetic HTTPS provider verified token rotation, ordinary reconnect, and reconnect with `--force`: the name survived all three. A different account replacing the same slot did not inherit the name. That flow adds no sign-in prompt or config write.
- Gateway tests covered non-admin denial, inherited and config-managed profiles, exact-row and priority preservation, and authorization-grant continuity. The protocol generation and compatibility checks passed without a protocol version change. All 72 focused tests passed, along with targeted lint, UI typecheck, and protocol checks.

- The follow-up reuses the existing form and chip styles. The Control UI budget check passed against the same base with zero added raw CSS (previously +359 B). All 64 focused UI tests passed; real Chromium verified rename, clear, and the editor at 390 px. The [Spanish settings-search CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44938469909/job/136950817376) also reproduces on clean `main` at `91566908` ([clean-main reproduction run, Team sign-in required](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8c4423af-5bfd-4b09-965a-558474623e67)). The `modelo` search returns the extra `Modo de código` result. This PR does not fix it; see #203201 for the separate change.

- **xAI reconnect (`a36e1e37`):** Both the `oauth` request and the legacy `device-code` request (now routed to OAuth) lost the saved name before this fix. The same tests now pass for ordinary reconnect and `--force`, including same-email replacement and missing subject without name inheritance. The matcher separately rejects a different or missing issuer and blank identity, and does not load the OAuth runtime just to compare accounts. All 127 focused tests in eight files passed; the reconnect suite took about 12 seconds including setup (about 89 seconds across all focused suites). Targeted lint, format, xAI typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **xAI token refresh (`fbb0c87b`):** At the real refresh-provider boundary with synthetic OAuth responses, a provider-supplied name replaced both a saved label and a cleared label before the fix. Both regressions passed after the fix while the access and refresh tokens rotated and the account subject stayed intact. All 132 focused tests in nine files passed in about 78 seconds (including the reconnect cases); targeted lint, formatting, xAI typecheck, and whitespace checks also passed. This is focused provider/CLI-flow coverage, not a new packaged Gateway upgrade run.
- **Stable-upgrade proof at `fbb0c87b`:** A stock `v2026.11.6` Gateway seeded two synthetic xAI accounts. On a copy, the candidate preserved the saved names, credentials, profile IDs, routing order, and configured override before the first edit. Real CLI reconnect kept the saved label; actual Gateway token rotation kept a renamed label and did not restore a cleared label. Only synthetic credentials and a loopback provider were used.

**Chutes reconnect:** The real CLI and an isolated Gateway reproduced saved-name loss on `935ceb59` and passed on [the Chutes fix `45473eef`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45473eef4ae1368cff1789f96acfee2718f035b4). With synthetic OAuth, the same authenticated UserInfo subject under the same OAuth client retained its saved label on ordinary reconnect and `--force`. A different subject or an absent subject did not inherit it, even with the same username. The persisted credentials were checked separately, and stock v2026.11.6 already stores the necessary identity fields. No live credentials were used. 35 focused tests, lint, formatting, typecheck, and runtime build passed on the Chutes fix.

**Current CI (`11be7dcc`):** The validator conflict was resolved by regeneration; the xAI and Chutes fixes were unchanged. All 34 focused tests and the protocol and formatting checks passed. The [hosted test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45163451477/job/137655324335) and Android Wear passed. All five assertions in the [failing required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45163451477/job/137667461469) reproduced on the [exact clean event base `0174cf4d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0174cf4d0083110f25893b3a3624b77f4402e3f5): two API-key authorization and three Gateway template publication assertions. The API-key matches were also reproduced locally on the CI merge snapshot `9e1b1bd3`; hosted CI showed the template failures on that same snapshot. No changes for these inherited failures are included.

**Earlier CI (`15931569`):** Sharing the xAI device-code test fixture brought the [hosted test-line ratchet to **394/400**](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45105249790/job/137465498873) with no dropped scenarios or production changes. All UI and UI E2E shards, Android Wear, and dependency review passed. The [required gate is still red](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45105249790/job/137472047671): all six Node assertions (three updater, one delayed session catalog, two requester revocation) reproduced with matching failures on both [the exact clean CI base `b151c830`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b151c830713020fe0de9e37c3d21b76671fe0add) and the CI merge snapshot `4d24e6fb`. No changes for those inherited failures are included here.

**Validator conflict resolution (`3055bc2c`):** Regenerated protocol validators after integrating `main`. 69 focused tests, protocol registry and version checks, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The Chutes and xAI implementations and their reconnect matcher are unchanged from `45473eef`. Full end-to-end proof was not repeated on this merge commit.

**Upgrade and xAI lifecycle on `935ceb59`:** Real Gateway/CLI proof passed from stock OpenClaw v2026.11.6 against two synthetic xAI accounts. Reconnect retained the saved name; controlled token rotation retained a renamed label and did not restore a cleared one. No live provider or inference was tested.

<details>
<summary>Public sanitized exact-head upgrade and token-rotation trace (935ceb59)</summary>


- **Earlier CI (`935ceb59`):** The [required gate failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45095667971/job/137441011379). prs.title: fix: verify clean shutdowns without a duplicate log in Gateway restart tests
prs.body:
Closes #207246

## What Problem This Solves

The Bun restart test can report a failed database close even when the final session database is correctly sealed. It looks for a fresh `written` log, but the database owner intentionally suppresses identical receipts. An interim `checkpoint-incomplete` receipt does not tell us how the final close ended either.

## User Impact

This changes only the restart test. Gateway shutdown, logging, SQLite checkpointing, and the ten-second shutdown limit are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test now checks that the stream session has no restart marker beforehand, that the marker summary precedes the start and completion of database shutdown, and that the exact session database has a valid seal and persisted marker after exit. It still rejects shutdown errors and backfill after database close. The per-receipt log parser is gone; the diff is one test file (+13/-16), with no production changes.

## Evidence

- **Main `9c9e3c74e3c6`:** I reproduced the false failure with two real SQLite closes and the exact assertion from the restart test. The second write invalidated the first seal; the final close restored it without another `written` log. The assertion failed with `expected -1 to be greater than 476`. [Controlled red run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9b14f3c4ff06f4c314201fcf7b75b652). The [ordinary baseline](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9754aa377ff0c5e298642cdcdeb524dc) passed both selected restart cases.
- **Fixed:** The same duplicate-close case passed. A reader that pinned the WAL still caused the seal assertion to reject the close. The full real Gateway restart file passed **11/11** on pinned Linux Bun; formatting and lint passed. [Green run and negative control](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_228dfde3ecb55b14d2fc9586f8745a0a).
- The [original CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46101868085/job/140846259792) failed before reading the seal. Its final on-disk state is unknown.

Reported and reproduced with @daniel-lxs.

Related: #203932 (container restart behavior, fixed in #205709).

## What Problem This Solves

Two Gateway heartbeat tests can fail in Docker even when the worker renews its locks correctly. With source workers, the temporary TypeScript entry is treated as CommonJS. With Docker’s default hostname, the custody test describes a restarted container rather than a peer observing a live heartbeat.

## User Impact

Developers can run the tests in a default Docker container without renaming it or putting the temporary directory inside an ESM package. No Gateway behavior or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained worker fixture declares its own ESM package scope, keeping the original entry extension and top-level import. The custody fixture gives the foreign PID namespace a distinct hostname so the production classifier checks the real lock mtime. All assertions are unchanged, including native worker retirement, renewal while the parent is blocked, and leaving the successor untouched.

## Evidence

- On main `b4cb9f3aa652`, both selected tests failed in Docker with Node 24.22.1 and source workers: `Top-level await is currently not supported with the "cjs" output format` and `expected 'dead' to be 'unknown'`. Changing only the hostname made the custody test pass on main.
- On `8c267625e121`, the complete heartbeat file passed with default Docker hostnames: 35/35 with source workers (16.72 s), 35/35 with compiled workers (56.61 s). Targeted typecheck, lint and format checks passed.

prs.title: improve: use less memory when the Gateway loads its model catalog
prs.body:
Related: #192547

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway's model catalog worker reads bundled channel metadata before processing its first request. Importing the two schema projection functions also constructed unrelated channel, DM, and agent tool policy schemas in each fresh worker.

## User Impact

A fresh model catalog worker uses less memory before its first request. Channel configuration, plugin SDK entrypoints, and validation behavior stay the same.

## Why This Change Was Made

The metadata reader now imports the JSON Schema and Zod builders directly from their implementation module. The existing channel config API reexports the same functions. Their implementations, issue paths, schema identity, synchronous validation, and the manifest fallback remain intact. This change leaves Gateway plugin selection and startup admission alone.

## Evidence

- At `3d1f9dfb`, a real bundled plugin's JSON schema could not be loaded with its channel policy module unavailable. The new regression covers successful projection, the applied default, and the validation error. The five focused files passed all 94 tests on `06a04cb1`. They include Zod v3/v4, JSON Schema, registry metadata, and Discord and Tlon schema surfaces. All four touched files passed formatting and lint.
- Four fresh Linux ARM64 Node 24.22.1 workers loaded the normal release package in stock/candidate/candidate/stock order. Both builds used `539f37f1` with the production sources from signed `06a04cb1`. Successor `5dc58d44` documents two existing type assertions and lowers the old file’s assertion allowance from 10 to 8. Pinned Rolldown 1.2.15 emitted the same 1,951 JavaScript bytes for the changed module on both revisions (SHA-256 `78a6386b09e3d1b9750763400606b6d844e5f04a6eff9b25a3e1bb971a96a9be`). Mean V8 used heap at the first worker-body marker went from 56.544 to 53.464 MiB, and mean physical heap from 63.438 to 61.773 MiB. Both candidate observations were below both stock observations. All four probes completed successfully and explicitly terminated their workers after the marker. Both probe arms used the same 268 MiB isolate heap ceiling. A separate instrumented Gateway reported a 524 MiB ceiling for its catalog worker.
- The statically reachable local module graph went from 1,209 files / 8,496,618 bytes to 1,197 files / 8,431,875 bytes. Neither agent-runtime policy nor core configuration policy schema chunks remained statically reachable. Cold imports took 1,633 and 1,710 ms on stock, compared with 1,766 and 1,633 ms on the candidate. Worker heap and packaged file sizes are separate measurements. [Native measurement run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46099015031)

- The separate default-Gateway candidate run used the original 768 MiB service limit. The Gateway became ready at 30.666 s and acknowledged chat at 34.561 s. It was killed at 39.804 s before the mock provider received a request. The service recorded two local OOM kills and the outer group recorded none. The constrained first-turn issue remains open.

- Local ClawSweeper 0.3.5 reviewed the entire signed range `3d1f9dfb..5dc58d44` and reported no code findings or open risks. The stock regression failure, packaged worker measurements and Gateway trial above address its request for runtime evidence. Both focused schema and metadata regression files passed again on the successor (12/12), together with the staged assertion-safety ratchet (2,345 files).

prs.title: improve: use less memory when sharing a downloaded model catalog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Publishing a nonempty downloaded model catalog encoded its JSON into a temporary UTF-8 buffer, then copied the entire buffer into shared memory for future workers. The publisher briefly paid for two copies of the same bytes.

## User Impact

Starting with a downloaded catalog or publishing an accepted refresh uses less temporary memory. The worker payload format, source and revision matching, and first-reader behavior stay the same. The null catalog path already skipped encoding.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publisher can size its final `Uint8Array` with `Buffer.byteLength` and write directly into it with `TextEncoder.encodeInto`. The code-mode worker already uses this pattern. The existing inheritance test now sends a multibyte model name to a real worker and checks it against the original rows.

## Evidence

Measured the actual publisher from the base and candidate in fresh macOS ARM64 processes. Each cell used 12 interleaved stock/candidate pairs on the same machine, with 10,000 synthetic model rows. The payload contained 1,267,942 bytes for ASCII and 1,269,820 bytes with multibyte names. Values below are median **paired changes** immediately across one publication. No allocation hooks or forced GC ran in the timed samples.

| Runtime | Model names | ArrayBuffer bytes | Process RSS | Publication time |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Node 24.22.1 | ASCII | −1,267,942 B | −552 KiB | −0.072 ms |
| Node 24.22.1 | Mixed UTF-8 | −1,269,820 B | −536 KiB | +0.085 ms |
| CI-pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 | ASCII | −1,267,942 B | −1,224 KiB | −0.142 ms |
| CI-pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 | Mixed UTF-8 | −1,269,820 B | −1,184 KiB | −0.018 ms |

A separate count observed one payload-sized temporary string-to-buffer conversion and one payload-sized copy on stock, and zero of both on the candidate. At 1,000 mixed-name rows (125,134 bytes), both runtimes also saved exactly one payload in reported ArrayBuffer memory. At 32 ASCII rows Node’s pooled buffers showed no measurable ArrayBuffer saving, while Bun saved 4,078 bytes.

Fresh real workers on Node 24.22.1, the pinned Bun, and Bun 1.3.14 verified byte-for-byte equality, Unicode including lone surrogates, late readers, superseded shared transfers, repeated read identity, and a null publication. This measures the nonempty catalog publication itself. Whole-Gateway capacity and first-turn success were outside the measurement.

prs.title: fix: load MCP tools their server marks as always-load upfront on Claude CLI turns
prs.body:
Closes #206938

## What Problem This Solves

When an MCP server marks one of its tools with `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"]: true`, that tool is supposed to load upfront in Claude Code while the rest of the server's tools stay behind ToolSearch. On managed Claude CLI turns with tool search on, OpenClaw serves configured MCP tools through its own loopback MCP server. Along that path the mark was lost: the catalog dropped it, the loopback `tools/list` did not include `_meta`, and the loopback server entry set `alwaysLoad: false`, which overrides any per-tool mark in Claude Code. The marked tool stayed deferred. The only workaround was `tools.toolSearch: false`, which loads every tool upfront and costs a lot of context on each fresh conversation.

## User Impact

A tool that its MCP server marks for upfront loading is available to Claude right away on managed Claude CLI turns, and the other tools stay deferred. Nothing else changes:

- `tools.toolSearch: false` still loads every tool upfront.
- Runs without any marked tool keep the current `alwaysLoad: false` server entry.
- A marked tool that policy hides is not listed and does not change how the other tools load.
- Calls still go through OpenClaw's tool policy.
- Existing native Claude conversations keep resuming when only this loading setting changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the mark through the existing MCP path instead of adding a new config selector:

- The catalog projection records `alwaysLoad` from the upstream tool's `_meta`. Materialized tool metadata carries it, and the loopback `tools/list` sends it back out as `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"]: true`. Only `true` is forwarded, so the `tools.toolSearch: false` opt-out can't be undone per tool.
- On deferred runs, CLI preparation leaves the server-level `alwaysLoad` unset when an authorized projected tool carries the mark. Claude Code [documents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#defer-a-servers-tools) that an explicit server value overrides per-tool marks, and that leaving it unset lets marked tools load upfront.
- The native-session resume fingerprint already treats `alwaysLoad: false` and `true` as the same. It now also treats an unset loopback value as the same, so a stored Claude conversation still resumes (#187114).
- The catalog refresh signature includes the mark, so a server that starts or stops marking a tool publishes a fresh catalog.

## Evidence

Regression test `keeps an upstream upfront-loading hint through the loopback under tool search` in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.configured-mcp.test.ts`. It runs the real configured-MCP path with a synthetic two-tool streamable-HTTP server: MCP client discovery, catalog projection, materialization, `prepareCliRunContext` with a ToolSearch-capable Claude backend, the production `createMcpLoopbackServerConfig` entry written to `--mcp-config`, and the loopback `tools/list` / `tools/call` handlers. It checks three settings:

| Setting | Server `alwaysLoad` | Loopback `tools/list` | Marked call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tool search on | unset | `marked` has `_meta`, `unmarked` has none | succeeds |
| `tools.toolSearch: false` | `true` | same | succeeds |
| tool search on, `marked` denied | `false` | only `unmarked` | refused |

It also checks that all three runs produce the same MCP resume hash.

- Red before the fix (this test file on top of unchanged production files): fails. With tool search on, the loopback entry has `alwaysLoad: false` and the loopback lists `marked` without `_meta`; the opt-out row also lists it without `_meta`.
- Green with the fix: passes, together with the rest of `prepare.configured-mcp.test.ts`, `prepare.command-continuity.test.ts`, `bundle-mcp.test.ts` and `src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` (34 + 62 tests). Before the final commit, `prepare.test.ts`, `agent-bundle-mcp-catalog-refresh.test.ts`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names.test.ts`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` and `tool-metadata.test.ts` also passed on this base.

Claude Code contract check: I ran Claude Code 2.1.332 directly (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`, `--strict-mcp-config`) against the issue's synthetic stdio fixture and read its `Dynamic tool loading` debug line:

| Server entry | Fixture | Deferred tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alwaysLoad: false` | `marked` has the mark | 15 |
| `alwaysLoad` unset | `marked` has the mark | 14 (marked loads upfront) |
| `alwaysLoad` unset | no mark | 15 |

So an unset server value releases only the marked tool. Unmarked tools stay deferred.

Other checks on the rebased branch: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files, and `tsgo` for `tsconfig.core.json`, all clean. I did not run the test-file typecheck shards locally.

Not verified: I did not replay the full scenario through an isolated Gateway with managed Claude CLI and a captured first model request. The two checks above cover each half of that path (the OpenClaw side through the production preparation and loopback handlers, and the Claude Code side through the CLI itself), but not the two together in one run.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduling a reminder in an existing conversation shouldn’t require a special action just for the agent’s main conversation. The editor, CLI, and agent tool offered two ways to schedule that work, with different delivery and execution rules.

## User Impact

Use an agent task with `session:<key>` to continue an existing conversation, including the main conversation. Control UI no longer offers **Post to main session** or **Runs in: Main session**. CLI scripts should replace `--system-event` and `--session main` with `--message` and the actual conversation key, for example `--session session:agent:main:main` or `--session session:global` on a global-scope install.

After upgrading, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor backs up cron state and reports each conversion. It rewrites eligible jobs in place, retaining their ID, schedule, enabled state, run history, scratch, and valid delivery settings. The target is the owning agent’s main conversation, with `session:global` for global scope. If Doctor cannot faithfully continue a job (for example, a headless script that used the old main-session notification behavior, a missing prompt, or an unresolved owner), it pauses the job and explains what to review before enabling it. The model now sees the reminder as a **task prompt**, not as a system notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit conversation key uses the same queue and execution path regardless of which conversation it names. Immediate hook wakes, channel join and lifecycle notices, and post-run notices from scheduled plugin commands still use the internal notice path where applicable: they report an event to the conversation, rather than being user-authored automation prompts. Backup schedules already run an isolated command and do not need the removed mode.

Expected overlap with the sibling automation cleanups: the shared cron schema and generated validators, Doctor’s cron repair, scheduler routing, CLI and agent tool descriptions, and the Control UI editor and docs. This change does not redesign the remaining modes or wake policy.

## Evidence

- Doctor’s SQLite repair tests passed for a named agent with a custom main key and for global scope (2 tests). They cover backup creation, preserved job ID, disabled state, schedule, last-run state, delivery, prompt, and a no-op second repair.
- Cron protocol validation passed (93 tests); generated-validator parity, core and UI typechecks, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. The focused CLI run was interrupted by a source change while the subprocess compiler was building; the full CLI, scheduler, native client, and upgrade suites were not verified here.
- Local Codex autoreview (P1, three passes) found that same-kind payload edits had lost their field updates. The update logic was restored; the follow-up core typecheck passed. The final delta was not independently re-reviewed.
- The real Control UI was exercised in Chromium with a mocked Gateway and a fictional weekly garden-inventory reminder. Both capture checks passed. The before capture used the original worktree UI source, which matched `origin/main` outside translation artifacts. The captures show the Action picker; no live model or channel delivery is demonstrated.

> [!NOTE]
> Draft for code-owner review. Not ready to land.

Co-authored by Vyctor Brzezowski (`vyctorbrzezowski`).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Vyctor Brzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)

## What Problem This Solves

Gmail Pub/Sub watches have their own start, reload, and shutdown paths in the Gateway. That makes them harder to maintain than other mail triggers, which use the standard plugin lifecycle. This draft moves watcher ownership first; it is not the complete Gmail cutover.

## User Impact

The bundled `gmail` plugin starts and renews the watcher. Existing `hooks.gmail` settings, HTTP mappings, `openclaw webhooks gmail` commands, and stored automations are unchanged. This slice does not rewrite, pause, or delete jobs, and adds no Doctor migration. If you restrict `plugins.allow`, include `gmail` for the Gateway-managed watcher; if plugins are disabled, the Gateway will not start it. Restart the Gateway after configuring the watcher for the first time so it loads the plugin. `OPENCLAW_SKIP_GMAIL_WATCHER=1` still opts out of Gateway startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin uses the existing scheduled service contract for startup, reload, and shutdown instead of a second Gateway lifecycle. The move exposes the shared process helpers needed to preserve executable lookup, Windows wrapper quoting, bounded diagnostics, and process-tree cleanup; it adds no Gmail-specific SDK API. The generated config inventory counts 24 additional standard plugin-entry fields for `gmail`; this slice adds no Gmail settings and leaves the core and channel counts unchanged.

Still to do before landing the full cutover: move the persisted settings and mapping defaults, add Doctor migration and upgrade proof (including restrictive plugin policy), remove the Gmail-specific model/reasoning precedence and startup model check, and move CLI registration and Gog Doctor diagnostics out of core. Likely sibling overlap is in Gateway reload, automation model selection, Doctor migrations, and generated config/plugin inventories. This slice does not change the automation protocol, agent tool, or editor.

## Evidence

- I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac`, retaining both SDK documentation sections and regenerating the config/plugin inventories. No rebase or force-push.
- I reproduced the port regression before fixing it: Gmail selected a service-only reload for `gateway.port`. The regression now passes, preserving the core Gateway restart policy from #138556 and hot reloads for hook settings. Implementation tests and private mocks now live with the plugin.
- I ran 542 focused tests across 20 files locally, without a VM, in 169.23 seconds. They cover Gateway reload/startup/shutdown, hook mapping, Gmail setup, CLI/Doctor and the relocated suites. The fake-Gog integration exercised real spawning, child-only token transport and process-tree cleanup, not live Google delivery.

Regeneration also removed an unrelated `optional` marker on `escape-string-regexp@4.0.0`, with no version changes. Against merged main: non-test +262/-235; tests +128/-500.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

## What Problem This Solves

Turning on an automation's failure alerts meant choosing among several overlapping settings. An option for best-effort delivery could also make a failed send count as a success and suppress the default alert.

## User Impact

User impact: The automation editor has one **Failure alerts** switch. The CLI uses `--failure-alert` or `--no-failure-alert`; the automation tool takes a boolean. Eligible automations ask the owning conversation to repair the problem. Otherwise the notice goes to the configured global failure route or the job's result destination. The Gateway-wide `cron.failureAlert` policy controls timing and routing. Failed required delivery stays failed, and schedule-error auto-disable safety notices still apply even when failure alerts are off. Main deliberately removed auto-disable after repeated execution failures in #203106; this PR preserves that behavior.

After upgrading, run `openclaw doctor --fix`. Doctor backs up cron state, converts custom job alert objects to On, preserves Off, and reports settings it drops per automation. It retires per-agent and per-creator alert routes and the best-effort delivery option. It pauses jobs whose old behavior cannot be represented, so operators can review them before re-enabling. It does not delete jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single switch makes the per-automation decision clear; timing and fallback routing belong to the Gateway policy. The likely overlap with sibling automation cleanups is in the editor, CLI/tool schema, Gateway protocol and its generated validators, scheduler tests, and Doctor's cron migration. prs.title: fix(talk): keep accepted agent work running when Gateway or Control UI Talk ends or drops
prs.body:
Related: #206329, #206333, #188134, #188798 (supersedes #206474)

> **End Talk ends the call, not the task. Once the session accepts work, its answer belongs in the original chat. Stop response is how you cancel it.**

## What Problem This Solves

In the Gateway and its bundled Control UI, ending, dropping, or reconnecting a Talk call cancels agent work that the session already accepted:

1. **Gateway default close / disconnect / reconnect:** `talk.session.close` (when `disposition` is omitted), `talk.client.close`, client WebSocket disconnects, OpenAI GPT-Live lease retirements, and provider continuity resets (`session.continuity.reset`) defaulted to aborting accepted agent runs. A dropped client cannot send `disposition: "detach"` after its connection is already gone.
2. **Control UI End Talk & browser-direct teardown:** Clicking **End Talk** in the browser (`state.toggleRealtimeTalk`) explicitly passed `{ disposition: "abort" }` (sending `disposition: "abort"` in relay mode and `chat.abort` in split mode), and stopping or dropping a browser-direct OpenAI WebRTC or Google Live session aborted its local consult `AbortController` into `chat.abort`.

Because the Gateway serves and ships the Control UI together, folding both changes as separate commits in one PR makes the merge boundary match the user promise.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once an agent session accepts a task, the Talk call owns microphone capture, audio playback, and whether to speak the answer—not whether the task finishes:

### Gateway (commits 1–2)
- `src/gateway/talk/relay/operations.ts` & `src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.ts`: default omitted `talk.session.close` disposition and `talk.client.close` / disconnect teardown to `"detach"` instead of `"abort"`, while keeping explicit `disposition: "abort"` on `talk.session.close` for callers that intentionally cancel.
- `src/gateway/talk/relay/state.ts`: `resetTalkRealtimeRelayContinuity` detaches accepted agent runs (`retireRelayAgentRuns(session)` with no abort reason) while clearing old audio and provider tool-call links on provider reconnect.
- `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-gateway-bridge.ts`, `realtime-quicksilver-session.ts`, `realtime-session-retirement.ts`: default OpenAI GPT-Live close and lease retirement to `"detach"`.
- `src/gateway/talk/voice-selection.ts`: remove unused `isTalkVoiceSessionReplacing` helper.
- `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md`, `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/voice-and-audio.md`, `docs/platforms/android.md`: document the `"detach"` default for omitted `talk.session.close` disposition and distinguish older Gateways with and without `talk-session-close-disposition`.

### Control UI / WebChat (commits 3–5)
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts`: `toggleRealtimeTalk` calls `stopChatRealtimeTalk(state)` (defaulting to `"detach"`) instead of `{ disposition: "abort" }`.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/split.ts` & `gateway-relay.ts`: default `stop()` disposition to `"detach"` while keeping explicit `{ disposition: "abort" }`.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/shared.ts`: add `detachSignal` to `submitRealtimeTalkConsult` so transport teardown stops local waiting without sending `chat.abort` or reviving `"listening"` status, while explicit `signal` and Gateway `aborted` chat events (**Stop response**) still cancel.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/webrtc.ts`, `google-live.ts`, `google-live-tools.ts`: default `stop()` / `release()` to `"detach"`, keeping explicit `{ disposition: "abort" }` and genuine Google Live `toolCallCancellation` aborting only the cancelled consult.
- `ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-start-stop.e2e.test.ts` & `ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-end-detach.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: update the browser Talk stop expectation to `"detach"` and add a real-Gateway + bundled Control UI acceptance E2E (with scripted voice and model endpoints) covering **End Talk** detach + reload vs **Stop response** cancellation.

### Scope Boundary
- This PR (with companion native PRs #206329 for Apple and #206333 for Android/Wear) covers **Talk** on Gateway, Control UI, iOS, macOS, Android, and Wear OS.
- The separate **FaceTime** plugin (`extensions/facetime/src/talk-driver.ts`) and carrier **Voice Call** plugin (`extensions/voice-call/`) do not go through the Talk close path and remain separate follow-up scope because they need an explicit result-destination policy after a call ends.

AI-assisted: drafted, implemented, reviewed, and verified with AI coding assistance, with unit tests, real-Gateway browser E2E, and linters run locally.

## User Impact

- Ending Talk in the browser, losing a connection, or reconnecting to a voice provider stops audio and waiting without canceling accepted agent work; the answer finishes once in the original chat.
- Explicit cancellation remains separate: **Stop response** (`chat.abort`), explicit `disposition: "abort"` on `talk.session.close`, `talk.session.cancelOutput`, `talk.session.steer` / `talk.client.steer`, and genuine provider `toolCallCancellation` continue to cancel work.
- RPC behavior change note:
  - `talk.session.close` now defaults to `"detach"` when `disposition` is omitted; callers that intend to cancel accepted work on relay close should pass `disposition: "abort"` explicitly.
  - `talk.client.close` takes no `disposition` field and now detaches accepted work on close, disconnect, or expiry; cancel client-owned runs explicitly via `chat.abort` or `talk.client.steer`.

## Evidence

- Combined **real Gateway and bundled Control UI, scripted voice and model endpoints** E2E regression test (not a live-provider test):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-end-detach.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: 1 passed (accepts a Talk consult, clicks **End Talk**, confirms relay closes while model turn stays alive, reloads chat and confirms the answer appears once in DOM and `chat.history`; accepts a second Talk consult, clicks **Stop response**, confirms model turn aborts and never persists after reload).
- Browser Talk E2E:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-start-stop.e2e.test.ts`: 11 passed.
- Combined Gateway + Control UI Talk unit tests on the merged head:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/index.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.close.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/split.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/webrtc.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/google-live.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/gateway-relay.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/consult.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/session.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 shards passed (Gateway relay & close-control + 7 UI files, 199 tests passed).
- `npx oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `npx oxfmt --check` (all files formatted), and `git diff --check` (clean).
- **Live verification checklist (for maintainer/reviewer testing):** accept a Talk task in chat A, test both clicking **End Talk** and dropping the connection, and confirm one answer lands in A with no more audio; repeat with **Stop response** and confirm it cancels.


## Live browser test (talkcli, 2a88079a306)

Two manual Control UI runs in a browser against a test Gateway built from this head (`2a88079a306`), real OpenAI realtime Talk (gateway-relay, agent-consult), 28 Nov 2026 HKT. Both show **End Talk** leaving the run alive so the answer still lands.

### 1. Same chat (10:40)
1. Talk starts ("Connecting voice input…", then "Stop voice input"). The question "Hey, can you tell me the weather in Paris for the next five days" is transcribed.
2. **End Talk** is pressed; the call ends and the mic control returns to idle.
3. After the call ended, "Fetched https://api.open-meteo.com/…" appears and the full five-day answer arrives in the same chat. **Pass.**

### 2. Switched chat (10:43)
1. In "Test chat", Talk transcribes "Hey, what's the weather in Moscow for the next five days", then the call is ended.
2. While the Moscow run is still in progress, the user switches to a different chat (an older talkcli test session).
3. Back in "Test chat", the Moscow answer ("Fetched https://api.open-meteo.com/…latitude=55.75…", then "Moscow is below freezing for the next five days, with some snow…") has arrived in the **original** chat. **Pass.**

Gateway log (talkcli, HKT; ids shortened):
```
-- same chat --
10:40:57.613 talk  transcript.done
10:40:59.156 talk  session.closed      <- End Talk
10:41:03.118 cli turn ... durationMs=6213 outBytes=418   <- answer, 4 s after close
10:41:03.192 model_fallback_chain_stopped reason=caller_signal_aborted
10:41:03.227 source-claim status=failed
-- switched chat --
10:43:18.693 talk  transcript.done
10:43:19.176 talk  session.closed      <- End Talk
10:43:24.503 cli turn ... durationMs=6277 outBytes=358   <- answer, 5 s after close
10:43:24.575 model_fallback_chain_stopped reason=caller_signal_aborted
10:43:24.611 source-claim status=failed
```
Caveats: the Gateway does not log a `detach` or `disposition` string, so detach is inferred from the answer completing after `session.closed`. The `caller_signal_aborted` and failed source-claim lines appear right after each turn completed; the answer was delivered in the chat both times, and I did not investigate those lines further. The chat switch is evidenced by the recording, not the log.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep every untrusted-content block closed and bound the MCP serving paths
prs.body:
**Depends on #207101** (stacked on its head `2ad43647`). Merge only after #207101, and only with the owner's OK: this touches the same untrusted-content boundary.

## Problem

Two gaps left open by #207101's one tool-result bound (`boundToolResult`):

1. **Multi-block results.** Only a result with exactly one text block that is one untrusted-content envelope had its body cut and its frame kept. With several text blocks, the truncator's per-block path falls back to a whole-prefix cut at small budgets, which drops an envelope block's end marker. Red at the 4,000-token minimum window, both for a header block beside a wrapped page and for two wrapped pages.
2. **Two MCP serving paths had no bound at all:** the Gateway MCP loopback (`src/gateway/mcp-http.handlers.ts`, used by CLI backends) and the plugin tools MCP server (`src/mcp/plugin-tools-handlers.ts`).

## Solution

1. In `boundToolResult` (one owner), every text block that is exactly one envelope is unwrapped to its body; the frames are reserved in both budgets; after the cut each surviving body goes back inside its own whole frame. The body carries its frame on a module-private symbol key, which the truncator copies with the block. When the truncator keeps whole leading blocks and replaces the first omitted block with a notice, that notice is placed inside the omitted block's frame. If the summed frames do not fit beside the non-text blocks (hostile metadata), the text is cut as plain text, as in #207101.
2. Both MCP paths call `boundToolResult(result, undefined, false)` on results with a content array, before content normalization. Observers, receipts and `isError` still read the raw result. Plain strings and other JSON results keep their existing normalization.

## Decision for the owner (MCP paths)

- The MCP serving paths have no context window, so the bound uses its existing unknown-window default: **16k chars**, with a size-only notice (no Gateway path; MCP clients read with their own tools). Before, the full result went to the client; clients such as CLI backends may apply their own, larger limits. This is a visible reduction for very large results through these paths. If that is not wanted, the alternative is to plumb the run's window into the loopback (a new parameter) or drop change 2.

## Gaps (named, not fixed)

- **Agents API (from #207101, not changed here):** the adapter joins the bounded blocks with newlines and image placeholders, then cuts the joined string with a raw prefix slice at the cap. When the joining overhead pushes the string over the cap, that slice can cut the last characters of a closing marker (reproduced: a header and two wrapped pages that fit by one char before joining). Two fixes were tried and dropped: bounding the joined string again replaces the first notice with a false count ("67 chars omitted" where 217k were cut); dropping the final cap lets output exceed the cap by one char per block and 54 per image. A correct fix needs the owner pass to budget the adapter's serialization, which is a design choice for the owner; the tried patch is kept on a parked branch.

- Frames are all-or-nothing: with many envelope blocks in one result (for example 12+ at a 4,000-token window, 25+ at 8,000), the summed frames do not fit and every block is cut as plain text. No known producer emits that many.
- A notice placed inside an omitted block's frame sits in an untrusted region and its count covers following blocks too (same class as #207101's residual).
- MCP results whose `content` is a string, or that have no content array, are not bounded (unchanged).

## Evidence

Red on #207101's head, green here:

| Area | Test |
|---|---|
| Bound | header + wrapped page at 4,000 / 8,000 / 16,000 / 128,000-token windows, and two wrapped pages at 4,000 / 16,000 / 128,000: every envelope block keeps start and end with one id |
| Gateway MCP loopback | oversized result: head + tail, size-only notice, no path; plain string / `undefined` / `null` / number results still succeed |
| Plugin tools MCP server | oversized wrapped result: bounded, wrapper closed, no path |

Consumer suites for #207101's routes (embedded, Codex, Copilot, Agents API, Tool Search) and the MCP server suites pass; prefix stability passes. Typecheck: core, core tests.

prs.title: feat: choose where automations run
prs.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Do not land.** Still in progress and under discussion. Talk to @vyctorbrzezowski.

Co-authored by [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2fa4bdf2-6cf6-4471-9df7-8c95bf40f48e)
- [Conflict repair and focused local verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-automations-cleanup-prs-s0ac320b6)

## What Problem This Solves

The automation editor offers Main and Isolated, but it can’t create an automation that continues a selected conversation. The team-server audit found 221 of 312 automations already use that kind of target.

## User Impact

- **New session each time** starts a fresh run. Enable **Include recent chat** to give it recent context without continuing the source transcript.
- **Continue a conversation** lets you pick a conversation, including the agent’s main conversation.
- Doctor backs up cron state, then converts `current` jobs to new sessions with recent chat while preserving their linked workspace and sandbox. It converts `main` jobs to the owning agent’s main conversation. If a target can’t be mapped faithfully, Doctor retains the job, pauses it, and reports why. Existing isolated and explicit conversation targets keep their placement. After a direct upgrade, run `openclaw doctor --fix` before relying on old jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A fresh run and a continuation are the two execution choices. Recent chat is a setting on a fresh run, not a third place to run. The editor, CLI, Gateway, and automation tool use the same two targets.

This draft overlaps the sibling cleanup that retires `main`/`systemEvent`, especially in the Doctor migration, payload validation, scheduler routing, editor, and tests. This change keeps the system-event payload working with an explicit conversation until that sibling removes it. Other automation editor and delivery cleanups may touch the same files.

## Evidence

I merged main at `fc25865d99bd0166efbe6f70d93df979e68e19ac` without rebasing or rewriting history, resolved the conflicts, and fixed the nine ClawSweeper findings. I also completed the affected consumer-test conversions after main's refactors and retained CLI system-event defaulting to an explicit main target.

I reproduced both migration defects before fixing them. The persisted Doctor regression uses execution hashes captured with main's real storage serializer. It checks valid authority rebinding, unchanged stale captures, preserved placement, and idempotence. The effective-agent regression fails before the repair and passes afterward.

I ran 42 focused test files locally, without a VM: 964 cases across the selected suites. After correcting the failures, I reran every failing file and the affected migration/notification suites on the final code; all passed. Core and UI typechecks, scheduler/Doctor/Gateway test typechecks, targeted production lint, UI copy validation, formatting, and the PR diff whitespace check passed. The broad selected run took 571 seconds; the final two-file rerun passed 39 tests in 133 seconds. CI duration is not measured.

I ran pr-simplify on this repair: I reused the existing agent resolver and Doctor repair path, retained runtime admission checks, and replaced duplicate binding coverage with an explicit-conversation case. No new runtime compatibility reader or execution-policy bypass was added.

Local autoreview was unavailable: the configured Codex installation could not execute inside its read-only reviewer sandbox. I did not broaden reviewer permissions or request a hosted re-review. This PR remains draft under the existing do-not-land hold.

Still needed before landing: final-head real-app editor screenshots; real-agent runs proving fresh-session recent context and selected-conversation execution, including main, workspace/sandbox inheritance, and delivery; and real supported-version updates to this head, including v2026.11.5, latest stable, 9.x extended-stable, and 10.x, preserving saved jobs and captured authority. The old updater round trip needs regression coverage. Previous UI evidence does not cover this repaired head. Full CI and native-app builds were not run.

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: open publisher-qualified Template links in the Control UI
prs.body:
Closes #198770. Follows #198831.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a creator's Template link in the Control UI can show a catalog error even though the Gateway found the requested release. This happens when the link uses the publisher-qualified name and ClawHub stores the Template under its bare name.

## User Impact

Both names open the same Template. File preview and Add use the package and version from the returned release. A different publisher, package, or pinned version still produces an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already returns the stored name and its verified publisher. The UI can match either the stored name or the qualified reference built from those two fields. The Gateway and UI use the same name check, including when the UI returns to the link to show an Add error or ask for ClawHub risk confirmation. The CLI keeps its existing exact-name preference and uses the shared formatter.

## Evidence

### Browser screenshots

Chrome opened `@atlas/research-briefing` at `1.2.0` on the base UI (`4cb16b351987`) and the PR UI (`e056a44e0812`). Both runs used the same Gateway build and synthetic ClawHub release.

**Before**

![Before the fix, the qualified link shows a release contents error and a Retry button.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xwl777/openclaw/688d8b82c8394540c2bea81fa1f440a31e1dd6c6/before.png)

**After**

![After the fix, the same link opens Research Briefing by @atlas and shows version 1.2.0.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xwl777/openclaw/688d8b82c8394540c2bea81fa1f440a31e1dd6c6/after.png)

**Annotated before**

![An arrow marks the catalog error on the base UI.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xwl777/openclaw/688d8b82c8394540c2bea81fa1f440a31e1dd6c6/before-annotated.png)

**Annotated after**

![An arrow marks the Research Briefing heading on the PR UI.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xwl777/openclaw/688d8b82c8394540c2bea81fa1f440a31e1dd6c6/after-annotated.png)

### RPC trace and local checks

The Templates page regression failed on the base revision and passed with the change. It covers a publisher-qualified link, the file preview and Add requests, and rejection of a response for another publisher, package, or pinned version. Two further regressions reproduced lost Add errors and confirmation prompts when returning to the link. Both pass with the shared name check.

Chrome opened the same publisher-qualified link on the base UI (4cb16b351987) and the PR UI (e056a44e0812), using the same Gateway build in separate isolated runs with a synthetic community Template. The bare-name link opened on both. Below are excerpts from the browser’s WebSocket capture. Each reply shows its success flag and the captured package name, preview text, or error message.

**Open the qualified link.** Both builds received this same reply. The base displayed “ClawHub did not return the contents of this Template release.” The PR displayed the “Research Briefing” heading.

```text
→ templates.catalog.detail {"packageName":"@atlas/research-briefing","version":"1.2.0"}
← ok=true "research-briefing"
```

**Open SOUL.md on the PR build.** The browser displayed the returned file contents.

```text
→ templates.catalog.preview {"packageName":"research-briefing","version":"1.2.0","kind":"instruction","name":"SOUL.md"}
← ok=true "# Research workflow\n\nSummarize the research findings and cite the original sources.\n"
```

**Press Add on the flagged release.** The Gateway required confirmation and Chrome displayed the security review prompt.

```text
→ templates.add.apply {"mode":"chat","source":{"packageName":"research-briefing","version":"1.2.0"},"agentId":"research-briefing"}
← ok=false "Explicit acknowledgement is required for this ClawHub release."
```

**Cancel, then press Add again.** The first prompt closed. The next request still omitted the acknowledgement, and Chrome displayed a fresh prompt.

```text
→ templates.add.apply {"mode":"chat","source":{"packageName":"research-briefing","version":"1.2.0"},"agentId":"research-briefing"}
← ok=false "Explicit acknowledgement is required for this ClawHub release."
```

Local checks passed for all 52 Templates page and Add tests, 60 ClawHub catalog tests, and the CLI Gateway Add test. The CLI integration test needed host process visibility to identify its isolated Gateway. The UI production build, UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and formatting checks passed.

prs.title: fix(updates): project older succeeded update runs as historical when gateway serves a different version
prs.body:
## Summary
Related: #197915

When OpenClaw is upgraded externally (for example, redeploying a Docker/container image from `2026.9.5` to `2026.11.3`), the Updates page still renders an older saved `succeeded` update run as the current result (`OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.5`) because `projectUpdateRunHistory` only projects `failed` runs.

## Changes
- Add `projectHistoricalSucceededUpdateRun` in `src/infra/update-run-history-projection.ts` (sharing drift resolution with `projectUpdateRunHistory`) to detect when a saved `succeeded` update run's recorded version/build differs from the currently serving Gateway identity.
- Keep `projectUpdateRunHistory` strictly failure-only so existing callers (`sidebar-attention-update.ts`, `status-update-restart.ts`, `updates-recorded-attempt.tsx`) do not treat a historical success as a warning or `historicalFailure`.
- Update `projectUpdateRun` in `ui/src/app/update-run-projection.ts` to render historical succeeded runs with the serving-version context and omit stale warnings/owed steps.
- Add unit tests in `src/infra/update-run-history-projection.test.ts`.

## Scope Note
This PR focuses on the stale historical succeeded-run display from #197915 without modifying `packages/gateway-protocol` schemas; exposing `installKind` to disable the in-place `Update now` button for container deployments can be handled separately once the protocol schema change is regenerated.

prs.body:
Related to #191855. This head owns the status half of the report: an unreadable capture directory, an unreadable capture root, an ancestor that denies search permission, or a root that lists but denies search (mode 0444 with a stray file) no longer erases the recovery-set list; each unreadable entry is reported beside the captures that can still be verified, including captures in the legacy state root. `openclaw backup create` keeps its documented refusal of unreadable sources (`docs/cli/backup.md`); the backup-walker symptom is deliberately not changed here.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update status --json` returned `recoverySetsError` and dropped every recovery set when one retained capture directory, the `.update-captures` root, or an ancestor of that root could not be read by the current user (#191855: a root-owned `.fseventsd` inside the state tree). Review reproduced two further forms: an ancestor denying search permission fails the root `lstat` itself before the `readdir` guard can run; and a root at mode 0444 with a stray file (e.g. `.DS_Store`) still `lstat`s that file for its size even though status turns byte measurement off — the EACCES escapes the whole inventory and hides a readable capture in the legacy root.

- Fix: the root `lstat` uses the same EACCES/EPERM classification as the existing `readdir` guard (a `protected` artifact with `reason: "unreadable-capture-root"`, listed as `unreadable`); the stray-file size read is skipped when `measureBytes === false` and tolerates EACCES/EPERM per entry when measuring. Other errnos still throw; an absent root still returns an empty inventory.
- Not changed: malformed/FIFO/oversized/present-but-unreadable markers still refuse; aliased or non-directory roots still fail globally; `backup create`, the tar walker, SQLite discovery and header probe keep their permission-failure contract. Per-path omission reporting for foreign directories belongs to draft #194166.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each reader already had a tolerant "entry is not here" path; permission failures landed in the fatal branch because the errno set was written for missing paths only. Classifying EACCES/EPERM where absence is already classified keeps the two-tier model (private capture stays protected and loud; a directory this process cannot inspect degrades to one `unreadable` entry) without a new shared policy module. Skipping the size read when bytes are not measured removes the last unconditional `lstat` in the listing path. A shared per-path warning/omission policy was rejected because #194166 owns it; making `backup create` skip unreadable directories was rejected because its documentation promises refusal.

## User Impact

`openclaw update status` (text and `--json`) keeps listing every recovery set it can verify — across the current and legacy state roots — when a capture directory, the capture root, or an ancestor of the root is unreadable: locked entries appear as `unreadable` with the OS error and the existing next action, instead of one `Update recovery sets unavailable` line hiding the healthy sets. `openclaw backup create` behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Shipped CLI matrix (`node openclaw.mjs update status --json`, isolated `env -i` HOME/state, real privacy markers). Before arm = reviewed head `0c4ada7` dist; after arm = this head `ff26d4e` rebuilt with only the stray-file guard added:

| Case | Before (`0c4ada7`) | After (`ff26d4e`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control: two readable captures | no `recoverySetsError`, 2 sets | identical |
| capture dir mode 000 | no error; 1 `unreadable` + 1 readable | identical |
| capture root mode 000 / 111 | no error; root `unreadable` | identical |
| parent of root mode 000 | no error; root `unreadable` | identical |
| **root mode 0444 + `.DS_Store`** (review repro) | `recoverySetsError: EACCES ... lstat '<root>/.DS_Store'`, sets missing | no error; 2 `unreadable` captures |
| **0444 current root + readable legacy capture** | same global EACCES; legacy set hidden | no error; legacy `incomplete` + current `unreadable` |

```console
# before, root-0444-stray (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '<evidence>/repro-r4/root-0444-stray/state.update-captures/.DS_Store'
recoverySets: <missing>
# after, root-0444-stray (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: <absent>
recoverySets: unreadable run-aaaa1111 | unreadable run-bbbb2222
# before, legacy-cross-scope (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '<evidence>/repro-r4/legacy-cross-scope/home/.openclaw.update-captures/.DS_Store'
recoverySets: <missing>
# after, legacy-cross-scope (verbatim)
recoverySetsError: <absent>
recoverySets: incomplete run-cccc3333 | unreadable run-aaaa1111
```

Earlier rounds' base→head cells (capture-dir-000 marker EACCES, root-000 scandir EACCES, parent-000 root-lstat EACCES) stay fixed on this head. The `backup create` surface is untouched this round; its earlier refusal cells were byte-identical across arms (unreadable workspace / malformed marker → exit 1 `... export refused.`; control → exit 0).

Regression folded into the existing root-unreadable case as `it.each([{root,000},{parent,000},{root,0444}])`, platform-guarded. RED with only the production guard reverted:

```console
FAIL  keeps the recovery set when the capture root is unreadable (mode 0444)
AssertionError: expected { update: { …(4) }, …(5) } to not have property "recoverySetsError"
+ Received: "EACCES: permission denied, lstat '/tmp/update-status-recovery-IUTbuj/state.update-captures/.DS_Store'"
Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
```

GREEN on this head: `Tests 31 passed (31)` (`vitest.cli.config.ts`). `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on both changed files; test-line ratchet +50 within the 400 allowance, no new test files.

Limits: EPERM shares the EACCES branch (exercised via EACCES on Linux); local `tsgo` needs a newer glibc than this host, CI type shards cover it. Collision check: #204709 (kitiyeung) touches the same status files for a complementary question; no other open PR touches `update-capture-cleanup.ts`.

prs.title: fix(updates): project older succeeded update runs as historical when gateway serves a different version
prs.body:
Related: #197915

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw is upgraded externally (for example, redeploying a Docker/container image from `2026.9.5` to `2026.11.3`), the Updates page still renders an older saved `succeeded` update run as the current result (`OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.5`) because `projectUpdateRunHistory` only projects `failed` runs.

## User Impact

Operators reading Settings → Updates need to distinguish a saved result from the version serving their current connection.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Add `projectHistoricalSucceededUpdateRun` in `src/infra/update-run-history-projection.ts` (sharing drift resolution with `projectUpdateRunHistory`) to detect when a saved `succeeded` update run's recorded version/build differs from the currently serving Gateway identity.
- Keep `projectUpdateRunHistory` strictly failure-only so existing callers (`sidebar-attention-update.ts`, `status-update-restart.ts`, `updates-recorded-attempt.tsx`) do not treat a historical success as a warning or `historicalFailure`.
- Update `projectUpdateRun` in `ui/src/app/update-run-projection.ts` to render historical succeeded runs with the serving-version context and omit stale warnings/owed steps.
- Add unit tests in `src/infra/update-run-history-projection.test.ts`.

## Scope Note
This PR focuses on the stale historical succeeded-run display from #197915 without modifying `packages/gateway-protocol` schemas; exposing `installKind` to disable the in-place `Update now` button for container deployments can be handled separately once the protocol schema change is regenerated.

## Evidence

The reporter captured Settings → Updates after a Docker Compose upgrade from 2026.10.9 to 2026.11.3. The page still highlighted the successful 2026.9.5 attempt. [Reporter screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197915)

At `e33189bef478b5a3d71ac623c09d4d61eaf909bb`, both tests in `src/infra/update-run-history-projection.test.ts` passed in an isolated Node container using Vitest 5.0.5 and a focused configuration. The tests cover a successful run with different versions, the failure-only projection for that run, and a successful run with matching identities.

The packaged Settings → Updates page with a connected Gateway still needs before/after verification. The review identified a standalone-repair regression: a serving-version change can replace the repair summary and its linked failure with a historical-update heading. The two tests above do not exercise that path. [Review of this revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207236#issuecomment-7234333607)

Two open PRs cover the same historical-success display. The browser captures on #201848 were made against that PR’s own revision. [#201848](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201848) · [#207219](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207219)

prs.title: fix: hide structured tool calls from session history by default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant recalls a session, `sessions_history` can return structured tool calls and their arguments even when tool activity wasn't requested. Tool-result messages were already hidden, but tool blocks inside other messages weren't.

## User Impact

Session recall omits structured tool calls and results by default. Set `includeTools: true` to see them. Message IDs, pagination, ordinary text, readable reasoning, and markup embedded in text are preserved. By default, recall also omits opaque thinking blocks that contain no readable reasoning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history tool filters structured blocks using OpenClaw's existing block-type contract before applying its response byte cap. It retains the parent message, even if the content becomes empty, so an existing message ID remains usable as an anchor. The shared classifier recognizes the lowercase `toolcall` spelling produced by the Claude CLI importer. Filtering affects the model-facing recall only; it does not rewrite imported JSONL, stored transcripts, or Gateway history.

## Evidence

- Two regressions failed on base `915669080` and pass with the fix: paged recall with and without tool activity, and an anchored tool-only row alongside user text and a structured tool result.
- 32 history tool tests and 16 prompt-prefix stability tests passed (54s and 62s wall time locally). Formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Self-reviewed the full diff. A separate P0–P3 Auto Review attempt against `915669080` timed out without a verdict; ClawSweeper found no correctness issues on the prior head `9705247ca1af`; its [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44940933995) passed. Follow-up-head CI and review are separate.
- The updated tool description is reflected in the three generated Codex fixtures. `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passes after regeneration.

- **End-to-end Gateway proof (rerun with the Claude CLI fix):** Two real OpenClaw agent turns wrote ordinary text, structured `session_status` calls, and tool results to the isolated Gateway's transcript. A separate real agent recalled that session via `sessions_history`. At the model-facing tool response, omitted and explicit `false` each hid both calls and results; `true` returned both. All three retained the visible reply. The default anchored read retained the tool-only message ID with `content: []`, the next page used `nextOffset: 1` and returned two strictly older rows, and a subsequent Gateway history read still contained the original tool call.
- The combined Gateway proof passed (16.4s test time; 53.7s including startup/transform). The Gateway, agent loop, tool execution, and transcript storage were real; the model endpoint was a deterministic loopback Responses provider, not hosted inference.
- **Claude CLI import proof:** A synthetic Claude JSONL transcript was linked to an isolated Gateway session and read through the actual importer. Raw Gateway history exposed lowercase `toolcall`, `tool_result`, and both opaque thinking variants. The registered `sessions_history` tool omitted all four with `includeTools` omitted or false, preserved readable reasoning and final text, and returned all blocks with `true`. A signature-only row kept its message ID and empty content when recalled by anchor. The imported offset view remained a terminal snapshot, and the source JSONL was unchanged. The focused regression failed on the previous PR head and passes with this change.

**Runtime output (isolated Gateway, deterministic loopback model):**

```text
Claude CLI JSONL → Gateway import → sessions_history → agent: omitted/false hid toolcall, tool_result and both signatures; true retained them; readable reasoning, final text, signature-only anchor and terminal snapshot passed; JSONL unchanged.
Gateway chat.send → real agent → sessions_history → provider tool output: omitted=false; explicit false=false; opt-in=true; anchor content=[]; nextOffset=1, older rows=2
```

The booleans in the second line indicate presence of tool activity in the returned content. Only assertion output is shown; endpoint and process logs are omitted. Hosted-model recall has not been run.

Exact-head [prompt snapshot check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44949200153/job/136983657136) and [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44950250315) passed.

Contributor: @TheAngryPit

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af8f1f56-dbda-4b18-b0b2-a2c7ca957d04)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit
