prs.title: fix(agents): preserve trusted daily quota assertions through failover
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserve trusted producer assertions for model-scoped daily quota exhaustion across streamed error projection, retry classification, and fallback normalization.

### Motivating scenario: Provider Cedar

“Provider Cedar” is an anonymized label for the motivating provider scenario, not a new public provider identifier. A producer can distinguish an explicit model-scoped daily limit from transient throttling, but core can lose that distinction while projecting streamed errors or normalizing nested failures. Treating the resulting error as transient can retry the same exhausted model without a useful recovery path.

The regression fixtures model this boundary with synthetic provider/model identities: a trusted producer emits numeric HTTP 429, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, and a typed daily-model assertion. The assertion must survive unrelated or truncated diagnostics; conflicting enclosing status/code aliases or request identities must reject it. This is synthetic regression evidence, not a claim of a live upstream daily-limit reproduction.

- Require coherent numeric 429 and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED facts on the asserting record; reject contradictory transport aliases and provider/model identities across wrappers.
- Capture the accepted assertion before diagnostic clipping or redaction. Diagnostic JSON cannot establish, erase, or resurrect the typed assertion.
- Suppress same-model transient retries only for the coherent typed daily-model assertion. Generic throttling remains unchanged.
- Preserve configured fallback precedence, explicit disablement, and selection locks. Unused switch-recovery policy and metadata are removed.

## Scope

Quota-assertion propagation and retry suppression only. Existing configured fallback progression is retained. No UI switch, resume action, prompt replay, dispatch journal, or storage migration is added.

### Resolved review items

- Session retry owner in `src/llm/utils/retry.ts` carries `quotaScope` and honors `sameModelRetry === false`.
- `assistant-failure.ts` preserves validated `quotaScope` when constructing `FailoverError`, with regression through outer fallback normalization.
- Removed unused switch-recovery policy, `quotaRecovery` metadata, `model-fallback-failure.ts`, and the leftover doc paragraph in `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins/runtime-hooks.md`.
- Consolidated the diagnostic-body rejection table in `src/agents/daily-model-quota.test.ts` and added registered stream-transport boundary proof in `src/agents/daily-model-quota.stream-boundary.test.ts`.
- Merged current `origin/main` cleanly to resolve merge conflicts while preserving both quota retry vetoes and upstream `route_unavailable` vetoes.

## Evidence

Head: `e9dc2372526dd74347bec073803b7c055cbd4d75`.

- **Committed registered stream boundary test:** supporting projection/classification proof only. It uses a fabricated stream and a handwritten retry loop; it does **not** create an AgentSession or execute the embedded runner. The fault-sequence suite mocks the embedded attempt. The real session/HTTP proof below supersedes the prior overstatement.
- **219 focused tests** across 7 files and **102 sibling retry/classification/fallback-transcript tests** across 3 files passed. All 17 embedded-runner fault-sequence E2E tests passed.
- **Data-model & existing-transcript compatibility (`session-manager-failure-context.test.ts`):** legacy stored assistant/transcript records without `quotaScope` load with settings and data intact, and serialized `daily-model` scope survives a SQLite transcript round trip without schema migration.
- Core typecheck, `tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` test-types check, scoped type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting, and diff checks passed.
- **Test-line ratchet:** `Test lines OK: 6564553; ceiling: 6564710; slack: 157` (exact allocation matches the consolidated test delta).
- **Canonical branch autoreview (pre-push on `e9dc23725` against `origin/main`, P0–P3):** `scoped-clean`, zero findings (`overall: patch is correct (0.85)`).
- Security budgets unchanged: 16 distinct quota objects × 11 own-data fields = 176 maximum descriptor reads, with accessors not invoked; diagnostic graph caps unchanged.
- Privacy audit passed.

### Real HTTP transport + shipped AgentSession behavior (red on base, green on head)

This additional runtime proof uses a real local HTTP fixture, the production `streamSimpleOpenAICompletions` adapter and HTTP client, `createAgentSession`, `AgentSession.prompt`, and production `runWithModelFallback`. It does not fabricate StreamFunction events, mock `runEmbeddedAttempt`, mock fetch, replace sleep, or implement a retry loop. Each fallback callback creates one real session and calls `prompt` once; the session owns all same-model retries. Resource discovery, authentication and session state are isolated; the credential is a synthetic fixture value. This is a real-transport/session-boundary proof, not a CLI/Gateway or full embedded-runner launch, nor a live upstream daily-limit claim.

The HTTP fixture observes POST request model IDs and returns:
```text
daily primary: HTTP 429
{"error":{"status":429,"code":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED","message":"429 request rejected","quotaScope":"daily-model"}}
ordinary primary, request 1: HTTP 429
{"error":{"status":429,"code":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED","message":"429 request rejected"}}
backup, or ordinary primary request 2: HTTP 200 text/event-stream
assistant content: "Cedar proof completed."
finish_reason: "stop"; terminal [DONE]
```

Configuration uses `provider-cedar/primary`, backup `provider-cedar/backup`, session retry `{enabled:true,maxRetries:2,baseDelayMs:1}`, and disabled automatic compaction. Scenario B has explicit configured `fallbacks: []` and `fallbacksOverride: []`. Retry counts below count actual `auto_retry_start` session events emitted at the real sleep boundary, with native timers left intact. Request counts independently verify those retries.

The identical temporary harness was executed with:
```sh
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/agents/sessions/quota-real-transport-proof.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
```
No proof code is committed; the reviewed PR head and its CI identity remain unchanged.

Pinned base `aa9531e37637d977792513c3082d575916bd4325` (the observed `origin/main`):
```text
daily-backup requests=[primary,primary,primary,backup] retries=2
terminals=[error,error,error,stop]; quotaScope absent on all errors; result=backup
daily-empty requests=[primary,primary,primary] retries=2
terminals=[error,error,error]; quotaScope absent; terminal reason=rate_limit
ordinary requests=[primary,primary] retries=1
terminals=[error,stop]; result=primary
Tests: 2 failed (daily request-count assertions), 1 passed (ordinary).
```

Pinned head `e9dc2372526dd74347bec073803b7c055cbd4d75`:
```text
daily-backup requests=[primary,backup] retries=0
terminals=[error(quotaScope=daily-model),stop]; result=backup
daily-empty requests=[primary] retries=0
terminals=[error(quotaScope=daily-model)]; terminal reason=rate_limit
ordinary requests=[primary,primary] retries=1
terminals=[error,stop]; result=primary
Test Files: 1 passed. Tests: 3 passed.
```

Daily quota scope is lost and two unnecessary same-model retries occur on base, but is retained with zero same-model retry delays on head. Explicit empty fallbacks remain terminal; ordinary throttling still recovers through the session's normal retry path.

### Latest-stable existing-state upgrade compatibility

Latest remote stable at verification: `v2026.11.2`, commit `b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce`. Its authentic source was run in a separate extracted source tree using installed dependencies (not a separately installed distribution). Its production `writeConfigFile`, `upsertSessionEntryCore`, `SessionManager.openAsync` and awaited `appendMessageAsync` created isolated persistent SQLite state, a named session, historical user/assistant messages, and compaction setting `keepRecentTokens: 4567`.

```text
STABLE_SEED_OK settings/session/user/assistant persisted
stable state schema=22; agent schema=27; both quick_check=ok
```

HEAD initially correctly refused the old agent schema and requested Doctor maintenance. Low-level migration without backed-up credential custody was also refused. The real production `doctorCommand(undefined, {fix:true,nonInteractive:true,yes:true})` orchestration then preserved original SQLite backups, acquired offline maintenance, migrated state schema 22 -> 39 and agent schema 27 -> 41, and wrote config migrations. No schema guard or migration-custody check was bypassed.

Qualification: the package-manager CLI launch could not build unrelated Control UI/plugin assets because this installation lacks required build dependencies. Source-level Doctor reached and completed the database migration phases; later unrelated checks exceeded the harness time limit. This is not a claim of an entirely successful CLI Doctor run. On subsequent access, the normal database owner detected the exited maintenance process and ran its integrity gate.

Actual HEAD load/append/reopen output:
```text
HEAD_EXISTING_STATE_OK historical assistant + settings preserved
HEAD_ROUNDTRIP_OK failures=2 quotaScope absent=>retryable true daily-model=>false
```

Both a new ordinary assistant failure with no `quotaScope` and a new daily-model assistant failure were persisted using awaited production `SessionManager.appendMessageAsync`, reopened through `SessionManager.openAsync`, and classified with production `isRetryableAssistantError`. Neither failure replaces the historical stable transcript. Post-upgrade `PRAGMA quick_check`: state=ok, agent=ok. Final schema versions: state=39, agent=41.

Fresh-process readback (exit 0):
```text
HEAD_SESSION_METADATA_OK label/sessionId preserved
HEAD_EXISTING_STATE_OK historical assistant + settings preserved
HEAD_ROUNDTRIP_OK failures=2 quotaScope absent=>retryable true daily-model=>false
```

Public evidence was audited before publication: provider/model identities are synthetic; credentials, transport locations and private filesystem locations are omitted. No source commits were added, and head remains `e9dc2372526dd74347bec073803b7c055cbd4d75`.

## Simplification

One coherence validator serves streamed and thrown errors. Diagnostic bodies cannot establish, erase, or resurrect typed assertions. Removed unused switch policy and doc reference; no persistence or lifecycle framework added.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The legacy account fixture uses the default name, so fallback behavior hides a missing name lookup. The batch capability fixture puts every distinguishing capability in its last payload, so it passes when earlier payloads are ignored.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. All seven cases remain and two existing cases now detect the regressions they describe.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a non-default legacy account name and matching request. Split media and presentation across the batch members so the existing exact union assertion requires both payloads.

## Evidence

- Removing only legacy name lookup passes the original four status cases and fails the repaired existing case.
- Processing only the last payload passes the original three capability cases and fails the repaired union case on missing media.
- Restored production passes all seven affected cases; scoped format, lint, channel test types and diff checks pass.

prs.title: fix(i18n): keep native builds working during locale preparation
prs.body:
Part of #188793. This is native-pipeline preparation; it does not activate European Portuguese. #188794 covers Control UI registration separately.

## What Problem This Solves

Native source verification requires translated artifacts before the translation refresh has produced them. The earlier revision also registered PT-PT too early, making Android generation and macOS resource compilation fail on the public Git tree.

## User Impact

The existing 21 native locales remain buildable. Source verification can run before a new translation artifact exists, and Android can project missing app-main strings from an available native artifact without replacing authored translations.

PT-PT app activation remains pending a complete artifact and an agreed upstream activation path. This PR does not deliver translated native apps or close the product-wide request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the active registry and refresh matrix at their existing 21 locales. Retain the source-verification separation and Android resource-owner correction, while leaving strict artifact readers unchanged. The Android fallback applies only to a missing authored XML file after its native JSON has been read; missing JSON, malformed resources and other read failures still reject.

The circular aligned-resource test is replaced with a fixed Wear resource mismatch that the checker must reject. Its independent lint assertion remains.

Commit `a145aaac8076` also declares localized app-main XML in the existing cacheable Gradle task inputs. File additions and removals now belong to that declared input set. Actual Gradle cache invalidation and Kotlin DSL formatting were not run locally because the pinned tools were unavailable; no tooling was downloaded.

## Evidence

The reproduction used only files committed at `bca6d16cb14b210883fd372d1349cd308d099dc7`. The repaired source used the same 21 public JSON artifacts, compared byte-for-byte. No local PT-PT JSON was supplied. Local paths below are redacted.

```text
# Earlier public revision, bca6d16cb14b
$ node scripts/android-app-i18n.ts generate
[Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<checkout>/apps/.i18n/native/pt-PT.json']
exit=1

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/apple-app-i18n.ts compile-macos --output <output>
apple-app-i18n: sourceMacosKeys=1655
Error: Apple/native locale parity drift: expected ["ar.json","de.json","es.json","fa.json","fr.json","hi.json","id.json","it.json","ja-JP.json","ko.json","nl.json","pl.json","pt-BR.json","pt-PT.json","ru.json","sv.json","th.json","tr.json","uk.json","vi.json","zh-CN.json","zh-TW.json"], got ["ar.json","de.json","es.json","fa.json","fr.json","hi.json","id.json","it.json","ja-JP.json","ko.json","nl.json","pl.json","pt-BR.json","ru.json","sv.json","th.json","tr.json","uk.json","vi.json","zh-CN.json","zh-TW.json"]
exit=1

# Repaired source c011ebe90bf8, reviewed delta c079d4afc563
$ node scripts/android-app-i18n.ts generate
exit=0

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/apple-app-i18n.ts compile-macos --output <output>
apple-app-i18n: sourceMacosKeys=1655
exit=0
```

Output inspection found 22 Android XML projections, including the base, and 43 macOS resource files. All 43 macOS files passed `plutil`. Neither output includes PT-PT.

- Native source verification and the full strict catalog check passed. The latter checked all 21 locales and reported 6,124 translation-quality advisories; this is not a translation-quality approval.
- Android owner tests passed 28/28 after correcting the synthetic missing-file fixture. Apple 10/10 and native inventory 47/47 passed in the preceding owner batch; their unchanged files were not rerun after that Android-only fixture correction.
- Source/script-test types, focused script/test lint and formatting, and the base-pinned test-line ratchet passed on `c011ebe`; those files are unchanged by the one-line Gradle follow-up. The per-change test allocation is 420; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Named comment review found no added comments or suppressions. Root independently inspected the source delta and hashed every generated output against its inventory.

On `a145aaac`, [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41205712153), [artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41205712047) and [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41205712126) passed. All six selected Android gates passed, including ktlint; Windows was skipped, not an executed pass. The [exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189089#issuecomment-6540020005) has no findings or further contributor-facing requests. Actual incremental Gradle remove/restore cache behavior was not exercised. No PT-PT native-app delivery, device installation, signing or rendered PT-PT app UI is claimed. Maintainer direction is still required for atomic PT-PT artifact availability and activation through the existing generated-file ownership policy.


<details>
<summary>Withheld-artifact and missing-authored-XML CLI evidence</summary>

### Additional provider-free CLI behavior proof

The current commands used a public `c011ebe` snapshot and synthetic file omissions. Baseline comparisons substituted only the original Android/Apple owner files from `60ba2bc1`; all other files stayed at `c011ebe`. This is an owner-level red/green comparison, not a complete base-revision build.

With the registered French native artifact withheld:

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts verify
# Original 60ba owner files: exit 1
native-app-i18n: entries=4545 changed=false
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<isolated>/apps/.i18n/native/fr.json'

# Current c011 owner files: exit 0
native-app-i18n: entries=4545 changed=false
android-app-i18n: appSourceKeys=21 thirdPartySourceKeys=4 wearSourceKeys=131
apple-app-i18n: sourceMacosKeys=1655

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/native-app-i18n.ts check
# Current c011 owner files: exit 1
Error: native locale artifact validation failed:
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<isolated>/apps/.i18n/native/fr.json'
```

With all native artifacts present and only authored `values-fr/strings.xml` withheld:

```text
$ node scripts/android-app-i18n.ts generate
# Original 60ba Android owner: exit 0, no stdout
# Actual file readback: generated values-fr/strings.xml absent.

$ node scripts/android-app-i18n.ts generate
# Current c011 Android owner: exit 0, no stdout
# Actual file readback: generated values-fr/strings.xml present.
```

Separate readback assertions passed for all 21 generated values against the committed French artifact and for their placeholders. Examples read from the actual output are `cancel = Annuler`, `trust_and_continue = Faire confiance et continuer`, and `about_build_version_accessibility = Version %1$s`. The XML is 3,134 bytes with SHA-256 `eb0657bd5c6007ef98c59a8d11c27f11faaad4f87533828ca906400864b4a221`. After restoring the authored French XML, another native generation exited 0 and removed the stale generated fallback while preserving `native_strings.xml`. The generated French XML was also retained separately with the same hash for inspection. All 20 authored locale XML files present during the omission stayed byte-identical. After fixture restoration, all 21 authored locale XML files, all 21 native JSONs and the source inventory matched their original hashes.

The follow-up adds localized app-main XML to the existing Gradle input file tree. Actual Gradle up-to-date/cache invalidation and Kotlin DSL formatting were **not run** because Gradle 9.7.1, its cached distribution, Android SDK and standalone Kotlin formatters were unavailable. No tooling was downloaded. These CLI cases prove producer behavior, not Gradle execution or rendered app behavior.

The existing inter-read disappearance negative remains as distinct defensive missing-projection rejection coverage. It is not Gradle cache proof or a general concurrency guarantee; the normal missing-at-planning case instead creates a valid fallback.

</details>

prs.title: feat(ui): clarify New Session project discovery and management
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197417

Replacement for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197419 at the original author's request. This is a contributor proposal, not accepted product direction; no merge is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

New Session makes saved projects, local folders and remote repositories hard to discover, and typing starts remote search without an explicit action.

## User Impact

Typing filters saved projects without contacting GitHub. Choose **Search GitHub** or press Enter on a plain-text query to search remotely. If a row is highlighted, Enter selects it; a pasted Git URL remains directly selectable. Saved checkouts with identical labels show their distinct paths or project IDs.

Administrators can remove a saved entry from the shared catalog after confirming the checkout. This does not delete the checkout, files or session history. Built-in workspaces cannot be removed. A failed request stays visible after the picker closes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing search header, keyboard navigation, menu rows, shared project catalog, native confirmation and page error toast handle the flow. The remote search timer is gone. A successful removal clears the matching saved preference before refreshing the catalog; it leaves a newer selection alone. Recent-folder dismissal, clone destination, protocols and permissions are unchanged. This carries the original proposal from #197419 forward without creating a replacement PR.

## Evidence

Verified revision: [4083cfcbe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4083cfcbed8e80be0492fb29abe3ae0a73bfb23a), integrated against main at [c6d94d5f5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c6d94d5f55e73c50773d857cf23cb485d1cffdef). prs.title: fix: keep HTML previews still when opened from chat
prs.body:
Closes #207218

## What Problem This Solves

Opening an HTML file from chat can show a control below the loading skeleton, then move it before the first click lands. A user can aim at the right place and still miss.

## User Impact

The preview stays in place while loading. Its controls appear where they can be clicked, with no setting or action required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iframe now takes its final space from the start. The existing skeleton overlays just that space until the sandbox reports the document rendered. File notices stay above it, and the frame is not presented or focusable early. The loading, error and retry flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

I opened a chat file link in the built Control UI with Chromium at 2×. The file contained a native “Batch notes” disclosure. I held the sandbox load acknowledgement to capture the transition, then clicked once at the first visible target. On main (`f75bd912f3fd`), it moved from y=262 to y=109 and the click missed. On `9e8557151d88`, the iframe stayed at y=84 and the first click at y=109 opened the disclosure.

The committed geometry assertion also [failed on main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b98c09340a79abd9410d90e94a299afe). The [fixed replay and all five preview E2Es passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a6b369c1594cfff90744681670703437), as did [UI typechecking and focused lint](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_034dd328573ea4ceae68c38e511c8bb7). The file data came from a Gateway fixture; the UI, sandbox listener and browser input were real. I did not measure natural miss frequency or test other browsers.

Each pair shows the preview while loading (left) and immediately after the first click (right). Published head `4c4b41d4c5b2` has the same complete source tree as the tested commit.

prs.title: fix: recover longer session history text within response bounds
prs.body:
Related: #64970

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

## User Impact

Callers can opt into `maxChars: 1..64000` for bounded visible-text recovery. Omitting it preserves the 4,000-character default. The 80 KiB response cap, access checks, physical-session checks, and existing reasoning/tool-preview limits remain in place.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. It preserves upstream truncation facts and marks a source-row group incomplete when the local byte cap splits its display siblings, rather than silently treating the surviving sibling as complete.

The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. Unlike the closed environment-override proposal in #65029, this is a bounded per-call option, not a new global setting or a higher default. It builds on the pagination owner in #97101 and structured truncation in #126342.

## Evidence

A Knowledge conversation-learning scribe operator reports that the fixed 4,000-character preview leaves some source intervals incomplete. This is a real-use report, not live validation of the patch; no private conversation content was used.

- **Current head:** `8ca678fa52adffaf2bb059c84e42a5c807c09a1c` integrates `a48440bbdf3e1f827e72eb7d674b63bcbb2fe4cf`. The published tree `2ee2ce64ef3f436feb4223bf09cb9709808906f9` matches the reviewed workspace. The two generated prompt snapshot conflicts were resolved with the canonical generator, not hand edits. The history implementation and regression tests are unchanged apart from inherited main changes in surrounding code.
- **Current-tree local checks:** all six prompt snapshots match the generator. Scoped TypeScript lint and formatting, base-relative whitespace, assertion-safety, and test-line budget (354/400) passed. The sandbox has an older patched Vitest than this main lockfile, so no fresh local runtime test pass is claimed here.
- **Prior-head proof** (`3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`): 95 affected tests, core and agents-tools test typechecks, and [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44606766159/job/135862438343) passed. The real-storage embedded regression failed before the adapter fix and passed afterward, recovering 16,000 characters and paging four rows without omissions or duplicates within 80 KiB per response. It is not a live Gateway/model run.
- **Review:** strict self-review of the complete nine-file, base-relative diff before push confirmed that the inherited changes were outside the PR delta and that regenerated snapshots contain the expected schema addition and derived sizes/hashes. The [completed exact-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) accepted the operator-supplied live proof without independently rerunning it. No findings or Before-merge items remain; the verdict is ready for maintainer review. Overall readiness is **4/6 (Platinum)**, proof confidence **5/6 (Diamond)**, and patch quality **4/6 (Platinum)**.
- **Current-head CI:** the [CI finalizer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44907727218/job/136859675158) and [consolidated `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44908717875) passed. Hosted production/test types, prompt snapshots, and the dependency and security review gates passed; the bounded check inventory does not establish that every job ran or passed.

Pit supplied the following exact-head evidence. The underlying measurements and verifier are retained by the operator and available on request; this run was not reproduced in the Linux sandbox.

### Isolated Gateway + real agent proof

Observed on macOS arm64 on 2026-11-21, testing PR head 8ca678fa52adffaf2bb059c84e42a5c807c09a1c (tree 2ee2ce64ef3f436feb4223bf09cb9709808906f9) against the unpatched selected base a48440bbdf3e1f827e72eb7d674b63bcbb2fe4cf. Both clean SSD worktrees were built with the frozen lockfile and the official build command (exit 0).

A fresh OCM environment used separate state/config/workspace/temp paths and an exclusive loopback port, with no channels, scheduled jobs or memory plugins. The owner performed a dedicated OpenAI device login for the test environment only; no credentials or private conversations from the daily setup were copied. A real OpenClaw agent ran through each live Gateway's normal agent endpoint and invoked sessions_history through its supported Code Mode bridge, not a mock or a direct operator invocation of the history function.

- maxChars:16000 recovered the synthetic 16,000-character message byte-for-byte. Source and recovered SHA-256: 6868e590b63de849692c4ce16ca1a7ad3dcc91311378e0615de4ee5f371a0cdb. contentTruncated=false; a separate 46-character control message was unchanged.
- Omitting maxChars preserved exactly the first 4,000 source characters plus the truncation marker (4,014 characters / 4,018 UTF-8 bytes), with truncated=true and contentTruncated=true. The unpatched baseline returned the same preview and hash: 48a905748127fa6fd3d3c81972d689ec13644ec95e29c67f6b7ec19d037bfda3.
- Three 40,000-character messages exceeded one page. With maxChars:64000, offset 0 returned two messages and offset 2 returned the remaining one: actual JSON result sizes were 80,796 and 40,514 UTF-8 bytes, both below 81,920. The first page had droppedMessages=true, hasMore=true and nextOffset=2; continuation completed without duplicates or omissions. Each recovered message matched its source SHA-256.
- A 200,000-character synthetic message remained explicitly incomplete at maxChars:64000: exactly the first 64,000 source characters plus the marker (64,014 characters), truncated=true and contentTruncated=true. Its actual JSON result size was 64,530 bytes; recovered-text SHA-256: b1acf38523b0fbc1749165b51cbc13dd66c758b0f1974e6b7ceee092c0e15cfc.

The four cases were first exercised in one normal agent turn. Because nested-tool display receipts omit large results, a second normal agent turn captured the same real results in bounded chunks; an offline verifier reconstructed the complete values, independently measured JSON bytes and hashes, and checked exact source equality and pagination. It passed. The initial guessed model was unavailable; supported same-account model discovery resolved setup before the successful proof runs.

prs.title: docs(gateway): say which role policy binds automatic utility work
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

`docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md` says that "bounded automatic metadata" keeps Gateway service authority, but does not say what that covers. #207070 bound progress narration to the turn's operator role and session observer digests to the session owner's role, so the sentence now reads as if those still bypass the role `modelPolicy`. Operators who restrict utility models cannot tell from the docs which automatic model calls their roles control.

## Change

Docs only. Replace the undefined term with the consumers and the authority each uses:

- Progress narration: the turn's role. Execution skips refused utility models; a role that refuses every utility model gets no narration.
- Session observer digests: the session owner's role, resolved once when a run's observation starts. A refusing owner role turns observation off for that run. Deleted owner profiles and sessions without an owner are observed on service authority.
- Automatically generated session and thread titles, inbound media preprocessing and host-owned execution approval keep service authority (unchanged; chat-send dashboard titles and channel thread titles pass no operator authority).

## Security note

Before #207070, progress narration and session observer digests ran the utility model even when the role's `modelPolicy` refused it (since #156346, 2026-09-23). The refused model ran on the Gateway's credentials and its short text was shown; main turns, tools and data access were not affected. #207070 fixed it on main; the narration part is being backported to the active extended-stable line and the fix pair to the next stable.

## Evidence

- Text checked against `src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator.ts`, `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-background.ts` on main.
- `oxfmt --check`, `check-docs-mdx`, `docs:check-links` (0 broken), `git diff --check`: clean.
- Local review: patch is correct, 0 findings.

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): link a first account from a device sign-in only when its verified email matches the sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a claw with OpenClaw ID remote access, a person who signed in through Tailscale or a trusted proxy can press **Link** in Settings → Profile (or finish **Turn on remote access**) to attach their OpenClaw ID to their profile. That uses a device code, and approving a device code (RFC 8628) does not show who approved it. Today the Gateway links whichever OpenClaw ID account approved the code to the profile on the connection, so a profile can end up linked to an account that is not its person's, and that account's devices then arrive as that person.

## User Impact

- **Link** still links in one step when your OpenClaw ID's email is verified by OpenClaw ID and is the same email as the sign-in you connected with (your Tailscale login or trusted-proxy identity).
- When the emails differ, the email is not verified, or your sign-in is not an email address, **Link** writes nothing, says that Link works only for a verified email that matches your sign-in, and says how to get linked instead: an owner invites this OpenClaw ID to your profile as **Existing person on this claw** and approves the request in People.
- After **Turn on remote access**, the setup notice shows nothing when your profile is linked. When it is not, it gives steps that work from a personal connection: open **Remote access** in an approved owner browser, choose **Invite someone**, enter this OpenClaw ID's email, pick your profile under **Existing person on this claw**, set **Role** to the role you have now, choose **Create invite link**, open that link and sign in with this OpenClaw ID, then choose **Approve** in People in the owner browser. The steps ask for your current role because approving an invitation assigns the invitation's role to the selected profile; changing that is a separate issue.
- Existing links, **Unlink**, `link_status` and the invitation flow are unchanged. No migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The device code cannot tell the Gateway who approved it, but the connection already carries a verified identity of its own. Requiring the issuer's `email_verified: true` and an exact match (after `normalizeProfileEmail`, which trims and lowercases) with the connection's own login email ties the account to the person on the connection without new infrastructure. The comparison never uses email aliases stored on the profile or invite reports: an account can report any address an alias happens to hold, and aliases come from many sign-in routes.

A first link that does not meet the rule goes through the existing owner-approved invitation, which already selects an existing profile. Held sign-ins (`link_held`, the remote access commit) come only from `device_poll` (`account-sign-in.ts` has the only `held.set`), so one rule covers all three paths. The PKCE popup is only available to the loopback operator, which never links.

Assumption for the feature owner to confirm: two OpenClaw ID accounts cannot hold the same verified email. Nothing in this repository states it. The protocol treats reported email as display only (`ReportedSender`, "display only, never authority", `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/discovery/mailbox.ts:138`) and says an email invite audience is not a boundary on its own (`statements/types.ts:87`); accounts are keyed by `sub`. If the issuer can verify one email for two accounts, the matching rule would accept either of them for a person with that login email.

Open question for the feature owner: whether a person whose OpenClaw ID email differs from their sign-in email should have another self-service path, for example a browser-bound grant on the personal origin. Today they go through an owner-approved invitation.

## Evidence

### Before and after

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profile A has no `openclaw.id` row; the account that approves the code has a verified email equal to this sign-in's email | linked | linked |
| Profile A has no `openclaw.id` row; a second account (different `sub`, same reported email, connection login differs) approves the code, `device_poll link` | `link: linked`, row inserted | `link: link_approval_required`, no row |
| Same, account email not verified or `email_verified` missing | linked, row inserted | `link_approval_required`, no row |
| Same, through `link_held` with the held token | linked, row inserted | same rule as `device_poll` |
| Same, remote access commit by a personal admin | profile linked | claw linked; profile linked only under the same rule |
| Account already linked to this profile | `linked` | `linked` |
| Account linked to another profile | `linked_elsewhere` | `linked_elsewhere` |
| Profile already linked to a different account | `profile_linked` | `profile_linked` ("Unlink it first"), no row |
| Owner invites the account as **Existing person on this claw** and approves | linked | linked (unchanged) |
| Settings → Profile, not linked | **Link** | **Link**, with a helper line saying when it links and that an owner invites it otherwise |
| Setup notice, `link_approval_required` | "Link it in Settings → Profile" | steps through an approved owner browser, the invite link and **Approve** in People |

### Tests

- `src/gateway/openclaw-id/account-link.persistence.test.ts` (real profile state, production `openclawId.account` handler and device sign-in flow, stubbed issuer):
  - one `first link for <case>` row per case: a matching verified email links, including case and spacing that `normalizeProfileEmail` makes equal; unverified, missing or string `email_verified`, a different email, the profile's own alias reported while the login differs, a login that is not an email, a provider login (`person@github`) and look-alike variants (`exampIe`, an inner space, a plus tag, a trailing dot, a Cyrillic letter) write no row;
  - `link_held` follows the same rule; once linked, the account is recognized and a second account on the profile gets `profile_linked` and is not added;
  - handler to handler, with the claw's own owner account as the redeemer: the setup connection gets `not_owner` from People and `not_direct` for registering or approving an invite; the owner browser registers the invite for the profile and approves it; the redemption is delivered as the mailbox reader delivers it; the link lands on the profile, the setup connection's `link_held` reports `linked`, and owner devices keep owner authority. The `/join` page and Discovery mailbox are outside this repository, so the redemption is injected at the mailbox reader.
  - Mutation check: forcing `emailVerified` to true fails the unverified case.
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id/remote-access-setup-handler.test.ts`: the remote access commit links only a verified matching email.
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-profiles.persistence.test.ts`: invitation approval, member sign-in and tunnel admission never link by email.
- UI: `openclaw-id-identity.test.tsx`, `make-reachable-dialog.test.tsx`, `link-profile.test.ts`: copy for Settings and the setup notice outcomes.
- Results at head `7c1b191c` (tests table-driven to fit the test-lines budget): gateway files (`account-sign-in`, `account-link-handler`, `account-link.persistence`, `member-profiles.persistence`, `remote-access-setup-handler`, `claw-store`) 70 passed; UI files 32 passed. `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and the test-lines, max-lines, assertion, timeout-race and mock-export ratchets pass. Earlier logs at `249a8ec7`: [green](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/tests-green-249a8ec.log), [red](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/tests-red-249a8ec.log).
- Against `main`: with the merge base's source and this branch's `account-link.persistence.test.ts`, 14 of 16 tests fail with `"link": "linked"` where `link_approval_required` is expected: every no-link row, the held sign-in test and the owner-browser invite test. The two matching-email rows pass on `main` too, as expected.

### Running Gateways, before and after

Two Gateways ran side by side in Docker, built with the repo's Dockerfile: A from this branch's merge base on `main` (`8a8e0177`), B from `734ade63`. The only later commit, `249a8ec7`, changes the setup notice wording, its UI test and the docs; it does not touch the Gateway or the Settings page shown below. Each had its own local OpenID issuer that puts `email_verified` in the ID token, a trusted-proxy front end whose identities are email addresses, and a fresh copy of the same profile state. Profile A had two email aliases, `person@example.test` and `other@example.test`, and no `openclaw.id` row; a maintainer and a member had their own rows. Issuer accounts: the person (`person@example.test`), a second account (different `sub`, also reporting `person@example.test`), and an other account (`other@example.test`).

Each leg ran on one of profile A's own personal connections: `device_begin`, the issuer approved that device code as the listed account, then `device_poll` with `link: true`. On A the profile was unlinked through the Gateway's own `unlink` between legs. Rows in `user_profile_identities` were read before and after every leg.

| Leg | Connection login | Account that approved (email, `email_verified`) | A (`main`) | B (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `other@example.test` | second account (`person@example.test`, true) | `linked`, row added for the second account on profile A | `link_approval_required`, no row |
| 2 | `person@example.test` | person (`person@example.test`, true) | `linked`, row added | `linked`, row added for the person on profile A |
| 3 | `person@example.test` | person (`person@example.test`, false) | `linked`, row added | `link_approval_required`, no row |
| 4 | `person@example.test` | second account (`person@example.test`, false) | `linked`, row added for the second account | `link_approval_required`, no row |

Rows in `user_profile_identities` on B (`provider, subject, profile`, IDs shortened):

```text
before:                 openclaw.id  ocid-maintainer  (maintainer profile)
                        openclaw.id  ocid-member      (member profile)
after legs 1, 3 and 4:  no change
after leg 2:            + openclaw.id  ocid-person    (profile A)
```

Email aliases (`user_profile_emails`) and profile roles were the same before and after every leg on both Gateways. Raw output for every leg (poll results and table snapshots before and after, profile IDs replaced with names): [evidence/](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence). For legs 3 and 4 the issuer set `email_verified: false` in the ID token, and B's `device_poll` result reports the account's `emailVerified` as false (`leg3-b.json`, `leg4-b.json`).

Settings → Profile on B, signed in through the trusted proxy as `person@example.test` (name and emails blurred). Each Link started a fresh device sign-in.

**Not linked**, the helper line and **Link**:

![Settings, Profile: OpenClaw ID shows Not linked with the helper line and the Link button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/settings-link-not-linked.png)

After **Link** approved by an account whose verified email is `other@example.test`, not this sign-in's email. The profile stays **Not linked**, the message says why, and no row was written:

![Settings, Profile: after Link with an account whose email does not match, OpenClaw ID still shows Not linked and the refusal message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/settings-link-after-refused.png)

After **Link** approved by the person's account, whose verified email matches this sign-in. The profile is linked and shows **Unlink**; one row was added for that account on profile A:

![Settings, Profile: after Link with a matching verified email, OpenClaw ID shows the linked account and Unlink](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/settings-link-linked.png)

### Upgrade from 2026.11.10

One Gateway started from the published `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.11.10` image on fresh state. That release created the profiles on each person's first sign-in and made the links with its own device sign-in, which still links on its own: profile A (`person@example.test`) linked to `ocid-person`, a member and a maintainer each linked and holding their roles, and profile B (`other@example.test`) not linked. The Gateway was then stopped and this branch's build (`249a8ec7`, repo Dockerfile) started on the same state, running its startup migrations (schema 40 to 42).

- Every column of `user_profile_identities`, `user_profile_emails` and `user_profiles` (id, role) is identical before and after the upgrade.
- On the upgraded Gateway, each device code approved at the issuer, `email_verified: true` in every ID token:

| Connection login | Account that approved | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `person@example.test` (profile A) | `ocid-person` (`person@example.test`) | `linked`: the existing link is recognized, no new row |
| `other@example.test` (profile B) | second account (`person@example.test`) | `link_approval_required`, no row |
| `other@example.test` (profile B) | `ocid-other` (`other@example.test`) | `linked`, one row added on profile B |

Email aliases and roles did not change in any of the three. Raw output (seed, table snapshots and diffs, schema versions, poll results; profile IDs replaced with names): [evidence/upgrade](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/upgrade).

### Remote access and invitation, on a running Gateway

Two more Gateways in Docker from the repo's Dockerfile: A from the merge base on `main` (`8a8e0177`) and B from this branch's head (`249a8ec7`), each on fresh profile state for every leg. The image has no iroh binding, so it was built from the same commit's `crates/openclaw-iroh-node` with the crate's own build command (what `pnpm build:iroh` runs) and placed next to `crates/openclaw-iroh-node/index.js`, as the source-checkout docs describe. No Gateway file was changed. The real tunnel child started on both. Each pod had a local issuer, a local Discovery service that checks requests with `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`, a relay that stays offline, and a trusted proxy. Commit needs a running tunnel child, not a relay connection.

The admin's profile has role `maintainer` and no `openclaw.id` row. The admin connects through the trusted proxy as `admin@example.test`, signs in from the account menu (the device code is approved at the issuer), then runs **Turn on remote access** in the Control UI: link code, claw name, recovery kit, commit. The sign-in alone wrote no row. The commit answer was read from the WebSocket.

| Leg | Account that approved (`email_verified: true`) | A (`main`) | B (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | `ocid-admin`, `admin@example.test` (the connection login) | claw linked, `profileLink: linked`, row added | claw linked, `profileLink: linked`, row added, no notice |
| b | `ocid-other`, `other@example.test` | claw linked, `profileLink: linked`, row added for `ocid-other` | claw linked, `profileLink: link_approval_required`, no row, setup notice shown |

Rows on B (`user_profile_identities`, then the claw link):

```text
leg a after:  + openclaw.id  ocid-admin  (admin profile)    claw linked, owner account ocid-admin
leg b after:  no change                                     claw linked, owner account ocid-other
```

In every leg the claw was linked with one owner device, and email aliases and roles did not change. The Gateway's own log on B for leg b: `remote access commit success route=personal_admin via=trusted-proxy`, then `link_profile failure code=link_approval_required`.

The setup notice on B after leg b:

![Turn on remote access on B: the claw is set up and the notice gives the invitation steps](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/remote-access/leg-b-other-email.B.setup-notice.png)

Then the notice's steps on B, with the same profile state:

1. Owner browser: the browser that ran setup, so it holds the owner device key. A real owner browser reaches the claw through the hosted claw loader and the relay, which are not in this repository. Here it connected as the local operator on the claw's computer instead. **Remote access**, **Invite someone**: **Existing person on this claw** = the admin's profile, email `other@example.test`, **Role** = `maintainer`, **Create invite link**.
2. Account side: the `/join` page is not in this repository either. A script sent what it sends, following the app's member join client (`OpenClawIDMemberJoin.swift`): it signed in as `ocid-other`, found the claw with `listClaws`, bound a new device key (`POST /v1/devices`) and mailed the device-signed `InviteRedemption` to the Gateway (`POST /v1/claws/{id}/mailbox`). The Gateway's mailbox reader picked it up and the owner browser showed "Other asked to join".
3. Owner browser: **Approve** in People.

```text
invite registered:  report pending, existingProfile = admin profile
redeemed:           report account = ocid-other
approved:           + openclaw.id  ocid-other  (admin profile)
                    member ocid-other, role maintainer
                    admin profile role: maintainer before and after
```

![Remote access, Invite someone on B: the admin's profile under Existing person, email blurred, Role maintainer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/remote-access/invite-1-form.B.png)

![People on B: the request is waiting, Will join as Admin, with Approve and Deny](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/remote-access/invite-2-people-pending.B.png)

![Settings, Profile on B through the trusted proxy after Approve: OpenClaw ID linked, with Unlink](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/remote-access/invite-3-profile-linked.B.png)

Raw output for every leg and step (table snapshots and diffs, commit answers, the Gateway's log lines, Discovery calls, the account side's steps, all screenshots; profile IDs replaced with names): [evidence/remote-access](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/pr206978-proof-assets/evidence/remote-access).

### Not shown on a running Gateway

- The owner browser reaching the claw through the hosted claw loader and the relay. In the run above it was the local operator on the claw's computer.
- The hosted `/join` page itself. Its messages were sent by a script, as described above.
- A remote access commit with `email_verified: false`. The device sign-in legs above cover unverified email, and `remote-access-setup-handler.test.ts` covers the commit.

prs.title: improve: reduce allocations when preparing session rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw prepares session rows that need plugin-backed ownership, each read creates and removes its own publication listener. A stale read also constructs an exception even when the caller only needs a yes-or-no answer.

## User Impact

Session-row preparation does less allocation work. OpenClaw still discards rows prepared across relevant plugin-state changes. Existing installations require no configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-state publication owner's existing observer now invalidates in-flight reads against the keys and source identity they actually used. This preserves exact-key invalidation and whole-source invalidation after a write with an unknown outcome. The physical database and schema owners expose their existing lifetime fences as Boolean predicates. Incognito callers can still request the original exception and diagnostics.

## Evidence

- At the reported Team peak on `6312d8be`, the 31.7-second allocation profile sampled 5,008 MB at 184 RPC/min, with the main thread 61% busy and GC at 13.8% of wall time. Plugin-state publication accounted for 77.8 MB sampled (1.6%). A 57.56 MB native frame appears under capture setup. The stale exception occurs in the later check, and the profile does not establish Team's stale rate.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix(commands): /compact in ACP-bound conversations reports success without compacting the harness
prs.body:
Closes #207039

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/compact` in a conversation bound to an ACP session replies "Compaction finished" when the harness context was never compacted. The Gateway compacted its own mirror transcript of the ACP session instead.

## User Impact

User impact: in an ACP-bound conversation, `/compact` now says that nothing was compacted (`⚙️ Compaction unavailable: this conversation is bound to an ACP harness, which manages its own context; nothing was compacted.`). It no longer rewrites the Gateway mirror, does not call the configured model, and does not report a success that never reached the harness. `/compact` in other sessions is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handleCompactCommand` had no ACP branch, so a session owned by ACP dispatch fell through to embedded compaction. The handler now asks the existing dispatch owner, `resolveSessionDispatchKind` (ACP session key or stored ACP binding), before it touches the session. For ACP sessions it returns the existing `compactionUnavailable` result. It does not forward `/compact` to the harness: ACP has no cross-backend compaction contract, and only some adapters (such as `claude-agent-acp`) treat a `/compact` prompt as a command. The ACP bindings doc now lists `/compact` with the other Gateway-local commands.

Not changed: the Control UI `sessions.compact` RPC (including its `maxLines` transcript trim) is a separate owner. This PR does not touch it.

## Evidence

**Regression** (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.test.ts`, two cases: an ACP session key, and a stored ACP binding under a non-ACP key). Both cases mock the embedded compactor to report success, as in the issue.
- On main, both fail with the reported reply: `"⚙️ Compaction finished (resulting context unknown) • Context 12.1k"`.
- With the fix, both pass. The compactor and compaction accounting are never called.
- The full `commands-compact` suite passes 14/14. The `commands-compact.lifecycle`, `commands-compact.runtime` and `get-reply-native-compact-authorization` suites pass 37/37. oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.

**Live Gateway proof** (built `openclaw.mjs`, isolated state dir, no credentials). Setup:
- A real `acpx` backend running a 30-line stdio ACP agent that logs every `session/prompt` it receives.
- A loopback OpenAI-compatible provider that counts requests.
- The ACP session was spawned with `POST /tools/invoke` `sessions_spawn {runtime:"acp", agentId:"fake", mode:"run"}`. `gateway.tools.allow` was widened in the throwaway config, because HTTP default denies are inherited by ACP children. Messages and `/compact` were then sent with `gateway call chat.send` to the `agent:main:acp:<uuid>` key.

Before (`ecea22292c0`, main):
```
user: spawn task for the harness
assistant: harness reply #2: I received 26 chars.
user: second message for the harness
assistant: harness reply #2: I received 30 chars.
system: Compaction
user: /compact
assistant: ⚙️ Compaction finished (resulting context unknown) • Context ?/128k ⚠️ Compaction completed with a degraded summary. …
harness prompts: "spawn task for the harness", "second message for the harness"
provider requests: 4   (the Gateway summarized its own mirror)
```

After (`c76f5ee0d79`, this branch):
```
user: spawn task for the harness
assistant: harness reply #2: I received 26 chars.
user: second message for the harness
assistant: harness reply #2: I received 30 chars.
user: /compact
assistant: ⚙️ Compaction unavailable: this conversation is bound to an ACP harness, which manages its own context; nothing was compacted.
harness prompts: "spawn task for the harness", "second message for the harness"
provider requests: 0
```

The harness receives `/compact` in neither run. That is intended: OpenClaw no longer claims it compacted anything.

Gaps: not run on a real Discord thread binding or a real Claude Code harness. Both entry points reach the same handler through the same session key, and the stored-binding case is covered by the regression.

prs.title: fix: hide sessions from Involving me immediately
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone chose **Hide from Involving me**, the session stayed in that list until the Gateway saved the choice and refreshed the roster. Reopening the menu in the Sessions catalog while a save was pending could offer the very action they had just taken.

## User Impact

Hide now removes the row from the current viewer’s **Involving me** list immediately. The session stays in **All owners** and the Sessions catalog, where the menu offers the reverse action. If the write fails, the previous choice returns and the existing error is shown. This does not change another person’s list, session access, or the open conversation. No migration or settings change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both menus use the same personal session operation. It overlays the chosen visibility on rows the Gateway already returned and sends opposite choices for the same session in click order. Only the Involving me query omits a hidden row; Show does not guess that an unseen row belongs in a filtered or paginated result. The Gateway remains the source of membership after refresh.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `fb3b8b228ce3` and verified on the changed implementation in Chromium, using the real sidebar controls with synthetic sessions and a held Gateway reply. Verified immediate removal, rejection and restoration without stealing focus from the next row, retry, Show from All owners, and the subsequent filter change and reload.
- Verified the Sessions catalog through its rendered menu: the row stayed put, the opposite action appeared before acknowledgment, and a rejected save restored the previous action and reported one error. Also exercised opposite writes and a viewer change through the real session state owner.

prs.title: fix: show where a scheduled account lookup failed
prs.body:
Related: #186008, #203391

## What Problem This Solves

When a scheduled job rejects a named account, the old error tells the operator to re-add it without saying which channel was checked. An account missing from configuration and a channel plugin missing from the process can produce the same message.

## User Impact

The error names the selected channel and account and reports what the process registry and the job's scoped registry found. For example: `Scheduled account "work" is unavailable on channel "telegram". Process registry: plugin not loaded; scoped registry: account listed.` No new setting or operator action is required to get these details.

## Why This Change Was Made

Report the lookup at the point of refusal. The process registry still decides whether the job can run; a scoped match is diagnostic only. The message distinguishes a missing plugin, an unlisted account, an unreadable lookup and the absence of a scope without printing other account IDs or raw plugin errors. The separate missing-creator-channel message is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: avoid false state heartbeat shutdown warnings
prs.body:
Related: #199025 · [CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46078267247/job/140771668337)

## What Problem This Solves

Short-lived database work can release its state owner while the heartbeat worker is still loading. Under CPU contention, the one-second close watchdog can report a possible lock descriptor leak before the worker has even started. That warning also fails the database cache retention test, which expects empty stderr.

## User Impact

Shutdown no longer reports a possible descriptor leak for a worker that never started lock I/O. A worker that may hold descriptors still gets the same one-second deadline and warning if it fails to close. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup claims a single shared state before its first lock I/O. If shutdown claims it first, native termination is safe and the worker cannot open locks even if it resumes before termination. If startup wins, the existing descriptor-close acknowledgment, watchdog, and async renewal join all stay in place. This avoids adding a readiness wait or widening the deadline.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24.22.1, pinned main `2ba1a2020747` failed the unmodified retention test under one-CPU contention with `GATEWAY_STATE_HEARTBEAT_CLOSE_TIMEOUT`. A separate trace reproduced the failure: the watchdog fired about 1.04 s after stop, before the worker entry ran or any lock I/O began.
- On the exact candidate tree, the same retention command (`CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-db-cache.retention.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`) passed with Vitest and a `sha256sum /dev/zero` competitor both bound to CPU 1. The live competitor’s affinity was verified before and after Vitest. The path/global retirement, empty-stderr, and garbage-collection assertions were unchanged.
- Focused local validation: 144 Node tests across 10 files, 35 lifecycle tests on the pinned Bun fork, then the three shutdown cases again on both runtimes after refining the watchdog fixture. These cover stop before lock renewal, two open lock descriptors before unlink and none after stop, and one warning at the unchanged deadline when an active worker fails to acknowledge close. Core and core-test typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Codex autoreview at P2 could not start: the installed reviewer failed its read-only sandbox preflight. No clean local review or hosted CI result is claimed.

## Contributor credit

Thanks to @daniel-lxs for directing the investigation and verification.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report queued work across chat history pages
prs.body:
Related: [Windows Companion issue #2310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/2310). Paired with [Windows Companion PR #2392](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/2392).

## What Problem This Solves

Chat history can appear to say a turn has finished while a follow-up is still queued. A page of cancelled receipts does not describe the whole queue, and a later terminal run read can contradict an earlier queue read.

## User Impact

Companion keeps showing progress while work is queued. Clients that understand `pendingInputs.hasQueuedInput` receive it through the existing connection capability mechanism. Older clients keep their response shape and can reopen their saved conversations. No new user setting, endpoint, migration or permission is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session store observes the persisted run and durable queue in the same snapshot and supplies a check bound to that observation. The Gateway uses that check instead of retaining or comparing run IDs itself. A later incompatible terminal projection returns retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; a live run still takes precedence. The existing live-RPC `queuedCount` and the model-facing history schema do not change.

## Evidence

- [Held Gateway red](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5d2b2683eddd6b637e862a4227e6d013): after a follow-up committed, the response carried a terminal run and an empty queue. [Final Gateway, authenticated WebSocket](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a5cc17056134405a639de57eeac77604): the early read reported queued work; the late read returned `UNAVAILABLE`; the retry returned the queued receipt. The [native Windows replay](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cf1c423e88f1ae8d361bfa302cc420ab) passed 3/3 with those exact captured response/error frames. The production client stayed active through retry on the same connection and settled on the genuinely empty control.
- [Old Chromium, held response](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0f919123da85e40e753856b9d037bb0d): cold reopen evicted the saved conversation. [Same old client, final response](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a5cc17056134405a639de57eeac77604): both messages reopened with identical stored bytes and no unadvertised field. Gateway head `179aacca0d55` and tested commit `712cad767863` share tree `45a301635b6689aa550441bd000401b4ad8bf55b`.
- The [session-identity ratchet on `4e58f2bb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46101868085/job/140846258652) was PR-caused. The [exact-tree AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a5cc17056134405a639de57eeac77604) passed it without an allowlist change, along with typecheck and 14/14 owner tests.
- **Bun restart:** the [held job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46101868085/job/140846259792) logged an interim blocked WAL checkpoint for `shared.sqlite` (`-1/-1`, 7,510,792 WAL bytes). No matching `written` log appeared after the restart summary; the test failed before inspecting the disk seal. The [complete unmodified AWS comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8a14b1b6f879a5f988c2bfbca6070a62) passed 11/11 on main parent `22a3aec1` and 11/11 on merge `b72524da`. The [final hosted Bun file](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46105164132/job/140856535250) also passed 11/11. A [separate main-only repro](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_269084a2ca0c19a09c671c7a6e5a8105) reproduced SQLite's exact busy `-1/-1` result when a peer held the checkpoint lock; a reader or writer alone gave nonnegative frame counts. A no-peer close wrote a seal. A separate fast second clean close wrote a valid seal without emitting a second identical `written` log. Both behaviors also occurred in [controlled main and merge probes](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_aa2bcce8873d10ed0056ae434a1a0aa4); an extra assertion in that probe failed on unavailable optional frame telemetry, which the main-only repro replaced with a direct native measurement. The mechanism exists on main; the old run did not retain the identity of the competing handle or the final disk seal. No shutdown change or weakened assertion is included in this queue PR.
- The earlier [OpenClawKit intersection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46085959869/job/140802556358) reported the same 17 findings as an [earlier Apple scan](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46084976608/job/140799914828) on identical scanned sources. [Five-revision AWS comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_df8f43c7b045cd3d1b476410344ea656). The earlier [HiDPI click assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46085960045/job/140795921550) did not reproduce [on the main parent, held merge or candidate with CI's browser](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_629fb9f21c7eb648bc84cbcddab7c95f). This does not prove the full shard failure was inherited.

- @daniel-lxs

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the tool calls in a chat are hard to read. Each call shows its tool name and raw argument in monospace ("Read synthetic.txt", "Knowledge status Original pending control"). A failed call turns red. Nested calls hide behind a "Tool details" disclosure, and tapping a row expands its raw output inline in the transcript. A finished run of commands is a list of separate rows. Repeated failures to the same chat repeat the same row, and a call to another chat can show that chat's raw session key. The Control UI already says what each call did in plain words and opens the details on demand.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **Each tool row says what the call did, in one quiet line.** "Checking knowledge status" while it runs, "Checked knowledge status" when it's done, "Couldn't read synthetic.txt" when it failed. Each row has an icon for its kind of tool. A failure shows a small "Failed" on the right in secondary text, not in red. Shell commands read "Ran cat index.txt", with the command itself.
- **Repeats share a row.** Failed calls to the same target collapse into one row with a count ("3 failed"). Each subagent launch keeps its own row ("Couldn’t launch subagent Reply images"). A message to another chat names the chat ("Send message to Composer fixes"), never its session key.
- **A finished stretch of work is one row named by what it did.** For example "Read files" or "Ran commands", or "Read and changed files" when it mixes both. It opens a timeline sheet that lists each call, with its target under it.
- **Tapping a call opens its details in a sheet.** The sheet shows the call's title and status, its Input (or Command, for a shell call) and Output, each with a copy button. A launched subagent's step has an Open chat button. A lone call opens straight to its details.
- **Only an OpenAI model's turn folds into "Worked".** A Claude turn's notes between tool calls stay where they were said.

Some parts still look old or are missing until later pull requests in the series:
- While a run is working, the working line doesn't yet name the current call, and there's no live sheet of the run's calls. The pull request for the working line adds both.
- The activity pills above the composer, the round header buttons and the new sidebar come with their own pull requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

A tool call matters for what it did, not for its tool name and arguments. So the row reads as a sentence, in the same words the Control UI uses (`tool-operations.json`), and the arguments and result move into a sheet that opens on demand. Grouping a finished stretch into one row keeps a long turn short. Grouping repeated failures by target keeps one broken target from filling the screen. `ChatCompletedWorkSummary` names a group by its kinds of work, `ChatToolRepeats` merges repeats and resolves chat names, and `ChatToolGroupSheet` draws the timeline and the detail page.

## Evidence

- Built the iOS app and both test bundles with the SwiftFormat and SwiftLint build phases. The native localization inventory matched (5,045 entries); `git diff --check` passed.

- On iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 27.2), all 12 tool-row and related UI cases and all 6 selected iOS unit tests passed. The 104 selected OpenClawKit tests passed.

- A separate existing transcript test failed at the rendered start of a long reply sent with the keyboard closed. The runs did not establish whether the patch caused it. The original assertion remains intact.

- The visual review found no material difference from the approved tool-row and detail-sheet design. The paired screenshots below use the same synthetic chat on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator in light mode. Before: `0d8e62f26004`. After: `64ed9d27efdb` (same native inputs as the tested candidate). No live Gateway or physical device was used.

## Screenshots

### Annotated comparison

| ![Before: red failure highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8554e3f9-c4eb-4787-9f29-ff85aa186c28) | ![After: row opening details highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c43a2ad5-2853-4369-8b65-bad5e56b84ed) |

prs.title: fix: keep storage initialization on the selected profile
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an uninitialized storage location is checked under a named profile, the CLI suggests running `openclaw storage init <name>`. If the default profile has a location with the same name, copying the suggestion writes the initialization marker to that other location instead.

## User Impact

The suggested command keeps the selected profile. For example, checking `archive` under `--profile work` suggests `openclaw --profile work storage init archive`. The message still recommends initialization only for a new location, and still tells users of an existing destination to reconnect the disk or check the bucket and prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The storage layer builds the missing-marker message shared by storage checks and backup listing. It now formats the recovery command with the same CLI context formatter used elsewhere. Nothing changes how a location is initialized or how its marker is stored.

## Evidence

- With two fresh filesystem destinations named `archive` in an isolated home, following the base CLI's suggestion from `--profile work storage test archive` created a marker only under `default`. The `work` destination remained empty and both configurations stayed byte-for-byte unchanged.
- On the fixed CLI, `storage test archive`, `storage list`, and `backup list --from archive` all suggested `openclaw --profile work storage init archive`. Following that exact command wrote the marker only to `work`. The default destination stayed empty and neither configuration changed. The default profile still showed the unqualified command. Only temporary directories were initialized.
- The named-profile regression failed on the base. All 17 focused storage and Gateway tests, formatting, lint, scoped typecheck, and build passed. No live cloud storage was used.
