prs.title: fix: show how much time is left on promotions ending after midnight
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An offer that expires after midnight can appear as “ends today” in `openclaw promos list`. The label used the number of whole 24-hour periods left, which doesn't tell you whether the offer ends on the same calendar day.

## User Impact

For offers with less than a day left, the list now shows the remaining time, such as `1h 15m left`. Whole-day labels and the deadline in JSON stay the same. This changes the listing only, not eligibility or claiming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The list already has the expiration timestamp. Using the existing compact duration formatter avoids a calendar guess and keeps the deadline on the offer's title line.

## Evidence

- With a synthetic offer served over loopback, the compiled base CLI printed `Evening offer (ends today)` at 8:05 PM in Los Angeles for a 12:15 AM deadline the next day. No claim was made.
- At 8:15 PM, the fixed CLI printed `Evening offer (3h 59m left)` for the same 12:15 AM deadline. Both versions returned the original timestamp in JSON. The test used a local HTTP fixture, not a live ClawHub promotion.
- A fixed-clock regression failed on the base at 11:30 PM for a deadline at 12:45 AM, then passed with `1h 15m left`. All 17 focused listing/parser tests, formatting, lint, scoped typecheck, and build passed.

prs.title: improve: open cold chats with the latest 24 messages
prs.body:
Related: #145679. Follow-up to #206816.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a chat without saved history fetches up to 80 messages unless the reader finds and enables a browser preference. Readers do not need to choose a page size to reach older messages.

## User Impact

Cold chats open with the latest 24 messages. Scroll up or choose **Show earlier** to read the rest. Find can search earlier pages. Reopening a chat can still reuse saved history. No settings changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early connection and the chat pane use the same cold-opening rule. The Appearance switch, settings search entries, English copy, and preference storage are gone. Cursor recovery and older-page requests keep their existing sizes.

## Evidence

### CI repair and browser-data compatibility at `ae86667ea7f2`

I replayed all three failures from [run 46104215847](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46104215847) on AWS CrabBox. All passed on main (`f75bd912f3fd`) and failed on the previous PR head (`78be4ee68238`).

- [UI shard 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46104215847/job/140853700902): both `/clear` assertions still expected an 80-message request after the local transcript was discarded. I changed those expectations to 24 and kept the warm recovery expectations at 80.
- [UI E2E shard 3/5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46104215847/job/140853700877): a cold-open marker survived a later full 80-message reconnect response. It prevented the short viewport from fetching its older page. A full page now replaces that marker; cursor deltas do not. The original reconnect test passes unchanged, including the assertion that the consumed prompt appears exactly once.

I ran three browser upgrades in Chromium. In each case the old production UI wrote a 731px reading width, an unsent draft and a real IndexedDB snapshot. I then switched only the served bundle, keeping the same browser tab, profile and origin; I did not copy or inject browser storage. The session history and Gateway transport were synthetic. I checked each loaded JavaScript entry against the served build’s SHA-256.

| Producer | Snapshot before | Snapshot after opening on this head | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Published v2026.11.10, npm integrity verified | v16, 80 rows | Rebuilt from Gateway history as v18, 24 rows | All 96 messages reachable, ordered and unique |
| Main with the old switch on | v18, 24 rows; saved key true | v18, 24 rows | All 96 reachable, ordered and unique |
| Main with the old switch off | v18, 80 rows; key absent | v18, 80 rows | All 96 reachable, ordered and unique |

In all three cases the width and unsent draft survived, the old switch was absent, and saving a new width omitted the retired key. Returning to chat restored the draft again. This is a browser-data upgrade check, not a Gateway process upgrade.

On this head, 279 focused unit tests and all five tests in the unchanged pending-handoff browser file passed. UI typecheck and scoped lint passed. The clean paired Chat budget passed at **1,335,975 bytes gzip** against **1,336,554** on the merge base, **579 bytes smaller**, with 21 requests on each. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46106039183) is separate from the CrabBox checks.

### Earlier bundle and cold-open comparison

I tested commit `78be4ee68238` on AWS CrabBox with Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5 and the repository’s normalized gzip measurement. All comparisons used main at `3c4362b3ad48`. The growth allowance was unchanged at 64 bytes.

| Chat boot JavaScript (bytes gzip) | Main | Original PR | At `78be4ee68238` | Vs. main |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Clean CI-style builds | 1,336,554 | 1,336,499 | 1,335,912 | −642 |
| Both sides fully packaged | 1,336,952 | 1,337,094 | 1,336,507 | −445 |

The previously reported **+540** compared a fully packaged PR with a clean main. With the PR source held fixed, the six additional packaged-plugin descriptors added exactly **595 gzip bytes** to the shared boot chunk. The emitted source maps showed no extra Chat modules. Even repeating the original, stricter comparison, that head was **47 bytes below** clean main (1,336,507 vs. 1,336,554). All runs used 21 boot JS requests.

The change keeps foreground history on its existing path. A background snapshot read for a sidebar link, including cursor reset and cache reconciliation, now loads only on navigation intent. In the production UI against a real Gateway, I saw zero prefetch-chunk fetches and zero speculative history reads on cold open, then one of each after focusing another session link. On the same 96-message fixture, main opened messages 17–96 (80); that PR build opened 73–96 (24). Scrolling reached message 1 with all 96 IDs present once and in order.

131 focused tests passed, along with the browser search and real-Gateway checks, UI typecheck, and scoped lint. The screenshots below show the unchanged visual comparison from the toggle removal. Hosted CI is separate from these checks.

### Appearance → Chat

| Main | PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main: opening-size switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0019e509-f0e4-49fe-bfba-1adc24e3b4d2) | ![PR: opening-size switch removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/169ec75c-6b0b-454c-b4db-387387ae8ae0) |
| ![24 messages required opting in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e9c341-fadb-4a98-8a60-19666c0e144f) | ![No opening-size preference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4555c9ac-197a-4758-848b-e062d8fc9570) |

prs.title: fix: clear the selected progress card immediately in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Choosing **Clear saved progress for everyone** closed the menu but left the same card on screen until the Gateway replied. On a slow connection it looked as though the click had done nothing.

## User Impact

The selected card disappears immediately from Details and the chat progress indicator. A failed clear restores the saved card and shows the existing error. A newer revision stays visible, and typing in the composer while the request settles does not lose the draft or keyboard focus. Hide and Undo are unchanged. No migration or setup is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The progress-card store can hide exactly the revision sent with the clear request without erasing its last confirmed snapshot or ending its lifetime. The Gateway still decides whether to clear the shared card. On desktop, focus moves from the disappearing menu to the open Details panel.

## Evidence

- In Chromium, opened Chat Details and selected **Clear saved progress for everyone** with the `progressCard.put` response held. On main (`1f0332980951`) the card remained; on the identical tree published at `ca6a7261b8f2` it disappeared while the same request was still pending. Used synthetic session data, a light theme, reduced motion, and a 390 × 844 emulated viewport, not a physical phone or live Gateway.
- Rejected the write, observed the error and restored checklist, then retried and confirmed removal. On desktop, activated Clear by keyboard and continued typing before rejection; the restored card did not take focus back.
- The progress-card store suite (50), pane identity suite (23), complete Details component browser suite (20), and focused desktop and mobile flows passed. The UI typecheck and formatting passed. No broad CI, live-service, or WebKit run was performed locally.

prs.title: fix: announce when Wear OS reads only the start of a reply
prs.body:
Closes #206658.

## What Problem This Solves

When a long reply reaches a Wear OS watch, the phone sends its beginning as a preview. Reading that preview aloud without saying it is incomplete makes the cut sound like the end of the answer.

## User Impact

Before reading a known partial reply, the watch now says “Here’s the start of the reply.” This applies to automatic speech and **Speak latest reply**. Complete replies sound the same as before. The watch does not fetch or speak the entire answer; **Read full reply** remains available when the phone can supply it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entry points use the truncation flag already supplied by the phone and the existing foreground speech guard. Identifying a preview before it starts works even when playback cuts off mid-sentence or the full reply cannot be fetched. No screen, wire protocol, or phone-side behavior changes.

## Evidence

- On a round Wear OS API 34 emulator, a controlled phone transport delivered a 2,317-character reply through the watch’s real decoder. The full reader reached the trailing sentinel. On the base, tapping **Speak latest reply** sent just the 250-character preview to the native TTS engine. With the fix, the same action sent 281 characters: the 31-character notice plus the preview.
- The app-level regression checks the exact text for automatic and manual speech. It failed on the base and passed with the change. All 23 focused speech, chat and full-reader tests passed, along with the Wear debug build and Kotlin lint.
- The native check measured successful TTS delivery, not perceived audio quality. Automatic playback was exercised in the app test, not on a physical watch. No user study was conducted.

prs.title: fix: tell the user when a finished subagent's report can't start in their chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a subagent finishes, OpenClaw runs a turn in the parent chat to report the result. If that turn fails before it starts (for example, the chat's access program is not available for the model), the user in the channel sees nothing. The completion ends undelivered with only a log warning.

## User Impact

When a channel-delivered subagent report turn (settle or announce) fails before it starts, the user now gets one failure notice in that channel: "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…". This is the notice requester turns already get when model-runtime admission refuses them (#171021), which keeps working for every delivered turn. A direct-message completion that owes the user a reply instead receives the child's result as plain text. Unchanged: ordinary chat turns keep their own failure surfaces for other errors; a turn that started and then failed gets no notice and no resend, because its reply may already have reached the user; private and internal runs, cancelled runs and revoked sources stay silent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The command runner (`run-embedded-attempt.ts`) owns the channel-visible failure notice for a turn that never started. #171021 qualified it only for a typed initial admission refusal (a wrapper class plus a first-candidate check), so it could prove the turn had committed no work. The runner already tracks that fact per run: `executionStarted` is set by the runtime's lifecycle `start`, and the runner already reports `providerStarted: false` on its lifecycle error when it is false. The qualifier is now `!executionStarted` plus either a subagent completion turn (any pre-start failure, on any fallback candidate) or a runtime admission refusal (any delivered turn, as before). A live model switch still retries. The `PreparedModelRuntimeInitialRunAdmissionError` wrapper and the candidate counter existed only for the old qualifier, so they are removed.

Direct-message completions run with `deliver: false`, so no command notice reaches them. For those, the rethrown error carries `providerStarted: false`, and `resolveFailedAnnounceResponse` takes its existing text fallback on that fact. It now reads a structural `incomplete_result` code instead of matching a message regex. The cases do not overlap: with `deliver: true` the command returns a failed result, so the announce error path is not reached.

Not changed, on purpose:

- No transcript-only notice (`recordGatewaySessionRunFailure` or chat inject): those never reach channel users.
- No resend on "any failure without send evidence". Message-tool send evidence exists only on successful results, so that rule would duplicate replies the model already sent by tool.

Known gaps, named but not coded:

- Gateway shutdown aborts every run with one shared reason object, so the mark is skipped when the run's abort signal has fired.
- The notice copy is generic. Billing and rate-limit specific copy (`resolveAgentRunFailureNotice`) does not apply to this path, as before.
- The WebSocket `callGateway` path loses the error cause, so there an incomplete model response no longer triggers text. Completions dispatch in-process.
- A custom CLI backend that sends through loopback message delivery without streaming tool starts could still get a duplicate. Bundled backends stream tool starts.

## Evidence

- Real access gate, in-process (throwaway test, not committed): the catalog advertised one access program and the session requested another. The `agent` dispatch (`deliver: false`) rejected with `GatewayClientRequestError` → cause `FailoverError(OPENAI_ACCESS_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE, providerStarted: false)`, with 0 provider requests.
- `agent-command.admission-failure.test.ts`: on a completion turn, an ordinary error, a missing runtime owner and a refusal after a live model switch each deliver one channel notice; a runtime refusal of an ordinary chat turn still does. Private, internal, cancelled, revoked-source, started-execution runs and an ordinary chat error deliver nothing. Owner mark: set before start, absent after start. The existing sent and failed delivery receipts still pass.

prs.title: fix: make nested Git branch discovery tests deterministic
prs.body:
Related: #204903
Follow-up to #204917.

## What Problem This Solves

The nested-repository branch picker test can fail even when the initial branch list is correct. The directory watcher intentionally triggers a catch-up read when it starts. A polling assertion can miss the first completed snapshot and see only the correct branch list with `refreshing: true` before its deadline.

## User Impact

No runtime change. The test still checks the exact outer and inner branch lists and HEAD branches, detects a new inner branch, and verifies the outer repository is unchanged. The branch picker still shows the previous list while refreshing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test uses the existing `onRefresh` callback for its initial read, so it checks the settled snapshot before asynchronous watch events can start a catch-up read. The 1-second assertion deadline, exact comparisons, real Git reads, and watcher coverage are unchanged. Production delta: none; test delta: +6/−2 lines.

## Evidence

- [Historical lane 19 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46078267247/job/140771659168): the only diff at the initial assertion was `refreshing: true`. The job log did not record individual watch events.
- Unchanged on AWS: both tests passed. The controlled AWS Linux replay on Node 24.22.1 warmed the real watch helper and delayed settlement of the first two real Git reads; it did not fake results or trigger metadata writes. The first result settled at +822 ms, and filename-less watch-admission notifications dirtied it at +823 ms. The next poll started the catch-up read at +867 ms; the last poll at +967 ms still saw both outer branches and `refreshing: true`. The original test failed with the historical diff, and both cases passed under the same schedule with the fixture change. This was a controlled reproduction, not a natural replay of the historical CI failure.
- With instrumentation removed, 59 targeted tests passed across four files on Node 24.22.1 (about 1.1 seconds total for the two changed cases). Targeted infra typecheck, lint, and formatting passed. The optional repository-wide dead-export scan reported two untouched exports (`AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`); this test-only change does not modify their definitions or imports. Local automated review was unavailable; hosted review is the follow-up route.

prs.title: fix: keep chat image generation working on text-only models
prs.body:
Closes #203374

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent with a text-only session model generates an image in a chat and no vision model can describe it, the image arrives but the agent's follow-up turn fails with "Image attachments could not be analyzed" and then retries forever ("Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input"). The chat session stays stuck until the Gateway restarts, so the agent keeps saying the picture is on its way, re-sends old images, and promises new ones that are never made.

## User Impact

User impact: chat image generation no longer gets the session stuck on a text-only model. When a vision model is configured, the agent still inspects its generated image (including `deliveryMode="review"` candidates) exactly as before; when no description can be produced, the turn continues and the agent is told it has not seen the image.

## Why This Change Was Made

The completion turn that hands a generated image back to the agent attaches the file for inspection, so on a text-only model it goes through image understanding, which throws when no vision model returns a description. That throw is fatal for an ordinary user photo, but for an `image_generate` completion it wedges the delivery loop. For that one source, a missing description now degrades instead of throwing: the pixels stay out of the text-only turn and the message gains a short note telling the agent the image was not inspected and not to claim otherwise. Image understanding still runs first, so configured vision models keep working, and every other input (user photos, other inter-session sources, revoked authority) behaves as before.

## Evidence

- Focused tests in `agent-image-understanding.test.ts`: a generated-image completion is still described when a vision model is configured; with no vision provider or an empty description it continues with the uninspected note instead of throwing; undescribed images from another inter-session source still throw; revoked request authority still throws for a generated-image completion. All tests in that file and in `agent-run-media.test.ts` pass, and removing the degrade branch makes the two new degrade cases fail (mutation-checked).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the changed files.
- Live: on a source build of main with a Matrix channel and a text-only session model, every chat image previously produced the analysis error and an endless idempotency loop. This revision was then run as a separate, channel-less Gateway (own state dir and port) built from this branch, with the same text-only session model and `imageModel` and a real ComfyUI image provider: the agent called `image_generate` in a session, the image finished in 13 s, image understanding failed as expected (`Model does not support images`), and the completion turn still finished normally (`stopReason=stop`) 5 s later with no announce failure. The agent replied "Done - the image of a red apple on a wooden table has been generated and sent.", describing only what it requested and not claiming to have seen the result.

<details>
<summary>Log excerpt before the fix (redacted)</summary>

```text
[gateway] Offloaded image for text-only model. Saved: media://inbound/<generated>.png
[media-understanding] image: failed (0/1) reason=Model does not support images
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed ... "Image attachments could not be analyzed. ..."
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed ... "Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input"
... (repeats every ~2 s until restart)
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: restore compaction counts after switching chat branches or upgrading
prs.body:
Related: #204060 and #204179 (the degraded-history warning).

## What Problem This Solves

Rewinding or switching branches could make `/status` report zero even when the selected branch still contained a compaction. Upgrading did not restore a count already cleared by an older version.

## User Impact

The first `/status` shows the count on the active branch since its last reset. The next compaction increments from that count. No navigation or configuration change is needed. Fork behavior and the degraded-history warning are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Navigation now saves the count with the selected path. Existing startup maintenance repairs a missing count for older cuts, whether the release rotated the session ID or kept it and marked the displaced branch. It preserves existing counts and ordinary forks. Normal session reads do not scan the transcript.

## Evidence

I ran the shipped 2026.11.10, 2026.10.34 and 2026.9.37 updaters on CrabBox AWS against [`c051f3f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c051f3f0f12686aaa82d6b818cd76ce8dc9ceb19). On each, the first Gateway `/status` showed `Compactions: 1` before navigation, still showed `1` after restart, and kept the untouched control at `2`. Session IDs, saved messages and active compaction IDs survived. On 11.10 the previous PR head still showed `0` on the same stored profile. [Upgrade logs, regression and paired timings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207046#issuecomment-7233690585).

Earlier navigation replay: [red on main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c6d21c81ee2204470dd5e1c1840ffbc6) `1 → 0 → 0 → 1`; [green on the navigation fix](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e1f915b22a2f0fc94461373f22faef88) `1 → 0 → 1 → 2`.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body:
## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Before this change, persistent OpenClaw agents were externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Historical proof head (2026-11-05):** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`). The receipts below are preserved for that exact head, not claims about the current PR head. It finished terminally **non-green**: 91 jobs (53 succeeded, 27 failed, 3 cancelled, 8 skipped) and 218,033 tests passed / 220 failed. - Its receipts are valid, routed equals planned, and every hosted job ran on the project's own runner pool. - **Its 64 distinct failing tests are exactly the previous accepted head's set** (the same sorted-set sha256 `185b6dea…`), and none is new. - The four shards the workflow cuts at 90 minutes were run locally at this exact SHA, serially with one worker: - two were clean; - two carry only baseline or test-order failures, each classified in the receipt with counterfactual runs. **Packet status: preserved, NOT acceptance-complete, NOT terminal.** Of 37 required rows, **0 pass, 1 partial (the recipient-authority row above), and 36 missing**. No live row has fired at this SHA, because no deployment runs it yet: the deployed fleet is on a separate, older line. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. They aren't exact-target execution, and no row is carried over from them as a pass: - Mode-B [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) at `3821eaef72`, 2026-09-18; - corpora [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) and [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393). The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) - Each packet's `METHOD.md` carries the exact reproducer commands. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers, because OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access. Structural completeness is not proof: a row counts only with an authoritative receipt at the exact SHA. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries. ## Evidence **What this PR solves.** Persistent agents act only when something prompts them, and what survives compaction is whatever the summarizer kept. This PR lets a session elect its own next turn (`continue_work`), send work to background sub-agents whose results return to it (`continue_delegate`), and ask for compaction once it has saved its state (`request_compaction`). It is designed so that accepted work survives restart, compaction and session rollover. The checks below cover regressions at this exact head; its live behavior proofs are still pending (see the end of this section). **Head checked:** `a329243bd1aa4e8677517a5eaf4a67aa30ca8647`, which carries upstream `main` at `5a3e6b1cb09bb886c4f9760d5d155353131e823a`. It fast-forwards the previous head, `16541aa5`, by 11 commits: a merge of upstream `main` (473 upstream commits past `1129d4c0`, 24 conflicting paths resolved), three fixes for merge semantics, one product fix (below), and six updates to tests, generated files and recorded budgets. "The intermediate candidate" below means `8fbf29f2`, this head without its last two commits, which this PR never presented. **Result: not green, and no failing test is attributable to this change.** - **Full CI run** (the fork's Mode-B, run `45008617882`, 2026-11-22): 257,852 tests passed and 117 failed. The failed count includes confirmation retries; 72 failures are deterministic. All 72 failing tests (23 files) are classified: - 24 tests in 8 files also fail at upstream. Six of them were reproduced at upstream `5a3e6b1c`; the other 18 were reproduced at upstream `1129d4c0` during an earlier head's classification. - 48 tests in 15 files fail because of the CI host environment, for example no Chromium, no systemd user bus, a 64 MiB `/dev/shm`, no `bun` or `setfacl`, a fixture guard that stops at the host's dirty-memory level, or a checkout path long enough to overflow one `exec` argument. Three of these tests (2 files) have no reproduced trigger. - **One failure found at the intermediate candidate is fixed here.** Its full CI run failed upstream's agent-deletion test from #203076 (`server.agents.config-readiness.test.ts`, "finishes agent deletion when personal pins change during cleanup preparation"). This branch takes the maintenance pins snapshot after the preserve providers prepare (`abc9ce5b`), so a pin written during that preparation no longer refused the deletion attempt. `bd709979` restores the refusal for agent deletion only; automatic maintenance keeps its ordering. Its output before the cut covers 414 test files, about half of the shard, with one failing test, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`, which also fails at upstream `1129d4c0`. - `compact-large-30` completed all 5 of its sub-shards in its first attempt. prs.title: docs: make the file path examples work as printed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Copying the Markdown example from the `path` reference makes the first lookup return `not found`: a filename comment comes before the frontmatter fence. The neighboring JSONC and YAML dry-run examples omit preserved comments and show different byte counts from the CLI. These discrepancies make it hard to tell whether a lookup or preview worked.

## User Impact

Readers can save each sample under the indicated name and compare the CLI output directly with the guide. The Markdown example also distinguishes the bullet’s path (`send-email`) from its field name (`send_email`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the examples and their explanations needed to change. The frontmatter fence now starts the Markdown file, and the preview examples explicitly request human output and show the comments the CLI preserves. Parsing, writes, and CLI behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- With the original Markdown copied literally, the compiled CLI could not find `tier`. The JSONC preview emitted 135 bytes rather than 142; the YAML preview emitted 136 rather than 99. Both preserved their leading comment.
- Ran all nine commands from the revised Markdown, JSONC, JSONL, and YAML recipes against isolated files in a terminal. Their output matched the examples, with the temporary directory normalized. Both dry runs left the input unchanged.
- An additional lookup returned the Markdown item for `send-email` and its value for `send-email/send_email`. Using a hyphen for the field instead returned `not found`.
- The changed file passed formatting and MDX validation; the documentation link audit reported no broken links.

prs.title: fix(codex): prevent macOS specialist startup failures through a launcher
prs.body:
Closes #207171

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, a Codex specialist can fail to start with `Cannot inspect Codex processes` when the app-server starts through a launcher such as `/usr/bin/env`.

## User Impact

A specialist can finish starting when its launcher briefly makes the child process arguments unreadable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup registration retries a transient `EIO` within the existing startup deadline. It checks the child's kernel start time, parent, and process group before retrying and after a successful retry.

## Evidence

In the supplied macOS reproduction, the fifth specialist failed on the base commit. With the fix, all 18 specialists started. I did not rerun the macOS reproduction or the test suite for this submission.

prs.title: fix: keep the selected channel account in removal suggestions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a channel plugin cannot delete a named account, the CLI suggests a second removal command without the account name. Following that command can open a confirmation for the default account instead. The opposite suggestion can likewise point at the wrong account and offers deletion even when the plugin cannot perform it.

## User Impact

The suggested command keeps the selected account and any explicit agent. The CLI offers disabling only if the plugin can disable the account. If deletion is the only alternative, it explains that deletion removes the account configuration and runs without confirmation. If neither action is available, it offers no command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The removal command already has the resolved account and the plugin's supported operations. It can use them to describe the available next step without changing account lookup, confirmation, or mutation behavior.

## Evidence

- With an isolated synthetic channel containing `default` and `work`, the original suggestion dropped `work`. Following it opened a confirmation for `default`. Canceling preserved both accounts.
- With the built candidate CLI, the suggestion retained `--account work --agent main`. Following it opened a confirmation for `work`; canceling preserved both accounts. A second, delete-only fixture produced a scoped deletion suggestion and the no-confirmation warning. The deletion command was not run.
- Three regression cases failed on the base. The 14 removal-command tests and nine plugin mutation tests passed on the candidate, as did the scoped typecheck, lint, formatting and build. The read-only code review found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the diff; it did not run the tests.

prs.title: fix(sessions): stop tool-usage retention from recreating a missing store
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway maintenance runs `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage` over every row in the agent database registry. Its `write` helper captured the execution with inherited creation authority and then called `execution.prepare()`, which materializes the SQLite file when it is missing.

Following Doctor's orphan-directory guidance — remove stale agent directories that are absent from `agents.entries` — leaves the registry row whose store is now gone. The next retention sweep then recreated an empty database at that path, and within minutes the removed directory was back with a fresh SQLite store. Doctor only swapped one warning for another; the cleanup never stuck.

## Solution

- `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage` now writes **existing-only**: the `write` helper captures without the inherited creation authority, skips `prepare()`, and treats an `undefined` `runExisting` result as "nothing to prune". Flush, reset and import keep their creating behavior.
- Doctor's orphan-directory warning now points operators at `openclaw agents delete <id> --force` after restoring the roster entry, and states that deleting the directory alone leaves the agent-database registration behind.

A retired agent whose directory the operator removed on purpose stays removed: retention no longer recreates its store, and its registry row is preserved for the owner to retire (an absent database is not deletion authority). Live stores keep pruning normally.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway + Doctor CLI proof (redacted terminal output)

A real `openclaw gateway` process (built `dist` CLI) and a real `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` run against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`chmod 700`, `{ gateway: { mode: "local" } }`). The driver registers a hand-removed agent `stale` in the `agent_databases` registry **without creating its file**, seeds live agent `main` with a fresh row plus a directly-inserted expired row (`now - 91d`), starts the Gateway with `OPENCLAW_TEST_MINIMAL_GATEWAY=0` so the shipped side runtimes run, and waits 160s for the Gateway's own **startup+130s tool-usage retention timer** to fire. It then runs the real Doctor CLI against the same state dir.

Driver + full redacted output: [`proof/retention-existing-only`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only) ([HEAD](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/head-gateway-doctor.txt) · [BASE](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/base-gateway-doctor.txt) · [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/retention-existing-only/.artifacts/proof/retention-existing-only/EVIDENCE.md)).

**HEAD (with fix) — PASS.** The running Gateway's retention timer pruned the live store and left the removed store absent; Doctor also left it absent and reported the skip:

```
[proof:head] after gateway retention cycle:
[proof:head]   expired row pruned=true
[proof:head]   fresh row preserved=true
[proof:head]   removed store recreated=false (false = stays absent)
[proof:head]   registry row survives=true
[proof:head] running real doctor CLI (openclaw doctor --non-interactive)...
[proof:head] doctor exit=0
[proof:head] after doctor:
[proof:head]   removed store recreated=false (false = stays absent)
[proof:head]   registry row survives=true
  doctor| │  - Skipped missing registered agent database
  doctor| │    <state>/agents/stale/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.  │
[proof:head] gatewayOk=true doctorOk=true
[proof:head] PASS
```

**BASE (before fix, `6356ddabdd3`) — FAIL (bug reproduced).** The same shipped retention timer recreated the hand-removed store:

```
[proof:base] after gateway retention cycle:
[proof:base]   expired row pruned=true
[proof:base]   fresh row preserved=true
[proof:base]   removed store recreated=true (false = stays absent)
[proof:base]   registry row survives=true
[proof:base] after doctor:
[proof:base]   removed store recreated=true (false = stays absent)
[proof:base] gatewayOk=false doctorOk=false
[proof:base] FAIL
```

Both runs prune the expired row and keep the fresh row (live-store pruning continues); only HEAD stops the removed store from being recreated, and only HEAD's Doctor reports `Skipped missing registered agent database`. Paths and tokens are redacted (`<state>/`, `token<redacted>`); no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints appear.

### Regression tests

`src/gateway/server.tool-usage-retention-existing-only-product-proof.test.ts` drives the shipped maintenance scheduler on a **controlled `createGatewaySchedulerClock`** (no wall-clock sleep): advancing past the startup+130s tick prunes the expired row, keeps the fresh row, and leaves the removed store absent with its registry row intact; a Doctor state-integrity pass on the same state dir does not recreate it either.

`src/config/sessions/tool-usage.test.ts` registers a missing store and seeds an aged live store, then runs retention: the missing store is not created and its registry row is still present; the live store's expired usage is still pruned. Red on base (`expected true to be false`), green with the fix.

```
pnpm vitest run src/config/sessions/tool-usage.test.ts src/gateway/server.tool-usage-retention-existing-only-product-proof.test.ts src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts
# all passed
```

`src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` asserts the new guidance text for both `agents.list` and `agents.entries` rosters. `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` — OK (no new violations or over-cap growth).

Closes #205927

prs.title: fix(doctor): Codex asset reminder follows plugin activation
prs.body:
## Problem
Doctor's "Personal Codex CLI assets found" reminder decides whether the Codex plugin is configured by re-reading `plugins.allow` by hand (#205672, case 1):
- `plugins.allow: []` hides the reminder, but an empty allowlist restricts nothing and the Codex plugin loads.
- `plugins.deny: ["codex"]` is ignored, so the reminder points at a plugin that cannot load.

## Change
"Configured" now means Codex is named (an `entries.codex` record or an allowlist entry) and the loader's own activation policy does not exclude it (`resolveEffectiveEnableState`). This is the same pattern as #205395. `enabledByDefault: true` asks only whether operator policy excludes the plugin.

## Not in this PR
The issue's other two cases are outside Doctor, so they are left for their owners:
- the `/tools` browser notice that blames `plugins.allow` whatever the cause;
- OpenShell's File Transfer gate, which compares unnormalized deny/allow ids.

Both have reviewed patches with red-on-main tests ready as separate PRs.

## Evidence
- Red on main, green here: `codex-native-assets.test.ts` "follows plugin activation with an empty allowlist" and "with a denylist".
- Adversarial review (Fable): no finding across `plugins.enabled=false`, a disabled entry, deny, empty and nonempty allowlists, channel bypass, slots, aliases and origin.
- `tsgo:core` clean.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep tool-usage retention from recreating removed agent stores
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Refs #205927 (two reporters).

Doctor tells operators to remove the directory of an agent that is no longer in `agents.entries`. Deleting the directory leaves the agent's row in the shared agent-database registry. Gateway tool-usage retention loops over every registered database and runs its prune through the same write path a live agent uses, which prepares, and so creates, the store. The next maintenance cycle brings the deleted directory back with a fresh, empty SQLite store.

## Change

`src/config/sessions/tool-usage.ts`: one private opener, `runUsageOperation`, with a `create` switch that sets both the capture's creation authority and `prepare`.

- Live-agent writes (ranking sightings, flush, reset, import) pass `create: true`. Behavior unchanged.
- Retention passes `create: false`. It prunes existing stores and skips a missing one. It never creates a store or directory.

Other loops over registered databases were checked; none needed a change:

- Session-registry maintenance returns early for a missing store (`session-registry-maintenance.ts:137`).
- The Doctor loops (usage-cost cache, memory schema, stale auth order) stat or inspect read-only before opening.

Credit: wangmiao0668000666 found the same create-on-prune path and the same capture detail in #205999.

## Not changed

- The registry row stays. Doctor still prints `Skipped missing registered agent database …` on each run until the registration is retired. That is the issue's remaining half and needs its own fix, so #205927 stays open.
- Known edge, also on `main`: if another caller opened the store in this process within the idle-handle window (30 min) before its directory was removed, that one retention cycle logs `tool usage retention failed` (worker `ENOENT`). It creates nothing, and the next cycle prunes normally.

## User population

Gateway installs that retired an agent by deleting its directory, as Doctor's state-integrity note advises. Retention runs on every Gateway (`server-maintenance.ts`, hourly, first run 130 s after start).

## Evidence

- `tool-usage.test.ts` regression: a registered database for an unconfigured agent, its directory removed, and a live store with an expired row, then `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage`.
  - Red on main `fd194285`: the directory is recreated.
  - Green here: the directory stays gone and the live store is pruned.
- Real Gateway, same steps on both sides. Each side has its own loopback port and an empty HOME and state directory.
  1. Configure `main` and `retired`, start the Gateway, and stop it: both stores are created and registered.
  2. Remove `retired` from config and delete `agents/retired`.
  3. Start the Gateway and wait 170 s, past the first maintenance cycle.

  ```text
  main fd194285: agents/retired exists again after 170 s = yes
    store born 09:18:41.315 (gateway ready 09:16:34.694, so the 130 s retention cycle)
    09:18:41.661 [cron/maintenance] Session registry maintenance completed
  this PR:       agents/retired exists again after 170 s = no
  registry on both sides afterwards: main,retired (the registration is untouched)
  ```

  The file is born just before "Session registry maintenance completed", which matches the issue's evidence.

prs.title: fix: show the saved quota reset when chat skips its only model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up chat could say only “Provider openai is in cooldown” even though OpenClaw knew when the model’s usage limit would reset. This happened when the embedded runtime skipped the only configured model without making another request. [Community report and follow-up](https://community.openclaw.ai/t/-/522/1).

## User Impact

The failure now names the model and gives both the wait and the reset date, time, and time zone. The OpenAI setup guide also distinguishes a saved subscription limit from a sign-in failure. No configuration change is needed. This does not change credit eligibility, clear credentials, send another model request, or replay work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure summary already has the earliest saved cooldown. When a single model is skipped for a rate limit, that deadline belongs to that model. The summary now passes it to the existing reset-time formatter. It does not attribute a deadline from a multi-model fallback chain to any one model. Native Codex already showed the correct deadline in the reproduced scenario; its auth paths are unchanged. This is distinct from #154631 (credit eligibility) and uses the formatter from #198324.

## Evidence

- Two real, isolated Gateways used synthetic OAuth and a loopback provider with a positive credit balance, exhausted usage, and a saved model-scoped subscription limit. On `c3127dc15fa65`, native Codex reported the deadline. With the embedded runtime, the next skipped turn instead returned “⚠️ Provider openai is in cooldown.” No provider request was made on that skipped turn.
- Repeated the embedded chat and opened the saved failure in the actual Control UI on the change: “openai/gpt-5.5 is rate-limited. The provider says to retry in 6 days (Dec 3, 2026, 5:45 PM UTC).” The existing model-picker and fallback guidance follows. The skipped turn again made zero requests. No real account, paid inference, or Telegram delivery was used.
- The persisted-store regression failed on the base because the reset was `undefined`; it passed on the fix. The three focused suites passed (75 tests), as did the core typecheck, scoped lint/format, line-cap check, docs link audit, and `git diff --check`. The working-source Gateway build and browser scenario passed. A bound automated pre-publication reviewer was unavailable; hosted review and CI are separate from these results.

**Before — expanded reply, `c3127dc15fa65`**

![Only the provider cooldown is shown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5942563-cd46-4011-a539-7c98302c9179)

**After — same fixture, `7f4d9c78e67f6`**

**After — annotated**

![Saved reset highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a1d8cb6-b716-4b3b-bcad-c53fbce5d4bc)

Thanks to @vyctorbrzezowski for bringing the community reports to the team.

prs.title: fix: stop background exec completion wakes from landing mid-line
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A background exec's completion wake lands mid-line when the output is long. The wake embeds a fixed 2,000-char slice of the command output, and on a long run that slice starts where the bytes happened to be, so the woken turn cannot tell whether the last line is the command's result or just where the cut landed.

This PR makes the wake carry the last non-empty line of the output instead, but only when the retained tail was actually truncated. Output that fit in the tail keeps the full tail exactly as before.

How it works: when the session's total output exceeded the retained 2,000-char tail, the wake producer selects the last non-empty line of the tail, strips a leading `OK: ` or `ERR: ` marker when one is present, trims it through the same 2,000-char cap when it is longer, and falls back to the previous slice when there is no usable last line (empty output, structured tails). When the output fits, the content is the trimmed tail, byte-identical to the pre-change behavior. Header, duration, output-file pointer, routing and delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-26: real Gateway run (head `197f535527a`)

Built and ran an isolated Gateway from this head (loopback, its own state dir and port, Node 26.12.1, Qwen3.8-27B through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). A background `exec` that wrote 300 rows (7,819 bytes) woke the session with:

```
Exec completed (swift-me, code 0, 7s), last line of 7819 output chars:
wrote 300 rows
Full output: <tmp>/openclaw-exec-4c73f763275911ae.log (7819 bytes)
```

A follow-up `read` of that path (`limit: 3`) returned rows 001 to 003 exactly. Steps and the redacted transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200854#issuecomment-7203987078.

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `197f535527a`)

Merged main `9fb2059f340` (`e5b7090ff22`, clean; 2,456 commits behind) and pushed two commits on it:

- `b037b26d50c` is oxfmt output only. The previous head `f92d202c20c` was not formatted, and hosted CI never ran on it (`action_required`), so nothing caught it.
- `197f535527a` answers the open half of the P2 "Preserve complete short output and disclose every omission". When a truncated tail is reduced to its last line, the wake no longer says `last 2000 of N output chars` above that one line; it says `last line of N output chars`. A structured tail shown whole keeps `last <n> of N`. On the previous head the updated test fails with the old header: `... last 2000 of 2022 output chars (process log keeps the last 2000; earlier output was discarded):\nall done, 3 files`.

Main `9fb2059f340` has not fixed it, and no main commit has touched the PR's files since (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`). `prepareExecExitWake` still sends `tail.trim()`, and on the merge `e5b7090ff22` with main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts`, the PR's test fails 10 of 11, including "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" (`not to contain 'OK:'`), the original defect.

- Each twice: `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content` 12/12 (9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases, 3 wake cases), `exec-background-followup` 28/28, `exec-notify.queue-full` 1/1, `.requester` 2/2, `.store-failure` 1/1. The follow-up suite's output-file assertion `last 2000 of 3008` still holds, because a one-line tail is shown whole.
- `tsgo:core` and the agents-tools test shard pass, each with a TS2322 control; oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Test cost: the completion-content file 5.1 s warm (26.6 s cold); each case 1 to 7 ms. +102 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance.

On the other P2, "Resolve the whitespace-only test's contradictory expectation": the test asserts `selectExecCompletionContent(raw)` returns `raw` and `selectExecCompletionContent(raw.trim())` returns `""`, and a comment says the caller trims first. Gap: the new header is tested on the process-log branch only. The output-file branch uses the same value, but no test covers it with a truncated multi-line tail.


**On main `eee7a1bd526`** (head `f92d202c20c` applied with no conflicts; main is 2,105 commits past this branch's base; macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`). These run the repo's own test runner; the loader-based proof below predates them.

- `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` and the three `bash-tools.exec-notify.*.test.ts` files: 5 files, 43 tests, 0 failed.
- With main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts` and this PR's test file, "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" fails (`expected 'Exec completed (wake-mar, code 0, 1ms…' not to contain 'OK:'`) and "keeps the full tail when the output fits the retained window" passes; the 9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases fail with `selectExecCompletionContent is not a function`, since main has none.
- `tsgo:core` 0 errors; the PR wrapper inventory test (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`) passes. On `a84c030947a` both failed against its own main base, which `7199e72e732` (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on `lines[i]`) and `f92d202c20c` (`sliceUtf16Safe` in place of `bash-process-registry.ts`'s `tail`) fix.
- v2026.11.7 (`e31bbf056de`) carries #199122 as the backport `66364847341` without this change; its wake output is still `tail.trim()`.

- 10 unit cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`: last line, trailing blank lines, `OK: ` / `ERR: ` markers, empty marker line, empty and whitespace fallback, JSON object/array tails.
- 2 wake-owner cases in the same file drive the real path (`appendOutput` + `maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`): a truncated oversized tail surfaces the stripped `OK: ` summary with the truncation header, and output that fits keeps every line of the tail.
- The existing wake tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` pin the header, the `with no output.` case, the bounded tail and the file pointer. Their fixtures end in a single line, so the selected line equals the old tail and those assertions hold unchanged.

Behavior proof (review host): `pnpm install`/build/test are not available on this host, so the proof runs the patched sources directly under Node 26 type-stripping through an ESM hooks loader (`node --import ./loader.mjs proof.ts`). The loader resolves the repo's `.js` specifiers to `.ts` sources and maps workspace packages to their `src`; the only shims are delivery plumbing the wake path does not exercise (logger, system-event queue, terminal-core pass-throughs, published `@openclaw/fs-safe`/`@openclaw/proc-safe` bindings, `chalk`/`tslog`/`semver`/`string-width`, and the parameter-property-only leaves `retry`, `runtime`, `env-substitution`, `plugin-instance-error`). Wakes are rendered through the real entry point (`maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`) with three synthetic fixtures:

```
=== (a) short multi-line output that fits the retained window (input 27 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-0, code 0, 0s):
line one
line two
last line

=== (b) oversized multi-line output truncated mid-line, last line is an OK: marker (input 2009 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-1, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2009 output chars (process log has the rest):
done

=== (c) structured multi-line JSON tail (input 2008 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-2, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2008 output chars (process log has the rest):
yyyy...yyy            (1,994 y's, abbreviated)

}
```

(a) fits, so the full tail is kept, the pre-change content, unchanged. (b) is truncated mid-line and ends in an `OK: ` marker, so the wake carries just `done`. (c) is a structured tail whose last line is a JSON closing bracket, so the whole tail is kept.

prs.title: fix: point to earlier logs when tail limits are reached
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a log tail is truncated at 5,000 lines and 1,000,000 bytes, the CLI tells the operator to increase the limits. The Gateway rejects either larger value, so following the advice cannot retrieve the earlier entries.

Related: #201052 addresses requests above the limits. This change addresses the notice for successful, truncated requests and does not change how options are validated.

## User Impact

At both limits, the notice points to the log file on the Gateway host, or to the local systemd journal if that is the source. If only one limit can increase, the notice names that option and also points to the source. Requests and JSON record shapes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI knows the requested limits and the source, but the Gateway does not say which limit caused the cut. The notice uses those known facts without promising that a larger request will recover the missing entries. When both options can increase, the existing notice is unchanged.

## Evidence

- On the base, an isolated Gateway truncated a request at both limits; the CLI suggested increasing them. Separate requests for 5,001 lines and 1,000,001 bytes were rejected.
- With the built CLI and a real isolated Gateway, the same capped request returned 4,999 synthetic markers. The first returned marker was 105; the reported file still contained marker 1. The notice directed the operator to the file and did not suggest either flag.
- 26 focused tests passed, along with scoped typecheck, lint, formatting, docs links and the build. The local review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. The Linux systemd journal was not exercised live.
