Fixes #207204

## What Problem This Solves

Contributor agents loading a skill for screenshots, extended-stable verification, or ordinary QA also load complete procedures for unrelated video, release, credential, and model-specific tasks. Five remaining entrypoints currently total 53,951 bytes.

## User Impact

The five entrypoints shrink to 26,796 bytes (50.3% smaller). Shared authority, safety, source ownership, acceptance rules, and existing heading anchors stay available; agents read the complete procedure selected for their task. There is no product runtime or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move specialty procedures into thirteen references owned by the existing skills: scorecard generation/completeness/decision records, QA credentials and specialty lanes, plugin-suite benchmarks, video capture/rendering, and release-track verification. Preserve the original content and commands, with two relative-path corrections and a neutral recording-fixture model label.

This reduces unrelated prompt loading. It adds referenced Markdown files rather than claiming to reduce physical file count or disk usage. Production and test LOC changes are both +0/-0; documentation is +627/-548, predominantly moves. No new tests or tooling are introduced.

## Evidence

- Five skill validators pass; pinned oxfmt 0.74.0 passes all eighteen changed Markdown files.
- `pnpm docs:list` succeeds; `git diff --check` passes.
- Source comparisons preserve all extracted procedures and command fences, except the documented path/fixture adjustments. All original entrypoint headings remain, and all 24 relative links/anchors resolve.
- Independent scenarios cover screenshot versus Control UI/native video; regular versus extended-stable publication verification and isolated smoke; QA defaults, secret-backed lanes, persona/Codex modes; plugin source versus package proof; and scorecard generation, Completeness, and optional decisions.

prs.title: chore: stop the Copilot attempt tests leaving an openclaw-agent.sqlite in the checkout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running `extensions/copilot/src/attempt.test.ts`, alone or as part of a full `pnpm test`, leaves an empty `openclaw-agent.sqlite` (700,416 bytes, agent `main`, schema only) in the repository root. It shows up as untracked in `git status` after every run, and a `git add -A` picks it up. I hit it in full-suite runs on 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10 and traced it to this one file.

## User Impact

No change for OpenClaw users. Contributors stop finding a stray database in the checkout after running the tests.

## Why This Change Was Made

`makeParams` sets `sessionTarget.storePath: "openclaw-agent.sqlite"`, a relative path. The file mocks five exports of `openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime` but not `withSessionTranscriptWrite`, which `appendToolGroup` in `attempt-transcript-journal.ts` calls to read the already-persisted idempotency keys. So the first test that completes a tool group (`replay-shim: consolidated mutating tool metadata makes the attempt replay-unsafe`) opens and migrates a real agent database at that path in the vitest cwd.

Every append in this file is mocked, so that database never holds a row and the real read always comes back empty. The fix mocks `withSessionTranscriptWrite` with a context whose `readMessageFacts` returns those same empty facts. I left the fixture's `storePath` alone: pointing it at a temp dir would also stop the stray file, but the suite would still open and migrate a real SQLite database for a read that can only be empty, in a file that already mocks the rest of this module. The journal's own tests keep covering the real write path against a temp directory.

`attempt.test.ts` was already past its line cap (2,041 counted lines against 1,000), and the line-cap ratchet in `check:changed` refuses any growth, so the stub inline failed it at 2,051. The file's transcript runtime mock, stub included, moves into `attempt-transcript-runtime.test-support.ts` with only the hoisted local renamed and two exports added. The test imports it first, the same way it already imports `attempt-selectors.test-support.ts`, and ends up 41 lines shorter than on `main`.

## Evidence

On `main` at `1d6b82d19344`, `pnpm test extensions/copilot/src/attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

- Before: 93 passed, `openclaw-agent.sqlite` (700,416 bytes) left in the root.
- After (`3e35bd50737`): 93 passed, no file.
- Control: with `withSessionTranscriptWrite` taken back out of the moved mock, 93 still pass and the file comes back, so the stub in the new module is what stops it.
- Wall time, two alternating warm rounds on a shared machine (Vitest shard time): 35.6 s and 28.1 s before, 27.3 s and 29.1 s after. No measurable cost change.

Locating the test, on `v2026.11.10`: a per-file bisect of the ten candidate files from the full-suite window named only this one. A 20 ms watcher on the root path then saw the file appear 228 ms after the previous test reported and 117 ms before `replay-shim: consolidated mutating tool metadata ...` did.

`oxfmt --check` is clean on both files. `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passes, and fails with TS2322 in the new module when a type error is injected there as a control. `pnpm check:changed` passes 24 of its 25 checks, the line-cap ratchet among them. The dead export scan fails on `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation` in `src/cli/run-main-policy.ts`, and plain `1d6b82d19344` fails it the same way. The branch merges into current `main` (`fd1942854a6`) without conflicts.

Not checked: hosted CI. I found no existing issue for this.

prs.title: fix: honor named voices in macOS Talk replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In macOS Talk, a reply that asks for a named voice such as `nova` can play with the configured default instead. The app drops short voice names before the Gateway has a chance to send them to the selected speech provider.

Closes #206624.

## User Impact

When a reply asks for a voice supported by its Gateway speech provider, the macOS app now sends that name with the speech request. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already resolves aliases and passes provider-specific voice names to the synthesizer. The macOS client still resolves voices locally for ElevenLabs, MLX and system playback; it no longer applies those local rules to Gateway synthesis.

## Evidence

- In an isolated macOS VM, a reply with `{"voice":"nova","once":true}` reached the app's speech request without a voice on the base. With the change, the request included `nova` and the spoken text excluded the directive. All 22 selected Swift tests passed. The test uses a simulated Gateway transport.
- In a separate check, a real isolated Gateway configured with default voice `coral` accepted a `talk.speak` request for `nova`. The OpenAI speech provider returned a decodable 1.55-second, 24 kHz WAV file. This checks synthesis, not the voice's identity by ear, desktop speaker playback, or a continuous microphone-to-speaker session.
- Local technical review of the two-file change found no actionable P0–P2 defect.

prs.title: fix(test): wait for the HTML preview to receive HiDPI pointer input
prs.body:
Closes #207179

## What Problem This Solves

The HTML preview browser test can click the right coordinates too early. On Chromium at 2× scale the disclosure has its final bounds, but the outer iframe can still receive the first click instead of the summary. The disclosure stays closed and the test fails.

## User Impact

Test only. No application behavior changes. A preview that never receives pointer input still fails the test.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test moves the mouse to the measured point until the inner summary receives a trusted `pointermove`, then sends one raw coordinate click there. The direct-page control, DPR check, loading and animation waits, and closed-to-open assertion stay in place. The simplification pass kept the gate in the existing test: no new helper, click retry, sleep, screenshot, locator click, or production code.

## Evidence

CrabBox AWS, same lease and Chromium fixture throughout:

- **Ordinary timing:** the [unchanged test passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d3a25b46664483ff0f1a7f2903b526dc). All [16 passive instrumented trials](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f842c86a4b169b7836342473e17219fd) opened. A separate probe in that run did not compile and is not counted.
- **Controlled timing on main:** [4/4 stayed closed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_159ddbccb21bdef840e1063dfdb66c6e). The probe clicked when both documents reported valid geometry, after the loading status disappeared and finite panel animations settled. All four trusted clicks at (896,109) hit `iframe.chat-html-preview__frame`. The iframe was at (800,84), size 480×636; the inner summary was at (8,8), size 176×34. No input was intercepted or synthesized in the DOM. A later patch-transfer error is not the red result.
- **Same controlled timing with the fix:** [8/8 opened](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7a81d704dba4a5e1f9ec5f76d630793e). Each trial recorded a trusted move and one click on the summary at inner (96,25). At a deliberately wrong point 80 px lower, the move reached inner `HTML` and the gate failed before the click. The uninstrumented full file passed 5/5. The chat E2E typecheck, targeted lint and format checks passed. The published head has the same full Git tree as the checked source.

Not verified: a missed physical-mouse click on an already visible label. This demonstrates Chromium routing, not incidence for people using the app. Independent local autoreview could not execute Codex inside its read-only sandbox; permissions were not broadened.

prs.title: fix: preserve newer scrolls after older chat messages load
prs.body:
Closes #207155

## What Problem This Solves

When older chat messages finish loading, a scroll that lands just after the transcript restores its reading position can be undone one frame later.

## User Impact

The transcript still keeps the same message in view when history expands. A newer scroll now stays where the reader put it. No settings or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepend anchor measures the retained message and applies an instant correction. It now ends that scroll command immediately: later layout changes are already handled by measuring the message again. This removes the virtualizer’s redundant final write without rounding the target or changing wheel and touch handling. The existing E2E test is byte-for-byte unchanged. The diff adds three production lines and 31 test lines.

## Evidence

I tested main `e85cda36996cc` and the fix on the same CrabBox AWS lease, using the real Control UI with fixture history. The ordinary main run passed; a diagnostic copy placed a 24 px step in the fractional anchor’s settlement frame to reproduce the race. The tested commit `22dd0a9eba84b` and published head `1ac2c4f4ccde4` have identical Git trees.

- [Red on main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ff91655d45a9d0b4e7ec33ff849c1d56): in 390 px Chromium the offset went `63755 → 63731 → 63755`. The last write targeted `63755.375`.
- [Green on the fix](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f8b5e9b053dc6d2d84e720ae329d78ef): all three timed cases passed (Chromium at 390 and 1280 px, WebKit at 390 px). The same Chromium step stayed at `63731`.
- The focused regression failed on main (`240` instead of `216`) and passed on the fix. All 19 prepend-anchor tests and all five tests in the unchanged history E2E file passed. [Final AWS checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4a747768c8ae942ce04b2a5fcf6ac2ad): UI typecheck, changed-file lint including Bun parity, and formatting passed. I released the lease and removed the temporary probes, captures, logs and test dependencies.

I did not repeat the 400-wheel experiment or test a physical device. No independent local automated review was available.

Reported and co-authored by @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-chat-history-scroll-anchor-race-s684c2659)

prs.title: fix: stop paused automations from sending a false resume warning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an automation paused without an assistant response, OpenClaw could send “Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.” to its delivery channel. If that delivery was mirrored into an active chat, it looked like a reply to the person chatting, even though their assistant had answered normally.

## User Impact

A pause with nothing to say no longer sends a message. Actual assistant replies and explicit acknowledgments still use the normal delivery path. No configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded runner was manufacturing a reply from the absence of continuation evidence. Removing that fallback fixes both channel delivery and the chat mirror at their source. The Gateway still records failures for registered waits it can no longer resume; the warning on truncated model output is unchanged. This does not change which yields an automation accepts (see #204291 and #204513).

## Evidence

- Repeated the real-model webhook reproduction on unmodified upstream main at `22a3aec1c899`: the tool ran, the scheduler marked the warning as delivered, and the receiver recorded it. Since `ef21b58`, #206441 changed unexecuted tool-call handling but did not remove this fallback.

- Replayed an isolated automation with a real model and a local webhook. The model called `sessions_yield` on both revisions. The base sent the diagnostic; the fix finished with no summary and no webhook request. A separate run on the same fixed Gateway sent its expected assistant text to the same receiver.
- A scheduler-owned yield regression failed on the base and passed on the fix. The Gateway steering test also verifies that an input consumed by the active run gets no assistant message of its own. 80 focused tests passed; core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Local independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings on `691f9be8c50a`. The channel replay used a webhook, not a live WhatsApp account.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On loaded Node CI runners, the native Talk registration test can exhaust its ten-second assertion budget during fixture startup and teardown. The following test can then see the prior provider still stopping. A separate Talk handoff test can fail its five-second poll while the real consult is still preparing.

## User Impact

CI still checks provider release, the controlling call, and exactly one controller-owned handoff. The checks no longer treat slow fixture work as a product failure. This changes tests only; there is no runtime or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set up the missing-registration fixture and wait for the real backend's registration attempt before starting the existing ten-second assertion. Always drain the fixture before the next test. For the handoff, capture the original source at publication and wait for backend entry or consult settlement instead of polling. The one-second readiness deadline and behavioral assertions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- [Original compact-large Node lane 14 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46078267247/job/140771659161). On pinned `main` (`2ba1a2020747`), the unchanged registration timeout, following closed-call assertion, and handoff assertion reproduced on AWS with both Gateway groups sharing two guest CPUs on Node 24.22.1.

After a formatter-only change, the exact candidate tree (`48daebe1c723`) passed the focused repeat: 32 tests across four Talk files with the same affinity.

prs.title: feat(ios): sign in to model providers and set effort from the model sheet
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, opening **Model sign-in** closes the model sheet. A separate sheet lists providers with broad status labels and puts sign-in options in a shared list instead of on each provider's page. When no native options are available, it directs you to Models in the web app or tells you to update the Gateway. Effort and speed are available above the composer but not in the model sheet, and a failed model list has no in-place retry.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees this on iPhone:

- **Provider accounts in the model sheet.** The sheet's last row is now **Provider accounts**. It opens a page inside the same sheet that lists providers under **Signed in** and **Not signed in**, with each account's status: "Sign-in expires in 1 day", "Sign-in expired", "Sign-in failed" and so on.
- **A page for each provider.** Tapping a provider opens its page with the sign-in options the Gateway offers: an API key, a browser sign-in page, or a code. After a key is pasted and sent, a spinner takes the place of **Continue** until the provider answers, with a **Cancel** row under it. A browser sign-in that has nothing else to say shows "Waiting for …" next to the spinner. Sign-out remains hidden on iPhone in this change.
- **Failures show where they happen.** If accounts can't load or sign-in fails, the page shows the problem where it happened and offers **Try again** when a retry can help. If the account status can't refresh or isn't ready yet, the last loaded details stay visible below the notice.
- **Effort in the model sheet.** When the selected model offers effort or speed controls, **Effort** opens a page for the controls it supports. The composer control stays.
- **The model list can be loaded again.** If the list fails and none is on screen, the sheet shows "Couldn’t load models." with a **Try again** row. Before, it showed only the message and loaded again only when the sheet was reopened.
- **Plainer notices for the selected model.** When its provider has no sign-in, the notice reads "This model needs a sign-in.", and when the provider rejected the sign-in it reads "Sign-in failed for this model." On iPhone, sign-in no longer opens a separate sheet. Open Provider accounts from the model picker, or use the contextual sign-in shortcut when it appears below the composer; both go to the same account pages.

On macOS, the composer keeps its "Model sign-in" button and the existing sign-in sheet. The new pages are iPhone-only.

In the screenshots, the xAI row with "Sign-in needed" and the accounts on the Provider accounts page come from demo data this change adds for screenshots and UI tests. The "Sign-in needed" label itself existed before.

Nothing changes in settings, stored data or Gateway methods. The pages use the same model sign-in methods as the old sheet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keeping models, provider accounts and effort in one sheet lets a person go from "this model needs a sign-in" to signing in, then back to the model, without losing their place. Each page is a step in the sheet's own navigation, so the back button returns to the models and closing the sheet closes everything. The accounts list and provider pages share the loaded status while the sheet is open. Opening an option picker inside a sign-in step keeps that step running. Going back from a provider page or closing the sheet cancels the active sign-in.

## Evidence

- Built the iOS app and focused test targets for the simulator with the pinned Swift tools. The native string inventory is current.
- All 8 focused UI tests passed on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2), with no skips. They covered navigation from the model picker to provider accounts, retaining an in-progress sign-in when choosing account options, keeping cached accounts and offering retry, clearing the post-sign-in status warning after a successful retry, blocking send when model sign-in fails, and keeping the composer effort control available during a response.
- OpenClawKit: 15 tests across the accounts, sign-in and sign-out logic passed. The subsequent changes were indentation and iOS UI test queries only.
- iOS typography audit: 15 of 16 passed. The lone failure is the unchanged Markdown table font call introduced in #206506, also present in the main branch's source. It is not changed by this PR; the audit fix is in #207187.
- A local review of the final staged diff found no actionable P0 or P1 issues. An independent visual review compared the port with the original design captures and found no material regression in the model picker, provider accounts, or Effort. The xAI waiting state was checked in source, not recaptured.
- The comparisons use the real main and candidate app builds on the same simulator in English, light mode, and with the status bar at 9:41. The candidate adds sample account states; the baseline sign-in screenshot shows its no-options fallback. Supplemental screenshots include dark mode. Model labels are masked. No live Gateway, provider login, physical device, or VoiceOver was exercised.

## Screenshots

iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.2. Before: `995d9bdc18f0` (main baseline; native inputs unchanged on the current base). After: `b880b285110f`. Demo data with extra account fixtures in the candidate; no live provider.

prs.title: fix(cron): show job notices when the owner conversation's model cannot run
prs.body:
## Problem

Cron's fixed notices reach the owner conversation only as a session-event model turn. These are the auto-disabled notice (including `account-unavailable` from #207097) and the failure alert when no direct transport delivers it, which also covers repair fallbacks and the #207091 reset alert. The notice text becomes the turn's input row. When the conversation's own model cannot run, for example on the same signed-out account, the turn fails before it starts and writes no row. The user never sees why their automation stopped.

## Fix

The Gateway cron adapter (`src/gateway/server-cron-targets.ts`) keeps the notice turn, because it is also the agent's repair turn (#188105). When a job notice's turn settles `failed` without starting and is not retained for retry, the adapter posts the same text through the existing session notice writer (`postSessionNotice`). This writes one transcript row, sends it to the conversation's channel unless the event is private, and adds the text to the next turn's context. No model turn is involved.

- It uses the captured target's store path and `deliver` policy.
- When the model works, nothing changes: the user sees the same row and the agent's reply.

## Review

Fable reviewed this adversarially. Applied: drop the extra flag (`jobId` already identifies job notices); skip retryable outcomes, because the retained event still owns its text; honor the captured target's `deliver` and store path.

Not applied:
- A re-check of requester authority before the post. Authority is decided once, when the turn target is captured. Repo rules forbid `assertCurrent()`-style re-checks.
- Always posting notices directly and hiding the repair input. That would change what users see when the model works, and would send a second channel message.

Accepted edge cases:
- A notice whose turn is `cancelled` by restart or supersession is not reposted.
- A session that does not exist yet (`createIfMissing`) and fails before creation has nowhere to post. The warning is logged.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/server-cron-notice-delivery.test.ts` uses a real Gateway target resolver, a real session-event handoff and an owner model with no usable account. On the merge base, 0 visible notices. On this branch, exactly 1.
- Cron failure-alert, delivery-outcome, startup-notification, Gateway notification and failure-repair final-effect suites pass.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): group chats recall and forget the owner's stored memories
prs.body:
Closes #200281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group or channel member gets the owner's stored memories in a reply, and can have the agent delete them, when memory-lancedb owns the memory slot.

## User Impact

User impact: by default only the owner's sessions recall or forget memory-lancedb memories. In groups, channels and direct chats with anyone else, `memory_recall` and `memory_forget` return a refusal with the reason and the next step, and automatic recall skips the turn before the prompt reaches the embedding provider. `ownerOnly: false` in the plugin config brings back today's behavior. `memory_store` and auto-capture are unchanged, and `openclaw ltm` still lists and searches for operators.

Owner sessions are the ones the Gateway gives an owner-private memory audience: direct chats with anyone in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, Gateway clients with `operator.admin` (the Control UI, WebChat and the TUI connect with it), `openclaw agent` on its default session, and sessions and linked scheduled runs that inherit one of these. Sessions without that audience lose recall they have today: `openclaw agent --session-key` on a key that names no chat, Gateway clients without `operator.admin`, `tools.invoke`, and unlinked cron and hook runs. The docs list them.

Update behavior: existing configs stay valid and nothing is migrated. After updating, those sessions stop recalling until an operator sets `ownerOnly: false`. The key is read from live config on every call, so setting it applies on hot reload with no restart. Checked on an upgrade from 2026.11.4 below. Separately, main's memory-lancedb already needs a core newer than 11.4 (it imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/node-crypto-runtime`), so a plugin-only update fails to load before and after this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin's provider already had the rule (`provider-runtime.ts`, `resolveReadDenial`), but the tools and the prompt hook never used it. This moves it into `memory-access.ts`, which the provider, both tools and automatic recall now share, and adds `ownerOnly` (default true) as the explicit way back. Automatic recall checks that the audience is still current once, right before it embeds the prompt; a recall that has started finishes, as root `AGENTS.md` asks. The provider's own answers stay owner-private whatever `ownerOnly` says, as on main.

Root `AGENTS.md` asks before new config options. If you'd rather ship this with no key, or with the default open, either is a few lines.

Not addressed here:

- `memory_store` and auto-capture still save group turns into the owner's store, as today, and `memory_store` still answers `Already stored` when the exact text is already there. Someone who can guess a memory's full text can confirm it that way.
- A session with `exec` or file tools on the Gateway host can read the LanceDB files directly, and no plugin check stops that. One of my live runs did exactly that, with the store under the workspace. The live scenario below denies those tools so it measures the plugin. Sandboxing non-owner sessions is the control for it.
- #196265 also edits `config.ts` and `index.ts`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `9519399f5e5`)

Upgrade proof from current stable, as the review asked. 2026.11.10 replaced 2026.11.9 as npm `latest` on 11-25 at 05:07 UTC, so the cell starts there. It installs published `openclaw@2026.11.10` and `@openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.10`, stores facts as the owner, runs 11.10's own `openclaw update` to a build of this PR, installs the PR's plugin on the same HOME and LanceDB directory, and repeats the probes. It is the body's 2026.11.4 cell with only the version changed.

Stable 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`), the bug:
- A non-owner chat (`chat.send` without `operator.admin`, its own session key) got both owner facts injected (`memory-lancedb: injecting 2 memories into context`), answered `4412`, and deleted the other fact: `Memory 376889ef-... forgotten.`
- tools.invoke `memory_recall` at a group key returned the owner's locker code.

Upgrade, same state:
- `openclaw update` rc 0, to `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (9519399)`. Plugin install and `doctor --non-interactive` rc 0.
- The plugin config entry is identical before and after; the only config changes are doctor's own `agents.entries.main` and wizard stamp.
- Before the candidate starts, the table 11.10 wrote is unchanged: same schema, version 4, 1 row, 11 files, 39,021 bytes, read with `@lancedb/lancedb` 0.41.0 outside the gateway.

Candidate (this PR merged with main `40b23868a5d`):
- The owner's direct chat recalls the row 11.10 wrote (`injecting 1 memories`, `memory_recall` `Found 1 memories ... 4412`, reply `4412`), and so does the CLI default session.
- A non-owner chat is refused. `auto-recall skipped: this session has no owner-private memory audience`, no embedding request, no memory block in the prompt. `memory_recall` and `memory_forget` both return `Stored memories are not available in this session: ...`, and the row is still there (`Total memories: 1`).
- tools.invoke `memory_recall` at `agent:main:main` and at the group key, and `memory_forget` at the group key, are refused with the same text.
- `openclaw config set plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly false` hot-reloads on the same gateway pid (`config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly)`). A new non-owner chat gets recall and auto-recall back (`injecting 3 memories`, reply `4412`), and after a restart on the same state, forget by id at the group key works again (`Memory 83eecfde-... forgotten.`).
- The final table keeps its schema, with the 11.10 row and the candidate's row side by side.

Limits:
- The published 11.10 plugin bundles only the linux-x64 LanceDB binding, so on macOS arm64 it cannot store anything out of the box (#203211; fixed on main by #203539, not released). The stable phase used the issue's workaround, the darwin-arm64 binding from npm. The candidate's plugin got its binding normally.
- Chat model: a local OpenAI-compatible Qwen3.8 27B endpoint. Embeddings: `text-embedding-3`, 4096 dimensions. No paid provider.
- An owner's `openclaw agent` turn on a custom session key has no durable chat type, so it loses auto-recall after the upgrade; on 11.10 it had it. That follows from the default this PR proposes, and `ownerOnly: false` restores it, but owners who script the CLI will notice.
- Not run: a real channel group (group refusal here is tools.invoke at a group key plus a non-owner direct chat; the earlier QA Lab runs cover real groups), a real `commands.ownerAllowFrom` sender, scheduled jobs and hooks.

The branch now has main `40b23868a5d` merged in (`9519399f5e5`); only `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` conflicted, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. No main commit has touched the PR's files since `40b23868a5d`, and the merge is clean with main `0f73e04b3f9`. The redacted step log is in the body, under Evidence.

prs.title: feat: find Knowledge records when a question has an extra word or a different word form
prs.body:
Closes #206610

Built with @TheAngryPit, who designed and wrote this change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/89e90c73-41e9-4f7e-acd4-bf39ee8e3c61)
- [Independent Gateway read-API verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b739ee22-b900-4db3-89cc-efc79b0c41b7)

## What Problem This Solves

An extra word in a question can hide a stored note. Searching for “orchid fertilizer” misses a note about orchids if it never mentions fertilizer. Searching for “deploying” also misses “deployed,” even when that word is all the agent needs to find the runbook.

## User Impact

Knowledge first looks for every query word, including matches in eligible superseded wording. Only when that finds nothing does an omitted-mode search try any word. Compact agent results disclose that with `queryMode: "any"`. Explicit all, any, and phrase modes do not widen. English word forms match in keyword search; passive recall uses lighter suffix folding that preserves the previous plural matches. Stored Markdown and citations do not change.

The next search or verification rebuilds only the queried scope’s keyword projections, moving them to v2. No action is required. The SQLite Porter stemmer also runs over non-English text, where English-looking endings can cause false positives. This change does not add CJK segmentation, approximate spelling, or embeddings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Miss-only widening keeps full matches ahead of loose matches without introducing another search engine. Both passes use the same filtered corpus and SQLite read transaction. FTS5 handles indexing and query stemming with its built-in Porter tokenizer over unicode61. The separate in-memory recall gate applies a deterministic transformation to the previous plural token; it does not claim to implement Porter.

## Evidence

Head `c18839dcfec4` changes only the retrieval guide relative to `8edc78a7a9ad`: it now names the agent tool `knowledge_grep` and the shared Gateway RPC `memory.search`. Verified the hosted one-file delta, formatter, all internal docs links and an independent review of the correction. All runtime and test files are unchanged.

On head `8edc78a7a9ad` (tree `8e8fc2e2de0f`), all 585 Knowledge tests and 16 prompt-prefix tests passed, as did the extension typecheck, targeted lint, format, docs-link check and strict independent review (no P0–P2 findings). Explicit all-word searches remain strict; the shared memory provider's search/get test exercises the new fallback. These are local results, not hosted CI or a ClawSweeper rating.

**Red on upstream, green on the candidate.** The focused Vitest run with the new assertions on upstream `91722468db0d` exited 1 (3 tests failed; 28 skipped by the filter). Its production retrieval and passive-recall modules were byte-identical to those at the integrated main base `63ca7be24454`. The following are the observed assertion results, not predicted failures:

| Regression | Base observation | Passing candidate observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Omitted-mode fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c18839dcfec4a9f18875295295b49411f6ec4330/extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts#L642-L656), `orchid fertilizer` | Returned query mode `all`; expected `any` | `any`, hit `orchid_care`; explicit `all` kept zero hits |
| [FTS inflection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c18839dcfec4a9f18875295295b49411f6ec4330/extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts#L658-L667), `deploying` vs. stored `deployed` | 0 hits; expected 1 | 1 hit in explicit all-word mode |
| [Passive-recall shortlist](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c18839dcfec4a9f18875295295b49411f6ec4330/extensions/knowledge/src/recall-keyword.test.ts#L17-L24), `deploying the changed code` | Returned `[]`; expected page `a` | Page `a` shortlisted; this assertion does not run the Decision model |

All three named tests passed in the 585-test Knowledge run at `8edc78a7`; the final head changes none of their production or test bytes.

**Exact-head Gateway reads (`8edc78a7`).** An authenticated `operator.read` client queried a loopback Gateway with Knowledge selected. The store contained “The orchid crate was deployed at dawn” and an unrelated control note. These are operator RPC responses, not an agent turn.

| Query | Knowledge `grep` via `plugins.sessionAction` | Shared `memory.search` v2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orchid zephyrium`, mode omitted | `queryMode: "any"`, 1 hit | 1 hit; `providerId: "knowledge"` |
| Same query, explicit `mode: "all"` | `queryMode: "all"`, 0 hits | No `mode` parameter on this RPC |
| `deployed`, then `deploying` | 1 hit for each with explicit `all` | 1 hit for each, complete coverage |

Every hit identified `operator_deploy_note`; none returned the control note. The `grep` citation was unchanged: `notes/operator_deploy_note.md`, revision `1`, SHA-256 `834071af9a972a51efb4ca2bca817d74687af6f0fa9d95402d48ca2c48d93984`, matching the fixture Markdown. All three shared searches returned the same store-bound reference and citation label. No live Decision-provider inference was exercised.

**Rollback compatibility, on one on-disk SQLite store and Markdown vault.** I alternated the [unchanged retrieval module from stable 2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6ea542fd97e2876aa4c871ccc494ed5419a03c5c/extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.ts) with the candidate's retrieval module. This tests the shipped index writer and reader, not two full Gateway binaries. Stable found “deployed” but not “deploying”; the first upgrade found “deploying” with the identical citation. While rolled back, the fixture added an active note and a superseded alias and withdrew an old note. The stable search indexed those writes into v1.

| First search after re-upgrade | Reviewed head `8746b096` | Repaired head `8edc78a7` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Newly added “daffodil” note | No hit | `active_note`, identical rollback citation |
| Withdrawn “lilac” note | Index unavailable | Index ready, zero hits |
| Superseded “saffron” wording | No hit | Current note via `earlier_note` |

The retained note's Markdown and vault manifest were byte-for-byte unchanged; its ID, path, revision and full citation hash survived the cycle. Both the shipped-module cycle and the [committed rollback-state regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8edc78a7a9ad054f7fd550a71388283b1183274a/extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts#L684-L734) failed on the reviewed head and passed after the fix. The fingerprint now includes the tokenizer so an older write cannot certify either retained v2 corpus; only changed rows are reconciled.

The contributor-supplied Gateway transcript shows stable 2026.11.10 missing “deploying” and “orchid fertilizer,” then finding the same seeded records after upgrading the same store to an earlier build labeled `77ad867`. It also records v1 → v2 index replacement and explicit all staying strict. This was a scripted model; it was not rerun on the final candidate. With Knowledge selected, the agent recall tool is [`knowledge_grep`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8edc78a7a9ad054f7fd550a71388283b1183274a/extensions/knowledge/src/service.ts#L110-L116); [`memory_search` is registered only when memory-core owns the slot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8edc78a7a9ad054f7fd550a71388283b1183274a/extensions/memory-core/index.ts#L347-L365). The shared Gateway API is `memory.search` (dot), not an agent tool named `memory_search`. Neither the contributor transcript nor the provider-adapter test is a live Decision-provider result. This sandbox cannot initiate an attributed agent turn against a disposable Gateway: the exact-tree [CLI process preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8edc78a7a9ad054f7fd550a71388283b1183274a/src/cli/gateway-agent-exec-input.process.test.ts#L71-L81) confirmed the exec-origin rejection happens before connection. No final-head agent-run transcript or live Decision inference is claimed.

### Two-turn live verification (not yet run)

Use a disposable, owner-private Gateway with Knowledge as its memory provider and an authorized real agent model and Decision provider. On stable `2026.11.10`, save two note pages through the normal Knowledge writer and verify their publication: **Dispatch log** — “Tamarind Finch deployed the orchid crate.” and **Garden ledger** — “Tulips need gravel.” Keep the answer in the first page’s body only; do not set an automatic recall summary. Upgrade the same fixture store to `c18839dcfec4`. Do not use a shared vault.

1. **Explicit search.** In a fresh conversation, ask the real agent: “Call `knowledge_grep` three times: `orchid zephyrium` without a mode, the same query with `mode: "all"`, then `deploying` with `mode: "all"`. Report each result.” Inspect the native tool calls, not just the reply: the first should disclose `queryMode: "any"` and find Dispatch log; the second should return zero hits; the third should find the same record and citation as the first. The control note should never appear.

2. **Passive recall.** With the [recall gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c18839dcfec4a9f18875295295b49411f6ec4330/docs/plugins/knowledge/memory-provider.md#recall-gate) configured `mode: "live", candidates: "keyword"` on the fixture, open a **different fresh conversation** with the same private store. Send only **“Who is deploying?”** The only matching content word is an inflection. Verify that the live Decision provider scored the Dispatch log ID, the gate logged `injected`, and **that same turn** received the excerpt and answered “Tamarind Finch” without a search or lookup. A reply alone, a `shadow` result, or a tool-assisted answer is not a pass. Report the actual outcome rather than changing thresholds to force it.

**Fixture check already run (shortlist only):** the two released/candidate keyword shortlists returned zero/one page respectively for “Who is deploying?”; both found only Dispatch log for “Who deployed?” and neither found anything for “Who is juggling?”. This checks that the prompt distinguishes the revisions, not that a provider ran.

**Evidence to return:** candidate SHA, confirmation of real agent and Decision models, sanitized tool arguments/results, and the matching `knowledge recall gate:` outcome with fixture record ID, score/tier and the same-turn reply. Retain raw logs privately; omit credentials, IP addresses, phone numbers, non-public endpoints, and unrelated messages.

## Related

#205754 independently changes the same v1 projections to v2 for CJK substring search. Whichever lands second needs a new projection version and integration testing. #206611 is a separate semantic-search proposal. A Knowledge owner should review the precision and multilingual tradeoff before landing.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Background plugin maintenance can defer repair after a config conflict while its child process exits successfully. On ordinary boots, or when the previous plugin result is already recorded, the Gateway drops that advisory instead of showing its recovery command.

## User Impact

The existing Gateway warning log retains plugin-repair guidance after readiness. Recorded update results, core readiness, capability consent, and notification behavior stay unchanged. Clean successful maintenance stays quiet.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintenance owner already projects warning messages into step detail. Let its existing fallback log any nonempty detail when history cannot receive it, rather than filtering by process-failure status. No new result type, state, helper, or config.

Production +3/-1 (net +2); tests +76/-1 (net +75). Release-note context: boot-time plugin repair advisories remain visible even when maintenance exits successfully.

## Evidence

- Signed head `f88e9c733173b19f96b96c640504e0f9ef4dc8a6`, frozen base `002e4b2ddf9d4f268b19e780b6ada5a985245c81`; two files only.
- Exact-head [hosted proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46100313654), direct changed-tests job 140841415150: all 29 Gateway trial cases passed, including both new absent/settled-history warning cases and existing offline, clean, active-trial, history, and notification controls. The job checks out the raw candidate, not its planning merge. All seven typecheck jobs and the changed core lint checks passed.
- Independent P0-P3 review and separate owner review found no findings. Both are source reviews. Formatting, whitespace, privacy inspection, and docs discovery passed.
- Local dependencies are unqualified. Testbox remained queued and was stopped without executing the proof command; exact-head hosted tests supply the owner-boundary proof. No baseline RED, installed-upgrade, or operator Gateway execution is claimed.
- Production imports, package boundaries, and schemas do not change; no full-package build is claimed.

Related owner change: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206926.

### Supplemental CI attribution

The manual run's dependency scan reports unused type `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and unused file `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/boot-plugin-convergence.mjs`. Both producers, their complete reference sets, inspected Knip configuration, and package/lock/workspace inputs are identical at frozen base and candidate. This two-file warning-sink patch removes no consumer of either. The failing supplemental scan is not described as passing, and no hosted-CI exception is requested.

## Review Follow-through

The [exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207163#issuecomment-7232893508) reports no findings and no before-merge action. Its optional production-path rank-up is skipped: no qualified installed Gateway is available, and the selected Testbox stayed queued and was stopped. The completed owner-boundary tests cover the warning sink; installed-upgrade, baseline RED, and operator Gateway execution remain unobserved. The superseded draft run was cancelled after its focused/type/lint jobs completed, once [normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46101369176) attached to the same head.

prs.title: fix: keep nightly Memory Dreaming Promotion sweeps from aborting after six minutes
prs.body:
Closes #193150

## What Problem This Solves

In multi-agent installs or workspaces with large transcript history, the built-in nightly **Memory Dreaming Promotion** cron job runs for more than 6 minutes inside `before_agent_reply`. Today, because the sweep never reports semantic progress back to the session watchdog, the watchdog treats the healthy job as `semantic_stall` and aborts it at ~360 seconds, recording an error even though the sweep finishes its work. After 10 consecutive recorded errors, the scheduler automatically disables Memory Dreaming Promotion.

## User Impact

Scheduled **Memory Dreaming Promotion** runs that take longer than 6 minutes across multiple workspaces or large single-workspace transcripts stay alive while actively making progress, complete with a normal status instead of false `semantic_stall` aborts, and are no longer auto-disabled by the cron scheduler. Genuinely stalled runs that stop making progress are still aborted 360 seconds after their last completed unit of work. No user configuration changes or migrations are required, and older hosts that omit `reportProgress` continue to work unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of raising watchdog timeouts or adding a blind keepalive timer (which would hide real hangs), this change adds a dispatch-scoped `reportProgress` callback on `PluginHookAgentContext` owned by `runBeforeAgentReplyForTurn`. Both the embedded runner and CLI runner pass their active run watchdog / diagnostic owner into that single shared boundary, where progress is forwarded only while the hook dispatch is active and the run is still current (retained callbacks become no-ops after settlement or abort). `memory-core` reports progress only after real completed work units: per-agent corpus enumeration, per-source session scan, per-batch recall recording, per-phase (`light`/`rem` ingest and prepare), and per-workspace completion. Cooperative cancellation of an already-aborted loop remains separate (#180658).

## Evidence

- **Before fix (`main` `4bc00fc6f`)**: Running `pnpm test -- --run --maxWorkers=1 src/plugins/before-agent-reply.progress.test.ts` reproduced the failure on an 18-workspace (396s) sweep with `Error: stopped:semantic_stall` at 360s against the real `createSessionControllerWatchdog`.
- **After fix (`2874a8764`)**:
  - `pnpm test -- --run --maxWorkers=1 src/plugins/before-agent-reply.progress.test.ts` — 2/2 passed: 396s fleet sweep completes without watchdog abort; a genuinely stalled hook still stops at 360s with `semantic_stall`; retained callbacks after settlement or stop are no-ops.
  - `pnpm test -- --run --maxWorkers=1 src/plugins/hooks.before-agent-reply.test.ts` — 3/3 passed.
  - `pnpm test -- --run --maxWorkers=1 extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-sweep-narrative.test.ts` — 12/12 passed: verifies `dreaming:light:ingest`, `dreaming:rem:ingest`, `dreaming:light:prepare`, `dreaming:rem:prepare`, and `dreaming:workspace_done` progress signals as well as compatibility when `reportProgress` is omitted.
  - `pnpm test -- --run --maxWorkers=1 src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts` — 27/27 passed.
  - `oxfmt` & `oxlint` on all changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- **Unverified boundary**: Watchdog timing was verified against the real `createSessionControllerWatchdog` with fake timers rather than a 6-minute live Gateway soak run.

prs.title: fix(doctor): report which config-flow owners have work
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` stops the Gateway and runs its config flow on every run, even on a healthy install. To make that stop conditional later, each step must first report truthfully whether it has work. The config flow reported `work` whenever anything other than its state schema input was involved, because only that one input had a read-only check. That answer said nothing about which owners actually had work.

## User Impact

None visible today: Doctor still stops the Gateway and runs every step exactly as before. The trace now shows, per owner, whether the config flow had work, and the step answers `none` only when every owner answers `none`. Three owners still have no read-only predicate, so on a healthy install the step still answers `work`, now with the reason in the trace.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each input calls the predicate its owner's writer acts on, decided from one config snapshot read without observation. Every SQLite read goes through `decideDoctorPendingFromLiveStores`, so a store nobody holds answers `undecidable`, and agent stores are listed inside the state database guard. Where a writer decided inline, the decision moved to a shared function the writer now also uses (retired state files, A2UI widget inspection, relative session stores, the legacy config file rename, cron preflight work, plugin obligations). Writer behavior is unchanged.

Inputs, in the order the flow reaches them:

| Input | Decides from | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `state-write-admission` | orphaned sidecars, state DB permission drift | the `r+` probe writes nothing and stays |
| `legacy-state-dir` | pending legacy state root | |
| `legacy-config` | legacy file name, invalid or legacy shapes, automatic repair plan, suspicious-config recovery | |
| `state-schema` | the existing plan from #206694 | |
| `retired-state` | retired runtime, delivery queue and plugin index files | |
| `session-entry-state` | the repair's own inspection (`apply: false`) | |
| `plugin-convergence` | `planStartupPluginConvergence().required` | any install record means work |
| `plugin-obligations` | the obligation ledger (pending and deferred rows) and the configured plugin set | no registry, no lifecycle lease |
| `cron` | partition selection, retired cron files, legacy quarantine, Codex policy targets | |
| `legacy-state-detection` | the migration graph's own detection, including plugin `detectLegacyState` previews and legacy exec approvals | |
| `agent-databases` | `planAgentDatabaseMigration(...).pending` from #206707, with the preflight's discovery | |
| `a2ui-widgets` | the retirement's own inspection | |
| `relative-session-stores` | the repair's own discovery | |
| `legacy-state-steps` | no check yet | always-run graph steps: delivery queue entries, workspace aliases, Skill Workshop proposals, ACP session metadata, orphan session keys, transcript directives, config machine state, shared auth store |
| `update-history` | no check yet | interrupted update reconciliation reads through a copy |
| `config-repairs` | no check yet | the config repair sequence, channel Doctor sequences, system agent workspace files |

Plugin obligations: any recorded obligation, pending or deferred, is `work` (the flow reopens and settles it again), and a configured plugin that is unavailable is `work` (it becomes one). A plugin refused by policy is not recorded by the flow and is not counted. The reopen behavior and the registry queries are unchanged.

## Evidence

Tested commits: base `870f9a62706` (main) and head `9fd46d12b73`. The PR head `c0d6346772f` differs from the tested head by a dropped unused export, test-only edits and a merge of `main` that touches none of these owners. Cells: Linux Docker, systemd user Gateway, npm install of a local pack under the unpublished version 2026.11.13, Telegram and X channels, three agents, no network. The healthy store was seeded with the base build, settled with two `doctor --fix` runs, and restored byte-identical (sha256 over all files) before every run.

Method: `strace -f` plus a preload that records every write-intent `fs` call and every `node:sqlite` open, write statement and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE` with its JS caller, limited to the `doctor.config-flow` span (and, on the head, to each `doctor.pending.config-flow.*` span).

**Red (base, healthy install):** `doctor.pending.config-flow pending=work check=owner`, with `config-flow.state-schema` the only input. What the flow still opens, writes or creates on that install (after #206694, #206707, #206513):

| Item | Caller | Needs an input? |
|---|---|---|
| `r+` open of `state/openclaw.sqlite` | preflight state write admission | no: writes nothing, the only writability proof |
| writable open of `state/openclaw.sqlite` with connection setup (`journal_mode=WAL`, `wal_autocheckpoint`, `synchronous`), no transaction, no row | Skill Workshop proposal retirement (`readDatabaseProposals`), a legacy graph step | yes: in `legacy-state-steps`, no predicate yet |
| private snapshot copy of the state database under `~/.cache/openclaw` with its staging token store | transcript directives step (`hasActiveAgentDatabaseLease`, artifact-preserving read) | no: private scratch, removed after the read |
| connection-local PRAGMAs (`writable_schema` catalog reads, `busy_timeout`, `cache_size`) on read-only connections | schema readers | no: change no file |

No file bytes, rows, leases or `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` in the span. With a configured plugin that cannot be installed (an earlier fixture had `slack` configured), the same span also wrote `migration_runs` twice, took the plugin lifecycle lease (four `state_leases` writes) and called npm; that case is the `plugin-convergence` and `plugin-obligations` guard below.

**Green (head, same restored store):** every input with a check answers `none`; the three without one keep the step at `work`.

```text
doctor.pending.config-flow.state-write-admission 0.6ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-dir 0.1ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-config 90.9ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.state-schema 85.9ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.retired-state 3.3ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.session-entry-state 31.3ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.plugin-convergence 2.2ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.plugin-obligations 94.0ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.cron 432.6ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-detection 629.1ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.agent-databases 524.4ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.legacy-state-steps 0.1ms pending=work check=default
doctor.pending.config-flow.a2ui-widgets 24.9ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.relative-session-stores 2.0ms pending=none check=owner
doctor.pending.config-flow.update-history 0.0ms pending=work check=default
doctor.pending.config-flow.config-repairs 0.0ms pending=work check=default
doctor.pending.config-flow 0.0ms pending=work check=owner
```

Cost of the check on this store: about 1.9 s in all (cron 433 ms, legacy-state detection 629 ms, agent databases 524 ms, the rest under 100 ms each). Inside each `config-flow.*` span the preload saw no write-intent `fs` call, no writable open of a real store, no `BEGIN`, and no copy: only read-only opens with connection-local PRAGMAs. The longest single SQLite statement the check issues is the agent database plan's read-only integrity check (the plan's `integrity` condition, run in its worker); it was not timed per statement here and grows with database size. The flow itself still runs everything after the check, so on large agent databases the integrity check now runs twice per `doctor --fix` until the stop becomes conditional.

**Guards** (base, then head on the same restored store, then head again without restoring). Schema and config seeds were applied while the Gateway was serving, because a Gateway boot heals them first.

| Seed | Base | Head, first run | Head, next run | Result content |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| state schema: drop `capture_events_flow_idx` | repaired | `config-flow.state-schema=work` | `none` | schema identical to base |
| agent database: drop an index in the `work` agent database | repaired | `config-flow.agent-databases=work` | `none` | schema identical to base |
| legacy config: retired `routing` key | migrated | `config-flow.legacy-config=work` (config-dependent inputs `undecidable` on the invalid config) | `none` | `openclaw.json` identical to base |
| configured plugin that is not installed (`absent-owner`) | obligation recorded `pending` | `plugin-convergence=work`, `plugin-obligations=work` | `plugin-obligations=work` (pending row); the flow then settles it | ledger rows identical to base |
| recorded obligation, plugin unconfigured | settled `completed` | `plugin-obligations=none` once settled | `none` | identical |
| Memory Core `detectLegacyState` preview (an invalid events file) | source kept, Doctor exits 1 | `legacy-state-detection=work` | `work` again: the plugin keeps the invalid source, as on base | identical |
| state database mode 0644 | healed before the config flow by an earlier step | all inputs `none` | `none` | identical |

Not run through the CLI: the legacy state directory. With `~/.openclaw` moved to `~/.clawdbot`, base and head both refuse before maintenance ("State directory selection changed before moving ...") because the service unit names the state directory; the input is covered by the unit test.

**Tests.** `src/commands/doctor-config-flow-pending.test.ts` (rewritten, 12 cases on real stores; fails on `main`, where the inputs do not exist): every input traced in order and the step `work` while an input has no check, with no file changed beside a held store; per-input `work`/`none` for permission drift and orphaned sidecars, a legacy state directory, a legacy config shape, a retired state file, a retired cron store (held store, no file change), a recorded obligation with and without a config file, an unavailable configured plugin; `undecidable` without sidecars for every SQLite-reading input when no connection holds the store; the agent database plan `undecidable` without the preflight's discovery. The one previous case (state-schema input only) is replaced by the first case, which covers it. Generic guards: `doctor-maintenance.stopped-systemd.test.ts` and `doctor-health-contributions.pending-read-only.test.ts` pass (75). Writer suites for every refactored owner pass.

**Checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: every lane passes except the dead-export scan, which reports `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation` in files this PR does not touch (inherited from `main`). Session identity ratchet: no entries in touched files. CI on `c0d6346772f`: green.

**Review.** autoreview, Codex route (gpt-6.1-sol), `--max-priority P2 --thinking high`, with the owners and callers as committed source context (15 to 16 files) and the contract in the prompt. Pass 1: four P2. Fixed: agent stores the session scanners open were not guarded (now listed inside the state guard), the ledger was skipped without a config file, permission drift was missing from admission. Rejected: a policy-refused plugin is not recorded by the flow, so it is not ledger work. Pass 2: one P2, rejected with evidence (a nested artifact-preserving scope does not copy the state database under live reads; `requiresArtifactPreservingSnapshot` and the direct-read branch take the live read), and a held-store cron test added. Pass 3: scoped-clean.

**Whole `doctor --fix` on the healthy install, head:** 95 of 110 decisions trace `none check=owner`. Not `none`: `client-credentials` (no check), `database-migrations` (`undecidable`), `config-flow` (via `legacy-state-steps`, `update-history`, `config-repairs`), contributions `auth-profile-migration`, `session-transcripts`, `state-integrity`, `codex-session-routes`, `legacy-cron`, `skills`, `memory-search`, `final-config-validation`, and `service-definition`.

Not proven: macOS, Windows, pnpm, Bun and Git installs, PostgreSQL, large stores, a check beside a serving Gateway (the checks ran inside the stop, beside Doctor's own connections). No timing comparison is claimed.

<details><summary>Red: measured list in the config-flow span (base, healthy)</summary>

```text
span doctor.config-flow: 5618 ms, origin pid 4975, 840 events in window
   1  fs openSync ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
   3  sqlite-open-rw  :memory:
   1  sqlite-open-rw  file://~/.cache/openclaw/<scratch>/owner.sqlite?mode=rw
   1  sqlite-open-rw  file://~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite?mode=rw
```

prs.title: fix(backup): name the stop step when a managed browser locks its profile
prs.body:
Fixes #187882
Refs #193673

## What Problem This Solves

On native Windows, a running OpenClaw-managed browser keeps durable profile files under `<state>/browser/<profile>/user-data` open and locked (for example `Default/Network/Cookies`, LevelDB `LOCK` files). `openclaw backup create` then fails with no supported recovery step:

- On current main it fails at SQLite discovery with the generic `Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.` The header-probe child threw the real `EBUSY` with its stack, and the parent replaced it with that text.
- When discovery passes and the archiver hits the lock (the report's 2026.10.8 shape), it fails with `Backup archive write failed: EBUSY ... (last offending path: ...Cookies, after 1 attempt)`.

Neither tells the operator which owner holds the file or what to do.

## User Impact

- When a backup source is in use (`EBUSY`), both failure stages name the file and code; for files under a managed browser profile they add the conditional recovery step `If the OpenClaw-managed browser profile "<profile>" is running, stop it with openclaw browser --browser-profile <profile> stop, then retry the backup.` Other in-use files get `Close that process, then retry the backup.`
- Access denials (`EACCES`/`EPERM`) are described as such (`could not be read (EACCES). Check that this user can read it.`) and never claim another process holds the file; under a browser profile the stop step is added only as a conditional, because Windows can surface a sharing lock as `EPERM`.
- Backup semantics are unchanged: locked profile files are never skipped, and no incomplete archive is published. Other probe failures keep the existing generic message.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the stop-and-retry procedure next to the managed-browser profile rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Verify the managed-browser stop/retry procedure on native Windows, then add actionable recovery guidance for both discovery and archive-read failures." The probe worker now reports an unreadable source as `{ code, path }` on stderr and sets `process.exitCode = 3` (no forced `process.exit`, per `openclaw-boundaries/no-forced-process-exit`) instead of throwing a stack trace, so the parent can keep the cause; one small helper (`describeLockedBackupSource`) derives the hint from the errno code and the `browser/<profile>/user-data` layout, and both `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` and `writeTarArchiveWithRetry` append it.

## Evidence

Local live run on native Windows 11, Node 26.12.1: isolated state, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw start` + `open https://example.com` (real Chromium-family profile on disk), then `openclaw backup create --no-include-workspace --verify --output <dir>` from a separate process, then `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop` and the same backup again. Same rig; only the build differs (main `9e86c84` vs this branch).

![backup with running managed browser on Windows, main vs fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/187882/proof-187882-v2.png)

| step | main | fix |
|---|---|---|
| backup while the managed browser runs | exit 1, generic "check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable" | exit 1, `<state>\browser\openclaw\user-data\Default\Extension Rules\LOCK is in use by another process (EBUSY). If the OpenClaw-managed browser profile "openclaw" is running, stop it with openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop, then retry the backup.` |
| incomplete archive published | no | no |
| after `openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw stop`, same backup | exit 0, `Archive verification: passed` | exit 0, `Archive verification: passed` |

This verifies the documented stop/retry procedure end to end on native Windows. The archive-read stage (`Backup archive write failed: ...`) is covered through its owner, `writeTarArchiveWithRetry`, in `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`: EBUSY and EPERM under a browser profile, EBUSY and EACCES on a non-browser file (asserting no "another process" claim for EACCES), and ENOENT unchanged. Against main's `backup-tar-retry.ts`: `4 failed | 1 passed`; with the fix: `5 passed`. `config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` (`no-forced-process-exit`) fails on the previous head's worker and passes now.

Checks run locally: `oxfmt`, `oxlint` on changed files, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-create-stream.test.ts`.


## Review round 3 (ff5f1e1)

Merged `upstream/main` (`66004e0`) to clear the merge conflict. The merge changed no PR code: `git diff a0f077c ff5f1e1` over `src/infra/backup-locked-source.ts`, `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts`, `src/infra/backup-tar-retry.ts`, `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.ts` and `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.worker.ts` is empty. In `docs/cli/backup.md` upstream rewrote the PostgreSQL section; the managed-browser stop/retry paragraph this PR adds is still the same 2-line addition against main.

Rerun on the merged head: `pnpm test src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts` → 5 passed; `oxfmt --check` clean on all 6 changed files; CI `ci-gate` and all `checks-node-changed-*` shards SUCCESS.


## Also covers #193673 (non-browser busy file during Windows update capture)

#193673 reports a Windows npm update that stopped during backup capture with `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, read` from the header-probe worker. The error carried no path. That `readSync` failure is what a SQLite-style byte-range lock produces. I reproduced it on Windows 11 with Node 26.12.1: PowerShell holds `[IO.File]::Open(path,'Open','ReadWrite','ReadWrite').Lock(0,4096)` on a file while the real `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` runs.

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/193673/proof-193673.png)

| Code | Busy-file result |
| --- | --- |
| main 9f3ed31 | Generic "Could not determine…". The cause is a worker stack trace `EBUSY … read { errno: -4082, syscall: 'read' }` with no path, the same as the issue. |
| this PR ff5f1e1 | `… <state>\agents\main\held.sqlite is in use by another process (EBUSY). Close that process, then retry the backup.` |

The PR still fails closed: no file is classified by guesswork and capture does not continue. Without the lock, both builds classify the files identically.



## Review round 4 (a53d039)

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed on the previous head in the test-lines ratchet: `Test lines: 6529371; ceiling: 6529344; over by: 27; net delta: +29`. The only test change in this PR is the new `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts` (29 lines; five cases through `writeTarArchiveWithRetry` covering EBUSY/EPERM under a browser profile, EBUSY/EACCES on a plain file, and unchanged ENOENT). Added `config/test-lines-allocations/backup-locked-source.txt` with a 29-line allowance, the documented route for a justified test addition; 29 is the exact net test-line delta the ratchet reported, so it clears the 27-line overshoot with 2 lines to spare and passes the allocation-credit check (`credit <= added lines`).

Local `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base HEAD^ --no-merge-base` on the merged tree reports `Test lines: 6529153; ceiling: 6529151; over by: 2; net delta: +29`: the allocation is counted, and the remaining 2 lines are main 7302f00's own tree sitting 2 over its baseline and allocations (6529124 vs 6529122) before this PR's file is added. The CI job checks out the two-parent merge of this head with the current main tip, where the previous run read `over by: 27` with `net delta: +29`, so the same 29-line credit clears it there. `src/infra/backup-locked-source.test.ts` → 5 passed.

prs.title: fix(cron): name the automations tool in outcome guidance
prs.body:
Closes #206426

## What Problem This Solves

The unattended cron preamble told the model: “If the automation tool offers record_result, record no_change…”. “The automation tool” is not a name the model can resolve: in the reported runs the model routed `action=record_result` / `outcome=no_change` into an unrelated ChatGPT connector (`page_*` automation tools), the connector rejected the arguments, and the run receipt reported that connector failure even though the work itself was fine.

This change binds the guidance to the scheduler tool’s real identity. `AUTOMATIONS_TOOL_NAME` (the single source of truth already used by the tool factory, policy lists, and prompts) is interpolated into the preamble, and the sentence now also says not to record through an MCP or connector automation tool. Availability stays conditional — a harness without the tool still skips recording.

## User Impact

Scheduled runs stop producing misleading error receipts from unrelated connectors and stop sending outcome arguments to tools that cannot accept them. Healthy no-change runs keep the quiet `no_change`/`NO_REPLY` behavior, and genuine failures still surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The outcome capability already has one canonical name owner (`src/agents/tools/automations-tool-name.ts`); the prompt was the only place spelling it as a generic phrase. Interpolating the constant keeps the preamble static for prompt caching (it is a build-time constant, not runtime data), keeps the alias contract (`cron` remains an accepted config alias), and avoids changing tool resolution or permissions — the reported bug is prompt routing, not authority.

## Evidence

### 1. Prompt the harness sends

- `src/cron/run-prompt.test.ts`: new case “names the exact automations tool instead of an ambiguous automation tool” asserts the preamble contains ``If the `automations` tool offers record_result``, contains the “not an MCP or connector automation tool” clause, and no longer contains the old ambiguous sentence.
  - Base (`4e06d657fcd5`, source checked out from the parent commit): `FAIL … names the exact automations tool …` — 1 failed / 2 passed.
  - Head (`89e99941f729`): 3/3 passed.
- Line-cap ratchet OK; test-lines +18/400; oxfmt/oxlint clean.

### 2. End-to-end scheduled run: naming → tool selection → run receipt

Real Gateway built from `dist/`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, one automation created and executed through the normal queue: `automations add … --no-deliver` then `automations run <id> --wait`, read back with `automations runs <id>`.

The provider is a local chat-completions stub. The stub is a deterministic model stand-in: it reads the naming clause in the preamble the harness actually sent and then follows the harness’s own recovery path. The connector is a local stdio MCP server that exposes `list_page_automations` with an empty closed input schema — the shape the reporter’s connector rejected.

| | before — `4e06d657` (PR parent) | after — `89e99941` (PR head) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preamble naming | ``If the automation tool offers record_result…`` — no tool named | ``If the `automations` tool offers record_result…; use that tool, not an MCP or connector automation tool.`` |
| Tool call | `notion__list_page_automations` `{action:"record_result",outcome:"no_change"}` (the only automation-shaped tool it can name) | `automations` `{action:"record_result",outcome:"no_change"}` → harness note → `dispatch_action {id:"automations", args:{…}}` (exact name from the preamble) |
| Tool result | `Validation failed for tool "notion__list_page_automations": action: schema is false · root: must not have additional properties` | `{"ok":true,"outcome":"no_change"}` |
| Run receipt | `status error` · `completionStatus failed` · `result` — · `⚠️ Notion List Page Automations failed: invalid arguments` | `status ok` · `completionStatus succeeded` · `result {"outcome":"no_change"}` · no diagnostics |

Both builds expose the same tool surface (`notion__list_page_automations` inline, `automations` deferred behind `dispatch_action`), so the only input that differs is the naming clause in the prompt.

- before run `cron-request.26ed1ae9-065a-4585-8a9c-45e6b54de735` — 2 model requests
- after run `cron-request.a8aeb50b-4cd1-4b70-9bff-26ba396b0100` — 3 model requests

![End-to-end scheduled run: preamble naming, tool call, and run receipt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/207071/proof2.png)

Earlier request-body capture from the same rig (prompt text only, no tool call):

![Live A/B prompt capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/207071/proof.png)

## What was not tested

- The model stand-in is deterministic: it proves the prompt is sufficient to drive the named call and that the harness accepts the outcome, not which tool a hosted model would choose. This host has no model credentials.
- Direct vs deferred tool presentation and a harness where the automations tool is unavailable are covered by the existing preamble tests, not by a live run.
- `openclaw/ci-gate` is red on this head because the `pull_request` workflows are parked at `action_required` (fork approval); no CI job has run. The changes are source + test only and were exercised locally with the head build.

prs.title: fix: tell the sender they were approved when the channel token is a SecretRef
prs.body:
Closes #206138

## What Problem This Solves

When a channel's bot token is kept in a secret (a SecretRef) instead of plain text, `openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> --notify` lets the sender in but never tells them: the CLI prints `Failed to notify requester: UnresolvedSecretInputError ...` and the person who asked for access is left waiting with no reply.

## User Impact

`--notify` sends the approval notice for channels whose tokens are SecretRefs, as it already does for plain-text tokens. Approval itself, plain-text tokens and approvals without `--notify` are unchanged. No setup or migration. If the secrets can't be resolved, the CLI still prints the same `Failed to notify requester` warning after a successful approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI sends the notice from its own process, but it passed the raw config, so the Telegram adapter read the token from an unresolved SecretRef. The fix resolves only that channel's secrets first, through the same path `openclaw message send` and `openclaw directory` use (`getScopedChannelsCommandSecretTargets` plus `resolveCommandConfigWithSecrets`), and keeps it inside the existing warning-on-failure block. The Gateway protocol is untouched (its `code` approval branch never notifies; changing that would be a protocol change).

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** a test Gateway with Telegram pointed at a local Bot API stub and the dummy token in the secret store. The stub's user DMs the bot, gets a pairing code, and the code is approved with `--notify`.

| Build | Token | CLI output after "Approved" | Notice sent to the requester |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Released 2026.11.10 | SecretRef | `Failed to notify requester: UnresolvedSecretInputError ...` | none |
| This fix | SecretRef | none (only the approval lines) | "✅ OpenClaw access approved. Send a message to start chatting." |
| This fix (control) | plain text | none (only the approval lines) | "✅ OpenClaw access approved. Send a message to start chatting." (unchanged) |

![Before and after: pairing approve --notify with a SecretRef bot token](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/90fb8dc6adf5fc9e21dbb889adb8a82b1cfe1ea4/before-after.png)

**Real Telegram:** the same fix build with a real bot whose token is a store SecretRef (`{"source":"store","provider":"default",...}`) and DMs on `pairing`. A real Telegram account DMed the bot from a phone, got a pairing code, and the CLI approved it with `--notify`: the CLI printed only the approval lines, and the phone received the notice (user id redacted).

![Real Telegram: pairing code, then the approval notice after pairing approve --notify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/90fb8dc6adf5fc9e21dbb889adb8a82b1cfe1ea4/real-telegram.png)

Tested on 43f00ec94b4 (base ae2d953b68f).

- Review: autoreview (claude), ae2d953b68f..43f00ec94b4: no findings at P2 or above, clean
- Tests: `src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts` gains one test that the notice gets the resolved config; it fails without the fix and passes with it (13 tests, 92 s wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`, almost all of it transform; the tests themselves take about a second).
- **No request proof:** the change touches no model request.

prs.title: fix: distinguish unreadable Swabble settings from a disabled wake word
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If Swabble cannot read its config, `status` reports the wake word as disabled. For a damaged config, `doctor` recommends running `setup`, which replaces the existing settings with defaults instead of repairing the file.

## User Impact

A user can distinguish a disabled wake word from an unknown one and still see recent transcripts. Doctor distinguishes a missing file from one that needs repair. Neither diagnostic recommends replacing a damaged config.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both commands already read the same configuration. They now share the explanation for a failed read. Valid configurations, transcript output, exit codes, and the behavior of an explicitly requested setup are unchanged.

## Evidence

With a synthetic config missing its closing brace, the original command reported a disabled wake word. Following Doctor's advice for that same file replaced a custom word with the default. In the compiled candidate, the diagnostics left the damaged file unchanged and the status report still showed its saved transcript. Restoring the missing brace recovered the original wake word.
