prs.title: fix(agents): CLI backend runs never report the serving model while they work
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #206980

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users chatting with a CLI-runtime agent (`claude-cli`) could not see which model serves the run while it works: `sessions.list` kept `activeModel`/`activeModelProvider` at `null` for the whole run and no `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` event was published, because the CLI output stream discarded the model identity named by the backend's `system` `init` and `assistant` records. A client therefore could not show which model is answering until the first run ended.
- **Related:** #206980 (reporter's source read confirms the missing observation-to-lifecycle path); no linked PRs.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** parity with embedded/harness/worker runs — once the CLI backend names its model (init frame or first assistant frame), the run publishes `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` with the CLI backend's provider id and the observed model, so the session row exposes the serving model while the run is active.
- **Out of scope:** no change to model selection, routing, or the persisted assistant message identity; backends whose output names no model keep emitting nothing.
- **Highest-risk area:** the CLI streaming parser sits at the repo's max-lines ratchet ceiling, so the parser only forwards the raw model field of parent init/assistant frames (`onObservedModel`); blank/`<synthetic>` filtering lives in `normalizeClaudeObservedModel` (next to the synthetic-marker predicate) and per-attempt de-duplication plus publication through the captured run owner lives in the CLI runner wiring. The `CLI_STREAM_JSON_MISSING_RESULT_ERROR` re-export moved to its defining module (`cli-output-stream-output.js`) to free the line budget — only consumer re-pointed, no behavior change.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** while a CLI-backend run works, a client watching the run's `agent` events sees `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` as soon as the backend names its model, and `sessions.list` reports `activeModel`/`activeModelProvider` for the active run instead of `null` until the run ends.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/cli-output-stream.ts` (two forward call sites), `src/agents/cli-output-records.ts` (`normalizeClaudeObservedModel`), `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts` (de-dup + `emitAgentEventForRunContext` publication); regression: `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.model-phase.test.ts` (`publishes the CLI-observed serving model as a lifecycle model phase`).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:**
  - Runner harness: worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-206980` at base 7ff54580e8b, running the real CLI runner stack (`runPreparedCliAgent`) with a stream-json fixture process (same harness as the repo's CLI reliability tests; only the CLI process itself is a fixture).
  - Shipped Gateway (gateway-level capture): the built Gateway of this branch (`a2721856`) started as its own process (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 41321 --auth token --token <redacted> --dev`) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, agent model `anthropic/claude-opus-5` pinned to `agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" }`, and a synthetic `claude` executable first on `PATH` that speaks the documented claude-cli stream-json control protocol (initialize handshake, user records, `init`/`assistant`/`result` frames) and holds each turn open for ~12 s. An operator client (`@openclaw/gateway-client`, the shipped protocol client) subscribed to the session's message events (`sessions.messages.subscribe`), sent one turn via `chat.send`, and polled `sessions.list` every 700 ms while the run was still active. No Anthropic credentials were used; only the `claude` CLI executable at the subprocess boundary is a fixture — the Gateway process, real subprocess spawn through the CLI runner supervisor, stream parser, agent-event enrichment, run registry, session-row projection, and operator RPC delivery are all shipped code.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.model-phase.test.ts \
    src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts \
    src/agents/cli-output-stream.test.ts \
    src/agents/cli-output-records.test.ts \

  # 定向验证环（格式化+lint+同目录测试+tsgo:core）

  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs evidence/.../gateway-live/driver.mts
  #   driver: sessions.messages.subscribe -> chat.send -> 轮询 sessions.list（run 进行中）
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**

      > publishes the CLI-observed serving model as a lifecycle model phase 6874ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  1 passed (1)

  - Runner harness: with the run context registered (as chat reply turns do), a CLI run whose `system` `init` frame names `claude-opus-5-5-20261101` publishes exactly one `lifecycle` `phase: "model"` event (`provider: "claude-cli"`, `model: "claude-opus-5-5-20261101"`) — repeated assistant frames naming the same model are de-duplicated — and `getAgentRunContext(runId).activeModel` (the sessions-row source fed by `recordAgentRunModel`) is set while the run is active.

- **What was not tested:** a live `claude-cli` binary against real Anthropic credentials (not available in this environment); the `claude` CLI executable at the subprocess boundary is a synthetic fixture emitting the documented stream-json frame shapes — the Gateway process, real subprocess spawn through the CLI runner supervisor, parser, agent-event enrichment, run registry, session-row projection, and operator RPC delivery are the real shipped code path.

prs.title: fix: stop saying a cron job uses the default agent when --session-key names its agent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron add` (and `openclaw automations add`) prints "No --agent specified; the job will run with the configured default agent" whenever `--agent` is left out of an agent-turn or script job. When the job is given an agent-qualified `--session-key` such as `agent:ops:telegram:direct:1`, that statement is wrong: the Gateway takes the owner from the session key, so the job runs as `ops`, not as the default agent. Operators reading the notice are told to fix something that is already set, or think the job landed on the wrong agent.

## User Impact

Creating a job with an agent-qualified `--session-key` and no `--agent` no longer prints the default-agent notice. Jobs that name no owner at all, by `--agent` or by session key, still get the notice exactly as before. No change to how jobs are stored or which agent runs them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now asks the existing cron owner resolver (`tryResolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId`, the same function the Gateway uses) whether `--agent` or `--session-key` already names an owner, without a configured default. That keeps one ownership rule instead of a second copy in the CLI. The CLI still does not read local config to decide this, because it may be talking to a remote Gateway whose `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` differs. The docs line in `docs/cli/cron.md` now says when the notice appears.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` drives the registered `cron add` command: with `--session-key agent:ops:telegram:direct:1` it expects no notice; with `--session-key telegram:direct:1` it expects the notice.
- Red on `origin/main` (fix reverted, test kept): `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`.
- Green with the fix: `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 65 of 65 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on the three changed files passed. `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests (services-cron, gateway-root, commands, plugins-platform, config-cli, other, cli-update) and all ratchets/guards passed. Its Knip dead-export scan was killed after about 400s (exit 143) on this shared host, so that scan did not finish; this diff adds no exports. Type-aware oxlint run directly on both changed source files: no problems.
- Local autoreview (Claude engine, one pass, P2 threshold): `scoped-clean`, no findings.
- Not run: a live Gateway `cron add`. The notice is printed by the CLI before the Gateway call, and the test exercises that command handler directly.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Checking or activating a saved model sign-in from the CLI required stopping the Gateway. An explicit connection check could also discard a temporarily rate-limited profile before contacting the provider, so it could not tell whether the model had recovered.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw models status --probe` or `openclaw models auth activate <profileId> [--agent <id>]` without stopping the local Gateway. A successful check clears only the matching cooldown. An activation changes the selected agent only after verification succeeds. Offline operation still takes the exclusive state lock.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI delegates to the Gateway that owns the state, preserving the selected agent, targets and probe limits. Explicit probes can retry a temporary cooldown without opening up ordinary selection or falling back to another credential. Failed or empty responses do not report recovery.

## Evidence

- Ran the public CLI against an isolated loopback Gateway and a live provider. Three profile/model pairs started in cooldown. After the requested checks, only the matching profile/model pair left cooldown. A cooldown for a different model and one for a different profile remained in place.
- With two agents, successful activation changed only the named agent. An activation with no usable model failed and left the previous selection intact.
- Local review covered the branch diff in three parts. It found no P0 or P1 issues; runtime behavior was verified separately with the public CLI as described above.

prs.title: fix(apple): keep accepted work running after End Talk
prs.body:
Supersedes #203889. Related: #206321, #206333, #188134, #188798

> **End Talk ends the call, not the task. You can hang up while a reply is running or a draft is open, without canceling either or switching chats. Stop response is how you cancel it.**

## What Problem This Solves

On iOS and macOS, ending Talk or losing the Talk transport cancels accepted agent work and hides or misroutes the hang-up control:

1. In the shared `.clean` composer chrome, an active run or open draft replaced the Talk button with **Stop** or **Send**, leaving no way to hang up without canceling the agent reply or clearing the draft.
2. On iOS and macOS, tapping **End Talk** ran the focus-update callback (`focusChatSession` / `recordActiveSessionKey`) before disabling Talk, which could retarget Talk and abort its run when the active call belonged to a different session than the displayed chat.
3. `RealtimeTalkRelaySession.stop()` omitted `disposition: "detach"`, and `TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.stop()` defaulted `preserveRuns` to `false` across End Talk, session-switch, background, disconnect, and push-to-talk teardown paths.
4. The iOS Talk footer showed a camera-flip button with no live preview or visual feedback that crowded the compact composer bar.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending or losing a voice call stops microphone capture, audio playback, and spoken delivery—not accepted agent work. Paired with Gateway + Control UI PR #206321, this makes Apple Talk detach cleanly across both existing Gateways advertising `talk-session-close-disposition` and Gateways with #206321:

- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatComposer.swift`, `ChatComposer+CleanControls.swift`, `OpenClawChatTalkControl.swift`: keep the active Talk button reachable beside **Stop** / **Send** in `.clean` chrome via `showsSeparateActiveTalkControl` across iOS and macOS, and add a narrow-width `ViewThatFits` fallback so End Talk, Stop, and Send stay reachable on compact widths.
- `apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift` & `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/WebChatSwiftUI.swift`: skip `focusChatSession(sessionKey)` / `recordActiveSessionKey(sessionKey)` when ending Talk (only focus when starting Talk), and use session-independent help text (`"Stop realtime chat"`) when Talk is enabled.
- `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/RealtimeTalkRelaySession.swift` & `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/TalkModeRuntime+Realtime.swift`: `stop()` and `stopAndWait()` always send `disposition: "detach"` when `supportsCloseDisposition()` is true, wait for any in-flight `talk.session.cancelOutput` before detaching so Stop Speaking followed immediately by End Talk still cancels the turn, and remove now-unused `stopAfterFailure()`.
- `apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkRealtimeWebRTCSession.swift` & `TalkModeManager.swift`: default `stop(preserveRuns:)` and `stopRealtimeSession(preserveRuns:)` to `true` across all teardown paths while keeping explicit `preserveRuns: false` available and locking the first stop's choice against subsequent cleanup calls.
- **Explicit UX tradeoff — iOS camera-flip control removal (`ChatCameraFlipButton.swift`, `NodeAppModel.swift`, `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`):** removes `ChatCameraFlipButton`, `OpenClawCameraFacingSelection`, `cameraFacing`/`flipCamera`, and the iOS mutation helpers (`flipPreferredCameraFacing`, `setPreferredCameraFacing`) along with their three i18n strings. Although the button had no live video preview or visual feedback, it did toggle the saved `camera.preferredFacing` preference read by later photo and clip commands when no camera is specified; removing it trades away that hidden toggle to clean up the compact composer and match Android (which has no camera-flip button), while retaining the fallback read of existing saved `camera.preferredFacing`.

AI-assisted: drafted, implemented, reviewed, and verified with AI coding assistance, with every change tested locally.

prs.title: fix: remove the unused automation wake setting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

“Now / Next heartbeat” looked like it controlled when an automation would run. In practice, both choices ran the job when its schedule came due. The setting gave people a choice that did nothing.

## User Impact

**User impact:** Set an automation’s timing with its schedule. The Android editor no longer offers Wake mode, and automation create/edit commands and API requests no longer accept `--wake` or `wakeMode`. The current web editor already didn’t render the picker; this removes its leftover data handling and fixtures.

Full job responses keep deprecated, derived `wakeMode: "now"` metadata for released protocol-v4 clients, including Android v2026.11.10. This is response-only compatibility, not a stored setting or a scheduling control; it remains until protocol v4 retires.

On upgrade, or with `openclaw doctor --fix`, Doctor backs up stored cron state and silently removes the old job field. It does not delete, pause, or reschedule jobs, change what they do, or reset their run state. Current approval references are carried forward; stale ones stay stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

A separate agent `automations` wake action can still send an immediate notice to a session. It has no timing selector: the previous default already sent immediately for a targeted session. Use a one-off automation for a later follow-up. The `next-heartbeat` **script result** is different: it can attach a notice to a real upcoming scheduled run, so it still works and is documented separately. The inbound `/hooks/wake` endpoint, hook mapping wake modes, and `openclaw system` are unchanged and can be reviewed separately.

This shares automation form data, Gateway job contracts, Doctor cron repair files, and generated validators or tool snapshots with the parallel automation cleanup PRs. The changes here are limited to Wake mode. The migration scans existing cron definitions and rewrites only affected jobs after one backup; it does not rewrite run history. Largest-deployment upgrade cost was not measured.

## Evidence

- On `b75aede9e48ae92eaa41a1804ad25af76e60f7c0`, I merged main at `3ffd7660334a88629e3c3c0d546a770fb9b78e7e` without rebase or force-push. The already-pushed Android compatibility fix is unchanged. All 270 focused tests passed across the protocol validators (93), Gateway validation (146), read projection (4), agent inputs (7), CLI edit (1), and Doctor migration (19). Core and cron-test typechecks, full protocol checks (including Swift/Kotlin determinism), focused lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. The six test shards took 188.03s.
- I applied pr-simplify to the merge delta: no new machinery, compatibility layer, or tests were added, and no existing assertions were weakened. The PR remains draft; I did not request another review. Runtime proof still needed on the final head: actual Android before/after screenshots and released-client new/migrated-job detail reads; shipped CLI/Gateway create/edit and immediate-wake behavior; real upgrades from latest stable and supported 9.x extended-stable/10.x, including the old updater round trip, preserving jobs, runtime state, and approvals. Final-head CI and fresh independent review remain unverified.

- On `c44441e467372699cf3345efda4582f111e06327`, I checked the unmodified Android v2026.11.10 `CronJobDetail.kt` parser against real isolated protocol-v4 Gateway add/get/update/list replies: all four pre-fix replies were rejected, and all four fixed replies were accepted. Create/update requests containing `wakeMode` still failed validation. I removed the test job and isolated Gateway state.
- I verified the regression assertions fail before the fix and pass after it. Final focused runs passed 93 protocol-schema tests and 4 projection tests, plus 27 tool/template consumer tests on the same production code. Core and cron-test typechecks, focused lint/format, and Swift protocol generation/determinism checks passed. Final schema/projection suite wall times were 34.97s (mostly compilation) and 1.27s; exact-head CI time is pending.
- I ran pr-simplify on this follow-up: compatibility stays in the existing read projection, is stripped from recovered writable definitions, and duplicate schema coverage was folded into an existing test. The follow-up changes five files (+17/-1 non-test lines, +14/-1 test lines). Against the PR merge base, the whole PR is +3751/-3863 non-test lines and +201/-525 test lines, including generated artifacts.
- I did not run Android UI/device proof or 9.x/10.x upgrades in this follow-up. No fresh independent local review completed: the existing Codex route failed its read-only sandbox preflight, and I did not broaden its permissions.
- I reproduced the remaining `wakeMode` schema/type failures locally and removed eight obsolete fields in two fixture files, without changing assertions, timeouts, or test cases. On `30994c4ee843bea44176462dcd1f1326f6ba8c6b`, PostgreSQL 17 passed 4/4 cron lifecycle tests, template automations passed 21/21, and the templates typecheck, focused lint, and format checks passed.
- PostgreSQL 16 initially passed 3/4. The graceful-stop test timed out waiting for `restart.close.http-server` after the cron finalizer exceeded its cleanup grace period. One bounded, unchanged rerun passed (1 passed, 3 deselected); that does not establish a fix for the timing failure. The containers were removed. Upgrade testing from 9.x/10.x remains separate.
- Focused Gateway, agent tool, scheduler, Doctor, and editor assertions passed. The SQLite Doctor test verified backup and idempotency, existing standing-grant continuity, and removal from a disabled job. Agent input and prompt-prefix tests passed again on the committed source after an earlier runner rejected files changing during compilation.
- Core, Control UI, and scripts typechecks passed; focused core lint passed on 30 files. Gateway validators, native string inventory, and prompt snapshots were regenerated. Baseline and patched Android debug APKs built, and 43 focused Android tests passed. Full CI and live upgrade E2E were not run locally.
- Visual proof gap: the web form had no rendered Wake mode on main. The Android view did change. The isolated Android emulator never completed boot in the capture window, so neither Android screenshot was captured or uploaded.

prs.title: fix: keep recovery prompts out of Claude chat history
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts:481 marks CLI input as host-generated only from the run's input provenance, but the stranded-reply retry (src/auto-reply/reply/stranded-reply-recovery.ts:56-89) correctly keeps the human turn's provenance, so Claude Code saves the retry prompt as a plain user row and chat.history shows it as the operator's own message.

Fixes #206304

Thanks @fray-ai for the report and the precise code trace, and @Tosko4 for the first fix in this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

With a `claude-cli` agent and `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, a turn that ends with plain text queues the stranded-reply retry (`[System] Your previous reply was not delivered ...`). That retry reached Claude Code as ordinary user input, Claude stored it as a normal user row, and the Control UI drew it as a right-aligned operator bubble.

## User Impact

The retry no longer appears as a message the operator wrote. The delivered reply still arrives. An operator who types the same `[System] ...` text still sees it as their own message, and existing history is not rewritten. Nothing changes for the embedded runtime or for permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The CLI candidate sets `promptOrigin: "host"` from the existing `FollowupRun.strandedReplyRetry` flag (`agent-runner-cli-candidate.ts`). `RunCliAgentParams` carries that one optional field, with the same value type `CliBackendExecuteContext.promptOrigin` already uses.
- The plugin CLI runner marks host input when that field is set or when the provenance is host-generated, as before (`execute-plugin.ts`). The Claude backend then sends `isSynthetic: true`, Claude saves an `isMeta` row, and the existing history import skips it.
- The retry's `inputProvenance` is unchanged (`external_user`). The first version of this PR switched it to `internal_system`; that value feeds requester-profile, continuation, collaborative-steering and personal-MCP requester checks (`reply-tool-authority.ts:353`, `reply-tool-authority-inbound.ts:83/116/214`, `agent-bundle-mcp-webchat-requester.ts:42`), reply threading and model urgency. Those changes are reverted, together with the `missingReplyNoticeAllowed` change it needed.
- No text classification: an operator who types the same `[System] ...` text still sees their own bubble. Existing history is not rewritten.

Production: +9/-1 lines in 3 files. Tests: one regression at the CLI dispatch boundary (+18); the PR's other tests are dropped.

## Evidence

Built Gateway + Control UI from `450c4b640ed6` (main) and this head in a secretless node:24.22.1 container. Agent `main` runs on `claude-cli` with a stand-in `claude` that writes a real Claude Code project JSONL (synthetic input -> `isMeta`) and calls the real OpenClaw MCP `message` tool; agent `embedded` runs on the OpenClaw runtime with a scripted model. Real Chromium (Playwright 1.64.1) drives WebChat sessions. Screenshots and the full table: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207128#issuecomment-7232846921

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| claude-cli stranded once: operator bubble with retry text (live / reload) | 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| same: delivered reply "Delivered answer P206304." | shown | shown |
| same: chat.history retry row | `role: user`, no provenance, importedFrom claude-cli | absent (meta row skipped) |
| Claude stdin for retry | `isSynthetic` absent | `isSynthetic: true` |
| control: operator types the identical `[System] ...` text | own bubble, `external_user` | own bubble, `external_user` |
| control: retry also ends with plain text (second miss) | retry shown as operator bubble; retry final shown; no "No answer" notice | no operator bubble; retry final shown; no "No answer" notice (same as main) |
| control: embedded (non-CLI) agent, stranded once | no retry bubble, delivered | identical |

Regression test `agent-runner-execution-cli-sessions.test.ts` "sends a stranded-reply retry as host input without changing its provenance (#206304)": fails with the candidate line removed (`- "promptOrigin": "host"`), passes at head.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state, schema, config or protocol change; a revert fully restores the old behavior. Blast radius: only stranded-reply retries on plugin CLI backends (Claude CLI) change their native input marker.

prs.title: fix: keep backup retries on the requested operation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw backup restore` cannot find a local archive, the error tells the operator to run `openclaw backup verify <archive>`. Even with the right archive, that command only checks the backup; it never restores anything to the chosen target.

## User Impact

The error now asks the operator to check the archive path and try again. It distinguishes the input archive from the restore target without directing the operator to a different command.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore and verification share the archive check. The message at that check should make sense for either operation. No target handling, validation, exit status, or JSON field changes.

## Evidence

On the compiled baseline, following the error with the corrected archive path verified the synthetic backup but left the target absent. Retrying the original restore with that path recovered the configuration byte for byte. The focused restore regression failed on the original guidance. In the compiled candidate, `verify` and `restore` both exited 1 for a missing archive in human and JSON modes without creating a target. Correcting only the input path let each original command finish: verification created no target, and both restores recovered the original bytes. The change replaces one shared diagnostic; it adds no new recovery path.

prs.title: fix(voice): answer phone, meeting and FaceTime consults on Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
Closes #202208

Related: #188440, #161885, #164229, #199379, #199378; supersedes closed #191683.

## What Problem This Solves

On an agent whose model runs on Claude CLI (or another CLI runtime), a phone call (Voice Call realtime), a meeting bot (Google Meet, Teams, Zoom, Slack huddles) or a FaceTime call cannot get an answer from the agent: every consult fails with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` or a sign-in error, and the caller hears an error. Typed messages and Discord voice to the same agent work.

## User Impact

User impact: phone, meeting and FaceTime voice consults run on the agent's own runtime, including Claude CLI and its configured fallbacks, like a typed message. Embedded-runtime agents keep working. Tool policy is unchanged: callers and meeting participants are guests, FaceTime owners stay owners, and a phone consult's `voice_call` can still only end the current call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared helper `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` always ended in `runEmbeddedAgent` with an explicit provider/model, which calls the provider API directly and never selects the agent's runtime. Discord voice works because it runs a normal agent turn through `runCommandFromIngress`.

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` gains `runner: "agent-turn"`: after the helper prepares the consult session (fork from the requester, lineage, delivery fields, lifecycle admission), the consult runs as a turn of that session through `runCommandFromIngress` with `deliver: false`. Prompt building, timeout, cancellation, `onRunStarted`, speakable-text extraction and yield acknowledgements are unchanged. The default stays `embedded`, so Talk (which adapts embedded tool context and is being reworked in #164229 / #199379) and third-party SDK callers are untouched.
- Voice Call, meeting-bot and FaceTime opt in. Voice Call passes a model override only when `responseModel` is configured and a thinking override only when `realtime.consultThinkingLevel` is set; otherwise the session's own selection applies. Meeting consults no longer force thinking `high`; they use the session default. A level a bridge does pass (FaceTime always asks for `off`, Voice Call passes `realtime.consultThinkingLevel`) is a one-run choice: a model without that level runs at its closest one, as on the embedded runner (`8711c7b5a`, below).
- Plugin ingress (`runCommandFromIngress` wrapper): a plugin may omit `messageChannel` for a turn on its own surface. Owner authority still needs a bundled or trusted official plugin, and a named channel must still be the plugin's own. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. **This widens the plugin ingress capability** (previously only channel plugins could admit turns); it stays narrower than `runEmbeddedAgent`, which any plugin can already call with an owner bit. Flagging for SDK/security owner review.
- The Claude CLI path carries `toolBindings` from the command attempt into the MCP loopback grant, as the embedded runner already does, so `voice_call` stays bound to the live call.
- Voice Call runs the consult in its service context so Gateway-dispatched tools such as `sessions_send` work from webhook handlers.

Not changed: the Voice Call classic (non-realtime) responder (#188440), Talk's Gateway consult path (#164229 / #199379), Discord voice.

The first FaceTime e2e (a stand-in plugin with FaceTime's consult parameters, `evidence-e2e-surfaces-red-503beb2ae.log`) failed on `503beb2ae`: FaceTime passes `thinkLevel: "off"`, and on the agent-turn route the command's model selection rejects an explicit level the model lacks, so every FaceTime consult on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` failed with `Thinking level "off" is not supported for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. ## Follow-up fix found while tracing a Google Meet e2e failure (`7f72cb5c7`)

Plugin `runEmbeddedAgent` runs its turn as a detached work continuation ("plugin turns can outlive both the triggering request root and its async work scope"); plugin `runCommandFromIngress`, which this PR's agent-turn route uses, did not. A meeting's realtime bridge is opened inside the `googlemeet.join` request, so a consult that reaches the command queue after the request that started it has ended lost its admission with `Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`, where the embedded route kept going. `runCommandFromIngress` now runs its turn as a detached continuation, the same way (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts`, one wrap). Test: `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ingress-continuation.test.ts` (an ingress turn that starts after its parent root and async scope ended), red on `8711c7b5a` with `GatewayDrainingError` at `enqueueCommandInLane` ← `runtime-agent.ts`, green after (`evidence-unit-ingress-continuation-7f72cb5c7.md`); the PR's test-lines allocation goes from 13 to 69 for it. A consult whose tool call itself arrives after that request ended still fails one step earlier, at `beginSessionEffect`, on `main` too; see "Pre-existing" under Evidence.

### Proof status: meeting callback path is blocked by a known bug on `main`

On this PR alone, as on `main`, a meeting consult that arrives through the normal provider callback cannot complete, because of a known bug on `main` that this PR does not touch: a realtime voice consult issued from a callback runs under the already-released root of the request that opened the call (`googlemeet.join` / `googlemeet.create`), and `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` refuses it with `GatewayDrainingError` ("Gateway is temporarily unavailable" / "Gateway is draining") before any runner is chosen. It fails the same way on the embedded route on `main`.

- Reported in #142610 (meeting, Google Meet) and #202915 (FaceTime).
- Fixed by #202979 (fresh root admission inside `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, covers every voice bridge) and, for meetings only, #142692. Both are open and waiting on maintainers.
- This PR only changes what happens after admission (which runner executes the consult), so it neither causes nor fixes that refusal. Once #202979 (or #142692) lands, the normal meeting callback reaches this PR's agent-turn route unchanged. This is shown below: with #202979 applied **temporarily** on top of `7f72cb5c7` (throwaway local branch, never pushed, not part of this PR), a meeting consult delivered through the normal provider callback after `googlemeet.join` returned was answered by the real Claude CLI; the same run on `7f72cb5c7` alone is refused at `beginSessionEffect` ("Meeting through the normal provider callback").

The meeting callback entry is shown too, with the separate fix applied temporarily; without that fix it stays blocked by the bug above, not by this change.

prs.title: fix: bound memory used by shared session sidebar views
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195497#issuecomment-6904038526.

## What Problem This Solves

A shared session can appear differently to each person who opens the Control UI. For example, two people can see the same parent session and different private child sessions. As more people viewed one long-lived session, the Gateway kept every distinct version of its sidebar row.

## User Impact

The Gateway now retains up to 64 audience-specific rows for each presentation of a session. If an older entry has been evicted, the next read rebuilds the row from the viewer’s current permissions. Repeated reads of a retained entry still reuse it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session publication owns the cached rows. It now discards the oldest entry when the per-view limit is reached, following the same policy used by child visibility and activity. All three owners share a constant in the existing dependency-free limits module. The change adds 18 net production lines to bound this cache.

## Evidence

- On the original code, 68 synthetic profile owners viewed one live shared parent. Each correctly saw only their own private child. The Gateway still held 68 distinct rows for the same sidebar presentation.
- The fixed Gateway held 64 rows. Returning to the oldest viewer reconstructed the same visible fields and child list. A conditional read with the earlier revision returned a valid replacement, and the next unchanged poll reused its revision.
- All 20 tests across the four focused suites passed on the signed candidate, including the Gateway sidebar delta tests. The stock regression failed at the retained-row count.

This reproduces one source of retention on an active shared session. The long-running production RSS reports still need their own measurements.

prs.title: improve: use less memory when capturing the first session checkout snapshot
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181432 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a session can capture a snapshot of its working directory. The Git worker loaded the workspace mutation and database schema code just to compare files, even when the repository was empty.

## User Impact

The first checkout snapshot uses less resident memory and finishes sooner. Creating a repository still uses the existing workspace owner and checks its authority immediately before initialization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workspace initialization is the only operation in this module that needs mutation support. Loading that support at its call site keeps it out of the read-only Git worker. The production change adds one net line. A regression test exercises a real checkout read with the mutation module unavailable.

## Evidence

The stock and candidate runtime packages used the same parent, Node 26 on macOS ARM64, and the same three repositories. Each pair started a fresh process and Git worker. All 48 results matched, including paths, file contents and modes. The worker loaded TypeBox through the Git chunk on stock. That import and its database schema chunk disappeared on the candidate.

| First checkout snapshot | Stock / patched time | Stock / patched process RSS at result | Worker physical V8 heap reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty | 357 / 240 ms | 204.50 / 164.49 MiB | 34.42 MiB |
| Tracked file | 356 / 221 ms | 201.48 / 164.51 MiB | 34.30 MiB |
| Untracked file | 387 / 222 ms | 203.08 / 164.18 MiB | 34.67 MiB |

Each value is a median over eight alternating pairs per fixture. Worker used heap was 0.4–0.6 MiB higher. The first genuine workspace initialization now performs the import. Both runtime builds passed. The new import-boundary assertion failed on stock, and all 15 checkout and workspace initialization tests passed on the candidate, including the host-refusal case.

Four additional fresh processes per build each kept one Git worker through six more snapshots. Warm median times on empty, tracked and untracked checkouts were 37.00 / 36.44 ms, 39.97 / 39.90 ms, and 38.74 / 36.32 ms (stock / patched). For these complete processes, including worker shutdown, macOS `/usr/bin/time -l` reported median maximum RSS of 203.40 / 163.41 MiB and peak physical footprint of 172.76 / 129.13 MiB.

The full Gateway and long-running NAS workloads have separate acceptance tests.

prs.title: fix: stop Git auto-updates accumulating unused builds
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

A dev-channel Git install kept a full day of builds after nothing needed them. One operator reported 21 non-serving builds using 105 GB. The disk filled, updates failed, and the Gateway could no longer write to its databases. Failed preparation could also leave a build behind. Simply deleting old builds can break ordinary commands that started before a release switch and still need their files.

## User Impact

The resident updater collects unused releases before allocating another build. It protects the serving release, active trial and fallback, running Gateway and updater, leased builds and open-run references. Failed preparation disposes of its own build. A command launched from the corrected release now holds the build it actually loaded until that process exits. Multiple commands can hold the same build; after the last holder exits, the next cleanup can reclaim it. No background job or new configuration. The change does not retroactively register commands already running older code.

If a command cannot safely mark its build as in use, it fails before doing its work and tells the operator how to proceed. Local `--version` remains available. This also covers the browser native host without writing diagnostics to its protocol output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original 24-hour rule (#198835) protected processes that might still load files from a deselected release. The new CLI entries reuse the existing process lease rather than retaining every build. For historical directories whose UUID differs from their run ID, cleanup checks the restore receipt and the verified running build against the release on disk. Legacy npm retains its conservative grace. Dev checks remain hourly, an already-current build is skipped, and pnpm's clone-or-copy import settings are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Ordinary command:** Previously, `openclaw config patch --stdin --dry-run --json` lost a required module after A→B→C. Through the production launcher, the corrected command waited across both switches, survived collection, finished schema validation and exited 0. The next collection removed A alone. B and C remained. Separate coverage exercised two simultaneous commands, forced exit, both executable entries, denied lease writes, and native-host protocol output.
- **Disk growth:** Four real isolated unpatched dev updates grew `releases/` from 4.45 to 8.90 to 13.35 to 17.80 GB apparent. An early fix bounded new builds but missed five historical ones. The corrected updater removed all five on its first driven update, without manual cleanup: eight trees / 35.60 GB fell to three / 13.35 GB and held there across three consecutive updates. Btrfs-exclusive usage fell from 8.84 to 3.32 GB. Every live build matched its target and trial receipt; these hops did not induce rollback.
- **Other checks:** The historical correction passed 34 focused tests. Earlier checks included 129 passing custody tests (four platform skips), 42 diagnostics tests, 64 CLI and census tests. Four journaled npm crash tests failed identically on base and patch because the checkout lacked the built sealed helper. Native Windows updates were not exercised. The reporting installation was untouched.
- **Known limits:** Status can omit a saved cleanup warning when its scan budget expires. The cleanup preview reports historical release warnings separately from live recovery totals. Unidentified trees can be recounted on later updates. The earlier disk proof also found 11 prunable Git worktree registrations (84.97 MB) outside `releases/`.

Reported by @jesse-merhi.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Ordinary command lifetime implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4d53737b-1157-4954-92b3-1cfb41d41c76)

prs.title: chore: reproduce replies stuck behind bound ACP questions
prs.body:
Related: #206954

## What Problem This Solves

When a bound ACP turn asks a question, the user's reply can wait behind that same turn and later run as an unrelated prompt.

## User Impact

A matching channel reply can answer the pending form without waiting for the asking turn to finish. Ordinary follow-ups continue through the normal queue. The PR is open for review. Live Discord/Claude verification is still outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the specific question for the admitted channel origin and sender before waiting for a new turn slot. If the question closes or is replaced, its captured reply must not become a fresh prompt or answer the replacement.

## Evidence

On refreshed base `4b752bd1` the channel answer waited for the asking turn. A second regression reproduced an ordinary follow-up being mistaken for a question answer while the first reply was being saved. Both pass with the fix. Across seven focused files, 124 tests passed. The routed test uses the Claude adapter's single-choice plus optional Other field, two conversations bound to the same ACP target, and redelivery after an injected persistence failure. It requires the original callback to accept Red, with no replay as a new prompt. Scoped formatting and lint passed. These are local tests, not live Discord/Claude proof. Separately, the [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097856850/job/140836904687) passed on `6e0db247`, and [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207035#issuecomment-7230574846) rated patch quality Platinum (4/6) with no actionable findings on that head. Core and core-test typechecks passed with the frozen dependency installation. The timeout and max-lines guards passed against the prepared base. The aggregate command was not clean: its nested max-lines comparison lacked merge-base history, and Knip flagged an unchanged CLI export outside this patch.

Author simplification: the question owner now decides whether a question is claimable for both capture and submission. The tests use Vitest cancellation rather than 12 separate wall-clock races. Cleanup uses runner-owned finish hooks to drain every routed dispatch before restoring the previous broker. Against the pre-pass head `84b3a1ab`: production +13/−17; tests +58/−68 (+38/−48 ignoring indentation). Across the whole PR against `4b752bd1`: production +211/−14; tests +226/−3. All 124 focused tests also passed on the final published tree. Retained proof distinguishes wrong-conversation input on the same target, stale or replaced questions, persistence failures/redelivery, and ordinary FIFO input.

prs.title: fix: let authorized orchestrators resume blocked goals
prs.body:
Closes #203683

## What Problem This Solves

An operator can resolve a blocker and ask an orchestrator to resume another chat, but the session tools cannot apply Goal Resume. Sending another message leaves the blocked goal unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly ask an authorized orchestrator to resume another chat's blocked goal. The caller needs a live host-issued operator write grant and existing session access as creator or administrator. Notes explain the request; they do not approve pending actions. Paused and limited goals keep the existing human controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `sessions(action: "goal_resume", sessionKey, expectedSessionId, note)` as an adapter to the existing public Goal Resume operation. It preserves the exact session and goal identities and uses the existing admission, budget, and receipt rules. A narrow optional blocked-status precondition is checked by the Goal writer so a newer Pause wins; ordinary human Resume requests are unchanged. The calling chat must finish its reply before resuming itself through the normal controls.

## Evidence
Current head: `f47b1e013595586ab127e2874f9f1d11f366c1be` (includes main `995d9bdc1` and a braces-only lint fix in the new test helper).

- **Passed on the published source tree:** `git diff --check`, formatting on 13 changed TypeScript/Markdown files, targeted type-aware core lint on 12 changed TypeScript files (0 warnings/errors), and the agents-tools and gateway-server test typecheck lanes. Used pinned pnpm 12.15.0.
- **Earlier focused run (before the fixture correction, author-reported):** 105 passed / 1 failed: Goal suite 74/74, prefix stability 16/16, and session authority 15/16. The Goal suite exercised the tool-to-Gateway path with a synthetic agent, including continuation after the caller ended, receipt replay, and rejection after a newer Pause. The failed negative case used a synchronous creator update that did not refresh the sharing projection. The current test fixture uses awaited session metadata writes; that corrected case and the full focused set have not been rerun on this head.
- **Still unverified:** full build, current-head focused tests (starting with the corrected negative case), and the isolated real-agent/model flow. No real-model completion is claimed. Existing human Resume, Snooze, and Wake are not intentionally changed.

This remains a draft. **Maintainer product decision required before merge:** whether an operator-authorized orchestrator may resume another session's blocked goal under the existing creator/admin access rules. The note does not grant authority or approve pending actions.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): carry provider-native chat id into session-event turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#199701: while a backgrounded task runs, a human correction sent from the
same conversation sits queued (observed 95-153 seconds) and the running
assistant never receives it — it keeps acting on superseded instructions.
Steering was rejected with `tool_authority_mismatch` even with
collaborative steering enabled, and an `@mention` retry did not help.

Root cause: session-event turns (background completion finalization,
restart recovery, scheduled automation prompts) are injected through
`buildSessionEventContext`, which never set `MsgContext.ChatId`. Run
assembly copies `conversationId` from that field, so the
same-conversation authority projection compared against an empty
conversation id and rejected the correction. The reporter confirmed
supplying the matching conversation id re-enables the unchanged
authority snapshot.

## The Change

- Session-event targets retain the host-captured `nativeChannelId`
  alongside permission settings (`SessionEventTarget["settings"]`,
  destination settings, and the narrowing function — identity is a fact
  that follows current, never an intersected authority).
- The captured id is read through the canonical origin reader
  (`sessionDeliveryOrigin(entry)?.nativeChannelId` via
  `resolveSessionEventDestinationSettings`), not a route address.
- `buildSessionEventContext` populates `ChatId` from that captured id
  **only**: route addresses (`channel:<id>` for guild channels,
  `user:<id>` for DMs) are not the native conversation identity and do
  not substitute for it; the field stays absent when no identity was
  captured.
- Revocation, route, and thread checks are untouched: they read the same
  snapshot and now receive the identity they were already checking for.

## Evidence

- **Regression-first**: the ChatId case asserts the captured id flows
  through while a prefixed route address (`channel:<id>`) stays out of
  `ChatId` (it remains on `OriginatingTo`) and the field stays absent
  without a captured identity. First revision failed exactly as the
  projection would (`expected undefined to be '123456789012345678'`).
  Full file: **8/8** (capture case covers a real-shaped session entry — `delivery.origin.nativeChannelId` — through destination settings into context construction) (`session-event-context.test.ts`).
- **Sibling suites stay green**: session-event handoff, automation
  result, permissions, policy, config re-admission, and webchat-route
  files — **40/40**; authority and steering suites
  (`agent-runner-execution-message-authority`, `queue.authority`,
  `agent-runner-fallback-steering`) — **23/23**.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.test.ts` on head

prs.title: fix(cron): keep required reports from going silent when nothing changes
prs.body:
Closes #206884

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled job can produce its required daily status and still suppress it because nothing changed.

## User Impact

Jobs that request a report every run are told to return it even on unchanged days. Conditional alerts stay quiet unless triggered. If an agent supplies the wrong field while recording an outcome, it gets a correctable input error instead of an internal error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner deliberately suppresses a recorded `no_change`. Rather than weakening that guarantee, the prompt distinguishes a required report from an intentionally quiet check and shows the optional recorder’s input shape. Only malformed outcome data is reclassified; the delivery and authorization paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Contributor-run live Gateway proof:** [DonnieFi’s run record](https://github.com/DonnieFi/openclaw/commit/864ee3fd6b4ebb02cfa19193c9dd9ba56260b3ff) documents two isolated Codex/OpenAI cron runs at `a383623b` with Code Mode and the same unchanged queue. The required report announced `Queue: IDLE` exactly once to the local QA adapter (`delivered`). The conditional alert recorded `no_change`, finished `ok/not-delivered/silent`, and produced zero captures. Neither was sent directly by a messaging tool. The JSON evidence record (`test/fixtures/cron-required-report-live-proof.json`) preserves those observations; it is not an executable replay.

- The new prompt and Code Mode regressions failed before their respective fixes. Through the actual Code Mode bridge, missing `outcome` (including `result` and `status` aliases) left the invocation unrecorded, and a corrected retry succeeded.
- A paired isolated-runner fixture supplied the same `Queue: IDLE` text in both cases. The announce adapter captured it once for the report and zero times for a recorded quiet check. Neither was delivered by a direct messaging-tool send. The fixture used synthetic responses.
- 107 focused tests across six files passed at local head `fbd664b10`, as did both paired fixture cases, targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and docs link checks. Independent agent reviews of the two code changes caught a conditional-alert ambiguity; the corrected prompt and recorder diff had no remaining review findings. Base: `0633f256`. Independent reviewers inspected supplied diffs; these are not hosted ratings or CI.

Simplification: removed 87 lines of test code that asserted literal observations, retaining all original fields in 65 lines of JSON. No runtime logic or behavioral regression tests changed in this pass (net −22 lines). Across the whole PR: production +5/−4, executable tests +32/−3, docs +1/−1, evidence +65/−0. All 20 focused tests passed after the conversion.

After integrating `c695d653`, the three generated prompt snapshots were refreshed (+15/−15 generated lines; no additional runtime or executable test changes). `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` verified all six snapshots and the three focused cron suites passed 23 tests on the published source tree.

Contributor: DonnieFi.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

### November 24 conflict refresh

Integrated upstream main `4708bac52397` into `04af0f2c2c3`. Only the two generated config baselines conflicted. Regenerated both using `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `pnpm config:docs:check`, scoped formatting, and `git diff --check` against the integrated main passed.
- Memory Core startup and config schema suites passed, 64 tests across two files.
- The live upgrade traces above are from earlier revisions. This refresh validates the integration with current main. The opt-in startup policy remains open for maintainer review.


### Generated baseline refresh

Integrated upstream main `328a43818a1` in `4114126f480`. The generated hash conflict is resolved by regenerating from the integrated configuration. The generated core hash matches the previous PR head, and the plugin hash matches current upstream. `pnpm config:docs:check` passed and all 64 Memory Core and config schema tests passed.

### November 27 configuration baseline refresh

Integrated upstream main `6089b804582` at `5835496e1f5` and regenerated both configuration baseline artifacts. The combined and core hashes now include the startup option. The channel and plugin hashes match upstream.

- `pnpm config:docs:check`, scoped formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All 64 tests in the Memory Core startup and config schema suites passed.
- The stable-release upgrade trace above predates this integration. The opt-in startup policy still requires a maintainer product decision.

### November 28 configuration baseline refresh

Integrated upstream main `4aa7c38c156` at `0715c1e0a47` and regenerated the configuration baseline. The channel and plugin hashes match upstream. The baseline check, scoped formatting, and diff check passed. All 61 Memory Core and config schema tests passed. A direct schema parse verified that the startup opt-in and the upstream partial media indexing option can be used together. The opt-in startup policy still requires a maintainer product decision.

prs.title: ci: check the Plugin SDK export surface on every pull request
prs.body:
## Problem

#206995 added a Plugin SDK export without a surface budget line and merged with green PR CI. Main's SDK surface check then failed (`public exports 3933 > 3932`, `public callable exports 2260 > 2259`) until a follow-up added the line.

Why PR CI did not catch it:
- `check:changed` selects `plugin-sdk:check-exports` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` for SDK paths. But PR CI calls it lint-only (`ci.yml`, "Run changed lint", `lintOnly: true`), so only lint commands run.
- The only other runner is the `generated-doc-baselines` job in `workflow-sanity.yml`. It runs only on `workflow_dispatch`, never on a pull request.

## Fix

The baseline-ratchets job (`scripts/ci-baseline-ratchets.mts`) already runs on every node PR. It now also runs `plugin-sdk:check-exports` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` on every run:
- The surface check is a large TypeScript program, so it runs in the same slot as the database-worker and database-dialect snapshots. They run one after another and never overlap (the memory rule from `c695d653`). The export check is light and joins the shared queue.
- It runs on every PR, not only SDK-path PRs: the SDK import closure reaches far outside `src/plugin-sdk`. For example, adding `@deprecated` to `src/channels/chat-type.ts` moves the deprecated-export count, and no changed-path rule sees that.

No new workflow or job.

## Impact

Contributors: a PR that changes the SDK export surface without its budget line now fails `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` instead of turning main red after merge. Cost per PR: one surface check (about 7 s and 3.5 GB peak locally) in the existing job.

## Evidence

- Red/green on a PR-like change set: a scratch copy of main with #206995's export added on top of a tagged base, run with `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base <base> --no-merge-base`:
  - a new SDK function without a budget line: `plugin-sdk-surface` fails, `public exports 3933 > 3932`, `public callable exports 2261 > 2260`, exit 1;
  - the same change plus the budget lines: `[ok] plugin-sdk-exports`, `[ok] plugin-sdk-surface`, exit 0.
- `test/scripts/ci-baseline-ratchets.test.ts`: the expected command list now includes both SDK checks in their slots (4/4).
- Adversarial review: a first version selected the checks by changed path. The review showed that version missed real budget inputs outside `src/plugin-sdk` and reproduced a miss. This version drops path selection.

prs.title: improve: reuse the active config for local inference
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local inference can run immediately after CLI startup has loaded and published the active config. Each invocation still constructed a config reader and captured the current environment before returning that same config.

## User Impact

Local capability commands can use the config that startup prepared. A standalone command with no published config still captures its environment and reads the config asynchronously.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local command already knows whether it needs a config immediately. It now checks the existing published snapshot before creating a reader. Caller-supplied config keeps precedence. The command still yields before resolving settings when it needs to obtain the config itself, and still publishes the effective config with its authored source.

## Evidence

- The registered local model command constructed one reader on the baseline with an active config. It constructs zero on this branch. The on-disk cold case constructs one on both revisions. These cases also check that the command resolves and publishes the intended config objects.
- The changed CLI suites passed 133 tests. The shared CLI option and async config-reader suites passed a further 25 against the same production change. Targeted TypeScript, type-aware lint and formatting passed.
- On Darwin ARM64 with Node 26.13.1, the median time per published config read with 64 synthetic environment entries fell from 138.065 to 0.058 microseconds. Eight alternating pairs ran 300 reads per arm. Every read returned the same published object. This measures the read alone. End-to-end command latency and physical-device timing remain unmeasured.
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper reviewed `f5453cb9..a3ce461c`. Both found the existing resolver and snapshot owner appropriate. The tests and measurement above supply the execution evidence the read-only reviewer requested.

prs.title: fix(release): retain validation artifacts by candidate commit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rebuilding the package for the same Full Release Validation candidate commit changed the package SHA. Two candidate validation lanes could no longer reuse their retained artifacts, even though the candidate commit had not changed.

## User Impact

Release operators can reuse artifacts from the original validation run when the candidate commit and workload inputs still match, rather than losing reuse after a package rebuild. No operator action or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before dispatch, the dispatcher looks up the original artifact source by exact candidate commit SHA and matching workload inputs. Artifact reuse still requires byte-level verification, and a failed verdict is never adopted.

## Evidence

- The dispatcher and retained-artifact suites passed, including CLI tests for matching and nonmatching candidate commits. Lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- A read-only dry run using the real 2026.11.11 candidate (C) and qualification (Q) commits selected workflow run `46072918899`, attempt `1`, without creating a request or dispatching a workflow. No hosted validation run was launched.
- The local tooling typecheck was blocked by the symlink custody guard.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix: keep completed worker runs visible after a follow-up
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a second task in a saved worker, the parent could no longer check how the first task ended. Even with its exact run ID, `subagents wait` reported `unavailable` while the result was still on record.

## User Impact

The parent can check the earlier outcome and delivery status without resending the task. The reply itself stays in conversation history. No settings or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The latest run still determines which workers the caller can see. An exact wait can also return a settled predecessor if the child owner, requester, controller and recorded store paths match. A historical row cannot make descendants visible. Listing, cancellation and retention are unchanged. The change adds 24 net production lines and 63 test lines.

## Evidence

I tested the repair in `c0de1314` on two otherwise identical development builds based on `5e245aa0`, including the same other fixes. Both used a real Gateway, Codex CLI 0.164.0, and a synthetic HTTPS model.

Reproduction steps

1. Create a worker with `sessions_spawn` and `cleanup: "keep"`. Let its first task complete and record the run ID.
2. Send a follow-up with `sessions_send` to the same worker and record the second run ID.
3. Verify that both tasks used the same native worker thread, produced distinct successful run IDs, and retained both exact assistant replies in history.
4. Invoke `subagents` through `tools.invoke` with `action: "wait"`, `runIds: [first, second]`, and `timeoutSeconds: 0`.

Before the fix, the first run returned `unavailable` after the follow-up. With the fix, both runs returned terminal `ok` status. The wait query made zero additional model calls in both builds.

On `1f033298`, the persisted regression returned only the current run and failed on the two missing earlier outcomes. With the fix, all 37 cases passed across the native tool, persisted tool and registry suites. The new case took 145 ms. The single-worker run took 161.61 s including startup. The test covers mixed success and failure, a running successor, an ownership change, a descendant behind that change and both store paths.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.registry.test.ts src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

I ran the repository's Vitest wrapper in isolation with cached dependencies from `82b682c6` because the package mirror lacked two locked versions. Formatting, targeted type-aware lint with type checking and whitespace checks passed. Full locked-dependency checks remain for CI.

Independent source review of the initial two-file diff on `1f033298` found no remaining issues after the store checks were added. Local autoreview could not start its reviewer and produced no verdict.

At `125b1255`, I restored the current-run ID lookup used on main after CI flagged a direct comparison. The historical path runs only on a miss. The session identity check passed with the original allowlist. Both affected suites passed again (11 cases, 118.65 s total, 157 ms for the new case). Formatting, type-aware lint with type checking, and independent review of this delta passed. The Gateway trial above used the first implementation.

#### Gateway capture on the updated code

I repeated the same two-task trial with the production diff through `125b1255`. The Gateway and Codex app server executed the tools and stored the replies. The HTTPS model was scripted. Both runs kept the same child thread and both exact replies. This excerpt projects the recorded wait responses, with generated IDs shortened to A and B within each trial.

```text
Control
before follow-up   2026-11-28T02:01:44.304Z   reason=completed   A=terminal/ok   modelCalls=0
after follow-up   2026-11-28T02:01:46.571Z   reason=unavailable   A=unavailable B=terminal/ok   modelCalls=0
Fixed
before follow-up   2026-11-28T02:41:27.761Z   reason=completed   A=terminal/ok   modelCalls=0
after follow-up   2026-11-28T02:41:30.104Z   reason=completed   A=terminal/ok B=terminal/ok   modelCalls=0
```

prs.title: feat(huggingface): offer optional Hub tools alongside inference
prs.body:
Related: #197384 (separate publisher-badge fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Hugging Face inference and Hub tools currently require separate plugins, making their setup and authentication easy to confuse.

## User Impact

The bundled Hugging Face plugin offers inference and optional Hub tools in one place. Hub access is off by default and uses a separate OAuth connection; existing inference settings and saved sign-ins are unchanged.

Existing `@openclaw/hugging-face` installations are not removed or disabled. To switch ownership safely, enable Hub tools in the bundled plugin, then disable (rather than uninstall) the old wrapper. An enabled old wrapper remains independent of the new toggle.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundled plugin declares the existing Hugging Face MCP endpoint instead of introducing another integration. A plugin-owned opt-in activates it without making inference users connect to MCP automatically. Disabled defaults cannot shadow an active legacy server or its data-directory ownership. Explicit operator MCP overrides still win.

## Evidence

- **Stable upgrade — passed:** The `v2026.11.10` release source (`6ea542fd97e2`) wrote an isolated config, a synthetic Hugging Face inference credential and a separate synthetic MCP OAuth sign-in through its normal storage APIs. A fixture for the legacy `hugging-face` plugin declared the real server name and endpoint. Both `906bf6f69ffa` and the conflict-resolved `23a64b4906f8` read the stable settings and credentials in a fresh process. The legacy plugin still owned the connection until the wrapper was disabled. Turning bundled Hub tools **on → off → on** changed the runtime owner to **bundled → absent → bundled**. At every stage the selected inference model, discovery setting, inference API key, and Hub access and refresh tokens matched their stable values. The proof used no network requests. It exercised the stable source tag, not the npm installer or the live service.
- **Gateway and stored sign-in:** An isolated Gateway completed an OAuth callback against a local issuer for a legacy plugin. After switching to the new opt-in plugin, its MCP tool returned an authenticated reply using the existing sign-in. Turning the opt-in off removed the server from the runtime catalog without clearing the stored tokens.
- **Hugging Face service:** An unauthenticated MCP client connected to `https://huggingface.co/mcp`, listed its four public tools and called the read-only `hf_whoami` tool. It reported anonymous access. No inference call was made. Live Hugging Face OAuth and an authenticated Hub call through OpenClaw remain unverified.
- **Settings:** The Chromium test passed against the production Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses. Hub tools start unchecked, the opt-in survives reload, and plugin enablement and model discovery keep their values. The existing screenshots below show that flow; the repair changes no UI rendering.
- **Ownership and generated files:** All 38 focused loader, manifest and extension-boundary tests passed. The core type-boundary guard, focused lint, relevant UI/Gateway typechecks, formatting, diff checks, and the test-line budget passed. The inventory check failed before regeneration and passed afterward. An upstream memory-search schema change caused a conflict in the generated config digest. `23a64b4906f8` integrates `002e4b2ddf9d` and regenerates that digest without changing the plugin, loader, or tests. The inventory and config-baseline checks both passed after integration; `hub` and `hub.enabled` account for the change from 5,690 to 5,692 plugin entries.
- [Required CI passed on the previous head, `906bf6f69ffa`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097948471/job/140837521989); see [current checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197387/checks) for the new head. The focused Gateway checks are not a claim that the entire OAuth suite passed. No clean local independent review is claimed.

### Before

![Before: Hugging Face settings only offer model discovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64013143-949d-4060-8f72-3ba26f3c7eed)

### After

![After: Hugging Face settings add separately opt-in Hub tools](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91829e88-9a93-49c7-a794-a1acc54afe6e)

Thanks to @VACInc for identifying the split setup and requesting this consolidation.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1cd65ad8-57f3-461a-942f-18e482c4a5da)
- [Follow-up discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4591147b-d110-4a05-a692-35247ed3a855)

prs.title: fix: let CLI onboarding retry a saved sign-in with another model
prs.body:
Related: #200112

## What Problem This Solves

CLI onboarding can save a provider sign-in before its completion check fails. The picker did not list a newly saved sign-in in that run, and a sign-in discovered from a prior run could only retry its starter model.

## User Impact

If the user allowed discovery, failed manual verification refreshes the saved choices. After a failed check, the user can select a newly saved or previously detected sign-in and, for a regular agent model, keep the suggested model ID or enter a different ID from the same provider. The default model stays unchanged until the selected model replies successfully. Declining discovery still skips the saved-sign-in scan. This change is CLI-only; there is no migration or native macOS change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing saved-credential inventory and the existing verification and activation path. A retry refresh reads persisted setup choices rather than repeating service/CLI discovery. It keeps the selected provider and sign-in fixed, and it never tests another model automatically.

## Evidence

- Comparison base: `ee4061ce5e81027d603acbd31e1e5ba9ea7f6ef5`. Current head: `e450ae370db7461a847ff44b932ba0f9cf2dccb5`; tested tree: `d205bc5c5d48b0772d7acbaa49bdce78e0adf4e2`.
- The original regression failed on the comparison base because the picker omitted the newly saved sign-in. On the previous PR head, the resumed-onboarding regression failed because the second attempt repeated the starter model. On the current head, both guided-onboarding suites passed (21 tests, 43.41 seconds local wall time). The unchanged detection and activation suites retain their previous evidence (65 passing tests on the previous tree); they were not rerun.
- Core and commands-test typechecks, targeted lint and format, the wizard MDX check, and `git diff --check` passed on this revision. The local `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` completed on the exact current head in 2m 40s with exit 0 and stamped that head. It emitted non-blocking Control UI budget warnings for CSS gzip and chat boot request count and JS gzip; these were not independently attributed.
- Full-priority (P0–P3) Auto Review found the missing model prompt after a previously detected saved sign-in failed. After the fix, the second full-priority static review and manual review found no remaining actionable issues.
- No live provider, real credentials, clean-host Ubuntu first-chat run, or native macOS test was used. The reported Ubuntu timeout remains unverified; exact-head hosted CI and maintainer review still apply.

Original patch by Richard O’Shaughnessy ([@oshaughnessy-junior](https://github.com/oshaughnessy-junior)).

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.
