prs.title: fix: stop native completion retirement from retrying forever
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #200892.

When a completed native Codex child can no longer retire its persisted assignment, the monitor currently retries the retirement write every 15 seconds forever. This bounds the retirement phase with the existing retry budget, then stops the in-memory monitor while preserving the unresolved assignment for Doctor repair.

## User impact

- persistent retirement-write failures stop producing an unbounded retry/log loop
- the completion result is still delivered at most once
- unresolved persisted assignment state remains available for diagnosis and repair
- transient retirement failures continue to retry and can still complete cleanup

## Implementation

- reset the existing completion-delivery attempt counter when entering the retirement phase, giving that mutually exclusive phase its own bounded budget
- charge every retirement retry against that budget
- unregister the in-memory child after persistent retirement exhaustion; the assignment-settlement guard retains the unresolved persisted locator
- add a regression that rejects every retirement write and proves finite termination, single result delivery, retained assignment state, and no transcript/system-note delivery

## Evidence

Candidate head: `17a80c2183d20765634d94b33eda7782ac1fc090`

- Regression first failed on base `8f321bcc7e14569939ee9648a9663f3927816f2c` because a retry timer remained after the bounded window.
- 63 focused assertions passed across `native-subagent-inventory.test.ts`, `native-subagent-completion-delivery.contention.test.ts`, and `native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts`.
- Extension source and extension-test typechecks passed.
- Focused oxlint passed for both changed files.
- Plugin boundary report, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent local P0-P2 autoreview reported no actionable findings (confidence 0.9).

The broader changed-lane wrapper completed its selected guards and Doctor tests, then exceeded the local 10-minute wrapper budget at the plugin-boundary phase; that boundary command passed separately. No live Gateway or live Slack configuration was changed for this proof.

## Codex contract check

I inspected `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs`. They expose thread/turn completion receipts and collaboration state, but no host assignment-retirement acknowledgement. The bounded retirement lifecycle therefore remains owned by the OpenClaw monitor.

## Scope

This does not delete unresolved assignment state, change delivery routing, resend completion output, or alter live authentication/channel configuration.

### Isolated runtime evidence at `17a80c2183d2`

An isolated packaged Gateway ran this head with a real native Codex child and loopback model. The parent completed and one child produced its final response. A test-only adapter returned a blocked delivery result and simulated a read-only store at retirement. The packaged retry code selected its normal backoffs (5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300 seconds); the harness compressed elapsed timer waits. Observed counters: 1 completion delivery attempt, 7 refused writes including the initial attempt, 6 scheduled retries, then exhaustion. The assignment store still contained the matching child at exhaustion. No second delivery attempt or further retry was observed during the observation window. This exercises the Gateway lifecycle with an injected write failure; the original live cause and real wall-clock waits were not reproduced.

### Captured Gateway output at `17a80c2183d2`

The retained projection of the Gateway run above was:

```json
{
  "parentStatus": "ok",
  "spawnCalls": 1,
  "childFinals": 1,
  "retirementWarnings": 7,
  "durabilityWarnings": 7
}
```

The storage adapter recorded these events in order. Delay values are the selected budgets in milliseconds. The trace ends after the retained-assignment readback; it contains one delivery attempt.

```text
loaded
delivery-attempt
write-refused
delay-5000
write-refused
delay-15000
write-refused
delay-30000
write-refused
delay-60000
write-refused
delay-120000
write-refused
delay-300000
write-refused
retained
```

prs.title: fix: finish updates of 2026-11-17 main checkouts automatically on Linux and macOS
prs.body:
Related: #204775, #206341, #205995, #204322, #204275

## What Problem This Solves

Git checkouts that tracked `main` between 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-19 (for example `8f80fe08cad`) still run the updater built then, and that updater cannot finish an update that migrates the databases. Since #206341 their `openclaw update` stops cleanly at the new release's check, every time, and prints a by-hand rebuild that keeps the Gateway down for about five minutes. The update never finishes unless the user runs that line.

## User Impact

A plain `openclaw update --yes` on such a checkout now finishes by itself, on Linux with a systemd user Gateway and on macOS with a launchd Gateway:

- The old updater still reports this one update as failed (it cannot be patched). Its output says the new release is finishing the update in the background and how to follow it.
- A few minutes later the Gateway serves the new version from the rebuilt checkout, on the migrated schema, and `openclaw update status` shows the recovery's run as `succeeded`. The next plain `openclaw update` runs normally.
- The Gateway is down only for the two restarts: 19.6 s (the boot migration of a 512 MB agent database) plus 6.7 s on macOS, against 286 s for the by-hand line.
- If the new release fails before migrating, the previous build is put back and serves. If something fails after the migration (for example `pnpm build` in the checkout), the release keeps serving, and the recorded outcome and the job log name the one command that finishes the update.
- When the recovery cannot run (another platform, no systemd user manager or no launchd login session, a stopped Gateway, another installation in the service or on `PATH`, a dirty checkout, less than 4 GiB free, no `pnpm`), the #206341 refusal and its rebuild line print as before, with the reason, and nothing changes.

Every other install is untouched: the check acts only on the early updater's release layout with a pending schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer decided on #204775 that the refusal from #206341 must become the fallback, not the fix: the stranded checkout has to reach the fix through its ordinary `openclaw update`. This restores the automatic recovery that #205995 retired (it came from #204322, systemd only) and adds launchd.

**Where it hooks in.** The installed updater runs this release's `update-migrated-finalize.worker --check` from `git-install/releases/<id>/build` before it switches its release link, with a 120 s limit, and kills the check's process tree when it ends. A non-zero check stops the update. That is the only point where the old updater runs this release's code before anything changes.

**What the check does.** When it recognizes the early layout and a pending schema change, it checks every precondition, moves the built release to `git-install/recovery/openclaw`, and starts the runner as a job of the user's service manager, outside the check's process tree, then exits 1:
- Linux: a transient systemd user service (`systemd-run --user --unit=openclaw-update-recovery --collect -p Restart=on-abnormal`), as #204322 did.
- macOS: a separate launchd job, `ai.openclaw.update-recovery`, bootstrapped into the user's GUI domain from a plist beside the kept release (`KeepAlive` only after a crash, output to `<state dir>/logs/update-recovery.log`). It retires itself with `launchctl bootout` when done. Its label does not match the `ai.openclaw.update.*` patterns that `launchd-update-jobs.ts` treats as leftover updater jobs.

Before building the launchd runner I checked the open question from the earlier lane in the VM: a job bootstrapped from a child of a KeepAlive LaunchAgent survives that agent's `launchctl bootout` and a new `bootstrap` (the job kept its PID and kept running; raw output below).

**What the runner does.** It waits for the old updater to exit, fast-forwards the checkout's branch to the release's commit, removes the early link `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw`, moves the Gateway onto the kept release with that release's `gateway install --force` (the release migrates state at boot), rebuilds the checkout with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` while the release serves, moves the Gateway onto the rebuilt checkout, and runs the finishing step from the rebuilt checkout: remove the kept release and the early layout's releases, `git worktree prune`, record the run.

**What #206341 taught, carried over.**
- On current `main`, `openclaw gateway install --force` binds the service to the early updater's launcher while the early link exists (`src/daemon/program-args.ts`). The runner removes the link before the first switch, puts it back only when the previous build comes back, and removes it whenever state moved (so the named finishing command binds the checkout).
- The old updater redacts the check's stderr (state directory to `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, home to `~`, `$` plus 16 or more name characters to a Matrix placeholder). Paths in the printed text are spelled from `$HOME`; a unit test runs every printed variant through the same redaction.
- A state directory the runner resolves differently from the service's stops it before it touches anything.

**Safety rules in the runner.**
- A switch counts only once the service manager runs a new process from the new definition (`systemctl show -p ExecStart -p MainPID`, `launchctl print` arguments and pid), not when the file on disk changed and the old Gateway still answers `/readyz`.
- The previous build is put back only on databases exactly as it left them, compared after a confirmed stop. Until the first switch, a different store inventory is not treated as a migration.
- The whole service definition is saved before the first switch: the systemd unit, or the LaunchAgent plist plus its environment file and wrapper, each with its mode. A put-back restores what changed.
- The service selectors (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL`, `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT`, port) go to the job, so its installs rewrite the same service the check inspected.
- Recording opens state through the new release, which migrates it. It records only once state moved, once it holds a run, or when it keeps the release, which migrates at its next start anyway.

**Removal condition.** In code and docs: remove the check and the recovery on evidence that no installed updater from that range still needs them, not on a date or a release.

**Files.** Restored from `b12552911c9^` and changed: `update-early-release-recovery.ts`, `-start.ts`, `-ready.ts`, `-record.ts`, `update-early-release-recovery.test.ts`. New for launchd and the shared service control: `update-early-release-recovery-service.ts`. Changed: `update-candidate-check-early-release.ts` (inspect plus format; the #206341 refusal text is the fallback), `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts` (the `--check` hook and the `--early-release-recovery` entry), their tests, `docs/install/updating.md`. No config key, stored field, schema, protocol, dependency, retention or permission change. `src/update/` is unchanged; the record module uses its public lock and run writers, as #204322 did.

**Update behavior.** The stranded checkout's own updater (`8f80fe08cad` and its siblings) reaches this through its candidate check on any target that contains this change. No other driver is affected.

## Evidence

**Fixture, every cell.** A checkout of `openclaw/openclaw` at `8f80fe08cad`, built and linked onto `PATH`, with a Gateway service from its own `openclaw gateway install --force`, and its `main` tracking a local upstream whose `main` is moved to set the target. A 512 MB agent database (state schema 40, agent schema 42) under about 1 MiB/s of writes, 1,000 marker rows checked by count and SHA-256, and a probe of `/healthz` and `/readyz` every second. "Not serving" is the time from the last `/healthz` 200 to the next. Driver in every cell: the checkout's installed updater `8f80fe08cad`, run as plain `openclaw update --yes`. macOS: clones of a Tart macOS 27.2 VM with a launchd Gateway. Linux: Docker containers with systemd as PID 1 and a systemd user Gateway. Synthetic state only.

**Before building the launchd runner:** a separate launchd job bootstrapped by a child of a KeepAlive LaunchAgent survives that agent's `bootout` and a new `bootstrap` (raw output at the end).

prs.title: fix(plugins): classify matching local archive installs as origin-path
prs.body:
Fixes #206723

## What Problem This Solves

A private plugin installed from a local archive keeps showing `provenance-invalid` in `openclaw plugins inspect` even after you rebuild, validate, repack, and successfully activate the exact same managed artifact — whose installed runtime SHA-256 matches the tested extracted runtime. This change classifies a matching local archive install as `origin-path` (a documented local override) instead of invalid provenance, so inspection and the loaded runtime finally agree.

- Problem: `resolvePluginTrust()` in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-record-match.ts` has branches for `bundled`, `owner-ambiguous`, `origin-path` (workspace/path/npm-with-artifact), `record-missing`, `install-path-mismatch`, `trusted-official`, `provenance-missing`, `third-party-npm`, and `git` — but none for `record.source === "archive"`. A matching local archive therefore falls through to the final `else` and is labeled `provenance-invalid`. The docs (`docs/tools/plugin.md`) state local path/archive installs classify as `origin-path`, and inspection plus runtime both rely on this single shared classifier (the suite asserts `inspected.trust === loaded.trust`).
- Solution: add an `else if (record.source === "archive")` branch that sets `reason = "origin-path"`, placed after the `install-path-mismatch` check (so a loaded path that diverges from the installed archive still warns) and after `owner-ambiguous`/`record-missing` (so ownership and record checks run first).
- What changed: `src/plugins/installed-plugin-record-match.ts` (one new branch + comment); `src/plugins/loader.trust-diagnostics.test.ts` (one `it.each` row asserting a matching local archive resolves to `origin-path`, `trusted: false`).
- What did NOT change: no capability decisions (`conversationAccessAccepted` below this branch already requires a path match); no remedy strings or rendering (`origin-path` already has a remedy in `plugin-trust.ts`); no other install sources.

## Why This Change Was Made

The classifier simply omitted an explicit branch for the archive source, so a legitimate local override was mislabeled as invalid provenance by fall-through. Adding the branch at the correct point in the decision tree restores the documented classification while keeping every existing guardrail (ownership ambiguity, missing record, install-path mismatch) ahead of it.

- Best fix: yes — the minimal change that makes the shared classifier honor the documented `origin-path` contract for archives, with the same `trusted: false` semantics as path/workspace overrides.
- Alternative: fold `archive` into the existing `origin-path` condition above. Rejected because that condition runs before `install-path-mismatch`, which would suppress the mismatch warning for an archive whose loaded path diverges from its installed record; placing the new branch after `install-path-mismatch` preserves that diagnostic.
- Risk / non-goals: archives remain untrusted local overrides (no trust elevation, no new capabilities); this does not address managed-artifact activation timing, which is a separate concern from the classification reported here.

## User Impact

After rebuilding and activating a private archive plugin whose installed runtime matches the artifact, `openclaw plugins inspect --json` now reports `trust.reason=origin-path` (a known local override) instead of `trust.reason=provenance-invalid`, matching the runtime's own classification. The plugin stays untrusted and capability-gated exactly as before — only the misleading "invalid provenance" label is corrected.


## Evidence

Observed result (shipped CLI, current head 09e40c88136): a synthetic local archive install classifies as `origin-path`; the identical install against the `origin/main` classifier reports `provenance-invalid`. Official trust is unchanged in both arms.

Fixture: minimal synthetic plugin (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `dist/index.cjs`), tar-packed `.tgz`, installed into isolated state (0700). Commands below run the shipped CLI via `node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts` (source entry). Both arms ran the same commands on the same fixture; the only runtime difference is `installed-plugin-record-match.ts` (head vs `origin/main`). Private paths redacted to `<state>`.

```text
$ openclaw plugins install ./archive-proof-synthetic.tgz --force --accept-capabilities
Installed plugin: archive-proof-synthetic        # exit 0 in both arms; record source=archive

$ openclaw plugins inspect archive-proof-synthetic
BASE (origin/main classifier):
Trust: reason=provenance-invalid; registryPath="<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite"; origin="global"; installSource="archive"; installSpec=null
WARN: OpenClaw can't verify where this plugin came from. […] reason=provenance-invalid […]
HEAD (09e40c88136):
Trust: reason=origin-path; registryPath="<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite"; origin="global"; installSource="archive"; installSpec=null
(no provenance warning)

$ openclaw plugins inspect archive-proof-synthetic --json
BASE: "trust":{"reason":"provenance-invalid","registryPath":"<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite","origin":"global","installSource":"archive"}
HEAD: "trust":{"reason":"origin-path","registryPath":"<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite","origin":"global","installSource":"archive"}
```

| arm | trust.reason | trustedOfficialInstall | provenance WARN |
|---|---|---|---|
| origin/main classifier | provenance-invalid | absent (untrusted) | present |
| head 09e40c88136 | origin-path | absent (untrusted) | absent |

`trustedOfficialInstall` is only emitted for `trusted-official` records; its absence in both `--json` captures shows the archive stays untrusted — no official-trust elevation.

Regression (folded `it.each` row, in-process): post-fix `15 passed (15)`; pre-fix the archive row fails with `expected { reason: 'provenance-invalid', … } to match object { reason: 'origin-path', … }` (1 failed | 14 passed). Adjacent provenance suites: 39 passed.

Scope: this exercises the shipped local-archive producer (`plugins install <file.tgz>`); managed artifact activation records the same `source:"archive"` shape and shares this classifier.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve exception causes in failure history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A failed update can save only the trailing frames of a long exception stack, losing its cause. Bare Bun-style stack headers can omit the message even before truncation.

## User Impact

New failure records retain the exception cause and first frames within the existing redacted, 1,024-character budget. Command failures keep their stderr-tail policy, preserving errors printed after warning output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing redacted exception formatter at the preparation catch, then bound its leading text before the shared failure recorder selects its tail. Remove the raw-stack/fallback branch; add no helper, schema, config, or dependency.

Production +3/-2 (net +1); tests +35/-23 (net +12). Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203502.

## Evidence

- Current signed head `35d22cd03f3a62aa703e788bb2ba624af6911d02`. The rebase preserves the real-Git cleanup regression from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207040; range-diff shows only contextual movement of this two-file diagnostic patch.
- [Current merge CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097065550/job/140831261686): **55/55 tests passed on Bun** — 9 preparation-failure and 46 preparation cases. Normal/bare-header cases passed in 1,252/1,320 ms; the preserved rejected-Git cleanup passed in 1,678 ms. Persisted cause/first frame, redaction, bounds, one terminal failure, and no trial are asserted.
- That run actually checks out merge `30fdad81e78d5e1b8a0f5309049f257464f8edfa`, whose ordered parents are `168b469579da50d7852f037cf9d15607a95234d5` and this head. Its tree was independently reconstructed; only the two updater files differ from its base. All hosted gates passed, including Docker and security: 34 jobs succeeded, 28 were skipped, and none failed or remained pending.
- Independent P0-P3 source review found no findings on the original patch; the rebased delta received direct review. The fresh exact-head ClawSweeper report also has no findings. Matching oxfmt 0.74.0, whitespace, scope, and privacy checks pass.
- No baseline RED, full-package build, installed-upgrade, or live Gateway execution is claimed. This diagnostic change adds no packaging or dynamic-module boundary.

### Review follow-through

ClawSweeper suggested optional baseline RED and public-CLI/Gateway saved-status capture. The current-head Testbox allocation remained queued and was stopped without executing a command. Local dependencies are unqualified, so those optional captures are skipped; current-merge tests above exercise the preparation and persisted-history owners. The earlier auto-merge request was natively retired before the branch rewrite. No replacement merge request is active.

prs.title: fix: show why a model tool call was rejected as malformed
prs.body:
Related: #202672

## What Problem This Solves

When a model streams a tool call whose arguments never arrive as a complete JSON object, the turn fails with a malformed-tool-call error. The `provider-error` log line for that failure showed only the error code and the provider's message id, so an operator reading the logs could not tell a truncated argument buffer from a buffer that was never JSON-encoded at all, and could not see how large the rejected buffer was or whether the string-literal repair had been attempted.

## User Impact

User impact: the `provider-error` log line for a rejected tool call now carries `argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, and `repairAttempted`, so operators can distinguish truncation from a never-encoded buffer without opening provider payloads. No argument text is added to the log, so the content-exclusion contract is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` already builds content-free diagnostics (`argumentChars`, `argumentHash`, `repairAttempted`) and attaches them to the error `cause` plus a mirrored `errorBody`. `assignTransportErrorDetails()` built the `provider-error` metadata from only `causeCode` / `code` / `type` / `requestId` / `responseId` / `status`, so those diagnostics never reached the log.

This change propagates the bounded diagnostics into that metadata and adds the transport-to-log regression coverage requested in #202672. The propagation is deliberately narrow:

- Only the fields produced by `parseTerminalToolCallArguments()` are surfaced, and only for the `malformed_tool_call_arguments` code.
- The argument hash is accepted only when it matches the base-36 digest shape OpenClaw produces, so a provider-crafted `cause` cannot smuggle argument text into the log.
- `errorBody` is **not** logged. For other error classes it can carry provider prose (prompts, tool results), so it must stay out of the log.
- Rejection behaviour, JSON repair, streaming, recovery, and failover are unchanged.

## Evidence

### After-fix behaviour, captured from a real Gateway run

A Gateway was started against a loopback Anthropic-Messages stub that emits a `tool_use` block whose accumulated `input_json_delta` is truncated mid-object (no closing brace), then `content_block_stop` / `message_delta(stop_reason=tool_use)` / `message_stop`. Loopback only, no credentials, no network egress. One tool-calling turn over the HTTP Responses entrypoint.

The `provider-error` line, verbatim from the Gateway log:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed sessionKey="agent:main:openresponses:pr-202717-proof" runId="resp_0b92ae46-b68b-47c5-a17a-115f225ac9f4" requestId="resp_0b92ae46-b68b-47c5-a17a-115f225ac9f4:model:1" requestNumber=1 provider=stubproof model=stub-anthropic-model name=Error code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_stub_20261127 argumentChars=61 argumentHash=d5087tksakfw repairAttempted=true
```

The rejected buffer for that run was 61 characters, and `argumentChars=61` reports it exactly. `argumentHash=d5087tksakfw` is the digest of that same buffer. The rejected argument text appeared in **neither** the Gateway log **nor** the HTTP response body.

### The same test fails on unmodified `main` (red on base)

With `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts` reverted to `origin/main` and no other change, the new test fails - the diagnostics are present in the error body but absent from the logged metadata:

```
❯ packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts:1951:24
    1951|         expect(metadata).toMatchObject({
       |                         ^
-   "argumentHash": "1ueauym1lk9dnc",
    "causeCode": "malformed_tool_call_arguments",
    "code": "malformed_tool_call_arguments",
-   "repairAttempted": true,
  }

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 57 skipped (58)
```

So the test is a genuine regression test for this change, not a restatement of existing behaviour.

### Automated coverage

New coverage:

- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` - *"surfaces bounded tool-call diagnostics in the provider-error log"* drives a truncated `tool_use` argument buffer through the loopback HTTP transport and asserts the `provider-error` metadata carries `argumentChars` / `argumentHash` / `repairAttempted` matching the terminal error body, that no `toolcall_end` is emitted, and that the rejected argument text appears in neither the log nor the error body.
- `packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` - *"does not log tool-call diagnostics that are not an OpenClaw digest"* proves a hash that is not an OpenClaw base-36 digest is dropped rather than logged, so a provider-crafted `cause` cannot inject argument text into the log metadata.

Existing coverage kept green: the truncated-sibling case in `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` still requires truncated sibling arguments to stay rejected, the bounded diagnostics to survive in `errorBody`, private argument text to stay excluded, and no sibling `toolcall_end` to be emitted.

Focused tests:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
```

Whole package suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/ai/
 Test Files  167 passed (167)
      Tests  2454 passed | 3 skipped (2457)
```

Format and lint on the touched files:

```
$ node scripts/run-format.mts --check packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.test.ts \
    packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <same files>
✓ No problems in 3 files
```

<details>
<summary>Log line before and after</summary>

Before, the failure was indistinguishable from any other malformed tool call:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_...
```

After, the metadata additionally carries the bounded diagnostics (no argument text, only a length, a digest, and a flag). Values below are the ones captured from the Gateway run in the Evidence section:

```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... code=malformed_tool_call_arguments causeCode=malformed_tool_call_arguments responseId=msg_stub_20261127 argumentChars=61 argumentHash=d5087tksakfw repairAttempted=true
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover-lock can clear the Linux legacy config lock that blocks Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
Related: #201472

Linux companion to #201912. #201912 lets macOS (like Windows since #182031) admit a stopped namespace-less legacy owner by itself and keeps Linux refusing on purpose, because a Gateway in another PID namespace can share the lock directory; its refusal on Linux tells the operator to remove the system-temp file by hand, because `recover-lock` does not inspect it. This PR makes `recover-lock` inspect that file on Linux, so the documented explicit recovery covers it. Rebased onto #201912 and narrowed to Linux; macOS and Windows behavior is #201912's and unchanged here.

This fixes the recovery route on a build that contains it. The issue's other ask, a route for an install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 (whose CLI has no `recover-lock`), stays open under the same issue for the maintainers.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Linux, `openclaw doctor --fix` (and so every update, which runs Doctor) refuses maintenance when an older Gateway left a per-config lock file in a separate system temporary directory (`$TMPDIR/openclaw-<uid>/gateway.<hash>.lock`) with no process namespace, even though its process exited long ago; and `openclaw gateway recover-lock`, the documented way to clear a lock whose owner cannot be verified, never inspected that directory, so it reported "No Gateway lock or owner lease is present." Since #201912 the refusal for that file says to remove it by hand after checking the process has stopped on the host and in every container sharing the directory.

Scope: this fixes recovery wherever the fixed `recover-lock` command is available. An install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 has no `recover-lock` command, so how such an install obtains the fixed command (for example the updater running recovery from the candidate) remains unresolved and is left to the maintainers under #201472. When the service's temporary directory sits inside the state directory, the historical lock path is the same as the state-local config lock that `recover-lock` already inspects, and #201912's refusal already names `recover-lock` there; this change does nothing for that layout.

## User Impact

User impact: on Linux, an operator blocked by "Legacy Gateway lock ... still has a live or unverified owner" can run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` (as the Gateway service account, with the same `TMPDIR`), see that record listed, and clear it with the printed `--confirm <fingerprint>` command; Doctor and the update then complete. For that file, the Doctor refusal now names that command before #201912's manual delete, which stays as the fallback when `recover-lock` skips the file or is not installed; the instruction to check the host and every container sharing the directory first applies to both. Nothing is reclaimed automatically: a record without a namespace is still "unverified", and the confirmation is the operator's statement that its process has stopped. A verified live holder is still refused.

If the file cannot be inspected safely (not owned by the operator, writable by others, under a parent directory another user could replace, not a regular single-link file, or larger than 16 KiB), `recover-lock` names the file and the reason instead of reporting an empty inspection, a confirmation that had to skip it says so, and a confirmation with nothing eligible says that nothing was recovered.

macOS and Windows are unchanged: they admit a stopped namespace-less record once its heartbeat is older than 90 seconds (#182031, #201912), so `recover-lock` does not inspect a separate system-temp copy there and #201912's Doctor message stays as it is. Other platforms (FreeBSD and the like) are also left out; the inspection runs only on Linux.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's maintenance admission checks the historical per-config lock under the system temporary directory, but lock recovery only observed the three state-local lock paths. Inspection now also observes that file on Linux, deduplicated when it is the same file as the state-local config lock; confirmation takes it first, so a failure to take custody of it leaves the state-local records untouched; and the Linux Doctor refusal for that file names the recovery command, as it already does for the state-local file. The ownership policy from #178076 is unchanged.

Because the file lives in a shared directory and confirmation deletes it, the checks are sized against what a wrong deletion could reach: the file and its directory must be owned by the current user and writable by nobody else (so the bytes shown are the operator's own record); the configured path's own components are checked first, and a symbolic link in it that another user controls is refused (it could redirect the lookup to a directory that passes every later check); the path is then resolved to its canonical form and every parent must be owned by the current user or root, and a parent writable by others must carry the sticky bit (otherwise another local user could rename a parent and redirect the confirmed path between inspection and confirmation); a symbolic link or directory that another account substitutes in the configured path is owned by that account, and the checks run again at confirmation, so it fails the owner test or the parent walk; that account cannot create components owned by the current user or root; the file is opened without following symlinks and without blocking (a FIFO cannot hang the command), must be a regular single-link file, and is read only up to the existing 16 KiB sidecar bound. Confirmation then re-verifies identity (device, inode, timestamps, size) and bytes before removal, as for the other lock files. POSIX ACL entries are not inspected; this is a known limit.

## Evidence

Full-product check through the shipped CLI (`openclaw.mjs` of a built tree, Linux container, root): the reporter's lock record (no `processNamespace`, exited PID, mtime 30 Sep 2026) at `/tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.<hash>.lock`, then `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `gateway recover-lock`, `--json`, `--confirm`, Doctor again.

### Full-product repro on main

main `d9e2d8a89dd` (includes #201912), 19 Nov 2026 (the next main, `d5f3e4d7b75`, changes no file this PR touches):

```text
== 1 doctor --fix --non-interactive (with the legacy lock)
doctor rc=1
  Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 28). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, remove that file as the Gateway service account. Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell.
== 2 gateway recover-lock (inspect)
recover-lock rc=0
  No Gateway lock or owner lease is present.
== 3 gateway recover-lock --json
  { "present": false, "holders": [], ... }
== 4 skipped: inspection listed no record to confirm
RESULT lock_after_recovery=present
== 5 doctor --fix --non-interactive again
doctor rc=1
```

### Live run with this PR

Same container recipe, same record, the patched build of this head on that main:

```text
== 1 doctor --fix --non-interactive (with the legacy lock)
doctor rc=1
  Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 28). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` as the Gateway service account with the same TMPDIR to inspect and explicitly recover it, or remove that file as the Gateway service account. Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell.
== 2 gateway recover-lock (inspect)
recover-lock rc=0
  /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock: holder 28 at unknown host, last renewed 4327232 s ago. Stop the holder before retrying; if it has already stopped, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` to inspect and explicitly recover the unchanged owner.
  Stop the recorded holder through its service manager or container first. If you have confirmed it stopped, recover exactly these unchanged records with:
  openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
== 3 gateway recover-lock --json
  { "present": true, "holders": ["/tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock: holder 28 ..."], ... }
RESULT recover_lists_legacy=yes
== 4 gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
rc=0
  Gateway lock recovery completed. Start the Gateway again.
RESULT lock_after_recovery=removed
== 5 doctor --fix --non-interactive again
doctor rc=0
```

Doctor still refuses before recovery (the owner stays unverifiable); the difference is that recovery now reaches the file and Doctor passes once it is gone.

Focused tests (`src/infra/gateway-lock-legacy.test.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-lock-recovery.test.ts`): the new cases fail on unpatched main (the "red" lane copies them there) and pass with the change under the node runtime. The direct consumers of the two changed modules (`gateway-lock-recovery.postgres.test.ts`, `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`, `doctor-maintenance.interruption.process.test.ts`, `update-command-service-drain.test.ts`) pass. Typecheck, lint and format run through CI's own `check:changed` on the bench.

### Upgrade run from a real 2026.11.4 install (Linux container, user `node`)

`npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.4`, state initialized by `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, a config marker set (`gateway.port 18799`), then the lock record above planted at `/tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock` (exited PID 273). The 2026.11.4 Doctor admits it (control). The candidate is this branch packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`.

Phase A, the real updater with the lock present (`openclaw update --yes --tag <candidate.tgz>`): the candidate's Doctor refuses with the new message and the update rolls back to 2026.11.4, as on 2026.11.5 today; the install is back on 2026.11.4 and the config marker is intact. This is the unresolved part: a rolled-back install cannot run recovery by itself.

```text
✗ openclaw doctor (2.6s)
  Failing check doctor (doctor-failed): Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock [redacted-path]
  ... Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 273). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` as the Gateway service account ... or remove that file as the Gateway service account.
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: doctor-failed.
RESULT A version_after=OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a) lock_present=yes
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

Phase B, the manual route (installing the candidate by hand, not through the updater): `npm i -g <candidate.tgz>`, then Doctor refuses with the hint, `recover-lock` lists the record and prints the confirm command, the confirm removes the file, Doctor exits 0, and the config marker and state database are intact.

```text
installed: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (ead12fa)
doctor (lock present) rc=1
recover-lock: /tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock: holder 273 at unknown host, last renewed 4329492 s ago. ...
  openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
confirm rc=0  Gateway lock recovery completed. Start the Gateway again.
RESULT B lock_after=removed
RESULT B doctor_after rc=0
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

Phase C, the real updater from the untouched 2026.11.4 state (restored from a copy taken before the lock was planted) once the file is gone: the update completes and the config marker is intact.

```text
installed: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a)
state restored to the 2026.11.4 copy; lock present: no
update rc=0
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.5 (from 2026.11.4); 23 warnings need attention.
RESULT C version_after=OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (ead12fa)
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

The candidate labeled `ead12fa` is the bench's own commit of this head's patch on top of main `d5f3e4d7b75` (the same content as this head, which passed the CI-style `check:changed` run there; the full-product runs above use the same tree). A first attempt at phase C reinstalled 2026.11.4 on a state that phase B's candidate Doctor had already migrated, which 2026.11.4 refuses to open ("uses newer schema version 40; this build supports 22"); that was the test's mistake, so phase C restores the pre-B state.

Proof artifice: the lock record was written by a script (the reporter's own recipe) with an already-exited child process as the recorded owner; no Gateway was running in any run; the candidate was packed from this branch rather than published to npm.

Proof gap: the bun test runtime is not installed in the bench containers, so the bun run of the focused tests is left to PR CI. This improves the guidance shown by the new build only; Doctor's message in an install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 is unchanged.

Data model: no stored data or record format changes. The lock record is read as before; the only new stored effect is the removal of the inspected file after confirmation, which the recovery test suite covers for both the state-local and the historical layout.

Test lines are net +54 against `main`: the recovery layouts (system temp dir, state tmp dir, non-regular path, world-writable parent) are four rows of one new `it.each` in the existing recovery suite, and #201912's platform table additionally expects the recovery command on Linux; no existing test covers the historical path in recovery.

prs.title: fix: auto-disable automations whose account was signed out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the account an automation was recorded with is removed or signed out, every run of that automation fails. A recurring automation then fails again on every scheduled run, indefinitely: the refusal is classified as `unknown`, and nothing ends the loop. On one production deployment, 11 automations on one signed-out account failed 270 times in 2.8 days. 170 of those were `All models failed (4)`, because every configured fallback was on the same signed-out account. Six of them were still looping when measured.

## User Impact

An automation whose recorded account was removed, signed out or replaced is now auto-disabled after the first run that nothing else could finish. It uses the existing auto-disable mechanism with a new reason, `account-unavailable`. The owner gets one notice that names the repair:
1. sign in again (`openclaw models auth login --provider <provider> --force`);
2. record the account (`openclaw automations edit <id> --model <provider/model>@<profileId>`, or a plain model to use a configured key);
3. run `openclaw automations enable <id>`.

`openclaw automations list` shows the job as `disabled (account)`, and `openclaw doctor` lists the recorded reason. The notice does not name the account; run history keeps the full refusal.

The job keeps running when:
- a fallback on another provider finishes the run (the run stays `ok`);
- a fallback failed for a reason that can pass, for example a 429 (normal retry schedule);
- the account store was only briefly interrupted, for example by a state database lifecycle change.

A forced manual run that preserves a scheduled one-shot occurrence leaves that occurrence alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix is at the owners that already exist:
- **Producer.** `acquireCronInferenceAuthorization` gives its refusal a code when the recorded account is gone or was replaced. The original `AuthProfileAuthorizationError` stays as `cause`. The code is added only when the authorization owner reports that the profile itself is absent, retired or expired: a new `accountGone` fact on `AuthProfileAuthorizationError`. Other retirements keep their old behavior.
- **Run inference.** It marks the refusal when a fallback candidate on another provider runs. From then on the recorded account was not the run's only way to execute.
- **Classifier.** `resolveCronConfigurationRefusal` classifies the refusal on both run paths (isolated and session target), and only when nothing else could run the job: either a surfaced refusal that no other provider bypassed, or a fallback summary whose every attempt was that refusal. It never matches error text.
- **Outcome.** `applyJobResult` calls the existing `autoDisableCronJob` once, with reason `account-unavailable` and the existing `auto-disabled` notification in place of the failure alert. Aborted and restart-interrupted runs never disable. The permanent-disable branch for plugin and operator-source jobs leaves this refusal to the auto-disable path.
- **Readers.** The new value is added to the Gateway protocol's `autoDisabled.reason` union, the Doctor reader, the CLI status label, and the Control UI sidebar's shape check, so such a job stays in the attention list.

**Downgrade check** (stable `v2026.11.10`, isolated state, host variables stripped). A store holding one job with `autoDisabled.reason: "account-unavailable"` and one ordinary job loads exactly like a control store holding `schedule-errors`:
- the list shows all jobs, and the new job reads as `disabled (1x)` (control: `disabled (schedule)`);
- `show` works for both jobs;
- `enable` clears the reason and re-enables the job;
- no load errors.

Stable therefore tolerates the new value, and no tolerant reader has to ship first.

Accepted edges:
- A job whose fallbacks keep failing for their own reasons keeps retrying on its normal schedule. Those failures belong to their own classes, for example long provider rate-limit resets.
- An account retired in the middle of a run disables at the next run.
- Fallback chains that return an "exhausted" result instead of throwing are not classified (the production failures threw).
- The `auto-disabled` notice is delivered as a session event turn, like the existing auto-disable notices. If the owner session's own model cannot run (for example on the same signed-out account), that turn fails, and the notice does not reach the transcript. The job is still disabled with its recorded reason, which the automation list and `openclaw doctor` show.

## Evidence

- **Red on main, green here:** `src/cron/session-run.cross-provider-fallback.integration.test.ts` runs a recurring session-target automation whose recorded account was removed or replaced and which has no other model to run on. On the merge base, the job stays enabled after the failed run. On this branch, it is auto-disabled with `account-unavailable` and exactly one notice, and a second settled result sends nothing. The same file keeps the fallback-success cases `ok`, and keeps a job running when its fallback failed with a 429.
- **Isolated path:** `isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts` asserts the permanent classification for a removed account on both the embedded and CLI routes.
- **No over-trigger:** `timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts` keeps a job running when only the authorization owner changed.
- **Real Gateway** (built dist, isolated state, no real credentials): an automation recorded on an API-key account; the account was then logged out, and two runs were forced.
  - Merge base: the job stays enabled with 2 consecutive errors and a next run scheduled, and the person gets no notice.
  - This branch: after the first failure the job is disabled, with no next run and `autoDisabled.reason = account-unavailable`. One notice lands in the agent's conversation as a system notice.
- **Behavior suite** (real gpt-5.4-mini, 11 cases): 11/11 gating on this branch vs 10/11 on the merge base. The base miss is the subagent-spawn case, unrelated to cron.

prs.title: docs: guide small-host setup from saved keys to verified chat
prs.body:
Related: #200110, #200111, #200112

## What Problem This Solves

Someone setting up one Linux agent has to connect installation, a saved API key or existing local model, service startup, and their first working chat across several reference pages. The existing secure credential-import transport does not by itself make that journey discoverable for a beginner.

## User Impact

User impact: a guide linked from Getting Started and onboarding connects saved credentials or an existing Ollama server to first chat, with reusable non-secret configuration and precise resume actions. It now also supplies an assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios aligned with the native macOS and model-management implementations below. Loading the dashboard is no longer described as proof that everything works.

This is a documentation-first contribution, not a new credential importer, profile format, installer, automatic receipt, or completed first-run UI. It should not close the broader workflow requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guides compose the existing onboarding, credential, config, service, Template, and plugin owners. They distinguish configured from exercised capabilities, explain that config dry-run is validation rather than a before/after diff, preserve separate plugin consent, and avoid replaying completed setup mutations.

Maintainer follow-up requested for #200110: its supported stdin/SecretRef transport is acknowledged. Please keep the basic-user access gap owned under #200112: a person with one API key in 1Password or a similar manager should be able to discover the supported connection path, authorize only the intended field, and reach verified chat without source inspection or assembling several internal workflows. A CLI pipeline is an optional route for people already using that CLI, not proof that password-manager selection is integrated into onboarding. No duplicate credential store/flag or reopening solely for the existing transport is requested.

## Coordination with implementation work

This PR supplies a shared assistant-facing workflow and acceptance scenarios for the work below; it is not a replacement implementation. States below were checked on 2026-11-18; the linked PR is authoritative. Cross-references are coordination context, not a claim that the authors have agreed to a dependency or handoff.

| Implementation work | Relationship to this documentation |
| --- | --- |
| #181011 (open) and #182075 (open, stacked on #181011) — custom endpoint editor and unified provider connection | Reuse Settings → Models, configuration/auth/discovery owners, and their preserved local-admin endpoint-definition boundary. Adding an endpoint or credential does not select or verify the primary model. Broader tracking: #177163 and #193323. |
| #200272 (experimental draft) — native macOS account/local-model onboarding | Apply the same detected → chosen → verified distinctions and first-chat acceptance, without treating the proposed picker as shipped or requiring a parallel CLI setup. |
| #200425 (merged) — native Gateway terminal-command installation | Preserve app/profile ownership and existing terminal defaults. For an app-managed Mac, use the bundled runtime and native setup; do not add a global runtime just because a CLI is not found. |
| #194841 (draft) — macOS existing-Gateway choice | The remote/attach acceptance scenario must not create or retain unwanted local hosting while approval is pending. Its native proof remains separate. |
| #200840 (draft) — compatible installed-browser dashboard handoff | Treat dashboard admission and an actual chat reply as separate evidence. The PR reports macOS dashboard validation but only partial onboarding proof. |
| #200329 (open) — Chat routes an unconfigured user to model setup | Preserve the unsent draft and use the existing setup entry point rather than making the user research model configuration. |
| #200858 and #200859 (open) — onboarding completion and diagnostic output | Keep phase completion and actionable diagnostics accurate; neither message formatting nor a success outro establishes working inference. |
| #200836 (open) — native macOS DMG captions; #200910 (open) — app-owned update guidance | Keep installation/maintenance instructions aligned with the native surfaces and installation owner. Installer presentation and update guidance are not first-chat acceptance. |

### Next implementation slice: let the setup agent use the framework

The documentation now defines **inspect → choose → propose through the existing owner → verify → resume → hand off** and four acceptance scenarios: a saved password-manager key, existing Ollama, native/remote macOS hosting, and interrupted setup. The assistant should do the routine inspection and present one next action, not assign these pages to the user.

**Current integration gap, verified in source:** the initial OpenClaw system agent receives docs/source locations, but its primary loop is restricted to the typed `openclaw` tool and its fallback planner explicitly has no file/network lookup. A pointer is not loaded documentation. Ordinary agents have separate docs-first guidance and may read/search only through their available tools. This PR does not claim to wire automatic documentation consumption into the initial bot.

Implementation should start at the existing `src/system-agent/assistant-prompts.ts` prompt builder and `src/system-agent/overview.ts` reference-discovery boundary, with the tool restriction in `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts`. Reuse the release-matched canonical guide through bounded, deterministic setup context; do not create another installer, config owner, unrestricted reader, public receipt format, or growing copy of the whole docs tree in the prompt. A runtime implementation must preserve the normal/native app action owners, prompt-prefix stability, capability limits, consent, and source-of-truth rules.

Keep #200112 open for that integration and real entry-point acceptance. Validate through the actual initial setup agent and native/CLI entry points: no human documentation hunt, no raw key in model context, no duplicate installation on resume, and an observed chat result or one precise blocker. A documentation-only check or a prompt-string test cannot establish that outcome.

## Evidence

### Bot-consumption and adversarial review

Three sequential rounds used fresh `openai/gpt-6-astra` instruction-following consumers and independent `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` adversarial reviewers: six child runs and 16 synthetic scenario responses across successive drafts. No unsafe next action was observed in those responses; this is not a 16-case live regression suite or a separate verified “Astra-scale” mode.

The review-driven changes stop failed/partial secret reads before import, preserve the actual agent ID, scope the shortcut to OpenAI keys, separate terminal selection from native automatic trials, require an actual intended-agent Gateway chat result, avoid creating an agent or broadening permissions for an optional tool check, reconcile failed rescue work before retry, and gate service start on successful install. A contradictory incidental planning-tool claim in the existing reference was removed rather than treated as a new capability.

### Executed Bash failure/control tests

Actual documented snippets ran in real Bash with synthetic `op`/`openclaw` functions only. **All six final fixtures passed:** failed read; partial read then failure; importer failure; successful import under inherited tracing/autoexport; failed service installation; successful installation control. The captured key was not traced or exported to the importer environment. No real credential, password manager, or OpenClaw service operation ran.

The original snippets wrongly continued to onboarding after read/import failure and started a service after installation failure. The intermediate pipefail-only revision still started the importer after a partial failed read. The final snippet starts neither importer nor onboarding on a failed read, and starts no service after a failed installation. Success controls still proceed.

### Documentation checks and limits

- MDX syntax and targeted formatting pass for all seven changed/new pages; six Bash-fence syntax/continuation checks and `git diff --check` pass.
- The full configuration-example audit validates 1,408 examples with no findings; both new JSON5 examples are included. Internal route checks report no broken routes.
- The anchor audit still reports three unrelated findings in untouched pages/targets: ACP setup duplicate heading, release 2026.10.1 OpenAI runtime anchor, and Code Mode troubleshooting loop-detection anchor. No changed-link anchor finding was reported. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their separate source checkout.
- Original source/draft review and this follow-up simplification keep the change documentation-only: no production code, state, new public command, receipt format, or competing config/installer owner.
- **Not verified:** a clean-host install, real password-manager import, actual initial setup-agent documentation loading, real model/provider/tool execution, native first-chat handoff, logout/reboot persistence, or outage failover. The synthetic reviews and shell stubs do not replace those implementation acceptance checks.

Requested by Richard O’Shaughnessy through the linked issues and discussion.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d1f8b252-c950-4999-b9ef-66e08f64c9a6)

## Worked on by

- @oshaughnessy-junior

prs.title: feat(ios): a sidebar with pins, and Sessions grouped by what needs you
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's navigation and chat screens in line with the Control UI. On iOS today, the sidebar opens on a brand header and a Pages list with an edit button, sessions sit in group sections with carets, and the Overview page and the Sessions page show dashboard tiles and long status lists. Pins live on the Gateway, so pinning a session on the phone changes it for every client. None of this matches how the Control UI presents the same sessions.

## User Impact

With this pull request alone:

- The sidebar opens on the current agent (with a picker when there are several), then Main chat, the pinned pages, and a More row that opens the pages editor. Pinned sessions and recent sessions follow in two folding sections, and a View all link opens Sessions. The footer keeps Settings, the connection button and a New Chat button.
- Each session row shows its title and, when something needs attention, one state line: a spinner while it works, a red dot when it is unread or failed, and "Subagents working" when its subagents run. Long-pressing a row offers Fork chat and the other session actions.
- Pins are personal to this device. Pinning a session in the sidebar or in a chat's More menu no longer changes it for other clients, and saved pins survive an app update.
- The Sessions page groups rows by what needs you: Needs you, Working, Pinned, user groups, then Recent. A filter menu switches between active, snoozed, archived and automation sessions, and a New Chat button sits at the bottom. A partial roster shows "Couldn’t load some sessions. Try again." with a Try again button.
- Settings opens as a sheet over the current screen, and the Overview page is gone.
- The connection button in the sidebar shows a green dot when online, a spinner while connecting, a slashed antenna when offline, and a warning badge on an error, and VoiceOver reads the same states.

Still old until later pull requests in the series:

- Search: the sidebar keeps its existing inline session filter, and the Sessions page has no search button yet. Full-screen search, pull-to-search in the sidebar and the Sessions search button come with the search pull request.
- The approval answer card remains in #206655. The screenshots and tests here show the existing pending-approval state with a local fixture.
- The connection button keeps its current glass circle; the connection menu with saved names and its new layout come with the connection strip pull request.
- Settings has no Chat, Skills or Plugins rows yet; those come with the Settings pages pull request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar and Sessions share one roster, so they move together. Grouping Sessions by what needs a person's attention, and keeping one state line per row, makes the list readable at a glance and matches the Control UI. Personal pins keep each device's sidebar under that person's control instead of rewriting a shared Gateway field.

## Evidence

iPhone 17 Pro, light appearance, English, with the same screenshot fixture arguments on both sides. Before: `main` iOS inputs from `58e358887b85` (unchanged on the projected merge base). After: `243d85881a65`. The earlier app does not recognize the session-state fixture, so it shows its default demo row; the new app shows the fixture’s synthetic roster. Gray bars cover model labels and internal fixture names, not the controls or status text.

**Local proof on `243d85881a65`**

- The app, OpenClawKit, and test bundles compiled. The canonical native localization inventory verified without changes.
- 18 focused unit tests passed: local pins, session grouping, and drawer-gesture policy.
- 4 simulator UI tests passed: session state labels without a raw session key, the contextual approval indicator, opening and closing Settings from Sessions, and the native back swipe from Licenses to About without opening the sidebar.
- No live Gateway, real account, real device, or VoiceOver run. The approval test checks the accessibility value rather than running VoiceOver.

## Simulator comparisons

### Sessions

#### Clean comparison

| Before | After |

| ![Sessions before: recent card with status tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fe926af-7bb3-4eb8-816b-db55d5df76e4) | ![Sessions after: grouped rows with status text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b528035-d680-4ab5-bc4e-ac9f3a8bd390) |

#### Annotated comparison

### Sidebar

#### Clean comparison

| ![Sidebar before: a separate Pages list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6d51444-366e-40d4-ae42-66b75b990a49) | ![Sidebar after: Main chat and pinned pages above sessions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36a5a030-d0e0-4c2d-8d86-86d4fa33d7fb) |

prs.title: fix: show context usage during Claude CLI turns
prs.body:
Related: #206974

## What Problem This Solves

A CLI-backed chat can show no context usage during its first turn. A delegated call can also replace the parent call’s last measured usage.

## User Impact

Claude CLI sessions now show measured parent-call usage while a turn is running. Other CLI dialects keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream parser separates parent-call context from child usage and whole-turn billing. The admitted session writer publishes the first measurement immediately and coalesces later measurements; pending writes cannot run after final settlement.

## Evidence

With diagnostics disabled, a real Linux Gateway and a controlled Claude CLI transport reproduced both failures through `sessions.list`: the first turn showed no count and the second kept its previous final count. With the fix, the row reported 19,302 → 28,517 and 19,402 → 28,617 during the two turns. A final parent update replaced each intermediate count; later child usage did not overwrite it. No live provider was used.

All 90 focused tests across six files passed, including partial and terminal-only usage, coalescing, delayed writes and final settlement. Seven regression guards passed against the prepared base. The aggregate local check is not green: installed dependency declarations differ from the refreshed lockfile, and core lint timed out. No exact-head CI result or ClawSweeper Platinum grade is claimed.

The author simplification pass removed redundant writer forwarding and an unused second pre-turn sample. All 20 affected Gateway and session-store tests passed after the pass, as did the line-cap check; independent static review found no material issue. Relative to the previous revision: production +12/−18, tests +1/−3. Relative to the merge base: production +177/−21, tests +274/−1, test registration +1/−0, docs +1/−1.

Contributor: DonnieFi

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

<!-- forone-current-submission:start -->
### Current integration and proof — 2026-11-14 UTC

Current head: `7fd85cd455b9ebe788e636e6d6c9c1c4d73f2f3a`; tree: `eddf10d8d4623636ca057db069c3a0bbc5788471`. This is a normal merge from prior head `98c42ea708ef2119ac495d362c4b4aabe93a6780` of immutable official main `d98f18ff7c3de4bf46706a71d25705cef346b3ab`, followed by a test-file split. Git reported a real conflict in `sessions-search-tool.ts`; this is not a freshness-only merge or a force push.

The resolution composes official main's slow-search measurement wrapper around the existing channel-aware implementation. Channel sidebar/sharedFacts candidate selection, admission/incarnation/scoped leases, and the final owner-backed synchronous disclosure filter remain. The redundant post-search pass and per-row list preparation removed in the earlier reviewed repair remain absent. Official timing/count diagnostics and their error propagation remain intact.

Integration pushed the existing search test file above its unchanged 1,000-line lint cap. The same three elapsed/failure diagnostic cases and pass-through logger mock now live in `sessions-search-tool.diagnostics.test.ts`; their former fixed fixture values are inline. No assertions, timeouts, caps, allocations, ignore rules or production seams were weakened.

Validation on Node24.19.0/macOS arm64 with the official pinned Bun and an isolated exact-lock install:

- The merged boundary scope passed **101/101** cases across search/list/access/scoped-access/history suites. After the test-only split, both search files passed **38/38**; the 63 unchanged sibling cases retain their earlier measured scope, rather than being counted as fresh runs.
- Production and agents-tools test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting, whitespace and the test-line ratchet against fixed main passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the full candidate diff against fixed main, then of the test split against the reviewed merge, completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. These were static patch reviews; they did not execute project tests or inspect every unchanged repository file. The later formatting change only wrapped one expression.
- **The local mock-factory guard still fails.** An actual fixed-main control and this candidate, using the identical lockfile/checker, both return exit1 with byte-identical diagnostics for untouched `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts` (output SHA256 `21c9dc574729a5769faed6e948c13851a8473a122d8d10c4d684f02ffef483c8`). This is bounded local-main attribution, not hosted CI proof. No baseline exception or unrelated worker repair was added.

Current-head [first native CI43603970421](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43603970421), attempt1, ended `action_required` with zero jobs and a public maintainer-approval banner. No native checkout or code/test outcome is established. It is bound through CheckSuite118064337468's workflowRun even though REST run listings omitted it. Prior head98's run43546612040 remains historical. No workflow approval or rerun was performed.

Earlier compiled public list/search proof remains bound to **a66/tree a49754e0**, not this head: normal `recordInboundSession` plus public `chat.inject` created seven synthetic sessions; list returned two legitimate rows and broad search two hits, excluding five foreign scopes with one search read. Source/dist were unchanged and all children joined, with external delivery/model calls zero. The old603 first CI43442275234 (92 terminal jobs, zero failures), published-upgrade, native-memory and Wiki proofs retain their original trees and scope. No new live Slack, employee deployment, complete updater or cross-OS acceptance is claimed here. Adoption, official distribution and employee acceptance remain separate.
### Current main integration — 2026-11-17 UTC

Normal merge of pinned official main `a958f1d25c1d77aff39bfcbf86d0d4c7bd8f539a`; exact head `26ca0f3a35387ffa9cbb2372c30fd0f6daeb1812`. The only conflict was canonical generated config metadata, regenerated by its owner; the authored channel-visibility implementation and tests are unchanged. Focused boundary proof passed 250 assertions across history, search, memory-core, direct Wiki and SDK suites; config docs and staged diff checks pass. Native fork CI and maintainer adoption remain separate.

<!-- forone-current-submission:end -->

Current author head: `b61e37141b7760e0933aedd671d9ee9f73a78b55`. The latest ordinary merge consumes official main `6f04e7abd6c645c3c030663e7fd369834998d8ac`, including the adopted native-touch timing repair #178645. prs.title: feat: let memory search index only supported media when requested
prs.body:
Closes #206587

Built with @TheAngryPit, who designed and wrote the per-model capability change.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/94e1be23-48bf-4e9b-8d25-011cfa7ffefc)
- [Fresh-install and release-upgrade verification on the earlier head](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b7a14971-9067-4b05-80fa-29a644197e5a)
- [Compatibility review with @daniel-lxs](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-205382-and-206615-review-fixes-s3e9b8445)
- [Strict-default implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1c07ecb5-3b46-4120-a47d-880a6f34d0c3)

## What Problem This Solves

An embedding model can support images but not audio. A provider-wide yes/no answer cannot express that difference. Some users want to index just the supported files; others need a rebuild to fail rather than silently drop configured media.

## User Impact

Existing media-enabled setups remain strict: if the model cannot embed every configured modality, status and rebuild reject the configuration. To use partial indexing, set `memory.search.multimodal.allowPartial: true`. Status lists skipped modalities. A forced rebuild removes unsupported entries from the index, not the original files. Configured media still requires `fallback: "none"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedding adapter can declare support per model. Providers using the existing boolean retain their behavior. The memory settings resolver uses the same capability information to reject a mismatch by default or filter unsupported media after explicit opt-in. No config migration is required.

## Evidence

[Detached CrabBox AWS CLI comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_52adcedf1e1ea0bbd9240f6b1c0e66a4), main `5aa4b8d4d291` against head `3e49e6db4204`, on the same populated SQLite index:

- With no opt-in and a text-only model, `memory status --json` and `memory index --force` both exited 1 on both revisions. All three index rows and their metadata were unchanged, with no embedding calls.
- With `allowPartial: true` on the head, status and forced rebuild exited 0. Status reported `image` and `audio` skipped. Only `MEMORY.md` remained indexed; the PNG and WAV remained on disk.
- 94 focused tests passed, including the image-only case. Core and extension typechecks, lint, format and the regenerated config baseline passed. The CLI proof used a loopback embedding fixture, not live Gemini. Earlier-version upgrades were not rerun on this head.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

prs.title: fix(logging): explain why an unsafe directory blocks file logs
prs.body:
Closes #207055. Related: #132672, #199589.

## What Problem This Solves

When a writable ancestor makes both default log directories unsafe, OpenClaw drops records before it opens the log file. The warning told operators to fix the file even when it was already a regular 0600 file.

## User Impact

The warning names the rejected directory and gives its owner the repair: `chmod go-w` for a private directory, or `chmod +t` for an intentionally shared temp directory. It displays an unsafe home directory as `$HOME`, with or without a trailing slash in the environment setting. OpenClaw still refuses the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the normal writer and the shutdown writer pass the resolver’s explanation to the existing redacted stderr warning. If the default and fallback directories are rejected for the same reason, the resolver reports it once. Actual append failures keep their original advice. The permission checks, fallback and retry behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

I ran `openclaw gateway run` on AWS CrabBox Linux as uid 1000 with a regular 0600 log file and a 0775 home directory.

- [Main `d3730fd`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_528222a2a7f3c6a21c7b77fc5fc4e646): the log stayed at 0 bytes and the warning blamed the file.
- [Previous PR head `996e806`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_32f33a2d599682c5a4deb2533958393b): both HOME spellings produced temp-root terminology. Adding a trailing slash also exposed the absolute path in both chmod commands.
- [Revised code](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a48976c628daf8c361a31cfcd36e519a): both spellings produced the same warning, with no absolute home path: `Directory $HOME is writable by group or others and has no sticky bit.` Both chmod commands named `"$HOME"`. Each refused run wrote 0 bytes; `chmod go-w` restored logging (100,974 bytes). The published head `be268362` and tested commit `6066f16d` have identical Git trees.

The trailing-slash regression failed against the previous resolver. All 57 focused tests passed on the revised code, along with formatting, scoped lint and the core typecheck. I did not run other operating systems or the full suite.

Reported and reproduced by @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-log-warning-names-wrong-cause-sd7fbcf42)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs
