prs.title: feat(message): let operators confine group-turn sends to the current conversation
prs.body:
Related: #190557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group turn's `message` send can reach the owner's DM or another chat when the operator wants group turns kept in their own conversation, because the existing `crossContext` switches confine every kind of turn or none.

## User Impact

User impact: existing configs behave exactly as on main; no default changes. An operator who sets `tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes: ["group", "channel"]`, globally or per agent, gets group and channel turns that can only send to their own conversation. Any other target, on the same provider or another one, fails with `message_cross_context_denied` before a transport call. DM turns keep their current permissions. Separately, under the existing `allowWithinProvider: false`, a Telegram forum-topic send or poll that names the chat id with the current topic's `threadId`, or inherits it, is no longer denied. Other actions from a topic turn, such as renaming a topic, still have to name the current topic, as on main. Two deliberate tightenings apply under `allowWithinProvider: false`, or when group turns are confined. A turn in a Telegram forum topic can no longer create a forum topic in that chat, even through its own topic target, which main allows; the new topic is a sibling conversation in the base chat, and a turn bound to the chat itself still can. Telegram topic creation and topic edits that name another chat through `chatId`, `chat_id` or `channel_id` are denied. In every mode, a target that disagrees with one of those fields is refused as conflicting input. A numeric `target`, `to` or `channelId` is now read as its string, so it follows the same rules as the string: with a target the target wins, and alone it is the destination the check judges. Before, a numeric `channelId` skipped the check and Telegram acted on it, and a numeric `to` or `target` was dropped for the current conversation. A number that is not a safe integer is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision (4b90fc67b80) flipped the shipped `allowWithinProvider` default to deny. That was the wrong shape. It reversed a deliberate default (#149875, #150157), it broke the required-delivery and context-isolation fixtures, and it changed bound broadcasts. My claim in the old body that broadcasts were exempt was wrong: child sends carry `toolContext` into the same check. Review also found a real matcher bug: the same-provider check ignored `threadId`, so a same-topic Telegram send could be denied.

This revision keeps the default and adds an opt-in inside the existing owner, `enforceCrossContextPolicy`:

- `confineChatTypes` keys on the conversation kind the host reports for the turn (`toolContext.currentChatType`). A listed kind may only target its own conversation; this overrides both `allowWithinProvider` and `allowAcrossProviders`. Unlisted kinds, and turns with no reported kind, keep those flags. A `POST /tools/invoke` call bound by the conversation headers reports the bound target's kind, so it is confined like a turn from that conversation. A per-agent list replaces the global one through the existing per-agent merge; `[]` lifts it.
- Broadcast child sends already go through this check, so a confined broadcast delivers the current conversation and reports a denial for every other target. There is no runner change.
- When same-provider sends are restricted, the check resolves the thread the send will actually use, with the same `resolveAndApplyOutboundThreadId` that delivery uses (on a copy of the params), and names the destination with the channel's own `resolveCurrentChannelId`. Policy and delivery now judge the same destination. Only `send` and `poll` are judged by that thread alone, because the runner delivers them into it. Other guarded actions only hand the thread to the plugin, so they are judged on their requested target as on main, and a thread they carry can only narrow that. `topic-create` must also name the current conversation through its parent chat, resolved with the channel's own conversation grammar (core's `resolveSessionConversation`, which asks `messaging.resolveSessionConversation`), because Telegram creates the topic in the base chat whatever topic or thread the request names. Telegram declares `chatId`, `chat_id` and `channel_id` as delivery-target aliases for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`, because its handler takes the chat from them ahead of the target. Normalization therefore canonicalizes them before the check, the same way the thread spellings are folded. Normalization also stringifies exact integer values of `target`, `to` and `channelId` before folding them: Telegram's chat reader accepts numbers, while the fold and the check read only strings.
  - When a Telegram target's encoded topic and an explicit `threadId` disagree, the check follows Telegram's delivery precedence: the explicit thread wins. Telegram's `resolveCurrentChannelId` now goes through `formatTelegramDeliveryTarget`, the helper Telegram already uses to name a delivered send (moved unchanged into `topic-conversation.ts`).
  - The shared param readers accept each key's snake_case form, and Telegram's handler reads `messageThreadId` or `message_thread_id` before `threadId` or `thread_id`. Action normalization now folds every one of those four spellings into one string `threadId` before any check, including a numeric `threadId`, which core's string reader would otherwise skip. Values that disagree are refused, and so is any value alongside an explicit `threadId: null`. On any channel, an action carrying only an alias, or a numeric `threadId`, gets that value as its string `threadId`.

What changed since `1cb5e029db3` (2026-11-10): `POST /tools/invoke` now reports the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, so `confineChatTypes` applies to header-bound direct calls as it does to a turn from that conversation (`9aadc2bbc5c`). The Bot API traces at `1cb5e029db3` showed the gap: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the topic-A headers, all nine direct calls were delivered, including a `sendMessage` to the owner DM and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on it. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` now sets `currentChatType` on the direct-invocation surface from the bound target, with the resolver outbound target resolution already uses, `inferChatTypeFromTarget` (now exported from `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`; for Telegram it asks the plugin's `parseTelegramTarget`). Calls without the headers, the RPC `tools.invoke` and the MCP loopback surface are unchanged. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` fails on `1cb5e029db3` (`promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting` for a sibling-topic send from a header-bound call) and passes on this head; `92aee940aa8` raises the test-line allocation by its 62 lines.

pr-simplify: compared with the first revision, the default flip and its three default-denial tests are gone. No new plugin API, no runner or broadcast changes. Every remaining test group fails on a named control (below). The remaining growth is one config field (4 schema paths), the denial reason text, thread-aware matching, the tests (493 net test lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/message-cross-context-confine-chat-types.txt`), and one qa-lab scenario. Against main `eee7a1bd526`, merged in at `fa529d45fb9`:

- production source +221 −58 (`outbound-policy.ts` +86 −11; `tool-resolution.ts` +15 −24 and `targets.ts` +2 −1 for the direct-invocation kind, where `tool-resolution.ts` also moves 23 lines of main's code (the configured-policy closure and its three imports) into the new 28-line `tool-resolution-policy.ts` to stay under the line cap; Telegram `topic-conversation.ts`, `channel.ts` and `action-runtime.ts` +35 −22 for the moved delivery-target helper and `channel-actions.ts` +11 for the topic chat aliases; `message-action-normalization.ts` +33; +11 across schema, help and labels)
- tests +493 (`tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` +62)
- qa-lab scenario +172
- docs +18, plus the regenerated config baseline counts and hashes

## Evidence

**Merged with main** (head `443035eb689`, main `eee7a1bd526`, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`). The branch was 2,253 commits behind. `fa529d45fb9` merges main; the only conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (core paths 2,671 -> 2,675 for the 4 `confineChatTypes` paths). `pnpm config:docs:check` passes.

Main brought `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` to exactly the 700-line cap, and this PR's direct-invocation chat type adds 3 lines (`check:line-cap-ratchet`: 700 -> 703; oxlint `max-lines` at 703). `443035eb689` moves `resolveConfiguredToolPolicies`, a closure over five values and the only user of three imports, into `tool-resolution-policy.ts` as `resolveGatewayConfiguredToolPolicies`, beside `tool-resolution-authority.ts` and `tool-resolution-completion.ts`. Both call sites keep the same order of also-allowed tools: the profile's own, the requested tools, then the runtime `message` tool.

- QA Lab `message-cross-context-confine-group` (host runner, mock-openai, qa-channel): passes 1/1, all 3 steps. A group turn's send to `dm:alice` is delivered by default. With `confineChatTypes` set, the same send is refused with ``Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target="dm:alice" while bound to "group:qa-confine-group" (channel=qa-channel). tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes keeps group turns in their current conversation.`` and nothing reaches the DM in the quiet window; the group's own conversation and a DM turn still deliver. With main's 8 production files (and no `tool-resolution-policy.ts`), the refusal step fails: the send is delivered to `alice` (`expected a cross-context denial naming confineChatTypes`).
- The PR's 5 test files and the other 8 `tool-resolution*` test files: 13 files, 201 tests, 0 failed. The PR's 5 test files on bare main: 43 of 114 fail: 26 send-policy rows, 14 normalization rows (the thread-id spellings and numeric targets), the confined-group case in `outbound-policy.test.ts`, the confined broadcast, and "judges a direct send to a sibling topic from a header-bound group call".
- Static checks on the merge, with `--base eee7a1bd526` where a check takes one: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `check:test-types` 0 errors; oxlint and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export ratchets, the conflict-marker check and the PR wrapper inventory test (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`) pass. `check-test-lines-ratchet`: net +493, allocation 493.

Everything below is from the pre-merge heads.

Focused suite (measured at `470c81210da` against its merge base `19aff5bfd42`; the current head's checks are below): `outbound-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-routing.send-policy.test.ts`, `message-action-runner.broadcast.test.ts`, plus the existing context-isolation fixtures in `message-action-routing.context.test.ts`.

- With the change: 51 of 51 pass, and the 15 context-isolation fixtures pass.
- `outbound-policy.ts` at the merge base: 8 fail, 43 pass.

On this head the Gateway logs each refusal. Under `confineChatTypes` it ends with the confinement reason, for example `MessageActionDeniedError: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target="<group>:topic:99" while bound to "telegram:<group>:topic:42" (channel=telegram). tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes keeps group turns in their current conversation.`; the `to`, `topic-edit` and `topic-create` rows name `target="telegram:<owner-dm>"`. The HTTP caller gets `500` with `{"type":"tool_error","message":"tool execution failed"}` for a refusal, on main as well.

What these runs also showed, and what they do not cover:
- At `1cb5e029db3` the `confineChatTypes` column was all delivered: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the same headers, all nine calls went out, including a `sendMessage` to `<owner-dm>` and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on `<owner-dm>`, because `/tools/invoke` reported no conversation kind. `9aadc2bbc5c` makes it report the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, which gives the refusals above.
- Without the conversation headers, `/tools/invoke` has no current conversation on either build (`Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`), so no `crossContext` switch applies. This is unchanged by `9aadc2bbc5c`: in both runs on this head, under `confineChatTypes`, a `threadId` of 99, string or number, went to topic 99, as it does on main. `topic-edit` with `channelId` `<owner-dm>` acted on `<owner-dm>` as a string on both builds, and as a number on this head; main refused the number with that "requires a target" error.
- The Bot API is a loopback, not Telegram. The traces show what the Gateway sent, not how Telegram would answer.

prs.title: refactor: remove automation reasoning and reminder context options
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

I am narrowing automation setup by removing reasoning delivery and the option to copy recent chat into new reminders. The current run style already provides conversation context.

## User Impact

I removed **Include reasoning**, its CLI switches and API field, and the automations tool's `contextMessages` option. Model thinking settings and existing reminder text are unchanged.

Combined chat + webhook delivery (`delivery.completionDestination`), primary webhooks, failure alerts, tool restrictions, and their documentation remain supported.

Existing jobs retain any inert `includeReasoning` metadata in storage, so retiring the option does not change their approval-bound definitions. The flag no longer affects execution and is hidden from public API reads. New requests cannot set it; recreating a job drops the legacy metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

I removed reminder-history fetching and reasoning forwarding, not existing delivery features. I also removed the unnecessary Doctor data rewrite instead of adding approval-rebinding machinery or relaxing authority checks. Doctor's migration and eligibility code now matches main.

## Evidence

- I rebased onto main at `bf298a53334aa01379f52e6fb4f87106f2743a4b` and folded the repair into the same commit. The final diff has 59 files: production/docs/generated +36/-299; tests/fixtures +70/-82.
- I reproduced the approval regression on `4555f42836c9`: [update Doctor removed the flag and left the execution revision inconsistent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893290620/job/140161780776). On final head `97803ada894e`, [the same test passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774379), including valid standing-grant use after Doctor, stale-source preservation, revocation, and a second no-op repair.
- I proved both legacy-flag API cases fail before the fix and [pass afterward without mutating the stored job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774185).
- Unsupported delivery rows retain main's early eligibility check and filtered legacy-notify migration. I verified those production files match main. The existing mode-42 preservation test passed on the regression baseline; I did not verify a final-head rerun of that unchanged test. No secondary-webhook deletion remains.
- I corrected the obsolete trailing argument without weakening recipient/thread assertions. [All four queued-delivery cases pass on the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774207). CI exposed the same stale expectation in cron failure delivery; I corrected it too, and [those cases pass](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734/job/140170774185).
- I pruned only the stale assertion-baseline counts for removed reminder code. [Final-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45895960734), including production/test types, lint, docs, and baseline ratchets. The required `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful.
- I regenerated Gateway validators, prompt snapshots, and the English UI baseline, and checked the final diff for whitespace errors. I did not run a live model E2E flow or the full supported-version upgrade matrix. Independent local autoreview could not start because its Codex installation failed the read-only sandbox preflight.

### Upgrade proof required before landing

I verified that this diff does not change the database layout/writer, Doctor production migrations, or updater code. It does change saved-job validation, normalization, public payload reads, and payload edits. I am treating that compatibility surface as upgrade-sensitive; real 9.x and 10.x updates remain unverified.

Before landing, the real update runs should:

- Start from each supported 9.x baseline, including extended-stable, and 10.x, using each old version's own updater to reach this head. Exercise the old updater's complete request/result/restart round trip, not just installing the new build over a copied database.
- Seed supported legacy jobs and approval state on each baseline. After upgrade, restart and run Doctor twice; verify job retention, correctly bound execution revisions, valid standing approvals on the next run, and continued refusal of revoked or stale authority. Where the baseline supports it, cover both reasoning-flag values and an unsupported delivery row beside repairable jobs.
- Verify combined chat + webhook delivery, legacy notify migration, tool restrictions, and edit/clone round trips. Existing reminder text must survive; retired reasoning metadata must remain inert and hidden from public reads, while final output still delivers normally.

### Historical UI evidence

I retained the original real-Control-UI screenshots below, captured with synthetic data and a mocked Gateway: before `2b58c8e5224ee0d2d9826467b5e1370e4091b1e9`, after `652f5503bde9193c87cc49fad8126c528974f105`. They illustrate the retained reasoning-toggle removal, not a fresh run of this rebased head.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![The automation Results settings show Include reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6498c8be-02e0-47f9-9f89-c14f19cda81a)

**After**

![The automation Results settings no longer show Include reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc495f16-f87d-48c7-b970-102c58fb489f)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The Include reasoning row is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9282345-dedc-46a9-8959-90d41fb31cb7)

**After**

![The next remaining Results setting is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5296351-8e19-4b53-84d3-05ca531cc887)

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfb77f08-1fd2-461f-ada5-4f3ff81fa044)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3030a105-2a21-460e-baf1-7f72cab4188a)

prs.title: fix(ci): keep baseline ratchets from exhausting hosted runners
prs.body:
Related: #203945 (earlier inventory heap issue; this change fixes overlap between checks).

## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite worker inventory and the SQL portability scan can run their large TypeScript snapshots at the same time. A [scheduled job on main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46082421256/job/140784500233) lost its hosted runner during this step. I reproduced the overlap on a 4-vCPU, 16-GiB AWS machine with no swap; the kernel killed `tsc` in the job's cgroup.

## User Impact

CI runs the same ratchets on the same runner size. There is no application behavior change. PR-only coverage, timeouts and cancellation are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The aggregate command already owns two managed child slots. One now takes the two large database checks in sequence. The other keeps smaller checks moving, and both can drain that queue once the database checks finish. No new workflow flag, heap setting or lock is needed.

## Evidence

I replayed the scheduled workflow step and frozen install from separate cold checkouts on the same AWS `m7i.xlarge` (4 vCPUs, 16 GiB nominal, no swap). In the [paired run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_dd2f28cf791da4e05d338e94a9ef558e), main `ecea22292` lost transport after the last sample at 110.5 seconds including install. Its figures are lower bounds. The wrapper exited 255; no job exit code survived. In a [separate replay of main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_34a53f2f1a0974af8032dc0560a42aef), the kernel explicitly OOM-killed the native compiler.

| Measurement (GiB) | Main, last observation | Fixed tree, completed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Job cgroup peak, including file cache | ≥14.33 | 14.31 |
| Peak summed process RSS, sampled | ≥14.18 | 11.77 |
| Peak cgroup anonymous memory, sampled | ≥13.69 | 11.31 |

All 12 checks passed in 133 seconds (192 seconds including install), exit 0, zero OOM kills. The fixed ratchets also passed in 141 seconds in a second replay. Five recent successful hosted scheduled steps took 105–158 seconds. I did not obtain a successful same-box pre-fix timing or a terminal pre-fix peak. The published and tested commits have identical Git trees.

Both scheduled and PR regression cases fail on the original scheduler at the overlap assertion and pass with the fix. All four focused cases pass, including fatal shutdown and sibling cleanup. Scripts typecheck, focused lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted PR CI, independent review and post-merge failure rate are not claimed here.

Reported and reproduced by @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-ratchets-runner-loss-sfe70e9c6)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(cron): wait for a provider's stated rate-limit reset before the next run
prs.body:
## Problem

On a production deployment, 126 scheduled-automation runs in 7 days failed with "<model> is rate-limited. The provider says to retry in 5-6 days". Recurring jobs ran again on every slot, or hourly once the error backoff reached its 60-minute maximum, and every run hit the same limit. Two jobs were still looping with 25 consecutive errors. Nothing in the cron scheduler read the provider's reset time; a rate limit counted as a transient error.

## Fix

- The run result now carries the provider's reset time as a transient fact (`rateLimitResetAt`, never stored). It is set only when every failed model attempt was rate-limited with a known reset (candidates skipped for a local cooldown are ignored), and the earliest reset wins. It reuses the existing reset facts on the failover error.
  - Session-target jobs: the settled failure cause already reaches the automation settlement in-process.
  - Isolated jobs: the run's catch, forwarded by the isolated execution adapter.
- `applyJobResult` uses it when scheduling the next run after an error:
  - The next normal slot is the first scheduled slot at or after the reset, so cron expressions stay on their schedule.
  - A reset before the schedule's own next slot moves the quick retry to the reset. A later reset skips quick retries for the first slot after it (an off-slot time there would be moved earlier by schedule maintenance), and the failure alert is not held for a retry that is days away.
- One-shot jobs are unchanged.
- Jobs are not paused; the failure notice already names the reset time (#206945).

## User impact

A recurring automation on a model with a multi-day limit stops hitting the provider, or the local limit gate, every hour. It runs again on its first slot after the stated reset, and the user gets the failure alert once instead of after every slot.

## Evidence

- `src/cron/rate-limit-reset.integration.test.ts`: a loopback provider returns 429 with `retry-after: 518400`. On both the session-target and the isolated path, the run makes one provider request and reports the reset (~6 days). Fails on main (no reset reported), passes here.
- `src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts`: an hourly `every` job and a weekday cron job land exactly on their first slot after the reset, schedule maintenance keeps that slot, and the failure alert is emitted. A 45-second reset moves the quick retry instead of skipping to the next day. Fails on main, passes here.
- The same file runs both execution adapters through the timer, schedule maintenance and the persisted store, including a 5-minute cron with a 20-minute reset: the stored next run is the first slot after the reset.
- Cron run, outcome, failure-alert and cross-provider fallback suites on both paths pass.

Accepted edge: a provider that states an absurd reset (for example years away) parks the job until then; the failure notice shows that date, and a reset the scheduler cannot represent is ignored.

prs.title: fix: let new agents use the default agent's subscription model catalog during creation
prs.body:
Related: #206921

## What Problem This Solves

When a user with a working subscription-backed default agent (for example ChatGPT/Codex OAuth serving `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` over `openai-chatgpt-responses`, with no OpenAI Platform API key configured) clicks **Create new agent** in the Control UI, `agents.create` verifies the prospective agent's primary model before persisting its roster entry. Because the new agent does not yet have its own published `configured` model-runtime owner, its static read-only runtime lease drops the default agent's published dynamic subscription catalog and falls back to the static API-key-only `openai-responses` route, failing agent creation with `No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai`.

## User Impact

Creating a new agent that inherits the default agent's credentials and provider configuration now sees the same published subscription model catalog during onboarding preflight as an ordinary turn on the default agent, instead of requiring an API key. If the candidate configuration diverges in `models`, `auth`, `plugins`, environment, or credential mode, it does not inherit the default agent's catalog. No user action, migration, or breaking change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts`, `acquirePreparedModelRuntimeLeaseAttempt` already reuses the passive published model catalog (`capturePreparedModelRuntimeCatalog`) from a matching `configuredOwner` without sharing execution plugins, session state, or workspace. When `configuredOwner` is absent because the target agent is prospective/unconfigured (such as during `prepareAgentOnboarding` in `agents.create`), `resolveInheritedCatalogOwner` falls back to the unique non-stale `configured` owner matching `owner.input.inheritedAuthDir` only when `skipCredentials`, `environmentFingerprint`, and `{ models, auth, plugins }` config fingerprints all match. This keeps execution isolation intact while closing the prospective-agent catalog gap described in `#206921` (distinct from `#200372`, which covers already-configured agents).

## Evidence

Verified on Node `v24.22.3` (commit `5bfc86ffb`):

1. **Base (`origin/main`) fails the prospective-agent subscription catalog test**:
   ```text
   $ pnpm vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.prospective-agent-catalog.test.ts
   × prospective agent creation inherits published subscription catalog > reuses the default agent's published subscription catalog when verifying a new agent candidate
     → readAdmittedPublishedModelCatalog(readOnlyLease.snapshot) is undefined (drops openai-chatgpt-responses)
   Test Files  1 failed (1)
        Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
   ```
2. **Fix (`5bfc86ffb`) passes all focused and adjacent tests**:
   - `pnpm vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.prospective-agent-catalog.test.ts` — **1 test file passed, 2 tests passed** (prospective agent inherits published `openai-chatgpt-responses` catalog; divergent candidate `models.providers` does not inherit it).
   - `pnpm vitest run src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-onboarding.test.ts` — **2 test files passed, 44 tests passed**.
   - Note: These tests exercise the real `prepared-model-runtime` lease and `applyAgentConfig` / `resolveSystemAgentConfiguredRouteFromConfig` paths with synthetic catalog entries; live Control UI + ChatGPT OAuth creation was not run.
3. **Lint & format**:
   - `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.prospective-agent-catalog.test.ts` — `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.`
   - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.prospective-agent-catalog.test.ts` — `All matched files use the correct format.`

prs.title: refactor(subagents): simplify queued registration recovery
prs.body:
Related: #206472

## What Problem This Solves

Queued subagent registration repeats recovery and row-eligibility decisions across launch, cancellation, and failure settlement. Maintaining those copies makes this already complex circuit harder to change safely.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Queued launches still wait for kill claims, preserve the first failure for retry, and refuse cleanup or replay when a write outcome is uncertain. Existing tests are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registration owner now uses one recovery classifier, one queued-row selector, and one shared acceptance predicate. The redundant persistence uncertainty flag and three single-use admission wrappers are removed.

### Circuit map

| State or input | Writer / owner | Required effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queued row and accepted address | Run-launch owner; persistence preserves the physical execution through rekeying | Read the current row through getCurrentSubagentRunOwner. |
| Pending or committed kill claim | Kill owner and persistence queue | Wait outside row admission; re-enter when a released claim is reacquired. |
| Queued launch failure | Queued-registration owner | Retain the first cause/time, prepare collector facts, and publish one failed row. |
| Cancelled collector awaiting settlement | Kill owner; queued-registration publishes collector completion | Preserve the kill outcome and captured output while completing launch cleanup. |
| Known refused write | Persistence reports no commit; registration retains retry state | Retry settlement without replaying launch or already completed cleanup. |
| Unknown write or committed publication failure | Persistence outcome owner; registration retains restore state | Refuse replay and session cleanup until canonical recovery. |
| Replaced row, newer sibling, or retired runtime | Registry/run owners | Stop stale launch/settlement and preserve the successor. |

Local state writers are also contained in this owner: the registration loop acknowledges registration; waitForClaim records restore failures; failIncompleteRegistration retains the first error and manages pending/retry state; prepareCancelled and settleCancelled own cancellation settlement; canContinueSettlement and settleFailedLaunch retire stale settlement; and publish records its own terminal execution after publication.

The retained inputs are the acknowledged row, database context, lifecycle generation, Gateway resolver, manager row/config reads, activation callback, and caller assertion. Effects remain claim waiting, collector preparation, serialized mutation, published-output cleanup, and observer activation. No durable shape changes.

### Deletions and remaining decisions

- The three inline unknown-or-committed error classifiers are replaced by requiresRegistryRestore; inline copies remaining: 0.
- The three repeated full queued-row gates are replaced by queuedEntry; inline copies remaining: 0. Retry-state classification still distinguishes a taken-over row from an active kill claim.
- getCurrentSubagentRunOwner already guarantees the physical-owner comparison, including queued/accepted address aliases. Re-comparisons of its selected row were removed; mutation-plan and sibling-candidate comparisons remain because those rows are not selected by that owner.
- persistenceUncertain, exactEntry, gatewayCurrent, assertLaunchCurrent and assertRegistrationCurrent references remaining in the changed owner: 0.
- Launch acceptance and accepted-run abort now consume the same predicate.
- Mechanical caller updates: none. No ACP files changed; those belong to R6.

### Complexity boundary

registerRequiredQueuedSubagent decreases from CC 128 to 107, and SLOC 328 to 303. This does not meet the numeric half-baseline target. The retained branches distinguish documented, tested outcomes: claim release/reacquisition, committed cancellation versus ordinary launch failure, refused versus unknown writes, registry/Gateway retirement, accepted-address rekeying, and newer sibling session ownership. They remain separate because they trigger different persistence, retry, or cleanup effects. No helper was extracted solely to move complexity out of the metric.

## Evidence

- Base: d2aceb13195154e0375f1f933ba4ca00292d99ba. Candidate: b5015aff23469dd4d9e34864acb03c9ed3212ab2.
- Production diff: 54 added, 70 removed; net **−16 lines**. Tests: unchanged.
- Selected predicate-call lines (unknown outcome, committed outcome, physical-owner comparison), measured with git grep -c: 10 → 4.
- code-sloppiness: complete one-file scope, identical pinned scb-check 0.2.0+vk.4 engine; baseline and candidate scans.
- Formatting and git diff --check passed.
- Independent branch review at P0–P2 completed with no actionable findings on 4375d7fbd6f (scoped-clean). The subsequent change only renames one local to fix a no-shadow lint diagnostic.
- Testbox tbx_01m8fnvzcqxrq5j9kz7szeh8js queued after source preparation and was stopped under the standing queue rule. Native cleanup confirmed completion with a cancelled workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46083431067. No requested test command completed.
- Diagnostic CI on 4375d7fbd6f: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46083874130. The unchanged queued-registration suite passed 31 cases; run-wait passed 4; completion-authority passed 66. Production types and all five core test-type stripes passed. Full-directory suite execution is not claimed.
- That run found one PR-caused no-shadow lint error, corrected by the local rename in b5015aff234. Required merge-checkout CI passed all 38 jobs on that head, including all five core lint shards: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46084650787.
- The diagnostic run's dead-export failure is inherited: src/cli/run-main-policy.ts exports isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation without an external reader. The file blob is identical on the base, PR and scheduled main 8b36e346b455. Main run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46082421256, job 140784501686, reports the identical production and full-tree failure.
- The first draft-CI command stopped before dispatch due to a live dependency-cache metadata owner. Its one retry succeeded after the lock cleared.
- The exact-file overlap search found no matching open PR among the inspected subagent candidates.

prs.title: fix(android): show device dictation availability
prs.body:
Related: #202818
Follows #206993
Fixes #206647

## What Problem This Solves

Voice settings used the Gateway transcription provider to report whether chat Dictation was ready. Chat Dictation uses Android's on-device recognizer, so the screen could show Needs setup on a capable phone or Ready on a phone without that recognizer.

## User Impact

Dictation now reports device availability under Microphone. Realtime Talk continues to report Gateway provider readiness. Recognition, microphone permissions, saved settings and voice-note recovery keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Settings and the chat recognizer now share the existing on-device availability query. The unused Gateway Dictation projection and target plumbing are removed; realtime parsing and Talk launch admission retain their existing decisions. The six existing localized readiness templates keep their translation identities.

## Evidence

The two mismatched device/Gateway cases failed through the real Settings route on base `d22090cf`, then passed after the cutover. The shared fixture repair is now merged in #206993. Candidate `4f59076d` is based on its merge `beb7dc1d`. They also assert that Realtime Talk still uses Gateway readiness.

All 195 affected tests passed in both phone flavors: Voice Settings, Gateway readiness, Chat Dictation, runtime agent selection and the composer. The final three Voice Settings tests passed in both flavors after removing the capture adapter and formatting the helper; all app ktlint passed. On the original stack parent `0f27f268`, 11 affected Settings/readiness/composer cases passed per flavor and app ktlint passed. The restack preserves all seven Kotlin files byte-for-byte and the identical generated-inventory site delta; native source verification passed again on `4f59076d`. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete range `0f27f268..5f00b72d`: no actionable correctness or security findings; patch assessed as correct. prs.title: fix: let updates pass validation when the Gateway uses Tailscale Serve or Funnel
prs.body:
Closes #205405

## What Problem This Solves

If your Gateway is reachable over Tailscale Serve or Funnel (`gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"` or `"funnel"`), `openclaw update` to 2026.11.10 always fails at the `candidate-gateway-startup` check with "Tailscale HTTPS port 443 is already owned by a route whose ownership OpenClaw cannot prove" (exit 78). The update rolls back safely, but the only way through is to turn Tailscale off, restart, update, turn it back on and restart again. That cuts tailnet access in between.

## User Impact

Updates go through on Gateways that use Tailscale Serve or Funnel, with no config changes or extra restarts. The live Gateway keeps its Tailscale route for the whole validation, as before. A normal Gateway start (not an update candidate) behaves exactly as before and still claims its managed route.

## Why This Change Was Made

The updater starts a candidate Gateway with `--update-canary` against a snapshot of the live config while the live Gateway keeps serving. Startup already skips the other things the serving Gateway owns when it sees `updateCanary`: portal ingress, the sandbox host and plugin legacy listeners. It did not skip the managed Tailscale listener, so the candidate tried to claim the route the live Gateway holds, and Tailscale refused.

The fix adds that same guard where the managed Tailscale listener is decided (`managedTailscaleMode` in `createGatewayHttpTransport`). That is the only place that creates the listener and calls `prepareManagedTailscaleIngress`, so one condition covers Serve and Funnel. The fix is in the candidate, so it also covers older installed updaters that launch the new release with `--update-canary`.

On the question in the issue: neither failed update report (installed and candidate admission) records any rehearsal override for `candidate-gateway-startup`; the step entry has only `exitCode: 78` and the `startupz` failure fact. The `gateway.tailscale.mode: "off"` layout is asserted by the doctor rehearsal inventory (`doctor-update-rehearsal-inventory.ts`). It isn't applied to the config the candidate Gateway boots.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction and fix on the real Tailscale node (isolated throwaway Gateway).** A Linux arm64 host whose production Gateway (2026.11.10) holds the Tailscale Serve foreground route on 443. A throwaway Gateway built from source was launched the way the updater's candidate check launches it: `gateway run --update-canary --update-canary --bind loopback --port <free port>`, with the same `OPENCLAW_SKIP_*` environment. It ran with a temporary HOME, state, config, workspace and TMPDIR, `gateway.tailscale.mode: "serve"`, token auth and its own cgroup. Tailscale CLI calls were traced with `strace -f -e trace=execve`. A runtime-only build (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`) was used for both runs.

| | base `645643d0fa4` (main) | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| `/readyz` | never ready | ready after 23 s |
| exit | 78, `Gateway failed to start: Tailscale HTTPS port 443 is already owned by a route whose ownership OpenClaw cannot prove` | 0 (clean SIGTERM shutdown) |
| `tailscale` processes run | `version`, `status --json`, `serve status --json`, `serve --yes --bg=false <port>` | none |
| leftover listeners | 0 | 0 |

The base failure is the same error the real 11.7 → 11.10 update reported. After every run, the production Gateway's foreground Serve session and backend were unchanged, and its `/readyz` returned 200.

<details>
<summary>Base run output (redacted)</summary>

```
== base 645643d0fa4
config validate rc=0
readyz=0 after 23s
gateway exit=78
[tailscale] serve failed: Tailscale HTTPS port 443 is already owned by a route whose ownership OpenClaw cannot prove; it was not modified. Foreground session <id> (https://<tailnet-host>:443/ -> http://127.0.0.1:<live-port>). ...
Gateway failed to start: Tailscale HTTPS port 443 is already owned by a route whose ownership OpenClaw cannot prove; it was not modified. ...
tailscale invocations (execve):
["/usr/bin/tailscale", "version"]
["/usr/bin/tailscale", "status", "--json"]
["/usr/bin/tailscale", "serve", "status", "--json"]
["/usr/bin/tailscale", "serve", "--yes", "--bg=false", "<candidate-port>"]
leftover listeners on port: 0
```

Fix run:

```
== fix
config validate rc=0
readyz=1 after 23s
gateway exit=0
tailscale invocations (execve):
  (none)
leftover listeners on port: 0
```
</details>

**Contributor end-to-end upgrade proof (2026.11.7 → exact base/head).** [stealthybear reports an isolated npm-global upgrade with systemd and a separately enrolled Tailscale device](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205443#issuecomment-7214987840): base `4300f41` fails `candidate-gateway-startup` with exit 78 while the serving route remains unchanged; head `80a5ac344d5` passes candidate validation and completes the upgrade with token, model, workspace and Tailscale settings retained. The final service restart had approximately 100 seconds of readiness failures; this is not a zero-downtime upgrade claim. Their config-recovery trace explains why a sufficiently reduced canary config can restore Serve from backup. These are the contributor's reported results, not a new author-run test.

**Independent contributor confirmation and accepted proof.** [daniel-lxs reports](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205443#issuecomment-7223399271) a real-route standalone canary failure on main and readiness on this PR with Serve preserved. Full upgrades from 2026.11.10 and 2026.11.7 passed on both revisions; those installed updaters did not run that canary, so these upgrades do not demonstrate the behavioral difference. These are independent contributor results, not a new author-run test. [The completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205443#issuecomment-7168579145) accepts the combined evidence as sufficient and explicitly considers the earlier latest-stable proof request satisfied. It reviewed `80a5ac344d5`, before the subsequent main merge to `7a5d4a9b3f3` (not a new exact-head review).

**Regression test.** I added `does not bind or claim managed {serve,funnel} ingress while validating an update` to `src/gateway/server-runtime-state.tailscale.test.ts`. On the base source both cases fail (`prepareManagedTailscaleIngress` called once); with the fix, all 8 tests in the file pass. The existing `keeps ordinary ingress closed until the managed route is claimed` test still passes, which shows normal startup still claims the route.

**Focused checks** (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`), all passing with the fix:
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-state.tailscale.test.ts` (8)
- `src/gateway/server-startup-update-canary.test.ts` (1)
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-state.test.ts` (13)
- `src/gateway/server-tailscale.test.ts` (17)
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-state.portals.test.ts` (3)

Also run: oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files (clean), the pre-commit staged-content guard, and `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`. Every lane passed, including typecheck for core and core tests, except the dead-export scan. That scan flags two existing unused exports in `scripts/e2e/parallels/` (`detectParallelsHostIp`, `listVmNames`), which are on main and untouched here.

**Gaps.**
- A full released-updater upgrade that itself exercises the changed canary is not claimed by the latest independent report. The combined standalone canary and upgrade evidence satisfies the reviewer's earlier request; Funnel live coverage remains absent.
- Funnel is covered by the unit test, not the live run.
- The live proof ran on `645643d0fa4`; the branch is rebased onto current main, where both touched files are unchanged.

**Upstream CI disposition (November 27, current head `126c163304e9`).** Main was merged again after the accepted review of `80a5ac344d5`; that review is not an exact-head review. [CI run 46045586909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46045586909) fails. `pnpm test:ci-failed 205443` and the job logs identify:
- `server.openclaw-id-member-suspension.test.ts`: three member-access cases (`admin-sets-null`, `owner-sets-null`, `owner-sets-reader`) fail at line 483 because `inFlightTurnAborted` is true instead of false.
- `server.chat-membership-authority.product.test.ts`: the transcript-persistence/agent-dispatch case fails at line 588 because terminal status is `error` instead of `ok`.

These supersede the previous head's skill-discovery and PostgreSQL failure report. The exact merged-main parent is `6bdb5284285c`; [its CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46045472052) was cancelled and provides no matching failure evidence. The PR diff against that parent still contains only the Tailscale canary guard and its regression tests (two files). Failure attribution remains unresolved: neither an introduced defect nor a matching pre-existing base failure is established. No local rerun pass is claimed.

prs.title: improve: avoid loading PostgreSQL schema data for SQLite commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite commands import generated PostgreSQL DDL and catalog data through the shared database-engine modules, even when no PostgreSQL schema value is used. The property getters defer construction, but the large literal source is still loaded.

## User Impact

SQLite commands avoid loading PostgreSQL-only payload source. PostgreSQL keeps the same synchronous lazy values, field order, descriptors and per-receiver memoization. No configuration, database schema/version, migration or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing generated schema owner now emits one factory asset per lazy field. The existing database-asset build plugin packages those factories for ordinary and sealed workers. Factories preserve independent mutable values for different receivers; payload load failures still throw synchronously without replacing the getter. The three self-contained recovery build configurations inline only their required PostgreSQL factories so handoff and activation remain independent of neighboring assets. Existing SQLite handling in those builds is preserved.

This moves work to the first PostgreSQL field access rather than removing that work. One warm-filesystem native source sample materializing all 12 fields measured 3.76 ms → 20.73 ms; it excludes the original eager module import and is not a database-latency benchmark. There are 12 logical payloads, totaling 747,035 uncompressed bytes in each layout. A matched stock total-package size was not retained, so this PR makes no compressed package-size claim.

## Evidence

- Matched full native builds and an ordinary built `infer model run --local` against a synthetic loopback Responses provider: both stock and candidate produced one expected POST, the expected text reply and exit 0. In the observed main isolate, the two affected engine modules acquired 552,267 → 44,656 source bytes before the POST and through exit (507,611 fewer). File count was unchanged. The candidate's observed main and secondary thread loaded zero PostgreSQL payload assets. This is source-load evidence, not a latency, RSS or per-isolate multiplier claim.
- `pnpm db:postgres:check`: 248 cases plus generated-file freshness passed. All non-runtime generated SQL/catalog outputs stayed byte-identical.
- Source-value, Knip-consumer and exact writer-guard tests: 159 passed. The guard retains its single admitted statement at the generated factory owner and rejects the retired location, altered or duplicated statements. The actual assertion-safety and database-worker ratchets passed against the frozen base; Knip clears every new factory/helper finding, with the same three untouched restart-sentinel exports also reported by [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46070235079/job/140745585990).
- Eight final native boundary tests passed: normal/sealed relocation, retained-generation reads after live assets are replaced, all 12 fields from a relocated self-contained recovery file, both actual staged recovery runtimes, and both reader build forms. Actual emitted sealed SQLite restore/export succeeded with PostgreSQL assets unavailable. Wrapper-source closure also passed.
- The original implementation fails the cold-import boundary in both normal/sealed layouts. The initial candidate exposed a real standalone recovery packaging gap: its relocated getter required a missing factory. The same all-field test now passes with only PostgreSQL factories inlined at the standalone build owner. The corrected real PostgreSQL handoff now passes in the hosted conformance run.
- Normal build, scoped formatting/lint and wrapper-source closure passed. Public SDK declarations were byte-identical to the baseline.
- After the canonical worker-bundle producer ran, an actual npm dry-run file-list audit included all 12 ordinary payload assets and the sealed worker archive, while excluding loose worker files. All 12 archive payload members matched ordinary asset bytes. The complete worker archive is 25,398,468 compressed bytes (87,013,088 uncompressed); the current pack audit reports 111,417,667 compressed / 305,592,701 unpacked bytes. These are current-layout totals, not a matched package-size reduction or a published-package install test.
- Independent source/behavior review passed on `ea667371ce6643e4b3f4561fadece7d392380e62`. Local ClawSweeper completed the final committed range from `e7325fb319c40b66a8519c2c3fc81f320d17c297` to that head with no findings or risks; its source review did not itself execute these proofs.
- Actual isolated PostgreSQL conformance passed on the corrected head in [CI 46076322720](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46076322720): all six PostgreSQL 17 shards succeeded (1,807 passing test executions and 40 explicit skips across their test groups), plus PostgreSQL 16 smoke 4/4. The real cold/warm shared-store, agent FIFO/Doctor/ownership and [managed Gateway handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46076322720/job/140765372942) cases ran and passed. The handoff group passed 70/70. These are backend tests, separate from SQLite and source-value proof.

Release-note context: avoid acquiring generated PostgreSQL schema payloads on SQLite-only startup while preserving PostgreSQL lazy schema semantics.

prs.title: chore(qa): compare archived worktree restore with clone selection
prs.body:
Part of #204058.

## What Problem This Solves

An archived conversation can keep its session ID even when selecting another local clone gives it a fresh checkout. That makes it easy to mistake a successful selection for recovery of saved work.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Reviewers can compare the two operator paths using local synthetic repositories without a live provider or real session data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QA scenario starts with two archived sessions as independent controls. Both clones contain the exact saved Git snapshots before the disposable Gateway reopens with a different worktree root. One session uses ordinary restore; the other selects the second clone through a managed-worktree request using its existing session key. The probe reports worktree identity and saved-note recovery independently. It does not require a fresh ID or a missing note to count as a valid observation.

## Evidence

On Linux, ordinary restore retained the original worktree ID and path, left the conversation archived until explicit unarchive, and restored its saved note and provisioned input (including mode `0640`). On the comparison path, the session ID stayed the same, but the worktree ID changed and Files reported the saved note missing. The original snapshot ref remained intact. This is a baseline for the issue, **not an implementation of alternate-clone recovery**.

Reproduce with:

~~~sh
OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-worktrees-archive-restore.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
~~~

Local run: one test passed; 56.81 seconds in Vitest, 65.38 seconds for the command. The E2E TypeScript project, targeted lint, format, scenario manifest loading, and whitespace checks passed. Author self-review covered the complete staged diff at base/HEAD `0174cf4d0083110f25893b3a3624b77f4402e3f5`, candidate tree `a83735067ae8cefc1cec8186bda61354da53425f`. The two published fixture files at `dffce1c9cc5fb04297bd1950fc66dd60765b5e79` match the locally tested bytes. These are local validation results, not a hosted CI or independent-review verdict.

The checked-in fixture uses two Gateway lifetimes in one test process. The separate cold-process control below runs the same assertions against two OS processes. Neither run tests a model turn, nonempty transcript, historical-link rewrite, PR routing, or private sandbox projection.

### Exact-head runtime receipt

On the clean published commit, the focused Linux fixture passed again. The receipt below contains selected fields from its native Vitest JSON report and the comparison it printed. A reports assertions that passed; B reports the observed values. This is an in-process **local** run, not a hosted CI check.

<details>
<summary>Inspect fixture-report.json · SHA-256 16d316c7e0ba1109fb0f12fe89d37049aa2bf0e51ed74de18e8e69f55014b132</summary>

```json

  "command": "OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm test test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-worktrees-archive-restore.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile.json=$REPORT",
  "startedUtc": "2026-11-23T13:33:49Z",
  "finishedUtc": "2026-11-23T13:34:46Z",
  "exitCode": 0,
  "scope": "Local Linux; two Gateway lifetimes in one process; no model turn or hosted CI. REPORT is the reviewer-selected local output file.",
  "vitest": {
    "success": true,
    "numTotalTests": 1,
    "numPassedTests": 1,
    "numFailedTests": 0,
    "assertion": {
      "fullName": "distinguishes restoring an archived worktree from selecting another clone",
      "status": "passed",
      "duration": 14239.925561000004
    }
  },
  "A_restore": {
    "evidence": "Assertions in the passing fixture",

```

The digest covers the displayed JSON, including its final LF.
</details>

### Cold-process control on the published head

One focused Linux run passed (`dffce1c9cc5f`, exit 0). The first real Gateway archived both sessions, then exited. A distinct Gateway reopened the same on-disk shared and agent stores. Before restore, both original session and worktree IDs were still bound and archived. **A:** ordinary restore kept the original worktree; Files returned the saved note, and the provisioned bytes and mode `0640` survived. **B:** selecting the other clone kept the session ID but returned a new worktree; after explicit unarchive, Files reported the note missing. Empty histories stayed empty. Both owned Gateway processes exited, and the disposable state was removed.

The process distinction was checked via the serving child and wire `system.info` PID, the Gateway process-instance identity, and OS process disappearance before restart. This was a local cold stop/start, not a hosted CI check, crash-recovery test or implemented rebind. No repository code was changed.

<details>
<summary>Cold-process receipt · SHA-256 a080d0b3f3b17b9d5f2a8604205366c51abd2ce310517c0c3b676da81efabaac</summary>


</details>

<summary>Repeat the cold-process control on a disposable Linux profile</summary>

1. Build the clean commit with `node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --require-current-head`; verify both build stamps and `build-info.json` name that commit. Use a fresh profile, operator token, loopback port and empty state directory. Do not use an existing Gateway.
2. Use the setup and A/B requests in the [published fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dffce1c9cc5fb04297bd1950fc66dd60765b5e79/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/managed-worktrees-archive-restore.e2e.test.ts). The temporary driver used the same test file with only its `withRpcGateway` import redirected. For each of its two calls, write the supplied worktree root to the same fixture config and serve `client.request` over the real Gateway WebSocket. The [existing process-replay test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dffce1c9cc5fb04297bd1950fc66dd60765b5e79/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/session-create-replay.e2e.test.ts#L49-L164) shows the build, client, stop and restart calls.
3. In phase 1, retain both `sessions.create` results. After ordinary removal, archive each exact session and transfer just its recovery ref into the second clone. Before stopping, use `sessions.describe` to check both original worktree IDs and `removed-snapshot` state; retain `chat.history` for both. Read `system.info` and confirm its PID matches the helper-owned child.
4. Disconnect, await `stopGateway()`, and verify the first PID no longer exists. Change only the allocation root and call `startGateway()` on the same instance. Verify a different serving PID and process-instance identity, unchanged shared/agent database file identities, and unchanged archived session/worktree IDs and histories **before** either recovery request.
5. Use `worktrees.restore` by original worktree ID for A; for B use `sessions.create` with the original key, the other clone as `cwd`, and `worktree: true`. Explicitly unarchive, then read through Files. Check the provisioned bytes and mode for A. Recheck both histories, stop the second process and clean up the synthetic state. No turn is needed.

Runner invocation: `OPENCLAW_E2E_VERBOSE=1 pnpm test "$driver" --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile.json="$report"`, where `driver` is the temporary transport-adapted copy and `report` is a private local reporter destination. The checked-in fixture command above still runs the two-lifetime/in-process control.
</details>

prs.body:
Part of #180298. ## What Problem This Solves The composer’s native Camera path only requests photos, and a delayed native return can begin attaching to a replacement draft. ## User Impact On the existing recognized Android browser route, Chat and New Session offer **Record video** alongside **Take photo**. A returned clip becomes a draft attachment and is sent only after an explicit send. Cancelled, detached, and replaced-draft camera returns are rejected. **This is a proposal for human review, not accepted picker policy or authorization to merge.** Desktop photo preview/capture/retake, other iOS photo routes, Safari’s **Photos & videos** and combined **Attach…** actions, image-only restrictions, upload safeguards, and unrestricted File selection remain unchanged. No custom recorder or microphone request is added by OpenClaw. Native browser/OS recording and permissions remain platform-owned. ## Why This Change Was Made A dedicated single-video capture input reuses the existing native-browser policy and attachment admission, preparation, preview and send owners. Explicit photo/video labels avoid implying that every platform has a video recorder. The native-return guard binds selection to the opening draft before asynchronous attachment reading starts. The merged existing-media contribution #180723 is incorporated through the refreshed main base: **Photos & videos**, Safari’s source-menu route, image-only restrictions and unrestricted File selection are preserved. Main’s lazy camera host is also preserved. Menu-heading proposal #180579, broader iOS capture policy and a desktop recorder remain outside this contribution. Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**. AI-assisted implementation. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfd1f162-7d1d-4dc0-a7e0-0a65c7817bd8) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/074b4e8e-6f15-40c7-9a31-e18ac3ab0f85) ## Evidence ### Current integration and CI repair — 2026-10-26 **Publication blocked; this PR is not yet merge-ready.** The tested, independently reviewed repair is preserved in the implementation session but has not reached this branch. The managed publisher rejected request `9ee1940f-f62d-4acd-8cf4-001375d7593d`: the requester needs full operator write authority for upstream workflow changes carried by the base refresh. The nine-file Camera delta against the verified refreshed base changes **no workflow files**. No workflow changes were removed to bypass the guard. A maintainer with full operator write access must publish the prepared update; then CI must pass on its exact head. Remote head was read back unchanged at `f36269109b8dbe32def219b35afd7828b5b5eb05` and remains conflicted with main. The original [UI-shard failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40086743010/job/120851466467) was reproduced: the Camera connected-input guard also rejected ordinary file-selection handoffs. The repair limits that guard to Camera returns; ordinary file/photo/media selection retains its existing handoff contract. Camera cancellation, opening-signal identity, detached-input rejection, disabled-state checks and image-only protection remain intact. Refreshed official-main base: `d46ce5ca6d6a067af0ab7a617750d082933e26c1`. Integrated candidate tree: `f57b2ecd842d77096474f17358d0bfc263c5fcb6`. Six shared-file conflicts were resolved with #180723 and main’s lazy camera host; the complete base-relative change remains nine files. No new recorder, picker-policy redesign or permission change was introduced. - **49 focused tests passed:** 27 native/desktop Camera and picker cases, plus all 22 isolated attachment-handoff cases, including both previously failing cases. - **18 production-browser behavior scenarios passed:** Chat/New Session video return, explicit exact-byte sending, cancellation/reselection, platform exclusions, preserved desktop photo capture, Safari picker behavior and mixed existing-media selection. Node 24.22.1 and the frozen dependency install retained integrity and release-age checks. - Test cost: component run 21.19 s total / about 0.5 s assertions; handoff run 8.63 s total / about 0.17 s assertions. The production-browser run took 71.92 s including build; the video-return file took 2.558 s. - Fresh independent P0–P3 review returned **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Before uses the five affected production modules from the exact refreshed base; candidate modules were restored and byte-verified after capture. These are production UI screenshots, not native Android certification.

All nine published files match the tested/reviewed source byte-for-byte; all three PR commits, including the managed base integrations, have the required TheAngryPit co-author trailer. - Prepared official-main base: `a6c561f954c41209124f7add70a13c59e883eda3`. Raw reports, local host inventory/paths and human intervention quotations are not published. prs.title: feat: browse and search Knowledge records from Memory Wiki
prs.body:
Related: #92462 (the Control UI browsing use case only).

## What Problem This Solves

When Knowledge is the selected memory engine, Memory Wiki shows compiled wiki pages but gives an operator no way to open that agent’s Knowledge records. A wiki with source and report pages can also appear empty if it has no overview cards.

## User Impact

Operators can browse records or enter a search term from Memory Wiki. Both actions open the existing reader for the selected agent, with the same access checks. No import, wiki compilation, migration, or change to `search.corpus` is required. A wiki with pages but no cards now says so.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Knowledge reader already owns browsing, search and access. Memory Wiki links there instead of copying records or adding a second reader. Other memory engines keep their existing wiki workflow.

## Evidence

### Browse and Search reach the same saved record

A disposable Gateway running the reviewed UI, with the Knowledge memory engine and Memory Wiki enabled at its **default settings**. The fixture published one synthetic note for agent `qa` (shown as **C-3PO QA**). No wiki import, compile, or corpus change was requested. The recording contains only the synthetic browser view; it does not include network traffic or credentials.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/939f25e0-fd2c-4b08-aa1d-04853f9f5957

- **0:02–0:05 — Browse:** From Memory Wiki, Browse Knowledge opens the selected agent’s list. Opening *Quartzmeadow field notes* shows “The inventory contains one cobalt ceramic van.”
- **0:07–0:12 — Search:** From Memory Wiki, entering `Quartzmeadow` returns the same note. Opening the result shows the same body and selected agent. Both detail routes were also asserted to contain the ID returned when that note was saved.

**Regression, red → green.** The [same focused test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/70dd8151df02683892d51b0e1df8e8f94a88d8b5/ui/src/pages/agents/memory/view.test.ts#L536-L567) ran against both versions. On base `9d39d4d8` with only the test added, it failed at the first behavioral assertion: expected the panel to contain `318 pages` (one failed). On the published tree it passed, including the Search submit and Browse click assertions (one passed). The other 20 tests in this file were filtered out for this comparison. Command for either version:

`pnpm --dir ui test src/pages/agents/memory/view.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'offers native Knowledge navigation even without curated Wiki cards'`

- In the original checkout, a disposable Gateway and Chromium opened the same synthetic record and body through both Browse and Search with the default Wiki settings. The fixture also exercised a compiled wiki with one source, nine reports, and no overview cards. The original focused run passed 104 tests, with one opt-in test skipped.
- This worktree’s nine-file diff matches the original byte for byte. Here, all 34 focused navigation, settings, and Wiki view tests passed, as did the Control UI i18n verification and `git diff --check`.
- Bound autoreview checked the complete local change against `9d39d4d8f535eb2bb7b8f4eb0edd86cbc56dd13c` at P0–P3: no findings. It did not independently exercise reader access; the disposable browser flow is the behavioral evidence.

The screenshots below show the real Control UI in Chromium, at a 1000 × 800 viewport with a synthetic vault (one source and nine report pages, zero overview cards). The baseline is `9d39d4d8`; the candidate is `18a3ed21`, whose Git tree matches the published head. On the candidate, Browse and Search opened the same saved record and body for the selected agent. Both disposable Gateways stopped after verification.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: the compiled Wiki is described as unpopulated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bcdfc331-5ffb-449d-9994-98644e18d870)

**After**

![After: the panel offers Knowledge search and browse, and reports ten pages with no overview cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61cefb81-0095-4a4b-bc6d-360dd4209052)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The old empty-state message is highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec0afa90-8ab1-4201-b27b-a4aa1231eac9)

**After**

![The new search and browse controls are highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/752cfb66-1109-40f9-a7dc-6c8dbc7528f5)

<details>
<summary>When the wiki actually has zero compiled pages</summary>

The same two UI builds, rendered in Chromium with the repository’s mock Gateway returning zero pages. This isolates the empty state; it is not a screenshot of a still-rebuilding dashboard.

**Before**

![Before: the empty message does not distinguish an empty wiki from a compiled wiki with no overview cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e5de0c5-d101-4c2e-b5b0-d7c78e4ffe90)

**After**

![After: No compiled wiki pages yet, with Knowledge navigation available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0ffa08e-1e33-4278-bedb-5c84bcfacb10)

Closes #207072

## What Problem This Solves

The dependency check fails on `main` because the CLI exports `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation` even though only the same file calls it. Early failure diagnostics make the same decision separately.

## User Impact

CLI behavior is unchanged. For `agent` without `--local`, normal startup and early failure diagnostics still select the gateway dotenv loader. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

[#205382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205382) moved the startup caller into `loadCliStartupDotEnv`. The predicate now lives in `argv-invocation.ts`, where both startup and diagnostics can use it. The existing container and `agent exec` diagnostic exclusions stay ahead of that check. No Knip rules or tests changed.

## Evidence

On CrabBox AWS at `4e06d657`, `pnpm deadcode:report` exited 1: both the production and full-tree scans named the unused export. On the [AWS run for `6e930925`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_34fb53dea888e3ad92a69de22903d17b), the checked Git tree matched the commit. All three Knip scans, all 8 profile-env tests, and the format check passed. The lease was released. The full test suite was not run.

prs.title: feat: explain pasted errors in Ask OpenClaw
prs.body:
Related: #205372

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenClaw command fails, the error can leave you unsure what to do next. Asking a model for help is particularly difficult when model setup or the local config is what failed.

## User Impact

In a ready Ask OpenClaw chat or the setup TUI, type `explain error:` followed by a redacted error line. On the command line, use `openclaw setup --explain-error 'OpenClaw config is invalid'` for local guidance. Add `--json` for a single `reply` field. This mode does not require a model or a valid config. Existing scripts using `setup --message` keep their inference check, exit status and JSON output.

## Why This Change Was Made

One catalog provides a likely cause and one safe next step for recognized errors. It does not run the suggested command. A dedicated CLI flag keeps offline help separate from inference-backed messages. In chat, the explicit prefix treats the paste as data rather than a request to execute it. The server saves a placeholder, but the client may display the original: remove private values before sending.

## Evidence

- [CrabBox AWS main comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1d1e5a7cd6c11bafb0999ad47d24b7dd): with no configured model, main `5aa4b8d4d291` and candidate `760f11519bfd` both exited 1 for `setup --json --message 'explain error:'` with identical `error`, `guidance`, `ok: false` and `status: "unavailable"` values.
- [Final-head AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d7068d5a9fd87e31e9db29a508af84e8): `58e176e006a0` matched that main output. With a configured but unreachable model, ordinary and prefixed messages both exited 1 and returned identical timeout JSON. With a working loopback fixture, the prefixed message exited 0 and returned the original overview shape, not a `reply` object.
- With malformed JSON on disk, `--message` retained its exit-1 `cli_error`; `--explain-error` exited 0 in both plain and JSON modes and suggested `openclaw config validate`. Combining the offline flag with `--wizard` failed. An offline-flag spelling passed as the value of `-m` remained a normal message.
- The final runtime build and 73 focused tests passed. The final-head check did not use an external inference provider or rerun the browser and TUI flows. [Compatibility repair and verification with @daniel-lxs](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-205382-and-206615-review-fixes-s3e9b8445).

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ed7f131e-8116-453e-912f-77cd26b2192e)
