prs.title: fix: keep Home in its workspace when starting project work
prs.body:
Related: #202306, #191622 (already-moved conversations are outside this fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Asking Home to work on a registered project could move Home itself into a new checkout. Later turns would then read and write in the project instead of the agent workspace, even though the user never chose **Move to project…**.

## User Impact

Home keeps its identity, history, and workspace. When project sessions are available, Home can start the work in a separate checkout. Other eligible conversations can still move, and an operator can still explicitly move Home. No migration or configuration change is needed. This does not undo existing moves or change PR publication adoption.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt previously told every eligible default-workspace conversation to move as its first tool call. Home now gets project discovery and separate-session guidance instead. The model tool also refuses a retained move call before handing off the turn. The tool schema uses the config selected for the run, including a configured Home key. The hint does not name a spawn tool that might be unavailable. The existing operator move and worktree allocator need no change.

## Evidence

- A disposable Gateway with a real Home session and a scripted provider reproduced the bug on `32b39885e8c7`: the same Home ID acquired the project checkout, and Files served its root.
- Revised head `a8385c6bf056`: published tree `1f83ec271eac` matched the locally tested tree. The disposable-Gateway regression passed (1/1): Home kept its key, ID and file root; a separate session owned and read the checkout. A retained model call could not relocate Home. Ordinary chat and an explicit operator move of Home both succeeded.
- **Required prompt-prefix gate:** `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passed **16/16** on the revised production code, part of **116/116** focused tests. Config-conflict and no-spawn hint cases passed. Core typecheck, formatting, changed-file lint and whitespace checks passed. The final commit changed only the Gateway test fixture.
- The first revised Gateway run timed out in the ordinary-chat control. The final fixture gives each scripted request a distinct trigger without relaxing any product assertions. Scoped static autoreview found no P0 findings in the revisions. The scripted regression does not exercise a live provider; the separate real-model receipt is below. No live-channel, seven-day GC or production recovery test is claimed.

### Real-model QA receipt

**PASS on the reviewed head.** @TheAngryPit supplied this redacted receipt in response to [ClawSweeper’s proof request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206695#issuecomment-7220108419). It is an operator-run observation, separate from the scripted regression above.

- **Build and isolation:** 2026-11-27 14:49:56–14:50:58 UTC. A disposable, loopback-only QA Gateway ran the checkout’s `dist/index.js`; `dist/build-info.json` reported `a8385c6bf05644fd809ecb97fec0be5a32942076` and the CLI banner showed `a8385c6`. Fresh state and workspace, no channels or delivery, heartbeat disabled, default product guidance and tools. Model: `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` via `openai-responses`, with no fallback. Two prior sign-in attempts ended before any model reply. This was the first and only attempt that reached the model.
- **Uncoached prompt to Home:** `Let’s work on Juniper.` via `chat.send`. Home called `session_project {action:"list"}`, received the registered `juniper` project, then called `sessions_create`. The receipt returned `<child-key>`, `<child-id>`, and `runStarted: true`. Home replied: “Juniper session started. What should we tackle first?” Direct and Code Mode calls were both observed; duplicate creation returned the same child key. There was only one child.
- **The child—not Home—moved.** On its first turn the child called `session_project {action:"move", projectId:"juniper"}` and received “This conversation moved into the **Juniper** project.” Gateway inspection showed one managed checkout owned by that child. This was a two-step route, not a `sessions_spawn` call. No file read occurred on the child’s first turn.

| Gateway observation | Before the prompt | After routing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home key / session ID | `agent:main:main` / `<home-id>` | Same key and ID |
| Home project / worktree binding | None / none | None / none |
| Home Files root (`sessions.files.list`) | `<home-root>` | Same `<home-root>` |
| Child checkout | No Juniper child | `projectId: juniper`; `worktrees.list` owner = `<child-key>`; child Files root = `<juniper-checkout>` |

**Separate verification turn:** Asked “What does project-marker.txt contain?”, the already-created child listed its checkout, read the file, and answered with the per-run value `<marker>`. The operator verified it matched the committed marker. That read proves work in the child checkout; the earlier unprompted tool calls prove routing. The QA Gateway was stopped afterward. This demonstrates the invariant for this run, not that every model will choose the same route.

**Release nomination:** P0 blocker for the next stable release containing #202306, not a stable-production P0. The separate #191622 trigger shipped in older stable versions. #196168 isolates new local publications in v2026.11.10; we recommend at least P1 for already-adopted sessions with no same-session return. A Home with a collected checkout cannot start a turn until explicit restore. Two of four linked scratch screenshots were already missing in the reported development-build incident; no transcript loss was established.

### Release evidence

<details>
<summary>Public evidence pack: observed impact, stable tags, idle cleanup, and failure wording</summary>

**Nomination:** treat prevention as a **P0 release blocker for the next stable cut containing #202306**, not as a P0 incident on stable. Separately, please consider **at least P1 for #191622**: Home sessions adopted by older stable publication flows have no supported same-session return. This PR fixes the model move, not publication adoption or return.

| Evidence | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Reporter observation, Nov 25–27, development build `14bac143` | An ordinary request to work on a registered project moved the same Home without an operator move. Its channel traffic continued in the checkout. Over about 37 hours the reporter counted 67 user messages, 617 assistant messages and 17 distinct file paths after the boundary. Two of four distinct linked proof screenshot paths were already missing from 24-hour scratch storage. That is observed file unavailability, **not transcript loss** or proof that idle GC caused it. No private paths or transcripts are needed to reproduce the bug. |
| Disposable Gateway | An ordinary project request changed Home’s root on the base revision; Files served the project checkout. With prevention, Home kept its key, ID and file root, and a separate session owned the checkout. Explicit operator moves and ordinary eligible chat moves still worked. |
| Runtime source | Session-owned checkouts become [eligible for idle collection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/agents/worktrees/gc-removal.ts#L519-L548) after the [seven-day idle window](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/agents/worktrees/retention.ts#L1-L2), with jitter and [owner protection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/agents/worktrees/owner-protection.ts#L68-L76). Home/channel routing is not itself an exemption. Once a checkout has been removed, [turn admission refuses it](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/agents/worktrees/session-lifecycle.ts#L36-L43); [rollover retains the binding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/auto-reply/reply/session-rollover-state.ts#L68-L77). Explicit checkout restore is not return to the configured workspace. No seven-day outage was observed on the reporter’s Gateway. |
| Stable reach | The model-move tool file is absent from the checked tags, including `v2026.10.34` and `v2026.11.6–v2026.11.10`. The local publication handler calls `adoptUnboundPullRequestWorkspace` in [v2026.11.9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.9/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github.ts) and each checked tag back to v2026.11.5. In [v2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github.ts) the handler calls `prepareGitHubPublicationTaskWorkspace` instead (#196168). The adoption helper’s presence in a tag does not establish that ordinary publication calls it. #206153 filters non-default workspaces but does not protect Home in its default workspace. |

**Failure wording:** the [Gateway product test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/src/gateway/server.chat-removed-worktree.product.test.ts#L98-L110) asserts restore guidance and the worktree ID on the terminal `chat` error event (test inspected, not rerun here). Four synthetic removed/missing-checkout cases exercised the resolver and returned that typed error. In a [Telegram non-spooled error branch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/extensions/telegram/src/bot-message.ts#L231-L269), a mocked dispatch propagating the error produced “Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again.” That is evidence for one branch only. No end-to-end Telegram, iMessage, Slack or Discord delivery was tested; do not assume all channels display “couldn’t finish this request.”

</details>

### Return decision

<details>
<summary>Decision document for #191622: same-session return and historical checkout retention</summary>

Gateway/session-storage and managed-worktree maintainers: please record whether you accept an explicit operator return for already-moved **and** publication-adopted sessions, ordered historical file sources, and custody of referenced checkouts. Keeping the physical checkout and branch for the lifetime of retained history consumes disk. Ordinary idle archival with time-limited restore is a weaker alternative; manual ownership alone is not lifetime protection. This proposal does not change future publication policy and is not a recovery runbook.

**Delivery order:** Land Home prevention independently. Its invariant is that an ordinary project request leaves Home in its configured workspace; which tool creates the separate project conversation is not a requirement. Keep isolation of new local publications in the release independently of return: [v2026.11.6 adopted the checkout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.6/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github.ts#L371); [v2026.11.10 already creates a publication task](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10/src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github.ts#L393) following #196168. Verify the selected release candidate retains that behavior; no duplicate publication fix is proposed. #191622 remains about conversations already bound to a checkout.

## Why the existing contract cannot serve a return

A project move and legacy PR workspace adoption both call `commitPreparedSessionWorkspace`. Each records the original file root through one transcript watermark. `prepareSessionFileWorkspace`, bulk file stat, and historical read checks consult that boundary while the current worktree ID matches. After it, a link is served from the current root. Clearing the binding loses the checkout-era source: a checkout-era link to `AGENTS.md` could silently return the Home file. Copying files, creating another chat or resetting the current one does not preserve the required identity and semantics. The PR adoption writer can have a worktree and no project ID; a return that requires a registered project ID would miss that case.

## Recommended contract

- The session workspace lifecycle admits an explicit return from a completed move/adoption. Keep the session key and window ID. Resolve the target from agent configuration, not a caller-supplied path. Use move-equivalent project/session authority and an expected session ID and lifecycle revision. At the transition boundary, idle means **no active turn and no queued input or other pending writer**. If either is present, refuse without changing the binding or the queue. Let the queued work finish in the old checkout before the operator retries. Check the actual binding; if its historical source cannot be established, refuse without mutation. Handoff at the turn boundary and invalidate only the next turn’s workspace bootstrap. Do not change reset semantics or rewrite the transcript as part of returning.
- Store source ranges tied to the session incarnation and transcript generation/watermarks. On the first return, consume the existing one-boundary record, close the checkout range at the current watermark, and start the configured workspace as the active source. An unpositioned Files listing uses the active root; message links, bulk stat and media serving use the positioned source. Identify a checkout by registry ID, not an absolute path alone. Resolve through current authorization and containment. Historical sources are read-only; do not revive stale edit tokens. Missing, expired, unauthorized, ambiguous or unrepresentable sources give **unavailable**, never an identically named current file.
- Transcript writers carry the relation for surviving or copied message identities, including compaction and replacement. A return adds metadata per workspace transition, not per message. Aim for no startup backfill or scan of the transcript at return; verify actual costs on synthetic long history. Retention follows surviving history, not merely whether the session is running. Compaction, transcript replacement, or deletion releases this protection **only when the last retained history reference is gone**, including any surviving copied messages. The checkout and branch then become eligible for normal cleanup under existing ownership rules; releasing history protection does not itself delete either. Scratch expiry remains unchanged. A historical checkout must not be selected as the active checkout by a subsequent move or adoption.
- Protect checkout custody before releasing the active binding. Both idle GC and capacity eviction at `worktreeMaxCount` must skip a referenced physical checkout and its branch. Evict an eligible unreferenced checkout instead; if none is available, refuse the new allocation without evicting retained history. The [inspected eviction path](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a6d787f18be79fa8d3a1ca13d51734f096c2b270/src/agents/worktrees/eviction.ts#L112-L123) captures a snapshot before purge, but a restorable snapshot is not the live checkout an old message links to. A crash or unknown write receipt must not expose an accepted historical checkout to either cleanup path. Re-read the lifecycle and registry before retry; do not reset or repeat an uncertain mutation. Retrieval is never authority to grant new filesystem access. Upgrade an existing one-boundary record on first return only if its sources are unambiguous; otherwise refuse without mutation. **Rollback:** an older Gateway must not serve state it cannot interpret. Demonstrate that the older binary refuses the converted store before serving Files, or require restoring a verified, consistent pre-conversion backup before starting that binary. A backup restore does not preserve subsequent turns; never perform it implicitly. An additive field that the older reader ignores is not a downgrade strategy.

## Separate proof required before shipment

On a disposable Gateway with synthetic data: write different bytes to the same relative filename in the Home and checkout roots. Use real messages and Files reads before and during the move; intentionally return the same session; send another turn. Assert the unchanged key, ID and prior messages, the effective default workspace, correct historical bytes in both ranges, unavailable rather than fallback for a missing file, and the new bootstrap only on the next turn. Repeat with adoption, including a worktree without a project ID; no GitHub publication is necessary for this proof. Also prove authority and stale-revision refusals, transcript rewrite carry-forward and a cold restart. The following are acceptance tests for the proposal, not results:

1. With no active turn but an input queued, return is refused and nothing moves. That input runs wholly in the checkout; after the queue drains, return succeeds and the next input runs wholly in the configured workspace.
2. Wait for a **completed** idle GC pass: an actually eligible unreferenced control is collected; the referenced checkout and branch survive. Separately hit `worktreeMaxCount`: evict an eligible control, then show a new allocation is refused when only protected checkouts remain. Old links still read the checkout bytes in both cases.
3. Upgrade state produced by an older release. Exercise the selected rollback procedure with an actual older reader and same-name files with different bytes: it must refuse incompatible state or use the verified pre-conversion backup, never silently serve current-workspace bytes.
4. Compact or delete history in two stages. With one surviving reference, the checkout and branch remain protected and readable. After the last reference disappears, prove normal cleanup can collect an otherwise eligible checkout.

[Related owner discussion: #191622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191622#issuecomment-6594403003) asks for a maintainer decision; its bot recommendation is not acceptance. [Repository review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/32b39885e8c7e1bd679b2c1cf70e17e40272c7e5/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes): “Before changing public contracts, schemas, durability, retention, or permissions, open or link a maintainer discussion and record acceptance of the design.”

</details>

Reported and scoped by @TheAngryPit.

## Worked on by

- @TheAngryPit

<!-- openclaw-publication:87d1d4fb-46ad-46ca-bf81-4b457511102b -->

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c99373a3-a033-48ef-8145-87c306f695d6)

prs.title: fix: keep the selected profile in onboarding next steps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After onboarding with a named profile, the skipped-service and skipped-AI next steps print bare commands. Copying those commands into a shell without an exported profile can select the default installation instead of the one just configured.

Bare commands already work when the shell exports OPENCLAW_PROFILE. This change preserves that behavior and makes the printed commands self-contained.

## User Impact

Onboarding includes the selected profile in its foreground Gateway command and the skipped-AI commands for onboarding, channels, and dashboard. Default-profile output stays unchanged. Existing container-hint precedence is preserved through the shared formatter. There are no configuration migrations or changes to service startup, model selection, or profile parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing formatCliCommand owner rather than constructing profile flags manually. Both skipped-AI branches pass formatted commands into the existing English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese translations. The explicit skipped-service message uses the same formatter.

The patch is limited to these next steps, not a CLI-wide wording sweep. The separate skipped-AI closing-headline change is not included and is not a dependency.

## Evidence

- Before the formatting change, four named-profile next-step cases failed at the missing qualified command, and the named-profile skipped-service case failed. Default cases passed. The first remote-chat fixture was corrected to accept setup risk before recording the actual boundary failure.
- Standalone patch: 84 focused tests passed across guided quickstart, setup application, and profile parsing/formatting; eight locale tests also passed. Both commands and services typecheck lanes, seven-file lint/format, and whitespace checks passed.
- Real source-built CLI in Linux PTYs with separate fresh HOME/XDG directories: explicit --profile novice-proof, exported OPENCLAW_PROFILE=novice-proof with no flag, and no profile each completed Quick start > One agent > Skip with exit 0. Named runs printed all four qualified commands and created no default-profile config. Default output stayed unqualified. No provider credentials or Gateway service installation.
- In the exported-profile environment, bare config file and explicit --profile novice-proof config file resolved the same named configuration.
- The standalone seven-file patch applies to pinned base 0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2 and matches the tested source bytes. Publication preparation independently reproduced patch SHA-256 4a86ead3529ad972f3c8eb07235dbfc30f7c9da8938578f7df26c916375f7336 and passed git diff --check. All seven baseline files also match inspected upstream 1ade2b7a8899ea45934f93e7ede48443dff7d515. Retained tests were reused because the patch and pinned inputs are unchanged; no fresh test run is claimed.
- The combined local headline/profile candidate additionally passed 42 onboarding tests; this does not replace either patch's independent proof.
- A user-authorized, isolated read-only reviewer reviewed the complete supplied patch and relevant source/test/formatter/translator snapshots against the pinned base at P0–P2 and found no issues. The reviewer did not rerun tests or independently verify base/hash bindings. Canonical Auto Review remains unavailable due its existing cachesInstructions configuration-schema incompatibility; no persistent configuration change or bypass was used.

Author simplification retains the existing formatter, translations, and test fixtures. No new policy parser, helper abstraction, persistent state, or dependency. Production +12/-6; tests +59/-11. Focused runner wall time: 47.14 seconds across three shards; locale suite 38.25 seconds including worker preparation. CI timings are unavailable.

The contributor reports independent macOS PTY replay of the pinned base plus this standalone patch: explicit, exported, and default profiles and config-path comparisons. The underlying macOS captures were not inspected in this closeout; this is not evidence on a refreshed head. Windows live replay, actual Gateway startup/status, normal inference, and container execution are not verified. The scope is printed next-step routing. This PR remains a draft. The [completed hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202183#issuecomment-7028564198) reviewed head 11ac9b6b69838e2af3fbfde57d53731c1a4e7d99 against upstream 1ade2b7a8899ea45934f93e7ede48443dff7d515 and reported no actionable code findings or introduced correctness defects. Its read-only review did not execute target code. The requested sanitized terminal excerpts for explicit, exported, and default profiles, with their exit/configuration receipts, are embedded below. They are the retained standalone-patch captures; the hosted review predates this evidence addition and did not independently execute these runs. No source change or test rerun was needed for this review outcome. The draft CI run skipped its main test/build lanes and openclaw/ci-gate, so exact-head broad CI is not verified and is not implied by the retained local proof.

### Retained real CLI captures

Added in response to the hosted review, from the already-completed standalone profile-patch runs on pinned base `0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2`. No rerun or combined-patch output is substituted. Each uses a separate fresh HOME/XDG environment, actual source-built CLI and PTY, and Quick start → One agent → Skip. ANSI escapes were removed, CRLF normalized, and isolated absolute home paths replaced with `[isolated-home]`. Startup/menu/progress output is omitted. The generic final headline is intentionally unchanged in this independent patch.

#### Explicit --profile novice-proof

```text
◇  Local setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                            │
│  Workspace: ~/.openclaw-novice-proof/workspace                                             │
│  Tool profile: full (tools.profile). This profile allows every tool, including files,      │
│  commands, the web and plugins.                                                            │
│  Gateway: service installation skipped. Run `openclaw --profile novice-proof gateway run`  │
│  to start it in the foreground.                                                            │
│                                                                                            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
◇  Next steps ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                                                    │
│  Workspace:                                                                                        │
│  [isolated-home]/.openclaw-novice-proof/workspace  │
│  Add AI later: re-run `openclaw --profile novice-proof onboard`                                    │
│  After AI connects, add a channel: `openclaw --profile novice-proof channels add`                  │
│  Open the dashboard: `openclaw --profile novice-proof dashboard`                                   │
│                                                                                                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  Everything's in place.
```


Terminal receipt:

```json
{
  "command": [
    "pnpm",
    "openclaw",
    "--profile",
    "novice-proof",
    "onboard"
  ],
  "mode": "explicit",
  "exportedProfile": null,
  "exit": 0,
  "steps": 4,
  "seconds": 63.2,
```

Published signed `b6ea12d3062cbf8b50d4cbe2e826cbfb161cb452`, tree `414757a92317e90779868cdb7232bda031ec2088`, integrates frozen main `b56baaec9b8bd79288e04b9b1f6189df8edc55e0`. **Canonical b56/b6ea paired budget gate PASS; normalized Chat 1,339,370 B <= unchanged MAX 1,339,420 B (50 B margin).** Functional evidence below retains its named source/dependency scopes. No CI/Claw redispatch is requested for superseded b6ea.

### Problem, owner, and canonical repair

Long native histories could remain strongly reachable through panes, projection/cache records, deferred work, and transcript layout after the resident window changed. Limiting rendered rows alone neither retired those sources nor provided lossless traversal.

Request/admission owns count/byte-aware windows, continuity receipts, cancellation/currentness, capacity refits and explicit outcomes. Native source identity stays separate from imported occurrences. Lossless older/newer traversal releases whole-conversation custody; physical snapshot suffix trimming preserves intrinsic/group accounting.

Transcript owners capture native facts before callbacks, measure current fractional geometry, use weak/scalar prepend facts and release settlement frames on reset. Reveal publishes before synchronous writes; settlement/anchor capture stay with the current observer through same-element reconnects. The existing input owner preserves wheel subscriber/nested-scroll rules.

Cold outbox/validators and Update/MCP English preserve eager admission, discovery, errors, receipts, labels and namespace identity. Ordered catalogs equal frozen main plus the capacity message. Pure MIME/auth-map initialization lets clients discard unused inverse-table/tuple reads; Node semantics, aliases/order/prototype, all 21 auth mappings and public resolvers stay intact. No new loader/config/compatibility path.

The b56 join records hidden delivery at the producer, correlates accepted-run custody before filtering, and ports the strict predicate to the extracted selector with a direct ID oracle. Completion receipts retain grouping/source state while the answer owns its header; named-grid alignment and router 0.1.3 lifecycle fixes remain.

Removed `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-older-history-page.ts`: paging uses canonical request/admission. `chat-thread-build.types.ts` becomes `chat-thread-contract.ts`. Owning modules also retire duplicate generation tokens, export-object adapters, reverse policy dependencies and obsolete strong custody. Main's prior removals are not credited here.

## Retained proposal and historical evidence

The material below preserves the original proposal and earlier evidence. Current functional scopes, paired/Chat-cap PASS, inherited diagnostics and pending landing gates are stated above.

## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

Integration is fixed at **b59c593cb0b7ad88ba2118768840c010e3253d95**, through signed native successors of earlier 650/21cd/ed40/99 integrations. The latest join preserves 13 reviewed manual resolutions and 20 clean overlapping postimages; this is source-composition evidence, not a current runtime pass. Navigation-only admission lives in the existing lazy packet runtime; ordinary hydration preparation stays eager, and successful navigation commits synchronously through the already-resolved module. The cold owner now preserves incoming boot boundary probing followed by at most one default 80-entry / 256 KiB fill. prs.body:
## Current CI repair — 6 November 2026

Head `034ba7118d534bcf956f3d8544b87f45120fbb4b` preserves the branch history and normally merges pinned main `8662f3bf78dc7d644d207c8afb6f2f8b8f5750b0`.

- The three failing Swift fixture initializations now specify the captured `role: "node"`; no identity, token, revocation or connection assertion was removed.
- The Node 24-only UI simulation supplies the TypedArray byte APIs required by the documented modern-browser/WebView floor and restores the original property descriptors after each test. Production byte encoders and device-identity paths remain those of main; experimental compatibility fallbacks were discarded.
- Native authorization reuses the existing translated credential error and one equivalent authorization-validation branch. The retired extracted parser had no references after main moved the live parser inline, so that duplicate module is removed.
- The scoped browser-API fixture adds 58 counted lines. Its existing feature allocation increases by exactly 58: the candidate adds 424 test lines against pinned main and records 424 lines of feature-specific credit. The shared scalar and all checks remain unchanged.

A fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review of this narrow repair found no actionable defects, including in padding/subarray semantics, descriptor restoration and preserved authentication guards. This is a supplied-patch/context assessment, not a review of the entire main integration or execution proof.

**Verification limits:** `git diff --check` passes. Earlier UI-build/performance measurements belong to their recorded intermediate source snapshots. The final local container refused its source-baseline preflight before running tests; therefore the new Node fixture, final build and native iOS compilation are **not claimed locally green**. Current-head hosted CI remains required. Intermediate runs with production byte fallbacks are not qualification of this candidate.

Pinned main itself is already 51 lines over its global test-line ceiling (6,550,629 / 6,550,578); the candidate's own 424-line delta is separately allocated, without hiding that upstream condition. CI/product acceptance is not waived. Historical proof below retains its original revision boundaries.

### Hosted CI follow-up — 6 November 2026

[Current-head CI 42276272124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42276272124) builds the automatic merge against newer main `0a6590652dc6465d5f055cf2d328104fc10514d1`.

- The actual Vitest module receipt reports **45 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** for `native-gateway-auth.node.test.ts`. All six test-type jobs passed; UI shards 1/3 and 2/3 and UI E2E 1/2 passed.
- UI shard 3/3 fails one Browser Panel refresh assertion (`null` versus `"false"`). Its test and `browser-panel.ts` blobs are identical on that main base and the CI merge. This establishes unchanged source, not an independent reproduction on main.
- Build artifacts, production types and downstream QA are blocked by Deep Research browser imports of missing `./client.js`. The browser directory contents and blob hashes match on main and the CI merge; this is outside this PR's changes.
- **Performance remains failing and is not attributed solely to upstream.** Main itself measures chat/new-session at 1,288,334 / 796,544 bytes, already above fixed limits 1,287,197 / 796,484. The candidate adds **453 bytes** to each, exceeding the 64-byte allowance for an already-over-budget base. Startup 89,934 / 89,946 and CSS 324,346 / 324,684 pass. No budget, guard or CI policy has been relaxed.
- The current test-line ratchet reports 6,552,094 / 6,552,042, 52 over, with the feature's exact +424 delta separately allocated. The earlier pinned-main 51-line excess above remains historical evidence, not a measurement of this newer base.
- Native iOS/macOS Periphery compilation is still running. The Swift fixture repair is not yet claimed native-green.

These results do not establish merge readiness. The unrelated upstream build failure and performance acceptance remain explicit gates; historical device and simulator evidence below retains its original revision boundaries.

---
### Native Dashboard admission refresh — 5 November 2026

Current head [`9868c3ddc8ead08d321d11cd765b85dd73b56c61`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163765/commits/9868c3ddc8ead08d321d11cd765b85dd73b56c61) removes only two allocation comments. Production and test blobs are identical to the qualified `fc9b5841` head below; allocation/line-cap ratchets and diff checks pass at this new head.

Head [`fc9b58417f0e3529bfe372cbc883048430fa297e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163765/commits/fc9b58417f0e3529bfe372cbc883048430fa297e) fixes two admission gaps: a matching personal recovery scope could be accepted from an unapproved Gateway boot, and the client could report connected before native admission. The existing admission owner now honors optional app-approved `expectedGatewayId` against `hello.server.bootId` and keeps connected pending until admission. Direct Serve callers without a boot expectation retain their existing behavior.

| Incremental proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original-production controls | Four intended failures: missing/wrong boot acceptance and connected before admission |
| Two focused UI suites | 63 passed; 1.92s Vitest duration with the documented single-worker cost measurement |
| UI types, typed lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line ratchets | Passed |
| Exact regression allocation | 48 net lines in a separate record; shared scalar unchanged |
| Fresh Codex AutoReview, Sol/medium, P0–P2 | `scoped-clean` for the supplied increment; shell access was denied, so unchanged-source inspection and independent test execution are not claimed |

This is UI bridge/handshake evidence. New-head CI and native execution remain separate; the existing PR merge conflicts were not changed by this increment.

### Earlier iOS identity proof

The selected `PersonalGatewayAuthenticationTests` passed on an ephemeral hosted iOS Simulator at head `6ff0ff5454ec618e07758204f388edf3c47495a1`: 14 tests, zero failures and zero skips. [Run 41636765728](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/41636765728) checked out the exact public commit and recorded the xcresult summary. This is simulator evidence, not a physical-device run or a replacement for canonical CI.

### Current integration and verification — 3 November 2026

Head `6ff0ff5454ec618e07758204f388edf3c47495a1` merges main `9066c989d58db469c2c748a5a8bec79b2eecdb29`, resolves the Dashboard connection conflicts and fixes live iOS roster reads in personal mode without enabling shared offline caching. A retired native connection plan is checked before it can affect the successor's admission.

The two affected UI suites passed 60 tests; targeted format, typed lint, and the test-line ratchet passed. The new held-plan regression failed on the expected leaked event without the currentness check and passed with it. The iOS roster fix previously passed its native 15-test suite and was verified on a personal device in a prior integration; native iOS execution on this new head remains outstanding. CI and maintainer review remain pending.

Related: #162164 (native identity umbrella), #136686 (cross-client personal sign-in).

## What Problem This Solves

iOS users need native chat and the embedded Dashboard to use the same Gateway-verified personal identity instead of grouping all paired apps under shared credentials.

## User Impact

Users can choose personal Tailscale sign-in when adding a secure Tailscale Serve Gateway, or change it through the visible control on an existing paired Gateway. Successful personal authentication is used for native chat and the existing embedded Dashboard/Profile; there is no second Profile screen.

Leaving the choice off preserves token/QR access. Personal sign-in does not grant administrator permissions, and a failed personal connection never silently falls back to Shared owner. Device/node admission stays separate from human operator identity. Personal mode still excludes persistent offline chat/outbox and Watch command delivery; existing saved history is not migrated or deleted.

The Gateway must serve the matching Control UI changes in this PR. Updating only the iOS app while retaining an older Dashboard parser is not sufficient.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app reuses existing Tailscale admission, signed-device challenges, connection settings and the Gateway registry. Pairing admits the node before starting the personal operator connection; route changes retire obsolete attempts. Trust/retry intent belongs to the matching connection attempt, not a recreated screen.

The Dashboard accepts credential-free Tailscale authorization only with a matching verified recovery scope. Its signing authority remains native and is retired on route changes.

Design help remains welcome: personal identity should follow the explicitly chosen and successfully verified authentication method. A Tailscale address alone is transport, not proof of a person. Broader Profile/account-linking UX, operator naming, local Mac Primary adoption and Cloudflare composition remain separate slices.

## Evidence

<!-- personal-ios-test-allocation-20261030 -->
### Test-line allocation, 30 October 2026

The separate allocation covers exactly 409 net regression lines for personal hello admission, credentialless native bridges, parser cancellation and retirement, and legacy iOS handoff. These checks exercise distinct protocol and lifecycle boundaries. One redundant device-ID assertion was removed because the retained complete-device comparison checks the same value. Every test case remains, and the shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

A secretless offline replay of the exact failed CI merge reproduced its original 410-line failure. The candidate passed the native test-line check, formatting, and all 69 tests in four affected browser and native-authorization adapter files. This is local adapter and gate proof; native iOS runtime, protected effects, revocation and upgrade qualification remain separate.



<!-- personal-ios-delivery-20261022:start -->
### Personal beta3 integration, October 22, 2026

A personal beta3 integration combining the required behavior from this PR and its companion #158051 was signed, installed over the existing iPhone app without uninstall/reset, and verified as `2026.10.10` / build `110994` with a launched process. The matching Gateway-hosted Dashboard UI was also deployed through the supported package updater, including a Gateway restart. Compiled backend/plugin bytes and the existing authentication policy were preserved; the macOS app was not changed.

This is **personal integration and installation evidence**, not a new exact-PR-head test run, official release, verified personal Dashboard session, final message attribution, revocation proof or full released-upgrade qualification. Three newly integrated native API tests remain unexecuted; physical Watch installation and preserved conversation contents are not claimed. The [October 22 delivery note in umbrella #162164](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162164#personal-beta3-integration-october-22-2026) records the cross-client dependency and remaining end-to-end criteria. Existing revision-pinned evidence below retains its original scope; the umbrella remains open.
<!-- personal-ios-delivery-20261022:end -->


### Current integration and qualification (2026-10-20)

Published head: `9838fd3baf043720cfdb4664d6db513ade8dc9f1`. It normally merges reviewed contributor integration `f96588f405b945b7bae87d8fc187991b0bd3efbb` with pinned main `3da32440469edba7c4b59ebc7d827fbe260e3ff5`. Both commits remain in history; this was a fast-forward update of the existing contributor branch, not a force push or upstream merge.

The latest main integration completed automatically. Of the 33 feature paths relative to that main, only `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` differs from the preceding reviewed integration: it includes main's Android attachment strings. The personal-auth, required-method/recovery-scope, connection-lifecycle, shared session and test files are unchanged. This is a bounded source comparison, not whole-main or native-runtime qualification.

Independent static review of the supplied preceding integration diff returned no actionable P0–P3 findings. At `f96588f`, the affected Control UI auth tests passed 51/51 assertions (11 gateway-connect and 40 native-gateway-auth); the six affected UI files passed formatting. The separate workflow suites passed 711/711, and native source inventory generation/verification passed at that preceding revision. These receipts are retained at their tested scope and revision; they do not mean the entire new merge, Swift, WebKit, a simulator, a real identity provider or a protected Gateway effect was executed locally.

The automatic [CI run 39480859811](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39480859811) completed successfully on this exact published head. At 2026-10-20 20:15 UTC, canonical checks showed 101 passed and 26 skipped, with no failures or pending checks; the PR was open, non-draft and mergeable. The policy statuses also passed after their automatic reconciliation. No contributor rerun, dispatch or second watch was used. Skipped native and release jobs are not executed proof, and successful CI is not maintainer product or authority acceptance. Earlier successful runs below remain earlier-head evidence.

Still outstanding: native personal attribution and an allowed protected effect; forbidden-principal denial; revocation/reassignment stopping pending effects before I/O; existing-data upgrade qualification; and maintainer product/authority decisions. Personal mode's offline-outbox and Watch exclusions remain. This does not implement personal identity for macOS local Primary. No disabled QA workflow was enabled or dispatched, and no new bot review was requested.

### Earlier published integration and qualification (2026-10-15)

The published head is 90e51342177437d9b2bedd338e232d480ecc07ae, a normal merge commit with parents 8ae893cc3f5a64a84d7c8e59d6b87abdd19ec9f1 and 236bdcb4cd3ab1cb6bf42a413a80a9405fd611d2, and tree fc53fc2edfc17c7311f9c9134de0083290ba95ca. It resolves the native iOS source-inventory conflict by regenerating apps/.i18n/native-source.json from the merged source; the generated delta adds the six inventory rows for four new native strings and main's source moves/removals. No translated locale file was edited.

The repository supports this source-only route: native source/inventory verification runs in the normal lane, while translated-locale refresh is handled after merge. The local native:i18n:baseline and native:i18n:verify commands passed. The strict full-locale check reports 84 missing localized values for the four new strings across 21 locales; the strict locale-parity job was skipped for this source-only change, so translation parity is not claimed. A scoped review of this generated inventory resolution found no actionable findings; its scope was the generated delta and source-only contract, not the full 33-file feature or runtime behavior.

The [automatic CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776996973) completed successfully for PR head 90e51342177437d9b2bedd338e232d480ecc07ae: 76 jobs succeeded, 18 were skipped, and none failed. The required [openclaw/ci-gate job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776996973/job/116581518819) succeeded. Workflow metadata identifies the PR head; the exact hosted virtual merge checkout commit/tree was not verified, so this result is not represented as proof that a particular local tree was executed.

Same-head [Shared OpenClawKit Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776996875) and [iOS Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776997087) completed successfully, including their applicable shared-kit and iOS scans. The [macOS Periphery workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38776996974) completed successfully, but its macOS dead-code scan was skipped after scope detection; that scan is not claimed as passing. The CI iPhone/iPad screenshot and screenshot-evidence jobs passed, but the iOS build and macOS Swift phases were skipped. Screenshot results do not establish native personal-auth runtime coverage. The docker-seed-e2e job also passed in the current run.

The PR remains open and non-draft. Product/operational proof and owner decisions remain open for native personal-chat versus protected-Dashboard effects, forbidden-principal denial, revocation or reassignment before pending I/O, released-install preservation of routes/credentials/settings/history/queued work, and the opt-in/offline-outbox/Watch exclusions. No architecture or behavior beyond the authorized conflict integration is claimed.

### Prior-head evidence retained

The earlier automatic CI run 38729878407 and its docker-seed-e2e job 116405372325 passed on an earlier head; the live-mode and cleanup-smoke checks were skipped. The attached earlier Docker failure 38314760469 remains unexplained and unassigned; the later success does not establish its cause or a causal fix. The previous scoped source review remains available at [the review comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163765#issuecomment-5961137563); its findings and scope are not recast as a review of this generated inventory change.
### Historical receipts (earlier heads)

Current head `0617f6b215b70c292d5928872360b28a8d469b9d` normally merges canonical main `0690a2ef175fc73d69d73105638b69a90af35fe6`. All 32 identity contributor paths, the existing focused native-test CI selection and the native source inventory are byte-identical to `76dcb5867dc565c7fdb024578dc5c1ac64c4497d`. It consumes canonical commit `11a1569887f`, which corrects the Dashboard route tests to expect the existing `rowMode: "dashboard"` query. There were no conflicts or new identity-source edits. Contributor whitespace checks and original commit hooks passed; fork and canonical head readbacks match exactly.

[Canonical CI 38140721782](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38140721782) remains failed in smoke-profile parts 2/6 and 3/6 and the aggregate gate. Both failing cases reported a readiness timeout after a forced in-process restart; the Gateway log reported failure to reacquire state ownership without exposing the underlying cause.

[Uninstrumented full-part proof 38162823598](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38162823598) passed both original parts on this exact product head: **3/3 scenarios in part 2 and 3/3 in part 3, zero failures or skips**. The selected cases include `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` and `subagent-empty-completion-recovery`, which failed in canonical CI. The workflow extracts the exact shell step from this head's `ci.yml`; both receipts and an independent source extraction match script SHA256 `804c55f3e5f668038edfba38b83b4a1fa501ba4961eadf94af3caf23b8714fd6`. Original requested concurrency 10, worker stagger 1,500ms, readiness 180,000ms and per-run 10-minute limit are unchanged. As in the original jobs, the planner isolates these flow cases: the aggregate records concurrency 3 and each child runs at concurrency 1. Positive counts, case selection, source-pristine receipts and completed logs were independently checked. [Part 2 artifact](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38162823598/artifacts/11711600134), [part 3 artifact](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38162823598/artifacts/11710064012).

The earlier [bounded diagnostic 38161188427](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38161188427) passed the existing run-loop suite (164 tests) and each failed case individually. Its reviewed QA-only cause logging was not applied in the full-part proof or published as a product fix. Both proof workflows use standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu in the public fork, synthetic inputs and no personal runtime or credentials; they were disabled after starting their single runs. They do not claim an identical canonical runner image or live personal authentication. The original failure was not reproduced, its cause remains unknown, and this PR has no speculative auth/lock repair. A maintainer must rerun the canonical jobs: this account has pull-only canonical permissions.

[CI 38137460530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38137460530) on the preceding head also failed in tooltip shutdown, SQLite built-CLI wait and an Android approval-dialog assertion. Their causes are not established. This merge is not a claim those three failures are fixed, nor evidence of an authentication regression. The fresh run must qualify the current head.

Preceding candidate `76dcb5867dc565c7fdb024578dc5c1ac64c4497d` integrates pinned main `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d` through a normal merge. All 32 contributor-owned paths are byte-identical to the preceding `830f5b8ae0b016c7ff4552705c2077eab26a0bd7` candidate. The sole conflict adopts main's markdown-table focus tests exactly. Upstream authorship and the existing Cloudflare ingress/admission owners are preserved. Personal auth is carried through the moved background-fleet owner and TLS trust/retry path; negotiated personal Tailscale auth still has no shared/device credential fallback and node admission remains separate.

The full 32-path integration received isolated Codex/Astra P2 review using exact public-source blobs. It found the duplicate Swift declaration; the correction received a scoped-clean follow-up review. `git diff --check` and the original staged-content hook pass. The six generated source-inventory additions were checked against their exact source literals and deterministic IDs.

[CI 38110487032](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38110487032) identified a Swift initializer argument-order error in the controller. The correction places personal auth before ingress authorization, matching the existing declaration and fleet caller without changing argument values. Its isolated P2 review completed with no actionable finding; original hooks passed and the published head was verified.

The earlier run failed two shared markdown-table focus tests. A test-only correction awaited the same expected buttons and passed scoped P2 review, pinned formatting and original hooks. That correction is now superseded by the exact canonical tests adopted in the latest merge. Production behavior, default timeouts, cancellation assertions and auth guards are unchanged.

[CI 38111749029](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38111749029) finished on `830f5b8`: all three UI shards, both iPhone/iPad screenshot jobs and all six QA profiles passed. Source-contract checking failed because the exact tested merge `b8eeaad3856bd927f0af6215da2f9cc3a0d64979` contained duplicate Doctor `intro`/`outro` exports. Current pinned main contains the upstream repair `3f08ea94a3373110e46b8f18cc4790344af4ecb3`; this PR consumes that repair without adding another Doctor implementation. The prior Gateway smoke failure is historical, not a claimed current-head result.

[Historical CI 38137460530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38137460530) ran on `76dcb586` and its failures are described above. Original merge hooks and exact public-head readback passed. No new full native build, visual or live-provider result is claimed by the current hosted smoke proof.

The following completed QA and CI belong to the previous candidate `706c6fccf7596f67f0504664bb3a74d7833dad65`, which integrated main `48c08e6ccba6b4cd12b2c7aafa75588abece6d18`. They remain historical evidence, not results for the new merge head.

The historical worker-setup failure was reproduced in the old merge, then traced to repairs already merged upstream: [`7ecc80a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7ecc80a457366091dd61448bcc319cf1a82a5da9) (setup/runtime-preference handling) and [#165166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165166) (concurrent placement-read/publication preparation). This PR integrates those repairs rather than duplicating a Core fix. Against that pinned main, the PR has no Gateway/placement or worker-setup fixture delta.

- [Exact-candidate isolated QA](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37266737400/job/111625056624): **102 tests passed** — owning placement/setup regressions (2 files / 27 tests), affected browser/native-authorization adapter tests (2 / 49), and the original 13-file real-Gateway E2E inventory (13 / 26). The previously failing worker-initial-setup case passed. Receipts verify product head, workflow `0721306776ae0691a0017645a30f4fef18702b7a`, frozen lockfile, Node 24.19.0 / pnpm 12.5.1, and clean product source before and after execution. [Receipt artifact](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37266737400/artifacts/11326064849).
- [Historical canonical CI at `706c6fcc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37266735131) and [its CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37267879156) passed. That incremental run's iPhone/iPad screenshot jobs passed; full iOS build/release-E2E and macOS Swift jobs were skipped, not newly verified.
- Independent Codex AutoReview of the full 32-file PR delta against pinned main completed **scoped-clean P2** before push. The separate fork-QA workflow also passed scoped P2 review. Review is static, not runtime or maintainer acceptance.

**Proof boundary:** the new QA used standard Ubuntu (4 CPUs), not the original Blacksmith runner. It verifies the integrated upstream repairs with the strengthened current fixture, not a byte-identical replay of the historical fixture. Ordinary real-Gateway E2E uses synthetic loopback admission; browser adapter tests are not a live personal Tailscale session. New full native authentication-suite execution, live protected administrative effects, revocation, second-principal/provider ownership, and App Store migration are not claimed. Earlier native/Simulator receipts remain stamped to their actual revisions below. This green CI does not claim a full repository build/check/test run or remove those live-service gaps.

<details>
<summary>Historical candidate receipts and earlier verification limits</summary>

These observations belong to the earlier candidates and their then-current CI. Their pending/failed checks are historical, not the current head's CI result.

Published candidate: `caf0363c3b0`, integrated with pinned main `c81d86e82f6022b5bcacf2b7ebe5bd0e7f3fcf20`. This adds a test-only repair to `9a29286`; the preceding native/parser receipts are at `020970f` and earlier slices, not a claim that every subsequently advancing main commit is integrated.

- Latest CI repair: the shared WebSocket fixture records the required connect role, but twelve existing expected frames omitted it. Expectations now explicitly assert `operator` for personal connections and `node` for legacy connections. The native `GatewayNativeTransportDeviceAuthTests` suite passed 7 tests (one with five parameterized controls) on the exact test patch; browser Gateway tests passed 45/45. Correct UI-chat test types, official focused Oxlint, formatting and two-file Codex AutoReview (scoped-clean P2) passed. Compiler warnings outside the changed assertions remain. No production authentication or role behavior changed. The unrelated Google Meet lint error from that CI run was not modified, and fresh hosted CI is not yet claimed green.

- `test-audit` found that the existing personal-mode Watch denial test opened the shared journal before exercising rejection, unnecessarily invoking legacy storage preparation. The test-only follow-up removes that setup, retains the actual admission error check and checks for no delivery warning. Source parity, pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.0 and independent scoped-clean P2 AutoReview passed. A fresh native rerun of this modified case is pending; no production auth, storage or Watch delivery behavior changed.

- Pairing regression failed before the repair (operator attempted before node admission); the repaired native selection passed 97 tests. After pinned-main integration, 140 selected native tests and 257 Watch-owner tests passed with no failures or skips.
- First-connection/settings verification passed 149 declared tests / 173 parameterized executions at the preceding integrated slice, including trust, retry, cancellation, target changes, saved-choice preservation and explicit off.
- Isolated Simulator Dashboard/Profile reconnect and automatic relaunch passed. A private-candidate over-install also retained the paired route without new QR or trust approval. These are Simulator/private-candidate observations, not App Store migration or every personal Gateway's compatibility.
- The final parser change passed 40 focused tests, UI typecheck, scoped lint and formatting. Official same-input comparison: startup JavaScript 373,444 bytes against the pinned baseline's 373,454 bytes; no budget or deadline was weakened.
- Independent Codex AutoReview completed scoped-clean at P1 for the integration repairs and the final three-file parser delta. Reviews did not execute tests or establish every live security boundary.
- The complete changed-file wrapper is **not green**: the final UI run stops at inherited environment-count drift (475 observed / 476 expected), also reproduced without the UI source change. No unrelated budget or source fix is included.

Vítor authorized publication using the completed QA and AutoReview, without additional visual proof on his personal installation. Existing sanitized recordings and the approved decision transcript are retained below as historical evidence, not final-head screenshots. Live second-principal/provider-ownership proof is not claimed. Simulator runs retain an unclassified responsiveness warning; the Watch suite retains audio-session main-thread warnings. Full repository build/check/test and new hosted CI are not claimed passed.

</details>

### Historical iPhone recordings

**Embedded Dashboard — previously published recording, 5.2 seconds.** Settings loads and remains rendered. This is visible Dashboard behavior, not a trace of authenticated administrative side effects.

<img width="300" alt="iPhone embedded Settings Dashboard loads" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/046082e6-b00f-449d-8aad-9cefb6301261" />

**Authentication selector — same previously published recording, 3.3 seconds.** Shows full access followed by the long-press menu offering “Use Shared Owner.” The clip demonstrates availability; it does not show executing that choice.

<img width="300" alt="iPhone authentication selector on a personal route" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/287517e7-4370-4144-a353-44c83f33c5d0" />

**Existing Profile — earlier recording, 4.3 seconds.** Shows Settings → the existing Profile and management permission. Historical evidence, not final-head Profile proof; personal details are redacted.

<img width="300" alt="Earlier recording of the existing embedded Profile" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5a035f3-c4bd-4be4-ba14-2f70d5d9d4c6" />

**TLS trust/reconnect — earlier recording, 6.5 seconds.** Shows a trust prompt, reconnecting and Settings. Historical evidence; it does not establish a visible Trust-button click. Fingerprint and private details are redacted.

<img width="300" alt="Earlier TLS trust prompt and reconnect sequence" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d5220fa-185f-45bd-a15c-6765d1a14871" />


<!-- agent-transcript:start -->
<details>
<summary>Agent transcript: Vítor's identity model, compatibility requirements, testing corrections and vanilla-first design decisions</summary>

**Scope and provenance.** Selected dialogue from September 30–October 2, 2026, checked against the original session rollout rather than reconstructed from an agent summary. The quotation blocks are English translations of Vítor's original Portuguese dialogue, not verbatim English speech. Obvious transcription errors and product-name misspellings are normalized without changing the intended meaning; `[…]` marks omitted portions. The surrounding explanations are editorial summaries, not invented dialogue. This is a partial, task-scoped transcript, not a complete session export. The original helper reported `sourceTruncated: true`; this expanded selection was independently checked by streaming the original rollout. Raw logs, tool output, instructions, private endpoints, account identifiers and unrelated work are excluded.

**Authorship.** Vítor supplied the product rationale, constraints, test observations and corrective decisions below. The assistant investigated and implemented the candidate, but does not claim authorship of those human decisions. Proposed directions are not presented as shipped behavior or maintainer acceptance.

**The governing idea is not “remove Shared owner” and not “always use Shared owner.”** Preserve shared/token access where that is the chosen admission model; allow verified personal authentication to identify the person instead of collapsing every app into the shared principal. Keep identity separate from permissions and device pairing. Vítor further questioned the word “Shared” for a single-user harness and proposed addressing that naming separately. These distinctions, rather than GIF preparation, are why the contribution exists.

### 1. The problem is person attribution, not a new role system

**Vítor — September 30:**

> This is not about roles. I don't want to change those for now; I want us to resolve Shared owner in the apps right now.

He distinguished the visible person identity from transport/client labels and permission policy. The immediate goal was to let native apps identify the person already authenticated, without redesigning roles or making every shared token claim to be a person.

**Vítor — October 2, comparing simultaneous clients:**

> All at the same time on my personal OpenClaw: three identities, one on Telegram, one in the app, and another in the browser's Control UI.

This was an operator-reported cross-client attribution problem, not proof that all three connections had the same verified principal. The distinction mattered: a personal display name or avatar alone must not be treated as verified identity.

### 2. Separate the person from app/device admission to a Gateway

**Vítor — September 30:**

> In other words, who you are in relation to that Gateway is one thing. Who you actually are is another. Do you see what I mean?

> At its core, the handshake between the app and the Gateway—or the apps and the Gateway, whatever the setup—is one thing. Your identity is another.

> And I can choose not to link any account and use a vanilla Gateway with a token […]

His conceptual model was a person who can interact through several apps or accounts, with Gateway admission remaining a separate concern. External-account linking must be optional; ordinary personal/local installations should remain usable through existing vanilla setup. This broader identity model motivates the umbrella; it is not a claim that this PR implements a portable global identity or changes Gateway trust policy.

He also asked to investigate existing enterprise/current-main behavior and reuse it if applicable, rather than invent another auth system. No enterprise implementation or maintainer approval is inferred from that request.

### 3. Keep Shared owner for compatibility; add personal adoption incrementally

**Vítor — September 30:**

> For compatibility reasons too, I don't want to lose Shared owner. It needs to exist, for now.

> I haven't configured that, versus I have configured authentication. So if I have authentication configured […] I should be able not to use Shared owner, do you see?

> I'm using multiplayer and want everyone to use the apps, but everyone in the iOS or macOS app appears as Shared owner. That doesn't make sense.

The retained requirement is compatibility with shared admission, alongside an explicit personal-authentication path for native human actions. The umbrella covers broader clients; this PR is the bounded iOS Tailscale implementation. Existing macOS personal sessions should be reused, not described as absent everywhere.

**Vítor — September 30:**

> But you need to look at this against current main, do you understand?

Current-main inspection was required before deciding what was missing. This transcript records that instruction, not a claim that the candidate is integrated with every subsequent main revision.

### 4. Profile is where optional identities should eventually come together

**Vítor — October 2:**

> We need a way to link people's accounts […] I should be able to say, look, this is my account, and add it to Profile, do you see?

> For anything that interacts directly with OpenClaw, such as channels, this matters, because otherwise the memory itself gets confused.

He connected attribution to an agent harness's longer-term memory: treating one human as unrelated app/channel identities can fragment the user's experience and memory associations. He reported that concern while using a memory integration; this is product rationale, not a measured memory-corruption result.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> And Profile should be where you link or configure identities.

> In more complex cases with multiple identities, such as channels plus authentication, they should all be able to belong to the same profile.

Optional account linking and a unified Profile belong to the umbrella's follow-up work. They must not turn this first slice into automatic account merging, role changes, or inferred identity equivalence between Telegram and an auth provider.

### 5. Authentication should drive identity, without removing the Dashboard

**Vítor — October 2:**

> You're using Tailscale Serve, but you haven't chosen to use Tailscale authentication, for example. That's fine: you use Shared owner. If you decide to use Tailscale authentication, you use Tailscale and automatically stop using Shared owner, do you see?

> In other words, I think this needs to be tied to authentication, do you understand?

The distinction is intentional: using Tailscale Serve as transport is not the same as choosing and successfully verifying personal Tailscale authentication. The preferred UX should follow the validated authentication choice instead of adding an independent “who am I?” switch. This is the requested design direction; the candidate still has the temporary explicit selector.

**Vítor — October 2, after reporting the missing native Dashboard:**

> Not having the Dashboard is unacceptable. If we've fixed the Dashboard issue and then introduce a regression ourselves in another fix, that makes no sense. We need both.

The requirement was **personal native attribution and a usable embedded Dashboard together**, with existing Gateway permissions respected. A chat-only fix that regressed Dashboard access was not acceptable. His report prompted the Dashboard correction; it was not an instruction to grant administrator permissions to every authenticated person.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> But logically, shouldn't it use whatever authentication the person has? Why complicate it?

> At its core, authentication should determine which auth you use, and Shared owner or Owner should be for when you don't have that and only have a token.

### 6. Upgrade observations must retain differences between saved setups

**Vítor — October 2, before replacement testing:**

> Let's test whether it breaks existing setups.

**Vítor — October 2, correcting an over-broad upgrade interpretation:**

> No, that's not what happened. My personal Gateway's setup was preserved. The other one wasn't—the Hive one wasn't. […] But mine, the normal one, started directly. […] We're also comparing different experiences.

The operator reported that one existing personal setup reopened directly while the other required QR pairing. His explanation of why the installations differed was tentative. The transcript must preserve the observed distinction, not convert it into “all saved routes upgraded without intervention” or a proven root cause.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> And we have video. We have the moment when I used the QR code; we have all of that.

> I think it's working. It connected and authenticated directly with the QR code, opened Profile, and my profile appears here.

**Vítor — later that day:**

> Right, but now I've recorded video and everything. […] You've fixed it, the Dashboard appears now; the UX question is where we put shared versus non-shared.

These are operator reports from physical testing. The attached GIFs show only their captioned portions; they do not independently establish complete cold-relaunch migration, forbidden final effects, or final-head coverage of every earlier observation. The remaining proof requests stay explicit rather than erasing the useful human observations.

### 7. Reuse the existing Profile; reject duplicated screens and shortcuts

The assistant introduced a separate native Profile wrapper and entry points while trying to make the selector discoverable. Vítor rejected that direction.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> The problem is that a Profile screen already exists. Creating another one makes no sense. None at all.

> And then you put shortcuts to that screen in several places. What sense does that make? It's vanilla first.

The correction was to remove the duplicate UI layer and keep the existing embedded Profile, personal admission and Dashboard work. That rejected UI experiment is not part of the reviewed candidate. The temporary selector should not be disguised as the final discoverable UX.

Vítor also explicitly requested the upstream `test-audit` workflow, not merely a generic principles review, and later checked that it had actually been used. The test cleanup removed redundant assertions without changing production behavior; its verification is reported separately in the PR evidence.

### 8. Small PRs, separate naming follow-up, and lead-designer integration

**Vítor — October 2:**

> Shared owner doesn't make sense unless it's a multiplayer harness. Otherwise, what does Shared mean? Shared with whom? […] I think we should keep it, but we need to think about this.

> Yes, but Shared should only be for multiplayer.

> We should split this into small PRs under the umbrella. One of them should cover those two options for Shared owner.

Naming “Owner” versus “Shared owner” for single-user/multiplayer contexts is a proposed separate small contribution. It does not authorize silently renaming the current shared principal or removing its compatible behavior in this PR.

**Vítor — October 2, authorizing this PR's temporary UX and design request:**

> Make the PR like this and ask the lead designer to help us integrate it. But suggest synchronizing it with authentication: if it's Tailscale, activate it automatically, as I already told you.

**Resulting contribution boundary:** ship no duplicate Profile, preserve existing shared admission, carry verified personal identity into iOS human operations and the embedded Dashboard, and ask the lead designer to integrate selection/recovery with the existing auth/Profile flow. Automatic identity adoption, account linking, naming, broader native-client adoption and maintainer acceptance remain separate proposals or gates. The transcript explains the human decisions behind the candidate; it is not a replacement for security or runtime qualification.

</details>
<!-- agent-transcript:end -->
