prs.title: refactor(skills): load procedures for the selected operation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #207107.

Several OpenClaw skill entrypoints inline complete workflows for mutually exclusive platforms or operations. An agent opening one for a narrow task loads unrelated procedures before selecting the actual operation.

## User Impact

Maintainer and contributor agents can load the selected procedure in full through an explicit required-read link. Across seven entrypoints, initial content drops from 152,784 to 57,983 bytes (62%). Entrypoints retain shared authority and safety boundaries and require the selected procedures before execution or proof acceptance.

This changes skill documentation loading. It adds 17 small reference files and approximately 7 KB overall; it does not claim to reduce installed file count or fix a dependency/cache leak.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move existing platform, changelog generation/mirror, release validation/lifecycle, live-maintenance, duplicate-triage, and plugin-proof procedures into task-specific references. Auto QA reuses its existing lane and live-proof references. Preserve original entrypoint heading anchors and command examples; adjust relative links and positional pointers for their new locations. Update the existing dispatch-documentation test to read complete skill bundles with the existing directory walker, preserving all assertions.

This is a maintainer-requested continuation of the skill cleanup in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/207053. That merged ownership change remains complete.

## Evidence

- All seven skill entrypoints pass the skill validator.
- All 26 changed Markdown files and the changed test pass repository-pinned oxfmt 0.74.0; `git diff --check` passes.
- Source-preservation comparison retains the moved instructions and all fenced command examples. Original entrypoint heading anchors remain; 74 relative Markdown links and anchors resolve.
- Independent routing checks pass for platform/update prerequisites, changelog/docs mirrors, release authority and failed validation, live maintenance/full validation, Auto QA rendered/remote evidence, duplicate setup/writes, and candidate-versus-diagnostic plugin proof.
- Final local ClawSweeper review of `94ae31d8491dc0f3215f2acc94ee70032e5776e4..47789b3f2bdf3990e4a3aafd343c23d41305ace4` reports no actionable correctness or security findings. Its documentation-test consumer finding is resolved.
- The existing documentation test body passes with the real directory walker and native Node assertions. CI also passed all **592 tests** in the affected workflow test file.
- Current exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46096886210) **passed**. Local Vitest and changed-check tooling were unavailable because this managed worktree has no qualified dependencies; CI supplied those checks.
- An earlier [manual CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46095952431) hit the existing Knip exports `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`, matching [main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089297581/job/140806522333). Those production inputs are untouched; the current PR CI above is successful and no inherited-failure merge exception is needed.
- Production LOC: +0/-0. Test LOC: +9/-2. No runtime or deployment behavior changed.

prs.title: fix: keep agent work moving past recoverable setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #204343 (reported during review; no Telegram changes).

## What Problem This Solves

A reviewer failed to start even though the correction had passed its tests. The agent handed setup back to the requester before trying supported recovery. Skipping that handoff left the requester having to ask again for work that did not depend on it.

## User Impact

The agent tries recovery it is already allowed to perform before asking for help. Skipping a manual step or letting it expire leaves dependent actions blocked, not the rest of an active request. Choosing **Stop this task** still means stop. If the user sends a new instruction instead, the agent follows that message without treating it as completion of the manual step.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct tools and Code Mode share the pre-handoff guidance. The existing `action_unresolved` result now carries the next action for its actual reason, so Code Mode does not lose the distinction when it receives structured data rather than display text. The same result producer preserves the composer replacement behavior from main. No approval, review, sandbox, or tool permission changes.

## Evidence

- Two unscripted turns on an isolated Gateway exercised the original fix on `82dec2b8174d`. With a missing primary review record, the agent used the documented mirror and wrote the decision and the independent tracking file without asking. After one Skip, it wrote the independent file, left the device-confirmation file absent, and did not ask again. The original 74 focused tests passed; [ClawSweeper found no actionable code issues on that head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204353#issuecomment-7121309564).
- The existing branch conflicted with main in the tool’s unresolved-result producer. On main `595c201f9f79`, a composer replacement returned `cancelled` without the instruction to follow the new message in structured data; the focused regression failed on precisely that missing field. On `971529aa8e87`, it passed. All 63 tests for tool results, model-facing descriptions, and prompt stability passed in 68 seconds. Core typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The earlier live runs were not repeated for this integration.
- [CI on the old head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45319110530) had 14 failing jobs; its 39 distinct diagnostics matched [an earlier independent run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312232532) and [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312791464). The new head includes [the upstream compaction fixture correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204443). All 43 tests across the three previously failing files passed locally on the published head (235 seconds), including both compaction replay cases, the scheduled-context budget and the preflight watchdog. It also includes [the upstream clean recovery-ref fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206830) for the [worktree failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45319110530/job/138194004473).
- **Landing remains blocked.** Git compares five changed paths against `main` at `595c201f9f79`; GitHub still compares against `0b295654fa14` and reports 9,493 files. [Dependency review and the CI gate are red](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097691131); [the exact-head ClawSweeper request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204353#issuecomment-7232321776) ended with a policy veto, not an accepted review. Use the [stale-comparison recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/595c201f9f7901baf2922490c3d07607a3e4394a/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/triage.md#recover-a-stale-pr-comparison) and verify the five paths before retrying the affected guard or review. Local tests do not waive either gate.

Reported by @VACInc.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

<!-- openclaw-publication:e39cb036-1a07-4e01-ae07-857ce60d349b -->

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a7a4e0e7-7845-4a9b-a26c-a32609f909d2)
- [Assigned PR sweep with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4591147b-d110-4a05-a692-35247ed3a855)

prs.title: fix(agents): apply the role model policy to every utility consumer
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Follow-up to #206962 (Activity recaps vs operator role model policy). The same role refusal reaches four other utility consumers, and the recap still retried its other owner refusals.

Real-user log signature (a production team Gateway; 331 on 2026-11-27):

```
[activity-summary] Activity recap deferred
  error: Your operator role cannot use this model. …
```

The Gateway's default role allows only main-chat models, so every utility model is refused for its sessions.

- **Progress narration** ignored the turn's role and ran the refused utility model (policy bypass).
- **The session observer** had no role check at all and ran the utility model for every session (bypass).
- **Titles** tried the refused utility model first, logged a false "Conversation label generation failed" warning, then made the regular-model pass.
- **The recap** turned "operator profile unavailable" and "role cannot access this agent" into a 120 s retry, re-run on every later activity.

## Change

`resolveUtilityModelSelectionForAgent` stays the one owner; each consumer now asks it with the relevant role:

- **Narrator:** uses the turn's `operatorAuthority`. A refusing role attaches no narrator. The narration completion carries the authority, so execution skips refused candidates in a partly allowed chain.
- **Observer:**
  - Resolves the session owner's role once per run through the recap's existing session-owner authority. The digest is persisted and shown to every viewer, so the owner's role applies.
  - An owner role that excludes the agent or refuses every utility model turns the run's observation off quietly: no degradation notice, no retry. A session whose owner profile was deleted still gets observation.
  - The authority reaches the completion.
- **Titles** (dashboard and channel thread): a refusing role makes no utility attempt and no warning. The documented regular-model title pass still runs; that is the session's own permitted model.
- **Recap:**
  - The authority returns a typed refusal instead of throwing.
  - A refusal ("profile gone", "role excludes the agent", "role refuses every utility model") publishes `unavailable` with no model call, no retry and no log line. The next activity asks again; a config or role change applies there with no extra state.
  - A role-changed read race keeps its existing retry.
- **Status and Doctor:**
  - When the Gateway substituted the agent's primary because no utility model is offered, `openclaw models status` shows `<model> (utility model not offered; using main model)`. A provider whose declared small model is the primary shows no note.
  - `openclaw doctor` reports the same line as an info finding.
  - No wire change.

## Not changed

- **Side chat:** it already makes no refused attempt. When the role refuses the utility route, it answers with the role's first permitted model, so a user's question is never refused.
- **Nothing offered at all** (`not-offered` with no listed primary): behavior unchanged from main.

## User population

- **Gateway:** multi-user Gateways whose operator roles refuse the utility models. Affected surfaces: narration in replies (`get-reply.ts` → `progress-narrator.ts`), observer digests (`session-observer.ts`), dashboard and thread titles, and Activity recaps.
- **Gateway and CLI:** `openclaw models status` and `openclaw doctor` users whose automatic utility routing falls back to the primary.

## Evidence

| Consumer | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Narrator, role allows only the main model | narrator attached; runs the refused utility model | options returned unchanged; no narration attempt |
| Observer, owner's role refuses the utility model | completion runs the utility model, no authority | refusal; 0 completions; the allowed case passes the owner's authority |
| Thread title, role allows only the main model | false "Conversation label generation failed" warning, then the main model | no warning; one completion on the main model |
| Recap, owner profile gone / role excludes the agent, 4 activity rounds 130 s apart | 120 s retry armed each round | 0 attempts, 0 retries; a committed config change lifts it on the next activity |
| Status, Gateway substituted the primary | `<model> (provider default)` | `<model> (utility model not offered; using main model)` |
| Status, provider's declared small model is the primary | - | `<model> (provider default)`; no note |
| Doctor, Gateway substituted the primary | - | info finding "utility model not offered; using main model" |

### Real CLI on an isolated Gateway

Each scenario runs its own Gateway (loopback port, empty `HOME` and state directory, `env -i`; no other OpenClaw state). The provider is a local fixture plugin, `w9-fixture`. Its manifest declares `defaultUtilityModel: "small"`, and its catalog `run` returns a `ready` outcome listing exactly the configured ids. `plugins.allow` holds only the fixture, so the published inventory is authoritative, as on a Gateway whose providers are all signed in. Base is this PR's merge base on `main` (`501ee911`); head is `ab1120a`. Same commands on both sides.

**(a) Utility model not offered.** Primary `w9-fixture/main`; the listing has only `main`. The Gateway publishes `{"modelRef":"w9-fixture/main","source":"provider-default"}` on both sides.

```text
# base: openclaw models status
Utility model : w9-fixture/main (provider default)
# base: openclaw doctor --lint --severity-min info --only core/doctor/model-references
(no findings)

# head: openclaw models status
Utility model : w9-fixture/main (utility model not offered; using main model)
# head: openclaw doctor --lint --severity-min info --only core/doctor/model-references
{"severity":"info","message":"utility model not offered; using main model","fixHint":"Configure agents.defaults.utilityModel with a model the catalog lists, or leave it unset to keep using the main model."}
```

**(b) The provider's declared small model is the primary.** Primary `w9-fixture/small`; the listing has `small` and `main`. Both sides print the same, with no note:

```text
# base and head: openclaw models status
Utility model : w9-fixture/small (provider default)
# base and head: openclaw doctor --lint --severity-min info --only core/doctor/model-references
(no findings)
```

An earlier head printed the note here from `doctor` only: Doctor has no current plugin metadata snapshot, so the declared model was invisible. `isUtilityModelNotOffered` now loads the manifests itself (`ab1120a`).

**(c) A role-policy refusal.** Primary `w9-fixture/main`; the listing has `main` and `small`. The default role `guest` allows only `w9-fixture/main`. The CLI connects as the token operator, so `models status` shows the agent's own selection (`w9-fixture/small (provider default)`) on both sides; a refused selection is not disclosed to a guest reader. The refusal and its reason come from config validation, identically on base and head:

```text
# base and head: openclaw doctor
[config] warnings: gateway.roles.definitions.guest.modelPolicy: Role "guest" allows no utility model for agent "main", so Activity recaps are off for sessions this role owns. Allow a utility model in this role's modelPolicy, or set a utilityModel the role allows.
```

Red on main (`501ee911`), green here: the recap "profile gone" and "role excludes the agent" cases (the retry was re-armed each round, with `Activity recap deferred` logged), and the title "no utility attempt or warning" case. The status and Doctor note is new; its tests cover the published wire shape and the declared-model false positive.

Checks on `ab1120adad`: touched suites green; `tsgo` core and test shards clean; oxlint, line-cap, session-identity and permission-read boundary checks clean; CI green. Local review: patch is correct, 0 findings.

Size: production about +200 lines; `list.status-command.ts` net −10 (the status field text moved to `list.status-utility.ts`).

prs.title: fix: honor native Control UI capabilities across gateway features
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native app UI connections can have the same operator permissions and supported capabilities as the browser Control UI but still miss startup model catalogs, agent-driven navigation, dashboard commands, or plugin guidance because Gateway paths check only the browser product ID.

## User Impact

Native Control UI clients can use the Gateway presentation features they actually support, without impersonating a browser or gaining additional permissions. This covers startup model catalogs, requesting-client UI commands and presentation results, capability-supported dashboard commands, and display-safe plugin notices in history, startup, delta reads, exact-message hydration, and live events.

This is Gateway-side parity, not full native-app UI parity. Native-mobile chat-first/navigation restrictions, Swift/Compose-specific plugin-notice rendering, and iOS lower-scope work-page entry policy remain outside this patch. No OS permissions, pairing rules, operator scopes, or configuration options change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one shared browser/native UI classification for the presentation paths that share that responsibility. Model-catalog startup honors its existing capability negotiation. Agent UI commands retain their required capabilities and exact requesting-connection/profile binding. Native dashboard recipients must advertise UI-command support, so an ordinary native chat socket is not mistaken for a dashboard renderer. Node-mode connections remain separate.

The existing plugin-activation checks now consume the same classification without changing their behavior. Display-safe plugin guidance remains separate from raw internal instructions, and existing session-sharing checks still govern reads and delivery. Inline native/CLI avatars, browser-origin authentication, and host-owned native navigation retain their existing contracts. The integration with `595c201f` keeps main’s exclusion of publication-only connections from catalog bootstrap.

## Evidence

**Real Linux desktop, head `8d0bace5072f`:** The checksum-verified OpenClaw 2026.11.10 Linux AppImage loaded the UI served by an isolated Gateway built from this head. The app rendered Settings → Models. Its authenticated UI connection issued the negotiated startup catalog request; the Gateway completed it on that same connection. Redacted Gateway trace:

```text
client connected  client=openclaw-linux  mode=ui  role=operator  build=2026.11.10-8d0bace5072f…
← req models.list  conn=[native UI]  id=catalog:[native UI]
→ res ✓ models.list  256ms  bytes=8723  conn=[native UI]  id=catalog:[native UI]
```

That trace proves the real native bootstrap reaches the catalog dispatcher. It does not show a WebView acknowledgement of `models.snapshot`, requester-only navigation, portal feedback, dashboard command application, or display-safe plugin guidance in the native renderer. No physical-device or native end-to-end pass is claimed for those features.

- **Browser:** [the hosted browser job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44257054709/job/134641852956) passed both requester-routing scenarios on the preceding head `cb90f1d7`. It used real browser pages, a mock Gateway, and a simulated native bridge—not the Linux app.
- **Current candidate:** The native catalog integration passed, as did the dashboard, UI-command, history, broadcast, and plugin-guidance tests (97 assertions reported as passing test cases across those five files). The gateway-server typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The UI built; its budget report flagged CSS gzip size and chat boot JS request count and size.
- **Original CI failure:** [this job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44257054709/job/134641853671) failed in the canceled CLI steer replay. This branch now includes the upstream repair [#201399](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201399); the exact failing test passed locally on the integrated candidate. No test was weakened or CI rerun for green.
- **Review and gates:** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200909#issuecomment-6966692683) found no actionable code issue on `cb90f1d7`; that is not a review of the updated head. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097844275) and [security/dependency review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46097841894) are separate from local evidence. At inspection, GitHub reported 16,415 changed files against a stale PR base; Git’s three-dot comparison to current `main` reported 17. No gate waiver is requested.

<details>
<summary>Earlier focused validation</summary>

On the original candidate, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base HEAD --no-merge-base` passed after replacing the catalog timeout race with `await withinTest(native.published, signal)`. Startup catalog, UI command, dashboard, history, live broadcast, plugin-guidance authorization, plugin activation, client-info, and protocol package checks passed. The original Gateway-side red/green tests included negative controls for capabilities, node-mode exclusion, session sharing, and recipient isolation. Local independent Auto Review was unavailable; the preceding head received hosted review instead.

</details>

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2faef201-83cd-43d4-a648-fd558efc9c1e)
- [Assigned-PR sweep with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4591147b-d110-4a05-a692-35247ed3a855)
- [Conflict repair and native verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d41eb478-309a-445c-bfa6-1fc46cfc99fb)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw `v2026.11.11` is tagged at `a257c0f4d6bcc313d116427963d884add5aad17f` (`v2026.11.10..v2026.11.11`) and needs its complete patch release notes page, native Markdown changelog mirror, and release navigation entries published to `main`.

## User Impact

Readers get the complete OpenClaw v2026.11.11 patch release notes at `/releases/2026.11.11` and as plain Markdown in `CHANGELOG/2026.11.11.md`, covering 90 user- and operator-facing fixes across updates, Doctor recovery, models, messaging, memory, skills, apps, Web UI, automations, plugins, browser handling, and security. No runtime behavior or existing release records are changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR uses the compact patch release-notes format across the 13 populated canonical release groups, keeping 44 maintainer-only CI, test, benchmark, locale-metadata, and release-script changes in internal accounting while preserving full release-wide counts (`100 pull requests, 34 direct commits, and 39 contributors.`). The flat changelog mirror is generated directly by `scripts/render-release-changelog.mjs` from `docs/releases/2026.11.11.md`.

## Evidence

- **Tagged release endpoint:** `v2026.11.11` tag commit `a257c0f4d6bcc313d116427963d884add5aad17f` (tag object `5a26c34824d26fd1c42a3133c3112da543218f13`, base `v2026.11.10` / `6ea542fd97e2876aa4c871ccc494ed5419a03c5c`).
- **Warmer completeness:** `refs/remotes/origin/release/2026.11.11` caught up at `134 / 134` commits (`commitsBehind: 0`, `unsatisfiedCommits: 0`, `lastCompleteHead: a257c0f4d6bcc313d116427963d884add5aad17f`).
- **1-to-1 unit coverage:** 134 / 134 units classified (90 public, 44 internal, 0 prior-release, 0 missing/invalid) verified via `export_editorial_packets.py verify`.
- **Verified release scale:** `100 pull requests, 34 direct commits, and 39 contributors.` (94 PR units + 6 full cherry-picks of upstream PRs = 100 PRs; 34 remaining direct commits; 38 packet handles + verified `@sunlit-deng` on `#205557` = 39 contributors).
- **Independent public-copy review:** Completed against the final formatted docs page and native mirror; surfaced required upgrade-hop and recovery actions into visible bullets (`#205078`, `#205666`, `#205669`, `#198880`, `#205665`, `#202288`, `#204979`) and standardized version prefixes, then regenerated both files.
- **Local checks passed:**
  - `export_editorial_packets.py check-page --version 2026.11.11 --release-type patch` (0 errors)
  - `release_source_attribution.py` (0 errors)
  - `oxfmt --check` on `docs/releases/2026.11.11.md` and `docs/releases/index.md`
  - `node scripts/render-release-changelog.mjs --version 2026.11.11 --check` (`Checked 1 docs mirror(s): 2026.11.11`)
  - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` (`Docs MDX check passed`)
  - `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` (`checked_internal_links=16919`, `broken_links=0`)
- **Remaining closeout hold:** `node scripts/release-changelog.mjs check` currently reports `Missing frozen contribution record for docs mirror 2026.11.11` until `v2026.11.11` main closeout lands `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.11.md` and the `CHANGELOG.md` entry on `main`.

prs.title: feat(ios): pick a model in a system sheet, with an effort bar over the composer
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the model name in the chat composer is a faint label that opens a small pop-up menu. The menu lists models by raw id (for example "openai/gpt-5.6-sol"), mixes a Default row and a "Changes the global default" note with the choices, and has no search, so finding one model among many providers means scrolling a long menu. Effort and speed sit behind the gauge next to it, in a second pop-up menu with "Fast" and "Thinking" submenus and choices such as "High (override)" and "Default (inherited)". The Control UI shows models by name with their provider's mark, groups them by provider and lets people search; the phone does not, so the same choice looks and works differently in the two apps.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees this on iPhone:

- **The model chip reads as a control.** It shows the model's name in full contrast with a small chevron, instead of a faint label.
- **Tapping it opens a Model sheet** instead of a pop-up menu. The sheet lists Favorites, Recent and Providers, each model by its name with its provider's mark and name underneath. A check marks the current model. Tapping a provider opens its models; with a single provider, its models sit on the first page. Recent shows models used lately in other chats, newest first.
- **Search.** A search field at the bottom of the sheet finds a model by its name, its id or its provider's name across every provider, and says "No results for “…”" when nothing matches.
- **Favorites.** A long press on a model offers "Add to Favorites" or "Remove from Favorites". Favorites lead the sheet.
- **Model sign-in** is a row in the sheet. Unavailable models show why, for example "Sign-in failed" or "Temporarily unavailable", and can't be picked.
- **The sheet opens with content at once.** The app keeps the last model list per server and agent (names, providers and capabilities, never credentials) and refreshes it quietly when the sheet opens. If the list can't load and nothing is kept, the sheet says "Couldn’t load models." and tries again the next time it opens.
- **Effort is a bar over the composer.** The gauge, now with a chevron, opens a floating bar above the composer with Effort, the current level's name (such as "Adaptive"), and a track with one stop per level the model offers. Dragging snaps to a stop. When the model has speed options, a Speed row offers Standard and Fast, and Ultrafast where the account supports it. Tapping the gauge again or the message field closes the bar. The bar also opens while a response is running.
- **The composer gets the keyboard back** after a pick in the model sheet.
- **Plainer messages.** Without permission to change the model, its hint reads "You don’t have permission to change the model.". The old "Model changes are available after the current response finishes." and "Available after the current response finishes." hints are gone.

Some parts still look old or are missing until later pull requests in the series land:
- Provider pages don't yet offer account sign-in per provider, and effort isn't yet a page in the Model sheet. A later change adds both.
- A failed model or effort change is recorded with "Couldn’t change the model" or "Couldn’t change effort" and a retry, but nothing on iPhone shows it until a later change adds the app's toast. I did not check what a failed change looks like on this change alone.
- Picking a model before the first send now persists in a local new-chat fixture. Saving that choice against a real Gateway was not checked.
- Connection problems and the Talk controls near the composer keep their current look.

On macOS, a failed model change now reads "Couldn’t change the model." in the chat's error text instead of the raw error. The Model sheet and the effort bar are iPhone-only. The kept model list lives in the shared chat code; I checked it only through the package tests on macOS.

No new setting, Gateway method or protocol change. The sheet and the bar change the same session model, thinking level and fast mode as the old menus.

## Why This Change Was Made

A sheet has room for names, provider marks, sections and search, which a pop-up menu doesn't, and it matches how the Control UI's model picker is organized. It uses the system list, navigation and search field, so it follows Dynamic Type, dark mode, the back swipe and VoiceOver like the app's other sheets. Effort is a quick, frequent change, so it stays one tap from the composer as a bar instead of moving into the sheet; its level names follow the Control UI's wording instead of raw ids.

Keeping the last model list on the device lets the sheet open with content even on a slow or dropped connection. Only what the sheet shows is kept, in a small per-server value. Recent comes from the models other chats report, so it reflects use on other devices too, and the sheet keeps its order while open so rows don't jump.

The old iPhone model menu (`ChatModelControlsMenu`) and its presentation tests are removed; the composer chips present the new sheet and bar through one panel host per chat.

These used the demo chat, not a real Gateway or account. The earlier sign-in and unavailable-model suite was not rerun for this port.

prs.title: feat: onboard personal channel users without external sign-in
prs.body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

## What Problem This Solves

A token/password-authenticated single-user Gateway cannot establish a personal channel identity when its only profile is shared Owner, leaving personal session creation dependent on an external sign-in provider.

## User Impact

An authenticated administrator can explicitly create a person and bind a verified channel sender without Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, or another proxy. Shared Owner stays separate. An explicitly assigned role can delegate session-only authority without granting channel-owner status or global operator write access.

This is a draft for local testing. Real channel end-to-end acceptance remains unverified; do not treat the passing local fixtures as live Discord or Slack evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add administrator-gated `users.create` using the existing profile writer, then reuse `users.linkChannelIdentity` for the exact `(channelId, accountId, senderId)` binding. Carry limited personal authority with the existing verified requester identity, independently of command ownership, and retain the original binding and current policy during queued recovery.

Default roles, display names, message text, and login-name role assignments do not delegate these session scopes. Conflict protection, account qualification, shared-Owner exclusion, access policies, and live revocation checks remain in place. No database schema change or automatic identity migration is introduced. Profile names are not unique keys, and repeated `users.create` calls create distinct people; setup and recovery are documented in [User model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ccb547a8062a35564f527c87708ce9baf5b647ae/docs/concepts/user-model.md#onboard-without-an-external-sign-in-provider).

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing onboarding method through registered Gateway dispatch before implementation: `users.create` returned `unknown method`.
- Onboarding/authority/recovery suites: **95 tests passed** in 139.14 seconds including compilation. They cover unauthorized creation, shared Owner exclusion, conflicting links, exact account matching, forged/asserted contexts, default-role non-escalation, multi-user behavior, demotion, unlinking, and queued recovery. The Discord and Slack host-ingress fixtures invoke the real `sessions_create` tool and verify persisted personal creator attribution, without owner fallback.
- Protocol/discovery/prompt-stability consumers: **56 tests passed** in 79.23 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, touched TypeScript lint/format, protocol registry, generated-validator consistency, native protocol generation, documentation configuration examples/links, diff checks, and the scoped test-line allocation check passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) covered the local candidate against base `1d6f75fd`. No concrete implementation defect was reported; its outstanding P2 finding is the missing real-channel acceptance proof.
- **Pending:** real verified channel turn → model tool invocation → new session under the personal profile's session-write authority. The QA credential broker was unavailable during the original implementation. No live Discord or Slack test turn ran then, and no production identities or permissions were changed. The requester explicitly asked to publish this draft for local testing.

### November 28 upstream verification

[#188910](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188910) lets a person link Discord from an **existing personal profile**. It does not create the first person. On upstream [`168b4695`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/168b469579da50d7852f037cf9d15607a95234d5), the leased Discord QA environment passed its doctor. An isolated, token-authenticated Gateway returned `gateway-owner` to `users.self`, then returned `unknown method: users.create`. No channel message or model invocation was needed to reach that failure.

On draft head `ccb547a8`, dependency installation succeeded, but the CLI preparing the QA build timed out waiting for the Gateway service lifecycle lock, before the draft Gateway started. The lock was left intact. No end-to-end pass is claimed. The branch conflicts with main; when porting the missing profile-creation step, retain the upstream channel admission policy rather than restoring the older grant restrictions.

### Local testing

1. Start an isolated token/password-authenticated Gateway whose profile directory initially contains only shared Owner. Add the explicit `sessionWriter` role from the documented setup; preserve any existing multi-user defaults.
2. From the authenticated administrator connection, call `users.create` with `{ "displayName": "Local tester", "role": "sessionWriter" }`; save the returned `profile.id`.
3. Independently verify the channel sender's immutable ID and configured account, then call `users.linkChannelIdentity` with that personal profile ID and the complete identity tuple. Do not bind shared Owner.
4. From that sender, submit a fresh, normally admitted channel turn explicitly requesting a new independent session. Verify the actual `sessions_create` trace and the stored human/profile creator ID. It must be the new person, not `gateway-owner`; administrator/global-write operations must remain unavailable.
5. Check a different account with the same sender ID, then unlink or demote the person. Confirm those paths cannot retain or regain the old session-write authority. Inspect existing profiles/links before retrying any uncertain creation or binding operation.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af7ce7b0-0fc4-4179-9e6e-9b3038d2dd2f)
- [Assigned PR review requested by @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4591147b-d110-4a05-a692-35247ed3a855)
- [Upstream verification and draft acceptance attempt](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9bec160b-c3ef-48c2-a2a2-baa7920dc1cf)

prs.title: fix: report channel plugin download failures to scripts without prompting
prs.body:
Closes #201990

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw channels add` cannot download a required plugin, it can find a local copy and ask whether to use it. A script has nobody to answer, so the prompt can hide the download error. The [earlier fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c9389a5ba9c21efa4b0c97dd55c57d0bc9c3112) already stopped the command from reporting success after a failed install.

## User Impact

Scripts see the download error once, exit with status `1`, and leave channel configuration unchanged. People running the command at a terminal can still choose the local copy. No migration or new flag is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer used to offer the local copy even when the command had already determined that it could not ask questions. The [five-file follow-up against `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/918d2f59ee155556aa6e89343233c4d6f44fec0e...01b4da6fd317b45b1d168c93288bd85f6a680d9c) ties that one question to terminal input and output. Guided setup, source selection and capability consent are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Integration verification

[Required CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45333547069/job/138244779537) on the [current head `01b4da6f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01b4da6fd317b45b1d168c93288bd85f6a680d9c). [ClawSweeper reviewed that same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202091#issuecomment-7024309261) and listed no findings or before-merge actions. The four installer regression cases and all four Chromium route benchmark cases also passed locally on the published tree.

The five changed installer and test files are identical to the versions exercised by the built-CLI proof below. On [upstream `595c201f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/595c201f9f7901baf2922490c3d07607a3e4394a), those five paths still match the PR’s [base `918d2f59`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/918d2f59ee155556aa6e89343233c4d6f44fec0e): the installer still offers the local path without checking whether the caller can answer. No benchmark assertions were changed by this PR.

### Earlier installer behavior proof

Ran the built `openclaw.mjs channels add --channel fixture-chat --name Example` at [the previously reviewed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a13c9dc3faf3fabba7b7454c04363fc5dc72d60) with a local copy present and a loopback registry returning HTTP 404. With stdin closed there was no prompt. In a real terminal the local-copy prompt appeared; answering **No** preserved the same error. Each run made one registry request, printed the cause once, exited `1`, and left the config byte-for-byte unchanged. The public registry was not contacted.

```text
Closed stdin:
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.

Real terminal:
Use local plugin path instead? ([fixture workspace]/plugins/fixture-chat)  → No
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.
```

The CLI regression test failed against the original implementation because it asked one question instead of zero. On that earlier head the command, setup-adapter and installer suites passed, as did scoped typecheck, lint and formatting. Independent autoreview of the complete five-file range found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

[Required CI on the earlier `4a13c9dc` head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623) **failed**. The [failing UI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623/job/136525382964) timed out waiting for rows on Skills and Plugins; Skill Settings loaded 33 assets against a limit of 31. The tested merge changed no UI or benchmark files. The [Skills and asset-count failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44803148089/job/136521248000) and [Plugins timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464/job/136497502162) also occurred on independent runs. Related upstream work: [#202694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202694) and [#202687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). Upstream subsequently replaced the Skills reader dialog with a page and repaired Skills/Plugins loading.

An independent replay on `4eb94c89`, the first parent of the [tested merge](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5a0796342287836329eacfc8f6c85dfa1a93c95e), reproduced all three failures without the installer change. Skills and Plugins timed out on the same selectors. Skill Settings requested the same 33 asset URLs against the 31-asset limit. Plugin Settings passed on both. The base push skipped this UI suite; the comparison was run locally with Chromium and Node 24.22.1.

The PR history credits @etzelm, @VACInc, and @vyctorbrzezowski as co-authors.

Contributor: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm). Reported by Anmol (@anmol0b).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2edc3159-c613-4611-ac1c-48d712e40c67)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e22c0f1b-d725-4148-b4d3-3a6437d47641)
- [Local fallback correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d7d74ff2-50f8-4b78-a6d7-f10ac7918e37)
- [Landing discussion and verification with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfbb8805-b4f2-4c40-ac84-ea5b941703a5)
- [Exact-base CI comparison, integration and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3e4c57f3-2562-41a7-b38e-85e9d34c1285)
- [Assigned-PR sweep discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4591147b-d110-4a05-a692-35247ed3a855)
- [Exact-head CI, review and upstream verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/21933028-46f3-4b95-8db7-374f008a80b5)

prs.title: fix: report OpenRouter spending caps as billing failures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenRouter returns HTTP 403 when an organization or workspace spending budget is exhausted. OpenClaw currently labels several documented budget responses as authentication failures and tells the operator to sign in again, which cannot resolve the spending cap.

## User Impact

OpenRouter spending-budget failures are identified as billing problems instead of failed sign-ins. Existing fallback behavior remains intact; ordinary permission refusals, authentication failures, rate limits, and timeouts keep their existing handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter plugin recognizes the documented `limit_source` values and narrowly identified budget messages before the generic HTTP 403 classification. This stays within the existing provider hook: no core classification policy, retry contract, configuration, or new failure reason is introduced. Provider documentation explains the reset/admin remedy, including lifetime budgets.

References: [OpenRouter budget errors](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging#budget-errors), [budget limits](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits#handling-403-budget-errors), and [workspace budgets](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/workspaces/workspace-budgets).

## Evidence

- On head `19b37e70e02acd2a2834552a9b5cc16c43c0f034`, the [required GitHub Actions CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44378055897/job/136344465510) passed and [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201395#issuecomment-6989463491) reported no actionable findings.
- The included provider regression fails on the unchanged implementation and passes with this fix. The focused provider suite and two provider-precedence/structured-signal consumer suites pass: **32 tests**. The provider test file took **4.94 seconds wall time** on its final local run.
- A real local HTTP 403 fixture through the production embedded agent and model-fallback runner changed from `auth` plus sign-in guidance on the base to `billing` on the fix. The raw provider message retained its administrator/reset guidance. Both versions sent exactly one primary request and one fallback request. A second patched case with neutral message text proved that the structured budget metadata reaches the classifier through the real transport.
- A separately launched, built, isolated Gateway completed `chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history` against the local HTTP fixture. Its persisted fallback notice says `billing`, the fallback answer is present, and the fixture observed exactly two inference requests. No paid provider calls or existing Gateway state were used.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, extension production and test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, documentation links (0 broken), and `git diff --check` passed. The runtime build emitted Control UI asset-budget warnings outside these changed files; this is not a claim that the separate asset-budget gate is green. Full package/declaration checks remain separate from this local proof.
- Simplification kept one provider-owned decision, reused existing JSON/coercion helpers, and added no state or framework: **+22 net production lines, +53 net test lines**, plus documentation.
- Local Auto Review was attempted against base `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea` and the complete three-file working-tree candidate. It failed without a report because its handoff response file was missing; the review linked above is the hosted review.

The transport/Gateway fixtures are temporary acceptance harnesses rather than committed additional runtime suites. Real OpenRouter budget exhaustion was not induced; the error envelopes come from its current public contract. This fix does not claim attribution to a particular historical support incident.

<details>
<summary>Retained before/after terminal evidence</summary>

### Inspectable retained terminal evidence

These excerpts were extracted from the original local proof logs, not regenerated model runs. ANSI color escapes were removed. HTTP records below are literal JSON output lines; the Gateway block is an explicitly selected-field projection of its larger recorded JSON line, omitting synthetic session identifiers and unrelated transcript metadata.

**Base** — implementation at `bde2e84084bffa49cad046351f7ddd739d26d9ea`; actual local HTTP response through embedded agent/fallback (original log line 8):

```json
{"requests":["openrouter/budget-fixture","backup"],"failures":[{"message":"⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`.","rawError":"403 Org member budget limit exceeded (weekly limit). Contact your org admin. $52.00 of $50.00 used; resets 2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z.","reason":"auth","status":403,"code":"403","provider":"openrouter","model":"openrouter/budget-fixture"}],"result":[{"text":"Fallback answered","replyToTag":false}]}
```

**Fixed** — tested provider files byte-match published head `19b37e70e02acd2a2834552a9b5cc16c43c0f034`; same HTTP scenario (original log line 8):

```json
{"requests":["openrouter/budget-fixture","backup"],"failures":[{"message":"⚠️ openrouter (openrouter/budget-fixture) returned a billing error — check your account's balance and usage limits before trying again.","rawError":"403 Org member budget limit exceeded (weekly limit). Contact your org admin. $52.00 of $50.00 used; resets 2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z.","reason":"billing","status":403,"code":"403","provider":"openrouter","model":"openrouter/budget-fixture"}],"result":[{"text":"Fallback answered","replyToTag":false}]}
```

**Metadata-only control** — neutral response message, spending-cap reason supplied by `metadata.limit_source` (original log line 12):

```json
{"requests":["openrouter/budget-fixture","backup"],"failures":[{"message":"⚠️ openrouter (openrouter/budget-fixture) returned a billing error — check your account's balance and usage limits before trying again.","rawError":"403 Request rejected","reason":"billing","status":403,"code":"403","provider":"openrouter","model":"openrouter/budget-fixture"}],"result":[{"text":"Fallback answered","replyToTag":false}]}
```

**Built isolated Gateway** — selected fields from original log line 58:

```json
{
  "requests": [
    "openrouter/budget-fixture",
    "backup"
  ],
  "status": "ok",
  "requested": {
    "provider": "openrouter",
    "model": "openrouter/budget-fixture"
  },
  "effective": {
    "provider": "fixture",
    "model": "backup",
    "responseModel": "backup"
  },
  "fallbackReason": "billing",
  "reply": "Fallback answered"
}
```

Each case observed one primary request and one fallback request. The HTTP base run failed the independent expected `billing` assertion; fixed runs passed. These are actual local synthetic-transport observations, not real OpenRouter spending exhaustion. Administrator/reset detail remains in the raw diagnostic; this PR does not claim the generic billing sentence renders that complete detail.

Retained original log SHA-256 values (provenance, not an independent attestation):

```text
HTTP base: 5df977fe9d2e08eca884ec9b54f4e675b374f0012a99c0258d87ccb2f3ea3f22
HTTP fixed: d8ada0caec5e224599c43b0708aac2f6ce11f7530649d06b1d4fda98b0343f38
Gateway: 73173c4ac4e701a38ac804b0699b2b709d5890bd916a8dce126c4353d0bdc377
```

</details>

Thanks to @etzelm for identifying and sponsoring this focused investigation.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ba8717b3-cf77-4a25-bcd9-79ff4fd42b6b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/605b468a-4ae0-4d91-a66e-13a67350bb92)

prs.body:
Related to #145679

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI asks for up to 80 messages when opening a chat without saved history. That can be more history than someone needs to see the latest exchange.

## User Impact

**Appearance → Chat → Open with 24 messages** is off by default. Enable it to request up to 24 messages when opening a chat without saved history. Reopening can restore saved messages. Scrolling up or choosing **Show earlier** loads preceding messages.

| Chat settings on main | Compact opening switch |
| --- | --- |
| ![Chat appearance on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18851ef8-ec04-4243-b56b-3e3ab840de6e) | ![Compact opening off by default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a2d5bea-b49a-4b6d-a823-7a2a184e3163) |

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup subscription and history loader use the same opening limit, so a saved cursor arriving during startup can reuse the response already admitted for that opening. A compact opening with visible rows waits for the reader before loading an older page. A tail with no visible rows can still fill once.

## Evidence

- The Linux base-relative performance check passed at `9ee1e33417d` with Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.3. Normalized Chat boot JavaScript was 1,336,642 bytes gzip versus 1,336,828 bytes on main. Both used 21 requests.
- I moved compact receipt continuity checking behind the actual compact response that needs it. The first history request and valid saved cursor deltas proceed without waiting for that module. Clear loads only when an explicit reset needs it, with the existing ownership checks applied before dispatch.
- All 130 targeted UI tests passed, along with UI typecheck, scoped lint and the controller guard. All three collapsed reply reveal cases passed in Linux Chromium. The inherited CI signature also appeared in scheduled main run 46033734976 and is covered by the fixture correction in #206811.
- I used the published 2026.11.10 UI (`6ea542fd97e2`) to write a browser-local message-width preference, an unsent draft and an 80-row IndexedDB transcript snapshot. On the same origin and browser profile, the production UI at `9ee1e33417d` kept the width and draft, rebuilt the older v16 projection to a persisted v18 snapshot after Gateway hello, and showed the transcript and draft again after reload. With the same synthetic Gateway, a fresh chat requested 80 by default and 24 after opting in. Older paging rendered the preceding messages, and the enabled preference survived reload.

prs.title: fix(ai): every stream transport records a measured or explicitly unavailable context size
prs.body:
## Problem

#207041 found that the Google stream completed turns without `usage.contextUsage`. The pre-request compaction check then re-estimated the whole history with its safety margin and compacted Gemini sessions early.

The same silent absence exists on main in other transports:
- **No measurement at all:** Mistral, Google Interactions and Radius.
- **No contextUsage when a turn completes without a usage report:** Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Azure, the OpenAI ChatGPT route, Google Generative AI and Vertex, the Google plugin transport, Bedrock and Ollama.

Nothing checked this contract, so a new or changed transport could reintroduce early compaction silently.

## Fix

Contract: every bundled stream transport completes a turn with `usage.contextUsage` either `available`, from a field the provider measured, or explicitly `{ state: "unavailable" }`.

- `test/provider-context-usage-contract.test.ts` runs the real registered `streamSimple` for each built-in API against a fake upstream, plus each plugin-owned transport.
  - Each transport has a case with measured usage and a case without usage.
  - The test also asserts that the registered built-in APIs equal its rows, so a newly registered built-in fails until it has a row.
- Measured sources added, each named after the provider's response field:
  - Mistral: `usage.prompt_tokens` (cached tokens included).
  - Google Interactions: `usage.total_input_tokens` + `total_tool_use_tokens`.
  - Radius: a forwarded `usage.contextUsage` is kept as is; without one, Pi usage `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`.
- Explicit `unavailable` when nothing was measured:
  - the shared `finalizeTransportStream`, which covers Anthropic, OpenAI Completions and Responses, Azure and Mistral;
  - the Google stream completion path and the Responses terminal (OpenAI Responses, Azure, ChatGPT);
  - Bedrock without a metadata event;
  - Ollama without provider counters, which previously left the field out.

Not a type-level requirement. The completed-message type is part of the public plugin SDK (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/llm`), and stored transcripts legitimately lack the field. Requiring it would break external plugin transports at compile time.

## Impact

- **Mistral and Google Interactions users:** compaction now starts from the measured request size instead of a padded re-estimate of the whole history, as for every other provider.
- **Turns with no usage report at all:** these are rare, since every provider normally reports usage. Such a turn is now an explicit zero-token `unavailable` marker, which the compaction check treats as a barrier, as it already does for OpenAI Completions and Anthropic. The next request re-estimates the history once, until the next measured turn re-anchors. That errs toward one early compaction, never an overflow. The status meter shows an estimate for that turn instead of a stale number.
- **Ollama turns with estimated counters:** these no longer count as provider measurements in compaction preparation or overflow checks.

## Evidence

- Contract test: main fails 15 of 30 cases; this branch passes 30 of 30. Each failure on main is `usage.contextUsage` received `undefined`.
- Touched transport suites green: 126, 149, 30 and 40 tests (Ollama, Bedrock, Radius, Google, Mistral, Interactions, shared transport).
- Updated consumer test: Ollama's counter cases expected the field to be absent when counters are missing; they now expect `unavailable`.
- Adversarial review: land with changes. Applied: Interactions measures only from the completed interaction's own usage, not a step's usage carried forward; a stray whitespace change was reverted.
- Local review: round 1 found that Radius replaced a forwarded context snapshot with its counters; fixed with a test. Round 2 on this head: patch is correct, 0 findings.
- The contract test reaches plugin transports through each plugin's `test-api` barrel, as the extension test boundary requires.
- Test-line allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/207102-stream-context-usage-contract.txt`, 89 lines): the contract covers 15 transports in measured and unmeasured cases, each against its real fake upstream; that is the requested guard against a silent absence.

prs.title: feat(ios): a sent message rises from the composer, and times show while dragging left
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the chat doesn't keep your place well when you send a message. With the keyboard down, the transcript jumps so your new message sits near the top of the screen. With the keyboard up, it follows the bottom. Every message you send also carries a relative time such as "Just now" under the bubble, which adds a line to every turn, while replies show no time at all. While an existing chat loads, the transcript shows a small "Loading chat" pill instead of the shape of what's coming.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- **A sent message rests just above the composer.** It moves up from the composer field into its place in the transcript, and stays still while the reply starts underneath it. The working row and then the reply's first line fit under it without moving it. Once the reply outgrows that room, the transcript follows the reply's end while the keyboard is up. With the keyboard down, the message rises only to a fixed reading position, so the reply reads from its start and **Jump to latest reply** takes you to the end. With Reduce Motion on, the message simply appears.
- **Times show while you drag the transcript left.** Hold a drag to the left and each message and reply shows its time on the right, on its first line. A message from another day also shows its date. Release, and the transcript springs back. The time follows the device's 12- or 24-hour setting.
- **No more time under your own bubble.** The "Just now" line is gone. VoiceOver reads each message's and reply's time as part of the message.
- **Loading an existing chat shows a skeleton.** Faint rows sit where the first messages will appear (a bubble, three reply lines, a bubble, two lines), and the transcript fades in over them. A new chat never shows a loading state. The "Loading chat" pill is gone.
- **The jump button is a glass circle** with the same arrow, and it glides to the latest reply instead of jumping.

Some parts still look old or are missing until later pull requests in the series:
- A message that hasn't been confirmed yet isn't dimmed, and a failed send shows no "Not sent · Try again" line under the bubble. That delivery status comes with the pull request that sends a message at the tap.
- The chat header, composer, tool rows and working line aren't updated yet.

The reading-position and time-reveal code is iOS-only. Mac chat windows keep the delayed spinner while a chat loads, and their reply footer keeps its time.

## Why This Change Was Made

A sent message is what you're looking at, so it should stay where you can see it while the reply arrives. Times are useful when you look for them and noise when you don't. Revealing them on a left drag, as Messages does, keeps every turn one line shorter. A placeholder in the transcript's own shape keeps the screen from jumping when the history lands. Where a sent turn rests, how long it holds, and when the reply takes over live in tested types: `ChatReadingPosition`, `ChatReadingPolicy` and `ChatMessageClock`.

## Evidence

- OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS: `ChatReadingPositionTests` and `ChatReadingSentTurnTests`, 31 passed, 0 failed.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatReadingPositionSendTests`, `ChatTranscriptTimeTests` and `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests` (including the new skeleton size test), 17 passed, 0 failed.
- UI test `testAssistantReplyHoldOffersActionsInMenu` passed.
- On the main-targeted candidate, both simulator UI tests passed with their original assertions: `testMessageTimesAppearOnlyWhileHoldingLeftDrag` and `testOlderMessageTimesStayWithEachBubbleAndPhoto`. The two demo chat fixtures now ship with their tests; they do not use a live Gateway.
- The iOS app and its test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` report no violations. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`; the canonical inventory removes the unused "Loading chat" entry and records the restored demo text. `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the demo chat in screenshot mode (no Gateway) on the same simulator, before and after. Light: times while dragging left, a sent message right after Send with the keyboard up, the sent message at rest with the keyboard down, the reply in, and the jump button in a long chat. Dark: times while dragging left. Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`.
  - In the two sent-message pairs (keyboard up and at rest), the reply has already arrived in Before. After holds the demo reply for 9 seconds with a fixture delay that this change adds.
  - The demo chat loads at once, so the loading state never stays on screen long enough to capture. The loading pair renders the old pill and the new skeleton on their own, in light and dark.
  - The screenshot test was added only for these runs and isn't part of this change.
- Not checked:
  - A reply arriving during the send animation, sending while scrolled far back, or individual timestamps on consecutive assistant replies in the same group.
  - The send motion itself, frame by frame (only where the message comes to rest).
  - A real Gateway with a slow history load or a long streaming reply.
  - VoiceOver on a device, Reduce Motion, larger text sizes, iPad and landscape.
  - The macOS app.

Before is on the left and After on the right in each image.

![Light: holding a left drag. Before, nothing moves and "Just now" sits under the sent message. After, each message and reply shows its time on the right, on its first line.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3051bc53-d411-4ae7-8006-dace7df96227)

![Dark: the same left drag. Before, "Just now" under the sent message. After, the times on the right.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33ecc54d-cd6e-4626-b903-3d94b71bbcfc)

![Light: right after Send with the keyboard up. Before, the reply is already in and "Just now" sits under the message. After, the message rests above the composer with the working row under it.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6828d543-e71b-415d-a959-6b787cc69a77)

![Light: the sent message at rest with the keyboard down. Before, the reply has already arrived. After, the message waits above the composer with the working row under it while the demo reply is held.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09ec5715-58b8-471b-b8e0-7a37f2b99334)

![Light: the reply in. Before, "Just now" sits under the sent message. After, there is no time line under it.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6073a7f3-e7e1-47d6-9741-0225193d34a1)

![Light: the jump button in a long chat. Before, a plain circle with a down arrow. After, a glass circle with the same arrow.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9053dec4-9cba-49a2-9a62-bd5c62f45739)

![Light: the loading state rendered on its own. Before, a "Loading chat" pill with a spinner. After, skeleton rows in the shape of two messages and two replies.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71b46d59-0f8e-4c0c-aea8-735a17f3262c)

![Dark: the loading state rendered on its own. Before, the "Loading chat" pill. After, the skeleton rows.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cbdcc5b-6130-4d7c-802e-0729278629fc)

prs.title: improve: reduce sidebar row rebuilds during child activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When many child sessions are streaming, a child activity timestamp can trigger a full rebuild of its parent’s sidebar row. The parent needs the new child activity facts, but rebuilding also resolves the parent’s model, thinking settings, and other unchanged row fields.

## User Impact

The Gateway does less row construction when a child reports activity. Sidebar rows and session events retain the same published values, ordering, and visibility. This requires no configuration or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection already has the accepted child entry and indexed parent links. It invalidates the affected parent’s presentation revision and lets the existing presentation owner update the compact child links. Reparenting updates both old and new links after the index changes. A parent that has received an incremental row patch still takes the existing full refresh path when needed to preserve canonical wire field order. The equivalent broadcast plans from #193692 adapt to the same published facts through their existing owner.

## Evidence

- The November 27 Team peak profile on `6312d8be` observed 184 RPC/min, 61% main-thread busy time, and 13.8% wall time in GC. Seven sites in the target row path accounted for about 270 MB of 5,008 MB sampled, including 125 MB in row materialization below `accept → refresh`. No Team data or access was used for the replay.
- The persisted synthetic replay used 15,000 sessions across four SQLite agent stores, eight active streams, six loopback subscribers, and 100-row sidebar pages. In 94 transcript events with a timestamp touch, direct row refresh, input derivation, and full build each stayed at 94. Parent refresh, input derivation, and full build each fell from 94 to 1. There were zero unrelated event-phase builds. Across the 470-event mix, total event-phase builds fell from 391 to 298. Patch freezes (212), unrelated archive evictions (40), and page-triggered builds (136) matched.
- All 2,820 ordered decoded event frames and 60 sidebar pages matched. The comparison expands shared sidebar facts, normalizes generated profile identity and snapshot clocks, and retains row field order, omission, and activity timestamps. The harness uses production write and row preparation owners over generated state and loopback sockets.
- The persisted refresh scope regression expects one full build on a child timestamp write and fails with two on baseline `7e7e84039907`. It also checks old/new parent links after reparenting, retained frozen sibling links, and unchanged unrelated rows. The focused Gateway suite passed 85 tests, and the sidebar identity browser check and nine Chromium E2E tests passed. Codex autoreview of the complete diff against `7e7e84039907` reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production +24 lines (+47/−23), test +4, replay tooling +244 (+261/−17). Production growth keeps the relation-only path inside the existing projection and preserves the full builder’s field order after row patches.
- Separate V8 sampling runs used two A/A pairs and five alternating allocation pairs. Median inclusive accept allocation fell from 49.76 to 38.82 KB per event (592.86 to 477.64 MB per replay minute), and full row construction fell from 15.80 to 12.02 KB per event. The whole replay stayed near 1.60 MB per event.
- Three separately profiled CPU pairs measured inclusive accept CPU at 184.64 → 155.59 µs per event and full row construction at 68.23 → 49.69 µs. Including the named lazy presentation refresh, accept plus presentation CPU was 191.15 → 203.47 µs/event, within the A/A spread. The initial 470-event timing series saw an adverse replay tail on a heavily loaded host. Five independent 1,410-event unprofiled pairs put replay main-thread CPU at 3.17 → 3.06 ms/event, whole-process CPU at 5.93 → 5.92 ms/event, and p99 event-loop delay at 9.10 → 9.75 ms. The longer series did not reproduce the initial 26.6% p99 increase.
- The changed-file check typechecked the production, test, and tooling sources. The unrelated Knip scan reported existing unused exports for `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and `isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`. #207061 and #205382 removed their last external consumers, respectively. The same two errors reproduced with the same Knip command on the PR merge ref’s first parent, `1f0332980951`.

prs.title: fix: return CLI agent replies after subagents finish
prs.body:
Closes #206136

Contributed by @MertBasar0.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/40481157-6b56-4491-9be0-92f1f8fa1274)

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway-backed `openclaw agent` call can exit successfully with no output after its agent spawns a subagent and calls `sessions_yield`. The eventual reply appears in session history but never reaches the script that requested it.

## User Impact

Without `--deliver`, the original request now returns the continuation’s reply instead of an empty success. Spawning without yielding, channel delivery, and `--local` are unchanged. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the external RPC response pending across the committed yield without keeping the first execution open. Only the continuation admitted for that child batch can supply the reply. The observer ends on timeout without stopping the continuation. A disconnect detaches the transport while retaining replay custody. A definitively retired wake that never started returns failure rather than leaving the caller waiting.

The final outcome is also recorded through the original request’s replay reservation, so a same-key retry returns the same final payload and run ID. The observer uses the admitted controller inputs and committed registry wake for correlation, with a `ChatRef` and a session-store entry view for transcript continuity across compaction. It no longer holds a parallel set of session identity pins. If the final continuation is retired before it can start, the CLI tells the caller to check the saved child results before retrying.

## Evidence

- **Published head:** `7ac4185dae49525f8190651f23dfc1608d1f496c` exactly matches the locally tested Git tree `fe48fcbee49f6788abc32e728994df0d8bf553c3` and is a direct child of `63e3c38df42e`.
- **Live CLI and replay, current tree:** `pnpm openclaw agent` → isolated loopback Gateway → Ollama 0.20.6 (`gpt-oss:20b`) exited 0 with `status: ok` and one `CONTINUATION-REPLY-OK` payload (189.39 s). History showed spawn → committed yield → child completion → final reply. A Gateway RPC using the first CLI run ID as the idempotency key returned the same run ID and identical full JSON (3.32 s).
- **Current-tree checks:** session-identity ratchet, formatting across 11 files, and diff checks passed. All 25 focused tests passed, including verification that the retired-continuation diagnostic is identical on the original response and replay. The ratchet and allowlist are unchanged.
- **Prior evidence:** the identity-custody tree passed 99 focused tests and core typecheck before the diagnostic-only follow-up. The prior published head `63e3c38df42e` also passed live CLI and same-key replay checks on its earlier tree. `bfe21c72890a` returned empty payloads in the same-key replay negative control.

## Worked on by

- @MertBasar0

prs.title: fix: keep past blockers from stopping current work
prs.body:
Related: #206900

## What Problem This Solves

An agent finished a repair locally but handed back a patch instead of pushing. It mistook an earlier worker’s report about a CI test for a restriction on the current task. The same commit was later pushed.

## User Impact

The agent reuses completed work and takes the next unfinished step in the current request. No new confirmation, configuration, or permission is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing [follow-through instructions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b468d58a4f30b11cec7bdfe14fae910c40151ff9/src/agents/promised-work-prompt.ts#L4-L8) now give two directions: use past reports as context for the current task, and report back on background or delegated work. This replaces longer wording rather than adding a separate recall note. The duplicate manual bullet is gone. Tool access and prompt pinning are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Prompt size:** 79 fewer tokens and 363 fewer UTF-8 bytes than the pre-PR base on each of four rendered prompts. Token counts use `o200k_base` (`gpt-tokenizer@3.4.0`, measurement only). These are full embedded prompts or the OpenClaw-owned Codex base instructions, not API billing totals.

| Rendered text | Before this PR (`de4d1cc8c1d9`) | This revision |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Fresh embedded | 2,540 | 2,461 |
| Configured embedded | 2,966 | 2,887 |
| Codex, Telegram direct | 1,380 | 1,301 |
| Codex, Discord group | 1,380 | 1,301 |

**Live behavior:** The [two-case regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b468d58a4f30b11cec7bdfe14fae910c40151ff9/qa/scenarios/agents/recalled-blocker-followthrough-live.yaml#L78-L105) passed on the published source tree. A live model used the prior lookup without reopening the catalog file in either case. It wrote the label when the current receipt approved it and left the label absent when the receipt was pending.

```text
Reused the completed lookup in both turns. Approved: label written. Pending: label absent.
```

All 30 affected prompt tests passed; all six generated snapshots are current. Local autoreview produced no verdict because its reviewer could not start in the read-only sandbox.

- @VACInc

prs.title: fix(memory): keep note frontmatter out of durable memory
prs.body:
Closes #148186

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes note bookkeeping such as `status: active` entering memory recall and durable-memory promotion when it appears inside complete leading YAML frontmatter.

## User Impact

Recall returns note bodies with their original citation lines, and promotion rejects stale frontmatter hits. Unchanged notes are reindexed after upgrade; YAML-looking session content and incomplete frontmatter remain eligible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Markdown Core's delimiter and newline grammar through one dependency-free extractor, preserve source-line offsets, and advance the chunking revision from 6 to 7. Indexing, `memory_get`, and promotion rehydration agree on LF, CRLF, and bare CR.

Thanks to @gisk0 for #148186 and the earlier #148190, closed **unmerged** for inactivity. This change addresses that PR's index-invalidation and CR-line findings, with committed regressions and an upgrade from genuinely contaminated pre-fix index rows. Its complete discussion and related PR discussions were checked again; open #151299 covers separate promotion-anchor ambiguity rules.

## Evidence

### November 28 upstream refresh

```text
mixed note:    2683805a8dbf5d631915d7ad09ea2749c3306bf34526fbcf86a103bf59055a46
MEMORY.md:     dfe17a95fc8727c05b954523bf247c8b3795a5bfa7505f034d16df1077cedfb5
```

Every explicitly supplied user setting was preserved, including workspace, agent, memory provider/model/base URL/key, vector-index setting, query settings and memory plugin selection. Whole config bytes changed because ordinary Doctor added its `meta`, `wizard`, and `skills` sections; this is not a claim that Doctor leaves the entire config byte-identical. The before/after SQLite SHA-256 values are `edd04a5c7eafb8eced53f99b18caf86795d021c12e18b8feadf0807663307703` and `c9e7d4d3f987a140ae471100445eb5ef1747a4eda66004e061f9b796d8789eab`.

Limitations: embedding responses came from a deterministic loopback HTTP fixture with an obvious non-secret key. Supported `store.vector.enabled=false` disabled the vector index; ordinary hybrid search can still use its embedding fallback. No live provider/channel coverage is claimed. A unique named profile, own state paths and the canonical external service-repair policy kept service install/start repair outside the run. Doctor's unrelated missing-channel/skill/security warnings remain in the retained logs; exit 0 is not a claim that every health check is green. This adds latest-stable CLI/Doctor/index/search upgrade proof; the earlier Gateway registered-tool and promotion proof remains scoped to its recorded inputs.

Completed on November 2, 2026. No product or test source changed for this additional proof.

prs.title: fix: let backups finish when Gateway startup creates a database
prs.body:
Closes #207019

## What Problem This Solves

When Gateway startup creates a managed SQLite database after `openclaw backup create --verify --json` has listed its inputs, backup exits without an archive even though an immediate retry can succeed.

## User Impact

Backup now retries automatically. No flags or archive format change. If it cannot snapshot a database it has already seen, or if another database appears on the third attempt, it still publishes nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rerunning tar alone would reuse the stale database list. Backup discards the partial attempt, keeps the original config and engine selection, and takes fresh snapshots after a short wait. Replacement of a known SQLite identity and ambiguous hardlinks remain errors, not reasons to retry.

## Evidence

- [Red on main `b5c0a7d`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e8cfee64f82d997d2275b2021082e1c7): I paused backup after discovery and started the Gateway. It created `control/services.sqlite`; backup exited 1 with an empty output directory. The [regression test on main](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c79a087eb8459785f9ab1c8fcf13eb35) failed only for the late store.
- [Green on published head `f8f1af0`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3340ec48d40d5af2a7cb0827b304e072): same race, exit 0, verified archive. I extracted `services.sqlite`, found both live runtime-pin tables, and checked that `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`. All 78 focused tests, core typecheck, lint, and formatting passed. The wrapper exited 0.
- [Safety controls](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1d3f64935511c928676ba7ffd0140f6e), also passed on the published head: a database created during initial identity discovery retained its test row. Repeated arrivals through attempt three and a previously observed database disappearing both exited 1 with an empty output directory.
- Linux/SQLite only. I did not run the 2026.10.34 release or other operating systems.

Thanks to @daniel-lxs for the report and reproduction.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-backup-races-gateway-startup-s60cf0f59)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs
