prs.title: feat(ios): messages read like the web, with quotes, softer links and Show more
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, chat messages don't read like they do in the Control UI:
- A Markdown quote shows as plain text, without its bar.
- Links are bright accent red, and messages with a link get a "Preview" row inside the bubble.
- A long message ends in "…" above a filled "Show more" pill.
- Raw harness context can appear in the transcript.

A conversation that looks right in the web chat looks noisier and harder to scan on the phone.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees these changes in a chat on iPhone:

- **Quotes** show with a thin bar and dimmer text, with a little space around them, as on the web.
- **Links** use a softer link color in message bodies. A web link has a small link glyph before it, a GitHub pull request has a pull request glyph, and file references have file glyphs sized to the text. Tables in messages use the same link color.
- **No link previews.** The "Preview · domain" row under a message with a link is gone on iPhone; macOS keeps it.
- **Show more.** A long message is cut after twelve lines or 700 characters, as before. Its last line now fades out instead of ending in "…", and "Show more" (or "Show less") is muted text with a chevron instead of a filled pill. The collapsed preview keeps its Markdown, so a long message that starts with a quote still shows the quote.
- **User message times** sit under the bubble instead of inside it. Assistant replies no longer repeat the time under every reply on iPhone.
- **Internal context is hidden.** OpenClaw's injected harness context no longer shows as a "System · injected context" row on iPhone, and internal context blocks are removed from message text everywhere. Background task notices still open on demand.
- **Code blocks** can wrap long lines when the app asks for it. The phone app doesn't set that until a later pull request.
- **Sheets.** The Select Text and Full Message sheets use the standard sheet close button. The Mermaid diagram preview puts its close button on the leading edge on iPhone.

Some parts still look old until later pull requests in the series land:
- The time under a user bubble shows all the time. A later change shows times only while dragging the chat left, and puts the send state there.
- Photos and files a person attaches still sit inside the bubble.
- File attachment rows keep their current icon.
- Tool rows keep their current look.
- The chat header and the floating composer layout this change prepares are switched on by a later change, so the composer looks the same as before.

No setting, data or network behavior changes. Message text is stored and sent unchanged. Only how it renders changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer gains a quote block and renders a collapsed message through the same Markdown path as an expanded one, so the preview and the full message format alike. Clipping the rendered Markdown, rather than a plain-text prefix with "…", is how the web clamps a message. The fade shows where the text continues without inventing an ellipsis. Inline glyphs take the font of the text they sit in, so they scale with Dynamic Type.

The chat view's column width rule and error presentation move into the shared chat configuration file, next to the environment values the app uses to place the composer and header. That is groundwork the later header and composer changes build on.

## Evidence

- The iOS app builds for the simulator with its SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases, and the app and test bundles compile. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` reports 0 violations, and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0 files to format. The string catalog check reports no pending changes.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatReaderHistoryRetentionTests`, 3 of 3 pass.
- OpenClawKit package tests on macOS (`swift test`, filtered to `ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests`, `ChatTranscriptExporterTests`, `ChatTranscriptRowTests` and `ChatUserMessageDisclosurePolicyTests`): 130 of 130 pass on the updated head.
  - The test `mixed CRLF and LF count as lines and keep the original preview text`, added on `main` in #205869, expected the collapsed preview to end in "…". This change removes the "…" in favor of the fade, so the second commit drops it from that test's two expectations. The test still checks that CRLF counts as one line break and that the preview keeps the original text.
- The transcript export regression test verifies that LF and CRLF line breaks hide internal runtime context while preserving the surrounding message.
- UI test on the same simulator: `testSystemNoticesExpandAndCollapseWithoutLosingTheirBody` passes. It checks that injected context no longer shows and that a background task notice expands and collapses with its whole body.
- Screenshots come from the demo chat in screenshot mode, with no Gateway or account data. A temporary UI test, not part of this change, sent a quote, a message with a docs link and a GitHub pull request link, and an 800-character message, on the same simulator with the status bar fixed at 9:41.
  - The images below use the previous stacked base. A second light-mode simulator run against the integrated composer (`cc7122603fc3`) reproduced the quote bar, softened links without preview rows, and the faded Show more control.
  - Before and After are scrolled to show the same messages; link previews make Before's transcript taller.

Before is on the left and After on the right in each image.

![Light: a quote and two links. Before, the quote is plain text and the message with links has a Preview row inside the bubble. After, the quote has a bar, the links are colored with a link glyph and a pull request glyph, and the time sits under the bubble.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ba686ad-feb2-47c0-94da-8f31b6adbf28)

![Dark: the same quote and links, before and after.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5ee7d52-97a1-470b-9fa4-cc06072840d3)

![Light: a long message. Before, it ends in "…" above a filled Show more pill. After, its last line fades out above a muted Show more with a chevron.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1398a61-a22a-45a8-b4d7-430ff80a6ef1)

Not checked:
- iPad and landscape.
- Larger text sizes.
- macOS. The OpenClawKit code compiles for macOS in the package tests, but I didn't open the Mac app.
- A real Gateway conversation.
- File chips inside a real assistant reply, because the demo chat doesn't produce file references.
- The full UI test suite.

prs.title: fix: preserve library names in worker startup errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A worker startup failure can show a garbled library name when the operating system splits a Unicode character across stderr reads. The reported name may then be hard to match to the library on disk.

## User Impact

The startup error preserves the library name across reads. The same startup failure and healthy-exit classifications apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup diagnostic keeps a UTF-8 decoder for its own stderr capture. That lets it join fragmented characters without changing encoding for other readers of the child process.

## Evidence

On Linux with Node 24.18.0, a real child process wrote `node: error while loading shared libraries: lib🧭.so` and exited with code 127. In the split case the child waited for a parent acknowledgment after the first stderr write. The parent received 49 and 6 bytes, with the four-byte character split after its first two bytes. The real startup observer returned the following diagnostics.

| Child case | Base `ddf0e2694` | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One stderr write, exit 127 | `lib🧭.so` | `lib🧭.so` |
| Two stderr writes, exit 127 | `lib���.so` | `lib🧭.so` |
| No stderr, exit 0 | No diagnostic | No diagnostic |

The checked-in regression uses the same pipe handshake. It failed on the base with the existing runtime-unavailable error missing the correct filename. All 13 focused tests passed with the fix.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/child-runtime-viability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

File-scoped Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. A source-scoped type comparison had the same 49 diagnostics on base and patch with the reused local dependency install, with none in the touched files. The child emits synthetic loader stderr. An actual missing shared library was not induced.

Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P3 findings in the patch committed as `626d3dd4d`.

prs.title: fix(media): read text attachments with encoded URL extensions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A remote text document can be left out of the model's context when the sender labels it as audio and the URL encodes the dot in its filename. For example, the same text at `notes.txt` was read, while `notes%2Etxt` was handed off as audio without being fetched by the document reader.

## User Impact

The document reader recognizes a text suffix in an encoded HTTP URL just as it recognizes the equivalent plain suffix. The subsequent checks still use the actual downloaded media and the configured file policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The document classifier already uses known text extensions to handle mislabeled attachments. When the existing filename lookup has no recognized extension, it now lets the shared media parser examine the original HTTP URL. The shared parser handles percent encoding in the URL's filename segment.

## Evidence

On Linux with Node 24.18.0, a real loopback HTTP server served the same UTF-8 `text/plain` body at both names. Each case called `extractFileContext` with a real `MediaAttachmentCache`, with private-network access allowed for this loopback fixture.

| URL filename | Sender MIME | Base `8b36e346b` | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notes.txt` | `audio/mpeg` | 1 HTTP request, 1 file block with the text | 1 request, 1 block with the text |
| `notes%2Etxt` | `audio/mpeg` | 0 requests, no file block | 1 request, 1 block with the text |
| `notes%2Etxt` | `text/plain` | 1 request, 1 block with the text | 1 request, 1 block with the text |

The base-only failure occurs before the fetch, because the initial extension lookup sees the encoded basename as a local filename. The fixed branch reaches the same extraction path as the plain URL. The control with the correct sender MIME also verifies that extraction from the encoded URL itself already worked.

The checked-in regression reuses a real HTTP fixture that serves Windows-1251 text. On the base only the encoded-suffix case failed, with zero file blocks, while the equivalent plain-suffix case passed. After the fix, the following command passed 16 file-context tests and 16 agent tool-prefix stability tests.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/file-context.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app still ships two pages that the Control UI no longer has: an Agents page (a roster of the Gateway's agents with status filters) and a Docs page (four links to the OpenClaw docs). Both appear in the sidebar's Pages list. Agent selection already lives in the sidebar's agent selector, so the Agents page is a second, older way to do the same thing, and the Docs page only links out to the web.

## User Impact

- The sidebar's Pages list (Edit Pages) no longer offers Agents or Docs. Someone who had pinned either page no longer sees it in the sidebar; the pin is ignored, as for any page that no longer exists.
- Launching with `--openclaw-initial-tab agent` or `agents` now opens chat.
- The Files page keeps working. It now opens through a small `AgentWorkspaceFilesTab` that shows the selected agent's workspace files, instead of going through the old Agents page with a Files route.
- Nothing else changes. The Overview page is still in the list; a later PR in this series removes it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is one of a series of pull requests that brings the iOS app in line with the Control UI. This one removes the old Agents and Docs pages and their sidebar destinations:

- Deletes `AgentProTab`'s roster, filters and Gateway data (`AgentProTab+Destinations.swift`, `AgentProTab+GatewayData.swift`, `AgentProTab+Overview.swift`) and `OpenClawDocsScreen.swift`. `AgentProTab.swift` keeps only `AgentWorkspaceFilesTab`, the Files page.
- Removes the `agents` and `docs` cases from `RootTabs.SidebarDestination` and `SidebarScreen`, their titles, icons and routes, and the `agent`/`agents` initial-tab alias.
- Updates the tests that listed those destinations, removes the two UI tests of the removed pages (`testAgentsNavigateToSettingsThroughSidebar`, `testAgentUsesToolbarFilter`) and the Overview-only sidebar check (`testSidebarOverviewNavigation`), and makes the release Agent screenshot open the sidebar and wait for the agent selector, which is where an agent is chosen now.
- Regenerates the string catalogs: the removed pages' strings go away. Strings that other screens still use stay.

## Evidence

- The iOS simulator app and test bundles build with SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint. The canonical native strings baseline verifies, and `git diff --check` is clean.

prs.title: fix: link sessions started from a selection back to their source chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you highlight text in a chat and choose **New session**, the new session starts with your selection quoted, but nothing says which chat it came from. You can't jump back to the original conversation, and the agent in the new session can't look at it for context.

## User Impact

The first message of a session started from a selection now ends the quote with a `From <session>` line. Chat already turns a bare session key into a link labeled with that session's title, so the line shows the source chat's name, opens it on click, and gives the agent the key it needs for `sessions_history`. Quoting from several sessions lists each source once.

Nothing changes in the sidebar: the new session stays a top-level session and does not become a sub-session of the source.

Accepted edge case: with `session.scope="global"`, the source key is `global`, so the line reads `From global` as plain text with no link. Making that a link would mean passing the agent ID through the chat props for a rare config, so this PR doesn't.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selection already carried its source session key; it was dropped when the quote was turned into message text. Putting the key in the message text reuses the existing session-link rendering. It needs no new session field and no protocol change. A durable "came from" field was considered and declined for now.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-selection-to-main.e2e.test.ts` › "starts a new session from the launcher with the selected excerpt attached" now expects `From agent:main:main` in the `sessions.create` message and passes locally (`pnpm test:ui:e2e … -t 'starts a new session'`). Without the fix, the message has no `From` line and this assertion fails.
- Rendering: a temporary mocked Control UI E2E (not committed) loaded a new session whose first user message was the old text versus the new text, at 1280×900, with fixture sessions named "Prompt length and context usage" (source) and "Duplicate AGENTS.md check" (new). It asserted that the new text renders a `.markdown-session-link` titled with the source session, and the old text renders none. Both captures use this branch's build, so "before" shows the old message text, not a build from `main`.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, the pre-commit hook, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Review: local ClawSweeper wasn't available, so an independent autoreview pass on the full diff (base `be3c73e2`, head `d5871ffc`) ran at P0–P2. It reported one P2, the `session.scope="global"` case above, which is accepted as an edge case. No other findings.
- Not run: full typecheck (left to CI), and a live Gateway run.

prs.title: feat(reef): add host-approved remote session prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Paired Reef Gateways can exchange guarded messages, but one Gateway cannot safely propose a prompt to a session owned by the other. There is no session-scoped mount, host approval, replay-safe admission, or immediate revocation path.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a text-only prototype that keeps the host Gateway as the sole session and execution authority. Reef carries typed, encrypted federation frames, while existing OpenClaw plugin approvals and canonical agent admission decide whether one exact remote prompt runs. The host revalidates the mount generation, session incarnation, and exact peer signing and encryption keys after approval and at canonical input-admission commit boundaries.

## User Impact

Operators with two paired Reef Gateways can:

- Share one exact host session with `/reef session share`.
- Propose text prompts from the guest Gateway.
- Approve once, always allow for that mount, or deny.
- Resolve approvals inline above the composer or through Inbox.
- Revoke a mount immediately from the host Gateway.

This prototype does not mirror transcripts, stream output to the guest, or transfer attachments.

## Latest experiment: plugin-gated native Reef Control UI

Commit [`f5c4349af9ebf58d33d103c66fc5284cfce461b1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f5c4349af9ebf58d33d103c66fc5284cfce461b1) adds an opt-in native Reef panel without widening the public protocol or plugin SDK. This is experimental remote delegation: a trusted guest proposes text to one explicitly shared host session, while the host remains the sole transcript, approval, admission, model-execution, and revocation authority. It is distinct from ordinary Reef messaging, whose existing guard/classification path remains unchanged.

The panel is hidden unless the Reef plugin is enabled and the connection has `operator.admin`. It covers setup/unavailable states, short-lived pairing codes and requests, trust removal, exact-session sharing, guest prompt proposals, proposal outcomes, pending revocation, and links to native approvals. Read status requires `operator.read`; every mutation requires `operator.admin`, strict bounded validation, and the canonical owner command path. The generic SDK/security-owner decision described below remains outstanding.

### Tested candidate provenance

- The complete dirty-tree candidate over published head `6ef84e685234984ba8cfdc887435c895e1c6577b` was frozen as a 58,582-byte binary patch with SHA-256 `9d8b106bb0bb13aaf299cb771852572b37a7f2ea170ba215dd631582bd55a240`.
- That exact patch was committed as `f5c4349af9ebf58d33d103c66fc5284cfce461b1`; no unrelated files were included.
- GitHub then exposed one assertion-safety ratchet requirement. Follow-up commit [`a7c456b504a229a6f028f67a7aee9aea79c1b79b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a7c456b504a229a6f028f67a7aee9aea79c1b79b) adds only the required `// SAFETY:` invariant comment. The ratchet and the 8 Control UI Gateway tests pass.
- The complete published delta from `6ef84e685234984ba8cfdc887435c895e1c6577b` through `a7c456b504a229a6f028f67a7aee9aea79c1b79b` has SHA-256 `3fed548004ddbd381867c306cf1d7c9d8505fa327738efb0be2c63213dc3b50f`.
- Fresh normal actionable P0/P1/P2 autoreview was scoped-clean with no findings and confidence `0.91`.
- Reef validation passed: **12 native Control UI tests**, **382 extension tests across 31 files**, type-aware lint with zero findings, formatting, `git diff --check`, plugin SDK/package-boundary checks, and the full repository build.

### Real runtime and browser proof

A two-Gateway loopback proof used OCM `0.2.33`, distinct registered Reef identities, a real local Wrangler Reef relay, OpenClaw runtime, and `openai/gpt-5-mini` with mocks disabled.

- Pairing and pinned trust survived Gateway restarts.
- Host sharing produced a real guest mount; the guest submitted through the native panel.
- Revocation while approval was pending denied admission with no run ID and no host-history mutation.
- A later **Allow once** approval produced the real host response “The shared answer is 42.”
- Same-session continuation retained both prior host context (`Harbor`) and guest-added context (`42`).
- The configured browser flow covered trust, session sharing, guest proposal submission, the real approval card in the exact host session, accepted outcome, revocation reflected on both peers, friend-code generation, pairing-request submission, friend removal, and disabled-plugin gating.

Limits: the proof used local loopback rather than a public multi-machine relay; it is candidate restart/reopen proof rather than older-release upgrade/downgrade proof; the guest receives proposal outcomes rather than streamed/final host output; attachment transfer and transcript attribution remain out of scope. Current published head `a7c456b504a229a6f028f67a7aee9aea79c1b79b` has triggered fresh exact-head CI, which is not represented as passed here until GitHub completes it. The dependency graph change in `extensions/reef/package.json` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` also requires the repository’s documented current admin or `@openclaw/openclaw-secops` `/allow-dependencies-change` override.

## Proposed SDK Boundary — Owner Decision Still Open

This PR proposes a generic, core-owned plugin runtime capability rather than Reef-only machinery. Explicit SDK/security-owner acceptance of that public durable authority surface is still outstanding; the rationale below is not an approval. Core owns session incarnation, approval scoping, plugin lifecycle, and canonical agent admission; Reef is the first consumer. Keeping the authority primitive at that owner boundary avoids duplicating security policy inside one channel plugin while preserving the strict trusted-official-plugin gate.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/reef/protocol/federation.ts` | Defines bounded typed federation frames and prompt bindings |
| `extensions/reef/protocol/pipeline.ts` | Opens federation traffic outside ordinary chat ingress |
| `extensions/reef/src/federation-state.ts` | Persists mounts, generations, grants, and proposal outcomes |
| `extensions/reef/src/federation-coordinator.ts` | Validates authority, requests approval, and admits host execution |
| `extensions/reef/src/flow.ts` | Sends federation frames through Reef E2EE transport |
| `extensions/reef/src/channel.ts` | Routes inbound frames and owner-visible outcomes |
| `extensions/reef/src/commands.ts` | Adds share, list, prompt, and revoke commands |
| `ui/src/components/exec-approval-card.test.ts` | Covers session-scoped approval presentation |
| `src/plugin-sdk/runtime-store*.ts`, `src/plugins/loader-channel-runtime.ts` | Keeps active plugin runtime stores owned by their registry through discovery and setup |
| `docs/channels/reef.md` | Documents the two-Gateway prototype workflow |
| `extensions/reef/**/*.test.ts` | Proves protocol, state, admission, replay, revocation, and E2E flow |

## Evidence

### Configured two-Gateway flow

Built and tested exact head `ebc20b31daf42cb41caa1cbb504bdb37a51efc09`. Two isolated Gateways, distinct registered Reef identities, real local Reef relay, encrypted transport, real host approval UI, and a recording loopback agent provider. No operator Gateway changes.

- Guest proposal reached the inline approval card. **Allow once** admitted its text into the host session and delivered `session.prompt.accepted` to the guest. Agent-provider requests increased from **1 to 2**.
- Both candidate Gateways were stopped and reopened against their retained state. The accepted receipt survived; the retained mount admitted another freshly approved prompt. Host-local chat used that same host session.
- Another proposal was left pending, its mount revoked, then approval attempted. The guest received `session.prompt.denied`; provider requests stayed **4 to 4**, and the revoked marker was absent from the host transcript. Reopening both Gateways again retained the denial and absence.
- This is **candidate restart/reopen proof**, not older-release upgrade/downgrade proof. The browser recording covers approval, reconnect, and host-visible input; the exact receipt/provider/absence assertions come from the running Gateway proof.
- **Guard boundary:** federation frames intentionally bypass ordinary chat classification. Host approval/grants and exact peer/mount/session bindings authorize these prompts. A separate ordinary Reef message received matching outbound/inbound **allow** verdicts from the live OpenAI guard for the same encrypted envelope; federation recorded **zero ordinary guard calls**. The agent provider was a recording mock, not a live model.
- An earlier attempt exposed signed-GET replay collisions when repeatedly polling remote friend lists; the final observer reads canonical local trust state without issuing those requests. The transport collision remains a named follow-up. A separate reopen attempt timed out before approval; its cause was not established. The final run used latest-response command assertions and passed the complete restart flow.

![Host approval for a guest prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8601af10-2086-4dae-93bd-434a8a670ee5)

![Host transcript after reopened admission and revocation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c49b0826-fa3e-4267-b0d2-4b6cceb7e9ba)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a77c0cd-510f-4302-9768-092310edb865

### Latest review repairs: admission and local-key recovery

- **Late revocation:** the plugin supplies a synchronous live-grant assertion through the existing canonical input-admission guard. Runtime options are snapshotted before asynchronous loading. Grant/peer revocation during preparation rejects before durable input acceptance; after acceptance, host-owned execution keeps its existing custody. No copied authority, weaker validator, or new store/schema.
- **Local-key rotation:** a failed exact core binding now produces a durable denial even when the display mount still looks valid. Recovery no longer dereferences a missing authorized mount; the denied outcome survives reopen and replay.
- Real Gateway regressions failed on the original producer for revocation before facade dispatch and before input staging, then passed repaired. Coordinator grant/peer regressions and the local-key rotation regression also failed pre-fix. The after-acceptance control remains accepted.
- **134 tests / 7 files passed**, covering canonical Gateway admission, registry/grant ownership, Reef coordinator/state/E2E. Naming-only lint cleanup was followed by **29 coordinator/state tests** passing.
- Complete changed-file check plan passed across the initial run and a serialized continuation from its lint failure (parameter reassignment/shadowing corrected). Core/plugin/test types, formatting, lint, SDK/storage/dependency guards and dead exports passed. The initially failed command itself is not reported as green.
- Full `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build` passed at the exact head. Fresh final P0/P1 autoreview was scoped-clean.
- Latest repair delta: production **+48/-44 (net +4)**, tests **+330/-188**, docs **+10/-1**. The small production growth adds the synchronous admission assertion contract; duplicated coordinator checks were absorbed.
- Controlled late-admission race tests are distinct from the video's pending-approval revocation scenario.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.agent-input-authority.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts src/plugins/registry-runtime.cross-session-grants.test.ts src/plugins/cross-session-grants.test.ts extensions/reef/src/federation-coordinator.test.ts extensions/reef/src/federation-state.test.ts extensions/reef/src/federation-e2e.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build
```

### Rejected-mutation expiry repair

Current published head: `6ef84e685234984ba8cfdc887435c895e1c6577b`. The preceding `ebc20b31daf42cb41caa1cbb504bdb37a51efc09` passed [full exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34325320063) and is the built two-Gateway recording above. This follow-up changes only rejected core grant mutations and their regression tests; it has not been represented as a new two-Gateway recording.

- ClawSweeper revision 9 confirmed the prior admission/recovery repairs and found that returning an existing grant from the atomic update callback renews its TTL. All four mutation operations now use the store's existing no-write sentinel on lifecycle, role, binding, and generation rejection. Successful host-authorized mutations are unchanged; no schema, API, config, or storage design change.
- **Original failure:** all four store-operation regressions changed `createdAt` and `expiresAt` after rejection. The real Gateway regression accepted a prompt after the original standing grant's deadline because a rejected peer revocation had renewed it.
- **Repaired proof:** actual SQLite metadata remains unchanged. Closing/reopening the candidate store retains the original deadline; authorization fails at that deadline. The real Gateway dispatch rejects the expired grant with zero pending inputs and no prepared execution. These are controlled-clock production-store/Gateway tests, not a seven-day live soak or a new relay recording.
- **93 tests / 7 files / 4 shards passed**, covering store expiry, grant ownership, canonical Gateway admission, and Reef coordinator/state siblings. A braces-only lint correction was followed by **9/9 Gateway tests** passing.
- Full changed-file plan passed across initial and resumed runs: all types, dead exports, formatting, lint, storage, runtime-loading, import-cycle, webhook and pairing guards. The initial run failed only on two missing test braces, which were corrected; no assertions or production behavior were weakened.
- Fresh P0/P1 autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Production delta **+9/-8** (eight corrected returns plus one invariant comment); tests **+98/-15**.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/cross-session-grants.test.ts src/plugins/registry-runtime.cross-session-grants.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent-input-authority.test.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.test.ts src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.expiry.test.ts extensions/reef/src/federation-state.test.ts extensions/reef/src/federation-coordinator.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/plugins/cross-session-grants.ts src/plugins/cross-session-grants.test.ts src/gateway/server.agent-input-authority.test.ts
```

### Automated checks

- Focused Reef protocol/flow/coordinator/state/command/channel tests, core grant and lifecycle tests, and approval UI tests passed. The initial configuration-inspection regression was repaired and rerun successfully.
- Registry ownership regression: SDK selection and all three loader setup/discovery cases fail on the original producer. The repaired runtime-store, loader, registry, and cross-session-grant suites pass **242 tests**.

prs.title: fix: let readers finish cleanup before the shared worker host stops
prs.body:
Closes #207065

## What Problem This Solves

The Bun `checks-node` lane fails during teardown even though both shared-state read-capacity tests pass. The reader asks its worker to close resources, but the shared host can stop the endpoint before it sends the receipt.

## User Impact

Readers can finish cleanup before terminal shutdown stops the remaining endpoints. An owner that reports a real cleanup failure keeps the host available for retry. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host stop introduced in #206930 ran alongside the owners that still needed it. This change moves that stop after successful owner cleanup. It keeps the original fix for otherwise orphaned endpoints, keeps independent owners draining in parallel, and leaves the missing-receipt error intact. The change adds no timeout or retry.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46076577020/job/140765956302): 797 assertions passed, but teardown failed. The same signature appeared in four consecutive hourly main runs and none of the preceding eight runs’ failed `checks-node` annotations.
- CrabBox AWS, Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, CI-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`: the affected file alone reproduced on `4e06d657fcd5` (2 tests passed, file failed). With the fix it exited 0, including under `vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts`.
- The extended shared-host test failed on the base because the endpoint had already stopped after an owner refused cleanup. On the fixed tree it passed, including the subsequent successful shutdown. All 28 tests across the three shared-host and native-lifecycle files passed. Core typecheck, targeted lint and format passed.
- No full GitHub matrix or independent local review is claimed. The change is +8/-2 production lines and +15/-1 test lines.

Reported by @daniel-lxs (co-author).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-worker-cleanup-receipt-failure-s28ab029e)

## Worked on by

prs.title: refactor(subagents): simplify kill claim and ownership handling
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The subagent kill circuit repeats decisions already made by its claim, retirement, and terminal-state owners. This maintainer-requested R1 cleanup removes those copies without introducing another owner or changing the supported cancellation flow.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Exact-run and full-session Stops keep their existing selection, acceptance, publication, and cleanup semantics. No config, SDK, protocol, or persisted shape changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing claim helper now records its claim or preparation failure once; three callers no longer unpack and copy the same outcome.
- Kill scope consumes the retirement owner's selected/retired/superseded observation. It no longer proves that returned entry's ownership a second time.
- Admin cancellation uses the existing killed-target predicate. The completion producer emits a cancelled target only with the canonical kill error.
- Settlement and publication use the same existing claim assertion, preserving their surrounding contextual error handling.
- Delete the run-local runtime cache guard (the effect runs once), the always-true read-failure conditional, the redundant selected-ID check, and the always-empty initial discovery-error test.

### Circuit map (before editing)

| Responsibility | Inputs and real states | Writer / effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Selection and discovery | exact run or latest owned run; verified, legacy-unverified, or mismatched identity; roots and descendants; newly published roots | `withSubagentKillScope` captures holds and session reads, serializes refresh, and releases its own resources |
| Retained identity | selected, retired, or superseded; same-owner queued-to-running rekey; a different generation or incarnation | `SubagentRunMap.set` publishes immutable records; `captureRetirement` exposes only the selected owner or no entry |
| Kill intent | unclaimed, claimed, reconciled, or released; active, queued, yielded, or terminal execution | `SubagentRunManager.claimSubagentRunKill`, `releaseSubagentRunKillClaim`, and `markSubagentRunTerminated` own durable mutations |
| Physical cancellation | captured inputs, operations, admissions, commands, and execution; ready, declined, or busy | session-controller owns interruption and release; kill acceptance records whether cancellation was accepted |
| Settlement and publication | current claim, superseded claim, pending cleanup, completed cleanup failure, terminal target | the kill settlement owner marks/retire obligations; scope publishes results, reconciles queued metadata, and releases holds |

Durable kill-field writer inventory (all unchanged outside R1):

- `SubagentRunManager.claimSubagentRunKill` and `releaseSubagentRunKillClaim` create/release the claim; `markSubagentRunTerminated` publishes termination through the existing terminal transition.
- `planTerminalCompletion` and `planTerminalTermination` in `completion/subagent-terminal-transition.ts` consume `killIntent`, derive `killReconciliation`, and preserve the winner between completion and cancellation.
- `normalizeSubagentRunState` reconstructs supported persisted claim/reconciliation shapes; `restoreSubagentRunMetadata` repairs the legacy interrupted-shutdown marker.
- `SubagentRecoveryManager.planSupersededKillReconciliations` records supersession; its replacement path clears the old claim/reconciliation for the new execution.
- `reconcileProvisionalSubagentKill` clears reconciliation after the requester outcome is confirmed; `mutateSubagentCompletionInDatabase` clears it in the `reconcileCancelled` transition.
- `SubagentRunMap` publishes/retains immutable rows and retirement observations. Maintenance/requester identity projections copy fields but do not decide or persist new kill state.

R1's local state writers remain the scope's selection/refresh/hold bookkeeping, acceptance's latched abort outcome, and the runtime's admitted claim/result. Physical abort, source settlement, and session metadata remain owned by session-controller, scheduler, and transcript/session writers.

### Complexity and remaining branches

Measured with the same `code-sloppiness` engine on fresh main `09d25c404a45b9943da4fee873e17eb32df31df6` (baseline run 14) and the production content at `c00f26a79d0f198150ba56b4141021d4abbc5938` (run 30); the later conflict-only merge `6bafcde68d1b24c73c3c8d006991125f6304e671` leaves all four production files byte-identical. Seven owned production files scanned; no parse failures. The supplied campaign baseline has the same target CC measurements.

| Target | Before CC / SLOC | After CC / SLOC |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mutateSubagentRunForKill` | 131 / 465 | 127 / 456 |
| `withSubagentKillScope` | 132 / 456 | 128 / 449 |
| cancellation prepare closure | 36 / 121 | 35 / 115 |
| cancellation run closure | 51 / 138 | 48 / 136 |
| capture closure | 48 / 136 | 44 / 129 |
| `killSubagentRunAdmin` | 49 / 128 | 44 / 126 |
| `createSubagentKillSettlementOwner` | 27 / 92 | 25 / 86 |

These targets are not halved. The remaining branches are retained for these concrete contracts, rather than extracted into single-use helpers to move the score:

- Runtime preparation must distinguish ordinary active work from pending launch/recovery, and exact-run interruption from full-session interruption. Claiming before active interruption and after pending-launch drain are different orderings; the two-attempt admission loop permits only the same owner's acknowledged queued-to-running rekey.
- Runtime settlement distinguishes refused/busy cancellation from accepted cancellation with failed reads, a terminal result that wins during admission, a lost claim, and a producer that ignores abort. Combining these loses either the terminal result or the original execution's cleanup obligation.
- Scope capture retains separate mismatch diagnostics, legacy exact selection, latest-generation selection, de-duplication, parent/requester constraints, and session-preparation failure. Retirement permits finishing the original row; it does not permit discovering work beneath a replacement ancestor.
- Scope's remaining queued-cleanup predicate applies only to a terminal killed collector that never started, after reservation cancellation settles. Removing its session, execution, claim, or ownership conditions can overwrite replacement-session metadata. Its refresh/publication branches retain late descendants, failures from sibling cleanup, and the final result before releasing scheduler/retirement holds.
- Admin keeps expected task/generation/requester filters, mismatch errors, cascading outcomes, freshness of the terminal projection, and requester-completion reconciliation. These are separate externally observed outcomes.

Existing unchanged coverage includes `subagent-control.test.ts` (24 concurrent same-ID successor kills, session rotation after claim, replacement metadata, yielded Stop), `subagent-control.concurrency.test.ts` (captured sources and queue cleanup), `subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`, `subagent-control.publication.test.ts`, `subagent-control.refresh.test.ts`, and `subagent-control-kill-settlement.test.ts`. No behavior tests were deleted or weakened.

Production diff: **55 added / 87 removed = net -32 lines**. Test diff: 0. Predicate-bearing lines across the seven owned production files, counted with `git grep -c -E 'if \(|for \(|while \(|&&|\|\|'`: **346 -> 335**. The three inline admin cancelled-target predicates and two copied settlement/publication claim assertions are gone; their existing owners remain.

### Mechanical caller updates

With the coordinator’s explicit authorization, shrink only the `subagent-control-kill.ts` entry in `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt` from 7 to 5. This is a verified shrink-only maintenance update; no other allowance changes.

### Overlap

Open PRs [#194275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194275) and [#189391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189391) also touch kill scope (and #194275 touches the kill entrypoint). Their changes are not included here. Related prior ownership cutovers: [#205940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205940), [#206405](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206405).

## Evidence

- [Current-head CI run 46091413136](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46091413136) passed for `6bafcde68d1b24c73c3c8d006991125f6304e671`: 41 successful jobs and 28 skipped by the native plan, no failures. All 12 selected Node test jobs passed, along with the ratchet, lint, production/test typechecks, boundary checks, and security gate. Preflight verifies merge checkout `2f7db672267efc876795c4a5e9892ca09b52f567`, with ordered parents `f43dbc41ddc9c6b41a3b49c8613a8c2b9656cd2d` and the reviewed PR head.
- Native review validation passed for the final head with zero findings. The independent P0-P2 branch review was `scoped-clean` on production commit `a02ea85d2c208d774fd8a509e932553efe954c61`; subsequent changes are the authorized one-line ratchet shrink and a conflict-only main integration. All four production-file SHA-256 values and reviewed kill-owner contracts are unchanged.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The dependency-free native identity-ratchet check against integrated main passed: 1,547 files, 6,144 pins.
- This was a code-only local checkout. The Testbox allocation queued and was stopped immediately, verified completed. The campaign-approved PR-CI fallback supplied executable proof. No independent execution of the entire `src/agents/subagents` tree is claimed.
- The broader [draft CI run 46089862604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089862604) passed its 14 selected Node jobs, including all 15 control/controller test files, but found the unchanged unused CLI export `src/cli/run-main-policy.ts: isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`. [Scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089297581/job/140806522333) reproduced that exact Knip error. It remains outside this PR; the final normal PR plan did not select that dependency job.
- Landed through normal native protected auto-merge as [99933281e6b544de1ea0059582b872ad6ff63cc5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/99933281e6b544de1ea0059582b872ad6ff63cc5). No inherited-failure exception was needed for the final green run.

### Conflict-only integration

Merged main `f43dbc41ddc9c6b41a3b49c8613a8c2b9656cd2d` as `6bafcde68d1b24c73c3c8d006991125f6304e671` after GitHub reported an allowlist conflict. The manual resolution preserves this PR's kill count of 5 and main's adjacent control-scope count of 2. Production source did not change; the diff against integrated main remains 56 additions / 88 deletions across five files, with production net -32.

prs.title: improve: reduce peak memory during Gateway startup update checks
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547.

## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway starts, it checks SQLite for interrupted updates before serving the first chat. Even an empty ledger made this short-lived process load the Gateway lease manager, database migrations and protocol schemas.

## User Impact

The startup check uses less peak memory and returns sooner. Update repair still verifies the identity of a live driver before it allows a process to continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only repair admission needs process ancestry. This change moves that check and its cache into the repair module. The SQLite reader keeps the same query and abandonment rules for both empty and populated ledgers. The legacy Gateway recovery check and the CLI and Doctor repair routes keep their existing behavior. The run record still owns the comparison between the inherited update ID and its recorded driver facts.

## Evidence

- On the production standalone SQLite child, stock and candidate loaded 774 and 71 files respectively. All 679 TypeBox modules and the state database engine disappeared from this read. Empty and populated ledgers produced byte-identical results. The populated case included a driver confirmed to have exited.
- On macOS ARM64, 24 alternating stock/candidate pairs per fixture reduced median empty-read time from 253 to 147 ms and per-child peak RSS from 137.4 to 105.5 MiB. The populated read fell from 269 to 171 ms and 138.0 to 105.8 MiB. Each arm returned identical rows. On a diagnostic second read in the same child, median latency was 39.06 vs 42.46 ms empty and 26.79 vs 26.51 ms populated. The normal startup path retires this child.
- The import regression fails on the base when reconciliation loads Gateway process cleanup. All 142 focused tests passed on commit `125641fea642`, across eight files covering empty and recorded updates, continuation, startup admission and Doctor revalidation. Both previously failing CI checks passed locally on this commit. The final change rebuilt all 114 standalone child package files byte-for-byte identically to the candidate measured below.

On native Linux ARM64 with Node 24.22.1, a separate run compared 12 alternating stock/candidate pairs for each fixture, on one CPU with a 4 GiB memory limit and swap disabled. All 48 child processes returned the expected result. Median within-pair reductions were:

| Fixture | First read | Child peak RSS | Sampled peak PSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Empty ledger | 284 ms | 26.9 MiB | 26.8 MiB |
| Populated ledger | 305 ms | 28.9 MiB | 29.3 MiB |

Every pair improved on all three measurements. A second read in the same child had mixed timing on populated ledgers: the paired median was 23.6 ms slower, with five of twelve pairs faster. On empty ledgers the second read was faster in all twelve pairs. The ordinary startup path retires the child after its first read. [Linux ARM64 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46088228255)

The full [constrained Linux Gateway first-turn issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547) remains open.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop fencing session recall on transcript-only refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #205386

## What Problem This Solves

On a busy Gateway, `sessions_search` called with a query but without `sessionKey` intermittently failed with:

> Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request

The failure was not one-shot: recall captures the disclosure revision before its SQLite worker read and re-validates it afterwards, twice. Any transcript activity happening anywhere on the Gateway reset that revision, so both read attempts were fenced and the call threw. Supplying `sessionKey` skips the recall path, which is why the same search worked when the key was passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/session-row-projection.ts` called `revisions.invalidate()` inside `transcriptUpdates.refresh()` on every transcript refresh — both the certified fast path and the materialized slow path. `invalidate()` clears the memoized sharing token that `searchRecallSessionTranscripts` captures as `projection.sharingRevision` and compares after each worker read (`sessions-search-recall.ts:55,187,197`). A transcript write to any unrelated row therefore looked like a disclosure-scope change.

Transcript-only refreshes update presentation facts (activity summary, preview, transcript watermark); they do not change who may read a session. The fix makes that invalidation conditional on the transcript generation: the publish path compares the incoming generation with the row's certified watermark before installing it, and only a rotated generation — a destructive transcript rewrite — fences recall. Pure forward appends preserve the generation and skip the fence. Every genuine scope change still invalidates the token through its own path:

- `mark()` for structural and visibility publications;
- `revisions.materialized()` for board and membership changes;
- `revisions.replace()` / `remove()` for row replacement and lifecycle;
- the catalog owner refresh.

Fact consumers are unaffected: `publishFacts` still runs on both refresh paths, so summaries and previews keep updating. No change to the recall fence itself, no new dependencies, no guard weakening.

## Revision 2: both review findings addressed

**Finding 1 — non-postimage receipts were dereferenced.** The publish guard only excluded `unchanged`; an `unknown` settlement (indeterminate worker outcome) or `absent` receipt carries no `value`, so reading its generation violated the `SqliteCommittedFact` union. The publish path now narrows explicitly: `const postimage = fact.kind === "postimage" ? fact.value : undefined`. Only a certified postimage can prove an append; `unknown`/`absent` receipts keep conservative recall invalidation.

**Finding 2 — summary-less rows missed destructive clears.** `activitySummaryWatermark` is only certified for rows carrying an activity summary, so a row without one had `previousGeneration === undefined` and a transcript wipe never fenced recall. Two changes close this:

- the sharing-revision fence is decoupled from presentation refresh: a dedicated `fence()` callback runs regardless of which refresh branch (full refresh vs. lightweight revision bump) the row takes;
- a row without a certified watermark classifies a clear by content: it held messages (`transcriptHasMessages === true`) and the postimage now reports an empty transcript (`rawSeq === null` — the production clear path writes no row transcript, so `hasMessages` alone is not sufficient).

## Revision 3: rewrite classification certified by the mutation owner

The remaining finding rejected the accepted edge case above: a summary-less row whose first observed publication is a **non-empty** destructive rewrite was still indistinguishable from an append. Per the review guidance, rewrite classification is now preserved through the existing transcript owner, independently of summary presence:

- `recordTranscriptReplacementMutation` / `touchTranscriptMutationInTransaction` accept a `destructiveRewrite` option. The replacement store passes `destructiveRewrite: deleted` — true when the replacement actually removed admitted content, whether the replacement list is empty or not. The payload-rewrite path passes it when it rotates the transcript generation (admission-invalidating rewrites).
- Both publish branches (actor hot-state and SQL `RETURNING`) carry the flag onto the `SessionTranscriptAuthority` postimage as a certified `destructiveRewrite?: true` fact; `isTranscriptReceipt` validates it.
- The projection fence (`session-row-projection-transcript.ts`) now fences recall when `postimage.destructiveRewrite === true`, with no dependence on a row watermark. The watermark comparison and the content-based clear classification remain as fallbacks for publications that carry no certification (older receipts, non-owner paths).

This closes the summary-less non-empty rewrite window at the producer: the mutation owner knows it deleted admitted rows and certifies that on the postimage, so the publish side no longer has to infer intent from watermarks the row may never have had.

## Revision 4: suffix removal certified by its producer

The remaining finding identified one more destructive producer that skipped certification: `replaceSqliteTranscriptSuffixInTransaction` deletes the trailing suffix and rotates the transcript generation, but its `touchTranscriptMutationInTransaction` call supplied only `projectionReady`. When a nonmatching prefix survives, the postimage keeps `rawSeq` non-null and `hasMessages` true, so a summary-less loaded row had neither a prior watermark nor an empty-postimage signal to fence on — a recall hit for the removed suffix could be returned. This writer is reached by `SessionManager.removeTrailingEntriesAsync` (embedded-agent recovery and `sessions_yield` cleanup).

The suffix producer now certifies the rewrite itself: `destructiveRewrite: plan.expectedRows.length > 0` — true exactly when existing suffix rows were removed, false for a pure append at the tail (which keeps the recall revision). The certification flows through the same postimage fact and projection fence as Revision 3, so no row watermark is required.

## User Impact

Session recall on a busy Gateway keeps working while other sessions are writing transcripts: `sessions_search` without a `sessionKey` no longer needs retries. Destructive transcript rewrites keep their protection: a rewrite landing during a read invalidates the stale capture, so recall discards hits for deleted content instead of serving them — for clears, non-empty replacements, and suffix removals that retain a prefix alike, with or without an activity summary, and for indeterminate worker settlements. Disclosure protection is unchanged — real visibility, sharing, membership, owner, or lifecycle changes during a read still fence the response and produce the same error.

## Evidence

Real runtime: the shipped `startGatewayServer` entry (`node --import tsx` against this worktree's source), a fresh `chmod 700` state dir, a real WebSocket protocol client, and 48 materialized busy sessions receiving continuous transcript writes while each search is in flight. Each scenario runs 4 recall searches without `sessionKeys` plus 2 searches with explicit `sessionKeys`, then one recall search while the visible target's transcript is repeatedly cleared through the production replacement path (`replaceSqliteTranscriptEventsInTransaction`). Revision 3 adds a non-empty replacement phase: each round seeds a fresh cold row holding the needle, materializes it through the worker row-fact reader (`sessions.list`, no activity summary and therefore no certified watermark), then runs sustained non-empty replacements while a recall read is in flight — every replacement deletes the admitted row and inserts a fresh needle message with a new event id. A returned hit whose `messageId` is not the final replacement's id is a stale capture of a deleted row. Every rewrite commits through the production store path and emits the owning mutation's post-commit transcript notification (`emitSessionTranscriptUpdate`), the same outward notification the production locked-write owner sends after commit.

Before the fix (bug present in the same harness):

```
[proof] round 3 recall without sessionKeys (1609ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (1972ms): {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request"}}
[proof] round 1 search with explicit sessionKeys (1430ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] RESULT: FAIL (recall reported a scope change)
```

After the fix (current head):

```
[proof] round 1 recall without sessionKeys (9612ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (3159ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] without sessionKeys: 4/4 succeeded, 0 threw scope-changed
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] recall during destructive rewrites (3 clears, 87ms): {"ok":true,"hits":[]}
[proof] append phase: PASS (recall tolerated transcript-only activity)
[proof] destructive-rewrite phase: PASS (no stale hits after destructive rewrites)
[proof] RESULT: PASS
```

Revision 3 runtime — non-empty rewrites on summary-less loaded rows (`proof-205386-r3.mts`, real `startGatewayServer` + signed WebSocket protocol client). Each round seeds a fresh cold row holding the needle, materializes it through the worker row-fact reader (no activity summary, so no certified watermark), then runs **sustained non-empty replacements** (a new event id each time, still matching the needle) while a recall read is in flight. A hit whose `messageId` is not the final replacement's id is a stale capture of a deleted row.

Fixed arm (current head) — the mutation owner certifies every replacement on the postimage; **141 receipts carry `destructiveRewrite=true`**:

```
[proof] receipt agent:main:replace-target-1: kind=postimage destructiveRewrite=true generation=...
[proof] non-empty replacement round 1: {"target":"agent:main:replace-target-1","ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request"},"inFlight":true,"searchMs":5642,"rewrites":132}
[proof] non-empty replacement phase: PASS (no stale hits on summary-less loaded rows)
[proof] RESULT: PASS
```

Base arm (previous head) — **0 receipts carry `destructiveRewrite`** (the field does not exist); the first replacement's publication installs a watermark on the row, after which the watermark comparison fences:

```
[proof] non-empty replacement round 1: {"target":"agent:main:replace-target-1","ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request"},"inFlight":true,"searchMs":6234,"rewrites":121}
[proof] non-empty replacement phase: PASS (no stale hits on summary-less loaded rows)
[proof] RESULT: PASS
```

Both arms fence under *sustained* rewrites: the fixed arm through the certified postimage (and the watermark), the base arm through the watermark it acquires from the first replacement's publication. The defect is the **first-publication window** — a summary-less loaded row receiving its first non-empty replacement before any watermark exists — which a runtime scan cannot isolate deterministically (the needle read lands at the tail of the search, with no observable marker for the read→revalidation gap). That window's red-on-base discrimination is carried by the parametrized unit regression below, which forces the ordering with a mock at the owning boundary: the summary-less non-empty cell returns the stale needle hit on the previous head and `results: []` with the fix. Production files were swapped back and byte-verified (`restore_ok=1`) after the base arm.

Regression tests (each guard verified red on base / green with the fix, production files swapped back and byte-verified after each base arm):

- transcript-only tolerance: red with the unconditional invalidation restored, green with the fix;
- destructive rewrite during the worker read, parametrized over **{with, without} an activity summary × {clear, non-empty replacement}** (4 cells): the summary-less non-empty cell is red on the previous head (the stale needle hit survived because the row had no watermark to compare) and green with the fix; all four cells green on the fixed head — recall returns `results: []`;
- suffix removal retaining a nonmatching prefix during the worker read, parametrized over **{with, without} an activity summary** (2 cells): the summary-less cell is red on the previous head (`expected [ { …(7) } ] to deeply equal []` — the removed needle hit survived because the retained prefix kept `rawSeq` non-null and the row had no watermark) and green with the fix; the with-summary cell is green on both heads (its watermark comparison already fences). These two rewrite-fencing regressions live in a dedicated sibling module, `sessions-search-rewrite-fence.test.ts`, extracted from `sessions-search-scope.test.ts` to keep both files within the line cap;
- unknown transcript receipt through the real projection (`session-row-projection.test.ts`, folded into the existing sharing-revision case): an indeterminate settlement published via `publishCommittedSessionTranscriptReceipts` must fence recall without throwing; red on base (revision unchanged), green with the fix.

Acceptance suites plus every consumer of the changed contracts (mutation-state publishers, replacement store, suffix producer, rewrite paths, receipt validator, portability conformance) — 15 files:

```

  src/gateway/session-row-projection.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.transcript-regression.test.ts \
```

`oxlint` on the touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors; the type-aware pass (`oxlint --type-aware`, tsgolint, 293 rules) also reports 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean. A standalone `tsc` program over the touched files does not complete in this environment (the import graph exceeds the local time budget), and full-graph `tsgo` cannot run here (system GLIBC is older than 2.32), so whole-project type checking is delegated to the exact-head CI run; the type-aware lint above is the local type signal. prs.title: fix(codex): list the model catalog again when the reported account changes
prs.body:
## Problem

`test/plugins/codex-model-catalog.gateway.test.ts` fails on main since #206994 (`expected 2 to be greater than 2`). It passes at #206994's parent.

#206994 reuses a Codex `model/list` discovery for the same client, the same account revision and 300 s. The revision advances on `account/updated` and on login, logout and config writes. An app-server that OpenClaw does not own (user-home mode over a socket, or a proxy) can switch accounts without sending `account/updated`. The catalog then kept serving the previous account's model list and account type for up to 5 minutes, even for `models.list refresh: true`.

## Fix

The memo owner (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.ts`) now reads `account/read` first (`refreshToken: false`, no `/models` fetch). It reuses a discovery only if Codex reports the same account as when it listed. The other reuse conditions stay: same client, account revision and scope, within 300 s.

The account response includes ChatGPT `userId` and workspace routing, so two workspaces of one email are told apart. The slow call that #206994 avoids, `model/list`, which refetches `/models`, is still skipped on a warm turn.

## Security check

A list cached for one credential cannot be served for another:
- The shared client key includes the auth profile, the auth binding fingerprint, the prepared auth, the auth requirement and native auth. A different credential or auth mode therefore uses a different client, and reuse requires the same client.
- `account/updated` advances the revision (`client.ts:656`).
- The gap fixed here is a silent account switch inside an app-server OpenClaw does not own.

## Impact

- Codex-runtime users on an app-server that switches accounts outside OpenClaw: the catalog follows the reported account on the next load, not up to 5 minutes later.
- Warm turns: one local `account/read` RPC instead of none. `model/list` and its `/models` refetch stay skipped, so the #206994 gain holds.

## Evidence

- Gateway test: passes at `f31a6781^`, fails on main `49c5e3ea`, passes on this branch (1/1, 300 s timeout, run alone).
- New unit test: one client and revision, accounts a, a, b, b, a. It lists exactly `[a, b, a]`. Red on main (main lists once), green here (model-catalog unit files 20/20 and 2/2).
- Known limit: two API-key accounts report the same `account/read`, so a silent key-to-key switch on an unowned server still waits for the 300 s TTL.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): consolidate terminal-effect retirement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal completion repeated the same callback-retirement decisions between timing, status, hooks, browser cleanup and MCP cleanup. This maintainer-requested R5 re-circuit replaces those copies with one ordered dispatch path. Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206454.

## User Impact

No intentional user-visible change. Completion still releases its scheduler slot, records timing, publishes status/progress, runs the ended hook, cleans resources, and hands off announcement or provisional-kill confirmation in that order. Duplicate completions can still drain announcement while another caller is waiting on browser cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

An explicit phase table shares preparation, retirement and suppression decisions. The continuing path stays synchronous between its final ownership decision and dispatch. The browser claim retains its own checks after lazy loading and inside the durable claim; those protect a real asynchronous boundary.

### Circuit map

- **States:** queued/running; yielded; terminal with provisional cancellation; canonical terminal; cleanup pending/completed; retired. Delivery and requester-settle obligations remain owned by their existing transition/announcement owners, including persisted legacy delivery shapes.
- **Inputs:** the completion request and expected runtime owner; producer reply/timing; the transition's effect plan; bound session effects; suppression and newer-session facts; existing browser/progress stamps.
- **Writers:** `subagentTerminalTransition.complete/terminate/cleanup` plan execution, cancellation and cleanup postimages; `mutateSubagentRuns` publishes them. `SubagentLifecycleController` owns runtime bindings, progress identities and explicit suppression. Sweeper/recovery writers retain their existing suppression and browser-reset responsibilities. The completion runtime resets `cleanupHandled` for a retry. This adapter alone claims `browserCleanupDispatchedAt`; its suppression write uses the existing lifecycle mutation owner. No writer or persisted field is added.
- **Effects:** release swarm capacity → timing → status/progress → ended hook → cleanup eligibility → browser → MCP → announcement/kill-confirmation. The phase loop now owns the common check between those steps. Browser loading and claim publication retain their separate checks because a successor or another claimant can arrive during either await.
- **Deleted copies:** seven inline supersession/retirement branches and their repeated callback checks; the separate ended-hook deferral derivation. References to `retireSupersededSession` and `shouldDeferEndedHook` in this adapter are now zero.

### Complexity and retained decisions

Measured with `code-sloppiness` 0.2.0+vk.4 over the same five files, with complete coverage and no parse failures. Base `3e9ac5fc6ce4d03a4c1851f53a1246b783b10cb1`, head `060f8fc55f972e79434bb9315380de48a60ee7d8`.

| Target | Base CC | Head CC | Retained contract |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `completeTerminalEffects` | 78 | 58 | Not halved: the remaining branches distinguish suppression, timing failures/unknown outcomes, optional status/progress/hooks, durable browser claim success versus known refusal versus unknown failure, run/session MCP cleanup, and provisional-kill versus announcement tails. These are distinct tested effects, not copies of the stage-retirement policy. |
| `completeSubagentRunAttempt` | 35 | 35 | The terminal transition already owns row decisions. This adapter retains result capture, collector session preparation, atomic publication, and two different resource lifetimes: release the completion lock before asynchronous effects, release the collector session on every exit. |
| `completeCleanupBookkeeping` | 24 | 24 | The transition already owns the cleanup decision. Keep durable publication before detached transcript/MCP/context cleanup and requester wake; retired-row effects still distinguish no replacement from a replacement. |
| `planTerminalCompletion` | 97 | 97 | Already moved by #206454 to `completion/subagent-terminal-transition.ts`, outside R5's owned files. Its producer-reply, timeout and cancellation reconciliation remains in that owner; this PR does not move or duplicate it. |

The completion runtime is unchanged: its recovery checks preserve pending result evidence, retry-versus-cleanup selection, yielded-settlement identity and unknown-outcome propagation.

- Production lines: **-30** (236 added / 266 removed; reindentation accounts for much of the diff). Tests: unchanged.
- Named callback/supersession/suppression decision references in this adapter: **29 → 10** (`git grep -c -E 'isCurrentTerminalCallback|newerGenerationOwnsSession|shouldSuppressSessionEffects'`).
- The original seven-instance clone group is gone. Two stop-dispatch blocks remain: the common phase boundary and the browser-loader boundary, which may be crossed asynchronously within one phase.
- Mechanical caller updates: none.
- Overlap search: #207030 touches the neighboring announcement owner, not this file. Existing completion/bookkeeping proposals #136554, #197335, #121309 and #187924 touch neighboring R5 files left unchanged here.

## Evidence

All runtime proof below used source `060f8fc55f972e79434bb9315380de48a60ee7d8` on [Testbox run 46089277424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46089277424). The wrapper verified the source tree and reported the command results; the full-suite wrapper exit was **0**.

- **236 focused tests passed across three unchanged files:** lifecycle (198), terminal-effects and completion-runtime (38 combined).
- **Full `src/agents/subagents` run:** 2,266 tests passed, 1 existing test skipped; 177 files passed, 1 skipped. This includes all 141 spawn production-boundary cases. The campaign's previously reported Stop-authority failure was not observed in this run.
- **`pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: passed.**
- **Changed-file oxlint:** zero warnings/errors. Local oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- **`pnpm deadcode:exports`: pre-existing failure, not called green.** The script scan passed with zero entries; production and full-tree scans reported only `src/cli/run-main-policy.ts:isRemoteAgentDispatchInvocation`, outside R5. Restoring this adapter to base `3e9ac5fc6ce` reproduced the same export finding. The reviewed adapter was restored and its blob checked before the full suite ran. No R5 export was reported.
- **Local autoreview, branch mode P0–P2:** scoped-clean, no actionable findings, with intact unchanged transition, lifecycle, persistence and terminal-effects test context. Reviewed base `3e9ac5fc6ce4d03a4c1851f53a1246b783b10cb1` → head `060f8fc55f972e79434bb9315380de48a60ee7d8`.
- **PR CI:** [run 46090443267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46090443267) passed, including its `openclaw/ci-gate`; the gate publisher also reports success for this head. The hosted review found no actionable defects.

prs.title: refactor(openai): send every tool strict: false on routes that accept the field
prs.body:
## Problem

Since #206735, OpenAI-protocol routes that accept the `strict` tool field send `strict: true` for each tool whose schema is strict-compatible as written. Measured on native OpenAI Responses, strict tools make requests slower and gave no measurable benefit.

Measurement: a mid-tool-loop request built by `main` (17 default tools, about 14.1k input tokens). Both arms closed the root of the two tools that pass the strict check (`apply_patch`, `write`). ON = `strict: true` on those two, OFF = `strict: false`; nothing else differs. Two warm-ups per arm, then 30 interleaved pairs per model. The cache was warm in both arms (about 14.1k of 14.1k input tokens cached on gpt-6.2-sol, 13.95k of 14.1k on gpt-5.4-mini; no request had 0 cached tokens).

| Model | Arm | n | Total p50 / p90 | First token p50 / p90 | Invalid / malformed args |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-6.2-sol | strict ON | 30 | 3,247 / 4,052 ms | 2,557 / 3,379 ms | 0 / 0 |
| gpt-6.2-sol | strict OFF | 30 | 2,273 / 3,363 ms | 1,209 / 2,654 ms | 0 / 0 |
| gpt-5.4-mini | strict ON | 30 | 3,129 / 4,364 ms | 2,002 / 2,699 ms | 0 / 0 |
| gpt-5.4-mini | strict OFF | 30 | 3,135 / 4,639 ms | 1,950 / 2,422 ms | 0 / 0 |

- Paired ON − OFF median, gpt-6.2-sol: total **+427 ms (95% CI +73 to +1,284)**, first token **+510 ms (95% CI +39 to +1,544)**.
- gpt-5.4-mini: no difference (total +145 ms, 95% CI −345 to +806; first token +68 ms, 95% CI −144 to +353).
- Benefit: **0 invalid or malformed tool arguments in 120 of 120 runs**, in both arms.
- On sol, all 30 calls went to the non-strict `edit` tool and the request was still slower, so the cost comes with the request, not with calling a strict tool.

## Solution

`compat.supportsStrictMode` keeps its documented meaning: the route accepts the `strict` tool field. A route that accepts it now sends `strict: false` on every tool; other routes still omit the field. Explicit `false` is required: a live request today showed that OpenAI Responses treats an omitted `strict` as `true` (and filled an optional argument).

Deleted, now unreachable: per-tool strict eligibility (`resolveOpenAIToolStrictFlag`), strict schema normalization (`normalizeStrictOpenAIJsonSchema` and the `strict` profile in tool-schema normalization), `isStrictOpenAIJsonSchemaCompatible`, the strict schema prewarm, and the strict arms of three perf scripts. Kept: `findOpenAIStrictSchemaViolations`, a public plugin SDK export.

**Turning strict on:** there is no config switch. A provider plugin can still set `strict` in its own payload hook. A config switch would need a new compat field, and strict has no measured benefit on any current request; the decision record was amended to this. Before #206735 (which is in no release tag), `supportsStrictMode: true` on a custom route already meant "send `false`", so no shipped config changes meaning.

## Impact

- Native OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, and routes that declare the field (ClawRouter `openai/*` Responses, Baseten, `compat.supportsStrictMode: true`): every tool goes `strict: false`. Default and code-mode requests already had no strict tool on `main` (0 of 17 default tools qualify as written), so their bytes do not change. A closed, all-required plugin or MCP tool loses `strict: true`; its tool bytes change once, so expect one prompt-cache miss per affected session.
- Undeclared custom endpoints: unchanged (field omitted).

## Evidence

- Touched and consumer tests pass (provider and transport serialization on declared and undeclared routes, runtime schema contract, prefix stability, schema reuse and truncation).

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206257

## What Problem This Solves

With `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`, scheduled coverage sees an empty tracked-test inventory because Git treats the optimized glob as a literal filename. That can silently omit tests from the daily uncovered-test plan.

## User Impact

Scheduled coverage retains the complete test inventory in literal-path mode. This changes CI tooling only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing full-inventory query in literal-path mode and retain the narrowed query otherwise. The existing suffix filter and Git inventory owner stay unchanged. A fresh-process regression avoids cached Git results hiding the failure.

## Evidence

- Native Node execution of the actual scheduled inventory: base returned 0 tests under literal mode; this head returns all 23,308 tracked tests. Full arrays match the independent full-inventory query with the variable unset, `1`, and `0`.
- Commit hook formatting and line-cap checks passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper completed against base `d22090cfb0e0efafe068dd58775c281511df9243` and head `1b8b958bf44ac4d1253a182920b6fc7b8b4063e6`, with no actionable findings. It independently reproduced the regression and verified the fix.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46077856943) passed. The scheduled-coverage suite passed all four tests, including the new literal-path regression (327 ms). Tooling typecheck, production types, lint, guards, and the remaining selected jobs passed. CI did not select a package build for this tooling-only change. Local dependency reuse was unqualified, so the focused suite and typechecks used this hosted proof.
- Simplification: 4 production lines added, 2 removed, and 13 test lines added; no new owner, cache, exported helper, or dependency.

prs.title: fix: avoid premature layout reads when opening chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a chat first mounts, transcript rows can register before the virtualizer attaches its scroll viewport. The missing attachment window then looks like a browser without ResizeObserver, causing premature synchronous layout reads.

## User Impact

Rows now wait for the existing viewport attachment before measurement. Measured initial placement, reconnects, and browsers without ResizeObserver retain their existing behavior. No settings or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row-ref owner retains mounted rows and lets the existing `_willUpdate` → `observeConnected` replay register them after attachment. This adds five production lines without a new scheduler, retry, or measurement fallback.

The regression preserves the original bind-before-attachment order. The geometry fixture also joins the real scroll-idle and end-settlement owners before checking steady-state coalescing; its zero-read and disposal assertions remain unchanged. Net test growth: 86 lines.

## Evidence

- Both original-order cases failed on unchanged production with the expected premature reads, after their positive controls passed.
- 45 focused cases passed on the exact repaired owner/test bytes: 20 fresh geometry, placement, and real Chromium saved-reader cases plus 25 authenticated unchanged row-ref and initial-range cases.
- The attachment and measurement owners match the frozen main baseline; its additional native-scroll reader settlement does not change this path.
- Scoped autoreview, targeted formatting, the native commit hook, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact published-head CI passed, including the combined CI, dependency, and security review gates.
- This repairs the attachment invariant; it does not establish an overall startup latency improvement.

Follow-up: audit the stale `chat-transcript-geometry.test.ts` entry in `test/vitest/vitest.ui-isolated-paths.mjs`. The actual `.tsx` suite uses canonical per-file cleanup; this proof does not claim isolated workers.

This fix has original-order RED→GREEN proof of the pre-attachment read invariant and real Chromium saved-reader placement coverage. It makes no measured startup-latency claim; no additional trace is claimed here.

Successor verification: the three signed-head file hashes match the preserved proof manifest. The raw 94036 archive and inner summary hashes were verified; its fresh 20 cases and separate 25 carried cases remain distinct. Current-main source still has the attachment defect. A fresh independent source/dependency review found no actionable findings. Local `git diff --check 501ee911942d217cb99c4e85f8e58bf1de9e7853 pr-207043` passed.
