prs.title: fix(google): attach provider_refusal diagnostics for policy stops and prompt blocks
prs.body:
## Problem

When Google GenerateContent streams stop due to content-policy or safety filters—either via a candidate `finishReason` (`SAFETY`, `PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `RECITATION`, `IMAGE_SAFETY`, `IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `IMAGE_RECITATION`) or a `promptFeedback` block (`SAFETY`, `PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `RECITATION`, `IMAGE_SAFETY`, `IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `IMAGE_RECITATION`, `MODEL_ARMOR`, `JAILBREAK`, or an uncategorized/missing `blockReason`)—`consumeGoogleGenerateContentStream` throws `google_generation_failed` or `google_prompt_blocked` without attaching a structured `provider_refusal` diagnostic to `output.diagnostics`.

Because OpenClaw's terminal error handling and refusal formatter rely on `provider_refusal` (already emitted by Anthropic and OpenAI):
- `formatProviderRefusalText()` returns `undefined`, so users see generic error copy (`OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply` / `Your request couldn't be completed.`) instead of the refusal category and guidance.
- `isTerminalAssistantError()` does not classify the response as a provider refusal.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Stream["Google SDK / Managed SSE"] --> Reducer["consumeGoogleGenerateContentStream"]
  Reducer -->|"policy finishReason or promptFeedback block"| Diag["output.diagnostics += provider_refusal"]
  Reducer -->|"technical stop (e.g. MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL)"| NonRefusal["no provider_refusal"]
  Diag --> Terminal["isTerminalAssistantError = true"]
  Diag --> Copy["The provider refused this request (category: ...). Revise the request and try again."]
```

## Changes

- **`packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts`** (shared by both SDK and managed SSE transports):
  - Record a bounded `provider_refusal` diagnostic (`{ type: "provider_refusal", timestamp, details: { provider, category? } }`) for:
    - Candidate policy/safety `finishReason` values (`SAFETY`, `PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `RECITATION`, `IMAGE_SAFETY`, `IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `IMAGE_RECITATION`), normalized to lowercase category.
    - `promptFeedback` blocks without a candidate, attaching the lowercase category when recognized (including `MODEL_ARMOR` and `JAILBREAK` from `BlockedReason`) and omitting `category` when `OTHER` / unspecified / absent.
  - Keep technical stops (`MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, `OTHER`, `LANGUAGE`, `TOO_MANY_TOOL_CALLS`, `UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL`, `NO_IMAGE`, `STREAM_INCOMPLETE`) free of `provider_refusal`.
  - Preserve existing candidate-failure precedence across later frames and settle both `promptFeedback` and candidate refusal diagnostics only after loop/iterator cleanup and the abort check so cancelled streams never carry `provider_refusal`.
  - Emit only the configured provider ID and allowlisted category (no raw provider prose).
- **Tests**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts`: candidate policy finish categories, non-refusal technical stops, cancellation precedence, and categorized/uncategorized `promptFeedback` blocks.
  - `extensions/google/transport-stream.lifecycle.test.ts`: managed SSE `SAFETY` prompt blocks, `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` candidate stops (preserving custom provider IDs), non-refusal `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, candidate refusal preserved across a later `STOP` frame, and cancellation during prompt-block body cleanup.
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`: end-to-end Google `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` formatting, `isTerminalAssistantError`, and `isProviderRefusalNoticeText`.

## Behavior (Before vs After)

| Google SSE event | Before (`3b9cf90709e`) | After (`7559b5437ad`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `finishReason: "PROHIBITED_CONTENT"` | `providerRefusal: null`; empty payload / generic failure notice (`fallbackSafe: true`) | `providerRefusal: { provider, category: "prohibited_content" }`; `"The provider refused this request (category: prohibited_content). Revise the request and try again."` (`fallbackSafe: false`) |
| `promptFeedback: { blockReason: "SAFETY" }` | `providerRefusal: null`; `"⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply..."` | `providerRefusal: { provider, category: "safety" }`; `"The provider refused this request (category: safety). Revise the request and try again."` |
| `finishReason: "MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL"` | `providerRefusal: null`; generic failure copy | Unchanged (`providerRefusal: null`) |

## Release Note Context

Google GenerateContent safety/policy refusals (`PROHIBITED_CONTENT`, `SAFETY`, `BLOCKLIST`, `SPII`, `RECITATION`, image safety/policy stops, and `promptFeedback` blocks) now emit structured `provider_refusal` diagnostics so OpenClaw displays the canonical refusal message and treats them as terminal refusals instead of generic reply failures.

## Verification & Proof

Tested commit: `7559b5437ad5da59858809518539eea5edbd1040` (base `3b9cf90709e537a202fdb669b31c1b9ad551ca3c`).

### Shipped CLI before/after proof (`openclaw agent --local --json`)

Run against a local `127.0.0.1` SSE server configured as a `google-generative-ai` provider (`apiKey: "test-dummy-key"`, isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), comparing the unpatched shipped `dist/index.js` (identical `packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts` to `3b9cf90709e`) against the built candidate `dist/index.js` (`7559b5437ad`):

```json
// 1. PROHIBITED_CONTENT candidate finish
// BEFORE:
{"exitCode":1,"payloads":[],"providerRefusal":null,"error":{"kind":"incomplete_turn","message":"Google generation stopped (PROHIBITED_CONTENT)","code":"PROHIBITED_CONTENT","fallbackSafe":true,"terminalPresentation":false}}
// AFTER:
{"exitCode":1,"payloads":[{"text":"The provider refused this request (category: prohibited_content). Revise the request and try again.","isError":true,"mediaUrl":null}],"providerRefusal":{"provider":"mock-google","category":"prohibited_content"},"error":{"kind":"incomplete_turn","message":"The provider refused this request (category: prohibited_content). Revise the request and try again.","code":"PROHIBITED_CONTENT","fallbackSafe":false,"terminalPresentation":false}}

// 2. SAFETY promptFeedback block
// BEFORE:
{"exitCode":1,"payloads":[{"text":"⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw logs --follow` in your terminal.","isError":true,"mediaUrl":null}],"providerRefusal":null,"error":{"kind":"incomplete_turn","message":"Google prompt blocked (SAFETY): Prompt blocked","code":"SAFETY","fallbackSafe":false,"terminalPresentation":false}}
// AFTER:
{"exitCode":1,"payloads":[{"text":"The provider refused this request (category: safety). Revise the request and try again.","isError":true,"mediaUrl":null}],"providerRefusal":{"provider":"mock-google","category":"safety"},"error":{"kind":"incomplete_turn","message":"The provider refused this request (category: safety). Revise the request and try again.","code":"SAFETY","fallbackSafe":false,"terminalPresentation":false}}

// 3. MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL technical failure (unchanged non-refusal control)
// BEFORE & AFTER:
{"exitCode":1,"payloads":[{"text":"⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw logs --follow` in your terminal.","isError":true,"mediaUrl":null}],"providerRefusal":null,"error":{"kind":"incomplete_turn","message":"Google generation stopped (MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL)","code":"MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL","fallbackSafe":false,"terminalPresentation":false}}
```

### Automated checks

- `pnpm oxlint` & `pnpm oxfmt --check` on all 4 touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm build:runtime`: succeeded on `7559b5437ad`.
- `pnpm vitest run packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.formatassistanterrortext.test.ts src/shared/assistant-error-format.test.ts src/sessions/session-run-error.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-outcome.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.refusal.test.ts`: 8 test files, 284 passed.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): "Media failed." replies give no cause in the Gateway log
prs.body:
Closes #206555

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a WhatsApp auto-reply's media fails to send (for example a spoken MP3 reply on a host without `ffmpeg`), the chat gets the text plus "⚠️ Media failed." and the Gateway log has two lines that do not say why, so the cause cannot be found.

## User Impact

The log now says which step failed (`loading`, `preparing`, or `uploading`). When a voice note could not be converted because `ffmpeg` is missing, it also says how to install it:

```
Failed sending web media to +15551234567 while preparing: ffmpeg not found in trusted system directories. Install it via your system package manager (e.g. brew install ffmpeg).
```

What the chat receives is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverWebReply` (`extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/deliver-reply.ts`) dropped the error in its `onError` handler. That is deliberate: `deliver-reply.test.ts` asserts that the error text, which can include the attachment URL, is not logged, and this PR keeps that assertion. Instead:

- `send` records the current step for each attachment: loading it (`loadWebMedia`), preparing it (`prepareWhatsAppOutboundMedia`, which converts non-Opus audio to a voice note with ffmpeg), then uploading it.
- `onError` logs that step to `whatsappOutboundLog` and adds `step` to the `replyLogger` warning.
- If the failed step is `preparing` and `resolveFfmpegBin()` (the shared resolver, already exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-runtime`) throws, its message is appended. That message is OpenClaw's own install hint and contains no message content.

Other conversion or transport errors still log only the step.

## Evidence

**Live WhatsApp.** I ran an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`) with a temporary home and state, linked by QR to a real WhatsApp account. Only the account's own "Message yourself" chat was admitted (`selfChatMode`, empty `allowFrom`). Afterward I ran `channels logout` and deleted the state. The agent model was a local stub that always replies "Sure, I can help with that.". Speech used the real Microsoft TTS provider with `tts.auto: "always"`. ffmpeg was hidden from the Gateway process by a macOS `sandbox-exec` profile covering the trusted directories. In each run I sent the account one self-chat message. The number is redacted.

Main (ff722f42f78): the phone received the text plus "⚠️ Media failed." and no voice note. The log gives no cause:

```
[whatsapp] Inbound message +15551234567 -> +15551234567 (direct, 68 chars)
[whatsapp] Failed sending web media to +15551234567
[whatsapp] Media skipped; sent text-only to +15551234567
WARN web-auto-reply {"to":"+15551234567"} failed to send web media reply
```

Branch (39ac4d405aa): the phone received the same text and warning. The log names the step and how to fix it:

```
[whatsapp] Inbound message +15551234567 -> +15551234567 (direct, 85 chars)
[whatsapp] Failed sending web media to +15551234567 while preparing: ffmpeg not found in trusted system directories. Install it via your system package manager (e.g. brew install ffmpeg).
[whatsapp] Media skipped; sent text-only to +15551234567
WARN web-auto-reply {"to":"+15551234567","step":"preparing"} failed to send web media reply
```

**Reply-path harness, for the ffmpeg-visible control.** I also called the real `deliverWebReply` directly. It ran the real `loadWebMedia` on an MP3 from the Microsoft TTS provider (`openclaw infer tts convert --channel whatsapp`), the real `prepareWhatsAppOutboundMedia` and ffmpeg conversion, and the real WhatsApp loggers. Only the socket (`reply`/`sendMedia`) was stubbed. This harness was a temporary test file and is not committed. With ffmpeg hidden, it gave the same main and branch lines as above. With ffmpeg visible, on both main and the branch, the MP3 was converted and sent as a voice note (`auto-reply sent (media)`, `mediaKind: "audio"`) and the reply had no warning.

Tests, in `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/deliver-reply.test.ts`:
- New case: a voice note whose conversion fails while `ffmpeg` cannot be resolved logs `while preparing: <install hint>`, does not log the attachment file name, and still sends "⚠️ Media failed.".
- Existing upload-failure case: now also expects `step: "uploading"` and keeps its "error text not logged" checks.

Both fail on main and pass on the branch. `pnpm test:extension whatsapp`: 198 passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +28/-11; test delta +24/-1 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the cause-free log lines with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the log output of failed WhatsApp auto-reply media; delivery behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice consult with no answer promises a follow-up
prs.body:
Closes #206572

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a realtime voice consult (Voice Call, FaceTime, meeting bot) finishes with no speakable text, the tool result tells the voice model "I need a moment to verify that before answering.", so the caller is told to wait for an answer that never comes.

## User Impact

The caller now hears that no answer was found and can ask again or move on, instead of waiting in silence. Consults that produce an answer are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgentInternal` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts`) returns `params.fallbackText ?? "I need a moment to verify that before answering."` after the agent run has completed with no visible text. Nothing schedules a later answer at that point, and none of the callers (`extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.ts`, `extensions/facetime/src/talk-consult-controller.ts`, `src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts`, the browser Talk path) passes `fallbackText`. The default is now `"I couldn't find an answer to that."`. A caller-supplied `fallbackText` still wins, and yielded consults keep their acknowledgement.

## Evidence

No real carrier call. I ran an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, temp `HOME`, state, config and profile) with the voice-call plugin on Twilio and realtime voice through the xAI realtime plugin. Its `baseUrl` pointed at a local stand-in for the xAI realtime websocket, which asks for one `openclaw_agent_consult` tool call and logs the tool result the Gateway sends back. The consult's agent run used a local OpenAI-compatible chat model (`responseModel`) that returns empty content. A local script played Twilio's side: the inbound webhook signed with `X-Twilio-Signature` (verification on) and the realtime media stream. Twilio REST hosts were blocked at DNS.

- Main: the agent run ended empty (the embedded runner retried once), the Gateway logged `[talk] agent consult produced no answer: agent returned no speakable text`, and the tool result was `{"text":"I need a moment to verify that before answering."}`.
- Branch: same run and log line; the tool result is `{"text":"I couldn't find an answer to that."}`.
- Control on the branch, with the model answering: the tool result is the answer, `{"text":"Sure, I can help with that."}`.

<details>
<summary>Realtime stand-in log</summary>

Main:

```
realtime -> tool call openclaw_agent_consult {"question":"What did the pharmacy say about my refill?"}
model request -> ""
model request -> ""
realtime <- tool result {"text":"I need a moment to verify that before answering."}
```

Branch:

```
realtime -> tool call openclaw_agent_consult {"question":"What did the pharmacy say about my refill?"}
model request -> ""
model request -> ""
realtime <- tool result {"text":"I couldn't find an answer to that."}
```

Branch control:

```
realtime -> tool call openclaw_agent_consult {"question":"What did the pharmacy say about my refill?"}
model request -> "Sure, I can help with that."
```

prs.title: fix(release): identify jobs blocking child evidence sealing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Full Release Validation cannot seal a child receipt because a predecessor is still nonterminal, the sealer reports neither the attempt nor the jobs. Operators cannot tell which exact jobs blocked sealing from the error.

## User Impact

The existing refusal now names the attempt, the count of nonterminal predecessors, and up to five job names, IDs and statuses. A nonterminal predecessor still prevents the receipt and upload output from being written. Terminal, provenance, and coverage gates are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

In [Normal CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45994871383/attempts/2), GitHub returned ten runnerless queued rows with the same name as the completed [Bun shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45994871383/job/140527140788). The [frozen sealer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45994871383/job/140552029527) checked raw rows and refused. Main already resolves the one real execution before applying the terminal gate (#204438); no retry or new filtering is needed. This adds the incident-shaped regression and improves the refusal for truly unresolved jobs.

## Evidence

- Replayed the complete recorded inventories (282 jobs in attempt 1, 292 in attempt 2) through both sealer entry points, reconstructing the active run/publisher status. Frozen `180ba41af126` reproduces the exact refusal; current tooling seals the real attempt-2 shard alongside retained work and preserves the failed [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45994871383/job/140551979980) and `workloadConclusion: failure`. No FRV was dispatched and no historical receipt changed.
- The CLI diagnostic test failed on the base, then passed with the fix and proved that no receipt or upload output is written for queued/running predecessors.
- 211 focused tests passed across the producer, child reuse, and FRV state suites. Targeted tooling typecheck, lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: improve: start the model catalog worker without loading channel schemas
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

A cold model catalog worker loaded the bundled channel configuration schemas solely to look up a fallback channel label and description. In the standard package, that import reached a 363,074-byte generated module before the worker accepted its first request.

## User Impact

The catalog worker starts with less JavaScript to load. Channel registration still recovers its released label, selection label, docs path and blurb when the installed catalog is unavailable. Config validation and Doctor keep their existing schema source. This measures one worker in isolation. The constrained Gateway's first-turn memory issue remains open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing generator already has the ordered and normalized channel rows. It now publishes a registration-only array carrying the channel ID, configurable flag, label and description. Registration keeps the same synchronous first eligible match and official fallback. The full schema publication and the channel ID index stay byte-identical, so history readers avoid loading the new projection. Registration adds no filesystem lookup.

## Evidence

Compared standard Darwin arm64 packages built from the same base with Node 26.7.0. Cold timings used 24 alternating stock/candidate pairs per worker, fresh workers, compile caching disabled and no instrumentation preload. A separate loader trace measured the actual files loaded.

| Measurement | Stock | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Catalog worker bytes loaded at ready | 9,708,264 | 9,348,155 |
| Catalog worker ready p50 / p95 | 467.158 / 498.325 ms | 451.953 / 494.917 ms |
| Worker V8 physical / used heap at ready, medians | 91.781 / 61.435 MiB | 90.812 / 61.384 MiB |
| Populated history first RPC p50 / p95 | 164.215 / 168.758 ms | 163.313 / 173.178 ms |
| Warm history RPC p50 / p95 | 1.235 / 1.318 ms | 1.225 / 1.302 ms |

- All 24 catalog worker pairs started faster, with a paired median change of −14.704 ms. The static ESM import graph independently shrank by 360,109 bytes.
- Two real catalog revisions returned identical ordered snapshots and runtime-model hashes. Each returned 13 entries, including eight remote and one configured entry, plus four runtime models. The single cold request took 1,517.385 / 1,517.404 ms.
- A real populated history RPC loaded the same 230 files and 4,155,179 bytes in both builds. The 229 shared content files were byte-identical. Only the build provenance field differed. All 96 history responses had identical bytes, including both seeded messages.
- The catalog import guard failed on stock at the registration-to-schema edge and passed on the change. The five focused files passed 54 tests, including all 28 released rows with the installed catalog absent, the nonconfigurable row, unknown channel and official fallback.
- Normal package build, generated-channel freshness, single-file CI routing, six-file formatting, and staged content/generated freshness checks passed.

The packaged measurements above used `1c3f30c3e909`. The successor `6c97150fc020` changes only a test-local identifier. The pinned repository linter reproduced the original shadowing error and passed the corrected file with the same command. All six registration tests passed again.
The final committed-range ClawSweeper review found no correctness issues. Both requested focused suites passed (7/7), and the generated-channel freshness check passed again on the successor.

prs.title: fix(android): preserve Watch Live progress during audio capture
prs.body:
Related: #202818
Fixes #206566

## What Problem This Solves

Watch Live treated each microphone acknowledgment as a Listening transition, replacing its working indicator while the agent was busy. Equal snapshots also bypassed StateFlow conflation and were sent through the phone-to-watch bridge again.

## User Impact

Microphone acknowledgments preserve Thinking and Speaking. Unchanged Talk snapshots no longer send redundant bridge events. Audio transport, session checks and permissions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Conversation progress belongs to the existing transcript/playback transitions. The existing snapshot owner now suppresses equal values without adding state, a cache or a transport filter.

The newly landed skills accessibility fixture also used two retired contracts. Its setup now uses the canonical connection display and direct skill list, preserving every assertion so Android tests can execute.

## Evidence

Baseline `d22090cf` versus candidate `0f27f268`:

| Workload | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50 microphone acknowledgments while Thinking | Listening; 50 additional Talk events | Thinking; zero additional events |
| Three identical ready events | Three additional Talk events | Zero additional events |

The regressions exercise the real controller, codec and bridge with a recording sender. They also cover Speaking, changed conversation text and a replacement attempt. Five affected suites passed in both phone flavors: 105 cases each, with the two ThirdParty skills cases retried after regenerating missing local Room output. The final two regressions and app ktlint passed after diagnostic cleanup.

Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range `d22090cf..0f27f268`: no actionable correctness or security findings; the patch was assessed as correct. Its offline proof assessment did not receive the executed results or media above. Paired-device validation remains unrun.

CI attempt 1 completed the third-party unit tests and Android app lint successfully, then the job exceeded its 20-minute deadline before final settlement. [The canceled job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46079573729/job/140775536629) contains no test assertion failure. The existing recovery route completed [attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46079573729/attempts/2) successfully at the unchanged head. The first timeout remains historical; no CI configuration was changed.

Production +2 lines; tests +109. No Bluetooth latency or battery measurement is claimed.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: microphone acknowledgment replaces working status with Listening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c33b2b0-514b-4a26-b773-0f2b9b170b8a) | ![After: working status stays Thinking](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca14e26c-84da-4edd-bb79-97e360084d5a) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Listening status highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdafc9ec-f50d-48da-b612-b914671af681) | ![After: Thinking status highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05bce5db-cb4d-43a8-a063-571828bcae37) |

prs.title: fix(agents): move active node presence to current-turn context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #192364. `active_node` and `active_node_identity` are on the Runtime line, and `openai-completions` routes relocate that line into the first user message. When a Mac app quits or comes back, the value changes, message 1 is rewritten, and everything after the system prompt falls out of an exact-prefix cache. The report measured 67-85 s replies instead of about 1 s on a ~90k-token session.

## User Impact

A node going away or returning no longer rewrites earlier messages, so the conversation stays cached. The model still sees the current active computer every turn, now in the newest message's runtime context.

Two visible changes:

- CLI backends now always get the fact in the turn context. It used to be skipped when the system prompt was sent, because the Runtime line carried it.
- **Known gap:** `settled-tool-finalization` and raw model runs carry no runtime facts by design, so those runs no longer see `active_node`. They previously saw it through the system prompt. The report also flags this. I kept their exact-prompt rule rather than adding text; a maintainer may want to weigh in if finalization needs it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direction comes from @dertbv's diagnosis and local test in the issue. The CLI and harness paths already deliver this as a per-turn fact, so this moves the embedded path onto the same model:

- Removes the two fields from `buildRuntimeLine`, the runtime info types, `buildSystemPromptParams` and the prompt-cache field labels.
- `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` runs `prepareActiveNodeContext` for the admitted run's operator profile and then adds `buildActiveNodeContextText` as a `conversation-data` fragment. The hint is read synchronously, so the keyed refresh has to come first or a revoked pairing could still show the retired node.
- `buildCliTurnAppendContext` appends it unconditionally, before media progress, which stays last.

## Evidence

![Prefix A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/192364/proof-192364.png)

Real Gateway on Windows with real agent turns in one session. A stub `openai-completions` provider diffs each request's messages against the previous request. Presence is on for requests 1-2, gone for 3-4, and back for 5.

| Request | Presence | Before: earlier messages | After: earlier messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `mac-node-1` | identical | identical |
| 3 | gone | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |
| 4 | gone | identical | identical |
| 5 | back | **`msg[1]` rewritten** | identical |

Before, the value lives in `msg[1]` and changes there. After, each turn's value is in that turn's own message (`msg[2]`, `msg[5]`, `msg[8]`, ...) and later requests leave those bytes alone. In the before run, the rewritten requests kept 54162 of 56011 and 54162 of 57600 characters as an unchanged prefix; the small size is the stub session's, not a real session's.

**CLI backend.** I registered a stub executable with `api.registerCliBackend` (`systemPromptArg`, `systemPromptWhen: "first"`, `resumeArgs`), so the real CLI runner builds the arguments. The stub logs what it received:

| Turn | Before: value in system prompt / prompt | After: value in system prompt / prompt |
|---|---|---|
| First (new session) | `mac-node-1` / none | none / `mac-node-1` |
| Resumed, node gone | not passed / `unknown` | not passed / `unknown` |
| Resumed, node back | not passed / `mac-node-1` | not passed / `mac-node-1` |

`system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` serializes the real system prompt plus a three-message history through `openai-completions` for the same session twice — once with `mac-123` connected and once with no node — and asserts that every message except the newest is byte-identical, that the relocated `Runtime: ` region really lands in `msg[1]` (so the test cannot pass vacuously), and that the newest message carries `active_node=mac-123` / `active_node=unknown`. With this PR's non-test sources reverted to main's behaviour it fails on the first byte-compare at `msg[1]`; with the change it passes. Suggested by @dertbv in the review thread.

Tests, with regressions in `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` that fail without the embedded fact and without the refresh before reading it:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` | 1 passed on `24ecacb` and on the merged head `157112b`; fails at `msg[1]` with this PR's non-test sources reverted |
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 21 passed |
| `system-prompt-params.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `runtime-facts-prompt.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `runtime-prompt.test.ts` | 8 passed |
| `gateway/node-registry-pairing.test.ts` | 12 passed |
| `worker-turn-launcher-remote-handoff.test.ts` | 2 passed on `42b8f41` |
| `tool-result-truncation.test.ts` | 1 failed, 55 passed: a Windows path error (ENOENT on a drive-letter path joined under the temp dir) in a spill-pointer test this PR does not touch; I did not rerun it on base |
| `attempt-prompt-build.*`, `attempt-prompt-submit`, `attempt-context-advancement`, phase and media-hint tests | passed |
| `cli-runner/prepare.durable-context.test.ts` | 13 failed, 7 passed, same as base |
| `cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` | 13 failed, 100 passed, same as base |

Those two CLI files already fail on this Windows machine (for example `/bin/echo` not resolvable and `EBUSY`). I compared failing test names with and without the change and none are new, but this means CLI path coverage is weak locally, so please check them in CI.

Passed locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (credited exactly by `config/test-lines-allocations/192423-active-node-prefix.txt`), `agents-root` and `agents-other` test types (the project CI failed on before).

**Merge of `upstream/main` @ `ae8155cf` (head `157112b`).** The branch had become `CONFLICTING`. One file conflicted, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-build.ts`, and only in its import block: upstream added `import type { McpToolCatalogDiagnostic }`, this branch adds `readAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` (still exported by `src/agents/admitted-run-context.ts:356`, still used at line 545). Both imports are kept; no behaviour changed by the merge. Re-ran on the merged tree in a git worktree with the main tree's `node_modules` junctioned in:

| Suite | Result on `157112b` |
|---|---|
| `system-prompt.active-node-prefix.test.ts` | 1 passed |
| `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` | 23 passed |
| `oxfmt --check attempt-prompt-build.ts` | clean |

Typecheck stays CI-only in this worktree (`run-tsgo` refuses a checkout whose declarations resolve through junctioned `node_modules`).

## What was not tested

- Presence was changed with a preload calling `setActiveNodeContexts`, because this box has no paired Mac. The node connect and disconnect path was not exercised; the report did exercise it on a similar patch.
- The stub compares bytes. I did not measure real cache hits or latency on a caching server; the report's numbers are from its own patched build.
- The CLI proof uses a stub executable through the real runner, not Claude Code or another real CLI.
- Requester-scoped refresh is covered by unit tests and the default-profile live path; I did not run a non-owner profile with a revoked pairing end to end.


## Related defect deliberately left out of this PR

The remote macOS skills note has the same effect on the cached prefix: `getRemoteSkillEligibility` builds `Remote macOS node available (…). Run macOS-only skills via exec host=node on that node.` in `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts`, `prepareSkillsForPrompt` appends it to the skills text, and that text becomes the `## Skills` section of the frozen system prompt. A Mac node going online or away therefore rewrites the same bytes this PR just moved out of the Runtime line.

@ensignwesley reproduced that on main with serialized-request evidence (two identical online requests, first differing byte at offset 6444; [run](https://github.com/ensignwesley/openclaw/actions/runs/43812563271)) and is preparing a separate embedded-only change that sends the note through the current-turn carrier introduced here, leaving CLI and Codex output byte-identical. It is not folded in because the note lives in the snapshot/projection path shared by the CLI and Codex skill-prompt builders, so including it would widen this PR's proof scope from presence placement to skills-snapshot behavior. It will be linked here once opened.

prs.title: improve: skip an unneeded sort in sandbox workspace scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before every sandboxed message, the workspace check scans the paths it already knows, one directory depth at a time. Each depth's list was first sorted with `localeCompare`, a locale-aware string sort. Nothing that consumes the scan depends on that order. Siblings in a depth already run four at a time, so the order in which results arrive was never fixed.

## User Impact

None visible. The sandbox workspace check does slightly less work before each message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consumers of the scan:
- `readActualWorkspaceManifestImpl` and `serializeWorkerWorkspaceManifest` sort entries themselves.
- `createLocalWorkspaceManifestTree` sorts its nodes, and `updateLocalWorkspaceManifestTree` sorts its changes in byte order.
- Fingerprint observations are keyed by path.
- The unchanged-file probe stops at the first change and has the same outcome in any order.

Within a depth, parent classification reads only facts from the deeper depth, which is fully joined before the next depth starts.

One behavior differs: when two paths in a depth fail at once, which error is reported now follows the caller's order rather than sorted order. Limit errors trip at the same totals.

## Evidence

- New randomized-order test (`local-workspace-manifest-scan.test.ts`): the real manifest scan runs with the canonical path set shuffled 8 times. Tree roots, pack preparations and both manifest documents equal the sorted run.
- Existing scan, manifest and warm-reuse suites pass, including the independent-writer reuse case.
- Linux profile on real `git ls-files` order (Docker on a shared dev host, overlayfs, 67,667 tracked files, known-path scan, median of 7): warm 262 ms → 255 ms, cold 549 ms → 568 ms. Both differences are within noise. Production order is already close to sorted, so the sort cost little there. The saving appears on unsorted input; a synthetic microbenchmark measured 94–115 ms for 60k shuffled paths in one depth.
- Adversarial review: no missed order dependency. My first test went through a path that sorts its output, so it could not show order independence. It was replaced with the scan-level test.

prs.title: fix(release): clarify pinned FRV recovery eligibility
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An operator can enable `reuse_evidence=true` on a full publication qualification and reasonably expect that the run will support pinned aggregate recovery. If no `publication_artifact_source_json` was selected, the protected recovery command instead refuses with a generic error after the run has already finished.

## User Impact

The dispatch helper now warns in previews and actual dispatch output when a candidate publish request with `rerun_group=all` lacks the explicit source. The run can still qualify normally. The pinned recovery refusal identifies the missing input and explains that it cannot be added to an existing admission. The docs distinguish pinned `--prepare-recovery` from `pnpm frv recover`, which has a separate evidence contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the already resolved dispatch inputs for an advisory warning and share the existing direct-plan/source check across recovery preparation, sealing, and verification. No source is inferred, no requirement is relaxed, and no artifacts, dispatch inputs, or release policy change.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original refusal read-only against FRV run `45993803508` attempt 1 from exact main `ec51f7fc6aee`. Repeating it with the fix named the missing source and wrote no recovery request. No validation or recovery workflow was dispatched.
- Both regressions failed as expected on the base, then passed. All four affected tooling suites passed: 222 tests in 163.14 s locally. The existing valid-source fixture still dispatches and emits no warning.
- Scripts and tooling test typechecks, targeted lint and format, and `git diff --check` passed. The repo-wide docs anchor audit listed 11 errors outside the changed pages and links; neither new reference was flagged.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, the chat composer takes up several rows even when it’s empty. During a reply, Stop and Send can appear side by side, and a long draft stops growing after only a few lines.

## User Impact

- An empty composer fits on one row with **+**, the message field, the mic, and **Talk**. Focusing the field opens the card and reveals permissions, model, and effort controls. A draft grows up to six lines, then scrolls.
- One primary button switches between **Talk**, **Send**, and **Stop**. A follow-up that can be sent during a reply brings back **Send**; clearing the field brings back **Stop**. When the Gateway supports queue choices, pressing and holding **Send** opens those choices without dismissing the keyboard.
- **New Chat** focuses a local draft without creating an empty session on the Gateway. The standard slash suggestions stay available when you type `/new`.
- VoiceOver announces the action the button performs now. **Model sign-in** remains reachable when authentication blocks sending or capture controls replace the model menu.

The macOS layout is unchanged. The iOS model sheet, attachment sheet, and the expanded layout after keyboard dismissal are separate changes in the series.

## Why This Change Was Made

The primary action stays in one place instead of putting Send and Stop next to each other. The compact row and the expanded card share the same text field, so switching layouts doesn’t reset the draft, selection, or focus.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, iPhone simulator:** Opened New Chat from the sidebar, confirmed the draft focused without creating a session on the Gateway, and confirmed `/new` still showed its standard suggestion. This flow used an isolated Gateway.
- **iPhone simulator, app fixtures:** Checked model sign-in while sending was blocked, the single Stop button while drafting during an active reply, voice recording during a reply, and the Send long-press queue menu. The fixture for the screenshot comparison does not offer an outbox, so the single action is Stop in that state.
- **Build and focused tests:** The exact patch built for iOS. On macOS, the selected SwiftPM filter passed 392 Swift Testing tests across nine suites and 12 XCTest cases. The native localization inventory and diff checks passed.
- **Existing UI test failure:** The nested-tool transcript test expanded and collapsed both results, then failed on the exact `Knowledge Status` accessibility label on both the base and this patch. The composer change leaves that assertion intact.
- **Other local UI test limits:** The original height assertion reported 56 points before and after typing. It passed only with a local diagnostic change that is not in this PR. A separate menu check did not refocus the composer after Permissions; that run did not establish an app defect.
- **Not covered:** Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, and camera capture. The simulator’s model sign-in scenario verifies that the entry point stays reachable, not that a real provider login completes.

Same iPhone simulator, dark theme, draft, and held reply. The app fixture does not support queueing in this scenario. Before: `c9761f6adc49`; after: `575254bfc607`. The model name is redacted.

prs.title: fix(cron): tell the agent how to reread a shortened job scratch
prs.body:
AI-assisted: yes

Closes #206807

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where a scheduled automation with an oversized job scratch (over the 2000-character prompt budget) received a truncation notice that told the agent to "reread the complete scratch" without naming any way to read it. The agent followed the notice literally and searched the filesystem and the live state database — on the reporter's deployment, one heartbeat job burned 121 guard-rejected tool calls in a day with a 3-minute search phase before any real work started.
- **Related:** #152916 (same subsystem, different symptom); #205770 (scheduled worker reporting). Fix signal: `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`, `issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** When the injected scratch is shortened for the prompt, the notice now names the concrete retrieval operation available to the running automation: the `automations` tool's `scratch_get` action, which is self-scoped to the current job and needs no job id. The agent gets an actionable address instead of an instruction to search.
- **Out of scope:** The 2000-character prompt budget itself is unchanged (documented behavior: scratch storage is capped at 256 KiB while prompt injection is bounded; full reads go through `scratch_get`). Truncation direction, the `openclaw cron scratch` CLI name resolution, and the store cap are not touched. The docs paragraph is aligned with the new notice wording.
- **Highest-risk area:** The notice text is embedded in the scheduled-run prompt, so wording changes must stay consistent with the tool descriptions the agent already sees.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The referenced action (`scratch_get`, self-scoped, documented in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`) already exists and is unchanged; only the notice and the matching docs sentence change.

## User Impact

- Scheduled automations with scratch longer than the prompt budget no longer receive an unaddressed "reread" instruction; they are pointed straight at the `scratch_get` action, avoiding the filesystem/database search loop and its wasted inference and tool calls.
- Short scratch behavior is unchanged: no notice appears, the full content is injected as before.
- **Success criteria:** With a scratch over the budget, the composed prompt contains a truncation notice that names `scratch_get`; with a short scratch, the prompt is byte-for-byte unchanged from before.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/cron/run-prompt.ts` (`appendCronJobScratchPrompt`), regression tests in `src/cron/run-prompt.test.ts` ("points a shortened scratch at the scratch_get action...", "keeps an unshortened scratch prompt free of truncation notices"), and the docs sentence in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Worktree build of this branch on Linux, two layers: (1) the real prompt composer (`prepareCronAutomationPrompt` → `appendCronJobScratchPrompt`, both execution paths share this composer) run against a real sqlite state store containing a 14,141-character job scratch (same order of magnitude as the reported 19,814-character deployment), before and after the patch; (2) a full scheduled-agent run through the shipped Gateway entry point — isolated Gateway booted from this branch's `dist/entry.js`, real model provider (OpenAI-compatible reasoning model `glm-5.3`), a job with a 23,611-character scratch forced through `cron.run`, transcript read back via `cron.history`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # Regression test (RED on main, GREEN with the patch)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cron/run-prompt.test.ts
  # Related suites touching the same composer paths
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cron/session-run.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts
  # Real-path prompt composition against a real state store (14,141-char scratch)
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs evidence-prompt.mts   # run once on base, once on this patch
  # Shipped-entry-point run: isolated Gateway (dist/entry.js) + real model + 23,611-char scratch,
  # forced via cron.run, verified via cron.runs + cron.history (harness: cron-scratch-real-run-v1)
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  [evidence] scratch content chars: 14141
  [evidence] prompt scratch section chars: 2119
  [evidence] scratch section tail (last 400 chars):
  ...checklist line 36: status ok, no new findings to 
  [Scratch shortened for this prompt; read the complete scratch with the automations tool's scratch_get action before replacing it.]
  [evidence] notice names scratch_get: true
  [evidence] unaddressed reread notice present: false
  ```
  Shipped-entry-point run (isolated Gateway from this branch's dist + real model `glm-5.3`, via provider credentials redacted from all artifacts):
  ```text
  [evidence] harness: cron-scratch-real-run-v1 (isolated Gateway, dist/entry.js @ 758c0eda)
  [evidence] job: agentTurn, sessionTarget=isolated, delivery=none; scratch 23611 chars (revision 1), prompt budget 2000 chars
  [evidence] run: cron.run force -> status ok, completionStatus succeeded, durationMs 53801
  [evidence] prompt (from cron.history): ...checklist line 31: routine heartbeat check ok, nothing to r
  [Scratch shortened for this prompt; read the complete scratch with the automations tool's scratch_get action before replacing it.]
  [evidence] tool calls in the run: tool_describe(automations) x2, automations(scratch_get), automations(record_result)
  [evidence] automations scratch_get call: {"action":"scratch_get","jobId":"<self job>"} -> full 23611-char scratch returned (isError false)
  [evidence] filesystem / database search tools used: none
  [evidence] run summary: STATUS = GLASS-OTTER-7419 (line 120), ANCHOR = north-harbor-88 (line 350), highest checklist line number = 360
  [evidence] STATUS and ANCHOR markers only exist beyond the 2000-char excerpt (lines 120/350 of 360), so the model could not answer without retrieving the complete scratch
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The shortened-scratch notice now names the `automations` tool's `scratch_get` action; the bounded delivery itself (2,119 of 14,141 characters) is unchanged, as is the unshortened-scratch prompt. In the shipped-entry-point run, the real model followed the notice: it inspected the `automations` tool, called `scratch_get`, and answered with the STATUS/ANCHOR markers and line count that only exist past the 2000-char excerpt — without any filesystem or database search tool calls.
- **Before evidence:** On base (`origin/main` @ 4bc00fc6f22), the same run produced `[Scratch shortened for this prompt; reread the complete scratch before replacing it.]` with no readable address (`notice names scratch_get: false`), reproducing the report's search-loop premise: 2,119 of 14,141 characters delivered, cut mid-sentence, with an instruction that cannot be followed without searching.
- **What was not tested:** The `openclaw cron scratch` CLI path is out of scope for this PR. The shipped-entry-point run used one real reasoning model (`glm-5.3`) on an internal OpenAI-compatible endpoint (endpoint URL and API key redacted from the Gateway log, transcript, and evidence artifacts); the base-side search loop from the report was not re-run with a live model — the base composer evidence above shows the address-free notice that motivated it.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (composer against a real state store, plus a real-model run through the shipped scheduled-agent path)
- **Proof limitations:** The Gateway log, transcript, and evidence artifacts are redacted (provider endpoint and API key removed); the model-side search loop from the original report was not replayed on base with a live model.
- **Review state:** Targeted suites and `tsgo:core` pass locally; GitHub CI workflows on this fork PR are pending workflow approval (all `pull_request` workflows, including `CI`, sit in `action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` cannot turn green from the contributor side until they run.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): call stops answering the callee after a failed greeting
prs.body:
Closes #206534

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on an outbound Twilio streaming call, if the opening line fails to synthesize (for example a transient TTS 5xx), the callee gets one reply and then nothing they say is answered for the rest of the call; the Gateway logs "Ignoring barge transcript while initial message is still playing" for each utterance.

## User Impact

A failed opening line no longer turns the call deaf. The callee's later turns are transcribed and answered. Speech over a greeting that is actually playing is still ignored, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`VoiceCallWebhookServer.shouldSuppressBargeInForInitialMessage` (`extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts`) suppressed caller speech for outbound conversation calls in `speaking` whenever `metadata.initialMessage` was set. `speakInitialMessage` (`manager/outbound.ts`) clears that field only after successful playback, so a failed greeting can be retried. After the first reply put the call back in `speaking`, the guard stayed true for the rest of the call.

The manager already tracks the greeting's actual lifetime in `initialMessageInFlight`, which covers synthesis and playback and is cleared in `finally`. The guard now asks the manager (`isInitialMessageInFlight(callId)`) instead of reading the stored text. Failed-greeting retry behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

No real carrier call. I ran an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, temp `HOME`, state, config and profile) with the voice-call plugin on Twilio and streaming on.
- The call was placed with the shipped CLI: `openclaw voicecall call --to +15550007777 --message "Hi, this is the clinic calling about tomorrow." --mode conversation`.
- Twilio REST requests were answered by an in-process stand-in for `*.twilio.com`; every other request used the real transport.
- A local script played Twilio's side: the answered-call webhook signed with `X-Twilio-Signature` (verification on), the Media Streams websocket, and playback-mark echoes.
- STT went to a local stand-in for xAI realtime STT. Telephony TTS went through the OpenAI speech plugin to a local stand-in whose first request returns HTTP 500. Replies came from a local OpenAI-compatible chat model set as `responseModel`.

Scenario: the greeting synthesis fails, then the callee says three things, 5 s apart.

- Main: greeting failed; the first utterance got a reply (13 audio frames and a playback mark); the second and third got nothing, and the log shows `Ignoring barge transcript while initial message is still playing (CAoutbound1)` twice. The model was called once.
- Branch: greeting failed; all three utterances were answered, with three model requests and three reply playbacks.
- Control, both main and branch: the greeting synthesizes and its playback mark is echoed 4 s late. Speech during the greeting is ignored, with the same log line, and the next two utterances are answered.

<details>
<summary>Simulated Twilio side and stand-in logs</summary>

Main:

```
[twilio] Twilio REST: create call to +15550007777 (stand-in answered sid CAoutbound1)
[twilio] callee answers; call webhook -> 200
[twilio] caller says "Hello? Who is this?"
[twilio]   after "Hello? Who is this?": 14 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio] caller says "Sorry, can you repeat that?"
[twilio]   after "Sorry, can you repeat that?": 0 audio frames and 0 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio] caller says "Hello, are you still there?"
[twilio]   after "Hello, are you still there?": 0 audio frames and 0 playback marks sent to the callee
[stub] tts voice=coral input="Hi, this is the clinic calling about tomorrow." -> 500 (injected)
[stub] model request -> "Sure, I can help with that."
[stub] tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Sure, I can help with that." -> 200
[voice-call] Failed to speak initial message: TTS conversion failed: openai: OpenAI TTS API error (500): injected synthesis failure; xai: not configured
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=19
[voice-call] Ignoring barge transcript while initial message is still playing (CAoutbound1)
[voice-call] Ignoring barge transcript while initial message is still playing (CAoutbound1)
```

Branch:

```
[twilio]   after "Hello? Who is this?": 13 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio]   after "Sorry, can you repeat that?": 13 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio]   after "Hello, are you still there?": 13 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[stub] tts voice=coral input="Hi, this is the clinic calling about tomorrow." -> 500 (injected)
[stub] model request ... -> "Sure, I can help with that."   (x3)
[stub] tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Sure, I can help with that." -> 200   (x3)
[voice-call] Failed to speak initial message: TTS conversion failed: openai: OpenAI TTS API error (500): injected synthesis failure; xai: not configured
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=19
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=27
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=27
```

Control (branch; main identical):

```
[twilio]   after "Hello? Who is this?": 0 audio frames and 0 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio]   after "Sorry, can you repeat that?": 13 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[twilio]   after "Hello, are you still there?": 13 audio frames and 1 playback marks sent to the callee
[voice-call] Ignoring barge transcript while initial message is still playing (CAoutbound1)
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=27
[voice-call] Auto-responding to inbound call ... chars=27
```

</details>

Tests, in `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.test.ts`:
- New case: a call in `speaking` that still holds a failed greeting's text, with no greeting in flight, answers caller speech. It fails on main and passes on the branch.
- Existing greeting-suppression case: now drives the manager's in-flight state.

`pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 624 passed. In the second shard, `manager/store.test.ts` failed once in the full run; it passes alone on both main and this branch (15/15) and is not touched here. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +9/-7; test delta +27/-0 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous guard with no state or config migration. Blast radius is caller-speech handling on outbound streaming conversation calls while the call is in `speaking`.

prs.title: fix(install): piped install-cli.sh --onboard fails after a successful install
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201388

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users who follow the documented `curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash -s -- --onboard` one-liner get a completed install followed by exit code 1: the final `openclaw onboard` step inherits the curl pipe as stdin, onboarding's interactive TTY guard refuses to start, and `set -euo pipefail` turns the already-successful install into a failure.
- **Related:** #201388; the clawsweeper review endorsed reusing the controlling-terminal handoff already shipped in `install.sh` (labels: P0, impact:ux-release-blocker, clawsweeper:queueable-fix).
- **Rebased** onto current main (now includes #202312 PATH handoff hint + #202385 JSON fd separation): the piped-stdin handoff itself is still unfixed on main (reproduced below against main `fd3e1dc0b16`), and this change composes with both — the no-terminal hint uses the same `printf %q` quoting as the #202312 hint, and the onboarding skip event rides the same NDJSON fd as #202385.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** `--onboard` in the piped form runs onboarding reading from the user's terminal, the same handoff `install.sh` already uses; with `--json` the event stream on stdout stays parseable as independent NDJSON records; with no terminal available the installer defers onboarding with a visible setup command and keeps exit status 0.
- **Out of scope:** onboarding's own TTY guard is unchanged (not weakened); `install.sh` is unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** the terminal handoff at the end of `main()` in `scripts/install-cli.sh`.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The `has_controlling_tty` / `controlling_tty_path` helpers are copied from the merged sibling installer (`scripts/install.sh`, including the macOS #200244 note), and regression tests pin the piped, no-terminal, and `--json` paths.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `curl … | bash -s -- --onboard` now drops the user into onboarding after the install and exits 0; headless runs get `No terminal available; run …/bin/openclaw onboard to finish setup.` on stderr plus an `onboarding` skip NDJSON event, and still exit 0.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `scripts/install-cli.sh` (terminal handoff at the end of `main()`) and `test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts` ("runs onboarding with stdin from the controlling terminal, not the installer pipe", "defers onboarding without a terminal and keeps exit status and JSON output clean", "keeps onboarding output out of the JSON event stream when a terminal exists").

## Evidence

The [maintainer correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201430/commits/f614c26fbdb3935cb50d72fdc3f4909dbb5a7b1e) preserves interactive stdin/stdout even in a session without a controlling terminal. When install output is redirected, the wizard receives both descriptors from the terminal. Its prompts stay out of redirected logs and JSON output. [Linux CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46081671971/job/140782408926) passed the real-PTY cases for redirected output, JSON, and inherited descriptors, plus the no-terminal deferral. The [final terminal handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201430/commits/0b1505a96191a3c11ea43eedd79339d08c1d0ca4) opens the terminal once for reading and writing. The [installer workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46081671929) passed, including ShellCheck on the assembled script. The PTY tests use a CLI fixture that enforces the wizard’s terminal requirement. The packaged-wizard run below is the contributor’s earlier Linux proof.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (EL8) at rebased head `245241f3194` (on main `fd3e1dc0b16`). **Real end-to-end product runs** — no installer function stubbed: the standalone distribution script (`install-cli.sh` with `install-policy.sh` inlined, the exact artifact shape `openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh` serves) was fed to bash through a pipe (`cat install-cli.sh | bash -s -- …`), run inside a real PTY (util-linux `script`, `stty cols 120 rows 36`) and under `setsid` without a controlling terminal. Node 24.22.1 was downloaded from nodejs.org (sha256 verified) and the real `openclaw` npm package was installed from the registry over the network, in isolated `HOME`/prefix directories.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # format + lint + same-directory tests + tsgo:core (rebased head)
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh scripts/install-cli.sh test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts   # all pass (99 tests)
  # installer test surface incl. upstream's new #202312/#202385 tests after the rebase
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts test/scripts/install-cli.freebsd.test.ts \
    test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts \
    test/scripts/website-installer-sync-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/install-smoke-candidate-payload.test.ts
  # -> 389 passed | 2 skipped
  bash -n scripts/install-cli.sh scripts/install.sh   # syntax OK
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** (real piped installer, real network install, real onboarding)
  ```text
  === run-base: current main fd3e1dc0b16, fresh real install 2026.11.5, PTY, plain --onboard ===
  install OK ("added 361 packages in 1m", OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15))
  final `openclaw onboard` step: "Onboarding needs an interactive TTY. Use `openclaw
  onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk ...` for automation."   -> installer EXIT 1

  === run-a: this patch, fresh real install 2026.11.5, PTY, plain --onboard ===
  install OK (Node 24.22.1 from nodejs.org, openclaw@2026.11.5 from npm)
  ```

prs.title: fix(voice-call): per-number TTS voice is ignored on streaming calls
prs.body:
Closes #206536

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a per-number `tts` override (`numbers["+1555..."].tts`) has no effect on Twilio streaming calls; the greeting and replies on the routed number are spoken in the global voice.

## User Impact

Calls to a routed number are spoken with that route's TTS settings, as `docs/plugins/voice-call/tts-and-inbound-calls.md` describes. Calls to other numbers keep the global voice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runtime.ts` builds one telephony TTS provider from the global `config.tts`. `speak()` (`manager/outbound.ts`) already resolves the call's effective config with `resolveVoiceCallEffectiveConfig`, but passed only a `voice` string to `playTts`, and `TwilioProvider.playTtsViaStream` called `synthesizeForTelephony(text)` without it. Now:

- `PlayTtsInput` carries `tts`, the call's effective voice-call TTS config, and `speak()` passes it.
- `playTtsViaStream` hands it to `synthesizeForTelephony(text, tts)`.
- `synthesizeForTelephony` passes it as `override` to the existing `prepareTtsRequest`, which deep-merges it over the provider's prepared config for that line.

Calls without a route pass the global block, so their synthesis is unchanged. The classic `<Say>` path still maps `voice` to Polly as before.

## Evidence

No real carrier call. I ran an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, temp `HOME`, state, config and profile) with the voice-call plugin on Twilio and streaming on. The global voice-call TTS was OpenAI with `voice: "coral"`, and `numbers["+15550009999"].tts.providers.openai` set `alloy`. Telephony TTS ran through the OpenAI speech plugin pointed at a local stand-in for `/v1/audio/speech`, which logs the requested voice. A local script played Twilio's side: inbound webhooks signed with `X-Twilio-Signature` (verification on), and the Media Streams websocket. STT went to a local stand-in for xAI realtime STT, and Twilio REST hosts were blocked at DNS.

Scenario: an inbound call to the routed number, then one to the main number; each plays its greeting over the media stream.

- Main: both greetings requested `voice=coral`. The routed number's `inboundGreeting` text was used, but not its voice.
- Branch: the routed number's greeting requested `voice=alloy`; the main number's still requested `voice=coral`.
- Branch, route written as in the docs example (`speakerVoice: "alloy"`): also `voice=alloy` for the routed number and `coral` for the main number.

<details>
<summary>TTS stand-in log</summary>

Main:

```
tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Routed line, how can I help?" -> 200
tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Hello! How can I help you today?" -> 200
```

Branch (`voice: "alloy"` route):

```
tts voice=alloy format=pcm input="Routed line, how can I help?" -> 200
tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Hello! How can I help you today?" -> 200
```

Branch (`speakerVoice: "alloy"` route):

```
tts voice=alloy format=pcm input="Routed line, how can I help?" -> 200
tts voice=coral format=pcm input="Hello! How can I help you today?" -> 200
```

Simulated Twilio side, branch: `routed number +15550009999: inbound webhook -> 200`, 12 greeting media frames received; `main number +15550002222: inbound webhook -> 200`, 11 greeting media frames received.

</details>

The greeting and agent replies both go through `speak()`, so replies take the same path; the live run exercised the greeting only.

Tests:
- `extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.media-stream.test.ts`: new case, stream playback passes the call's `tts` to `synthesizeForTelephony`. It fails on main and passes on the branch.
- `extensions/voice-call/src/manager/outbound.test.ts`: the existing voice cases now also expect the effective `tts` in `playTts`, including the routed `alloy` for the inbound Twilio call. They fail on main and pass on the branch.

`pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 624 + 184 passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +16/-10; test delta +27/-0 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores global-voice streaming playback with no state or config migration. Blast radius is Twilio streaming playback; calls without a number route resolve to the same TTS config as before.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): second inbound caller is held forever while a call runs
prs.body:
Closes #206590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with Twilio streaming on, an inbound call that arrives while another call has a live media stream is told "Please hold while we connect you." and placed in a Twilio queue that nothing ever dequeues, so the caller is never connected.

## User Impact

The overlapping caller now hears a busy signal right away and can call back, instead of waiting on hold music for a connection that cannot happen. The first call is not affected, and the next caller after it ends connects as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`TwilioProvider.generateTwimlResponse` (`extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts`) returned `<Enqueue waitUrl="/voice/hold-music">hold-queue</Enqueue>` whenever `callStreamMap` was non-empty (added in #29223 to avoid connecting a second stream). No `<Dequeue>`, `<Dial><Queue>` or queue REST call exists anywhere in the plugin, so a queued caller only leaves the queue by hanging up. This keeps the one-stream guard and replaces the queue with Twilio's terminal `<Reject reason="busy"/>`. The `/voice/hold-music` route in `webhook.ts` served only that queue's `waitUrl`, so it is removed.

Unchanged: the rejected call still gets a voice-call record from the `call.initiated` event, as the queued call did; the stale-call reaper ends it.

## Evidence

No real carrier call. I ran an isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway run`, temp `HOME`, state, config and profile) with the voice-call plugin on Twilio and streaming on, and played Twilio's side with a local script: inbound status webhooks signed with `X-Twilio-Signature` against the configured `publicUrl` (signature verification on), and the Media Streams websocket with the issued stream token. STT went to a local stand-in for xAI realtime STT and telephony TTS to a local stand-in for the OpenAI speech API; Twilio REST hosts were blocked at DNS.

Scenario: call A rings in and opens its media stream; 3 s later call B rings in; call A hangs up (stream stop plus `completed` status callback); 2 s later call C rings in.

- Main: call B got the hold TwiML with `<Enqueue>`. After call A ended nothing reached B, and call C was connected with `<Connect><Stream>` while B was still queued.
- Branch: call B got `<Reject reason="busy"/>`. Call A's greeting and stream were unaffected, and call C was connected with `<Connect><Stream>` and opened its stream.

<details>
<summary>Simulated Twilio side</summary>

Main:

```
[twilio +0.1s] call A inbound webhook -> 200
[twilio +0.1s] call A media stream open
[twilio +3.1s] call B inbound webhook -> 200, TwiML:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Response>
  <Say voice="alice">Please hold while we connect you.</Say>
  <Enqueue waitUrl="/voice/hold-music">hold-queue</Enqueue>
</Response>
[twilio +3.1s] call A hangs up
[twilio +3.1s] call A completed status callback -> 200
[twilio +5.1s] call C (after call A ended) inbound webhook -> 200, <Connect><Stream> TwiML
[twilio +5.1s] call C media stream open
```

Branch:

```
[twilio +0.1s] call A inbound webhook -> 200
[twilio +0.1s] call A media stream open
[twilio +3.1s] call B inbound webhook -> 200, TwiML:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><Response><Reject reason="busy"/></Response>
[twilio +3.1s] call A hangs up
[twilio +3.1s] call A completed status callback -> 200
[twilio +5.1s] call C (after call A ended) inbound webhook -> 200, <Connect><Stream> TwiML
[twilio +5.1s] call C media stream open
```

Gateway, branch:

```
[voice-call/events] Created inbound call record: 5c5b5d27-... caller=sha256:7a8e1bad4241
[MediaStream] Stream started: MZstreamA (call: CAcallA)
[voice-call] Speaking initial message for call 5c5b5d27-... (mode: conversation)
[voice-call/events] Created inbound call record: 88d09aeb-... caller=sha256:6bd648cf8bf3
[MediaStream] Stream stopped: MZstreamA
[voice-call/lifecycle] [voice-call] Call finalized callId=5c5b5d27-... providerCallId=CAcallA endReason=completed
```

</details>

Tests: in `extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.test.ts`, the overlapping-call case now expects `<Reject reason="busy"/>` and no `<Enqueue>`; it fails on main and passes on the branch. The three cleanup cases now check that the next caller is not rejected. `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 623 + 184 passed. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +4/-18; test delta +8/-10 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the queue TwiML with no state or config migration. Blast radius is inbound Twilio calls that arrive while another call holds a media stream.

prs.title: improve: speed up sandbox workspace checks by listing only build-output ignores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandboxed project sessions check the workspace for changes before every message. Part of that check lists every ignored file in the guest workspace with `git ls-files --others --ignored --directory`. That command walks the whole tree. Its only consumer asks about two build-output roots: `dist` and `.cache/openclaw-bun`.

On a production deployment, the two workspace checks take p50 1.27 s and 0.67 s before every sandboxed message (48 h, read-only journal).

## User Impact

Sandboxed messages reach the model sooner. Nothing else changes: files under `dist` and `.cache/openclaw-bun` that Git ignores are still treated as build output, not as workspace edits.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readLocalWorkspaceGitExclusions` has three callers: the manifest scan (`local-workspace-manifest-scan.ts`), the scanner it drives (`workspace-actual-manifest.ts`), and the worker capture (`local-workspace-state.ts` → `workspace-manifest-worker.ts` → `workspace-manifest-computation.runtime.ts`). All three read the set only through `isIgnoredWorkspaceBuildOutput` (or its empty-set short-circuit, which gives the same answer). That predicate answers only for paths under the two roots, checking each path and its ancestors. The listing now passes those roots as pathspecs. Both sides share one constant, so they cannot drift apart.

Accepted edge case: if a guest replaces the `.cache` directory with an ignored symlink, the full listing named `.cache` and the scoped one does not. A stored `.cache/openclaw-bun/...` record is then scanned instead of being excluded as build output. This is rare, and the result is visible as a workspace change, not a silent loss.

## Evidence

- New differential test against Git (`local-workspace-inventory.test.ts`): four ignore layouts with the host index read against a separate projection work tree. For every path and ancestor, the scoped listing gives the same build-output answers as the full listing.
- Existing warm-reuse and reconciliation tests (`local-workspace-projection.test.ts`, including the independent-writer reuse case) and the worker/manifest-scan suites pass.
- Linux profile (Docker on a shared dev host, overlayfs, git 2.39.5, the OpenClaw tree with 67,667 tracked files plus `node_modules`; median of 7, page cache dropped before each cold run; host load 50–99): ignored-files listing cold 299 ms → 58 ms, warm 60 ms → 27 ms. On macOS (APFS, warm): 310–890 ms → 105–194 ms.
- Adversarial review: no missed reader. Fixes made: the comment now sits on the listing function, the test uses a separate projection, and the vacuous case is removed.

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-history-control.test.ts` › "captures settled evidence after durable control history" fails on main for both `file` and `sqlite` storage. Every PR that changes `package.json` runs this lane, so each one needs a CI override.

- This branch: 7 passed / 7 (file and sqlite). The branch summary expectation also uses `BRANCH_SUMMARY_PREFIX`/`SUFFIX`, so the next reword of either does not break this test.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the provider reset in agent-route failure notices
prs.body:
## Problem

On a production deployment over 7 days, every user turn that failed on a provider rate limit (36 of 36) showed a wrong failure notice in the session:

- 26: "Your request couldn't be completed." The run had already rendered "⚠️ <model> is rate-limited. The provider says to retry in 6 days (Nov 30, …)".
- 10: "⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes." The models were limited for 4–6 days.

All 36 ran on the Gateway `agent` route. This route serves `openclaw agent` and subagent completion announcements. chat.send shows the correct copy.

Retries are not the cause. Long limits already end after one attempt, and later turns are refused locally by the shared rate-limit gate with no network request. Of 3,193 rate-limit attempt rows, 2,087 are per-minute TPM retries, and 99% of those recover on the same model.

## Cause

On chat.send, `handleAgentExecutionError` emits the run's lifecycle error with `errorNotice` set to the rendered reply (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-error-handler.ts:100-108`). The `agent` route's catch (`src/agents/command/run-embedded-attempt.ts`) emits only a formatted error string. `recordGatewaySessionRunFailure` (`src/sessions/session-run-error.ts:53-66`) then rebuilds copy from that string, and the reset time is lost.

## Fix

At the `agent` route catch, the code now emits `errorNotice` from `resolveReplyFailureSummary`. chat.send uses the same function for capacity copy (rate limit, overload, billing). It uses the configured time zone and fallback attempts. Other failure classes keep their current notice. Retry, backoff, the shared gate, copy renderers and the recorder do not change.

## User impact

Gateway `agent` and `openclaw agent` users, and subagent announcements whose run hits a long rate limit, now see the model and the provider's reset time. The notice matches chat.send.

## Evidence

- Regression test `src/agents/agent-command.settled-recovery.test.ts`. It covers the gate-refusal shape on one model and an "All models failed" aggregate in a non-host time zone. It fails on main (no `errorNotice`) and passes with the fix.
- Real Gateway from dist (`dist-nodts`), with a fake OpenAI-compatible provider. It returns `429` with `retry-after: 518400`; the fallback model returns a weekly-limit body without a header.

| Shape | Route | Provider requests | Session notice on main | Session notice with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| single model, 6-day limit | `agent` | 1 | "Your request couldn't be completed." | "⚠️ fake/long-limit is rate-limited. The provider says to retry in 6 days (Dec 4, …)." |
| single model | chat.send | 0 (shared gate) | reset copy | reset copy (unchanged) |
| both fallbacks limited | `agent` | 2 (1 per candidate) | "⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes." | same reset copy, naming the first limited model |
| both fallbacks limited | chat.send | 1 | reset copy | reset copy (unchanged) |

Attempt counts are the same on main and on this branch.

## Not covered

- A chain that mixes a rate limit with another failure (for example, a timeout) gets no capacity summary. It keeps the recorder's notice on both routes.
- A 429 after committed tool effects ends through `emitResultError`, not the catch. This is unproven; none of the production inputs took that path.
- The aggregate copy names the first attempt with a structured reset. That owner behavior also applies on chat.send and does not change here.
