prs.title: improve: avoid copying the published model catalog when a worker starts
prs.body:
## Change

A prepared model-catalog worker's first request deep-cloned the active remote catalog, even when the worker had inherited the same published catalog bytes. The receiver then discarded the clone. The publisher already owns an immutable shared backing for this snapshot.

This change selects that backing when an unacknowledged task is dispatched and its captured catalog is still the publication's exact object. A worker whose inherited revision differs uses the bytes sent with the task. An independent or superseded snapshot retains its original transport, an explicit absence stays absent, and an acknowledged worker context continues to omit the catalog. Catalog publication, auth selection, pricing and storage retain their existing contracts.

## Verification

A fresh-thread probe exercised the actual publication helper and the worker's source-level restore branch using ordinary `postMessage`. A fixed 380,515-byte fixture contained 30 providers and 1,500 models (SHA-256 `2a33e32417ff2f4dfc81fe41e98e5a8bd7998702ac00a78247238bb94d4c8210`). With the same publication inherited, the wire went from 1,500 separately cloned model rows to zero. Both arms decoded the published bytes once and returned the same revision and price.

| Runtime | Synchronous post, median | Full round trip, median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node 24.16.0 | 0.919 → 0.008 ms | 7.065 → 1.295 ms |
| Bun 1.3.14 | 1.120 → 0.009 ms | 2.625 → 1.364 ms |

Four fresh workers per arm per runtime, interleaved. Additional single-worker controls covered publication rotation in both directions, independent scoped snapshots and explicit absence. This measures the worker transfer of an active overlay. Whole-Gateway RSS and empty-catalog startup were outside this comparison.

The integration test observes outgoing messages through the real prepared-worker service and verifies model prices, auth reuse and withdrawal across the same physical worker. Exact committed-range local review passed.

On the final signed head `64a31ad8c1ca`, the normal runtime build passed and all 54 tests across the five worker and remote-overlay suites passed. The same regression on the base returned the correct 3 → 7 → 3 → absent prices on one physical worker, then failed its wire assertion because both published revisions carried their model maps. On the candidate they carried shared bytes, auth reuse omitted the field, and the superseded owner's direct request and explicit null remained distinct. The real catalog returned all four expected results.

## Problem

The Codex runtime sends a 13.8 KB `<thread_policy>` developer message on every request. 9.5 KB of it is the full `<available_skills>` catalog: name, description and file location for every installed skill.

The embedded runtime stopped doing this in #206537. When `skills_read` loads a skill by name, the location is unused. When `skills_search` is callable, it matches descriptions on demand. The Codex plugin renders its own catalog section and kept the full form.

Measured on main `e916ef677a95` through an isolated Gateway: `<thread_policy>` 13,801 B, of which `<available_skills>` 9,469 B.

## Solution

`renderCodexSkillsInstructions` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts`) passes the catalog through the core owner `compactCatalogForSkillRead`, as the embedded route does:

- `skills_read` and `skills_search` callable: names only;
- only `skills_read` callable: names and descriptions;
- `skills_read` not callable: unchanged XML with locations. The Gateway-only location rewrite still runs for remote workspaces.

`compactCatalogForSkillRead` is added to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`, next to the other harness prompt builders.

## User impact

- Population: every Codex-runtime turn with installed skills (Gateway and one-shot).
- `<thread_policy>`: 13,801 → 4,511 B per request (−9,290 B).
- No change to which skills exist or how they load.
- Existing threads see the changed instructions on their next cold resume: one prompt-cache miss per thread.

## Evidence

- Isolated Gateway bench, fake provider: `<thread_policy>` 13,801 → 4,511 B; tool schemas unchanged.
- Codex-route behavior suite, gpt-5.4-mini, 3 trials per case, model-judged:
  - main 24/30, this PR 26/30;
  - skill loading 3/3 on both, through the same path (`skills_read` first in 6 of 6 trials, no extra tool search);
  - reply-directive 0/3 on both: an existing Codex-route gap, not caused here.
- Tests: `dynamic-tool-skills.test.ts`, `run-attempt.remote-skills.test.ts` and `run-attempt.skills.native.test.ts` pass. `plugin-sdk:check-exports` passes.
- Local ClawSweeper on this head: patch is correct, no findings.

prs.title: test(feishu): drop the stale never-iterated assertion on storage failure
prs.body:
## Problem

`extensions/feishu/src/media-download.test.ts` › "closes an acquired stream on storage failure even when teardown throws" fails on main: `expected "Mock" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`. Every PR that changes `package.json` runs this lane, so each one needs a CI override.

## Root cause

#206815 (`d1a11af0`, "keep the Gateway running when a WhatsApp attachment fails to decrypt") made the shared sink `saveMediaStream` (`src/media/store.ts:557-588`) start reading its source on entry, before directory and temp-file setup, so a hot source that fails early rejects the save instead of crashing the Gateway. Its body names Feishu as a caller that gets the same guarantee. When staging then fails, the sink closes the source.

The Feishu test still asserted that the stream is never iterated when storage fails, which contradicts that intended contract.

## Fix

Drop the stale "never iterated" assertion and its spy. The test keeps what it is about: on a storage failure the download rejects with the storage error, the stream is destroyed even though `destroy()` throws, and the server sees the connection close. No production change.

## Impact

Contributors only. The extension lane no longer fails on main.

## Evidence

- Main `de4d1cc8`: 1 failed / 1 (`iterate` called once).
- This branch: 1 passed / 1.
- Adversarial review: the remaining assertions still catch the failure the test exists for. Remove `teardownSource()` from the outer catch in `media-chunk-idle.ts` and `stream.destroyed` and the server close both fail; remove its try/catch and the rejection becomes the teardown error.

prs.title: fix(ai): never send an empty tools array on Chat Completions
prs.body:
## Problem
Chat Completions requests sent `tools: []` when there were no tools but the history had tool calls. Whether this happened depended on the URL:
- Routes with a configured, non-OpenAI base URL (`usesExplicitProxyLikeEndpoint`, managed mode only) deleted it.
- Routes with an unset base URL or an OpenAI/Azure host, and every direct-mode call (for example `/btw`), sent it.

`tools: []` breaks real servers:
- Bailian/DashScope: `400 [] is too short - 'tools'` (#53472, #54482).
- LiteLLM → Anthropic: LiteLLM forwards `tools: []`, and Anthropic needs a non-empty list when the history has tool blocks. When `tools` is absent, LiteLLM adds its own placeholder tool and the request succeeds (`litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py`: `if "tools" not in optional_params and has_tool_call_blocks(...)`).

## Change
- Never send an empty `tools` array on any route or mode. A request without tools says nothing about tools.
- Send `tool_choice` only together with `tools`. A `required` choice with no surviving tool still fails, as before.
- Delete `hasToolCallHistory` and the URL-gated delete (one `usesExplicitProxyLikeEndpoint` branch).

## User impact
- Fixes tool-free requests (side questions, history with tool calls) on servers that reject `[]`, including LiteLLM → Anthropic.
- OpenAI is unchanged in effect: real `gpt-5.4-nano` with tool-call history returns 200 both with `tools: []` and without `tools`.

## Evidence
- **Red on main, green here:** `openai-completions-params.test.ts` "never sends an empty tools array or an orphan tool choice" (direct and managed).
- **Byte diff:** every bundled Chat Completions route (690 cases: catalog rows, unset base URL, plugin hosts, relays, local servers), built on main and on this branch.
  - With tools: 690/690 byte-identical.
  - No tools, tool history: 222 bodies change, and the only change is removing `"tools":[]` (−13 B, for example 560 → 547 B). Affected: 194 unset-base-URL catalog routes, plus OpenAI/Azure hosts and a few extra provider ids with no base URL.
- **LiteLLM 1.x proxy → fake Anthropic upstream** (same history):
  - main body `tools: []`: LiteLLM forwards `tools: []`, the upstream returns 400.
  - This branch: LiteLLM forwards its placeholder tool, the upstream returns 200.
  - The fake applies Anthropic's documented non-empty-tools rule; what LiteLLM forwards is measured.
- Provider-branch ratchet: 837 → 836 grandfathered branches (allowlist pruned).
- Adversarial review (Fable): one gap, fixed here. Direct mode could send `tool_choice` with no `tools`; it now needs tools, and a `required` choice still fails. Fable also raised a LiteLLM→Anthropic risk; the LiteLLM run above shows the opposite: this change fixes that route.

prs.title: refactor(agents): exec records its output file in the shared details.spill shape
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A tool result can point to a file holding its full output. Two shapes record that pointer:
- web_fetch and the record-time bound (#206880) use `details.spill { path, chars?, truncated? }`;
- exec uses flat `details.fullOutputPath` plus `details.spillTruncated`.

So every reader handles both shapes:
- `getToolResultSpillDetails` (history elision and the bound's producer-spill reuse) falls back to the flat fields. It also reads a `spilledChars` field that nothing writes.
- The persisted-details allowlists keep both shapes (6 extra keys).
- The tokenjuice plugin checks exec's flat field to leave spilled results alone.

## Fix

Exec records `details.spill { path, truncated? }`, the one shape. Exec has bytes, not chars, so it does not set `chars`. The flat fields and every reader of them are removed:
- the flat fallback, and the never-written `spilledChars`, in `getToolResultSpillDetails`;
- `fullOutputPath`, `spilledChars` and `spillTruncated` in both persistence allowlists;
- tokenjuice now checks `details.spill`.

Accepted edge case: no migration. Exec results recorded before this change keep their text footer (`Full output: <path>`), but history elision no longer finds their pointer in `details`. The owner approved this. Spill files live in the OS temp directory anyway, so old pointers rarely outlive the session.

Not touched: `fullOutputPath` on the session `BashResult`/`BashToolDetails` types and the agent-core bash-execution message. Those are a different, extension-facing contract, and exec never writes them.

## User impact

None visible. The exec result text is unchanged. Model-visible behavior is the same: elision and the bound reuse exec's file as before, through the shared shape.

## Evidence

- `session-tool-result-guard.test.ts`: an exec output file cut at its limit records `spill: { path, truncated: true }`.
- `tool-result-truncation.test.ts`: history elision with an exec-shaped spill keeps its pointer.
- `runtime.integration.test.ts` (tokenjuice): a spilled exec result is left to the host.
- `tool-result-bounds.test.ts` (owner, unchanged) and `session-tool-result-guard.tool-result-persist-hook.test.ts` (fallback keeps `spill`) still pass.
- `bash-tools.exec-approval-output.test.ts`: a real exec spill path, read through workspace-only `read` (#206972), comes from `details.spill.path`.

prs.body:
Closes #194842

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `swabble serve` replaces the user's config with defaults when the existing file fails to load (e.g. a JSON typo).

## User Impact

User impact: a broken config makes `serve` exit with the load error and leaves the file unchanged. A missing config still gets defaults written, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`serve` caught every load error and saved defaults over the file. It now only does that for `ConfigError.missingConfig`, and other errors propagate.

## Evidence

- New `CLIProcessTests.testServeLeavesUnreadableConfigUntouched` runs the real binary against a config missing its closing brace.
  - Without the fix it fails: the file is rewritten with `"command":""` (was `/usr/bin/say`).
  - With the fix: exit 1, file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- `swift test --package-path apps/swabble`: 13 passed, 0 failed (macOS 26, Swift 6.4.2).
- `apps/swabble/scripts/lint.sh` (SwiftLint strict): 0 violations. SwiftFormat lint: clean.


**Real CLI proof** (debug builds of `main` and this branch, macOS 26, temp dir as `HOME`). The `Abort trap: 6` is the speech pipeline starting in a headless shell after the config loaded:

```
## main (before)
$ swabble setup --config sw.json && set hook.command=/usr/bin/say
"command":"\/usr\/bin\/say"
$ # drop the closing brace (hand-edit mistake)
$ swabble serve --config sw.json
Abort trap: 6   (exit=134)
sha256 before: b2f3703f5df4b151 / after: 3b217deac2bd2ab3  REWRITTEN
"command":""

## this PR (after)

error: DecodingError.dataCorrupted: ... The given data was not valid JSON ... "Unexpected end of file"
sha256 before: 9caeef3f98ec539d / after: 9caeef3f98ec539d  UNCHANGED
"command":"\/usr\/bin\/say"
$ swabble serve --config missing.json   # no file yet
missing.json created with defaults: "word":"clawd"
```

**Existing config compatibility:** the loader and format are unchanged. A config written by the `main` binary works with this branch:

prs.title: fix(codex): discover the model catalog once per Codex cache window
prs.body:
## Problem

On the default Codex app-server runtime (native OpenAI models), every chat turn loads the Codex model catalog three times. Each load sends `model/list` to the catalog app-server. Codex refetches `/models` for every uncached `model/list` and keeps no record of a failed fetch: it logs `failed to refresh available models` and returns its bundled catalog after the fetch timeout (`codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs:609-618`, timeout `model-provider/src/models_endpoint.rs:49`).

When `/models` is unreachable (TLS-intercepting corporate proxy, firewall, offline), each `model/list` waits about 3 s, so each turn waits about 9 s before the model is called.

Reproduced on main `e916ef677a95` through an isolated Gateway with a fake provider behind an HTTPS proxy that Codex's `/models` client cannot use: 10 `model/list` calls in 3 turns, 2.86-3.19 s each.

## Solution

The plugin's catalog owner (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/model-catalog.ts`) reuses a discovery while all of these hold:

- the same catalog app-server client (a credential change that needs a new client rediscovers);
- the same account revision (`account/updated`, login, logout and config writes advance it);
- the same plugin config, auth profile and scope (agent, agent dir, workspace);
- less than 300 s old, which is Codex's own `/models` cache TTL (`DEFAULT_MODEL_CACHE_TTL`, `models-manager/src/manager.rs:43`). A user with a working network never sees an older catalog than Codex would show.

Hidden-model filtering stays per call, so callers with different configured models get their own rows.

## User impact

- Population: every Gateway and one-shot user on the Codex runtime; all core catalog reads reach `harness.loadModelCatalog` (`extensions/codex/harness.ts:318`) from `src/agents/harness/model-catalog.ts:223`.
- `/models` unreachable: about 9 s per turn becomes one ~3 s refresh per 5 minutes.
- Working network: unchanged (Codex already served these calls from its cache).

Accepted edge: an external `codex login` change in native-home mode shows in the catalog after the next refresh (at most 5 minutes), unless Codex reports it through `account/updated` sooner.

Not fixed here: Codex's own `turn/start` also refetches an uncached `/models` (`core/src/session/turn_context.rs:868-873`), about 3 s per turn when `/models` is unreachable. That is upstream Codex behavior.

## Evidence

| Isolated Gateway, fake provider, `/models` unreachable | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `model/list` calls | 10 in 3 turns | 2 in 4 turns (startup + turn 1) |
| Warm turn wall | 15.9 s, 14.6 s | 5.1 s, 5.5 s, 4.0 s |

- Real network, gpt-5.4-mini, Codex and embedded routes through a Gateway, chat and code tasks, 4 turns each: all turns exit 0 on main and on this PR.
- Regression test `discovers once per catalog app-server, account revision, scope and Codex cache TTL`: fails on main (`model/list` called 2 times, expected 1), passes here. `model-catalog.test.ts`, `model-catalog.process.test.ts` and `model-catalog.timeout.test.ts` pass.
- Local ClawSweeper on this head: patch is correct, no findings.

## Current fresh-worktree round: STOPPED (source floor)

Published head `08d5c11ea9ad922a45ea5fce18d0efa81088ecf0`; frozen main `659febe4cafaa837bd1d22d0e9116024e7e75274`.

Created an independently owned task worktree through GWT at the published PR head, then rebuilt its clean source baseline on frozen main. Existing PR checkouts were left untouched. Fresh preservation review rejects the original whole-suite deletions: their named area-level keepers do not replace the distinct behavioral guards.

| Safe candidate | Supported net removal | Retained proof |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Outbound interactive action limits | 8 lines, measured in memory | All six literal input/output contracts; no dense formatting compression. |
| Gateway memory-search validation and legacy-manager unavailability | About 52 lines, source estimate | Seven distinct invalid inputs, exact errors, no manager/default-agent acquisition, backend gating and acquisition count. |
| ClawHub legacy publication recovery table | About 25–45 lines, source estimate | Exact response sequences, fetch counts, recovered-failure and deadline/wait behavior. |

The supported total is approximately **85–108 lines**, below the requested approximately 200-line floor. Only the interactive candidate was measured as an in-memory rewrite; the other values are estimates, not a committed or tested diff. No larger coverage-preserving cut was established. No production change is needed or proposed. Paths already absent on main, including the old update-runner candidate and ci-node-test-plan suites, contribute zero new removal.

No dependency install, source patch, commit, push, fresh lint/typecheck/test result, exact-head ClawSweeper clearance, green CI or merge is claimed for this attempt. Disk remained above 60 GiB; the 10 GiB install floor was never approached. This PR remains open.

## What Problem This Solves

Preserves distinct current-main regression coverage while retaining the existing test-consolidation scope for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737. This is a fix-only update of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198950; it is not merged.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Five suites are restored exactly from current main, their test selection is retained, and one unused Telegram test helper is removed with its deleted consumer.

## Current Head and Scope

Published head: `08d5c11ea9ad922a45ea5fce18d0efa81088ecf0`. Frozen main/base: `2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4`. Prior published head: `ba2a3c02b3e60ff69e5660cc576373848365ca1c`.

**35 suites and one 44-line orphan helper deleted; +79/-33106; 33027 net lines removed; 33185 changed lines across 58 paths. Production source delta: 0.**

The final test delta is rebased onto the frozen main. Nine modify/delete conflicts and the package/selector conflicts were resolved only within the owned test scope. Windows script resolution preserves every current-main token except the deleted state-ownership test. Existing fixture corrections and historical test measurements remain intact.

| Suite | Reason |

All twelve self-keepers in the manifest, including the seven earlier retentions, match frozen main byte-for-byte. Other changed deletion candidates contain fixture or wording updates: GC tests capture the existing worker context and freeze timing; Control UI text uses the web-app name; attributed identity selects the activity summary; warm boot updates its expected module count. Those changes add no distinct coverage requiring another retention in this repair.

## Evidence and Limits

- Native source admission and exact-main checkout completed. The normal commit hook passed formatting and both staged-content scans, then failed because the AGENTS-size command preloads absent local dependencies. Used the documented `CONTRIBUTING.md` iterative-commit `--no-verify` exception for this signed commit after equivalent checks passed: canonical private-literal scan, cached markdownlint-cli2 0.24.0 on the changed doc, AGENTS size (27 files), line-cap ratchet (15 changed source files), scoped formatting, syntax, JSON and whitespace. No hook settings or dependencies changed.

prs.title: fix: stop Workboard updates from resending the whole card history every time
prs.body:
Closes #162498

## What Problem This Solves

Every Workboard write tool (`workboard_comment`, `workboard_move`, `workboard_heartbeat`, `workboard_release`, `workboard_claim`, `workboard_proof`, ...) answers with the whole card: notes, every past comment, events and proof. An agent that keeps a card current pays for that history again on each call, and the result grows with every comment. #162498 measured 21 KB on average per `workboard_comment` call, and #180394 measured ~28 KB per heartbeat.

## User Impact

Write tools now answer with the same compact card summary `workboard_list` uses (id, title, status, claim state, links, diagnostics), plus the id of what they added: `commentId`, `attachmentId` or `proofId`. `workboard_claim` still returns its token. `workboard_read` still returns the full card. Agents that read history from a write result need `workboard_read` instead. Nothing in the repo did that: the dispatcher, worker prompts and Control UI use the store or the read path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Most write tools share one result helper, which returned the full redacted card. This PR changes that helper's contract once, keeping the card nested under `card` so its status is never mistaken for the tool result's. The writes outside the helper (create, link, claim, proof, decompose) get the same summary. `summarizeCard` moves next to the helper unchanged, so list and write results share one shape.

## Evidence

**Real deployment:** over 3 days and 184 agent sessions, `workboard_comment` results over 12 KB totalled 2.32M characters in 92 calls. The largest single result was 35,302 characters, 24.7K of them past comments and 5K events.

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways, tools called through `POST /tools/invoke`. A card gets 30 comments of 700 characters, then each tool runs once on it. The numbers are `details` JSON characters.

| Tool, on a card with 30 comments | 2026.11.6 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `workboard_comment` | 27,145 | 222 (`card`, `commentId`) |
| `workboard_move` | 27,277 | 171 |
| `workboard_claim` | 27,719 | 341 (token still returned) |
| `workboard_heartbeat` | 27,760 | 292 |
| `workboard_proof` | 28,029 | 343 (`proofId` still returned) |
| `workboard_release` | 27,967 | 171 |
| `workboard_dispatch` (due card with 30 comments, promoted) | 27,181 | 238 |
| `workboard_read` (control) | 32,706 | 32,706, all 31 comments |

Tested on `86a84515286` (rebased onto main) against 2026.11.6.

- Tests: new `tools.compact-results.test.ts` checks that comment, move, heartbeat and release results stay small and leave out metadata and notes while read keeps them (fails on main, passes here). `tools.test.ts` assertions that read history from write results now read it from the store. On `86a84515286` the workboard suite passes (32 files, 333 tests), and lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude) on the pre-rebase head `3b0d6fc24e8`, no P0–P2 findings, clean.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Credit: @-mentions are left out on purpose. #162498 (21 KB on average per comment call) and #180394 (heartbeat/release, ~28 KB per heartbeat) both measured this.

Alternatives considered: a per-tool `compact` flag or a comment-only patch would leave move, heartbeat, release and the rest echoing the card. Trimming comments inside the full card would still send notes, events, proof and attempts. The list summary already exists and is what agents use to choose work, so writes reuse it.

Repro script (needs `openclaw plugins enable workboard` on the test Gateway): creates a card through `/tools/invoke`, adds the comments, then prints each write tool's result size, with `workboard_read` as the control.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): infer tts voice-note example names a file it never writes
prs.body:
Closes #206612

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw infer tts convert --channel telegram --output ./voice.opus --json`, the voice-note example in `docs/cli/infer.md`, writes `./voice.ogg` instead of `./voice.opus` when the provider returns Ogg Opus. The TTS JSON output also omits `mimeType` and `size`, which the same page tells automation to read from `outputs`.

## User Impact

The documented voice-note command writes the file it names, and scripts can read `path`, `mimeType` and `size` from `tts convert --output` the same way they do for image and video outputs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extension-follows-bytes is intended (#175615): the shared writer `src/cli/media-output.ts` sniffs Ogg Opus as `audio/ogg` and publishes it as `.ogg`. This PR keeps that rule and fixes the two places that disagreed with it:

- `docs/cli/infer.md`: the example now uses `./voice.ogg`, and a note says the extension follows the returned audio and that `outputs[].path` is the written file.
- `src/cli/capability-cli/tts-runtime.ts`: the TTS envelope now carries the `path`, `mimeType` and `size` returned by `writeOutputAsset` instead of copying only `path`. Without `--output` the output entry is unchanged.

`.opus` requests still land at `.ogg`; changing the shared MIME/extension policy would affect image and video outputs too.

## Evidence

Built main and this branch and ran the shipped CLI (`pnpm openclaw infer tts convert --local ...`) with an isolated `HOME`, state dir, config and profile. The real OpenAI speech provider plugin was pointed at a local stand-in for `/v1/audio/speech` that returns an Ogg Opus file (made with ffmpeg/libopus). The Microsoft provider's free endpoint does not return Ogg, and I had no OpenAI key, so the Opus bytes come from the stand-in, not from OpenAI. The provider sent `"response_format":"opus"` for the Telegram target, as it would to OpenAI.

- Main, docs example `--output voice.opus`: exit 0, file written as `voice.ogg`, output entry `{ path: ".../voice.ogg", format: "opus", voiceCompatible: true }` with no `mimeType` or `size`.
- Branch, corrected docs example `--output voice.ogg`: `voice.ogg` written (`Ogg data, Opus audio`), output entry `{ path: ".../voice.ogg", mimeType: "audio/ogg", size: 4994, format: "opus", voiceCompatible: true }`.
- Branch, `--output voice.opus`: still written as `voice.ogg`, now with `mimeType: "audio/ogg"` and `size`.
- Branch control, Microsoft provider (real endpoint) `--output build-complete.mp3`: written at the requested path, `mimeType: "audio/mpeg"`, `size: 12960`.

<details>
<summary>CLI output</summary>

Main:

```
$ openclaw infer tts convert --local --channel telegram --text "Voice-note format" --output ./voice.opus --json
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": ".../out-main/voice.ogg",
      "format": "opus",
      "voiceCompatible": true
    }
  ]
$ ls out-main
voice.ogg
```

Branch:

```
$ openclaw infer tts convert --local --channel telegram --text "Voice-note format" --output ./voice.ogg --json
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": ".../out-fix/voice.ogg",
      "mimeType": "audio/ogg",
      "size": 4994,
      "format": "opus",
      "voiceCompatible": true
    }
  ]
$ openclaw infer tts convert --local --text "Your build is complete" --output ./build-complete.mp3 --json
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": ".../out-fix/build-complete.mp3",
      "mimeType": "audio/mpeg",
      "size": 12960,
      "format": "audio-24khz-48kbitrate-mono-mp3",
      "voiceCompatible": true
    }
  ]
$ file out-fix/*
build-complete.mp3: MPEG ADTS, layer III, v2,  48 kbps, 24 kHz, Monaural
voice.ogg:          Ogg data, Opus audio, version 0.1, mono, 48000 Hz
```

Stand-in request log: `POST /v1/audio/speech {"model":"gpt-4o-mini-tts","input":"Voice-note format","voice":"alloy","response_format":"opus"}`

</details>

Tests: the existing `keeps TTS publication and source custody for normal` case in `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` now also expects `mimeType: "audio/wav"` and `size: 64` for the written file. It fails on main with the fix lines reverted (`mimeType` and `size` missing) and passes on the branch. (The file is at the repo's line cap, so the assertion goes into the existing publication case rather than a new one.) `pnpm test src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`: 119 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` on the touched files, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Production delta +3/-4 (plus docs +2/-1); test delta +1/-1 against main.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous output entry with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the JSON output of `infer tts convert --output`, which gains two fields.

prs.title: fix: reject unknown TTS provider ids when selecting one locally
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw infer tts set-provider --local --provider <id>` accepted and saved any non-empty id — including typos such as `elevenlab` — then reported success and exited 0. The local path only checked that canonicalization returned a value, but the canonicalizer returns the normalized input when no provider matches, so the `Unknown speech provider` branch was unreachable. Because a saved preference outranks configured routing, later replies were synthesized by a fallback provider while status reported the mistyped id. The Gateway path (`tts.setProvider`) already rejects unregistered ids.

Closes #206619

## User Impact

A mistyped TTS provider id now fails loudly: nonzero exit, an `Unknown speech provider: <id>` error, and the saved preference stays unchanged. Registered providers still save normally, including aliases (`cli` → `tts-local-cli`, `edge` → `microsoft`), and registration alone is enough — selecting a provider does not require synthesis credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match the Gateway's validation at the local mutation boundary: after canonicalization, require `getSpeechProvider` to resolve the id before writing the preference. Shared canonicalization semantics stay untouched, so aliases, case folding, and credential-independent selection behave exactly as before; only ids that no registered provider owns are rejected.

## Evidence

Live, isolated state directory (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), built CLI. Main accepts the typo and persists it:

```
$ openclaw infer tts set-provider --local --provider elevenlab --json
{ "provider": "elevenlab" }                     # exit 0
$ cat state/settings/tts.json
{"tts":{"provider":"elevenlab"}}
```

With this change:

```
$ openclaw infer tts set-provider --local --provider elevenlab --json
{ "error": { "type": "cli_error",
             "message": "Unknown speech provider: elevenlab" } }   # exit 1
$ cat state/settings/tts.json
{"tts":{"provider":"tts-local-cli"}}            # unchanged

$ openclaw infer tts set-provider --local --provider tts-local-cli   # exit 0
{ "provider": "tts-local-cli" }
$ openclaw infer tts set-provider --local --provider cli             # alias, exit 0
{ "provider": "tts-local-cli" }
```

Regression coverage in a new `src/cli/capability-cli/tts-runtime.test.ts` (the existing `capability-cli.test.ts` is already over its line cap, so the cases live beside it):

- `rejects an unregistered provider id without saving it` — fails on main (the typo is accepted and persisted), passes with the fix.
- `saves a registered provider without requiring synthesis credentials` — keeps the accepted path working.

`pnpm test src/cli/capability-cli/tts-runtime.test.ts` → 2 passed.

`pnpm check:changed` → all gates pass (typecheck core and core tests, lint, format, line-cap, SQLite worker ratchet, mock export ratchet, import cycles, and the rest) except `dead export scan`, which also fails on unmodified main at `src/agents/btw-runtime.ts: toSimpleContextMessages` and is unrelated to this change. `git diff --check` is clean.

Sibling suites: `pnpm test src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts src/tts/provider-registry.test.ts` → 119 + 6 passed, 1 failure (`reports empty audio results (action transcribe, file memo.m4a, missing provider false)`). That failure reproduces on unmodified main in this environment because the suite ran on Node 25.8.2, an unsupported runtime that truncates diagnostic text; it is unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(agents): surface system-event queue exhaustion to sessions_send notify
prs.body:
Closes #206751

## What Problem This Solves

A `sessions_send` notify to a session whose passive system-event pool is full (20 pending) returns only `Notification was not queued.` The queue owner logs the capacity refusal, so the sender cannot tell capacity exhaustion from a duplicate or no-op and cannot take the documented next step.

## User Impact

The notify caller now receives the queue owner capacity explanation with the failure: `Notification was not queued: System event queue is full (20 pending).` Non-capacity refusals keep the existing generic receipt, and the notification stays passive: no wake-pool occurrence is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`notifySessionsSendSession` called the non-throwing passive enqueue, which collapsed capacity refusal into null. The passive entry now accepts an opt-in `throwOnFull` so notify can distinguish the queue owner error and return its capacity message; passive and no-wake semantics are unchanged.

## Evidence


### Result

`sessions_send` with `mode: "notify"` now returns the queue owner's capacity explanation when the target session's passive system-event pool is full instead of only `Notification was not queued.`

### base-red (same focused command on the base commit, before the fix)

prs.title: fix: preserve Codex worker ownership when chat resumes after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart, a chat can receive its worker's answer and still be unable to give that worker another task. The Gateway resumes the same conversation, but a change in the tool list causes Codex to start a new parent thread. The worker belongs to the original parent.

A cold Gateway forgets the human turn's `skill_library` definition. For a text-only WebChat client it also adds `show_widget` for one recovery turn. Each change can replace the parent.

## User Impact

An interrupted chat can keep using its worker. A session that offered inline widgets can still pin a dashboard with the browser disconnected. Scheduled turns and clients without a recorded catalog retain their fallback behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the two settings that determine how skill authoring appears to the model alongside the current session ID and lifecycle revision. Record them during human turn admission. The embedded runner uses only a matching session entry to recover the definition. Personal library calls still need a fresh human grant. A restart also respects an existing text-only tool list. No new setting or SQL migration is needed.

## Upgrade and rollback

Existing chats need one eligible human turn after the update to record the settings. Other tool changes can still replace the native thread. This fix cannot reassign a worker whose parent was already replaced.

The new field is private. Older builds can copy unknown fields into session responses. The field contains the default target, a multiple-profile flag and the session and revision IDs. It contains no profile ID, credential or grant. Use a return build that keeps the projection exclusion. Please review this compatibility tradeoff before merging.

## Evidence

The widget and cold skill regressions each failed against `4520b75d`. Before the final file-length cleanup, the two test files and three neighboring suites passed 53/53 with the patch. The cold single-worker run took 252.8 seconds. After moving presentation into the existing reply initializer and grouping variable declarations in the dispatcher, I reran the seven Gateway tests on `dc415582` (156.2 seconds). All seven passed, as did formatting and type-aware lint. The earlier local core typecheck reported the same 53 errors on base and candidate with cached dependencies, including fs-safe 0.27.1. Hosted CI needs to check the current lockfile.

CI on `dc415582` found a duplicate check of the session ID and revision. In `54fb216b`, the runner consumes the presentation already validated by the session store. The reset regression now sends the changed revision through the same store admission. All 27 affected tests passed in 173.4 seconds. The session identity check, formatting and type-aware lint passed. I repeated both abrupt-restart trials with the runtime changes from `54fb216b`. The update and return trials below predate this last correction.

### Integration with main

The prior [PostgreSQL conformance job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46038781772/job/140641850424) reported an undeclared PostgreSQL pool in the CLI updater test. I merged main at `30398df5` to include #206837. The resulting head `bfcad32d` has exactly the same 13-file PR diff as `54fb216b` against their respective bases. All seven updater conformance tests passed on the combined source with local PostgreSQL 16.15.

### Release upgrade and fresh install

I built the [v2026.11.10 release tag](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10) at `6ea542fd` and this PR at `54fb216b` from unmodified source without the auxiliary fixes. I used cached dependencies, including fs-safe 0.27.1, the same external Codex 0.164.0 app-server, and scripted Responses. The PR lockfile specifies fs-safe 0.28.2.

I created two chats using the configured default model, gave one a distinct label and exchanged a turn in each. I stopped both processes, kept the read-only configuration and SQLite files and ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` from this PR. After relaunch each chat recalled its own earlier answer. The label and chat identity survived. The new metadata appeared only after an eligible human turn and stayed private through a subsequent settings write. The fresh control ran the same sequence starting in an empty directory on the PR build.

Redacted verifier output follows. Schema pairs are shared and Agent state. The four presentation checks are before Doctor, after Doctor, after the new human turn, and after an authenticated `sessions.patch`. Each response matched exactly one saved turn.

```json
{"case":"upgrade","builds":["6ea542fd","54fb216b"],"doctorExit":0,"schema":[[40,42],[42,45]],"configSame":true,"sameLabel":true,"presentationRecorded":[false,false,true,true],"defaultModel":true,"http":[200,200,200,200],"sameChats":true,"nativeThreadsPerChat":[2,2],"priorAnswersRecalled":[true,true]}
{"case":"fresh","builds":["54fb216b","54fb216b"],"doctorExit":0,"schema":[[42,45],[42,45]],"configSame":true,"sameLabel":true,"presentationRecorded":[true,true,true,true],"defaultModel":true,"http":[200,200,200,200],"sameChats":true,"nativeThreadsPerChat":[1,1],"priorAnswersRecalled":[true,true]}
```

Both native thread IDs changed across the release upgrade. This check establishes existing chat data compatibility. It does not establish worker transfer when other tool definitions change or repair the separate saved-provider migration.

### Restart with a worker running

I used the real Gateway, remote Codex 0.164.0 over authenticated WSS and scripted Responses in an isolated container. I killed only the Gateway while the second worker task was running. The worker finished during the outage. After restart the parent received that result, continued its goal and assigned a third task to the same worker. The test checked the native parent ID, all three saved worker turns, both later answer receipts, and the refusal of a personal library read.

Without this change, a text-only client used three different parents and a widget-capable client used two. With the change, both kept the original parent. Each had a distinct clean receipt for the second and third tasks. Redacted verifier output follows. Time runs from the start of observation after readiness through completion and idle.

```json
{"client":"textOnly","nativeParents":1,"childTurns":3,"receipts":2,"skillRead":"refused","elapsedMs":12765,"goal":"complete"}
{"client":"inlineWidget","nativeParents":1,"childTurns":3,"receipts":2,"skillRead":"refused","elapsedMs":13392,"goal":"complete"}
```

The paired restart tests used `5e245aa0` with #193024, #205298, #206231, #206529 and #206753 on both sides. The only difference was the runtime patch through `54fb216b`. All affected runtime files on that base matched the preimages on `4520b75d`. The focused tests above used the standalone change on `4520b75d`.

In a separate same-schema update and return before the file-length cleanup, both chats kept their own native thread, selected model and earlier answers. Doctor exited 0, the config stayed unchanged and all six requests returned 200. The updated build kept the new field private across a label change. On return the older build did include it in the authenticated `sessions.patch` result. Neither build exposed it in `sessions.list`.

I also tested a compatible return build. It kept the earlier runtime plus the private field exclusion, reserved slot and type declarations. Through an update to the runtime code in `dc415582` and a return, all six requests succeeded, both native threads stayed intact and neither session API returned the field. This verifies a same-schema return for these two chats. It does not establish general downgrade compatibility.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session listing, search, and navigation currently read raw subagent rows and repeat their display decisions in Gateway. This continues the approved ownership cleanup from [the Stop cutover](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206444), [dormant Stop decisions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206479), and [Swarm summaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206545): registry queries should supply display facts while Gateway owns stored-session fallbacks and wire presentation.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change or migration. Live and queued activity, paused children, follow-up session timing, model search, and child navigation retention keep their existing behavior. No public SDK, protocol, configuration, or persisted shape changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing read index now supplies `getSessionDisplayFacts`: selected identity, model, owner, activity, status, timing, and child-link retention. Resident/retained/historical selection stays in the registry; current custody and runtime are read at query time. Gateway keeps its stored-session fallback and controller-authority decisions. The raw `getDisplaySubagentRun` method and unused metric exports from the read barrel are deleted with no compatibility path.

Production delta across touched files: **−2 lines**. Tests/support: **+38 lines**. In the original 121-file Gateway scope, registry/announce importer files stay 45→45, all subagent importer files stay 70→70, and subagent-mentioning lines fall 1,308→1,290. This slice removes raw display access rather than moving the read-index import. Remaining old-method references: **0**; the Gateway display projector no longer computes registry liveness, pause, status, execution timing, or display owner from raw rows.

### Mechanical caller updates

- `src/gateway/session-list-filters.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-presentation.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-projection-ancestors.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-utils-row.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-projection.test-support.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-child-controller.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-list-search.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/session-row-projection-context.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-queries.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-read-context.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-read.scoped.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-liveness.owner-integration.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.test-helpers.ts`
- `scripts/perf/session-row-presentation-reuse-measure.ts`
- `scripts/perf/subagent-liveness-measure.ts`

The presentation benchmark counts the replacement query. The liveness benchmark captures the same prepared resident rows through existing index inputs; its timed live-owner predicate remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Native Node comparison: 720 old/new Gateway projection cases and 1,440 cache-identity checks passed, including the final owner-key resolver. This uses real projection/metric/resolver code with synthetic custody predicates; it does not prove native execution ownership.
- Syntax checks passed for all 19 changed files; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Session identity ratchet passed: 1,549 files, 6,170 grandfathered pins.
- Code-sloppiness: the Gateway run projector falls from CC 37 / 95 SLOC to CC 33 / 84 SLOC. Its measured preimage is byte-identical to the frozen task base; the four-file final candidate scan has no clones or parse failures.
- Existing selection and live-owner contracts migrated. Owner-query coverage checks execution timing and inclusive child-link expiry; captured selection coverage also checks custody after release without publication.
- Final independent local autoreview of the complete candidate against `863249caa4ed3e4f3a1c14b734dbaa78fd3fff96`, P0–P2: scoped-clean (0.93 confidence). Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this execution route; the established fallback uses autoreview and one hosted request when ready.
- Exact-head [CI run 45991935876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45991935876), `7bd8f690dff6a70361b2517a0ac1902d9906cad4`: build, production/test typechecks, lint, and all scheduled node-test jobs passed. The manual run finished with 47 passing jobs, 27 skipped jobs, and three failed jobs: the dependency check below, one UI timeout below, and their aggregate gate. Normal ready-PR CI subsequently passed on attempt 3, as recorded below. Local application dependencies are unqualified; dependency-backed proof comes from CI. No Testbox is allocated.

- Independent [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206617#issuecomment-7218329531) passed at the exact final head with no findings.

The manual CI dependency check (`140482529056`) reports `GatewayRestartStartupFailureHandler` in `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop-startup.ts` and `settleRunFromTrial` in `src/update/gateway-trial.ts`. Both appear in scheduled main [run 45982074926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45982074926), job `140448759293`, at `28dbf4784175a64d6bb22a1b82ed9f9538b0d4d2`. Both source files are unchanged from that baseline through this PR. This is an inherited failure, not a passing check.

The other manual-run failure is **unclassified**: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)` / job `140482527845`, `config-form.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:205`, timed out after 30 seconds waiting for “Profile saved” during the second cloud-worker profile save after a stale-hash rejection. The test, profile-save implementation, runtime-config owner, and config RPC source are unchanged from the inspected main baseline; that baseline UI job passed. The flow uses `config.patch`/environment metadata and forbids session creation/dispatch. This is recorded as a config-save follow-up, not claimed as pre-existing or fixed by this refactor. No local UI reproduction was run in the code-only checkout.

Normal PR CI [run 45993960220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45993960220), attempt 1, was interrupted in `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` / job `140489357133`: the GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` worker received a shutdown signal during the database-worker inventory (`SIGTERM` / exit 143, “operation was canceled”). The runner failure is not claimed as a reproduced baseline defect. At the end of attempt 2, the required normal PR gate was failed and the native auto-merge request was pending. prs.title: fix(agents): resolve utility models against the session owner's role
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Activity recaps for sessions owned by a role that refuses every utility model fail every time, and the failure repeats on every new activity.

Real-user log signature (a production team Gateway; 331 on 2026-11-27):

```
[activity-summary] Activity recap deferred
  error: Your operator role cannot use this model. Choose an allowed model or ask a gateway administrator to update your role's model policy.
  retryScheduled: false
```

- The Gateway's default role allows only main-chat models. The utility chain (`gpt-6-luna` → `gpt-5.6-luna`) has no model that role may use.
- The recap picked its model without the session owner's role. The fallback runner then refused every candidate, and the recap treated the refusal as a failure: `unavailable` plus a 120 s retry, re-run on every later activity, with no reason shown anywhere.

## Change

`resolveUtilityModelSelectionForAgent` is the one owner of utility model choice. It now takes the session owner's role policy and returns either a model or `{ disabled: "config" | "role-policy" | "not-offered" }`.

- **Role refusal disables.** Every utility candidate (declared, fallbacks, explicit chain) is checked against the role before inventory. A refusal never falls back to the main model: the operator restricted that role, so spending the main model would override them. The answer does not depend on catalog publication timing.
- **Absence still recovers.** When the small model is simply not offered and no role refused it, the existing offered-primary fallback stays.
- **Deleted:** the branch that returned the declared model already known to be unoffered (`utility-model.ts`, old 256-258). With nothing offered (neither the small model nor the primary listed), utility routing is now `not-offered`: narration is off, recaps are `unavailable`, and optional utility callers use the agent's main model through simple completion. Before, they got a guaranteed missing-model failure at execution.
- **Recap:** the recap's authority owner (`session-activity-summary-authority.ts`) already resolves the session owner's role in `prepare()`. It now also reports whether that role refuses every utility model. A run with model work checks this after the "already current" check and before it publishes `updating` or arms its timer. On refusal it publishes `unavailable` with no model attempt and no retry. Execution's fallback runner still picks the allowed model from the run's chain, so there is one model resolution per run.
- The recap's static system prompt moved, unchanged, to `session-activity-summary-prompt.ts`. That keeps the service under its line cap.
- **The selection decision moved, unchanged, to `src/agents/utility-model-selection.ts`.** It takes the published inventory as a lazy input, so config validation can ask it without importing the runtime catalog. That would otherwise create an import cycle through `config/config.ts`. `utility-model.ts` keeps the catalog read and its exported API.
- **Visible reason, no wire change:** config validation warns at `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.modelPolicy` when a role allows no utility model for an agent it can use. `openclaw config validate`, `openclaw status` and `openclaw doctor` all show it.
- **Docs:** `docs/concepts/models.md` now describes both outcomes. When nothing is offered, narration and recaps pause and other utility tasks use the primary. A refusing role pauses that owner's recaps.
- `resolveUtilityModelRefForAgent` no longer accepts a role policy: a bare ref drops the reason, and simple completion would turn `undefined` back into the main model.

## User population

- **Gateway** users on multi-user Gateways with operator roles whose `modelPolicy` excludes the utility models: Activity recaps (`session-activity-summaries.ts`).
- **Gateway and one-shot** users with nothing offered for automatic utility routing: utility routing is now off (`not-offered`) instead of sending a request to a model the catalog already reported missing (`utility-model.ts`).

## Not changed (follow-ups)

- **Titles, companion, observer and narrator still resolve without the role.**
- **A queued recap with no summary yet still shows `updating` before `unavailable`** (`schedule()` can't know the role synchronously, and remembering the refusal would be new state).
- **The recap catch block still retries other authority refusals** (operator profile unavailable or role changed).
- **The gate re-resolves on each view of a refused session** (cheap, no model call), and one explicit-chain case still reaches the runner's refusal: one ref unparseable and the rest refused.
- **One previously working config now has no recaps:** the role refuses the provider's declared small model, the catalog lacks it, and the role allows the main model. On main that ran on the main model; this PR treats it as the role's refusal.
- **`not-offered` is not shown in `models status`**: that needs a new wire value.

## Evidence

| Proof | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Recap regression (`session-activity-summaries.retry.test.ts`): role allows only the main model, 4 activity rounds 130 s apart on a fake scheduler clock | model attempts on every round | 0 attempts, `unavailable`, 0 armed wakes |
| Utility selection: role refuses the small model, with and without it in the catalog | n/a (no role input) | `role-policy` both ways; a permissive role with the small model missing still gets the offered primary |
| Config validation, explicit and automatic utility routing | no warning | one warning on the refusing role's `modelPolicy` |
| Real CLI, scratch config in the incident's shape: main `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`, automatic utility, default role `guest` allowing only the main model (base `b82c5504` vs head, dist builds) | `config validate`: valid, no warning | `config validate`, `status` (Utility model row) and `doctor` (`[config] warnings`) name `Role "guest"` |

Suites: `utility-model`, `config.utility-model-warnings`, `session-activity-summaries`, `session-activity-summaries.retry`, `list.status`, `dashboard-session-title`, `session-observer-stdout`, `session-row-transcript-backfill`, `models-list-result.configured-static`.

prs.title: fix(openrouter): BYOK turns record $0 spend when OpenRouter reports only its fee
prs.body:
Root cause: packages/ai/src/transports/openai-transport-shared.ts:412 (main 8ae0874) stores OpenRouter's `usage.cost` as the provider-billed turn total, but on BYOK responses that field is only OpenRouter's fee (often 0); the inference billed to the user's own provider key is in `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost`. Session rollups add `cost.total`, so the session and usage-cost totals stay at $0.

Fixes #195259

Thanks @AS76 for the detailed report with the real BYOK usage shape, and @Shizoqua for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: session cost, `session_status` and the usage-cost report show $0 for OpenRouter turns billed through a BYOK provider key, even though tokens and per-component prices are recorded.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenRouter BYOK turns record what the turn actually cost (OpenRouter fee plus the upstream inference cost), so session totals, `session_status` and `openclaw gateway usage-cost` show real spend. Non-BYOK OpenRouter turns and other providers are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenRouter documents `cost` as the amount charged to the OpenRouter account and `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` as the amount charged by the upstream provider; `is_byok` marks requests made with the user's own key ([usage accounting](https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting), [ChatUsage](https://openrouter.ai/docs/client-sdks/typescript/models/chatusage), [BYOK](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/auth/byok)). OpenClaw's provider-billed total is the turn's spend as reported by the provider and takes precedence over catalog estimates (`docs/reference/token-use.md`), so for BYOK it must be fee plus upstream cost.

When `is_byok` is true the parser now records fee + `upstream_inference_cost` as the provider-billed total. If a BYOK response has no usable upstream amount, the parser keeps the catalog estimate (no `provider-billed` origin; unpriced models stay unpriced) instead of recording the fee alone as the whole bill. Non-BYOK responses, including a billed 0 for free models, are unchanged.

## Evidence

Built Gateway (`pnpm build:docker`) in a secretless node:24.22.1 container, an OpenRouter-compatible stand-in returning the usage shape from #195259 (`cost: 0`, `is_byok: true`, `upstream_inference_cost: 0.021008625`), one agent turn per route; `session_status` read through a real agent tool call, plus `openclaw gateway usage-cost --agent <id>`.

| Route | main 8ae0874 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter BYOK: turn `cost.total` | `0` (provider-billed) | `0.021008625` (provider-billed) |
| OpenRouter BYOK: `session_status` | `Cost: $0.0000` | `Cost: $0.02` |
| OpenRouter BYOK: usage-cost | `Total: $0.0000` | `Total: $0.02` (`totalCost` 0.021008625) |
| OpenRouter non-BYOK (control) | `$0.0005` billed | identical (same JSON hash) |
| Direct provider (control) | `$0.0002` estimate | identical (same JSON hash) |

Regression `openai-completions-usage-parity.test.ts` ("OpenRouter BYOK fee plus upstream inference cost"): fails on main (`expected 0.000001 to be close to 0.0000166`), passes here.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196880#issuecomment-7229393526

prs.title: fix: cron jobs treat node policy denials as failures
prs.body:
Related: #166763 (wrapped remote-node policy denial and persisted cron diagnostics).

## What Problem This Solves

Unattended cron runs could report success when a remote node rejected an exec command with `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED`, including when the Gateway wrapped the native denial in an `UNAVAILABLE` error.

## User Impact

Cron jobs now preserve native node policy denials as fatal execution failures. The persisted run keeps the original denial text and a structured tool diagnostic; ordinary node transport failures retain the existing nonfatal policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node exec path retained structured failure metadata, but a Gateway wrapper could obscure the denial code and the cron projection discarded the tool name and code. This change:

- recognizes the native denial marker through the Gateway wrapper;
- carries the denial message and code through sanitized tool results;
- persists the original denial text without classifier decoration;
- retains `toolName` and `code` in normalized cron diagnostics.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(models): declare every Chat Completions compat default
prs.body:
## Problem

Chat Completions request shape is decided by guesses on the provider id, the host and the model id in `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-compat.ts`. For six fields a guess is the only source: model compat cannot set them at all.
- `seedField` (`random_seed` on Mistral)
- `emitsDsmlToolCalls` (DeepSeek tool-call markup)
- `requiresTypedUnionBranches` (Moonshot schema profile)
- `requiresNonEmptyUserOrAssistantMessage` (Model Studio)
- `cacheControlSystemOnly` and `cacheControlSharedSystem` (Anthropic-style markers on OpenRouter models)

So the guesses cannot be moved to declarations. A user behind a relay also cannot declare any of these for their route. For example, a Mistral model behind a relay always gets `seed`, which Mistral ignores.

## Fix

- Add the six fields to the model compat contract: `OpenAICompletionsCompat`, the catalog compat type and normalizer, and the config schema.
- Declared values override the guessed default.
- No defaults change.

This is the first step of the D4 cutover (provider and host guesses become manifest declarations).

## User impact

- No change for existing configs; nothing is sent differently unless a user declares one of the new fields.
- Users on relays can now declare these behaviours in `models.providers.<id>.models[].compat`.

## Evidence

- A throwaway harness built the request body for 496 routes on base and head and compared them: every bundled `openai-completions` catalog row on its own and on the default route, every plugin-declared host under a custom provider id, generic relay and localhost routes, and OpenRouter, DeepInfra, together and dashscope extras. All 496 bodies are byte-identical.
- New test: a declared `seedField: "random_seed"` on an unknown host sends `random_seed` and no `seed`.
- `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.test.ts`: 56/56.
- `pnpm config:docs:gen` refreshed the config baseline hash.

prs.title: fix: resume interrupted shell work without retrying it
prs.body:
Related: #205859

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart can interrupt a shell command after it has changed something but before its result is saved. Today the turn stops at a warning: someone has to check what happened and ask the agent to continue.

## User Impact

Eligible turns continue in the same conversation without another user message. The agent reuses saved results, checks an uncertain effect only when needed, and continues work that does not depend on it. It reports what it verified and what remains unknown without retrying the command or replaying the request. Separately queued messages still get their own replies. A recovered external reply stays in the original thread and replies to the original message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing receipt writer decides which shell results are durable. Startup reuses the existing restart continuation and, only for an unresolved command, adds a short checkpoint. The ordinary restart prompt, approvals, permissions, configuration, and stored formats are unchanged. External delivery uses the recorded source route and reply anchor; unavailable admission still produces a local diagnostic.

## Evidence

- The loopback Gateway reproduced the pause on `9eaf1b7d19edd`. On the repaired code (`d1ea8a45797e`), the shell-checkpoint test passed in 15.5 seconds: an effect already committed, an expected file still absent, an unknown job with independent work, and a saved terminal result. The original command was not repeated. The provider was a deterministic fixture, not a live model.
- Both queued-follow-up cases passed with one visible answer each (already queued, 13.5 seconds; admitted as its own turn, 11.7 seconds). An earlier full-file run was 10/11: the admitted case timed out waiting for a provider observation. Its strengthened test checks visible delivery instead; the earlier timeout’s cause is not established. The full file was not rerun locally just to obtain a green count.
- The [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206900#issuecomment-7226249805) found a dropped reply anchor and restart expectations that still required a pause. Both were repaired. The anchor regression failed before the fix and passed afterward; all eight routing tests passed on that unchanged routing code. The failing hosted typecheck leaf also passed locally, along with the Gateway build, targeted lint, formatting and `git diff --check`.
- The added unresolved-shell instruction fell from 526 to 218 bytes; the ordinary restart prompt was byte-identical. This is a prompt-size comparison, not a claim about live latency or billing. Local independent autoreview could not start in its read-only sandbox; see the Checks and review on the current head for hosted results.

Contributor: @VACInc

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ce1a777a-7764-4517-bc15-f839008dc25b)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1cc16a14-9597-4dad-88f8-b00dbc214f24)
- [Review fixes and restart verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/72a669f0-39ce-4eb8-b85b-4a35bccb2eff)

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

prs.title: fix(macos): launch app-managed Gateway under signed helper
prs.body:
## Summary

App-managed macOS Gateway LaunchAgents now start the signed `openclaw-mac` helper as their first executable. The helper supervises the existing private environment wrapper and stable Bun runtime, so launchd has an app-associated executable while the Gateway keeps its current command and environment. Standalone CLI-installed services retain their existing runtime identity.

## Root cause and owner

The app installed a Gateway LaunchAgent whose first executable was `/bin/sh`, followed by the generated environment wrapper and Bun. macOS therefore had no signed OpenClaw app executable at the launchd boundary. The LaunchAgent writer owns the plist; the macOS app owns selection of its signed helper and bundle ID. The private helper keeps the app process alive instead of replacing it with Bun.

The readback, restart rewrite, audit, and native app service inspection now understand the helper prefix. The release and debug bundle IDs are passed from the running app and emitted as `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers`. The helper validates its managed Bun, entrypoint, and environment paths before spawning. No generic CLI service route or public configuration surface changes.

Production code: +230 net lines (native supervisor and path validation, plus launchd/app lifecycle wiring). Tests: +180 lines. The growth establishes the signed app process as the service owner and keeps the existing secret and rollback boundaries intact.

## Proof completed

- Focused LaunchAgent suite on Blacksmith Testbox: 21 passed, including stored generic plist compatibility, same-runtime reinstall identity, runtime conversion warning, and release/debug restart round trips.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed on Testbox.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, Swift parser, standalone strict Swift typecheck of the helper, and repository-config SwiftLint passed.
- The signed-helper parser passed a local native compile/run smoke with the legacy entrypoint and all four installer-supported dist entrypoints; an unrelated entrypoint was rejected.
- A scoped local native CLI build reached the protocol generator, then stopped because this code-only worktree has no `esbuild`. The native package build and tests still need CI proof.
- Native recovery tests now cover fresh installs and retained service selection; they have only parser and lint proof until macOS CI runs.

## macOS acceptance gate

Keep this draft until an isolated, disposable macOS VM with a consistently signed app verifies both the System Settings entry and the real operation. Do not use the operator's TCC database or running Gateway.

1. Install the app-managed Gateway; confirm the plist starts with the signed `openclaw-mac` helper, its Team ID matches the app, and `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` equals the running bundle ID. Confirm the Gateway starts, stops, drains, and restarts.
2. Grant and exercise each relevant permission separately: Desktop/Documents read and write through Gateway file tools and `system.run`; Peekaboo screenshot, Accessibility inspection, and click/type; Xcode Automation using an Apple Events action aimed at Xcode, then `xcodebuild` through `system.run` as a separate exec check. A successful `xcodebuild` alone is not Automation proof.
3. For each operation, record the prompt and Privacy row name, actual success/failure, and whether a generic `node` or Bun row appears. Repeat after Gateway restart and signed app update. Include the native worker's file transfer and an app-routed exec child.

Apple documents `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers` for legacy LaunchAgents whose executable shares the app's Team ID. TCC responsible-code attribution for descendants remains an observed-behavior question, so this PR does not claim that every bucket will merge into one OpenClaw row before VM proof.

prs.title: improve(memory): use less memory when listing large note folders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw lists an indexed folder, it prepares one filesystem callback for every candidate path before it starts resolving any of them. Only four lookups can run at once. On the 101,963-note shape reported by @jzmudzinski in [the Linux watcher issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/200227), the queued callbacks occupy heap during the scan.

## User Impact

Listing files still resolves each path, preserves the first spelling of an alias in discovery order, and uses the original path when a lookup fails. The paired Gateway result and CPU tradeoffs appear below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Yield one callback when the existing scheduler requests a path. The scheduler already uses an iterable, returns the complete ordered array of keys, and drains active work on failure. Its input type now accepts the generator. The later file-inspection step, the watcher and persisted index rows have separate ownership. Production diff is +8/−6 lines. Existing owner tests cover discovery order, out-of-order completion, lookup errors and failure draining.

## Evidence

On an isolated Linux x64 AWS host, stock constructed 101,963 callbacks while the first four filesystem lookups were blocked. The candidate constructed four and reached five as soon as one slot opened. Both made all 101,963 real filesystem lookups, capped concurrency at four and returned the same ordered path digest. [Construction check and focused tests](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_59fd772909bb9c968119a2c053b4f050)

Five interleaved pairs on the same 101,963 real files, with the construction counter removed, gave these collector-only results. Peak sampling started at the four-slot hold, then ran every 1,024 lookups and at completion. The nearest-rank p95 is the maximum of five arms. [All ten phase measurements](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fac260a091d9c8e2ac1900fbc51e35e6)

| Metric (MiB) | Stock median | Candidate median | Stock p95 | Candidate p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Post-GC used heap, four lookups blocked | 41.271 | 31.158 | 41.273 | 31.161 |
| Sampled peak used heap, canonicalization | 123.525 | 103.760 | 123.570 | 103.813 |
| Sampled peak process RSS, canonicalization | 283.699 | 271.977 | 285.492 | 272.996 |

### Gateway acceptance rule, recorded before formal timing

Use [frozen main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9845bf5b8e4d6504cdf06846ecf2563b0700151c) and this source change, the same AWS host, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependencies and the [unchanged committed driver](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/074cfad15678c42eb6084a6de2f40fe246f895c9/scripts/perf/memory-gateway-append-measure.py) (SHA-256 `78f8e3f804cdd5dfa6f0831d5564ab24bf00165a0eab7d22133d0773efb5ad9b`). Initialize one 101,963-file/7,778-directory fixture with the stock CLI. Restore that same indexed database byte-for-byte for every process at the same workspace path. Run five serial matched pairs, alternating which build goes first, beginning with stock. Every process must warm resident search, register the watches, publish five appends before the next search RPC, return all five paths, then settle. Require zero observer overflow and the driver's 100 ms sampler coverage through the search RPC. Separately check the equal-size, restored-mtime sibling edit on both builds.

Primary outcome is sampled peak RSS of the Gateway listener process, first append through settled search. Require a lower candidate median **and** lower peaks in at least four of five pairs. Report medians, nearest-rank p95 and ranges, including warm-up, main and total CPU, publication and search latency, time through settlement, open/read counts and sample gaps. Record every adverse movement. A phase-only gain or a failed primary criterion ends this candidate. A regression needs explicit maintainer acceptance before landing.

## Gateway result

The candidate met the preregistered primary rule. Median listener-process peak RSS from the first append through settled search fell **93,488 KiB (4.01%, 91.30 MiB)**, with lower peaks in four of five pairs. Two CPU measurements crossed 20% in the adverse direction. They require an explicit maintainer decision before merge. [All ten Gateway arms](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2ec462e74652da55637dad525b3d2ec4)

| Pair | Stock peak KiB | Candidate peak KiB | Paired change KiB | First interval containing the eventual peak, stock / candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 2,179,124 | 2,289,088 | +109,964 | After RPC / By RPC return |
| 2 | 2,329,088 | 2,193,908 | −135,180 | By RPC return / After RPC |
| 3 | 2,322,116 | 2,173,428 | −148,688 | After RPC / After RPC |
| 4 | 2,372,100 | 2,235,600 | −136,500 | After RPC / After RPC |
| 5 | 2,362,008 | 2,253,644 | −108,364 | After RPC / After RPC |

Each cell below gives **median (minimum–nearest-rank p95)** over five processes. With five observations, p95 is also the maximum. CPU is in milliseconds. RSS is in KiB.

| Measured outcome | Stock | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Checkpoint verification through first successful seed search, s | 27.083 (26.705–27.244) | 26.553 (26.502–26.592) |
| Resident search return through warm-up settlement, s | 64.543 (64.044–64.547) | 64.545 (64.535–65.534) |
| Warm-up peak RSS | 1,514,892 (1,501,088–1,569,284) | 1,531,824 (1,504,120–1,641,296) |
| Warm-up ending RSS | 1,374,852 (1,373,212–1,388,616) | 1,383,136 (1,374,600–1,466,236) |
| Warm-up main CPU | 80 (80–90) | 90 (80–90) |
| Warm-up total CPU | 1,230 (1,210–1,300) | 1,250 (1,180–1,780) |
| First 30 seconds of appends, main CPU | 7,830 (7,260–10,000) | 9,480 (8,490–9,740) |
| First 30 seconds of appends, total CPU | 51,810 (50,600–56,550) | 55,860 (53,500–56,700) |
| First append through five indexed paths before RPC, s | 36.017 (34.012–37.02) | 34.513 (33.511–35.516) |
| Search RPC, s | 0.853 (0.832–0.86) | 0.854 (0.843–0.86) |
| First append through five successful search hits, s | 36.866 (34.844–37.873) | 35.358 (34.354–36.376) |
| First append through settled search, s | 69.397 (66.866–70.396) | 67.881 (67.377–68.901) |
| Full interval main CPU | 20,420 (19,800–21,050) | 19,780 (19,390–20,860) |
| Full interval total CPU | 89,790 (87,940–91,650) | 88,420 (87,140–89,680) |
| Full interval peak RSS (primary) | 2,329,088 (2,179,124–2,372,100) | 2,235,600 (2,173,428–2,289,088) |
| RSS at settled endpoint | 2,078,272 (1,969,308–2,168,260) | 2,114,364 (2,013,640–2,162,412) |

In the first 30 seconds of writes, median main-thread CPU rose **7.83 → 9.48 s (+21.1%)** and total CPU rose **51.81 → 55.86 s (+7.8%)**. Across the full interval median main CPU fell 0.64 s and total CPU fell 1.37 s. Warm-up p95 total CPU rose **1.30 → 1.78 s (+36.9%)**, with p95 warm peak RSS up 72,012 KiB, warm time up 0.987 s and median full-interval ending RSS up 36,092 KiB. Median search RPC time rose 1 ms. Time to five hits fell 1.508 s at the median and 1.497 s at p95. These are observed workload tradeoffs.

All ten Gateways restored the same stock-generated checkpoint (`89e74c2f9228a57998feaa00bbd2c09914ffe2e94fa0f8527becb74ee3f95979`), registered 7,781 watches for 7,778 observed directories, indexed the five appends before the next RPC, and returned all five expected paths. Each recorded 305,912 file-access events, 101,968 distinct Markdown paths and zero overflows. There were 668–704 interior samples during the primary interval (maximum gap 100.3 ms) and 8–9 during the RPC (maximum gap 100.1 ms). Both builds also found the equal-size restored-mtime sibling edit. [Checkpoint and sibling checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5feaa68b70a24b0d6349b5ffeabf29f7)

Eight of ten arms first reached their eventual peak after the search RPC returned. In the other two, the peak had been reached by RPC return and exceeded the earlier publication-window peak. In every arm, the interval from the pre-RPC counter read through settlement added 101,968 access events and zero new distinct paths. The driver records counts and timing. It does not identify which owner triggered those reads.

The production diff is +8/−6 lines and the test diff is zero. All 48 existing focused tests passed. Formatting, targeted lint and both runtime builds passed. [Source checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cb039effa7e4905f40757498aaa3a735) · [Hosted CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46015515760/job/140573397584) · [Hosted review of the signed head, no source findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206734#issuecomment-7221064746)

A private direct-mapper alternative used less main-thread CPU than the generator in all five paired warm listings of the same 101,963 files. The median paired saving was 9.915 ms per listing. Median canonicalization CPU fell 2.38%, below the 10% threshold, and median sampled peak heap rose 13.388 MiB (103.978 → 117.366 MiB). All listings returned the same paths in the same order. We stopped before a Gateway comparison. The cause of the earlier 1.65 s Gateway main-thread CPU difference remains open. [Collector measurement](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bd31af9ee569f5f678fea41ae5674c5c)
