prs.title: fix(sessions): let a fallback run after the turn was dispatched without a projection
prs.body:
## Problem

On a production deployment, one user turn failed with "All models failed": two fallback models refused it with `Model prompt projection must be captured before provider dispatch`.

The turn was a forwarded inter-session message (`sessions_send`). The primary model ran on the embedded runner, sent the turn unchanged without a model prompt projection (by design for unchanged inter-session text), and then hit a rate limit. The fallback models ran on the Codex harness. Its capture step only checks whether a projection already exists, so it tried to freeze one after the turn had already reached a provider. The transcript recorder correctly refused the write and threw, so every Codex fallback failed and the user got no answer.

## Fix

The transcript recorder owns the "capture before dispatch" rule. A turn that was already sent without a projection is now treated as frozen at its transcript text: a later candidate's capture or prepare makes no write and returns the message unchanged. A dispatch that races a capture write still throws, as before. The embedded runner, which threw when capture returned no projection, now keeps the transcript text for that turn.

Production code: +7 / −4.

## User impact

A fallback candidate no longer fails a turn that an earlier candidate already sent without a projection, on any harness (Gateway and `openclaw agent`). The stored turn keeps the text the first provider received.

## Evidence

- New test `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.prompt-projection.test.ts` ("runs after an earlier candidate dispatched the turn without a projection"). It fails on main with the production error and passes with this change.
- New test `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-submit.projections.test.ts` ("sends the transcript text when an earlier candidate dispatched without a projection"): a harness that sends without capturing, then an embedded fallback with hook context. It fails on main (the fallback never reaches the provider) and passes with this change.
- Updated recorder contract test `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts`: a sent turn is still never given a projection; capture now resolves without one instead of throwing.
- Projection suites on both routes pass: `attempt-prompt-submit.projections.test.ts` and `attempt-prompt-context.test.ts` (embedded), and `run-attempt.prompt-projection.test.ts` (Codex).

## Not covered

On such a fallback, Codex still sends its own hook-wrapped prompt for that attempt; the stored canonical text stays the transcript text. This matches how Codex treated every turn before projections existed.

prs.title: fix(agents): read cannot open the full output of a large tool result under workspace-only read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#206880 saves the full output of a large tool result to a private file and tells the model `Full output: <path> (page it with read offset/limit)`. exec and web_fetch already did the same for their own output. In host sessions with workspace-only file access (`tools.fs.workspaceOnly`, or guarded/read-only permission modes), `read` refuses that path: the file sits in the OS temp directory, outside the workspace. The model is told where the omitted output is but cannot open it, and falls back to rerunning the tool.

Review of #206880 flagged this in both rounds. The owner approved this follow-up with a fixed scope: `read` may open the session's own spill files, and nothing broader.

## Fix

The private spill writer (`sessions/tools/private-temp-file.ts`) owns the allowlist:
- `writePrivateTempFile` and `openPrivateTempFileStream` take an optional `owner` (`{ agentId, sessionKey }`). After the exclusive create, the writer records the file's realpath under that owner. Registration happens only there. A path taken from a tool result (`details.spill.path`, `fullOutputPath`) is never trusted, so a plugin cannot name an arbitrary file.
- `resolveOwnSpillFile(owner, path)` admits a path only when its realpath was recorded for that same owner, and it is a regular file owned by this uid.
- The list is process memory with caps: newest 64 paths per owner, 256 owners. A restart or eviction makes old paths unreadable again, and `read` then refuses them visibly.

The owner is computed once per embedded attempt, with the same expression tool construction already uses for its session key. The same value goes to the #206880 bound step, exec's output file, web_fetch's spill, and the `read` guard. web_fetch's result cache is scoped by owner, so a cached result never points one session at another session's file.

The `read` guard (`wrapToolWorkspaceRootGuardWithOptions`) gets `ownFile`. On an admitted path it skips only the root-containment check, and every other read step still runs. Only `read` receives it; `ls`, `write`, `edit` and `apply_patch` keep the plain workspace guard. Sandboxed sessions are unchanged: their spills are already staged inside the workspace.

Two existing helpers moved verbatim into sibling modules so the touched files stay under their line caps: `assertSandboxPathWithinAnyRoot` → `agent-tools.workspace-roots.ts`, `sanitizeWebFetchUrl` → `web-fetch-utils.ts`. One exec auto-review state block moved to `bash-tools.exec-auto-review-state.ts`.

Accepted edge cases (named, not coded):
- After a restart or cap eviction, older spill paths are refused again.
- A subagent cannot read its parent's spill files.
- A same-uid local process could swap the file between the check and the open. It can already read everything.

## User impact

- Gateway and one-shot users on the embedded runtime with workspace-only file access can now page the full output that a large tool result points to, instead of rerunning the tool.
- No new config, no schema change, no new retention rule. The spill location and lifetime stay those of #206880: the OS temp directory, 0600, OS cleanup.

## Evidence
End to end, through `openclaw agent --local` on a cheap OpenAI model, in an isolated state dir and HOME, with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly: true`. The model runs `head -c 4000000 /dev/urandom | base64 -b 76 | head -n 50000` (random lines, so line 30000 cannot be guessed) and is asked for line 30000:
- Merge base `59e5c7309581`: the 64 KB exec result keeps head and tail and names the full-output file. `read` on that file fails with `Path escapes sandbox root (<workspace>): <tmp>/openclaw-exec-<id>.log`, and the model replies UNKNOWN.
- This PR: the same `read` (offset 30000, limit 3) succeeds. The reply equals line 30000 of the spill file on disk.

`src/agents/sessions/tools/private-temp-file.test.ts`, through the production `createCoreCodingTools` workspace-only `read`:
- A session reads its own spill outside the workspace with offset/limit. Without an owner record, the same production `read` refuses the path with the workspace-containment error (the "fresh owner" and "plugin path" cases below), which is what main does for every spill path.
- Denied:
  - a file at a plugin-chosen path;
  - an unissued file with a spill-like name;
  - another session's spill (same agent);
  - the same session key under another agent;
  - a fresh owner;
  - an admitted path replaced by a symlink or a directory;
  - a neighbour file reached through an alias;
  - `write`, `edit`, `ls` and `apply_patch` on an admitted spill;
  - a missing file, and a file owned by another uid.
- Allowed: `..` and `/private/var` aliases of exactly the issued file.
- Caps: the newest 64 paths per owner and 256 owners are kept.

Also: exec and web_fetch register their own files (`bash-tools.exec-approval-output.test.ts`, `web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts`), and the attempt's bound step passes the owner (`attempt-context-guards.test.ts`).

The design was reviewed adversarially before coding; the rejected alternatives were session-tagged file names (they admit a name pattern) and a per-session directory root (it admits any file in the directory).

Opening a chat from the Sessions table or sidebar can leave the browser waiting for the chat renderer after the click.

prs.body: Closes #205656 Related: #205674 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: opening the Control UI Terminal fails with `failed to load Ghostty WASM | Failed to fetch WASM: 404` when a tab recovers from the cached offline shell and reconnects to a Gateway with Terminal enabled. ## User Impact User impact: Terminal stays safely disabled on the offline shell until config refresh triggers the existing guarded reload into a live document with a WASM-compatible CSP, without breaking unsaved-work reload guards or requiring any configuration changes. ## Why This Change Was Made The offline shell's CSP intentionally omits `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, but `precacheOfflineShell()` in `ui/public/sw.js` did not emit `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"` on ``. Without that marker, `readDocumentTerminalEnabled()` returns `null` and `config.refresh()` skips its document-reload check, enabling Terminal inside an incompatible document. Adding `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"` at the offline-shell producer aligns the cached document with its CSP and reuses the existing reload guard rather than widening CSP or adding a second reload path. *(Note: #205674 addresses the same issue; this PR keeps the change minimal with a targeted assertion on the generated offline shell HTML in `service-worker-cache.test.ts`.)* ## Evidence Verified on head `a1d2be28ab1c914a4cf70eaf9823b7b11fb8b800`: ### 1. Focused unit & policy tests (red on base → green on head) - **Red before fix** (base `ui/public/sw.js` with the new assertion in `ui/src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts`): - `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts` → **3 failed | 46 passed (49)** (all 3 scope variants failed at line 606: `` omitted `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"`). - **Green with fix** (`a1d2be28ab1`): - `pnpm --dir ui test --run src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts src/app/document-reload-owners.test.ts src/app/config.test.ts` → **3 test files passed, 67 passed (67)** (including `document-reload-owners.test.ts` verifying unsaved-work reload veto and reload on subsequent refresh after release). - **Formatting / whitespace:** `git diff --check` → passed (0 issues). ### 2. Production Control UI build & browser recovery trace - `pnpm ui:build` succeeded (`dist/control-ui/sw.js` emits `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"`). - Exercised the production `dist/control-ui/` bundle in headless Chrome over a local loopback HTTP/WS Gateway harness (no private endpoints/credentials): 1. **Live load & SW cache:** `/settings/connection` returned `200`, `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="true"`, live CSP with `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; SW activated and cached `__offline_shell__` (`hasTerminalFalseAttr: true`, `cspHasWasm: false`). 2. **503 fallback:** Simulated HTTP `503` on navigation to `/chat/main/main` → SW served cached offline shell (`status: 200`, `fromServiceWorker: true`, `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"`, `offlineCspHasWasm: false`). 3. **Recovery & reload:** Restored `/control-ui-config.json` returning `{ "terminalEnabled": true }` → config refresh detected `"false"` vs `true` and reloaded into the live document (`data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="true"`, live CSP with `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`). 4. **Terminal initialization:** Opened `openclaw-terminal-panel` → Ghostty WASM compiled and rendered `` visible (`terminalCanvasVisible: true`, `hasGhostty404: false`, `pageErrors: []`, `non503FailedRequests: []`). ### Remaining local gaps - `pnpm tsgo:ui`: `@tsrs/win32-x64` is unsupported on Windows x64 and the fallback `tsc` timed out locally; UI typechecking remains pending GitHub Actions CI. - Browser recovery ran against the production `dist/control-ui/` bundle with a local loopback HTTP/WS Gateway fixture rather than a full built `dist/index.js` daemon; the unsaved-work reload veto is proven in `ui/src/app/document-reload-owners.test.ts` (green above).

prs.title: fix: find and resubmit failed events with channel aliases
prs.body:
Closes #205001

## What Problem This Solves

When operators inspect failed inbound events with `--channel Telegram`, `imsg`, or `teams`, the dead-letter commands select a different queue from the one used by the channel. Inspection reports no failures, and resubmission reports an existing event as not found.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect and resubmit failed events using bundled channel IDs regardless of case, or their known aliases. Unrecognized ingress plugin IDs retain their spelling and case. Account selection keeps its existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve bundled IDs and aliases through the existing `normalizeChatChannelId` owner in the scope resolver shared by both commands. Fall back to the trimmed input for other ingress plugins. This follows the normalization boundary described in #205001, which replaced the closed PR #190470, and avoids duplicating the alias catalog or changing queue storage.

Add one parameterized regression to the existing real-SQLite command suite, covering mixed case, two bundled aliases, and a case-sensitive custom plugin ID. Document the accepted selectors in the CLI reference.

## Evidence

Validated on Windows x64 against base `74a707bc1d50ea1bd9edbfa04b64fe0ca8b58a07` and the local patch. Tooling used Node 24.20.0; the real CLI selected Node 24.22.3 through its normal launcher.

- Red: `pnpm test src/commands/channels/dead-letters.test.ts -t 'resolves channel selector' --maxWorkers=1` produced the intended three failures on unchanged production code. The custom plugin control passed.
- Green: `pnpm test src/commands/channels/dead-letters.test.ts src/cli/channels-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 34 tests across both files. Tests used `CI=true` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. Subsequent formatting only wrapped the new test without changing its logic.
- Targeted oxlint, formatting of all three files, the changed page's MDX check, `pnpm tsgo:core`, the canonical `core-test-commands` typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The normal CLI runtime build and bootstrap import guard passed before and after the fix. Baseline build: 4m 58.3s. Fixed build: 4m 16.4s.

Real CLI proof used an isolated home, config, and shared SQLite state. Synthetic failures were created through production `enqueue`, `claim`, and `fail` operations. No command implementation or queue was mocked.

| Selector / operation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list --channel Telegram --account ops --json` | Exit 0, empty queue despite the retained event | Exit 0, canonical `telegram`, same retained event |
| `list --channel imsg --account ops --json` | Exit 0, empty queue | Exit 0, canonical `imessage`, retained event |
| Resubmit through an iMessage alias | `imsg`: exit 1, event not found | Both `IMSG` and `imsg`: exit 0, `resubmitted` |
| Inspect and resubmit through `teams` | Reproduced by the red regression | Exit 0, canonical `msteams` |
| Inspect and resubmit through `custom-Ingress` | Inspection finds its case-sensitive queue | Both operations exit 0 with the original ID |

The first four fixed flows used the same retained events as the baseline fixture. An additional failed iMessage event verified the exact lowercase `imsg` CLI argument after those flows. Production `claimNext` then recovered every resubmitted event from its canonical queue with its original ID and payload.

Limits: no live channel delivery, Gateway recovery sweep, or model call was exercised. Full package/declaration/release builds and broad CI were not run. The frozen install used `--ignore-scripts --no-optional` to avoid unavailable optional provider binaries; those providers are outside this proof.

Author-side scope and diff review completed. Independent local autoreview was not run because the shared helper is not installed.

AI assistance: Codex was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting.

prs.title: docs: stop teaching Knowledge automations a failure marker the scheduler ignores
prs.body:
Closes #206769
Related: #170267

## What Problem This Solves

When someone asks their agent to schedule a Knowledge ingestion job, the bundled `knowledge-automation` skill tells the agent to make the job reply `AUTOMATION_FAILED` on its first line when ingestion fails. Since #170267 the scheduler no longer recognises that token. The failure report is delivered or kept as ordinary output, the run is recorded as successful, and nothing alerts. The skill teaches a failure signal that no longer does anything.

## User Impact

New Knowledge automations describe unresolved failures in plain prose and deliver them where the owner will see them, matching the current unattended run contract. Nothing changes for existing jobs, and there is no runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` ("Unattended run contract") and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md` already say that blocker reports are ordinary output and that the scheduler does not classify assistant prose as an execution error. The skill is the only remaining first-party instruction that still names the token, so this aligns that one step with the documented contract.

## Evidence

**After-fix run through the shipped scheduler.** I built this branch (`OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (897d29e)`) and ran a gateway with fresh, isolated state and config: Knowledge as the memory slot, `openai/gpt-6-astra`, no channels. The source was a synthetic folder with one Markdown meeting note.

1. From an owner Control UI chat, I asked: *"set up a scheduled Knowledge ingestion that pulls new notes from ~/notes-export into my Knowledge vault every day at 07:00 Asia/Jakarta. Use the knowledge-automation skill and follow it. If a run can't do its job, I want to hear about it here."*
2. The agent read the revised skill, spawned and kept the worker session, and created the job, paused, with `openclaw automations add --disabled`. The failure clause in the job message it wrote:

   ```text
   On unresolved failure return a concise visible report of what failed and what you tried; NO_REPLY only for verified successful no-change runs.
   ```

   The job has `delivery.mode: "announce"` and `failureAlert.after: 1`. `AUTOMATION_FAILED` appears nowhere in the generated job, the session transcripts or the run records (`rg -c AUTOMATION_FAILED` over the state directory finds nothing).
3. The agent then forced scheduler runs itself: one ingested the note and saved a verified checkpoint. A rerun with the source unchanged added nothing.
4. I moved the source folder away, the way an unsynced or unmounted export would leave it, and ran the job through the scheduler with `openclaw automations run <id> --wait`. Run record from `openclaw automations runs`:

   ```json
   {
     "action": "finished",
     "status": "ok",
     "error": null,
     "summary": "Blocked: the source directory `<state>/home/notes-export` is missing. Fresh Gateway acquisition and a direct path check both confirmed this.\n\nKnowledge scope/access passed. No records or checkpoints changed; the previous verified checkpoint is preserved. Restore the source directory before retrying.",
     "deliveryStatus": "not-delivered",
     "deliveryError": "Channel is required when delivery.channel=last has no previous channel."
   }
   ```

   The scheduler records the blocker as `status: "ok"`, as the revised bullet says, and the reply says what failed and what was checked. The same report shows in the Control UI automation history:

   ![Control UI automation history showing the blocker report for the forced run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brandon-julio-t/openclaw/pr-206765-proof/proof/206765-blocker-run.png)

**Limits.**

- This test install has no messaging channel, so `announce` delivery had no route. The "Error" badge in the screenshot is that delivery failure; the earlier successful ingest run shows the same badge. The report is visible in automation history, not in a chat. The agent noticed the missing route during setup and left the job paused rather than enabling it without failure delivery, which is what the revised bullet asks for.
- Runs were forced with `automations run`; I did not wait for the 07:00 timer.
- Before the fix, the existing regression `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts` already shows `AUTOMATION_FAILED` prose being delivered unchanged. I did not repeat the live run on `main`.
- `rg AUTOMATION_FAILED` on `main` (ef39ce4c010), outside release notes, finds only this skill and that test.
- Docs-only change; I did not run the test suite.

prs.title: fix: warn when OpenAI realtime voice falls back
prs.body:
Fixes #206604.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI GA realtime calls silently replace unsupported voice settings such as `nova` with `alloy`. Calls can still work, but operators have no diagnostic explaining why the configured voice is not being used.

## User Impact

GA bridge and browser session creation now log a warning naming the requested and effective voice when an explicit unsupported choice is replaced. Calls retain the existing fallback: a supported configured voice after an unsupported browser override, otherwise `alloy`. Supported voices and an unset voice do not warn.

No configuration migration or new option is required. GPT-Live keeps its separate voice policy. This adds an operator log warning, not a browser notification.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small resolver in the existing OpenAI provider factory owns GA voice selection and its diagnostic for both entry points. This preserves working calls rather than turning an unsupported voice into a startup error.

Simplification pass: the browser's separate fallback expression is absorbed into that shared owner; no new exported API, state, or test-only production seam. Against base `f4e5600135121f8d46cf2c06e939290502a52d02`: production +15/-5 lines, tests +70, documentation +5.

## Evidence

- Before production edits, two regression groups exercised the real provider `createBridge` and `createBrowserSession` entry points on refreshed main. Three unsupported-voice cases failed specifically because the warning logger received zero calls; their outgoing effective-voice assertions already passed. Four supported/default/override controls passed.
- With the fix, **88 tests passed across four files**:
  ```sh
  RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-connection.test.ts \
    extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts \
    extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-routing.test.ts \
    extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ```
  The run covers bridge readiness, serialized session-update/client-secret voice selection, browser override precedence, GA/Azure behavior, and GPT-Live routing. Wrapper wall time: 66.72 seconds including compilation; the three-file shard containing both changed suites took 8.03 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.
- **Simulation boundary:** synthetic API keys, fake provider WebSocket events and client-secret HTTP responses. Existing suite credential/keychain mocks isolate host storage; the new cases use explicit synthetic keys. Production provider selection and session assembly execute normally. No live OpenAI request, isolated Gateway RPC session, browser microphone, or audible output was exercised.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed. `check:changed --staged --base <base> --dry-run` selected the expected four files; the full check suite was not run.
- Targeted lint could not complete SDK declaration preparation, and scoped typechecking failed in unchanged core files: the prepared dependency installation contains `@openclaw/fs-safe` **0.27.1**, while this base declares **0.28.2**. prs.title: feat(ios): a reply's actions move into its long-press menu, with one reactions pill
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, each reaction on a chat message is its own chip with its own count, so a message with a few reactions grows a row of chips under it. The Control UI shows one compact pill instead. Holding an assistant reply also lifts a shrunken copy of the whole reply, with its reactions and footer, above the menu, which for a long reply pushes the menu around and hides the text you held.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app's chat in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person on iPhone sees:

- One reactions pill per message instead of one chip per emoji. The pill shows up to three emoji, most used first, and the total once there is more than one reaction. On your own message it sits on the bubble's lower-left corner; under an assistant reply it sits where the chips were.
- Tapping the pill opens the **Add Reaction** sheet, which now lists the message's current reactions with their counts at the top. Tapping one adds or removes yours. VoiceOver reads who reacted with what.
- Pressing and holding an assistant reply lifts only its opening lines (up to eight, at reading size, without code blocks or diagrams) above the menu. A reply's actions are **Add Reaction**, **Copy Message**, **Select Text**, **Reply** and **Listen**, plus **Open Full Message** for a shortened reply. VoiceOver offers the same actions on the reply.
- Pressing and holding your own message opens the same menu as before, with the reactions pill attached to the bubble.
- The progress card and the sheets that already had a long-press menu use the same menu presentation as messages.
- The iOS docs describe the press-and-hold actions and the reactions pill.

Some parts of these screens still look old until later pull requests in the series: the chat header and the composer, the "Just now" time under messages and inside your own bubble, and the layout of your own bubble. The macOS app keeps its current message menu.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI already groups a message's reactions into one pill and puts a reply's actions in its menu. Doing the same on iPhone keeps the transcript quiet at rest and makes the long-press menu the one place for a message's actions. The held reply shows an excerpt rather than a scaled snapshot so the menu stays on screen for any reply length and the text stays readable. The summary rules (which emoji show, their order and the total) live in one tested place, `ChatReactionSummary`, and the excerpt rules in `ChatReplyMenuPreview`.

## Evidence

- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `ChatReactionSummaryTests` and `ChatReplyMenuPreviewTests`. 6 passed, 0 failed.
- UI test `testAssistantReplyHoldOffersActionsInMenu` passed: an unreacted reply has no footer or action bar at rest, and holding it opens the menu with its actions.
- UI test `testSavedPromptReactionsAndQuickPalette` fails before it reaches the reaction checks, in the same place before and after this change and on the finished series: the shared helper that sends the fixture message taps a fixed point to hide the keyboard, and that point lands on the fixture's diagram, which opens its full-screen preview. The screenshots below show the reaction behavior. With a local test-only change to that helper, all three focused UI tests passed: assistant reply actions, dark appearance, and saved-prompt reactions. This PR does not include the helper change.
- The iOS app builds with its SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` report no violations. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`; the one new catalog entry is "Current reactions". `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: the same fixture chat in screenshot mode on the same simulator, before and after, in light (transcript, user message menu, reply menu) and dark (transcript). Before is the series up to the previous pull request, not `main`.
- Not checked: the macOS app, the OpenClawKit SwiftPM tests on macOS, VoiceOver on a device, the Add Reaction sheet's current-reactions row in a screenshot, and a physical device.

In each image, Before (the series up to the previous pull request) is on the left and After is on the right.

prs.title: test(agents): gate prompt and tool bytes on the Gateway, configured-agent and Codex routes
prs.body:
## Problem

The only prompt byte gate (`FRESH_INSTALL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_BUDGET_BYTES`, 12,288 B) checks a hand-written fresh-install renderer fixture. Every other surface the model receives can grow without a failing check:
- the system prompt and the compacted tool definitions that the embedded runtime sends for a Gateway WebChat turn and for a configured channel agent;
- the Codex app-server prompt layers and dynamic tool specs, which are the default route for native OpenAI.

Tool and prompt bytes are a reported cost (#200920). A 2026-11-27 audit of production first requests measured them at 18–56 KB of tools per request, with no gate on any route except the fresh fixture.

## Solution

Gate each route at the owner that already builds it. Each new ceiling is the size measured on main plus 5%, rounded up to 256 B. Growth within that margin passes.

| Route | Surface | Measured on main | Ceiling | Test |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Fresh install (renderer fixture) | system prompt | 11,395 B | 12,288 B (unchanged) | `system-prompt.inventory-snapshot.test.ts` |
| Gateway WebChat turn, fresh install, embedded runtime | system prompt | 13,599 B | 14,336 B | `attempt-prompt-budget.test.ts` (new) |
| Gateway WebChat turn, embedded runtime | compacted tool definitions | 17,927 B | 18,944 B | same |
| Configured Telegram agent (workspace files, setup complete) | system prompt | 13,676 B | 14,592 B | same |
| Configured Telegram agent (workspace files, setup complete) | compacted tool definitions | 21,058 B | 22,272 B | same |
| Codex app-server Telegram turn | model-bound layer text | 12,981 B | 13,824 B | `test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts` |
| Codex app-server Telegram turn | dynamic tool specs | 62,551 B | 65,792 B | same |

- `attempt-prompt-budget.test.ts` runs the production attempt pipeline:
  1. `prepareEmbeddedAttemptToolBase`
  2. `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBundleTools`
  3. `prepareEmbeddedAttemptToolCatalog`, which compacts the tools as sent
  4. `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSystemPrompt`, with the tool directory, skills and bootstrap files
- Installed plugin tools, bundle MCP servers and paired-node probes vary by host, so they are mocked out. The budget covers core output.
- The workspace path is pinned to `/workspace` and the docs and source paths to `/repo`, because the prompt contains them. The `Runtime:` line (host, OS, Node version) still varies by about 20 B across hosts.
- The fresh WebChat turn has first-run bootstrap pending. The configured agent has recorded setup complete.
- Tool bytes are compact JSON of `{ name, description, parameters }` for the compacted set. Deferred tools reach the model by name only, so their schemas are not in these numbers.
- The Codex prompt is the sum of every non-`json` fenced layer body in the generated happy-path snapshot, from the layers heading to the end of the file. Renderer prose is not counted, and a relabeled or new layer is still counted.
- The embedded ceilings live in one table, `PROMPT_BUDGET_BYTES`, in `src/agents/system-prompt-manifest.ts`. The Codex pair sits beside its snapshot test.
- A PR that shrinks a surface should lower its ceiling. Nothing enforces that.

## Impact

Contributors only. There is no runtime change. A change that grows a route's prompt or tool bytes past 5% fails CI until the growth is cut or the ceiling is raised on purpose in review.

## Evidence

- Green on main `28b6938f` (rebased), final head: inventory 3/3, `attempt-prompt-budget` 2/2, prompt snapshots 8/8.
- Red on a synthetic regression against the same code (throwaway edits, removed): +1,512 B in the shared Execution Bias prompt section, +2,016 B in the `exec` description and +3,990 B in the `sessions_spawn` description. All 7 gates fail:
  - fresh prompt 12,908 > 12,288
  - WebChat prompt 15,112 > 14,336; WebChat tools 19,944 > 18,944
  - Telegram prompt 15,189 > 14,592; Telegram tools 23,075 > 22,272
  - Codex prompt 14,494 > 13,824; Codex tools 66,540 > 65,792
- Adversarial review, two rounds. Round 1 found tools measured before compaction, a Gateway fixture without the directory, skills or bootstrap, and a markdown slice with renderer prose. Round 2 found a Codex sum that could drop to 0 B on a relabeled fence, a configured agent measured in first-run state, and host checkout paths in the prompt. All six are fixed here.
- Known gaps:
  - Deferred tool schemas are not gated on the embedded routes. On the Telegram route, 29 deferred tools (about 84 KB, `automations` alone 23.7 KB) appear in the prompt by name only. The Codex dynamic-tool gate covers `sessions_spawn` and the `openclaw` namespace in full.
  - The Telegram `message` schema comes from a two-action test channel plugin, not the real Telegram plugin.
  - Plugin, MCP and node tools and new bundled skills are not budgeted.
  - Steps after the catalog are not measured: the listing pin, the prompt-build tool policy and transport serialization.
  - Not covered: the Codex-owned native layers (`AGENTS.md`, environment, memories) that Codex adds after OpenClaw sends the thread params.
  - A failing gate prints the total only, not a per-tool breakdown.

prs.title: fix(infra): join the shared worker host at terminal native close
prs.body:
## Problem

On macOS, a stable 2026.11.10 install rolls back when it updates to current `main`.

- The updater runs the target's `update-migrated-finalize.worker.js --doctor`. Doctor finishes ("Doctor complete."), then the worker exits 1 and the updater restores the previous package and databases.
- The saved failure keeps only `exit; └ Doctor complete.; Doctor: Update schema admission`, plus a truncated `Native worker execution owners have not joined`.
- Reproduced in scratch: a fresh `openclaw@2026.11.10` (setup baseline, Gateway started and killed) running `openclaw update --tag <main package>`. 2 of 3 runs rolled back.
- Every `doctor` run on `main` against that state prints `CLI cleanup failed: shared-state: Native worker execution owners have not joined` (5/5).

Cause (regression from #206721):

- The finalize worker runs with the `cli-oneshot` database role (`src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts:92`). Since #206721, `claimsSharedHostSlot` therefore hosts its core workers in the shared worker host. That includes the plugin model catalog reader, a plain task pool with no native close of its own.
- The shared host's physical worker is a retained native worker. At exit, `closeDefaultRetainedNativeWorkerSource` (`:649`) finds it still alive, because the catalog reader endpoint was never stopped. `source.close()` throws (`src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.ts:398`), and the worker's catch sets `process.exitCode = 1` (`:675-677`).
- Before #206721, that reader was a plain worker outside native custody.

Bisect: the teardown error appears in 0/3 Doctor runs at `afa038c1` (parent of #206721), 3/3 at `a6d787f1`, and 5/5 at `8bd18635`.

## Fix

`src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts`: when the host starts, it registers with its native source. Terminal close of that source stops the endpoints that are still live (reason `shutdown`), so the host joins before the source checks for live workers. No new state, flag or option.

## Impact

| PR | Population | Failure class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| this | Every install that updates through a shipped updater (2026.11.10 and earlier) to a release that contains #206721: the target's finalize worker exits 1 and the update rolls back. Every one-shot CLI command on `main` (`doctor`, `agent --local`, …) also prints the false teardown failure. Gateway: shutdown with the lean profile, through the same native source close. | Update/Doctor, cluster A (target Doctor gates the update) | `src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts:92,649,675-677`; `src/infra/shared-worker-host.ts:84-105`; `src/infra/worker-native-lifecycle.ts:397-398` |

User signal: the 2026.11.10 → main scratch upgrade (the release path for every stable user). Cluster A has 57 reports of target-Doctor exit 1 rolling back updates, for example #200606 and #203211. This regression is a new, unreleased instance of the same class.

## Evidence

- Red on base, green with the fix: `src/infra/shared-worker-host.test.ts` › "joins the host at terminal native close when an endpoint's owner never stops it". On the merge base it fails with `Native worker execution owners have not joined`.
- `doctor --fix --non-interactive` on 2026.11.10 state, built CLI: `main` 5/5 teardown failures; this branch 0/2.
- Sibling tests pass: shared-worker-host (unqualified close), worker-native-lifecycle, worker-task-host, sqlite-worker-broker (lifecycle and core), agent-local cold start, agent-cli recovery.
  - `agent-local-rpc-cleanup.process.test.ts` fails on the merge base too: its background command hit the overall timeout at host load 40-58.
- Upgrade from the latest stable, in scratch (`env -i`, own HOME, state dir, config path and npm prefix; fresh `openclaw@2026.11.10` from `setup --baseline`; Gateway started and killed; `openclaw update --tag <package> --yes --no-restart --json`):

  | Target | Runs | Outcome | `openclaw doctor` step |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `main` `8bd18635` (full build, packed) | 3 | 2 rolled back (2026.11.10 restored); 1 passed, with a tracer attached | exit 1 after "Doctor complete." in the 2 failed runs |
  | this branch `099d54f3` (full build, packed) | 3 | 3/3 `ok`, `openclaw --version` = 2026.11.10 (099d54f) | completed/0, no teardown error |

- Local ClawSweeper on `099d54f3`: complete, patch correct, no findings.

Main's dependency check fails on an access-loss helper exported only for tests from its RPC module and an unregistered native tool-wording generator. The failures block the dependency gate even though both pieces are maintained.

## User Impact

Restores the dependency gate while preserving role-access behavior, existing regression coverage, and native tool wording. No user action or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the unchanged access-loss comparison into the existing operator-role policy owner, with the RPC handler and tests consuming it. Register the exact tool-wording generator path as a maintained Knip entrypoint; its generated catalog is consumed by `ToolOperationCatalog.swift`.

The permission-reader guard transfers the existing comparison reference from the RPC module to the policy owner (25 + 3 becomes 26 + 2). The combined allowance stays at 28; no new live permission read is added. The existing exact-count regression remains in force.

The change removes one line overall. It adds no dependency, production wrapper, or test case.

## Evidence

- [Main dependency failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46049728794/job/140678289563): unused `roleChangeLosesAccess` export and `scripts/tool-operations.ts` file.
- Reproduced both findings on unmodified `b607eb7b6915c6fa830e23768fc767bfbe0ce4b3` in isolated Linux. The patched `pnpm deadcode:report` and `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` pass.
- The unchanged comparison and role-write path passed 44 tests across the role policy, access-loss, self-lockout, and worker suites. The final source also passes both `users.list` role-source cases.
- Final-source Oxfmt, targeted Oxlint (zero warnings/errors), and Gateway root/method test typechecks pass. Native package-boundary declaration preparation succeeded. The tool-wording generator consistency check passed.
- The old permission-reader counts reproduce the boundary-lint failure; the transferred counts pass boundary lint and all 41 boundary-guard tests.
- Final committed-range review found no actionable issues; security review cleared.
- Proof used Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork on Linux. Broader PR CI remains pending.

prs.title: improve: shrink the database code loaded by the model catalog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The packaged model catalog worker imports a database reader that carried two extra copies of the entire shared SQLite schema. Each copy added 103,952 bytes of JavaScript source to the worker’s startup imports.

## User Impact

The worker’s local static imports are 207,871 bytes smaller. Operators keep the same database format, upgrade behavior and model catalog. The measurement covers packaged JavaScript bytes. Process RSS and the constrained Gateway memory limit remain unmeasured for this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared schema projection now compares the input with the canonical SQL once. Its cache and historical-table check reuse the result. This lets the bundler keep one shared SQL literal while preserving the distinction between the current layout and older layouts that omit optional tables.

## Evidence

- Two normal package builds on the same host and lockfile, from `cbfed7c16140` and the exact source change in `2ebc3b4e4bff`. The catalog worker’s 1,325 local static imports went from 9,894,540 to 9,686,669 bytes. The affected database chunk went from 214,035 to 6,164 bytes. The worker graph contains one copy of the canonical literal, down from three.
- Both packaged implementations produced identical SQL for 48 cases covering current and historical schemas and both projection flags, including repeated and interleaved calls. The schema generator’s 162 shared-state inputs, including all 28 runtime projections, had the same byte hashes on cold and warm calls.
- All 243 tests passed across the generated catalog equivalence, runtime compatibility, additive schema and upgrade replay suites.
- Local ClawSweeper 0.3.5 reviewed the full one-file range with no priority filter and reported zero findings. A second independent source and package check verified the remaining literal and chunk size.

Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547.

prs.title: fix(cron): filter completed silent cron-based heartbeat spans
prs.body:
Fixes #204878

## What Problem This Solves

In 2026.11.6+, completed silent main-session cron automations remain in subsequent model requests: the wake's `internal_system` / `cron_execution` provenance is not recognized by `isHeartbeatUserMessage()`, so the heartbeat span stays in the compiled model context and in every following provider request, growing context and input token consumption.

The first revision recognized cron provenance, but routed every cron wake through the legacy heartbeat scanner, which could remove turns that (a) had delivered a visible message via the modern `message` tool, or (b) were interrupted before their terminal acknowledgement. This revision narrows eligibility: a cron span is removed only when the run demonstrably finished quietly and delivered nothing visible.

## What Changed

- `isHeartbeatUserMessage()` recognizes cron-execution provenance (same as the first revision).
- `resolveHeartbeatArtifactSpanEnd()` now treats cron-execution spans separately from legacy heartbeat spans:
  - **Silent terminal ack required.** The terminal acknowledgement must be a real silent control token (`NO_REPLY` or `HEARTBEAT_OK` text). `display: false` alone is not sufficient — cron turns stamp every non-error assistant row invisible, so display-based silence would classify any final text as an ack.
  - **Delivered messages keep the span.** A span containing a delivered visible message stays in history: detected via the persisted delivery mirror (`openclawDeliveryMirror` kind `message-tool-source-reply` with `final: true`, through `readTerminalSourceReplyDeliveryMirror`) or a tool call to a messaging tool (`message`, `conversations_send`, `conversations_turn`).
  - **Interrupted runs keep the span.** Tool activity with no terminal ack, and any non-silent assistant output, keep the span (a quiet run that completed after tool activity with a final `NO_REPLY` is still removed).
- Legacy heartbeat spans (prompt text, retired `heartbeat_respond`) keep the historical scanner behavior exactly.

This is the "narrow quiet-outcome eligibility" from the review: omission requires an actual silent completion and no recorded delivery, using facts already present in the transcript rows.

## Evidence

`src/auto-reply/heartbeat-filter.test.ts`: **34/34 pass** on this head via the repo's vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run`). The `cron-execution heartbeat wakes` suite covers:

- the issue's source-level repro: cron wake + `NO_REPLY` ack filtered to `[]` (fails on main — both messages retained);
- **delivered message kept** (new, fails on the first revision `a6f6b2eb2`): wake + `message` tool call + result + `final: true` delivery mirror + `NO_REPLY` → kept in full;
- **interrupted run kept** (new, fails on `a6f6b2eb2`): wake + `exec` tool call + result, no ack → kept;
- **non-ack final text kept** (new, fails on `a6f6b2eb2`): `display: false` assistant text that is not a silent token → kept;
- quiet completion after tool activity removed: wake + `exec` + result + `NO_REPLY` → `[]`;
- visible text reply kept; external lookalike text without provenance kept.

Red→green verified on this sandbox: the three new keep-cases fail on the first revision head and pass here; `oxfmt --check` is clean on both changed files, and the dependent suites (`heartbeat.test.ts`, `heartbeat-filter.browser-import.test.ts`, `attempt.spawn-workspace.context-injection.test.ts`) all pass.

The Gateway/provider-path proof asked in the first review still needs an after-fix run against a live provider; I don't have provider keys in this environment. The span-eligibility findings themselves are covered by the unit suite above, which exercises the exact transcript shapes from the review.

prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck; the current-head Gateway run is under Real behavior proof below. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

### Real behavior proof

Current head `1bb85c8a42c`, built with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, port 28789, throwaway token). A command job (`openclaw cron add --command`, then `openclaw cron run`) printed one line per second for 20 s, including a synthetic token, a synthetic private key split across polls, and one stderr line. I polled `cron.liveOutput` with `openclaw gateway call`, sending back the returned `cursor` and `runAtMs` (trimmed):

```
11:22:28 cursor=0   -> active:true reset:true cursor:14  "line 1 stdout\n"
11:22:31 cursor=14  -> active:true cursor:56  "line 2 stdout\nline 3 stdout\nline 4 stdout\n"
11:22:34 cursor=56  -> active:true cursor:174 "line 5 stdout\napi token=sk-pro…7890 used\nline 6 stdout\nline 7 stdout\nwarn 7 on stderr\n"
11:22:37 cursor=174 -> active:true cursor:310 "line 8 stdout\nline 9 stdout\n-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…redacted…\n"
11:22:40 cursor=310 -> active:true cursor:381 "…redacted…-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\nline 13 stdout\n"
11:22:43 cursor=381 -> active:true cursor:426 "line 14 stdout\nline 15 stdout\nline 16 stdout\n"
11:22:46 cursor=426 -> active:true cursor:471 "line 17 stdout\nline 18 stdout\nline 19 stdout\n"
11:22:49 cursor=471 -> active:false cursor:0 ""   (run ended, buffer discarded)
```

Each poll returned only new complete lines, stderr arrived in order, the token and the private key (across polls) were masked, and `active` flipped to `false` when the run ended. `cron.runs` then recorded the finished run with its full, unchanged summary. Not re-run on this head: the Control UI panel (the screenshots above are from an earlier head).

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

**Agent:** Touched Gateway and UI live-output tests pass. Pushed as a merge commit, no force push.

prs.title: feat: review dictated paragraphs and lists before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #205634

Part of #205634

## What Problem This Solves

People dictating paragraphs or shopping lists into the Control UI currently receive a text transcript and must manually recreate its structure. Treating every occurrence of “bullet” or “new paragraph” as a command would also corrupt ordinary discussion, quotes, and code. This contribution adds an explicit, reviewable formatting path while retaining the current recognized-text behavior by default.

## User Impact

Users can opt into **Interpret explicit structure (English)** in the existing microphone controls. After Stop, they can compare semantic, plain, and original-text previews, confirm ambiguous paragraph commands, and apply an eligible result or copy it for recovery. Formatting never continues into Send. The draft remains editable in Explicit mode; editing it invalidates the captured insertion target instead of allowing an older result to overwrite it.

The initial grammar supports paragraphs, line breaks, ordered and unordered lists, and nesting up to the proposed depth of three. Explicit item numbers, order, quantities, negation, names, protected strings, and literal marker discussion stay source-backed. Headings, tables, inferred Suggest structure, attachments, spreadsheet operations, and document automation are outside this initial scope.

| Representation | Supported boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Plain text | An unchanged direct-dictation field whose actual capabilities support safe multiline text and an existing undoable adapter; otherwise review/copy. |
| Markdown (`commonmark-0.31.2-lists`) | The built-in Markdown composer with an empty draft or the entire captured draft selected. Partial insertion is refused because surrounding Markdown could reinterpret the result. |
| Rich preparation (`safe-blocks-v1`) | Allowlisted paragraph/list HTML and semantic preview only. **No native/external rich insertion adapter is qualified by this PR.** |
| Unknown, stale, or revoked capability | Readable review/copy recovery; no guessed target and no automatic fallback write. |

**This PR must remain a draft.** See Evidence for the checks that ran and the remaining qualification and maintainer decisions.

Rollback is the existing mode control: choose **Preserve recognized text**. Absence, malformed policies, unsupported versions, and Preserve normalize to the previous behavior. The version-1 Explicit opt-in is stored in the existing Gateway-scoped browser preference record; it is not synchronized through server `ui.prefs`. Disabling it preserves drafts, speech-provider selection, unrelated preferences, and message history.

## Why This Change Was Made

One bounded semantic document drives plain text, Markdown, and allowlisted HTML. Its validator checks source coverage and order, consumed-marker reasons, source/grapheme ranges, protected content, cycles, node kinds, and resource bounds before any representation is used. Markdown is checked with independent `markdown-it` parsing; rich output is checked with `parse5`. No generated HTML or remote resource is trusted, and spoken URLs are never fetched by formatting.

Live triage did not establish an accepted physical M11 parent to stack on. This PR therefore implements the minimal private lifecycle prerequisite in the **existing** dictation owner/session: immutable capture policy and source revision, generation and deadline eligibility, current target/selection/capability, cancellation, and truthful delivery receipts. It does not claim the wider M11 proposal is complete. Optional M01/M02/M03/M05/M08 integrations are not implemented as new renderer-local rewrites. The formatter adds no speech/model request, durable transcript store, clipboard manager, automation owner, or public RPC.

Related parallel proposals now published are [M01 punctuation #205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788) and [M02 cleanup #205789](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789). Both remain drafts; neither establishes an accepted M11 parent. Their shared owner/policy boundaries require consolidation and enabled-together proof before joint acceptance. This contribution does not claim that integration.

Preparation and insertion are separate. Main, Side chat, and New Session reuse their existing draft owners and editor history boundary. An attempted indivisible edit produces `not-committed`, `committed`, or `outcome-unknown`; uncertainty cannot trigger a plain-text retry. Rich preview success does not qualify an external rich editor. A proposed 2,500 ms Explicit finalization deadline cannot turn partial recognition into a complete formatted result.

The implementation is cohesive across recognition finalization, validation, preview, settings, and reviewed placement. A renderer-only slice would leave the required lifecycle and user recovery behavior unimplemented. The stateless helper extraction keeps lifecycle authority with the existing owner. Test growth is +2,842 LF lines against the integrated `main` base, with a 2,442-line allocation request above the 400-line default. Separate suites cover independent parser/source invariants, owner races, settings retention, real owner/adapter/component boundaries, submission guards, and the canonical browser fixture; the test file cap remains unchanged.

## Evidence

### Current draft head `473945834326cec0d52e42fa58b57d0f96927f6c`

**Fixed and verified:** At a 1200 × 820 viewport, the review panel could shrink the semantic preview to one line even though the remaining items existed in the DOM. Size the grid rows to their contents; the outer panel retains its existing scrolling. The bundled New Session regression failed before the CSS change and passed after it (12/12 bundled dictation tests on the same tree). Formatting, UI typecheck, i18n and the test-lines ratchet passed.

**Local exact-head production-path proof:** Chromium on Linux, built Control UI and production Gateway/Deepgram adapter, with a scripted loopback STT provider and an audio fixture. Chromium received the final segment at **4.479 s** and the terminal event at **4.977 s**; Explicit review opened **19.8 ms** after terminal. The 122 px preview fit both list items without internal scrolling. Apply preserved the surrounding draft; native Undo restored it. **Zero send RPCs.** This is not cloud STT, physical microphone, or upstream CI proof.

**Local paired Control UI budget passed** against `e769c8ba051b21832d54ae7249c816f496a897d9`: Chat boot gzip JS **−1,277 B**, New Session **−1,143 B**, CSS **−17 B** on each route; request counts unchanged. No threshold or baseline changes. The unpaired local hard-ceiling check is not green; the paired comparison accounts for the base. Hosted evidence below belongs to its historical head.

**General fork CI on the previous head** ([attempt 4](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46032873093/attempts/4)): `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` was already over allowance on the merged upstream input against the fork’s older base `514ee60d`; the feature passes against `e769c8ba`. The Mantis savings-label timeout (E2E shard 4) reproduced on both `e769c8ba` and `866b6bc`. E2E shards 6 (async-answer submit), 9 (routed-model attribution), and 12 (transcript-search reply reveal), and the separate CLI update-resume job have matching signatures on [an unrelated fork run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46032731733). [WebKit sidebar filter (1/3)](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46032873093/job/140656926971) is **unclassified**: Escape did not dismiss the 390 px LTR popover in that run, and the local environment could not launch WebKit for a controlled comparison.

#### Clean comparison

**Before** — `e769c8ba` Control UI, using the same scripted Gateway path: the spoken structure stays in the raw draft.

![Before: spoken structure commands remain plain text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b851f08e-f91e-4f8d-b791-67c64d1ed524)

**After** — `4739458`: both list items are visible in Explicit review before Apply.

![After: the semantic preview visibly contains the milk and eggs list items](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51f50451-2501-4bce-86c6-3de0441bec58)

#### Annotated comparison

![Before: highlighted raw dictation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fced85bb-9166-4424-b484-3c554834b3ab)

![After: highlighted shopping list with both items visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1abbc7fc-11af-4e6b-be77-abfd022a1105)

Same 1200 × 820 viewport, theme, and scripted audio fixture. Cropped to the composer; a local checkout label is masked in the baseline. Human microphone testing, feature-owner approval, and upstream workflow approval remain separate.

### Historical draft head `866b6bccabc4c565b33f6d5a579efb6ec3bd59ab`

**Exact-head evidence-only proof passed:** [scripted-audio job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/job/140655329025) · [proof bundle (GitHub sign-in may be required)](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/artifacts/15220374853). This head retains the four follow-up fixes and merges `main` at `e769c8ba051b21832d54ae7249c816f496a897d9`.

- **Revision 5 / P2 — wait for the streaming relay:** Explicit dictation no longer stops recognition at the former 2.5-second cutoff. The relay owns finalization, and the separate formatting budget is unchanged. The timed regression exercises a final segment at 4.5 seconds and a terminal close at five seconds.
- **Production-Gateway browser journey:** [`late-streaming-final--alloy`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/job/140655329025#step:16) passed. Provider final at **4.500 s** after Finalize; Chromium final at **4.497 s** and terminal close at **4.996 s** after audio commit; Explicit review opened **31 ms after close**. The preview contained both items, Apply inserted the formatted list, native Undo restored the draft, and the browser sent **zero** send RPCs. The WAV played through Chromium into the production Gateway relay with a scripted loopback Deepgram endpoint. This was not cloud STT or a physical microphone test.
- **Paired Control UI budget passed** against the merge parent `e769c8ba051b21832d54ae7249c816f496a897d9` in the [check step](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/job/140655329025#step:10), with no budget or baseline changes. The same job also passed the nine-file focused test selection, UI typecheck, i18n verification, test-lines ratchet, UI build, and 20 bundled browser tests.
- This is the evidence-only fork lane, not general fork or upstream CI. Upstream workflow approval and feature-owner approval remain separate maintainer decisions. Physical-microphone checks are not claimed.

### Historical draft head `aff75fc28ec3172eb3a4d779ffb0e46c420c3536`

Fast-forward update from the prior draft head. The `main` merge `93d1202c3145404053cfdb6df8dfbdb722752f86` has the prior head as its first parent and `6d2cb0379cb66e9fc25584f978b71750e29b916a` as its second. The published tree matches the locally checked candidate; the final lint correction changed only a picker test.

- **Unchanged paired budget against the merged base:** Chat startup JS gzip 1,336,724 → 1,336,079 B (−645 B, 21 requests on both); New Session 819,932 → 819,497 B (−435 B). Microphone-device discovery now loads when the picker opens, not at startup. No budget limits or baselines changed.
- **Production Gateway relay and Chromium:** Scripted loopback Deepgram sent the last segment at 4,501 ms after provider Finalize. Chromium received the last segment at 4,497 ms after the audio commit and terminal close at 4,995 ms; Explicit review opened after close and contained both list items. Enter did not submit during finalization; Apply succeeded and native Undo restored the draft. Zero send RPCs. This is not cloud STT or a physical microphone run. The initial Apply failure was missing fonts in the Chromium harness, not an invalid insertion target.
- Focused tests, 20 bundled Chromium cases, UI typecheck, i18n verification, targeted lint, and the unchanged test-line ratchet passed locally. The author’s fork proof is pending. No new hosted review has been requested, and the feature-owner decision is still required.

### Historical draft head `b682e77091c8be85cee269051ad6b828e4b2b2a0`

**Local product checks passed; OpenClaw-hosted execution is still pending.** Published by @roboclaw-bot without rewriting the existing branch. ## Problem
`main` fails two checks:
- `plugin-sdk:surface:check`: public exports 3932 > 3930, callable exports 2259 > 2258. #205963 added `AgentHarnessSideQuestionRequest` and #206839 added `hasReplyRestartResume` without budget lines.
- Dead-export scan: `buildRestartSentinelRow`, `nextRevision` and `readRestartSentinelRowForKeySync` in `src/infra/restart-sentinel-store.ts` have no outside readers after #206700.

## Change
- Make the three restart-sentinel helpers module-private. The read-worker test and the managed-handoff lifecycle fixture write their rows directly. The lifecycle test decodes the row and compares it with the payload, so a wrong column fails it.
- Record the two SDK exports in the budgets. Both have bundled consumers (copilot side questions, telegram restart recovery).

None. Behavior does not change. The diff touches only CI budgets, export visibility and one test fixture.

- `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`: exit 0.
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`: script, production and full-tree scans each report 0 entries.

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: clean.



**Note on the SDK export limit:** 3930 to 3932 public and 2258 to 2259 callable is public-surface growth, not a waiver. The two exports are used by bundled plugins (copilot, telegram), and the limit tracks the real public surface.

prs.title: ci: prune the provider-branching allowlist to main
prs.body:
## Problem

`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` fails on every PR merged with current main: `provider-branching` asks to shrink 3 allowlist entries. The allowlist from #206878 was taken at `ea77ca3d`. PRs merged later removed provider branches (#206735 deleted `openai-strict-tool-setting.ts`, and others touched `attempt-stream.ts` and `openai-tool-schema.ts`). The shrink-only ratchet fails when a file's count drops below its entry.

## Solution

`--prune` on current main `8a8e0177`:
- `src/agents/openai-strict-tool-setting.ts` 3 → removed (file deleted)
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream.ts` 2 → 1
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-tool-schema.ts` 1 → removed
- `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-compat.ts` 61 → 63: #206735 moved the strict-mode default from the deleted helper into the compat owner before the ratchet existed. This records main as it is; no branch is added here.

Net: 840 → 837 branches, 218 → 216 files.

## Impact

Contributors only. PRs are no longer red on `provider-branching` for branches that main already removed. There is no runtime change.

## Evidence

- Before: `check-provider-branching-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` on main `8a8e0177` lists the 3 shrink entries (the same list as the CI failure on #206948).
- After: `Provider branching ratchet OK: 216 files, 837 grandfathered branches.`

prs.title: feat: review finalized dictation before inserting it
prs.body:
Related: #205845

Part of #205845

## What Problem This Solves

Dictation users need a way to stop capture, inspect the completed transcription, and choose when it becomes editable draft text. Optional refinement needs one current-result lifecycle so a delayed transcription or cancelled rewrite cannot replace a newer draft.

This PR implements the private M11 coordinator and a working opt-in review path in the main Chat composer. **M11 is not fully qualified. This PR remains a draft and the tracking issue stays open.**

## User Impact

- Open **Dictation text options** in the main Chat composer and enable **Review dictated text before inserting**. The choice defaults off for each composer instance.
- Provisional captions stay separate from the editable draft. Stop releases capture through its existing owner and shows finishing while waiting for eligible final text.
- Inspect the candidate and original, then choose **Use reviewed text** or **Keep raw transcript**. Acceptance inserts once. Finishing a review-required recording does not send a message.
- Edits/replacement, including immediate edit followed by undo, new captures, owner/account/connection/target/locale changes, capability withdrawal and cancellation retire the old result.
- Incomplete captures remain manual recovery; oversized text is rejected visibly without clipping. New Session and Side chat do not advertise refinement because their insertion/submit contracts differ.

The browser uses conservative local text cleanup (outer whitespace only). Its UI says model-assisted refinement is unavailable in this build and distinguishes local text processing from the separately selected speech-recognition provider. There is no persistent configuration migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The neutral immutable request/plan/result owner is independently usable without M01–M10 feature stores. Optional handlers contribute authorized edits and combined model instructions; absent features are disabled capabilities or explicitly labelled conformance fixtures. Existing capture, provider/authentication, draft and delivery owners retain their responsibilities.

The core validates schema/revisions, half-open UTF-16 ranges at grapheme boundaries, protected bytes and opaque identities. Only outer whitespace changes are eligible for automatic semantic acceptance; uncertain material changes require review. One current operation, bounded snapshots/payload/output, and an absolute deadline constrain the lifecycle. Default ceilings are 32 KiB transcript/output, 8 KiB context and vocabulary each, 64 KiB combined payload, and 2,500 ms.

A real private selected-model adapter and optional measurement route reuse exact provider/model/profile, credential and transport ownership, disable failover, and permit one bounded streaming completion with cancellation and lease disposal. Logical adapter attempts are distinguished from observed HTTP requests.

Public request/RPC exposure, authoritative speech/refinement locality ownership, and admission-versus-revocation semantics still need maintainer acceptance in #205845. The automated issue review is not approval. The browser does not expose an unaccepted model route. Historical #187371 and other dictation drafts are not parents or accepted dependencies.

## Evidence

### Current fork proof — `1a1060d`

"$proof/venv/bin/pip" install vosk==0.3.45

ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -i "$proof/voice.wav" -af 'adelay=300,apad=pad_dur=1.5'   -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le "$proof/mic.wav"

parts = []

cat > "$proof/browser.cjs" <<'JS'
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const path = require('node:path');
const {chromium} = require(require.resolve('playwright', {paths:[process.cwd()]}));
const {PROOF, PORT, TOKEN, LABEL, ROUTE} = process.env;
(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({args:[

    const page = await browser.newPage({viewport:{width:1200,height:900}, permissions:['microphone'], locale:'en-US'});
    const calls = new Map(), routes = [], closes = [], requests = [];
    let sent = 0, done = 0;
    page.on('websocket', socket => {
      function parse(payload) { try {return JSON.parse(String(payload));} catch {return null;} }
      socket.on('framesent', ({payload}) => {
        const m = parse(payload); if (m?.type !== 'req') return;
        if (m.method === 'chat.send') sent++;
        if (m.method === 'talk.catalog') calls.set(m.id, m.method);
        if (m.method === 'talk.session.close' && !m.params?.discard) requests.push(Date.now());
      });
      socket.on('framereceived', ({payload}) => {
        const m = parse(payload);
        if (m?.type === 'res' && calls.delete(m.id) && m.ok) routes.push(m.payload?.transcription?.source);
        if (m?.event !== 'talk.event') return;

    const screenshot = stage => shell.screenshot({path:path.join(PROOF,'share',LABEL + '-' + stage + '.png')});
    if (LABEL !== 'before-file') {
      await mic.getByRole('button', {name:'Dictation text options', exact:true}).click();
      await review.getByRole('checkbox', {name:'Review dictated text before inserting'}).check();
    }
    async function start() {
      await mic.getByRole('button', {name:'Dictation',exact:true}).press('Enter');
      await shell.locator('.agent-chat__dictation-status [data-status="listening"]').waitFor();
    }
    await start();
    await page.waitForTimeout(4200); // fixture duration plus lead-in; let the WAV reach the provider
    await shell.getByRole('button', {name:stopName,exact:true}).click();
    if (LABEL === 'before-file') {
      await page.waitForFunction(() => /review the project plan today/i.test(document.querySelector('.agent-chat__composer-combobox textarea')?.value || ''));
      await screenshot('01-stop-auto-insert');
    } else {
      const preview = review.getByRole('textbox', {name:'Text preview'});
      await preview.waitFor({timeout:15000});
      const recognized = await preview.inputValue();
      assert.match(recognized, /review the project plan today/i);
      assert.equal(await draft.inputValue(), initial);
      assert.equal(sent, 0);
      await screenshot('01-stop-review');
      await review.getByRole('button', {name:'Use reviewed text',exact:true}).click();
      assert.ok((await draft.inputValue()).includes(recognized));
      assert.equal(sent, 0);
      await screenshot('02-explicit-insert-unsent');
      const inserted = await draft.inputValue();
      await start();
      await page.waitForTimeout(3500);
      await review.getByRole('button', {name:'Cancel text refinement',exact:true}).click();
      await page.waitForTimeout(6000);
      assert.equal(await preview.count(), 0);

    }
    assert.equal(sent,0);
    assert.ok(done > 0 && closes.some(e=>e.reason === 'completed'), 'missing terminal Gateway evidence');
    assert.ok(routes.some(s => ROUTE === 'file' ? s === 'media-understanding' : ['streaming','streaming-auto'].includes(s)), 'wrong Talk catalog route');

## What Problem This Solves

Detached requester expiry is tested twice against the same scope owner.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Requester expiry remains covered through the real hook runner; normalization, invalid lineage and concurrent-requester isolation checks remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the direct expiry case in favor of the stronger existing hook-runner case. That case verifies detached work loses requester authority after its handler returns, while another handler is still active.

## Evidence

- Disabling scope expiry makes both the original direct case and the hook-runner keeper fail.
- With the direct case removed, the same fault still fails the keeper. Restoring the owner passes all 5 remaining cases across the two suites (1.22 seconds wall time).
- Targeted format, lint, type and whitespace checks pass.
- Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: 18 lines and 1 duplicate case removed; no helper or assertion changes.
- Independent preservation review and exact-range local review found no actionable correctness or security issues.
- Native exact-head PR review passed both suites: 5 cases, no skips (2.03 seconds).

## CI Status

[CI run 46072078658](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46072078658) passed at the reviewed commit `fa2da9905e1f7f7626603faad5fc8adb71412880`. Native review passed all 5 cases across the reduced suite and its keeper. Native completed-hosted preparation passed without changing the commit.
