prs.title: feat: review exact developer syntax before inserting dictation
prs.body:
Related: #205848. Shared-contract proposal: #205845.

Part of #205848

## What Problem This Solves

Code/configuration dictation needs exact symbols, case, and whitespace. Prose insertion can trim meaningful whitespace or reinterpret command-looking drafts, while symbol words need explicit scope before becoming punctuation.

**Remain draft; keep #205848 open.** The merged head passed the paired UI startup budgets and exercised exact review and native undo in a built UI. The [placement and ownership decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205845) is still open.

## User Impact

Users can opt into English (en-US) Prose, Literal, or Developer modes with plain-code, JSON, TypeScript, or Python fragment profiles. Literal/Developer captures stop for exact preview, diagnostics, alternatives, character inspection, original recovery, preview undo, copying, or unsent insertion. Bytes already altered by recognition cannot be recovered.

The disabled, closed disclosure does not request the optional engine/profile/refinement/owner/target/panel implementation or review stylesheet. Opening it or restoring settings that require review loads them. Capture before readiness is declined before microphone/provider preparation; retry after loading. Load failure never falls through to raw insertion. Closing settings retains unfinished profile JSON and exports.

Insertion remains unsent, rejects stale destinations, and supports real native textarea undo. Unavailable editing APIs, CR/CRLF, and replacements leaving a nonempty wholly whitespace-only draft remain copy-only because existing owners cannot preserve those bytes. 

Browser/Gateway-scoped profiles are bounded data, excluded from server appearance sync. Authored JSON survives disable/re-enable and failed imports; retained future settings can be exported. This feature persists no dictated original/preview. The tested upgrade preserves existing preferences/navigation/exact drafts. **Old v2026.11.10 UI startup drops the new profile envelope**, even without manual preference changes. Disable/re-enable is the supported profile-preserving rollback; export profiles before binary downgrade. No second store or downgrade shim was added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit deterministic scopes distinguish commands from prose. A versioned profile supplies symbol/spelling/casing/spacing rules; the planner emits bounded exact edits, diagnostics, and protected ranges. Composition validates capture/generation/transcript/profile identity and UTF-16 ranges, with explicit offset conversion and grapheme checks.

Existing capture/session/FIFO owners retain microphone settlement and ordered delivery. Profile/destination admission stays synchronous before microphone work. The existing chat loading boundary defers optional code without another capture queue or authority. Exact insertion retains current input/history ownership and stale, permission, cancellation, and representability checks. Optional prose refinement sees only unprotected text; no M01–M05 model/context/vocabulary stage is enabled.

### Shared ownership and scope decisions

[M11 now has an actual draft implementation, #205973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973), observed at `7dab77ee268617d70ab5f035bb7864cc278aa327`. It remains open, draft, unmerged, and unaccepted as a shared contract. Its finality, target/context, policy/result states, and 32 KiB/256-edit bounds differ from M08's private 128 KiB/64-edit boundary. Its [unresolved final-drain P2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205973#issuecomment-7193928672) concerns a 2,500 ms review deadline versus the relay's 5,000 ms drain; this repair does not adopt that policy or coordinator.

[M07 draft](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/2) is a design reference only. M11 `authorizedEdits` integration remains a proposal; #205845 still needs human core/plugin, scope, profile/refinement ownership, and lifecycle decisions.

The full PR has **2,229 net test lines**: 400 normal + [1,829 allocated][test-allocation]; follow-up +532. All seven prior mounted capture cases retain their assertions in the focused review file. No dependency, second capture owner, public SDK, performance-baseline increase, or budget suppression. Final source/diff inventory: 25 follow-up files, +1,118/−406; full PR 49 files, +6,184/−289.

## Evidence

### Current head — `ab47497`

[`ab47497`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/ab47497e388a917fc1f8814879bd10c4ed40a1fa) is a direct child of `418fa41` and changes only `src/shared/dictation-refinement.ts`. It names the two local values as **dictation capture** generations. Exports, the `generation` fields, and strict stale-plan rejection are unchanged. The ratchet and allowlist were not edited.

**Verified:** The unchanged session-identity scanner rejected both `418fa41` and the old fork synthetic merge for `2 > 0` pins in this file, then passed for each tree with only this repair applied. The published tree matches that reviewed candidate. The one-file source review reported no findings; formatting and `git diff --check` passed. This was a static check, not an execution of the dictation tests or browser.

**Test-line comparison:** The unchanged guard passes the published tree against the PR’s upstream merge parent: +2,221 lines versus 1,829 allocation credit plus the 400-line allowance. Applying the current repair to the old fork synthetic tree instead yields +2,472 versus 1,834 plus 400 (238 over). That is a reconstruction of the older comparison, not the new hosted preflight. No allocation was raised.

**Pending:** [Fork CI on `ab47497`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46073735740) has no terminal result. The earlier `418fa41` fork CI was cancelled after this head superseded it. The scripted-audio runner was re-pinned to this head and syntax-checked with the unchanged scenario file; it has not run. The 9/9 live result below is still only for `878550b`. Current-head build/typecheck, browser layout and settings-menu behavior, before/after visuals, live transcription, and stable-to-head settings upgrade remain unverified. No ClawSweeper re-review has been requested on this head.

### Fork CI follow-up — `418fa41`

[`418fa41`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/418fa41d6cbe166f82bacec1687dafe8fea56b60) is an additive child of `878550b`. Dictation syntax settings now open from the composer’s **+** menu; the idle review takes no space in the composer. The patch also breaks two static import cycles and removes four redundant type assertions. The shared `dictation-refinement.ts` blob is identical to `878550b`; #206273’s planned use of its exports and behavior is unchanged.

**Verified on this head:** The published tree matches the reviewed candidate. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. A source-only TypeScript parse/import-graph check reproduced both cycles on `878550b` and found neither in the repair. The source-only review reported no P0 findings; it does not establish browser behavior. The full local UI compiler check could not complete. [Fork CI for the repair](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46073206493) has no completed result recorded here yet.

**Earlier fork CI:** [Run 46011764850](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46011764850) exposed the import cycles, type assertions, and a consistent 31–34 px boot-to-ready composer size change. Matching [upstream main failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46007024811) include the tool-surface policy tests, Doctor duplicate startup traces, protocol fixture missing `direct-run.mjs`, SQLite tooling fixture, and Madge self-test. Hosted CLI update-resume, routed-model author attribution, and async questions also reproduce [on main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46024795114). [Tooling shard 6](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46011764850/job/140656630377) is a separate fork-only fixture mismatch: the tooling donor keeps the upstream origin while the temporary checkout inherits the fork origin. A controlled read of the unchanged tooling loader admitted `openclaw/openclaw` and returned the exact `Different repository.` error for `CompleteDotTech/openclaw`, with otherwise identical fixture inputs. The settle timeout, side-chat typography, and footer/Mantis failures still have no independently matching control signature.

The [ratchet job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46011764850/job/140656613644) checked a synthetic merge against the fork’s older base. Relative to the PR merge parent, the patch’s original test-line delta fits its existing allocation plus the shared allowance; the synthetic merge included another 251 test lines and five lines of credit from upstream drift, and exceeded the check by 230. No budget was raised. The identity ratchet flags both sides of the same comparison of **dictation capture** generations; it is not a Gateway chat-session identity check. The comparison was retained unchanged so a stale capture plan cannot be applied to a new capture.

**Not yet verified on `418fa41`:** browser boot/layout (including phone and keyboard focus), the new settings entry point, exact-head live transcription, and a fresh stable-to-head settings upgrade. The 9/9 scripted result below remains evidence for `878550b`, not the new head. The [maintainer decision on feature placement and downgrade](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205845) remains open.

### Final scripted-audio proof — `878550b`

[Contributor-hosted Chromium/Gateway proof](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46012366465/job/140583446064) passed **9/9** on published head `878550be341eebac52bebec21bf76d83d118d915`. This is the publication commit above the merge of upstream `main` at `89425fd75d4e278b28c5a9b8def98fed0ef2831d`. The job used synthesized clips as Chromium microphone input and the real Gateway’s OpenAI transcription path. Its public log includes the per-take transcripts and results.

| Browser case | Transcription model | Alloy / Nova / Sage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact LF copy, then Cancel | `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | PASS / PASS / PASS |
| Identifier Insert, then native Undo | `whisper-1` | PASS / PASS / PASS |
| Incomplete command blocks insertion; Cancel preserves draft | `whisper-1` | PASS / PASS / PASS |

No physical microphone, broad upstream CI, or fresh stable-to-this-head upgrade is established by this run. Earlier results below remain tied to their recorded heads.

**Downstream stack:** [#206273 (voice snippets)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206273) will build on this PR’s [`src/shared/dictation-refinement.ts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/878550be341eebac52bebec21bf76d83d118d915/src/shared/dictation-refinement.ts), adding snippet-specific behavior in its own commits. This PR keeps the module’s exports and behavior unchanged by the base merge. The broader ownership and scope decision in #205845 remains open.

### After merging upstream `main` — `22347650b`

Published head: `22347650b31422c227b64e39d0ec0ad8a6c038dc`. Merge commit `15efb4524` combines the prior branch head with upstream `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa` without rewriting history. GitHub reports the draft mergeable, not ready to land. The resolution retains main’s background recording and explicit mouse/keyboard Stop, and keeps syntax capture admission synchronous before media setup.

- **Local checks on the published source tree:** 175 focused tests across eight files, three bundled Chromium scenarios with a mocked Gateway, UI typecheck, i18n verification, and focused lint/format passed. The scoped static review found no P0/P1 issue in the merge resolution.
- **Paired Control UI check:** Regenerated the boot manifest (unchanged output) and ran `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`. Limits are unchanged.

| Metric | Merged upstream base | Published tree | Limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total CSS gzip | 348,614 B | **348,603 B** | 348,683 B |
| Chat startup JS gzip | 1,336,502 B | **1,336,207 B** | 1,336,272 B |
| Chat startup CSS requests | 3 | **3** | 3 |
| Chat startup JS requests | 21 | **21** | 20 |

The paired check accepts the inherited, unchanged 21st request.

- **Hosted CI for this head:** The [contributor-fork attempt](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45876281890) produced no build or test evidence and is not being used for validation. The [upstream checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205892/checks) include PR metadata/governance and security reporting, not a completed candidate build/test run. No OpenClaw-hosted exact-head build, test, or real-Gateway proof is claimed.

- **Built Control UI + real Gateway and local Vosk on the merged source:** Chromium 158 used fake-media input from a prerecorded WAV with a bounded English vocabulary. Stop showed the exact `hello_world` preview without changing the draft. Preview Undo restored recognized prose. A second recording inserted only `hello_world` without sending; native Ctrl+Z restored the original draft. With review disabled, the loaded chat documents requested no optional syntax assets. The insertion and Ctrl+Z screenshots were byte-identical to the retained captures and reuse their links. No physical microphone or cloud provider was used.

**Before — OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (retained capture): Stop inserts prose into the unsent draft**

![The released composer shows recognized words in the unsent draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dae54db-be5c-4ddc-b2da-8b934294dbea)

**After — merged Control UI `22347650b`: Stop opens exact review while the draft is unchanged**

![The unchanged composer shows the recognized original and a separate hello_world preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/370e61db-23f5-4af8-b506-edce0400cd55)

**Annotated before and after**

![Before: recognized words enter the draft as prose](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26a75bcb-e2c2-4c81-a3cd-5071f6e23e54)

![After: the exact preview appears before insertion](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a7697dc-7dce-4ac7-a937-36087514d24a)

prs.title: fix(talk): explain why an interrupted xAI call cannot resume
prs.body:
Fixes #206569

## What Problem This Solves

When a ready xAI realtime socket drops with the default resumption setting, Talk ends without explaining why it cannot reconnect. The client receives only a generic close error.

## User Impact

Talk receives an actionable explanation before closing. Users can start a new call, or opt into the existing `sessionResumption` setting if provider-side conversation retention is acceptable. Reconnection defaults and retention policy do not change. Opaque routes still receive only a generic public error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway relay already receives a reconnect-blocked event but discards it. Project that event into the existing public error channel. Only a recognized local reason is translated; raw provider diagnostics are never forwarded. Preserve an earlier provider error rather than replacing it. The fix adds no configuration, retries, or new state owner.

## Evidence

- Base: `fde2c6cb4d69848b74fa7aa081a6235d3afaeb4b`, freshly fetched upstream main.
- Before production edits, two regressions failed with `["close"]` instead of `["error", "close"]`. They exercise the real bundled xAI provider bridge and Gateway relay owner with isolated database state and a loopback WebSocket server. The simulated provider acknowledges `session.update` with `session.updated`, then terminates its ready socket without sending an error frame. The cases cover normal and opaque routes.
- After the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/index.test.ts src/gateway/talk/relay/xai-interruption.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/talk/gateway-relay.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **164 tests passed**, including both regressions. Total wrapper wall time 88.56 seconds, including compiler preparation; the new cases took 2.856 seconds and 0.109 seconds. CI seconds unavailable.
- Targeted format, oxlint, `git diff --check`, and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json --incremental` passed. A final test-only lint correction made the Promise executor explicitly void; no behavior changed.
- Local autoreview of the three-file change: no findings at its default P0 scope. Simplification retained the existing event/error owners; production delta +17/-1 lines, tests +95 lines.
- **Proof still owed by @anmol0b:** a real xAI socket-drop run through an isolated Gateway and Talk client, including before/after error-state capture. No provider key was available here. Full Gateway RPC-server/browser end-to-end, native-device, screenshot and hosted CI proof were not run.
- Keep this PR a draft. No ClawSweeper review is requested until the outstanding proof is posted.

Co-authored with @anmol0b.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/28aa0084-d3fb-4c42-9d24-af2fc4856619)

## Worked on by

- @anmol0b

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep saved models on read-only Codex provider routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An upgrade can silently change a saved conversation’s model. With `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1`, Doctor leaves the provider catalog in place but can rename `codex` to `openai` in the session database. The saved choice then points to a route the catalog never offered. The next turn can use the default instead.

## User Impact

An externally managed installation keeps the user’s selection while its configuration still declares that provider. Removing the provider from the configuration allows the normal migration on a later repair. This change can’t recover a selection that has already been cleared.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Doctor’s existing migration exclusions for provider names retained in read-only configuration. Mutable configurations and unconfigured legacy aliases keep their existing behavior. No schema or new setting is needed.

## Evidence

- The SQLite regression failed on `5e245aa0` and passed with this patch. It checks both provider/model pairs, the user selection and migration of the other, unconfigured alias.
- All 12 tests passed in `provider-rename-state.test.ts`, `codex-route-session-repair.test.ts` and `doctor-health.readonly-config.test.ts`. The cold `pnpm test` run took 212 seconds with one worker. Formatting and type-aware lint passed.

### Upgrade and fresh install

I built the [v2026.11.10 release tag](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.10) at `6ea542fd` and this PR at `301ce545`. Both source trees were unchanged. I used cached dependencies, including fs-safe 0.27.1, and the same external Codex 0.164.0 app-server binary with scripted Responses. The PR lockfile calls for fs-safe 0.28.2. This was a source-built upgrade. The published npm package was unavailable on the test runner.

I created two chats on the first build, selected a non-default model for one through `sessions.patch`, and sent one turn to each. I stopped both processes, left the config and SQLite files in place and ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` from the PR with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1`. After relaunch, each chat used its original Gateway ID and recalled its own earlier answer. Both native thread IDs changed across the upgrade. This check covers saved model selection and chat history. Worker ownership needs separate verification. The fresh-install control started in an empty directory with the PR build and followed the same steps.

Redacted terminal output from the test verifier follows. Schema pairs are shared state and Agent state. Each saved tuple records provider, model and selection source. The four Responses requests are the default chat and selected chat before Doctor, then the selected chat and default chat after Doctor. Model names are replaced by their roles. Each request matched the native model and exactly one saved reply.

```json
{"case":"upgrade","builds":["6ea542fd","301ce545"],"doctorExit":0,"schema":[[40,42],[42,45]],"configSame":true,"saved":[["codex","selected","user"],["codex","selected","user"]],"requests":["default","selected","selected","default"],"http":[200,200,200,200],"sameChats":true,"nativeThreadsPerChat":[2,2],"priorAnswersRecalled":[true,true]}
{"case":"fresh","builds":["301ce545","301ce545"],"doctorExit":0,"schema":[[42,45],[42,45]],"configSame":true,"saved":[["codex","selected","user"],["codex","selected","user"]],"requests":["default","selected","selected","default"],"http":[200,200,200,200],"sameChats":true,"nativeThreadsPerChat":[1,1],"priorAnswersRecalled":[true,true]}
```

The separate failing comparison used an older Gateway at `82b682c6` and a candidate at `5e245aa0` with #193024, #205298, #206231 and #206529. The two builds above omit those auxiliary patches. Please review the saved-session migration before merging.

prs.title: feat(dictation): propose personal vocabulary groundwork
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205856.

Part of #205856

Personal spellings need an explicit lifecycle: authenticated storage, deliberate learning, accessible editing, stable identity, bounded per-turn hints, import/export, conflicts, deletion, and recovery. Existing provider hints in #191109 do not supply that lifecycle.

**This is an incomplete design-review draft. P03 is not implemented in full, every complete AC01–AC12 remains unmet, and #205856 must stay open.** This PR preserves reviewed private groundwork while the required storage and public-contract design decisions remain outstanding.

## User Impact

This candidate does not activate a dictionary editor, durable entries, correction learning, or provider dispatch. Its reusable preparation work preserves exact canonical text, produces immutable bounded personal snapshots, previews explicit imports and existing Deepgram keyterm strings, and prepares canonical hint data for a future admitted caller.

No user-data migration is activated. Reverting these private modules and their benchmark removes the proposal; there is no new stored user data to transform. The eventual feature still needs disabled-mode retention, upgrade/downgrade, scoped recovery/export, and rollback proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current authenticated preferences are owned by `users.prefs` and worker-backed state. Their 4 KiB value, 32-entry mutation, and 128-key profile limits do not directly accommodate the proposed 1,000-entry dictionary. Sharding or silently adding a namespace would still change persistence and lifecycle semantics.

The [storage review checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1c3de7eb68481e5d7656e21ec96d43855789fbb0/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes) requires accepted design before material persistence or public-contract changes. The [automated issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205856#issuecomment-7186791734) also requests a coordinated owner, minimum client flow, and vocabulary contract with M06. That review is advisory, not maintainer acceptance. No accepting maintainer decision was found.

The implementation therefore prepares these private boundaries:

- One shared validator preserves canonical Unicode/case/punctuation and uses NFC only for comparisons. The existing M06 locale normalizer and bounded JSON parser are reused.
- Personal snapshots carry copied profile/workspace identity, a pinned revision, deterministic locale-aware selection, a 64-entry bound, and private omission explanations. Supplied scope IDs are isolation metadata, not authorization.
- Import previews attribute invalid rows, duplicates, and ID/canonical conflicts. Every row requires an explicit decision; replacement preserves an existing stable ID and must target a previewed match. Resolution returns a complete proposed term set and expected revision; it performs no CAS or durable write.
- Export projects personal term fields only. The proposed schema and entire envelope are bounded; unknown versions remain errors. Explicit Deepgram strings can be previewed without discovering or rewriting configuration.
- Hint preparation distinguishes term lists, encoded prompts, unavailable capabilities, and unsupported pronunciation. Adapter-owned exact measurement bounds the actual fixture representation. A local-only/remote projection stops preparation before measuring private strings; this is not real egress enforcement.
- Aliases remain candidates. Ambiguous hints are omitted rather than used as unconditional transcript replacements. Numeric summaries exclude term text, scope identifiers, and hashes.

### Reused source and semantic dependencies

The branch now merges `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `47027a257c728b267390eaac72147eaea55f0283`, without rewriting fork history. No sibling transport change is a branch dependency. Current OpenAI transcription prompt and Deepgram batch keyterm transport already exist; this draft does not advertise another endpoint or unverified Google Live fields.

Three foundation files originate from M06 commit `4780aeb034e72a6557f12a54ed506d5e4c690d98`: `vocabulary-types.ts`, `vocabulary-terms.ts`, and `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`. The draft retains the types these helpers use and removes unused shared authority declarations. It exposes the shared comparison/locale helpers, extracts bounded JSON parsing, and fixes canonical precedence before alias conflict indexing. No M06 persistence or lease layer is imported. M06 #205820 was rechecked open/unmerged at `56aef23a43aea74de1f20ed6e1cf81cc3c1756a5`.

P02 remains a sibling, not a dependency. M11 #205845 would consume typed vocabulary; M06 #205633 later owns the authorized shared overlay. None of those proposals establishes an accepted P03 store or provider contract.

The author simplification pass retained one validator/parser/resolver owner and no second store, context collector, or provider constructor. The separable first foundation is the shared validation/resolution source; personal consumers follow it. These helpers have no production caller; this is not a complete feature.

## Evidence

### Published draft at `bf530fa3f500bbf3146d021f8731a1c782ed448c`

- **Branch refresh.** @CompleteDotTech merged upstream `main` at `c7ea9f418610b2d5d336d0df191c8e4660202efb` into the fork branch. The PR remains draft. `git diff --check` passed against that merge parent.
- **PASS — canonical suites and core typecheck.** The contributor’s [#205880 proof job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/job/140655328799) pinned this exact head. It ran `personal-vocabulary-import.test.ts`, `personal-vocabulary.test.ts`, and `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`: **3/3 files, 56/56 tests**. `pnpm run tsgo:core` also passed. The parent matrix includes unrelated PR jobs; this result is for #205880 only.
- **PASS — scripted dictation compatibility, 6/6 on the same head.** `single-utterance` and `two-utterances` passed **3/3 each** (alloy, nova, sage). Chromium replayed synthetic WAVs as microphone input; the Gateway used live OpenAI transcription; **Stop and keep text** left an editable, unsent Control UI draft. The [per-take artifact](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/artifacts/15220864021) is in the fork run. This exercises the existing dictation path, not production personal vocabulary: the draft has no production caller. It does not establish recognition gains, real-mic behavior, accessibility, or persistence/recovery.
- **Physical microphone — still to do by @CompleteDotTech.** Check real microphone permission, device selection/switching, and real speech through **Stop and keep text** to an editable, unsent draft.
- **CI is separate.** [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46032399561) awaits maintainer approval. The separate [fork CI run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46032401007/attempts/4) is not green; the passing proof job is not a substitute for either CI gate.
- **Runner handoff.** [Exact commands and artifacts to capture](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/bf530fa3f500bbf3146d021f8731a1c782ed448c/docs/experiments/personal-dictation-vocabulary.md#local-proof-handoff). The three canonical test files are new; their absence on base is not a red assertion.
- **Remaining design and production proof.** Maintainers still need to decide the scope, including the minimum accessible editor-to-dictation flow, authenticated storage and revisions, egress, and the shared contract with #205820. To prove personal vocabulary, save or select a synthetic term through the shipped editor, dictate through the normal composer, show that the intended provider received the term, and verify the editable draft. A future shared relay caller in #205820 would prove the shared-vocabulary flow, not the personal one.
- **Prior review.** The [last ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205880#issuecomment-7188365505) covered `e3a1b8ddfb649f2ccdb314c00e7ffc736d524eee`, not this head.

### Earlier evidence (not current-head checks)

- On `34eb161f573465301820e44a42d0e1c215a3e79d`, the [pre-refresh fork job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45944789015/job/140327144486) also passed all 56 tests, `tsgo:core`, and 6/6 scripted takes. The [earlier audio-only run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45938967474/job/140308968609) passed 6/6 but did not run the tests or typecheck.
- At the prior refresh, pinned oxfmt, `bash -n` on the handoff block, and the staged test-line ratchet passed. Auto Review reported `scoped-clean` through P2 after the type-only fix; a synthetic probe reproduced `TS2339` with the old discriminant and compiled with the split discriminant. These were scoped checks, not an upstream CI result.
- The benchmark below is from reviewed head `9b8bba978eabe63170081bd5161c3f08b59d62cf`, against implementation base `1c3de7eb68481e5d7656e21ec96d43855789fbb0`. Earlier canonical attempts did not reach test cases. At the subsequent docs-only head `158d1928c28b71608e0a0a7add08bb996fc1daa3`, Crabbox authentication failed before a lease started and [GitHub CI reported `action_required`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45858501294). These attempts establish neither a pass nor an assertion failure.

### Measured preparation only

Reviewed-head run (`9b8bba978eab`): 2026-11-26T09:20:08.504Z; AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor; Linux 6.18.57 x64; Node 24.22.3 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.63. Nine logical CPUs are visible; affinity provides one available CPU. Load averages before/after were 0.16 / 0.37 / 0.79.

The deterministic fixture has 1,000 entries, 950 enabled, 334 aliases, and 200 entries for each neutral/en/en-US/es-ES/fr-FR locale category. Selection uses en-US. Terms serialize to 106,733 bytes. Quotas are fixture limits: 64 terms, 8,192 JSON bytes, 512 synthetic token units, one unit per term.

One first call, 25 warmups, then 200 serial samples; nearest-rank percentiles. Imports, admission validation, persistence, authentication, microphone, network, and actual provider tokenization are excluded.

| Stage | First call ms | Warm p50 ms | Warm p95 ms | Warm p99 ms | Warm max ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Snapshot | 8.625574 | 1.250781 | 1.635430 | 5.551681 | 7.497758 |
| Snapshot plus hint preparation | 8.975661 | 1.275168 | 1.756432 | 5.574776 | 7.523106 |

Both outputs retained 64 terms. Hints used 1,089 JSON bytes and 64 synthetic units. Omission counts were 50 disabled, 350 locale-ineligible, and 536 beyond the snapshot bound; 22 selected entries had unrepresented aliases. The proposed warm snapshot p95 below 50 ms was observed on this host only. This is not speech-quality, real provider quota, cold-process, or full dictation latency evidence.

The [committed experiment record](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/9b8bba978eabe63170081bd5161c3f08b59d62cf/docs/experiments/personal-dictation-vocabulary.md) retains an earlier measured run at `46c74099c7360a4f8ecbfc556df9ba5cfa936903`; the reviewed-head rerun above is separate.

### Complete P03 acceptance ledger

Every full criterion is **unmet**.

| Criterion | Current preparation and remaining requirement |
| --- | --- |
| AC01 — atomic CRUD and exact identity | Validation and proposed stable-ID replacement only. Canonical unit tests pass; durable add/edit/disable/delete, atomicity and revision checks remain unproven. |
| AC02 — explicit correction learning | Confirmation, locale/scope display, and proof that normal edits create no entry absent. |
| AC03 — bounded scoped snapshots | Pure deterministic snapshot code and measured workload present. Canonical unit tests pass; authenticated account/workspace isolation and capture integration remain unproven. |
| AC04 — supported hints | Pure representation/budget preparation present. Real adapter payloads, unsupported-field handling and endpoint qualification absent. |
| AC05 — ambiguity | Candidate conflict logic present. Canonical unit tests pass; no-dictionary/helpful/misleading recognition comparison remains unproven. |
| AC06 — strings are data | Data-only encoding and schema tests authored. Actual STT/refinement route/tool isolation proof absent. |
| AC07 — concurrent edits/import | Preview, explicit choices and proposed replacement present. Two-window conflict UI, actual CAS and atomic durable import/recovery absent. |
| AC08 — future exclusion | Pure snapshot inputs can omit disabled/deleted entries. Durable changes followed by actual capture proof absent. |
| AC09 — revision-pinned retry | Immutable value reuse modeled. Real capture/edit/retry and disclosed reprocess flow absent. |
| AC10 — selected egress | Pure local-only projection present. Actual destination observation through STT, refinement, retry and diagnostics absent. |
| AC11 — private diagnostics | Numeric summary/error boundary present. Default logs, crashes, telemetry and correction privacy qualification absent. |
| AC12 — migration/recovery | Proposed versioned scoped export/preview present. Accepted storage, upgrade/downgrade, unknown-schema recovery, disablement and rollback absent. |

The supplied archive-level `IMPLEMENTATION_WORKFLOW.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `STACKING_PLAN.md`, `VALIDATION_PLAN.md`, and `references/upstream-snapshot.json` were not supplied or found in bounded searches. The three attached P03 files were read; missing specifications are not treated as accepted contracts.

**Remain draft:** obtain maintainer acceptance of storage, authenticated scope/revisions, minimum accessible client flow, shared vocabulary/provider contract and egress ownership; finish the full lifecycle; then complete production integration, recognition, accessibility, migration, build and required upstream CI proof. No issue closure or upstream merge is requested.

Contributor: @CompleteDotTech

prs.title: fix: stop sandboxed file reads from crashing when a parent directory is missing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Debian/Ubuntu-based sandbox containers (where `/bin/sh` is `dash`), an agent reading or checking a file whose parent directory does not exist gets an internal shell error instead of the normal "file not found" result. This breaks optional-read and path-fallback handling that depends on a clean not-found signal.

## User Impact

Reading or checking a path inside a sandboxed agent run now returns a normal "not found" result when the parent directory is missing, matching the existing behavior for a missing file itself. No action required. Behavior for an existing-parent/missing-file, a real existing file, and a permission-denied parent is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`SandboxFsBridgeImpl.stat()` already classifies "not found" by matching GNU `stat`'s own locale-pinned error text for a missing basename. The fix stats the parent directory with that same GNU `stat` binary before `cd`-ing into it, so a missing parent is classified through the exact same, already-trusted check instead of leaking `cd`'s own shell-dependent failure text (dash says `can't cd to <dir>`, with no "No such file or directory", unlike bash) as an uncaught error. This avoids adding a second, weaker heuristic (such as matching `can't cd to`) that would also swallow genuine permission-denied failures, which must keep throwing.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the exact reported error against the real `/bin/dash` binary and a real GNU `stat` (via a local `coreutils` install, since macOS's default `stat` does not support `-c`): the pre-fix script fails with `cd: can't cd to <dir>` (exit 2) for a missing parent; the fixed script instead produces `stat: cannot stat '<dir>': No such file or directory` (exit 1), which the existing classification already treats as "not found."
- Also verified unchanged: a missing basename with an existing parent, a real existing file, and a permission-denied parent (`chmod 000`) -- the permission-denied case still throws rather than being silently treated as "not found."
- Added a focused regression test asserting the dispatched script now stats the parent before `cd`-ing (`src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts`).
- `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.boundary.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.mounts.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-mutation-helper.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 47 passed, 10 skipped (Docker-backed e2e tests, not run in this environment).
- `pnpm format:check`, oxlint, and `pnpm tsgo:core` on the touched files: clean.

Closes #185552

prs.title: feat: let clients load agent rosters without portraits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large inline portraits can dominate `agents.list` responses and delay mobile clients that need the agent roster before opening a conversation.

## User Impact

Clients can request a fresh authorized roster without downloading portraits by sending `includeAvatars: false`. Existing clients keep the same response when they omit the option or pass `true`.

This is opt-in: clients must request the lightweight roster. It does not change portrait caching policy, authorization, or the default avatar representation, and it has not been deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing roster projection now skips avatar resolution and omits `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` on explicit opt-out. Names, emoji, theme, routing and model metadata remain intact. This removes image work from roster bootstrap without introducing a server cache or a second roster endpoint.

The schema, generated validator, and protocol documentation are updated. Older gateways can reject the new parameter; clients may retry the legacy request only for that parameter-validation error.

## Evidence

- Five new regression cases exercise the real RPC handler, validator, authorization, and roster projection for local, inline-data and remote portraits, plus Control UI HTTP avatar representations. They fail against the base with `INVALID_REQUEST` and pass with this change.
- Lightweight requests make zero avatar-resolver calls, omit both image fields, and preserve the rest of the authorized roster. Legacy and explicit-true responses match. A synthetic 32 KiB local image loses its image payload from the serialized response.
- 14 focused tests pass: five new roster cases, five existing roster authorization cases, and four existing avatar cases.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Protocol schema generation, Swift/Kotlin native protocol generation, and generated validator freshness checks pass.
- Local canonical autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) completed on the full working-tree change against `6bd45e1ba9820b30300db404037bc5aa76648c02`, with the affected production owners supplied as source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review was static; it did not execute project code.

Not verified: end-to-end mobile latency or live gateway deployment. The tests establish work and payload removal, not a measured network speedup.

### Running-Gateway transport and latest-stable compatibility proof

Verified on reviewed head `0329434db09ac58286eca3ddf400f39addcf563e` using isolated synthetic state and real authenticated loopback WebSocket connections. Started the official latest-stable `openclaw@2026.10.8` package (`dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`), captured legacy requests, stopped it, ran the reviewed runtime's ordinary backed-up `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` migration, and started the reviewed Gateway against the same state.

- Configured valid local PNG, inline data-URI, and public-placeholder remote portraits.
- Stable `{}` response: 200,220-byte payload. Stable rejects the new option with `INVALID_REQUEST: unexpected property 'includeAvatars'`.
- After upgrade, `{}` is deep-equal to the entire stable legacy payload. `{includeAvatars:true}` is also deep-equal to `{}`.
- `{includeAvatars:false}` returns 2,517 bytes, deep-equal to the legacy payload with only `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` removed from each agent. All non-portrait fields are preserved.

prs.title: fix: stop recopying sandbox skills after idle periods
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In sandboxed sessions, the Gateway copies the session's skills into the sandbox before each message. A safety refresh runs every 30 minutes to catch file changes that the file watcher missed. Each refresh marked every skill file as changed, even when nothing had changed. So after a pause of 30 minutes or more, the next message recopied every skill tree before it reached the model.

Signal from a production deployment (48 h, read-only): the skills copy ran on 81% of sandboxed sends (p50 370 ms, p90 1.17 s). It scales with the time since the session's previous send: 6% under 60 s, 29% under 5 min, 69% under 30 min, 98% after 30 min or more.

## User Impact

Sandboxed chats no longer pay a full skills recopy on the first message after an idle period. When a skill file really changes, including an edit that the watcher missed, the next message still copies the new bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The safety refresh stays: it is the recovery path for missed watch events. The discovery scan now records a content digest of each skill tree that the sandbox copy reads. The digest uses the same selection as `copySkillTree`: bytes and mode of each file, directory modes and symlink targets, without `.git` or `node_modules`. It never uses timestamps. The refresh owner (`src/skills/runtime/refresh.ts`) marks the copies stale only when that digest differs from the source's previous one. It also marks them stale when a tree cannot be read; a read failure never fails the scan. A tree shared by several sources is hashed once per pass.

Accepted edge case: a source registered with `watch: false` gets no safety passes, so another source's pass no longer invalidates copies on its behalf. Previously this happened only by accident.

Not in this PR: other sources of version bumps (`remote-node` changes are global, and the first scan of a new source key marks). The post-deploy share of `copy_tree` will show how much remains.

## Evidence

- Deterministic test, red on main and green on this branch: `src/skills/runtime/discovery.integration.test.ts`, "recopies sandbox skill files after a safety pass only when their bytes changed". Native watch events are silenced. A safety pass with no edit keeps the synced copy (main: copy reconciled, marker removed). A same-size out-of-band edit followed by a safety pass copies the new bytes.
- `waitForLiveWatch` now waits for the workspace's passive scan pass instead of a resource revision, because a marker that changes no synced skill bytes no longer publishes one.
- Focused suites: `discovery.integration`, `discovery.worker`, `workspace-skill-sync.runtime`, `workspace-skill-sync-files`, `session-snapshot-content`, `workspace-skill-loader`. On the development host, two native-watch tests ("observes edits inside an admitted external symlink target" and, intermittently, "discovers external edits…") time out on both main and this branch: Node `fs.watch` delivered no callbacks on that host, even in a standalone control. CI on Linux is the proof for them.
- Adversarial design review: the findings were read errors failing the scan and no per-pass sharing. Both are addressed.

prs.title: fix(agents): record the tool name of a degenerate-output abort
prs.body:
## Problem

When the stream owner stops a tool-call argument stream at the 4 KiB consecutive-whitespace limit, the aborted assistant message keeps no partial tool call (`removeNonExecutableToolCalls`), so nothing records which tool ran away. Production evidence (7 days, one team Gateway): 355 such aborts in 196 sessions; the tool could only be inferred from the model's next message, and a replay cannot resolve a ~0.19%-per-call rate.

## Solution

At the existing abort in `packages/agent-core/src/agent-stream-response.ts`, the terminal message gets one `AssistantMessage.diagnostics` entry: `{ type: "degenerate_output", details: { toolName } }`. No argument content, no request body. The field already exists and is persisted with the transcript message; the Gateway chat display projection already strips it, so nothing changes for users.

The decision record also asked for the whitespace run length. It was cut on review: the guard trips at 4 KiB, so the value is always 4,096 plus at most one provider chunk and carries no information.

## Impact

- Users: no visible change; the abort, its message and its retry are unchanged.
- Operators: the next runaway is attributable from the transcript row without inference.

## Evidence

- `agent-loop.degenerate-output.test.ts` (real HTTP, Chat Completions transport): asserts the diagnostic with the tool name and that the argument text is absent. Red on `main`, green here.
- Real `agent --local` from a dist build against a fake Responses endpoint streaming a whitespace runaway in an `exec` call: the persisted transcript row carries `diagnostics: [{ type: "degenerate_output", details: { toolName: "exec" } }]` and the argument marker text is not persisted. Run on this head (`2cdaa493`).
- Adversarial design review: no reader matches the new diagnostic type; every `finalizeAssistantMessage` path keeps it.

prs.title: improve: simplify the automation editor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When creating an automation, Advanced settings exposes a raw routing field and lets you save a job that never starts or keep a one-time job around after it has succeeded. The editor also shows a second copy of the prompt you just typed.

## User Impact

New automations start active, and new one-time automations use the Gateway’s existing cleanup default after a successful run. The create and edit forms no longer show **Session key**, **Turn on after creating**, **Delete after it runs**, or the duplicate **Prompt preview**. You can still choose **Runs in**, read the saved prompt, and pause or resume an automation after creating it.

Existing automations are not migrated, rewritten, or deleted by this change. Saving an unrelated edit leaves the job’s existing routing, pause state, and cleanup policy alone. The Gateway API and CLI are unchanged. A duplicate retains its source’s routing, paused or active state, and keep-after-run setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor now relies on the Gateway’s defaults instead of maintaining its own. The revamp had kept the editor’s Markdown **Prompt preview** under Advanced → Task; this removes that duplicate, not the saved prompt shown outside the editor.

The rebase retains main’s current schedule controls and model pickers. Model-agent resolution now reads the saved job’s routing instead of the removed form field. This PR does not change the backend or job migrations.

## Evidence

- I verified [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/attempts/2) succeeded on `6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67`, including the typechecks, UI shards, bundled UI E2E, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The original UI failure was the unchanged model-setup wizard timing assertion; [checks-ui (3/3) passed on rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172498438).
- I inspected the final-head logs: [38 cron controller tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499534), including preservation of a paused one-time duplicate with `deleteAfterRun=false`; [27 save/reopen tests passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499774), exercising the real normalization, patch, and public read-projection owners in process. The [built-editor create flow passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45893648192/job/140172499864) against a mocked Gateway.
- **Stored data and updates:** I inspected the complete diff: only `ui/` files change. The removed fields belong to transient `CronFormState`, not the persisted job schema. [Edits omit hidden fields and duplicates copy their saved values](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67/ui/src/lib/cron/index.ts#L249-L305); the [unchanged Gateway patch owner preserves omitted values](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c79ecde79453c5c6118e08a364b207478762b67/src/cron/service/jobs.ts#L295-L348). There is no storage-format change, migration, install-time rewrite, or updater change. New jobs use the Gateway's existing activation and one-time cleanup defaults. I found no source basis for the older review's stored-data incompatibility warning, so this diff does not trigger the 9.x/10.x update-proof requirement.
- **Other proof limits:** The real-Gateway CI lane was skipped; the separate run is recorded below. No real 9.x/10.x updates or relevant before/after editor screenshots are supplied here. Local Codex autoreview previously stopped at its read-only sandbox preflight without a result.

### Real Gateway proof

Supplied results cover clean builds of main `65a8bc8` and head `6c79ecd`, each served by its own loopback Gateway in a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 VM (4 GiB). Chromium 156 was paired through the normal dashboard handoff. No mocks or model credentials.

- Both revisions passed browser creation of a one-time automation, with a separate CLI connection confirming `enabled=true` and `deleteAfterRun=true`; duplication of a paused automation with keep-after-run and a saved session key, confirming a new ID and all three settings retained; prompt editing, reload and reopen, confirming persistence and the original intact; and pause/resume from the editor header.
- Regression replay applied the PR's four test files to main without changing production source. Main had **70 unit tests pass, 2 fail, and the browser test fail**: edits still sent `sessionKey`, schedule-kind changes still sent `deleteAfterRun`, and **Turn on after creating** remained visible. Head had **72 unit tests pass and the browser test pass**.

Not covered: scheduled firing, model output, or delivery.

Co-authored with [Vyctor Brzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

prs.title: feat(active-memory): let Decision models decide deep-recall escalation
prs.body:
Closes #151178

## What Problem This Solves

Active Memory's `escalate` mode decides whether to run deep recall only with its bundled language matcher, so operators cannot use a faster or broader model for that decision.

## User Impact

Operators who enable Decision assistance and select a Decision model can set `escalationDecision: true` so that model decides whether a turn without a strong deterministic hit needs deep recall. Defaults are unchanged: without that opt-in, Decision assistance or a selected model, the built-in matcher decides as before. Hosted Decision models receive the bounded latest message and search query and may charge per evaluation, so a local model suits per-turn use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions added a dedicated, model-free escalation registrar. Now that Decision Models have landed, this revision drops that registrar, its SDK subpath and the `escalationProvider` setting and consumes the shared Decision runtime instead, following ClawSweeper's revision 17 recommendation.

After a weak or empty deterministic lookup, Active Memory asks one Boolean `deepRecall` question with purpose `active-memory/escalation` for the owning agent, at optional priority so it never takes a provider's last free slot. A `probabilityTrue` of at least 0.5 runs deep recall and a lower value skips it. The request must answer within the remaining preflight budget, capped at one second. Late answers are discarded, and unavailable, failed or invalid answers keep the built-in matcher. Modes `off` and `always` never ask. The consumer uses the host's automatic-consumer eligibility rule (Decision assistance plus an effective Decision model). Following `main`'s rule that authority is checked once, when work starts (#204249), the opt-in and targeting are read from the config that admitted the turn, and a change applies to the next turn; the shared Decision runtime is unchanged. Caller cancellation and closed-consumer rejection are terminal, not permission to launch fallback recall. Once per-task selection (#156407) lands, the purpose can become the plugin-owned task ID so operators can pick a model just for recall escalation.

## Evidence

Head `3028d65b01e`. Consent is now checked once, when the turn starts (#204249): the shared Decision runtime is unchanged from `main`, and Active Memory reads its opt-in and targeting from the config that admitted the turn.

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`: clean. `src/decisions` and `extensions/active-memory`: 24 files, 520 tests passed. oxlint, oxfmt, `config:docs:check`, `lint:docs` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` (+387 of 400): clean.
- The escalation timeout rows now run on a fake clock. The standalone batch-shape test is removed.

Installed run, [bundle](https://gist.github.com/fransqaas/d41e47ebd9de77c56eced300de6fc412/0b658bee2c66e78bee3d134ba558b29c33289bed):

- Clean Multipass Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1. Baseline: published `openclaw@2026.11.10` (`6ea542f`, npm `latest`) with `@openclaw/typesafe@2026.11.10` and hosted `typesafe/jev-latest` as the Decision model. Candidate: this branch, packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` (sha256 `dd47d390…5597`) and applied with the baseline's own `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz>`.
- Upgrade: result `ok`, `openclaw config validate` passes, 56 of 57 authored settings unchanged. The only change is `skill-workshop` added to `plugins.allow` by main's doctor migration. The upgrade does not set `escalationDecision`.
- Chat and recall inference are a loopback fixture; only the Decision model is real. Deep recall counts only when a real `memory_search` returns the stored fact.

| Message | 2026.11.10 matcher | Candidate, opted in |
|---|---|---|
| "Which deploy window are we using again?" | no recall | Jev asks for recall (367 ms), grounded |
| "Last time I checked, Python lists start at index zero…" | recall | Jev skips (230 ms), `decision-skip` |
| 「继续上次的排障」 ("continue last time's troubleshooting", from #151178) | no recall | Jev asks for recall (279 ms), grounded |

- Without the opt-in (right after the upgrade, and after opting out), with Decision assistance off, and in `always` mode, Active Memory does not ask and the matcher decides. With the TypeSafe plugin disabled the runtime returns `unavailable: not-configured` without dispatching, and the matcher decides.
- Settings: on 2026.11.10 the Active Memory "Memory recall" group has no Decision field. On the candidate, "Use decision model for escalation" was switched off and on in the Settings form, the saved config read back each value, and it was still checked after a full reload. Screenshots are in the bundle.
- The VM was purged afterwards.

Maintainer decision still needed: whether Active Memory should ship this default-off Decision consumer.

prs.title: ci: ratchet provider/model/URL branches on the request path
prs.body:
## Problem

Request and history shaping keeps growing branches keyed on a provider id, model id, API name or URL (for example `usesExplicitProxyLikeEndpoint`, `isZai`, `isSmallModel`). The 2026-11-27 provider-branching audit counted 330 regex hits plus 31 named-helper calls on main. Each guess fixes one route and silently mis-shapes the next one: relay users lose `prompt_cache_key` (#104533, #118605), and custom provider ids at known hosts get a different payload than the plugin-owned route. No check stops new branches.

## Solution

`pnpm check:provider-branching-ratchet` counts branches per file and fails when any file grows. It is a tripwire on spelling, not a parser.
- **Scope, by path:** `src/agents`, `src/plugins/provider-replay*`, `src/plugins/provider-runtime.ts`, `packages/ai/src`, `packages/llm-core/src`. Excluded: tests and test helpers, generated files, and the owners whose subject is provider identity (CLI backend adapters `cli-output*`/`cli-runner*`, `auth-profiles`, `model-auth*`, `model-catalog*`, `model-selection*`).
- **Counted, once per occurrence:** an identity field (`*provider`, `*providerId`, `*modelId`, `*modelApi`, `api`, `model.id`, `endpointClass`, `hostname`) compared with a literal; a call to a vendor-, endpoint- or base-URL-named predicate (`is|uses|supports|needs|requires|should|has…`); `case "<vendor id>"`; `startsWith`/`endsWith`/`includes` probes for a vendor, host or localhost; vendor regex literals with `.test(`; and an identity field in `.has(…)`/`.includes(…)`. Also counted: the named URL and model-size guesses `usesExplicitProxyLikeEndpoint`, `isLocalModelLeanEnabled` and `isSmallModel`.
- **Not counted:** declarations, imports, `typeof` checks, and `transport`/`auth` mode comparisons.
- **Baseline:** `config/provider-branching-allowlist.txt`, 861 branches in 223 files on main `b42b9f88`. This number cannot be compared with the audit's 330, which counted lines only in files that mention a request-path word. Here a file is in scope by path, so editing a comment cannot add or remove a file's debt.
- Runs in `check:baseline-ratchets` (CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`) on the existing `runPerFileCountRatchet` framework. A PR that removes branches runs it with `--prune`.

## Impact

Contributors only. There is no runtime change. A PR that adds a provider, model or URL branch on the request path must remove one in the same file, or declare the behavior as model compat in the owning plugin.

## Evidence

- `test/scripts/check-provider-branching-ratchet.test.ts`:
  - A fixture repo passes at its allowlisted count and fails (`src/agents/example.ts: 2 > 1`) when one branch is added.
  - 25 spelling cases pin the counted and uncounted forms.
- That fixture test caught a bug in the earlier head: plain git pathspecs need a directory for `**/`, so no file directly under `src/agents/` or `packages/ai/src/` was counted. The fix is `:(glob)` magic.
- `ci-baseline-ratchets.test.ts` passes. `--base origin/main` passes on the clean tree: `Provider branching ratchet OK: 223 files, 861 grandfathered branches.`
- Adversarial design review: the earlier request-path word filter was a cliff. Adding `tools:` to any of the 250 unmarked files in scope moved that file from 0 to N. It also let 686 hits escape, for example `model.provider === "cloudflare-ai-gateway"` in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts`. Both are fixed by scoping by path.
- Known gaps (accepted): a rename or a `Set` can dodge a pattern, and a few non-routing names still count (for example `isResponsesServiceTierRejection(`). For a shrink-only ratchet, extra counts cost nothing after the first day.

prs.title: fix(agents): large tool results lose their last lines and cannot be recovered
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool returns more text than its context budget, OpenClaw keeps only the start, discards the rest, and tells the model to "rerun with narrower args". The end of the output, where commands print errors, totals and exit status, is lost unless a keyword list happens to match it. MCP and plugin tools have no other copy, so the model cannot get the cut text back.

Production signal (a production deployment, 2.76 days of Gateway logs):
- 102 `[tool-result-truncation] Truncated N tool result(s) for prompt history (maxChars=64000 …)` lines, up to 96 results in one session.
- 310 context-overflow diagnostics in the same window, driven by long sessions full of tool output.

Reproduced on main (`ab296c23d2c4`) through the real record path (`guardSessionManager`, 200k-token window). The fixture is a 180,015-character plain log, the same for exec, read, web_fetch, an MCP result and a plugin result:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Characters the model sees | 63,973 | 63,961 |
| Last line kept | no | yes |
| Full output recoverable | no (dropped) | yes, 180,015 chars in a file |
| Notice | `[... 116116 more characters truncated; rerun with narrower args if needed]` | `[... 116221 chars omitted. Full output: <path> (page it with read offset/limit)]` |

## Fix

The bound has one owner, at record time:
- `boundToolResult` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-bound.ts`) runs once at the end of `afterToolCall` (`run/attempt-setup.ts`), after tool-result hooks and before the result is first sent. It applies to every executed tool: core, MCP and plugin.
- It keeps the head and the tail and puts the notice at the cut. The full text goes to an owner-only file through the existing `writePrivateTempFile` (tmpdir, 0600; staged in the workspace for sandboxed sessions), the same rule as `exec` and `web_fetch` output files. A tool that already saved its own file (`exec`, `web_fetch`) keeps that file, and the notice names it.
- The budget comes from the transcript guard's registry, so the existing synchronous cap leaves a bounded result byte for byte. Prefix stability holds, because a recorded result never changes after it is recorded.
- If the file write fails, the result passes on unchanged, and the existing transcript cap bounds it with head, tail and the character count.

Deleted:
- `context-truncation-notice.ts`: the "rerun with narrower args" notice and its `sessions_send` variant.
- `hasImportantTail`, a keyword regex that decided whether the tail survived, and the head-only branch it guarded. Head+tail is now unconditional for any window over 4,000 characters. Smaller windows keep a whole prefix, so short records are not split.

Fixed on the way (exposed by the shorter notice):
- The aggregate planner sized notices with a count of 1, so a notice carrying a real count could be cut. That dropped the spill path from a disclosed `Full output:` pointer. It now sizes the notice for the largest count it can show.
- A multi-block result made only of short records keeps whole leading records with one notice (#201795) instead of cutting every record.

## User impact

- Gateway and one-shot (`agent --local`) users on the embedded runtime. Both run `installEmbeddedAttemptContextGuards` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-runtime-prepare.ts:515`).
- A large tool result keeps its last lines (errors, totals, exit status), and the model can read the omitted middle from the named file instead of rerunning the tool.
- No config change. Results within budget are unchanged.
- Not covered: the Codex app-server and Claude CLI runtimes, which do not run this loop.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/tool-result-bounds.test.ts`: one case per tool family through the real guard registry:
  - exec (`buildExecForegroundResult`), MCP (`projectMcpCallToolResult`) and plugin: head, tail, spill file with the full text, and the recorded bytes equal to the bound bytes (fixed point);
  - web_fetch reuses its own spill file;
  - read reaches the middle of a 180k one-line spill page by page, and no page needs a second spill;
  - a failed spill write falls back to head, tail and the count, with no path.
- `run/attempt-context-guards.test.ts`: the installed `afterToolCall` bounds the result an earlier hook returned and restores the previous hook on removal.
- Touched suites pass (8 files), and `agent-tools.prefix-stability` passes. All core test typecheck shards pass.
- The prompt-cache prefix-stability journeys fail the same way on the merge base `ab296c23d2c4`, so these failures are not from this change:
  - They expect a summary marker ("compacted into the following summary") that #205584 replaced.
  - Google also counts 2 compactions in its overflow run where the test expects 1 (`expected 2 to be 1`, reproduced on the base).
  - The breaks they report are the allowed compactions; no tool-result bytes change after they are recorded.
- On main, the same contract test fails 5 of 5 families (63,973 of 180,015 characters kept, tail lost, no file).
- **End to end, real model.** Isolated `openclaw agent --local` (scratch HOME, state and config), `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` on the embedded runtime. The agent runs `seq 1 60000 | sed 's/$/ padding padding padding/'` through `exec`, calls no other tool, and replies with the last line of the output:
  - main `ab296c23d2c4`: `UNKNOWN` (the recorded result kept only the head of exec's retained window);
  - this PR: `60000 padding padding padding`. The notice points at exec's own output file; no second file is written.
- Review fixes, each with a test that is red on the earlier head:
  - a notice that gains a digit no longer pushes head+tail over the cap;
  - the separator newlines are reserved at the caller's weight (the context guard counts 2 per char), so a dense single-line result keeps its tail.
- Workspace-only host sessions cannot open tmpdir paths with `read`; exec and web_fetch spill paths are in the same position on main. Letting `read` open this session's own spill paths is the follow-up PR.

prs.title: fix(ios): setup steps push with the system back and neutral ink
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The manual gateway setup on iPhone (Gateway Setup, Gateway Details and Authentication, reached from **Connect Manually** on the Connect Gateway screen) uses a custom back button drawn over the screen instead of a navigation stack. Each step replaces the previous one in place, so there is no back swipe, and the back button and the screen's "Close" are small red text pills. Red ink also runs through the rest of setup: the `openclaw qr` command, **Connect Manually**, **New to OpenClaw? Start here**, **Restart Discovery** and the setup guide's numbers and links are all accent red, so the one primary action on each screen doesn't stand out.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI, and it is the last one. With this change, a person setting up the app sees:

- **The manual setup steps push like any iOS screen.** Gateway Setup, Gateway Details and Authentication are pushed over Connect Gateway. The system back button (a glass circle with a chevron) and the back swipe go back one step at a time, and the swipe reveals the previous screen underneath. Reaching the success screen replaces the steps without a back animation.
- **Close is a glass `xmark` button at the top right** of the intro, Connect Gateway and success screens, where a sheet's close button sits, instead of a red "Close" pill at the top left. The Quick Setup sheet uses the app's standard sheet close button.
- **Neutral ink.** The accent red is kept for the one primary action on each screen (Scan QR, Connect, Continue when enabled). The `openclaw qr` command, the copy button's checkmark, **Connect Manually** and other secondary buttons, **New to OpenClaw? Start here**, **Restart Discovery**, the setup guide's step numbers and **Connection help**, **Apply** next to the setup code, and the keyboard's dismiss control now use the primary text color.
- The Gateway Setup step's **Continue** button has the same height as the other primary buttons.
- The success screen ("You're connected") uses the same header as the other full-screen steps, so the mark keeps its size and place between screens; the green check badge sits on the mark.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OnboardingWizardView` now drives a `NavigationStack` whose path is derived from the current step (`OnboardingStep.pushedSteps`). The view still owns `step`: forward navigation sets it as before, and the path's setter only accepts pops from the system back button or the back swipe, each of which goes through the existing `navigateBack(to:)` cleanup (cancel the attempt, clear failures). That replaces the hand-drawn back button, `OnboardingStep.previous` and `canGoBack`, and `OpenClawCloseButtonStyle`, which has no other users. The close control sits in an overlay rather than a toolbar item so the full-screen steps don't get a navigation bar that would push the hero down. `OnboardingHeroHeader` gains `showsConnectedBadge` so the success screen reuses it. The ink changes swap `OpenClawBrand.accent` / `activationPrimaryAction` for `.primary` on secondary elements. The UI test that walks back from the Gateway Details step now taps the system back button (`BackButton`), and the string catalog is regenerated.

## Evidence

- Rechecked the independent head 40669d8f59d0 on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): 5 permission tests and the back-and-retry UI test passed, with no skips. The diff matches the original onboarding patch and does not include Talk. Native localization verification reported no generated changes.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `DevicePermissionsTests`, 5 of 5 passed, including the new `manual onboarding steps pop back one at a time to Connect Gateway`.
- UI test on the same simulator: `BootstrapSetupFailureUITests/testOnboardingPreservesFailedBootstrapSetupForRetry` passed. It goes intro → Connect Gateway → Connect Manually → Home Network → Continue, taps the system back button to return to the setup code, and checks that a refused setup code is kept for retry. The first two runs failed before reaching any changed code: the simulator's first camera prompt (raised by the Connect Gateway screen) reached the test's "Allow" interruption handler, which found two matching buttons. With camera access granted to the app on the simulator, it passed.
- The iOS app and its test bundles build with the SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `native:i18n:verify` reports `changed=false`, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- Screenshots: first-run onboarding on the same simulator with no gateway configured, in light and dark (the app's `--openclaw-appearance` launch option). These captures predate the split: before is the prior stacked base (31da59193e61), and after is the original onboarding commit (8287534f4dc8). The first-run screens and their navigation are unchanged in the cut onto main. The wizard differs only in protocol-mismatch recovery, which the captures do not exercise. Screens: Connect Gateway, Gateway Setup (step 1) and Gateway Details (step 2). In the Gateway Details captures, the name of a gateway discovered on the capture machine's network is covered with a gray bar.
- Not checked:
  - The back swipe by hand (the UI test taps the system back button), and the Authentication step.
  - The success screen and the Quick Setup sheet; neither was captured.
  - Accessibility text sizes, where the step title moves from the bar into the form, and VoiceOver on a device.
  - iPad and landscape.
  - Setup against a real Gateway.

![Gateway Details, step 2 of manual setup, light. Before: a red chevron pill for Back and a red Restart Discovery. After: the system back button in a glass circle and Restart Discovery in the normal text color.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfbe8e88-4877-4e31-a61f-5ee1304c281f)

![Gateway Details, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f5b373d-71c4-4ece-84af-92f472b51051)

![Gateway Setup, step 1 of manual setup, light. Before: a red chevron pill for Back and a shorter Continue button. After: the system back button in a glass circle and Continue at the height of the other primary buttons.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdcb8456-41cb-4f06-9f1a-5abecd479bf2)

![Gateway Setup, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07e6f41b-9e71-4b54-9c9b-b01ebc712625)

![Connect Gateway, light. Before: a red Close pill at the top left, and the openclaw qr command, Connect Manually and New to OpenClaw? Start here in red. After: a glass close button at the top right and those three in the normal text color; only Scan QR stays red.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c4d25e9-3034-4bce-9f13-c7bb12592ac8)

![Connect Gateway, dark. Same comparison as the previous image.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6470c1a-723a-42de-b2a1-957a4b02ff9c)
