prs.title: feat: review spoken self-corrections before adding dictation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205645

Part of #205645

Dictation can leave an original phrase and its spoken correction in the unsent draft, such as “Meet on Tuesday sorry Wednesday.” This draft now tests a narrower behavior: retain and optionally review the words the recognizer actually provided, without guessing which words to change. It also keeps received dictation when the browser–Gateway connection drops in the same conversation.

**This is still a draft for design acceptance and client qualification.** Whether original-only review should ship with a saved preference, and whether eventual correction support should be built in or plugin-owned, remains open.

## User Impact

**Spoken corrections** defaults to **Off**. The optional **Review original (corrections unavailable)** mode offers **Keep original** or **Cancel** after recording, with no production candidate or rewrite. **Literal for this recording** skips that review for one uninterrupted recording when its draft is still current. Neither review action sends anything. Choosing Off leaves existing draft text intact and restores ordinary raw dictation for future recordings.

The capture cannot change a sent message, run a tool, enter Talk, or replace a selection that predates the recording in review mode. A real destination, permission, or draft change still prevents stale insertion. The saved preference is scoped to the browser and Gateway; pending review text and Literal are not saved as preferences. There is no new public refinement contract or native-client integration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture and composer owners retain transcript text and check live pane, physical session, compose authority, capture identity, and both component and authoritative draft revisions before keeping an original. A review choice is consumed before handing text to the insertion owner. A temporary transport outage no longer masquerades as a destination change.

The unused edit-plan validator, preparer, and per-event recognition metadata are deferred. Only raw interim and final text, capture/draft ownership, and the original-only review are needed here. The [issue proposal review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205645#issuecomment-7178569403) was advisory, not product acceptance.

## Evidence

### Current draft head: `432aa3b022e43cdf87fde450efdd1c2844728665`

Timothy Wayne Gregg (@CompleteDotTech) ran the paired Control UI check and the scripted browser proof on the exact draft head in [fork Actions run 45955334981](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45955334981) · [#205794 job and log](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45955334981/job/140379168164) · [proof bundle](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45955334981/artifacts/15182220641).

- **Paired Control UI asset gate: PASS.** The job ran `pnpm ui:check-performance:base d6d289ee13ff163c20e64b8cbb008312f3181d3f` before using secrets. Chat boot JS gzip was **1,336,811 → 1,336,529 B (−282 B)**, requests **21 → 21**; new-session boot JS gzip was **820,019 → 818,819 B (−1,200 B)**, requests **17 → 17**. Chat boot CSS stayed at **3 requests**. Largest CSS was **58,626 B gzip** against the **58,315 B** hard ceiling (311 B over); the base was already over, so this was a warning, not a paired-gate failure. No budget was changed.
- **Scripted Chromium microphone → live OpenAI transcription: PASS, 18/18 takes.** Chromium fed TTS WAVs (alloy, nova, sage) through its fake microphone to the built Control UI and isolated Gateway, using live OpenAI Realtime transcription (`gpt-4o-transcribe`). All six cases passed 3/3: Off, Keep original, Cancel, Literal, failed full-review download → Keep original, and failed full-review download → Cancel.
- **Recovery when the full review cannot load:** Ordinary Chat does not load the capture or full-review code on boot. Recording loads the recovery UI with capture, so it does not depend on a second download. The two recovery cases blocked only the built full-review JS asset after Stop, verified that the unchanged provider transcript was visible in a read-only field alongside the load error, and confirmed that **Keep original** inserted it into the unsent draft without sending and **Cancel** left the draft unchanged.
- **Local checks on the published tree:** UI typecheck and 109 focused tests passed. The local paired gate against the same base also passed (Chat boot gzip −436 B); the fork’s exact-head measurements above are from its own paired build.
- **Scope:** This run is not a physical-microphone or screen-reader test and does not decide whether original-only review and its saved preference should ship.

### Historical draft head: `8d399bf4575d40a12146b68616974b99defbcfa0`

- **Local checks on the merged source:** 158 focused tests and 14 Chromium component tests passed, as did the UI typecheck, UI i18n, and `git diff --check`. The test-line budget passed against upstream main at `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa` (+1,777 lines; 400 ordinary + 1,383 allocated). These checks do not repeat the earlier built-UI disconnect and upgrade runs below.
- **Timothy's fork CI ([CompleteDotTech/openclaw#10](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/10), exact head above):** [CI run 45875396886, attempt 1](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886) had no conclusion at the 19:13 UTC check on November 26: 1 pass, 219 queued, 20 skipped, 0 failures reported. [`preflight`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140101226574) passed. [`build-artifacts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102563048), [`checks-ui`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102563344), [`checks-ui-e2e`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102564119), [`checks-node-worker-e2e-1`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102571965), [`control-ui-performance`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102563598), [`check-prod-types`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102565029), [`check-test-types`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102565052), and [`check-lint`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102565236) were queued. The [real-Gateway E2E lane](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102566738) and [`control-ui-i18n`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396886/job/140102565468) were skipped. Queued and skipped jobs are not passes.
- **Separate workflows on Timothy's fork:** [Blacksmith Build Artifacts Testbox: `build-artifacts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396548/job/140101072354) passed, including the dist build and artifact verification. It used the fork PR merge ref, whose source tree matches the branch head. [Workflow Sanity: `actionlint`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396467/job/140101071377), [OpenGrep: `Scan changed paths (precise)`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396444/job/140101071463), and [Node Runtime Conformance: `Rust workspace`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396516/job/140101435286) / [`TypeScript contracts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875396516/job/140101435323) passed. [Labeler: `label`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875392538/job/140101062921) failed before labeling because the fork workflow had no GitHub App private-key input. It did not test this patch. None of these results replaces the pending CI workflow or upstream gates.

- **Scripted Chromium microphone input → live OpenAI transcription (exact draft head):** Timothy Wayne Gregg (@CompleteDotTech) ran [Scripted audio proof #205794](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45935736954/job/140298920731) on November 27. The job built the pinned SHA above and ran `live-dictation-proof.mjs` against its built Control UI and an isolated Gateway. Chromium replayed OpenAI TTS WAVs (alloy, nova, sage) as a fake microphone; the Gateway used live OpenAI Realtime transcription (`gpt-4o-transcribe`). [Run and artifacts](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45935736954) · [proof bundle](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45935736954/artifacts/15170384656).
  - `off-keeps-recognized-words`: **PASS 3/3**.
  - `review-keep-original`: **PASS 3/3**.
  - `review-cancel-preserves-draft`: **PASS 2/3**; sage was **INCONCLUSIVE_STT**, not an app failure.
  - `literal-keeps-correction-words`: **PASS 3/3**.
  - **11/12 takes passed**, with one inconclusive recognition result and no app failures or send attempts. The passing takes exercised the unsent draft and the original-only keyboard choices, not a generated correction. **Still to do:** Timothy will run physical-microphone checks; screen-reader testing is also still outstanding. The asset-budget failures below applied to this older head; see the passing comparison above for the current head.
- **Native Chromium zoom and accessibility tree:** Built Control UI against an isolated Gateway with fake microphone input and a deterministic streaming transcript. Changed the browser's actual tab zoom to 200% (1,280 to 640 CSS px); the review and actions had no horizontal overflow. Chromium exposed the review heading, verbatim original in a named region, a polite/atomic status without the transcript, and the unavailable Accept correction action as disabled. From the original region, Tab reached Proposed correction, Cancel, and Keep original. Keyboard Cancel discarded the recording; Keep original inserted the transcript once; neither sent a message. This is browser accessibility-tree and keyboard proof, not a screen-reader run.
- **Offline acoustic replay through the running app:** Replayed the PocketSphinx sample “go forward ten meters” through Chromium's test microphone, the isolated Gateway's speech relay, and a loopback adapter that ran PocketSphinx on the relayed audio. The recognizer returned “go forward and mirrors.” The review showed that exact output; Keep original inserted it once into the previously empty draft, with zero send requests. The accuracy assertion did not pass; preserving the actual recognizer output did. This is recorded speech replay—not a physical microphone or a hosted provider qualification.
- **Control UI asset gate: failed locally against upstream main `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`.** Ran `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` with the published candidate tree and the same Node/Vite toolchain on both sides. The comparison failed four metrics: total CSS gzip **348,614 → 349,567 B** (cap 348,683 B); total CSS raw **1,792,629 → 1,795,278 B** (cap 1,794,106 B); chat boot CSS **3 → 4 requests** (cap 3); chat boot JS gzip **1,336,502 → 1,339,556 B** (+3,054 B, versus 64 B allowed above the already-over-budget base). Largest CSS and the 21 chat boot JS requests were inherited, not new comparison failures. The fork's hosted performance lane was still queued at the 19:48 UTC check. No budget was changed.

![Original-only review at Chromium’s native 200% zoom, with the unchanged transcript, Cancel, Keep original, and disabled Accept correction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a97c61d-b8fc-400a-90ae-f60cc80b52ad)

### Earlier proof on `69442207b3eb`

[ClawSweeper Revision 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794#issuecomment-7184671680) reviewed this earlier head after the Revision 2 follow-up: proof 4/6, patch quality 4/6, no actionable findings, awaiting a maintainer decision.

- **Production build, Chromium + isolated Gateway:** Four browser–Gateway WebSocket disconnect/reconnect cases passed: active recording and finalization, each with Off and review. For each, Chromium’s fake microphone supplied audio and the local streaming fixture emitted the interim transcript “I work Tuesday, no Wednesday shifts are available.” The finalization cases cut the browser socket after the fixture observed the provider finalization request and while it was withholding the final transcript; the recording cases cut it while the recording control was still active and before such a request. Each case observed a closed socket and a new successful Gateway handshake. Off retained the text in the draft; review held it outside the draft until keyboard **Keep original**. The final draft equaled the received text exactly once in all four cases, with no Gateway send request. This proves transport and draft behavior using deterministic transcription, not acoustic recognition.
- **Same recovery assertions, red/green:** Ran the five production-pane lifecycle cases unchanged on `95b1575` and on the candidate. All five failed on the old head: the two Off cases lost the received text and the three review cases dropped the review. All five passed on the candidate, including disconnect while review was already pending. The final focused run passed **152/152** tests, and the Chromium component run passed **14/14**. The presentation fixture injects an original-only view, not a generated suggestion or a real capture.
- **Build and checks:** Production UI build, production and test UI typechecks, targeted lint/format, UI i18n, and `git diff --check` passed. Test-line budget passed at **+1,783** (400 ordinary + 1,383 allocated). The report-only asset check listed six overages (largest and total CSS gzip, total CSS raw, chat boot JS and CSS request counts, and chat boot JS gzip); no budget was changed and no exact-base attribution is claimed. Local autoreview stopped before model assessment at its pass-budget preflight; no clean result is claimed. Full hosted CI is not claimed here.
- **Earlier proof, on the previous candidate:** Upgrading the same Chromium profile, origin, and isolated Gateway from stable `2026.11.10` kept the saved draft and Light preference, defaulted Spoken corrections to Off, and retained explicit opt-in on reload. A deterministic CLI transcription fixture also preserved a pending original-only review across reconnect and allowed keyboard Keep original. The local recognizer attempt did not complete successful recognition. No successful acoustic recognition, physical microphone, screen-reader application, actual browser zoom, production suggestions, native clients, or combined cleanup/punctuation behavior were qualified.

### Clean comparison — stable to candidate

Before: stable shows the saved draft (model label redacted).

prs.title: fix(dictation): honor realtime transcription authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205855.

Part of #205855

Realtime transcription already requires a session to stop when its existing `assertCurrent` callback rejects. Deferred setup and inbound messages did not consistently honor that contract: a retired URL resolver could continue into credential preparation, and a provider message could reach capture, parsing, or transcript callbacks after authority was revoked. OpenAI client-secret creation also sends configured transcription hints before the WebSocket exists, so the HTTP dispatch needs the same assertion.

This PR repairs those existing transport boundaries. The broader P02 context-aware transcription feature remains unimplemented, and #205855 stays open.

## User Impact

Revoked or retired transcription work stops at the affected setup, HTTP-dispatch, and message-processing boundaries. Authorized sessions retain startup, queued audio, reconnect behavior, and delivery of their final transcript after Stop.

The patch adds no context source, setting, permission, RPC schema, migration, or audio-retention behavior. Configured OpenAI prompts are inherited behavior. Reverting this PR restores the previous transport behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair stays with the existing owners:

- The shared WebSocket session checks attempt settlement, generation ownership, closure, and current authority before URL work and again before deferred headers. A retired attempt cannot abort its replacement.
- Inbound messages check socket ownership and authority before capture, parsing, or provider callbacks, while preserving the authorized graceful-finalization window.
- The OpenAI transcription factory forwards its existing assertion to the private client-secret helper. That helper checks before preparation and at the guarded-fetch `beforeRequest` boundary after asynchronous DNS/transport preparation. The existing voice caller can continue omitting the optional private argument.
- The Gateway relay retains its existing publication checks.

The OpenAI authority regression replaces the earlier mocked fixture with a four-case test using the real OpenAI factory, shared session, guarded fetch, response parser, native HTTP, native hostname lookup, and a real local WebSocket server. It counts HTTP request arrivals before body completion and covers credential-await revocation, DNS-await revocation, revoked late-final delivery, and authorized startup/Stop/final delivery. Cleanup uses the existing test-port and fixture-cleanup owners; all imports cross the public extension SDK boundary.

The [issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205855#issuecomment-7186786824) still requests a maintainer decision on a composer-only per-turn contract, consent ownership, collection limits, and revocation semantics for already-admitted context-derived requests. This transport repair does not establish those new semantics. M11 (#205845), M10 (#205846), and P04 (#205852) remain semantic design dependencies for the feature; #191109 is an adjacent hints request, not a physical parent branch.

## Evidence

### Current head: `59dc2607f00d`

The [fork workflow’s pinned run manifest](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/cba2d6d389612b460f86091a94bd9ff91b20e089/proof/run.json) lists the same 11 focused files recorded below and the full build. The focused-test step passed, and the full `pnpm build` exited 0, including declaration emission. Both ran before live provider credentials were exposed. This is the result for the #205876 job, not a verdict for the other PRs in the same matrix.

- **Live scripted dictation: 6/6 takes passed.** Chromium’s fake microphone fed scripted WAVs into the Control UI through the built Gateway and live OpenAI transcription. `live-start-and-vad` verified the final before Stop (3/3); `stop-keeps-final-transcript` verified the final after Stop (3/3). Both checked the final text stayed in the composer without sending.
- **Limits:** Not a physical-mic test; the environment-key path does not exercise the client-secret POST. The matched loopback evidence below covers deferred credential/DNS revocation and revoked late-final delivery.
- **Upstream gates:** [OpenClaw CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46032444280) and [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/46032444274) for this head report `Action required`. The passing fork job is not a substitute for maintainer approval and upstream checks.

#### Proof logs


[Download the exact-head proof bundle](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46042833058/artifacts/15222075622) for the full focused-test and build logs, per-take state, and browser captures. This is a GitHub Actions artifact link, not inline screenshots.

### Previous proved head: `532c7d9532a5`

[Timothy Gregg’s fork proof run 45955334981](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45955334981), [#205876 job](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45955334981/job/140379168223), passed on [`532c7d9532a52cdcabfaf53f0f9bd2a40372af8a`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/532c7d9532a52cdcabfaf53f0f9bd2a40372af8a). Both used `alloy`, `nova`, and `sage` and checked that the final text stayed in the composer without sending. The Chromium fake microphone is not a physical-mic test.   - `stop-keeps-final-transcript`: **3/3** (same voices); the final transcript arrived after Stop. Both cases verified the final text stayed in the composer without sending.
  - This job passed even though the multi-PR workflow was red for a different matrix job. It did not run the listed test/check lanes, full declaration emission, or physical-mic testing. The environment-key path does not exercise the client-secret POST; the matched loopback tests below are the evidence for credential/DNS revocation and revoked late-final suppression.
- **Upstream CI is still open:** [the upstream CI run for this SHA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45875137110) reports `action_required`. The fork job proves the runnable browser/Gateway build and authorized live flow, not the full build or required upstream checks.
- `roboclaw-bot` merged upstream `main` at `2fda93cf03a8` into the existing PR branch without conflicts or rewriting history, then published [`45971d0305bf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45971d0305bfaf4a7096d14ba7dbfe3e28b18b3a). - **Timothy’s fork CI (secretless, not upstream CI):** [CompleteDotTech/openclaw#17](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/17) shares PR head `45971d0305bfaf4a7096d14ba7dbfe3e28b18b3a`. [Run 45875138236, attempt 1](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236) was **queued** as of 2026-11-26 19:19 UTC. This verifies source identity for preflight, not execution of the queued tests.
- **Fork job status:** [`build-artifacts`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236/job/140102135906) and [`checks-node-agentic-gateway-core-1`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236/job/140102146791) were **queued**. The [run graph](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875138236) showed **0/173** Node matrix jobs and **0/12** `checks-ui-e2e` jobs completed; `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` was **skipped**. ### Previous main integration: `ac30e5d72f6f8`

- `roboclaw-bot` published [`ac30e5d72f6f8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ac30e5d72f6f8ae57b518c5b4e3cf6ebe34ad756) to the existing fork branch. Merge commit `5123c5d87199` retains both the prior PR head `40cef00eabcc` and upstream `main` at `47027a257c72`; no conflicts or history rewrite. Verified the fork and PR refs, the merge parents, and the published tree against the staged tree.
- Against `47027a257c72`: five files; **+16 net production lines**, **+383 net test lines** (under the 400-line allowance). All five PR blobs match `40cef00eabcc`. `git diff --check` passed; the static simplification pass kept the existing authority and transport owners, with no new public API, flags, or configuration. Bound Auto Review reported **scoped-clean (P0)**; this was static analysis, not ClawSweeper or runtime proof.
- **Not run on this head:** fork-code tests, browser/Gateway behavior runs, live OpenAI Realtime, and the full build. The finite and static-check results below are historical results from before the main merge, not a new exact-head pass. Hosted product checks are not verified green for this draft.

Live OpenAI is deferred and no re-review was requested.

### Historical GitHub readback at `40cef00eabcc`

- Verified both the PR head and fork ref, the one-file delta from `854d3a5a74e3`, and the published fixture SHA-256 below. No production files changed in this delta. This follow-up was read-only with respect to source and did not rerun tests, lint, types, or the build.
- The completed finite results below are the author’s previously recorded runs: 58 passed and 3 intended failures on the implementation-base production overlay; 61 passed on the repaired OpenAI cases, plus 124 passed in affected consumers. The fixture uses real local HTTP, DNS, and WebSocket transport with synthetic credentials and provider responses. **No authenticated live OpenAI Realtime run or Gateway/UI startup and Stop trace was recorded.**

### Pre-merge revision and independent review

- Implementation base: `1c3de7eb68481e5d7656e21ec96d43855789fbb0`.
- Previous repair: `854d3a5a74e31eaa8e13346ed29b3f9ddbd9ca16`.
- Pre-merge head: [`40cef00eabcc6a22919c0bffba02c9bbfb4e9848`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/40cef00eabcc6a22919c0bffba02c9bbfb4e9848), on `CompleteDotTech/openclaw:feat/p02-context-aware-transcription`.
- Verified tree: `0c523f13638e0659fdea1cb718d2feef40cb3d4e`. The connected GitHub publication produced the identical tested local tree; the remote commit was fetched, compared, and adopted locally without resetting work. The working tree is clean.
- This iteration changes only `extensions/openai/realtime-transcription-authority.test.ts`. The PR still contains exactly five files; production bytes are unchanged from the previous repair. Net added test lines are **383**, below the 400-line allowance.
- Final authority-fixture SHA-256: `a6d0ee3ff94aa6c0d1e72ba9984815f76799051501d0bb120a23b7cdc2baa167`.
- Independent agent source review found no actionable issue in the final fixture. A separate evidence audit checked case inventories, commands, source hashes, immutable baseline production objects, restoration, log digests, and full wrapper completion. These are independent source/evidence reviews, not human approval or a ClawSweeper/autoreview verdict.

### Completed matched baseline/candidate proof

The same final fixture and two existing OpenAI regression files ran against exact parent production bytes and then the repaired production bytes, using the same checkout, frozen physical dependency installation, command, and isolated environment. Git HEAD remained the previous repair during the temporary baseline production overlay; the original production bytes were restored and hash-verified afterward.

| Observed boundary | Baseline production | Repaired production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Revoke while controlled credential service awaits | **1 physical HTTP request arrival**; intended assertion failure | **0 HTTP arrivals, 0 DNS lookups, 0 WebSocket connections**; one authority error |
| Revoke after native hostname lookup, before releasing its await | **1 physical HTTP request arrival**; intended assertion failure | **0 HTTP arrivals, 0 WebSocket connections**; one authority error |
| Revoke after Stop/commit, before the server sends the final events | **1 late transcript callback delivery**; intended assertion failure | **0 transcript callback deliveries**; one authority error |
| Authorized startup, audio, Stop twice, and server final | Pass | Pass: one commit and one final transcript |

| Selected OpenAI file | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Authority fixture | 1 passed, 3 intended failures | 4 passed |
| Transcription provider | 29 passed | 29 passed |
| Browser voice authentication | 28 passed | 28 passed |
| **Total** | **58 passed, 3 intended failures** | **61 passed** |

Both finite commands completed compiler-generation verification, cleanup, and final shard settlement. Neither used watch mode nor timed out. On November 26, 2026, the baseline ran 12:00:56–12:03:09 EST, **133.177 s**, exit **1** from the three intended assertions; the candidate ran 12:03:28–12:05:41 EST, **133.317 s**, exit **0**.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/openai/realtime-transcription-authority.test.ts \
  extensions/openai/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

### Affected consumers and static checks

A second finite canonical command completed **124/124 cases across eight files**, with no failures or skips. All five shards and compiler-output verification/cleanup completed; exit **0**, **172.160 s**.

| Consumer | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| Shared WebSocket session | 30 |
| Gateway transcription relay | 18 |
| Gateway client authority | 2 |
| Agent tool prefix stability | 16 |
| Deepgram transcription provider | 18 |
| ElevenLabs transcription provider | 15 |
| Mistral transcription provider | 18 |
| xAI transcription provider | 7 |
| **Total** | **124** |

Together, the final candidate commands passed **185 cases in 11 selected files**. This is the affected regression scope, not the entire repository suite.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/transcription-relay.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/client-authority.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  extensions/deepgram/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/mistral/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/xai/realtime-transcription-provider.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

The consumer command used `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`; every shard independently passed. Execution stayed serial. Tests used Node **24.22.3**, pinned pnpm **12.15.0**, a complete frozen-lockfile physical installation, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, one worker, a 1,536-MiB Node heap, and native worker pools limited to one. The isolated environment supplied private state and loopback networking, with no operator credentials or inherited proxies. Typechecks and extension lint used a 3,072-MiB heap. No dependency or lockfile change was made.

| Check | Final observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Core production types | **PASS**, canonical `tsconfig.core.json` |
| Core test types | **PASS**, canonical `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.other.json` |
| Extension production types | **PASS**, canonical `tsconfig.extensions.json` |
| Extension test types | **PASS**, canonical `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` |
| Core lint | **PASS**, both changed shared files |
| Extension lint | **PASS**, all three changed OpenAI files; zero warnings/errors |
| Extension test import boundary | **PASS**, 5,129 extension files checked |
| Formatting and whitespace | **PASS**, all five changed files and `git diff --check` |
| Physical dependency ownership | **PASS** |
| Full build | **BLOCKED**, normal build stopped at memory admission before removing any output because the process cgroup memory limit is not visible |
| Hosted workflow runs | **ACTION REQUIRED** at the published head; no successful CI claim |

Canonical type commands were `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental`, the corresponding core-test project command, and the package-script extension production/test commands with their standard `.artifacts/tsgo-cache/` build-info paths. Lint used `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` or `extensions/tsconfig.json`; formatting used `scripts/run-format.mts --check`. All final passing records match the published source bytes. Earlier core records were reused only after verifying the unchanged shared-file hashes.

The full-build attempt used `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts` with full declarations enabled. It exited **1** after **2.950 s** with: “The process memory limit is not visible through this cgroup mount namespace.” No memory-admission override was set. Completed test compilation and SDK declaration preparation are not claimed as a full build.

The first extension-lint attempt timed out after SDK declaration preparation; it was not a pass. Its retained lock was released only after verifying termination of the isolated process namespace, and the normal wrapper validated and reused the completed declaration receipt. The subsequent owned lint diagnostics were fixed, then final lint and matched runtime proof passed on the exact published fixture. Earlier incomplete/watch-mode results are superseded by the finite proof above.

The earlier body mislabeled a broad unused-file scan as a required gate for this patch. The maintained-command/dynamic-child rule does not add a new Knip entry requirement here: this PR adds neither. The historical killed scans are not passing evidence.

At `40cef00eabcc`, [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077500), [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077252), [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077317), [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077275), [macOS Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077359), and [OpenGrep](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45866077249) each conclude `action_required`. Upstream workflow action is still required.

### Proof limits and P02 acceptance

The new four-case fixture uses synthetic credential-service results and a synthetic provider protocol over real local transports. It does **not** establish live OS keychain integration, actual OpenAI endpoint/model/hint-field acceptance, TLS/WSS behavior, microphone or browser-permission behavior, native accessibility interaction, or transcription accuracy. The extension fixture proves late transcript callback suppression; the separate shared-owner tests cover admission before capture.

No full P02 acceptance criterion is complete:

| Criterion | Remaining feature work |
| --- | --- |
| AC01 — disabled means zero reads/fields | Disabled/default feature and authoritative consent resolver are unimplemented. |
| AC02 — bounded selected sources | Collector, source categories, aggregate budgets, and timeout behavior are unimplemented. |
| AC03 — denied/secure/unknown/stale targets | Target checks and context-free fallback are unimplemented. |
| AC04 — cancellation/revocation | Existing transport-contract foundation only; feature consent revisions, lineage, and recovery are unimplemented. |
| AC05 — focus isolation | Transport generations are covered; original-target snapshots and field/application switching are unimplemented. |
| AC06 — capability negotiation | Inherited configured prompt transport only; new negotiation and real endpoint qualification are unimplemented. |
| AC07 — adversarial context isolation | Integrated context path and adversarial-output qualification are not run. |
| AC08 — recognition improvement/regressions | No audio/provider outcomes for useful or misleading context. |
| AC09 — Unicode/deterministic bounds | Feature context-budget/truncation owner is unimplemented. |
| AC10 — permitted destinations | P04 policy integration and its destination matrix are unimplemented. |
| AC11 — private diagnostics | Feature redaction qualification is not run; debug capture retains its existing semantics. |
| AC12 — disable/rollback/teardown | Feature controls, snapshots, and baseline-dictation qualification are unimplemented. |

The full context-bearing STT/consent-revocation lineage case, independent-baseline refinement recovery, explicit retranscription using already-permitted retained audio, and no-audio/manual recovery remain **NOT RUN**. Already-transmitted bytes cannot be recalled.

The [previous ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205876#issuecomment-7187811502) covered `532c7d9532a5` and found no code issues; proof was sufficient and upstream approval remained with a maintainer. The new exact-head fork proof above is separate from that verdict.

### Before merge

- An OpenClaw maintainer still needs to approve upstream CI and obtain the applicable required CI/security checks and review. The fork workflow supplies exact-head test, full-build, and scripted-dictation evidence, not upstream approval.

Physical-mic qualification remains Timothy’s follow-up; this run used scripted audio through Chromium’s fake microphone. Keep this PR **draft**. The separate P02 product decision remains with #205855. No merge or issue closure is requested.

prs.body:
Depends on #205880

**Stack boundary:** #205880 owns `vocabulary-terms.ts`, `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`, and the base `vocabulary-types.ts` contract. This draft owns shared collection operations and audit, snapshot authority/lineage, the optional Talk relay guard, and their evidence. This is a content dependency, not a requirement to preserve #205880 as a Git parent: OpenClaw squash-merges. The content-only stack is published in `38f4fc01b1a`. It carries #205880’s own patch, not the newer `main` changes on that branch. The preceding managed preparation commit `87380810726` has the same tree as the previous PR head `432b13edab0`. Resync this branch with `main` after #205880 lands.

**Shared branch commits (excluding base merges):** `4780aeb034e`, `fca28902f5a`, `5373babbbbd`, `927da4c148b`, `70bac82c4c2`, `56aef23a43a`, `23d1c727c5e`, `bc79270a1ef`, `baab314d1b5`, `935d6865917`, `c41e5d1ad9d`, `d069e0395fd`, `432b13edab0`. The early foundation commits remain in history; the stack resolution takes the common foundation from #205880.

## What Problem This Solves

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205633.

Part of #205633

Teams need an explicitly selected shared vocabulary without publishing personal dictionary entries or treating a known collection ID as authorization. The existing transcription-provider prompt setting does not supply collection membership, revision ownership, or per-utterance source provenance.

**Design-review draft: M06 is incomplete and the issue must remain open.** This PR presents the prerequisite proposal and its observed evidence for the required owner/design decision. It does not enable a production shared-dictionary capability or claim acceptance of its proposed permission, persistence, retention, or public contracts.

## User Impact

There is no enabled shared-dictionary user flow. The proposal provides reviewable validation/resolution, scoped collection operations, immutable snapshot leases, and an optional guard at the existing Talk publication boundary. Existing personal records are not migrated or written. No new audio retention, automatic replay, recognizer, or provider route is introduced.

Every client and provider remains unqualified for this shared-vocabulary feature. Collection selection/management, visible source/conflict inspection, accessible recovery, live provider disclosure, and full P03/M11 integration are still required. The proposed mid-utterance revocation semantics need an explicit owner decision against the existing admitted-request policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collection operations use the existing action-bound V2 worker-store interface, with injected host authority and expected-revision CAS. Real retained-worker tests now cover two editors, atomic malformed-import rejection, tombstones after orderly close/reopen, final commit-admission refusal, and an exact 400-KiB/5,000-term draft with the full audit ring. Those grants are synthetic; no production collection namespace, membership mapping, public RPC/UI, or provider capability is registered.

The proposed representation, retained tombstones, 32-event private audit ring, scope/visibility rules, and rollback/retention contract require the recorded design acceptance in #205633 before production wiring. Unknown versions are preserved and rejected. The current unregistered proposal migrates no existing data. An eventual rollout/rollback must be implemented and qualified by the accepted store owner. M11 remains the intended sole request/result coordinator.

The commits separate term/budget foundations, collection operations, snapshot/relay boundaries, and qualification evidence. No reviewed physical P03/M11 parent was identified. The internal term/resolution contract is a proposed minimal P03 prerequisite, not a completed personal-dictionary feature. Optional management placement should be decided through the existing plugin/SDK boundary. #191109 is adjacent provider-hint transport, not a stack parent or closing target.

Source and merge base: `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`. Target: `openclaw/openclaw:main`, observed at `954928a0bf1c1dc72ab43152f62a7c15577815a7`. Head: `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-shared-dictionaries` at `56aef23a43aea74de1f20ed6e1cf81cc3c1756a5`, tree `60df11f79aa0ceedc5ccfc05b60c2bfaca19f86d`. The original four commits were published through the authenticated GitHub connection with each complete tree verified equal to the saved local commits; only metadata changed. The qualification commit adds the real-worker proof, exact existing test-lane registrations, explicit synchronous benchmark GC, and updated evidence. A final documentation commit records the upstream review and CI observations. The earlier fork-local review is https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/1; this upstream draft owns continuing design review.

## Evidence

### Fork offline regression proof — November 27, 2026

[Passing fork Actions run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/46034508273) exercised PR head `ab64087ebe3ce3155b57247dfb0f1007d8003264` with `live: false`.

- `vocabulary-terms.test.ts`: 23/23 passed.
- `transcription-relay.vocabulary.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `provider-admission` red/green: failed on baseline `af23a024cf8ef3e7793976ea54cb0191b03044ab` at the expected assertion (a new vocabulary admission is required after provider creation fails), and passed on the PR head. The shadowed-alias regression is owned by #205880 and is not a separate case in this lane.

This is focused offline fork proof, not upstream required CI or a live Talk/provider run. The PR remains a design-review draft and #205633 stays open.

### Timothy Wayne Gregg’s fork CI — November 26, 2026

[CompleteDotTech/openclaw#15](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/15), branch head `935d686591746fbeff2335e14877213679340635`. Preflight checked out fork merge commit `0d3b0663c214ca6db05bd73ca212a77f1f63e666`, verified to have the same Git tree as the head (`2048f4e085aff1d57327c2790c94c35a41ba3baf`). The branch retains both the prior head `baab314d1b5486644e0a5e145f08dd2021cb2db1` and upstream `main` at `2fda93cf03a882cd080e7984392d50b95c4737aa`. The merge had no conflicts and preserved the feature diff against its base. These results are fork CI, not upstream required checks.

| Job that ran | Result | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [preflight](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875412536/job/140101161676) | PASS | Verified checkout and created the matrix; not a test pass. |
| [build-artifacts](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875412275/job/140101135735) | PASS | Separate hosted run: **Build dist on cache miss** and **Verify build artifacts** passed, including verification of 1,122 finalized Control UI sidecars. |

**Not verified as of 20:08 UTC:** The [primary CI run](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/actions/runs/45875412536) was still queued, with 219 jobs waiting for a runner after preflight. No hosted result was established for the focused resolver, Talk admission, or collection worker tests, primary build, production/test semantic typechecks, or lint. No dependency/Knip job was scheduled in the observed matrix; the earlier production unused-file result below is historical, not a rerun. This does not establish red-on-old/green-on-head regressions or real shared vocabulary through shipped Talk.

### Main refresh and review follow-up — November 26, 2026

The draft at `baab314d1b5486644e0a5e145f08dd2021cb2db1` contains both upstream `main` at `d344e991bd7a74142013b3508c5b333613ff7d72` and the prior PR head `bc79270a1ef44d26c05a0580ed6a6081a5271162`. The refresh had no conflicts. Compared with their respective bases, the original and refreshed feature deltas had identical paths and zero-context hunks (ignoring blob IDs and offsets) before the review fixes. No production path was enabled.

- Addressed ClawSweeper’s [canonical override finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205820#issuecomment-7185670785): resolve canonical precedence before building the alias index. The regression expects personal Alpha and shared beta to survive with no false conflict. The follow-up also makes the prototype’s prepared Talk admission single-use, with a regression for retry after provider creation fails. Neither regression claims to exercise a real provider.
- **Ran:** remote ancestry, exact tree and contributor-credit readback; `git diff --check`; Node syntax checks and pinned Oxfmt on the five edited TypeScript files; repository test-line ratchet against pinned main (1,461 added test lines = 400 standard + 1,061 allocated). The new test lines cover the separate resolver and relay contracts.
- **Static review:** bound Auto Review (OpenClaw, `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`, through P2) on the staged candidate against pinned main. The final run found no additional in-scope findings. The previously reported production Knip failure remains open: the collection service has no production registration pending the scope decision. No production entry or ignore was added to make it look used.
- **Not run on this head:** behavioral tests (including red/green runs of the new regression cases), a full build, semantic typecheck, lint, Knip rerun, or the stable-to-draft upgrade again. This session had no approved secretless runner for the fork's target code. The compatibility result below applies to the earlier pinned runtime only. No current-head CI pass or live provider/Talk behavior is claimed.

The real shared-vocabulary proof remains deferred: select an authorized catalog, show disclosure, verify the exact hints sent to a real provider, then verify transcript return and supported recovery through Talk. The owner, common personal/shared contract, persisted representation and retention, and admitted-request/revocation policy remain undecided in [#205633](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205633).

### Latest-stable saved-data compatibility — November 26, 2026

**PASS for the data exercised.** Tested the actual npm release `openclaw@2026.11.10` (`6ea542fd97e2`) → exact draft runtime `23d1c727c5ec` (tree `2881525aff81`). The branch had advanced from ClawSweeper's `56aef23a43ae` review by one documentation-only commit. No runtime or scope changes were made for this follow-up.

| Ran | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Candidate `pnpm build` (includes Control UI); served entry-module SHA-256 comparison | Built and served the exact candidate assets. The build reported CSS gzip (57.3 vs. 56.9 KiB) and chat-boot request (21 vs. 20) budget violations; this is not a clean budget result. |
| Stable `config set --batch-file`, `config validate`, `sessions.create`, and `backup create --no-include-workspace --verify` | Wrote fictional data through stable owners. Stopped stable and verified its backup before starting the candidate on the same isolated state and config. |
| Candidate `config validate`, `config get`, `talk.config`, `talk.catalog`, and `sessions.describe` | Config bytes unchanged; the exact timezone, Talk locale, and interruption setting loaded. The original session ID, key, and label reopened. Transcription remained unconfigured and no shared selection was exposed. This did not exercise speech. |
| Playwright Chromium, same origin and persistent browser profile | Dark appearance and the exact unsent New Session draft reloaded on stable and on the candidate; the restored draft was editable. This verifies rendered appearance, not an independent candidate profile-preference RPC read. |
| Focused MDX and `git diff --check` | Passed on the evidence-only change. |

**Not run:** real-provider speech, selected shared vocabulary through Talk, transcript recovery, managed updater, direct downgrade, backup restore, or new CI. No shipped personal-dictionary store was identified on stable, so no personal-term rows were seeded; [#205880](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205880) remains separate. The owner, persisted format, and mid-utterance revocation decision remain open; real shared-vocabulary behavior proof is deferred until scope is accepted.

[Detailed compatibility record](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/bc79270a1ef44d26c05a0580ed6a6081a5271162/docs/experiments/shared-dictation-vocabulary.md#observed-stable-to-draft-compatibility--november-26-2026).

### Historical prototype evidence

Full owner/procedure/AC mapping and benchmark methodology are in [the committed experiment record](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/56aef23a43aea74de1f20ed6e1cf81cc3c1756a5/docs/experiments/shared-dictation-vocabulary.md). A validation receipt binds source hashes, commands, raw logs, original-to-published commit mapping, and historical results to the published head. Evidence below is self-reported local execution and independent automated source review, not maintainer acceptance or CI success.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete physical dependency install | PASS: frozen lockfile, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, 215 workspaces; supply-chain check passed for 1,764 entries. |
| Standard vocabulary behavior | 39 passing cases across three files. Their initial combined unit-src command also ran the new worker suite in an incompatible thread owner and failed setup; the corrected worker run is separate below. |
| Real retained-worker integration | PASS: 4 cases in the standard isolated-process infra lane, with compiled production runtime declarations and synthetic grants. |
| Existing and vocabulary Talk relay | PASS: 30 cases across two files in the existing aggregate Gateway configuration; 18 existing regressions and 12 vocabulary cases. Provider callbacks remain synthetic. |
| Runtime selection / file ownership | PASS: 51 existing selection tests and the separately selected complete file-ownership audit. The latter selected one case and filtered out 40. The broader project-config suite stalled after two passing cases and was stopped by its unchanged 120-second no-output watchdog (exit 143); it is not a full-suite pass. |
| Targeted static proof | PASS: canonical tooling test type leaf, type-aware scripts lint after the GC repair, syntax-only lint on all 14 changed TS/MTS/MJS files, formatting on 15 supported changed files, and test-line budget (+1,435 net, 400 allowance, 1,035 allocated for distinct boundaries/real worker proof). |
| Core static proof | BLOCKED: canonical core types exited 137; native type-aware core lint received SIGKILL. Other full core/test/script type graphs are not claimed complete. |
| Documentation | Changed-document MDX sanity passed. Global link/anchor audit found eight failures outside this document in unchanged source/target files; the global audit is not a pass. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their external mirror. |
| Full build | BLOCKED: default preflight could not observe its memory limit. A supported explicit 1,536-MiB attempt completed protocol/scripts/assets/AI/packages, then main tsdown received SIGKILL; overall exit 1. |
| Required unused-file gate | FAIL: production scan reports `vocabulary-collections.ts` because the proposal has no production registration. Full-tree scan exhausted its 1,536-MiB JavaScript heap (SIGABRT). No fake entrypoint or ignore was added. |
| Fresh maximum-bound benchmark | EXECUTED, target partial: 20 warmups + 100 samples per operation/workload, all 5,000 terms. Combined p95: **50.20 / 43.72 / 41.22 ms** for compact / raw-cap / normalized-cap cases. The compact case misses the strict below-50-ms target. Linux x64, Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, Node 24.22.3. Occupancy counters are not cumulative allocations; auth/network/model/provider quotas remain unmeasured. Historical passing and initial failing runs are retained separately. |
| Required CI | NOT RUN to completion. At `56aef23a43aea74de1f20ed6e1cf81cc3c1756a5`, [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45774508027) reports `action_required` with zero jobs, and [Proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/runs/139754789345) is skipped. Metadata/dispatch success is not build/test proof. Upstream workflow action is required before those checks can execute. |
| Production qualification | NOT RUN: accepted host ACL/disclosure, production namespace, migration/rollback, accessible clients, real hint payload/quotas, spoken corpus, and M11/M10 recovery integration remain absent. |

The original worker failure was diagnosed as missing host-broker ownership in a thread. The existing database-worker registry routes the new test to a fork process. Full fixture-worker preparation also hit exit 137; independent inspection qualified these exact worker/relay tests for the existing production-runtime preset because their test helpers execute in Vitest and their child entries are production code. Broad/mixed selections retain the full graph. No compiler integrity, admission, IPC, lifetime guard, assertion, or timeout was weakened.

Independent agent review repaired and rechecked mutable selection across authorization awaits, provider-error leakage, sparse aliases, stage/provider admission, and the persisted-winner assertion in the two-editor test. A final review of the new worker/routing delta and explicit synchronous-major-GC callback found no remaining actionable code finding in that scope. This is automated source review, not a local ClawSweeper/autoreview tool result or human owner approval.

Current official OpenAI documentation confirms the existing adapter's optional transcription prompt field, but no live M06 hint request was made and exact current token/byte/term budgets remain unverified. The archived 2025 Cookbook's numeric prompt limit is historical only. The 5,000-term/400-KiB collection ceiling is not an advertised provider payload allowance; the committed record links the primary documentation and model-lifecycle constraint.

| AC | Status | Remaining production proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 — Authorized scope | PARTIAL | Accepted real membership/disclosure, scoped store opener and RPC guessed-ID/export matrix |
| 02 — Resolution | PARTIAL | Accepted P03/private personal lifecycle and visible effective-source/conflict controls |
| 03 — Provider contract | PARTIAL | Verified current endpoint fields, exact real budgets, authorized transmission and visible capabilities |
| 04 — Revocation | PARTIAL | Production STT/refinement/insertion races, accepted mid-utterance policy and explicit recovery |
| 05 — Concurrent edits | PARTIAL | Production namespace/authority and actual management conflict recovery; real worker CAS/reopen is now observed |
| 06 — Migration | PARTIAL | Accepted and exercised saved-state migration, rollback and retention |
| 07 — Offline lifecycle | PARTIAL | Actual client offline/reconnect reauthorization and personal-only recovery |
| 08 — Isolation | PARTIAL | Live adapter, tool/mode/route and cross-scope transport inspection |
| 09 — Accessibility/clients | BLOCKED | Selection, management, source/conflict and recovery UI with keyboard/screen-reader proof |
| 10 — Privacy | PARTIAL | Production telemetry/cache/admin/audit/export review and accepted retention |
| 11 — Performance | PARTIAL | Repeatable latency target, cumulative allocation/resource proof and actual provider quotas |
| 12 — Semantic regression | PARTIAL | Spoken common-word/identifier/negation/number/literal corpus and unaffected personal-only dictation |

Requested design decision: establish the vocabulary owner and common P03/M11 contract, map collection selection/management/export/provider disclosure onto existing live authority, and accept the namespace/representation/retention and minimal Talk integration. Keep this PR draft and the umbrella issue open until the agreed scope and required proof are delivered. No merge is requested.

prs.title: feat(ios): native Settings with plain copy, one text style per role and General first
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone and iPad, Settings is one long screen that mixes device controls, a Gateway status card, reconnect and diagnose actions, and Gateway setup. Device options are buried under a single "Device Settings" row, and the screen uses its own colored icons, red accents and type sizes. It doesn't look or read like Settings in the Control UI, so people have to relearn where things are on each device.

## User Impact

This is one of a series of pull requests that bring the iOS app in line with the Control UI. With this change alone, a person sees:

- **A native Settings list, General first.** The root has three groups. General holds Appearance (a Light, Dark or System picker), Voice & Talk, Permissions, Accessories, Keep screen awake, and Storage. App holds Sidebar and About. OpenClaw holds the Gateway row and Advanced. Rows use thin neutral icons and one text style per role, matching the Control UI.
- **Separate pages instead of one long Device Settings page.** Voice & Talk and Permissions are now their own pages. Permissions shows the agent's camera and Health access, then each iOS permission with its status and a link to iOS Settings. Accessories opens Apple Watch and ESP device setup.
- **A shorter Gateway page.** It offers Add Gateway, then Connection details and Diagnostics. Manual connection and advanced options sit in Connection details.
- **About** groups device information and Diagnostics, then Support, Website, Docs and the other links as plain rows. Third-party licenses live there too.
- **Sidebar** in Settings edits the pinned pages as a normal page inside Settings.
- **Storage** is a new page. It shows the size of the local chat cache and how many conversations it holds, and Clear Cache removes those local copies while keeping drafts and queued messages.
- **Advanced** opens the Dashboard settings when the connection has full access, and otherwise says that full access is required.
- **Plainer wording** throughout these screens, for example "Header names can’t include spaces or special characters."

Some parts still look old until later pull requests in the series land:

- Settings still opens full screen with the sidebar button, not as a sheet with a close button.
- The root has no Notifications, Chat or personal rows yet, and no Tools group with Skills and Plugins.
- The Gateway page is still titled "Gateway", and the saved-gateways list keeps its current layout.
- The list of pages under Sidebar is still the current set.

`docs/platforms/ios.md` describes Settings as it works in this PR, including Storage. The sheet and the Chat, Skills, Plugins, and Notifications pages belong to the later PRs that add them.

No setting or permission changes meaning. Clearing the chat cache removes only the local copies of conversations on this device.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root moves from one scrolling screen to a navigation list with one destination per topic, the way iOS Settings and the Control UI organize it. Device controls keep their existing preferences, consent prompts and iOS permission requests. Only where they appear changes. Gateway connection details move behind one row, so the root stays short for people who are already connected. The chat cache gets its own page, so the local copies of conversations are visible and can be cleared without touching drafts or queued messages. Text styles come from one small set of roles, so the same kind of label looks the same on every Settings page.

## Evidence

- The iOS app builds for the simulator with its SwiftFormat and strict SwiftLint build phases. `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` reports 0 violations, and `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0 files to format. The string catalog check reports no pending changes.
- Unit tests on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2): `SettingsHubTests`, `SettingsHubVisualProofTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests`, `NodeAppModelInvokeTests` and `ChatSessionsCodingTests`, 313 tests in all. All pass. This includes the new check that clearing the chat cache keeps drafts and queued messages.
- All five UI flows pass on the same simulator: connected Settings, offline device settings and saved appearance, returning to Chat from Gateway settings, reaching Watch Message Delivery, and keeping a valid custom header after reopening the editor. The unit and UI checks ran at `ca4ffeb5751d`; the follow-up changes only `docs/platforms/ios.md`, which passed the MDX check.
- [Verified clean and annotated Settings comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206496#issuecomment-7226999849) on the connected simulator fixture. The earlier series captures below show additional screens. No live Gateway or account data was used.
- [Simulator captures of the invalid custom header and Watch and Storage errors](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/206496#issuecomment-7227162302). A failed Watch discard preserves the message, and Storage can recover after local read and clear failures. The failure inputs were synthetic.
- A simulator test against a local WebSocket fixture verified that the global timeout warning appears only when both Gateway connections time out and clears after recovery. This does not cover the longer connection-setup message. In Gateway settings, a synthetic write failure kept the paired Gateway in the list; removing the fault and trying again removed the entry and showed confirmation.
- Advanced has integration coverage for active admin admission, the embedded route, upgrade guidance, and plain-text Gateway error responses. The Advanced page was not manually retested against a live Gateway.
- Not checked: a physical device, iPad layouts, larger Dynamic Type sizes, VoiceOver, the macOS app, a live Gateway connection, or a HealthKit API failure during the permission request.

## Screenshots

Before is on the left and After on the right.

Settings, light:

![Light Settings: one long screen with a Device group, a Gateway card and red actions on the left, a native list with General, App and OpenClaw groups on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61a97a88-24ae-449a-957f-fd8e5492a7b4)

Settings, dark:

![Dark Settings: the same long screen on the left, the same native list on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8266fe84-aba4-4b9f-b011-3bb0a7194f61)

Gateway page:

![Gateway page: status card, Reconnect, Diagnose and inline setup fields on the left, Add Gateway with Connection details and Diagnostics on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0aa1036b-2ca3-4bbb-a000-cf877084fcac)

Device Settings before, Permissions after:

![The old Device Settings page with red toggles on the left, the Permissions page with Agent access and iOS permissions on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79040653-6b41-4216-bc3f-a3fa1bcc6758)

About:

![About: links with colored icons and red labels on the left, a Device group with Diagnostics and plain Resources rows on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/164cc65d-184a-4b0f-bcf7-cd42732885fd)

Sidebar pages:

![Pages: a sheet with red icons and a Done button on the left, a page inside Settings with neutral icons on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a511171b-90a7-4fde-b790-01c4d6d61e96)

Storage (new, After only):

![Storage: the Chat cache group with Cache size and Cached conversations, and a Clear Cache button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dbba6d4-73cb-4ac6-8cae-54cde9b5dcc0)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## 2026.12.1-beta.1

### Highlights

- Updates: Git installations use prepared releases and a resident launcher, while package updates prepare without stopping the serving Gateway. (#203194, #203497) Thanks @obviyus.
- Prompt caching: compaction reuses the warm prompt cache across routes, read-only prewarms keep idle caches warm, and automatic compaction starts at 85% of the context window. (#204111, #204219, #204210) Thanks @obviyus.
- Templates: share an agent from its menu, preview a Template without expanding files into chat, and manage planned automations from chat cards. (#201644, #202060, #202126) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Session Share: pull authorized shared sessions over outbound WSS and open them in their source Control UI. (#201075, #203044) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Lean Gateways: share core worker code in one host and admit worker growth within a memory budget to reduce small-machine memory pressure. (#202495, #202507). Fixes #202377, #202376 Thanks @jalehman.
- Skills: browse and search the ClawHub catalog by category, and open installed skills as full pages rather than dialogs. (#202756, #202581) Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen and @vyctorbrzezowski.

### Changes

- Control UI: give Sessions its own rail destination and move Code Mode, Tool Search, and Templates out of Labs. (#201208, #203096) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski, @vincentkoc, @fuller-stack-dev, and @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Access management: administrators can share specific projects with restricted roles and assign profile roles from chat. (#203470, #202315). Fixes #202311 Thanks @jalehman.
- Trusted-proxy authentication: add opt-in Cloudflare Access JWT verification instead of relying only on forwarded identity headers. (#200376). Fixes #200361 Thanks @daniel-lxs.
- Knowledge: let agents list Slack channels, choose the reading token, and learn from Slack through Knowledge. (#202410, #202411) Thanks @jalehman.
- GBrain: connect through the plugin installer, including native installation without Bun on Apple Silicon Macs and x86-64 Linux. (#200625, #200987) Thanks @obviyus.
- Model settings: choose harnesses for primary and fallback models, and control individual plugin tools from Settings. (#203358, #201453) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski.
- OpenCode: sign in to OpenCode Console and OpenCode Go through the browser. (#202949) Thanks @obviyus.
- Codex: target a branch, commit, or custom instructions with `/codex review`. (#202114) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Automations: back off when a provider pushes back, allow up to eight extra runs when memory permits, and name new jobs from their prompts. (#197395, #197394, #201184) Thanks @daniel-lxs and @vyctorbrzezowski.
- Providers: add Nano Banana 2.1 image generation and route qualified Bedrock Converse streams through ClawRouter. (#200468, #192450) Thanks @markmcd, @obviyus, and @vincentkoc.
- Slack: present streamed reasoning as task rows and continue long native streams in follow-up messages. (#143882) Thanks @n1hility and @sallyom.
- Codex: update the bundled app-server and matching ACP runtime to 0.172.0, refresh protocol validation, and recognize externally managed GCP accounts during connector migration. Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- Windows updates: replace migrated state databases, keep read-only database readers from breaking upgrades, and restart correctly after rollback. (#204094, #204095, #204224). Fixes #204085, #204078, #204196 Thanks @obviyus.
- Update handoff: keep self-updates running through the first ready signal, run plugin maintenance after the replacement Gateway starts, and roll back stalled startups sooner. (#204215, #204127, #203990). Fixes #204035 Thanks @obviyus.
- Git updates: prevent half-switched checkouts when older November 17 main updaters encounter a schema change. (#204275) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Doctor and plugins: finish updates with npm-installed official provider plugins or plugins that do not ship a Doctor artifact. (#204122, #204129). Fixes #203604 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @AS76.
- Backups and reset: back up long-running installations with large session inventories, and leave state intact when a live Gateway refuses reset. (#203923, #202088). Fixes #203082, #202023 Thanks @vincentkoc, @sukhdeepjohar, @obviyus, @dygg2001, @etzelm, and @anmol0b.
- Installation: keep `openclaw` available in new terminals after `gateway install` runs from npx. (#203943). Fixes #203942 Thanks @Satoshi-Kusumoto.
- Chat history: preserve the reading position as old rows remeasure, keep earlier history reachable, and hold the top position when reading there. (#204153, #204216, #204220) Thanks @obviyus and @Patrick-Erichsen.
- Unread indicators: advance only after a new visible reply, excluding hidden coordination and failed child activity. (#204281, #204143). Fixes #204164 Thanks @obviyus.
- Subagents: settle undelivered child completions into parent history, preserve yield settlement through cleanup, and avoid duplicate final replies. (#204260, #204178, #203222, #204098) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus.
- Claude CLI: preserve completed tool calls and inline widgets across chat reloads. (#203877, #204102) Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski, @fonchaves, and @obviyus.
- ACP: settle prompts that also deliver to channels and keep replies alive while tool results are still returning. (#202048, #202276). Fixes #202047 Thanks @ElanHasson, @obviyus, and @vsgik.
- Codex sessions: prevent handoff stalls when a retired writer remains loaded. (#196172) Thanks @montrellcruse and @RomneyDa.
- OpenAI: include the system prompt in uncached ChatGPT Responses input and keep account limits aligned while loading. (#202720, #204264). Fixes #202372 Thanks @Avi974, @RomneyDa, @migelizaga-rgb, and @jesse-merhi.
- Model discovery: refresh cold catalogs during setup, report discovery failures in models status and Doctor, warn on small-context manual picks, and display provider plugin labels. (#202019, #194951, #200923, #204230). Fixes #202016 Thanks @etzelm, @VACInc, @daniel-lxs, @Satoshi-Kusumoto, @sallyom, and @obviyus.
- Teams and Feishu: deliver the remainder of rejected Teams stream endings without duplicating the reply, and honor Feishu card mode for non-streaming block replies. (#158429, #202368, #169681). Fixes #158103, #169550 Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @rdbartram, @obviyus, @Anurag-5ingh, and @name5566.
- Discord and Telegram: use live voice-transcription configuration, refresh native commands after registry replacement, and preserve linked identity in private Telegram topics. (#202362, #199743, #198832). Fixes #199612 Thanks @obviyus, @555aaditya, @eliavb43, and @dankarization.
- Quiet automations: preserve successful optional-silent collector runs, treat empty checklists as intentional skips, and avoid spurious failures after repeated result recording. (#164949, #202390, #202142). Fixes #164887, #203821, #202350, #202140 Thanks @jayzhou2309, @obviyus, @Hensarj, @ArthurBook, @herosuncy, and @jalehman.
- Automation delivery: notify script webhooks when restarts interrupt a run and route owner-targeted failure alerts to the owner rather than the last chat. (#204201, #189953). Fixes #204194, #189947 Thanks @daniel-lxs, @Satoshi-Kusumoto, and @obviyus.
- Templates: allow adding without model sign-in, use the adding device’s time zone for automations, and start ready Templates during background refreshes. (#204234, #202175, #202960). Fixes #204207 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @daniel-lxs, @Patrick-Erichsen, and @vincentkoc.
- PostgreSQL: let Gateways start with plugin-backed secrets and load Talk and plugins without worker-boundary failures. (#201976, #201063). Fixes #201969 Thanks @etzelm, @VACInc, and @Staruy.
- Doctor recovery: retry heartbeat migration after a full-disk archive write instead of leaving it permanently stuck. (#201345). Fixes #200083 Thanks @anmol0b, @sallyom, and @wangmiao0668000666.
- Credential and execution boundaries: apply credential limits to assistant media URLs, reject hidden shell-startup assignments in env commands, and bind realtime voice streams to signed calls. (#204154, #203934, #136506) Thanks @mmaps, @pgondhi987, and @drobison00.
- Packaged Windows: preserve managed GitHub command execution. (#201712) Thanks @bkudiess and @RomneyDa.
