prs.title: feat(feishu): Feishu / Lark leaves core for the official feishu plugin (installed by default, idle until configured)
prs.body:
## Review fix (head `d060f77674a7`)
Live leg K (Feishu in `plugins.disabled`, `FEISHU_*` set, default installer placed then removed `feishu`) logged two wrong lines per gateway start. A probe of `gateway.run_startup.recover_left_core_in` on `519860552ce8` showed both. On this head both are gone:

| `plugins.disabled` | `519860552ce8` | `d060f77674a7` |
|---|---|---|
| `[feishu]` + `_default_plugins_installed: [feishu]` | `…does not have, so it is off` logged **2×**; `'hermes-tag' platform plugin is not installed` logged + kept | off-line logged 1×, kept 1×; no hermes-tag line |
| `[feishu]` (catalog miss) | catalog-miss line logged 2×; hermes-tag line | 1×; no hermes-tag line |
| `[platforms/feishu]`, `[feishu-platform]` | hermes-tag line for `platforms/feishu` | nothing |

- `ac1d5b84ef6e` fix(left-core): the catalog miss / `so it is off` report stamps the row's failure marker. That changes the settings fingerprint, so `recover_at_startup` runs a second pass, and `_pending` reported the row again (`tried` only held installable rows). `_pending` now takes the start's `seen` set and skips a plugin an earlier pass handled, before any report. The hunk is identical in #159640. Test: `test_left_core_migration.py::test_a_start_reports_a_row_once_when_its_pass_repeats[gateway-start|watched-start]`, red on the old head (`assert 2 == 1` log records).
- `d060f77674a7` fix(feishu): `catalog_platforms._left_core_env` counts every left-core platform's `enable_env` as claimed, disabled or not. `FEISHU_*` belong to Feishu, and hermes-tag extends the Feishu adapter, so it is no substitute for a Feishu the user turned off. This reverses the earlier "a home that disables feishu is still told about hermes-tag". Test: `test_left_core_feishu.py::test_feishu_credentials_never_name_the_hermes_tag_override` (4 cases; `disabled-feishu` and `disabled-platforms/feishu` red on the old head).
- Local: the `test_left_core_*` + catalog_platform listing/install-race files ran 255 passed + 54 passed / 0 failed. Full `scripts/check` ran 22 checks, ok.

## What this does, in plain words

Feishu / Lark (as a Hermes messaging platform, plus its five `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*` document-comment tools) leaves Hermes core. It becomes the official `feishu` plugin in [NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/tree/main/feishu), maintained by Nous Research, installed by default on every home (catalog `tier: official`, `default: true`, like Weixin and QQ Bot) and idle until configured.

**Existing Feishu users do nothing.** The first `hermes update` (or the next agent/gateway start) installs the plugin once; the plugin's adapter connects in that same gateway start. Same env vars, same `platforms.feishu` config, same `FEISHU_HOME_CHANNEL`, same tool and toolset names, and the `feishu_*` tools stay off on the platforms where core had them off. **New users** get the plugin installed once by the default-plugin installer. Until a profile sets `FEISHU_APP_ID` + `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` (or `platforms.feishu` `app_id` / `app_secret`) it starts no adapter and adds **zero** Feishu names to the model's `tools[]` (hermes-official-plugins#517 gates the tools' `check_fn` on those credentials). Once they are set, the next session has the tools without a reinstall, on the Feishu platform only (they only work inside a Feishu comment run; `hermes tools` can still turn them on elsewhere). Removing the plugin sticks.

Slate (merge in this order): **1. this PR** (core removal, LEFT_CORE row, one-install-per-home seam) → **2.** NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#517 (the `feishu` plugin, history kept; its `plugins validate` is red on main until this lands: built-in `feishu_*` tool-name clash, expected) → **3.** NousResearch/hermes-agent#159650 (`plugin-catalog/feishu.yaml`, `hold`, `tier: official`, `default: true`, re-pinned to the merged plugin sha).

Built on `laneb/left-core-platform-predicate` (the shared `platform_in_use` factory); that commit is the first one here.

## Round 17 (head `cfe91a1c7942`)
- Rebased onto origin/main. Main's newer hot-start suite used `Platform.FEISHU` as the named profile's first fresh platform and in the parked-profile case; those now take `telegram` (`59a35d9efc8b`). That was this PR's red `Run tests 1/3`.
- **Silent off after removing the default copy** (Greptile on #159641/#159650): `443284d0addb` (same `_pending` hunk as #159640 `5b609cf830f8`, equal `git patch-id`). The `[removed]` case of `test_a_feishu_home_the_default_installer_reached_first_keeps_its_scope_and_is_not_reinstalled` now requires the one "…so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install feishu`" line (red on the old head, green here); the toolset scope is still kept.
- Review threads: `63da8b24f19d` (a non-list `requires_env` / `optional_env` reads as no env names; shared with #159640); `11c5a13f5fa4` (cron reports a skipped moved-platform destination; shared); `1ebbdf0b89ec` (a bot that binds no port writes `listener_base: null`, so the dashboard stops showing an earlier run's port); `83eb1d895bf4` (one default per plugin toolset: scoped only when every tool in it names platforms); `dc53e181708e` + `71aa9acbb1a9` (an automatic install keeps `plugins.disabled: [feishu]`; the notice names `hermes plugins enable feishu`); `cfe91a1c7942` (the hermes-tag notice names the replacement without claiming Feishu runs). Each has a red-on-old-head test.
- Local: the PR's touched test files + left-core / default-plugins / catalog-platform / platform-plugin / hot-start / held-route / bound-port suites + `tests/cron/`: 3,242 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped. `scripts/check --only health`, boundary lint, no-tmp-literals, doc links ok.

### Live, round 17 (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME, endpoints behind a closed proxy)
Trees: `v0.23.4` (stamped `0.23.4` by `deb_version.py --release-version v0.23.4` → `write_install_stamp.py`), and the removal heads stamped `0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z` by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4`. The fixture catalog pins qqbot `7e8bc4e` / feishu `2c8be75`, `default: true`. Each home had creds in `.env`, then ran v0.23.4's real `default_plugins.install_defaults` (the `hermes update` step): both plugins were placed idle and recorded in `_default_plugins_installed`.

| Leg | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|
| removed the idle copy (`hermes plugins remove <x>` on v0.23.4), then upgrade: new head | not reinstalled; logs `⚠ QQ Bot moved out of core into the 'qqbot' plugin, which this profile does not have, so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install qqbot`.`; one kept notice | not reinstalled; same line for `feishu`; one kept notice (logged twice on this first start, because the toolset-scope conversion changes the settings fingerprint and the start re-passes; the kept-notice queue dedupes) |
| same, old head (80868f4 / 99beefcc) | silent, not reinstalled | silent, not reinstalled |
| existing user (idle copy kept), upgrade | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` connects in the same start (refused at the closed proxy); `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]` | `hermes_plugins.feishu` `✓ feishu connected` in the same start; `_left_core_installed: [feishu]` |

Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 `c72b5ba9…` before and after.

## Round 16: staged transition instead of a version floor

The `>=0.23.5` floor is gone. Stable and canary both report 0.23.4 today (canary payloads read `0.23.4+canary.<stamp>`), so that floor locked every shipping build out, including a canary that has already dropped core's adapter. Both plugins now install on **Hermes 0.23.4 or later**. They do nothing while the running core still bundles the same platform. The check is whether core's files are present: `plugins/platforms/qqbot/` for QQ Bot; `plugins/platforms/feishu/` or `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` for Feishu. On such a core `register()` registers nothing and logs one DEBUG line (`... the plugin stays inactive until core drops it`), and core's own adapter and tools keep serving. The first core without them gets the plugin's adapter, with the same settings and tool names.

- Feishu's `plugin.yaml` now ships `provides_tools: []`. `hermes plugins validate` fails any declared name that collides with a built-in, and core still ships `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*`. On that core the plugin registers none of them, so it validates cleanly on main. **Follow-up after the core removal merges:** put the five names back in `provides_tools`. Until then, validate on the post-removal core reports "undeclared tools registered" for `feishu` only. Runtime is unaffected, because user plugins load eagerly and register the tools from `register()`. The catalog entry keeps listing the five tools.
- Seam used: the plugin's own presence check, which already existed. Main has no registry rule that prefers one side cleanly. Platforms are last-writer-wins, so the user plugin would replace core's adapter. Tools are core-wins, and the plugin's `register_tool` returns `None` with a WARNING on every start. Staying inactive avoids both.
- Cost on a core that still ships the platform: the package import, measured on a 0.23.4 CLI process at +0.08 s (qqbot) and +0.17 s (feishu).

**Rollout order:** fixed plugin PR merged → catalog entry re-pinned to the plugin's MERGED sha → check that the published catalog (`hermes plugins browse` / a catalog fetch from main) returns the entry → core removal merges LAST (→ Feishu only: the `provides_tools` follow-up).

### Live probe (real version strings, real installs, real `gateway run --force`)

Version strings came from the real producers. The `v0.23.4` worktree goes through git (`0.23.4`). The `canary.20261126T064809Z-v0.23.4` worktree got its stamp from `scripts/termux/deb_version.py --release-version <tag>`, then `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` with the Termux build's arguments (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`). The removal heads ran twice: once stamped by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4` (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`), and once through git (`0.23.4`, display `0.23.4+777`). The fixture catalog in each tree pins the pushed plugin commit (qqbot `7e8bc4e`, feishu `2c8be75`) with `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.4"` and `default: true`. Endpoints sat behind a closed proxy; each home had creds in `.env`.

| Leg | Core (reported version) | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing profile, default install on the old core | v0.23.4 (`0.23.4`) | installed + enabled; core adapter `hermes_plugins.platforms__qqbot` serves; plugin `tools []` + DEBUG stand-down | installed + enabled; core adapter `platforms__feishu` connects; plugin `tools []`; no shadow warnings |
| Same | canary.20261126 (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`) | same | same |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, git (`0.23.4`) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` attempts the token in the same start; no reinstall (plugin dir mtime unchanged) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.feishu` connects; 5 tools from `hermes_plugins.feishu.feishu_doc_tool`; no reinstall |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, canary-stamped (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`) | same | same |
| Existing profile, no plugin (left-core migration) | removal head, canary-stamped | installed once (`_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`) + plugin adapter in the same start | `✓ Installed the 'feishu' plugin…` + connects in the same start |
| Same | removal head, git | same | same |
| hermes-tag profile: stable, then removal head ×2 | v0.23.4, then canary-stamped removal head | — | stable: `Hermes Tag` serves Feishu over core, official plugin inactive. First removal start: one `⚠ The community 'hermes-tag' plugin…` line, also kept in `left-core-notices.jsonl` for the next attended turn, and the official plugin connects. Second start: no repeat |

Cross-check from the same runs: on the Feishu removal head, the default-installed qqbot plugin stays inactive (core still ships QQ Bot), and the reverse holds too. `hermes plugins validate` passes for both plugins on main, v0.23.4, the canary and the QQ removal head. Feishu on the Feishu removal head reports "undeclared tools registered" until the follow-up above. The real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 was the same before and after (`c72b5ba9…`).

**Round 16 commit `99beefcc`: one-time notice for hermes-tag users.** The community `hermes-tag` plugin overrides Feishu by importing core's `plugins.platforms.feishu.adapter`. On this core its Feishu override cannot load. `LeftCoreFeature` gains `converted_notice`, said once per home during the row's one-time toolset-scope conversion (`_record_migration`) whatever the install outcome. This catches the common staged case: the default installer placed `feishu` before the update, so no install outcome line is there to carry `notice`. The Feishu row's sentence appears only when `plugins/hermes-tag` is present. It reaches `hermes update` output, and at gateway/agent start the log plus the kept-notice queue for the next attended turn. Tests: `test_left_core_feishu.py::test_a_hermes_tag_home_is_told_once_feishu_runs_on_the_official_plugin[left-core|default]` fails on `d561c62ce397` (2 failed) and passes here. With `test_a_feishu_home_without_hermes_tag_hears_nothing_about_it`, `test_left_core_feishu.py` is 30 passed, and the left_core / default_plugins / catalog_platform / platform_plugin_install files are 279 passed / 0 failed. `scripts/check --only health` ok, boundary lint ok, no-tmp-literals ok. Shared commits with #159640 keep the same patch-id: `f9be92efa16b` = `dd3669581f63` and `d561c62ce397` = `80868f4d77c1`.

**Release note:** Feishu / Lark is now the official `feishu` plugin. If you use the community `hermes-tag` plugin, its Feishu override, which extended core's built-in Feishu adapter, stops loading. Feishu keeps running on the official plugin with your `FEISHU_*` settings, and Hermes tells each affected profile once.

_Round 16 supersedes the sections below wherever they mention a `>=0.23.5` floor, a probe tree stamped `0.23.5`, or a different merge order. The rollout order above is the current one._

## Changes

- **Removed:** `plugins/platforms/feishu/**`, `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py`, `tools/feishu_drive_tool.py`, `tools/feishu_lark.py`, the Feishu-only tests (22 files; they moved to the plugin), `Platform.FEISHU` (`Platform("feishu")` resolves once the plugin registers), the `hermes_cli/platforms.py` row, the toolsets `feishu_doc` / `feishu_drive` / `hermes-feishu` and the `hermes-gateway` include, the `platform.feishu.*` strings in all 17 locales (the plugin carries them in its own `_i18n.py`), the `_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS` / dashboard env-fallback / `hermes dump` rows, the cron home-target, webhook deliver, startup allowlist, `/update` allowlist and Channels-page order entries, and the ACP kind-map names.
- **Name-keyed core tables are now `PlatformEntry` traits the plugin sets** (no `"feishu"` checks left in core):
  - `binds_port_fn(extra)`: replaces `PORT_BINDING_CONDITIONAL_MODES = {"feishu": "webhook"}`. `platform_binds_port` asks the entry, so a multiplexed secondary's Feishu in webhook mode still runs in shared-listener mode, and websocket mode never counts as a port.
  - `listen_port`: replaces the dashboard topology table's `"feishu": ("webhook_port", 8765)` row.
  - `thread_reply_anchor`: replaces the `platform == "feishu"` checks in `_reply_anchor_for_event`, the progress/status metadata in `run_turn`, and the interim-commentary reply anchor in `stream_consumer_fallback`.
  - `opus_voice`: replaces `"feishu"` in `OPUS_VOICE_PLATFORMS` (auto-TTS `.ogg`).
  - `gateway.platform_registry.registered_trait()` reads them.
- **Migration** (`hermes_cli/left_core_migration.py`): a LEFT_CORE row `feishu` with `feishu_in_use = platform_in_use("feishu", ...)`. It counts as use when what made core run Feishu holds:
  - core's `EnvCred` row: `FEISHU_APP_ID` + `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` in the env;
  - core's `is_connected`: a `platforms.feishu` block carrying `app_id`;
  - the platform turned on in config;
  - a `feishu_doc` / `feishu_drive` / `hermes-feishu` toolset selected for another platform.

  An explicit `enabled: false` vetoes, and `plugins.disabled: [platforms/feishu | feishu-platform]` is not use. The row also carries:
  - `secret_env` / `private_env`, so the child-process strip set is **identical to main**: 9 `FEISHU_*` names in `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`, and the encrypt key / verification token in the adapter-secret tier. A test pins this.
  - `legacy_toolsets=("hermes-feishu", "hermes-gateway")`, so a disabled bundle keeps the tools disabled.
  - Derived `off_platforms`, so the `feishu_*` tools stay off everywhere except Feishu's own sessions, as when they lived only in `hermes-feishu`.
  - No placement notice, like the other official rows. `_feishu_notice` only adds a sentence when it applies to the home: `plugins.disabled` lists a bare `feishu` (which now turns the plugin off), or the profile sets `plugins.isolation: host` (platform adapters can't load there).
- **Review round 3** (`1bfbe97`):
  - a saved explicit `toolsets: [hermes-feishu]` resolves again: core's old bundle (core tools + `feishu_doc` + `feishu_drive`), built from the row's `legacy_toolsets`, only in a profile where the plugin registered both toolsets (`toolsets._left_core_bundle`, `left_core_migration.legacy_bundle_toolsets`);
  - a routing row whose platform is not registered yet (Feishu loaded only in a secondary profile at boot) is held and written back by main's held-route seam (#160253); this PR no longer carries its own copy;
  - `bind_listener` records the port it really bound and `_mark_connected` stamps it as `listener_base`, so the dashboard reports another profile's standalone Feishu webhook port without loading the plugin.
- **Round 4** (`afeb699`, Teknium's ruling: Feishu is a default plugin once its tools only appear when Feishu is set up):
  - one automatic install per plugin and home across both installers is main's seam (#160177: `_DEFAULT_INSTALLED_KEY` / `placed_by_default`, `default_plugins._recorded`); this PR only pins it for the Feishu row. **Difference for Feishu:** its row carries toolsets, so a home the default installer reached first still gets `_record_migration` (its core-era scope: `feishu_doc` / `feishu_drive` off where core had them off); only the install and the "not installed" notice are skipped. The QQ hunk skips the whole row, which would have left a migrated Feishu user's CLI/Telegram with the five tools. If this merges after those PRs, the `_pending` hunk conflicts; keep this version (it is a superset);
  - docs (en + zh-Hans) say installed by default, idle until configured.
- **Round 5** (`9df6569`, the Feishu gap: a new home that sets Feishu up had the five tools on CLI, Telegram and every other platform). A generic plugin-API seam, no Feishu name in core:
  - `ctx.register_tool(..., default_platforms=("feishu",))`: the tool's toolset defaults on for those platforms only, until the user saves a choice in `hermes tools`; a toolset named in a saved selection is on wherever it is named. Read at the one plugin-toolset default (`tools_config._enabled_plugin_toolsets`).
  - Carried where plugin toolset keys already travel: the plugin toolset key cache (`cache/plugin_toolset_keys.json`, field `toolset_default_platforms`, served while background discovery runs) and the gateway's `plugins.list` toolset rows (`default_platforms`), so a classic CLI on a gateway session resolves the same scope (`gateway_plugin_commands.toolset_default_platforms`). `toolsets()`'s return shape is unchanged.
  - Documented in the plugin guide (`developer-guide/plugins/index.md`). hermes-official-plugins#517 `18add6c` registers the five tools with it.
- **Kept:** the shared helpers Feishu inspired stay in core and keep working for the other adapters. Telemetry: the five tool names and the `feishu_doc`, `feishu_drive` and `hermes-feishu` toolsets stay valid as retired values in `shared_metrics_contract.py` (now 1,984 lines). The `hermes_agent/compat/required_names.py` rows for `plugins/platforms/feishu/*` stay; `generate_shims.py --check` passes. Session-source lists that only name a source (`tui_gateway` messaging sources, `session_rules`) stay, since the plugin keeps the name.
- **Docs:** `messaging/feishu.md` (+ zh-Hans) is now a short "moved to the official feishu plugin" page: installed by default, idle until `FEISHU_APP_ID` + `FEISHU_APP_SECRET`, the reinstall command, and the upgrade note. The tool/toolset references (+ zh-Hans), the messaging index (+ zh-Hans), `tools/AGENTS.md`, `plugins/AGENTS.md` (canonical adapter example is now `irc` only) and the bundled hermes-agent skill reference are updated. No optional skill named Feishu.

## Composite-round fixes (same hunk in #159640 and #159651)

- **Off-platforms come from the rows.** A row whose tools lived only in its own platform's bundle (Yuanbao, Feishu) sets `own_platform_only`, and `_derive_off_platforms` gives it every platform core knows plus every platform any LEFT_CORE row moved out. The hand lists `_YUANBAO_OFF_PLATFORMS` / `_FEISHU_OFF_PLATFORMS` are gone, so whichever of QQ Bot / Feishu merges second cannot leave `qqbot` off Feishu's list (or either off Yuanbao's). Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_left_core_off_platforms.py` (stand-in rows + the shipped rows).
- **Saved routes to a platform that left core behave the same for QQ Bot and Feishu.** Webhook route load accepts any LEFT_CORE platform (no hand-kept `qqbot` entry), so a route a secondary profile's plugin serves is not skipped. Cron `deliver: <platform>:<chat>` delivers through the plugin's sender once it is loaded; without the plugin the delivery error and the preflight message name `hermes plugins install <plugin>` instead of "no delivery target resolved". Test: `tests/cron/test_cron_left_core_platform_route.py` (red on the previous head: the no-plugin cases and the webhook load of the other left-core platforms).

## Round 12: rebased on main's enablers (#160253, #160177, #160180, #160183)

- **Dropped for main's copy:** the held-route hunks (`gateway/session.py`, `session_lifecycle.py`, `session_persistence.py`, `tests/gateway/test_unparsed_route_survives_save.py`) and the one-install-per-home `_pending` / `default_plugins._recorded` hunks. Shared hunks (predicate factory, `own_platform_only` + `_derive_off_platforms`, cron/webhook left-core routes) stay byte-identical to #159640. #159640's `/reload` fix for platform-plugin env names (`9ad0342f`) is cherry-picked as is, so whichever move lands first carries it.
- **New fix (red on the previous head in CI):** main's gateway-start catalog recovery stays quiet about a catalog platform whose credentials another platform serves (`hermes-tag` needs the same `FEISHU_*`). Core's bundled Feishu always served them. With Feishu moved out, a Feishu home without the plugin yet was told on every start that 'hermes-tag' is not installed, and `test_platform_plugin_install_race.py::test_a_catalog_platform_whose_credentials_another_platform_serves_is_not_reported` failed. Now the credentials of a platform that left core count as served unless the home disables that plugin, because the left-core migration reports its own outcome (`catalog_platforms._left_core_env`). Test: `test_left_core_feishu.py::test_a_feishu_override_is_reported_only_when_nothing_serves_the_feishu_credentials` (2 cases, `feishu-pending` red on the previous head).

- **Review fixes (Greptile, round 12):** a platform manifest whose `requires_env:` key has no value now parses as an empty list (`plugins_manifest.py`). The cherry-picked `/reload` hunk had unpacked it and taken discovery down. Test in `test_platform_plugin_env_injection.py`, red on the previous head. hermes-tag 0.5.0 imports `plugins.platforms.feishu.adapter`, so #159650 now caps that catalog entry at `<0.23.5`. Core keeps no shim for an internal path.

| leg (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME, process on the install's PM base generation without lark-oapi, fixture catalog feishu → official#517 `27e4756`, open.feishu.cn through a closed loopback proxy) | observed | P/F |
|---|---|---|
| existing user: `.env` FEISHU_APP_ID/SECRET, no plugin | 1 dependency install, "Plugin feishu: loaded its Python dependencies from the dependency environment published after this process started", `✓ Installed the 'feishu' plugin`, Lark `connect failed … 127.0.0.1:45309` 1.3 s later, same start, 1 "Gateway Starting", no hermes-tag line | PASS |
| running gateway, no creds, no plugin; `hermes config set FEISHU_APP_ID`, then `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` | 1st set: "Running gateway does not serve Feishu / Lark yet … `hermes plugins install feishu`"; 2nd: "Running gateway is installing the plugin …"; +6 s `✓ Installed`, deps adopted in-process, `Platform reconcile: installed ['feishu']` → `start=['feishu']`, Lark connect attempt, same PID | PASS |

prs.title: refactor: QQ Bot leaves core for the official qqbot plugin (installed by default, auto-migrated)
prs.body:
## Review fix (head `596edd4390b4`)
- `596edd4390b4` fix(left-core): a start reports each row once when its pass repeats. This is the same hunk as #159651 `ac1d5b84ef6e`. A catalog-miss or `so it is off` report stamps the failure marker, so the start re-passes, and `_pending` used to report the row again: the line was logged twice per gateway start. Test: `test_left_core_migration.py::test_a_start_reports_a_row_once_when_its_pass_repeats`, red on `4a9075b40157` (2 failed, `assert 2 == 1`) and green here. Local: `test_left_core_*` + catalog_platform files ran 267 + 17 passed / 0 failed. Full `scripts/check` ran 22 checks, ok. This PR has no hermes-tag change: its `catalog_platforms.py` has no `_left_core_env`.

## What this does, in plain words

QQ Bot (Tencent QQ's official Bot API v2, as a Hermes messaging platform) leaves Hermes core. It becomes the official `qqbot` plugin in [NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/tree/main/qqbot), maintained by Nous Research, and like Weixin it is **installed by default on every Hermes home** (catalog `default: true`), idle until a QQ App ID and secret are set.

**Existing users do nothing:** the first `hermes update` (or the next agent/gateway start) sees that the profile ran QQ Bot and installs the plugin from the catalog once, and that same gateway start serves it. Same `QQ_*` / `QQBOT_*` env vars (legacy `QQ_HOME_CHANNEL` included), same `platforms.qqbot` config, same `QQBOT_HOME_CHANNEL`. **New users** already have it: the existing default-plugin installer (`hermes_cli/default_plugins.py`) puts it on every home once, and with no QQ credentials the gateway never starts the adapter (zero qqbot log lines). Whichever installer runs first, each home gets exactly one automatic install, and a later `hermes plugins remove qqbot` sticks.

## Round 17 (head `a6f9ca44b9c0`)
- Rebased onto origin/main. Main's newer hot-start suite listed `Platform.QQBOT` among the named profile's fresh platforms; it now names `discord` (`b3e418368eea`).
- **Silent off after removing the default copy** (Greptile on #159641): a home that ran QQ Bot in core and removed the idle copy the default installer placed was skipped quietly after the upgrade. `5b609cf830f8` (same `_pending` hunk as #159651 `443284d0addb`, equal `git patch-id`) keeps the removal and says the existing "…so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install qqbot`" line on the install backoff. Test `test_a_qqbot_the_default_installer_placed_and_the_user_removed_stays_removed_and_is_said_off` is red on the old head (1 failed), green here. The docs page says the same.
- Review threads: `d31fbbfa076a` (the later of `qqbot` / `qqbot-platform` replaces the other, as the gateway reads them; 2 tests red → green); `e485f9960ac0` (a non-list `requires_env` / `optional_env` reads as no env names, so one bad manifest cannot stop plugin discovery; shared with #159651); `66f891f77f0c` (cron reports a destination skipped because its platform left core, also beside a delivered one and for a saved `origin`; shared); `304de8b2a9ea` + `a6f9ca44b9c0` (an automatic install keeps a `plugins.disabled` entry the home already lists; shared). The `/reload` env thread is answered inline: core's existing rule for its own names, unchanged.
- Local: the PR's touched test files + left-core / default-plugins / catalog-platform / platform-plugin / hot-start / held-route suites + `tests/cron/`: 2,760 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped. `scripts/check --only health`, boundary lint, no-tmp-literals, doc links ok.

### Live, round 17 (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME, endpoints behind a closed proxy)
Trees: `v0.23.4` (stamped `0.23.4` by `deb_version.py --release-version v0.23.4` → `write_install_stamp.py`), and the removal heads stamped `0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z` by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4`. The fixture catalog pins qqbot `7e8bc4e` / feishu `2c8be75`, `default: true`. Each home had creds in `.env`, then ran v0.23.4's real `default_plugins.install_defaults` (the `hermes update` step): both plugins were placed idle and recorded in `_default_plugins_installed`.

| Leg | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|
| removed the idle copy (`hermes plugins remove <x>` on v0.23.4), then upgrade: new head | not reinstalled; logs `⚠ QQ Bot moved out of core into the 'qqbot' plugin, which this profile does not have, so it is off. Run `hermes plugins install qqbot`.`; one kept notice | not reinstalled; same line for `feishu`; one kept notice (logged twice on this first start, because the toolset-scope conversion changes the settings fingerprint and the start re-passes; the kept-notice queue dedupes) |
| same, old head (80868f4 / 99beefcc) | silent, not reinstalled | silent, not reinstalled |
| existing user (idle copy kept), upgrade | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` connects in the same start (refused at the closed proxy); `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]` | `hermes_plugins.feishu` `✓ feishu connected` in the same start; `_left_core_installed: [feishu]` |

Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 `c72b5ba9…` before and after.

## Round 16: staged transition instead of a version floor

The `>=0.23.5` floor is gone. Stable and canary both report 0.23.4 today (canary payloads read `0.23.4+canary.<stamp>`), so that floor locked every shipping build out, including a canary that has already dropped core's adapter. Both plugins now install on **Hermes 0.23.4 or later**. They do nothing while the running core still bundles the same platform. The check is whether core's files are present: `plugins/platforms/qqbot/` for QQ Bot; `plugins/platforms/feishu/` or `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` for Feishu. On such a core `register()` registers nothing and logs one DEBUG line (`... the plugin stays inactive until core drops it`), and core's own adapter and tools keep serving. The first core without them gets the plugin's adapter, with the same settings and tool names.

- Feishu's `plugin.yaml` now ships `provides_tools: []`. `hermes plugins validate` fails any declared name that collides with a built-in, and core still ships `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_*`. On that core the plugin registers none of them, so it validates cleanly on main. **Follow-up after the core removal merges:** put the five names back in `provides_tools`. Until then, validate on the post-removal core reports "undeclared tools registered" for `feishu` only. Runtime is unaffected, because user plugins load eagerly and register the tools from `register()`. The catalog entry keeps listing the five tools.
- Seam used: the plugin's own presence check, which already existed. Main has no registry rule that prefers one side cleanly. Platforms are last-writer-wins, so the user plugin would replace core's adapter. Tools are core-wins, and the plugin's `register_tool` returns `None` with a WARNING on every start. Staying inactive avoids both.
- Cost on a core that still ships the platform: the package import, measured on a 0.23.4 CLI process at +0.08 s (qqbot) and +0.17 s (feishu).

**Rollout order:** fixed plugin PR merged → catalog entry re-pinned to the plugin's MERGED sha → check that the published catalog (`hermes plugins browse` / a catalog fetch from main) returns the entry → core removal merges LAST (→ Feishu only: the `provides_tools` follow-up).

### Live probe (real version strings, real installs, real `gateway run --force`)

Version strings came from the real producers. The `v0.23.4` worktree goes through git (`0.23.4`). The `canary.20261126T064809Z-v0.23.4` worktree got its stamp from `scripts/termux/deb_version.py --release-version <tag>`, then `scripts/write_install_stamp.py` with the Termux build's arguments (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`). The removal heads ran twice: once stamped by the same producer for `canary.20261127T024356Z-v0.23.4` (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`), and once through git (`0.23.4`, display `0.23.4+777`). The fixture catalog in each tree pins the pushed plugin commit (qqbot `7e8bc4e`, feishu `2c8be75`) with `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.4"` and `default: true`. Endpoints sat behind a closed proxy; each home had creds in `.env`.

| Leg | Core (reported version) | QQ Bot | Feishu |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing profile, default install on the old core | v0.23.4 (`0.23.4`) | installed + enabled; core adapter `hermes_plugins.platforms__qqbot` serves; plugin `tools []` + DEBUG stand-down | installed + enabled; core adapter `platforms__feishu` connects; plugin `tools []`; no shadow warnings |
| Same | canary.20261126 (`0.23.4+canary.20261126T064809Z`) | same | same |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, git (`0.23.4`) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.qqbot` attempts the token in the same start; no reinstall (plugin dir mtime unchanged) | plugin adapter `hermes_plugins.feishu` connects; 5 tools from `hermes_plugins.feishu.feishu_doc_tool`; no reinstall |
| Upgrade of that home | removal head, canary-stamped (`0.23.4+canary.20261127T024356Z`) | same | same |
| Existing profile, no plugin (left-core migration) | removal head, canary-stamped | installed once (`_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`) + plugin adapter in the same start | `✓ Installed the 'feishu' plugin…` + connects in the same start |
| Same | removal head, git | same | same |
| hermes-tag profile: stable, then removal head ×2 | v0.23.4, then canary-stamped removal head | — | stable: `Hermes Tag` serves Feishu over core, official plugin inactive. First removal start: one `⚠ The community 'hermes-tag' plugin…` line, also kept in `left-core-notices.jsonl` for the next attended turn, and the official plugin connects. Second start: no repeat |

Cross-check from the same runs: on the Feishu removal head, the default-installed qqbot plugin stays inactive (core still ships QQ Bot), and the reverse holds too. `hermes plugins validate` passes for both plugins on main, v0.23.4, the canary and the QQ removal head. Feishu on the Feishu removal head reports "undeclared tools registered" until the follow-up above. The real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 was the same before and after (`c72b5ba9…`).

**Round 16: no code change in this PR.** The floor lived only in the plugin and catalog: official#520 `7e8bc4e`, catalog #159641 `7cd30f6`. The live table above ran this head (`80868f4d77c1`) as a git checkout and canary-stamped. Shared commits with #159651 keep the same patch-id: `dd3669581f63` = `f9be92efa16b` (predicate factory) and `80868f4d77c1` = `d561c62ce397` (empty `requires_env`).

_Round 16 supersedes the sections below wherever they mention a `>=0.23.5` floor, a probe tree stamped `0.23.5`, or a different merge order. The rollout order above is the current one._

## Slate (merge order)

1. **This PR** (core removal + LEFT_CORE row)
2. NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#520, the `qqbot` plugin (history kept: 157 commits; replaces the closed Labs PR NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#110)
3. Data-only catalog entry: NousResearch/hermes-agent#159641 (`tier: official`, `default: true`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.5"`; `hold`, re-pinned to the merged plugin sha)

Until 3 lands, a migrating home logs "cannot find in the plugin catalog yet" plus the notice and retries with backoff; a release never sees the gap if all three land before it.

## Changes

- **Removed:** `plugins/platforms/qqbot/**` and its 8 test files (moved to the plugin), `Platform.QQBOT` (`Platform("qqbot")` resolves once the plugin registers), `toolsets.py` `hermes-qqbot` and its `hermes-gateway` include, the `hermes_cli/platforms.py`, `tools_config`, `dump`, setup home-channel and web-messaging rows, the `QQ_*` `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` / env-key list entries, webhook deliver set, startup allowlist list, `/update`'s built-in list entry (the plugin's entry keeps `allow_update_command=True`), the shipped `qqbot: [hermes-qqbot]` row in `cli-config.yaml.example`, the compat required-name rows for the deleted folder (as the Yuanbao/HA moves), and the qqbot boundary-baseline lines. Shared tests drop only their qqbot cases.
- **Migration** (`hermes_cli/left_core_migration.py`): a `LEFT_CORE` row `qqbot` whose `in_use` is one `platform_in_use("qqbot", ...)` call replicating core's gate on main (`register.is_connected` + the `EnvCred` row): `app_id` + `client_secret` from the merged `platforms.qqbot` block (extra or top level; a top-level `qqbot:` block bridged), else `QQ_APP_ID` + `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in the home's env layers / secret scope; `platforms.qqbot` on; or `hermes-qqbot` selected for another platform (the Home Assistant precedent). `enabled: false`, or `plugins.disabled` naming `platforms/qqbot` / core's manifest name `qqbot-platform`, is not use. The row:
  - `plugin_key="platforms/qqbot"`, `plugin_names=("qqbot-platform",)`: core's old disable keeps holding over the plugin;
  - `secret_env=QQ_CLIENT_SECRET`, `private_env` = the other manifest names: `_HERMES_PROVIDER_ENV_BLOCKLIST`, `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS` and `_ADAPTER_SECRET_ENV` are **identical to main** (checked by importing both trees; 14 QQ_/QQBOT_ names). `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` joins `QQ_STT_API_KEY` on `local_env_policy`'s short adapter-secret list because `gateway_restart_env` reads that set directly;
  - no toolsets/off_platforms/legacy_toolsets: `hermes-qqbot` carried only core tools and the plugin registers none; Yuanbao's derived `off_platforms` now lists `qqbot`;
  - `platform="qqbot"`, `enable_env`, and `_qqbot_notice`: no placement sentence (official rows carry none, as Feishu's), only what changed for the home: a bare `qqbot` in `plugins.disabled` now turns it off, and `plugins.isolation: host` keeps a catalog platform adapter off. Yuanbao keeps its own Labs notice unchanged.
  - Profile-gate detection now takes every LEFT_CORE platform as a gate prefix, so `QQBOT_*_ALLOWED_*` stays a profile gate without `Platform.QQBOT`. This also makes `YUANBAO_*` / `HOMEASSISTANT_*` gate names count again, as they did before those platforms left the enum. `QQ` stays in `_EXTRA_GATE_ENV_PREFIXES`.
- **One automatic install per plugin and home** comes from main (#160177: left-core `_pending` + `_DEFAULT_INSTALLED_KEY`, default_plugins `_recorded`); the QQ Bot row only joins it. Held routes for a late-registering platform also come from main (#160253); this PR no longer carries its own copy of either.
- **Kept:** the shared own-policy helpers (comments only), cron's home-target order and the `QQ_HOME_CHANNEL` legacy alias, doctor's rename warning, the `QQ_` prefix alias for profile channel ownership, the `session_rules` route enum, desktop/TUI source lists. `hermes-qqbot` stays valid as a retired telemetry toolset value (`RETIRED_TOOLSET_NAMES`; the contract file is 1,982 lines).
- **Docs:** `messaging/qqbot.md` (+ zh-Hans) is now a short "moved to the official qqbot plugin, installed by default" page; toolsets reference, messaging index and other mentions say the same.

## Live migration probe

Real `gateway run --force` processes (own PID, killed after ~45 s) in a fake `HOME` + `HERMES_HOME` + `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` + `HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR`, on a `git archive` of this head `2d034b04c21`. The catalog fixture's `qqbot` entry is `tier: official`, `default: true`, pinned to plugin PR #520 head `20a9a52ed021`. All outbound HTTP goes through a proxy on a closed loopback port (QQ's token URL is not env-overridable; `NO_PROXY` exempts the git/package hosts), so the connect is refused after the adapter is created. The md5 of the real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` was equal before and after (`d57827e7…`).

| Leg | Home | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 first start | `QQ_APP_ID`+`QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env` | `✓ QQ Bot moved out of core — installed the 'qqbot' plugin from the catalog (QQ_*/QQBOT_* settings … unchanged).` once; 0 lines with "not supported"/"Labs"; the **plugin's** adapter (`hermes_plugins.qqbot.adapter`) fetches a token (refused) in the SAME start; `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`, enabled |
| 2 second start | same home | no install line; plugin tree mtime unchanged; plugin adapter connects again |
| 3 fresh, no creds | `install_defaults(home)` (fixture default) then a gateway start | `✓ Installed default plugin 'qqbot'`, enabled, `_default_plugins_installed: [qqbot]`; the gateway logs **zero** qqbot lines (no warning, no error), `No messaging platforms enabled.`, no connection opened |
| 4a install-once | creds; `migrate_home` → `install_defaults` → `migrate_home`, then `hermes plugins remove qqbot`, then both again | exactly 1 install (left-core), `install_defaults -> {'installed': [], 'owed': []}`; after remove neither reinstalls (dir stays gone) |
| 4b install-once | creds; `install_defaults` → `migrate_home` → `install_defaults`, remove, both again | exactly 1 install (default), `left_core -> []`; after remove neither reinstalls |

Earlier legs on the previous head (base creds = core adapter; no catalog entry = "cannot find in the plugin catalog yet"; multiplex secondary with creds only in `profiles/b/.env` = installed only into b and connects there) are unchanged by this placement change. First start also logs that the plugin's `qrcode` dependency was installed after the process started (setup-only; harmless).

## Round-12 rebase onto the merged enablers (head `1ee397fc8c24`)

Rebased onto main after #160253 / #160177 / #160180 / #160183 / #160200. Dropped this PR's own copies for main's: every `gateway/session.py` / `session_lifecycle.py` / `session_persistence.py` hunk and `tests/gateway/test_unparsed_route_survives_save.py` (main's `test_held_route_late_platform.py` covers the same cases), and the `_pending` / `default_plugins` one-install hunks. `git diff origin/main -- gateway/session*.py hermes_cli/default_plugins.py` is empty. The predicate factory and the off-platforms/cron/webhook commit are unchanged (same patch-ids), so other move PRs can carry them byte-identically.

Live, real `gateway run --force` on a `git archive` of this head, fake `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/lock dir, fixture catalog `qqbot` (official, `default: true`) pinned to #520 head `20a9a52ed021`, all other HTTP through a closed loopback proxy. Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 equal before/after (`d57827e7…`).

| Leg | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A existing user | `QQ_APP_ID`+`QQ_CLIENT_SECRET` in `.env`, no plugin | one `✓ Installed the 'qqbot' plugin from the catalog for QQ Bot…` line; `hermes_plugins.qqbot.adapter` fetches a token (refused) in the same start and retries; `_left_core_installed: [qqbot]`, enabled |
| B creds added live | fresh home, gateway running ~60 s (no qqbot dir), then `hermes config set QQ_APP_ID …` and `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET …` | 2nd `config set` prints "Running gateway is installing the plugin this platform needs…"; the live reconcile installs `qqbot` and the plugin adapter starts in the same process ~10 s later, no restart |
| C setup listing | `available_catalog_platforms()` | fresh home lists `qqbot` (`official`, installable); the leg-B home (installed) does not |

The probe tree carries an install stamp with `baseVersion 0.23.5` because #520 declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.5"` and main currently reports 0.23.4; without it the install is refused with the version message.

## Composite-round fixes (same hunk in #159640 and #159651)

- **Off-platforms come from the rows.** A row whose tools lived only in its own platform's bundle (Yuanbao, Feishu) sets `own_platform_only`, and `_derive_off_platforms` gives it every platform core knows plus every platform any LEFT_CORE row moved out. The hand lists `_YUANBAO_OFF_PLATFORMS` / `_FEISHU_OFF_PLATFORMS` are gone, so whichever of QQ Bot / Feishu merges second cannot leave `qqbot` off Feishu's list (or either off Yuanbao's). Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_left_core_off_platforms.py` (stand-in rows + the shipped rows).
- **Saved routes to a platform that left core behave the same for QQ Bot and Feishu.** Webhook route load accepts any LEFT_CORE platform (no hand-kept `qqbot` entry), so a route a secondary profile's plugin serves is not skipped. Cron `deliver: <platform>:<chat>` delivers through the plugin's sender once it is loaded; without the plugin the delivery error and the preflight message name `hermes plugins install <plugin>` instead of "no delivery target resolved". Test: `tests/cron/test_cron_left_core_platform_route.py` (red on the previous head: the no-plugin cases and the webhook load of the other left-core platforms).

## Tests

- Round 12 (this head): touched tests + `test_left_core_*`, `test_default_plugins*`, `test_held_route_late_platform`, `test_platform_hot_start`, `tests/cron/`, catalog-platform/reconcile files via `scripts/run_tests.sh`: 234 files, 2,581 passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped (Windows-only). CI 16 passed / 20 skipped.
- New `tests/hermes_cli/test_left_core_qqbot.py` (21 cases): `in_use` true for `.env` creds, config-only extras, `platforms.qqbot` on, a top-level `qqbot:` block, `hermes-qqbot` on another platform; false for a fresh home, half a credential set, `enabled: false` with env creds, `plugins.disabled` `platforms/qqbot` / `qqbot-platform`; install once with no placement notice; a plugin the default installer placed and the user removed is not reinstalled by left-core, and vice versa; gate-env and strip-set parity. **Red on base** `70634248084b` (15 failed, 4 passed: the parity and fresh-home cases hold there by design), green on head.
- 78 touched/related files through `scripts/run_tests.sh` (fake HOME): 1,566 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped (previous head); after this placement change the left-core + default-plugin files: 131 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/check --only health`, `boundary_lint.py --check`, ruff on touched files, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_doc_links.py`: ok.
- Plugin suite against a `git archive` of this branch (QQ Bot dir and enum member gone): 116 passed; `hermes plugins validate` passed; `scan_plugin` `safe` on main and `v0.23.4`.

## Not covered

- Version gate: #520 needs Hermes >= 0.23.5. On a main checkout that still reports 0.23.4, a QQ Bot home gets "requires hermes >=0.23.5" and retries at the next start; it resolves once the release ships.

- The QQ backend itself: every connect is refused at loopback once the adapter exists.
- The multiplexed-secondary leg uses creds in the secondary's `.env`, not an external secret source (that path is the shared Yuanbao code, unit-tested there).
- `required_names.py` rows dropped as in the Yuanbao move: an update swap from v0.22.3–v0.23.2 no longer finds the QQ folder during the swap scan.
- Open PRs touching the old `plugins/platforms/qqbot` path are not ported here; they belong in hermes-official-plugins now.

prs.title: fix(plugin-catalog): update talaria-webui to 1.7.0
prs.body:
Updates Talaria WebUI's optional API plugin from 1.6.2 to 1.7.0, following #153859. Version, source, documentation and gallery URLs are pinned to `2b413412f959449c8e47174841c39ece43218fb5`.

- Use the session store Hermes 0.23.3 introduced. On current Hermes, 1.6.2's rewind, branching, history search, response details, context meter and slash commands were unavailable, and runs skipped the profile's instructions and saved model.
- Require Hermes 0.23.5 (`requires_hermes` in both `plugin.yaml` and this entry, up from 0.21.5) and remove the code paths for older releases.
- Release a `/compress` session lease that stops unexpectedly instead of holding it for five minutes, and recheck the transcript just before a rewind writes.
- Measure the context meter against the window Hermes compacts at.
- After an update, keep a running gateway on the code it loaded and report that a restart is due.

[Changes since the published pin](https://github.com/liamsmith86/talaria-webui/compare/2001c5b0fa0aac70e5cf8aa129068a0fe932d03f...2b413412f959449c8e47174841c39ece43218fb5) · [Plugin README](https://github.com/liamsmith86/talaria-webui/tree/2b413412f959449c8e47174841c39ece43218fb5/src/talaria/hermes_plugin)

Requires Hermes >=0.23.5 in its default `in_process` mode. On an older Hermes, `hermes plugins update` keeps 1.6.2 until Hermes is updated. Update Talaria to 0.4.0, then restart the full gateway process after active work finishes.

## Data and permissions

Unchanged: the same `api_server` handler, five hooks, local storage and disclosures. The entry's description stays as it is.

## Validation

- [Talaria full CI](https://github.com/liamsmith86/talaria-webui/actions/runs/46116226926) of this tree: platforms, browsers, native Hermes v0.23.5 and the install walkthrough passed, as did the [Hermes main and latest-release run](https://github.com/liamsmith86/talaria-webui/actions/runs/46116229050).
- Hermes's catalog CI scripts pass locally at `d71a65744c`: `validate_plugin_catalog.py`, `catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py` (security scan `safe`, no core overrides) and `catalog_core_imports.py check`.
- Internal-import warnings against the published pin: three removed (`agent.context_compressor.split_user_originated_turn`, `tools.clarify_tool.clarify_tool` and `TIMEOUT_RESPONSE`) and four added: `session_rules.turns.split_user_originated_turn` (the same helper's new home), `process_identity.holder_namespace_token` (replaces the plugin's copy of it), `agent.turn_facade_lease.DurableTurnLease` (the `/compress` lease) and `gateway.session_ingress_media.native_inputs_root` (removing a failed branch's media).
- Rehearsed the catalog CLI upgrade from 1.6.2 to this pin in an isolated home on Hermes main: no new hooks to confirm, the plugin stays enabled, and a repeated update is a no-op.

prs.title: fix(agent): reinforce lean compaction summary instruction and reject tool-call replies
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes lean-mode context compaction where local/smaller models continue the conversation instead of writing a structured summary because the closing user turn only pointed back at the typed turns while the summarization instructions sat tens of thousands of tokens earlier in the system message.

1. Appends a concise closing `TASK REMINDER` directly in `TYPED_TURNS_POINTER` (still inside the final `role="user"` message, preserving role-typing and system-prefix caching) instructing the model not to continue the conversation or call tools and to emit only the structured checkpoint summary.
2. Rejects summarizer responses that attempt `tool_calls` (`finish_reason == "tool_calls"` or non-empty `message.tool_calls`) in `_call_summary_llm()` via `response_attempted_tool_calls()`, so a model-generated agent continuation routes through retry/fallback instead of being persisted as the checkpoint summary.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160985

- `agent/context_compressor.py`: Check `response_attempted_tool_calls()` in `_call_summary_llm()` before accepting content.
- `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_summary_roles.py`: Add regression tests for the closing task reminder and tool-call response rejection.

prs.title: fix(plugins): send explicit User-Agent on outbound A2A requests
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an explicit `User-Agent` header (`hermes_user_agent("hermes-agent-a2a")`) to outbound A2A HTTP requests when the caller has not already supplied one, and surfaces HTTP 403 response details instead of assuming every 403 is a bad bearer token.

Previously, `plugins/platforms/a2a/tools.py::_http_json()` built `urllib.request.Request(...)` without a `User-Agent`, so `urllib` sent `Python-urllib/3.x`. Cloudflare's default Browser Integrity Check treats that User-Agent as a bot signature and rejects `a2a_discover`, `a2a_call`, and `a2a_orchestrate` with HTTP 403 (`error code: 1010`), which `_HTTP_CALL_ERRORS` then reported as a token error. Push callbacks in `plugins/platforms/a2a/security.py::post_callback()` now share the same default header helper (`default_user_agent_headers`).

## Related Issue

Fixes #161003

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/a2a/security.py`: Add `default_user_agent_headers()` (non-mutating, case-insensitive `User-Agent` check, lazy `hermes_user_agent("hermes-agent-a2a")` call) and apply it in `post_callback()`.
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/tools.py`: Apply `security.default_user_agent_headers(headers)` in `_http_json()`; add `_http_error_detail()` so HTTP 403 errors in `a2a_discover` and `a2a_call` include a concise body snippet and note proxy/WAF rules alongside token checks.
- `tests/plugins/test_a2a_outbound_user_agent.py`: Add tests for default/custom `User-Agent` in `_http_json` and `post_callback`, and HTTP 403 error detail formatting in `a2a_discover` / `a2a_call`.

## How to Test

1. Run `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_a2a_outbound_user_agent.py tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py tests/plugins/test_a2a_callback_ssrf.py tests/hermes_cli/test_deferred_platform_client_tools.py -q`.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add helmswap
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/helmswap.yaml`, for the HelmSwap plugin. It is an Agent Plugins v1 package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + two `SKILL.md` files) that connects Hermes to HelmSwap's hosted MCP server at `https://helmswap.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in). The server offers two tools: `get_quote` (read-only swap quote) and `build_swap` (an unsigned swap transaction for the user's own wallet to sign) on Solana, Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Ink, HyperEVM, Elysium and Arc. The fee is disclosed in every quote.

I own the plugin repository (`gambrelcolby63/helmswap-agent-plugins`, submitted by the owner under rule 5). The entry pins `96187994e6262f4353791b00f78f86905349c6e1`, subdir `plugins/helmswap`. It follows the shape of the existing `aave-mcp` entry.

## Hermes surfaces used

Configuration only: one MCP server declaration and two skills. No Python, no hooks, no middleware, no `requires_env`, no desktop surface.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Network:** every tool call goes to `helmswap.com`. The privacy policy (https://helmswap.com/privacy, last updated November 27, 2026) describes HelmSwap as a non-custodial swap interface for Solana, Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Ink, HyperEVM, Elysium, and Arc. It states that the user reviews and signs every transaction in their own wallet, that this server never signs and never broadcasts, and that ordinary technical logs typically include IP address, request path, user-agent and timestamps. A wallet address passed to `build_swap` is processed to prepare the unsigned transaction. It states the interface uses no third-party product-analytics or advertising SDKs.
- **Keys:** the server never receives private keys or seed phrases and never signs or broadcasts. `get_quote` is read-only. `build_swap` returns an unsigned transaction; the user signs in their own wallet. The package marks the server `untrusted`, so Hermes asks before write-capable calls.
- **Solana:** Solana builds need a free HelmSwap API key sent as an `X-Helm-Key` header. The package does not configure one; the README explains where to set it. EVM chains need no key.
- **No self-update, no binaries, no background process.** The tool set is served by the remote server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha (same disclosure as `aave-mcp`).
- **Rule 20:** not built around any one coin or token. It is a multi-chain swap quote and transaction-building service (exchanges and markets are listed as fine).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate plugins/helmswap` on a checkout at the pinned commit: portable manifest, server trust `untrusted`, security scan `safe`, "Validation passed" (run locally on Hermes 2026.9.24).
2. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: OK with the entry added.
3. `hermes plugins install helmswap`, then ask: "Quote 0.05 ETH to USDC on Base." The agent calls `get_quote` and reports the net output and fee. Nothing is signed or sent.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] Searched existing PRs; no existing HelmSwap entry
- [x] Only one file added: `plugin-catalog/helmswap.yaml`
- [x] Plugin validation passes at the pinned commit

prs.title: catalog: add a2a-async — mTLS A2A task admission and status
prs.body:
## What & why

Adds `a2a-async` to the plugin catalog: a stdlib-only, mutually-authenticated
asynchronous A2A (`protocol v1.0`) task-admission and status plugin, maintained in
its own repo (<https://github.com/davewilliamson/hermes-a2a-extended>).

It is the server-side half of a bounded agent-to-agent transport: a `kind: platform`
mTLS JSON-RPC listener that admits tasks from trusted peers, records a durable
receipt, and lets callers poll for results. It exposes two tools
(`a2a_extended_dispatch`, `a2a_extended_status`) and a `pre_approval_request` hook so
a caller cannot drive the agent as a shell, route to another profile, or pick scope.

Owners are intentionally kept independent ("community" tier); the repo ships MIT
licence, gitleaks + pytest CI (ubuntu + macOS), and full docs (install, config,
architecture, security, testing, troubleshooting) plus an authoritative `SPEC.md`.

## Disclosure

- Opens an **inbound mTLS listener** (`ThreadingHTTPServer`); requires
  mutually-authenticated TLS.
- Reads its **own CA / server cert / private key** and **per-peer client-certificate
  SHA-256 fingerprints plus directional bearer-token files** from paths declared in
  `config.yaml` (nothing from `.env`, `auth.json`, or other tools' credential stores).
- Stores a **local SQLite receipt/idempotency journal**.
- Makes **no outbound network calls except to the configured A2A peer**.
- Runs **in-process on the gateway event loop**; no background process.
- Ships **no telemetry**.
- **Requires operator approval before enabling** on any machine.

## How to test

```console
$ hermes plugins validate a2a-async          # manifest, capability probe, security scan, no-core-override
$ hermes plugins install https://github.com/davewilliamson/hermes-a2a-extended \
      --ref d267431f400b286d8e9916848d0affd060038b06 --subdir a2a-async
$ hermes plugins list                        # a2a-async present, tools a2a_extended_dispatch/status
```

`hermes plugins validate` passes clean at the pinned SHA (manifest parses,
`requires_hermes >=0.23.0` parses, capability probe runs in isolation, declared
tools/hooks match registrations, security scan safe, no runtime rebinds of Hermes
core).

## Platforms

- macOS (developed/verified on M-series, macOS 26.x)
- Linux (CI-tested on ubuntu-latest)
- Windows not tested; stdlib-only so expected to work but undeclared.

## Related issues

N/A (new entry).

---
Maintainer: `davewilliamson` · tier `community` · owner-submitted per catalog rules.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep bounded control reads off the serial queue
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

`session.control.read` can miss the client's 30-second deadline while it waits behind a slow request on the same WebSocket. Switching from native Desktop to the gateway-hosted Webapp does not remove that transport queue. The ordinary dispatcher still awaits each serial request before taking the next frame; even existing concurrent reads were admitted into that queue before they could start.

Start the two allowlisted read projections at admission instead: `session.context_breakdown` and the pure `session.control.read` snapshot. Existing bounds remain **2 running + 8 waiting**; a flood still parks the reader. Mutations retain their arrival order.

## Ordering and profile boundaries

These snapshots are deliberately unordered relative to queued mutations. A client needing read-after-write consistency must await the mutation's reply. Desktop/Webapp `session.control` already awaits and consumes the returned snapshot; Ink's explicit control read hydrates the session once and receives later updates as events.

A read naming a hot-starting profile waits within the existing 20-second profile-start budget before taking a running read slot. It still counts against admission, cannot starve ready profiles' running slots, and is dropped when its viewer disconnects. Profile-bound grants naming another profile still fail immediately through the unchanged authority checks. The serial mutation hold lane is preserved.

Completed slow dispatches now log peer, request ID, method and elapsed time at a fixed 5-second threshold. IDs and methods use escaped repr; no request parameters or response bodies are logged. Cancellation and dispatch-crash paths keep their existing diagnostics. A handler that hands work to a pool is timed only through that handoff, not until its eventual reply. No new environment setting is added.

## Verification

Refreshed against upstream snapshot `8112254f8a934626032579cae967b25b7795836d` on 4 November 2026, preserving the published branch's history with a normal merge. Final head: `f41ee761ab98f1e0ab9c245d182a8aa0e59e9838`.

- **80/80 tests passed** across the concurrent-read, real ticketed profile-start, session-control, orphan-race and socket-send-deadline suites, using `scripts/run_tests.sh` with pinned Python 3.14 and two workers.
- The control-read regression fails on unmodified upstream: the read starts only after the gated mutation finishes. With the patch it replies while that mutation remains blocked, while a later mutation stays ordered. Both `prompt.submit` and `session.control` are exercised.
- `scripts/check --base origin/main`: **14 checks passed**, code health 0 blocking / 0 advisory. `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Claude code/security/concurrency review: no remaining blocker or major for PR publication, conditional on passing the revised tests. The 80-test run above is that revised run. An earlier Gemini review raised the same profile-wait and ordering questions; the follow-up Gemini call hit quota and is not reported as a pass.

The first broader worktree run hit the repository's real-home I/O guard when bootstrap inspected its Git metadata under the live install. Verification was moved to an isolated clone outside the live home; the guard remained enabled.

## Limits

This proves the serial-queue regression, not the exact blocker on every naturally timed-out socket. Later independent-socket controls answered in 26–1685 ms while the user's original 30-second failure remained valid evidence. GIL pauses, database waits, read-lane saturation and full `session.resume` cost remain separate possible limits. See the new cross-surface evidence comment on this PR.

No live installation has been patched or restarted by this refresh. Installed activation and sustained real-use validation are outstanding. GitHub reported no configured CI checks; local test success is not a claim that GitHub CI ran.

prs.title: fix(discord): harden outbound image URL fetches
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Hardens Discord's outbound fetch path for agent-supplied image and GIF URLs, and places that behavior behind focused Discord media/fetch modules rather than regrowing the monolithic adapter.

The previous implementation validated a hostname before a separate client resolved and connected, performed synchronous DNS checks inside async handlers, read complete response bodies without a strict streamed aggregate boundary, trusted response metadata when choosing an image attachment type, and had no cumulative limit across a multi-image operation.

This PR makes that boundary fail closed:

- direct connections resolve, validate, and dial a vetted public IP while preserving the original Host/SNI;
- every redirect is followed manually and re-enters the same SSRF-safe connection path;
- URL safety checks are awaited, so DNS resolution does not block the event loop;
- each decoded response is streamed in chunks of at most 64 KiB with a strict 50 MiB aggregate limit, including missing or falsified `Content-Length` and multi-chunk bodies;
- one `send_multiple_images()` operation has a 100 MiB remote-response budget shared across Discord's 10-file chunks and native-to-base fallback;
- downloaded bodies must have PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP magic bytes before Discord receives an image attachment; animation uploads require GIF bytes.

### Security impact

This closes DNS-rebinding SSRF, async event-loop blocking, unbounded-body resource-exhaustion, and non-image attachment gaps in Discord's outbound URL-image handling. Explicitly configured proxies remain the trusted DNS/egress boundary, matching the existing `tools.url_safety` policy.

### Contributor credit and prior work

Salvages #60395 by @isheng-eqi. The following original commits were cherry-picked with their authorship preserved and remain separate from the follow-up fixes:

- `284856db946f6386f976c3ebe506a321d7398cf3` -> `a030399d633765f1febb69881c77be4753aba239`
- `c17fda6cedd06a16840eeaa8957dc7bb59a63775` -> `4d629a7134ab1599422808661350b4ae7002e307`

The media-send seam is adapted from #79652. Its current-tree extraction commit `cb116912b5da9384e28c776861570175145a5ca5` retains `Andrex Ibiza, MBA` as author.

The Discord async URL-validation slice is adapted from #40255. Commits `bbd171e3e6c53a8485c1714176018c0a32bc44c0` and `9adbb95905eb82fcb7e4b2416b89fc96532eef77` retain `nftpoetrist` as author. Other-platform migration remains outside this PR.

The redirect-target validation work from #62932 was already salvaged and merged through #69482. This PR builds on current `main` rather than re-cherry-picking that lineage.

### Architecture

There is one authority for each responsibility:

- `plugins/platforms/discord/outbound_image_fetch.py` owns SSRF-safe client creation, connect-time IP pinning, async redirect validation, bounded decoded reads, the 50/100 MiB limits, response cleanup, and magic-byte classification;
- `plugins/platforms/discord/media_send_mixin.py` owns Discord media-send policy and composes `send_multiple_images()`, `send_image_file()`, `send_image()`, `send_animation()`, `send_video()`, and `send_document()` with the fetch module;
- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py` composes `DiscordMediaSendMixin` before `BasePlatformAdapter` and retains only the compatibility imports/wrappers needed by existing callers and monkeypatch seams.

The stale branches from #79652 and #40255 were not merged wholesale. Their useful architecture, tests, async policy, and contributor credit were applied to the current tree without their unrelated workflow, contributor-mapping, moved-path, or other-platform changes.

## Related Issue

- Salvages #60395
- Related: #40255, #62932, #69482, #79652

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`
  - composes `DiscordMediaSendMixin` and keeps compatibility wrappers/re-exports;
  - awaits URL validation for the remaining Discord attachment fallback path.
- `plugins/platforms/discord/media_send_mixin.py`
  - owns single-image, multi-image, animation, and local media-send behavior;
  - preserves adapter- and method-global monkeypatch seams while consuming the focused fetch module.
- `plugins/platforms/discord/outbound_image_fetch.py`
  - owns bounded streaming and cumulative download-budget enforcement;
  - creates the SSRF-safe `httpx` client for connect-time IP validation and pinning;
  - awaits validation at the current URL and every redirect target;
  - bounds decoded iterator chunks and validates PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP magic bytes.
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_image_download_bounds.py`
  - covers DNS rebinding before raw connect, redirects, proxies, chunked bounds, decoded chunk sizing, cleanup, magic bytes, animation, and forum behavior.
- `tests/gateway/test_send_multiple_images.py`
  - covers batch limits across Discord chunks, invalid/non-200 accounting, missing and falsified lengths, exhaustion, and budget propagation into fallback.
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_attachment_download.py`
- `tests/gateway/test_discord_document_handling.py`
  - verify the async URL-safety seam for attachment/document fallback.
- `tests/plugins/discord/test_outbound_image_fetch_seams.py`
  - verifies fetch-module ownership plus compatibility patches and awaited URL validation.
- `tests/plugins/discord/test_discord_media_send_seam.py`
  - verifies mixin-first MRO, method ownership, and adapter-level patch compatibility.

Other platforms, dependencies, and configuration are unchanged.

## How to Test

1. Run focused security, media, and seam tests:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/plugins/discord/test_outbound_image_fetch_seams.py \
     tests/plugins/discord/test_discord_media_send_seam.py \
     tests/gateway/test_discord_image_download_bounds.py \
     tests/gateway/test_send_multiple_images.py \
     tests/gateway/test_discord_attachment_download.py \
     tests/gateway/test_discord_document_handling.py -q
   ```

   Result: `62 passed`.

2. Run URL-safety and adjacent attachment/document regressions:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/tools/test_url_safety.py \
     tests/gateway/test_discord_attachment_download.py \
     tests/gateway/test_discord_document_handling.py -q
   ```

   Result: `74 passed`.

3. Run the full Discord regression shard:

   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/gateway/test_discord*.py \
     tests/gateway/test_send_multiple_images.py \
     tests/plugins/discord/test_outbound_image_fetch_seams.py \
     tests/plugins/discord/test_discord_media_send_seam.py -q
   ```

   Result: `310 passed` across 49 files.

4. Run repository checks:

   ```bash
   .venv/bin/ruff check .
   python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all
   python3 scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py
   python3 -m py_compile \
     plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py \
     plugins/platforms/discord/media_send_mixin.py \
     plugins/platforms/discord/outbound_image_fetch.py
   git diff --check
   ```

   Results: all checks passed; Windows scan covered 1020 files and attribution is mapped.

The earlier repository-wide canonical runner was not green because unrelated local environment/system-dependent tests failed. The complete Discord shard and adjacent URL-safety tests pass as listed above; the full-suite checkbox remains unchecked pending hosted CI.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - focused, adjacent, and the complete Discord shard pass as listed above; hosted execution remains pending
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.5.2

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation - N/A; no user-facing configuration or workflow changed
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys - N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows - N/A; this follows the existing focused-module policy
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact; the Windows footgun scan passes
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior - N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

prs.title: feat(plugins): add bounded completion policies
prs.body:
Adds a `before_turn_end` plugin hook. A plugin reviews the candidate answer before Hermes delivers or stores it. Related: #101910. This extends #124956 by @ciaomrgrey.

## Changes

- The hook returns `allow`, `continue` (with feedback), or `fail` (with a user message).
- `agent.max_final_continuations` limits the repair rounds. The default is 2.
- While a callback is registered, Hermes withholds all output until review ends.
- Rejected candidates do not reach history, SQLite, trajectories, or compression.
- Without a callback, delivery does not change.
- `_is_real_user_message` moves to `conversation_compression_scaffolding.py` to keep the file under its size cap.

## Tests

53 of 53 gate tests pass. A broad run gives the same 20 environment failures as `main`. `scripts/check` passes.

## Limits

Hermes refuses the `codex_app_server` runtime while the gate is active.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stamp idle session.info frames and include provider (salvage #139022, #145409)
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Idle picks repaint now. Before: Publish: no stamp/provider; Viewer: fence drops frame. After: Publish: stamped + provider; Viewer: pill updates live. Change: publish_local_session_info.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/306e1fe1-f1c8-4bd6-ae51-2f7bbfd3ccc0)

## What does this PR do?

Fixes a gateway bug where switching models or session settings in an existing conversation after the first turn commits on the backend, but Desktop, Webapp, and TUI viewers keep showing the previous model until another message is sent. Once a turn settles and `live.event_stream.execution` clears, idle `session.info` broadcasts omitted `execution_generation`, `revision`, and `provider`, so Desktop's `acceptUnstampedLifecycle` fence dropped them as late stragglers. With this fix, idle `session.info` snapshots carry `execution_generation`, `revision` and the resolved `provider`. The provider is left out while an `auto` route's provider is still unknown. Partial idle updates, such as the `/fast` frame, carry the generation and revision. All attached viewers now repaint immediately.

This salvage combines @KoNit-K's #139022 (`provider` in `local_session_info`) and @duxingx1a's #145409 (stamping idle `session.info` at publish time, plus the Desktop fence test). Both are cherry-picked with `-x`, so each contributor stays the author of their commits. My follow-up commits address the review feedback on #145409 and #139022: they extend the stamp to every sibling idle publisher, preserve named `custom:<name>` provider identities, and map @duxingx1a's email. This PR pairs with desktop PR #161014. A rebase-merge or merge commit keeps each contributor as the author of their commits, while a squash merge keeps them only as co-authors.

Points to review:
- **Stamp at publish time, not inside `local_session_info`:** `publish_local_session_info` attaches `execution_generation` and `revision` (without `authority_epoch`) under `event_stream.lock`. That keeps `CanonicalSnapshotInfo` (`extra='forbid'`) valid on `session.create` / `session.resume` (unlike #144368). It covers `_project_committed`, `apply_chat_pick`, `session_policy_refresh._publish`, the auto-title republish, and `service_tier_config`. Lightweight unit-test stubs without `_handle` or a stream lock keep working.
- **Custom provider identity:** `_session_provider` and `messaging_route_info` route bare `'custom'` through `session_provider_identity` inside `owner_scope`. So `snapshot_info` (`{**inventory, **info}`) and `publish_settled_info` never downgrade named `custom:<name>` providers to bare `'custom'`.
- **Frames that now land have to be right:** once idle frames stopped being dropped, three snapshot gaps showed, and review found each of them:
  - `d373a58b05` reads and publishes the auto-title republish on the turn's loop. A snapshot read on the title thread could land after a model pick and repaint the old model.
  - `9cc48098ba` reports a session's `/fast` pin over the agent's or the policy's tier, so an idle reasoning edit no longer resets the speed pill. The same change makes the `session.info` snapshot after an editor reload report the pin, so `5f972a4d30` updates the ACP reload test, which had asserted the old `''` as its premise.
  - `7ebbbc99df` leaves an unresolved provider out instead of sending `''`, which Desktop would store as the provider.

## Related Issue

Refs #139015, #144367, #154229, #139022, #145409, #144368, #161014

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_local_session_info_fields.py tests/gateway/test_session_service_tier_options.py tests/gateway/test_session_mutation_model.py tests/gateway/test_adversarial_mutation_lifecycle.py tests/gateway/test_session_resume_config_refresh.py tests/acp_adapter/test_gateway_model_pick_provider.py
cd apps/desktop && HERMES_PYTHON=/nonexistent npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/execution-authority.test.ts
```

Manual steps: start a chat in Hermes Desktop, send one message, and wait for it to finish. Then pick a different model or provider in the composer pill. The pill, and any second attached viewer, should update immediately without sending another message.

Tested on Linux arm64 (Python 3.14.9):
- At `5f972a4d30`, the six files above pass 50/50. Together with every test file that mentions service tiers (95 files), 1993 tests pass. Three `api_server` files can't import `aiohttp` in this venv.
- At `7ebbbc99df`, a 32-file set covering the touched symbols passes 974 tests. It also has two `test_session_client_env.py` PATH-order failures, which reproduce identically on `a036d7ae58` with the same interpreter, so they're environmental.
- Each review-fix test fails on the code before its fix.
- `execution-authority.test.ts` passed 7/7 on `a036d7ae58` (Node 26.12.1), and no desktop file has changed since.
- `scripts/check --only ruff,health` is clean.

Live Desktop and Webapp browser E2E were not run.
