prs.title: Long-running MCP tools finish through MCP Tasks instead of holding the call open
prs.body:
Some MCP servers run long jobs (a CI pipeline, a nightly export) as MCP Tasks: instead of holding the tool call open, they hand back a task handle and finish in the background. Hermes never told servers it understood Tasks, so those servers had to hold the call open or refuse it. Now Hermes declares the extension, follows the handle to the finished result, and the agent sees an ordinary tool result.

## Why now

Anthropic made MCP Tasks generally available in Claude and Claude Code on Nov 24, 2026 (https://claude.com/resources/articles/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more). Claude Code shipped task support in 2.1.319, and 2.1.332 fixed "MCP tool calls failing with 'malformed task handle' when the server's task ID is longer than 128 characters; IDs of up to 1,024 characters now work" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Spec: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks (schema v2). The scout ledger had this as "blocked: the SDK has no client tasks API". The installed `mcp` 2.3 SDK still has none, but its `ClientSession(extensions=…, result_claims=…)` hook lets a client parse a claimed `resultType`, which is all this needs.

**How Claude Code does it:** a task-backed tool call runs in the background and notifies when it finishes (`DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND` turns that off). **How this differs:** Hermes keeps the call synchronous. It polls inside the existing tool call, so the turn, timeout, interrupt and stdio-death paths stay exactly as they are; only the wire shape changes. Moving the wait to the background (via the process-notification path) is a possible follow-up.

## What changes

| Server answers `tools/call` with … | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| a task handle (`resultType: "task"`) | Hermes never declares Tasks, so the server can't send one. A Tasks-only server refuses or blocks | polls `tasks/get` at the server's `pollIntervalMs` (clamped 0.2–10 s) → the final `CallToolResult` |
| task ends `failed` | n/a | tool error carrying the server's JSON-RPC error message |
| task ends `cancelled` | n/a | tool error, with the server's status message |
| task asks for input (`input_required`) | n/a | task cancelled + tool error saying Hermes can't answer `tasks/update` yet |
| Hermes stops waiting (timeout / interrupt) | n/a | best-effort `tasks/cancel` (shielded, 5 s) |
| `tasks/get` keeps failing (expired token, dropped session) | n/a | after 3 failed reads in a row: tool error naming the task ("may still be running, do not start it again"); the `tools/call` is never replayed by the re-auth/reconnect recoverers |
| legacy (`initialize`-era) server | unchanged | unchanged (the SDK only advertises claims on modern wires) |
| `mcp_servers.<name>.tasks: false` | — | extension not declared; the server answers synchronously |

Task ids of any length are accepted (the test peer uses 304-character ids).

- `tools/mcp_tool_tasks.py`: new `mcp_tool_*` sibling (the pattern `tools/AGENTS.md` prescribes): the claim model, `session_kwargs()`, the poll loop, `call_tool()`.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py::_session_kwargs`: adds the Tasks extension + result claim.
- `tools/mcp_tool_handlers.py::_call_tool_racing_stdio_death`: calls through `mcp_tool_tasks.call_tool`, so polling stays inside the stdio-death race and the tool timeout.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/features/mcp.md` § Long-running tools (MCP Tasks).

## Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, real gateway, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` via Nous Portal)

A real stdio MCP peer (`tests/tools/fixtures/mcp_tasks_server.py`, 2026-07-28 stateless). It returns a task handle for `slow_job` when the call declares Tasks, and otherwise refuses with `sync fallback: job not started`, which makes the difference visible. Planted result: checksum `ORCHID-5521`.

- **main:** `✗ Tasks Peer · slow job [sync fallback: job not started]`. Wire: `tools/call` ×1, `tasks/get` ×0.
- **this PR:** the model answered `Checksum: ORCHID-5521`. Wire: `tools/call` ×1 (its `_meta` clientCapabilities name `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`), `tasks/get` ×3. The state.db tool row holds the result.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_mcp_tasks_stdio.py` (2 tests, real stdio peer, real `register_mcp_servers` + registry dispatch, wire-log assertions). The first test is red on `origin/main`. The second (`tasks: false` keeps the extension off the wire) passes on both, as the control.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every `tests/tools/test_mcp*.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp*.py`: **1405 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped** (128 files).
- `scripts/check --only health`: ok (one waived catch-all on the best-effort cancel, logged with traceback).

**Edge paths, real stdio peer + real client** (no model): `ask_job` (task goes `input_required`) returned `MCP task … asked for input mid-task, which Hermes cannot answer yet (tasks/update); the task was cancelled`, wire `tasks/get` ×3 → `tasks/cancel`. `slow_job` under a 1 s tool timeout with polls slower than that returned `MCP call timed out after 1.0s`, wire `tasks/get` ×1 → `tasks/cancel`.

## Infographic

![mcp-tasks](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab4389f/3Sbci3WxYuY7y_OH3aD-o_anMtDhLh.png)

prs.title: Custom endpoint test names the API mode the host does serve (port Roomote#3729)
prs.body:
When you test a custom endpoint in Desktop's settings and the host lists its models but refuses the API mode you picked, the warning used to end with "Pick the API mode it does serve." and leave you to guess. Now the test also tries the other API modes and tells you the one that works, e.g. "It does serve Responses API (POST /responses): set API mode to Responses API."

The custom-endpoint test names the working API mode when the selected one 404s.

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py::_probe_transport_route`: on a 404/405/501 for the selected route, probe the other transport routes (Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages) and name the first one the host serves. Extra probes run only on a miss. An inconclusive probe (network error, timeout) never counts as served, so the old "Pick the API mode it does serve." stays the fallback.
- The POST builder moved into `_transport_route_status` (status or `None`) so the miss and the alternates share one request shape; its catch narrows from `except Exception` to `httpx.HTTPError`/`OSError`.

| Host / selected mode | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Responses-only gateway, mode auto or Chat Completions | `... POST /chat/completions returned HTTP 404: this host does not serve the Chat Completions API. Pick the API mode it does serve.` | `... does not serve the Chat Completions API. It does serve Responses API (POST /responses): set API mode to Responses API.` |
| Responses-only gateway, mode Responses API | ok | ok (no extra probe) |
| Host serving neither / unreachable alternates | `Pick the API mode it does serve.` | unchanged |

Ported from RooCodeInc/Roomote#3729 (their OpenAI-compatible connection save checks the selected protocol's route and, on a miss, says "It does serve <other>; switch the API protocol"). Hermes already had the Responses API mode and the selected-route probe (#93622); this adds the cross-mode hint.

**Live repro:** a real local HTTP gateway (GET `/v1/models`, POST `/v1/responses` 200, everything else 404) and a real `hermes dashboard --isolated` per tree, `POST /api/providers/custom-endpoints/validate` with the session token. main: `Pick the API mode it does serve.` Head: `It does serve Responses API (POST /responses): set API mode to Responses API.` for auto and `chat_completions`; `codex_responses` → `ok: true`, gateway log shows a single `/v1/responses` POST (no extra probe on success).

**Tests:** `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::...::test_custom_endpoint_validate_fails_when_the_transport_route_is_missing` now asserts the hint (red on main, green here). Its "last POST was the chat probe" assertion now picks the last chat POST, since the alternate probe follows it; only the patched call moved. `test_web_server.py` + `test_web_routers_endpoint_probe.py`: 195 passed. `scripts/check --only health` clean.

**Not covered:** no Desktop screenshot of the toast. Desktop shows the backend `message` verbatim in the existing warning toast (`custom-endpoints-settings.tsx`), and no renderer code changes.

prs.title: mcp: configurable oauth.bind_host for proxied callbacks on remote hosts
prs.body:
## Problem

`hermes mcp login <server>` binds the OAuth callback listener to `127.0.0.1` unconditionally. On a headless/remote host (Hermes on one machine, browser on another) the documented **proxied callback** recipe — set `oauth.redirect_uri` to an HTTPS endpoint that forwards to the host — cannot complete: the reverse proxy dials the host's LAN address, and a loopback-bound socket never receives it. The flow just sits at *"Open this URL in your browser…"* until it times out, leaving paste-back or an SSH tunnel as the only options.

## Change

Thread a configurable bind address through the callback-port plumbing, defaulting to today's `127.0.0.1`:

- `oauth.bind_host` (new, optional) is read by `_bind_host(cfg)` and passed to `_bind_reserved`, `_reserve_callback_port`, `_pick_cimd_port`, `_start_callback_server` and `_make_callback_waiter`.
- Config-shaped like the docs recipe now works end to end, e.g. `redirect_port: 8765`, `redirect_uri: https://cb.example.ts.net/callback`, `bind_host: 192.168.10.240` (or `0.0.0.0`).
- Unset `bind_host` changes nothing: every default is the current `127.0.0.1`.

Test stubs that monkeypatch `_start_callback_server` gained a `bind_host="127.0.0.1"` parameter so they forward it to the real implementation (5 stubs across the two callback tests).

## Verified

- `pytest tests/tools/ -k oauth` → **196 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Live against Firecrawl's remote MCP (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`) with Caddy on a separate LXC forwarding `https://<vhost>/callback` → `192.168.10.240:8765`: listener bound the LAN address, `curl` through the vhost returned the handler's *Authorization Successful* page, and the token landed.

prs.title: fix(tools): echo caller input and recovery hint on malformed JSON-string envelope
prs.body:
## What & why

`tool_call`'s deferred-tool bridge (`tools/tool_search_validation.py::normalize_tool_call_entries`)
tolerates `calls`/`arguments` emitted as a JSON string, but when that string is malformed —
commonly truncated immediately after the last value, surfacing as `Expecting ',' delimiter`
at the final column — it returns the bare `json.JSONDecodeError` with no recovery path. A
model handed a bare parse error re-sends the same broken string and the deferred call never
recovers.

This hardens both JSON-string paths (the batch envelope and each entry's `arguments`) to:

- echo the caller's own (truncated) input, and
- name the native wire shape to re-emit (`a JSON array` / `a JSON object`),

mirroring the caller-echo idiom already used by `local_batch_error` for the same reason
(a small model can only self-correct when it sees what it actually emitted).

Fixes the non-recoverable `tool_call 'calls' is not valid JSON: …` /
`tool_call calls[i].arguments is not valid JSON: …` failure. Builds on #114484 (which added
the JSON-string tolerance this path now recovers from).

## How to test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py
```

The new invariant `test_normalize_malformed_json_error_echoes_input_and_directs_recovery`
is proven red on the base and green after the change (it pins the malformed-string recovery
contract: parse cause named + caller input echoed + native shape to re-emit).

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` → 39 passed, 0 failed
- `scripts/check` (lefthook pre-commit) → `1 checks, ok`
- `ruff check` → `All checks passed!`

## Platforms tested

- macOS (arm64), Python 3.14

## Related issues

- #114484 (prior tolerance for model-emitted JSON-string envelopes)

prs.title: MCP servers can hand Hermes their skills: list, approve, verified load (salvage #148240)
prs.body:
An MCP server can now publish skills (step-by-step playbooks plus their supporting files), and Hermes could not use them: the agent saw only the server's raw resources. Now Hermes lists a server's skills, asks you before loading one, checks every file against the server's own listing, and asks again if the skill changes.

**Salvage of #148240 by @codeJRV** (commit cherry-picked unchanged, authorship kept), rebased onto current `main` (base was ~15.7k commits behind; it applied clean). Related alternatives that stay open for comparison: #137746 (@dxianping, native skill-index integration, ~4.7k LOC) and #104353 (@dschnurbusch, prototype with a skills guard, ~6.9k LOC). This one was picked as the base because it is the smallest (≈890 LOC) and follows the published beta spec.

## Why now

Claude Code 2.1.332 (Nov 25, 2026) shipped "skills from MCP servers (beta)", shown as `server:skill`, the same day Anthropic announced Skills over MCP as a public beta across Claude and Claude Code. The GitHub MCP server already serves skills behind `--features=skills`.

- Changelog: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md (2.1.332, first bullet)
- Announcement: https://claude.com/resources/articles/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more
- Spec (beta): https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills/blob/main/specification/beta/skills.mdx

**How Claude Code does it:** served skills join the normal skill list as `<server>:<skill>`; in auto mode a classifier decides the load without reading it, in Manual mode the user gets an "Allow this version" prompt that lasts until a file changes; 11 frontmatter fields (`allowed-tools`, `hooks`, `model`, …) are ignored and `!` shell lines don't run.

**How this differs:** Hermes has no classifier: every load is a real user prompt (fail-closed in `-q`, cron and unattended runs). Skills are reached through two per-server utilities, `mcp__<server>__list_skills` and `mcp__<server>__skill_view`, which register only when the server advertises the `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension plus `resources`. So servers without the extension keep exactly today's tool list, and the system prompt does not change. Like Claude Code, remote frontmatter never grants permissions and never triggers shell preprocessing.

## What changes

| Server advertises skills | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent asks "what skills does `docs` have?" | only `list_resources` / `read_resource`; no `skills/list` method is ever sent | `list_skills` pages `skills/list` and downloads no files |
| Agent loads a skill | it can `read_resource` the raw `SKILL.md` with no check and no prompt | `skills/get` → you approve → size + SHA-256 + frontmatter checked |
| Server changes a file after approval | n/a | the old revision is refused; the reload asks again |
| Agent reads a skill file through the generic `read_resource` | read goes through | refused, and the agent is pointed to `skill_view` (seen live below) |
| `-q` / cron / unattended | n/a | load declines (nobody can approve) |

Config: on by default only for servers that advertise the extension; `mcp_servers.<name>.tools.skills: false` turns it off (`tools.resources: false` turns both off).

## Live repro

A real interactive `hermes` CLI in tmux (scratch HOME, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` via Nous Portal, ~$0.02), with a real stdio MCP peer speaking the 2026-07-28 stateless protocol that serves a `review` skill whose `references/check.md` holds the planted value `TANGERINE-4471`:

- `mcp__docs__list_skills` → listed `skill://review/SKILL.md`
- `mcp__docs__skill_view` → consent card shown → **Allow once** → loaded
- the model's parallel `mcp__docs__read_resource` on the skill file → refused: "This file belongs to a loaded MCP skill. Read it with this server's skill_view tool…"
- `skill_view(uri, revision, file_path="references/check.md")` → verified → answer: **TANGERINE-4471**
- Server wire log: `server/discover` ×1, `skills/list` ×1, `skills/get` ×1, `resources/read` ×2 (lazy, only on demand). State.db tool rows match.

On `main` the same server registers no skill utilities (`tools/mcp_tool_skills.py` doesn't exist there); the contributor proved `test_mcp_skills_stdio.py` red on base.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every `tests/tools/test_mcp*.py` + `tests/tools/test_approval*.py`: **3015 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** (166 files).
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

## Known gaps (not in this PR)

- Served skills don't show up in `<available_skills>` or the `/` menu as `server:skill` the way Claude Code lists them. The agent finds them through the utility tool, so the system prompt doesn't change. #137746 builds that native index and could stack on top if wanted.
- The CLI consent card is titled "⚠️ Dangerous Command" for this prompt (and for every other MCP elicitation consent), because the classic CLI approval panel ignores the `title` argument. That is an older bug, not one this PR adds. It is fixed in #160969.
- `"dynamic"` skills (no stable manifest) are listed but can't be loaded, which the spec allows.

## Infographic

![skills-over-mcp](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab43779/9dWGAZFJTMJavDiQEAkK7_5tVnxIHd.png)

prs.title: fix(tools): convert MSYS directory paths and use NUL-delimited git check-ignore
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes `search_files(target="files")` on native Windows returning unconverted MSYS `/c/...` directory paths and failing to filter `.gitignore`'d directories (as well as non-ASCII gitignored paths on all platforms).

### Root Causes

1. **`tools/file_operations_search.py` (`_search_directories_with_find`)**: GNU `find` runs inside Git Bash on Windows and emits MSYS paths (`/c/Users/...`). Unlike the `find` fallback in `_search_files`, `_search_directories_with_find` did not convert those paths with `_msys_to_windows_path` before calling `_filter_hidden_descendants` and `_filter_gitignored_paths`. Because `_filter_hidden_descendants` compares against `Path(path)` (Windows form), a search rooted under a dot-named ancestor (such as `~/.hermes` or `.t3`) hit `ValueError` on `relative_to` and dropped every directory; otherwise raw `/c/...` paths leaked into `result.files` and failed `git check-ignore`.
2. **`tools/file_operations_search.py` (`_filter_gitignored_paths`)**:
   - Used `_escape_shell_arg(root)` instead of `_escape_native_tool_arg(root)` on Windows host environments, passing `'/c/...'` to native `git.exe -C` under `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` (exiting 128).
   - Used `git check-ignore --stdin` without `-z`, causing `git` to C-quote Windows backslashes (`"C:\\..."`) and non-ASCII characters (`"...\320\277..."`), so `item_path not in ignored` failed to match.

## Related Issue

Fixes #159933

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/file_operations_search.py`: Convert `find` directory results and `hidden_root` via `_msys_to_windows_path` when `_IS_WINDOWS and env_uses_host_filesystem(self.env)` before hidden-descendant and gitignore filtering; use `_escape_native_tool_arg(root)` on Windows host filesystems and `git check-ignore -z --stdin` with NUL-delimited input/output.
- `tests/tools/test_file_operations.py`: Add `test_rg_target_files_excludes_gitignored_non_ascii_directory` and `test_filter_gitignored_paths_uses_nul_delimited_check_ignore`.

## How to Test

1. Run `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_search_git_fsmonitor_hardening.py -q` (3 passed — previously 2 failed on Windows).
2. Run `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_file_operations.py -k TestSearchFilesIncludesDirectories -q` (9 passed — previously 3 failed on Windows).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] `scripts/check --only health` passes (0 blocking, 0 advisory)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A

prs.title: perf(desktop): stop re-rendering the whole room transcript on each composer keystroke
prs.body:
## What this fixes

Typing in a long-lived Bot Mode **group chat** gets laggy — the composer stutters on every keypress — while ordinary chat composers in the same app stay smooth.

## Cause

`CanonicalRoomView` owns the composer draft (`const [draft, setDraft] = useState('')`), so every typed character re-renders the whole workspace. The transcript was rendered inline with three inputs that were **freshly allocated on each render**, so the entire message log re-rendered per keypress:

- `avatarFor` — an inline arrow,
- `replyTo` — an inline arrow,
- `pause={{ busy, maxContinues, onContinue, onStop, stopping }}` — an inline object literal.

On a room with ~1.3k events this is a full transcript re-render per character.

## Fix

- Render the log through a memoized shell (`GroupTranscript`), so the transcript only re-renders when the log, roster or driver pause state actually change.
- `useCallback` for `avatarFor` and `replyTo`.
- `useMemo` for the `pause` descriptor, with the two handlers read through a ref so they stay current while the object itself only changes when `busy` / `stopping` / `maxContinues` change.

## Measured

On a room with ~1,300 events (≈570 messages) the desktop renderer sat at **~75% of one core** while idle in that room, and typing was visibly delayed. Gateway and the rest of the app were idle; this is desktop-only.

## Test

Added to `canonical-group-render-cost.test.tsx`: types into the composer and asserts the transcript's render count does not move. It **fails** on the current code (3 keystrokes → 3 transcript re-renders) and passes with the change; the first version of this PR only memoized the component, and that test is what surfaced the inline `pause` descriptor keeping the memo ineffective.

## Verification

```
pnpm vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots   →  162 files, 1621 tests passed
pnpm exec eslint <changed files>          →  0 errors (2 pre-existing warnings on untouched lines)
```

(Local run needed `node >= 26`, installed separately; the repo `.npmrc` is untouched by this PR.)

## Scope

Deliberately minimal. Rendering the whole log at once is the other half of the cost — a very long room still gets slower to *open* — and capping the transcript to a windowed view is a separate change I did not attempt here.

prs.title: fix(cron): a host sleep no longer makes a live cron run look wedged
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The cron stale-claim sweep judged a live owner "wedged" by the wall-clock age of its last `progress_at` stamp. A host that sleeps freezes the stamper together with the run, so a night of sleep read as hours of silence and a healthy run was reclaimed and killed within seconds of wake.

`touch_execution_progress` now also stores the machine-wide awake clock (`agent.sleep_clock.awake_seconds`, the same clock #131682 and #122282 use) in a new `progress_awake` column. The sweep measures silence in awake time while that stamp is comparable, and falls back to the wall age when the clock has gone backwards (a reboot rebased it) or for rows without the stamp. The awake age never exceeds the wall age (`min`), so this can only make the sweep more patient, not less. The race-guarded reclaim `UPDATE` also matches `progress_awake`, like it already does for `progress_at`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160680

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/executions.py`: `progress_awake REAL` column (added with `add_column_if_missing`), stamped next to `progress_at`; `_stale_age_seconds` takes it into account; the sweep selects and guards it.
- `tests/cron/test_stale_running_recovery.py`: `test_host_sleep_is_not_silence` (slept host kept; real awake silence still reclaimed; a stamp from another boot falls back to wall age).

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/cron/test_stale_running_recovery.py tests/gateway/test_cron_owner_progress_stamp.py`
2. Without the change the new test fails (the slept run is reclaimed); with it all pass.
3. `tests/cron` + the stamp test: 1836 passed. The 2 failures in `tests/cron/test_cron_plugin_api.py` fail on main the same way in a full `tests/cron` run and pass when the file runs alone.

prs.title: Plugin settings can be viewed and edited from the terminal: hermes plugins config <name>
prs.body:
Plugin settings were only editable from the Desktop app, or by typing hidden keys like `hermes config set plugins.entries.<plugin>.settings.<key>` after digging through a README. Now `hermes plugins config <name>` opens an interactive editor in the terminal that lists every setting the plugin declares, with its current value, and edits them one at a time.

A plugin gets this from its manifest alone. The fields come from its `config_schema` and its `requires_env` list, the same data the Desktop settings form already renders, and edits save through the same writers.

## What changes

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| See a plugin's settings from the CLI | read `plugin.yaml` or the README | `hermes plugins config <name>` lists each one with its value |
| Change one | `hermes config set plugins.entries.<id>.settings.<key> <value>`, unchecked | pick it from the list; choices and on/off come up as pickers, numbers and JSON are type-checked before saving |
| Set a plugin's API key | `.env` by hand, or the install-time prompt once | masked prompt, saved to the profile's `.env` through the same credential route as Desktop; shown only as `set` / `not set` |
| Script or pipe (no TTY) | none | prints each setting, its value and where it is stored |
| `hermes plugins show <name>` | no mention of settings | `Settings: 6 — edit with hermes plugins config <name>` |
| `hermes plugins install` | no mention | `Change its settings any time: hermes plugins config <name>` when the plugin declares settings |

- New `hermes plugins config <name>` (aliases `configure`, `settings`), in `hermes_cli/plugins_settings/cli.py`.
- `hermes_cli/plugins_settings.py` becomes the `hermes_cli/plugins_settings/` package. `fields.py` is the old module unchanged; the facade re-exports its three public names, so `tui_gateway` keeps importing `hermes_cli.plugins_settings`.
- Saves go through `save_plugin_settings` (schema-validated, the `ctx.set_config` writer) and `save_provider_env_credential` (the `PUT /api/env` route). Secrets never reach `config.yaml`.
- Labels without a manifest `label` are humanized with the same rules as the Desktop form (`maps_api_key` becomes "Maps API key"), so both surfaces read the same.
- The full-screen menu clears earlier output, so the result of each edit ("✓ Saved Model to ~/.hermes/config.yaml", "✗ … not saved: 'soon' is not a whole number") is shown in the menu title.
- Docs: user guide command list, `cli-commands.md` reference row, developer guide (plugin authors get the CLI editor for free; give each key a `label` and `description`).

## Live run

A real `hermes plugins config elevenlabs-music` in tmux, against the plugin's actual manifest from hermes-official-plugins main, in a scratch `HERMES_HOME`. Every field type was exercised: a secret, choices, on/off, an int with bad and then good input, and Esc to exit.

| Settings list | Masked secret prompt | After saving the key |
|---|---|---|
| ![list](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/01-list.png) | ![secret](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/02-secret-prompt.png) | ![saved](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/03-after-secret.png) |

| Choice picker | On/off picker | Bad number refused | Good number saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![enum](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/04-enum-picker.png) | ![bool](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/06-bool-picker.png) | ![bad](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/08-bad-number.png) | ![good](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/09-after-number.png) |

What the run wrote to disk:

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    elevenlabs-music:
      settings:
        music_model: music_v2
        store_for_editing: false
        chat_app_wait_seconds: 45
```

- `.env` gained one key, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.
- `config.yaml` contains no copy of the secret.
- The refused `soon` left the old value in place.

The no-TTY listing was also run against the Claude subscription plugin's real 10-key schema, and an unknown plugin name gives `Plugin 'nosuch' not found`.

## Tests

- 2 invariant tests in `tests/hermes_cli/plugins_settings/test_cli.py`:
  - Edits land where the plugin reads them, and a secret never reaches `config.yaml`.
  - Without a terminal the editor lists settings and never prints a secret.
- 147 passed across the touched suites: `plugins_settings/`, `tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_settings.py`, `test_plugin_validate.py`, `test_plugins_cmd*.py`, `ci/test_docs_drift.py`.
- `scripts/check --only health` passes.

## Not covered

- Native Windows has not been run. The editor uses the same curses menus and masked prompt as `hermes setup`.
- Desktop is unchanged. It already renders the same schema.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab32ee2/KAv52Nif_0-Q3gnkKpHvI_Ag7nLVOy.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): repaint live session slice on model pick and adopt mutation generation (salvage #152523, #139279)
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Live pill tracks picks. Before: Pill: slice stays stale; Preset: effort skipped; Next edit: stale_generation. After: Pill: slice repaints; Preset: effort applies; Next edit: gen adopted. Change: paintLiveSession, adoptGeneration.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2852918c-4776-4b65-b516-1afcf8f426c3)

## What does this PR do?

Fixes two Desktop client gaps that kept the composer model pill stale and broke follow-up reasoning/effort edits when switching models in an existing live session. `PRIMARY_SESSION_VIEW.$model` and `$provider` read `$sessionStates[runtimeId]` once a session has a live runtime, while `useModelControls.selectModel` painted only global composer atoms—leaving the collapsed pill on the old model and causing `useModelMenuController`'s `applyPreset` check (`view.$model === row.model`) to skip the new model's effort preset (for example picking a Claude SDK model with Medium effort after the first turn). Separately, `CanonicalDesktopProtocol.mutationReceipt` ignored `execution_generation` on its own reply, so any follow-up option edit sent before `session.updated` arrived was rejected with `stale_generation`. With this fix, primary picks optimistically repaint the live session slice (rolling back cleanly from the live slice, including after navigating away) and adopt `execution_generation` directly from mutation receipts. Pairs with gateway PR #161013.

This salvage combines @Loo1015's #152523 (non-merge commits `5957d454c1` and `b90e2976b8`, verified tree-equal to `git merge-tree origin/main c97ee7fa7a` before follow-up commits) and @jbradf0rd's #139279 (`14f733af63`), each cherry-picked with `-x` so contributors keep their author on their commits (`5957d454c1`'s placeholder `Administrator <admin@local>` author was normalized to @Loo1015's `lhn1015@qq.com` email from `b90e2976b8`). Two follow-up commits add a combined live-slice + preset + generation-adoption regression test, resolve ESLint/Prettier lint issues in the salvaged files, and map @Loo1015's email. Two review commits route tile picks through the same slice write as the primary session (Greptile) and pin monotonic generation adoption against a late receipt (Sol). A rebase-merge or merge commit preserves each contributor's author on their commits, whereas a squash merge keeps them only as co-authors.

Points to review:
- **Foundation choice (#152523 over #142328 / #144048):** #152523 already aligns with `main`'s sticky-intent split (`composerSelection`), snapshots the live slice rather than stale draft globals for rollback, and restores an abandoned session's slice without clobbering a newly focused chat; the new test covers the preset-ordering invariant explored in #144048.
- **Immediate generation adoption:** `CanonicalDesktopProtocol.adoptGeneration` advances `this.generations` monotonically from `mutationReceipt` so an immediate `applyPreset` reasoning write right after a `model` switch carries the new `expected_generation`; a receipt older than a broadcast the client already saw never moves it back.
- **One slice write for both surfaces:** `paintSelection` and `restoreSnapshot` call `paintLiveSession` for tiles as well as the primary session (`f698ba2`), so a pick or rollback that changes nothing hands back the same state and the session cache skips the publish.

## Related Issue

Refs #97425, #142037, #150119, #154229, #156496, #152523, #139279, #142328, #144048, #161013

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
cd apps/desktop
HERMES_PYTHON=/nonexistent npx vitest run --project ui \
  src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.test.tsx \
  src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls-stale-pick.test.tsx \
  src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls-live-preset.test.tsx \
  src/api/canonical-reasoning-generation-adoption.test.ts \
  src/api/canonical-protocol.test.ts \
  src/app/shell/model-menu-panel.test.tsx
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

Manual steps: open Hermes Desktop, send one message in a session, wait for the reply, then pick a different model and effort level in the composer model menu; the collapsed pill should repaint immediately and the effort edit should apply without `stale_generation` or needing another message.

Tested on Linux arm64 (Node 26.9.0, pnpm 12.15.0) at `55dc36e`: 95/95 passed across the 6 focused UI/protocol vitest files (124/124 across the 9 test files that import `useModelControls`, the pick ledger or the canonical protocol), `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean on all 5 touched TS/TSX files, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean, `scripts/check --only health` clean (0 blocking, 0 advisory), and `scripts/ci/check_contributor_emails.py` passed. With the two production files reverted to base `d71a65744c`, the new tests produce 9 behavioural failures across `use-model-controls.test.tsx` (5), `use-model-controls-live-preset.test.tsx` (2), and `canonical-reasoning-generation-adoption.test.ts` (2); the late-receipt test passes there (base never adopts from receipts) and fails once the adoption guard is replaced by an unconditional set. Full JS/Python suites and live Electron/Webapp browser E2E were not run locally and are left to CI. Not covered: a model switch from another surface, or a stale `session.info`, that races an in-flight pick can still leave the pill on the wrong model until the next `session.info`; that race family is a follow-up.

prs.title: fix(kanban): preserve approved continuation and recovery identity
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve approved same-owner continuation without disabling duplicate-worker admission, and keep recovery triage on the existing acceptance rather than generating another implementation graph.

- Bind one-use continuation to the responsible profile, source attempt/claim, newest evidence, acceptance fingerprint and expiry; recheck/consume atomically when opening the successor run.
- Retain dependency, current-assignee CAS, authorization/cooldown, allowlist/profile, workload, memory and model gates. Refuse worker self-authorization and stale/consumed replay.
- Keep `--owner-profile` separate from the launcher's global `--profile`; test the actual top-level launcher.
- Admit only fresh, never-executed intake to automatic decomposition. Filter recovery before the candidate limit and before auxiliary inference; recheck durable history inside both fanout and single-specification write transactions.
- Preserve original card metadata/progress on recovery, ordinary dependency semantics, legitimate fresh decomposition and explicit specification. Cover concurrent callers, history arriving during inference and re-triage after unlinking.

Related proposals: #120705 and #150513; related issue #62418. This does not modify or presume acceptance of those proposals.

## Current verification

Qualified source base: `3113542d64752423e1e9d2ff13bfbd2ce764dea9`. Current head: `61acd76b9ba0dc91be029f4988f9fa116405488a`; reviewed tree: `d06bb8e99841c7311bb438d438a1f882621d1708`.

- Test-first recovery reproduction generated four replacement children before the fix. The recovery suite now rejects that path before inference and at both native writes.
- On the current exact tree: **121 focused tests passed across 15 files**, covering recovery/replay/concurrency, specification/decomposition, watcher scope, continuation, current claim allowlist, live-claim completion, write guards, goal/memory admission and parent invalidation.
- Canonical `scripts/check --staged --base 3113542d64752423e1e9d2ff13bfbd2ce764dea9`: **22 checks passed**, zero blocking/advisory findings.
- Independent minimal-tree review and separate exact-tree port review passed with no blockers; the clean port retains newer upstream admission gates.
- Same guard on the minimal current-installation-base candidate: **673 passed, 45 failed, 11 skipped** across 94 files. Its unmodified intermediate ancestor: **655 passed, the same 45 failed, 11 skipped** across 93 existing files. Full failed-node comparison found zero introduced failures. These are retained environment/baseline failures, not a clean full-suite claim and not a broad-run claim for this newer source tree.

## Retained qualification history

Previous head `50672c4c35c90a4310a5a4c179c85b58084ab3ec` had 138 focused passes and a complete Kanban run of 691 passed/39 failed/11 skipped versus unmodified upstream656 passed/the same39 failed/11 skipped. Those earlier receipts remain history; they are not relabeled as full-suite results on this new head. Linux-only cases were not exercised on this macOS host.

## Operational limits

Source publication for maintainer review only: not merge, installation or resident-gateway activation. Existing execution source remains immutable. The separate minimal current-installation-base variant permits scoped operational qualification without importing unrelated upstream changes. An operator must use normal supported staging/activation and verify actual loaded behavior; no restart, global guard disable, assignment bounce, false handoff or new implementation graph is part of publication. Fork Actions remain disabled; no hosted-runner migration or settings change is requested.

prs.title: fix(matrix): gate only the olm-bound E2EE part to Linux so plaintext Matrix installs on macOS
prs.body:
> **Rebased onto current `main` (418ed92573) on 2026-11-10.** The first version of this PR split `LAZY_DEPS["platform.matrix"]` in `tools/lazy_deps.py`. `main` has since replaced that mechanism with `hermes pm`, so the branch was rebuilt from scratch on `main`. An adversarial self-review then found 16 issues: 15 are fixed in ffd9d25, and one (nix-darwin) is listed below as a follow-up. The rebase onto current `main` picked up three interactions with code that landed since, plus two claims that main's new pins made stale. **Rebase onto current `main`** below lists them. Earlier review comments refer to the first version.

## What does this PR do?

On current `main`, **Matrix cannot be installed on macOS at all**:

```
$ hermes pm install --extra matrix
✗ venv: extras ['matrix'] are not supported by this Python/platform — choose a supported provider; no dependency environment was changed
```

`[tool.hermes.extras-platforms]` (settled 2026-09-02) gates the whole `matrix` extra to Linux. pm's first-generation migration (`legacy_selection`) also drops mautrix from existing Mac installs on purpose, so a working Mac setup loses Matrix on update.

The gate's stated reason is python-olm: `mautrix[encryption]` pulls it in, and its bundled libolm builds on Linux only. **Plaintext Matrix never needs it.** Bare mautrix is pure Python, the adapter imports `mautrix.crypto` only for E2EE, and `ANCHORS["matrix"]` already leaves olm out.

This PR narrows the gate to what it exists for, without reversing it:

- **Dependencies:**
  - **`[matrix]` on Linux is byte-for-byte unchanged.** It still pulls `mautrix[encryption]`, so existing Linux E2EE installs keep python-olm.
  - **`[matrix]` on darwin** installs bare `mautrix` plus the plaintext runtime (asyncpg, aiosqlite, aiohttp-socks, aiohttp).
  - **win32 stays gated,** because plaintext Matrix is unverified on native Windows.
  - **New `[matrix-e2ee]`** carries only the olm-bound part and is gated to Linux, the same way `[stt-whisper]` names faster-whisper inside `[voice]`.
- **Setup wizard:**
  - It offers E2EE only where pm can install python-olm. It asks pm's gate rather than the running venv, as pm's own install policy does.
  - Where python-olm can't install, a previously saved required mode (the #62401 state) gets an offer to turn it off, instead of the claim that Matrix "runs unencrypted".
  - Where python-olm can install, the answer replaces the saved mode.
- **Adapter:**
  - Required E2EE on a host that can never install python-olm now sets a **non-retryable** fatal error (`matrix_e2ee_unavailable`), with the remedy (`MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=off`, or Proxy Mode). Matrix is parked instead of re-authenticating forever. Telegram and Discord handle a missing dependency the same way.
  - E2EE hints are built per host, including the #131778 warning for encrypted events that arrive with E2EE off.
- **Hints:** every install hint names `hermes pm install --extra matrix`. On `main` the platform hint says `pip install 'mautrix[encryption]'`, which bypasses pm and can't build on macOS. A bare `hermes pm install` or `hermes setup` doesn't install Matrix for an already-configured platform.
- **Setup menu:** it hides Matrix exactly where pm's `matrix` gate refuses the extra, instead of using a hardcoded win32 check whose python-olm rationale this PR makes false.
- **Docs:** the real python-olm build prerequisites, plus corrected fallback, Proxy Mode and Windows wording.

## Rebase onto current `main` (2026-11-10)

- **Conflicts:** `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `pm/extras.py`, the adapter and `tests/pm/test_extras.py`. Every resolution keeps `main`'s newer pins (asyncpg 0.32.0, aiohttp-socks 0.12.0, aiohttp 3.14.5, slack-sdk 3.45.0), so Linux `[matrix]` is still byte-for-byte `main`'s.
- **`uv.lock`:** taken from `main` and relocked with `hermes pm lock`. The diff against `main`'s lock is +31/−11 and touches only the Matrix entries: asyncpg's macOS wheels, the new extra and the darwin fork in `resolution-markers`.
- **New `main` code this PR had to meet:**
  - The encrypted-event warning from #131778 used the `_E2EE_INSTALL_HINT` constant this PR replaces. After the rebase that was a `NameError` the moment an encrypted event arrived with E2EE off, and the message still said `pip install 'mautrix[encryption]'`. It now gives the per-host remedy: the pm command where python-olm installs, Proxy Mode where it can't. Its test covers both kinds of host and asserts that no `pip install` text appears.
  - The new boundary lint (`scripts/boundary_lint.py`) flagged the adapter's `from pm.extras import …`. The adapter now goes through the public `pm` facade, as the other platform adapters do, and `pm` exports `extra_supported` next to `install_hint`.
  - `legacy_selection` gained declined-extras handling on `main`. The `matrix-e2ee` exclusion is merged with it.
- **Stale claims corrected:**
  - asyncpg 0.32.0, which `main` now pins, ships `win_arm64` wheels. win32 stays gated, but only because plaintext Matrix is unverified on native Windows. The comments, docs and notes below no longer cite asyncpg.
  - pm now builds with GCC by itself when Clang isn't installed (`pm/build_compilers.py`). It keeps Clang when Clang is present, and Clang still fails on libolm, so the docs keep the `CC=gcc` advice with the corrected reason.

## Related Issue

Fixes #62401
Fixes #85588

Related: #122733, where python-olm's source build fails under CMake 4 in the Linux pm takeover. That is not fixed here, because Linux resolves exactly as before. The docs now give the working prerequisites for that build.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pyproject.toml`:
  - `[matrix]` markers now read linux+darwin, except `mautrix[encryption]`, which stays linux-only.
  - Plain `mautrix` is added for darwin, and a new `[matrix-e2ee]` extra is added.
  - The `extras-platforms` gates are `matrix` = linux+darwin and `matrix-e2ee` = linux.
- `uv.lock`: relocked with `hermes pm lock`. The only additions are asyncpg's macOS wheels, the new extra, and the platform fork in `resolution-markers`. No other version moved.
- `pm/extras.py`:
  - `ANCHORS["matrix-e2ee"] = ("mautrix", "olm")`.
  - `legacy_selection` never carries `matrix-e2ee` on its own. Without that, a Linux venv holding only `mautrix[encryption]` would put a python-olm source build into the first pm sync.
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`:
  - `_e2ee_installable()` and a per-host `_e2ee_install_hint()`.
  - The non-retryable fatal error for required E2EE that can't install.
  - No install hint on runtime crypto failures, where the deps are present.
  - Setup handles the saved mode: it offers to turn a stale required mode off where olm can't install, and elsewhere the answer replaces the saved mode. A Yes also clears an explicit `MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=off`, which outranks `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION`.
  - pm install hints, imported through the public `pm` facade.
- `pm/__init__.py`: the facade exports `extra_supported` next to `install_hint`.
- `hermes_cli/gateway_setup_wizard.py`: Matrix is hidden where `extra_supported("matrix")` is false.
- Tests, one invariant per behaviour, each red on `main`:
  - `tests/pm/test_extras.py`: `test_plaintext_matrix_never_needs_python_olm`. `matrix` is supported on darwin. Wherever `matrix` runs without E2EE, it selects nothing olm-bound, and a plaintext install doesn't read as E2EE-capable. `matrix` availability never needs olm. A non-vacuity guard fails if no target exercises the olm checks.
  - `tests/gateway/test_matrix_plugin_setup.py`: `test_e2ee_setup_follows_the_python_olm_gate` has 5 cases. It asserts the mode the adapter actually resolves from the `.env` setup leaves behind, not which keys were written.
  - Extended: the E2EE hard-fail test (parked vs retryable, by installability), the `legacy_selection` test, and `main`'s #131778 encrypted-drop warning test (one case per kind of host).
- Docs (EN and zh-Hans), `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/matrix.md`:
  - E2EE is Linux-only.
  - The real build prerequisites. `apt install libolm-dev` was wrong: python-olm compiles the libolm it bundles.
  - The fallback note now matches the E2EE modes.
  - The Proxy Mode intro is corrected for Windows.
  - A warning to keep Matrix credentials off a Proxy Mode host.
- `contributors/emails/donald@ddj.co.za`: the attribution mapping.

## How to Test

On an Apple Silicon Mac:

```bash
hermes pm install --extra matrix        # main: refused; this branch: ✓ venv +matrix
hermes pm install --extra matrix-e2ee   # refused cleanly: "no dependency environment was changed"
hermes gateway setup                    # Matrix: no E2EE question; plaintext deps prepared
```

**Re-verified on the rebased head** (macOS arm64, Darwin 27, pm's Python 3.14.9), in an isolated `HERMES_HOME` activated with the documented developer workflow:

```
hermes pm install --extra matrix        ✓ venv +matrix
                                        → mautrix 0.21.1, asyncpg 0.32.0, aiohttp-socks 0.12.0; `import olm` fails
hermes pm install --extra matrix-e2ee   ✗ venv: extras ['matrix-e2ee'] are not supported by this Python/platform — … no dependency environment was changed
in that venv: ensure_matrix_deps()=True  extra_supported(matrix)=True  extra_supported(matrix-e2ee)=False
              E2EE hint: "E2EE needs python-olm, which installs on Linux only; set MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=off to run Matrix unencrypted here, or use Proxy Mode"
```

`main` still gates `matrix` to `sys_platform == 'linux'`, so the "before" result below still holds.

**Verified end-to-end on macOS arm64** (Darwin 27, pm's Python 3.14.7), before the rebase:

1. The pm install, in an isolated `HERMES_HOME` built with the documented developer workflow:

   ```
   before (main 41303b379e): ✗ venv: extras ['matrix'] are not supported by this Python/platform
   after  (this branch):     ✓ venv +matrix
                             ✗ venv: extras ['matrix-e2ee'] are not supported by this Python/platform — … no dependency environment was changed
   ```

2. The self-review fixes, with real imports against a temp `HERMES_HOME`. The host gate was evaluated for real and the `.env` was really written. Only the prompts were scripted, and the "homeserver" was a local stub:

   ```
   host gate            : supported(matrix)=True  supported(matrix-e2ee)=False  available(matrix)=True  olm importable=False
   setup, .env holding MATRIX_ENCRYPTION=true (the #62401 state), reconfigure:
                          asked "E2EE is set to required, but it cannot run on this platform … Turn E2EE off?" (default Yes)
                          .env afterwards has no E2EE key → the adapter resolves "off"
   required E2EE through the real registry (create_adapter) and connect():
                          connect()=False  fatal=matrix_e2ee_unavailable  retryable=False
                          "Matrix E2EE is required. E2EE needs python-olm, which installs on Linux only; set MATRIX_E2EE_MODE=off to run Matrix unencrypted here, or use Proxy Mode."
                          homeserver saw one request: GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami (no retry loop)
   ```

3. A live multiplexed gateway on this Mac (v0.22.5 since 2026-10-28) runs this branch's darwin package set: mautrix 0.21.1 without `[encryption]`, asyncpg 0.32.0, aiosqlite 0.22.1 and aiohttp-socks 0.12.0. It serves three Matrix bots that log in, sync, and answer messages with no python-olm present.

## Test scope

- **Each fix is pinned by a test.** Undoing each fix makes its test fail:

  | Fix undone | Test that fails |
  |---|---|
  | `legacy_selection` exclusion | the `legacy_selection` test |
  | fatal not set | hard-fail `[installable=False]` |
  | gate read from the venv | 2 setup cases |
  | turn-off offer | the `#62401` setup case |
  | Linux "No" keeps E2EE | the saved-mode setup case |
  | explicit `off` outranks Yes | the explicit-off setup case |
  | olm added to `matrix` anchors, or dropped from `matrix-e2ee` | the pm invariant |
  | darwin `[matrix]` pulls `mautrix[encryption]`, or `matrix` gated back to Linux | the pm invariant |
  | #131778 warning back on a fixed `pip install` hint | the encrypted-drop warning's `off` cases |

- **Targeted, on the final head:** 38 files (every Matrix test file, pm extras, platform gating, boundary lint, provider plugin discovery). In a CI-like environment, with the extras from `tests.yml` and no `matrix`, 436 passed, 0 failed and 10 skipped. With the `matrix` extra installed (the macOS runtime case), 437 passed. The only failures there are the two `test_matrix_deps_rebind.py` tests, which fail the same way on `main` whenever the extra is installed: they assume the Matrix packages are missing, and CI doesn't install them.
- **Full suite, after the rebase** (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, CI-like environment): 7,453 files, 74,202 passed, 313 failed, 64 errors, 2,099 skipped. All 112 failing files were rerun on `main` in the same environment, and 369 of the 381 failing ids fail there too: git, worktree, update and state-db tests that depend on this host. The other 12 were rerun on both trees. Two reproduced only on the branch:
  - the boundary lint, which was real and is fixed in ffd9d25;
  - provider plugin discovery, caused by an empty leftover directory in my local checkout that isn't in git.
  The other ten fail or pass the same on both trees.
- **`tests/pm/` after the boundary fix:** 149 files. Nothing fails on the branch that doesn't also fail on `main`. The failures are download and pause timing tests, which fail identically on `main` when rerun.
- **Lockfile:** `python -m pm.build_env --source . --check-lock` passes, which is the `uv-lockfile-check` job.
- `ruff check` is clean on every changed Python file, and `git diff --check` is clean.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Why not ungate `[matrix]` entirely?** I can't vouch for plaintext Matrix on native Windows. The old reason, asyncpg lacking a `win_arm64` wheel, no longer applies as of asyncpg 0.32.0, so extending it is an easy follow-up for someone who can test it.
- **Why keep `mautrix[encryption]` inside `[matrix]` on Linux?** pm-era installs record `matrix` in their ledger. Moving olm out of it would drop python-olm on the next sync and break working Linux E2EE. With this layout, Linux resolves exactly as before.
- **Relation to the 2026-09-02 gate:** its rationale is python-olm on win/darwin. This keeps olm off those lanes and restores only the part that rationale never covered.
- **Behaviour changes to be aware of:**
  - A Mac with leftover `MATRIX_*` credentials now starts a plaintext Matrix client, where on `main` they did nothing. For a Proxy Mode host this means a second client beside the container, so the docs now say to remove them there.
  - Required E2EE where python-olm can't install is now a non-retryable fatal error. If Matrix is the gateway's only platform, the gateway exits 78 (EX_CONFIG), which systemd, s6 and the generated launchd plist treat as "stop, don't respawn". This is the same outcome as any other unrecoverable platform config.
  - On Linux, setup's E2EE prompt now defaults to the saved mode, and answering No turns a saved mode off. On `main`, No left `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION=true` in place.
- **Verified before documenting:**
  - python-olm 3.2.16, still the latest, has wheels only up to cp312. pm's Python is 3.14, so every Linux E2EE install builds the bundled libolm from the sdist, with CMake or GNU make.
  - pm's Linux Python (python-build-standalone, now 3.14.9+20261021) records `CC=clang -pthread`, as `pm/build_compilers.py` also notes. pm now swaps in GCC when Clang isn't on `PATH`, but keeps Clang when it is.
  - A current Clang fails on libolm's `include/olm/list.hh:106` (`cannot assign to variable 'other_pos' with const-qualified type 'T *const'`). I reproduced that here.
  - CMake 4 rejects its `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.4)` unless `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` is set.
  - Debian sid/forky builds the same unpatched `list.hh` with GCC.
  - pm forwards `CC`, `CXX` and `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` to the build, because `_base_environment` keeps the ambient environment.
- **Follow-ups, not in this PR:**
  - **Native Windows.** asyncpg 0.32.0 now ships `win_arm64` wheels, so the dependency-side blocker is gone. Opening `[matrix]` to win32 needs someone who can verify plaintext Matrix there.
  - **nix-darwin.** `nix/packages.nix` still adds `matrix` on Linux only, citing an `oqs/liboqs` reason that matches nothing in the lock, so nix-darwin doesn't get plaintext Matrix. It needs a darwin nix build to validate.
  - **Gate-name spelling.** pm judges gates by the raw extra name, so `--extra matrix_e2ee` is treated as ungated. That's harmless here, because the per-package markers still select nothing off Linux, but it applies to every gated extra.

prs.title: feat(web): let SearXNG authenticate with a signed-in provider's credential
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**SearXNG behind an authenticating gateway couldn't be used:** the backend sent no credentials, so a gateway that requires a bearer token rejected every search.

`web.searxng.auth_provider` names a provider, and the SearXNG backend sends that provider's pooled credential as the bearer. Selecting it from the pool first renews an OAuth token the pool sees expiring, which covers a provider plugin that signs in with the PKCE helper.

```yaml
web:
  search_backend: "searxng"
  searxng:
    auth_provider: "my-llm"
```

Where it differs from the issue, and why:

- **A config key, not an env var.** `.env` is for secrets; behaviour goes in `config.yaml` (AGENTS.md).
- **No refresh-and-retry on a 401**, unlike the xAI backend. There the token and the API belong to one service. Here a gateway that keeps refusing a valid token would force a refresh on every search, and a refresh that fails takes the credential out of rotation for the model too. The cost: a token the pool can't see expiring, or one revoked early, is replaced only when the provider's own requests refresh it.
- **https only**, or plain http to `127.0.0.1` / `::1`, because a credential is sent. The PKCE helper applies the same rule to its endpoints.

**Security:** the named provider's credential is sent to `SEARXNG_URL` and nowhere else; both are operator config, and nothing logs it. A failed search can still go to the keyless rescue, as any SearXNG failure does today (#155901); the docs point at `web.keyless_rescue: false`.

The static-key PRs (#46214, #101329) cover a different case: a short-lived OAuth token needs the pool's refresh. `credentialed_provider_request` doesn't fit either: its origins are declared ahead of time, in core or in a plugin manifest, not taken from the operator's `SEARXNG_URL`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160986

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/web/searxng/provider.py`: `_auth_header()` reads the key, checks the URL and selects the credential.
- `plugins/web/searxng/plugin.yaml`: `config_keys: [web.searxng.auth_provider]`, so `hermes config get/set` recognizes the key.
- `tests/tools/test_web_providers_searxng.py`: five tests, run against a loopback gateway, the fake PKCE IdP and the real credential pool. `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_runtime_keys.py`: the key joins the recognized-key cases.
- Docs: a subsection in `user-guide/features/web-search.md`, one line in `developer-guide/web-search-provider-plugin.md`.

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/tools/test_web_providers_searxng.py tests/hermes_cli/test_config_runtime_keys.py`. With `provider.py` and `plugin.yaml` reverted, the tests of the new behaviour fail.
2. Sign in to a provider whose token your gateway accepts (`hermes auth add <provider>`), set the config above, point `SEARXNG_URL` at the SearXNG behind that gateway, and run a web search.

I ran step 2 on this commit against a real deployment: an OIDC provider, a gateway that checks its tokens, and SearXNG behind it. The search returned results, and with the stored expiry moved to a minute away, the token was renewed before the request went out.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (amd64 container)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A

prs.title: catalog: repin openrecall-memory to 0.4.0 (backup/restore/verify/rekey)
prs.body:
## What

Repins the `openrecall-memory` catalog entry to `dc8417b900c924351f3c91224d7b1ef9432c95b4` (v0.4.2) of https://github.com/reverb256/hermes-openrecall-provider. Supersedes #159234 and the earlier `32e71a65` and `ce68fab` pins.

## Delta from the earlier pins

- **0.4.0 (`32e71a65`)**: `backup`, `restore` (with cross-namespace re-encryption), `verify`, and real passphrase `rekey`.
- **0.4.1 (`ce68fab`)**: passphrase read through profile-scoped `get_secret`, config writer via `set_config_value`, cross-origin redirect refusal, bounded `cryptography`.
- **0.4.2 (`dc8417b`)**: the two blocking items from the 2026-11-26 re-review.
  1. The API key is read through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret("OPENRECALL_API_KEY")`, declared optional in `plugin.yaml`, and no longer read from `config.yaml`. The wizard's `.env` write is now actually used by both the provider and the CLI.
  2. The default namespace is profile-specific (`agent:<profile>`), derived from the active profile's `get_hermes_home()`. An explicit namespace (constructor config, `OPENRECALL_NAMESPACE`, or `config.yaml`) still wins and can be shared deliberately.

## Disclosure

Entries are encrypted client-side with AES-256-GCM; only ciphertext bodies reach the configured server URL. Entry names and the namespace are not encrypted. The passphrase and API key stay local and are routed through the profile scope. No telemetry, self-updater, core overrides, or third-party binary downloads.

## Verification

- 34 tests pass, including 12 new checks in `tests/test_security_contract_round2.py`.
- `hermes plugins validate` passes.
- `scripts/ci/catalog_entry_fields.py`: PASS (40-hex SHA). `scripts/ci/catalog_validate_pinned_entries.py`: PASS at the pinned SHA.
- Live check: `hermes openrecall status` with a scoped key reports `api_key: set`, profile-scoped passphrase, server alive; `_default_namespace()` returns `agent:<profile>` with an explicit config namespace still taking precedence.
- The earlier backup/restore/verify/rekey evidence from this PR remains valid for the carried-forward 0.4.0 code.

Requesting re-review of the `ce68fab..dc8417b` delta.

prs.title: fix(config): accept space-separated key in `config set`
prs.body:
Refs #50553.

`hermes config set memory provider holographic` (space-separated key) fails: the `set` subparser declares only `key` and `value` positionals, so the trailing token is rejected with `unrecognized arguments: holographic` and nothing is written. The issue was closed as solved, but the bug still reproduces on current main (`d71a65744c`):

```
$ hermes config set memory provider holographic
hermes: error: unrecognized arguments: holographic
```

This adds a hidden `extra` (`nargs="*"`) positional and folds trailing tokens into a dotted key, so `config set memory provider holographic` resolves to `memory.provider = holographic`. The dotted form and the two-word form are unchanged.

**Tests:** 4 regression tests in `test_set_config_value.py` (three-word, four-word, dotted, parser-level). `118 passed` in that file; `334 passed, 4 skipped` across the config and subcommand suites.

prs.title: fix(bluebubbles): repair same-host webhook flow and iMessage sanitization
prs.body:
## Summary

- Makes the native BlueBubbles adapter actually work on a same-host install (BlueBubbles Server + Hermes on one Mac, the recommended topology).
- Fixes two independent failures that each block all inbound messages (#9263, #9265), plus a macOS IPv6 resolution footgun, plus outbound rendering tofu on iMessage.

## What's in this PR

All four fixes live in `gateway/platforms/bluebubbles.py`:

1. **Drop invalid `"message"` event from the webhook registration payload** (fixes #9263). BlueBubbles Server only accepts `new-message` / `updated-message` (among others) and 400s the entire `POST /api/v1/webhook` if `"message"` is in the list — so on stock main, no events get subscribed at all.

2. **Embed the password in `_webhook_url`** (fixes #9265). BlueBubbles `WebhookService.dispatchEvent()` has no auth-header configuration, so every dispatch was being rejected by `_handle_webhook`'s password check with 401 Unauthorized.

3. **Use the `127.0.0.1` literal in `_webhook_url` instead of rewriting loopback hosts to `"localhost"`.** On macOS with modern Node.js, BlueBubbles Server resolves `localhost` → `::1` (IPv6 first), but the adapter's `aiohttp.web.TCPSite` binds IPv4-only, so every same-host dispatch fails with `ECONNREFUSED ::1:8645`. Switching to the literal avoids the AAAA lookup entirely.

4. **Strip iMessage tofu characters in outbound sends.** Apple Color Emoji has no glyphs for two ranges that routinely leak through the pipeline:
   - Block Elements (U+2580..U+259F) — streaming-cursor artifacts like `▉` that the agent's stream renderer can leave in the final message.
   - Private Use Area (U+E000..U+F8FF plus the two supplementary PUAs) — Slack custom workspace emojis are stored here and get carried through whenever Slack history / SOUL / memory feeds back into model context.
   A new `_sanitize_for_imessage()` helper is called from `send()` and `format_message()` before the outbound REST call so the user sees clean text instead of boxes.

#1 and #2 each independently prevent any inbound message from reaching the agent, and #3 prevents anything if you run BB Server and Hermes on the same Mac (which is the documented recommended setup). In combination, the native BlueBubbles adapter has not worked out of the box for same-host installs since it was added. #4 is a quality-of-life fix that becomes visible as soon as the first three are in place.

## Test plan

- [x] With the `"message"` event removed, `_register_webhook` returns `status=200` against a real BlueBubbles Server 1.9.9 and `GET /api/v1/webhook` shows the new entry with `events: ["new-message", "updated-message"]`.
- [x] With the password embedded in `_webhook_url`, inbound iMessages from BlueBubbles dispatch to Hermes and hit `_handle_webhook` as 200 OK instead of 401; the agent actually runs and produces a reply.
- [x] With the host rewritten to `127.0.0.1`, `aiohttp.TCPSite` bind and BB dispatch target are both unambiguously IPv4; same-host dispatch succeeds where it previously returned `ECONNREFUSED ::1:8645` in `~/Library/Logs/bluebubbles-server/main.log`.
- [x] `_sanitize_for_imessage` unit-sanity tested against `"Hello ▉"`, `"Done ▉"`, strings with `\uE001\uE002` PUA chars, strings with legitimate `🙂 ✅` emoji (preserved), and mixed strings. Trailing-whitespace cleanup works as expected.
- [x] End-to-end: an iMessage sent from a real user handle to the BlueBubbles Mac reaches the Hermes agent, the agent replies via the adapter's outbound send path, and the reply appears in Messages without any tofu characters.

## Notes

- Each fix is small and localized to a single file, so they are bundled into one commit for easier review; I can split them if you'd prefer separate commits.
- I also filed #9270 about a related (but not co-located) issue where `gateway/run.py` substitutes the literal `"(No response generated)"` into empty agent results and it ends up being delivered to users (and to cron home channels). Not fixed in this PR since it lives in different files and touches the cron scheduler's empty-skip path.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(profile): surface turn error on empty oneshot response
prs.body:
Addresses #50420.

`hermes -z` printed the opaque `no final response was produced; treating the run as failed` for non-default profiles, hiding the real cause. `_run_agent` (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`) ran the turn via `AIAgent.chat()`, which returns only `final_response` — but every non-success terminal path in `conversation_loop.py` returns `final_response: None` *plus* a descriptive `error` (provider/API failure, invalid model id, unusable credentials for the resolved provider, etc.). `.chat()` discards that `error`, so oneshot only saw an empty string and printed the generic message.

Fix: `_run_agent` now calls `run_conversation(prompt)` (the full result dict); when `final_response` is empty but `error` is set, it raises `RuntimeError(error)`, which oneshot's existing handler reports as `hermes -z: agent failed: <real error>`.

This surfaces the swallowed error that made the reported failure undiagnosable. Note: the exact reporter scenario depends on a credential topology where a named profile's `provider: auto` resolves to a provider that fails while default succeeds — I couldn't fully reconstruct that here, so this targets the confirmed underlying error-swallowing defect; happy to refine if the resolved-provider failure needs separate handling.

**Tests:** +1 regression test; 15 oneshot tests pass.

prs.title: fix(agent): record cwd for TUI-created sessions
prs.body:
Closes #50438.

Standalone `hermes --tui` sessions persisted `cwd=NULL`, so the Desktop list (which groups by cwd) collapsed every TUI session under "No workspace". `explicit_cwd` was only set when the client sent a `cwd` param, which a terminal TUI launch never does.

The real discriminator is the transport, not `source` (the Desktop client also defaults `source="tui"`): a standalone terminal TUI rides the module-level `_stdio_transport`; the Desktop GUI dispatches over a bound `WSTransport`. Fix: in `session.create`, when no explicit cwd was sent, set `explicit_cwd = current_transport() is _stdio_transport` — so terminal TUI sessions record their real launch dir while Desktop sessions keep the explicit-choice-only rule (shared launch dir stays null).

(Note: did not apply the maintainer comment's suggested one-liner — it would have stamped the Desktop's *shared* launch dir onto every Desktop session, which the existing docstring deliberately avoids.)

**Tests:** +2 regression tests; 22 pass.

prs.title: feat(webhook): hand off completed sessions to messaging platforms
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a trusted webhook-route contract:

```yaml
handoff_to: discord
```

After a successful webhook agent run, Hermes durably requests one handoff of the exact webhook session, creates one thread under Discord's configured home channel, and atomically moves routing ownership from the webhook source key to the destination thread key. The session ID and role-aware transcript are preserved, the source route is removed, and the next Discord thread event resolves to that same session.

### Verified premise and cause

Before this change, `gateway/platforms/webhook.py::_handle_webhook` created a one-shot `webhook:{route}:{delivery_id}` session, `_record_delivery_id()` deduplicated only in process memory, `send()` handled legacy delivery, and `on_processing_complete()` closed the webhook session. The adapter never durably bound a provider delivery ID to that exact session or requested the existing handoff machinery, so a completed webhook run could not safely become a restart-surviving conversation on another platform.

This PR extends the existing session/handoff infrastructure rather than adding a model tool or parallel routing system.

### Contract

- `handoff_to` is trusted route configuration; webhook payload fields cannot select or interpolate the destination.
- The initially supported destination is `discord`, using its configured home channel.
- Delivery is exclusive: no legacy parent-channel response is also emitted.
- `deliver_only: true` and incompatible profile combinations are rejected.
- A stable provider delivery ID is durably claimed before agent admission.
- Retries, concurrent duplicates, and restarts cannot create a second agent run, handoff, or thread.
- A delivery tombstone is global to the route and delivery ID, not destination-namespaced. If a route is retargeted, an old delivery ID remains owned by its first target and returns terminal `200 OK` with `status: conflict`; an intentionally new event must use a new ID.
- The exact session and transcript move through a compare-and-swap route transition; one live session cannot remain reachable through both source and destination keys.
- Failure, cancellation, missing home configuration, invalid targets, and ambiguous hard-crash ownership finalize visibly without silently falling back to the parent conversation.
- Pending work is restart-recoverable. Already claimed work is not replayed after ambiguous process loss because the external thread/send may already have occurred.
- Existing webhook routes without `handoff_to`, and existing CLI/TUI handoffs, retain their prior behavior.

The implementation uses existing SQLite metadata and routing records. It adds no database migration, dependency, new framework, project-specific behavior, or model-tool surface.

## Related Issue

Related to #31565.

Companion Discord participation-tracker fix: #90348. That fix is intentionally not included in this PR; it was included only in the local manual-test composite so mention-free continuation could be validated after a gateway restart.

#31566 is adjacent active-run clarify-routing work and is not resolved here. Searches of open and merged issues/PRs found no duplicate implementation of durable exact-session webhook handoff.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/webhook.py`: validates the trusted route contract; fences durable input admission; suppresses legacy delivery; claims stable delivery IDs; handles duplicate, restart, and retarget recovery; requests the exact session once; and finalizes failure/cancellation atomically.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py` and `gateway/run.py`: replace the private dynamic runner-result attribute with typed `MessageEvent.agent_run_failed: Optional[bool]`; preserve event identity across rewrites; generalize handoff processing; reject unsafe parent-channel fallback; and fence stale, failed, partial, interrupted, cancelled, or unadmitted turns.
- `gateway/session.py`, `gateway/turn_context.py`, and `hermes_state.py`: add token-fenced active-turn admission, durable request/claim ownership, compare-and-swap route moves, restart reconciliation, compression-lineage handling, source-route removal, and exact-session transcript preservation using existing storage structures.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`, `agent/turn_context.py`, and `run_agent.py`: carry and reconcile the durable active-turn boundary through persistence, compression, interruption, and recovery.
- `gateway/config.py` preserves authenticated Discord home provenance and default-profile safety.
- `cli-config.yaml.example` and `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/webhooks.md` document configuration, exclusive delivery, stable-ID requirements, retarget conflicts, restart behavior, and hard-crash no-replay semantics.
- Tests cover exact-session movement, durable admission, concurrency, duplicate deliveries, retargeting, real-SQLite restart/cancellation recovery, compression, source cleanup, destination failures, legacy webhook behavior, and CLI/TUI compatibility.

### Review-feedback dispositions

1. The dynamic `_agent_run_failed` convention was replaced by typed `MessageEvent.agent_run_failed`. `False` is authoritative success, `True` is failure/partial/interrupted/cancelled, and `None` means no authoritative result.
2. Delivery claims deliberately remain global to route + stable delivery ID. Namespacing by target would allow a replay to create a second run/thread after configuration changes. A retargeted replay instead remains owned by the first target and terminates with `200/conflict`.
3. The no-parent-fallback behavior and failure taxonomy were preserved.
4. Real temporary `state.db` coverage includes:
   - `test_real_state_db_duplicate_replay_survives_adapter_restart`
   - `test_real_state_db_duplicate_preserves_interactive_handoff`
   - `test_real_state_db_offloaded_claim_cancellation_is_reconciled`
   - `test_real_route_move_error_after_cancellation_cleans_source`
   - `test_pending_handoff_recovers_after_real_db_restart_and_creates_one_thread`

## How to Test

All repository tests were run through `scripts/run_tests.sh` with isolated temporary runtime state.

### Latest current-main integration

- Current main: `f751a8c5467c41500e505d90cb0eb8b70929080f`
- Final public PR head: `704b661a5ed57c69c61dae5a88881b8942738cd6`
- Local-only integration: `9b16936537f228ef40eb759860fed4ab26730c54`
- Integration parents: current main and the final PR head above
- Integration tree: `2e3998058a927f3d20f0910a5e1395574908612c`
- New-main semantic seam selection: **9 passed**
- Fresh integration full suite: **38,386 passed, 214 failed, 328 skipped**
- Fresh exact-main full-suite baseline: **38,183 passed, 216 failed, 328 skipped**
- Both runs had the same 70-file failure set. All 203 additional candidate tests passed; the two-failure count difference was in host/process-sensitive baseline tests.

The fresh merge was textually conflict-free across a 184-commit main advance. The two deterministic failures in changed test files reproduced on exact current main: the FTS projection assertion and TUI custom-model assertion. No webhook/handoff feature test failed.

A separate checkpoint-summary scratch probe failed identically on exact current main and the local integration. It is an upstream follow-up, not a PR regression, and is not used here as evidence for broader checkpoint-v2 semantics.

After the PR was marked ready, GitHub continued to serve stale synthetic merge `1854ecebf5ff112a5591e478dab8e5ee9881b3fe`, whose first parent is older main commit `62b2d78025c349996e753c6f7c748de035eb8048`. It is therefore not cited as current-merge evidence. The conflict-free local merge above was constructed from the actual current branch tip and exact public head; its full-suite comparison is the current validation boundary.

### Focused and compatibility matrices

1. Durable handoff/state/config matrix:

2. Webhook + CLI/TUI + destination compatibility matrix:
