
   Fresh integration result: **704 passed, 1 failed**. The single TUI failure reproduced on exact current main.

3. Focused durable-admission/recovery selection: **91 passed**.

### Static checks

- `ruff check .`: **passed**
- `python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: **passed across 1,014 files**
- `git diff --check`: **passed**
- `python scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py`: **passed**
- Independent read-only review of session aliasing, concurrency/idempotency, failure/restart recovery, backward compatibility, and the current-main delta: **PASS; no unresolved PR finding**

### Companion-PR seam verification

A local-only composite combined final #90385 with #90348 head `8fcbb1374fbd68b7340bfa0b0c44cfade98a0bfd`.

- Composite SHA: `5415079b95716120c84873a685f6842f20b170b9`
- #90348 focused tests: **7 passed**
- #90385 composite-focused tests: **145 passed**
- Seam matrix: **401 passed, 1 exact-main-reproduced FTS failure**

No #90348 code is included in this PR.

### Manual end-to-end validation

Validated on the standard macOS Hermes installation using the local-only composite above and a temporary loopback-only route in the default profile:

1. Stable delivery ID `manual-pr90385-default-001` returned **HTTP 202 Accepted**.
2. Exactly one private Discord destination thread was created and received the Hermes handoff response.
3. No legacy response appeared in the parent channel.
4. Replaying the same delivery ID returned the expected **HTTP 200 duplicate** response and created no second run or thread.
5. The default gateway was restarted before the destination reply.
6. A fresh message inside the private thread, without mentioning the bot and without replying to another message, requested the original context token.

This behaviorally demonstrated restart-surviving context continuity through the exact handed-off session without inspecting the live state database.

prs.body:
Adds `multiplayer-outpost` (`v0.4.0`, pinned to `antimeme-ai/multiplayer-plugins@94bb670da1221c1bc97dcbcd61a92bb00bb32f16`, `subdir: hermes`) to `plugin-catalog/`.

### Summary
- **Tier 1 (MCP Wiring):** `hermes multiplayer setup [--write]` atomically configures `mcp_servers.multiplayer` (`timeout: 90`, `connect_timeout: 30`) exposing all 13 `mp-outpost` MCP tools (`outpost_status`, `party_list`, `party_members`, `party_friends`, `party_invite`, `party_join`, `party_leave`, `friend_add`, `party_poll`, `board_read`, `party_wait`, `party_send`, `board_post`).
- **Tier 2 (1-Verb CLI & Unread Hook):** Registers `hermes multiplayer {login, add, invite, join, leave, friends, setup, status, doctor, parties}` and a non-blocking `pre_llm_call` unread-message pulse check (`UnreadNotificationHook`).
- **Tier 3 (Gateway Platform Adapter):** Registers `MultiplayerPlatformAdapter` via `ctx.register_platform("multiplayer", ...)` for bounded `party_wait` delivery over Room Protocol v2 (`mp2`) TLS 1.3 WebSockets, 1-verb room/friend helpers, pre-exec secret/flag refusal, and per-message 64-bit CSPRNG nonce fencing for remote peer chat and `agent_card` payloads.

### Rule 13 Disclosures & Verification
- Spawns the user-installed local `mp-outpost` binary on `PATH` (`shell=False`, bounded timeouts); does not auto-download or install binaries.
- When configured as a Gateway platform, runs a bounded `mp-outpost --json party wait` loop (`<= 45s`) and terminates child processes cleanly on `stop()` / EOF.
- `hermes multiplayer setup --write` updates Hermes YAML configuration (and `.bak`) with mode `0600`, refusing symlinks; zero files written during import or `register()`.
- `requires_env: []`; never reads Hermes secret stores or local private keys; pre-exec secret refusal blocks invite tokens, recovery keys, device credentials, and PEM keys before spawning `mp-outpost`.
- No telemetry, no self-updater, no core overrides.
- Verified with `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py`, `scripts/ci/catalog_entry_fields.py`, `scripts/ci/check_contributor_emails.py`, and `hermes_cli.plugin_validate.validate_plugin_dir` (15/15 PASS, `security scan: safe`, 0 warnings).

prs.title: Cursor rule files now apply by type: always-on in the prompt, file-scoped on touch, described ones on demand (inspired by Cursor)
prs.body:
A project's Cursor rule files say when each rule applies, but Hermes put every one of them, settings header and all, into every conversation. Now only the always-on rules sit in the prompt, a rule for certain files shows up the moment the agent opens one of those files, and the rest are listed so the agent can read them when they fit.

**Outcome:** `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files load by the rule type their front matter declares, as in Cursor, so scoped rules stop costing tokens on every turn and the front matter no longer reaches the model.

Source: Cursor rules docs (https://cursor.com/docs/rules: Always / Auto Attached by globs / Agent Requested by description / Manual) and Cursor CLI changelog v2026.11.19 ("Rules whose front matter includes a YAML comment ... now apply as written", https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog). Also lines up with CLI v2026.11.12 "file-scoped rules ... it now gets that rule even if the file is empty".

## What changes

| Rule file front matter | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `alwaysApply: true` (or none) | body + raw front matter in system prompt | body in system prompt, front matter stripped |
| `globs: *.tsx` | body + front matter in system prompt on every turn | one index line; body appended to the tool result of the first file-tool call naming a matching file (once) |
| `description: …` only | body + front matter in system prompt | one index line with path + description; agent `read_file`s it on demand |
| `alwaysApply: false`, nothing else | same as above | index line marked "manual rule" |

Every rule stays reachable (the index names its path). `.cursorrules` (plain file) is unchanged. An `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.hermes.md` still shadows `.cursor/rules` entirely, at startup and for glob attachment.

Front matter is Cursor's dialect, not YAML (`globs: *.ts` is a YAML alias error), so it is read line by line: unquoted, quoted, `[...]` and `- item` list values, and a trailing `# comment` are accepted.

## Changes
- `agent/cursor_rules.py` (new, ~160 lines): rule parser, glob matcher (`**` spans dirs, a slash-free pattern matches any basename), startup split into always-bodies + index.
- `agent/prompt_builder.py::_load_cursorrules`: uses the split. Net +3 lines.
- `agent/subdirectory_hints.py`: `SubdirectoryHintTracker` loads glob rules once at init/rebind (only when `.cursor/rules` exists and is the active context type) and attaches a matching rule's body to the tool result, once per rule, through the same injection scan + 32K cap as subdirectory hints. The system prompt is never rebuilt, so prompt caching is unaffected.
- Docs: `user-guide/features/context-files.md` rule-type table.

## Live repro (real `hermes chat`, Nous `openai/gpt-6-luna`, isolated HOME, reading the run's own `state.db`)

Project: `style.mdc` (alwaysApply), `react.mdc` (`globs: *.tsx  # react files only`, marker ZEBRA-7731), `deploy.mdc` (description only, marker OKAPI-4410), `src/App.tsx`.

| check | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| ALWAYS body in system prompt | yes | yes |
| GLOB body in system prompt | yes | **no** |
| DEPLOY body in system prompt | yes | **no** (index line only) |
| `globs:` / `alwaysApply` text in system prompt | yes | **no** |
| "read src/App.tsx, what ZEBRA marker do the rules require?" | `ZEBRA-7731` (from prompt) | `// ZEBRA-7731`; `read_file` tool result ends with `[Cursor rule attached: .cursor/rules/react.mdc (matches src/App.tsx)]` |
| "which region do staging deploys go to?" | (in prompt) | model ran `read_file .cursor/rules/deploy.mdc` from the index, answered `OKAPI-4410` |

## Tests
- `tests/agent/test_subdirectory_hints.py::test_cursor_rule_types_split_startup_prompt_and_file_touch`: red on main, green here (startup split, attach-once, non-matching file, AGENTS.md shadowing).
- `::test_cursor_rule_front_matter_dialect` (parametrized): comment stripping, unquoted/quoted/list globs, glob semantics.
- `tests/agent/` locally: 15097 passed, 0 failed (one collection error in `test_vault_key_storage.py`: `keyring` not installed on this host, unrelated). `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

## Not covered
- Glob attachment reads `path` / `file_path` args only; a terminal `cat src/App.tsx` does not attach (directory hints do scan terminal commands). V4A `patch` headers attach once #143868 lands its header-path collection here too.
- Rules attached mid-session are not re-attached after context compaction (same as subdirectory hints today).
- Heads-up: #112432 (PermissionError guard) touches `_cursorrules_candidates`; no overlap with the lines changed here.

prs.title: chore(plugin-catalog): update detonator to v0.5.2
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Updates `plugin-catalog/detonator.yaml` from v0.4.0 to **v0.5.2**, pinned to `shreyasudupi/hermes-plugin-detonator@74aaaf1a74d5bd8244e28f389fb2e66c101ee1ce` (tag `v0.5.2`). v0.5.0 and v0.5.1 were never tagged on their own, so this covers everything since v0.4.0.

### Major changes

1. **Skill testing (new): `/detonate-skill` and `hermes detonate-skill`.** It tests a Hermes skill from a folder, an installed skill's name, or `owner/repo/folder@sha`.
   - First it reads the skill's files (SKILL.md and up to 400 files) for planted instructions, hidden text and download-and-run lures. These checks run on the host and only read the files.
   - Then it runs up to 24 command blocks and 10 scripts from the skill in the sandbox, with both outside monitors watching. It compares the hosts the skill reaches with the hosts it names.
   - A new NOT ENOUGH COVERAGE verdict covers a run where too little could be run.
2. **Disk protection (new rule `disk_flood`).** A test that writes more than 256 MB to its output folder, or prints more than 64 MB, is stopped and reported. The folder is checked five times a second, so a very fast writer got to 1.3 to 3.5 GB before the stop in tests. Free disk space is watched once a second. An MCP package install that grows by more than 512 MB is stopped.
3. **Stronger detection, from testing on 4 real malicious MCP servers** (run only in a cloud sandbox, never on a personal machine).
   - The fake internet now answers on every port.
   - Three new rules: `reverse_shell`, `obfuscated_code` and `collection_service`.
   - Wallet decoys and install-time `curl`/`wget` checks.
   - v0.4.0 rated two of the four only REVIEW. v0.5.2 rates them DANGEROUS, DANGEROUS, SUSPICIOUS and SUSPICIOUS.

### Minor changes

- **Fewer false alarms on honest servers and skills:**
  - A tool reading its own config, such as Kubernetes and `~/.kube/config`.
  - Python servers whose `requests` opens `~/.netrc`.
  - Address variables such as `SIYUAN_URL`.
  - Sentry's telemetry being called a time bomb.
  - Emoji in tool descriptions.
  - A few `/proc` and time-zone cases.
- **Fail closed.** For MCP servers and skills, a full test whose outside tracer failed or never attached gives ERROR instead of a clean verdict. (The text-only skill check, which the user picks, runs no tracer and says so.)
- **Hostile SKILL.md files can't stall the text check for minutes.** It is cut off about 30 seconds in, and a check that runs out of time is reported (`skill_not_fully_read`, high), never clean.
- **Download hardening:**
  - git ignores the user's personal and system git settings (only network settings are kept: proxy, TLS, client certificates, and `core.longpaths`).
  - npm refuses git and web-address dependencies and stops past 1 GB.
- **Smaller items:**
  - `/detonate-mcp <server-name>` now passes the entry's `env:` names, so servers get their fake keys.
  - An io_uring warning in the report.
  - Clearer verdict lines.
  - Tighter CI.

Entry changes:
- The description now covers skills and disk protection, and the disclosure is updated (see below).
- New cover image (now names plugins, MCP servers and skills).
- A 7th screenshot showing a skill result (`docs/store/7-skill-trojan-helper.png`).

## Hermes surfaces used

- `ctx.register_tool`: `detonate_plugin`, `detonator_report` (unchanged, both declared in `capabilities`)
- `ctx.register_command`: `/detonate`, `/detonate-mcp`, `/detonate-skill` (new)
- `ctx.register_cli_command`: `hermes detonate`, `hermes detonate-mcp`, `hermes detonate-skill` (new)
- No hooks, no middleware and no core overrides.
- **Rule 9 notes** (unchanged since v0.4.0):
  - `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home` finds the Hermes home folder.
  - `hermes_cli.plugin_catalog` is read to resolve catalog names.
  - `hermes_cli.config` is used to read the named `mcp_servers` entry through Hermes's own reader.
  - `hermes_yaml` loads `plugin.yaml` the way Hermes does.
  - Happy to switch to a public seam if one exists.

## Security scan: why it says caution

`hermes plugins validate` passes with Hermes v0.23.4. The security scan now says **caution** (v0.4.0 was safe). It reports 23 high hits. Every one is in Detonator's own detection code, its sandbox preparation, its CI check or its docs, not something Detonator does on your machine:

| Hits | Scanner rule | Where | Why it is there |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | `tunnel_service` (8), `exfil_service` (3) | `engine/rules.py` 177, 554, 557, 1718; `engine/mcp.py` 964; `engine/skill_text.py` 306, 308; `ci/check_fixtures.py` 137 | The tunnel and request-collector host names (ngrok, Pipedream, webhook.site, ...) that the `collection_service` rule matches (`rules.py` 554, 557), the finding text that names them, the list of paste and tunnel hosts the skill text check treats as a lure (`skill_text.py` 306, 308), and the CI fixture check that expects that rule. Detonator never contacts these hosts. |
| 5 | `inline_shell_exec` | `engine/rules.py` 402; `engine/skill_text.py` 72, 73, 807, 811 | The pattern that finds inline ``!`command` `` snippets in a skill (72), the pattern for ordinary inline code next to it (73), and the report text that warns about them (rule `skill_inline_shell`). Detonator never runs them on the host. |
| 2 | `curl_pipe_shell` | `engine/rules.py` 346; `docs/RULES.md` 176 | The explanation text of the download-and-run finding, and its row in the rules doc. |
| 2 | `dump_all_env` | `engine/skill_text.py` 331, 469 | Patterns that recognise secret file paths (`~/.ssh/`, `.aws/credentials`, ...) and `echo 'export ...' >> ~/.zshrc` lines in a skill's text. |
| 2 | `sudo_usage` | `engine/skill.py` 205, 220 | Removes `sudo` from a skill's commands before running them in the sandbox, which has no root, so the command is tried as the normal user. |
| 1 | `eval_string` | `engine/mcp_sources.py` 785 | Part of the `obfuscated_code` check: flags a package that calls `eval(` on code decoded from a long list of numbers. |

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- Bumps `sha`, `version`, `description`, `image` and `screenshots` (all pinned to the same commit), and adds screenshot 7.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

Unchanged from v0.4.0:
- Requires Docker.
- Runs `git` and `docker` only after you approve each run (except `docker info` and `docker image inspect` for `/detonate check`).
- Refuses to run unattended.
- Writes reports under its own plugin-data folder.
- Never reads your `.env`, `auth.json` or keys.
- For `/detonate-mcp`, reads only the named `mcp_servers` entry and downloads packages in a separate locked-down container.

New since v0.4.0:
- **Skills.**
  - For an installed name, it reads only `SKILL.md` files under the Hermes `skills/` folder and its `.hub/quarantine`, plus the current project's `.hermes/skills` and `.agents/skills`, to find the skill.
  - It copies the skill into the run folder. Nothing in the user's skills folder changes, and nothing from the skill runs on the user's machine.
  - Skill commands run in a sandbox built from a digest-pinned `python:3.11-bookworm`, with `node` copied from a digest-pinned `node` image, under the same locked-down settings and a 240-second limit. One difference: the skill's fake home may hold runnable files (skills install tools there).
- **Monitor image.** It now installs `iptables` as well as `strace` from Debian's signed archive. The fake internet uses one `iptables` rule inside its own empty network to answer every port.
- **Clean-up container.** If the tested code locked its folders, they are removed with a short-lived container from the sandbox image (no network, no capabilities, non-root).
- **git settings.** git runs without the user's personal and system settings. Only network settings (proxy, TLS, client certificates) and `core.longpaths` are kept, so a filter or credential helper the user installed never runs on downloaded code.
- **Disk.** A test is stopped when it writes or prints too much, or when the disk's free space drops too far (by more than the limits plus 1 GB, or under 512 MB free). So other disk activity of more than about 1.3 GB (1.8 GB for an MCP install run) while a test runs ends that test early, as ERROR.

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins install detonator --enable` (Docker must be running).
2. `hermes detonate memanto` (choose the full test) gives NO FINDINGS.
3. `hermes detonate-skill NousResearch/hermes-agent/optional-skills/productivity/siyuan@77236c4ad3b31764732b3d91f7fc5aefbabf5093` gives NO FINDINGS.
4. CI: https://github.com/shreyasudupi/hermes-plugin-detonator/actions

## Checklist

- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] `hermes plugins validate` passes with Hermes v0.23.4 (security scan: caution, every hit explained above)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Apple Silicon, Docker Desktop), Ubuntu (GitHub Actions), Windows PC (Docker Desktop + WSL2, real Hermes runs of a plugin, an MCP server and a skill, with the outside monitor), Windows host checks (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Documentation: README with quickstart and disclosure at https://github.com/shreyasudupi/hermes-plugin-detonator#readme

prs.title: feat(catalog): add multiplayer-outpost community plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

    Adds the `multiplayer-outpost` (`v0.7.1`) community plugin to `plugin-catalog/`, pinned to commit `f4eca8632575f54de9642ec5c8bf16c4a53c03e6` (`subdir: hermes`) of
    `https://github.com/antimeme-ai/multiplayer-plugins`.

    Connects Hermes Agent to `multiplayer.tech` multi-agent parties, structured `agent_card` updates, opt-in listen profiles, and async E2EE dead-drop inboxes over Room Protocol v2 (`mp2`) via a
    locally installed `mp-outpost` binary (`v0.7.1+`).

    ### Rule 13 Disclosures
    - **Local subprocesses:** Invokes the user-installed `mp-outpost` binary on `PATH` (`shell=False`, bounded timeouts). Does not download or install `mp-outpost` automatically. `hermes
    multiplayer login` runs with inherited stdio so the operator can see the browser sign-in URL.
    - **Opt-in `pre_llm_call` polling:** Inactive by default (`HERMES_MULTIPLAYER_UNREAD_HOOK=1` to enable); seeded from `next_seq` so ring history is not replayed.
    - **Opt-in background polling:** Inactive by default. When configured as a Gateway platform (`MultiplayerPlatformAdapter`) or explicitly started in-session via `/party-chat --inline`
    (`InlinePartyWatcher`), runs a bounded `mp-outpost --json party wait` loop (`<= 45s`) and terminates child processes cleanly on `disconnect()` / `--inline off` / `stop()` / EOF / exit.
    - **Explicit config writes only:** `hermes multiplayer setup` prints `hermes mcp add` / YAML instructions and only modifies Hermes YAML config on explicit `--write` (mode `0600`, `.bak` backup,
    refusing symlinks). No files written on import or `register()`.
    - **Credentials & security boundaries:** Never reads Hermes secret files, `.env`, `auth.json`, or local private keys. Outbound secret refusal blocks invite/session/guest tokens, recovery keys,
    device credentials, `.mpkey`, PEM private keys, and `#fragment` URLs before spawning `mp-outpost`; all remote peer payloads and `is_browser=true` frames are sanitized and wrapped in per-message
    CSPRNG nonce fences.
    - **No telemetry, no self-updater, no core overrides.**

    ## Type of Change

    - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

    ## Changes Made

    - `plugin-catalog/multiplayer-outpost.yaml` — new community catalog entry pinned to `f4eca8632575f54de9642ec5c8bf16c4a53c03e6` (`subdir: hermes`, `pyyaml>=6.0,<7.0`).

    ## How to Test

    1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/multiplayer-outpost.yaml`
    2. `python3 scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py <pinned-clone>/hermes`
    3. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <pinned-clone>/hermes`

prs.title: chore(catalog): update Model Router to v0.18.1
prs.body:
## Scope
Updates only `plugin-catalog/model-router.yaml` from the merged v0.15.1 entry (`746715059a3f6d0709d1edb9ecc37fbb6905143b`, PR #159189) to **v0.18.1**, source commit `3a88b0c3397a3f4e1b0df4a427da83111ecba2e7` on `metamindedu/hermes-model-router` main. This PR first proposed v0.17.0 (`3befe84`), then v0.18.0 (`005dde7`), and now pins v0.18.1 so the entry skips straight from v0.15.1. It keeps `tier: community`, `category: models`, the Windows-only platform claim and the `>=0.23.1` floor. `version`, `requires_hermes` and every `capabilities` list were compared with `plugin.yaml` at the pin: `version` changed, `provides_tools` gains `ask_advisor` (v0.16.0), and `provides_hooks` drops `api_request_error` (its only user, the retired process-job observer, was removed in v0.18.0). The screenshot is byte-identical and re-pinned to the new SHA.

## What changed for users since v0.15.1 (from `docs/releases/` at the pin)
- **v0.16.0 / v0.16.1, `ask_advisor`:** a built-in `advise` slot and a tool that consults that slot's model synchronously in one fresh native child kept read-only by a `pre_tool_call` guard (fixed 300-second limit); the `advise` purpose is refused through ordinary `delegate_task`. The status line names the child `조언`.
- **v0.17.0, custom task slots:** up to four operator-defined slots `custom:<name>` with a label and one-line scope, shared by every profile; each profile picks the model. The purpose enum lists them from new sessions, with label and scope marked as untrusted descriptive data.
- **v0.18.0, equal slots and per-slot runtime limits:**
  - The Heavy/Light classes are removed everywhere (code, settings page, bundled policy skill v2.0.0, docs). Every slot follows the profile's main model or uses its own model.
  - Each slot has its own total runtime limit; a slot without one stops after **two hours** (`0` = no plugin limit). The ordinary delegation limit stays separate and off by default.
  - The plugin reads only its current formats (settings schema 5, timeouts schema 3, per-slot native continuation blocks). The retired process-job paths (`coding_route` start/status/join, worker, `lib/`) and routing rerun spares are removed; `coding_route` only reads settings.
  - Upgrading from older versions uses the one-time operator script `scripts/migrate_to_v018.py` (dry run by default, `--apply` writes): it keeps every slot's effective model, resets slot limits to the default, keeps originals once as `<file>.pre-v018`, and refuses (writing nothing) states it cannot carry over.
- **v0.18.1, custom-slot limit cleanup:** removing a custom slot now also removes its runtime limit from every profile's `timeouts.json` in the same preview/apply flow, so defining the same ID again starts on the two-hour default. Previews list each profile cleanup, fence absent/unreadable timeout files and profile inventory against concurrent changes, and report incomplete post-save cleanup as `partial` (repaired on the next custom-slot save).

The description and known issues (upgrade order, partial save, custom slots, delegation model and validator warnings) were updated for these. No other entry text changed.

## Validation of the exact source
- `hermes plugins validate <clean clone at 3a88b0c> --install-deps` returns **`ok: true`** with two warnings:
  1. `security scan caution: exec_string (plugin.js:3495)`: the page's own staged-save `exec('stage', …)` call to the plugin's CLI command through Hermes `cli.exec`. No `eval`, `new Function` or dynamic code.
  2. **Private core imports: 34 sites** (68 at v0.17.0; the removed process-job stack accounted for the difference). Same inherited public-surface debt as the earlier entries.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/model-router.yaml --json` returns ok with no errors or warnings.
- Tests on this Windows host with the installed Desktop source, at the exact commit (`3a88b0c`):
  - Python (clean clone): 1301 passed; the 33 failures are identical to the v0.18.0 / v0.17.0 baseline (environment-dependent tests against the installed core), none new.
  - Node: 535 tests, 527 passed; the only 8 failures are identical by name to the base (`actual SDK …` tests). Without `HERMES_DESKTOP_SOURCE_ROOT` (as in CI): 521 tests, 487 passed, 34 skipped, 0 failures.
- Independent read-only release reviews: v0.18.0 GO-WITH-FIXES (blocking findings fixed before commit); v0.18.1 underwent three review rounds (two NO-GOs catching late-limit, unreadable-recovery, and inventory races; all fixed with regression tests, then GO).
- GitHub Actions `Desktop plugin tests` passed on `3a88b0c`.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: feat(desktop): introduce redesigned agent workspace with classic recovery
prs.body:
Introduces the redesigned Hermes Desktop & shared web workspace as the default shell, with one-toggle recovery back to the classic shell unchanged. - **Toggle & recovery:** **Settings → Appearance → Advanced → This device → Redesigned interface** turns the redesign off and restores the classic shell unchanged (classic exposes the same switch under **Appearance → Window & layout**). Sessions, profiles, pins, backend `projects.db` projects, and settings keep their identities across the switch; pane layout persists independently per shell. - **Navigation & splits:** One global rail (`Chats`, `Agents`, `Capabilities`, `Library`, `Routines`, `Settings`) with right-click **Open in split** on every route-backed destination (`route-tile.tsx`, `RouteTileContext`), a chat sidebar grouped `machine → agent → project → chat`, a dedicated per-agent hub (`Overview`, `History`, `Settings`), `⌘⇧S` status-bar toggle (`store/portal-status-bar.ts`), and a live design system reference at `#/design-system` (`⌘K` → *"Design system"*). ## Before / after | | Classic (`main`, or toggle off) | Redesigned (default) | | --- | --- | --- | | New chat | ![classic landing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/classic-landing.png) | ![redesigned landing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-landing.png) | | Conversation | ![classic conversation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/classic-conversation.png) | ![redesigned conversation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-conversation.png) | | Capabilities | ![classic capabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/classic-capabilities.png) | ![redesigned capabilities](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-capabilities.png) | | Settings | ![classic settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/classic-settings.png) | ![redesigned settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-settings.png) | New surfaces with no classic counterpart: | Agents | Agent settings | Light | Phone (390px) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ![agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-agents.png) | ![agent settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-agent-settings.png) | ![light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-light.png) | ![phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-phone.png) | ## Shell gate & classic recovery One persisted choice, one presentation read, one CSS gate (`html[data-shell='portal']`). Nothing else decides which shell renders. ```mermaid flowchart LR Choice["$shellChoice
localStorage, null = default on"] --> Preferred["$portalPreferred
behaviour every window agrees on"] Choice --> Portal["$portalShell
this window renders the redesign"] Portal --> Hook["usePortalShell()"] Portal --> Attr["html[data-shell='portal']"] Attr --> CSS[":root[data-shell='portal'] rules"] Preferred --> Policy["shell-policy.ts
named behaviour gates"] ``` ```ts // apps/desktop/src/store/shell-variant.ts export const $shellChoice = persistentAtom('hermes.desktop.agentShell.v1', null, …) export const $portalPreferred = computed($shellChoice, choice => choice !== false) // HUD wears the redesign's tokens (portal-hud.css); popped-out Browser stays classic. export const rendersPortalShell = (choice: boolean | null): boolean => choice !== false && !isBrowserWindow() export const $portalShell = computed($shellChoice, rendersPortalShell) ``` - `installShellAttribute()` runs before the first paint so no surface flashes a mixed shell. - Wording follows the toggle via typed per-locale overlays (`apps/desktop/src/i18n/redesign/`, `electron/shell-wording.ts`, `src/lib/shell-copy.ts`): | Classic | Redesigned | | --- | --- | | Sessions | Chats | | Artifacts | Library | | Profiles | Agents | | Connectors | Connections | | Cron jobs | Routines | | Gateways | Machines | ## Sidebar, projects & agents - **Backend-unified Projects (`store/portal-projects.ts`, `store/portal-projects-sync.ts`, `portal-agent-projects.tsx`, `portal-create-project-dialog.tsx`):** Per-agent projects sync with `projects.db` (`projects.list` / `create` / `update` / `delete` / `add_folder`), supporting both lightweight folder-less chat groups and folder-backed workspaces. Session membership matches explicit assignments (including explicit detach) first, then longest `cwd` prefix; folder-backed `+ New chat` launches in the project's `cwd` via `requestStartWorkSession`, and project menus expose *Reveal folder*, *Add/Attach folder*, *Appearance* (`ProjectAppearancePicker`), *Rename*, and *Delete*. - **Sidebar ergonomics (`portal-sidebar.tsx`, `portal-sidebar-head.tsx`, `use-agent-sidebar.ts`):** Active rail icon toggles its panel (`⌘B` still toggles); drag-to-pin, drag-to-unpin, and drag-to-split work on redesigned rows; sidebar search surfaces archived matches while keeping them hidden at rest; *Mark all read* appears in the header only when unread chats exist; per-agent chat caps water-fill the live Agents viewport (`agent-chat-cap.ts`, `portal-sidebar.tsx`) with session-only stepped *Show more* (+10) and a sticky *Show less* footer (`simplified-session-list.tsx`). - **Agents & Bot Mode parity (`agent-dialogs.tsx`, `overview-actions.tsx`, `directory.tsx`, `portal-agent-menu.tsx`, `portal-bot-agent-items.tsx`):** - Agents UI exposes *New window*, *Export agent…*, and *Import agent…* alongside *Duplicate*, *Set default*, and *Copy agent folder path*. - Bot Mode's empty chat screen (`[data-slot='bot_chat_empty']`) and live Screen viewer/thumbnail (`screen-pane.tsx`, `screen-hero.tsx`, `portal-shell.css`) wear the redesign's display/mono hierarchy and surface tokens. ## Capabilities, Library & Routines - prs.title: Termux: messages no longer fail because Python lacks os.link (fixes #158513, salvage #155843)
prs.body:
On Termux (Android), Python has no `os.link` at all, so the first message after install crashed while the gateway created its log-hashing salt, and every later turn failed with "The admitted turn failed." The places Hermes uses hard links now treat a missing `os.link` like a filesystem without hard links and take their existing fallback, so turns work on Termux.

Fixes #158513. Salvage of #155843 by @Ficeto (main fix) with the RoomLink cleanup commit by @kvnloo; both commits are kept with authorship intact. Related narrower attempts that this covers: #140083 (@KoNit-K, updater sites) and #141113 (@Mohd-Mursaleen, RoomLink secret).

## What changes

| Python without `os.link`, fresh `HERMES_HOME` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| First inbound message (`hash_for_log`, creates `log_hash_salt`) | `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'link'`, turn fails | `h:4289c54933`, 32-byte salt created |
| RoomLink grant secret (`hosted_room_peer`) | AttributeError (only `FileExistsError` was caught) | synced temp published with `os.replace` under a sibling flock; racing first users all get the same complete secret |
| Cron cancel marker, update marker | AttributeError | exclusive-create fallback |
| Update artifact staging / backup, local-model sideload, macOS libpython anchor | AttributeError | copy / symlink fallback as before |

**Root cause:** each site guarded `os.link` with `except OSError` (the hosted-room one with `FileExistsError` only), but a missing attribute raises `AttributeError`, so the documented "no hard links" fallback never ran. All 8 runtime `os.link(` sites on main are covered (`git grep "os\.link(" -- ':!tests' ':!evals'`).

## Our changes on top
- RoomLink fallback (6188865dd8, Greptile P1): the contributor fallback wrote the final secret in place, so a concurrent first user could read it empty or cache bytes a failed fsync then deleted. It now publishes the already-synced temp atomically under a lock and re-reads the winner.
- Trimmed the 8 new tests to 2 invariants in `tests/gateway/test_os_link_unavailable.py`: one parametrized case per publish site, plus a 16-thread concurrent first-use race (fails 3/3 on the in-place fallback, passes 3/3 now).
- Contributor email mapping for @Ficeto.

## Evidence
- **E2E (fresh interpreter, `del os.link` to imitate Termux, real `gateway.platforms.helpers.hash_for_log` on a fresh home):** main `CRASH: AttributeError module 'os' has no attribute 'link'`; head `hash: h:4289c54933`, `salt bytes: 32`.
- **Red on main:** with the 5 source files swapped back to main, all 6 test cases fail; on head, 6 pass. Hosted-room + test files: 22 passed.
- Neighbouring suites (hosted_room_peer, cron cancel ×2, update_lock, update_zip_two_phase): 144 passed, 2 skipped. Health check clean.
- Not covered: a real Termux device (none on this host). The reporter's traceback matches the main leg exactly.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab364a5/zHfk0Kjh-8A4FcKxZKXlc_JsOgGttZ.png)

prs.title: Fix(desktop): add reduced effects preference
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a device-local **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects** preference with **Full** and **Reduced** modes.

Reduced mode preserves visible working-state indicators while replacing continuous shimmer and moving-gradient effects with static equivalents. It also prevents the shared status pulse from scheduling Web Animations and renders the shared SVG loader once instead of maintaining a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.

**Full remains the default**, so existing visuals are unchanged unless the user explicitly enables Reduced mode.

Continuous CSS animations, Web Animations, and frame-driven SVG loaders can keep Chromium's compositor active even when the surrounding UI is unchanged. Merely slowing the animations does not materially reduce that cost because frames are still composited at the display refresh rate. This preference provides an explicit, reversible control without forcing Electron into software rendering or changing the operating system's global reduced-motion setting.

## Related Issue

Mitigates 
[#73082](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73082)
[#53902 ](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/53902)

This PR addresses persistent decorative and status-animation work. It does not claim to eliminate every feature-specific animation loop in Desktop.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Added a persisted, device-local reduced-effects preference in `apps/desktop/src/store/reduced-effects.ts`.
- Added Full/Reduced controls to Desktop Appearance settings.
- Disabled continuous CSS animations and transitions in Reduced mode.
- Rendered shimmer text and the active-session arc as static indicators in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the shared `StatusPulse` Web Animation timer in Reduced mode.
- Changed the shared SVG `Loader` to render one static frame instead of scheduling continuous frames in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the pending-image canvas shimmer loop in Reduced mode, preserving static output through resize/theme changes and retaining Full mode's existing animation cap.
- Added translated settings copy for all nine bundled Desktop locales.
- Added regression tests for persistence, startup restoration, live mode switching, status pulses, loader and canvas frame scheduling, static-canvas repainting, and settings-search routing.

## How to Test

1. Launch Hermes Desktop and open **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects**.
2. Leave the setting on **Full** and confirm shimmer, the moving active-session arc, status pulses, and loaders retain their current behavior.
3. Select **Reduced** and confirm the change applies immediately without restarting Desktop.
4. Start a chat or compaction and confirm status text and the active-session indicator remain visible but static.
5. Quit and reopen Desktop and confirm the Reduced preference persists.
6. Compare Hermes Helper (GPU), Hermes Helper (Renderer), and WindowServer activity before and after enabling Reduced mode.

Manual testing on macOS arm64 showed a dramatic reduction in GPU activity after selecting Reduced while preserving working-state visibility.

Automated validation of the refreshed source (Node 24.15.0, npm 11.17.0):

- Final focused effects/settings/canvas/i18n suites: 103 tests passed across 18 files.
- Full Desktop UI run before the final two-file canvas follow-up: 10,880 passed, 2 failed across 1,241 files. Both failures reproduce unchanged on upstream `300228d24c` in `src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts`; that file is not changed here. The final canvas follow-up passed the focused suite and fresh checks below.
- Desktop TypeScript check passed.
- Full Desktop ESLint passed with no errors; existing warnings remain, with no new warnings retained.
- Prettier and PR-relative `git diff --check` passed.
- Production Desktop build passed.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not run because this is a Desktop-only TypeScript/CSS change; focused Desktop tests and the production build passed
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26, Apple Silicon

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Relevant documentation update is N/A; the preference is described directly in the Appearance UI
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update is N/A; this is device-local Desktop display state
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update is N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: the implementation uses browser APIs supported by Electron on macOS, Windows, and Linux
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update is N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before/after Activity Monitor screenshots can be attached during review. Reduced mode was manually verified with active-session and compaction status states in the packaged macOS application.

prs.title: fix(cli): resolve whoami.exe from System32 for the Windows gateway identity check
prs.body:
The Windows gateway identity check runs whoami.exe by bare name, so a process whose PATH puts the Desktop app's bundled Git ahead of System32 resolves the coreutils whoami instead of the Windows one, which rejects /USER and fails with service_identity_unverified after an unclean shutdown

whoami.exe is now resolved from SystemRoot's System32 through a new hermes_platform resolver helper, so the Windows semantics are always the copy that runs

The home directory ACL fallback resolves whoami.exe through the same helper now, so the bundled Git coreutils copy cannot break _whoami_sid either

Verified with regression tests that shadow the bare name on PATH (fails on the previous code, passes with the resolver), the gateway runtime service suites, and the isolated-fixture suites the ACL module ships in locally; not exercised on native Windows

Related to #144907, which routes the other system tools through System32 but keeps this call site on the bare name

Related to #157671, which reports the same shadowing from the Desktop app

Fixes #157356

prs.title: chore(deps): allow Python 3.15 alongside the shipped 3.14
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets Hermes install and run on Python 3.15, and adds a non-blocking CI lane that runs the test suite there. PM still ships 3.14, so no user install changes. This is the groundwork for switching the bundled interpreter in #138139: it shows what breaks on 3.15 before anyone commits to the switch.

**Why now:** the `<3.15` cap exists because "3.14 is the newest python we know we have wheels for". That is no longer true for most of the lock. uv only records wheels for interpreters inside `requires-python`, so the lock *looked* 3.15-hostile. Checking PyPI showed that most compiled pins (`pydantic-core`, `jiter`, `cffi`, `markupsafe`, `pillow`, `lxml`, `numpy` and others) already ship `cp315` wheels at the locked version. Only a handful need a bump or a gate.

**Approach:** raise the ceiling, bump the two core pins that have 3.15 wheels in a newer release, and gate off 3.15 the dependencies that have none, using the existing `[tool.hermes.extras-platforms]` mechanism so PM refuses those extras with a clear message instead of failing a build.

## Related Issue

Refs #138139. That issue asks for the bundled-Python bump, which is a follow-up (see "Not in this PR"). A local 3.15.2 pilot is reported in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/138139#issuecomment-6724255957, and the Windows installer gap is #158064.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

**`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`**
- `requires-python` raised from `<3.15` to `<3.16`. The 3.11 floor is untouched, so the pre-PM updater bridge (`tests/compat/README.md`) is unaffected.
- `httptools` `>=0.6.3,<0.9` → `>=0.9.0,<0.11` (0.9.0 is the first with 3.15 wheels; pre-1.0 ceiling per the pinning policy).
- `pywin32` `<312` → `<313` (312 has 3.15 wheels).
- Gated off 3.15 (`python_version < '3.15'`), each with its reason in a comment:
  - `ruamel.yaml.clib` (core): no 3.15 wheels. ruamel.yaml falls back to its pure-Python loader there.
  - faster-whisper / `av` in `[voice]` and `[stt-whisper]`, `[kittentts]`, `[piper]`: onnxruntime has no 3.15 wheels in any release, and the misaki fork caps Python `<3.15`.
  - sherpa-onnx / sherpa-onnx-core / sentencepiece in `[wake]` and `[wake-sherpa]`: sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 has no 3.15 wheels (2.0.0 does, but that is a major bump for another PR).
- The matching `[tool.hermes.extras-platforms]` gates for `stt-whisper`, `kittentts`, `piper` and the new `wake-sherpa` entry, so the declared gates keep agreeing with dependency selection.
- Relocked with PM's pinned uv (0.13.5). The lock diff is large but mechanical: the only version changes are `httptools` 0.8.0 → 0.9.0 and `pywin32` 311 → 312. The rest is 613 added `cp315` wheel entries plus the gate markers.

**`.github/workflows/python-3-15.yml` (new)**
- Runs the full suite on 3.15 in 3 slices, daily, on `workflow_dispatch`, and on PRs that touch `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`.
- A separate workflow on purpose: `tests/ci/test_classify_changes.py` forbids `continue-on-error` in workflows that feed `all-checks-pass`, and this lane should report without blocking merges. It is not in `all-checks-pass`.
- Actions are SHA-pinned (copied from `tests.yml`) and the job ends with the clean-worktree step.

**Tests**
- `tests/pm/test_extras.py::test_faster_whisper_targets_are_gated` and `tests/test_project_metadata.py::test_wake_dependencies_and_runtime_gate_agree_on_supported_targets` evaluated platform markers against whichever interpreter ran them. They now pin `python_version` to the shipped 3.14, so they keep testing the platform contract on both lanes instead of failing on 3.15. No new tests: the change is dependency metadata, and the existing gate/selection contract tests cover it.

## How to Test

1. `uv lock --check` with uv 0.13.5: the lock is current.
2. On Python 3.15, a sync that may not build anything from source succeeds:
   `uv sync --locked --python 3.15 --extra all --group dev --extra anthropic --extra mistral --extra fal --extra modal --extra daytona --extra parallel-web --extra keychain --no-build`
3. With an isolated `HERMES_HOME`, `hermes --version` reports `Python: 3.15.x`, and `hermes --help` and the main entry modules (`run_agent`, `cli`, `gateway.run`, `hermes_cli.web_server`, `model_tools`) import.
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_project_metadata.py tests/pm/test_extras.py tests/ci tests/compat` on 3.15.
5. Dispatch the `Python 3.15` workflow for the full suite on Linux.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`chore(deps):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (open PRs mentioning a `<3.15` ceiling, #74244 and #83433, are the 3.14 work)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. On macOS three `tests/ci` files (`test_prompt_surface`, `test_update_ci_routing`, `test_update_transitive_routing`) fail identically on `main` because of the host (no `mapfile` in macOS bash, Linux sysconfig data), not this change
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes: existing contract tests adjusted, see above
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.4 arm64, Python 3.15.2 (Homebrew)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A: N/A. The supported/shipped interpreter is still 3.14, and the `pyproject.toml` comments explain the 3.15 allowance
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A: see "Not in this PR" for Windows
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Not in this PR

- **Bundled interpreter switch** (#138139): `pm/pyproject.toml`, `pm/uv.lock`, `pm/lock.json`, `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`, the Termux build and `scripts/build/mint_launchers.py` stay on 3.14. That is a release decision best taken once this lane is green.
- **Windows on 3.15:** `winrt-*` 3.2.1 has no 3.15 wheels (only the 4.x line does), so Windows 3.15 would build it from source. The CI lane is Linux only.
- **sdist-only on 3.15:** `pilk` (`[silk]`) and `python-olm` (`[matrix]`, Linux) build from source. The Linux lane will show whether they do.
- **Re-enabling the gated extras:** once onnxruntime ships 3.15 wheels, sherpa-onnx moves to 2.x and misaki lifts its cap, the `python_version < '3.15'` markers can go.

prs.title: fix(todo): refill a rebuilt agent's task list from the session store
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The todo list lives in memory on the `AIAgent`. The gateway builds a fresh agent per message, and that agent refills its list only by replaying the window it is handed (`_hydrate_todo_store`, through `_latest_todo_response`). Compaction archives the pre-boundary rows out of that window.

So whenever the last todo write predates the latest compaction and a new agent is then built (a backend restart, a session resume, a model switch), the next `todo_list` read answers an empty list at revision 0. An in-process compaction in the middle of a turn does not lose it, because it is the same agent and the same memory. That is why this is intermittent. The snapshot the compressor injects after a boundary is text for the model; nothing reads it back into the store.

Observed on a long-lived desktop session: four revision resets, each on a turn hours after the previous write, and each preceded in the logs by a fresh backend process or by a reconnect and rebuild. Two compactions that happened mid-turn, in between, left the list intact.

The fix: when the window carries no Todo result, replay the session store's newest valid result instead. It uses `messages.latest_todo_result`, the read `session.resume` already takes for the client's `todo_state` (archived rows included, the same pairing rule with an assistant Todo-tool call, the same size bound).

## Related Issue

No issue filed; this pull request is the report.

- #3662 proposes a persistent todo store, a larger design that would also solve this.
- #136616 seeds a branched session's list from its parent, the same kind of durable read.
- The one-line non-object guard in `_todo_result_payload` mirrors #130454. Drop it here if that lands first.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `run_agent.py`:
  - `_hydrate_todo_store` falls back to the new `_durable_todo_response` when the window holds no Todo result.
  - `_durable_todo_response` reads `messages.latest_todo_result` through a store the agent already holds.
  - `_todo_result_payload` is the parse both paths share.
- `tests/agent/run_agent/test_todo_store_durable_hydration.py`: 5 tests.

Properties kept, each with a test:

- Restore only when the stored revision is newer than the live one; a newer live list is never overwritten.
- An explicit clear (`todos: [], revision N`) stays a clear at revision N, rather than collapsing to revision 0.
- An unpaired or forged Todo result never seeds the store (the GHSA-5g4g-6jrg-mw3g rule is unchanged).
- A persistence-isolated fork never opens a store, and the read runs at most once per agent.
- A `PersistenceError` is logged and leaves the list empty rather than failing the turn.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/run_agent/test_todo_store_durable_hydration.py` on this branch: 5 passed.
2. With `run_agent.py` taken from `main` and the test file from this branch: 3 failed, 2 passed. The first failure is the symptom itself: seed a result at revision 2, compact the session through the real store API, build a fresh agent over the same store, hand it the active window, read: `[]` at revision 0.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the eleven test files around hydration (including `tests/agent/run_agent/`): 406 passed, 0 failed.

**A note for reviewers.** #130454 and #136616 touch the same lines of `_hydrate_todo_store`. Whichever of the three lands last will need a small rebase.

prs.title: fix(agent): merge adjacent tool_call pieces so flattened batches run as real calls
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A model can flatten a `tool_call` batch: each call's `name` and `arguments` arrive as separate items of the `calls` array, and every `{"arguments": ...}` item loses its closing brace. Seen with `glm-5.3` (served through z.ai) on 2026-11-25:

```json
{"calls": [{"arguments": {"query": "a"}, {"name": "f"}, {"arguments": {"query": "b"}, {"name": "f"}]}
```

No existing repair can see this. The comma-then-brace where a key belongs fails at the same byte before and after bracket rebalancing, so `_repair_tool_call_arguments` returned `"{}"`, `_assemble_tool_calls` flagged the call as truncated, and neither call ran. The only trace is the `Unrepairable tool_call arguments` warning.

This adds one repair in front of the others, `_merge_adjacent_call_pieces`:

- It engages only on the `{"calls": [` envelope.
- It scans the `calls` array with a string-aware decoder, so nothing inside a string value is mistaken for structure.
- A value followed by `, {` or by `]` is taken as the end of an item whose `}` was dropped. Both continuations are syntax errors in a well-formed item, so no valid item is ever split.
- Each lone `arguments` piece is re-paired with the one `name` piece beside it, and vice versa.
- Anything ambiguous returns `None` and every existing repair stands: a lone piece, a same-key neighbour, a key other than `name`/`arguments`, a truncated array.

Nothing is invented. Each merged call carries exactly the model's own two values, and the name must be a non-empty string.

Why this approach: it follows the same rule as the passes below it, repair only what can be repaired deterministically and never guess, and it leaves a well-formed batch byte for byte alone.

**A note for reviewers on scope.** The streaming call site (`_assemble_tool_calls`) only invokes the repair on `JSONDecodeError`. So the well-formed variant of this shape, valid JSON that would pass through as four nameless calls, is merged only when the function is called; in production it reaches the executor and is rejected there. I did not widen the call site, because routing valid JSON through the repair would re-serialise every valid argument blob. If you want that variant handled too, `normalize_tool_call_entries` is the better home.

## Related Issue

No issue filed; this pull request is the report.

Related, other argument-repair shapes with no overlap in code: #129278 (a call that streamed without its head), #138059 (a stream cut at a dangling delimiter), #16505 (repair at the recovery write site), #89246 (distinguishing a failed repair).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/message_sanitization.py`: `_merge_adjacent_call_pieces` and its helpers (`_skip_json_whitespace`, `_decode_piece_pair`, `_read_call_piece`, `_scan_call_pieces`, `_pair_call_pieces`); called first in `_repair_tool_call_arguments`.
- `tests/agent/test_repair_tool_call_arguments.py`: the dropped-brace case and the well-formed-pieces case, and a guard that ambiguous shapes (an unpaired piece, a lone piece, a foreign key) keep today's behaviour.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_repair_tool_call_arguments.py` on this branch: 16 passed.
2. With `agent/message_sanitization.py` taken from `main` and the test file from this branch: 2 failed, 14 passed. The failing assertion is `assert {} == {'calls': [{name, arguments}, {name, arguments}]}`, with the log line `Unrepairable tool_call arguments for tool_call — replaced with empty object`.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every test file that references `message_sanitization` (22 files): 379 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped.

prs.title: feat(desktop): let plugins relabel and split messaging sidebar sections
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a declarative `session.sourceLabels` contribution area so a desktop plugin can change how messaging sections are labelled and grouped in the sidebar, without core hardcoding any one integration.

A rule maps a session `source` to a display `label`, optionally restricted to one `profile` and to a `sessionIdPrefix`. Prefix rules match the durable lineage root (`_lineage_root_id`, falling back to `id`), so compression keeps a session in its section. Use cases: show "iMessage" for the Photon source, or split sessions that a Home Assistant integration created (stable id prefix) out of the generic "API" section.

Nothing changes unless a plugin registers a rule. Disabling or removing the plugin restores the stock grouping live. Stored sessions and the backend source are never modified, and "load more" still queries the original backend source.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched open and merged PRs for a source-label hook; the nearby PRs (#154673, #63266, #102760) change which sources exist or how they group, not who can relabel them.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `src/contrib/session-sources.ts`: new area, contribution type and rule resolver.
- `src/lib/session-source.ts`: label consumer that honors contributions.
- `src/app/chat/sidebar/messaging-groups.ts` (+ test): the messaging grouping extracted from `index.tsx` into a pure `buildMessagingGroups` helper, with group ids distinct from backend source ids.
- `src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx`: uses the helper and subscribes to the area.
- `src/sdk/index.ts`: exports `SESSION_SOURCE_LABELS_AREA` and its type.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk.md`: contract, example, and feature-detection note.

## How to Test

1. Drop a plugin in `$HERMES_HOME/desktop-plugins/<name>/plugin.js` registering `{ source: 'photon', label: 'iMessage' }` on `SESSION_SOURCE_LABELS_AREA`.
2. The Photon section is labelled "iMessage". Unload the plugin: it reverts without a restart.
3. `npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/sidebar src/lib/session-source.test.ts` passes (57 files / 409 tests in the sidebar folder).

# Hermes Agent v0.23.5

**Release Date:** November 27, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~338 PRs merged since v0.23.4 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.24.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `a428f5344f77`, the window since v0.23.4 contains **1,262 non-merge commits** across **1,146 changed files** (+57,989 / −5,346), **338 merged PRs** and **92 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: the CLI and TUI support the OSC 7577 program resume protocol, idle gateway chats compact in the background on every route, `read_file` tails with a negative offset and lists directories, `search_files` says when a content search is the whole answer, a bounded default-plugins preflight before the local gateway starts (Desktop, Docker and CLI), plugin OAuth entries that can pin their redirect URI, the Solstice provider moved to the stateless Interactions API, new plugin API surfaces (turn origin, how a session was created, cron scheduling, gateway silence helpers), the dashboard's "your dashboard is moving" notice, raw arrow keys working in the sessions and plugins pickers, and a long series of fixes that keep plugin work bound to the right profile when a profile is renamed, moved or removed.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.24.0**, which will document everything from v0.23.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.23.4...v0.23.5](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.23.4...v0.23.5)

issues.title: Telegram channel: attachment download bypasses settings.proxy and connects directly
issues.body:
The Telegram channel downloads attachments (photos, files) with a direct connection and ignores the channel's `settings.proxy`. Only the Bot API client (telego) uses the proxy, so on networks where api.telegram.org is reachable only via a proxy, `getFile` succeeds but the actual file download hangs until the timeout.

### Cause
In `pkg/channels/telegram/telegram.go`, the file is downloaded with:

```go
return utils.DownloadFile(url, filename, utils.DownloadOptions{
    LoggerPrefix: "telegram",
})
```

`DownloadOptions.ProxyURL` is not set. In `pkg/utils/media.go`, an empty `ProxyURL` creates a plain `http.Client` with no proxy.

### Expected behavior
Attachment downloads use the same proxy as configured in the Telegram channel `settings.proxy`. Setting global `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` is not an option, since only the Telegram channel should go through the proxy.

### Suggested fix
Pass the channel proxy to `DownloadOptions.ProxyURL`. Optionally make the download timeout configurable: the default is 60s including retries, which is short for slow devices and proxies.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run PicoClaw on a host with no direct access to api.telegram.org, reachable only via an HTTP proxy.
2. Set the proxy only in the Telegram channel config:
   ```json
   "telegram": { "enabled": true, "settings": { "proxy": "http://<proxy-host>:<port>" } }
   ```
3. Send a photo to the bot.

### Actual result
The user gets "I couldn't download the attachment (photo)...". The gateway log (debug) shows that `getFile` succeeded, but the download failed exactly 60s later:

```
telego    API response getFile: Ok: true ... "file_size":30338,"file_path":"photos/file_1.jpg"
telegram  File URL: [https://api.telegram.org/file/bot](https://api.telegram.org/file/bot)<TOKEN>/photos/file_1.jpg
telegram  Failed to download file: failed to sleep: context deadline exceeded  (pkg/utils/media.go:158)
```

The file is about 30 KB, so the 20 MB limit is not the cause.

### Environment
PicoClaw 0.5.6 (git 43001a01), Linux arm64, systemd, no Docker.

prs.title: fix(claude): resolve empty tool name in Claude API requests
prs.body:
## Summary

- Fix 400 Bad Request errors when using Claude/Anthropic as the LLM provider
- The `ToolCall` struct stores tool names in `Function.Name` (OpenAI format), but `claude_provider.go` was reading `tc.Name` (top-level), which is always empty
- Also handles `Arguments` stored as a JSON string in `Function.Arguments` rather than the top-level map

## Root Cause

In `pkg/agent/loop.go`, tool calls are stored in OpenAI's format:
```go
ToolCall{
    Function: &FunctionCall{
        Name:      tc.Name,      // name goes here
        Arguments: string(JSON),  // args go here as string
    },
    // tc.Name is empty
    // tc.Arguments is nil
}
```

But `pkg/providers/claude_provider.go` reads the top-level fields:
```go
anthropic.NewToolUseBlock(tc.ID, tc.Arguments, tc.Name)  // both empty/nil
```

This causes every multi-turn conversation with tool calls to fail with:
```
messages.N.content.0.tool_use.name: String should have at least 1 character
```

## Fix

Fall back to `Function.Name` and `Function.Arguments` when top-level fields are empty:
```go
name := tc.Name
if name == "" && tc.Function != nil {
    name = tc.Function.Name
}
args := tc.Arguments
if args == nil && tc.Function != nil && tc.Function.Arguments != "" {
    json.Unmarshal([]byte(tc.Function.Arguments), &args)
}
blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewToolUseBlock(tc.ID, args, name))
```

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` compiles
- [x] Tested with Claude Sonnet 4.5 via setup-token auth — multi-turn conversations with tool calls work correctly
- [x] Verified on Telegram channel with real tool executions (web search, file read)

issues.title: [capability] Make Vault-held credentials usable through the credential gateway (no double registration)
issues.body:
## Problem

Agents (notably the personal assistant "Tanx") repeatedly stop on credentials that live in HashiCorp Vault, because the installed credential gateway (OneCLI) only injects secrets registered *in OneCLI*. Vault is our source of truth for secrets (KV-v2), so every credential an agent needs currently has to exist in two places, and the agent has no reliable way to know which.

## Observed (2026-11-27)

- Agent reported a vault credential was "not registered with the OneCLI gateway (proxy is intercepting)" and asked the operator to register it in the console.
- Operator pointed out the key is in Vault and had been updated ~20 min earlier. The agent then claimed it could not bypass the proxy, and finally said it was trying to register the credential itself via the gateway API from inside the container.
- Net effect: work blocked (note captures, resume drafts, scheduled curation) on a credential that exists, because the agent conflates "in Vault" with "usable through the gateway".
- Separate but related: the agent's account of what it did and why was inconsistent between turns (see the stale-code "nothing was sent" alert on the same host). That needs its own investigation and is not the subject of this issue.

## Why it happens (hypothesis, not yet verified in code)

Gateway seam (docs/gateway-seam.md) has no notion of an external secret source. Provider contract covers sessions, approvals, and container-spec contributions; credential population is entirely provider-owned and manual (operator console). Agent guidance comes from the gateway's container skill, which only describes OneCLI-registered credentials.

## Desired outcome

Any of these would fix the class of problem:

1. **Vault-backed gateway source:** a provider/adapter option that resolves credentials from Vault at request time (or syncs them into OneCLI on a schedule/on change), so Vault stays the single source of truth.
2. **Registration sync tool:** a host-side command (e.g. `ncl` verb or script) that reconciles a declared set of Vault paths -> gateway credentials + host patterns, idempotent, no secret values in logs.
3. **Truthful failure surface (minimum viable):** when a request is blocked because no gateway credential matches the host, return a distinct, machine-readable error naming the host and "no credential registered", and have the agent skill instruct the agent to report exactly that and the registration path, rather than speculating or attempting self-registration.

## Acceptance criteria

- A credential rotated in Vault becomes usable by agents without operator console steps (options 1/2), or
- A missing registration produces a distinct error and agent guidance that prevents the agent from attempting to register credentials itself or claiming the credential is absent from Vault (option 3).
- No secret values enter the container, chat context, or logs.

## Notes

- Agents must not self-register credentials; that would let an agent widen its own egress/credential scope. Registration stays host/operator-side.
- Consider proposing upstream once a fork-local shape is settled.

issues.title: Rootless Docker: setup writes the user unit without the user's Docker endpoint, then suggests setfacl on the system socket
issues.body:
**Version:** v2026.11.0 (also current `main`, `setup/service.ts`).

**What happens:** on a host where the service user runs rootless Docker (not in the `docker` group), the CLI works because the user's Docker context or shell `DOCKER_HOST` points to `unix:///run/user/<uid>/docker.sock`. The systemd user unit written by `setup/service.ts` carries only `HOME`, `PATH` and the proxy environment, so the service talks to `/var/run/docker.sock`, gets `permission denied` and crash-loops. `setup/lib/docker-access-hint.ts` then proposes `sudo setfacl -m u:$(whoami):rw /var/run/docker.sock`, which gives the user root-equivalent access to the rootful daemon — the opposite of what a rootless install wants.

**Reproduce:**
1. User without `docker` group, rootless dockerd running (`dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install`), `docker context use rootless` (or `DOCKER_HOST` in the shell profile).
2. `docker ps` works in the shell; run setup.
3. Service log: permission denied on `/var/run/docker.sock`; the wizard shows the setfacl hint.

**Proposal:** at setup, resolve the endpoint the CLI uses (`docker context inspect --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}'`, or `DOCKER_HOST` if set) and, when it differs from the default socket, write it into the unit as `Environment=DOCKER_HOST=…`; skip the setfacl hint when the endpoint is a rootless socket. Related: #3174 (container user mapping on rootless), whose detection also relies on `DOCKER_HOST` and names the CLI-context case as a known limitation.

issues.title: Gateway webhook server listens on port 0, so a host firewall that limits loopback cannot allow it
issues.body:
**Version:** v2026.11.0 (also current `main`, `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts`: `server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', …)`).

**What happens:** the local webhook server that the Discord Gateway listener forwards events to binds a random loopback port on every start. On a host where an nftables/iptables rule limits loopback for the service user to a fixed set of ports (a reasonable hardening for a dedicated agent user), there is no port to allow: every forwarded event fails with `fetch failed`, and the bot looks connected but never answers.

**Reproduce:**
1. As the service user, allow only fixed loopback ports, e.g. `nft add rule inet f out meta skuid <uid> ip daddr 127.0.0.1 tcp dport != { 3000 } reject`.
2. Start NanoClaw with the Discord channel and send the bot a DM.
3. Log: `Local webhook server started {port: <random>}`, then `fetch failed` for each forwarded event; no reply.

**Proposal:** an optional `GATEWAY_WEBHOOK_PORT` (via `config.ts`/`.env` like the other settings), default `0` (unchanged behaviour); close the server on teardown. I run this as a local patch (3 files, ~30 lines plus a test that starts the bridge with the variable set and checks the bound port) and am happy to open a PR if you want it.

issues.title: [capability] Network mailbox so session runners don't need a shared session dir
issues.body:
Session runners currently need the host's session directory mounted: the two session DBs, the heartbeat and the outbox. That rules out runners that can't see host paths: remote or hosted ones, Kubernetes, and sandbox runtimes like OpenShell.

The mailbox seam from August should make a second implementation possible. What I have in mind:

- The host would keep its SQLite DBs as they are. A small host service would expose the runner's `MailboxOperations` for one session, backed by the existing SQLite mailbox.
- On the runner, a remote mailbox would load a snapshot in `run()` and commit the changes when it resolves (the ops are sync inside `run()`).
- Each session would get its own credential at spawn, scoped to that session only.
- The heartbeat and outbox would use the same connection. The group folder would stay a mount for now.

It would be runtime-neutral, and I'd try it on plain Docker first. My use case is OpenShell, along the lines of OpenClaw's worker mode.

Is something like this already planned, maybe for a hosted setup? If so I'd rather align with it than build a parallel one. If not, I'm happy to prototype it.

@zvi-fried @gavrielc

issues.title: [bug] A stored message that reads as /clear or /upload-trace runs as a command on the next turn
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

`main` at 6b57f87f8

### Host platform

macOS (runner logic, not platform-specific)

### What happened?

In a chat where the agent stores messages not addressed to it (`ignored_message_policy='accumulate'`), an admin's `/clear` or `/upload-trace` that is not addressed to the agent is stored as a context row (`trigger=0`). When the next message wakes the agent, the runner runs that stored row as a command: the session is reset and "Session cleared." is sent (or a trace upload starts), in the same pass as the answer to the new message.

### What did you expect?

A stored context row never acts as a command. Only a command that woke the agent runs. Open question: whether the stored text should then reach the agent as context or be dropped.

### How can we reproduce it?

Runner-level, on `main`: insert a `trigger=0` chat row with text `/clear` and a `trigger=1` chat row with a normal message, then run `runPollLoop` with the mock provider. The log shows "Clearing session (resetting continuation)" and a "Session cleared." reply, then the turn for the normal message.

Cause: the command checks in `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.ts` do not look at `trigger`. The host stores the row because `gateCommand` allows an admin's command and the row is then written with `trigger: wake` (`src/router.ts`).

Not yet tried on a live chat.

### Related

#4289 keeps context beside a command pending and lists this as out of scope. #4159 edits the same block.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-remote-mailbox — session mailbox over HTTP instead of a mounted session dir
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

**Why:** today every agent must run somewhere the host can mount its session folder (the two session DBs, the heartbeat, the outbox). That rules out runtimes that can't mount a host folder into the agent: sandboxes like OpenShell, a remote machine or hosted sandbox, Kubernetes.

This skill takes the shared folder out of the session's IO path: the agent reaches its mailbox over HTTP, so a new runtime only needs a driver and network access to the host, not a shared filesystem. It is the approach proposed in #4543.

**Proof it does that:** I run an OpenShell MicroVM driver on top of it for one agent group. That driver isn't in this PR; it would be a separate skill if there's interest.

**Other potential benefits:**
- **Smaller agent reach**: the agent no longer has the session folder mounted. It can only make mailbox calls for its own session, with a token that dies with the container.
- **No SQLite across a mount**: all SQLite access stays on the host, so these sessions no longer depend on file locking and visibility through the Docker Desktop file share.
- **Room for other storage**: the runner only sees mailbox calls, so the host could later keep session mailboxes in something other than per-session SQLite files without touching the runner.

**Cost when applied:** each mailbox call becomes a local HTTP round trip, about 0.2 ms. No difference noticed in daily use.

**What it does:**
- A `remote-mailbox` session driver wraps the existing driver (`docker` by default, or the one `NANOCLAW_REMOTE_MAILBOX_INNER_DRIVER` names). Only groups in `NANOCLAW_REMOTE_MAILBOX_GROUPS` use it; every other group is untouched.
- For a listed group, the session-folder mount is replaced with a scratch folder, and the container gets a mailbox URL plus a bearer token for that spawn only.
- The host serves the runner's own mailbox SQL against the unchanged session DBs. No core changes: it uses the existing driver registry, mailbox and heartbeat-path seams.
- `operations.ts` is a host copy of the runner's SQLite mailbox code; `drift.test.ts` fails when the runner files change, so the copy can't silently fall behind.
- Under egress lockdown, one small forwarder container forwards only the mailbox port.

**Out of scope:** Linux hosts (a container can't reach the host's `127.0.0.1` there).

## Related work

Implements the proposal in #4543.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Skill applied to `main` 310f739b → `pnpm run build` ok; `vitest run src/mailbox/remote` 118 passed; full `pnpm test` 5403 passed.
- `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean; `bun test src/mailbox/remote` 19 passed (in the agent image).
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts` 286 passed (its scratch root now seeds `src/drivers/installed.ts` so a driver skill's append applies).
- Manual, macOS + Docker Desktop: a daily-use agent has run on the remote mailbox for several days — text, voice, attachments, web, question cards, host restart with container adoption, egress lockdown.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact
