## Security and trust boundaries

The service binds `127.0.0.1` only. Each spawn gets its own bearer token, scoped to one session and revoked when the container ends. A listed container no longer has the session folder mounted. Under egress lockdown the forwarder exposes only the mailbox port.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): apply media-failure note at the inbound boundary (follow-up to #2895)
prs.body:
## What

Follow-up to #2895 (merged). A high-effort review of that PR surfaced a regression on the approval-answer path, plus a minor cleanup.

## The bug

`appendMediaFailureNote` was applied to `content` **before** the pending-question slash-command handler. When an approver answers a pending question with a slash command carried as an image caption (e.g. `/approve`) and the image download fails, `content` becomes `"/approve\n[image could not be downloaded]"`. The handler does `cmd = content.trim().toLowerCase()` and exact-matches against the option commands, so the answer no longer matches: the approval is silently dropped, `pendingQuestions` is not cleared, and the raw text is forwarded to the agent. Narrow trigger (slash answer + media + download failure), but a real regression of a sensitive path.

## Fix

- Apply the media-failure note at the inbound `text` boundary, leaving `content` pristine for the slash-command and bot-message matching above.
- Tighten the empty-message guard so a message carrying only a *failed* download still survives (`failures.length === 0` added to the skip condition) — preserving the original intent of #2895.
- Swap an em-dash for a hyphen in a new comment.

The `appendMediaFailureNote` unit tests from #2895 still cover the helper itself; this change only moves where it is applied.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): keep context beside a command pending
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stored context no longer starts a turn just because a runner command shares its batch.

- **Problem**: when `/clear` or `/upload-trace` reached the runner in a batch whose other rows were all accumulated context (`trigger=0`), the runner ran the command, then started a turn on the context rows alone. The agent answered messages it was only meant to store, and the command replied in the first context row's thread.
- **Fix**: a batch with no waking non-command row now takes only its waking commands. The context rows stay pending and ride along with the next message that wakes a turn, as the accumulate gate already does for context-only batches.
- **Out of scope**: a context row that itself reads as a command (an admin's `/clear` not addressed to the agent) still runs as a command, as on `main`; whether it should is a separate question. Which thread a turn replies to when context sorts first is https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159.

## Related work

Split out of https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159 at review, as a separate behavior change. No issue. Both PRs touch the runner's command block in `poll-loop.ts`, so the second to merge needs a small rebase.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test --isolate` → 629 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json` is clean.
- New `poll-loop.command-context.test.ts`, red on `main`. For `/clear` and for `/upload-trace` batched with one context row, `main` sends two replies to the context row's thread (the command's reply and an answer to the context) and acks the row. Here the command replies in its own thread, no turn starts, and the row stays pending until it reaches the next turn with the next message.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
In chats where the agent only stores messages not addressed to it, `/clear` or `/upload-trace` no longer makes it answer those stored messages; they wait for the next message that addresses it.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Only the runner's batch selection changes; the host's command gate is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): escape the attachment type in agent-facing XML
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code

## Description

`formatAttachments` in `container/agent-runner/src/formatter.ts` escapes every rendered field except `type`:

```ts
const name = a.name || a.filename || 'attachment';
const type = a.type || 'file';                    // <- not escaped
const localPath = a.localPath ? `/workspace/${a.localPath}` : '';
const url = a.url || '';
if (localPath) {
  return `[${type}: ${escapeXml(name)} — saved to ${escapeXml(localPath)}]`;
}
return url ? `[${type}: ${escapeXml(name)} (${escapeXml(url)})]` : `[${type}: ${escapeXml(name)}]`;
```

`name`, `localPath`, and `url` all go through `escapeXml`; `type` does not. A MIME/type string containing `<`, `>`, `&`, or `"` therefore lands unescaped inside the `<message>` block the agent parses — in all three return branches.

Channels populate this field from platform-supplied attachment metadata, so its content isn't fully under our control. This makes `type` consistent with its siblings: one call, no behavior change for well-formed types.

**Testing:** three assertions added covering the `localPath`, `url`, and bare branches. Full container suite passes (301 pass / 1 skip), `tsc --noEmit` clean.

prs.title: feat(dsh): add plugin ecosystem compatibility and external session sync
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements DSH plugin ecosystem compatibility (thin host protocol boundary + full-view escape hatch) and external DSH session synchronization:

- **DSH Dynamic Plugin Model Catalog**: Consumes DSH `session/modelCatalog`, filters out LobsterAI-synced providers, surfaces third-party plugin models in `ModelSelector` with lazy refresh, and passes `{ provider, model, reasoningEffort }` through `session/selectModel` while bypassing LobsterAI quota/credit reporting.
- **Agent Preset Bridge & Persona Yield**: Discovers third-party presets via `agentPresets/list`, exposes a preset control for new blank sessions in `CoworkPromptInput`, passes `agentPreset` to `session/create` and persists `dsh_agent_preset`, and yields default LobsterAI prompt injection in `persona-scope.mjs` when a non-`lobsterai` preset is active.
- **Plugin Skills & Ecosystem Escape Hatch**: Adds `listPluginSkills` to `ops-rpc` to display DSH plugin skills read-only in `SkillsManager`, adds an "Open in DSH Full View" escape hatch in `DshEmbeddedPluginView`, and adds `DshAdvancedRuntimeModeModal`.
- **External DSH Session Sync**: Translates and syncs external DSH sessions (e.g., from full DSH Web view or `dsh-pocket`) into LobsterAI's sidebar with `traceId` credit attribution, local session binding store, workspace sync, and legacy session seeding.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- **IPC & Preload**: Added DSH host IPC handlers and preload bridges (`src/main/ipcHandlers/dshHost/handlers.ts`, `src/main/preload.ts`, `src/shared/dshEngine/hostConstants.ts`) for plugin model catalog, agent presets, plugin skills, and advanced runtime mode.
- **Storage**: Added SQLite schema/store support for `dsh_agent_preset` (`src/main/sqliteStore.ts`, `src/main/coworkStore.ts`) and local DSH session binding persistence (`src/main/libs/dsh/localDshSessionBindingStore.ts`).
- **Runtime Startup & Configuration**: Updated `dshBootstrap.ts`, `dshHostManager.ts`, `dshRuntimeAdapter.ts`, `dshTypertClient.ts`, `openclawTokenProxy.ts`, and `dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/plugins/*` (`agent-workspace-sync`, `model-bridge`, `ops-rpc`, `persona-scope`).

## Verification

- `npx tsc` — passed
- `npm run compile:electron` — passed
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored <changed-ts-files>` — passed
- `npm test` — 886/887 passed locally (only unrelated `tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts` due to local `node_modules` patch state)

prs.title: fix(im,dsh): harden Telegram/Discord access control and throttle streaming updates
prs.body:
## Summary
- **Telegram & Discord fail-closed access control**:
  - Added strict fail-closed DM and group allowlist helpers (`access-policy.mjs`) used by Telegram and Discord channel drivers.
  - Changed default `dmPolicy` for Telegram and Discord from `open` to `allowlist` and added a one-time `IMStore` migration (`migration:telegram_discord_allowlist_v1`) to harden existing Telegram/Discord instances without affecting domestic/enterprise IM channels.
  - Added empty-allowlist hints and open-policy security warnings in Telegram and Discord settings UI with `zh`/`en` i18n entries.
- **DSH streaming message update throttling**:
  - Added `DshStreamUpdateThrottler` and wired it into `DshRuntimeAdapter` and `DshSideChatManager` to throttle rapid streaming persistence/IPC emits and clear pending timers on session stop/completion.
  - Coalesced live streaming `messageUpdate` bursts per frame in `CoworkService` (`src/renderer/services/cowork.ts`) and prevented stopped sessions from flipping back to `running`.
  - Removed the persistent focus ring on the stop button in `CoworkPromptInput.tsx`.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- **Storage**: One-time SQLite `im_config` migration (`migration:telegram_discord_allowlist_v1`) in `IMStore` to default existing Telegram/Discord instances to fail-closed `allowlist` policies.
- **Runtime / IPC**: Throttled streaming `messageUpdate` persistence and IPC emission in `DshRuntimeAdapter` / `DshSideChatManager` and per-frame coalescing in the renderer `CoworkService`.

## Verification
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 --no-warn-ignored <changed files>` — passed
- `npx tsc && npm run compile:electron` — passed
- `npx vitest run` on all 6 affected test suites (113 tests) — passed

prs.title: feat(runtime): migrate agent engine from OpenClaw to DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
prs.body:
## Summary

Replaces OpenClaw (`v2026.8.1`) with **DeepSeek Harness (`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.5`)** as LobsterAI's single bundled agent engine (`CoworkAgentEngine = 'dsh'`), consolidating the migration, desktop integration, IM channels, data backup/migration, plugin ecosystem, and UI upgrades developed on `feat/migrate-openclaw-to-dsh` (`#3123`–`#3238`, 1,957 files changed, already synced with `main`).

- Removes all OpenClaw runtime code, 176 runtime patches, 6 local extensions, and dual-engine branches in favor of two first-party Cordis bundles (`@lobsterai/dsh-bundle` and `@lobsterai/dsh-channels`) plus 3 minimal version-scoped DSH patches.
- Decouples user assets (agent personas, Markdown memory + FTS5 index, SQLite scheduled tasks, MCP OAuth, and model auth proxy) into engine-agnostic main-process services.
- Provides an automatic, offline 6-step atomic migration with rollback and legacy archiving for existing OpenClaw users.

Design reference: [`specs/refactors/deepseek-harness-migration/2026-11-20-openclaw-to-dsh-migration-design.md`](specs/refactors/deepseek-harness-migration/2026-11-20-openclaw-to-dsh-migration-design.md)

## Changes Made

### 1. Core DSH Engine & First-Party Host Bundle (`@lobsterai/dsh-bundle`)
- **Runtime adapter & isolated profile**: Replaced `OpenClawRuntimeAdapter` with `DshRuntimeAdapter` communicating over Typert WS/HTTP against an isolated App-Owned Profile (`<userData>/dsh-profile/`, isolated `DSH_AGENTS_HOME`, pnpm store, and CLI shim). Decoupled DSH startup from window launch for instant main UI boot and reduced cold-start latency.
- **Host Cordis plugins (`dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host/`)**: Added 11 modular plugins covering in-memory model/provider bridging (with thinking defaults, W3C `traceparent`, Codex Responses & Kimi K3 compat), unified native `web_search` routing, persona/project memory & skills scoping, host-tool RPC callbacks, progressive tool disclosure, cross-agent delegation, native permission presets (`read-only`, `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access`) with human-readable approvals, NetEase Mail quota guard, log forwarding, ops RPC, and embedded plugin shell (`lobster-embed-shell`).
- **Privacy & upgrade gates**: Disabled all 7 upstream DeepSeek telemetry/account plugins and redundant DSH components (`office-kit`, `skill-office`, `schedule`, `session-title-llm`, `mcp-resources`, `web-search-deepseek`, `web-deepseek-api`, etc.) in `cordis.patch.yml`; added `npm run dsh:upgrade-check` and reduced runtime patches to 3 files in `scripts/dsh-patches/0.2.2-rc.5/`.

### 2. IM Channels (`@lobsterai/dsh-channels`)
- Implemented native DSH channel drivers for **8 platforms**: **Feishu/Lark, Weixin, DingTalk, WeCom, QQ, Telegram, Discord, and POPO**.
- Added channel permission presets, approval relay, shared group task/session routing, Feishu topic & DM scheduled delivery, DingTalk card finalization, Weixin auth preservation across upgrades, and IM media support.
- Retired and archived legacy NIM, NetEase Bee, and Email IM channel drivers (historical conversations remain read-only).

### 3. Offline Upgrade Migration & Data Backup (Manifest v3)
- **Legacy OpenClaw migration (`src/main/migration/`)**: Added `LegacyOpenClawMigrator` (offline 6-step atomic migration before DSH boots) preserving scheduled tasks, sessions/subagent history, personas/agent collaboration, Weixin credentials, and legacy media while archiving retired modules and pre-v2 SQLite snapshots under `<userData>/legacy-openclaw-backup/`; cleaned up legacy experimental DSH configs.
- **Data backup & restore (`src/main/ipcHandlers/dataMigration/`)**: Overhauled backup/restore to DSH-only Manifest v3 (compatible with DSH v2) with streaming `.tar.gz`, full-table SQLite integrity verification, cross-machine path rewriting & `safeStorage` sanitization, missing DSH plugin detection, and a standalone restore progress window; removed legacy `sqliteBackup`.

### 4. Engine-Agnostic Platform Services
- **Personas & memory**: Moved `SOUL.md` / `IDENTITY.md` / `USER.md` / `MEMORY.md` / `memory/*.md` to `<userData>/workspaces/<agentId>/` with main-process `better-sqlite3` FTS5 search and project/expert scoping; removed legacy Dreaming/embedding config.
- **Scheduled tasks**: Migrated scheduler ownership to SQLite `LobsterScheduler` with CWD binding, reload/interruption recovery, stopped-run persistence, repeated-run session folding, and IM delivery.
- **MCP, models, skills & browser**: Hardened MCP sync, OAuth 2.1 PKCE, SSE bridge, and tool filters; added NetEase Mail MCP integration; added live provider model discovery and model editor dialog; streamlined bundled `SKILLs/` (mounted read-only, retired legacy `web-search` server & 11 legacy/heavy skills, added `lobsterai-image-processing`, upgraded Office skills); consolidated web browsing to the built-in In-App Browser.

### 5. Plugin Ecosystem, Cowork, Artifacts & UI Polish
- **DSH plugin ecosystem**: Added full plugin lifecycle management (registry/git/local install, version check & hot update, enable/disable/remove, surface classification) and chromeless embedded plugin shell (`DshEmbeddedPluginView`) integrated into the sidebar and settings.
- **Cowork & branching**: Aligned conversation editing with DSH's append-only log (native fork from history, queued-message edit/retry), redesigned multi-tab Side Chat (`btw`), and added turn rail outline, context breakdown popover, initial context token optimization, and session scroll restore.
- **Artifacts, Office & media**: Added isolated Word editor (`word-panel.html`), workspace file browser, blank Office doc creation & inline rename, native OOXML SVG chart rendering in PPTX preview, Electron HTML-to-PNG/JPEG rendering, and restored image/video generation & library previews.
- **UI & desktop polish**: Refreshed Home (composer layout, showcase hub, credits badge, forced-login gate for fresh installs), Sidebar (pinned task reordering, hover cards, full-access confirmation, typography/surface polish), Settings (redesigned save model, agent draft/rules & memory tabs, split data privacy tab), Skins (direct image reuse, backdrop clarity), Update modal, and Desktop Companion (on-demand context actions & sprite atlas animations).

### 6. Packaging, Build & Docs
- Packed pruned `dsh-runtime` (`mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `win-x64`) inside `app.asar` and `dsh-bundles/` in `extraResources`, added `scripts/unpack-dsh-resources.cjs`, simplified the Windows installer (with on-demand elevated process stop), updated `.github/workflows/openclaw-check.yml` for DSH validation, and updated `README*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING*.md`, and `AGENTS.md` guides.

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (replaces OpenClaw runtime with DSH; retires NIM / NetEase Bee / Email IM channels and legacy OpenClaw v1 backup restore; automatic offline migration upgrades existing users)
- [x] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Performance improvement

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] **Main process (`src/main/`)**: Replaced OpenClaw runtime/adapter with `DshRuntimeAdapter`, `DshBootstrap`, `DshHostManager`, `DshTypertClient`, `LegacyOpenClawMigrator`, `LobsterScheduler`, and `LobsterMemoryService`; decoupled DSH startup from main window launch.
- [x] **Preload script (`src/main/preload.ts`) & IPC (`src/main/ipcHandlers/`, `src/shared/`)**: Added IPC modules and preload bridges for `dshHost`, `dataMigration`, `artifactWorkspace`, `wordPanel`, `coworkSideChat`, `coworkPinned`, `coworkMessageEdit`, `contextCleanup`, `providerModelDiscovery`, `authGate`, and `migrationV2`; removed legacy `openclawUserConfig`, `plugins`, and experimental `dsh` IPC handlers.
- [x] **Storage & runtime config**: Migrated agent workspaces to `<userData>/workspaces/`, isolated DSH profile under `<userData>/dsh-profile/`, archived legacy OpenClaw data to `<userData>/legacy-openclaw-backup/`, upgraded backup archives to Manifest v3, and updated SQLite tables/snapshots.
- [x] **Window management & packaging**: Added isolated Word panel window (`word-panel.html`), standalone restore progress window (`restoreProgressWindow.ts`), and embedded DSH plugin webview shell (`DshEmbeddedPluginView`); updated `electron-builder.json` to package `dsh-runtime` in `app.asar` and `dsh-bundles/` in `extraResources`.

## Testing
- Constituent PRs (`#3123`–`#3238`) merged into `feat/migrate-openclaw-to-dsh` were individually verified with Vitest, `npx tsc`, `npm run compile:electron`, ESLint, `npm run dsh:upgrade-check`, and desktop E2E/packaging checks.
- Branch is merged cleanly with latest `main` (`0d1da7349`); full GitHub Actions CI (`CI`, `OpenClaw Integration Check`, `Security`) will validate the combined PR.

## Additional Notes
- Release builds must build and verify the pinned `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.5` runtime (`npm run dsh:runtime:<platform>`, `npm run dsh:runtime:verify`, `npm run dsh:upgrade-check`) before packaging installers.
- Supported platforms for this release: macOS (`arm64` / `x64`) and Windows (`x64`).

prs.body:
## 问题与修复

OpenClaw 默认将没有单独指定负责人的机器人路由给主 Agent。迁移版沿用了这个规则，但编辑页标题只统计显式绑定，导致两个开关已经打开时仍显示「未绑定」。

编辑页现在按当前可见、已启用的渠道和机器人实例解析归属。摘要、开关和 DSH 使用相同的实例及平台回退规则。保存只修改用户切换过的机器人，保留同平台其他实例和隐藏渠道的配置。

定时任务使用旧版短账号时优先匹配完整实例绑定。同一个机器人在同一个群留下多个 Agent 的历史时，通知目标优先选用当前负责人的会话。

| 修复前 | 修复后 |
| --- | --- |
| ![两个开关打开，标题显示未绑定](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/0d13bd3254e3178db57a94a25b9d53035951d24d/docs/res/screenshots/agent-im-bindings/before.png) | ![相同三个机器人，标题显示已绑定两个](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/0d13bd3254e3178db57a94a25b9d53035951d24d/docs/res/screenshots/agent-im-bindings/after.png) |

- Windows Electron 43.5.0，Playwright/CDP。用同一份 OpenClaw 配置复现，验证了主 Agent 收回机器人、取消、保存、重新分配和完整重启。
- 两台飞书、一台 POPO 和一台钉钉机器人实连。两台飞书机器人各自向同一验收群执行一次定时投递，平台回读确认了发送方、目标群和正文。微信单渠道覆盖了离线显示。
- 本地飞书协议回放验证普通群在绑定不同 Agent 时分开，收回后续到主 Agent 原任务，私聊独立。
- 427 项定向 Vitest、渲染进程和主进程 TypeScript 检查、变更文件 ESLint 均通过。

## Summary

### 1. Bundled Skills Streamline, Read-Only Mount & Marketplace Migration
Design doc: `specs/features/bundled-skills-streamline/2026-11-27-bundled-skills-streamline-design.md`

- **Streamline bundled skills to 9 always-enabled core skills**: retain `web-search`, `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `pdf`, `lobsterai-image-processing`, `frontend-design`, `skill-creator`, and `imap-smtp-email` in `SKILLs/skills.config.json` with `alwaysEnabled: true`; remove 10 vertical skills from the bundle (soft-preserved in existing users' `userData/SKILLs/` as user-managed skills).
- **Read-only bundled mount & reserved ID protection**: load core bundled skills directly from `Resources/SKILLs/` via DSH `skillsPolicy` instead of copying ~47MB into `userData/SKILLs/`; migrate `imap-smtp-email` credentials to `<userData>/email-skill/` before cleaning up legacy bundled copies; enforce reserved core skill IDs on user imports.
- **Kit-managed `skin-creator`**: move `skin-creator` to `resources/skin-pack/skin-creator/` and manage its installation/uninstallation via `skinPackKitLifecycle`.
- **DSH invocation policy & UI**: wire `disable-model-invocation` / `user-invocable` through `@lobsterai/dsh-bundle` (`persona-helpers.mjs`, `ops-rpc.mjs`, etc.); hide toggle/delete controls for `alwaysEnabled` core skills in `SkillsManager` and exclude them from context cleanup; add missing-skill auto-install and status/retry UI for preset experts (`expertSkillInstaller`, `AgentSkillSelector`).
- **Marketplace trust & security scan routing**: skip client static security scan only for verified official marketplace packages (`marketplaceTrust.ts`), keeping mandatory scanning for user-imported and untrusted sources.

### 2. Clean Markdown Rich-Text Copy & Opaque Theme Colors
- Add `clipboardRichText.ts` (installed in `main.tsx` and `desktopCompanion.tsx`) to sanitize copied Markdown HTML (stripping theme colors, backgrounds, and UI chrome such as `CodeBlock` headers).
- Update `src/renderer/theme/tailwind/plugin.cjs` to emit bare `var(--lobster-*)` for opaque theme colors and only use `color-mix()` for fractional opacity modifiers, avoiding CSS Color 4 `color(srgb ...)` paste issues in rich-text editors.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- **Packaging**: updated `electron-builder.json` (`extraResources` for `resources/skin-pack`) and `tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts`.
- **Storage & Migration**: `<userData>/email-skill/` credential migration + whitelist entry in `archiveWhitelist.ts`, cleanup of legacy bundled skill copies in `userData/SKILLs/`, and clearing stale `enabled: false` states for core skills.
- **IPC & Runtime**: updated `skills` and `kits` IPC handlers, `dshRuntimeAdapter`, `dshBootstrap`, `dshHostManager`, `dshAgentSync`, and `dsh-bundles/lobsterai-host`.

prs.title: fix(im): 修复 QQ、Telegram 和 Discord 群聊路由
prs.body:
## 问题

QQ 的群 OpenID 属于各自的机器人应用。只按这个标识路由，同一个群切换机器人可能新建任务，不同群的标识碰巧相同时也可能串聊。Telegram 和 Discord 在要求 @ 的群里仍会处理发给其他机器人的消息。Telegram 还会把论坛里的不同话题合并到同一任务，在两个群出现相同消息编号时漏收其中一条。

## 修复方案

- QQ 使用平台提供的跨应用群 OpenID 关联同一 Agent 下的群任务。跨应用标识不同的群独立排队和读取历史，每台机器人保留自己的群 OpenID 发送回复。
- Telegram 和 Discord 按群配置识别发给当前机器人的提及和引用回复。
- Telegram 按聊天区分消息编号，按群和论坛话题保存任务，并将即时回复和定时投递送到对应话题。

## 问题

切换到 DSH 后，同一个 Agent 的多个机器人加入同一普通群时，分别 @ 它们会在桌面创建多个任务。后一个机器人无法接着前一个机器人的对话回答。

## 修复方案

按渠道、群 ID 和 Agent 复用群任务并串行处理消息。每轮仍按被 @ 的机器人和发送者路由回复与审批。升级时优先续接旧版群任务，已有分支的历史记录继续保留。

钉钉的整群会话采用相同规则，投递时使用原始群 ID。私聊和飞书话题继续按各自的会话范围处理。

prs.body:
## 问题

迁移到 DSH 后，POPO 群任务会显示首位发言人的名字，同一群的消息看起来像按人分开。普通飞书群还可能在升级后新建任务，与原 OpenClaw 群聊历史分开。多位成员连续 @ 机器人时，后到的消息也可能打断前一人的回复。

## 修复方案

- 按群标识生成任务标题并显示渠道图标，按机器人、专家和群查找原会话。能够确认来源时修正旧自动标题，保留自定义名称。
- 同群不同成员的发言依次处理，每一轮保留发言人和回复目标。不同机器人、群、私聊及飞书话题各自独立。
- 飞书、企微和钉钉的群事件缺少群标识时跳过该事件，避免用成员 ID 错建任务。

prs.title: fix(im): prevent legacy 60s timer from racing DSH approvals
prs.body:
## Summary
- Fix IM approval prompts timing out at 60s despite displaying a 300s timeout (DEFAULT_IM_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000) and falsely notifying IM with ℹ️ 该操作已在电脑端处理。.
- Root cause: IMCoworkHandler (legacy OpenClaw handler instantiated by IMGatewayManager) and ImApprovalRelay (DSH handler instantiated by DshImInboundHandler) both subscribe to permissionRequest on the shared CoworkRuntime. IMCoworkHandler had a hardcoded 60s fallback deny timer and did not listen to permissionResolved, so at 	 = 60s it denied DSH approvals first and triggered permissionResolved externally, which ImApprovalRelay interpreted as a desktop-side resolution.
- Changes:
  - Skip DSH approval (dsh-approval:) and question (dsh-question:) requests in IMCoworkHandler.handlePermissionRequest.
  - Subscribe/unsubscribe permissionResolved in IMCoworkHandler so any externally resolved legacy permission cancels its 60s timer cleanly.
  - Add unit tests in src/main/im/imCoworkHandler.test.ts and a co-registered regression test (IMCoworkHandler + ImApprovalRelay) in src/main/im/imApprovalRelay.test.ts.

## Electron / Runtime Scope
- Main process IM runtime event handling (src/main/im/imCoworkHandler.ts). No IPC, storage schema, preload, or windowing changes.

releases.body:
## What's Changed

This release moves the agent engine from OpenClaw to **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** — 106 PRs, the largest architectural migration in LobsterAI's history. Sessions, experts, memory, IM channels, media generation, office editing and plugins were all rebuilt on the new engine, closing every capability gap left by the old one.

## ✨ Highlights

- **New engine, same app** — DSH is now the default runtime, with native desktop integration across sessions, tooling and packaging ([#3239](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3239))
- **Agents that work together** — cross-agent collaboration and specialist delegation let the main agent hand off subtasks to dedicated specialists ([#3137](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3137))
- **Every IM channel back online** — POPO added; WeCom, Weixin, Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, Telegram and Discord all restored with group-chat routing ([#3160](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3160), [#3232](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3232))
- **Plugin ecosystem** — marketplace, version checks, hot updates and an embedded plugin shell ([#3202](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3202), [#3207](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3207))
- **Instant launch** — the main UI no longer waits on engine boot; cold start is substantially faster ([#3157](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3157), [#3213](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3213))

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

- **The agent engine is now DSH.** Existing sessions, agents, experts, memory, IM bindings and settings migrate automatically on first launch — back up your workspace before upgrading.
- **The legacy web-search server is retired** in favor of native `web_search` routing. Any custom configuration pointing at the old server must be updated ([#3155](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3155)).
- **Experimental DSH flags and dead IPC channels are removed**; config files relying on them no longer take effect ([#3224](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3224)).
- **Bundled skills are mounted read-only.** To customize one, copy it into your user skills directory ([#3236](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3236)).
- **Fresh installations now require sign-in**, and Full Access permissions require explicit confirmation ([#3212](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3212), [#3165](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3165)).
- **Backup and migration were rebuilt**; older backup archives must go through the new migration flow ([#3190](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3190)).

## 🧠 Core Engine: OpenClaw → DSH

Engine migration and native desktop integration ([#3239](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3239), [#3136](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/3136)) by @fisherdaddy

issues.title: [Feature]: Add an Appearance page in Settings Center for welcome screen & background customization

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

Give Console users a single place in Settings Center to personalize the empty-state chat screen: custom welcome avatar, greeting text, its layout position, and a selectable background color/style. Most of the underlying pieces already exist in the codebase; this request is about exposing the missing ones through the UI instead of requiring a plugin or hand-written CSS.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) — only for persisting the new fields
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

I checked the current `main` branch before filing this, so this is not a request to build a theming system from scratch:

- Settings Center already has light/dark mode, six color presets, and custom accent / accent_hover / accent_bg / radius / dark surface values (`console/src/pages/SettingsCenter/GeneralSettings.tsx`, `themePresets.ts`, merged in #7741).
- Avatar upload and selection already exist (`console/src/api/modules/avatars.ts`, `console/src/layouts/LocalAvatarPicker.tsx`), but they are wired to the user profile, not to the welcome screen.
- The welcome screen (`console/src/pages/Chat/components/ChatWelcome.tsx`) takes `avatar`, `greeting`, `description` and `prompts` as props, yet in `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` those values come from i18n defaults (`qwenpaw.png`) or from plugin extension slots (`ChatScalar.welcomeGreeting`, `welcomeDescription`, `welcomeAvatar`, `welcomePrompts`, `welcomeRender`). There is no Settings UI for a normal user to change any of them, and no control over where the avatar and greeting sit on the page.
- `ThemeConfig` (`console/src/api/modules/theme.ts`) has no dedicated chat-area background field (only `accent_bg` and `dark.surface`). A user cannot pick a background color, gradient, or wallpaper style from the UI.

So the capability is scattered: theme colors in General, profile avatar in a sidebar picker, welcome content behind a plugin API, background effectively unavailable. The only workaround today is to write an appearance plugin or inject CSS, which is exactly the fragility described in #8071 (marketplace appearance plugins break whenever Console markup changes). For non-technical users, and for people running several QwenPaw instances who want to tell panels apart (see #7648), a built-in personalization page would be much more approachable.

## Proposed Solution

1. **One Appearance page** in Settings Center that groups the existing theme controls with welcome screen and background options, keeping the current live-preview behaviour.

2. **Welcome screen section**
   - Upload or pick an avatar (reuse `avatarApi`), edit the greeting text, subtitle/description, and the suggested prompt chips.
   - Layout controls: show/hide avatar, avatar size, alignment (centered / left), stacking (avatar above the greeting or beside it), greeting size, and vertical spacing. A live preview would make these safe to try.

3. **Background section**
   - Extend `ThemeConfig` with a background layer: solid color, gradient, or image, with separate light/dark values plus opacity or blur intensity where relevant.
   - Ship a small set of background styles alongside the existing six palettes (plain, soft gradient, glass, etc.), and keep a "reset to default" action.
   - Apply a contrast guard so custom backgrounds never make text unreadable. Ideally build this on QwenPaw's own semantic tokens, consistent with the direction discussed in #8071, rather than exposing raw CSS injection.

4. **Persistence**: store the new fields through the existing `/config/theme` and `/profile/avatars` endpoints so they survive upgrades and stay per-user where Console auth is enabled.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Plugin extension slots** (`welcomeRender`, `welcomeGreeting`, `chat.theme.set`): already cover part of this, but require plugin authoring and often direct CSS/DOM injection; not realistic for most users and vulnerable to Console changes.
- **External skin gateway / custom frontend** (#7287): closed as not planned, and far too heavy for a simple avatar + greeting + background tweak.
- **Editing i18n files or CSS by hand**: works locally, breaks on upgrade, and is lost on reinstall.

## Additional Context

- Related, checked before filing: #7741 (merged theme customization), #8071 (plugin-facing semantic token overrides, open), #2865 and #4974 (agent avatar requests, completed), #7648 (custom page title, open), #7287 (skin gateway, not planned). This proposal is about user-facing exposure and a few missing fields, not a new theming engine.
- Local install: QwenPaw 2.3.0 on macOS; `main` branch inspected on 2026-11-14.
- Happy to provide screenshots or a mockup of the proposed Appearance page, and to help verify a PR build.

## Willing to Contribute

- [ ] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

---

### 中文摘要

QwenPaw 的 Console 已经有设置中心（语言、明暗、6 套配色、强调色与圆角自定义，见 #7741），也有头像上传接口和欢迎页组件；但欢迎页的头像、欢迎语、提示词只能通过 i18n 或插件扩展点修改，头像与欢迎语的排版位置完全不可配，`ThemeConfig` 里也没有独立的背景字段。普通用户想换个头像、改句欢迎语、调个背景色，只能写插件或注入 CSS，而 Console 一改版就失效。

建议：在设置中心收拢一个「外观」页，把已有主题设置、欢迎页内容（头像/文案/提示词）、布局位置（对齐、上下或左右、显隐、间距）和背景层（纯色/渐变/图片，明暗各一套，带对比度保护）放到一起，沿用现有的 `/config/theme` 与 `/profile/avatars` 持久化，不另起一套主题引擎。与 #8071 的语义 token 方向保持一致即可。

issues.title: Console: markdown tables overflow the message bubble with no horizontal scroll
issues.body:
## Summary Markdown tables inside assistant messages are wider than the message bubble, are painted past the edge of the message list, and cannot be scrolled horizontally. The overflowing columns are effectively invisible, although the text can be selected. ## Environment - QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1, QwenPaw Desktop (Tauri webview) - Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045), WebView2 / Chromium 126 - Viewport 1366 x 705 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Ask the agent for a response containing a markdown table with a few wide columns (a two-column table with a long first column is enough). 2. Look at the table in the rendered message. ## Expected The table either fits the bubble, or is horizontally scrollable inside it. ## Actual The table extends beyond the bubble and beyond the right edge of the message list. There is no horizontal scrollbar, and the columns that fall outside are not readable (but remain selectable/copyable). ## Measurements From the live DOM for one such table: | Element | Value | | --- | --- | | `` width | 1007 px | | `.qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper` width | 898 px (overflow 109 px) | | list right edge | 1299 px | | table right edge | **1377 px** | | list `clientWidth` / `scrollWidth` | 930 / 930 (no horizontal scroll available) | Ancestor chain of the table: ``` table .x-markdown.qwenpaw-markdown overflow-x: visible .HostBubbles-module__quoteResponse__ overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-content-wrapper overflow-x: visible, 898 px wide .qwenpaw-bubble.qwenpaw-bubble-start overflow-x: visible .qwenpaw-bubble-list-scroll overflow-x: auto, scrollWidth == clientWidth .qwenpaw-bubble-list-wrapper overflow-x: hidden ``` ## Root cause The Console stylesheet applies the overflow rule directly to the table: ```css [class*=bubble-assistant] .x-markdown table { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` `overflow-x: auto` has no effect on a `
` element, because a table box is not a scroll container. The same rule works on `
`, which is why code blocks scroll correctly and tables do not.

## Suggested fix

Wrap rendered tables in a block-level scroll container, for example in the markdown component:

```jsx
…
``` ```css .qwenpaw-table-scroll { max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; } ``` The same treatment is worth applying to wide standalone images and to `
` wrappers for consistency.

issues.title: [Bug]: QQ channel reconnect supervisor exits permanently after websocket cleanup error, leaving worker ready and disconnected
issues.body:
## Current conclusion — minimal QQ-only repair

**Implemented scope: only the QQ plugin's minimal reconnect and cleanup fix in PR #8963.** The complete self-healing design described later in this issue is a **suggestion for upstream evaluation only**. It has **not** been implemented, and no framework follow-up work has been performed.

### Implemented in PR #8963

- Ordinary disconnect cleanup errors are logged with traceback and no longer terminate the reconnect loop.
- Stale `_close_errors` are cleared at platform/supervisor startup.
- Explicit-stop failures still report `QQ_NATIVE_CLOSE_FAILED`; `stop()` performs a final close/connectivity check for a socket retained by a disconnect/stop race.
- Reconnects reap only exited heartbeat controllers; live controllers remain retained for stop handling.
- Failure-state publication errors are logged instead of silently swallowed.
- Changes are confined to the QQ plugin and `tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py`.

### Validation

- Latest revision `d1ff5e5`: **83 QQ tests passed**; Black, Flake8, `add-trailing-comma`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- An earlier PR revision was also exercised against the real QQ Gateway: initial connection, two disconnect/reconnect cycles, and explicit-stop failure reporting behaved as expected.

### Explicitly not implemented

- No `PluginProcess` or `ChannelManager` changes.
- No `restart_limit` change.
- No host-level `platform_state` watchdog.
- No outage-message replay, duplicate-workspace/AppID redesign, or other framework lifecycle work.

The full worker-restart and host-watchdog ideas below are retained only as design context. They need upstream evaluation and are outside this minimal repair.

---

## Description

After the official QQ channel was migrated to the plugin worker (`qwenpaw_channel_qq` 0.1.0.dev0), a normal QQ Gateway disconnect can permanently stop reconnect attempts:

- the platform state changes `connected -> disconnected`;
- the worker process remains alive and `ready`;
- no later `connected` state is published;
- the channel stays deaf until the whole application is restarted.

This reproduces repeatedly on QwenPaw **2.3.0.post1**. A channel close does not crash the worker process, so the host's process supervisor sees nothing wrong.

### Root cause

In `qwenpaw_channel_qq/platform.py`, `_close_errors` is an instance-level list initialized once. Connection cleanup appends to it when heartbeat join / websocket close fails, including the deliberate incomplete-close check:

```python
except Exception as exc:
    self._close_errors.append(exc)
...
try:
    ws.close()
    if ws.connected:
        raise RuntimeError("QQ_SOCKET_STOP_INCOMPLETE")
except Exception as exc:
    self._close_errors.append(exc)
...
if self._close_errors:
    return False
```

It is not reset per connection or when the reconnect loop starts. Consequently, **one cleanup error after one server-side disconnect permanently disables all later reconnect attempts**. `_ws_connect_once()` returns `False` immediately, before backoff. `_run_ws_forever()` then publishes `failed` and exits its thread.

The older built-in 2.2.2 QQ implementation caught close exceptions and continued to the backoff path; it did not have this sticky fatal gate.

I verified on upstream `main` (2026-11-27, QQ `platform.py` blob `5ec1b0c1d7244aa256737cf19d0ae1a9e42b1f5c`) that the same `if self._close_errors: return False` gate is still present.

### Why the host does not self-heal

Pluginization introduced a process boundary, but neither layer recovers the dead connection:

1. The QQ WebSocket runs in a daemon thread. Its death does not terminate the plugin worker process.
2. `ChannelProcess._monitor()` watches the worker process / JSON-RPC transport, not the platform connection thread.
3. `LaunchSpec.restart_limit` defaults to `0`, so even a worker process exit is not restarted automatically.
4. `IsolatedChannelProxy._wait_connected()` waits for `connected` only during initial startup. Later `disconnected` / `failed` states are recorded but do not trigger reconciliation.
5. `ChannelManager` exposes manual `get_channel_health()` and `restart_channel()`, but no periodic platform-state watchdog invokes restart automatically.

As a result, the host can show an alive worker while the actual QQ connection is permanently gone.

## Design suggestions only — not implemented

1. A cleanup error after a peer/server-side disconnect must not terminate the reconnect supervisor. Close/heartbeat cleanup errors should be scoped to the current connection, logged, and followed by normal exponential-backoff reconnect.
2. If the WebSocket reconnect supervisor does terminate, the worker should either exit so the process supervisor can handle it, or publish a recoverable failure that the host reconciles with backoff.
3. The host should monitor `platform_state` after initial startup, not only during `_wait_connected()`, and restart/reconcile a worker that remains `failed` or `disconnected` beyond a threshold.
4. `restart_limit` should be non-zero for long-lived channel workers (with capped backoff), or channel-specific recovery should be implemented at the manager level.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1 with the official QQ channel connected (`platform_state=connected`).
2. Trigger a QQ Gateway / server-side websocket disconnect where close handshake cleanup is incomplete, or inject an exception from `ws.close()` / heartbeat `join()`.
3. Observe `_close_errors` become non-empty and `_ws_connect_once()` return `False`.
4. The worker remains `state=ready`; platform state stays `disconnected` / `failed`; no later reconnect attempt occurs, even if QQ Gateway is reachable again.
5. Restarting the whole QwenPaw app restores the channel.

## Observed evidence

Sanitized state transitions from the application log over two days:

```text
previous_platform_state=connected
platform_state=disconnected
worker_state=ready
```

There is no subsequent `platform_state=connected` for that worker generation; only a full application/channel restart brings it back. This occurred across many normal disconnects and was reproducible in multiple workspaces (`default` and `cronman`). Exact close exceptions were not persisted because the broad cleanup handlers currently discard or only store them internally, which is another diagnostic gap.

## Related but distinct

- #8748 / PR #8749: the same failure class for Feishu (cleanup exception terminates the reconnect supervisor). That fix is Feishu-specific and does not cover QQ.
- #8669: initial startup race where the `disconnected` sentinel was treated as fatal. Fixed separately; this report is about an established connection later dropping.
- #8394: XiaoYi WS disconnect behavior, different platform and lifecycle.
- #4788: legacy OneBot reconnect, different implementation.
- #6932: LLM network recovery, unrelated to channel worker lifecycle.

## Environment

- QwenPaw: 2.3.0.post1
- Channel: official QQ plugin 0.1.0.dev0
- OS: Linux x86_64 (Debian 12 / fnOS)
- Python: 3.12
- `process_mode: runner_process`
- `max_reconnect_attempts: 100`

## Security considerations

No credentials, AppID/AppSecret, QQ numbers, message contents, or user identifiers are included.

---

## 中文摘要

QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1 的官方 QQ 通道在插件化后，普通网关断线可能永久停止重连：

- `_close_errors` 是实例级粘滞状态，未按连接清零；
- close/heartbeat 清理出现一次异常后，`_ws_connect_once()` 直接返回 `False`，退避重连不会执行；
- WebSocket 线程退出并发布 `failed`，但插件 worker 进程仍然 `ready`；
- 宿主只监控 worker 进程/RPC，没有平台状态看门狗，且 `restart_limit=0`；
- 最终只能重启整个 QwenPaw。

这与飞书 #8748 / PR #8749 属同类但不同实现；上游 `main` 当前仍保留 QQ 的粘滞 `_close_errors` 终止逻辑。建议按连接隔离清理错误，并增加 worker/host 两级的平台状态恢复机制。

labels.name: question
labels.description: Further information is requested

issues.body:
# [技术评审] 企业版 Platform-Worker 实现及上游整合建议 ## 背景 我们基于 QwenPaw 开发了一套企业版，目前已经形成完整的可运行实现，并已在实际项目中部署运行。 我们希望请维护团队 Review 当前实现，重点讨论： - 哪些改动适合整理后贡献到上游； - 哪些模块适合继续作为独立扩展； - QwenPaw 是否需要补充通用扩展接口； - 后续 PR 如何拆分。 完整企业版目前属于内部研发成果。代码开放仍需走完内部流程。 ## 代码基线 - QwenPaw tag：`v2.2.2.post1` - Upstream commit：`b6715daabaa4f966626317452980fb84b8be9ab9` `v2.2.2.post1` 是当前分支的 Git 祖先，可以直接作为 diff 基线。 正式提交 PR 时，我们会按维护团队建议选择目标版本，并针对每个 PR 重新移植和验证。 ## 架构 ```mermaid flowchart LR C[Console / API Client] --> HTTP ADM[Admin Control Plane] <--> HTTP subgraph P[QwenPaw Platform] HTTP[Enterprise HTTP Middleware] A[QwenPaw Agent Runtime] M[Enterprise Tool Middleware] PE[Execute in Platform] WM[WorkerManager / Worker RPC] TC[ToolCoordinator] HTTP --> A A --> M M -->|PERSONAL / SHARED: Platform tools| PE M -->|Tools sent to Worker| WM PE --> TC WM --> TC TC --> A end WM <-->|PERSONAL / SHARED| W[Managed Worker] WM <-->|LOCAL: all tools| D[Device Agent] ``` | 组件 | 当前职责 | | --- | --- | | Platform | 运行 QwenPaw Agent，负责模型、会话、Workspace、ReAct、调度和权限上下文 | | Admin Control Plane | 为企业模式提供用户认证、用户状态、共享空间及成员角色；当前为独立部署 | | Worker 执行层 | 通过统一的 WorkerManager 和 Worker RPC 将远程工具调用作为 Tool Job 执行 | | Managed Worker | 由 Platform 管理，在 PERSONAL 或 SHARED 空间的隔离环境中执行工具 | | Device Agent / Local Worker | 安装在用户电脑上，通过相同的 Worker RPC 执行 LOCAL 空间工具，并增加设备绑定和本地访问授权 | | PostgreSQL | 保存企业用户投影、OwnerSpace、Agent、epoch、Worker assignment 等 metadata | Agent、Session、Workspace、ToolCoordinator 和 ReAct 流程继续使用 QwenPaw 原有实现。Agent 运行在 Platform，工具根据类型和空间在 Platform、Managed Worker 或 Device Agent 中执行。 Managed Worker 和 Device Agent 是同一 Worker 抽象的两种实现，共用 WorkerManager 和 Worker RPC。Managed Worker 由 Platform 创建和回收；Device Agent 由用户安装，通过设备注册、反向通道和本地授权接入。 ## Admin 控制面及与 Hub 的关系 当前 Hub 模式以用户为单位管理完整的 QwenPaw Runtime。企业版在一个 Platform 服务中根据 OwnerSpace 选择配置、Workspace 和 Worker，并增加 SHARED 和 LOCAL 空间。企业版当前不要求修改 Hub，两种部署方式可以分别保留。 当前实现通过独立管理服务完成用户和共享空间接入。企业架构只依赖以下控制面能力： - 用户登录认证； - 稳定用户标识及用户启用、停用状态； - SHARED OwnerSpace 的创建、启用、停用和删除； - SHARED OwnerSpace 的成员关系和空间角色。 Admin 控制面当前采用独立服务，后续也可以将这部分能力内置到 Enterprise Platform，减少部署组件。 ## OwnerSpace | 类型 | 资源归属 | 工具执行环境 | | --- | --- | --- | | `PERSONAL` | 单个用户 | 对应空间的 Managed Worker | | `SHARED` | 团队及授权成员 | 对应空间的 Managed Worker | | `LOCAL` | 用户及其绑定电脑 | 对应的 Device Agent / Local Worker | PERSONAL 空间只属于一个用户，Agent、配置、Provider、Workspace 和 Worker 都按空间分别加载，访问时会检查当前用户是否有权限。SHARED 空间由成员共同使用，空间内的 Agent、会话和项目文件对成员共享，系统仍会记录每次操作的实际发起人。目前权限控制到空间和角色，不支持在同一个共享空间内进一步限制某个成员只能访问部分 Agent、会话或文件。LOCAL 空间对应用户的一台电脑，工具调用由这台电脑上的 Device Agent 执行。 ## 请求和工具执行流程 1. 用户登录并选择 OwnerSpace 和 Agent。 2. HTTP Middleware 验证访问凭据并解析 OwnerSpace。 3. Platform 选择该空间对应的 config、Provider 和 Workspace。 4. 请求指定 Agent 时，Platform 检查 Agent 是否属于当前空间。 5. QwenPaw Agent 处理消息并产生 tool call。 6. Enterprise Middleware 取得 Agent、session、tool call 和项目目录信息。 7. 工具类型、ToolDescriptor 和 OwnerSpace 类型共同决定执行位置。 8. LOCAL 空间的工具调用通过 Tool Job 发往 Device Agent / Local Worker。 9. PERSONAL 和 SHARED 中，标记为 Platform 执行的工具经过权限检查后在 Platform 运行。 10. 其余工具以当前 `tool_call_id` 作为 `job_id`，通过 `tool.start` 创建 Tool Job，并发往对应空间的 Managed Worker。 11. Worker 检查空间、Agent 和当前 Worker 是否仍然有效，并返回排队、运行、输出和最终结果。 12. Platform 等待 Job 结束，将工具结果返回 ToolCoordinator，Agent 继续当前 ReAct 流程；调用中断时发送 `tool.cancel`。 请求级身份在 Platform 内通过 `ContextVar` 传递。进入 Worker、后台任务或其他进程边界时，只发送当前执行环节需要的身份字段。 以下情况会阻止工具执行： - 用户失去当前空间的访问权限，或者空间已经停用； - Agent 在任务创建后被停用、删除或重新创建； - 当前空间已经改用其他 Worker 或 Local Device； - Worker 没有对应工具； - LOCAL Device Agent 离线； - 项目目录无法映射到当前空间资源。 ## Worker 执行层 Platform 把每次远程工具调用作为一个 Tool Job 发给 Worker。Worker 在执行过程中返回状态和输出，Platform 可以设置超时或取消任务。Platform 收到最终结果后，Agent 再继续执行。Worker 的启动和回收、可用工具查询以及交互式终端不使用 Tool Job，分别通过对应的控制接口完成。 Platform 通过统一接口管理 Managed Worker 和 Device Agent 的连接、回收与重连。Device Agent 在统一 Worker RPC 之外增加了： - 一次性 enrollment ticket，用于首次绑定设备，短时有效且只能使用一次； - 设备密钥和签名证明； - TLS control/file 双通道； - timestamp 和 nonce 校验，防止旧的连接请求被重复使用； - binding epoch、换绑和撤销，设备换绑后让旧连接失效； - 本机文件访问范围，由用户选择 Device Agent 可以访问的目录； - 工具取消和连接恢复。 本地文件和 Shell 执行会检查授权范围。设备绑定变化后，旧连接和旧 Worker 状态会被清理。
Enterprise 模块目录 | 目录或文件 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/identity/` | 用户、Admin 控制面和设备身份验证 | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/metadata/` | 用户、空间、epoch 和 Worker assignment | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/config/` | 空间级 root config 和 Agent config | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/worker/` | Tool Middleware、WorkerManager 和远程传输 | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/pc_worker/` | Device enrollment、反向通道和 Device Agent | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/http/` | Enterprise API 和 HTTP 权限检查 | | `src/qwenpaw/enterprise/workspace_registry.py` | 空间级 Workspace 和后台任务隔离 | | `deploy/enterprise/` | Platform、Worker、Firewall、PC mount 和集成部署测试 | | `scripts/pack-device-agent/` | Windows Device Agent 打包和验收 | | `console/src/enterprise/` | 登录、空间切换和设备状态界面 | | `tests/unit/enterprise/` | Enterprise 单元测试 |
## 对 QwenPaw 扩展机制的复用 当前实现使用了 QwenPaw 已有的： - Plugin HTTP Router； - Agent Middleware； - Runtime Hook； - startup/shutdown hook； - Workspace 和 WorkspaceRegistry； - ToolCoordinator； - Provider、Channel、Cron、MCP、Skill 和 Session。 Enterprise HTTP Router、Worker Middleware、Runtime Hook 和生命周期 hook 通过现有 Plugin Registry/API 注册。 ## 对 QwenPaw Python 核心的修改 相对 `v2.2.2.post1`，当前收敛版本修改了 13 个已有 Python 核心文件。`src/qwenpaw` 的非 Enterprise 区域没有新增文件。 | 文件 | 修改内容 | | --- | --- | | `src/qwenpaw/__init__.py` | 支持专用启动入口跳过 persisted environment bootstrap | | `src/qwenpaw/app/_app.py` | 支持 Provider wrapper 和 WorkspaceRegistry factory | | `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/coding_mode.py` | 使用能够保留 ContextVar 的同步 I/O helper | | `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py` | 为后台聊天任务增加请求级命名空间，Enterprise 使用 OwnerSpace 作为命名空间 | | `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/service_manager.py` | 允许 WorkspaceRegistry 指定部分服务的初始化方式，并保留原有生命周期管理 | | `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py` | 提供公开的 Workspace 服务初始化接口 | | `src/qwenpaw/config/context.py` | 增加请求级 config path 和配置存储接口 | | `src/qwenpaw/config/utils.py` | root config cache 按实际路径隔离 | | `src/qwenpaw/config/config.py` | Agent config cache 按实际路径隔离 | | `src/qwenpaw/providers/provider_manager.py` | 支持独立存储目录和请求级 ProviderManager | | `src/qwenpaw/runtime/tool_registry.py` | 增加工具执行位置和 Platform 权限元数据 | | `src/qwenpaw/utils/runtime_api.py` | 支持受同源限制的动态请求 Header | | `src/qwenpaw/plugins/api.py` | 注册工具时传递执行位置元数据 | ### 这些核心改动解决的问题 1. **初始化时机**：Enterprise 需要在 ProviderManager 和 WorkspaceRegistry 创建前安装空间级资源选择。 2. **请求级资源**：config、Provider 和 Workspace 需要根据当前 OwnerSpace 选择。 3. **配置缓存隔离**：同名 Agent 在不同空间中使用不同文件，缓存需要按实际路径区分。 4. **工具执行位置**：工具通过描述元数据选择 Platform 或 Worker，避免维护工具名路由表。 5. **后台身份传播**：Channel 和 Cron 调用本地 Runtime API 时，需要在受信任的同源请求中带上当前身份。 6. **ContextVar 传播**：同步配置读写需要保留请求上下文。 7. **Workspace 服务初始化**：WorkspaceRegistry 可以在 Workspace 启动前指定部分服务的初始化方式，同时继续使用原有的启动、关闭和异常处理流程。Enterprise 当前用它接入空间级 Channel 和 Agent 配置监听。 OwnerSpace、权限判断和 Worker 路由继续留在 Enterprise 模块中。 ## 跟随上游版本演进 企业能力主要位于独立的 Enterprise 模块，并通过 Plugin API、Middleware、Runtime Hook 和生命周期 hook 接入。当前没有复制一套 Agent Runtime 或 ReAct 流程。对 Python 核心的修改集中在上表中的 13 个文件。 这种组织方式降低了跟进上游版本时的移植范围。Platform-Worker、OwnerSpace 和 Device Agent 模块可以保留，升级工作主要集中在扩展接口和核心接入点。架构划分不依赖 `v2.2.2.post1` 的某一段 ReAct 执行逻辑。 当前实现尚未针对最新 `main` 完成完整验证。每次升级仍需完成差异检查、接口适配和跨空间回归测试。 ## Console 改动 Enterprise Console 代码主要位于 `console/src/enterprise/`，提供登录、OwnerSpace 切换、LOCAL Device 状态和 Enterprise 初始化。 公共 Console 文件增加了以下接入点： | 文件 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `console/src/App.tsx` | 选择登录页并安装 Enterprise Bootstrap | | `console/src/api/authRuntime.ts` | 配置认证相关接口 | | `console/src/api/requestScope.ts` | 提供请求级 OwnerSpace 上下文 | | `console/src/api/authHeaders.ts` | 将请求上下文加入 Header | | `console/src/api/requestErrorMessages.ts` | 注册错误码提示 | | `console/src/api/request.ts` | 解析结构化错误码 | | `console/src/api/modules/auth.ts` | 使用可配置认证端点 | | `console/src/auth/gate.ts` | 使用当前认证 Runtime 校验登录状态 | 后续计划将目前分散在多个公共文件中的改动收敛为一个统一的 Console 接入接口。公共代码只负责加载 Enterprise 初始化、调用认证适配器和取得当前 OwnerSpace 请求上下文；登录页面、空间切换、错误提示和恢复逻辑继续放在 Enterprise 模块中。 ## 验证情况 2026-11-24 的验证账本记录了以下结果： | 项目 | 记录结果 | | --- | --- | | 全量 unit | `17,300 passed, 187 skipped` | | contract | `412 passed, 1 skipped` | | Enterprise Python 单测 | `199 passed` | | Enterprise Console 定向测试 | `47 passed` | | Hub + local runtime e2e | `1 passed` | | PERSONAL、SHARED、LOCAL API | 三类空间的 context、Agent、coding-mode、Skill 和 Agent config 请求通过 | | 双用户 PERSONAL 隔离 | 各自资源请求返回 200，互相访问对方 PERSONAL 空间返回 403 | | SHARED 授权和撤权 | 授权后的空间请求通过，撤权和临时用户清理完成 | | Worker 生命周期 | 完成创建、复用、取消和恢复验证 | | Device Agent | 完成首次绑定、重放拒绝、断线恢复和旧连接失效验证 | | Windows Shell 和文件访问 | PowerShell、CMD 和授权目录文件访问通过 | | Enterprise 关闭后的普通模式对照 | 该次验证源码与原版在同条件检查中结果一致 | 现有验证覆盖 API 权限、空间配置、Workspace 选择和 Worker 路由等边界。PERSONAL 和 LOCAL 空间属于用户私有边界；SHARED 空间属于团队共享边界，授权成员可以读取空间内的共享 Agent、会话和项目数据，管理操作由 `SPACE_ADMIN` 和 `SPACE_USER` 角色区分。 提交正式 PR 前，我们会针对每个 PR 的准确 commit 重新执行测试。 ## 希望维护团队 Review 的事项 1. 当前方案将用户、空间、权限和 Worker 相关代码保留在 Enterprise 模块中，只向 QwenPaw 核心增加必要的接入接口。维护团队是否接受这样的代码边界？ 2. 如果整体方向可以接受，维护团队希望我们先整理哪一部分代码？ ## 后续贡献 在公司审批允许的范围内，我们可以： - 按维护团队意见调整接口； - 将改动移植到指定的上游版本； - 将改动整理成便于 Review 和维护的 PR； - 补充默认模式和扩展模式测试； - 提供兼容性及安全边界说明； - 参与后续维护。 具体开放范围和许可证将在内部审批完成后确定。

issues.title: [Bug]: Cron API endpoints return 500 — `_get_default_cron_mgr` references non-existent `mam._workspaces

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Description

The cron REST API is unusable. All three `@api_action`-generated cron routes return **500 Internal Server Error**:

- `GET /crons/jobs`
- `POST /crons/jobs`
- `DELETE /crons/jobs/{job_id}`

The cause is a typo in the instance getter registered for `CronManager`: it reads `mam._workspaces`, but `MultiAgentManager` has no such attribute — it has stored workspaces in `self.agents` since the multi-agent refactor (#1375).

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw version | `2.3.1b2` (`main` @ `0853f0cad2ad76e7b96bb87ec9afe4e2a77e727b`) |
| Install | `pip install -e .` from source |
| Launch | `python -m qwenpaw app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18088` |
| Python | 3.11.15 |
| OS | Linux 6.8.0 |
| Auth | enabled, one user registered |

Also verified present in tags `v2.1.0`, `v2.2.1`, `v2.2.2`, `v2.3.0`, `v2.3.0.post1`, `v2.3.1-beta.1`.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# start the app, then:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://TARGET:8088/crons/jobs
# -> 500

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE http://TARGET:8088/crons/jobs/any-id
# -> 500

# sanity check: the handler is being reached at all
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://TARGET:8088/crons/jobs
# -> 422 {"detail":[{"loc":["body","name"],"msg":"Field required"}...]}
```

## Expected behavior

`GET /crons/jobs` returns the job list (e.g. `[]`), `POST` creates a job, `DELETE` removes one.

## Actual behavior

All three return 500. Server log:

```
File ".../qwenpaw/app/_api_action_routes.py", line 67, in endpoint_path
    return await getattr(mgr, spec.name)(**kwargs)
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'delete_job'
```

The getter swallows the real problem: instead of raising, it returns `None` because the attribute lookup fails, and FastAPI then tries to call a method on `None`.

## Root cause

`src/qwenpaw/app/_app.py:397-404`:

```python
def _get_default_cron_mgr(app_inst: Any) -> Any:
    mam = getattr(app_inst.state, "multi_agent_manager", None)
    if mam is None:
        return None
    # pylint: disable-next=protected-access
    ws = mam._workspaces.get("default")      # <-- line 402: attribute does not exist
    return getattr(ws, "cron_manager", None) if ws else None
```

`src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:58`:

```python
self.agents: Dict[str, Workspace] = {}
```

`MultiAgentManager` never defines `_workspaces` and has no `__getattr__` fallback, so `mam._workspaces` raises `AttributeError` on **every** call.

Verification:

```bash
$ grep -rn "self\._workspaces\s*=" --include=*.py src/
src/qwenpaw/plugins/testing.py:166:        self._workspaces = {}

$ grep -c "_workspaces" src/qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py
0
```

The only assignment in the tree is in a test stub (`plugins/testing.py`), not in `MultiAgentManager`.

## Suggested fix

```diff
-                ws = mam._workspaces.get("default")
+                ws = mam.agents.get("default")
```

Two notes on the fix:

1. **`get_agent()` is not a drop-in replacement.** It's declared `async def` (`multi_agent_manager.py:363`), and `_get_default_cron_mgr` is a synchronous callable used by `_make_endpoint`. Using it here would require making the getter async.
2. **The workspace may not be loaded yet.** `ensure_default_agent_exists()` (`app/migration.py:644`) only ensures the agent exists in *config*; it does not populate `self.agents`. On a freshly started instance the dict can still be empty, in which case `agents.get("default")` returns `None` and the endpoints keep returning 500 until something else touches the agent. Worth either loading the workspace lazily in the getter or returning a clearer error than `'NoneType' object has no attribute ...'`.

I confirmed locally that after changing line 402 to `mam.agents.get("default")` (and once the default workspace is loaded), all three endpoints behave correctly:

```
GET    /crons/jobs   -> 200 []
POST   /crons/jobs   -> 200
DELETE /crons/jobs/x -> 200 false
```

## Related

- #1375 — `feat!: Multi-agent/multi-workspace architecture`, the refactor that replaced `_workspaces` with `self.agents`. The getter was not updated in that change.

issues.title: Creator App Tests red on main since #8785: shared recovery budget re-runs the plugin's terminal forced step (extra provider call)
issues.body:
## Summary

`2fc5f1c` (#8785, merged 2026-11-26) gave `call_with_overflow_recovery` a shared recovery budget: when the recovery's retry is refused again with a *different* exception object, the boundary spends more budget instead of ending the turn. The terminal give-up signal stayed **object identity** — `retry_exc is exc` — which was never part of the public contract and which the QwenPaw Creator's recovery cannot satisfy: its terminal step raises a freshly-built `AgentModelError` that carries the user-facing "what was given up" report.

Result on current `main`: the Creator's forced recovery step runs twice per terminal overflow and the provider gets one extra burned call, and the `Creator App Tests` workflow is red for every open PR that touches creator paths (five PR branches failed on it today, 2026-11-27).

## Reproduction

```
pytest plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/file_agent_runtime/test_model_client.py::test_a_refusal_that_survived_both_recovery_steps_says_what_it_gave_up \
  plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/backend/tests/file_agent_runtime/test_model_client.py::test_the_forced_step_is_handed_the_request_the_provider_just_refused
```

```
assert provider.calls == 3          -> AssertionError: assert 4 == 3
assert forced == [_TEXT_BUDGET // 2] -> AssertionError: assert [20000, 20000] == [20000]
```

Reproduced on Linux and Windows (fork CI runners, fresh environments) and locally on Windows 10 / Python 3.11.6.

## Root cause (bisected)

First bad commit: `2fc5f1c` (#8785). Immediately-before parent `204fb07` passes both tests; `2fc5f1c` and every later commit fails them.

Chain of events for `failures=2` (refusal, compacted retry refused, forced step also cannot fit):

1. Creator's recovery boundary (`call_with_overflow_recovery`) sees the first refusal, runs compaction, re-calls.
2. Second refusal reaches the creator's forced step, which cannot fit either and raises `AgentModelError` — a *new* exception object carrying the give-up report.
3. Under the new boundary loop, `retry_exc is exc` is false, so the boundary reads it as "a second refusal about a different part of the same request", spends the remaining budget, and re-invokes the recovery — the forced step runs a second time (extra provider call, doubled demotion notes) before finally surfacing.

The boundary's give-up contract exists only in a code comment ("Re-raising the same exception means the recovery gave up"); nothing in the module or its tests establishes it, and the Creator's terminal state cannot use it without losing the report the `test_..._says_what_it_gave_up` test exists to protect.

## Suggested directions

- **Host-side signal (preferred):** give the boundary an explicit terminal signal — e.g. a small `RecoveryGaveUp` exception (or respect a marker attribute) that the loop always honors — so plugins can report give-up with their own user-facing wrapping while still stopping the loop. The Creator's forced step would raise it (with the report attached) and map it to `AgentModelError` at its own boundary; the two creator tests then keep their original, documented expectations (one forced step, three provider calls).
- **Creator-side adaptation:** the forced step re-raises the original refusal object so the identity check stops the loop, and the give-up report moves to the creator's outer layer. Loses the direct single-point report; more churn in the creator.

Either way, the regression also highlights the gap that let it in: the Creator App Tests workflow is path-filtered to `plugins/apps/qwenpaw-creator/**`, so a change to the host recovery boundary that the Creator imports never ran it.

## Environment

Windows 10 (build 19045) + fork CI (Linux ubuntu-latest and windows-latest runners), Python 3.11.6, current `main` (`7e27b9f`).

AI assistance disclosure: this investigation was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding tool; the bisect and reproductions above were executed locally.

cc @BeiMu-new (author of #8785) — this looks like an interface gap between the boundary and its only plugin consumer rather than a fault in either change, so your read on the intended contract would settle the direction fastest.

issues.title: [Feature]: 治理层内置规则（governance builtin rules）无法配置或禁用，与工具守卫层的开关相互独立造成困惑

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
# [Feature]: 治理层内置规则（governance builtin rules）无法配置或禁用，与工具守卫层的开关相互独立造成困惑

## 环境

- QwenPaw 版本：2.3.0.post1
- 系统：Linux (Alibaba Cloud Linux 8, x86_64)
- 渠道：微信（`qwenpaw_channel_wechat` 插件，iLink 协议）

## 问题描述

QwenPaw 有两层独立的命令拦截机制：

1. **工具守卫（tool_guard）**：`config.json` → `security.tool_guard.disabled_rules`，可在控制台「设置 → 安全 → 工具防护」里管理（如 `TOOL_CMD_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION`）；
2. **治理层（governance）**：`qwenpaw/governance/policy.py` 的 `_BUILTIN_ASK_SPECS` 硬编码内置规则，例如 `("Bash(sudo *)", "Privilege escalation, ASK")`。

第 2 层**没有任何配置入口**：

- `load_governance_policy()` 故意忽略 `policy.yaml` 里的 `builtin_rules` 键（防篡改设计，可以理解），日志只有一行 warning；
- `GovernancePolicy.evaluate()` 的 Phase 2 先遍历 `builtin_rules` 再遍历 `user_rules`（first-match-wins），因此用户审批产生的 allow 规则（`add_rule` 只能加 user_rules）**永远无法覆盖** builtin 的 ASK；
- 文档（security.zh.md / security.en.md）只介绍了 tool_guard 层，没有说明 governance 层的规则也无法通过控制台配置。

## 复现步骤

1. 在控制台「工具防护」里禁用 `TOOL_CMD_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION` 并保存（`config.json` 确认已写入 `disabled_rules`）；
2. 在微信渠道会话里让 agent 执行 `sudo whoami`；
3. 命令仍被拦截：`Approval for 'Bash' timed out after 300s. [INFO] Governance reason: Privilege escalation, ASK`。

## 期望 vs 实际

- **期望**：控制台的"禁用规则"能覆盖所有拦截层；或至少存在官方途径（config/policy.yaml/API）配置 governance 内置规则。
- **实际**：用户在控制台怎么关都没用（那开关只管 tool_guard 层），治理层的 `Bash(sudo *)` 写死在代码里；配合 IM 渠道审批通知不可靠，等于 agent 在 IM 渠道里完全无法执行 sudo 类命令。

## 根因定位

- `qwenpaw/governance/policy.py`：`_BUILTIN_ASK_SPECS`（约 L203-247）、`DEFAULT_BUILTIN_RULES`（约 L261-267）；
- `load_governance_policy()` 中 "builtin_rules: ALWAYS sourced from code (not from YAML)" 的注释段（约 L1330）；
- `GovernancePolicy.evaluate()` Phase 2：先 `for rule in self.builtin_rules` 后 `for rule in self.user_rules`（约 L797-880）。

## 本地 workaround（不改主包源码）

- 实际权限边界收敛到 `/etc/sudoers.d/` NOPASSWD 白名单（仅允许低风险命令免密）；
- 让 agent 用 `/usr/bin/sudo` 绝对路径绕开 `Bash(sudo *)` 的 glob 匹配（利用了 fnmatch 不匹配绝对路径的特性，见 `_check_shell_danger_keywords` docstring 里也提到该局限）——这个绕行方式很脆弱，不建议作为长期方案。

## 建议

1. 为 governance 内置规则提供官方配置口子（如 `config.json` 的 `security.governance.disabled_rules`，或允许 `policy.yaml` 的 `builtin_rules` 在显式开启 `allow_override: true` 时生效）；
2. 或允许"用户已审批过的 allow 规则"覆盖 builtin ASK（用户审批本身就是授权行为）；
3. 至少在文档里明确两层拦截的区别、各自的配置位置，以及"控制台禁用规则"只对 tool_guard 生效这一点。

Thanks for the great work on QwenPaw!

issues.title: [Bug]: Spawning a subagent from a Code Mode session leaks the parent's _execution_toolkit into the child — run_code fails with ToolNotFoundError
issues.body:
## Summary

In a Code Mode session, spawning a subagent through the `agent_tools_spawn` plugin tool makes the child session inherit the parent's `_execution_toolkit` ContextVar. The child session builds normally (`tools=1`), but every `run_code` call fails with:

```
ToolNotFoundError: The tool named 'run_code' doesn't exist.
```

The child has no working tool entry point at all, because `run_code` is the only tool exposed in Code Mode.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop `2.3.1b1` (`/api/version`), backend exe `qwenpaw-backend.exe`, 63,525,559 bytes, mtime 2026-11-23 10:42:58, sha256 `506339c3ef04fb9b59b4d31f520c722385122e2108feff7dea01c0abc1a5b336`
- Windows 11 Pro 26H2, build 26300.10075 (AMD64)
- Model: `commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Plugin: `qwenpaw-plugin-agent-tools` 0.2.5 (`LOCAL_PATCHES.md`: no local modifications)

## Reproduction

1. Open a Code Mode session.
2. Inside `run_code`, call the `agent_tools_spawn` tool to spawn a child session, with a task that itself calls `run_code` (for example `print('PROBE-OK')`).
3. The child session is created successfully (`source=subagent`, `depth=1`, `parent_session_id` points to the parent), but its first `run_code` call returns `ToolNotFoundError: The tool named 'run_code' doesn't exist.`

A fresh reproduction was run on 2026-11-27 16:25:

- Parent session: `1793323033659-icxd5yu` (Code Mode)
- Child session: `sub-8d96d5f4`
- `chats.json`: `source=subagent`, `group_id=subagents`, `meta.agent_tools.depth=1`, `parent_session_id=1793323033659-icxd5yu`
- Child's single `tool_call` is `run_code`, recorded at `2026-11-27T16:25:34`, and it failed with the error above.

## Evidence

### Session files (`sessions/console/default_sub-*.json`, counted per `tool_result` block)

| Session file | tool_call | failed | tool | failure window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default_sub-861b090b.json` | 2 | 2 | run_code | 2026-11-27T15:51:00 → 15:52:41 |
| `default_sub-c2349343.json` | 2 | 2 | run_code | 2026-11-27T15:02:19 → 15:02:24 |
| `default_sub-d7d4def4.json` | 20 | 20 | run_code | 2026-11-27T15:02:51 → 15:04:49 |
| `default_sub-8d96d5f4.json` | 1 | 1 | run_code | 2026-11-27T16:25:34 |

25 out of 25 `run_code` calls failed. 14 other subagent session files show no `ToolNotFoundError`.

### `qwenpaw.log`

```
24586:2026-11-27 15:02:14 | INFO | qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py:589 | builder: built agent for session=sub-c2349343 agent=default model=commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
24587:2026-11-27 15:02:14 | INFO | qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py:589 | builder: built agent for session=sub-d7d4def4 agent=default model=commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
26779:2026-11-27 15:50:52 | INFO | qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py:589 | builder: built agent for session=sub-861b090b agent=default model=commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
27393:2026-11-27 16:25:29 | INFO | qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py:589 | builder: built agent for session=sub-8d96d5f4 agent=default model=commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=1
```

`tools=1` is consistent with Code Mode exposing only `run_code`. The child agent build itself succeeds; the failure happens on the first tool call.

## Root cause

`src/qwenpaw/modes/coding/code_mode.py` (tag `v2.3.1-beta.1`):

- Lines 35-36: `_execution_toolkit: ContextVar[Toolkit | None] = ContextVar("code_execution_toolkit", ...)`
- Lines 151-160:

```python
async def call_tool(self, tool_call, state):
    invocation = _execution_toolkit.get()
    target = invocation if invocation is not None else self
    if target is self:
        async for chunk in super().call_tool(tool_call, state):
            yield chunk
    else:
        async for chunk in target.call_tool(tool_call, state):
            yield chunk
```

- Lines 248-251: `execute_tool` sets `invocation = Toolkit(tools=[tool])` and `token = _execution_toolkit.set(invocation)`
- Lines 271-272: the same value is reset only in the `finally` block of the current coroutine.

`src/qwenpaw/app/task_tracker.py`:

- tag `v2.3.1-beta.1`, line 399: `run.task = _create_task(_producer())`
- `main`, line 763: the same statement
- `_create_task = asyncio.create_task` (tag line 32, main line 46)

The trigger chain:

1. The parent is in Code Mode. While `run_code` is executing, `CodeModeTool.execute_tool` sets `_execution_toolkit` to `Toolkit(tools=[current tool])`.
2. The script inside `run_code` calls the plugin tool `agent_tools_spawn`. The plugin submits the turn in-process through `console_channel.stream_one(payload)` (`submit.py:106`, `:147`).
3. `task_tracker.py` starts that turn with `asyncio.create_task(_producer())`. `create_task` copies the current context, so the child task inherits `_execution_toolkit = Toolkit(tools=[agent_tools_spawn])`.
4. The child is built successfully, but when it calls `run_code`, `CodeModeToolkit.call_tool` sees a non-empty `invocation` and forwards the call to a toolkit that only contains `agent_tools_spawn`. `run_code` is not found, and `ToolNotFoundError` is raised.

The official `spawn_subagent` path (`src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/agent_management.py`) uses `submit_agent_chat_task` (`asyncio.to_thread`) with an HTTP self-call, so it crosses a thread/process boundary and does not inherit this ContextVar. The failure only appears on the in-process `agent_tools_spawn` path.

A minimal ContextVar check confirms the language-level behavior:

```python
cv.set("Toolkit(tools=[agent_tools_spawn])")
task = asyncio.create_task(child())
# child sees: Toolkit(tools=[agent_tools_spawn])
```

## Relation to #8903 and PR #8923

This is the same underlying mechanism as #8903: `execute_tool` creates a single-tool temporary `Toolkit`, and `call_tool` forwards to it without checking whether it can handle the requested tool.

PR #8923 changes `call_tool` so that when `invocation.get_tool(tool_call.name) is None` it falls back to `target = self.catalog`. That fix does not cover this scenario: `run_code` is registered on `CodeModeToolkit` itself (`super().__init__(tools=[code])`), not in `self.catalog`. Falling back to `self.catalog` still cannot resolve `run_code`, so a child session would keep failing.

## Suggested fix

Two independent options, both of which need to hold:

1. In `CodeModeToolkit.call_tool`, before forwarding, check whether `invocation` can resolve the requested tool (`get_tool(tool_call.name)`); if not, fall back to `target = self` rather than `self.catalog`.
2. Isolate the ContextVar when a turn is started from within `execute_tool`: start the producer task with a fresh `contextvars.Context()` (`_create_task(_producer(), context=contextvars.Context())`) or explicitly reset `_execution_toolkit` in the spawned task. This prevents any in-process submission from inheriting a temporary toolkit.

## Additional observation

The same mechanism appears with other catalog tools. `default_sub-fa1355f2.json` (2026-10-29 09:37, version not recorded) contains 2 `view_image` calls that failed with `ToolNotFoundError: The tool named 'view_image' doesn't exist.` This is consistent with the same leak, but it is listed separately because that run predates the version under test.

issues.title: Repeated identical tool calls are never interrupted: the doom-loop gate records at most one call per reply
issues.body:
## What happens

With `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=128`, a 400 MB probe process is terminated
correctly and the tool result reads:

```
exit code 15. [resource protection] Shell memory limit exceeded (RSS 134881280 bytes > 134217728 bytes)
```

The same `Bash` invocation was then approved **14 times** between `09:09:10`
and `09:10:22` — one every 6–7 seconds — and the user had to press stop twice.
Nothing in the agent loop noticed that the same call was repeating.

## Correction to the earlier report

The first version of this issue claimed the model never received the result and
therefore retried. That is wrong, and I am correcting it here rather than
leaving a misleading cause in place.

The result did reach the model. The stored turn at `09:11:01` ends with the tool
result carrying the full text shown above plus `state=error`. Draining the same
tool response directly returns it as a normal tool response as well.

So the retries were not caused by a missing result. They were caused by nothing
stopping them.

## Why nothing stopped them

`loop/gates/doom_loop.py` is enabled in the default mode — `window_size=3`,
`similarity_threshold=0.5`, `stop` after 4 hits — but the gate has never fired.
`_auto_record_from_ctx` de-duplicates on the **message** id:

```python
last_msg = context[-1]
if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
    return
```

Inside a single reply, every assistant message is written with the same
`state.reply_id`: `agentscope` creates one `ReplyContext(reply_id=…)` per reply,
and `AgentState.append_context` either extends the existing message or appends a
new one **with that same id**. From the second iteration onwards `last_msg.id`
already equals `state.last_recorded_msg_id`, the function returns before
recording anything, and the history never grows past **one** entry.

| iteration within one reply | message id | recorded calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 2 | `reply_id` | 1 |
| 3 … 14 | `reply_id` | 1 |

A three-entry window can never fill, so `_detect_repetition` cannot return true
and no stage is ever reached.

Reproduced against the real `DoomLoopGate` with two synthetic contexts:

| context shape | history after 8 iterations | fired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same message id every iteration (actual behaviour) | stays at 1 | never |
| distinct message id per iteration (hypothetical) | reaches 3 on iteration 3 | on iteration 4 |

Production logs agree: `qwenpaw.log` since 11-13 contains no `DoomLoopGate` and
no `Doom loop` line at all.

## Scope

This is not specific to resource-protection terminations. **Any** tool invoked
repeatedly with identical arguments inside a single reply is invisible to the
gate. The shell case only made it visible because each attempt was expensive
and the user was watching.

## Expected

Repeating the same tool call with the same arguments past the configured window
should reach the configured stage, instead of running until the user stops it.

## Proposed direction

Record per tool-call block rather than per message: make the de-duplication key
something that differs between two calls inside the same reply — the tool-call
block id, or `(reply_id, block_id)` — and scan the blocks appended since the
last observation instead of only `context[-1]`.

I am explicitly **not** proposing a change to `_with_shell_guard`. Overriding the
result state with `ERROR` is a separate question, it is not the cause of the
repetition, and changing it would not make the gate work.

## Second observation — explained, not a defect

While reproducing, a bare script that set `QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB=96`
before importing `qwenpaw` still ended up with `ShellGuard.from_environment`
returning `None`, and a 300 MB process ran to completion.

The cause is `load_bootstrap_envs()`: at import time it replays
`$QWENPAW_HOME.secret/envs.json` over `os.environ` with `overwrite=True`, and
that file contained `"0"` for this key, so the value set by the script was
replaced (96 → 0). Setting the variable **after** the import creates the guard
as expected (96 MB, kills a 300 MB process).

That is documented behaviour — "persisted values override existing
process/system values" — and the Console path writes through the same store, so
a limit configured there is applied correctly. I am recording it only so the
reproduction in this issue can be run; it is not a defect.

prs.title: fix(runtime): prevent injected context from persisting
prs.body:
## Description

Fix an upstream QwenPaw behavior: system-level reminders supplied via the public plugin hook `HookContext.inject_context()` reach the current model turn, but are also written to durable conversation storage as if they were user messages. A reload or subsequent turn can then reuse context that was intended for the earlier request.

Refreshed against upstream `main` at `0853f0cad2ad76e7b96bb87ec9afe4e2a77e727b`, including #8532. Related: #6360 and #6358.

## Evidence

Ran the same local probe against clean upstream and the refreshed branch. It used a synthetic reminder injected at `PRE_EXECUTE`, a real `Runtime`, `QwenPawAgent`, `SessionSaveHook`, and `DatabaseSession`, and a local recording model in place of external inference. Scroll and the transcript shared the actual per-conversation SQLite database. The probe committed the turn and read back the current snapshot, immutable turn revision, and Scroll rows.

| Observed behavior | Upstream main | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model saw the injected reminder on the current turn | Yes | Yes |
| Reminder stored in current session state | Yes | No |
| Reminder stored in the committed turn revision | Yes | No |
| Reminder stored in Scroll history | Yes | No |
| User-role messages stored in runtime state | 2 | 1 |

The actual user question was retained in all tested stores. The probe requires no external model service or credentials.

## Changes

- Tag request-local context and remove the exact injected message from agent state before normal and interruption saves.
- Exclude request-local context at Scroll serialization, before rows or search entries are written. Sanitize restored state, history rendering, and direct slash-command loads, covering both findings from the September review.
- Clean up only explicitly tagged old Scroll rows. The data-only migration uses a completion marker and keeps the shared database schema version unchanged. In a conversation database, it records the existing Recall purge event in the same transaction so projection replay does not resurrect removed rows. Legacy Scroll import also excludes explicitly tagged rows before writing events.
- Existing event payloads, untagged Scroll rows, prior immutable turn revisions, and existing summaries are outside the historical cleanup. Normal session loads still filter the structurally identified legacy context message.

## Testing

Windows, Python 3.12, isolated workspace. The related regression run covered runtime, context, hooks, chats, commands, backup, and the history conversion integration suite.

```text
2084 passed, 17 skipped, 14 warnings in 262.63s
```

The final focused run for Scroll migration, SQLite paths, event replay, and turn revisions returned `105 passed, 2 skipped`. It covered FTS cleanup and rollback, preservation of ordinary history on projection rebuild, and tagged-row filtering on legacy import. Pre-commit checks on all PR-changed files and `git diff --check` against upstream passed.
