issues.body:
### Summary

Add a `channel-buzz` channel so an agent can hang out in a Buzz (buzz.xyz) community and answer in its groups and DMs, the same way it already can in Slack.

### Problem statement

Buzz (https://github.com/block/buzz) is basically a free, open-source Slack. It's from Block, it's Apache-2.0, and you can self-host it or use a Block-hosted community at `https://<community>.communities.buzz.xyz`. You get the familiar Slack shape: channels, threads, DMs and mentions. The difference is that AI agents are first-class members instead of bolted-on bots.

ZeroClaw already talks to Slack, Mattermost and friends. Teams that picked Buzz because they want the Slack experience without the Slack bill (or without handing their chat to a SaaS) can't bring a ZeroClaw agent along yet.

You might expect our existing Nostr channel to cover this, since Buzz is built on Nostr, but it doesn't:

- `channel-nostr` only does DMs (NIP-04 and NIP-17) and kind-1 notes across a pool of public relays.
- Buzz conversations happen in relay-based groups (NIP-29): kind-9 messages tagged with an `h` group id, and the relay decides who's a member.
- A Buzz community is a single relay URL, and the relay wants NIP-42 auth before it lets you read or write anything.

Hermes Agent already ships a native Buzz adapter, so we're behind on parity here too.

### Proposed solution

Add `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/buzz.rs` behind a `channel-buzz` feature. Think of it as the Slack channel's counterpart for Buzz: same job, different wire.

It should talk to the relay directly over WebSocket using the `nostr-sdk` dependency the Nostr channel already pulls in. No shelling out to `buzz-cli`, and no dependency on Buzz's own crates (they're not on crates.io).

How it behaves on the wire, following Buzz's `NOSTR.md` guide for third-party clients:

- **Connecting:** one relay URL per configured alias, authenticated with NIP-42 using the agent's keypair.
- **Listening:** subscribe to kind-9 messages in the configured groups (`#h` filter), plus kind-1059 gift wraps addressed to the agent (`#p` filter) for NIP-17 DMs.
- **Replying:** kind-9 messages with the group's `h` tag, and NIP-10 `e` root/reply tags when replying in a thread. DM replies go back as NIP-17 gift wraps.
- **Ignoring noise:** drop events we've already seen (by event id) and anything the agent posted itself.
- **Mentions:** like a Slack bot, in groups it only speaks up when someone mentions it (a `p` tag or `@name`). DMs don't need a mention.

Config sketch. It starts off closed:

```toml
[channels.buzz.default]
enabled = false
relay_url = "wss://<community>.communities.buzz.xyz"
private_key = "<nsec-or-hex>"        # secret; give the agent its own keypair. Can also use Iron Vault or similar credential injection tool as a credential-less proxy
groups = []                          # NIP-29 group ids (UUIDs) to listen in; empty = DMs only
allowed_pubkeys = []                 # hex or npub; empty = nobody gets an answer
require_mention = true
reply_in_thread = true
excluded_tools = []
```

A quick note on naming: Buzz calls its groups "channels", just like Slack does. In ZeroClaw, though, a "channel" is the whole integration (Slack, Telegram, Buzz...). To avoid saying "the Buzz channel's channels", the config and docs call them `groups` and mention the Buzz name once.

### Non-goals / out of scope

To keep the first PR small, v1 leaves out:

- The other ways to hook an agent into Buzz: the `buzz-acp` bridge and the Buzz Desktop managed-agent runtime. This issue is just about the native channel.
- Buzz's extras beyond chat: workflows, canvases, Git hosting, search (NIP-50) and the audit log.
- Buzz-only event kinds: edits (kind 40003) and rich content (kind 40002).
- Media (NIP-94 `imeta`), in either direction. Fetching attachments from URLs the relay hands us is its own trust-boundary question and deserves its own issue.
- Creating groups or managing members. The operator adds the agent to groups from Buzz itself.
- Teaching the generic `channel-nostr` about NIP-29 groups.
- Hosting or bundling a Buzz relay.

### Alternatives considered

- **Bolt NIP-29 groups onto `channel-nostr` and treat Buzz as a preset.** It's tempting, but the two have different shapes. The Nostr channel is DMs over a pool of public relays. Buzz is one authenticated relay per community, where the relay enforces membership (much closer to a Slack workspace). Keeping them separate keeps each one's config and trust model simple. They can still share key-parsing helpers.
- **Shell out to `buzz-cli`, like Hermes does for sending.** That means an external binary on `PATH`, a process spawn per message, and tracking the CLI's JSON output format. Talking WebSocket directly keeps the channel self-contained. So: native for chat, and we can revisit `buzz-cli` if media or Buzz-only event kinds come into scope. That's where the CLI earns its keep, since it already handles media uploads and keeps up with Block's custom kinds.
- **Use `buzz-sdk` / `buzz-ws-client` directly.** They're well-shaped: pure event builders on `nostr` 0.44, the same version we're on, and they'd save us maintaining Buzz's tag conventions ourselves. But they aren't on crates.io, and `deny.toml` disallows git dependencies. So v1 builds the handful of kind-9, NIP-10 and NIP-17 events with `nostr-sdk`. If Block publishes the crates, switching to `buzz-sdk` for event building is a cheap follow-up. We've asked upstream: block/buzz#10000.
- **Just use `buzz-acp` with ZeroClaw's ACP channel.** That works today with no code changes, but it skips ZeroClaw's allowlist, mention gating and reply handling.

### Acceptance criteria

- There's a `channel-buzz` feature. It's not in the default bundle, but it is in `channels-full`.
- `BuzzConfig` is in the config schema with `private_key` marked `#[secret]`. Validation rejects a relay URL that isn't `ws://` or `wss://`, a bad key and malformed group ids.
- The agent authenticates with NIP-42, picks up kind-9 messages from its configured groups and NIP-17 DMs, and replies either in-thread or flat depending on config.
- It ignores messages from pubkeys outside `allowed_pubkeys`, its own messages, duplicate event ids, and group messages that don't mention it (when `require_mention = true`).
- If the connection drops, it reconnects and re-authenticates.
- Tests at the channel boundary cover event parsing, tag construction (`h`, NIP-10 `e`, gift wrap), allowlist and mention gating, and dedup.
- Someone has run it by hand against a local Buzz relay (`just relay` in the Buzz repo).
- Docs: a row in `docs/book/src/channels/overview.md` next to Slack and Mattermost, a channel guide, and onboarding text through Fluent keys.
- `docs/book/feature-matrix-parity.toml` gets a Buzz row.

### Architecture impact

- `crates/zeroclaw-channels/`: new `buzz.rs` and feature flag. It reuses the existing `nostr-sdk` dependency, so we don't expect any new heavy dependencies.
- `crates/zeroclaw-config/`: new `BuzzConfig` implementing `ChannelConfig`.
- Channel factory wiring and onboarding (i18n keys in the runtime Fluent catalogue).
- `docs/book/src/channels/`.

Like any new channel, this is a user-visible trust boundary. Inbound auth, mention gating and the reply lifecycle should follow `docs/book/src/architecture/channel-runtime-lifecycle.md`. We don't think it hits an RFC trigger: it's a bounded, feature-gated adapter that doesn't change anything that exists today.

### Risk and rollback

The main risk is the agent answering people the operator didn't mean it to. That's why it ships with `enabled = false`, and why an empty `allowed_pubkeys` means it answers nobody.

One thing worth spelling out in the channel guide: DMs are NIP-17 gift wraps, but group messages are readable by whoever runs the relay. It's the same as Slack, where the workspace host can read the channels.

Rollback is simple: set `enabled = false`, or build without `channel-buzz`. Nothing else changes.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage

### Next decision surface

Ordinary triage is enough.

### Breaking change?

No

### Data hygiene checks

- [X] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [X] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

prs.title: feat(channels/discord): add thread_mode to answer mentions in a thread
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `channels.discord.<alias>.thread_mode` (`off` by default, or `on_mention`). With `on_mention`, an @-mention in a regular guild channel starts a thread on that message (or reuses the thread it already has) and the reply goes into it, so agent conversations stop taking over shared channels.
  - In a thread the bot's account created, follow-ups from people are admitted without a mention even when `mention_only = true`, so the conversation can actually continue there (the same default the Slack channel uses for thread replies). Other bots, and every other thread, keep the `mention_only` rule, so `listen_to_bots` cannot turn the bot's thread into a bot-to-bot loop.
  - "Did the bot create this thread?" comes from Discord: the existing `GET /channels/{id}` thread lookup now also keeps the thread's `owner_id` in the same per-channel cache, and a newly created thread is cached from Discord's create response. No local thread registry is added.
  - A message that gets a thread is marked `explicitly_addressed` (it was an @-mention), so the reply-intent precheck cannot leave a freshly opened thread empty. Reactions the orchestrator places on the triggering message are sent to the parent channel, where that message lives, rather than to the new thread.
  - Failure handling: a `403` falls back to the channel with a `WARN` naming the two permissions; Discord's "thread already exists for this message" (`160004`) reuses that thread; any other error or a stalled request (10 s cap, the call runs inside the gateway loop) falls back with a `WARN` carrying Discord's status and body.
  - Docs: the setting, its interaction with `mention_only`, the two extra bot permissions, and troubleshooting rows in `docs/book/src/channels/discord.md`. The `mention_only` field description now notes the thread exception.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to DMs, to messages already inside a thread, to slash-command interactions, to the Discord WASM plugin, or to any other channel. No `always` mode (the issue lists always-threading as likely too surprising); the enum leaves room for it. Discord still does not set `explicitly_addressed` for ordinary mentions; this PR sets it only when it opened a thread. No change to the shared orchestrator lifecycle: the adapter points `reply_target` / `thread_ts` / `interruption_scope_id` at the new thread, exactly as it already does for messages that arrive in a thread.
- **Blast radius:** Discord channel inbound routing only, and only when `thread_mode = "on_mention"`. With the default `off`, the listener does the same lookups and admission as before. Two shared Discord paths changed shape: the thread-metadata cache value (`Option<String>` parent to `Option<DiscordThreadMeta>`, whose existing readers `discord_thread_parent` and `discord_thread_parent_cached` return the same parent as before), and `add_reaction` / `remove_reaction`, which now redirect only when the message id equals the channel id (true only for a thread's starter message, which never happens with `off`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #7849

### What this does, simply

When people @-mention a Discord bot in a busy channel, the back-and-forth (follow-up questions, tool output, long answers) lands in that channel and drowns everything else. Other agents solve this by opening a thread on the mention and talking there.

This PR adds that as an opt-in Discord setting. Set `thread_mode = "on_mention"` and a mention in a normal channel opens a thread named after the message; the bot answers inside it, and you can keep talking there without mentioning it again. Mentions inside existing threads and DMs behave exactly as today. If the bot is not allowed to create threads, it simply answers in the channel like before and logs which permissions are missing. Nothing changes unless you turn it on.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord bot with Message Content Intent, in a test server, with Send Messages, Read Message History, View Channels, Create Public Threads and Send Messages in Threads. Config:
  ```toml
  [channels.discord.default]
  enabled = true
  mention_only = true
  thread_mode = "on_mention"
  ```
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In a regular text channel, send `@bot what is 2+2?`.
  2. In the thread that appears, send `and times 3?` without a mention.
  3. In the channel (not the thread), send a message without a mention.
  4. Remove Create Public Threads from the bot's role and repeat step 1.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** (1) a thread named `what is 2+2?` is created on the message, the 👀 ack lands on the original message, and the answer is posted inside the thread; (2) the bot answers in the thread without a mention; (3) the bot stays silent; (4) the answer is posted in the channel and the daemon log has a `WARN` "thread_mode: could not start a reply thread, replying in the channel instead" whose `reason` names the missing permissions.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** (1) the answer is posted in the channel; (2) not reachable, no thread exists; with a manually created thread, a follow-up without a mention is ignored under `mention_only = true`; (3) silent; (4) the answer is posted in the channel.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI` Rust lint (clippy `-D warnings`, rustdoc, comment hygiene) and `cargo nextest` cover the new routing helpers, thread-name builder, metadata parser, REST helper (mocked with wiremock) and the config parse test; `parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` covers the channels crate under parallel load; `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown lines.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The gateway WebSocket loop itself is not exercised end to end in CI (it needs a live Discord gateway); the manual smoke below covers it.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on macOS (aarch64), `rustc 1.99.1`, at the PR head on top of `master` 2f3bcab.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 58s

  $ cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config
     Generated .../target/doc/zeroclaw_channels/index.html and 1 other file

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib discord::
  test discord::tests::thread_mode_starts_a_thread_only_for_a_mention_in_a_guild_channel ... ok
  test discord::tests::thread_mode_waives_the_mention_only_for_humans_in_the_bots_own_thread ... ok
  test discord::tests::own_thread_means_discord_names_the_bot_as_owner ... ok
  test discord::tests::reply_route_follows_the_started_thread_and_falls_back_to_the_channel ... ok
  test discord::tests::reactions_on_a_threads_starter_message_go_to_the_parent_channel ... ok
  test discord::tests::thread_name_drops_mention_markup_and_fits_discords_limit ... ok
  test discord::tests::thread_meta_reads_parent_and_owner_from_thread_channels_only ... ok
  test discord::tests::start_reply_thread_creates_it_on_the_message_and_caches_its_owner ... ok
  test discord::tests::start_reply_thread_reuses_a_thread_the_message_already_has ... ok
  test discord::tests::start_reply_thread_falls_back_when_discord_refuses_or_fails ... ok
  test discord::tests::start_reply_thread_gives_up_when_discord_hangs ... ok
  test discord::tests::thread_parent_cached_reads_cache_without_rest ... ok
  test discord::tests::autocomplete_authorizes_parent_allowlisted_thread_only_when_cached ... ok
  test result: ok. 325 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1797 filtered out

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config
  zeroclaw-channels lib: test result: ok. 2120 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
  zeroclaw-config lib:   test result: ok. 2040 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
    (includes schema::tests::discord_config_thread_mode_defaults_off_and_parses_on_mention)
  zeroclaw-runtime lib:  test result: FAILED. 6330 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored
    relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener
    relay::local_dial_tests::a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget
    (both panic with "could not stall a loopback connect: the listener backlog never filled";
     they fail identically on unmodified master 2f3bcab on this macOS host and do not touch
     anything this PR changes; Linux CI runs them)
  all other integration/doc test binaries: ok

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n
  test result: ok. 50 passed; 0 failed (catalog parity across en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN)

  $ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw --tests
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 10s

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed Rust files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

  $ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/channels/discord.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  $ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/channels/discord.md bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.

  $ bash scripts/check-pr-title.sh "feat(channels/discord): add thread_mode to answer mentions in a thread"
  (exit 0)
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Manual smoke on a live bot in a test server, with synthetic prompts, running this change backported unchanged onto v0.9.0 (aarch64 Linux build) with `mention_only = true` and `thread_mode = "on_mention"`. Steps 1-3 of "How you can test" behaved as expected: the mention opened a thread on the message and the answer was posted inside it, a follow-up in that thread without a mention was answered, and an unmentioned channel message was ignored. The daemon logged no `thread_mode` warnings. Not verified manually: step 4 (permission removal), the reuse of an existing thread, and the reaction placement; those paths are covered by the wiremock and routing tests above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no ZeroClaw interface changes; the visible effect is Discord thread placement, described above).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Unit and gate evidence at the PR head (one commit on `master` 2f3bcab); manual smoke on the same diff applied to v0.9.0; interface `channel` = `discord`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See the manual steps above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` was run but stops at the two macOS-only relay failures above before reaching the channels binary; the full `zeroclaw-channels` lib suite passed in the plain `cargo test` run. `cargo nextest` is not installed locally; CI runs it. Full `--features ci-all` workspace clippy is left to CI; local clippy covered the three changed crates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? Yes
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The bot needs two extra Discord permissions (Create Public Threads, Send Messages in Threads) only when an operator opts into `on_mention`; without them it falls back to the existing reply path. The one new call is `POST /channels/{id}/messages/{id}/threads` to Discord's existing API host, with the bot token the channel already uses. The mention waiver applies only to human authors in threads whose Discord `owner_id` is the bot (`owner_id` is set by Discord from the creating identity and cannot be set by users), and the sender allowlist, guild and channel filters still run before it. The thread name is derived from the user's own message (bot mention stripped, capped at 100 chars) and is not shown to the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. The new key defaults to `off`, so existing configs behave as before. To opt in, set `channels.discord.<alias>.thread_mode = "on_mention"`, grant the two thread permissions, and reload or restart the daemon (the Discord listener reads the value when it is built).

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `channels.discord.<alias>.thread_mode = "off"` (or remove it) and reload; or `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.discord.<alias>.thread_mode`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `WARN` events with the message "thread_mode: could not start a reply thread, replying in the channel instead" (attrs `channel_id`, `message_id`, `reason`, `error` with Discord's status and body); replies landing in the channel instead of a thread.

prs.title: fix(providers): carry the paired tool name on recovered tool results
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The damaged-envelope recovery branch added in #12188 restored `tool_call_id` but still constructed the `NativeMessage` with `name: None`.
  - Groq rejects every role-tool message without `name` (`Tools should have a name!`), so replaying an already-damaged conversation on Groq kept failing even after the id was restored.
  - The recovery branch now resolves `name` through the same `tool_name_map` lookup the whole-envelope branch uses, keyed by the raw id recovered from the leading envelope.
- **Scope boundary:** only the partially-parseable-envelope branch of `OpenAiCompatibleModelProvider::convert_messages_for_native()`. No channel normalization, no contract/id-rewrite behavior, no change to the whole-envelope path; undamaged conversations serialize exactly as before (`name` stays unset there).
- **Blast radius:** strict OpenAI-compatible providers that require `name` on role-tool messages (Groq class), and only sessions already carrying the pre-#12188 corrupted form; new corruption is prevented by the channels half of #12188.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12665. Depends on #12188 — the first three commits on this branch are that PR's head `c36b3c068`; only the last commit `24a0cced8` is new.

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw continues a saved conversation, it replays the stored messages to the provider. A historical bug could merge a follow-up user turn into a stored tool-result message, leaving its JSON envelope only partially parseable. #12188 taught the OpenAI-compatible serializer to recover the `tool_call_id` from such a damaged envelope, but it left the tool name empty. Some providers — Groq — refuse a tool result with no name. This change fills in the name by looking up the tool that issued the original call, so conversations damaged by the old bug can replay on those providers. Conversations that were never damaged behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the conversion boundary is covered by the unit regression test; a live strict-provider replay additionally needs a Groq key plus a hand-crafted damaged stored session (repro described in #12665).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required CI suite runs the full-workspace `Lint` (clippy `-D warnings`), `Test`, and `Greptile Review` on this exact head; the parent stack's suite is already green at `c36b3c068`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none — the `name` lookup itself is provider-independent; only its requirement is Groq's.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # clean, no output

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib convert_messages_for_native
  # cargo test: 35 passed, 1963 filtered out (1 suite, 0.01s)

  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
  # cargo clippy: 0 errors, 1 warnings
  #   unused workspace dependency `zeroclaw-dist` (1x) — Cargo.toml:19
  ```
  The single warning is a cargo manifest notice present at the parent commit as well — it only shows on package-scoped runs, and the touched diff is `compatible.rs` only; the full-workspace clippy gate in CI covers it.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** the new regression test asserts the recovered result resolves `tool_call_id` through the contract map and carries the paired assistant tool call's `name` (`shell`); the other 34 `convert_messages_for_native*` tests confirm no drift in sibling paths. I did not run a live Groq replay (no key at hand); the acceptance contract comes from #12665's reported error.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed; request serialization only.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `24a0cced8`, worktree `zeroclaw-pr12188`, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib convert_messages_for_native`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A` (no presentation-sensitive change).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** replaying a damaged-envelope tool result through `convert_messages_for_native()` now yields a role-tool message with both `tool_call_id` and `name` populated, per the regression test above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace `cargo test` and full-workspace clippy — delegated to the required CI `Test`/`Lint` jobs that run on this head; the scoped local run covers the changed module.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` — the populated `name` is resolved from the same conversation's assistant tool call, which the same request already sends to the same provider.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` — populates a previously-unset field on the recovery branch only.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- Upgrade steps: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert 24a0cced8` is the plan.

prs.title: fix(mcp): evict poisoned connections instead of reusing them
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - One failed recovery attempt used to poison an MCP connection permanently. `RecoveryBarrier::poison()` sets a flag nothing clears, and `McpServer::health_check()` only asked the transport, which still answered `true`. Every later tool call on that server failed closed against a connection the rest of the system believed was healthy. `health_check()` now also reports poisoned recovery as unhealthy.
  - Region: the daemon's registry reconciliation (`health_check_all` → keep healthy, drop dead, reconnect) now sees the poisoned server as dead, drops it, and establishes a fresh connection instead of reusing a permanently failed one.
  - Remote MCP POSTs no longer follow redirects automatically. A 307/308 can arrive after the first server already received and executed the request; following it replays the JSON-RPC body against a second endpoint, so a `tools/call` with side effects could run twice. The original response is surfaced as an HTTP status instead.
  - A connect-stage failure restores the `REQUEST_PRE_WRITE` classification. A connect error proves nothing reached the server, so the request may be retried, instead of staying at "outcome unknown" and being blocked from ever retrying.
- **Scope boundary:** The poison flag itself is still never cleared — a poisoned server is evicted and re-established, not repaired in place. No change to retry/backoff policy, no second recovery attempt, no change to the stdio transport, no change to the TLS-CA loading path other than the redirect policy it shared.
- **Blast radius:** Remote HTTP/SSE MCP transports and MCP registry health reporting. The redirect policy is strictly narrower, so an MCP endpoint configured to rely on an https→https redirect now receives the redirect status instead of being followed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #10807

### What this does, simply

When a remote MCP server blips — container restart, proxy reload, laptop sleep — ZeroClaw makes one reset-and-handshake attempt. If that attempt fails, the connection was marked unrecoverable forever, but nothing outside the connection knew: health checks still passed, so it stayed in rotation and every tool call on it failed from then on. This PR makes that state visible to the health check, so the dead connection is dropped and replaced by a fresh one.

Two related hazards came out of the same code path. A redirected POST could be re-sent to the new location after the original server had already acted on it, so a side-effecting tool could run twice — redirects are no longer followed. And a connection error that happened before any bytes were sent was being classified as "outcome unknown", which blocked safe retries; it is now classified as pre-write.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior is covered by unit tests in `zeroclaw-tools` plus required CI; no manual setup is needed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `None`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the workspace `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`, which is exactly the surface this touches; `MSRV (declared floor)` confirms no toolchain-floor drift, and the platform build checks (incl. `Check x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) confirm the transport change compiles where `reqwest` picks a different TLS backend. All green on this head.
- **Commands run:** the workspace-wide fmt / clippy / test commands above, executed by the required CI gate on this head — I did not run additional commands beyond that.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Nothing beyond the tests below; the failures are exercised with in-process fake transports and `wiremock`, not against a live MCP server.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface changed.

The tests added on this branch, by claim:

- `poisoned_recovery_is_reported_as_unhealthy_to_registry` — a server whose transport answers healthy but whose recovery is poisoned now reports unhealthy.
- `poisoned_http_recovery_is_evicted_without_replaying_unknown_tool` — after a failed background re-handshake, the registry reports the server unhealthy, `kill_dead_connections` evicts it, the registry empties, and the tool body was written exactly once (no replay).
- `http_post_redirect_is_not_followed_or_replayed` — a 307 pointing at a dead port is surfaced as `HTTP 307`, the mock received exactly one request, and the lifecycle is left neither `outcome_unknown` nor `pre_write`.
- `pre_write` classification on connect errors, and the existing HTTPS→HTTP redirect rejection updated to assert the original `HTTP 302` is reported rather than a post-follow failure.
- `cargo fmt` applied to the redirect regression test (`style(mcp)` commit) after a reviewer run flagged formatting.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No` — the opposite: automatic redirect following is removed, so an MCP POST can no longer reach a location the operator did not configure.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` — session headers are applied exactly as before; they are not attached to a redirected request any more, because there is no redirected request.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No` — tool results are unchanged; what changed is whether a failed call can be retried and whether it can be replayed.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: —

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No` — narrowly: an MCP server URL that relied on the client following an https→https redirect now returns that status to the caller.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: point the MCP server entry at the final endpoint URL instead of a redirecting one. Nothing else changes — the request that used to be replayed to the redirect target is now a normal non-2xx response the caller can inspect.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk PRs: `git revert <sha>` is the plan unless otherwise noted.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the branch as a whole (the commits are independent and revert cleanly in reverse order).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** after a revert, `MCP server <name> is unavailable: a prior request's outcome became unknown and recovery failed` reappears in logs after a single failed recovery and never goes away for that server; registry reconciliation keeps listing the server as healthy.

prs.title: feat(channels): let a Discord channel opt out of the built-in /ask
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - New `channels.discord.<alias>.slash_builtin_ask` (default `true`). When `false`, the channel registers only its `slash`-tagged skill commands.
  - Disabling deregisters our own `/ask` on the next READY, from the active scope and the inactive one. Today the reconcile never deletes an `/ask`, so an operator has no way to remove it from ZeroClaw.
  - Motivation: a server running several ZeroClaw applications shows one `/ask` per application in the picker. Members pick the wrong one and get a rejection or silence.
- **Scope boundary:** does not let skills claim the `ask` name, does not rename the built-in, and does not change how an arriving `/ask` interaction is gated or served. @-mention handling is untouched.
- **Blast radius:** Discord slash registration only. With the default, the registration body is built exactly as before (same constructor output, same order), so the persisted fingerprint should not change and existing deployments should not re-register.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11150
- **Labels:** `channel:discord`, `enhancement`, `risk:low` (size set by the labeler)

### What this does, simply

A Discord bot built on ZeroClaw always adds an `/ask` command. That is fine for one bot. With two or three ZeroClaw bots in the same server, members see several identical `/ask` entries and cannot tell which one will answer them. This adds a switch so an operator can turn `/ask` off on the bots that should not offer it. Turning it off also removes the `/ask` that bot registered earlier. Nothing changes for anyone who leaves the switch alone.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior boundary is Discord's REST API, which the new tests exercise against a mock server; a live check needs a real application and bot token.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`.

### How I tested

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord round trip.

prs.title: feat(channels/discord): offer the built-in chat commands as slash commands
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - With `slash_commands = true`, Discord's `/` menu offers `/ask` and `slash`-tagged skills, but the built-in chat commands the channel runtime already handles (`/model`, `/models`, `/thinking`, `/new`, `/clear`, `/stop`, `/config`) only work as typed text. Telegram already lists its built-ins in its native command menu; this brings the same discoverability to Discord.
  - The command list is derived from `zeroclaw_commands`: channel-surface commands whose `execution` is `RuntimeCommand`. That excludes `/goal` (goal admission, not yet dispatched on channels) and `/help` (client-local). Each command registers its catalog description and, when its catalog `usage` shows arguments, one optional free-form `args` string option whose description is that usage (for example `[--user|--agent] [model]`). The command grammar is not duplicated.
  - An invocation is acknowledged with an ephemeral message and forwarded as the equivalent typed command (`/model <args>`), from the invoker, routed to the invoking channel or thread exactly as the message path routes a typed command (`reply_target` = channel, `thread_ts` / `interruption_scope_id` = thread when in one). So the existing `parse_runtime_command` / `is_stop_command` handle it, and it acts on that conversation's session. Routing it through the `/ask` interaction sentinel instead would give every invocation its own one-shot session, so `/new`, session-scoped `/model` and `/stop` would act on nothing.
  - Supporting changes:
    - Built-ins are owned by projection, like `/ask`, when reaping an inactive scope after a global/guild switch. A same-named foreign command is spared.
    - A `slash`-tagged skill cannot take a built-in's name.
    - Reactions are skipped for interaction-originated message ids. The orchestrator's ack reaction would otherwise target a message that does not exist.
    - The `command-*-description` strings the catalog already declares (but no locale defined) are added for these seven commands in all five locales, plus one acknowledgement string.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No new command behavior: every built-in is executed by the existing parser exactly as if typed.
  - No autocomplete or per-command typed options. Arguments are free-form, as when typed.
  - `/ask` and skill commands are unchanged.
  - Nothing registers unless `slash_commands` is already on.
- **Blast radius:**
  - Discord slash registration and interaction dispatch, only with `slash_commands = true`. The registered set grows by seven commands, so the first READY after upgrade re-registers once.
  - `1 + 7 + MAX_SKILL_SLASH_COMMANDS (90) = 98`, which stays within Discord's 100-command cap; a test pins this.
  - `zeroclaw-channels` gains a dependency on the workspace-internal `zeroclaw-commands` crate, which depends only on `serde`.
- **Linked issue(s):** None found. The Discord interaction-parity tracker (#7831, closed as complete) covered embeds, typed skill options, components and modals but not the built-in commands.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw already understands chat commands like `/model`, `/thinking`, `/new` and `/stop`, but on Discord you had to know them and type them. Discord's own `/` menu only showed `/ask` and skills. With this change, those commands appear in the menu with descriptions. Picking one does exactly what typing it in that channel or thread would do: same conversation, same result, posted in the channel as usual. Discord shows you a small private confirmation. If the bot's slash commands are off, nothing changes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord channel with `slash_commands = true` (guild scope propagates instantly).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. In a channel, type `/` and pick `/model` with no arguments, then `/thinking` with `args: high`.
  2. Have a conversation, then pick `/new` in the same channel and ask what was said before.
  3. In a thread, start a long request and pick `/stop` in that thread.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** each command appears in the menu with a description; the invoker sees an ephemeral "Sent `/…`"; the command's normal reply is posted in that channel or thread; `/new` resets that channel's conversation; `/stop` cancels the turn in that thread.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** only `/ask` and skills appear in the menu; the built-ins work only when typed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** clippy and `cargo nextest` cover the registration body, the catalog-derived set, the routing of the forwarded message, reaction skipping, projection-owned reaping (wiremock), and the drift guard that every registered built-in is handled by the channel runtime parser.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Live interaction delivery from Discord is not exercised in CI; covered by the manual check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on macOS (aarch64), `rustc 1.99.1`, at the PR head on top of `master` d4a5d2a.

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output)

  $ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 35s

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord:: every_discord_builtin
  test discord::tests::registration_offers_the_runtime_builtins_only ... ok
  test discord::tests::command_set_stays_within_discords_limit ... ok
  test discord::tests::skills_cannot_take_a_builtin_command_name ... ok
  test discord::tests::builtin_invocation_becomes_the_typed_command ... ok
  test discord::tests::builtin_command_message_targets_the_invoking_conversation ... ok
  test discord::tests::reactions_skip_messages_that_came_from_an_interaction ... ok
  test discord::tests::scope_switch_reaps_our_builtins_but_spares_foreign_ones ... ok
  test result: ok. 322 passed; 0 failed

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib every_discord_builtin
  test orchestrator::tests::every_discord_builtin_slash_command_is_a_runtime_command ... ok

  $ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n
  test result: ok. 50 passed; 0 failed

  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.

  $ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/channels/discord.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
  ```

  Three existing tests were updated because the desired command set grew, not because behavior they pin changed:
  - `registration_body_contains_ask_plus_skill_commands`: the count now includes the built-ins, and it also asserts that built-ins do not match the skill ownership shape.
  - `reconcile_skips_unchanged_and_spares_foreign_commands`: the steady-state listing now includes every desired command.
  - `guild_scope_registers_to_the_guild_endpoint`: the POST count is now the registered set size.

  Built-ins are appended after skill commands so positional skill tests are unchanged.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On a live bot with global scope and `slash_commands = true`, READY registered the seven built-ins alongside `/ask` and the existing skill commands. Discord rate-limited part of that first, larger global registration. The existing cooldown path then registered the remaining commands on the next READY. I have not yet invoked a built-in from Discord's picker on the live bot. Routing, the acknowledgement and reaction skipping are covered by the unit tests above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (Discord's own command picker; described above).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** This commit applied on the `v0.9.0` release together with #12762, #12763 and #12770, built for aarch64 Linux and run on an Android device in an Ubuntu chroot. Interface: `channel` = `discord`. Evidence: registration events in `runtime-trace.jsonl`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace suite and `--features ci-all` clippy are left to CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. Built-in invocations pass the same `interaction_gate` (peer, guild and channel allowlists with the thread-parent fallback) as `/ask` before anything is forwarded. The interaction token is used only for the immediate ephemeral acknowledgement and never enters `reply_target`, logs or session keys.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No (only the `slash_commands` field description, which previously still called it a single-`/ask` prototype)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; or set `slash_commands = false` (disabling does not deregister existing global commands, as before).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `channels.discord.<alias>.slash_commands`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `discord command acknowledgement failed` WARN events; built-in commands missing from the `/` menu after READY (reconcile errors are logged as before).

prs.title: feat(tools): add feature-flagged macOS computer_use tool and OpenRouter tool-result image delivery
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions) - **What changed and why:** - Adds an opt-in, feature-flagged built-in `computer_use` tool (`tool-computer-use`, default off in Cargo features and default closed in config under `[risk_profiles..computer_use]`) so agents can observe and control a local desktop GUI without external third-party binaries. - Introduces a platform-agnostic `ComputerUseBackend` trait, pure image-to-logical coordinate scaling (`scale.rs`), key-chord parser (`keys.rs`), and a macOS prototype backend (`macos.rs`) using CoreGraphics/ApplicationServices FFI + `/usr/sbin/screencapture`, with an `UnsupportedBackend` stub on non-macOS targets until Linux/X11 and `sandbox_computer_use` backends are added. - Supports `screenshot`, `click`, `drag`, `move`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, and `wait`, with auto-downscaled image coordinate mapping (Retina-safe), `allow_secondary_displays = false` default policy, `ReadOnly` observation-only enforcement (`screenshot`/`wait` allowed, input actions blocked), agent-workspace screenshot persistence (never polluting ACP/Code session cwds), serial batch execution in `should_execute_tools_in_parallel`, `RateLimitedTool` wrapping, and full Fluent localization (`tools.ftl`). - Fixes `OpenRouterModelProvider` (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openrouter.rs`) to honor `tool_result_image_policy` (default `Relocate`, matching `compatible.rs`) and deliver declared `MarkerKind::Image` tool-result attachments so OpenRouter vision models can inspect tool-generated screenshots instead of falling back to `file_read`. - **Scope boundary:** - macOS prototype only; Linux/X11 (`x11.rs`), Windows, `sandbox_computer_use`, and Phase B window/app/clipboard helpers (`list_windows`, `focus_window`, `open_app`, `clipboard_*`) are intentionally deferred to follow-up PRs. - Leaves `[browser.computer_use]` sidecar client behavior untouched. - Does not modify other Chat Completions providers (`azure_openai`, `openai`, `copilot`) or OpenAI Responses (#12104). - **ADR-016 note:** Bounded wiring in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/{Cargo.toml,locales/en/tools.ftl,src/tools/mod.rs,src/agent/tool_execution.rs}` will require a Core Team-approved exception row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` before marking ready for merge. - **Blast radius:** - `zeroclaw-config`: new `tool-computer-use` feature, `OptInTool::ComputerUse`, `ComputerUseToolConfig` nested on `RiskProfileConfig`, and risk-profile validation / `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` warnings. - `zeroclaw-tools`: new `computer_use` module (gated behind `tool-computer-use` + optional PNG-only `image` dependency), attribution, inventory entry, and `locales/en/tools.ftl`. - `zeroclaw-runtime`: opt-in tool registration under `risk_profile.computer_use.enabled`, serial batch guard for `computer_use` in `should_execute_tools_in_parallel`, and canonical `locales/en/tools.ftl`. - `zeroclaw-providers`: `OpenRouterModelProvider` tool-result image attachment delivery via `tool_result_image_policy`. - Packaging/installer generated feature lists (`Cargo.toml`, `Containerfile`, `Dockerfile*`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`, `dist/aur/PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix`, `setup.bat`) regenerated via `cargo generate installers`. - **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12774, Related #12104 ### What this does, simply Previously, ZeroClaw agents had no built-in way to interact with native desktop applications without installing external sidecars or CLI tools, and OpenRouter vision models could not see images attached by native tools (like screenshots) because OpenRouter's message converter dropped tool-result `attachments`. This PR adds a feature-flagged, default-disabled `computer_use` tool with a macOS prototype backend that captures downscaled screenshots directly into the agent's workspace and translates pixel clicks, drags, scrolls, typing, and keyboard shortcuts back to macOS logical points. It defaults closed per risk profile (`enabled = false`, `allow_secondary_displays = false`) and requires explicit opt-in. It also fixes OpenRouter to forward declared tool-result image attachments so vision models actually receive the screenshots. Non-macOS builds compile cleanly with a stub backend that reports macOS-only support until Linux/X11 and sandboxed backends land. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` / `tui` (ZeroCode / `zeroclaw agent`) on macOS with Screen Recording + Accessibility permissions granted to the host terminal. - **Setup / preconditions:** 1. Build on macOS with `--features tool-computer-use`. 2. Grant Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions to the terminal app in *System Settings → Privacy & Security*. 3. Enable `computer_use` on a risk profile assigned to a vision-capable agent (e.g. OpenRouter or Anthropic): ```toml [risk_profiles.desktop.computer_use] enabled = true # allow_secondary_displays = false # default ``` - **Steps to run:** ```sh # Unit + mock suite cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use computer_use # Live macOS screenshot smoke test (requires Screen Recording permission) cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use macos_live_screenshot_smoke -- --ignored --nocapture # Build and run an interactive macOS agent session cargo build --features tool-computer-use ``` Then ask the agent to take a screenshot and perform a GUI task (e.g. click, drag, and type in a macOS drawing app or text editor). - **Expected on this branch (after):** - `macos_live_screenshot_smoke` passes and returns a valid PNG. - The agent sees the downscaled screenshot directly on OpenRouter/Anthropic without attempting `file_read` on the PNG. - Coordinates map accurately on Retina displays; clicks, drags, chords, and ASCII typing work in both native AppKit and custom-drawn/Skia apps; screenshots are stored under `/computer_use/` rather than the session cwd. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** - No built-in `computer_use` tool exists, and OpenRouter drops declared tool-result image attachments from `role = "tool"` messages, causing vision models to fail trying `file_read` on binary PNG files. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required PR CI workflows (`fmt`, `clippy`, workspace tests, `xtask` installer/feature-matrix checks, docs inventory drift) will run on this PR head across default and `ci-all` feature sets. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Linux CI cannot link macOS `CoreGraphics` / `ApplicationServices` frameworks or run live desktop capture/input against macOS TCC permissions; covered locally on a real Mac (`macos_live_screenshot_smoke` + live interactive VectorCraft/Ghostty testing) and via cross-platform unit tests for `macos.rs` keycodes, capture args, display ordering, text segmentation, and drag interpolation. - **Commands run and tail output:** ```text $ cargo fmt --all -- --check fmt: OK $ cargo generate installers --check ok: install-sh in sync ... ok: tools-en-ftl in sync ... ok: zerocode-themes in sync (22/22 in sync) $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime \ --features zeroclaw-runtime/tool-computer-use --all-targets -- -D warnings clippy+feature: OK $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime \ --all-targets -- -D warnings clippy-default: OK $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --features tool-computer-use computer_use test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config computer_use test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers openrouter test result: ok. 87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use computer_use test result: ok. 36 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use inventory test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored (+ docs_tier_tables_match_the_inventory: ok; outside_inventory_entries_are_current: ok) $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --features tool-computer-use computer_use test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --features tool-computer-use maximal test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime maximal test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored $ cargo test -p xtask --lib generate::spec test result: ok. 29 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored ``` - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** - Ran `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use computer_use` (33 passed, 1 ignored) and `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --features tool-computer-use macos_live_screenshot_smoke -- --ignored --nocapture` (1 passed) on real macOS hardware. - Verified live interactive agent execution on macOS via OpenRouter: Retina coordinate scaling (`1512x982` logical → `1280x831` screenshot), screenshot image attachment delivery on OpenRouter, click + drag + keyboard chords + ASCII typing in VectorCraft (custom-drawn Skia UI) and Ghostty. - Not verified: multi-monitor secondary-display live capture on physical macOS hardware (covered by unit tests with negative-origin displays). - **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `03d8da12e6` on macOS desktop (`VectorCraft` / `Ghostty` via OpenRouter vision agent) - **Screenshots:** - **Action or changed state and observed result:** - Agent captured macOS desktop screenshots, received them directly as OpenRouter image attachments, clicked tools/dialogs, typed numeric dimensions via hardware ANSI keycodes, and performed click-and-drag drawing in VectorCraft. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally on the Linux dev host because macOS FFI tests require macOS (verified separately on macOS hardware) and full workspace suites are covered by PR CI. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes` - New external network calls? `No` - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No` - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No` - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes` - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: - **Desktop GUI capture & synthetic input capability:** `computer_use` can capture displays and inject mouse/keyboard events into foreground applications. Mitigated by double opt-in (excluded from default Cargo features, `[risk_profiles..computer_use].enabled = false` default), primary-display-only default (`allow_secondary_displays = false`), `AutonomyLevel::ReadOnly` blocking all mutating actions (`click`, `drag`, `move`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`), `RateLimitedTool` wrapping, macOS TCC Screen Recording + Accessibility preflight checks, atomic screenshot writes confined to `/computer_use/` (never touching session cwd/git repos), and omitting typed text from tool output (`chars` count only). - **Relocated tool-result images on OpenRouter:** Moving tool-result images into a following `role = "user"` message could blur trust boundaries if unframed. Mitigated identically to `compatible.rs` by reading only declared `MarkerKind::Image` attachments (never scanning body text), framing each relocated image with `[external tool output - image from tool result N]`, and supporting `tool_result_image_policy = "omit"`. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config / env / CLI surface changed? `Yes` - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No` - If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: - Additive only; existing configs load unchanged with `computer_use` disabled by default. To enable `computer_use`, build with `--features tool-computer-use` (included in `tools-compat` / `dist` / `ci-all`) and set `[risk_profiles..computer_use] enabled = true`. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert ` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** Disable at runtime without rebuilding via `[risk_profiles..computer_use] enabled = false` (or `allow_secondary_displays = false`); disable at build time by omitting `tool-computer-use`; disable OpenRouter tool-result image delivery via `tool_result_image_policy = "omit"`. - **Observable failure symptoms:** Tool calls returning `TOOL_COMPILED_OUT` warnings when compiled out, `BackendError::PermissionDenied` for missing macOS Accessibility/Screen Recording TCC grants, or OpenRouter HTTP 400 errors on relocated tool-result image turns.

prs.title: feat(webchat): wire ACP startup cutover and switch dashboard transport to /acp
prs.body:
## Summary

This final layer lets operators switch the dashboard from `/ws/chat` to ACP at gateway startup. With `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover = true`, the gateway imports readable legacy `gw_*` conversations, advertises ACP in the served HTML, and returns HTTP 410 from `/ws/chat`. With the flag off, the dashboard uses `/ws/chat`.

- **Base branch** `master`, stacked on `feat/acp-gateway-auth-and-reconnect`
- **What changed and why**
  - The conversation picker and session API keep the existing WebChat `gw_` key format. History and rename accept both the full key and bare session ID.
  - The ACP adapter resumes a saved chat and reattaches to an active turn after reload. Replayed completions refresh the saved transcript while keeping displayed tool cards and thinking. The saved answer appears once. Scoped Clear waits for ACP to close the active conversation before enabling a new one. Switching conversations keeps the composer disabled until the new socket is ready. When ACP refuses to resume a tombstoned session with `FORBIDDEN`, the adapter closes the socket and stops automatic reconnects.
  - Operator WebChat reads and writes use ACP during cutover. Other conversations retain their legacy REST access and agent lifecycle handling.
  - Delete cancels the running turn, removes the old operator WebChat copy, and clears the ACP transcript. Tool-only assistant steps with no text are omitted from REST history.
  - An unreadable legacy transcript reserves its session ID in the import ledger. Resume refuses the session while the import is pending. Repairing the file and restarting the gateway restores its history under the original ID. Readable transcripts still import at startup.
- **Scope boundary** The startup switch defaults to `false`. Removing `/ws/chat` and the voice route split are follow-up work.
- **Blast radius** `zeroclaw-config`, gateway startup, ACP relay and dashboard session routes, the infra session store, the channels ACP back-channel, and the web dashboard. ACP `session/request_permission` carries `_meta.zeroclaw.expiresAtUnixMs` for IDE clients as well.
- **Linked issue** Depends on #12653

### What this does, simply

Operators can bring their existing dashboard conversations over to ACP, reopen them from the picker, and continue a reply across a browser reload. The gateway switch lets operators choose when to move.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface exercised** `surface: web`.
- **Setup** Enable cutover and start a gateway with an agent and an existing `gw_*` session.
- **Steps** Open the dashboard, select the imported conversation, verify its history, send a prompt, and reload before the reply completes.
- **Expected on this branch** The replacement socket reattaches and the browser displays the completed reply once.
- **Prior behavior on `master`** WebChat connected to `/ws/chat` and kept its own transcript and transport.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on** `CI Required Gate` covers workspace lint, build and tests. Focused checks below exercise the specific cutover changes.
- **Commands run and results**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` exited 0.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-infra --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` finished successfully.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib acp_ws_cutover_restores_legacy_dashboard_session` (1 passed) checks the live HTTP and WebSocket routes, picker response fields, both REST key forms, continued channel access, and removal of the legacy transcript after Delete.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib legacy_gateway_import` (6 passed) verifies import, retry and preserved deletion. `operator_webchat_routes_ignore_other_sessions_and_empty_assistant_steps` also passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib acp_channel::tests --features channel-acp-server` (33 passed) checks the approval deadline using the clock independently of the production helper.
  - `npm run build`, `npm run test:acp` (6 passed, including a live socket reconnect that receives the tombstone refusal and makes no replacement session or further connection attempt) and the session lifecycle test (65 passed).
- **Import recovery at `7eb780d41`** The JSONL regression imported a readable chat alongside a corrupt transcript, reopened the ACP store, verified the pending ID could neither resume nor be claimed by a new session, and recovered its history under the same ID after repair. Six import tests and six ACP web tests passed. Scoped infra Clippy passed with warnings denied.
- **Scoped Clear and replay follow-up at `aff5fcaa9`** The ACP server tests passed for cancellation of a parked turn before close returns and for reporting a committed transcript on successful completion. The dashboard build, 103 session lifecycle tests and six ACP socket tests passed. The reload regression covers history arriving with and without the completed answer, including identical answers in separate turns.
- **Replay display follow-up at `98ce3968f`** Both reload tests keep the earlier thinking, the replayed thinking, and the completed tool card when the first history fetch includes or misses the current reply. Identical replies in separate turns each appear once. The dashboard build, 103 lifecycle tests, and six ACP tests passed.
- **Beyond CI** With cutover enabled, Chromium opened an imported JSONL conversation through the picker and rendered its saved answer. It streamed a new reply. During another streamed turn, it reloaded the page, opened a new `/acp` socket, received an active-turn reattach acknowledgment, and rendered the completed reply once. A corrupt JSONL transcript alongside the readable ones was logged and the gateway still started.
- **Known coverage gap** The browser run used a loopback gateway with a scripted streaming provider and pairing disabled. The pairing and OIDC browser matrix remains for staging.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact final-interface output from Chromium at `b41555c40`.
- **Action and observed output** Selected “Imported conversation smoke” and saw “Imported smoke answer.” Reloaded during the second streamed turn and saw one additional “Streamed reply complete,” with an active-turn reattach acknowledgment on the new socket.
- **Commands intentionally skipped** Full workspace tests are covered by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets, tokens, or credential handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced or changed? No.

The session routes retain operator authentication and enforce owner and surface checks on ACP-backed operations.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with cutover opt-in.
- Config, environment, or CLI surface changed? Yes, `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`.
- Rust or toolchain floor changed? No.
- To upgrade, stop the old gateway, enable `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`, and restart. The ACP database is `sessions/acp-sessions.db`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback** Set `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover = false` and restart to return to `/ws/chat`.
- **Feature flag** `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`, default `false`.
- Each transport writes to its own store. Re-enabling cutover skips previously imported keys, so turns written during rollback stay in the legacy store. Back up both stores if those turns must be retained.
- **Observable symptoms** The disabled legacy socket returns HTTP 410 during cutover. The gateway logs unreadable legacy transcripts and fails startup if the configured legacy store is unavailable.

prs.title: fix(web): render context meter cells without font fallback
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** `master` - **What changed and why:** The web chat context meter drew `█` and `░` as text. JetBrains Mono is loaded from Google Fonts, whose subsets omit U+2588/U+2591, so Chrome fell back to system fonts. On Windows the two fallbacks can differ in height, which made empty cells taller than filled ones. The meter now renders 16 fixed-height CSS cells. - **Scope boundary:** Only the web chat meter. Token accounting, `context_usage` frames, RPC, zerocode TUI/CLI, and the Dashboard cost bars are unchanged. - **Blast radius:** The change is local to `web/src/lib/contextBar.ts` and `web/src/pages/AgentChat.tsx`, plus their unit and DOM tests. No shared runtime or accounting code is touched. - **Linked issue(s):** Fixes [\[Bug\]: Web context meter cells render at different heights on Windows Chrome #12743](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12743). ### What this does, simply Before this change, the meter's blocks were text characters. The dashboard font does not contain those characters, so the browser substituted fonts installed on the machine, and on Windows the shaded substitute was taller than the filled one. The meter is now drawn with plain CSS boxes at a fixed height. The token label, percentage, fill count, and trim marker behave as before. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes - **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web` - **Setup / preconditions:** An agent chat with some context usage, opened in Chrome on Windows. - **Steps to run:** Send a message and wait for the `done` frame so the meter shows partial usage. Compare the cells next to the context label. Switch to a session whose `max_context_tokens` is below the model window to see the trim marker, then to one with trimming disabled to see it disappear. - **Expected on this branch (after):** All 16 cells have the same height. The trim marker is a vertical divider and is absent when trimming is disabled. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The `░` cells are taller than the `█` cells. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet. This head has not run required CI. - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI runs on Linux and has no browser rendering step, so the Windows font fallback is not covered. - **Commands run and tail output:** ``` npx tsc -b ``` ``` (no output) ``` ``` npm run test:contexts ``` ``` ℹ tests 50 ℹ pass 50 ℹ fail 0 ``` - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The context tests cover the token count, brackets, percentage, trim marker, and the hidden state when the budget is disabled or unknown. I did not exercise the Windows rendering in a browser. - **Visual interface evidence:** None. No Windows Chrome is available here; the reviewer steps above are the manual check. - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `a2c5d7961`, `surface: web`, agent chat context meter. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Not attached. - **Action or changed state and observed result:** The context tests mount the real chat page and check the meter text and trim marker across `done`, `history_trimmed`, and session reset frames. They do not cover font substitution. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `npm test` and `npm run build` were not run; `tsc -b` and the focused context tests cover this change. Browser smoke was skipped because no Windows browser is available. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No - New external network calls? No - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No - If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? Yes - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No - If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 2f3bcab` - **Feature flags or config toggles:** None - **Observable failure symptoms:** The meter loses its cells, or the filled width no longer matches the percentage in the label. Both are visible in the agent chat.

prs.title: feat(config): control OpenRouter balance reporting in web settings
prs.body:
## Summary





- **Labels:** docs, dependencies, channel, config, gateway, provider, channel:core, channel:telegram, risk:medium, web, size:XL, channel:acp





Base branch: `master`.





Add explicit per-alias opt-in for OpenRouter balance reporting and fixed-mask editing of saved secrets. Depends on #11845.





### What this does, simply





Balance reporting defaults off. Disabling it preserves credentials. Saved secrets show a constant mask; replacement starts with an empty draft.





<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at f2e86cd77. Retained the new scoped-chat authorization tests and the balance/secret-field tests. Canonical API generation, npm run test:permissions, npm run test:auth, and the production build passed in a dedicated validation checkout. The dependency on #11845 remains.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)





### How you can test (when useful)





Run the hosted Web Permission Tests and gateway/config regressions, then exercise opt-in, save/cancel and secret replacement in the authenticated dashboard.





### Earlier validation (historical)





Current-head CI Required Gate passes at 72b345ba975a64316d9c77da4438449abf803467, including the hosted Web Permission Tests. This refresh integrates master and resolves the package.json conflict by retaining both the SecretField regression and the new authentication suite. Local navigation/secret-field tests passed; the first local authentication-suite run lacked generated API descriptions, so it is not cited as passing evidence. Hosted current-head checks supply the integrated coverage.





Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.





## Security & Privacy Impact (required)





No new permissions or network destinations in this refresh. The feature adds authenticated balance reporting through the configured provider/proxy; provider credentials remain server-side. Stored secret values and lengths are not returned to the browser.





- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: No


- New external network calls: Yes — inherited authenticated OpenRouter balance requests from #11845; configured proxy routing remains enforced.


- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes — fixed-mask replacement editing preserves saved secret values until an explicit replacement.


- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.


- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No





## Compatibility (required)





Backward compatible. The feature adds the documented opt-in setting, default false. No toolchain-floor change. Merge #11845 first, then reconcile the stacked branch against master.





## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)





Revert the feature commits. Reporting can be disabled through its opt-in setting while preserving saved credentials. Verify that the dashboard hides unavailable balances and stored secrets remain masked.





## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)





None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.



## Review follow-up - 2026-11-09



Refreshed onto current master and resolved web/package.json while retaining both SecretField navigation coverage and all current authentication tests, including CommandPalette access. npm ci and test:navigation passed. The local full test:auth run stopped at a missing generated api-descriptions module in the recovered checkout after its earlier auth suites passed; this is not reported as a complete auth pass. Fresh CI must regenerate the canonical API and run the entire suite on this head. #11845 remains the landing prerequisite. Metadata encoding and label snapshot were corrected.




SQLite follow-up: the workspace-only bridge from #12322 was removed from this independent PR after review identified the crates.io consumer limitation. Registry dependency compatibility is preserved. The shared security advisory remains tracked in #12320; #12322 is not a merge prerequisite for this PR.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

### OpenRouter merge sequence

This branch includes the current #11845 head and adds the settings, explicit per-alias opt-in and account label. Merge #11845 first. After a squash merge, re-stack this follow-up on the resulting master and review only its incremental diff. The upstream HTTP client change #12323 is already merged.

### Preserved test evidence

- [Settings, desktop](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/961792a571b522301c3bdcfbd4b1da8e5dd86700/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings-desktop.png)
- [Settings, mobile](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/961792a571b522301c3bdcfbd4b1da8e5dd86700/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings-mobile.png)
- [Account label, desktop](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/961792a571b522301c3bdcfbd4b1da8e5dd86700/.pr-evidence/openrouter-account-desktop.png)
- [Account label, mobile](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/961792a571b522301c3bdcfbd4b1da8e5dd86700/.pr-evidence/openrouter-account-mobile.png)
- [Settings test notes](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/961792a571b522301c3bdcfbd4b1da8e5dd86700/.pr-evidence/openrouter-settings.md)
- [Balance card, desktop](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/fd85bbffc5d5c8722df678c29c7c9bf6bc18a690/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-desktop.png)
- [Balance card, mobile](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/fd85bbffc5d5c8722df678c29c7c9bf6bc18a690/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance-mobile.png)
- [Balance card test notes](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/blob/fd85bbffc5d5c8722df678c29c7c9bf6bc18a690/.pr-evidence/pr-11231-openrouter-balance.md)
