prs.title: feat(browser): scope username/password and TOTP access independently
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #12517, #12438 and the bounded runtime placement record #12266. RFC #12422 remains the scope decision owner.
- **What changed and why:** add independent browser grants to username/password and TOTP catalog records, an operator Permissions panel, and the `submit_credential` action on the existing agent-browser backend. The agent passes an alias; resolved values travel on child stdin and only a fixed localized result returns to the model.
- **Scope boundary:** this PR is draft. The action is implemented and becomes usable when an operator grants an origin. It does not yet isolate browser sessions by task or suppress generic snapshots, screenshots and evaluation on credential-bearing pages. It is not ready for upstream deployment until these acceptance gaps and the RFC/dependencies are settled.
- **Blast radius:** grant mutation API, encrypted catalog revisions, browser release, form selectors, HTTP Basic admission, and credential-use audit metadata. Underlying SSH/HTTP layers remain reviewed in their own PRs.

### Behavior and review repairs

- Match the saved encrypted record before and after an awaited lookup. Replacement, revocation and deletion refuse release.
- Require `expected_revision` for every permission mutation, including legacy `http_allowed` and `browser.origin` forms. Stale or missing revisions return 409.
- Clear browser and HTTP grants when replacement changes the suggested service. Rotation for the same service preserves them.
- A named OTP field must match `autocomplete="one-time-code"` or `name="otp"`; segmented controls must each accept one character. Ordinary text/search selectors cannot receive a code.
- Reject HTTP Basic grants for colon-bearing usernames; the HTTP consumer also refuses them before resolving a password.
- Log one browser-use result with validated alias, HTTPS origin, stage, refusal phase and bounded status. Never log values, seeds, selectors, scripts or raw backend errors.
- Run the form-script boundary tests in CI and include the design contract in the book.

An origin grant also authorizes later password-confirmation prompts on that origin, including sensitive actions. A submission acknowledgement is not proof of authentication. An unconfirmed result can follow a page-handled submission: inspect page state before retrying.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Use a disposable HTTPS login and synthetic records. Grant password and TOTP independently; exercise staged forms, a same-origin iframe and segmented OTP. Try an ordinary text selector, another origin/window, multiple submitters and fields from different forms. Pause an external lookup, then rotate, revoke or delete its record. From two operator tabs, change grants and submit the stale tab. Change the suggested service and confirm both grant lists clear.

### How I tested

- `node --test crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/browser_credential_form.test.mjs`: **19 passed, 0 failed** on the repaired source.
- Added Rust regressions for lookup replacement/revocation/deletion, early denial, service-change grant clearing, legacy revision enforcement and colon-bearing Basic usernames. [Linux Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926130632), Lint and Security passed on **7a2acc241c**. The main test log records PASS for service replacement, stale-tab, colon-username and shared sandbox regressions. The browser lookup regression runs in [Test (opt-in tools)](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926130637), which passed and records its PASS. [Repository Structure](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45824802280/job/139926129896) passed with the Node script tests.
- Earlier reviewer and production results apply only to the revisions named in their comments.
- **Known coverage gaps:** managed session isolation and observation suppression, final-interface Permissions-panel screenshot on this head, and independent browser acceptance against disposable HTTPS fixtures remain open. The script fixture is not real-browser acceptance evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** pending, which is one reason this stays draft.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities/file scope? **Yes:** independent browser origin grants, denied by default, authorized only by the config operator.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the authorized browser submits to the granted HTTPS origin; vault resolution uses the existing provider adapter.
- Secrets handling changed? **Yes:** values are resolved just in time, revalidated and sent on stdin; the current browser's session/observation limitations above remain a release blocker.
- PII/real identities in the diff? **No.** Tests use synthetic identities and values.
- Prompt-injection/untrusted input changed? **Yes:** page content and model selectors are untrusted. Origin, form, frame, field and current-record checks bound release. They do not prevent a same-origin page script from observing its own form values.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for unversioned permission writes:** older clients must GET the catalog and include its `permission_revision` as `expected_revision` on every edit. Refresh the dashboard bundle after upgrade.
- Config/env/CLI surface changed? **Yes:** additive browser grants and action parameters; no grant is inferred from an alias or page prompt.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast path:** revoke browser grants, stop affected tasks and close the browser session; deploy the previous integrated binary with a protected compatible state backup.
- **Toggle:** empty browser-grant lists disable release. There is no claim of task-isolated browser profiles in this implementation.
- **Symptoms:** `browser_credential_use` reports `refused_or_unconfirmed` with a bounded phase; stale editors get 409. Do not automatically retry a page-handled submission.

## Documentation

The browser consumer design page is linked from the book. Environment-specific probes have been removed from that contract; historical evidence stays in the PR discussion. English Markdown is canonical; generated translations are omitted from this maintenance change.

prs.title: fix(channels): keep a tool-result envelope intact when a follow-up turn follows it
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `normalize_cached_channel_turns()` no longer merges a `user` turn into a preceding `role=tool` turn. Tool content is a structured result envelope, so the merge produced invalid JSON; the OpenAI-compatible adapter then emitted `role=tool` without `tool_call_id`, and strict providers rejected the entire request (DeepSeek: `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`). Because the damaged pair is replayed from the persisted transcript, every later message in that conversation failed the same way.
  - The OpenAI-compatible adapter now recovers the id from the leading JSON value of a tool-result content string (tolerating trailing bytes) and falls back to the most recent assistant tool call, so one damaged envelope can no longer take down a whole request.
  - Two regression tests: `tool -> user` normalization keeps the envelope intact and keeps the user turn; the id recovery handles trailing content.
- **Scope boundary:** does not change the alternation merging added by #1057 for consecutive `user` / `assistant` turns, does not rewrite or drop the follow-up user turn, and does not touch the tool loop, persistence, or provider retry policy.
- **Blast radius:** channel cached-turn assembly (shared by all messaging channels) and OpenAI-compatible request serialization. ACP, ZeroCode, gateway sessions, and non-compatible provider adapters are untouched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12187

### What this does, simply

A channel keeps the recent turns of a conversation and replays them to the model. When a turn is interrupted, or hits the tool-iteration cap, the stored conversation can end up as `assistant asked for a tool -> tool result -> the user's message again`. The code that restores strict user/assistant alternation handled that by appending the later turn to the previous message. When the previous message was a tool result, prose was appended to a JSON object, and a strict provider answered `missing field 'tool_call_id'` — failing that message and every message after it in the same conversation, which looks like a credential or model problem to the operator.

This PR keeps the follow-up turn as its own message (providers accept `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user` directly), and adds a small safety net in the request builder: even if some other path hands over a damaged tool result, the id the result belongs to is read from the beginning of the object and included on the wire. No user or assistant text is dropped.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel`
- **Setup / preconditions:** any channel that keeps tool turns in its cached history (`keep_tool_context_turns`, default) plus a conversation whose stored history contains `assistant(tool_calls) -> tool -> user`. A strict OpenAI-compatible provider makes the failure loud; this was reproduced against DeepSeek's official API (`https://api.deepseek.com`, model `deepseek-flash`).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On `master`: obtain a conversation whose stored turns end with a tool result followed directly by the user's request (a tool-capped turn does this), then send a follow-up message.
  2. On this branch: replay the same conversation data and send the same follow-up message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the request carries the tool message with its `tool_call_id` intact and the follow-up user message as a separate turn; the provider answers 200.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the tool message content is `<envelope>\n\n<user text>`, the adapter emits `role=tool` with no `tool_call_id`, and the provider answers `422 ... missing field 'tool_call_id'`; every later message in that conversation fails identically.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels normalize_cached_channel_turns
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers recover_leading_tool_call_id
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets
```

Tail of the runs that produced this branch:

```text
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_passes_through_tool_messages ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_merges_consecutive_assistant_turns ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_merges_consecutive_user_turns ... ok
test orchestrator::tests::normalize_cached_channel_turns_keeps_tool_envelope_when_user_follows_tool ... ok
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 2014 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

test compatible::tests::recover_leading_tool_call_id_tolerates_trailing_turn ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1983 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the workspace `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` lanes cover both crates; both regression tests are unit-level and run in the normal test job.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none specific to this diff. The end-to-end replay below adds provider-behavior coverage that unit tests cannot express.
- **Commands run and tail output:** shown above; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** With a local `webhook` channel instance (the same orchestrator path; no chat platform involved) against DeepSeek's official API:
  - Before: one request logged, in causal order, the merge into the tool turn (target 82 chars, incoming 54 chars), the envelope going invalid (82 -> 138 chars, exactly the appended `\n\n` plus the user turn), `role=tool` serialized without `tool_call_id`, and then `422 messages[N]: missing field 'tool_call_id'`.
  - After: the same stored transcript (still containing `tool -> user`) returned 200; the tool message kept its envelope and `tool_call_id`, the user turn arrived as its own message, and the turn completed with real tool calls.
  - Not verified: other channel transports and non-OpenAI-compatible adapters were not exercised individually (they share the same normalization function).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible layout, styling, or presentation state changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head, `channel` path, evidence = the unit tests above plus the local replay logs (redacted).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** replay of a stored transcript with `tool -> user` adjacency; before = 422 on every message, after = 200.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` was not completed locally because this machine's toolchain (rustc 1.99.1) flags pre-existing lints outside this diff (`needless_borrows_for_generic_args` in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, a deprecated API in `zeroclaw-runtime`); with those allowed, the two affected crates report no warning attributable to this change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No` — the recovery path only reads an id the runtime itself wrote into the tool-result envelope; it adds no new text to the request and does not widen what the model can see)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes` — existing transcripts still load; the only behavior change is that a follow-up turn is delivered as its own message instead of being concatenated into a tool result)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Labelled `risk:medium`; rollback is `git revert c248be44d a6638545e e4a30049f` (this PR's three commits, newest first).

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded RPC denial reason exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the stable RPC denial reasons and reason-keyed denial records in #11289, the feature PR for #11005. The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #11289 (`src/rpc/auth.rs:97`, 2026-10-12), which found that no recorded exception covers RPC denial reporting.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11289 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `b5ca9dbb203676232e190026ce8b914c07734e90` against master `dfe8ab35bd682e3510fe81856f27c0926742cd25` (three files: `src/rpc/auth.rs`, `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`): the `RpcDenialReason` identifier type with `as_str`, its private `code` and `message_key` mappings and `From<DenyReason>`; on the existing `AuthDenied`, the private `reason` field and `reason()` accessor, the private `new`, `with_message` and `with_values` builders, the `quoted` helper, the 24 named `pub(crate)` constructors that replace `auth_required` and `forbidden` (with `from_deny_reason` rebuilt on the private `with_message` and the five other `auth.rs` functions named in the row, including the shared `authenticate_checked` implementation, building their denials through them), and `audit_attrs`, which gives the existing `RPC authorization denied` record its `method`, `reason`, `denial_message`, `code`, `principal_id` and `auth_provider` attributes; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `audit_denial` emitting those attributes, `RpcDispatcher::refuse`, the `authorize` gate and the 24 other refusal functions named in the row building their denials through the constructors or refusing through `refuse`, the gate attributing a denial after a failed revalidation to the principal whose binding it drops, the `steering_admission` closure's record changes (its session-ownership, revoked transport-owner and remote local-capability refusals recorded under their own reasons, the latter with that reason's `-32003` on the record while the steer is still answered `-32012`; the refusals its binding checks record themselves recorded once rather than twice, so a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved leaves no denial record), the selectors' and cron write rechecks' no-binding refusals now recorded, the retired `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL` literal, the fourteen added `rpc-auth-*` keys and their translator comment (including `rpc-auth-session-transport-ownership-changed`; thirteen replacing an inline literal, `rpc-auth-session-local-capabilities` feeding only the record), and reuse of the existing `sop-rpc-principal-ceiling-required` and `rpc-cron-agent-principal-required` keys, and focused tests. `RpcDenialReason`, `as_str` and `reason()` are `pub`; no other crate consumes them. `DenyReason`, the JSON-RPC error codes and the grants stay in `zeroclaw-api`, and the record sink in `zeroclaw-log`, so they need no runtime permission; the root `AGENTS.md` bullet and the `docs/book` section that #11289 adds are outside the holding crate. It excludes any identifier in a client response, recording a refused `initialize` handshake or the other refusals answered without an `AuthDenied`, and any new RPC method, grant source, config key, record kind, record sink, retained runtime state or non-English locale.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The prior enumeration was approved by @Audacity88 on 2026-10-29; its permalink remains in the row. This amendment updates the SOP constructor/helper, adds the cron-principal and revoked transport-owner constructors, and replaces the removed SOP Fluent key with the transport-owner key. @JordanTheJet approved this amended enumeration on 2026-11-09 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12062#pullrequestreview-5821600639); that approval is now recorded in the Approved-by cell. The earlier @Audacity88 decision covers only the prior enumeration. On November 21, @Audacity88 approved the in-process credential refusal, its stable reason and its constructor. It reuses the existing locale key and keeps the refused initialize handshake outside denial recording. [Core decision](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12062#issuecomment-7059353151)
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11005 and #11289 (head `b5ca9dbb203676232e190026ce8b914c07734e90` against master `dfe8ab35bd682e3510fe81856f27c0926742cd25`). #11289 lands after #11326, whose global-stream wording the row's key note reflects. Precedent: #11701, #12058, #11963, and the #11286 row already in the table, which covers `src/rpc/auth.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl` but is limited to roster-bound pairing tokens.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #11289 gives every RPC authorization refusal built through `AuthDenied` a stable identifier such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, writes that identifier into the denial record the daemon already emits (the refusal text moves to its own `denial_message` attribute), moves the refusals' inline English literals into the Fluent catalogue (the gate's grant refusal and the global-stream, session-environment, upload-ownership and revoked transport-owner refusals as well as the selectors'; SOP and cron-principal refusals reuse their existing Fluent keys), and keeps the principal and provider on the record when a policy change drops a connection's binding. Clients receive the same codes and English text as before (the global-stream refusal takes the wording #11326 gives it), and never the identifier. The set of recorded refusals changes slightly: the selectors' and cron write rechecks' no-binding refusals are now recorded, a steer refused by its agent, workspace or environment check is recorded once rather than twice, and a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved is no longer recorded. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the RPC authorization-gate and inbound-authentication owners in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

Why placement is right: every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. On master, `AuthDenied`, with its `auth_required`, `forbidden` and `from_deny_reason` constructors, sits in `src/rpc/auth.rs` next to `RpcInboundAuth`, `AcceptedAuthState` and `AuthorityLease`; `RpcDispatcher::authorize`, `audit_denial` (which already writes the `RPC authorization denied` record, with the message as its `reason`), `current_authority`, the selectors and `still_authorized` sit in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`; and the handshake denials already resolve `rpc-auth-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The reason is set by the code that decides to refuse, so it lives where that decision is made, and it reaches only the log record: `rpc_err(denied.code, denied.message)` still sends the client the code and text alone, so the identifier is not part of the wire contract `zeroclaw-api` owns, and `zeroclaw-log` records whatever attributes the gate hands it. Moving the vocabulary out on its own would split the gate from its refusals ahead of the kernel extraction that owns the RPC boundary, which is the case the exception policy describes. #11005 names `src/rpc/{auth,dispatch}.rs` and the catalogue among the work's likely files.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; documentation-only change to a Markdown table. Please review the row's scope against #11289 at `b5ca9dbb203676232e190026ce8b914c07734e90`: `git diff --stat dfe8ab35bd682e3510fe81856f27c0926742cd25 b5ca9dbb203676232e190026ce8b914c07734e90 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` lists the three files it names.

The refresh on `93c8bd374e` adds one exception row to master `d4a5d2afdd` and preserves every other row. The implementation at `b5ca9dbb20` has 31 reason variants and 24 named constructors. All 14 newly introduced locale keys are accounted for. The in-process refusal reuses `rpc-auth-inproc-token-required` with `AUTH_REQUIRED`. The row records the three Core decisions and their separate scopes. The refreshed file passed `git diff --check` and the documentation quality gate with zero markdownlint errors. The Ubuntu docs link gate passed all eight collector tests and found the three approval links. Each decision was also verified directly on GitHub.

The one-row amendment follows #11289 at `8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79` against master `afd6cf912e413c36a8ba7b23c55bb66d48e52782`: 30 reason variants, 23 named constructors, 24 other dispatcher refusal functions, and 14 added `rpc-auth-*` keys. The SOP and cron-principal constructors retain existing Fluent keys. The row records the revoked transport-owner refusal and cites @JordanTheJet's 2026-11-09 approval of the amended enumeration, keeping the note that the earlier decision covers only the prior enumeration.

`git diff --check` passed. prs.title: feat(gateway): show Codex subscription usage in web chat
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; stacked on the CLI/provider work in #12641 at `ea56e7cb8`. Until that PR lands, GitHub's Files changed view includes the dependency. [Web chat–only comparison](https://github.com/vadelma-agent/zeroclaw/compare/ea56e7cb8bf0c80a9d8fab87ee32d578be080eef...9e35182b7054972c176a981fd5c63dfd5b254c19).
- **What changed and why:** Add an on-demand **Codex usage** panel beside the chat model picker. Operators can see the subscription windows the provider reports (5-hour, weekly, or both), reported reset times, and when the check ran, even before the first message.
- **Scope boundary:** No background polling, inference, automatic model switching, new credentials, or separate Codex CLI dependency. This is not the Cost dashboard or a guarantee that a future turn will be accepted.
- **Blast radius:** Adds an operator-only chat WebSocket request and response. It reuses the native provider lookup from #12641. The usage-only auth reader refuses external secret references rather than launching a resolver subprocess; normal login and inference are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12641.

### What this does, simply

Before sending a message, you can check how much of the Codex subscription's short and weekly allowance is already used. The gateway chooses the account from the chat's native Codex route: the configured fixed route before the first message, or the installed route after initialization and a successful model switch. The browser cannot choose an account or endpoint. If the route or account access cannot be verified, the panel does not show numbers. Refreshes clear the previous result; a missing window is not shown as zero.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if you have an operator account and a configured native Codex route.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Pair as an operator or sign in as a dashboard administrator. Select an agent with a fixed native Codex primary route and an existing ZeroClaw OAuth login.
- **Steps to run:** Open a fresh chat. Before sending a message, open **Codex usage** beside the model picker and click **Check Codex usage**. If a second route is available, switch models and check again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Reported usage windows and local reset times appear without a chat turn. A switch clears the previous reading; a non-Codex or unverifiable route reports unavailable. Reconnect after a gateway configuration change if needed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The model picker has no subscription usage control.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted [Semgrep code scanning](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/runs/137826378773) passed on `b0edc5796` with no new alerts. The dependency audit reports the same advisory as [upstream `master` CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45149764803/job/137608134100); this stack does not modify `Cargo.lock`.
- **CI-only follow-up (`b0edc5796`):** The WebSocket admission test reuses the loopback-only request helper. The lint cleanup names the installed-route state and avoids cloning a test token; it does not change route selection or authorization. All 9 focused gateway tests and `cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the follow-up.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The browser smoke used a production WebUI build against synthetic loopback REST/WebSocket fixtures. It did not contact a real Codex account. The provider's live endpoint smoke is documented separately in #12641.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib codex_usage -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib read_oauth_access_only -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib codex_usage_route -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
  npm run typecheck
  npm test       # 202 passing tests
  npm run test:auth  # 225 passing tests; overlaps npm test
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  git diff --cached --check
  gitleaks git --staged --redact
  Docs Markdown lint: 0 errors; added-link gate: no added links.
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The loopback gateway test completes a usage check before the first turn, discards an in-flight response after a route change, and closes the socket without sending usage after administrator access is revoked. The credential tests cover local encrypted/plaintext access tokens and refusal of external references before resolution. An independent checkout-based review of the complete WebUI patch and relevant dependency code found no blockers; it was a source review, not a test run or maintainer approval.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot, Chromium, 1280 × 813, synthetic route and usage.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Final targeted offline test and review artifacts were checked against source tree `af9f436160da5d6c9c0cf0ace63d2ba0e92394b2`; the published commit adds only the evidence image to that tree. The browser and runtime routing checks ran on the preceding candidate with identical WebUI and runtime routing files. Browser evidence: `web`, chat model picker, `.pr-evidence/codex-usage-synthetic-chromium.png`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Open synthetic browser screenshot](https://github.com/vadelma-agent/zeroclaw/blob/9e35182b7054972c176a981fd5c63dfd5b254c19/.pr-evidence/codex-usage-synthetic-chromium.png).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Chromium showed both windows before any chat message. Opening the panel did not check usage automatically. Refresh sent only a usage frame, and a denied refresh cleared both previous percentages. Delayed model-picker label hydration did not discard an otherwise valid result.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live WebUI request or full local workspace run; the former is covered at the provider boundary in #12641 and the latter is left to hosted CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes. Adds an administrative capability, not a new permission grant or directory scope. It is denied on open gateways and scoped accounts, and access is checked again before replying to the initiating socket.
- **New external network calls?** Yes. An operator-initiated check uses the same bounded, fixed first-party read as #12641. No automatic refresh, browser-selected endpoint, retries, or redirects.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** Yes. The native usage-only read selects the existing ZeroClaw OAuth login and refuses references that would invoke an external resolver. The response contains no auth material, account IDs, or raw upstream errors.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No. The screenshot and examples are synthetic, and the generated conversation label was redacted from the screenshot.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No. No inference is started and the response is not written to the transcript or model prompt.

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Yes. Existing chat flows do not need to send the new WebSocket message.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No additional changes beyond #12641. The WebUI and chat WebSocket protocol add an optional action.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing installations. To use the panel, pair or sign in with the required operator access and select a native Codex route.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the WebUI follow-up or reinstall the previous matching gateway and WebUI build. The CLI/provider foundation can remain installed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The network read runs only when explicitly requested.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A check returns unavailable or the usage panel does not update; ordinary chat and the CLI should continue to work. No database or credential migration to undo.

## Supersede Attribution

Not applicable; this PR depends on, rather than replaces, #12641.

### Follow-up: display only reported windows

A weekly-only response shows only the weekly row. A reported window with a missing value still shows **Unknown**; a real zero still shows **0% used**. This is a WebUI-only change; the gateway and CLI JSON are unchanged.

On `5833a2e0a`, `cd web && npm test && npm run typecheck` and `git diff --check` passed. The new chat DOM regression failed against the prior rendering as expected.

prs.title: fix(providers): pair damaged tool results with the remaining call
prs.body:
## Summary

- Depends on #12704 and #12188. Related #12665.
- Recover the result ID and name together when a stored tool-result envelope is damaged and only one call remains unmatched in the current batch. Explicit IDs remain authoritative and go through the same provider-specific normalization as the assistant call.
- Consume answered IDs as results arrive. Once an anonymous result cannot be attributed, stop inferring IDs within that batch. Start fresh at the next conversation turn.
- The follow-up changes one provider source file. The GitHub diff against master also includes the parent PRs until they land. [Review the follow-up commit](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/2651c296d3e389c232f7ef7c5d001591471616e3).

### Landing after the parents

I simulated squashing the parents onto master at `d4a5d2afdd`. The stacked branches would conflict in `compatible.rs` if merged as-is after those squashes. Applying only `24a0cced8` after #12188 and only `2651c296d` after #12704 produced the exact published tree `2f5a29d32a53d19de91242405f1f6e358b018f02`. Refresh against the actual landed parent revisions and rerun CI before marking this draft ready.

### What this does, simply

When two tools ran together, replaying damaged history could accidentally give both results the first tool’s ID, or send a result without its name. Strict providers can reject that conversation. The adapter now tracks which calls still need a result and recovers the pair when the remaining evidence identifies it. A genuinely ambiguous result may still be rejected by a strict provider.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

Run `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib replay_pairs_parallel_result_ids_and_names_after_damage` and `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib a_new_turn_ends_id_recovery_for_the_previous_batch`. The first test supplies two differently named calls, returns the second one first and checks the name and normalized ID of each result. The second checks the new-turn boundary. Both run without a provider credential.

### How I tested

- On `2651c296d3`, this draft’s own workspace Test job passed the two converter regressions, both pairing tests, and the existing contract-ID and tool-name regressions. Lint and the required gate passed. [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/46100242449/job/140840801208) · [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/46100242449/job/140843858792)
- An independent Linux Rust 1.98 test checked the exact new pairing helper against all 4,283 permutations and missing-ID subsets for zero through five calls. It verified each inferred ID, explicit IDs after ambiguity, and the absence of duplicate pairings for those valid source batches. Two negative controls failed as expected when the helper was changed to reuse an answered call or guess in an ambiguous batch.
- `git diff --check` and Rust formatting passed. Visual evidence is N/A for request serialization. The testing used fixtures rather than a live provider account.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities or filesystem access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential handling changed? No.
- Personal data in fixtures? No.
- Model-visible changes? Yes. Tool results can recover the paired name and ID. Warning logs record the content length and omit its contents.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for intact, explicitly paired results. An anonymous result with multiple possible origins can no longer inherit an arbitrary call’s ID.
- Config, environment or CLI changes? No.
- Rust or toolchain floor changes? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert `2651c296d3` to restore the earlier pairing behavior. The parent fixes are independently reviewable.

prs.title: fix(providers): deliver declared OpenRouter tool-result images across chat paths
prs.body:
## Summary

- Fixes #12774. Related #12776.
- OpenRouter now delivers an image declared by a tool through the configured `tool_result_image_policy`. The default moves it into the following user message. `image_url` keeps it on the tool result. `omit` removes the declared image and adds an omission notice.
- Tool chat, streaming tool chat and history requests use the same native message conversion. The change is confined to the OpenRouter adapter and its factory.

### What this does, simply

When a tool returns an image, the model needs the image to make sense of its next step. The dedicated OpenRouter integration previously dropped it on the native tool path. The history method could instead send the entire attachment envelope as text. This change makes both paths honor the operator’s chosen delivery mode and keeps the result attached to its original tool-call ID.

The first commit preserves @tidux’s provider work from #12776. The follow-up commits add the history-path repair and compare the actual native-chat and history requests. The desktop implementation stays with #12776.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

Run `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib openrouter::`. The tests use synthetic inputs and a loopback endpoint. With two tool results followed by a real user turn, the regression compares the native chat and history request bodies for all three modes. It checks for the synthetic URI exactly once in the expected message for inline and relocated delivery, and zero times in the entire request for omission. It also checks the tool-call ID and ordinary request parameters.

### How I tested

- Compared the provider files taken from #12776 with the original contribution. Verified the split contains only `factory.rs` and `openrouter.rs`.
- `git diff --check` passed. The modified OpenRouter module passed the repository Rust formatter.
- On `502624bfcc`, hosted `Test` records PASS for `chat_with_history_sends_declared_images_according_to_policy`, default relocation, inline and omit behavior, and literal tool-body markers. The loopback regression makes six HTTP requests. Lint and the required gate passed. [Hosted test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/46099448359/job/140838421936) · [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/46099448359/job/140841700742)
- Visual evidence is N/A for this HTTP serialization change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. The adapter uses its existing chat endpoint.
- Secrets or credential handling changed? No.
- Personal data in the fixtures? No.
- New model-visible content? Yes. Only declared native tool image attachments become image parts. Tool body text stays text. The omission regression inspects the entire outgoing body.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. This applies the existing configured policy to OpenRouter.
- Config, environment or CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust or toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the provider change and its regression commits together. An operator can select `omit` to suppress declared tool-result images. Symptoms to check are an unexpected image in the outgoing request or a provider rejecting the message order.

prs.title: feat(web): enable browser voice for OIDC sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

An OIDC session needs `features.config` to open Browser Voice and Audio. Enabling voice and using the microphone and speaker in chat requires both `features.config` and `features.chat`, including in a fresh browser without device pairing. A Chat-only session cannot access voice settings or enable the OIDC controls. Preferences are stored per verified account in the browser, using a SHA-256 account digest. Capture and playback state reset when the account changes. The paired-device flow, dashboard permissions and global silence setting continue to use their existing paths.

## Merge order and scope

#12269 merged first in fa48765b3e3c80681d01d637b3629af37cb0398f. That merge is an ancestor of this PR head. The nine parent screenshots are outside this PR's diff. The URL/Ruma security remediation is inherited from master; Cargo.lock is no longer part of this PR’s diff.

## How I tested

Historical frontend evidence: `8ad61210cc6924f3849e3fecef79b285a05e566d`. Follow-up commit `50945fa04` changed only the permission documentation. Current rebase validation is recorded below; the linked earlier CI is not claimed as a run of the new head.

- Local Node 24: production frontend build and `npm run test:voice` passed, 42/42.
- [Hosted Web Permission Tests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45079738616/job/137385031992) explicitly ran `npm run test:voice` and passed **OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts**. The [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45079738616/job/137396536637) passed.
- Real Chrome and Keycloak OIDC on Jarvis, from fresh browser profiles with no paired token. The browser served the compiled frontend of this PR head only in the test window. Jarvis provided the real authentication and gateway endpoints. Entry asset `index-DFCfYcNp.js`. The build reused the generated dashboard API type inputs from the Jarvis integration. The voice source files were from the stated PR head.
- Both viewports showed the enabled settings and the chat microphone and speaker. The screenshot check did not record audio or test audible playback.

## OIDC evidence

### Desktop settings
![Browser Voice and Audio configuration on desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-settings-desktop-8ad61210.png)

### Mobile settings, 390 px
![Browser Voice and Audio configuration on mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-settings-mobile-8ad61210.png)

### Desktop chat
![Microphone and speaker in the OIDC desktop chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-chat-desktop-8ad61210.png)

### Mobile chat, 390 px
![Microphone and speaker in the OIDC mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-chat-mobile-8ad61210.png)




## Rebase validation (2026-11-23)

Rebased onto master `74c8af5cf` as `bb72687f8`. The branch is one commit ahead and zero behind that base. The old history carried copies of the already-merged #12269 parent; the refreshed branch contains only this PR’s seven-file delta. The complete diff is byte-identical to the pre-rebase delta at `95e01f1be5c3e768949d838fe11a68f1ca9c359c`. Administrator paired-device selection, account isolation, permission checks and narration fixes are preserved. No new interface change was introduced by the rebase.

Local Node 24.19.0, using the Windows Jiti equivalent of `npm run test:voice`:

```text
✔ OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts
ℹ tests 43
ℹ pass 43
ℹ fail 0
```

`git diff --check` passed. The voice runtime files, voice test file and npm lockfile are unchanged from the previous head. The local suite emits the existing react-test-renderer deprecation warning; no warning suppression or dependency change was introduced. The earlier screenshots remain historical evidence at their stated source revisions. New hosted CI is running for the rebased commit; earlier passing checks are not reported as current-head results.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose a holding-crate exception for Discord peer routes
prs.body:
## Summary

#12271 removes the Discord-specific branch introduced by its parent, #12116. This PR proposes a narrower ADR-016 exception for what remains in `zeroclaw-runtime`. It changes one row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, not the routing implementation.

- `send_message_to_peer` uses one config snapshot for the send and looks up the external peer's route in the sender's own groups. Conflicting routes are refused. The runtime forwards the peer or the configured destination with `PeerAddressing` through `deliver_announcement_addressed` and `DeliveryFn`. Ordinary announcements remain `Direct`.
- The row also covers the two existing test closures, focused tests, and English route messages. The channel declares whether it supports routes; the Discord adapter renders the mention and sets `allowed_mentions`. Neither responsibility is granted to runtime. Peer admission and agent-to-agent dispatch do not change.
- The destination owners and review condition are unchanged: the agent-loop/peer-delivery and cron owners reconsider this at the first relevant extraction review, or before routes cover another channel or an agent peer.

[Core's earlier approval](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12271#issuecomment-6879906154) was for the previous design. **Please confirm the narrower placement in the revised row before merge.** This is a placement decision, not implementation approval for #12271.

**Base:** `master`. **Related:** #12271, #12116, #10557.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer check:** Compare [#12116 `2c650ee7f` to #12271 `f6abbf66e`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/compare/2c650ee7ffa01391cd7d27db3acb2320ce5470ab...f6abbf66e8ef9460ce2042759e33e262ef710a7c). In `zeroclaw-runtime` only the tool, scheduler, two test closures, and two English catalogs change. Compare that with the route-support check and Discord mention rendering outside runtime.
- **Docs check:** Verified the PR adds one four-cell row and changes no other row or file. `git diff --check` passed. The docs quality gate found no book files; the link collector ran, and the prior approval link was checked directly via GitHub. No Rust build or runtime test: this PR changes no executable code.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, if Core approves: the row permits the named additions in the holding crate. It grants no runtime authority.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commit. If #12271 has merged by then, its code stays; reverting withdraws the permission for further additions under this row.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** None; documentation only.

prs.title: fix(gateway): validate on-disk config before admin reload
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base:** `master`. Previously `POST /admin/reload` acknowledged an invalid on-disk candidate and signalled teardown. Check the candidate with the existing strict config preparation and full validator **before** clearing the pending flag or notifying the gateway or daemon.
- Return HTTP 400 for a rejected candidate and name known settings using field metadata and fixed reasons, not validator messages. If an error has no safe location, give a generic refusal. Do not rewrite the file. Keep TOML source, proxy URL contents and secret-resolution error chains out of the response.
- **Scope / blast radius:** the HTTP admin endpoint, strict deserialization and validation diagnostics, and config lifecycle docs. No change to admission, cold-start recovery, RPC or other reload triggers. No change to draining in-flight work. No linked issue.

### What this does, simply

If a proposed setting is incompatible with another setting, the operator can fix the file and retry while the old gateway keeps serving. A successful request still *initiates* a reload: the supervisor reads the file again after drain. This is not an atomic snapshot swap or a guarantee that every subsystem can start; don't change the file between acceptance and readiness.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested:** Yes. **Interface:** web gateway's HTTP API, no messaging channel. Use only a disposable daemon with an isolated HOME, config, runtime paths and loopback port; not a standalone gateway or an existing installation.
- Start with the gateway under `/old`, SQLite memory and `memory.consolidation_extract_facts = true`. Confirm `GET /old/health` works. In the on-disk file, change `gateway.path_prefix` to `/new` and set one configured agent's `agents.<alias>.memory.backend` to `markdown`.
- `POST /old/admin/reload`, then make a fresh `GET /old/health` after one second. **Before:** the POST returned 200 and the listener was replaced. **After:** the POST returns 400 naming both settings, the old listener still serves `/old/health`, and the candidate file is unchanged.
- Change that agent's memory backend to `sqlite` and retry the POST. Expect 200 and then `GET /new/health` → 200 in the same daemon process.

### How I tested

Tested `4f95f9bf0a497f9f4b5182df8f979b0bca0924e9` in a loopback-only network namespace with a fresh HOME, install and runtime directory. The before case was verified on `d4a5d2afd`: the same memory conflict returned 200 and replaced the listener. On the revised head, the HTTP responses included:

```text
400 Reload refused: agents.probe.memory.backend: conflicts with memory.consolidation_extract_facts
400 Reload refused: heartbeat.agent: referenced entry does not exist
400 Reload refused: gateway.port: expected integer
400 Reload refused: schema_version: expected a supported schema version
```

Each refusal left the candidate file unchanged. Fresh connections still got 200 from `/old/health` on the original listener. Asserted the synthetic marker was absent; also checked missing and malformed TOML and a fixture generated with a different throwaway encryption key (`config generate 1 --encrypt`).

**Timeout and retry:** with `gateway.request_timeout_secs = 1`, a fake local secret resolver took three seconds. The POST returned 408 before resolution completed. After it completed and the delayed-shutdown window had passed, `/old/health` still returned 200 on the same socket. With the same file and a responsive resolver, retry returned `200 {"success":true,"message":"Daemon reload initiated"}`. `/new/health` returned 200 on a new listener in the same process. No timeout policy change.

```text
cargo build --offline --locked --bin zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,gateway   OK
cargo test --offline --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --no-run   OK
Isolated test binary: admin_reload 12 passed; migrate_refuses 2 passed
cargo fmt --all -- --check; git diff --check; docs quality and links gates   OK
```

**CI / gaps:** rely on normal required CI for the wider build/lint matrix. Did not run the full workspace suite, connect a real channel account, or exercise a graphical UI. No UI layout or client code changed; the user-facing evidence above is the HTTP response. The regression tests check neither signal fires after rejection, both fire after acceptance, and the migration response retains its underlying field diagnostic.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions or filesystem access scope: **No**. Same active installation's config and secret store, checked after existing admission and supervisor checks.
- New external network calls: **No new network endpoint.** Strict deserialization now uses the already-locked `serde_path_to_error` crate to locate a field without printing its value. Existing configured secret resolution now also runs at preflight and can invoke a configured external resolver; the smoke test used only synthetic local keys and a fake resolver.
- Secrets handling changed: **Yes**. Strict preparation resolves secrets before accepting reload. Don't return raw preparation error chains, source lines or invalid proxy URL values. No secret fixtures or real keys committed.
- PII in the diff / tests / docs: **No**. Prompt injection or model-visible text changes: **No**.

## Compatibility

- **Valid requests:** unchanged success response. **Intentional change for invalid candidates:** HTTP 400 instead of acknowledging shutdown. Fix the reported setting and retry; no upgrade steps or migration needed.
- Config/env/CLI surface changed: **No**. Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed: **No**.

## Rollback

Revert the merged PR (or revert `4f95f9bf0` followed by `c6ce2770d`) and rebuild. No feature flag, config rewrite or data migration to undo. Watch for a valid on-disk candidate unexpectedly returning `400 Reload refused`, or a rejected request causing the old health endpoint to disappear. Reverting restores the previous risk of tearing down before validating.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose the owner-plane routing row for bounded delegation (#9872, #10391)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10391 (the #9872 fix) makes a bounded delegate's target use the owner's plane when the session has an owner. The target's session memory route is pinned to the owner's plane for that target; the child of the rebuilt `spawn_subagent` runs on it, `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` start and advance runs and write their audit rows through it, and `sop_status` shows the runs of that plane and not the caller's. A hop whose target inherits one of those tools is refused when that plane cannot be opened.
  - Review on #10391 pointed out that `src/tools/sop_status.rs` is not in the path list of the ceiling-carriage row (#11652) or of any other row. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` says a feature pull request cannot grant itself an exception, so the record has to come from a separate change. #10391 also changes runtime paths that the #11652 row does not list (`src/composition.rs`, `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, `locales/en/cli.ftl` and the tests of the ceiling carriage); those are the subject of #12403, a separate pull request that is still open, and this row does not cover them.
  - This adds one row, directly under the #11652 row, for the owner-plane routing. The approval cell says "Pending Core Team approval on this pull request", the wording the table already uses for a row awaiting its decision. Every existing row is unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. The row adds no tool, route, delivery path, public API, capability kind or tool grant, and does not change approval, admission or budget authority. It does not cover independent delegation (its registry pins its own route in the native factory, `src/tools/mod.rs`), a delegate with neither a root nor a target configuration (the production registry sets a root configuration, so it does not build one, and such a delegate is not rebuilt: it keeps the caller's instances), the tools of a recipe or factory that builds them itself, or the SOP engine and its storage.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of the owner-plane part of #10391 under ADR-016. No runtime behavior changes here. This row and the composition-seam row proposed in #12403 both sit under the #11652 row, so whichever lands second needs its placement refreshed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9872, Related #10391, Related #11652, Related #12403

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core decision. #10391 fixes a lost-binding defect in bounded delegation, and in an owned session that fix also has to keep the work a target starts on the owner's plane for that target: before it, a target's SOP tools wrote their audit rows and read run status through the caller's plane. The change touches `sop_status.rs`, which no row names, and gives `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` a different route than the ceiling-carriage row describes. This row lists those paths and states the behavior, so Core can approve, narrow or refuse it explicitly. If it is narrowed or refused, the matching part of #10391 can be cut back to what the existing rows cover. One cost to know about: in an owned session a hop whose target inherits `spawn_subagent`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` or `sop_status` now opens the target's memory before it starts, so a memory source that cannot provide it refuses the hop even if the model would never have called the tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope only.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None. This changes a governance table, not a `surface` or `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A checkout of this branch and of #10391's head.
- **Steps to run:** Compare the row's path list with `git diff --name-only master...<#10391 head> -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_status.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_execute.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_advance.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/delegate.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/scoped.rs`, and check that each path is named by the new row or by the #11652 row; then read the claims in the row against the code they cite in the next section.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One added row with four cells; every existing table line unchanged; `src/tools/sop_status.rs` named by the new row.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `src/tools/sop_status.rs` is named by no row, and the #11652 row describes `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` only as ceiling carriage.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` runs markdownlint and the em-dash check on the changed file, and the docs link gates; it does not check the claims in the row. `CI Required Gate` for the rest. Live result: see the checks on this pull request.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after the docs and links gates. The claims in the row are not machine-checked; they are checked by reading, listed below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on commit `e643cc1d0c` (WSL, `BASE_SHA` = `master` `ad4c1f6c3a`, `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`):
  - `bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` → rc=0: `No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.`, `Linting docs files: crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, `markdownlint-cli2 v0.20.0 (markdownlint v0.40.0)`, `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
  - `bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` → rc=0: `Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).`, `No added links detected in changed docs lines.`
  - `python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py` → rc=0: `Checked authored Markdown links in 220 file(s); no broken local targets.`
  - `git diff --numstat ad4c1f6c3a HEAD` → `1 0 crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` (one added line, none removed).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each claim in the row against #10391's code at head `0f9890b856` (read on 2026-11-19):
  - the route is pinned to the owner's plane for the target: `delegate.rs` `route.pin(plane, …)` and `target_owner_scope = Some(owner_scope)` (~`:5904-5912`);
  - the hop is refused with the existing tool-initialization error and a log record that names the step, not the source's error: `bounded_owner_plane_refusal` (~`:1839`), the reason `"target_memory_unavailable"` (~`:5897`), `sealed_route_refusal` (~`:1850`) and the guard on the sealed registry (~`:6868`);
  - `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` take the target's route through their existing `with_session_memory` (present on `master`); `sop_status` is rebound through a crate-private method added in `sop_status.rs`;
  - `sop_approve` is not rebound: a refusing stub takes its place (`BoundedSopApproveDenied`, ~`:6050`; the stub is part of #10391, not of `master`);
  - the names of the tools that share the route and of those that only read it are two lists in `scoped.rs` (~`:382`, `:390`); the registry's memory-work check uses the first, the pipeline and `sop_approve`, and the hop uses both;
  - the exclusions: the native factory pins its own route (`src/tools/mod.rs:4062-4073`); the production registry sets the root configuration (`src/tools/mod.rs:5544`; it also sets the runtime, `:5524`), and the route is only made when a configuration is in hand (`delegate.rs` `rebuild_config`, ~`:5800`); the sealing pass uses a default config so no pipeline tool is minted (`delegate.rs` ~`:6829-6832`).
  The behavior itself is covered in #10391 by regression tests that were checked by reverting the guarded line. What I did **not** verify: that Core agrees the `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` routing fits the scope of the #11652 row; a skill wrapper around these tools was traced by reading only, not by a test, and the row says nothing about it.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch at `e643cc1d0c` on `master` `ad4c1f6c3a`; the code the row describes is #10391 at head `0f9890b856`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None of the three docs gates. Not run: the optional HTTP(S) link check, because the row adds no link and `lychee` is not installed on my machine; `cargo` checks, because no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A for the runtime. The row is a table entry (the record ADR-016 asks for) that approves code which keeps a target's work on the owner's plane for that target; it grants no runtime capability and changes no file system scope. One behavior the row's code introduces, so reviewers can weigh it: in a session with an owner, a hop whose target inherits `spawn_subagent`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` or `sop_status` now asks the caller's memory source for the target's memory, and is refused if the source cannot provide it. That includes a target that inherits only `sop_status`, which starts no memory work itself but shows the runs of the plane the route is pinned to. A target that inherits none of the four opens no plane.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` (one table row).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** None at runtime; this is a governance table.

prs.title: fix(memory): honor recall date bounds for suffixed Markdown logs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The date filter recognizes a bare date in a daily Markdown filename. When the filename also has a suffix, such as a session label or time of day, the entry is treated as undated and can appear outside the requested window.
  - Use the leading calendar date for daily filenames with dash or underscore suffixes, both of which memory hygiene already recognizes.
- **Scope boundary:** Recall time bounds for Markdown entries with dated filenames.
- **Blast radius:** When callers provide time bounds, daily Markdown entries with a date suffix now appear only in the applicable day range.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #7192, which added since and until support to Markdown recall.

### What this does, simply

When you search memory for a particular day, a daily file named 2026-01-02-0800.md belongs to January 2. Recall now uses that date, while core notes in MEMORY.md remain available in the same search.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The regression below runs the before and after cases.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI Test runs workspace tests through cargo nextest, including the memory integration test. CI Fmt checks Rust formatting. Upstream checks are pending until the PR is opened.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation covered keyword recall in a Linux Markdown workspace. Recent recall, other memory backends and cross-agent reads were outside this check.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-memory --test markdown_suffixed_dates -- --nocapture
Base with the test applied
  left: ["release checklist", "release follow-up", "release policy", "release preparation"]
 right: ["release checklist", "release policy"]
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
Head with the same command
test markdown_recall_applies_time_bounds_to_suffixed_daily_files ... ok
```

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The log filter compares timestamps as text. A whole-second bound ending in Z sorts after timestamps with a fractional part at the same second. Equivalent offset timestamps also compare as different times.

- **Scope boundary:** Timestamp bounds in the single-file and segmented log page readers.
- **Blast radius:** The log REST and RPC query paths use the same segmented reader. Legacy callers of load_page receive matching filtering behavior.
